# Śiva-mahāpurāṇam \[Eng\]

## Mahatmyam

## Chapter 1 - The glory of the Purana

Saunaka said- “O Suta, you are well-aware of the doctrines of all the Sastras, O Best of the learned people, O Great Lord, you speak out to me the gist of stories of the Puranas.”

The persons, getting involved in the worldly pleasures and passions, travel over the noble path, with their minds filled with devotion. How does their wisdom keep on increasing and how do they overcome their own mental short comings. You kindly deliver your discourse on these matters.

In this immensely sinful age of Kaliyuga, all the creatures have started behaving like the asuras or demons, what is the best path for their improvement.

You speak out the method to me, by which the task could be well established, which is best in the welfare padarthas, having the purifying effect. You kindly speak out the same quite convincingly to me.

You speak out the method to me, by which or with the use of which the persons with spotless clean mind getting free from all the sins, could achieve lord Siva.”

Suta said- “O Best of the sages, you are indeed graceful because a desire in your mind has developed to listen to the narration of the (divine) story, therefore I, quite thoughtfully narrate the best of Siva Purana.

This Purana deals with all the principles, increases the devotion etc. delights lord Siva, possesses all the divine merits, therefore, O Son, you listen to it, which is like the nectar for the ears.

This Purana is the best remedy for the biggest danger like the death, which bites like the snake and is the biggest danger. The Siva Purana is the best of all the Puranas. O Great ascetic, initially it was spoken by Lord Siva himself.

Thereafter, the sage Vyasa briefly narrated it at the instance of Sanatkumara, for the benefit of the people of the Kaliyuga.

Except the Siva Purana, there is no other remedy in the age of Kali, to purify the minds of the people.

O Best of the sages, only such of the intelligent person gets an opportunity to listen or read it, who has to his credit the noble deeds of the earlier births.

The Siva Purana is admittedly the best of the Sastras and is also the true form of Siva on earth, therefore, it should be read, narrated, listened studied and well thought over.

The best of a person who with the reciting or listening of this Purana with devotion, achieves Siva-loka quite easily, with all the means of pleasure.

Therefore all types of people should recites it. By listening to Siva-Purana all the desires of a person are fulfilled.

By listening to the Siva-Purana with devotion, a person is relieved of all the sins and enjoying all the pleasure in this world, ultimately achieves the Siva-loka.

The merits which cannot be earned with the performing of the Rajasuya and other yajnas, such great merit is achieved with the mere listening of the Siva-Purana.

O Great sage, such of the people who listen to this Purana should not be treated as humans, because they actually become the form of Siva.

Wherever the dust of the persons who listen to the Siva-Purana falls, it becomes a sacred or holy place.

The persons who become desirous of visiting the extremely holy place, they should instead listen with devotion, the narration of the Siva-Purana.

O Best of the sages, in case a person is unable to listen to the Siva-Purana always, then he controlling all the senses for just two muhurtas (a few moments only) should listen to it.

O Lord of the sages, in case a person is unable to listen to it daily, then he can do so in the auspicious months.

Otherwise, such of the persons who listen to the Siva-Purana for a muhurta (a few moments), or half of it or further half of it or for even a moment, they never have to face the misfortune.

O Great sage, a person who listens to this Purana, he, burning the vast thorny forest of grave sins, crosses the ocean of the universe.

O Great sage, the merit one earns by performing various types of charities or the merit one earns by performing of various types of yajnas the same merit is surely earned by a person with the hearing of the Siva-Purana.

O Great sage, in fact except to the listening of Siva-Purana in the age of Kali, there is no other better dharmo, which could make them achieve moksa.

The listening to the story of Siva-Purana or the reciting of the name of Siva, are like the Kalpavrksas for a human being and bestow the auspicious rewards. There is no doubt about it.

Such of the people who have stopped the religious activities in the age of Kali, lord Siva, keeping in view the welfare of such people, has composed the Siva-Purana.

Such of the people who consume the nectar, they become eternal but a person who consumes the nectar of Siva-Purana his entire family becomes eternal.

The story of Siva-Purana is extremely auspicious which "should be consumed like nectar, by all the people.” This should be repeated thrice, which removes all the doubt.

What could be said about the reward one gets by the reciting of Siva-Purana? It would be enough to say that (by doing so) that lord Siva starts living in the heart of his devotee.

The Siva-Purana has twenty four thousand verses and comprises of seven Samhitas and deals with the stories relating to devotion, knowledge (jnana) and vairagya (renunciation) therefore one should listen to it quite attentively.

The Samhitas included therein are Vindhyesvari Samhita, Rudra Samhita, Satarudriya Samhita, Koti-Rudra Samhita.

Uma Samhita, Kailasa Samhita and Vayaviya Samhita. These are the seven Samhitas included in the Purana.

This is the divine Purana, including these Samhitas and equates with Parbrahman and is said to be the bestower of the salvation.

This Siva-Purana comprises of the seven Samhitas. Whosoever, recites the same with devotion daily, is considered to be free from the worldly bondages.

O Munisvara, the human wonders in the universe overpowered with the darkness of ignorance till such time he does not listen to the stories of Siva-Purana. In other words after listening to the Siva-Purana all the worldly fetters of a person are automatically removed.

What is the use of listening to the other Sastras or the Puranas which create confusion in the mind. Therefore, one should listen to the Siva-Purana, which always thunders about the providing of the salvation.

The house in which the recitation of Siva-Purana is carried out, it is turned into a sacred place and the persons living therein are freed from all the sins.

Hundreds of Vajapeya-yajnas and thousands of Asvamedha sacrifices, cannot equate even the sixteenth ray of recitation of the Siva-Purana.

O Best of sages, a sinner could be called as such, till such time, he dose not listen to the auspicious narration of the story of Siva-Purana.

The seven rivers like the Ganga and others, (Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, Sarasvati, Narmada, Sihdhu, Kaveri) the seven cities (Ayodhya, Mathura, Mayapuri, Haridvara, Kasi, Kanci, Avantika and Dvarkapuri) and the region of Gaya, cannot equate with the auspiciousness of Siva-Purana.

In case a person is desirous of achieving of the salvation, then he should recite a verse or half of it, of the Siva-Purana daily.

A person who recites the Siva-Purana daily with its meaning, or recites only the verses of the same, he undoubtedly becomes the noble soul.

The one who listens to this Purana at the time of death, Lord Siva, getting pleased with his devotion bestows him his own place.

A person, who adores the book of Siva-Purana daily with devotion, he after enjoying all the pleasures in this world, ultimately achieves the place of Siva.

Giving up lethargy if a devotee adores the book of Siva-Purana wrapping it in a silken cloth, he always remains comfortable in the world.

The Siva-Purana is completely spotless, and auspicious. It is everything for the human life, therefore the people should respect and recite the same with devotion, which would bestow comfort in the present as well as the future world.

The Siva-Purana is the best of all and the destroyer of the sins, and bestows all the padarthas like dharma, artha, Kama and moksa. Therefore, all the people should listen to it with devotion, besides reciting it.

The people desirous of salvation, should consider Siva-Purana to be more auspicious than the Vedas and the treatises on lustory.

The Siva-Purana is indeed the best for the persons engaged on the task of self realisation. This Purana is a divine padartha and is fit to be adored by the noble people and removes all the three types of miseries. It always bestows welfare and is loved by Brahma, Visnu, Siva and other gods.

I adore Siva-Purana always with a devoted mind and pray that let lord Siva be pleased with me and bestow the devotion of his lotus like feet on me.

## Chapter 2 - Glory of the Purana

Saunaka said**-**

“O Magnanimous one, you are well aware of the supreme tattva, therefore you are quite graceful because you have narrated the divine story to us, which indeed is surprising.

This wonderful story, listened to by us is bound to destroy all the sins, purifies the mind and pleases lord Siva at the same time.

There is nothing comparable in the universe with this story. We have surely learnt about it.

O Suta, with the mere hearing of this story, which one of the sinners are not relieved of their sins? You kindly grace us by telling the same.”

Suta said, “Such of the people who always remain engaged in sinful ways, and wicked activities, who are degraded by nature and are always engaged in worldly passions, even they are purified with the hearing of this story.

The recitation of Siva-Purana and listening to it, both are said to by jnana-yajnas. With these, a person achieves all the pleasures during the present birth and salvation after this birth or after death. The complete recitation of this Purana, destroys all types of sins and delights lord Siva.

The greedy persons, indulging in falsehood, those denouncing the parents, deceitful ones and the killers of the human beings, are also relieved of all the sins by listening to the Siva-Purana, getting purified.

Such of the people who have fallen from their Varnasrama dharma or have fallen from their race, who are full of jealousy, such people also with he performing of the jnana-yajna of Siva-Purana are completely purified.

The deceitful people and those who are cruel by nature, are also purified in jnana-yajna in Kaliyuga.

Those who maintain their bodies usurping the wealth of the Brahmanas, and are always engaged in incestual practices or adultery, such people also get purified by joining the jnana-yajna of Siva-Purana in the age of Kali or listening to this Purana.

The people who always perform sinful deeds, are wicked, and of degraded nature, are also purified with jnana-yajna during the age of Kali.

The people full of blemish, the evil minded ones, who are disturbed by nature, are also relieved of all the sins, by participating in the jnana-yajna in the age of Kali.

With the listening of this Mahapurana and also by reading it, the terrific sins are washed out and the person enjoying all the pleasures in this world, achieves salvation ultimately, pleasing lord Siva at the same time.

In this connection a historical episode is being narrated; listening to which all the grave sins are washed out.

In the city of Kirata, there was an illiterate Brahmana who was very poor and earned his living by selling of juice. He never cared for listening to Puranas or visiting temples, or to perform other religious activities.

He never took his bath, performed sandhya or other noble deeds. He was known by the name of Devaraja and he used to cheat everyone including his own faithful people.

This Devaraja kept on fighting with Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras, and usurped their riches on one pretext or the other by beating them.

In this way, he collected a lot of money by evil ways, but that sinful person did not spend even a small amount for religious works.

Once the said Brahmana went to a tank for taking his bath, finding a. whore named Sobhavati there, he was infested with passion and became anxious.

Finding that a rich Brahmana had been attracted towards her the whore was very much pleased. He also got delighted by conversing with her.

Devaraja on the other hand intended to take her as his wife and she also wanted to be his wife. Thus having been influenced with the passions, both of them kept on wandering for a long time.

Both of them started behaving like a husband and wife while sleeping, eating, drinking and several other types of sports.

The parents of Devaraja besides his wife tried to dissuade Devaraja from following the evil path, but he did not listen to them.

One Devaraja, snatched away the riches of his parents and his wife killing them when they were asleep.

All the riches Devaraja snatched from his parents and wife were given over by him to the whore towards whom he had fallen in love.

Devaraja ate the things, the use of which was prohibited for the Brahmanas, which always increased rajoguna (the cause of vice) and tamoguna (property of darkness). He started taking of wine as well and started eating with her in the same vase.

As luck would have it, the sinful Brahmana once reached a city named Pratisthana, where he found a Siva temple surrounded by the ascetics.

Reaching the temple, the Brahmana caught high fever. Therefore, he was forced to stay there, where he started listening to Sivakatha daily from the Brahmanas of that place.

Thus listening to the story of Siva, the Brahmana died in a month’s time. The messenger of Yama arrived and binding him in fetters, carried him to the abode of Yama.

At the same time the ganas of Siva, clad in white garments, holding tridents in their hands, applying ashes over their entire bodies and wearing the garland or rosaries of Rudraksa arrived from Sivaloka. But without finding the body of the Brahmana, they got angry and proceeded on to the abode of Yama. They scolded the messengers of Yama, beating them at the same time. They got Devaraja released from their fetters. They made the Brahmana board the surprising type of plane and got ready to take him to Kailasa.

A tumult arose in the middle of the city, hearing which the Dharmaraja himself came out of his abode. Thereafter, Yama, finding the messengers to resemble Rudra, adored all the four messengers appropriately.

Yamaraja came to know of the factual position by means of his divine sight, but he did not discuss the matter, out of fear with the messengers of Siva. After the adoration of the Siva’s ganas by Yama, they proceed on to Kailasa, where they handed over Devaraja to the compassionate Siva and Parvati.

This story of Siva-Purana is graceful and auspicious, listening to which even the sinful persons achieve salvation.

Sadasiva happens to be Mahasthdna, Paramadhama and Paramapada which is conceived to be the highest place by the learned people well-versed in the Vedas.

The sinful person, who under the influence of greed, killed many of the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras, besides his wife and the parents, who was a drunker, such a sinful Devaraja was purified in the Siva temple in a moment.

## Chapter 3 - Renunciation of Cancula- a Brahmana widow

Saunaka said**-**

“O resplendent Suta, you are well aware of everything. By your grace have repeatedly been successful.

My mind feels delighted by listening to the episode of history, therefore you narrate another story relating to lord Siva, by which my devotion at the feet of the lord may go on increasing.

The people who consume nectar, can never achieve salvation, but the people who hear the nectar like story of lord Siva, their achieving of salvation becomes quite conspicious.

Graceful is the story of Lord Siva and so is the case with you O Suta, because one achieves Sivaloka simply by listening to this story.

Suta said, “O Resplendent Saunaka, you please listen to me. Though the story is quite secret, still I would like to reveal it before you, because you happen to be the foremost of the devotees of lord Siva and are well-versed in the Vedas

There is a village named Vaskala on the seashore, which is inhabited by the sinful people who do not believe in the Vedas.

Those people were of evil nature, wicked, unfortunate, harsh in their behaviour, lived on farming, were holders of weapons, misbehaved with the others wives and were quite foolish.

They were unaware of jnana (knowledge), vairagya (renunciation), besides the dharma which bestowed welfare on the people. They were evil minded and were devoid of wisdom like the animals and they engaged themselves in listening to the evil stories of their own faith.

The people of other varnas also lived there, who were also evil minded and did not believe in their own dharma were cruel, degraded and were always engaged in the worldly pleasures.

All the women of the village were of harsh temperament who moved at will, always desirous of committing sins, evil minded, unchaste, having misconduct, and were averse to noble conduct.

Thus in the habitation of the noble people, in the village of Vaskala, there lived an extremely degraded Brahmana known by the name of Binduga.

He had a wicked soul, was extremely sinful, followed the evil path inspite of his having a beautiful wife. Ultimately having been overpowered with the passions, he became the husband of a whore.

The degraded Brahmana, discarding his chaste Brahmana wife named Cancula, used to have union with the whore.

In this way much of the time of Benduga Brahmana was spent with the whore, enjoying all the conjugal pleasures. His wife Cancula, getting afraid of falling from her dharma, inspite of her having been infested with lust, also fell from her dharma.

But later on as her youthful health and boisterous virility increased, her passion’s onslaught became extremely unbearable for her and she fell from her virtuous conduct.

Thereafter she escaping from the sight of her husband, destroying her chastity, having a union with some other man, she took refuge in the evil way.

O Great sage, once Binduga Brahmana, found his wife Cancula becoming lustful, enjoying the union with some other man.

The said Brahmana, finding his wife following an evil path, and sleeping with another man was enraged and at once rushed towards her.

Finding the wicked Binduga arriving in his house, the deceitful lover, ran away from his house at once.

Thereafter the degraded Binduga caught hold of his wife and beat her with his fists scolding her at the same time and putting her in fetters.

Then Cancula who had started moving freely, after having been beaten by her wicked husband, she was enraged and becoming fearless, she spoke to husband thus.

She said, “O Evil minded one, discarding your young and chaste wife who had been devoted to her husband, you had been daily enjoying the company of that whore.

I am young, beautiful and remain infested with passions. You tell me, what would be my condition without enjoying the love sports with my husband.

I am extremely beautiful and am quite youthful and remain upset because of my passions. How could I manage without union with you.”

Suta said, “When the wife so spoke to her husband, then the foolish, wicked and degraded Binduga, spoke to her.”

Binduga said, “Having been infested with passions, whatever has been spoken by you is correct. Therefore I speak some welfare words to you, listening to which you shall be fearless.

From today onwards you can freely enjoy the company of your lover without hesitation. You must receive money, in exchange for your enjoying love-sports with him.

You give away that money to me, because I am attracted to the whore and by doing so, the purpose of both of us would be served.

Thus listening to the words of her husband, Cancula, the wife of the Brahmana was very much pleased.

With the development of the above understanding between them, both the husband and wife moved on the evil path which was quite sinful.

Thus having been engaged in evil ways, considerable time of both of them was passed.

Thereafter the husband of the evil and wicked woman died after sometime and fell in the hell.

The wicked Brahmana after suffering the pain of the hell for a long time was born as a pisaca (goblin) in the Vindhya mountain.

After the death of the wicked and sinful husband, the foolish woman Cancula, lived in her house with her sons for a long time.

The said woman Cancula, indulging in love-sports, kept on roaming about with her lovers for long and while so enjoying, her youthful age was over.

Once as a move of the destiny, the said woman went to the Gokarna-tirtha with her brothers and relatives.

After taking a bath in a particular tirtha, she kept on roaming about with her relatives quite casually.

Going to a Deva temple, she listened to a beautiful Pauranic story relating to Siva from the mouth of a Brahmana.

According to that story, the women who enjoy union with other men, neglecting their husbands, are carried by the messenger of Yama in the hell who place the burning iron musalas in their vaginas.

Thus listening to the story of Siva, from the mouth of the Brahmana, well-versed in the Puranas, which increased vairagya, Cancula, getting terrified started shaking.

After the narration of the story was over and after the departure of the listeners, she went to the orator when he was lonely and asked the Brahmana.

Cancula said, “O Brahmana, I have knowingly travelled over the evil path. Therefore, listening to my story, showering your enormous compassion, you kindly redeem me.

O Lord, because of my evil mind, I have indulged into enormous sin, having been infested with passion and lust, I have spent my entire youthful age.

Today, I, listening to your words full of vairagya I feel extremely fearful. The heart of the widow, has started shaking.

Disgrace to me who had been infested with passions and lust. I discarded the path of chastity, followed the deplorable sinful path. I, innocently, destroying dharma and the noble deeds, for petty gains and performed the enormous sins which are extremely painful and terrific.

Alas! I am going to face distress which would be enormously painful, who is going to save me from the hell because I had followed the evil path?

How would I face the terrific messengers of Yama, after my death? How should I be able to keep patience when the messengers of Yama would bind me by the throat? When the messengers of Yama would injure my body, and cause pain by several other means, then how shall I be able to bear them?

How could I be able to sleep in the night having been reminded of the misdeeds or sinful activities performed by me during the day.

Alas! I am dead, burnt out, my heart has burst out, I have been completely destroyed and I am extremely sinful.

Alas! O destiny, what have you done by making me an evil minded woman? It is surprising that a person is dragged away from dharma, which provides all types of pleasures and comforts. I am facing crores of times more pain emerging out the piercing of a thorn, or falling from the peak of the mountain.

There could be no repentance to my sins even with the performing of a hundred Asvamedha sacrifices, or taking bath in the Ganga for a hundred years. What should I do? Where should I go? With whom should I take shelter? Who would save me when I am drowning in the ocean of the universe.

O Brahmana, you are my preceptor, you are my parents. I have taken refuge at your feet. Therefore, you redeem a miserable person like me.”

Suta said- Thus having been influenced with vairagya, she fell at the feet of the Brahmana. Then lifting her up the intelligent Brahmana said.

## Chapter 4 - Redemption of Cancula- the Brahmana widow

The Brahmana said, “Because of good fortune, by the grace of Siva, you have woken up timely by listening to the story of Siva Purana which enlightens the people with the feeling of renunciation.

O Brahmana’s wife, don’t be afraid and take refuge with lord Siva. By the grace of Siva, all your sins would be immediately destroyed.

I shall narrate to you the story which highlights the yogic aspect of Siva, which would lead you to the life of comforts.

With the listening of the pleasant story of lord Siva, there has been such a change in your mind, which has made you repent. Your mind has been purified and has renounced the worldly pleasures.

The best remedy to wash out the sins is the repentance. The people with wisdom have prescribed repentance to get rid of all the sins.

Such of the people who cannot be freed with the repentance, they should perform the penance. The noble people have prescribed penance for all types of sins.

A person even after performing penance, is not mentally freed from fear of the sins nor can he achieve salvation, but a person who performs the penance is freed from the sins undoubtedly, and achieves salvation.

The way in which the mind is purified with the listening of the story of Siva Purana, such purification cannot be achieved by any other means.

As the mirror becomes spotless, after cleaning, similarly with the listening of the Siva Purana the mind is undoubtedly purified. Both Siva and Parvati reside in the mind of the people, when they are completely purified. Thereafter, such a person with a spotless soul, achieves the highest pada of Siva.

Therefore people of all walks of life should listen to this story. Because of this, lord Mahadeva, due to the extreme insistence of Parvati, had composed this story. With the listening of this story one’s mind becomes firm at the feet of Siva, the husband of Parvati. By meditation one attains knowledge. After attaining of the knowledge, one surely gets moksa.

The one who is not allowed to meditate upon lord Siva, or the one who listens to his story alone, he in the next birth is engaged in the meditation of Siva and then achieves the highest place in the abode of Siva.

With the listening of the story of this Mahapurana, and then meditating on Siva, several of the people performing penance achieve the siddhis (success).

To hear to the story of lord Siva, is the basic cause for all types of welfare. Therefore one should meditate upon Siva, in order to get rid of all the ailments.

With the listening of the story of Siva, or thinking about the same, by keeping it in mind always, the mind is purified in no time.

In this way, both the sons of Siva (Ganesa and Karttikeya) are also adored and by their grace the divine devotion is achieved.

Thereafter, the salvation is achieved undoubtedly.

It is true that a person, without the devotion of Siva is himself unable to get freed from the bondages of the delusion in the world.

Therefore, O wife of the Brahmana, freeing your mind from the worldly attractions, listen with devotion the story of Siva.

By listening to the story of lord Siva your mind would be purified and you would be freed from all the bondages.

A devotee, who, with a spotless and devoted mind meditates upon the lotus like feet of Siva, he achieves salvation in a single birth. I am speaking the truth to you there is no doubt in it.

Suta said- The Brahmana, who recited the Siva Purana in the temple of Siva, with a spotless soul and was a param-saiva who showered his grace on the woman, and then with his mind engrossed in the meditation of Siva, he became silent. Then the woman Cancula, was pleased, at the words spoken by the Brahmana and tears started flowing from her eyes.

Then suddenly getting pleased, Cancula fell at the feet of the Brahmana, and said, “I feel beholden at the words spoken by you.”

Canada said- “O Best of the devotee of Siva, O Svami, the bestower of the parmartha, O Brahmana, you are graceful. You are always engaged in doing good to others, therefore you have to be treated as the best of the noble persons.

O Noble Brahmana, you better redeem a person like me from falling in the ocean, by listening to the story of Siva relating to the Purana.

I have started feeling detached from the worldly pleasures. I have presently developed immense faith for listening to this Purana.”

Suta said: Thus speaking the woman Cancula, with the compassion of the Brahmana, with folded hands expressed her desire to listen to the Purana and got ready to serve the Brahmana.

Thereafter the Paramamahesvara and intelligent Brahmana, narrated the story of Siva Purana to her in the same temple.

Thus she heard the auspicious story of Siva Purana from that Brahmana.

Cancula also listening to the story of Siva Purana, which increased devotion, jnana, vairagya besides bestower of the salvation, she felt successful in her life.

With the grace of that noble preceptor, her heart was soon purified and by the grace of the lord, she meditated upon the true form of Siva.

Thus getting refuge with a noble preceptor, she developed in her the noble wisdom for achieving Siva. Thereafter she started meditating upon the conscious and blissful form of Siva.

She daily took her bath in the tirtha- water, developed locks of hair over her head, and clad herself in bark garments, applying the ashes over her body and use the Rudraksa beads as her ornaments.

She engaged herself in the reciting of the name of Siva, she maintained the vrata of silence, took little food, she started pleasing lord Siva, as per the path shown by the preceptor.

O Saunaka, in this way Cancula, meditated upon Siva appropriately for a long time.

In due course of time she was fully endowed with devotion, jnana and vairagya. Then Cancula, without much effort, met with her end.

Thereafter, the plane sent by lord Siva arrived there, which was variously decorated. The ganas of Siva having the divine form were seated in the vimana.

Because of the destruction of all the sins, Cancula boarded the plane and the messengers of Siva carried her to Sivapuri.

At that point of time, the body of Cancula was turned into a divine form. She herself also looked divine. All her limbs were shining. She was adorned with all the ornaments like Parvati and the crescent moon appeared over her head.

Reaching Sivaloka she found that the gods like Brahma, Visnu and others were serving the Sanatana Mahadeva.

Ganesa, Bhrngi, Nandikesvara, Virabhadra and other ganas were adoring lord Siva with devotion. Lord Siva had the lustre of crores of suns, who was being worshipped by gods.

She found that the throat of Siva was of blue colour, had five heads, three eyes. The crescent moon was lodged over the head. Gauri having the lustre of lightening was lodged to his left.

She found that Siva was adorned with all types of ornaments and his body was plastered with white ashes. He was clad in white garments and his complexion appeared like comphor.

The woman Cancula finding Siva in this form was immensely pleased and she started offering her salutation to him again and again.

With her heart filled with love, folding her hands, with pleasing mind, shedding blissful tears, she felt extremely delighted.

Then both Siva and Parvati cast a compassionate glance over her. Then they called her and made her sit in their vicinity.

Parvati on her part, lovingly made Cancula, the wife of Binduga, as her hand maid and showered all the divine pleasures on her.

Then Cancula in the eternal abode of Siva, was filled with light, achieving the infallible abode, started living there enjoying all the comforts.

## Chapter 5 - Salvation of Binduga

Saunaka said, “O Graceful Suta, you are quite magnificent and fortunate, your mind is always devoted to the devotion of lord Siva. The story of Cancula narrated by you is quite surprising and increases one’s devotion towards Siva.

In this way, after having been redeemed, Cancula, proceeded on to Sivaloka and started living there. O Immensely intelligent Suta, you also tell me what happened to Binduga-her husband?”

Suta said, “Cancula, once came to Parvati and with folded hands she offered her salutation to her and blissfully offered her prayer to her.”

Cancula said- “O Goddess Girija, you are the mother of Skanda- Karttikeya and bestow all the comforts and pleasures. You are the beloved of Siva and are the form of Brahman. Therefore all the men and women serve you.

Not only that even Brahma, Visnu and other gods also serve you. You have both the visible and invisible forms. You happen to be Adi-Prakrti. You have the subtle sat, cita and ananda (bliss) forms.

You create, maintain and destroy the universe, you are known by Triguna (sattvas, rajas and tamas) forms. You are the refuge of all the three gods, and you also establish them.” (This eulogy is according to the Sakta principle).

Suta said, “Then Cancula who had achieved liberation (became emotional) and her eyes were filled with tears of love, lowering her head, she kept quiet after offering prayer to Parvati.

Then Parvati, the beloved of Siva, and affectionate to her devotees, spoke to Cancula, with compassion and love.

Parvati said, “O Beautiful handmaid Cancula, I am extremely pleased with your prayer. You ask for any boon you like. There is nothing which cannot be given to you.”

Suta said- At these words of Girija, Cancula offered her salutation to her appropriately and folding her hands with devotion lowering her head she asked her.

Cancula said, “Where is my husband at the moment? I am unaware of the condition in which he has been placed at the moment. My only desire is that I should live with him. You kindly do something for the purpose. O Parvati, you shower welfare on all, are compassionate on the miserable people and you are the best of all the goddesses. My husband was visiting the whore, but that sinful person died ahead of me. I know not in which condition, he is placed.”

Suta said- “Thus listening to the words of Cancula, the goddess Girija who had always been graceful to her devotees, lovingly replied.

Girija said, “O Daughter, your husband Binduga, was extremely sinful, had degraded thoughts, lover of whores, and was immensely foolish. After his death he fell in the hell.

The sinful person had to suffer miseries for many years in the different hells, and then became a pisaca (goblin) in the Vindhya mountain because of the remaining sins. Even the wicked Binduga suffering from several types of pains inhaling air only, is leading a miserable life in the Vindhya mountain.”

Suta said, “Thus listening to the words of Parvati, Cancula, with noble thoughts, felt extremely painful (knowing about the miserable condition of her husband).

Then, she, making her mind stable, and offering her salutation to Parvati, with painful heart asked again.

Cancula said, “O Goddess Parvati. O Mahadevi, you kindly redeem my husband who had been indulging in evil ways since long.

O Goddess, you kindly tell me, the way by which my sinful and degraded husband with evil wisdom could be redeemed from the miserable condition. You tell me.”

Suta said, “Then Parvati, to whom her devotees are quite dear, feeling delighted said to Cancula.

Parvati said, “In case your husband can listen to the story of Siva Purana, which bestows merits, then he would be relived of his miserable condition and would be redeemed.

Thus listening to the nectar like words of the goddess Gauri with respect, Cancula lowered her shoulders with folded hands and offered her salutation again and again. Then she prayed to Parvati that she should do something for the destruction of her husband’s sins and move in such a way that her husband is in a position to listen to the story of Siva Purana.

Suta said, “The woman Cancula offered prayer to Parvati, the beloved of Siva, again and again. Thereafter the goddess Gauri, possessing enormous fortunes was pleased with Cancula.

Thereafter Parvati summoned lovingly, Gandharvaraja Tumburu, who recited the glory of lord Siva and said to him.

Girija said, “O Tumburu, you are loved by Siva, therefore you obey my command. You go to the Vindhya mountain with this woman. You would be bestowed with welfare.

A huge and terrible pisaca lives there. I tell you his life story from the beginning and you listen to it attentively.

In earlier birth this pisaca had to been a Brahmana named Binduga. He had been the husband of my handmaid. He was attracted towards the whore.

He never took his bath nor did he perform sandhya or other noble deeds. He always remained unclean. Because of anger, he had lost his wisdom. He consumed the unedible things, was inimical with the noble people and earned his living by evil means.

He killed the creatures, always carried the weapons with him. He took his food with left hand and always tortured the poor people. He was cruel and merciless and lighted the houses of others.

He loved the degraded people, visited the harlots, was extremely clever, and disowned his wife. The sinful person always kept the company of the wicked people.

He lost all his merits with keeping company of a harlot and becoming greedy for money he made her own wife as unchaste fearlessly.

Till his death he followed the evil ways and he died ultimately. Thereafter he fell in the terrific hell, where the sinful people have to reap the reward of their sins.

Reaching in the hell, he had to face the reward of his sins in several types of hells. He was thrown out of the hell and is now suffering the agony of his remaining sins in the Vindhya mountain, as a terrific pisaca.

You better go there and recite before him the auspicious story of the divine Siva Purana which destroys all the sins.

By hearing the story of the divine Siva Purana, he would soon be relieved of his form of pisaca, getting free from all the sins.

When the pisaca Binduga after listening to the auspicious story of Siva Purana, achieves salvation, then you make him board the plane and carry him at my command, to lord Siva.”

Suta said, “At these words of the goddess Parvati spoken by her to Tumburu- the lord of Gandharvas, then Cancula felt herself to be quite fortunate in her mind.

Then Tumburu, who was quite dear to Narada, boarded the beautiful plane with the chaste Cancula- the wife of Binduga and reached Vindhyacala in no time.

Reaching there he found the pisaca having a terrific and gigantic body, vast chin, who was sometime laughing, sometime weeping, sometimes jumping from one place to another.

The valorous Tumburu, who was always engaged in reciting the prayer of Siva, forcefully caught hold of the pisaca and bound him with ropes.

Then deciding to perform the parayana (reading the book from beginning to end of Siva Purana, he made arrangements with all the festivities.

At the command of Parvati, Tumburu reached the Vindhya mountain, in order to get the pisaca freed by reciting of the Siva Purana.

The news about the parayana of Siva Purana was spread in all the three worlds. Therefore the gods as well the ascetics arrived there in large number for listening to it, and the place was therefore crowded very much.

There was a surprising crowd there, which was for the welfare of all. All of them had collected there in order to listen to the recitation of Siva Purana.

The pisaca was made to sit there bound with ropes. then the king of Gandharvas holding the vina in his hands started singing the story of lord Siva, playing on vina.

Starting from the first Samhita, ending upto the seventh Samhita, together with glory of the Purana, Gandharva-raja Tumburu sang over the vina quite clearly.

Listening to the story of Siva Purana comprising of seven samhitas the listeners became successful in their desires.

Listening to the extremely meritorious story of Siva Purana, the pisaca was relieved of all the sins as a result of which he shed away his form as pisaca.

Soon he attained a divine form. He got a fair complexion and a divine body. He was clad in white garments and was adorned with all the ornaments. He appeared graceful like the three eyed Siva having a crescent over his head.

Then with his divine body, and accompanied with his wife Cancula, he started reciting the divine story of Siva and Parvati.

Finding the wife of Binduga with him, all the gods were surprised and were delighted at heart.

Listening to the astonishing life stories of lord Siva, all the gods started singing the glory of Siva collectively and retired to their respective abodes.

Binduga on the other hand, having been transformed as the auspicious soul, mounted over a beautiful plane, looked graceful, while flying in the sky with his wife.

Then Binduga accompanied with his wife and Tumburu, singing the auspicious merits of lord Siva, soon reached at the highest place of Siva.

Reaching there both Siva and Parvati welcomed Binduga, who was then included by lord Siva in his army of ganas, while Cancula was taken by the goddess Parvati, as her handmaid.

Both Binduga and Cancula, by achieving a place in the blissful, illumining and eternal abode of Siva, felt extremely comfortable.

This historical story, which removes all the sins has been narrated to you, which increases the spotless devotion and bliss.

Whosoever, listens to this Purana with devotion, or performs its recitation in the form of parayana, he, after enjoying all the pleasures in this world, ultimately achieves salvation.

## Chapter 6 - Method of listening to the Purana

Saunaka said, “O Suta, the fortunate one, you are extremely intelligent and are the disciple of the sage Vyasa. Salutation to you. You are graceful all your virtues are worth highlighting.

You kindly tell us the method of listening to the Siva Purana, by which all the listeners should achieve the best of the fruit.”

Suta said, “O sage Saunaka, I am now going to tell you the method of the achieving of the complete reward of the listening of the Siva Purana.

Summon an astrologer in your house, who should be pleased by offering the daksina by all the members of the family and ask him the auspicious time at which the recitation should be started for a successful end.

Thereafter the news should be spread in all the countries, about the recitation of the Siva Purana and the people desirous of their own welfare should attend the same.

Some of the people remain away from Hari-katha, while others keep off from the Sankirtana of lord Siva. Besides the above, all the men, women, Sudras and others should also be invited to enable them to gain knowledge. The news should be sent everywhere.

All the devotees of Siva, who might be anxious to listen to the name of Siva and his recitation, should be respectfully invited for the hearing of the Sivakatha.

The ascetics should also be invited with a message that at the completion of the Siva Purana surprising festivities would be celebrated.

In order to consume the nectar like juice of *Siva Purana,* with respect, you kindly arrive here with a devoted heart.

In case you have no time to listen to the complete Purana, then you should attend atleast part of it. Whatever might be the case, you should arrive, because such opportunities are quite rare in the life.”

Such type of invitation should be humbly sent and when the devotees arrive to join the recitation, they should all be honoured appropriately.

A beautiful mandapa (pavilion) should be made in a Siva temple, a sacred place, or in one’s own home, for the listening of the Siva Purana.

The place at which the mandapa has to be prepared for the purpose of recitation, the land of that place should be purified. Then it should be plastered and decorated with red ochre or the powder of the metals. Then auspicious formations should be made with the red colour.

Such of the things which are not of daily use in the house should be removed and kept concealed properly in the corner of the house.

The mandapa should be raised and decorated with the trunks of the banana trees. The flowers and fruit should be collected in large number and the balconies should be prepared decorating them with flowers and fruits on all the four sides.

The mandapa should be decorated with flags and banners on all the sides (while doing so,) one should remain devoted at the feet of lord Siva, who bestows all types of bliss.

Performing oblation a divine seat should be left for lord Siva and a comfortable seat should be kept for the speaker.

O Great sage, appropriate seating arrangement for the (ascetics or other) listeners should be made and ordinary listeners should also be provided with the appropriate seats.

The arrangements which are made for the people for the joining of the marriage of the girl, similar arrangement should be made with the auspicious intentions. O Saunaka, during that period, one should free himself from the worldly attachments.

The Orator should face towards the north, while the listeners should face towards the east. The listener should sit with legs rolled round. No controversy should be picked up during this time.

The eastern direction has been considered to be the best between the worshipper and the worshipped or otherwise the speaker should face the listeners.

When the Brahmana narrating the Purana occupies the seat of Vyasa, then till such time his narration is completed, no one should disturb him till then or offer even salutation to him.

The narrator of the Purana, could be of any age viz. boy, young man or an old man, irrespective of his being a poor or a rich person or even a weak person. The people desirous to gaining merits should extend all respect to such a person, adoring him at the same time.

The person well-versed in the Purana, should never be looked down upon, because the words spoken by him, serve like a kamadhenu (with fulfilling cow) and fulfils all the desires.

After the time of the birth, many of the people, are like the preceptors, because of their high merits, out of all of them the one who is well versed in the Purana is indeed the best.

The reason is that the jivas feel painful situations on earth, having been born in crores of yonis, therefore the one who showers nectar with the reciting of the Purana, which lead to the salvation, is indeed is the best. There could be no other preceptor better than him.

Only such of the person deliver discourse on the auspicious Siva Purana, who is well-versed in the Purana, is quite pure, clever, peaceful by nature, free from jealousy, should be noble by heart, is compassionate on all the creatures and is a good speaker.

Since the morning to the end of three and a half praharas, the learned person should recite the story of the Siva Purana and speak out the same to the listeners.

This Purana should not be recited before the people, who are wicked, are ill mannered and wicked, who are desirous of defeating others and are the degraded ones.

The narration should not be made before the wicked people, or the country infested with thieves and decoits, or in the house of the cunning or the deceitful people.

During the noon time the narration of Siva Purana should be stopped for a muhurta to enable the orator and the listeners to get themselves relieved of motion or easing etc. Even after getting relieved of the same, one should keep on devoting his mind towards the story of Siva.

The orator should have his hair cut a day before the start of the narration. All the daily routines like sandhya and others should be performed quite briefly.

An other learned person having the similar type of qualifications, should be designated as the helper of the orator. Such a helper orator, should be able to explain the problems of the narration as well as remove the doubts of the listeners.

For the removal of the obstructions in the recitation of Siva Purana the lord Mahaganapati should be adored. Siva, the lord of the recitation as well as the Book of Siva Purana should also be worshipped.

A person with noble wisdom should particularly listen to the story of Siva Purana with respect. The listener should also get himself mentally and bodily purified.

The listener whose mind is engaged in various matters, or is filled with the blemishes of kama, krodha (anger) etc., the one who is attracted towards the woman, who is a cheat, is not entitled to attaining the merit for the listening of this Purana.

A listener who setting aside the worries of the world, the riches, the house, the son and others, or the devotes with his spotless mind and concentrates towards the listening of the story, he achieves the best of the reward.

Such of the listeners whose minds are filled with faith and devotion, detracting their minds from other worldly affairs, and listen quietly with their minds and bodies purified the Siva Purana attentively, they achieve enormous merits.

The degraded people who listen to the meritorious story without devotion, they earn no merit of listening to the Sivakatha.

Such of the foolish people, who without offering the presents according to their capacity and without worshipping it, listen to the Sivakatha, they instead of getting purified, become paupers.

Such of the people, who roam about here and there after the start of the Sivakatha, their wives, sons, and riches are lost in the next birth.

The listeners who listen to the Sivakatha wearing turbans over their heads, their sons become sinful and earn blemish for the race.

Such of the persons who listen to Sivakatha while chewing the betels, after their death, the messengers of Yama, force them to consume their own refuse.

Such of the people, who listen to the Sivakatha seated at a place higher than that of Vyasa, they after their death, suffering all the pains of the hell are reborn as crows.

Such of the people who listen to the Sivakatha seated in Virasana etc. they suffering all the pains of the hell are ultimately are born as the poisonous trees.

Such of the people who listen to the Sivakatha without offering their salutation to Vyasa, they, in the next birth, after suffering several pains of the hell are born as the arjuna tree (Terminallia alatagoba).

Such of the people, who, without suffering from any ailment, listen to the katha, lying down, they after suffering all the pains in the hell are born as python in the next birth.

Such of the people who listen to the katha occupying a place comparable to that of Vyasa, they earn the sin of humiliating the guru.

Such of the people who denounce the orator as well as the katha, they, after suffering all the pains in the hell are born as dogs.

When the recitation of the katha is on, one who denounces the same he, after suffering several severe pains of the hell is reborn as donkey.

Such of the people who never listen this auspicious katha, they suffering all the pains of the hell are reborn as wild boars.

Such of the people, who create obstruction in the recitation of the katha, they suffer the enormous pains in the hell, become the village pigs and consume the human refuse.

In this way both the orator and the listener should recite and listen to the katha, with utmost devotion.

In order to avoid any obstruction in the recitation of the katha, Sri Ganesa should be adored and after performing daily routine the repentance should also be made.

He shall worship the nine planets, and deities in the Sarvatobhadra style. He shall worship the book as per the rites of Siva’s adoration.

In addition of Ganesa, the nine planets like Surya and others, gods of Sarvatobhadra, lord Siva and then Siva Purana should be adored. At the end of the adoration, one should humbly, with folded hands, offer prayer to Siva Purana as follows.

“You are Siva Purana and represent lord Siva himself. I have decided to listen to your parayana; therefore be pleased with me.

You bestow success to my desire, to enable me to listen to the katha without any obstruction.

O Lord Siva, the crocodile in the form of the bondages of karmas has enslaved me. I am your slave and am drowning in the ocean of the universe. You kindly make a miserable person like me to cross the ocean of the universe.

This Siva Purana is the form of Siva himself’- reciting these words with devotion, the Vyasa should be adored.

The orator (Vyasa) should be adored in the same way, as Siva is adored, offering the flowers, cloth, ornaments, incense, lamp, and other materials.

After the completion of the worship, the listeners should follow all the regulations according to his means upto the end of the katha.

The listeners should adore the orator of the Purana, thus- “You are yourself the form of Vyasa, bestow the best of knowledge, you are an expert in the Siva Purana with the light of which you remove the darkness of ignorance in us.

For the purpose of performing of japam, five or one Brahmana should be selected with devotion. All of them should continue to recite the Siva-mantra.

Suta said, “O Saunaka, I have explained the proper method for listening to the Purana with devotion. Now you tell me, what more do you want to listen from me?”

## Chapter 7 - Description of the worship of the book and the orator (speaker)

Saunaka said, “O Intelligent Suta, you are graceful, foremost of the devotees of the lord, the story you have narrated is quite surprising and bestows welfare on all.

O Great sage, those who listen to Siva Purana performing the vrata and for the welfare of the entire universe, you kindly spell out the related regulations.”

Suta said, “O Saunaka, listen to the related regulations. Because with the listening of this katha appropriately, one achieve the best of the reward free from obstructions.

The persons without diksa are not entitled to listen to this katha. Therefore, O Best of the sage, whosoever is desirous of listening to this katha must received mantra-diksa from the acarya who narrates Sivakatha.

The one who has taken a vrata to listen to the katha, he must observe a celibacy or vrata or Brahmacarya, should sleep on the ground, should consume fruit alone on a leaf-plate. Such food should be taken daily at the end of the katha.

Or a listener who is quite healthy, should keep fast till the end of the katha, getting purified. He should listen to the story of Siva Purana with devotion. One should listen to the katha with comfort consuming ghee or the milk.

The orator or the speaker should consume fruit or take food once in a day and recite the Siva Purana.

The one who has observed vrata for the listening of the katha, he should have havisyanna food only once a day or he should make arrangement by which he could be able to listen to the katha appropriately.

Even when one is inclined to listen to the katha after his taking food, then he should take light food. In case an obstruction is created while keeping fast, then fasting would not be undertaken.

Heavy items of food which digest after long time, all types of pulses, burnt food, kidney beans, defiled pulse, the stuff polluted by feeling and state food, should not be consumed by the listener.

The Brinjal, watermelon, snake gourd, radish, pumpkin, coconut etc. should not be consumed by the listener who listens to the katha daily.

Onion, garlic, as asafoetida, carrots and other intoxicating drinks should not be consumed by the person listening to the katha daily.

Indulging into six types of blemishes, like, passions, anger, greed, delusion, arrogance and cheating are prohibited besides the denouncing of the Brahmanas, the chaste women, and the noble people who are engaged in the listening the Sivakatha daily.

One should not look at the women in period and the Siva story should not be repeated to the degraded persons, or to those who are jealous of the Brahmanas, or those who are not entitled to recite the Vedas. The person listening to the Sivakatha should not talk to such people.

The listener of the Sivakatha should daily remain truthful, pure, compassionate, silent, simple, and maintain large heartedness.

In case this katha is listened to by a person with a desire or by a person without desire quite regularly, then the desire of the former is fulfilled, while the latter achieves moksa.

The persons who are poor, suffering from consumption and other ailments, sinful, unfortunate, and those having no sons, should listen to this katha with devotion.

The seven types of shortcomings including having a child only once, usually found in the women or those who have to face abortion repeatedly, should listen to the Siva Purana.

O Best of the sage, all the men and women should listen to the story of Siva Purana with devotion appropriately.

The days whenever the parayana of Siva Purana is performed, are considered to be the most auspicious days and are like the performing of the crores of yajnas.

During these days whatever little is given with devotion, appropriately, it bestows unlimited reward which is everlasting.

Performing the vrata in this manner and listening to Sivakatha, the performer of the vrata should observe udyapana or the religious rite performed at the end of an observance.

The complete method for the performing of udyapana is the same as that of Caturdasi. Therefore the noble persons should perform for achieving of the best reward.

The devotees of Siva, who are poor, for them there is no necessity of performing of udyapana rites. They are purified with the mere listening of the Sivakatha, because they have no desires.

After the festive celebration of the sacrifice of the discourse on Siva Purana, is conclude the listener shall perform the worship.

The book of Siva Purana should initially be adored like Siva himself appropriately. Thereafter the orator should be adored.

To cover the book of Siva Purana new and fresh and durable cloth would be given and the silken cord should be given to bind it.

Such of the devotees, who give away the new cloth and the cord for the covering of the book of Siva Purana, they enjoy pleasure for many births and achieves jnana as well.

The orator should be given several types of valuables and the best cloth and ornaments.

Such of the people, who give away the blankets, deer skin, silken cloth, pedestal, wooden board, to serve as a seat to the book, they reaching the heaven, enjoy all the divine pleasures there, occupy the Brahmapada for a kalpa and finally achieve Saivapada.

By adoring the book in this manner the orator should be adored with great festivities.

The person with similar qualifications who had been engaged to help the orator, has also to be adored similarly, but the amount of his daksina has to be a little less than that of the orator.

The Brahmanas arriving at the place of recitation, should be given charities like food, money etc. as well. At the end of the katha there should be singing, dancing besides arranging of other festivities.

O Great sage, in case the listener is an ascetic then as a special arrangement, on the day next to the ending of the recitation of Sivakatha, the Sivagita which was spoken by Siva to Rama, should be recited.

In case the listener is a house holder, then the wise people should perform homa with pure ghee of a cow for the santi of the katha.

O Great sage, listen, reciting every mantra of Rudrasamhita, or the Gayatri as the gist thereof, or with the reciting of the verses of Siva Purana, one should perform homa, appropriately.

Or otherwise reciting the mantra om namah Sivaya, homa should be performed. In case the host is unable to perform the homa then the articles kept for offering in the homa should be given over to the Brahmana.

For the removal of whatever shortage or excess types of blemishes are there at the time of the reciting of the Purana, one should recite Sivasahasranama himself or should listen to it.

In this way the hearing of the entire Siva Purana meets with success. There is no doubt about it, because there is nothing more important in this world, except this in the three worlds.

Eleven Brahmanas should be served the honey and the payasam, giving them appropriate daksina for the completion of the vrata.

In case the listener is quite well off, then he should make a lion weighing three palas (twelve tolas) get the important verses of this Purana engraved on it and should be consecrated appropriately. Then offering the daksina one should adore the same. The intelligent listener should adore it offering the costumes, ornaments, fragrance, flowers etc. and give it to the learned acarya having controlled all his senses, for the pleasure of Siva.

O Saunaka, in this way, with the influence of the charities, earning the grace of Siva, a person is relieved of all the worldly bondages.  
In this way, with the listening of the complete Siva Purana appropriately it bestows the desired reward besides the moksa.  
In this way, I have spoken everything to you. What more do you want to listen from me? The glory of Siva Purana fulfils all the desires.

The Siva Purana has been treated to be the best of all, which is immensely dear to lord Siva. It is quite pleasant, and redeems one from all the worldly bondages.

The people who have taken birth on earth, and those who are devoted to lord Visvanatha and offer always prayers to Siva, whose both ears listen to the praise of Siva, they easily cross the ocean of the universe.

I take refuge with lord Siva, who pervades in the universe in the forms of sattva, rajas and tamas, who spreads the light of his glory inside and outside the world, who always pervades, the mind, the speech, who is blissful beyond measure and is known as Paramasiva.

## Vidyesvara Samhita

## Chapter 1 - Discussion on Sadhya and Sadhana

Salutation to Ganesa; first of all Vidyesvara Samhita is being started. I meditate upon Siva the lord of Parvati who is the form of welfare in the beginning as well as at the end of the universe, who has similar feelings for all which are unprecedented. Therefore he is always engaged for the welfare of his devotees for all times to come. He is the best of all, who is free from the bondages of the birth and death, who is self illumining, having the five faces, who is competent enough to remove the five types of grave sins which cause obstructions in the achieving of the salvation, I adore such a type of lord Siva with my devoted heart.

Vyasa said, “In the Mahaksetra of the Dharmaksetra at the confluence of the Ganga and the Yamuna, there is an auspicious and sacred place like the path of Brahmaloka, known as Prayaga.

The great ascetics, who were praised by all, possessing all the knowledge, who were truthful, immensely illustrious, enormously fortunate started for a long time yajna.

Learning about the performing of a yajna there, the great sage Suta, the disciple of the sage Vyasa, foremost of those knowing about the mysteries of the Puranas, arrived there to meet the ascetics.

Finding the arrival of Suta there, all the sages present there were delighted. Getting pleased, they all adored him appropriately.

Then all the sages were happy and with folded hands they praised him appropriately and submitted to the sage Suta, quite humbly.

“O Omniscient sage, we all feel beholden with your arrival here. Because of the height of our fortune, you have been able to attain the knowledge of all the Puranas.

Therefore you happen to be the treasure of all the astonishing episodes of the Puranas, in the same way as Ratnakara (ocean) happens to be the abode of the diamonds.

You are well aware of all the events of present, past and future and nothing is unknown to you.

Your arrival here is a matter of great fortune for us and you will not leave this place without doing enormous good to us. This is certain.

Even earlier we had listened from you many of the good and evil stories. But our mind does not feel satisfied by listening to the same. We want to listen to those types of the stories again and again.

O Sage Suta, possessing the noble wisdom, presently we intend to listen from you only one story. In case you are graceful on us then narrate the same story.

Reaching in this terrific Kaliyuga, the people would be devoid of the merits, all would become wicked and start indulging in falsehood.

They would engage themselves in denouncing others, would be desirous of usurping the wives and riches of others. They would enjoy pleasures with the wives of others. Besides they would torture and even kill others.

They would treat this body as the soul, besides being foolish, atheists, having animal like wisdom in the world shall denounce their own parents, adoring their wives like the gods, and would be passionate by nature.

The Brahmanas would be greedy, would earn their livings by selling the Vedas, would be devoted to the earning of the wealth, and feel intoxicated by getting educated.

They would fall from their own Varnasrama-dharma. Usually they would cheat others. They would never perform sandhya thrice a day and would be deprived of the knowledge of Brahman.

They would be merciless, consider themselves as learned inspite of being fools. They would never perform Vratas of the noble conduct, would be engaged in ploughing the fields. They would be of harsh temperament and would have deceitful minds.

All the Ksatriyas would also be devoid of dhama and the noble deeds. They would never take the side of the noble people, would be engaged in the sinful ways, and would be extremely wicked.

They would be cowards by nature, would avoid the battle ground, would take to fleeing and they would earn their living by stealing like the thieves. The Sudras would always be engaged in passionate designs.

They would have no knowledge of the use of weapons. They would discard the dharma of serving the cows and the Brahmanas, and would never save the people seeking refuge with them. They would be engaged in sports with their beloveds, and would look like the deer or animals.

They would be deprived of the dharma of serving the people and would always by engaged in the worldly pleasures. They would be instrumental in the destruction of the people. They would be wicked and kill the creatures without any reason.

The Vaisyas would be deprived of their samskaras and would leave their dharmo. They would follow the degraded path, would always be engaged in earning wealth, by using the evil tricks of the trade.

They would never be devoted to the preceptor, the gods, or the Brahmanas. They would always possess evil wisdom and would never serve food to the Brahmanas. Usually they would be miserly and would never give away anything in charity.

They would enjoy the conjugal pleasures with the wives of others as the second husbands and would possess the ugly ideals. They would always be caught in greed and delusion. They would discard the meritorious deeds like the digging of the well, setting up of gardens etc.

Thus those who are Sudras, would conduct like the Brahmanas. They would possess beautiful complexion become foolish and would desert their own religion.

They would perform the tapas, steel away the glory of the Brahmanas, become killers of the children, and would become the reciters of the Vedic hymns.

They would adore Saligrama-sila and Sivalinga, arranging for the homas as well as the yajnas at the same time. They would be of opposite thoughts, wicked at heart, and would be inimical to the Brahmanas.

They would become wealthy, would be engaged in evil deeds, become learned, develop controversies, would discourse on dharma and scriptures, besides destroying the real dharma.

They would clad themselves like the kings, would be deceitful, project themselves like the great donors, extremely proud and would force Brahmanas and others to be like their servants and themselves project as their masters.

They would be irreligious, foolish, of mixed castes, possessing the wicked wisdom, extremely arrogant and would devote themselves in the destruction of the dharmas of all the varnas.

They would project themselves to be of high caste and make the other people faithfully following their own dharma, to fall from the righteous path. They would be fools and would act like the Brahmanas.

The woman would also indulge in misconduct and would never obey the command of their husbands. They would be envious of their parents-in-law. They would be fearless and would eat the prohibited things.

They would be of deplorable activities and temperament. They would be anxious and passionate. They would enjoy conjugal pleasures with their lovers (instead of the husbands). They would move against their husbands.

The offsprings would not be interested in the service of their parents, would be of evil mind, practising the harmful vidyas and would suffer from various types of ailments.

O Suta, thus what could be the position of the people who discard their own dharma, in this as well as in the future world. How would they, achieve salvation.

We always feel worried for the same. Surely there is no other dharma better than doing good to others.

You please tell me presently some easy method, by which their sins could be destroyed, because you are well-versed in all the Puranas and other scriptures.

Vyasa said- Listening to the words of the omniscient sages, Suta, adoring lord Siva in his heart, thus spoke to them.

## Chapter 2 - Reply to the question of the sages

Suta said, “O Great sages, you have put me a very good question, which is for the welfare of all the three worlds. Because of the love you have for me, I, bowing in reverence to my preceptor, give a reply for the same.

The Siva Purana happens to be the gist of the Vedas, which redeems the people of all the sins and bestows moksa after death.

In this Siva Purana the glory of Siva is contained which removes all the sins in the age of Kali. Therefore, O Brahmanas, it bestows the reward for all the dharma, artha, kama and moksa.

O Brahmanas, with the study of this Purana, a person achieves the best of Sivapada (after death).

It is surprising that the sins like the Brahmahatya and others could stand only till the rising of the Siva Purana in the world.

It is surprising that all the horrible disturbances in the age of Kali, move, only upto the time, the recitation of the Siva Purana is not started in the world.

All the Sastra quarrel among themselves till the Siva Purana does not rise in the world.

Even the great yogis are unable to understand the real form of Siva till the rising of the Sun like Siva Purana in the world.

The wicked messengers of Yama, wander hear and there in the world, till the rising of Siva Purana in the world..

All other Puranas thunder in the world, till the rising of the story of Siva Purana on earth.

All the holy places pick up the controversies in the world till the rising of Siva Purana on earth.

All the mantras uselessly quarrel among themselves in the world till the rising of the Siva Purana on earth.

All the tirthas, quarrel with one another till the rising of the story of Siva Purana on earth.

All the divine places on earth quarrel among themselves till the rising of the story of Siva Purana in the world.

All the charities enter into controversies in the world, till such time story of Siva Purana does not rise in the world.

Upto that time alone the gods enter into discussion on earth till the rising of the story of the Siva Purana.

All the principles clash on earth only upto the rising of the story of Siva Purana in the world.

O Brahmanas, I am not in a position to speak out the reward, one achieves by listening to the reciting of the story of Siva Purana.

O Brahmanas with noble souls, still, I would like to place before you some of the glories of the Siva Purana, which had been spoken to me earlier by the sage Vyasa. You please listen to me attentively.

With the reciting of a single verse or half of it, from Siva Purana, with devotion daily, by a person, he is relieved of all the sins in a moment.

The one who recites the Siva Purana discarding laziness, with devotion, he is freed from the bondage of the worldly life.

The one who adores the Siva Purana with devotion daily, he undoubtedly achieves the rewards of an Asvamedha sacrifice.

In case a person listens to the Siva Purana from others, for achieving an ordinary position, he, because of my grace is relieved of all the sins.

The one who offers his salutation to the book of Siva Purana from the close quarters, he achieves the reward for the adoring of all the gods. There is no doubt about it.

The one who presents a copy of this Siva Purana writing it with his own hands to the devotees of Siva, you listen to the reward he gets for the same.

The reward which is difficult to be achieved by the study of the sastras and the Vedas, he also gets the same.

Keeping fast on the fourteenth day of the fortnight, the one, who, in the assembly of the devotees of Siva, delivers discourse on this Purana, he becomes the best of the human beings.

The reward one gets with the purusacarana of the each one of the letter of the Gayatri-mantra, the same could be achieved with the recitation of this Purana. He enjoys all the comforts of this world and ultimately achieves salvations.

Observing fast on the fourteenth day of the fortnight, keeping himself awake during the night, the one who recites this Mahapurana or listens to it (he gets enormous merits) which I am going to tell you.

The merit one gets at the time of solar eclipse at Kuruksetra, by giving charities is equal to one’s own weight (tuladana), given away to the Brahmanas (like Vyasa and others), the same reward is received by the aforesaid person. This is true, there is no doubt about it.

The one who arranges the singing of the story of Siva Purana throughout the day and night, even the gods like Indra and others, remain anxious to obey his command.

All the noble deeds performed by a person while reciting or listening to the Siva Purana, he gets the reward crores of time more (than the ordinary one).

The one who recites the Rudra Samhita with an alert mind, he gets purified even from the sin of Brahmahatya within the three days.

The one who recites Rudra Samhita quietly before the image of Bhairava, thrice, he gets all his desires fulfilled.

The one who recites the Rudra Samhita seated under a banyan tree or the wood-apple tree going round it, he is relieved of the sin of Brahmahatya.

The glory of Kailasa Samhita is far greater than the Rudra Samhita, which is the form of Brahman and reveals the meaning of omkara.

Only Siva is aware of the complete glory of the Kailasa Samhita. The half of its glory is known to me.

Therefore whatever I am going to speak about it could not be taken to be complete, by listening to which the minds of the people are purified.

O Brahmanas, there is no sin in the world which cannot be destroyed with the recitation of Rudra Samhita, because I have never come across such a type of the sin even after strenuous search.

Lord Siva, after churning the ocean in the form of Upanisads, had extracted the nectar, which was given over by him to Kumara Karttikeya, consuming which he became eternal.

For the removal of the sins like the Brahmahatya and others, the people should recite this Samhita for a month, which is bound to free them from the sins.

The sin one earns, by accepting the money from prohibited characters, or by the words which should not be spoken or to which one should resort to, are all destroyed with the reciting of this Samhita.

The one who recites this Samhita in a Siva temple or the forest of wood-apple trees, he achieves he reward which is beyond the description of my speech.

A person, who reciting this Samhita during the days of Sraddhas, serves food to the Brahmanas, with devotion, all his moves achieve the supreme position with Siva.

Fasting on the fourteenth day of a fortnight, sitting under the shade of a wood-apple tree, one who recites this Samhita, he is treated like Siva himself and even the gods adore him.

The other Samhitas also bestows the desired reward. Both of them should be treated as the best; because both of them contain the knowledge and the sports of Siva.

Therefore this Siva Purana has been equated with the Vedas, which was initially composed by Siva himself.

Because of the inclusion of the twelve Samhitas like Vidyesvara, Rudra, Vinayaka, Uma, Matr Ekadasa, Kailasa, Sata-rudra, Koti-rudra, Sahasra-koti, Vayaviya and Dharma represent the twelve parts of this Purana.

Since it comprises of the twelve Samhitas, it is extremely auspicious one. O Brahmanas, I shall now speak about the number of the verses in these Samhitas, which you please listen with respect.

The number is given below:-

(I) Vidyesvara 10,000 verses  
(II)& Rudra and Vinayaka 10,000 verses  
(III)  
(IV) & Uma Samhita and 16,000 verses  
(V) Matr  
(VI) Ekadasa Rudra 13,000 verses  
(VII) Kailasa Samhita 6,000 verses  
(VIII) Sata-rudra 3,000 verses  
(IX) Koti-rudra 9,000 verses  
(X) Sahasra Koti 11,000 verses  
(XI) Vayaviya 10,000 verses  
(XII) Dharma Samhita 12.000 verses  
1.00.000

Thus Siva Purana initially had a lac of verses Vyasa briefed it reducing the number to twenty four thousand. This is presently the fourth Siva Purana comprising of the seven Samhitas. There were three Siva Puranas in between the earliest and the present one, which are not traceable during the present times.

At the beginning of the creation of the universe, the number of the verses of Siva Purana was a hundred crores.

The sages like Vyasa and others in the Dvapara-yuga, distributed the Purana in eighteen parts, briefing them by reducing them by four lacs of verses.

On the basis of the number of slokas, it is conceived to be of twenty four thousand verses. It contains seven Samhitas which are attributed to Brahman.

These Samhitas are as follows:-

(I) Vidyesvara Samhita  
(II) Rudra Samhita  
(III) Sata-rudra Samhita  
(IV) Koti-rudra Samhita  
(V) Uma Samhita  
(VI) Kailasa Samhita  
(VII) Vayaviya Samhita

Thus there are seven Samhitas in all.

These seven Samhitas are included in this divine Purana, which is equated with Parabrahman and bestows the best of the position.

A person, who recites the seven Samhitas with respect, he achieves salvation during this life itself.

The Vedas, Smrtis, Purana, history and hundreds of other scriptures, cannot equate or even slightly compare with the Siva Purana.

This spotless Siva Purana was composed by Siva himself. Vyasa, the devotee of Siva, collected it in brief. It, while doing good to all the men, removes three types of sufferings, bestows welfare on the noble people.

In this Siva Purana dharma has been described without any sort of deceitfulness. The mystery of Vedanta based on science is its main subject. It is to be known by the spotless learned people. It bestows dharma, artha, kanta and moksa to the learned people on the basis of their karmas or performance.

It is the best of all the Puranas, therefore it is also called the Satya Purana. There is a mention of divine mothers in it like Vedas and Vedanta. Whosoever listens or reads this Purana with devotion, such a devotes of Siva, surely attains the place of Siva.

## Chapter 3 - Discussion on Sadhya-sadhana

Vyasa said, “Thus listening to the words of Suta, the Maharsi said, You better relate to us the wonderful stories of Siva Purana which comprise of the gist of Vedanta in totality.”

Listening to the words of the ascetics, the delightful Suta, bowing in reverence to lord Siva, spoke to the Maharsis.

Suta said, “O Sages, you please listen to me. I am going to recite the story of Siva Purana which is the gist of the Vedas, offering my salutation to lord Siva.

In this Purana the subjects like devotion, knowledge and vairagya besides other matters which are worth knowing have been discussed.”

O best of sages! Now you listen to Siva Purana which is the gist of the Vedas. From ancient times with the passage of the kalpa again and again and with the arrival of the Sveta-varaha-kalpa, and at the beginning of the creation, the six ascetics of the pure race, expressed their respective opinions.
