“This Purana is great, but not the best.” This type of great controversy developed. Then all of them went to Brahma the eternal one, to find out the solution from him.

All the sages spoke to Brahma with humble voice folding their hands. They said, “O Creator of the Universe, you are the cause of all the causes. Who is the creator of the five Mahabhutas, who happens to be the oldest one, and is beyond all the tattvas born out of Mahat?'

Brahma said, “Wherefrom the speech returns along with mind not attaining him. Wherefrom all the gods like Brahma, Visnu and Siva emerge, together with the gods, panca-mahabhutas with the organs?

He is called lord Mahadeva who is omniscient and is the lord of the entire universe. He could be visualised with extreme devotion, otherwise he remains invisible.

Even the gods like Rudra, Hari (Visnu) Hara and other gods, besides their lord, as well, getting devoted to lord Mahadeva, become desirous of having an audience with him.

What else could be stated in this connection. With the devoting of the mind towards Siva, a person gets redeemed. The devotion of the god can be achieved with the grace of the god and with the devotion of the god, he gets pleased.

Therefore, O Brahmanas, you go to the earth and start a yajna to be completed in a thousand years in order to please Siva.

In the same yajna the mysteries of the gist of the vidya propounded in the Vedas, would be revealed by the grace of Siva, besides its power, means and the gist.”

The sages said, “All right, you please tell us as to what is extremely attainable for a human being and what are the means for it? What type of means should be made use of for the same? You kindly give us the purposeful replies to these questions.”

Brahma said, “The object to be achieved in this connection is the devotion of lord Siva and the purpose is to always remain devoted to lord Siva. The devotee should be such, who would be unmindful of the reward or the heaven in the form of everlasting and the fortuitous (deeds performed by him.

With the performing of the karmas as propounded in the Vedas, the one who dedicates the reward thereof to lord Siva for the achieving of the Sivapada, such a devotee gains the sayujya devotion (intimate union) of the lord.

With the performing of the same type of devotion a devotee earns the same type of reward. Lord Siva has defined several means for the sake of his devotees.

I am going to reveal the gist of the same. You should listen to them with the attentive ears and recite them with your tongue.

To repeat them again and again in the mind is called the means. Therefore one should listen to the merits of lord Siva, recite them in the form of kirtana, and should keep on muttering them always.

This sruti is authentic in the above passage and there is no other means. Therefore in order to collect all the means, the people should make Siva Purana as the only means.

It has been stated in the Vedas, that one should initially take care of the soul, then listen to it, but this goes against the human behaviour, because the soul cannot be visualised easily and no attraction develops for a padartha without looking at it. Therefore one should first listen about his caritra (conduct) and then engage himself in the other activities.

Therefore, after listening to the Purana initially from the mouth of the preceptor, then the learned person should resort to its kirtana or recitation.

In this sequence, when a person gets the means of understanding, only then he would be able to achieve Siva-yoga and then the salvation.

By doing all this, all the worldly ailments are removed and all types of bliss is also absorbed in the same. During the initial stages, one has to face several difficulties, but it ends in enormous comfort.

## Chapter 4 - The glory of listening, recitation and study of the Purana

The sages said, “O Brahma, how is the thinking, listening or the recitation of Siva Purana resorted to? You kindly tell us correctly the method of the performing the same.”

Brahma said, “The adoration, japam (muttering), the qualities of Isvara, pleasure and reciting of the name of the lord, purifies the mind and it is called the thinking, which could be achieved by the grace of the lord. This is the best of all the means.

The prayer of lord Siva, which is offered with the singing of the Veda-mantras or the eulogy offered in one’s own language, about the adventures of lord Siva, and the praise of his virtues offered with the sweet voice is called kirtana (recitation with music). This is treated as the middle of the path.

By whichever means the words in praise of Siva enter the ears, which are pleasant like the sports of the women, is called sravana or listening by the people of wisdom, which is well-known in the world.

First of all with the association of the noble people, one listens to the merit of the noble people, then the sound of Pasupati’s qualities is heard which inculcates deep devotion in the mind ultimately with the grace of lord Siva. This is the best of means.

Suta said, “O Sages, I am going to relate an ancient episode in connection with the means for the devotion of Siva.

In the ancient time Vedavyasa, the son of the sage Parasara, our preceptor, was performing tapas at the bank of the river Sarasvati.

At that very moment, my preceptor, Parasurama spotted Sanatkumara, moving on, boarded in a plane illumining like the sun.

Inspite of having been in deep meditation he woke up and offered his salutation to the son of Brahma and then asked him.

He offered him arghya-padya and the seat fit enough to be occupied by the gods. Thereafter feeling delighted, Lord Sanatakumara spoke to the humble Vedvyasa with deep voice.

Sanatakumara said, “O Great sage, do you meditate upon the truthful Siva tattva? Siva helps you, who could be visualised by the organs of senses. Then what for are you performing the tapas.

At these words of Sanatakumara, the sage present there started revealing his thoughts. You hold in high honour the dharma, artha, kama and moksa and the path prescribed by the Vedas.

By your grace, I have specifically consecrated my mind to the lord in the world. I happen to be the preceptor of all in this world.

The supreme knowledge of advaita (non-dualited) fails to develop in my mind. I am unaware of the reason for the same. Therefore I am performing tapas for the achieving of the salvation.”

When Vedavyasa, thus spoke to Sanatakumara, then Sanatakumara highlighted before the Brahmanas present there, the definite cause of salvation.

He said, “According to the Vedas, there are three best means for the achieving of salvation which include listening to the good qualities of Siva, kirtana and recitation and the study of the same.

Initially, I too had to wander following other means, and started performing tapas over the Mandaracala mountain.

Then Nandikesvara arrived there at the command of lord Siva. He was quite compassionate on me, while lord Ganesa happens to be the witness of all.

He lovingly enlightened me about the best means for achieving the salvation. He told me that the listening, reciting and study of the qualities of Siva are the means propounded by the Vedas for the achieving of the salvation.

These means were told to me for the achieving of the salvation by Siva himself. He said to me, “O Brahmana, you should resort to the use of these three methods, again and again,”

Thus speaking to Vedavyasa, Sanatakumara, the son of Brahma, mounted over his beautiful plane and left the place.

O Ascetics, in this way, I have narrated to you the earlier story.” The sages said, “O Suta, you have highlighted three methods like listening etc. for achieving of the salvation.

A person who does not resort to these three methods, how could he be able to achieve salvation?”

## Chapter 5 - The glory of Siva-linga

When a person is unable to adopt the three means of adoration like the listening and others, he should establish Siva-linga in the form of the body of lord Siva and adore it daily. By doing so, he would cross the ocean of the universe.

Without cheating the god he should offer as much riches to Siva-linga as he can. All the padarthas which are kept for the worship should be offered to the Siva-linga as the form of the body of Siva. He should always remain devoted to the same.

He should build a mandapa, a gopura, a tirtha, a matha and a ksetra for the sake of Siva and organise festivities as well and should offer him costumes, fragrance, flower garland, incense, lamp, etc.

Besides these, various types of food, naivedya, fried sweet items, and other edible stuff should be offered to him, including the chatra flag, fan, flywhisk, etc.

For the adoration of Siva in the form of linga or the body, all the adorable material should be like those of the kings. After performing of pradaksina and salutation, one should perform the japam (muttering) according to one’s capacity.

Right from the stage of invocation, to the stage of departure, the adoration of Siva should be made daily with devotion. In this way while adoring the Siva-linga or the body of Siva.

Leaving the three means as already explained above, the people achieve success in the worship of Siva by his grace. With the mere adoration of Siva-linga or the body of Siva, many people were redeemed in the ancient times.”

The sages said, “All the gods are adored in the form of images, then why is Siva adored in the form of linga as well as the image?”

Suta said, “O Sages, this question is quite surprising and increases the merits. Lord Siva happens to be its speaker and no one else.

I have heard from the tradition of preceptors, that this Sivamahapurana was composed by Siva himself, who himself is the form of Brahman. Therefore, he is called niskala.

He is called saguna because of his being beautiful, saguna is called sakula spotless and niskala means devoid of art or beauty. Because of his being niskala he is called invisible or without form. The formless Siva takes the form of linga.

Because of his being saguna, he is conceived with form. Because of his having saguna and nirguna form (with form or formless), he is called as sabda-brahma or the best of all.

He is always adored in the form of linga or the image or the body. Except Siva no othergod has been called as sabda-brahma. Therefore they could never be called as niskala.

This is the reason that no other god is comparable with him, who could be adored in the form of nirguna or absolute god, because he is not but jiva. Similarly other gods are also there.

Being the form of silence and absolute, and being invisible form, the body or the image is worshipped. All other gods except Siva, have jiva in them while Siva possesses the form of Brahman.

Because of his having the essence of Vedanta and because of bringing to light the meaning of Omkara, the Upanisads are the witness. The same question was asked from Nandikesvara over the Mandaracala mountain from Sanatakumara, the intelligent son of Brahma.”

Sanatakumara said, “Except Siva, all other gods, are overpowered by their devotees.

In the adoration of other gods their images or the bodies only are seen or are heard. But in the adoration of Siva, linga and the images are both adored.

Therefore you explain to me the topic in an easily understandable manner.” Nandikesvara said, “Though your question relates to Brahman and is of secret nature, as such its reply cannot be given.

Still since you happen to be a noble soul, and a devotee of Siva, therefore, whatever has been heard by me from Siva, I am going to repeat the same to you. Siva is the form of Brahman and is devoid of digit, therefore he is treated to be absolute.

All the Vedas accept the form of the adoration of linga. This is the nirguna form of Siva. Because of the association of the digit with him, he has the qualities of saguna.

As saguna, Siva is adored in the form of images. Except Siva, all other gods are adored in saguna form.

The Vedas also admit the image worship. When the gods appear their in their concrete form. In the sastras relating to Siva, both his linga form as well as the images are adored.”

Sanatakumara said, “O Auspicious one, you have mentioned about the worship of Siva-linga as well as his images.

You have also mentioned about Siva and other gods. Therefore, you tell me about the genesis of the great linga as well as the images of Siva.

O Yogindra, we intend to listen to the same.” Nandikesvara said, “O son, you listen to me. Keeping in view your devotional feelings. I am going to reveal before you the factual position.

In the first Sveta-Varaha-Kalpa in ancient times and as is well known in the world, there had been a great war between Brahma and Visnu. In order to remove the arrogance of both of them lord Siva, appeared in between them in the form of a column.

Thereafter lord Siva, for the welfare of the creatures of the world,, of the absolute Siva, turned himself in the form of linga, which issued immense lustre.

From that day onwards, the niskala form of Siva came to be known in the form of linga and was also established in the form of image which bestows all the comforts and the pleasure to the people. But the worship of Siva-linga as well as his images bestow welfare to the people, besides the moksa.

## Chapter 6 - Fight between Brahma and Visnu

Nandikesvara said, “O Yogindra, once in earlier times, lord Visnu was sleeping gracefully over the serpent bed, surrounded by Garuda, and other attendants.

At that point of time, Brahma, well-versed in the Vedas, arrived there of his own sweet will and questioned the lord Visnu who was lying in his serpent bed.

He then asked him, “Who are you? You are sleeping like an arrogant person even after finding that I have arrived. O Son, you get up and meet me. I am your master and have arrived here before you.

Finding the adorable preceptor having arrived before you. You are behaving like an arrogant person. The one who does so, he has to repent for the same, being a fool.”

Listening to the words of Brahma, lord Visnu was enraged within, but out worldly he remained peaceful and said, “O Son, let welfare be ‘ bestowed on you. You are welcome, you take your seat here.

Presently, you have an upset like face. Your eyes are curved.” Brahma said, “O Son Visnu, presently, because of the influence of the time, you have become proud.

O Son, I happen to be your protector, and the great grandfather of the universe.” Lord Visnu said, “The entire universe is lodged in me. You consider it to be our own like a thief.

O Son, you have been born out of the lotus emerging from my navel, therefore you are not correct. Thus speaking both of them started fighting with each other for the purpose of killing.

Both the gods then started fighting seated over their respective vehicles viz. Garuda and the swan.

At that point of time all the gods travelling in their respective planes, arrived there in order to witness the astonishing type of war.

The gods, observing the battle the gods showered flowers, which Visnu shot several types of weapons and arrows over the chest of Brahma, which were unbearable. Thereafter Brahma also getting annoyed shot several unbearable arrows and weapon over the chest of Visnu. The battle of both of them was extremely surprising.

Brahma shot the arrows like fire and also other weapons, several times. Thus the battle between both of them was quite surprising.

Witnessing the battle between the two of them all the gods became anxious and started discussions among themselves. Then lord Visnu was breathing heavily, having suffered from the war.

Then the intelligent lord Visnu, used the Mahesvara-astra for the killing of Brahma. Then Brahma getting immensely enraged, making the entire universe to shake.

Placed the disastrous Pasupata weapon over the bow and shot it at the chest of Visnu. Thereafter both the weapons shot by Brahma and Visnu appeared in the sky which were like the ten thousand of suns, and violent like thousands of mouths, like the terrific and forceful wind.

In this way both Brahma and Visnu fought with each other a terrific war. Finding this, became all the gods were disgusted and are anxious, in the same way as the minds of the Brahmana is upset at the fight of the two kings.

Salutation to lord Siva, who happens to be the cause of creation, preservation, destruction, concealment and grace Thus all the gods were frightened with that battle. There the gods searching for the house of lord Siva, reached the Kailasa mountain, where Siva was lodged.

Without the permission of lord Siva, no one is in a position to destroy even a blade of grass.

Thus all the gods were frightened with that battle. There the gods searching for the house of lord Siva, reached the Kailasa mountain, where Siva was lodged.

Finding him there, all the gods were delighted and finding him in the form of Pranava they offered their salutation to him and then entered his place.

The gods found Siva the best of gods, seated with Parvati over the gem studded bed, in the sabhamandala (assembly).

He possessed the best of symbols and whose hearts were filled with devotion, besides the damsels well-versed in rendering special service, were moving fans. The Vedas were eulogising him. Siva looked at the gods with compassion.

O Son, looking at the crowns of gods, Mahadeva- the god of all the gods, delighting all the gods, delivered welfare speech. Blessing all the gods, he spoke sweet and pleasant words which bestow welfare.

## Chapter 7 - Contest between Visnu and Brahma,victory of the former

Isvara (Siva) said, “O Sons, who always obey my command. Do you enjoy the pleasure always? Are all the gods and the creatures of the world engaged in this respective assignments? I have already learnt about the news relating to the fight between Brahma and Visnu, observing your pain, it appears to have been repeated.”

Thus O Sanatkumara, speaking such sweet words, Siva, the lord of Parvati pleased the crowd of gods.

Then lord Siva, commanded a hundred of his ganas to move to the place where Brahma and Visnu were fighting.

Thereafter, at the time of the departure of Siva, several types of large Kattle drums were sounded. The Ganesvaras, having been adorned with all the ornaments, and mounted over the different types of vehicles, got ready to depart.

Then lord Siva, and his spouse of Parvati, mounted over the chariot named Bhadra-ratha, decorated with pancamandala. His son Ganesa and other ganas also went alongwith him, in addition to Indra and other gods.

Various types of flag and banners, of different colours, the fans, flywhisks, rain of flowers, music and dance accompanied with various types of musical instruments, both Siva and Parvati went to the place where Brahma and Visnu had been engaged in a fight, together with army.

Finding them engaged in fight, Siva halted concealing himself with Parvati and the army. The playing of the music was stopped together with the movement of the army.

At that point of time both Brahma and Visnu, in order to kill each other, were using Mahesvara and Pasupata weapons.

Thereafter with the flames of the weapons shot by Brahma and Visnu, for killing each other all the three worlds started burning. Siva also observed the destruction which was the cause of great misfortune, and untimely dissolution of the earth.

He appeared himself in between them as the form of a horrible burning column, of the absolute Brahman.

The weapons which were competent enough to destroy the entire universe, fell in the column of fire produced by Siva and were destroyed in a moment and reduced to ashes.

Observing the astonishing and benevolent event of the destruction of the weapons, all the gods whispered among themselves, “what is this with an astonishing form?

(Then Brahma and Visnu said,) “What is this pillar like formation resembling the fire flames, which has been raised above? What is there at its top and the bottom. Both of us should find out the same.”

Thus speaking both of them thinking themselves to be extremely valorous, engaged themselves to find the truth about the same.

“In case both of us go together, it would not be possible to establish this gigantic task.” Thus thinking Visnu taking to the form of a boar went downwards towards the root.

Then Brahma, taking to them form of a swan, flew up towards the sky in order to measure its height. Lord Visnu piercing through the Patalaloka (nether world) went too far.

When Visnu in the form of a boar could not reach the bottom of the column of fire, then he felt tired and returned to the battle ground.

O Vedavyasa, Brahma, your father, while flying in the sky found the ketaki flower falling.

The Ketaki flower had been separated from its stem long time back, still it had enough of fragrance and had not been faded out. Lord Siva found that both of them had been unsuccessful in their respective efforts.

He laughed at them, as a result of which his head started shaking. Thereafter the extending of grace over him, the Ketaki flower fell down.

Brahma said, “O King of the flowers, why are you falling? Who had held you?” Then the flower said, “I had fallen long back, before the creation, this pillar appeared without any authority, I was lodged in the middle of it and reached here.

Till date, I have not been able to locate the beginning or the end of it. You also give up this hope.” Then Brahma said, “I have also arrived here taking to the form of a swan to know about the same.

O Friend, you accomplish my task. You get alongwith me and speak to Visnu accordingly, “that Brahma had found the end of this column. You say that you are my witness.” Thus speaking, Brahma, offered his salutation to the ketaki flower again and again, because it is not a sin to speak untruth at the time of misfortune. This has been propounded by the sastras.

When Brahma found Visnu having been exhausted, and with a disturbed mind then he started dancing in delight. Talking like a eunuch, Brahma said to Visnu.

“O Hari, I have seen the top of this pillar and this flower is my witness for the same.” At the instance of Brahma the ketaki flower made a false statement before him. Taking the words of Brahma to be true, Visnu offered his salutation to the form and adored him in sixteen ways.

But Siva appeared suddenly from the pillar in order to punish Brahma. Brahma Visnu touched his feet with his shaking hands.

He said, “You have a body without a beginning or the end. Because of his ignorance, a person is unable to find you inspite of much efforts. O Compassionate one, you be pleased with me. By an audience with you, all my sins have been washed out. You kindly forgive me. You have done all this quite playfully.

Isvara said, “O Son Visnu, I am pleased with you, because you have spoken the truth becoming desirous of achieving the form of Isvara. Therefore you would achieve divinity in the world and will also earn my grace.

From today onwards your images shall be adored in the different parts with festivities.

Lord Siva was pleased with Visnu because of his truthful conduct and in full view of all the gods he bestowed on him, equality with himself.

## Chapter 8 - Shattering the pride of Brahma

Thereafter, Siva, in order to shatter the pride of Brahma, produced an astonishing type of a person from out of his eyebrows.

Soon after his emerging, he offered his salutation to lord Siva in the battle ground itself and asked him, “O Lord, what have I to do? You kindly get me the command at once.”

Siva said, “O Bhairava, you better, adore Brahma, the primeval lord of the earth, with a sharp edged sword (or kill him)”.

On hearing this Rudra caught hold of the hair of Brahma’s head in his hand, and severed his fifth head which told the untruth and got ready to kill him.

Then your father- Brahma, shedding away the costumes and ornaments besides the scarf, having grey hair, started shaking like the banana leaves or the leaves of the creeper and fell down over the feet of Bhairava.

Looking at the precarious condition of Brahma, shedding tears over the feet of lord Siva, folding both his hands, he spoke in sweet tongue in the same way a child speaks to his father.

Lord Visnu said, “O Lord Siva, by your grace, Brahma had been awarded five heads by you, out of which one has been destroyed. Therefore you be merciful over Brahma.

When Siva was so prayed by Visnu, then he stopped Bhairava from proceeding further (in cutting of his remaining heads) and said, “Don’t punish Brahma any further.

Then Siva said to Brahma, who had been deprived of a head, “You played a trick in order to earn your worship in the world and becoming its lord.

Therefore no one on earth, would adore you, honour you or arrange for the festivities in the world in your name.” At this Brahma said, “O Lord, you always bestow the boons. You be pleased with me today. With the severed head, I consider it to be the salutation at your feet.

O Lord, you are the close relative of the universe. O Visvayoni, you tolerate the blemishes. O holder of the great bow, O Siva, salutation to you.

Siva said, “O Son, the entire universe would get destroyed by fighting, without a king. Therefore, you award punishments to the culprits and carryon the burden of the earth.

I give you a boon which is difficult to get. You should accept it. You would be the preceptor for the Vedic yajnas and those propounded by the Smrtis.

Without you the entire yajna, would become infructuous.” Thereafter lord Siva addressing the ketaki flowers who appeared as a false witness, said, “O wicked ketaki flower, you disappear to a far off place. From today onwards, I would not like you to be offered at the time of my adoration.”

At these words spoken by Siva, the gods started removing ketaki flowers and other related species from their vicinity.

Then the ketaki flower said, “O Master, with your present curse on me my birth on earth would become infructuous. Therefore you kindly forgive me for my sin and allow my life to be successful.

With the mere reciting of your name all the sins committed innocently or deliberately are washed out. Then after having an audience with you, how could the sin of speaking untruth remain?”

When the ketaki flower, thus spoke to Siva in the assembly, then the lord said, “You have become unfit to be offered to me because my words cannot be untrue.

But Visnu and all other gods would accept you as their offering and your life would be successful. You would be used for the making of the mandapa for me.

In this way, lord Siva, showering his grace over Brahma, Visnu and the ketaki flower, after having been praised by all the gods, was seated in the assembly.

## Chapter 9 - Consecrating of the Siva-linga

Nandisvara said, “At the same time, both Brahma and Visnu offering their salutations to the lord Siva, quietly stood to the right and left of the lord. Both of them then seated Siva with his family over a high pedestal and adored him with auspicious padarthas emerging from purusa-samkalpa.

The things which emerge from the samkalpa of a purusa should be considered as long lived or remaining for long. There are some padarthas in them which could be given over, and they include garlands, anklets, armlets, crowns, gem studded kundalas.

Yajnopavita, scarf, garland, silken cloth, rosary of Rudraksa, finger ring, flowers, betel, camphor, sandal paste, aguru-paste, incense, lamp, white umbrella, fan, flag, flywhisk, and several other divine presents, which are beyond the divine gifts, mind and riches.

They also offered things, which were beyond the ideas of the humans to lord Siva. O Sanatakumara, the best among the well-wishers, whatever the best padarthas are there in the world, they could be offered for the adoration of Siva.

Lord Siva on his part, in order to maintain ancient traditions, distributed to them all those present there.

For achieving that thing, there was a great rumour there. First of all, at that time Brahma and Visnu, worshipped Siva.

Lord Siva, who always increases devotion, then said to Brahma and Visnu delightfully, “Let both of your remain happy.” Siva again said, “O Sons, this is the great day and I am happy with your worship for me.

Since then, the day is considered to be most auspicious and yields merit. This is the date dear to lord Siva and is well known by the name of Sivaratri.

Whosoever would adore Siva’s Image or a Siva-linga, he becomes competent to the creation, maintenance and the destruction of the universe.

On the occasion of Sivaratri whosoever, controlling his sense-organs, fasting totally for twenty four hours, shall adore Siva according to his capacity, without deceitfulness, he shall earn the merit equal to the performing of my worship for a year. The merit equal to my worship for a year shall also be achieved by a person who performs my adoration on the day of Sivaratri.

As the ocean increases with the rise of the full moon, similarly on that very day my dharma also increases. On that very day my benevolent function is performed.

O boys, I had earlier appeared in the form of a pillar, it was the month of Margasirsa and the constellation was Ardra.

In the month of Margasirsa, during Ardra constellation, whosoever has an audience with me (Umapati) or the one who adores my image or Siva-linga, he becomes dearer to me than Karttikeya even.

On that auspicious day, one achieves sufficient of merit even by looking at me, but in case lord Siva is appropriately worshipped during that day then the reward for the same is beyond the description from the speech.

In this battle ground of both of you, I had appeared in linga therefore the place will be known as Linga-sthana.

O Sons, this is without beginning or the end. This is a huge pillar, but for the sake of the human beings, it would become smaller.

This linga would be the cause of pleasure as well as the redemption. By having a look at it or by touching it and meditating it, one would be freed from the bondage of the birth and death.

This linga appeared at this place like the mountain of fire, therefore, this place would be known in this world by the name of Arunacala.

The place would become an immensely sacred tirtha. Those who would live here and meet their death here would be redeemed.

Rathayatra would be performed here and the place would be quite benevolent, fit for human habitation. The japam, homa, charities, performed here would yield crore times more than the ordinary merit.

This would be considered to be the best of all my ksetras. The person, who, reaching here would recite my name, he would attain rapid salvation.

Because of this, the region would be quite great and immensely graceful, bestowing welfare to all besides the salvation.

The one who would conceive me as lingesvara in this linga, he would achieve lokva, samipya, sarupya and sarsti types of salvations.

The sarupya salvation would be achieved according to one’s own job. All of you would also get your own desires fulfilled.”

Nandikesvara said, “Thus lord Siva showered his benevolence over Brahma and Visnu quite humbly. Such of the soldiers who had been killed in the war.

Were brought back to life with showering of the nectar. Then the lord Siva said to both of them in order to remove their ignorance and enmity.

“I have two forms viz. Saguna and Nirguna (absolute), there is no other Isvara except me, therefore, they cannot have two forms.

I initially took to the form of a pillar and then to the form of a human being. The one which is niskala of the two is the form of Brahman and the one having the form of Isa, is sakala.

My both these forms are established and could not belong to any one. Therefore neither of you or any one else can achieve the stage of Isatva.

Both of you out of ignorance believed yourselves to be Isvara, and the same was the surprising aspect. I have appeared in the battle ground in order to remove your fallacy.

Both of you should now shed away your pride and be devoted to me. Various types of bhavas (feelings) appear in the world by my grace.

The words spoken by me as a preceptor, are quite authentic for you. I am going to reveal the Brahma-sattva to you, because of my love for you.

I happen to be Para-Brahman, I become Isvara and I remain compassionate over the moveable and immovable creatures of the world.

O Brahma and Visnu, because of my being of all pervading nature, expanding the universe, I am Brahma. O Boys, since all the creatures are equal for me and because of my being omniscient I am also known as Atmarupa.

The jiva is not completely Atmarupa. It is jiva alone. There is no doubt about it. From the beginning to the end of the universe, there are five deeds in the world.

Isatva (supremacy) is enshrined in me. Therefore, all these activities can be attributed to me and none else. Initially my absolute form appeared in order to enlighten you on the subject of Brahmatva.

Because of this, I remain in invisible form. I took to my saguna form in order to appear before you.

You should consider my present form as saguna and the form of my pillar represents Brahma.

Because of the symptoms of the linga, this would be my absolute form. O Sons, you should daily adore it.

This linga is the form of my soul and bestows my vicinity. Both linga and lingi are in separable, it should be treated as my form and should be worshipped daily.

O Sons, whosoever might have consecrated the linga at any place, I reside there even without its consecrating.

As a result of consecrating a linga one achieves my form and with the consecrating of a second linga by the devotee of Siva, he gets absorbed in me.

After consecrating the linga arrangements for its worship should also be made. The main task is the consecration of the linga while the consecration of an image of Siva is metaphorical, because, even after the consecration of an image of Siva at a particular place, it cannot be described as the sacred place.”

## Chapter 10 - Discourse on Omkara

Brahma and Visnu said, “O Lord, you kindly speak out the symptoms of Pancakrtyas, including sarga etc.” Siva said, “My motive remains extremely sacred. But being merciful to you. I am going to speak out the same.

O Brahma and O Visnu, the five worldly krtyas or motives are creation, preservation, destruction, concealment and grace.

The creation of the universe is called sarga. Its establishment is called preservation, while its destruction is called samhara. The absence of the same is called concealment.

When a person achieve moksa from the world, it is called anugraha. These five activities are attributed to me. The earth etc. reflect these motives of mine like the reflection of gopura, quietly.

The four activities like sarga and others are used for the expansion of the universe, while the fifth called grace or anugraha becomes the cause of salvation, which is always lodged in me.

My devotees visualise it with the five Mahabhutas and creation is in the earth. Preservation is in the water, destruction is in fire. Concealment in the wind, and anugraha (grace) is in the sky. This should be known by the people with wisdom.

To carry the burden of these five krtyas, I have five faces. Four are for the four directions, while the fifth one is in the centre.

O Sons, you have earned the two krtyas with the performing of the tapas, which are called the creation and preservation. Both of them have been delightfully bestowed on you as boons.

Similarly, I have entrusted two jobs to Rudra and Mahesa, but no one is competent to receive the krtya called anugraha (grace).

You have forgotten about the earlier karmas due to the passage of time, but Rudra and Mahesa have not forgotten them at all.

I had awarded equally to Rudra and Mahesa, in the form, beauty, activities, vehicles, seats and the weapons.

O Sons, you had developed ignorance, because of your forgetting my adoration. Had you remained conscious about me, this situation would not have arisen, because my devotee, who meditates upon me, turns like Mahesa, in wisdom and beauty.

Therefore, you in order to achieve success in wisdom and beauty should perform japam of the omkara-mantra, which is sure to destroy the arrogance.

Thus I have delivered discourse to you about the omkara-mantra, first of all emerged out of my mouth. It is my form.

This is the speaker, while I am the indication and this mantra is my soul. To recite it daily is like reciting my name alone.

From the face towards the north, emerges akara from the face to the west Ikara, from the face to the south makara and from the mouth to the east emerges the spot (or bindu).

Nada (sound) emerges from the mouth in the centre. Thus, omkara appeared in five ways; with the coming of all the sounds from the five mouths, there emerged omkara.

This omkara because of its form having been related to name and the Vedas, symbolises Siva and Sakti.

Omkara of the five letters has emerged from the same, which represents the entire universe. Nakara emerged from akara, makara emerged from ukara, si emerged from Makara vd was produced from the spat and ya appeared from nada or the sound.

From the same Pancaksara (five letters) five Svaras or tunes have emerged. Siromantra appeared from the same, besides the four faced and three footed Gayatri.

All the Vedas emerged from the same, besides crores of mantras. One meets success with the mantra, but with the Pancaksara-mantra one achieves all types of success.

With this basic mantra one can achieve all the pleasure as well as the salvation. All types of the great devotees, are bestowed with all the types of pleasures and comforts.”

Nandikesvara said, “Thereafter, lord Siva, in order to keep the mantra a secret, placed a cloth over their heads, and placing his hands over their heads, stood facing north with Parvati and spoke the best of mantra for them.

By the method of yantra and tantra, the mantra was repeated thrice by both of them and then they accepted that supreme mantra. Thereafter both the disciples dedicated themselves to lord Siva in the form daksina.

Both Brahma and Visnu with folded hands, spoke to lord Mahadeva- the god of gods and the preceptor of the universe with folded hands.”

Brahma and Visnu said, “O Formless one, you are immensely illustrious inspite of your having no form. Salutation to you. You are the lord of the entire universe. You take to saguna form, salutation to you.

You are Pranavavacya (named by Om) and are Pranava-linga, (identified by Om) salutation to you. You are the first creator of the universe, and have five faces, salutation to you.

You are the form of five Brahmas, Pancakrtyas, form of atman, Brahman, having virtues beyond measures, possessing enormous prowess, salutation to you.

You have the virtuous as well as the absolute forms. You are known as Siva and the supreme preceptor. Salutation to you. In this way both of them praised lord Siva with the aforesaid verses and then offered their salutation to him.

Siva said, “O Sons, for the sake of your welfare, I have spoken to you about all the tattvas and have also shown you the way like a guide. Therefore both of you should perform japam of the divine Pranava mantra, which is said to be my own form.

With the reciting of the mantra, the wind and the fortunes are stabilised and all the desires are fulfilled for long. Its recitation should be done on the fourteenth moon day during the Ardra constellation, as a result of which the reward of the recitation becomes everlasting.

In case the recitation of this mantra is started when the Sun is in Ardra constellation, the reward for the same multiplies to a crore of times. The effect of Punarvasu and Mrgasira constellations, also becomes the same like the Ardra constellation and the puja, homa oblations etc. should be similarly performed. In the morning or at the time of the dawn, its darsana provides enormous merit.

When the fourteenth tithi fells during the night, it should always be treated as sacred. Some of the acaryas patronise the pradosavyapini Caturdasi, while others do so for the fourteenth tithi combined with other tithi.

The worship of linga as well as the worship of the image is like my own worship. But for the worshippers, the worship of linga is better than the worship of the images. Particularly the persons desirous of achieving moksa, should worship linga only.

The worship of linga should be done with omkara-mantra, while that of the image should be done with the Pancaksara-mantra. They should be consecrated by himself or though a priest.

In case the linga is adored appropriately using the prescribed material for worship, then it becomes easier for a devotee to achieve my position or the pada." By thus delivering discourse to Brahma and Visnu, lord Siva disappeared.

## Chapter 11 - Worship of Siva-linga and its consecration

The ascetics said, “How should the linga be consecrated? What are the symptoms of the linga and how should it be worshipped in different times and places.

Suta said, “I am going to tell you the method for the same. You please listen to it carefully. During the time favourable according to the planets and the constellations, during the auspicious time, at the bank of some river in a sacred place, the linga should be consecrated. It should be made in clay, stone or of metal etc., where it could be daily worshipped.

By adoring the linga by Siva-puja-vidhana in case the linga is worshipped, one gets its complete reward, because when the worship is performed with all the symptoms methodically, it bestows immediate results.

The moveable linga should be smaller in size and the immovable linga should be bigger in size, because such types of lingas are always the best. Such lingas should have all the symptoms besides the lion-thrones. Such types of Siva-lingas should be consecrated.

For the consecration of immovable linga, the pitha or the pedestal should be of circular or triangular type. A khatvanga in the form of banner should also be installed. The pedestal of the small linga bestows great merit.

The linga should initially be made of clay, stone, iron, or other metals. The material which is used in the making of the Siva-linga, the pitha or the pedestal should also be made of the same material or the metal as that of the linga. This is the speciality of the making of the permanent linga.

Except the bana-linga, all other lingas should be made with the pitha or the pedestal. The height of linga should be twelve times of the finger of the maker, which is treated to be the best.

In case the height is lesser than the twelve fingers, then its reward is also reduced. In case the height of the linga exceeds the twelve fingers, there is no harm in the same. Even if the height of the linga is lesser by a finger of the maker, even then, there is no harm. This rule is also applicable in case of the moveable linga.

First of all the artisan well-versed in the making of the images should make a vimana with all the gods, which should be quite neat and clean and shining like a mirror.

It should be decorated with nine gems. Two doors should be provided towards the east and the west. The nine gems include, sapphire, lapiz-lazuli, emerald, pearl, gomeda,coral, sardonic and ruby, are called the nine-ratnas or nine gems which should be used in the vimana.

Thereafter reciting the Sodyojata and other mantras, the linga should be adored from all the sides (viz. all the four sides) and the top. Then offering oblations ghee in the fire.

One should adore me in Saguna form, the preceptor an the acarya with riches etc., and also honour all the relatives with food etc. Then he should offer charities like giving away of the houses and cows, horses etc.

Thereafter one should please all the moveable and immovable creatures, reciting the Sodyojatamantras, in the pit filled with gold and nine types of gems, devoting the mind to the extremely benevolent Siva, utter the sound of omkara.

Then the linga should be placed in the pit and joined with the seat (or pitha). The linga should be joined with the appropriate material.

Similarly the linga with images should also be consecrated. The image should be kept out for celebrating it with Pancaksara-mantra.

The image should be got accepted from the preceptors as well as the great sages. The worship of the linga as well as the linga with image should be worshipped, which bestows the highest position with Siva.

Still they are conceived to be of two types viz. moveable and immovable. The lingas made of wood of trees and shrubs, are called permanent or Sthavaras (immovable).

The linga with insects and worms are moveable. The immovable linga should be served with water, and offering food etc. to it, amounts to its tarpana.

The people of wisdom should understand that one gets all the pleasures with the adoration of Siva. All the recitations are natural, and all the lingas are the form of wisdom.

As Parvati is always lodged in the lap of Siva, similarly the linga always remains in the pitha.

In this way after consecrating the linga appropriately one should adore it daily offering presents as per one’s means. The banners and other offerings should also be made to the same.

By consecrating the linga in this way, which bestows the place of Siva, one should adore it by sixteen ways.

Linga should be worshipped appropriately which bestows the place of Siva. The method of adoration is like this: First is invocation, offering of the seat, arghya, padya, invocation, sipping of the water for invitation or bath, anointing of oil on the body, the costumes, fragrance, incense, lamp etc. should be offered.

In addition to the above, the light, betel, salutation, arghya etc., the naivedya (food) should also be properly offered.

Then the offering of the naivedya, abhiseka, salutation and tarpana should be offered regularly according to one’s means. All these offerings bestow the place of Siva.

The people should make appropriate offerings with suitable gifts at the Siva-lingas, which are consecrated by the humans, which appeared of their own, or those which are newly consecrated, by appropriate means.

By doing so one achieves some reward. One achieves the place of Siva, by circumambulating the linga.

In case a person daily visits the Siva temple and has an audience with lord Siva, one achieves the place of Siva. One could make Siva-linga by mixing of the cow-dung with dust, flowers of oleander, with several types of fruits.

With sugarcane cakes (guda), butter, ashes, various types of cereals, or with any other material according to one’s liking.

Some of the intellectuals, adore Siva by the thumb, because in that case linga worship can be done anywhere, and there is no prohibition in the same.

Based on the efforts of his devotees, lord Siva, bestows the reward or otherwise with the donating of Siva-linga or paying the cost of making of a linga.

With great devotion and faith, the devotee gets the place of Siva or alternatively one should perform the japam of ten thousand times of the omkara-mantra.

Or one should perform japam of omkara-mantra a thousand times, during the morning as well as the evening separately, which bestows the place of Siva. At the time of japam, om purifies the mind.

Mental japam should be performed at the time of meditation, while all the time he should perform the japam in a way in which no one hears it. The Pranava mantra with the spot is common in all the japams.

Or otherwise, one should recite the Pancaksara-mantra with faith and devotion, daily ten thousand times in the morning as well as the evening; which bestows the place of Siva.

While reciting the Pancaksara-mantra, the Brahmanas should add omkara before it, and for the achieving the merit, the mantra should be properly received from the preceptor.

The Brahmana should resort to kumbha-snanam (bath by. pitcher) should received mantra-diksa and perform matrikanyasa. He should speak the truth, and should be self-conscious.

While muttering the mantra the word namah should be prefixed to the mantra, while those of the established castes, should add the word namah at the end of the mantra. (As for example Om namah Sivaya and Om Sivaya namah). Some of the learned woman also should use the word namah at the end, which has been ordained.

Some of the people with wisdom are of the opinion that the Brahmana women, should also use the word namah at the beginning of the mantra. In this way by performing the japam five crore of times a person is turned into the form of Sadasiva.

By performing the japam for one, two, three and four crores, a devotee receives the palace of Brahma, Visnu and Siva respectively. Otherwise each word should be recited separately a lac of times.

Or otherwise one should perform ten lakhs of japam in a thousand days or whatever be the number of letters in the mantra a devotee should perform an equal number of japam, a lac for one letter each, to achieve the place of Siva.

The merit (dharmo) which is achieved with the performing of pilgrimage and with the japam it bestows the everlasting pleasure. Now I shall speak out the method of earning the riches. The riches or wealth should earned with justice and carefully.

With the reciting of the mantra daily and serving food to the Brahmana, at the same time, the task of the devotee is established. One should recite the Gayatri-mantra a thousand and eight times in the morning daily.

The Dasarna-mantra should be recited more than a hundred times or as much as possible. One should not recite less than a hundred times. Irrespective of the fact that it is recited a thousand or ten thousand times, but the recitation should never be less than a hundred times.

With the complete recitation of the Vedas also one achieves the place of Siva. The several other mantras should also be recited a lac of times of the number of letters contained therein.

Ekaksara-mantra should be recited a crore of times. Thereafter omkara-mantra should be recited a thousand times.

In this, with the reciting of the Siva’s mantra according to one’s capacity, one gradually achieves the place of Siva. This mantra which delights the heart should be recited till death.

With the reciting of the omkara-mantra a thousand times all the desires are fulfilled at the command of Siva. A devotee of Siva who plants the flower, sets up a garden, cleans his temple, and does other such jobs for the sake of Siva, or for his use, he achieves the place of Siva. One should live in the temple of Siva in the abode of Siva (Sivalaya) daily with devotion.

The devotion of Siva bestows the conscious as well as the unconscious pleasures, therefore, one should live in the ksetra of Siva till death.

An area up to a hundred feet on all the sides of the Siva-linga established by the people is considered to be quite auspicious. The area up to a thousand feet around the Siva-linga consecrated by the sages is considered sacred.

An area of a thousand feet around the Siva-linga consecrated by the gods is considered to be sacred. The land over which the Siva-linga has itself appeared, the area around it up to four thousand feet is treated to be auspicious.

In this way, such auspicious places include the step-wells, wells, tanks, and other water reservoirs which are sacred and should be treated as Sivaganga. This has been pronounced by lord Siva.

By taking bath, performing charities, etc., in that area, a person achieves the place of Siva. A person should live in Siva-ksetra till his death.

Whatever rites after death like the burning of the body, or the rites performed up to ten day after the death of a person, pindadana, sraddha, rites on the twelfth day of the death, rites performed after a month, as well as the year, in the Siva-ksetra, and by doing so, the sins earned by a person are washed out and he achieves the place of Siva. Or otherwise, by the stay in the Siva-ksetra for five, or seven, three or one night, one achieves the place of Siva. The Brahmana and the people of the other castes, reap the reward according to the deeds performed by them.

The varna or the devotion multiplies the merits of the deeds. Therefore a person who performs the deeds by his own sweet will, he achieves the reward for the same, quite quickly.

In case a person adores Siva without a desire in his mind, he surely achieves the place of Siva. In case a person adores Siva thrice (morning, noon and the evening) in a day.

In that case the adoration in the morning is the part of the daily routine. The adoration in the noon is meant for the achieving of the success in the desires, while the adoration in the evening bestows peace over the devotee. Similar is the reward for the adoration of Siva during the night.

With the passage of the two praharas of the night it is called midnight. The adoration of Siva performed at that time bestows special reward to the devotee.

When a devotee adores Siva, knowing all these details, he achieves special types of reward. Particularly in Kali-yuga, the reward is achieved on the basis of the deeds performed by a person.

A person who performs the adoration of Siva in any way he likes, he is called the virtuous person and the one who is afraid of sins he achieves the reward accordingly.

The sages said, “O Suta, now you enlighten us about the auspicious regions of the earth, taking refuge in which, all the men and the women could achieve the place of Siva.

O Suta, you happen to be the best of the yogis. You are well-versed on the Saivaganas as well as the places sacred to Siva.” Suta said, “You better listen with devotion about the Saivaganas as well as the places sacred to Siva.

## Chapter 12 - Description of the Siva-ksetras

Suta said, “O wise sages, all of you are the learned ones. For the welfare of the world, I am going to highlight, the Sivaksetras which bestow salvation as well as their co-relation with the Agamas. All of your should listen to me.

The earth which is spread into fifty crores of yojanas, at the command of Siva, has been distributed in mountains, forests, huge forests, and carries the universe.

Lord Siva has established several different ksetras for bestowing salvation to the concerned people.

In order to free the human beings from the influence of the gods and the sages, lord Siva has created Svayambhu as well as the other ksetras.

All the people should take bath, perform charities as well as japam (recitation) at these places. Failure to do so, a person can attract ailments, poverty, dumbness and other diseases.

Such of the people, who meet with their death, at the svayambhu ksetras, or Bharatavarsa is a holy centre where there is a self resin phallic emblem of Siva they are reborn again as humans.

O Brahmanas, such of the people who are engaged in evil deeds at such sacred laces, they have to face miseries. Therefore, no one, should perform the slightest sin, while living at such sacred places.

Some how the men strive to find a residence at a holy centre, on the shore of an ocean. At the confluence of hundreds of river’s there are many holy centres besides the temples.

The holy river Sarasvati, is said to have sixty months or holy centres on its banks. Therefore an intelligent man should stay over its banks by which he will attain Brahma’s region gradually.

A person should try to live in the sacred place somehow or the other. There are several sacred places at the banks of the river Sindhu as well as the Ganga.

In the month of Magha and when Brhaspati is in Makara-rasi, the great river Sonabhadra with a thousand months, becomes auspicious and bestows great merit of one’s own liking.

By living over its bank, taking bath in its waters, besides observing fast, one achieves the place of Ganesa. The river Narmada with twenty four months is quite sacred and auspicious.

By taking bath in it or by living over its bank, one achieves the lace of Visnu. The river Tamasa has twelve mouths, while the river Reva has ten mouths.

The river Godavari bestows enormous merits. By having a bath in it a person is relieved of the sin of Brahmahatya as well as that of the killing of a cow. It has twenty one mouths and bestows the place of Siva.

The river named Krsna-veni, is quite auspicious and destroys all the sins. It has eighteen mouths and bestows Visnuloka.

The river Tungabhadra has ten mouths and bestows Brahmaloka. The Svarnamukhari river has nine mouths and is quite auspicious.

The people who fall from Brahmaloka, are born at this place. The people, who live here over the banks of Sarasvati, Pampa, Kanya and Sveta rivers, achieves the place of Indra. Kaveri is a Mahanadi and tarts from the Sahya river.

It has twenty seven mouths, fulfils all the desires. Its banks bestow the regions of Brahma and Visnu.

These places of Siva, bestow Sivaloka, besides having all the desires fulfilled. In the Naimesaranya and Badrikasrama, are quite auspicious and a person should take a bath there, when Brhaspati and the Sun are in the Aires Zodiac cycle.

In the Sindhu river one should take bath in the months of Bhadrapada and Margasirsa, and by doing so one achieves Brahmaloka.

To take a bath in the water of Kedara-tirtha and to drink the same, increases wisdom. In the river Godavari, one should take a bath when Brhaspati and the sun are in Leo.

By doing this, one achieves Sivaloka. This is what had been spoken by Siva earlier. When the sun and Brhaspati are in Virgo. One should take bath in the Yamuna and the Sonabhadra river.

In case one takes a bath on the Yamuna and the Sonabhadra, one achieves the place of Ganesa. When the Surya and Brhaspati are in Libra Zodiac, one who takes bath in the Kaveri river, he, with the glory of the words of Visnu, has all his desires fulfilled.

By taking a bath in the river Narmada, one achieves the place of Visnu. When Brhaspati and Surya are in the ninth sign of Zodiac, and in case one takes a bath in Svarnamukhari, and when Brhaspati and Surya are in tenth sign of the Zodiac (Capricorn), one achieves the place of Siva. This has been ordained by Brahma. Such a person enjoys the places of Brahma and Visnu and ultimately he achieves wisdom.

By taking a bath in the Ganga in the month of Magha, and by performing pindadana and sraddha with sesamum and offering oblation in water, his innumerable manes of both the races, are redeemed. For the river Krsnaveni, when Surya and Brhaspati are in the twelfth sign of Zodiac, they get praiseworthy.

By taking bath in those sacred laces during the prescribed period, one achieves the position of Indra. A person with wisdom should reside over the bank of the rivers Ganga and Kaveri.

By doing so the sins committed at that time are surely lost. There are several regions for achieving the place of Indra.

The rivers named Tamraparni and Vegavati bestow the reward of Brahmaloka. At the banks of these rivers, there are several regions which bestow the heaven to the people.

There are several auspicious regions in between. By living there the persons achieve the appropriate fruits.

A person should be noble in approach, well-behaved and should have the best of intentions, he should behave with wisdom, and be compassionate to all. Otherwise, he would not be able to achieve its fruit.

The noble deed performed in the auspicious place, bestows several types of rddhis. Similarly even the smallest sin performed at a sacred place gets increased.

For the sake of repentance, one shall have to perform noble deeds for the same period, only then the sin could be washed out. All the fortunes can be achieved by means of merits and the sins relating to one’s mind, body and speech, get destroyed. The mental sins are like the paste and the sins performed in several other births get destroyed by meditating upon lord Siva and not otherwise. The sins of speech are removed by recitation, the sins of body are removed by fasting.

By performing charities, the sins relating to the riches are destroyed. Otherwise the sins cannot be removed in a hundred crores of years and with the increase of the sins, even the merits vanish. The wisdom vanishes with bijansa and its increase has been discussed earlier.

Bhogansa is destroyed with the enjoying of the pleasures, otherwise it cannot be destroyed by the performing of the crores of noble deeds. With the destruction of the sprouting of the sins or the source of the sprouting of the sins, the rest of the sins are washed out by facing them in life.

By adoration of the gods, giving away charities to the Brahmanas, performing of the tapas, by experiencing the pains according to the times, the sins are destroyed. Therefore the person desirous of pleasure should never commit sins.

## Chapter 13 - Description of a righteous person

The rsis said, “O Suta, now you quickly speak out about the righteousness by which a person could be victorious in the society as well as in the world or the position of the heaven or the hell.”

Suta said, “A righteous person who conducts himself according to the path of the Vedas, possessing all the virtues is called as a Brahmana.

The person who conducts himself slightly, and has studied the Vedas too slightly, and a Brahmana in the royal service is called as a Ksatriya-Brahmana. A person who slightly follows righteousness and is engaged in tilling the land or some business, is called Vaisya-Brahmana.

The one who himself ploughs the field, he is called Sudra-Brahmana. The one who indulged in denouncing or back-biting others, a jealous person, the one who has hatred against others, he is called the Candala-Brahmana.

The one who rules the earth, is called the king while others are called Ksatriyas. Those who are engaged in purchase and sale of cereals are called the Vaisyas, while others are called the traders or the merchants.

Those who serves the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and Vaisyas are called the Sudras. The one who is engaged in farming, is called Vrsala or a Sudra. The rest of the people are called Sudra-dasyus.

The people of all the varnas should get up early in the morning, meditate upon the gods facing east. Then they should think about dharma, artha or the body related pains as well as the income and the expenditure.

Facing towards the east and other directions, one should get up. There are different effects of facing the different directions viz.:- life, jealousy, death, sin, fortune (based on evil or noble deeds), ailments, growth and strength. These are the eight fruits of the eight directions.

The end of the night is called the dawn; half of its prahara is called sandhi or combination. A Brahmana should get up at the same time and free himself from the calls of the nature etc.

One should go far away from his abode and covering his head with the cloth, one should be seated facing the north, and should not look to other sides.

One should not be seated facing water, fire, Brahmana or the god. One should hold the phallus with the left hand and covering the face with the right hand.

One should drop the refuse. Then he should get up and do not look at the refuge. Carrying water in a vase, one should go out of the tank and then clean himself.

Otherwise except the gods, manes or the tirthas or the rsis, a person getting water from the tank cleaning the rectum with dust three, five or seven time and wash it with water from the tank.

For cleaning the phallus, one should apply very small quantity of dust while for the cleaning of the rectum half a fist of the dust should be used. Then cleaning the hands one should rinse the mouth eight times.

Employing any tree-leaves or wooden material and sitting outside the water, leaving the little finger, one should brush his or her teeth.

Then he should take bath offering his salutation to the water god, reciting the mantra. In case he cannot dip his head in water, then he should have- a dip up to the waist or the neck and take a bath.

Entering the thigh deep water, he should recite the mantras. A learned person should offer oblation to the gods, rsis and the manes with the same water of the tirtha.

Then he should wear the dhoti in pancakaccha manner. In the auspicious functions, the scarf should also be worn.

After taking the bath in a river or a sacred place, the clothes used in bathing should not be washed. In case one has to take a bath in a well or a step-well, then the clothes should be washed before taking the bath.

O Brahmanas, cleaning the dhoti or the towel, should washed and squeezed them and then the oblation of water should be offered to the names.

Carrying the ash, reciting the mantra prescribed by the sage Jabali, one should draw three lines over the forehead. The one who drops the ashes in the water except this method, falls in the hell.

Reciting the mantras apohista etc. one should sprinkle water over his head. Reciting this mantra water should be dropped over other limbs of the body and then one should take his bath.

The intelligent people resort to mantra-snana sprinkling water over different parts of the body reciting the mantras, on heart, head, feet, etc.

In case per chance a person touches an unclean thing or when suffering from some ailment, when in danger from the king on the country, while travelling or in other such situations, one should resort to mantra-snana.

In the morning reciting the Suryanuvak mantra sipping the water and then the sprinkling should be done as before.

With the reciting of the Gayatri mantra, one should sprinkle water upwards, thrice. O Brahmanas during the mid-day sandhya, reciting the mantras, arghya should be offered to fhe Sun in the sky.

Then in the evening time facing the west, one should offer oblation with fingers to the sun, in the same way as is done in the morning and the noon.

Then he should look at the sun through the cavities of the fingers and performing circumambulation, should sip the water.

In case the sandhya is performed before time in the evening, it becomes infructuous. Therefore the discussion on the appropriate or the in appropriate time has been made. In case sandhya is performed after the day is over, it becomes infructuous, and the repentance for the same has been prescribed.

After the day is over if Gayatri mantra is recited, then a hundred times more recitation of Gayatri mantra should be recited. In case this repentance is not done up to ten days, then one has to recite the Gayatri mantra a lac of times more.

Upanayana should be done after a month. All the gods like Siva, Parvati, Karttikeya, Visnu, Brahma, Indra and Yamaraja, should all be pleased for the fulfilment of one’s desires. Thereafter dedicating the entire activity to Brahman, one should perform the sipping of the water.

A person should recite the mantra to the south of a sacred place, in a matha, consultation room, a temple, in the house or any other prescribed place.

The person who receives the mantra, should bow in reverence to all the gods, concentrating his mind, getting firmly seated over an asana. He should first recite omkara and thereafter the Gayatri mantra.

Learning about the union of the jiva and Brahman, one should recite omkara. Brahma is the creator of the universe, Visnu is the preserver, and self-illumining lord Siva, who destroys the world should be adored. One should concentrate with all the organs of knowledge jnandriya, the movements of the mind, besides the intelligence, towards dharma which bestows the comforts and moksa. Thus diverting the mind in this manner (towards devotion) a person surely achieves Brahman.

The best of Brahmana, for the preservation of his position as a Brahmana, should recite omkara mantra at least for a thousand times in a day.

The people of other castes should recite this mantra in the noon time according to their capacity or a hundred times. During the evening, the same mantra should be recited a thousand times or twenty times (according to his convenience).

Starting from the muladhara-cakra to Brahmarandhra one should perform the japam in all the cakras, concentrating over Vidyesa, Brahma, Visnu, Siva, Jivatma and Paramatma.

Involving all with the noble intelligence, considering them to be equal and taking them to be like self-soham the reciting should be done. Then conceiving Brahmarandhra and other cakras to be out of the body, one should meditate upon them.

Staring from the Prakrti, one should think of the thousands of the bodies, which one had achieved due to his karmas, and should then slowly deviate from each body.

The jiva should be united with Parabrahman. This is the realistic tattva of the japam. This recitation should be made a thousand or a thousand and eight times.

This is the first sequence of the reciting of the mantras. The omkara mantra when recited a thousand times bestows Brahmapada and in case the japam is performed a hundred times, it bestows the position of Indra.

By reciting the mantra lesser than the one prescribed above, one is born in the family of a Brahmana. Therefore standing while facing the sun daily, the recitation of the omkara-mantra should be performed.

The reciting of the Gayatri mantra twelve lakhs of times, is called Purna-Brahman. A Brahmana who has not performed the Gayatri mantra a lac of times, he should not be included in the Vedic rituals.

One should spend disciplined life up to seventy years and then should embrace Sanyasa. After embracing sanyasa one should recite omkara mantra twelve thousand times in the morning.

Thus with performing of the japam daily regularly, after the passage of a month, a lac and a half of the japam of the omkara mantra is completed.

With this, all the blemishes are washed out. When the number of the japam is increased further, then one should receive the sanyasa-mantra, otherwise the reciter falls in the hell called Raurava.

A person desirous of the worldly pleasures should learn the method of dharma and artha from him and not about any other topic. A Brahmana, desirous of salvation, should practice only theosophy.

Dharma gives rise to artha, while artha gives rise to the pleasure and the pleasures give rise to the detachment or vairagya or in other words the artha and pleasures are earned from dharma and one achieves thereafter, detachment of vairagya.

In case the riches are used in a contrary manner, a person feels attracted with the worldly pleasures. Dharma is of two types, one is from matter or substance and the other from the body.

With the riches one earns dharma by performing of the yajnas, while dharma from the body is performed by the visiting of the sacred places. One earns wealth from wealth, while with the performing of the tapas one achieves the divine beauty.

With the performing of the karmas without desires, the heart is purified. With the purification of the heart, one achieves divine wisdom. There is no doubt about it. Earlier in the Satya-yuga, the tapas was always praised. But in the age of Kali, earning of the wealth is the only dharma.

In the age of Satya-yuga one could achieve jnana (knowledge or wisdom) by meditation. During the Treta-yuga the same was received with the performing of tapas or yajna. In Kali-yuga, the jnana is achieved with the worship of the images.

Whatever evil or noble deeds are performed by a person, he reaps the similar type of reward. Because of the dravya or the body there is the increase or decrease of the sins or the merits.

In case one enters into the killing which is prohibited in the scriptures it is against dharma. By behaving in an irreligious manner, one has to face the pain, and in case, one moves according to dharma the pleasures are increased.

With the evil behaviour one feels painful and with the noble conduct, one achieves the comforts. Therefore the persons desirous of pleasures and the moksa, should move on the path of dharma, earning the merits.

A donor should provide the means of living, wit family to a Brahmana for a hundred years. With the merit of the same the donor achieves Brahmaloka.

With the performing of a thousand Candrayana-vratas, one achieves Brahmaloka. A Ksatriya, who arranges for the livelihood of the ten thousand Brahmanas with families he achieves Indraloka. A Ksatriya who arranges for the livelihood of ten thousand Brahmanas achieves Brahmaloka. A person who donates in the name of a particular god, he achieves the place of the same god. This has been told by the people well-versed in the Vedas. A person having been deprived of riches should earn the riches of tapas.

The merit (dharma) which is achieved with the performing of pilgrimage but with the japam it bestows the everlasting pleasure. Now I shall speak out the method of earning the riches. The riches or wealth should be earned with justice and carefully.

The Brahmana should earn his living by charities, with the performing of the yajnas, by spotless conduct, being large hearted, or performing hard labour(?)

The Ksatriya should earn his living with the strength of his arms, the Vaisya, by farming, protecting the cows, besides earning livelihood by trade. By earning wealth by judicious means, and giving it in charities, a person achieves success.

With the achieving of jnana, all achieve moksa. By the grace of the preceptor, one achieves the beautiful form after achieving moksa. Thereafter one achieves the highest bliss.

O Brahmanas, all these benefits could be achieved by keeping company of the noble people. A householder should give riches and cereals in charity to the Brahmanas.

A householder, desirous of his welfare, should give to the Brahmanas, whatever things (or fruits etc.) are produced in a particular season, including the fruit, cereals, etc.

For the subsiding of hunger, thirst, ailment, the food and water should be given to the Brahmanas. Besides the land, cereals, uncooked and cooked food, all the four types of sweets, could also be given to the Brahmanas.

With the food and other things given by the donor to the Brahmanas, whatever noble deeds are performed by the latter, like the listening of the recitation of scriptures, and other noble deeds performed by him, half of the merit thereof goes to the donor.

The Brahmana, who receives the donation, should perform the repentance for the same,otherwise he is sure to fall in the terrific hell.

One should divide the wealth earned by him in three parts. One part should be for dharma, the second should be for development and third part should be used for the pleasure (or the daily life). He should perform all the auspicious karmas regularly daily.

The donor should utilise the development money for the sake of expansion and for that purpose, he should not trouble any one. He should not behave in an undesirable manner. He should consume wealth meant for pleasure slowly and gradually.

One tenth of the part of the farming produce should be donated for the sake of purification. With the remaining wealth one should perform the religious activities otherwise one has to go to the terrific hell.

A person who increases his wealth by sinful means, his crops would indeed be destroyed. One sixth of the wealth earned in trade should be donated.

The best of the Brahmana should give away in charity one fourth of his net income. In case one gets sudden money from somewhere, then half of it should be given in charity.

In case a Brahmana receives charity of illegal wealth, it should be thrown in the ocean and for his own uplift, he should distribute it among the Brahmanas.

One should give money to the beggars as per one’s own capacity. In case when one does not give, the charity after promising it, he becomes his debtor in the next birth.

A person with wisdom should not highlight the blemishes of others, even when they are well known to him.

A person with wisdom should not speak anything which could incite others. For the upkeep of one’s own fortunes, one should perform homa in the morning as well as in the evening.

In case a person is unable to perform the homa twice a day, then he should adore the sun and the fire once only appropriately, offering oblation of rice, cereals, ghee, fruit, roots etc.

He should prepare the offering in the appropriate manner. In the absence of the proper offerings one should perform the ordinary homa.

The fire, which is always consecrated is known by the name of Ajasra by the learned people or alternatively one should perform Surya-namaskara or the japam.

In this way the person desirous of knowing the atmatattva or the people desirous of wealth, should perform appropriately Brahma-yajna or the adoration of the god daily.

Such of the people, who adore with devotion, the fire as well as the preceptor, and provide food to the Brahmanas, are all entitled to a place in the heaven.

## Chapter 14 - Agni-sacrifice

Rsis said, “O Suta, you kindly narrate to us the performing of Agni-yajna, Deva-yajna, Brahma-yajna, Guru-puja and Brahma-trpti.”

Suta said, “The material which is offered in fire for the purpose of yajna, is called the Agni-yajna. A person in brahmacarya-dsrama should perform homa daily with pieces of wood (Samidha).

Î Brahmanas, the fire in which the homa is performed with Samidhas (pieces of wood) is the homa which should be performed from the age of boyhood till the marriage. This is the duty with a Brahmacari.

Î Brahmanas, those who have consecrated the fire in their own soul for such forest dwelling ascetics, are treated to perform the homa, when they take a little of food. They should be appropriately protected with devotion performing homa in the fire. This is called Agnihotra or homa for them.

With the performing of homa and meditation, they should be adequately protected. The fire should be preserved in a kunda or a vase appropriately.

Because of the fear of the god or the king, the one who preserves the fire in his own self or in arani (wooden drill), it is called Samaropana.

Î Brahmanas, the offerings made in the fire during evening time are called sampatkari. The offering made to the sun in the morning is called ayuskari.

The merging of the sun (rays) into the fire, is called Agni-yajna. The one who performs homa for the sake of Indra and others, (it is called Deva-yajna) Sthalikpdka and the rest of adoration is the worldly type of adoration and is established in the fire.

The Brahmanas should perform the Brahmayajna in order to please the gods daily. The study of the Vedas is also called the Brahmayajna.

It is not to be performed from morning till the evening or from evening to the night (or it could be performed during evenings alone). The Deva-yajna is performed without fire, and you listen to its method with faith and devotion.

At the beginning of creation, the universal knower and kindful Lord Siva, for the welfare of all the worlds, conceived of the valorous warriors.

First of all he created Sunday, which was the physician for the ailments of the world, was omniscient and was Osadhi for all the opadhis.

Then he created Monday- the day for the moon, which bestowed all the riches and was the form of his illusion. Thereafter Tuesday was created, which was painful at the birth of the son.

Then Wednesday was created which destroyed all the sins and laziness. Then with the desire of the welfare of the people, Thursday was created which was also the cause of its protection.

For the purpose of preservation and protection Friday was created. Then Saturday was created for the bestowing of the long life.

Thereafter Brahma, the creator of the universe who is called ParamesthI as well, created these weak days on earth.

First of all Brahma, for the sake of the expansion of the three worlds, created Indra and Yama, who gave rise to the merits and the sins respectively.
