In this way the week days like Sunday and others came in use according to their own names, which were indicative of the pleasure and pains of the people of the world, besides being the cause of facing the pleasure and pain and destruction of death.

Conceiving the masters of these week days, they were established in the astrological world. By adoring the respective gods in the respective week days, one achieves the appropriate reward, (it is said that Siva is the lord of Sunday, Durga is the mistress of Monday, Skanda is lord of Tuesday, Visnu for Wednesday, Yama for Thursday, Brahma for Friday and Indra for Saturday.)

Health, wealth, removal of ailments, increase in life, achieving of the pleasures, and destruction of death are the fruits of these week days respectively.

The result of the week days for their lords is that they please their lords always. Lord Siva of course bestows the reward for the worship of different gods.

There are five types of worship for pleasing the gods, which include mantras, japam, homa, charities and tapas.

Besides the images consecrated over the pedestals, offering oblations in fire, and the sixteen types of adorations performed in the fire or to the Brahmanas are other means of worship.

The above three types of worship when performed by a person, is the best and removes eye ailment, headache, besides the leprosy.

The one, who, after worshipping the sun serves food to a Brahmana for a month and &pound; day, or for three years (he achieves all the merits). In case the luck is favourable, then the ailments, or untimely old age would vanish.

One should pacify the sun on the Sunday, for the pleasure of the gods should also offer the appropriate wealth. The Sunday bestows special merits to the devotees.

The goddess Laksmi should be particularly adored on Monday for the achieving of the wealth. The sweets fried in ghee should be specifically served to the Brahmanas as food, by the devotee with his wife.

On Tuesday, one should adore goddess Kali for the removal of ailments. The Brahmanas should be served food with an adhaka (a measure) of cooked rice, black gram and green gram.

A learned person should adore Visnu offering the curd and cooked rice and by doing so the sons, friends, wife and other relatives remain happy and healthy.

The learned person desirous of long life, for pleasing the gods, adore them offering sacred thread, costumes, milk and ghee.

In case one is desirous of enjoying the pleasures, then he should attentively adore the gods on Fridays. For pleasing the Brahmanas, he should serve sixteen types of dishes to the Brahmanas.

In order to please the wives of the Brahmanas, one should give away the beautiful costumes. To safeguard against the untimely death, one should adore Rudra and other gods on Saturdays.

On Saturdays, one should serve the food with sesame, besides performing homa, and charities of the same. By thus adoring the gods, one gets the rewards like attaining good health.

By adoring the gods daily as well as on special occasions, one should resort to taking both, recitation, performing of charities, japam, homa and serving food to the Brahmanas.

With the combination of the day as well as Jagadlsvara only (Siva) serves as the lord of all the days and bestows the rewards like health, etc. according to the time, the country and the devotee.

The gods bestow the reward taking into consideration the material for adoration, the devotee, his faith, his intentions and make him healthy besides bestowing other rewards.

The Sun and other planets should be worshipped at the start of an auspicious occasion, at the end of it, and for seeking welfare for the household, the constellation of the birth, should be worshipped.

In this way the Deva-yajna bestows all types of the desired fruits. The adoration in the Brahmanas should be performed reciting the mantras, while in the house of Sudras and of the other varnas, the method prescribed in the tantras should be followed.

According to their means, for the purpose of achieving the auspicious reward, all the chiefs of the week days should be adored by the people.

The poor person should perform the tapas. The rich person should adore the gods with riches. Thus whosoever performs these religious deeds with great devotion, he, enjoying different types of the heavenly pleasures, and is reborn on earth. With the planting of the shady trees, building of wells, step-wells, setting up of schools, composing of religious books, are the acts which should be performed by the wealthy people, for the sake of enjoying comforts. After sometime when the merits are this earned one earns wisdom.

Î Brahmanas, a person who listens to this chapter or reads or recites it for others, he achieves the fruit of the Deva-yajna.

## Chapter 15 - Description of the country, time and vessel in Deva-yajna

The sages said, “O Suta, you are well aware of everything, therefore you kindly speak about the country and the time suitable for the adoration.” Suta said, “For the performing of the good deeds like the Deva- yajna, in one’s own house, yields equal merit.

One achieves ten times more of the reward by performing so in a cowshed, and ten times more of it by doing so at the bank of a river or a tank. Still one earns ten times more the reward by doing so under a creeper, the Tulasi plant (holy basil) or a plpala tree.

Still ten times more of the reward can be had by doing so in the temple of the god, and ten times more by doing so in one’s own house. One can get the reward ten times more of it, by performing at the river bank and still times more by doing so over the river bank at a sacred place.

Further ten times of the reward can be achieved by performing over the banks of the Saptaganga river, which include, Ganga, Godavari, Kaveri, Tamraparni, Sindhu, Sarayu and Reva. Still ten time more the reward can be achieved by performing at the seashore. Still ten times more reward can be had by performing over the mountain peak.

Indeed the best place is where a person is able to concentrate his mind. One gets the complete reward for the performing of the yajna, charities etc. in Satya-yuga.

In the Tretdyuga, the reward is reduced to a third of fit, while in Dvapara it is reduced to one fourth of it, which is further reduced towards the end of Kaliyaga.

A person with a spotless mind, when performs an auspicious deed on an auspicious day, it bestows equal rewards. Further ten times of the reward is achieved by a devotee on the SUrya-Sankrdnti day.

In case the first day of the month falls in Aries and Libra Zodiac signs, one gets ten times more the reward. It multiplies to ten times more, on the day the sun goes in the north of equator or in the south of equator, one gets ten times more reward. On the first day of Margas'Irsa, one achieves ten times more the reward, while on the day of lunar eclipse, the reward is further increased by ten times.

The reward is further multiplied to ten more times when the performance is made on the day of solar eclipse, which is the best because the visayoga of the sun, in the form the universe, which causes ailment to the people.

Therefore in order to pacify that poison, one should take a bath and perform charities as well as the japam. Because of it being the period of pacifying the poison, it is considered be the auspicious time.

At the end of the constellation of birth, the effect of the charities is like the solar eclipse. The keeping of the company of the ascetics is comparable to a crore of the solar eclipses.

Those performing tapas, the learned people, yogis as well as the yatis are adorable and by worshipping them the sins are washed out.

Or a Brahmana having recited the Gayatri mantra by twenty four lakhs of times, he also is adorable and by adoring him one gets all the comforts.

The one, who saves others from falling, is called Patra in the scriptures. One who protects donor from sins is also called Patra.

The one who saves a singer from falling in the hell is called Gayatri. In other words, the one who always recites Gayatri-mantra, the said mantra protects him. As the penniless person cannot give money to the other person, and the rich man can give wealth to others, similarly a person, who himself is spotless and pure, can protect others.

A Brahmana who recites the Gayatri- mantra is considered to be purified. Therefore in the activities like giving of charities, japam, performing of homa and adoration, for the receiving of the donations and to protect the host, Brahmana is the appropriate person. He is also the suitable person to receive the food. Whosoever, be a man or a woman, when invites the excellent Brahmana, then he should carefully give the charities. His word and its meaning portrays the intelligence and bestows the desired reward.

A Brahmana who is in need, when given the charity, it would bestow the complete reward. The charity which is given after begging, bestows half the merit.

The charity which is given to a servant bestows one fourth of the merit. Î Brahmanas, a Brahmana, whose entire family is poor, in case the charity is given to him, the donor achieves comforts, for ten years on earth. By giving the charities to a Brahmana, well- versed in the Vedas the donor earns comforts for ten years in the heaven.

The Brahmana who recites Gayatri, and if the charity is given to him, the donor, as a reward thereof, enjoys pleasures in Satyaloka for ten years. The one who gives charity to a Brahmana, who is devoted to Visnu, the donor achieves Vaikuntha (after his death).

By giving charity to a Brahmana devoted to Siva, the donor achieves Kailasa, the abode of Siva. The charity is given for achieving of those respective places.

If a donor gives charity food to the ten Brahmanas with the incense composed of ten ingredients (which is used at the time of worship), he, in the next birth remains healthy and without any ailment for ten years.

The dasanga donation of the food includes to respect, application of invite, an ointment over the body, pressing of the feet, adoring with costumes, fragrance and then adoring a Brahmana, offering sweet cakes, six types of eatables, betel, offering of money as daksina, salutation to see off some one after walking some distance are called the dasanga- annadana.

When a donor gives dasanga food to the Brahmanas on Sunday, he remains healthy for a hundred years.

The giving away of the food on Sunday and other days is rewarded according to the quality of the food. By giving away the food, one is reborn as a human being in the next birth.

When the Brahmanas are served dasanga food on all the seven days of the week, he is rewarded with health and other benefits.

Similarly when a donor serves food to a hundred Brahmanas on Sunday, he remains hale and hearty for a thousand years, and then achieves the place of Siva.

By serving food to the ten thousand Brahmanas, one enjoys all the pleasures for ten thousand years. Similar is the case with Monday and, other week days.

By serving food to ten thousand Brahmanas, who purify themselves with reciting of the Gayatri-mantra, the donor remains healthy for long in the Satyaloka.

A donor by serving food to ten thousand Brahmanas achieves the Visnuloka, and by serving food to a lakh of Brahmana he achieves the Indraloka.

The persons desirous of achieving wisdom or knowledge, should serve food to the Brahmana boys with Brahmabuddhi. The persons who are desirous of sons, should serve food to the young Brahmanas taking them to be lord Visnu.

The people who are desirous of achieving prana or wisdom, should serve food to the old Brahmanas taking them to be Siva. The girls should be served food taking them to be Sarasvati, with the intention of achieving wisdom.

The persons who intend to enjoy comforts, should serve food to the young damsels, taking them to be the form of Laksmi. The persons desirous of self consciousness, should serve food to the old Brahmana women taking them to be Parvati.

The amount earned with getting of the grain after harvest, or having livelihood from the gleaning of the field, or the amount earned by means of guru-daksina, is considered to be quite pure. One achieves full merits by donating the same.

The money received from the Brahmana as the amount of donation is called the dravya of middle rung. The amount earned by forming and trade is treated as the inferior.

The money earned by the Ksatriyas by means of prowess, the money earned by the Vaisyas by trade, and the money earned by the Sudras, by means of serving others, is called the best.

The amount the women receive from their husbands and the parents is fit for religious purposes. On the month of Caitra, and others, one should give away twelve things including the cows.

Or one should give away these things for the sake of charity during the auspicious time, which include the cow, land, sesamum, gold, ghi, costumes, cereals, guda, silver, salt, pumpkin and the girl. These are the twelve dravyas which would be given in charities. Giving away of a cow, or the padartha made of cow’s milk, and the cow-dung which does good, to remove the pains of the people who are dependants financially on others. With the use of water, cow’s urine etc., the miseries of the dependants should be removed.

Similarly with the use of the milk, curd and ghee, the sins committed by body, speech and the mind are removed and the merits are increased. This should be understood by the people with wisdom.

Î Brahmanas, with the donation of land, a person is honoured in this world as well as the future world. With the giving away of sesamum, the strength is increased and one overcomes the death.

With the giving away of the gold, the power of digestion is increased besides the strength. The body becomes stronger with the giving away of ghee. The age is increased with the giving away of the clothes.

With the giving away of the cereals, the fortunes are increased, by giving of the guda, one gets sweet food. By giving away the silver, strength is increased and by giving away of the salt, all the six rasas are increased.

Î Brahmanas, the pumpkin, bestows all types of fortunes, and all the pleasures in both the worlds.

By performing kanyadana a person enjoys pleasure throughout the life. The jack-fruit, mango, the wood-apple, the fruits of banana and other osadhis or those which emerge from creepers and shrubs besides the black gram, green gram, green vegetables, black pepper, mustard seeds, or whatever vegetables or fruits are grown in whatever season, they should be given to the Brahmanas.

The learned people should give to the Brahmana, such of the things which please the ears and other organs of the body. By giving away the ten things relating to the sound, all the ten directions are pleased.

The devout people say, by hearing the Vedas and other scriptures from the preceptor, one surely gets the reward.

By fear of the relatives or friends or the king, the devoutness which develops in a person, is considered to be a bit lesser than best of devout wisdom. The poor people in the absence of all the dravyas noted above should adore the lord with their sweet voice and noble deeds.

The reciting of mantras, strotras (eulogy), japam (muttering) should be treated as the adoration by the tongue. The vratas (fasting) and going on pilgrimage is to be treated as the adoration with the body.

Whatever deed is performed in honour of the god or the slightest dedication to him bestows comfort to the performer.

The charities and the tapas should be performed daily. Beautified with one’s own varna and the noble qualities, even the house should be donated.

With the charities given for the pleasure of the gods, one achieves all types of comforts and by doing so, one achieves comforts in the present as well as the future life. In case the charities are dedicated to the lord Siva, one achieves salvation.

A person who listens or reads this chapter, he attains devotion in dharma as well as the spotless wisdom.

## Chapter 16 - Description of the adoration of Parthiva Linga

The sages said, “O Suta, you kindly explain to us the Parthiva(clay idols) type of adoration, performing which one achieves all type of success.”

Suta said, “O Sages, you have asked me the best question which always bestows the fulfilment of all the desires and by which all the miseries are over, I am going to speak to you about the same.

Î Brahmana, the Parthiva type of adoration, drives away the untimely death, as well as the natural death and bestows, always, the wealth, cereals, wife and the sons. Since all the padarthas like the food, cereals, costumes etc.' emerge out of the earth, therefore the linga made in earth makes one succeed in all his wishes.

Both the men and women can equally participate in the same. For (the purpose of making an earthen linga) the clay from the water in the middle of the river, tank, or the well has to be collected.

Then the clay should be purified adding to it, the fragrant powder. It should then be carried to a well built mandapa, and milk should be mixed with it. The image or the linga should be made of clay using the milk.

All the limbs should be made, while the weapons should be placed in the appropriate limbs. The image should then be placed over the lotus seat and then adored with respect.

A Brahmana should adore Ganesa, Surya, Visnu, Parvati, Siva, besides Sivalinga, with sixteen types of worship in order to achieve the best results. Then showering the flowers, he should perform the abhiseka reciting the Vedic hymns.

For the Sivalinga consecrated in the house, the one kudavanaivedya of fine rice should be offered, while the linga consecrated by the people, a prastha (a particular measure) of naivedya should be offered.

Besides double or three times of the naivedya could also be offered.

A thousand prasthas of naivedya when offered by a Brahmana, he achieves the Satyaloka in reality. The linga when made twenty five fingers in length, and fifteen fingers in height, in iron or wood, the people with wisdom call it Siva.

Its one eighth part is called prastha, and one fourth of it is called kudava. The water, oil, fragrance and other dravyas, should be offered to the linga consecrated by a person, in the aforesaid manner, offering ten prasthas of the naivedya. To a linga consecrated by a rsi a hundred prasthas of naivedya should be offered and the linga which appeared of its own should be offered a thousand prasthas of naivedya adoring it, which is called Mahapuja.

With the offering of abhiseka to the said linga one’s soul gets purified, one achieves merits by offering, the fragrance to it. The offering of naivedya, increases the length of life and satisfaction, and by offering the same one achieves merits.

With the offering of the lamp, one achieves wisdom, the offering of the betel bestows the worldly pleasures, therefore one should adore the linga by six types of methods.

With the offering of salutation as well as performing of japam all the desires are fulfilled. The people desirous of pleasures as well as the moksa, should make use of the salutation and the japam at the end of the adoration.

In the mental puja as well as in all the six types of methods of adoration, should also be made use of and by doing so, the people achieve the respective places.

Î Brahmanas, the devotees of this type also enjoy all the pleasures of the intervening lokas which I am going to speak out to you. You please listen to me carefully.

On the fourth day of the bright fortnights of he months of Sravana and Bhadrapada, on Friday, Ganesa should be adored appropriately. In this way by adoring Ganes'a, a person achieves the desired things in the world.

On the day of Satabhisa constellation in the month of Tausa, Ganes'a should appropriatel) adored. Thus adoring Ganesa in a hundred or ã thousand times, a person enjoys comforts foi an equivalent number of days.

By adoring the god or the fire-god daily, with devotion, a person is relieved of all the pains of the sins.

By adoring Siva and other gods on theii respective week-days, the soul gets purified or the basis of the favourable day, constellations and the yogas, all the desires are fulfilled.

A day which is free from rise or down fall, is like the Purna-Brahman. In the activities of the Brahmanas, the day of rising and the week day have been taken into account.

The adoration of the god which is done at the end of lunar day, it bestows complete reward. In case the tithi is in the afternoon, then the first part of the same combined with the night, is considered to be good for performing rites for the manes.

The next day is considered to be auspicious for the performing of the auspicious deeds. In case the tithi is upto noon, then it should be taken to have been the rising one.

The deeds relating to the gods should be performed in the auspicious constellations, etc. The appropriate week day should also be taken into consideration, before performing the adoration or japam.

In this way, the method prescribed in the Vedas is also established. Such type of adoration, also bestows all the pleasures and the desired rewards.

With the achieving of all the desires of the mind, one also achieves the desired padarthas, and this is called the adoration. This interpretation of adoration is popular with the people as well as the Vedas.

The karmas of the casual as well of daily nature, bestow the reward after sometime, while the kamya karmas bestow quick results. The karmas of daily nature, bestow awards according to the fortnight, month, year respectively.

By performing adoration, one achieves the respective fruits. The sins are also destroyed in the same sequence. On the fourth day of the black fortnight, Mahaganapati is adored, which destroys the sins of a fortnight, and bestows pleasures for the same period. On the fourth moon day of the month of Caitra, when Mahaganapati is adored, its effect lasts for one month.

With Leo in the Sun, during the fourth moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, the adoration of Mahaganapati, bestow comforts for a year. On the seventh moon day of the month of Sravana, falling on Sunday, during the Hasta Constellation, and on the seventh bright day of the month of Magha, one should adore Suryanarayana. During the months of Jyestha and Bhadrapada, on the tenth moon day, during the Sravana constellation, if Lord Visnu is adored bestows the desired reward. The adoration of Visnu, performed during the month of Sravana, bestows the desired reward besides keeping the healthy body.

The person who achieves the reward by giving away in charity the twelve padarthas (see ch. 15.43-44) earning the related reward, the same reward is achieved by adoring Visnu on the twelfth day of the moon.

On the twelfth moon day when a person adores the twelve Brahmana, extending sixteen modes of worship, with twelve names of Visnu, the gods feel pleased with the same.

Similarly by serving food to the twelve Brahmanas, with the respective names of the gods, the gods feel pleased with the same.

On the ninth day of the moon when the sun is in the Cancer cycle of zodiac, during the Mrgasira constellation, a person desirous of pleasures, should adore the goddess Amba, who bestows all the pleasures.

During the bright ninth day of the month of Asvin, in case the goddess Bhagavati is adored, she bestows the desired rewards, particularly so, during the fourteenth dark day, falling on Sunday.

Particularly during the Ardra or Maha-ardra constellation the adoration of Siva results in bestowing the best reward. Further the Siva-puja performed on the fourteenth dark day of the month of Magha, fulfils all the desires.

It increases the age, destroys the death and bestows all the success to the people on the fourteenth moon day falling in the Ardra constellation during the month of Jyestha, one should adore Siva.

During the Ardra constellation of the month of Margasirsa, one should adore lord Siva with the sixteen methods, in the form of the images. Their feet are worth seeing.

By adoring Siva, a person achieves the pleasures as well as the moksa. On the seven week days, when the gods are adored in the month of Kartika, they bestow special merit.

On the arrival of the month of Kartika the learned person, should adore all the gods and give away charities, perform puja, tapas, homa and should lead a disciplined life.

When the image of a particular gods has to be adored by sixteen methods, it should be adored by the Brahmanas reciting the mantras and should serve food to the Brahmanas in a detached manner. By doing so all the pains are removed.

During the month of Kartika, the adoration of the gods, bestows comforts of all the types. The ailments and goblins also get destroyed.

On a Sunday in the month of Kartika, one should adore the sun offering sesamum, and cotton and by doing so, leprosy and other ailments disappear.

By giving away the black myrobalan, pepper, clothes, and milk, and by honouring the Brahmanas, the consumption is removed.

By giving away the lamp and mustard oil, the ailments like epilepsy get removed. In case one adores lord Siva on Monday in the Krttika constellation, his poverty is destroyed and his house is filled with fortunes. By giving away house, fields, and house-hold things, one gets all types of riches.

On Tuesday during Krttika constellation, in case Kartikeya is adored, giving away a lamp, bell, etc., a person achieves excellence in his speech.

In case Visnu is adored on Tuesday during the Krttika constellation, and with the giving away of the curd and cooked rice, one achieves competent children.

In case one adores Brahma with riches during the Krttika constellation, giving at the same time, honey, and ghee, a person rises in heights and there is an increase in the comforts.

By adoring Ganesa on Friday during the Krttika constellation, offering the fragrance and flowers, the homely pleasures of the people are increased.

By giving away in charity the gold and the silver, even the barren woman gets the son. When the Krttika constellation falls on Saturday, then the Dikpalas should be adored.

By adoring the elephants of the directions, the serpents, the protectors of the Setu bridge, Trayambaka the destroyer of the sins, Rudra and Visnu, Brahma, the bestower of wisdom, Dhanvantari and Asvani-kumaras, the ailments as well as the untimely death are destroyed and one feels peaceful.

By giving away in charity, salt, iron, oil, black gram, ginger, chillies, pepper, long pepper, the fragrant stuff, besides the water and other liquid things, in addition to the hard stuff equivalent to a prastha or sixty four tolas when given in the month of Pausa, and adoring them in the early morning, Siva and other gods, when adored appropriately, bestow all types of success. The naivedya of superior quality of rice, or that of havisya is considered to be the best.

In the month of Pausa, in case several types of naivedya are offered to the sun, one gets excellent reward. A person who gives away in charity, the food in the month of Margasirsa, all his desires are fulfilled.

The ritualistic performance for the washing out of the sins, the success in one’s mission, removal of ailments, achieving of dharma, proper knowledge of the Vedas, devotion towards the noble deeds, the gaining of the best place in the present as well as the future world and an increase in the knowledge could be achieved in case a person gives food in charity in the month of Margasirsa, or other wise, if a person, getting up early in the morning during the month of Margasirsa, desirous of enjoying pleasure for three days, should adore the gods, but before the start of the month of Pausa, till the next day of the month does not start, upto that time the month of Pausa remains. By controlling all the senses during this one month, observing fast (without taking food), one should recite the mantra of Gayatri- the mother of the Vedas. Thereafter till a person goes to sleep, one should recite the Pancaksara or other mantras.

While achieving wisdom in this way, the Brahmana achieves salvation after his death. The woman of other varnas can achieve the same reward by taking bath thrice a day (i.e. in the morning, noon and the evening).

By reciting of the Pancaksara-mantra always, one achieves the spotless wisdom. By the reciting of the favourite mantras the terrific sins are washed out.

In the month of Pausa, the maha-naivedya should be offered. A bhara (ninety five kilos) of superior type of rice, a prastha of black pepper, and the other padarthas should be given, twelve times more in weight, the honey and the ghee should be given a quarter in weight. The queen grain should be given a drona (sixteen sears) in weight. Besides these eighteen edible things should be given.

The sweet balls fried in ghee, the modaka besides the twelve padarthas including the superior type of rice should also be given.

The coconut, the betel nut, should be given, each twelve in number. The betel leaves should be thirty six in number.

The fragrant powder, five types of fragrances (camphor, cloves, gourd, betel, nut, nutmeg) should be added in the betel. The naivedya thus offered is called Mahanaivedya.

After offering the Mahanaivedya to the god, the people who are devoted to the said god, should distribute the naivedya according to the sequence of the varnas.

By giving away the Mahanaivedya in charity, together with the cooked rice, the devotee becomes the ruler on earth.

Î Brahmanas, by giving away the Mahanaivedya a thousand times, with cooked rice, the donor lives full life in this world and even in Satyaloka.

A devotee who donates the Mahanaivedya three thousand times, he achieves the heaven and is never born on earth again.

The thirty six thousand of Mahanaivedyas are called Janma-naivedyas. To donate Mahanaivedyas of this member is quite important and has been called as Mahapurna.

The naivedya of Siva is called Janma- naivedya and by giving away the same in charity, a person has not to be reborn on earth.

On an auspicious day in the month of Kartika, or on (the first day of the said month) in the Vyatipata-yoga, during the constellation of the birth or on the full moon day, Janma-naivedya should be got prepared, or otherwise when the constellation of the birthday falls in any other month, or when the Ðīãñṁ-yoga is there, one should arrange for the Janma-naivedya.

Or alternatively when the Saturn is in combination with the constellation of the birth, Janma-naivedya should be given and by doing so one achieves the fruit of Janmarpana.

With the performing of Janmarpana Siva is pleased and he bestows the Sdyujya type of salvation. This Janma-naivedya should be offered to Siva alone.

Because of the form of linga and yoni, Siva give the birth. Therefore, in order to relieve oneself of the rebirth, Siva should be adored.

The entire moveable and immovable world is the form of the bindu (spot) and nada (sound). The spot stands for sakti, while Siva stands for nada (sound). Therefore the entire world has the form of Siva and Sakti.

Nada (sound) is the base of bindu (spot) and the base of bindu is the world. Both nada and the bindu have been established as the base of the world.

With the union of the bindu and nada, it units with all the arts. This is the cause of the creation. There is no doubt about it.

Linga is the form of bindu and nada, which is the cause of creation of the universe. Bindu is the goddess while linga is the form of Siva.

Therefore in order to escape from the rebirth, one should adore Sivalinga, because the bindu in the form of the goddess happens to be the mother and linga in the form of Siva is the father.

By adoring the parents, one achieves immense bliss. Therefore in order to achieve the highest bliss, one should adore Sivalinga.

The goddess happens to be the mother of the entire universe, while Siva is the father. Such of the people who adore the parents, they remain graceful over their sons.

Î Munisvaras, Siva bestows the fortunes over his devotees by his grace alone and one has the benefit of the bliss as well.

Taking it to be the form of the parents, Sivalinga should be adored. Siva has the form of a male, while Prakrti has the form of a female.

Those who live in it are called unclear womb is called the purusa and the one who clearly lives in the womb in the form of Mahat-tattva, is called Prakrti.

The Adi-garbhapurusa alone because of his relationship with Prakrti, is conceived with womb. Therefore he is called Janaka. When the Purusa and Prakrti are united, then it is called the first birth.

With the emerging of Prakrti, it is called the second birth. The Jiva therefore gets the birth and the death from Purusa.

Certainly the birth is induced by Maya as an extraneous source. The word Jiva means that which gets decayed even from the time of birth.

Another meaning of the Jiva is that which is born enmeshed and entwined. Hence the devotee shall worship the primordial phallic image for loosening the knot and the nooses of the birth.

The word Bhaga means the primordial nature because it increases and flourishes. The Sabda-matras etc. (the cosmic sound principle i.e. all objects of enjoyment) evolved out of Prakrti, being enjoyed by the sense organs, the word Bhaga comes to mean that which gives Bhaga. Bhaga is of course the Prakrti and Bhagavan is Lord Siva himself.

Bhagavan alone bestows the worldly pleasures. No one else except him bestows the worldly pleasures. Bhagavan is indeed the lord of Bhaga, therefore he is also called Bhaga.

Bhaga is meant for linga and the linga is meant for bhaga in this world as well as in the paraloka.

Sivalinga of Mahadeva should be adored with bhaga. The Sun is the creator of the universe, therefore it is also called as bhaga.

Siva should be adored in the form of linga, which produces the world. The symbol which stands for linga is called Sivalinga.

The Purusa, who is revealed by the speaking of the world linga, he is called Siva. The combined form of Siva and Sakti is called linga.

With the adoration of Sivalinga, Siva gets pleased. There is no other purpose for this linga. This symbol is the initial cause of birth, and by adoring the same, a devotee is freed from the birth.

Even the foolish (Prakrta) people should adore the linga by sixteen outer as well inner methods.

By adoring the linga thus, on Sundays, one is relieved of the rebirth. On Sunday the Mahalinga should be adored with the om- mantra.

On Sunday particularly, Siva should be bathed with pahcagavya which include cow- dung, urine, milk, curd, and ghee, which should be mixed together and this mixture is called pahcagavya.

The linga should be bathed separately with milk. The naivedya should be prepared with payasam made of honey, juice of sugarcane, and milk and should be offered to Sivalinga reciting the omkara-mantra.

Omkara is the dhvani-linga, while mdalinga is Svayambhu. Bindulinga is the form of yantra, in which Makara is established.

Ukara is Caralinga (moveable), Akdra is the body of the guru. In this way the six types of lingas should be adored, and by doing so one is freed from the bondage during the life time.

Adoring Siva with devotion relieves the people from the cycle of birth and death and bestows salvation. By wearing the rosaiy of Rudraksa one earns one fourth of the merit. By application of the ashes, one earns half the merit.

The reciting of the mantra earns one third of the merit and with the performing of the adoration, one earns full merit.

Î Brahmanas, whosoever reads this chapter with devotion or listens to it, his devotion in Siva is established and it keeps on increasing.

## Chapter 17 - Glory of Pranava-paficaksara-mantra

The rsis said, “O Great Muni, Î Lord, you kindly enlighten us on the glory of Pranava {omkara) Sadalinga and the worship of the devotee of Siva.

Suta said, “You the ascetics, have put me a very good question, the answer to which is known only to lord Mahadeva alone and none else.

But still I shall speak out the same by the grace of lord Siva. Let Siva protect you and me by all means.

You should be treated as the boat created by the wise Prakrti, to enable you to cross the ocean of the universe.

The three letters combined in omkara means thus:- Pra (???)= of Prakrti or the world devolved out of it, (delusion), na (???)= no, va (???) to you; in other words with the reciting of the Pranava mantra, you would be free from delusion.

It is also called Pranava, because it destroys all the karmas of the yogis reciting it and bestows the fresh divine wisdom to them.

Since Pranava is devoid of delusion, it is called new. It particularly bestows on the great sages, new spotless form.

Because of its bestowing the new, fresh and spotless form, the intelligent people call it Pranava. The Pranava is of two types viz.: gross and subtle.

The subtle form has a single letter while the gross form comprises of five letters. Its subtle form is invisible, while Pancdksara form is visible.

A person who is free from the worldly bondages, represents the gist of all the Vedas. The yogis carry on research on this mantra throughout their lives.

In this way when the body becomes weak while engaged in meditation, then a yogi ultimately achieves Siva in the long run. Only a person who recites the mantra achieves yoga.

A person who recites the mantra thirty six crores of times he surely achieves the yoga. Its subtle form has two types viz.:- short and long.

Pranava is the combination of akara, a, ukara, u, Makara, m and the bindu or the spot which represents nada, besides the words, time and the rays.

Omkara which comprises of the three short vowels, always resides in the hearts of the yogis. The tritattva (???) (makara) (???) is known as small Pranava.

With the combination of Siva and Sakti, makara combines in itself the three tattvas viz.: sattva, rajas and tamas. The people desirous of the removal of all the sins should recite the Hrasva or small Pranava.

There is a link between Prthivi (earth), Vayu (wind), teja (light or fire), Sabda or the sound, and the ten directions. Therefore all these ten follow the path of pravrtti (or remain in attachment with worldly objects). This is the opinion of the great sages.

Such of the people who are involved in the worldly affairs, should meditate upon the Hrasva (small) îḍêīãṁ and those who are desirous of retirement from the world they should recite dirgha-omkara. In the beginning of the Vydhrtis or the mantras one can use hrasva or dlrgha Pranava according one’s liking. This Pranava should be used on both the times (morning as well as the evening) in combination with the Vedic hymns. By reciting this mantra nine crores of times, a person gets purified.

Again by reciting the mantra nine crores of times a person could conquer the entire world. By further reciting the mantra by nine crores of times, one can conquer the tattva of the water.

Then by further performing of the japam nine crores of times one can conquer the tejas or fire tattva-, by further reciting the mantra nine crores of times, one can conquer the tattvas of the wind and the sky.

Then by further reciting the mantra nine crores of times one can overpower the fragrance and arrogance.

Î Brahmanas, by reciting this Pranava mantra by a thousand times daily, one gets purified, earning self-consciousness.

In this way, by reciting the omkara mantra hundred and eight crores of times a person achieves self consciousness and also achieves the spotless yoga.

By achieving of the spotless yoga, a person is relieved of all the worldly bondages. There is no doubt about it. Therefore, one should always meditate upon Siva, the form of Pranava.

A MahayogI engaged in meditation represents the form of Siva himself. Keeping in mind the rsi, meter and the god etc. in his body, one should them recite the mantra.

The Pranava, combined with śḍ and with due ritualistic is lodged in the body which turns into the rsi. By invoking the ten Matrikas and six adhvas (pathas) one achieves the complete reward of the nyasa or the pledge.

The sthula-Pranava should be recited by both the types of people, engaged on the worldly affairs as well as those who feel detached from it. The Siva-yogis are of three types based on the activities, tapas as well as the difference in tapas.

Such of the people who adore Siva offering the riches, serving with hands or other parts of the body or offering their salutation to the lord, are called the kriya-yogis or yogis with action.

Those who are engaged in Siva’s adoration, taking little food, exercising control over the outer organs and those free from the jealousy of others are called the Tapo-yogls.

Those performing the adoration, who always remain spotless, free from kama (desire), krodha (anger) etc. always engaged in recitation, with peaceful mind, are called Japa-yogls.

The one who adores Siva-yogi with sixteen methods, he getting purified, achieves the sdlokya type of salvation.

Î Brahmanas, now I am going to speak on japa-yoga. You please listen to the same (with devotion). Only a tapasvl (an ascetic) has the right to perform the japam, and by doing so all the sins committed by a person, through out the life are washed out.

Î Brahmanas îḍ namah Sivaya is the Siva-mantra of five tattvas and is the original form of Pranava.

A person by reciting this Pancaksara mantra achieves all the success in his life. Therefore, a person should recite this Pancaksara-mantra in combination with omkara.

Î Brahmanas, according to the command of the preceptor, one should be clad in beautiful garments, should be seated over the ground on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight and start the japam of the mantra, which should be ended on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.

For this purpose the months of Bhadrapada or Magha are considered to be the best. The devotee should take small quantity of food once a day, should speak little and control his senses.

He should serve the manes of his king daily, otherwise he remains indebted to them. He should recite the Pancaksara mantra, atleast for a thousand, times in a day for the purpose of self purification.

One should invoke Siva adorned with the Ganga and the crescent moon over his head and seated peacefully over an asana in padmasana posture and should recite the Pancaksara mantra five lacs of times, which bestows welfare.

Siva has Parvati seated to his left, is surrounded by the ganas, who display the abhaya and varada-mudras in their hands. Lord Candrasekhara, and all merciful Sadasiva should be adored. Then he should adore Siva in his mind and then in the solar disc.

The devotee of Siva then should face east, engage himself in spotless deeds, should get up early in the morning on the dark fourteenth day of the fortnight, and free himself from the daily routine and then should recite the Pancaksara mantra.

He should be seated at a beautiful and auspicious place and with a pure mind recite twelve thousand times, the Pancaksara mantra.

The devotee of Siva with his wife, should patronise the Brahmanas, and should also patronise a Brahmana, as the form of Siva and Parvati.

He should also patronise five more Brahmanas devoted to Siva, in order to represent five forms of Siva viz. Isana, Purusa, Aghora, Varna and Sadyojata.

Collecting the material for adoration, Siva should be worshipped appropriately, performing the homa at the same time.

He should perform homa in the fire according to the Grhyasiitras making the offerings of ten hundred or ten thousand oblations.

The host himself should offer in the fire the oblation of the ghee of the white cow and also make the devotees of Siva to make a hundred and eight offerings in the fire.

At the end of homa, the Brahmanas representing Isana and others, besides the preceptors, and Samba Siva, should be given the daksina and two cows or a cow and a bull.

The water which is left after washing the feet of the Brahmanas, should be sprinkled by the host over his head, and by doing so he earns the merit of having a bath in thirty six crores of the auspicious places.

After giving das'anga food to the Brahmanas, then the wife of the preceptor should also be adored. The Brahmanas should be adored in the form of Isana and others.

Offering them the payasam according to one’s ability, they should be adored offering Rudraksa, costumes, sweet balls etc. should also be given to them.

At the end, performing the sacrifice, food should be served to the Brahmanas. Then offering prayer to Mahadeva, the japam should be concluded.

In this way when a repetition is done in a properly, the devotee attains success in the mantra. Then after reciting the mantra five lacs of times all his sins are destroyed.

With the performing of the five lacs of japam from Atala-loka to Satyaloka, one achieves the fortunes of each one of the five lokas.

In case the performer dies during the course of japam, then the said devotee of Siva, after enjoying the effect of all his noble deeds, is reborn on earth and he again resorts to japam. By performing the japam of five lacs times, he achieves the Brahma-Sayujya.

By further reciting of five lac times, he achieves the Sarupya fortunes. By reciting the mantra a crore of times, he is turned like a Brahmana.

Thus with the use of karya brahman he achieves Sayujya and he enjoys all the pleasures according to his own liking till the end of Brahma’s kalpa.

Again with the arrival of the next kalpantara, he becomes the son of Brahma, then with the performing of the severe tapas, he becomes illustrious and achieves salvation.

These lokas have been formed with five mahabhiitas including the earth. From Patalaloka to Satyaloka, there are fourteen lokas.

From Satyaloka to Ksama (Vaikuntha) are fourteen Visnulokas. Vaikuntha, which is the best of the place, is also called Ksamaloka, which is the dwelling place of Visnu.

The MahabhogI lives there for the protection of all. Above that there are twenty- eight lokas upto Suciloka.

Kailasa is lodged above the Suciloka, which is the abode of Rudra who destroys all the creatures. Further above, there are fifty six lokas upto Ahimsaloka.

Residing at Ahimsaloka, Karyesvara concealing all, lives at Jnanakailas'apura.

Above the Ahimsaloka, there is the Kalacakraloka and still further is the Kalatltaloka. It happens to be the dwelling place of Kalacakresvara.

Getting established in Mahisadharma, he unites eveiyone with the time. Falsehood, blemish, violence, and shamelessness, are the four amsas of Siva, the atheist Laksmi, evil company, Vedabahya (driven out of the Vedic faith), the anger, black colour, Mahamahisa forms, have Mahesvara as their lord. By the grace of Siva the anger etc. disappear.

Thereafter, karmabhoga, jndnabhoga, karma-maya and jndna-mdya are there. The word Maya represents Laksmi or the knowledge.

In other words, Maya, is so called because Laksmi makes a person to enjoy all the pleasures and the knowledge.

Beyond these bhogas is the nitya-bhoga and before that is nasvara and then concealment, which is not after it.

Before that is pasabandhana (binding in fetters), but thereafter, there is no pas'abandhana. Before that the creatures return on the basis of the deeds performed by them.

After that starts the niskamakarmayoga. In the loka earlier to it the people remain engaged in the adoration qf the bindu (spot), who return to earth according to their karmas.

The devotees of Siva who adore linga without any desire achieve the still higher loka. The devotee who adore the gods other than Siva reach the place lower than that of Siva.

Those who adore Siva alone, reach the place still higher than that. jivakoti is before that place and beyond that in Sivakoti.

Prior to that place, the worldly jivas reside. Those who attain salvation live beyond that place. Those who adore the natural dravyas live in the lowest of the lokas.

In the loka, far from this, there live the devotees of Paurusa-dravyas. The sakti-linga precedes them while the Sivalinga follows them.

Saguna linga is lodged before it while the Nirguna-linga is above it. Ahead of it is, the kalpita linga and still further is the akalpita- linga.

Thereafter, there is the Adhibhautika Brahmalinga, after which there is the Adhydtmika Antaranga linga and beyond that are a hundred and twelve Sakti-lokas.

Beyond them, there are Binduriipa, Nadarupa, Karmaloka and Jnanaloka.

Further beyond, there is a loka named Namaskara which removes the pride and arrogance. Further beyond that, there are Jana and Tirodhana lokas, from where the people never return.

The meaning of jnana means, the removal of Tirodhana. Beyond that place the people are engaged in adhibhautika type of adoration.

Those who perform the adhyatmika (divine) type of adoration, live above that place in the Mahaloka called Atmalinga for a long time.

The people living there are aware of the eight types of the bondages like Prakrti, Mahatattva, pride and pahca-tan-matras. Thus they have the worldly as well as the Vedic divisions.

Those who are truthful and adore lord Siva, they cross the kdlacakra who rides over the buffalo in the form of adharma.

The Vrsabha as dharma taking to the form of Brahmacarya is found there. It has the four feet like truth and others and is lodged beyond Sivaloka.

The best of the bull has forgiveness as the horns, peace is the ear and is decorated with the sound of the Vedas. The faith represent his eyes, and the mind is the preceptor's wisdom in the form of his breath.

This is to be known that these all deeds (dharmas) of bull are lodged always in karana-Brahma (primary cause). Beyond these all kalatita (Siva) is mounted there.

The day is counted of their own life of Brahma, Visnu and Mahesa. Beyond that there is neither the day nor the night. Further there is neither the birth nor the death.

Then till Satyalokas, the cause of the kdrana Brahma have been lodged always over the subtle elements smell etc. and other Bhutas.

The fourteen lokas are established with the subtle gandha form. The kdrana- Visnu's fourteen lokas are lodged beyond that.

Then the twenty eight lokas of karana- Rudra are said to be there. Still beyond them are the fifty six lokas of karana-lsvara.

Beyond them, there is a brahmacarya-loka recognised by Siva. There is also the Adilinga with Adisakti, in Jnana-Kailasa-loka combined with Pancavarana (covered from five ways), five mandalas and the five kalas of Brahma.

This place happens to be the Sivalaya or the abode of supreme-souled Siva. It is this place, where lord Siva lives with his Sakti.

Lord Siva, who creates, preserves, destroys, conceals and showers his grace, is lodged there in the form of sat-cit and ananda (bliss).

The one whose dhydna is the dharma, who is always compassionate to the people, the one who is seated in meditation and is absorbed in self, looking graceful.

One can have audience with him by adoring him. By performing the karmas daily one develops the inclination by adoring Siva.

One should attain the knowledge about Siva by performing his adoration daily. On whomsoever, the lord Siva casts his benevolent sight, he indeed achieves salvation. There is no doubt about it.

The bliss of self consciousness is called salvation. Such a person is devoted to his actions, tapas, japam, jnana, meditation and dharma.

By having a look at Siva, a person achieves self consciousness. As the sun removes the blemish (darkness with its rays, similarly the immensely compassionate lord Siva removes the ignorance of the devotees. When the ignorance is removed duly then the wisdom is attained.

By attaining the knowledge of Siva, a person achieves his self consciousness, after which a person is deemed to be successful in his desires.

Then he, after performing the japam by a hundred lacs of times achieves the highest place of Siva becoming Para-Brahman. Then by performing a hundred lacks of japam one achieves the place of Visnu.

By further performing the japam for a hundred lacs more, one achieves the place of Rudra. By further continuing japam for a hundred lacs more, he achieves Aisvarya- pada.

By performing the similar type of japam with alertness, he achieves the kalacakra which is the creation of the Sivaloka.

In the sequence of Øṁṣṁêãṁ one achieves also the panca-cakras. Maha-Bahma-cakra, Bhoga and Moha are Vaisnava cakras.

Kopa (anger) and moha (delusion) are Raudra cakras. The wandering is the Isvara cakra jnana and moha are the Siva-cakras. These are called the ðṁñṣṁ cakras.

Again by performing japam by ten crores of times, one achieves karana-Brahman. By performing ten crores of japam again, one achieves Aisvarya of the place.

In this sequence, by attaining the places of Visnu and others, the great and valorous noble soul, achieves the Aisvarya pada.

Shedding away the laziness, performing the japam, by a hundred arid five crore times, the devotee comes out of the five curtains and achieves Sivaloka.

There, one would find Rajamandapa, the best place of Nandi, and the bull in the form of tapas.

After the five curtains, there is the place of Sadyojata. In the fourth curtain, there is the place of Vamadeva.

After the third curtain, there is the place Aghora, and the place of Sambapurusa or Ardhanarfsvara is in the second curtain.

The place of Isana is in the first curtain. Than there is the fifth mandapa which is the place of dhama and dhyana (meditation).

The place of Siva, the lord of Bali bestows complete nectar. The fourth mandapa has the image of Candrasekhara.

Somo-Skanda is lodged in the third mandapa. The place of the believers is in the second mandapa which is also called the dancing hell.

The place of Maya (illusion) is in the first mandapa. Then there is the garbhagrha and beyond that is the auspicious lingasthana.

Behind that is the place of Nandi and at the place beyond that no one is aware of the fortunes of Siva. Remaining outside, Nandisvara always recites the Pancdksara mantra.

In this way I procured the text of the conversation between Sanatkumara and Nandisvara, by means of the tradition of the preceptor and the disciple. The subject beyond this is to be known by himself, which could be attained by the grace of Siva.

Those who believes in lord Siva, are of the opinion that the real treasure of Sivaloka could be known only by the grace of Siva himself and there is no other remedy for the same.

With this sequence the Brahmanas who had controlled this senses, were redeemed. Now I shall speak about the sequence of the other varnas like Ksatriyas and others you kindly listen to me with devotion.

As per the advice of the preceptor, the Brahmanas should add the word namah (××:) at the end of the mantra and should recite the mantra five lacs of time. This leads to the increase of the age.

For the wiping off of woman-hood, one should recite the mantra five lacs of times. After achieving manhood, she gets redeemed.

A Ksatriya should recite this mantra five lacks of times, then he is freed from duties of a Ksatriya. By again reciting the mantra by five lacks of times more, he becomes a Brahmana.

By again reciting the same number of the mantra, one achieves the siddhi in the mantra and one gets free from reciting the japam. By performing the japam of the mantra five lacs of times, a Vaisya is freed from Vaisyatya or remaining as Vaisya.

By reciting the mantra for five lacs of times, it is called as mantra-Ksatriya. By reciting further by five lacs of times his Ksatriyahood is removed.

By further reciting the mantra by five lacks times more, he is called the mantra- Brdhmana. In case a Sudra adding namah at the end of the mantra, recites the mantra by twenty lacs of times, then he achieves the position of a mantra-Brahmana. After reciting the japam by twenty lacs of times again, a Sudra is turned into a pure Brahmana. Irrespective of the one, being a woman, man, a Brahmana or anyone else, all are purified with the reciting of this mantra.

A sick person using the word namah in the preceding or the following of the mantra, should recite it always. The preceptor should give the mantra to the women and the Sudras, without omkara.

After the completion of the five lacks of the japam of the mantra five lacs of times, then he should, in order to please lord Siva, offer to the lord the Mahabhiseka and naiveyda and then he should adore the devotees of Siva.

Siva feels extremely pleased with the adoration of his devotee. There is hardly any difference between Siva and his devotees because these devotees too become the form of Siva.

By embracing the mantra of Siva, he becomes Siva himself. The body of Siva’s devotee, turns like of Siva himself.

The devotees of Siva are aware of everything including all the methods prescribed in the Vedas. Whosoever might have recited the Sivamantra by any number of times, achieves nearness to Siva with the same proportion. There is no doubt about it. The woman devotees of Siva, achieves the form of Devi-linga.

Whatever be the number of the mantras recited by them, they achieve the nearness of the goddess Bhagavati with the same proportion. The learned people who adore Siva, become entitled to s'abda-ãīðṁ themselves.

One should adore Para-sakti (Parvati) conceiving, himself to be the form of Siva. One should adore Sakti and one image of Siva getting free from illusion.

Sivalinga should be treated as the form of Siva, the soul as the form of Sakti or Saktiliriga, than conceiving the goddess he should consider himself, as the form of Siva.

One should take Sivalinga as form of nada and Sakti should be treated as the form of bindu or spot. Then omkara should be taken as linga with Sakti, then on should adore Siva and Sakti. One should also adore the devotees of Siva who are believed to be the form of Siva’s mantra as well as Siva; and by doing so such adoration is equated with the worship of Siva by the sixteen methods (upacaras). The same reward can be achieved by adoring the Lingayata devotees of Siva.

By doing so, the learned man feels comfortable and lord Siva feels pleased. One should with his wife offer food to the Brahmana couples and adore them as well, who could be five, ten or a hundred in number. One should preserve the feeling of Siva in his mind as well as the body, free from cheating.

Then he, getting the form of Siva-sakti is never born on earth again. Brahma is lodged below the navel, while Visnu is lodged above the neck.

The form of the face of Siva’s devotee is the form of linga. Those who are dead or those who have been cremated or even those who have not yet been cremated, for the sake of those, Siva should be adored first of all and then the eternal mother Sakti should be adored. The devotees of Siva should be adored thereafter.

In this way the person reaching in pitr-loka is redeemed in due course of time. A Brahmana, engaged in tapas is considered to be greater than the ten Brahmanas engaged in ordinary activities.

A Brahmana performing the japam is considered to be more important than a hundred Brahmanas engaged in tapas. A Brahmana with Siva-jnana is considered to be better than a thousand Brahmanas engaged in japam.

Among a lac of Brahmanas with Siva- jnana, a meditating Brahmana is considered to be the best. Out of a crore of Brahmanas engaged in meditation, one who is engaged in samadhi is considered to be the best.

By these methods, the superiority is gradually increased and by adoring them gradually, and the reward achieved for the same is unknown even to the learned people.

Because of this, who could be aware of the glory of the devotee of Siva. Indeed the adoration of a Siva’s devotee amounts to the adoration of Siva and Sakti.

A person who adores Siva, with devotion, he is himself turned to the form of Siva and also achieves Siva. The one who reads with meanings this chapter based on the Vedas, such a Brahmana, becoming a Siva-jnam remains happy with Siva. Î Sages, a Brahmana well-versed in the scriptures should narrate this chapter to the devotees of Siva.

Î Brahmanas, (by doing so), he achieves the grace of Siva, as well the success in all the walks of life.

## Chapter 18 - Glory of Sivalinga

The Rsis said- “O Suta, you are well- versed in all the topics, therefore you speak to us on the subject of the bondage as well as the release from the same.” Suta said, “O Ascetics, I am going to explain the bondages as well as the methods used for the release therefrom or redemption from these bondages. You better listen to me with respect.

Because of the remaining in eight types of fetters, the soul is called the Jiva. When a person is freed from these bondages, the person is called redeemed.

The controlling of the bondages of Prakrti and others is called self-redemption or liberated. The one who is caught in the bondages is called the jiva and the one who is freed of the bondage is called redeemed.

Prakrti comprises of wisdom. After wisdom is the gunatnaka ahamkara and the panca-tanmdtras (five subtle rudiments of five elements). All these eight when combined are called Prakrti.

The body is formed by the eight beings. The activities of the body are called the karmas. Then the process of karmas from the body and the body from the karmas starts.

The body is of three types viz.: gross, subtle and casual. The gross body relates to the worldly affairs. The subtle body is meant for the pleasures of the organs of senses.

The casual body is meant for soul’s performance due to the karmas. The karmas (deeds) are the cause of pleasure or pain, sins and the merits.

Therefore, the jiva after having been bound with the rope of karmas, again and again, wanders in the three types of bodies like a wheel.

In order to avoid the wandering of the jiva always like a wheel, one should adore Jagadisvara who is the creator of the universes. There are the eight mahdcakras including Prakrti. Siva is beyond these cakras.

Because Siva, the creator of the cakra of the universe is beyond Prakrti. As a living child drinks water and then vomits it, similarly, Siva also has overpowered Prakrti. The entire universe has been controlled by him, therefore he is called Siva. Siva is omniscient, complete and free from desire.

Because of his being omniscient his is called Anadi-bodha. Because of the freedom possessed by him he is conceived with the visible prowess. He is the prowess of Mahesvara beyond measure. His mental fortunes are known only to two Vedas.

Because of this, Prakrti and other elements could be controlled by the grace of Siva. For gaining the grace of Siva, he should be adored.

How can one adore, the complete and without desire lord Siva? Therefore the deeds which are performed for the sake of Siva, he feels pleased with the same.

One should adore Siva, in the form of linga, image, his devotees take them as Siva. Then he should be adored by the speech, body, mind and with the offering of riches.

Mahesa, who lives beyond Prakrti, bestows his special grace in his devotee, when he adores him.

With the grace of Siva, one can exercise all the control over all the things; when everything from Prakrti to the karmas is controlled, at that very moment the devotee is freed and he becomes the supreme spirit. By the grace of the lord when this karmadeha comes under control, a person who then lives in Sivaloka, achieves Salokya-mukti. By exercising control over the tanmatras (subtle essence of five elements) one achieves the closeness of Samba (Ardhanarisvara).

Thereafter he achieves closeness of Siva by means of ayudhas (trident etc.) with the achievement of the food offered to the deity, even the wisdom comes under control.

Wisdom is the job of Prakrti which is called Sarsti (the one having similar place and power). Then with the mahaprasada (cooked food offered to the deity) even Prakrti also is controlled.

Then the mental fortunes of Siva are achieved without much effort. By achieving the fortunes of Siva like omniscience, the devotee looks graceful in himself.

The same has been termed by the Vedas and post Vedic literature as Sayujya salvation. In the same sequence, by adoring lingo etc. one achieves salvation automatically.

Therefore for the achieving the pleasure of Siva, he should be adored appropriately. By adoring Siva offering the lotus flowers, a devotee achieves Sivaloka.

The knowledge of Siva, meditation of Siva, should be practised by a devotee regularly from morning to the time of sleep or going to bed. One should always keep Siva in mind.”

The rsis said, “O Suvrata Suta, what is the process of the adoration of the lingal You kindly speak out the same to us.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, I am going to speak out to you, the process of adoring Siva in the form of lingo, in a sequence, which should be listened by you. You listen to the same quite attentively (of all the lingas) Pranavalinga happens to be the first.

Siva is the subtle form (or formless) of Pranava, whereas the gross lingo, is associated with the time. The same is also called Pancaksara.

The adoration of both of them is called the tapas which bestow moksa. There are several lingas made by human efforts a well as the natural ones, their detailed account could be provided by Siva himself and by none else. But whatever is known to me about the Parthiva-linga (or the lingo of clay) the same is being repeated by me to you.

The first is Svayambhii-linga the second is Bindu-linga, the third category includes the lingas which are consecrated and the fifth category comprises of the Guru-linga.

With the performing of the tapas by the ascetics and the gods, lord Siva was pleased to grant closeness to them. He lives on earth in the form of the seed and sound (nada).

As the seed sprouts piercing through the land, similarly the lingo which is self born, is called Svayambhu.

With the adoring of such a type of linga one achieves wisdom automatically. A linga made in gold, silver, earth or which is drawn over a pedestal with one’s own hand or writing the spotless Pranava mantra over a yantra, should be consecrated by invoking.

This happens to be moveable and immovable forms of Bindu-linga. This is totally emotional and this way one come face to face with Siva.

The one who believes in Siva, he is surely rewarded by him. The yantras written in one’s own hand, immovable or at the natural place, should be adored after invoking the lord. By doing so, one achieves the fortunes and by practising the same, one achieves wisdom.

The linga which is consecrated by the gods and the ascetics for their own success, reciting the mantras in the auspicious mandala, with the spotless emotions, it is called the Paurasa- linga or the consecrated one.

By daily adoring such a linga one achieves courage and fortunes. The intelligent Brahmanas, the kings or the Ksatriyas, or wealthy people, when get a linga prepared by the artisans, and consecrating it with the reciting of the mantras is called the Prakratika-linga. By adoring it one achieves the natural fortunes.

The one which possesses the prowess, being everlasting, the same is called Paurusa- linga. The one which is weak and impermanent, it is called Prakrt-linga.

The adhyatmika (spiritual), Cara (moving) should be consecrated over linga, navel, tongue, tip of the nose, from the tuft of the waist, heart and the face.

Paurusa-linga should be lodged in a mountain, while the Prakrta-linga should be lodged on earth. Further the Paurusa-linga should be lodged in a tree and Prakrta-linga should be lodged in a shrub.

The linga in the form of Sdthl rice is called Prakrta-linga and the one made by paddy or the wheat should be treated as Paurusa. With the consecrating of the Paurusa-linga one achieves fortunes as well as the eight siddhis like anima etc.

The learned people say that by adoring the Prakrta-linga one achieves a good wife and enormous riches. Rasa-linga is considered to be the best among the moveable lingas.

With the adoring of the Rasa-linga all the desires of the Brahmana are fulfilled. The Bdna-linga bestows the Ksatriyas with kingship.

The gold linga earns enormous riches for the Vaisyas. The linga made in stone, purifies even the Sudras.

The crystal linga as well as the Bana-linga fulfil the desires of all. In case the linga prescribed for a particular caste is not available any other linga could worshipped.

The Parthiva-linga is more important for the women whose husbands are alive. The widows who are engaged in the worldly activities, the adoration of the crystal linga has been prescribed.

The widows who are free from the worldly activities, the Rasa-linga is the best. Î Sages, during the childhood, youthful age and the old age, the spotless and the auspicious linga of crystal stone, fulfils all their desires. The women who are desirous of the worldly pleasures, the adoration of the pitha or the pedestal of the linga is more beneficial to them.

A devotee having been inspired by the preceptor, should perform all types of adoration. At the end of the abhiseka the naivedya of best quality of cooked rice should be offered.

After the completion of the linga ’s worship, it should be placed in a vase and kept separately. The Brahmanas who have become free from the adoration, should then be served with food.

Those who have renounced the world, they should adore the subtle linga. It should be adored with ashes which should also be offered to it.

After adoration, the linga should be placed over the head. The vibhiitis (ashes) are of three types viz.: Loka, Veda and the one produced by Sivagni.

The ashes of the worldly fire are meant for the cleaning of the vases. The wcfldly fire purifies the dust, iron, cereals, sesame, and other things besides the costumes and the left over or weathered things.

The things polluted by the dog could also be purified with the ashes. It could be used with or without water.

The ashes of the domestic fire is called Vedagni-bhasma. It should be collected at the end of the function. The fire produced by mantras and action, is called karmagni which turns into ashes.

With the application of the ashes over the body one is bestowed with the influence of the relative karmas. The fire in the wood of the woodapple trees should with the Vedic aghora-mantra.

This is called Sivagni which also produces pure ashes. With the igniting of the Sivagni (fire) with the cow-dung of the white or cow or cow of any other colour, wood of sami (thorny shrubs), holy fig tree, Palas'a (Bitea fromdosa), banyan, Amaltasa (cassia fistula) and the wood apple trees, when burnt in Sivagni and the ashes produced therefrom are treated as pure.

Or otherwise, by burning of wood in the Durbhagni and then refining it should be put it in a new pitcher.

This type of ash should be applied over the body for the purpose of grace and by doing so a person gains respect and glory. Siva had initially defined the bhasma (ashes) thus.

As the king accepts taxes for the people as the gist. As a person takes other gist of it by husking of the paddy, as the stomach fire which digests food, bums the food consumed by a person and using its essence keeps the body healthy, similarly lord Siva, who creates the entire universe, burning the delusion with him, accepts its essence.

Then he applies the ashes of the delusion over his body, with the application of the ashes over his body, he carries the essence of the world with him.

He has used his gem in the form of the ashes over his body. With the essence of the sky his hair emerged and with the essence of the wind, his mouth was formed.

The heart was formed with essence of the fire, and the essence of the water produced the waist. The thighs were created with the essence of the earth. All his limbs were thus formed.

Tripundra (three lines drawn over the head) is the essence of Brahma, Visnu and Siva and tilakam over the head stands for Mahesvara.

As lord Siva is considered to be all competent in the expansion of the earth, similarly the entire earth has been overpowered by Siva.

Therefore, there is none else to overpower him. Only Siva is there. As a lion is the killer of all the wild animals, and there is none else to kill it. Because of this, it is called Simha = ??? (sam) stands for eternal pleasure, (i) ??? stands for blissful Purusa, ??? (v) stands for Sakti and the nectar. With the combination of all the three letters, the word Siva is formed. Therefore the soul should be adored in the form of Siva.

Before the start of the adoration of Siva, one should apply ashes over his body, draw tripundra (three horizontal lines over the forehead). During the time of adoration one should take ashes with water. One should take ashes without water for self purification.

Whether it is day or night, irrespective of being a man or a woman, one should mix ashes with water and then place it over the forehead in three horizontal lines.

One who adores Siva, with a tripundra over his forehead, he achieves the entire reward of the adoration of Siva.

The one who applies the ashes over his body reciting the Siva-mantra he belongs to the best ds'rama. The one who feels absorbed in Siva, he is called Sivagni.

A person who is engaged in the vrata of Siva, he neither attracts impurity nor the defilement caused by the birth or death. One should apply ashes over the forehead and tilakam of the dust.

This could be done by a person himself or through his preceptor. This is the symptom of the devotee of Siva, gu or (???) stands for gunas or merits and ru (???) stands for planting. Therefore the preceptor who plants the virtues in the disciples is called guru. This is the formation of the word.

The one who himself is without blemish, removes the rajogunas of the disciples, he is called gunatita (or the one who is free from all the properties) and Parama-Siva.

Otherwise, when a preceptor, removing all the three (sattva, rajas and tamas) gunas from the trusted pupils, bestows the complete knowledge of Siva, in them, he could be called as a preceptor in the true sense of the term.

Therefore the body of the guru is called Gurulinga. By adoring the same, one achieves the reward for serving the guru.

The one who obeys the spoken command is called Susrusa, which should be followed by action, thought and behaviour. Whatever be the command of the preceptor and whether the pupil is competent to obey it or not, the one who with the pure and auspicious soul, performs it even at the cost of his life or wealth, he is considered to be a true pupil and well disciplined.

The suitable pupil should give away something which is useful for the body to the preceptor, including the eatables. He should then consume it with the permission of the preceptor.

Being capable enough the pupil is always called the son, because with the tongue as the linga, and the semen in the form of mantra is poured into the ears like the yoni, the mantra emerges in the form of a son. Therefore he should always adore the preceptor. The father produces the son in the world.

The preceptor as a father, with the bestowing of wisdom and knowledge, makes the pupil to cross the ocean of the universe. Therefore realising the difference between the two, one should adore the preceptor like the father.

A pupil should serve the body of the preceptor, with the wealth earned by him, because the body of the preceptor from top to bottom is considered to be the form of Siva.

A pupil should adore his preceptor with the sandals in the form of wealth, pressing of the feet, bathing him, performing of abhiseka, offering of naivedya and the food.

In fact the adoration of the preceptor is the adoration of Siva. All the materials which are remnants of the service of the preceptor, purify the soul.

The padarthas made of cereals and water which are left after the adoration of the preceptor are like the left over of Siva. Therefore, Î Brahmanas, they should be consumed by the devotees of Siva or the pupils.

The things which are accepted by the pupils without the consent of the preceptor, it amounts to stealing. The specialist preceptor should be honoured as such with much efforts.

The removal of ignorance is the duty of the preceptor, which could be done by a special preceptor. For the successful completion of the job without interruption one should make efforts for the removal of the obstructions.

A deed performed completely without obstruction, becomes successful. Therefore, at the start of all the functions Ganesa should be essentially adored.

A learned person should, for the removal of all the obstructions, adore all the gods and by doing this, all the ailments like fever, pain of joints, outer and the spiritual diseases, get removed.

The appearing of pisaca, jackal, white ant, sudden fall of the lizard, tortoise, snake, evil woman, observing the birth of a child given by a woman, or the littering of a calf by a cow, are indicative of the future misfortune and are called the material sins. The inauspicious thing, like the falling of vajra or epidemic, deadly fever, cholera, foot disease in cows, measles, influence of evil planets in the constellation of birth, exercising of the influence of the evil planets over the zodiac cycle, witnessing of the evil dreams, are called the miseries brought by the evil spirit or the fate. In case one enters the house by touching the dead body, Candala, and the degraded people, or facing such types of calamities, indicative of misfortune, a person with wisdom, should perform yajna for the subsiding of these evils.

One should make square pedestal, two feet in height in a temple, cowshed, place of yajna or courtyard of the abode, decorating it at the same time.

A bhara (a hundred seers) barley should be spread. In between decoration should be made with lotus flowers on all the sides.

The thread should be placed round the pitcher and incense as well as the gugulu should be burnt inside the pitcher. Similar types of four pitchers should be placed in each directions.

The mango leaves with branches should be placed in the pitchers reciting the mantras together with the five dravyas (cloves, aguru gourd, nutmeg and camphor).

Besides the nine gems should also be placed in the pitchers. For this purpose the Brahmana with his wife, well versed in the performance of the yajna should be invoked.

Thereafter the gold images of Visnu and Indra should be placed in each one of the pitchers. Over the pitcher in the centre, a complete or filled vase should be placed. Visnu should be invoked in it and adored appropriately.

In the eastern and other directions, Indra and the respective gods should be adored and adding namah after their the fourth inflexion of their names.

The invocation and other types of puja should be performed by the acarya. One should himself also recite those mantras with the priest.

Î Intelligent people, after the completion of the japam, towards the west of the pitchers, one should give the offerings of a crore, a lac, a thousand or a hundred.

The homa should be performed for a day, nine days, or collectively according to the time and the country.

For the purpose of peace, the homa of thorny shrub (Sami), and for livelihood homa of palasa should be performed. The small sticks, food and ghee should be poured in the homa by the reciting of the mantras.

The dravya with which the homa is started, should be used upto the end. After getting the Punyahavdcana done, then the water of the pitcher should be sprinkled everywhere.

At the end, food should be served to the Brahmanas on the basis of the offerings of the fire. The acaryas and the priests should be served with the food.

After the completion of the homa Sun and the planets should be worshipped besides the priests, and the daksina of nine gems should be given in due course.
