Thereafter one should perform ten types of charities besides donating of the land. These charities should be extended to brahmacaris, the householders as well as those living in the forest.

The charities should be given to the unmarried girls, the virtuous women and thereafter the widows. The material offered in the adoration should entirely be given to the acaryas.

Yama happens to be the lord of epidemics as well as the misfortunes, therefore an image of Kala should be given in order to please Yama.

An image weighing a niska{a hundred and eight tolas) or ten nisks, of the life size, should be made, with a noose and an ankusa in his hands shown as his attributes.

This image should be given to a Brahmana with daksina. Thereafter for the enjoying of the full age, sesamum should be given.

Then pouring ghee in a bronze vase one should look his face therein and give it away for the removal of the disease. A person who is well off should feed a thousand Brahmanas while a person not so well off should feed a hundred Brahmanas.

A poor person, for want of money, should feed as many Brahmana, as he can. For the pleasing of the goblins and pretas, Bhairava should be adored.

At the end, Mahabhiseka of Siva should be performed offering him naivedya at the same time. Thereafter, the Brahmanas should be fed.

With the performing of the yajna in this way, all the blemishes are removed. This Santi-yajna should be performed yearly, in the month of Phalguna.

With the inauspicious vision one. should perform Santi-yajna for a month at once. In case some grave sin is committed, one should adore Bhairava for its removal.

Because of the disturbance created by some terrific epidemic, one should take a resolve again. A poor person having little money with him should give away a lamp in charity.

In case one is unable to do even that much, then he should give away something as he can after taking a bath. He should offer salutation to the sun, reciting the Siva-mantra a hundred and eight times.

Or otherwise he should offer salutations, a thousand, ten thousand, a lac, or a crore of times to the sun. With this namaskara-yajna also the gods are pleased.

Then he should pray, “O Lord Siva, I have dedicated my intelligence to your Saguna form. Now it does not stick to your nirguna or absolute form and whatever pride I possessed has been removed because of an audience with you.

I offer my salutation at your feet with my body. Î Lord, you are great. My body happens to be your form only. I am humble. Î Lord you are great. My body is your form. Therefore it is not Sanya. Presently I am your slave.”

Thus praying, one should complete his atma-yajna, offering his salutation the food and betel to him.

One should go round Siva, a hundred and eight times and make others to do so, a thousand ten thousand, a lac or a crore of times.

By circumambulating Siva all the sins are washed out in a moment. Ailment is the root of the pain and the root of ailment is the sin.

The sin is washed out with dharma, which has been prescribed in the scriptures. The deed which is performed to please Siva, destroys the sins.

In the Saiva-dharma, there is the special importance for the circumambulation. The recitation of Omkara with activity is the sort of the best circumambulation.

The birth and death are said to be Mayacakras, but the Mayacakra is said to be the Bali-pitha.

Starting from the Bali-pitha, moving two feet forward, reaching close to the Bali-pitha.

One should offer his salutation. This is called circumambulation which is the cause of the birth whereas the salutation amounts to complete surrender.

One should dedicate both his birth and the death of the Maya, (illusion) of Siva. When one dedicates this conflict to Siva, then the soul is freed from both of them.

Till such time the body is governed by the activity, upto that time, because of its remaining in he bondage, it is called Jiva. When it overpowers all the three types of the bodies, then he achieves salvation.

Lord Siva, the creator of Kalacakrn is the main reason for the same. Therefore when the conflict of Maya or illusion is offered to Siva himself, then he himself relieves his devotee of his Maya.

Siva has created the conflict in the universe. Therefore, the same should be dedicated to him. Î People with wisdom, Siva likes circumambulation and the salutation the most.

The mahapuja of lord Siva, performed by sixteen methods, circumambulation and salutation, yields auspicious reward.

There is no sin in the world which cannot be removed or destroyed with the circumambulation of Siva. Therefore you should destroy all the sins by going round Siva.

A speechless person engaged in the adoration of Siva, earns the merits or truthfulness, tapas, wisdom and meditation.

Besides the superhuman power, divine body, knowledge, removal of ignorance, closeness of Siva and other noble merits. This is the result of the such deeds.

With the activity, the ignorance is lost and removing the sins, created by the inspiration of Brahman throughout the birth, the devotee of Siva should engage himself in the activities suited to time, country, strength of the body and the riches.

A person with wisdom should live in the ksetra (region) of Siva with the earnings of fair means. He should not resort to the killing of the jivas nor should he create trouble for others.

With the reciting of Pancaksara mantra the water and the food are purified. For a pauper, the food received in charity has been said to be the bestower of wisdom and knowledge.

For a devotee of Siva, the food received in charity increases his devotion in the lord. The food received by Siva-yogls, compares with the prasada received from Siva-yajna.

Where the devotee of Siva lives on earth should consume the pure food; he should keep quiet and should never reveal the secrets of Siva.

He should enlighten the people over the glory of Siva. In fact no one knows about the secret of Siva’s mantra except Siva himself.

A devotee of Siva, should always live close to Siva-linga. Î Brahmanas, by taking refuge in a motionless linga of Siva, his devotee turns like Siva.

By adoring the moveable linga a devotee is surely relieved of the cycle of the birth and death. Thus in this chapter, the best of the means of devotion as well as attainment of salvation, have been discussed.

Whatever had been spoken by Vyasa earlier, and whatever had been heard by me from him, the same has been repeated by me before you in totality. Let you and I meet welfare with this and let your faith in Siva be stronger.

A person who goes through this chapter or listens to it, Î Great souls, he by the grace of Siva achieves the jmna of Siva.

## Chapter 19 - Glory of the adoration of Parthiva or clay Siva-linga

Rsis said, “O Suta, you remain alive for long. You are graceful. You have enlightened us on the glory of Siva-linga and the\* way it bestows success, has been well spoken.

You have brought out the glory of Parthiva-linga, which is the best, briefly. Now you kindly speak out the same in detail.

Suta said, “O Rsis, all of you should listen to me. Having been pleased with your devotion and respect, I am now speaking out the glory of the Parthiva-linga of lord Siva.

Of all the Siva-lingas described earlier, Parthiva-linga is the best. Î Brahmanas, by adoring the Parthiva-linga several people have met with success.

Î Brahmanas! even Hari, Brahma and Rsis alongwith Prajapati, adoring the Parthiva- linga had their desires fulfilled.

By adoring it several of the gods, demons, human, Gandharvas, serpents, Raksasas, and several other people have met with success.

In the Satyuga, the linga of gold was the best. In the Dvaparayuga, the linga built in silver was treated as the best, while in the Kaliyuga the Parthiva-linga is treated to be the best.

Of the eight types of the images of Siva, the one made of earth is treated to be the best. Î Brahmanas, by adoring it with immense devotion, one achieves the best reward.

As Mahesvara is the best of all the gods, similarly Parthiva-linga happens to be the best of all.

As the river Ganga is the best of all the rivers, similarly Parthiva-linga is the best of all the lingas.

As omkara mantra is the best of all the mantras, similarly Parthiva-linga is considered to be the best of all the lingas.

As Brahmana is considered to be the best of all the varnas similarly Parthiva-linga is considered to be the best of all the lingas.

As Kasi is the best of all the towns, similarly the Parthiva-linga is said to be the best of all the lingas.

As the Sivaratri-vrata is the best of all the vratas similarly the Parthiva-linga is considered to be the best of all the lingas.

As the goddess Parvati is considered to be the best of all the goddesses, similarly, of all the lingas, Parthiva-linga is treated to be the best.

The one who adores the other gods leaving aside the Parthiva-linga which has already been made, his entire adoration, bathing, etc. becomes infructuous.

The adoration of Parthiva-linga is quite auspicious and the person who performs the same is indeed graceful. It increases the age, health and wealth. Therefore, a devotee should worship the same.

Whatever material be available for the purpose, a devotee should worship the Parthiva-linga with devotion and immense faith and by doing so all his desires are fulfilled.

A person, who after making the Parthiva- linga adores it placing it over the pedestal, he achieves the best of riches and grace in the same birth and becomes Rudra ultimately.

A devotee who after making the Parthiva- linga daily adores it thrice (morning, noon and evening) offering the leaves of the wood apple tree, you listen to the related merits, he achieves in Rudraloka with the same body. The very sight and touch of such a person destroys all the sins.

He is filled with knowledge, is freed from the worldly bondages, and undoubtedly becomes Siva. The mere sight of such a person bestows salvation.

Such of the people, who making a Parthiva-linga, adore it throughout life, they ultimately achieve Sivaloka.

He stays in Sivaloka with Siva for a large number of years. Thereafter he is born in the land of Bharata, becomes the best among the kings.

A person who adores Parthiva-linga, without any desire, he after living in Sivaloka for long, ultimately achieves the Sayujya type of salvation.

In case a Brahmana does not adore Parthiva-linga, he after being pierced with spear, falls in the terrific hell.

The Parthiva-linga should be prepared appropriately. The process of panca-sutra should not be adopted in the making of Parthiva-linga.

The Parthiva-linga should be made undivided and complete in all respects. In case the linga is made in two parts the devotee is deprived of the reward of the same.

In case the Parthiva-linga is made by using gems, gold, silver, crystal, topaz, still it should be made complete and undivided.

The moveable linga is called as Akhanda while the immovable linga is called Dvikhanda. The difference of breaking and complete is related to the movable and well as immovable lingas.

The pedestal stands for the Mahavidya. Linga represents Mahesvara. Therefore duplex is not considered to be good in the case of immovable linga.

According to the prescribed method, the immovable linga should be in duplex form. This is the opinion of the people well-versed in the Saiva principles.

The people devoid of wisdom make the moveable linga in duplex form or of two kharidas, such ascetics could not be treated as well-versed in the scriptures.

The akhanda-linga is immovable while the moveable linga has the duplex form. The person who violates the provisions of the scriptures, he is deprived of the merit of the adoration.

Therefore, the akhanda linga should be immovable, while the caralinga should be moveable and made in duplex form, which should be made with devotion.

The adoration of akhanda-caralinga bestows complete reward. The adoration of caralinga with two parts is extremely harmful.

The adoration of akhanda-sthavara-linga does not yields the desired reward and is harmful to the contrary. This has been ordained by those well-versed in the scriptures.

## Chapter 20 - Method of adoring Parthiva-linga

Suta said, “Now we shall describe about the Parthiva-pUja for the devotees of Siva, who are well versed in the Vedas, which bestows the pleasures as well as the salvation, following the path of the Vedas.

One should take bath in the manner already described in the aforesaid sutra and then perform the Sandhyavandana appropriately. Then he should perform the Brahmayajna and then offer the oblation with water to the gods, rsis, and manes.

Completing his daily routine pretty well and after its completion, the devotee of Siva should, reciting the name of Siva, apply ashes over his body and then wear the rosary of Rudraksa.

For the achieving of the complete success, performing (the adoration) according to the method prescribed in the Vedas, with utmost devotion and then should worship Parthiva- linga which is considered to be the best.

The Parthiva-linga can be adored at any auspicious place like bank of the river or a tank, mountain top, in a forest, or a Siva temple.

Î Brahmanas, one should collect the clay or earth from some auspicious place and should prepare the Parthiva-linga quite carefully.

Brahmana should collect the white earth, a Ksatriya- the red earth, Vaisya should collect the yellow earth and Sudra should collect the black earth.

Collecting the appropriate type of clay, a person of the respective varna should prepare the linga quite carefully and then install it at an extremely sacred place.

Purifying it with water, a small lump should be made slowly. Thereafter he should prepare the Parthiva-linga as prescribed in the Vedas.

Thereafter he should adore the linga with devotion for the sake of pleasure and the salvation. Now the method of its adoration is being explained by me and you listen to me appropriately.

Then the water should be sprinkled over, the entire material collected for the purpose of adoration, reciting the mantra “namah Sivaya ”. Then reciting the mantra bhurasi the siddhi should be done for the region.

Then reciting the mantra apo'sman, the water should be purified. Then reciting the mantra “namaste Rudra ” the door should be closed.

Then reciting the mantra “namah Sambhavaya’’ the ksetra should be purified. Reciting the mantra “namah Sivaya" the pancamrta should be sprinkled.

Reciting the mantra, ’namo-nilagrivaya' a devotee should properly consecrate the linga.

Then reciting the mantra “Etatte rudrdya", the devotee should offer the seat of Siva.

Reciting the mantra “mano-mahdnta” lord Siva should be invoked over the linga. Reciting the mantra “yate-rudra”, Sivalinga should be placed over the seat. The nyasa of Siva should be performed by reciting the mantra yamirum.

Then reciting the mantra “adhyavocat" the devotee should pray the lord to stay.

By reciting the mantra “asau-jiva nyasa should be performed and then reciting the mantra “asau yovasarpati” the god should be brought closer.

The by reciting the mantra “namostu- nilagrivaye ” one should offer water for padya. The arghya of Rudra-Gayatri should then be offered. The water should then be sipped reciting the mantra of “Trayambakam”.

Reciting the mantra “payah-prthivyam’‘ the devotee should pour the milk over Siva for bathing. Then the curd should be poured.

Reciting the mantra “ghrtamyana" the ghee should be offered, and with the reciting of the three mantras viz.: ‘madhuvata, madhunaktam and madhumdnnam’.

Siva should be bathed with sugar and honey. All these combined make pancamrta or otherwise reciting the appropriate mantras pancamrta bath should be given.

Reciting the mantra “manastoka” the waist band should be bound with devotion. The reciting the mantra namo-dhrsnave the upper garment should be offered.

Reciting the four mantras like "yataheti”, the devotee of Siva should offer costumes to Siva with devotion.

Reciting the rca “namah Svabhaya” the devotee should offer fragrance with devotion and then reciting namastaksabhyah the rice should be poured over Siva.

Reciting “namah paryaya, the flower should be offered. The leaves of wood-apple tree should be offered reciting the mantra namah parnaya.

With the reciting of the mantra namah kapardine, the incense should be offered. Reciting “namah asave’’ the lamp should be offered.

Naivedya should be offered reciting the mantra namo-jyesthaya. With the reciting of the “trayambakam" mantra the devotee should sip the water.

With the mantra imd-rudmya, fruit should be offered to the lord Siva. By reciting namo- vrajyaya all the padarthas should be offered to Siva.

Reciting the mantras mano-mahant and manastoka, other Rudras should be offered the unbroken rice.

Reciting the mantra, Hiranyagarbha, the devotee should offer daksina. By reciting the mantra devasyatva, the abhiseka of the priest should be performed.

Then the lamp should be offered to the deity. By reciting the three mantras uma- rudraya, the bench of flowers should be offered to Siva.

The devotee should go round the deity reciting “mdno-mahanta”. With the “manastoke” one should prostrate before the deity.

With the mantra “esa-te” one should display the Siva-mudra. With yato-yotah the abhaya-mudrd should be displayed and with Trayambaka mantra jnana-mudra should be displayed.

With the muttering of the mantra ‘‘namah senanye” the mahamudra should be displayed.

The devotee of Siva should make Sivamudra, displaying the five mudras. He should also recite Satarudriya mantra as found in the Vedas.

Thereafter he should recite the Vedic pancanga and send off Siva reciting the mantra of devagatu.

The Vedic method of Sivapuja has been explained. Now listen to the same method in short.

Reciting the mantra sadyojatam, the earth should be collected. Reciting the mantra vamadevaya the water should be poured into it.

Reciting the mantra of 'Aghora' the Parthiva-linga should be prepared. With the mantra of “tatpurusdya” Siva should be invoked appropriately.

The linga should be consecrated in the pedestal by reciting “Isan-Sarvo-vidyanam” after which a person with wisdom should repeat the entire process quite briefly.

Adoration by sixteen methods should be performed with the reciting of the pancaksara mantra or by the mantra given by the guru.

We meditate upon Mahadeva, who is the destroyer of the universe and who is the form of the same. Salutation to lord Candrasekhara, who has the terrific form but is the destroyer of the people with terrific form.

The people with wisdom should adore Siva with this mantra with devotion. A devotee who, with devotion and setting aside the confusion, adores Siva, the lord rewards him well.

In this way the Vedic method of the adoration of Siva has been explained. Î Brahmanas, the other method of adoration in ordinary way is also being explained.

The adoration of Parthiva-linga with the reciting of the names of Siva has been prescribed. Î Sages, you please listen to the same.

These names respectively are Íṁãṁ, Mahesvara, Sambhu, Sulapani, Pinakadhrk and Mahadeva.

The earth should be collected and placing water in it, it should be mixed, preparing a Parthiva-linga with the same, it should be consecrated and then invoked. Offering bath to it, one should adore it, beg forgiveness and then it should be sent off.

By combining the name of Siva with omkara-mantra one should adore it reciting the names of Siva, with devotion following the entire process.

Taking bath by six methods, then the devotee, should meditate upon Siva with six letter mantra.

Siva seated in a lion throne at Kailasa and is being adored with respect by the devotee. “Lord Siva is like the forest fire to destroy the sins of his devotees. I therefore meditate upon Siva who is being embraced by Parvati. He is the ornament of the universe. I adore him.

I adore Mahes'a daily, who is as beautiful as the mountain of silver, adorns his head with crescent, has the body shining like the gems. He has a battle-axe, deer, Varada and abhaya mudras as his attributes. He has the smiling face and is seated over padmasana. He is surrounded by the gods on all the sides and is clad in the tiger skin. He is the eternal god of the universe, is the cause of the creation of the universe, removes all the dangers of the world, and has three eyes and five heads.

Meditating upon Siva in this way, one should adore the best of Parthiva-linga. Then he should recite the pancaksara mantra received from the preceptor.

A wise one should pray lord of gods with many recitations, Î Brahmanas, one should recite Satarudri in several ways.

Then carrying the flowers and unbroken rice in his hands, one should offer prayer to Siva with devotion.

“O Siva, I belong to you. The reciting of your praise is the base of my life. My mind remains attracted towards you always. Î Ocean of compassion, Î Lord of the goblins, you be pleased with me.

Whatever tapas I have performed knowingly or unknowingly, let it meet with success by your grace.

Presently, I am a grave sinner. You happen to be quite great in purifying others. Î Lord of Gauri, realising this, you may do whatever is best for me.

Even the Vedas, the rsis, Puranas, and others have not been able to know you properly, then Î Sadas'iva, Î Mahadeva, how can I know about you.

Î Mahesvara, whatever may be the case, I belong to you. You kindly protect me.”

With this prayer, the flowers and unbroken rice should be offered to Siva, and then he should prostrate before Siva.

Thereafter the person with wisdom should take a round of Siva appropriately. Then with faith and devotion one should offer prayer to the lord.

Then he should produce the sound of a goat from the throat quite humbly and offer his salutation to the lord.

Î Sages, I have explained properly, the method of the adoration of Parthiva-linga, which bestows devotion as well as the salvation besides increasing faith in Siva.

A devotee who listens to this Chapter or reads it, his soul is freed from all the sins. All his desires are also fulfilled.

This entire story bestows healthy life, increase fame, bestows heaven, besides sons and grandsons, as well as the pleasures.

## Chapter 21 - Worship of Parthiva-linga

The Rsis said, “O Fortunate one, Î Suta, the disciple of Vyasa, salutation to you. You have explained to us the method of adoring Parthiva-linga in an appropriate manner.

Because of the difference in desires, you please speak out the number of Parthiva- lingas to be adored, because you are compassionate to the down-trodden people.”

Suta said, “O Ascetics, you please listen to the method of Parthiva-linga's adoration, with the performing of which a person becomes successful in his mission.

A person who adores other gods in preference to the Parthiva-linga, his adoration becomes infructuous, besides the efforts to control the mind and the giving of the charities.

Now I shall speak out the number of the Parthiva-lingas to be adored, based on one’s desires to be fulfilled. Î best of the sages, the number surely bestows the quick reward.

Initially the invocation should be done and then the consecration. All the lingas should be made of the same size separately.

The person desirous of knowledge and wisdom, should make a thousand lingas with devotion and then adore them, which would surely fulfil his desires.

A person desirous of riches should make five hundred lingas, a person desirous of son should make fifteen hundred lingas, while those desirous of then costumes should make five hundred lingas.

The people desirous of moksa, should make a crore of lingas. The one who is desirous of land, should make a thousand lingas. The one who seeks compassion of the lord, should make three thousand lingas and the one desirous of going on pilgrimage should make two thousand lingas.

One who is desirous of a friend should make three thousand lingas, the one desirous of glamour or conjuration should make eight hundred lingas, the one desirous the destruction of others should make seven hundred lingas, and the one who intends to create confusion, should make eight hundred lingas.

The one desirous of separation or defection should make one thousand, for creating hindrance one thousand, for creating bitterness, five hundred lingas should be made.

To get free from the bondage fifteen hundred, to be free from the danger from the king, five hundred, to be relieved from the danger of thieves, two hundred Parthivas should be adored. To be free from the danger of sorceress, five hundred Parthivas should be adored.

To be relieved of poverty, five thousand and for attaining all round success, ten thousand Parthivas should be adored. Î Sages, now I am going to speak out the method of the performing of the adoration daily, which should be listened by you.

The adoring of a linga removes the sins, adoration of a couple of lingas bestows success in money matters, while the adoration of three lingas fulfils all the desires.

Thus more the number of lingas are adored, by a person, the more would be the success achieved by him. Now I world speak out the number of the lingas, because of the difference of opinion among the sages.

The people with wisdom surely get themselves freed of the danger from the king after adoring ten thousand Parthiva-lingas.

To get free from the prison, one should adore ten thousand Parthiva-lingas. To get relieved of the danger from sorceress, seven thousand Parthivas should be adored.

A childless person for seeking a child should adore fifty five thousand of Parthivas. By adoring ten thousand Parthivas one gets a daughter.

By adoring ten thousand Parthivas one achieves the fortunes of Visnu and others and by adoring ten lakhs of Parthiva-lingas one achieves enormous riches beyond measure.

The one who adores a crore of Parthiva- lingas, he becomes Siva himself. There is no doubt about it.

The adoration of Siva, bestows reward equivalent to the performing a crores of yajnas. The person desirous of pleasures, the adoration of Parthiva bestows pleasure to him in the start and moksa at the end.

When the time of a degraded and the wicked person, is spent without adoration of a linga daily, he has to face considerable harm.

All types of charities Vratas, tirthas and yajnas are on the one side, and on the other side is only the adoration of Parthiva-linga.

The sanctity which has been attached to the adoration of Siva-linga in this age of Kali, the same importance is not attached to anything else. This has been decided by the scriptures.

The adoration of linga bestows several types of pleasures and salvation. It also removes several types of misfortunes. Therefore, by adoring it daily, one achieves, Sayujya of Siva or final emancipation.

The linga having the form of Siva, should be adored by the great sages as has been prescribed in the Siva-puja-vidhana.

There are three types of lirigas viz.: upper, middle and the lowest. The size of the respective lingas has been prescribed in the scriptures, which I am going to speak out. You please listen to it.

The learned people, well versed in the sastras have described that the linga consecrated over the pedestal with the height of four angulas is the best.

The pedestal having half of the aforesaid height is considered to be a middle one. When the linga is established in a pedestal having the height further half of the above, is considered to be the lowest.

The one who adores several types of lirigas daily, all his desires are fulfilled.

According to the four Vedas, there is no other auspicious deed better than the adoration of Siva. This is the conclusion of all the sastras.

Discarding all the bondages of the karmas one should adore linga along with great devotion.

The one who has adored the linga, he has adored the entire moveable and the immovable creatures. This is the best remedy for the redemption of the people drowning in the ocean of the universe.

The people who have been blinded with the darkness of ignorance and whose minds are attracted towards the worldly pleasures, there is no other remedy except that for the adoration of Siva.

By adoring Sivalinga with devotion, Hari, Brahma and other gods, besides the sages, Raksasas, Gandharvas, Caranas, Daityas, Danavas, Sesa, serpents, Garuda and other birds, Prajapati, Manu, kinnars and humans, have all the desires of their hearts fulfilled.

With the reciting of the respective mantras, adoring Siva by methods of Vedas and the Puranas, the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vais'yas, Sudras and the people of mixed generation, should adore Sivalinga.

Î Sages, what is the use of talking more, Î Brahmanas, besides the above varnas, even the women have the right to adore Sivalinga.

The Vedic Brahmanas can adore Siva as prescribed in the Vedas or the Puranas. For the people of the other varnas, the Puranic way of the adoration of Siva has been considered to be quite proper.

The Vedic Brahmanas should adore Siva by the Vedic method. This has been ordained by lord Siva himself.

The Brahmanas whose hearts have been burnt out because of the curses of Dadhici, Gautama and other rsis, have usually little faith in adoring Siva according to the Vedic method.

The one who disregarding the Vedic of Smarta (of smrtis) method adores Siva by other means, he does achieve he full reward for the same.

Thus adoring Siva properly upto the offering of the naivedya, one should also adore the eight images which represent the three worlds.

The eight images are the earth, water, fire, wind, sky, sun, moon and the sacrificer, as himself defined by Siva.

Besides the images of Sarva, Bhava, Rudra, Ugra, Bhima, Isvara, Mahadeva and Pasupati should be adored in the form of images.

Thereafter the family of Siva should also be adored with devotion. The sandal paste and unbroken rice etc. should also be offered.

Thereafter, Isan, Nandi, Canda, Mahakala, Bhrngl, Vrsa, Skanda, Soma and Sukra, should also be respectively adored.

Virabhadra should be in the fore while Klrtimukha should be behind. Thus the eleven Rudras should also be adored appropriately.

Thereafter reciting the Pancaksara mantra, the recitation of Satarudriya should also be made, followed by the Sivastotra and the pancdnga.

Thereafter, one should circumambulates, offer salutation and rendition should be made of the linga. In this way the entire adoration of Siva has been narrated respectfully.

The work of Siva should be performed at night facing east. Similarly, the adoration of Siva should also be done, getting purified facing the north.

One should not sit towards or the east of Siva nor should anyone sit with his spouse to the north of Siva, nor in the west. One should sit towards the north alone.

The learned devotee should not perform adoration of Siva, without application of the ashes on the body, tripundra over the forehead, without wearing the rosary of Rudraksa and without the leaves of wood- apple trees.

Î Sages, when the ashes are not available, a devotees should take some dust and apply it over the forehead in the form of tripundra.

## Chapter 22 - Glory of Siva naivedya and bilva (wood-apple)

Rsis said, “O Sage, we have earlier heard that Siva naivedya should not be consumed. Then the exact position about the same as well as the glory of wood-apple may please be stated.”

Suta said, “O Sages, you are all graceful being performers of the vratas of Siva. I shall lovingly speak out the same. All of you should listen to the same attentively.

A devotee of Siva, purifying himself, undertaking the vrata with a firm mind, should accept the naivedya of Siva.

With the very sight of the naivedya of Siva all the sins disappear in no time and by consuming it crores of merits automatically arrive before the devotee.

There is no need for performing the yajnas in thousands or crores, by consuming the naivedya of Siva, a devotee achieves the Sdyujya of Siva.

A house is purified with the mere mention of the naivedya of Siva. It also becomes the cause of the purification of the other houses.

Finding the arrival of the naivedya it should be placed over the head and it should be consumed reciting the name of Siva.

When the naivedya arrives in the house (it should be taken at once) because by delaying it saying that it would be taken subsequently, the naivedya is insulted and a person earns a sin.

The one who does not feel interested in having the naivedya of Siva, he, the grand sinner surely falls in the hell.

A devotee who wears the small image of Siva, made in gold, silver or other metals, with utmost devotion, is entitled to receive the naivedya, it is said.

A devotee of Siva, having received Sivadiksa is entitled to consume the naivedya of all types of Sivalingas.

Those who have received other dlksas, but are devoted to Siva, the decision about their taking the Siva’s naivedya is as follows.

Î Brahmanas, the consuming of the naivedyas of the linga which emerges out of Saligrama, in Rasalinga, stone-liriga, silver-linga, gold-linga and the lingas consecrated by the siddhas and the gods, in the crystal linga of Kasmira, Ratnalinga, besides all the Jyotirlingas, rewards like the performing of the Candrayana-vrata.

The person committing brahmahatya when getting purified consumes the offerings made to Siva, all his sins are washed out.

The food offered to the goddess Candl should not be consumed by the human beings. The place which is out of control of the goddess Canda, should be consumed with devotion.

The same Canda has no control over the lingas like Âīñṁ, iron, siddha and SvayambhQ, besides the other images of Siva.

After bathing Sivalinga properly, if the said water is sipped thrice, all his three types of sins are washed out.

The Siva naivedya which has been termed as not fit for consumption, it gets purified including the leaves, flowers, fruit, water etc. coming in touch with the Saligrama sila.

Î Sages, the material placed over the tip of the lingo, is not to be consumed. The stuff which is beyond the touch of the linga remains auspicious and can be taken.

Î Sages, I have spoken before you about the sanctity of the naivedya. Now you listen to the glory of wood-apple quite respectfully.

The wood-apple tree is the form of Siva. In a way it has been praised even by the gods. How can one know about its glory.

The places of pilgrimages which are well known in the world, all reside at the roots of the wood-apple tree.

The one who adores Mahadeva Siva in the root of the wood-apple tree, he surely achieves Siva.

The one who pours water over Siva lodged in the roots of wood-apple tree, he becomes self purified having himself taken bath in all the sacred places. He becomes auspicious on earth.

At the root of the wood-apple tree, if one pours water in the basin round it, lord Siva gets leased finding its base filled with water.

A person who adores the root of the wood- apple tree offering fragrance, unbroken rice, flower etc. he achieves Sivaloka and his progeny comfortably develops.

The one who lights lamp at the root of wood-apple tree, he after achieving the taltvajnana becomes the form of Siva.

A devotee, who plucking the uninjured leaves of the wood-apple tree and offers them to Siva, he is surely freed from all the sins.

The one who making a Brahmana to sit under the wood-apple tree and serves him food with devotion, he earns the merit of feeding a crore of Brahmanas.

A devotee of Siva, who serves the food prepared in milk and serves it to devotee of Siva, he never becomes poor.

The adoration of Sivalinga has been stated to be complete in all respects and has been stated to be of two types taking into consideration the paths of perseverance and renunciation.

Those who are indulging in the worldly affairs, they should adore the pedestal on earth, which fulfils all the desires. It should be adored through a competent Brahmana.

After the Rudrabhiseka, one should offer naivedya of the best quality rice. After the end of the worship, the linga should be placed in the house at an auspicious place separately.

After the finishing of the balipuja, food should be served to devotees of Siva and those who are detached from the world, they are required to worship the subtle linga.

Worshipping with the ashes, the same should also be offered to Siva. At the end of the adoration, the Sadasiva-linga should be placed over the head.

## Chapter 23 -Glory of the names of Siva

The Rsis said, “O Suta, Î Virtuous one, Î Disciple of Vyasa, salutation to you. You please tell us the best of the glory of the ashes (of Siva).

Besides you also speak out the glory of Rudraksa as well as the names of Siva, in order to delight my heart.”

Suta said, “You have put me good questions for the welfare of the world. You people are great, graceful, auspicious as well as the gems of your own respective race.

Lord Siva is your Supreme God. Even otherwise, you always like he life story of Siva.

Those who adore Siva, are graceful, successful and their having the human body is also successful. They have redeemed their race.

The one who always recites the name of Siva from his mouth, the sins do not touch him like the fire of the burning coal of catechu.

When some one recites Srl-Sivaye namah from his mouth, at that point of time his mouth becomes the auspicious place of pilgrimage and all his sins are washed out.

Whosoever filled with devotion looks at his face, he earns the merit of having a bath at a sacred place. There is no doubt about it.

Î Brahmanas, wherever a person who wears the rosary of Rudraksa as well as the ashes, and the person reciting the name of Siva live, they earn the reward of having a bath at Triveni, by a mere took at them.

The reciting of the name of Siva, wearing of the rosary of Rudraksa, and applying of the ashes over the body, bestow enormous merits. Therefore they are believed to be rewarding like Triveni.

In case all the three of them remain in one’s body, the very sight of him, removes all the sins.

There is absolutely no difference by looking at him or at Triveni. The one who does not believe so, he is surely a sinner.

One who does not apply ashes over the head, the body is without Rudraksa, and the name of Siva is not recited from the mouth, the company of such a degraded person should be discarded.

The name of Siva has been conceived to be the Ganga, the ashes as the Yamuna, and Rudraksa as Sarasvati. ṀṢ of them destroy the sins.

The one who has all the three in his body his reward is safely lodged at one place. The learned people have equated them with the bath at the Triveni.

Brahma, who is desirous of the welfare of the universe, had weighted both of them which were found to be equals. Therefore the ashes should be applied always.

Since that day, all gods alongwith Brahma, and Visnu always make use of these three which are destroyer of sins even by their sight.”

The Rsis said, “You have revealed the same reward for all the three of them. Therefore, Î Suvrata, you kindly speak out the special glory of the same.”

Suta said, “O Rsis, you are quite intelligent and devoted to Siva, besides being the best among the learned people. Î Brahmanas, you listen to the special glory of the same.

Though its glory is unknown even to the Vedas, Puranas, as well as Sastras, still, Î Brahmanas, I am revealing the truth about the same, because of your devotion.

Î Brahmanas, the real glory of all the three, except lord Mahesvara., who is beyond sata and asata, none else knows.

I am going. To narrate their glory in brief because of your devotion. Î Brahmanas, you listen with delight, which removes all types of sins.

The name of Siva is like the forest fire which destroys the mountain of sins and all the sins are reduced to ashes with the same.

Î Saunaka, all types of miseries emerge from the sins and they are destroyed with reciting of the name of Siva. There is no doubt about it.

The person who always recites the name of Siva, he is Vedic, is the noble soul, is graceful and a learned one.

Î Sages, he is bestowed with several types of rewards by dharma at once, the belief of which could be realised with the reciting of the name of Siva.

Î Munisvaras, the number of sins which are destroyed with the reciting of the name of Siva, the equivalent number of sins cannot be committed by a person in the world.

Î Munisvara, with the reciting of the name of Siva, all the sins including brahmahatya and others are destroyed.

Such of the people who cross the ocean of the universe using the name of Siva as the boat, all their sins relating to the world are washed out.

Î Great Sage, for the destruction of all the sins relating to the world, the battle-axe in the form of the name of Siva is quite enough.

The people who are suffering from the forest fire of sins, should be made to consume the nectar like name of Siva. The person who is suffering from the forest fire of sins, cannot get peace except with the name of Siva.

Such of the devotees who are soaked with stream of nectar in the form of the name of Siva, they never get worried even after falling into the fire of the universe.

Such of the noble people who preserve in their heart the devotion for the name of Siva, such people achieve redemption quite suddenly.

Î Munisvara, those who have performed tapas for many births, they achieve the adoration of Siva, which destroys all the sins.

The one who preserves an unwavering devotion towards Siva in his mind, he alone can achieve moksa, and none else. This is my feeling.

The one, who remains devoted to Siva even after the committing of the grave sins, he is relieved of all types of sins. There is no doubt about it.

As with the single forest fire many trees are burnt out, similarly with the reciting of the name of Siva all the sins are washed out.

Î Saunaka, the person whose body gets purified with the ashes, and the one 'who respectfully recites the name of Siva, such a person, even if he be a grave sinner, crosses the ocean of the Universe.

The sinner who kills the Brahmana, or steals his riches, is relieved of the sins with the reciting of the name of Siva.

After going through all the Vedas, we have come to the conclusion, that of all the remedies used for the crossing of the universe, the reciting of the name of Siva is the best. This is what has been concluded by the ancient rsis.

Î Sages, what is the use of talking much, the name of Siva destroys all the sins.

The strength of Siva’s name in the destruction of the sins, is extremely auspicious. A person cannot commit as many sins as can be destroyed by the reciting of the name of Siva.

Î Sages, with the influence of the name of Siva, the extremely sinful king named Indradyumna, had achieved the best place.

Besides the wife of a Brahmana was extremely sinful. She also achieved the best place with the influence of the name of Siva.

Î Best of the Brahmanas, I have spoken to you about the best of the glory of the name of Siva. Now you should listen from me the importance of the ashes which purify all.

## Chapter 24 - Process for the application of the ashes

Suta said, “The ashes are believed to be of two types. I shall now narrate the process of the same, which you should listen attentively.

One of them is called mahd-bhasma (ashes the great) and the other one is called Svalpa- bhasma (short ash). Several types of ashes put together are called mahd-bhasma.

It is called of three types viz.: Srauta, smarta and the laukika. The ash known as svalpa-bhasma is also of three types.

Srauta and the smarta ashes are to be used by Brahmanas. The Laukika-bhasma can be used by the people of the remaining varnas.

The sages have allowed the ashes to be taken by the Brahmanas, only after the reciting of the mantras. There is a provision that people of the all other varnas except the Brahmanas can apply the bhasma without reciting of the mantras.

Î Great sage, the ashes which are prepared with burning of the cow-dung is called the Agreya-bhasma. This is the best stuff used for making tripundra.

Or otherwise, the people with wisdom should collect the ashes after the performing of the homa. The ashes collected from other types of yajnas are also used for tripundra.

The mantras quoted in Jabalopanisad starting from Agni etc. should be recited, and while doing so the ashes should be soaked in water and applied over the body.

Jabali, the great sage has explained the process of respectfully applying of the ashes over the body with the reciting of the mantras or without it and the drawing of the tripundra our the body.

The application of the ashes and to make the slanting tripundra of Visnu, should not be forgotten by a person, desirous of moksa. This has been ordained by he Vedas.

The tripundras of Siva and Visnu are praised by Parvati and Laksmi every day.

The tripundra was patronised by Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, the people of mixed varnas, and those of the other lowers castes, applying over their bodies.

Those, who do not apply ashes over their body and do not wear tripundra, they are considered as out castes from the society.

The one who does not apply the ashes over his body with devotion, he can never be redeemed from the world even after crores of births.

Those who do not apply ashes and tripundra over their bodies, they cannot know about Siva in crores of births.

The one who does not apply the ashes over the body with faith and devotion, they are surrounded by the sins. This has been revealed by the scriptures.

Those who do not apply ashes and tripundra quite faithfully, the noble deeds performed by them bestow opposite reward.

Î Sages, a sinful person, and the one who is jealous of all the creatures, is also envious of the ashes and tripundra.

The people who securing the ashes from Sivagni, apply it over the body by reciting of Traydyusam mantra, he, with the touch of the said ashes, is relieved of all the sins.

The one who makes tripundra with the white ashes, thrice a day, he getting relieved of all the sins, always remains happy with Siva.

The one who makes tilakam of tripundra with the white ashes over the head, he after his death, achieves the place of eternal bhutas.

One should not recite the six letter mantra without having a bath with the ashes. He can recite the mantra appropriately by' applying the ashes and making a tripundra.

Even the cruel, degraded, extremely sinful, of the grave as well as light sins, and the foolish person having fallen from grace, when lives in a country, applying the ashes over his body, all the sacred places and the yajnas also reside there.

A person who has applied tripundra as well as the ashes with devotion and faith becomes adorable by humans, gods as well as the danavas. Even if he commits the sins, even then his soul remains purified.

All the sacred places arrive at the place where a person well-versed in the tattvas of lord Siva arrives.

What is the use of speaking too much, the learned people should always apply the ashes over their bodies, adore the linga as well as recite the six letter mantra.

The glory of the application of the ashes is unknown completely even to Brahma, Visnu, Rudra and other gods as well as the sages.

A person who has destroyed the activities as well as the tradition of his race, in case he applies tripundra even once over his body, then he is relieved of all the sins.

The people, who discarding the use of the ashes, engage themselves in other religious deeds, they cannot achieve redemption from the world, even in crores of births.

A Brahmana, who has decorated his head with tripundra, he has completed all the studies and has done everything.

A person who punishes a person with his head having been decorated with tripundra, he should be treated to have been born of Candala.

By reciting the mantra of Trayambaka, a Vaisya, and with the reciting of Pancaksara mantra by the Sudras the ashes should be applied over the body. Other people as well as the widows should also follow the procedure of the Sudras.

Manu has allowed a house-holder to apply ashes reciting the Pancabrahma-mantras. A Barhmacari should apply the ashes reciting the Tryambaka mantra.

A vanaprastha should apply ashes reciting the Aghora-mantra. The Ascetics should apply ashes and tripundra reciting omkara mantra.

The one who is beyond the traditions of varnas and ds'ramas he should apply ashes as well as the tripundra with the feeling of Sivoham (I am Siva) A Sivayogi should apply ashes, reciting the Isana mantra.

This is the best form of the application of the ashes, which should be respected by the people of all the varnas. Besides the above, other people should also apply ashes at the command of Siva.

The particles of the dust, which stick to be body after the bath with ashes, are like carrying an equal number of Sivalingas over the body.

In case the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Sudras or the people with mixed castes, widows, children, girls, the cheats, Brahmacaris, householders, sanyasis (ascetics) and women apply the ashes as well as the tripundra over their bodies, and by so doing they would get redeemed.

When a person who touches the fire knowingly or unknowingly, it burns in both the cases, similarly the ashes applied over the body knowingly or unknowingly, purifies the person concerned.

Those who do not use the ashes as well as Rudraksa rosary, no one should accept even the slightest food or water in the houses of such people. By consuming the food and water of a householder, Vanaprasthi, Brahmacari or a person of mixed race, one earns the sins and goes to the hell. By taking food in the houses of such people, the people of all the three varnas, get purified with the reciting of the Gdyatri-mantra, while the ascetics get purified with the reciting of omkara mantra.

Those who denounce tripundra, they seem like denouncing Siva. Those who decorate themselves with tripundra, they actually carry Siva with them.

A forehead without the ashes and the village without the temple of Siva are to be denounced. Disgrace to a person who has not adored Siva. Disgrace to the wisdom devoid of the refuge of Siva.

Those who denounce Siva, who happens to be the base of the three worlds, and also his devotees who apply tripundra over their bodies, they do so because of the fault of their vision because inspite of their being humans they have been born like a person of the mixed races, or pigs, demons, donkeys, dogs, jackals or the insects. They have been born only to proceed to the hell.

Even after seeing the sun and the moon throughout the day and night, they are unable to visualise them correctly. Can such people, be purified with the reciting of RudrasQkta with devotion? One has to face the pain of the hell even after talking to such people. No one should talk about the repentance of such people. In fact, those who denounce the people, having applied the ashes and the tripundra over their bodies, they are big fools.

Î Great sage, those who introduce tantric practices in Sivayajna, decorating the heads with upwards tilakam or those having embossed the conches, cakras, by heating them in fire, such people have no right (to say anything).

Out of such people, many are influenced with the magic of the sages. They should apply the ashes after a considerable thought.

Those who use only the sandal paste and mix the ashes in the sandal paste, they are quite right. An intelligent person, should some how apply tripundra over his body.

The Brahmanas, the virtuous women, and the widows, should apply tripundra over their foreheads. Similarly the people of all the asramas should apply ashes over the body, because it removes all the sins and bestows moksa.

A person who applies tripundra of ashes m a noble way, he is relieved of sins and the grave sins.

The Brahmacaris, householders, vanaprasthis, yatis, (sages) Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, Sudras, degraded people, or the fallen people, by using the ashes or Tripundra, they get purified getting relieved of all the sins.

Especially the devotee of Siva, who applies the ashes over his body, is relieved of the sins like killing of woman, cow, horse etc.

The stealing of other’s riches, to keep illicit relations with other’s wives to denounce others, to usurp other’s fields, to torture others, to usurp the field with crop and the garden, to burn other’s houses, or to steal the cow, buffalo, gold, silver, sesamum, blanket and other costumes, to accept charities of food, cereals, water and other things from the degraded people, to enjoy the company of the fisher women, a whore, wife of a Candala, the female dancer, to cohabit with a woman in period, a girl or a widow, or carry on trade in meat, skin, juice, salt, to indulge in backbiting, to speak deceitful words, to give false evidence and there are numerous such sins which are destroyed with applying of the tripundra over the body.

To steal the riches of Siva, to denounce Siva or his devotees, are the sins which cannot be washed out even by repentance.

The one who wears Rudraksa over his person, tripundra over the forehead, even if he is born as a Candala, he is considered to be the best of all the varnas.

Whatever might be the number of the holy places on earth, like the Ganga, the person whose forehead is adorned with tripundra, he is supposed to have taken bath in all these holy places.

Pancaksara mantra and several other seven crores of Mahamantras are there, in addition to the crores of mantras which bestow the eternal emancipation or liberation of Siva, Î Munisvara, the mantras of other gods also bestow many comforts to the people but all of them remain under his control. But the one who applies tripundra tilakam over the body, such a person (with tripundra) redeems a thousand of his ancestors and an equal number of his future relatives.

He attains long age during the present birth, remaining healthy. After enjoying all the comforts, he meets with a comfortable death.

Thereafter he possessing all the eight fortunes, with a benevolent body, he is mounted over a divine plane and is served by the gods.

He enjoys his stay with all the comforts in the places of Vidyadharas, Gandharvas and immensely valorous Indra, besides the Lokapalas respectively.

He enjoys all the comforts, the positions Prajapatis and Brahma. He remains there upto the age of Brahma and enjoys the company of hundreds of divine damsels.

There also, he enjoys all the comforts besides the pleasures of Visnuloka and lives there upto the age of a hundred Brahmas.

Then he reaching Sivaloka, getting innumerable desires fulfilled, ultimately achieves Siva’s Sayujya liberation. There is no doubt about it.

After referring to the gist of all the Upanisads, it has been decided that tripundra - is immensely beneficial and should be applied over the body.

The Brahmana, who denounces the ashes, he could never be treated as a Brahmana. He suffers in the hell till the age of Brahma.

The one who applies tripundra over the body during the performing of Sraddha, yajna, homa, balivaisvadeva as well as during the time of the worship of the gods, he actually overpowers the death.

After going to toilet, one should take bath with water, thereafter one should have bath with ashes which are quite auspicious. By bathing with the mantras, the sins are washed out and by having a bath with jnana (knowledge) one achieves the highest place.

Whatever merit and reward one gets by visiting all the holy places, the same merit or reward is achieved by a person who bathes himself with ashes.

The bath with ashes is the biggest tirtha. One should have a bath in the Ganga daily. The ashes represent Siva himself and it purifies all the three worlds.

The bath, charities, meditation, and japam performed by a Brahmana are of no consequence, in case they are performed (by a Brahmana), without the application of tripundra over the body.

A Vanaprasthi, a girl and a person without having received diksa should take their bath before noon time with water. Thereafter they should have bath in ashes.

Thus, a person who applies tripundra over his body daily, such a devotee of Siva achieves all the pleasures besides moksa.

The one who does not wear a single Rudraksa over the body, which provides the highest merit and in case he is without tripundra then his life is of no consequence.

In this way I have narrated the glory of mahatmya. This is the sacred of all the people and it should be kept as a secret by you all.

Î Great sage, there are three lines of tripundra over the forehead or other parts of the body.

Starting from the centre of the eyebrows, one should draw tripundra upto the end of both the eyebrows.

The lines drawn by middle and ring fingers, with inverted thumb are called tripundra, carrying the ashes quite carefully in the three fingers, tripundra should be drawn because it bestows the pleasure as well as the salvation.

In the sequence of three lines, there are nine gods, who are lodged in all the limbs. You listen to me carefully, I am going to describe the same.

Akara is the domestic fire, bhu is rajoguna, Rgveda is the power of activity and pratahstavan (morning ritual).

Î Sages, Mahadeva happens to be the god of the first time. The devotees of Siva, who have received Sivadiksa should know about the same.

Ukara is the fire of the southern quarters, akasa (sky) is sattvaguna and the Vedas are yajuh. Madhyandin is the Savana (the mid-day ritual. The desire is the inner soul.

Î Sages, the devotees having Sivadiksa should know that the god of the second line is Mahesvara.

Makara is the invoking fire. Paramatma is form of tamoguna, jnana-sakti is Samaveda and is the form of the third place of sacrifice.

The god of the third line is Siva, which should be known by the people having Sivadiks&.

Thus, getting purified daily offering salutation to the gods of the three lines, if a devotee applies tripundra over the body with devotion, he achieves all the pleasures as well as the salvation.

Î Sages, the gods of all the limbs and their places have been defined. Now you listen to the placed connected therewith.

They should be grouped either in thirty- two places, or half of that-sixteen, or in eight or in five places.

The thirty-two limbs include, head, forehead, both the ears, both the eyes, nose, mouth, throat, both the hands, both the elbows, wrists, heart, ribs, navel, testicles, thighs, ankles, knees, legs and feet which are the best. The fire, water, earth, wind, directions, Dikapalas and Vasus are the excellent places.

The eight Vasus are Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, water, wind, fire, day break and light.

Reciting their names, the learned people should apply tripundra or becoming careful tripundra should be applied over sixteen limbs.

These are the head, forehead, neck, both the shoulders, arms, elbows, wrists, heart, navel, two sides, and the back. After applying the tripundra over these limbs, one should worship Asvanikumaras. Siva, Sakti, Rudra, Isa, Narada, and nine Saktis or goddesses like Vama and others. These are said to be sixteen gods, besides these Nasatya and Oasra have been stated to be Asvanikumaras.

Or otherwise, the ashes should be applied over sixteen limbs viz.: the head, hair, ears, face, both the arms, heart, navel, both the thighs, both the knees, feet and back. The sixteen places or gods include, Siva, moon, Rudra, Brahma, Ganesa, Visnu.

Laksmi in the heart, Siva in the navel, Naga damsels and both the ãṁ-damsels, then in the feet, the plthas or the seashore are the sixteen places. The eight places are further being described.

Rectum, forehead, both the ears, both the shoulders, heart and navel, are the eight places.

Brahma and the seven Rsis are their gods. Î Great sages, this is what has been spoken by the people with wisdom well-versed in the use of ashes.

Or otherwise (the ashes should be applied over the) forehead, arms, heart, navel, the five limbs of the body.

Keeping in view, the time and the place, one should do whatever is possible. In case it may not be possible to apply ashes, one should himself make use of tripundra, or get it used.

(The devotee of Siva), concentrate on the three eyed Siva who is the base of three gunas, the creator of the three gods, and applies tripundra, reciting the mantra namah- Sivaya.

Reciting the mantra Is'abhyam namah tripundra should be applied on both the ribs. Then reciting the mantra bijabhydm namah tripundra should be applied over the forearms.

Then reciting the mantras pitrbhyam namah and umes'abhyam namah tripundra should be applied over the upper limbs. Then uttering Bhlmaya namah back and the back of the head (should be painted with).

## Chapter 25 - The glory of Rudraksa

Suta said, “O sage Saunaka, Î Great Soul and highly intelligent one, you please listen to the glory of Rudraksa which I am going to speak out in brief.

This Rudraksa is an extremely auspicious bead and is extremely dear to Siva. By its mere sight or by performing japam with the same, or using it as a rosary, all the sins get destroyed.

In earlier times, lord Siva, in the presence of the goddess Parvati, for the purpose of the welfare of the people, had narrated the importance of Rudraksa.

Siva said, “O Goddess, Î Mahesani, for the sake of your pleasure and for the welfare of the devotees, I narrate the glory of Rudraksa.

Î Mahesani, earlier, my mind felt disturbed after performing tapas for a divine thousand years.

Î Parmesvari, I happen to be the supreme lord of the- universe, and being self-possessed, I then opened my both the eyes.

Then drops of tears fell on the ground from my half-opened eyes, which produced the trees of Rudraksa.

For the welfare of the devotees those drops of tears took to the form of trees. Being immobile, they were given to the devotees of lord Visnu, belonging to the four varnas.

They became the Rudraksa trees in the Gauda country, which became greatly favourite of Siva. They were also grown in Mathura, Ayodhya and Malayacala.

They were also grown in the city of Kasi, for the destruction of the sins at the instance of the Vedas.

At my command the Rudraksa beads could be used by Brahmana, Ksatriya, Vaisya as well as the Sudras. These Rudraksas are of auspicious nature.

The learned people should know about their shades as well. They are of white, red, yellow as well as of black colours. The people should wear them according to their varnas.

The people desirous of the worldly pleasures as well as the salvation, should wear Rudraksa according to their Varnas. The devotees of Siva, particularly, in order to please Siva and Parvati, should wear Rudraksa.

Rudraksa of the size of Embolic myrobalan, is considered to be the best. The one of the size of jujube fruit is considered to be the middling one.

Rudraksa of the size of a gram is the meanest, but still its processing is being spoken. Î Parvati, you, with the desire of the benefit of the devotees should listen to it with devotion.

Î Mahesvarl, Rudraksa of the size of jujube fruit increases the comforts and fortunes in the world.

Rudraksa of the size of Embolic myrobalan, destroys all the misfortunes. Then Rudraksa of the size of gunja (a poisonous plant’s fruit) fulfils all the desires.

The smaller it becomes in size, the greater is the benefit yielded by it. Each one of these is fruitful. Each one bestows one tenth of the merit than one another. This has been the opinion of the learned people.

Rudraksa has been prescribed for the removal of sins. Therefore one should wear this Rudraksa which fulfils all the desires.

Î Paramesvara, as the rosary of Rudraksa has been found to be rewarding in this world, no other rosary can bestow such a reward.

Î goddess, Rudraksas of even size, with gloss, firm, thick and having thorn like shape yield desires and bestow worldly pleasures besides salvation for ever.

The defective Rudraksas which are damaged by worms, or are cut or broken, without thorn- like prostrations, have cracks and are not round.

The bead having the natural hole from one end to the other is the best and the one which is bored by human efforts is treated to be middle one.

With the wearing of Rudraksa beads, the grave sins are washed out. By wearing eleven hundred Rudraksa beads, a person is turned like Rudra himself.

The merit which is derived with the wearing of eleven hundred Rudraksa'beads, cannot be described in hundreds of years.

A person who wears five hundred and fifty Rudraksa beads with devotion, he is called the crown. He is considered to be the best of the devotees.

A devotee should wear three strings of three hundred and sixty Rudraksa beads like a yajnopavita.

One should tie six beads on the right and six to the left of the tuft over the head.

One should wear a hundred Rudraksa- beads in the neck, eleven in each one of the arms, elbows and the fore-arms each.

A devotee of Siva should wear three beads in the yajnopavita and five in the waist.

Î Parvati, the one who has worn the beads this number, his beauty is beyond description and he becomes adorable like Siva himself.

By thus developing his outward appearance, when a devotee, is seated over an asana in meditation, then at the sight of such a person, the people get redeemed. Upto this stage the method of wearing eleven hundred of Rudraksa beads has been explained. In the absence of the same a simple method is being highlighted.

A Rudraksa should be tied to the tuft, thirty in the head, fifty around the neck, sixteen in each arm, twelve in each wrist, five hundred on each shoulder, besides a garland of a hundred and sixty beads should be worn like a yajnopavita.

In this way when a devotee with firm resolve wears a thousand beads, all the gods offer their salutation to him, because he becomes adorable like Siva.

A Rudraksa should be tied in the tuft, forty of them over the head, thirty-two around the neck, hundred and eight in the heart.

One each in the two ears, six each around the arms, sixteen around both the hands, or twenty four of them.

The one who wears the prescribed number of Rudraksa beads on his person with devotion, he is considered to be the best of the devotee of Siva. He is adored like Siva and all the people offer their salutation to him.

One should wear Rudraksa reciting the Isana-mantra, with Tatpurusa in the ears and with Aghora mantra, over the heart. Rudraksa should thus be worn.

The wise devotee shall wear Rudraksa around fore-arms, with Ahogra-bija mantra and a string of fifteen Rudraksas reciting the Vamadeva mantra over the stomach.

With the reciting of the five Sadyojata Brahma mantras, one should wear three five or seven rosaries in the rest of the limbs. Or otherwise all the Rudraksas should be worm by reciting of the mula-mantra.

A person wearing Rudraksa beads, shall not eat meat, garlic, onion, red garlic, potherb, glutinous fruits, pig of rubbish and wine.

Î Parvati, the white Rudraksa should be worn by the Brahmanas, the red by Ksatriyas, yellow by the Vaisyas, while the black should be used by the Sudras. This has been propounded by the Vedas.

Rudraksa should be worn by Brahmacari, householder or the forest dweller ascetic of any order. This is the extreme secret. Rudraksa is found by great merits. By disowning it, one has to fall in the hell.

The persons desirous of welfare should not wear Rudraksa of the size of Emblic myrobalan, or those of lighter weight, but depressed with thome, those eaten by worms, or without holes, or those having other defects, should not be worn. Rudraksa of the size of a gram should be avoided. Î Uma, Rudraksa is my symbol which should always be worn.

People of all the varnas and asramas, besides Sudras and the women should wear Rudraksa at the command of Siva. The ascetics should wear it reciting the omkara- mantra.

By wearing Rudraksa during the day, the sins committed during the night and by wearing it during the night the sins committed during the day, get destroyed.

Such of the people who wear Rudraksa, locks of hair as well as tripundra, on the forehead, they never have to visit the abode of Yama.

The one who wears a Rudraksa over the head and tripundra over the forehead, and those who themselves recite the Panmksara mantra, such type of ascetics are always adored.

Yama has commanded his messengers, “the one who has no Rudraksa over the body, or no tripundra over the forehead, nor Pancaksara mantra in the mouth, they should be carried to the abode of Yama.

One should well realise the effect of wearing Rudraksa as well as the ashes, which are adorable for us always. They should never be carried to the abode of Yama.”

Yama has also commanded his messenger, accordingly “that the persons using ashes over the body or wearing Rudraksa are adorable by us.” Thus thinking all the messengers of Yama cannot carry such people to Yamaloka.

Î Mahadevi, Î Parvati, Rudraksa destroys all types of sins. Therefore the one who wears the same is dear to me.

The one who wears Rudraksa in his hands, arms, and the head, no one can kill him. He wanders in the universe in the form of Siva.

He remains always adorable by gods as well as the demons, like Siva, destroyer of sins of any one seen by him.

A person who is devoid of wisdom as well as meditation, while wearing Rudraksa, he is relieved of all the sins and achieves the highest position.

The performing of japam by the rosary of Rudraksa beads, multiplies the reward crores of times.

Till such time, a person wears Rudraksa rosary over his body, upto that time the untimely death does not bother him.

A person whose body looks fine with tripundra and Rudraksa and also who recites the mantra of Mrtunjaya, the very sight of a person bestows the reward like that of having an audience with Siva.

Î Dear Parvati, a person who adores the five gods, or who adores all the gods, he should recite all the mantras with the rosary of Rudraksa.

Even the devotees of Visnu and other gods should undoubtedly use Rudraksa. It is essential for the devotee of Siva to wear Rudraksa.

Rudraksas are said to be of various types, the divisions of which are going to be related by me, which should, Î Parvati, be listened by you with devotion. They bestow pleasure and devotion.

Rudraksa with a single mouth is indeed the form of Siva, which bestows the comforts as well as the salvation. A very look at it relieves a person of the sin of brahmahatya.

The place where the said bead is adored, Laksmi does not leave that place, and all the disturbances are removed besides all his desires are fulfilled.

The bead with two mouths, fulfils all the desires. This Rudraksa especially washes out the sin of Brahmhatya.

The Rudraksa bead with three mukhas or mouths, provides all the means always, with its influence all the lores are firmly established.

Rudraksa with four mouths represents Siva himself and the one who wears it, is relieved of the sin of killing of a human. With the mere sight of it, it bestows the four aims of life (i.e. dharma, artha, êīḍṁ and moksa).

A Rudraksa with five faces, represents Rudra himself and is known by the name of Kalagni. It fulfils all the desires, bestows salvation to the devotees.

Rudraksa removes the sins of cohabiting with degraded woman, and eating of forbidden food etc.

Rudraksa with six mouths, represents Karttikeya and should be tied to the right arm, which relieves one of the brahmahatya and other sins.

Î Parvati, Rudraksa with seven mouths is called Ananka, Î Mistress of the gods, by wearing the same, even the pauper becomes rich.

A Rudraksa with eight mukhas is called Vasumurti and is considered to be the form of Bhairava, by wearing it one enjoys his full life, and becomes Siva after his death.

Rudraksa with nine mukhas is called Bhairava or Kapila the great sage. Its presiding deity is Navadurga or Mahesvari.

This Rudraksa should be worn over the left arm with devotion and by doing so, he surely becomes Sarvesvara like me.

Î Parvati, Rudraksa of ten faces is Janardana himself, Î Mistress of gods, all the desires are fulfilled, by wearing the same.

Î Parmesvari, the one who wears Rudraksa with eleven faces, be becomes Rudra himself and is victorious everywhere.

The one who wears Rudraksa with twelve mouths over the head, he becomes illustrious like the twelve Adityas.

Rudrdksa of thirteen mouths represents Visvadeva and by wearing it all the desires of a person are fulfilled, besides gaining fortunes. The good fortunes always

overshadow his house.

A Rudraksa with fourteen faces, resembles Sadasiva, which should be worn over the head with devotion and all his sins are washed out.

Thus the different types of Rudraksas based on the different number of mouths, have been spelt out. Î Parvati, now you listen with devotion to their respective mantras.

Mantra No. of faces

(I) Orit Hririt namah (obeisance) Single faced  
(II) Orit namah (obeisance) Two faced  
(III) Orit kllrit namah (obeisance) Three faced  
(IV) Orit Hrim namah (obeisance) Four faced  
(V) Orit Hririt namah (obeisance) Five faced  
(VI) Orit Hririt Hunt namah (obeisance) Six faced  
(VII) Orit Hririt namah (obeisance) Seven faced  
(VIII) Orit Hririt namah (obeisance) Eight faced  
(IX) Orit Hath namah (obeisance) Nine faced  
(X) Orit Hririt namah (obeisance) Ten faced  
(XI) Orit Hririt Hurit namah (obeisance) Eleven faced  
(XII) Orit Ksaurit Raurit namah (obeisance) Twelve faced  
(XIII) Orit Hririt namah (obeisance) Thirteen faced  
(XIV) Orit namah Fourteen faced

Î Goddess, a person having a great devotion and faith, for the achievement of all the desired objects, getting freed from laziness, should wear Rudraksa.

A person who, on earth wears Rudraksa without the reciting of the related mantra, he has to stay in the hell for a kalpa.

A person who wears the rosary of Rudraksa, observing him, all evil spirits, ghosts, pisacas, witches like Dakinis and sakums besides other malignant spirits, evil dreams and spells etc. fly away from a distance.

Î Parvati, finding a person wearing the Rudraksa rosary all the gods like Siva, Visnu, the goddess, Ganesa, the sun and other deities feel delighted.

Î Mahesvari, thus realising about the glory of Rudraksa, a person should wear it with devotion for the increase of dharma.

In this way, lord Siva narrated before Parvati, the glory of Rudraksa as well as the holy ashes, which bestow the pleasure and salvation.

The one who always applies the holy ashes and also wears Rudraksa rosary, he becomes dear to lord Siva. With the influence of wearing the same, one achieves worldly pleasure and salvation.

The one who always used only ashes as well as Rudraksa, he becomes the devotee of Siva. The one who is engaged in the reciting of Pancaksara mantra, he is said to be a complete person in all respects.

The adoration of Siva, performed without tripundra, or holy ashes, and Rudraksa, becomes infructuous.

Î Great sage, I have narrated to you whatever had been asked by you. The glory of the holy ashes as well as Rudraksa, fulfils all desires.

A person who listens to this auspicious Mahatmya daily, he, with the glory of the holy ashes and Rudraksa, has all his desires fulfilled.

Such a person, enjoying all the pleasures in this world, together with sons and grandsons, achieves moksa after his death becoming dearer to Siva.

Î Sages, the Vidyesvara Samhita, has been narrated to you, which at the command of Siva, bestows all the success daily on earth and salvation after death.

Thus ends the first Vidyesvara Samhita

Siva-Mahapuranam

Rudra Samhita

## (1) Srsti Khanda

## Chapter 1 - Question by the Sages

Visnu Prayer:-

I offer my salutation to lord Siva, the spouse of the goddess Gauri, who happens to be the sole cause of the creation, maintenance and the destruction of the universe, the one who is well aware of all the tattvas, who is of endless renown and has the refuge in Maya (illusion), such a lord of Gauri, possesses endless glory, unthinkable beauty, form of wisdom, and the spotless one.

I offer my salutation to lord Siva, who is beyond Prakrti, without beginning, extremely calm and quiet, the best among the Purusas, who has created this universe with the help of his Maya, and is lodged inside and outside the same.

He is the one, who dwells in the hearts of all in a subtle form, who creates the universe without the help of anyone else and around whom, the universe rotates as the iron rotates around the magnet.

Vyasa said-

After offering my salutation to Siva- the father of the universe and Parvati, the mother of the universe, besides Ganesa, their son, now I narrate Rudra Samhita.

Once all the sages Saunaka and others of Nemisaranya, asked Suta, with utmost devotion”.

The Sages said**-**

“In the Sadhya Sadhana Khanda of Vidyesvara Samhita, there is a story which has been listened by us with devotion. It happens to be the first and delightful compendium, which is dear to the devotees attracting their minds.

Î Blessed Suta, Let you enjoy your life for long, quite comfortably because you narrate to us the best story of Siva.

We do not feel satisfied by consuming the nectar of wisdom. Î Sinless one, we intend to ask something more from you.

O Omniscient one, by the grace of Vyasa, you have achieved contentment. No event of the three times (past, present and future) remains unknown to you.

With your total devotion towards your preceptor Vyasa, and with his grace you have attained knowledge of everything and have known well all the subjects, making your life a success.

O Learned one, now you kindly describe the best form of Siva and the divine events of the life of Siva and Parvati.

Lord Siva has the Nirguna or absolute form, (devoid of attributes). When does he take to Saguna form in the world? We are unable to know about the true form of Siva inspite of serious deliberations.

How was Siva lodged in his own form, at the start of the universe and how did he sport in the middle of the creation.

How does Siva behave at the end of the creation. How could Siva, the benevolent one, could be pleased.

What type of reward is bestowed by Siva, when he gets pleased with his devotees. You kindly speak out to us in detail.

We have heard that lord Siva is pleased quickly. Because of the compassion he is unable to bear the labour undertaken by the devotee for his sake.

All the three gods viz.: Brahma, Visnu and Mahesa have emerged from the limbs of Siva. Mahesa is Siva himself possessing all his amgas (substrata of elements) distinct from Mahesa.

Î Lord, you kindly enlighten us about his manifestation and his life story. You kindly narrate the same to us. You tell us about the birth of Uma and her marriage with Siva as well.

On Sinless one, you particularly describe about their house-hold and narrate other activities.”

Vyasa said**-**

“Thus listening to the question of the sages, Suta was pleased, and meditating upon the lotus like feet of Siva, he spoke to the sages.”

Suta said**-**

“O Sages, you have put me a very good question. Therefore all of your are graceful, by your own wisdom, you are always devoted to the story of Siva.

The listening to the story of Siva, purifies three types of people viz.: the speaker, the one who enquires, an the listener.

Î Brahmanas, except for the killer of the animals, who could be averse to the hearing of the glory of Siva, which delights three types of people.

The glory of lord Siva sung by a person without any lust, desire, or greed, is the best remedy for the ailments of the world, which pleases the eyes as well as the ears.

O Brahmanas, I am narrating the sports of Siva according to my wisdom and your question. All of you should listen to it with respect.

The way you have asked the question to me today, similarly having been inspired by Siva and Hari, Narada had once asked the same question from Brahma.
