Brahma, the devotee of Siva, listening to the words of Narada, which delighted him, pleasing Narada narrated the glory of lord Siva.

Vyasa said, “The learned Brahmanas, on hearing the words of Suta, became eager to know more of the conversation and they asked him.” The sages said, “O best of the devotees of Siva, Î Suta, the fortunate one, listening to your pleasant words, our mind has become curious. When was this pleasant conversation between Brahma and Narada held, in which the sports of Siva were narrated? Î Dear one, you tell us about the story that emerged from the conversation between Brahma and Narada. What were the questions and how were they answered? Please enlighten us.”

On hearing these words of the sages, of noble wisdom, Suta was very much pleased, and he spoke out everything about the said conversation.

## Chapter 2 - Deputing of Kamadeva by Indra to disturb the tapas of Narada

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, once Narada the best of the sages and the brilliant son of Brahma, having meek temperament thought of performing the tapas.

There was an extremely beautiful cave near the Himalaya mountain, besides which the divine Ganga flowed with great force.

There was a charming asrama which looked quite beautiful, there. The sage Narada with divine vision went to that place for performing of tapas.

Observing the place Narada, the best of the sages, sat in meditation, maintaining silence, and started performing tapas after practising ðrṁñaóaḍṁ.

Î Brahmanas, Narada performed the contemplation, wherein the feeling of “I am Brahman” is generated leading to the direct perception of Brahman.

When the great sage Narada was thus performing the tapas, the mind of Indra was exceedingly agitated and he started shaking with the mental agony.

Indra thought that Narada was trying to usurp his kingdom, therefore the tapas of Narada should be disturbed.

Then Indra the lord of the gods, remembered the god of love, who arrived there in no time with his queen Rati and his friend- the spring season.

At the arrival of the god of love (Kamadeva), the king of Devas, Indra with selfish and mischievous intelligence, spoke to him.

Indra said, “O Valorous friend, possessing immense strength, you always act for my welfare, you lovingly listen to my words and then help me.

On the basis of your strength, I have shattered the pride of several people performing tapas. Î Friend, my kingdom has been stable by your grace.

The sage Narada is performing severe penance in a cave in Himalaya, controlling all the senses with firmness and keeping the mind in the form of Siva, the Lord of universe.

I am afraid, that, he might beg for my kingdom from Brahma. I have developed this doubt in me. You proceed today itself and create disturbance in his tapas.”

At this command of Indra the god of gods, Kamadeva, the beloved of Madhu and Rati, arrogantly, reached the place of Narada and started making efforts.

Reaching there he applied all his arts, while the spring season also arrogantly spread its different type of prowess.

Î Sages, the mind of Narada, felt the least disturbed. On the other hand his pride was shattered by the grace of Siva.

Î Saunaka and other sages, you listen from me the reason for the same. By the grace of Siva, Kamadeva could exercise no influence on Narada.

Because Siva, the enemy of Kamadeva had also performed tapas there itself. It was this place, where Siva had burnt to ashes the god of love who created disturbance in the tapas of the sages.

Rati prayed to gods to bring back Kamadeva to life. Thereafter the gods prayed to Siva, who said to them.

Î Gods, Kamadeva would become alive after some time. But his efforts would never bear fruit here.

O Gods, the land which is visible before you (would become auspicious) and the people who would live here would be immune to the arrows of Kamadeva.”

At these words of Siva, Kamadeva, found himself incapable to deal with Narada, who at once returned to the heaven before Indra.

Kamadeva apprised Indra of the prevailing situation at the place of Narada and also about the influence of Narada. With the permission of Indra, Kamadeva, returned to his abode with the spring season.

Listening to the news about Narada, Indra felt surprised and started praising Narada, because, having been overpowered with influence of the Ṅaya, Siva is in comprehensible in the world. A devotee having dedicated his soul to Siva, leaving him, Siva’s Ṅaya overpowers every one else.

At the insistence of Siva, Narada also stayed there for long. He completed his tapas there.

With his victory against Kamadeva, the heart of Narada was filled with pride. Thereafter with the influence with Ṅaya of Siva, he was deprived of the true knowledge.

Î Sages, graceful is the Ṅaya of Siva and its movements, which are beyond the comprehension of Brahma, Visnu and other gods.

Having been puffed with delusion, the arrogant sage Narada, went to Kailasa to apprise Siva of his own achievement.

Then Narada having been filled with pride, bowed in reverence at the feet of Siva and considering himself as a great soul, conqueror of the god of love and a lord, he narrated the entire story to Siva.

On hearing this, Siva, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, realising that Narada had been overpowered with his Ṅaya and was ignorant of the factual position, said to him.

Siva said, “O Dear Narada, you are an immensely learned one, you are graceful, you listen to my words. Whatever have you spoken to me, don’t, speak it to anyone else. You should particularly avoid telling it to lord Visnu.

The facts about yourself which you have spoken to me, should not be spoken to anyone else, even when you are asked to do so. This is extremely secret and should not be revealed to anyone.

I am requesting you particularly because you are dear to me and are devotee of Visnu, who happens to be my follower.”

Thus Siva advised him variously, because Rudra remembers all. But Narada, who had been overpowered with the Ṅaya of Siva, could hardly appreciate the words of the lord.

The future course of events could be known by the people of wisdom. No one can move against the wishes of lord Siva.

Then Narada, the great sage, went to Brahmaloka, and offering his salutation at the feet of Brahma, narrated the story of his performing of tapas and his victory against Kamadeva.

Hearing the words of Narada, Brahma, mentally offered his salutation to lord Siva and realising all the causes, prohibited his son from repeating the story to any one else.

Narada is the foremost of all the learned people, but he could hardly appreciate even the advice of Brahma, because he had been overpowered with the Ṅaóa of Siva and the seed of arrogance had sprouted in his heart.

Everything moves in the world as per the desire of Siva. He controls the entire universe. The entire universe moves at his will.

With the loss of wisdom, Narada then reached Visnuloka at once, because the seed of the pride of overpowering the god of love, had already sprouted in his heart. Because of the same he had gone to apprise Visnu about the same.

Finding the arrival of Narada, Visnu respectfully got up, moved a few steps forward to respectfully welcome him. Without realising the cause of his arrival, Visnu embraced Narada.

Then Visnu made Narada to occupy his own seat and with his mind devoted at the lotus like feet of Siva, Visnu spoke truthfully, with the intention of the removal of the pride of Narada.

Lord Visnu said, “O Dear one, where from have you arrived and is the purpose of your visit? Î Lion among the sages, you are extremely graceful. Your visit has purified me.”

On hearing the words of Visnu, the pride of Narada was further increased. With his mind having been filled with pride and he narrated the story of overpowering Kamadeva in an immensely naughty manner.

Listening to the arrogant words of Narada, Visnu, mentally adored the lotus like feet of Siva and could know the factual position.

Lord Visnu prayed Lord Siva, with great devotion, lowering his head and folded hands.

Visnu said, “O Mahadeva, you are the god of gods, Î Paramesvara, be pleased with me. Î Lord Siva, you are graceful. Your Maya infatuating for all.

Offering prayer to lord Siva, thus, Visnu closing his eyes and meditated upon his lotus like feet, and then kept quiet.

Visnu happens to be he protector the universe, keeping in his mind the task of Siva, and at his command, he spoke to Narada, the best of the sages.

He said, “O Lion among the sages, the ocean of tapas, large hearted sage, you are graceful. Î Great sage, the one who does not preserve in his heart, the devotion for three gods, he is influenced by passions, delusion etc.

These defects are painful for him. You are a perpetual brahmacari. You are endowed with supreme knowledge and are devoted to non-attachment.

How could you be overpowered with the passions. You are free from all the defects since birth.” Hearing such words the great sage, mentally offering his salutation Narada said to Hari.

Narada said “O Master, What is the influence of Kamadeva? In case I enjoy your grace, then you kindly speak out.” Thus speaking, offering his salutation to lord Visnu, Narada, who always moved at will, left the place.

## Chapter 3 - Svayamvara of Srimati and Narada’s humiliation

The Rsis said, “O Blessed Suta, the disciple of Vyasa, salutation to you. You please continue to narrate this interesting story to us.

Î Dear one, after the departure of the sage Narada, what did lord Visnu do? Where did he go from there, you please speak out to us.”

Vyasa said, “Suta, well-versed in the Puranic texts, listening to their words, reciting the name of Siva internally, spoke many praiseworthy words.”

Suta said, “When Narada left of his own accord, then honouring the wishes of lord Siva, Visnu who is past master in illusion, atonce displayed his Ṅaya (illusion).

He created a great city on the way of the sage, which was spread in four hundred miles and was surprisingly charming.

It was far more beautiful than even Visnuloka, where several beautiful things looked charming.

A king named Silanidhi ruled that city which was filled were all the fortunes. He was making preparations for the Svayamvara of his daughter.

His palace was fully occupied with the princes having arrived from all the four directions. They were all anxious wearing the best of costumes for wooing the girl.

Narada was fascinated at the sight of such a city. Having his mind filled with passion, he went at the royal gate.

Finding the arrival of the sage Narada, the king Silanidhi, seated him over the gem studded lion-throne and then adored him.

Then the king summoned his daughter named Srimati, made her bow at the feet of Narada.

Looking at the girl, Narada felt surprised and said, “O King, who is this girl resembling the daughter of gods?

On hearing the words of Narada, the king spoke with folded hands, “She is my daughter, known by the name of Srimati.

The time of her marriage has arrived. She is in search of a suitable match for herself. She possesses all the auspicious symptoms.

Î Great sage, you please foretell about her destiny and also about the groom my daughter is going to achieve ultimately.”

At these words of the king, the sage Narada felt passionate with a desire to achieve her. Then discussing with the king, Narada said, Î King, your daughter is blessed with all the auspicious symbols. She is immensely virtuous, is graceful, and is the mine of virtues like Laksmi.

Her husband would be Sarvesvara, infallible, valorous resembling Siva, fortunate and would conquer even the god of love. Her husband would be the best among the gods.”

Thus speaking, Narada having the independent nature, left the place taking leave of the king. At that point of time Narada had been overpowered with the Maya of Siva.

The sage Narada then started thinking in his mind, how to achieve the girl? He thought, “How would she select me alone among so many kings present there?

All the women are attracted by beauty and with the same beauty, she could be attracted towards me. There is no doubt about it.”

Thus thinking the sage having been overpowered by the passion at once went to Visnuloka in order to achieve the beauty of Visnu.

Bowing in reverence to Hrsikesa, the sage Narada said, “I would like to tell you my entire story in a lonely place.”

Then lord Visnu, who always acted according to the wishes of Siva, agreed for the same and asked him to narrate his story. The sage Narada then said-

Narada said, “The king Silanidhi, is always devoted to you. His daughter Srimati is in search for a husband for herself.

She is well known to impress the three worlds. She is a most beautiful girl in the three worlds. Î Lord Visnu, I intend to marry her today itself.

The king has arranged for a Svayamvara as desired by the girl. Thousands of princes have arrived from all the four directions, to attend the Svayamvara.

In case you bestow your beauty on me, then I can surely get the girl. Without your beauty, she would never put the wedding garland around my neck without your form.

Î Lord, you bestow your form on me. I happen to be your dearest slave. You do something by which the girl should choose me.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the sage, and realising about the greatness the Maya of Siva, the compassionate lord smilingly said-

Lord Visnu said, “O Sage, you can go if you so like, but I shall surely do favour to you, as the best of the physician, does good to the patient, because you are dear to me.”

Thus speaking lord Visnu bestowed on Narada, the face of a monkey (Hari). Thus bestowing grace on Narada, Visnu disappeared.

Then Narada, getting the face of a monkey from Visnu, thought himself as having been succeeded in his mission, but he could not understand the intentions of Visnu.

Thereafter, the Narada, foremost among the sages reached at the place of Svayamvara filled with many kings.

The assembly created for the purpose of Svayamvara was quite divine. The princes were present there. Î Brahmanas, it appeared like the assembly of Indra.

Narada also seated himself in the said assembly and sitting there delightfully he thought.

“Leaving aside me the beautiful damsel would never choose anyone else, because I am in the form of Visnu.” The poor sage was unaware of the ugliness of his face.

The people who had arrived there found the sage Narada in his old form. Î Brahmanas, this secret remained unknown to the princes and others who gathered there.

Two of the ganas of Siva had arrived there for the protection of Narada in the form of Brahmanas, who were well aware of the secret (about Narada).

Both the ganas finding the sage having been be fooled, went to him and got themselves seated besides him and started joking him.

They said, “Look at the form of Narada, which is as graceful as Visnu, but his head is as horrible as a monkey.

Having been infested with passion, he uselessly is desirous of wooing the princess.” They kept on making such comments; they kept on laughing at him.

The sage Narada who was infested with passion took no notice of their words. He was only interested in achieving Srimati.

In the meantime, the princess arrived there from the inner quarters, having been surrounded by her handmaids.

The princess possessing all the auspicious symbols, carrying the golden garland in her hands appeared graceful in the place of Svayamvara resembling Laksmi.

The princess holding the garland in her hand started wandering in the place of Svayamvara in search of her groom.

She felt agitated finding Narada in the form of Visnu, except for the face which resembled to that of a monkey and turning her face from there, she felt painful and left the place.

Finding no groom suitable for herself the princes did not offer the wedding garland to anyone of the people who assembled there.

In the meantime Visnu arrived there in the form of a king, who was spotted by the princess alone.

The arrival of Visnu in the form of a prince, delighted the princess, and she placed the garland around his neck.

Visnu in the form of a king, disappeared from that lace with the princess and reached his abode.

All other princes were disappointed, having lost Srimati. The passionate sage Narada was extremely upset.

Then both the Siva ganas who had taken to the form of Brahmanas, said to the lustful Narada.

Both the ganas said, “O Sage Narada, you are uselessly feeling lustful in the hope of getting the princess. You first look at your deplorable monkey like face.”

Suta said, “On hearing the words of the ganas Narada felt surprised. Influenced with the Ṅaya of Siva, he looked his face in a mirror.

Finding his face resembling that of a monkey, he felt enraged and in a of confusion, the sage pronounced a curse on the ganas.

He said, “You have laughed at a Brahmana like me, therefore both of you would be born of the semen of a Brahmana but would be turned as Raksasas.

The Siva ganas, who were the foremost of the learned people, hearing the curse pronounced by Narada, realised that he had been overpowered by the Maya of Siva and kept quiet.

O Brahmana, both of them felt gloomy, feeling that it was the wish of lord Siva. Thus thinking they left for their respective abodes, praising Siva at the same time.

## Chapter 4 - Narada reaches Vaikuntha and curses Visnu

The Rsis said, “O Suta, the great intellect. You have narrated wonderful story. Graceful is the Maya of Siva and all the moveable and immovable things are dependent on him.

What did the enraged Narada who had been overpowered with passion, do after the departure of the ganas of Siva?”

Suta said, “Having been overpowered with the Maya of Siva, and getting confused, Narada, after pronouncing a curse over the ganas of Siva, at the desire of Siva, looked his face in the water.

Because of the will of Siva, Narada was unable to understand the trick used by Visnu. He was overpowered by the unbearable anger and then he went to Visnuloka.

His intelligence was lost because of the wishes of Siva, he started burning in rage, Narada uttered abusive language blazing like the fire flames. His intelligence had already vanished because of the will of Siva.

Narada said, “O Hari, you are extremely wicked, a cheat, and an enchanter of the universe. You are never desirous of the well- being of others. Your intentions are always dirty.

Earlier, you taking to the form of Mohini, had played a trick and made the demons to consume the wine instead of nectar.

Had Siva, mercifully not consumed the poison, then Î Hari, the deceitful one, all your Ṅaya would have been destroyed.

Î Visnu, your are more inclined towards deceitfulness. You do not have a noble temperament. The lord has made you free from control.

Siva- the supreme soul has not done well in this way. You behave independently because of his influence as well as the prowess.

Siva repents at your performance. On the testimony of the Vedas, he has declared the Brahmanas to be the best of all.

Knowing this fully well, Î Hari, I advise you today. You never behave like this in future.

Even today, you are fearless because your coming in conflict with a person having the terrific temperament. Today, you shall have to reap the reward of your misdeed.”

Then Narada having been overpowered by the Ṅaya of Siva, thus speaking to Hari displayed the excellence of the power of a Brahmana, feeling painful and pronounced a curse on Visnu.

He said, “O Visnu, your form (monkey) by which you have cheated me, Î Hari, you becoming a human in the same form would face grief. The way you had given me a monkey face, the same monkeys would help you.

You cause trouble to others, therefore, you would also suffer pain from the separation from your wife. Getting confused with ignorance, you would have to act as a human being.”

Then Narada, having been overpowered by ignorance, after thus pronouncing a curse to Visnu, kept quiet. Visnu on the other hand, praising the Ṅaya of Siva accepted the curse pronounced by Narada.

Thereafter Siva- the lord of illusion, withdrew the Maya which confuses the world and had also overpowered Narada.

With the removal of Siva’s Ṅaya, Narada reverted to his earlier self as a man of wisdom. With the regaining of the true wisdom, he felt extremely surprised and was freed from confusion.

He started repenting (for his behaviour) denouncing himself at the same time. Then he started praising the Maya of Siva, which confuses even the people possessing wisdom.

The sage then came to realise that his earlier performance had been due to the illusion. (Realising this) Narada, the foremost of Vaisnavas, then fell down over the feet of Visnu.

Then the lord Visnu, lifted up Narada, who having been relieved of the evil thoughts, spoke to Visnu thus, “I, the evil minded one, having been overpowered by Ṅaya, had spoken evil words to you.

Î Lord, whatever curse has been pronounced by me on you, you better falsify it. I have committed a grave sin, which would surely throw me in the hell.

Î Lord, I happen to be your slave. You kindly tell me the way out by which my sins are washed out and I could be saved from falling in the hell.”

Thus speaking the noble minded Narada, fell at the feet of Visnu with great devotion. He started repenting.

Then lord Visnu lifted up Narada, and spoke truthful words to him. Visnu said, “You are the best of my devotees, no doubt, Don’t feel painful at heart. Î Dear one, you listen, I am surely going to speak out something for your good. You will not have to go to the hell. Siva would surely bestow his grace on you.

You having been overpowered with arrogance, did not care for the command of Siva, he has therefore punished you in this way.

Whatever has happened is because of Siva’s will. You should surely understand it. Paramesvara, removes the arrogance of all.

He is supreme Brahman, the supreme soul, blissful and the supreme knowledge. He is absolute, without any blemish and is free from all the three gunas viz.: sattva, rajas and tamas.

With the use of his Ṅaya he takes to the three forms, of Brahma, Visnu and Siva. He is nirguna as well as saguna (formless and with form).

In his absolute form, he appears in the forms of Siva- the supreme soul, or Paramesvara, the Supreme Brahman, Mahesvara, the undecaying and the endless lord.

While serving he happens to be the sustainer of the world, besides being the creator. In the form of Rudra, he himself destroys the universe.

Beyond Maya he is the cosmic witness, absolute, the form of Siva, who wanders at will and indulges in divine sport. He bestows his grace on the devotees.

O Sage Narada, you listen to the best of the remedy which removes all the sins and bestows the pleasure and salvation.

Leaving aside all the doubts, you recite the best of the glory of Siva and his stotra of a hundred names.

With the reciting of which, all your sins would disappear atonce.” After thus speaking to Narada, feeling merciful, Visnu again said to Narada.

“O Sage, don’t feel painful of heart. You had done no harm. Whatever has been done, is at the will of lord Siva. There is no doubt about it.

Because of the passions which were aroused in you and the related arrogance, he had extracted your wisdom and then lord Siva got the curse pronounced on me from your mouth.

In this way lord Siva displayed his conduct in the world. He is the conqueror of the death, an the Kala of Kala, always engaged in the rescue of his own devotees.

There is no benefactor in the world for me, better than Siva himself or the master. The same Paramesvara bestows all types of strength for me.

Î Sage, you devote yourself to him besides adoring him. Listen to his fame, eulogise him and worship him daily.

The one who achieves the closeness of Siva with his body, mind and speech, he becomes the person with wisdom and enjoys all the pleasures during the life time and is called a liberated soul living on earth.

With forest fire in the name of Siva all the mountains in the form of sins get destroyed without much effort. There is no doubt above it.

There are several types of pains emanating from the sins, which get destroyed with the worship of Siva and not by any other means.

Î Sage, the one who seeks refuge in Siva is considered to be the real follower of the Vedas, or the supreme soul, a blessed learned person. You must adore him with your body, speech and mind forever.

There are different types of dharmas of those who worship Siva, (their devotion) yields quick results.

The number of the sins which are destroyed with the adoration of Siva, the same number of sins cannot be committed in the world.

O Sage, there are innumerable heaps of sins of the brahmahatya which all get destroyed with the mere mention of the name of Siva. This is the truth whatever has been spoken by me.

A person, who by getting the boat in the form of the name of Siva, tries to cross the ocean of the universe, all his worldly sins undoubtedly get destroyed.

Î Great sage, the worldly sins surely get destroyed with the axe in the form of the name of Siva.

The persons suffering with the sins in the form of forest fire, should consume the nectar like name of Siva, because such people can never be peaceful without consuming the same.

Those who are drenched with the stream of the rain of nectar in the form of the name of Siva are not distressed in the midst of the conflagration of the worldly existence. There is no doubt about it.

The persons who are drowned in the attractions and the jealousy, can never be the devotees of Siva, while those with the opposite performance, surely attain salvation.

The one who might have performed tapas in may births, only he develops the sense of devotions towards Siva.

The one who has a casual faith in Siva, would be of no consequence. Therefore one should be totally devoted to Siva.

The one who has exclusive and unflinching devotion for Siva, can achieve salvation quite easily and not otherwise.

After committing innumerable sins, in case one develops devotion at the feet of lord Siva, even then he is surely freed from all the sins. There is no doubt about it.

As in the wild fire the trees are reduced to ashes, similarly the sins of the devotees of Siva, are burnt out in the fire of the reciting of the name of Siva.

The one who purifies himself with the application of holy ashes on all the limbs and then adores Siva, he crosses the unending and the terrific ocean of the universe.

A person who steals the wealth of a Brahmana, and even after killing a Brahmana, he is devoted to Siva, he does not earn the relevant sin.

All the Rsis and great Rsis, after going through the Vedas, arrived at a conclusion that the adoration of Siva is the only remedy for freeing himself from the worldly bondages.

From today onwards, getting alert, with efforts and due observance of the rules of procedure, always adore great lord Sadasiva with Parvati with devotion.

After applying the holy ashes from the head to feet, one should recite the mantra "om namah Sivaya” which is well known in the world.

A devotee should wear Rudraksa, which is dear to Siva, over all the limbs, reciting the mantras.

Then listen to the story of Siva, himself and recite the same to others, adoring the devotees of Siva at the same time.

You should remain under the refuge of Siva quite carefully because by adoring Siva, on achieves the everlasting bliss.

One should installs the lotus like feet of lord Siva in his heart and should travel to the places holy for Siva.

Keeping in view the spotless glory of high- souled lord Siva, you should visit Anandavana (Kasi) which is dearest of Siva.

Offering your adoration to lord Visvesvara there, you should worship him with devotion, offer your salutation to him, offer prayer to him, you will be freed from all the doubts.

Î Sage, thereafter, you with my permission and for the fulfilment of your desire, should surely go to Brahmaloka.

Î Sage, you then offer your prayer and salutation to your father, and ask him again and again about the glory of Siva.

Brahma who is immensely devoted to Siva, will narrate to you the glory of Siva quite pleasantly besides narrating the satanamas stotra of Siva.

O Sage, from today onward, you become the devotee of Siva following the Saiva faith. Siva would bestow welfare on you and your would be entitled to achieve salvation.

Thus lord Visnu, getting pleased, delivered discourse to Narada and he himself remembering, saluting and adoring Siva, disappeared from the place.

## Chapter 5 - Narada’s visit to Kasi

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, at the disappearing of Visnu from the site, the sage Narada, with his mind filled with devotion kept on visiting the Sivalingas on earth.

Î Brahmanas, by thus wandering over the earth, he came across several Sivalingas lovingly, which bestowed pleasure and salvation to the devotees.

When the two Siva’s ganas came to know, that the sage Narada with his divine vision was so wandering on earth, they went to Narada having a peaceful mind.

Being desirous of getting relieved of the curse, both of then offered their salutation to him, with folded hands and falling over his feet.”

Siva’s attendants said, “O Sage- the son of Brahma, you kindly listen to our words quite lovingly. We are the Brahmanas, and we have actually not committed a crime against you.

Î Sage, Î Brahmana, in the Svayamvara of the princess, we jeered at you, when you had been confuse with the Maya of Siva.

Having been influenced with the Maya of Siva, you pronounced a curse on us. Since the time was not favourable for us, we kept quiet then.

We have reaped the reward of our actions and no one is therefore at fault. Now you be pleased with us and be compassionate on us.”

Suta said, “Listening to the respectful words of the attendants of Siva, the sage while repenting, lovingly said to Sivaganas.”

Narada said, “O Ganas of Siva- adorable by the noble people, you please listen tome. Presently my words are free from confusion, pleasant and realistic.

This is certain that I had acted earlier foolishly because of the will of Siva and my words were devoid of wisdom. Having been completely confused, an evil minded person like me had pronounced a curse on you.

On Siva-ganas, whatever had been spoken by me, has to happen and cannot be averted. Still I am going to speak out the remedy to escape from the curse. Both of you will please forgive me for my sin.

You would be born of the semen of a sage, would become demons, but still you would be quite glorious and famous.

Both of you would be the kings of the entire universe, devotees of Siva, and controlling all your senses, you would be the form of Siva. After your death you would achieve the place of Siva.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the sage Narada, both the attendants of Siva felt immensely pleased and retired to their respective abodes.

Narada on the other hand, feeling delighted, reciting the name of Siva with utmost devotion, visiting the places sacred to Siva, kept on wandering on earth.

The sage Narada had the best of all in the sphere of grace and he ultimately reached the city of Kasi which was the form of Siva, was comfortable and dear to Siva.

Finding the city of Kasi with the lord of Kasi, he felt successful and worshipped him with great love and pleasure.

Delightfully he stayed at Kasi and he felt contented. Becoming humble with his devotion, he extolled the virtues of the lord and remembered him with glory.

With the remembering of lord Siva, Narada achieved the noble wisdom, but he developed a desire to know deeply about the tattva of Siva and for that purpose he went to Brahmaloka.

Reaching there, he offered his salutation to Brahma appropriately. Then he eulogised him with the reciting of several stotra. Then feeling immensely devoted to Siva, Narada enquired about the reality of the tattva of Siva.

Narada said, “O Pitamaha (Grand sire) you are well aware of the form of Brahman, by your grace, I have learnt about the complete glory of lord Visnu and the path of his devotion, path of knowledge, difficult path of tapas, path of charities, besides the path of the sacred places.

Î Master, I remained ignorant about Siva- tattva. Besides I could not know about the method of his adoration, therefore you tell me all about them besides the episodes connected with his life.

Î Dear one, how could Siva who is absolute and free from attributes, become full of attributes? Having been overpowered with the illusion of Siva, I remained unaware of the tattva of Siva.

How did Siva remain in his original form before creation? How did he function in the middle of the creation?

How does he behave at the end of the universe? How does Siva, who is benevolent to all, get pleased.

Î Brahma, how does Siva reward his own as well as the devotees of other gods when pleased? You kindly speak out all the details to me.

We have heard that lord Siva gets pleased in no time and that the merciful Siva, cannot bear the pain of his devotees.

Brahma, Visnu and Siva- all the three have been born of the amsa of Siva. Out of then Mahesa is the complete form of Siva. Therefore Siva is the supreme tattva.

Î Master, you please tell me about the origin of Siva and Uma.

How were they married? You please tell me. You particularly tell me about their married life as a householder, besides other sports. Î Sinless one, you also narrate other stories connected with them as well.

You kindly enlighten me about the birth of Siva, then the birth of Uma, the marriage of both of them besides the story about the birth of Karttikeya.

O Lord of the Universe, though I have listened to the story from several other people, but I still am not fully satisfied. Therefore I have taken refuge with you. You kindly be compassionate on me.”

Thus listening to the words of Narada- his son, Brahma, the Pitamaha of the world, said.

## Chapter 6 - Mahapralaya and Visnu’s origin

Brahma said, “O Brahmana- best among the learned people, you have put me a very good question, because you are desirous of the welfare of the people. You have asked this question for the good of the people.

The story by listening to which, the sins of all the people would be washed out, the same beneficial Siva-tattva is being narrated by me.

Truly speaking, I am myself unaware of Siva-tattva, nor does anyone else know about it.

When at the time of dissolution the entire mobile and immobile world had been destroyed, and in the absence of the sun and the stars, there was darkness everywhere.

There were no moon, day, night, fire, wind, land, water, or anything else. Even the sky had been deprived of the lustre.

At that point of time, the word, touch etc. could no where to be found. The fragrance, form or beauty, had also vanished.

Thus, there was the continued darkness everywhere, which could not be pierced through with a needle. Then what is mentioned in the Vedas as existent and Brahman was only present.

Sat and asat nowhere could be found, which is visualised by the yogis always in their minds.

It is beyond the comprehension of mind and speech, it is beyond expression by words. It has no name or the colour. It is neither gross nor subtle.

It is neither brief nor vast, neither small not big. It neither expands nor does it squeeze.

Even the Vedas, getting surprised conceive it as the truth, knowledge, having the form beyond measure, blissful and eternal.

It is beyond measure, beyond change, formless, having no attributes, who is perceptible to the absolute yogis, all pervasive and the only cause of the universe.

It is without alternative, without beginning, free from illusion, it is without beginning, end or blemish, unparallel, and is the form of consciousness or the pure knowledge.

Its names go on changing. After a long time a desire developed in him to get him self multiplied. Or in other words he thought that he was one and he should be multiplied into many form.

The said being, having no form of his own, created an auspicious image, during the course of his own sport, possessing all the virtues and fortunes, besides the power, qualities and knowledge.

A form which could move everywhere, displays all the forms, could visualise everything, should be all powerful and respectable by all, should be the ancient most and which could make all the people civilized.

Then he created the auspicious image of Isvara, then the original being who was beyond comparison, eternal, beyond measure, form of consciousness, which illuminates everything, form of pure knowledge, all pervading, indestructible, and supreme Brahman, disappeared.

The manifest form of formless being is Sadasiva who is presently called by the people of wisdom as Isvara.

The lonely Isvara produced from his own body an everlasting Sakti. This Sakti did not effect his original body in any way.

The said Sakti is variously known as Pradhan-Prakrti, Ṅaya, Gunavati, Para. She happens to be the creator of the Buddhi-tattva (cosmic intelligence) and is unblemished.

The same Sakti is also called Ambika, Prakrti, besides being the mistress of the three worlds. She is the mother of the three gods. She is everlasting and the main cause of the creation.

She has eight arms, divine beauty and her face has the lustre of a thousand full-moons.

She has been adorned with various ornaments and holds several attributes and weapons. Her eyes resemble the blossoming lotus flowers.

She possesses the lustre beyond comprehension and creates all the movable and immovable creatures of the world. She is the lonely Ṅaya, who takes to many forms.

Thereafter the said Parama-Purusa Siva also known as Isvara, having no other lord over him, who holds the Ganga over his head. He has three eyes and a crescent moon on his forehead.

Siva is five faced, a pleasant soul, holder of a trident, having complexion as white as the camphor, keeps on applying holy ashes over the body.

The same Parabrahman, in the form of Kala, in company of that Sakti, collectively built the Sivaloka.

The best of that place is known as Kasi. The place bestows salvation, therefore it is considered as superior to all.

The holy place is considered to be the place of supreme bliss, because the primordial lovers who were extremely blissful, made that lace as their permanent abode.

The city of Kasi is called an Avimuktaksetra, the holy place because Parvati and Siva can never be separated from each other even at the time of dissolution.

In the ancient times, Pinaka-bearing Siva had initially given the name of Anandavana (Blissful forest) to this place and subsequently it was known as Avimuktaksetra due to the cause of bliss.

Î Narada, the rsi of the gods, both Siva and Parvati, while roaming in the Anandavana, developed a desire for the creation of another being, entrusting on whom, the entire responsibility, they could move freely in the city of Kasi, embracing vairagya (detachment).

Let him perform all the functions always create everything and ultimately at my bidding he should dissolve the entire universe.

Shaking with the waves of anxiety, in the ocean of anxiety, expanding with the tree of rajoguna, then achieving the games in the form of sattvaguna which consumes tamoguna, we might be able to carryout all our outer worries and live comfortably thereafter.

Thus thinking, with the consent of Siva, the supreme lord, then poured in the tenth limb, the fluid of nectar.

Then a person, who was the most beautiful in the three worlds appeared, who was peaceful possessing sattvaguna and resembled the ocean of immeasurable majesty.

Î Sage, he was endowed with patience, and had the lustre of sapphire. He was beyond comparison. His eyes resembled the lotus flowers.

He had the complexion of gold and two scarfs were used as upper garment. He had two invincible arms.

The said Purusa then offered his salutation at the feet of Siva and said, “O Master, give me a name, and also define my duties.”

On hearing his words, Lord Siva with smile spoke to the said Purusa the words thundering like the clouds.

Siva said, “Because of your being of all pervading nature, you would be known as Visnu. Besides this you would be known by several other names, which would please your devotees.

You better perform tapas conducive to the achievements of the assigned task. Thus speaking, he produced the Vedas through his breathing (and because of this, it is said Yasya nisvasitam vidah.)

Thereafter lord Visnu, offering his salutation to Siva, performed great penance. Paramesvara, disappeared and proceeded to his place with his Sakti.

Lord Visnu then performed tapas for twelve thousand divine years, but he could not have an audience with Siva, who bestows everything.

Then feeling doubtful in his mind, he kept on reciting the name of Siva mentally, became anxious, about the future course of action.

At the same time he heard the words spoken by Siva, which said, “In order to relieve your mind of the doubt you perform tapas again.”

On hearing these words, Visnu again performed tapas. After a long time, he could learn about Brahman, by the path of meditation.

Then Purusottama Visnu, woke up by the path of meditation and felt surprised delightfully and said, “Is it the same tattva ?

With the influence of the Maya of Siva, several streams of water emerged from the body of Siva.

Î Great sage, all the streams of water merged into the sunya and the water was turned into the form of Brahman, the very touch of which destroys all the sins.

Then lord Visnu, getting fatigued and feeling, confused, kept on sleeping in the water.

At that point of time he was known as Narayana, which was authenticated by the Vedas. At that stage, there was nothing except Purusa and Prakrti.

Î Immensely intelligent one, Î great Intellectual, at that stage several tattvas appeared, from the great Purusa, the forms of which are being told by me, you kindly listen to the same.

From Prakrti, came into being the Mahat (the cosmic intellect) from Mahat emerged the three gunas. Then the cosmic ego arose there from according to the three gunas.

The subtle form of the nether, the five mahabhutas (elements) emerged from them. From there appeared the organs of knowledge and action.

Î Best of the sages, I have counted the tattvas before you. All these principles originating from Prakrti, are insentient but not the Purusa.

The number of all the tattvas combined is twenty four. Visnu- the Purusa accepted all the tattvas and went to sleep at the will of Siva in water as Brahman.

## Chapter 7 - The dispute between Brahma and Visnu

Brahma said, “After Lord Visnu went to sleep a huge lotus flower emerged from his navel.

The lotus had an endless stalk. Its pericarp was full of lustre. It was many yojanas vast and similar was its height.

It had the brilliance of crores of suns, possessing the beautiful tattvas, it was quite surprising and charming besides being attractive.

Siva the great lord with Parvati as his better half, had produced me from his right limb.

Î Sage, “Mahesa over-shadowed me with his illusion immediately, and in the course of his sport, produced me from the umbilical lotus of Visnu.

O Narada, thus I being Hiranyagarbha was produced from that lotus, with four mouths, with red complexion with my foreheads adorned with tripundra.

Having been influenced with the illusion of Siva I could recognise none else except the lotus. Î Dear one, being ignorant I could hardly recognise the person who produced me.

I could not know about my creator, myself, the place from where I had arrived, what were my functions, and about my father, besides, the person who had produced me. I could know nothing about all these facts.

Then having been in doubt, I could realise that I had been ignorant. “It is easy to gain the knowledge.

The place of growth of this lotus would be below, which must have given birth to me. There is no doubt about it.”

Thus thinking, I descended below holding the lotus stalk, and for doing so it took me hundreds of years.

Still I could not know the place of the origin of the lotus. Then becoming doubtful, I again tried to reach the same lotus flower.

Î Sage, when I was about to move up holding the lotus stalk but I failed to locate the blossomed lotus flower, which upset me.

Then by moving up as well downwards, a hundred years passed. Then getting upset, I stopped for a moment.

At that point of time, with the will of Siva, I heard a divine voice which said, “You perform tapas”

Listening to the divine voice, I performed tapas for twelve years in order to know about my father.

Then four armed lord Visnu, having beautiful eyes, showering his grace and appeared before me.

He was holding a conch, a wheel, a club and a lotus as attributes in his four hands. His limbs had the cloud complexion, and was clad in a yellow lower garment.

He was adorned with a crown over the head and several other ornaments over the body. I having been confused, looked at lord Visnu who had a smiling face.

On seeing the beautiful complexion, I was struck with great surprise. He was in four¬armed, shining like Kala, of golden hue, and soul of all creatures.

Looking at the four-armed Narayana, depicting sata and asata in himself I felt delighted.

Having been overpowered with the illusion of Siva and failing to recognise my own father, I spoke to him quite delightfully.

Brahma said, “Who are you?" please tell me. Thus speaking, I lifted up the Sanatanapurusa, with my hands, forcefully.

The lotus eyed lord who was fast asleep, woke up, having lotus like eyes, and had enormous self-control. He found Brahma there.

When lord Hari looked at me illumining with his lustre, seated before him, then he smilingly spoke the sweet words.”

Lord Visnu said, “Welcome, welcome to you dear son, you are Pitamaha of great brilliance, Don’t be afraid, I shall surely bestow on you whatever is desired by you.

You are the foremost among the gods.” On hearing these words spoken by Visnu with smile, I feeling inimical to Visnu said to him.”

Brahma said, “O Sinless one, I happen to be the cause of the destruction of all, you address me as the child as a preceptor addresses a disciple.

I am the creator of the universe, I activate Prakrti, unborn, eternal, all pervading Brahma and am born of Visnu.

I happen to be the soul of the universe, the destiny or the providence, therefore, Î Lotus eyed one, how do you call me a child.

The Vedas describe me as self born, without birth, all-pervading, grand-sire, self- governed, and the excellent supreme being.”

Listening to the words spoken by me lord Visnu, the lord of Rama, felt enraged and said, “I am aware of the worlds having been created by you.”

Visnu said, “For the sake of the creation, you have emerged from everlasting limb. Have you forgotten me as lord of the universe, also known as Narayana and Jagannatha.

The one who is adored by the supreme soul, Indra and other gods, the one who is known by the name of Visnu, Acyuta and Isana; and who creates and preserve the universe, the one who is Narayana, Mahabahu (Long-armed) and all pervading Isvara, I happen to be the same, from whose navel a lotus emerged with you. There is no doubt about it.

You are not at all at fault in this. You have been overpowered with my illusion. Î Brahma, listen, I happen to be the lord of all the gods.

There is none comparable with me as the creator of the universe, its preserver and the destroyer of the same. Î Brahma, I happen to be the Supreme Brahman as well as the supreme tattva.

I am the supreme light, the supreme soul, I am omnipresent and all pervading, besides whatever mobile or immobile is found in the world presently.

Î Brahma, all this is enveloped in me. I had in earlier times created this universe with twenty four tattvas.

It is connected with the eternal atoms. The anger and fear have emerged out of the same. You have been born because of my prowess and all the limbs have been produced because of my sport.

I have created wisdom in the same as a result of which three types of pride has been created. I have evolved the five subtle elements, besides the mind, the body and the sense-organs.

I have created the panca-mahabhutas (five other elements) and all the material padarthas of the world. Therefore, Î Brahma, Î Lord of the people, you better take refuge in me.

I shall protect you from all the troubles. There is no doubt about it.” Brahma said, “On hearing these words, I being proud of becoming Brahma, became angry. Having been overpowered with the illusion, I shouted at him saying “who are you?”

Why are you speaking uselessly? Your are not at all the lord nor the Supreme Brahman. There must be some one else who created you.

Overpowered by the Maya of Siva, the supreme lord, I fought a terrific battle with Visnu.

Influenced with rajoguna we became inimical to each other, and fought a fierce battle in the middle of the vast ocean of the time of dissolution.

In the mean time in order to remove the controversy between us and in order to educate us both, a linga appeared between us.

It was beyond the beginning, middle or end and had thousands of flames resembling the fire of the time of dissolution.

It was - without comparison, beyond expression, unmanifest universal being. Lord Visnu, at the sight of its thousand flames became unconscious.

When I too lost my senses, then Brahma said, “What for were you praising yourself? What is this third element before us? Let us stop quarrelling.

Let us examine the fire which has suddenly emerged between us? How has it arisen? I shall go down below this pillar.

O Lord of the people, with the speed of wind, you better fly upwards in order to examine its top.

Brahma said, “O Sage, thus speaking, Visnu, the soul of the universe, took to the form of a boar and I myself took to the form of a swan.

From that day onwards, I was called by the name of Hamsa-virat, all illustrious being. Therefore the one who recites the name of Hamsa, shall become the symbol of purity.

I became a vast bird Swan of extremely white complexion, with two wings on either side. Then I flew upwards with the speed of wind and mind.

Narayana, the soul of the universe also became white complexioned boar of gigantic size of a hundred yojanas.

He had the gigantic body resembling the Sumeru mountain, possessing the lustre of the time of dissolution and white fangs, long nostrils, creating the terrific sound.

He had small hoofs and surprising limbs. He took to the form of a charming boar and went downwards with great speed.

Going downwards, Visnu, kept on wandering for a thousand years. From that time onwards, Sveta-Varaha-Kalpa was started.

Î Sage of the gods, this Sveta-Varaha, became useful in the counting of the human times. The all powerful Visnu, kept on wandering in the nether world for long.

Visnu in the form of Varaha, could not find even the slightest end of the linga. Î Destroyer of the enemies, for the same period, I also kept on wandering above.

I tired my best by all the means to find out the top of the linga but could not succeed. Therefore, I also went back.

Similarly the lotus eyed lord Visnu too feeling tired, inspite of his having the gigantic body which could accommodate all the gods, came back from the nether world at the same time, as I did from the sky.

He arrived with me and offering salutation to Siva again and again, getting influenced with his Ṅaya stood there with an upset mind.

Visnu together with me started offering salutation to Sivalinga from back side, front, and both the sides. Then we started thinking. “What can this be?”

This form cannot be expressed clearly. It is without action and name. It is without any sex destination but still appears as a linga and is beyond the path of meditation.

Both myself and Hari controlling our minds started offering our salutations to the linga.

They said, “We are not at all aware of your true form, Î Great lord, salutation to you. Please reveal your true form quickly to us.

Î Best of the sages, both of us having been infested with pride, continued offering salutation to the linga for hundreds of years.

## Chapter 9 - Siva-tattva highlighted

Brahma said, “Siva on hearing his praise from Visnu, felt delighted with his Sakti.

He was five faced, three eyed, with his head adorned with the crescent moon, wearing matted locks of hair over the head, white complexion, vast eyes and had applied the holy ashes over the body.

He had ten arms, blue throat, adorned with all the ornaments, over all the beautiful limbs of the body, having applied tripundra over the forehead.

Thus looking at Siva with his Sakti, lord Visnu again eulogised him in a charming fashion.

Thereafter the compassionate lord, gave to lord Visnu all the four Vedas from his breath.

Thereafter he bestowed the divine knowledge to Visnu, which, Î Sage, was passed on by Visnu to me gracefully.

After receiving the knowledge of Vedas from Siva, lord Visnu felt extremely beholden, and with both his hands folded, he enquired from Mahesvara, offering his salutation to him.

Lord Visnu said, “O Lord, how do you get pleased? How could I adore your? How should you be meditated upon? How are you impressed by anyone?

O Mahadeva, what should we do at your command? Î Siva, you kindly issue your command to be followed by us in future for our pleasure.

Î Lord, taking us to be your slaves, you tell us whatever is further required to be told to us.”

Brahma said, “The compassionate lord Siva, getting pleased, said, “I have been immensely pleased with your devotion. Facing Mahadeva, don’t be afraid in any way.

You should always adore my linga and the way you have meditated upon me presently, you should do so in future as well.

In case, I am adored in the form of a linga than I bestow all types of rewards to the people as per their desire.

Î Best of the gods, whenever you face any type of misery, then by adoring my linga all the miseries vanish atonce.

I create, maintain and destroy with the three gunas, sattva, rajas and tamas. Lord Siva has three different gunas (i.e. sattva, rajas and tamas) and is beyond Prakrti and Purusa.

A day of Brahma comprises of four thousand yugas. The period of night is also similar.

Till such time Sadasiva breathes and when he exhales the breath, it merges into Sakti.

Î Best of the gods, twenty one thousand six hundred respirations constitute the period of a day and night.

A pala comprises of six respirations. Sixty such palas constitute one ghati. Sixty ghatis constitute a day and a night (6 x 60 x 60 = 21,600). There is no limit to the number of respiration of Sadasiva and as such he is undecaying.

Therefore at my command, you should protect this form and should engage yourself for the preservation of the universe .”

## Chapter 11 - Method of worshipping Siva

The Rsis said, “O Disciple of Vyasa, Î Suta salutation to you. You have narrated the wonderful and auspicious story of Siva today in which we have learnt about the immensely surprising and divine origin of the linga, with the influence of which, all the miseries in the world disappear.

Î Ocean of mercy, following the conversation between Brahma and Narada, now speak out the mode of the worship of Siva, which pleases the lord.

Listening to the beneficial words based on the Vedas, Suta lovingly started to answer his questions.

Suta said, “O Sages, you have asked me a very good question, I am going to reveal its secret as has been learnt by me, based on my own wisdom.

The way you have asked me today, similarly, the same question had been asked by Sanatkumara, and Upamanyu had learnt from him.

Vyasa learnt it from Upamanyu. The sage Vyasa, taught me the same mode of adoration of Siva, for the benefit of the people.

The similar details were heard from the sage Upamanyu by Krsna, which I am going to repeat to you, as had been spoken by Brahma earlier.”

Brahma said, “O Narada, you listen to me, I shall briefly speak out the method for the adoration of linga. Î Sage, it cannot be narrated in a hundred years extensively.

In this way the form of Siva bestows comforts, who is spotless and eternal. The adoration of same should be done with devotion.

The pains emanating from poverty, ailments, danger from the enemy and all the four types of sins, trouble a person till such time he does not adore Siva.

All types of pains and miseries vanish after the worship of Siva and a person is endowed with all types of comforts in the world and ultimately he achieves salvation at the end.

A person, who after attaining the human life intends to get progeny, he should adore Mahadeva, who bestows all the comforts.

The Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras, should adore Siva appropriately and by doing so all the desires are fulfilled.

One should get up early in the morning at the Brahma-muhurta, remember the preceptor and then recite the name of Siva again and again.

O Sage, remembering the holy places as well as Hari, Brahma and other gods and sages.

Thereafter the Siva-namastotra should be recited. Thereafter he should go to the south and relieve himself of the bowels.

The bowels should be evacuated in a lonely place. Î Sage, I am going to speak out the method for the same, which you should listen attentively.

A Brahmana should use earth five times for the purpose of cleaning. A Ksatriya should do so four times and a Vaisya should do so thrice.

A Sudra should use the earth twice for the purpose of cleaning, or he should clean the rectum twice and the linga once.

The earth should be applied ten times with the left hand and seven times with both the hands. Î Dear one, a person shall wash the feet seven times and both the hands thrice.

The women should apply the earth in the method prescribed for the Sudras. They shall first wash the hands and the feet and then make use of the earth as before. One should use the twig as per his caste.

The Brahmana should use the twig as brush, which is twelve angulas (fingers) in length. A Ksatriya should have it eleven angulas in length, the Vaisya should use ten angulas in length.

While the size of the twig for Sudra has been prescribed to be of nine angulas. This is in accordance with the smrtis. Taking into consideration the time, the defective twig should be discarded.

The brushing of the teeth, should not be done, on the sixth moon day, moonless day, ninth day of the moon, the day of Vrata, after sunset, on Sunday, and the day of performing Sraddha for the manes.

One should take bath at sacred places, reciting the mantras, keeping in view the time and the place.

Wearing a dhoti, one should sip water at a good and lonely place, and then perform the Sandhya-vandana.

The worship should be performed entering the place of worship concentrating the mind, appropriately.

Sitting over a proper seat and performing the nyasa etc. according to the prescribed mode of worship, one should worship Siva.

Ganesa and other ganas, the Lokapalas should be worshipped and thereafter the pedestals should be arranged.

Or otherwise, one should get himself seated close to the material for worship and making the eight petalled lotus, lord Siva should be consecrated over the same.

Then he should thrice sip the water and after washing the hands should perform pranayama, concentrating his mind on Siva having five faces, ten arms, having the form resembling the spotless crystal gem, adorned with all the ornaments, using the scarf of the tiger skin, conceiving him in the same form, a person is relieved of all the sins. Then lord Siva should be adored raising him up from the pedestal.

Then purifying the body, one should recite the mula-mantra appropriately. The nyasa of the mula-mantra should be performed with holy water, and that of the six angas with Pranava (omkara).

After ritualistically touching the heart, the worship should be started. Different vases should be used for the purpose of padya, arghya and acamana.

A person with wisdom should consecrate nine pitchers of different sizes and covering them with durva grass, sprinkle water over them, and then pour the cool water in them. Sprinkling water over them, the person with wisdom should pour the dravyas in then reciting the omkara mantra.

The fragrant usira plant and the sandal paste should be poured in them, together with nutmeg, gourd, camphor, roots of the banyan tree, and tamalaka should be put in the water to be used for sipping purpose.

Nandisvara should be adored at the back of Siva. Siva should be worshipped offering fragrance, unbroken rice, incense, lamp and other dravyas.

Then a person with a delightful mind should sanctify the linga starting with omkara mantra adding namah at the end.

The linga shall be purified and installed reciting the various mantras beginning with Pranava, and ending with namah. The pedestal should be in the form of Svastika or lotus shall be assigned with Pranava. In the eight petals in eight quarters, the eight achievements are identified viz.: the eastern is Anima (minuteness), the southern is laghima (lightness), the western is mahima (greatness) the northern is Prapti (power of reaching), the south-eastern is Prakamya (sufficiency), the south-western is Isatva (becoming a lord), north-western is vasitva (power of control) and pericarp is the moon.

The sun is beneath the moon and under the same is the fire and under them one should conceive of dharma etc.

Avyakta etc. should be in all the four quarters. In the end of moon, the three gunas should be lodged. Reciting the mantras Sadyojatan praviksami Paramesvara should be involved.

Reciting the mantra Vamadevaya one should be seated over the asana. Then reciting the Rudra-Gayatri, sannidya rite shall be performed and the rite of nirodha shall be performed with Aghora-mantra.

Then adoration should be done reciting the mantra, Isanah Sarvavidyanam, offering padya, arghya and acamana.

The sandal paste, fragrance, unbroken rice should be offered, consecrating Rudra. Carrying pancagavya in a vase and they should be sanctified with mantras.

The deity should be bathed with the milk of the cow, reciting omkara mantra, offering curd honey and sugar cane juice.

Rudra should be bathed with ghee and by doing so all the sins are washed out. One should bathe Siva with these dravyas reciting îmkara mantra.

A devotee should collect this water and straining it with white cloth, and put it in the sacred vases.

The sprinkling of this holy water should not be done, till the sandal paste is put on it. Thereafter, one should adore Siva offering the unbroken rice over him.

Some rare flowers like those of kusa, apamarga (medicinal plant), camphor, jasmine, campa, trumpet flowers, white oleander jasmines and lotus, and several other types of flowers, should be offered to lord Siva, with sandal paste and stream of water, adoring him at the same time.

Filling water in various types of vases, Siva should be bathed. All types of worship should be done reciting the mantras. Only then the adoration is well-rewarding.

O Dear one, I shall speak out the mantras bestowing all types of success in brief. You listen to me attentively.

These include, the mantras which are taught, the mantras which are remembered by heart, mantras from Rudra-sukta, Nilasukta, and the mantras from the sukla-yajurveda.

Hotaram mantra from Yajurveda mantras from Atharvasirsa, santi-mantra, Aruni- mantra and the mantras from Aruna.

The desired Rama-mantra, besides the Devavrata-mantra using Puspa-sukta and Rathantara-mantras, then by reciting the Mrtunjaya mantra, Pancaksara-mantra, pouring a thousand streams of water or by a hundred and eight streams of water, according to the provision of the Vedas should be done, with the reciting of the namah-mantras of Siva.

Thereafter water should be poured over Siva. Then reciting the omkara-mantra the betel should be offered.

Then Siva-tattva has been conceived and worshipped, which is like the spotless crystal, the unsullied, undecaying, the cause of all the world, the supreme lord, identified with the created world, the lord who is beyond the comprehension of Brahma, Indra, Upendra, Visnu and other gods, the lord who is mentioned in the Vedanta, by those who are well-versed in the Vedas, as incomprehensible, the lord without the beginning, middle or the end, the medicine of all the ailments, this Siva-tattva is enshrined in Siva-linga.

Reciting the îḍkarṁ mantra one should offer incense, lamp, naivedya, good betel leaves, and adore Siva. Then arati should be offered waving the lights before linga, then the salutation should be offered, reciting the stotras and several types of mantras.

Then offering arghya, the flowers should be placed at the feet, bowing in reverence at the same time and adore lord Siva, by heart.

Carrying flowers one should fold his hands. Then getting up from his seat, the devotee should offer prayer to Isana Siva.

“I, Î Lord Siva, whatever adoration has been performed by me knowingly or unknowingly, let it be successful by your grace.”

Thus reciting the above mantra one should offer the said flowers delightfully over Siva. Than reciting Svastivacana he should receive blessings from the Brahmanas.

Then he should sprinkle water over Siva, offering salutation and should seek forgiveness for his sins. Thereafter, acamana (sipping) should be offered to Siva.

Reciting the Aghora-mantra salutation should be offered and then one should bow in reverence to Siva, offering prayer from mind and body.

“Let me remain devoted at the feet of Siva in all my births. There is no one else to help me, you are my only refuge.”

In this way he should offer prayer to the lord who bestows all the success, and adore him with utmost devotion, uttering the sound of a he goat.

Íṛ should then offer salutation to lord Siva, with all the family members and feeling delighted, he should engage himself in other works.

If a person devoted to Siva, adores the lord in such a way, he achieves success at every step.

He becomes a great speaker, gets all the desired padarthas. All his ailments, miseries, grief, uneasiness, falsehood, wickedness, poisoning and everything distressing are destroyed by the grace of Siva quickly.

He always meets with welfare. He grows daily like the crescent moon of the bright fortnight. Because of the adoration of Siva, all his merits keep on growing.

Î Sage Narada, in this way, I have spoken out the method of the adoration of Siva. Now what else do you intend to know further.

Brahma said, “O Gods and sages, you listen from me with a devoted heart, the mode of the worship of Siva lovingly, which bestows the pleasure and devotion.

The human life is most difficult to achieve among all the living beings in the world. Î Gods, Î Sages, it is still difficult to be born in a high race.

One behaving well with a noble Brahmana, because of the merits accumulated by a person earlier, one should engage himself to please Siva.

Whatever method has been prescribed for a particular caste or a varna, it should not be neglected. One should give away charities according to his means.

Î Brahma, the persons with wisdom become aware of the Parama-Siva-tattva they don’t have to bother for the pleasure and the pain, virtue or evil, sacrifice or japam, meditation or the related rules. By virtue of their learnings they are free from these passions, physical changes and the decay.

Î Gods, this Siva-linga bestows the highest bliss, and welfare, auspicious, eternal, all-pervasive and unsullied and is lodged in the hearts of the yogis.

Î Brahmanas, linga is of two types i.e. interior and exterior. The exterior is gross and the interior a subtle.

Those who are engaged in karma-yajnas they adore the gross linga. Those who are unaware of the subtle linga, the gross- linga has to be used for making them understand the reality or the factual position.

The one who is unable to visualise the spiritual or the subtle linga, he should meditate initial upon the gross linga.

The people having the spotless heart, can visualise the subtle linga by means of their true knowledge, but those who do not possess the same, the worship or the gross linga is quite important for them.

It is surprising that according to the opinion of the people following other tattvas, there is no difference, because he lives in the hearts of all in invisible form, and the entire universe is the form of Siva.

In this way the ignorant people earn no blemish and for them no method (for adoration) has been prescribed nor is anything prohibited for them.

As the lotus flower growing in the water is not soaked with water, similarly the people with wisdom, even after living in the house¬hold always remains free from the bondage of the karmas.

Till such time this type of knowledge does not sprout in the heart of a person, he should continue to worship Mahadeva.

A single sun, in order to convince the world, appears in several ways in pitchers filled with water.

Similarly, whatever Sata and asat is found in the world, Î Gods, should be taken as the form of Siva.

There is difference in the vases, but not in water they contain. This is what has been conceived by those who can well interpret the Vedas.

Lord Siva, remains in the hearts of all living beings on earth, therefore for those possessing the true knowledge, the images are of no consequence.

Therefore, the one who is deprived of the true knowledge, he should continue to adore the images. The image worship is the best source for reaching the highest stage of worship.

It is difficult to reach the highest place without a support. The image is a source to achieve the Nirguna Siva.

It is a fact that Nirguna tattva could be achieved by worshipping Saguna Siva. This belief is further authenticated by worshipping the images of the other gods.

Siva is the greatest of all the gods and for adoring him, the fragrance sandal paste, flowers etc. are used, which are of no use without the image.

The adoration of the images should be continued till the achievement of the true knowledge. The one who stops worshipping the images without attaining the true knowledge, he is sure to fall.

Î Brahmanas, therefore you listen to my realistic words, the karmas (activities) which have been prescribed in the sastras for a particular caste should be performed making all the efforts.

The type of adoration prescribed at different stages, the same should be followed accordingly. One surely earns the sin without worshipping or giving away the charities.

Till such time the accumulation of the sins continues in the body, the success could hardly be achieved. With the destruction of all the sins, he succeeds in his life.

In case the cloth is dirty, it cannot be dyed well. In case the cloth is washed before dying it, its colour becomes bright.

Similarly by adoring the gods quite well, the spotless body when dyed with the colour of knowledge, then the true knowledge would arise.

The true knowledge bestows the pious devotion. True knowledge is said to be the real root of devotion.

Noble deeds are the roots of devotion. The noble deeds and to adore the presiding deity is the main cause of the same. The root cause of the same is the noble preceptor, and the root of the same is keeping company of the people with wisdom.

The company of the learned people leads to the achieving of the preceptor. With the mantras achieved from the preceptor, the god is adored, and the said adoration leads to achieving of the true knowledge.

The true knowledge, leads to the perfect knowledge, which in turn leads, to the realisation of the Supreme Brahman. With the perfect knowledge, the controversies cease to exist.

When a person is relieved of the controversies, and miseries, he takes the form of Siva himself.

Î Divine Rsis, after the disappearing of the differences, the misery of the mutually clashing of the opposites, a person with wisdom is freed from any type of the pleasure and the pain. The rules of do’s and don’t do not bind him.

One seldom comes across a person who has not entered a household and in case there is one, all the sins would stand washed out at the mere sight of such a person.

The holy places also praise such a person possessing the true knowledge, as the rsis praise Siva the form of the Supreme Brahman.

Even the holy places, or the images made in clay or stone cannot equate him, which purify a person after a long time, but a person with true knowledge purifies with his sheer vision.

Till such time a person remains in the household, he should continue worshipping the images of five gods, or otherwise one should adore only Siva, who happens to be the root of all, because when the root is watered, all the branches are well taken care of.

Î Best of the sages, in case the branches are watered, it could not mean that the root is also taken care of. Î Ascetics, even when all the god are adored, it does not mean that Siva also stands adored with the same.

Siva cannot be pleased in this way, which should be understood by the people with sharp wisdom, that by adoring Siva, all the gods stand adored.

Therefore a person who is desirous of doing good to all living beings, shall worship Siva, the benefactor of the world, for the fulfilment of all the desires.

## Chapter 13 - Mode of the adoration of Siva

Brahma said, “O Sages, Î Devas, you listen to me. I shall now explain the mode of worship, which bestows the fulfilment of all the desires and the comforts.

One should rise in the early morning an hour before the dawn and remember Siva and Parvati both, lowering one’s head offering prayers at the same time.

“O Lord of the Devas, Î Lord lodged in the heart, Î Lord of Parvati, you just rise up and bestow benevolence over the universe.

But mind does not attract to that side. I am aware of the fact that this is sinful, but still I do not feel inclined to work it up. Î Lord, in whichever way you inspire me seated in my heart, I perform accordingly.”

In this way, reciting the name of the lord with devotion, one should devote his mind at the sandals of the preceptor, then he should move out of the house, towards the southern direction to answer the calls of the nature.

Thereafter purifying the body with the dust and water, washing his feet brush his teeth.

One should brush his teeth before the sun¬rise and then rinse his mouth, purifying the same, sixteen times.

Î Gods and Î Rsis, one should not brush his teeth on the sixth, ninth and moonless day of the fortnights, besides on the Sundays.

As per one’s convenience, the bath should be taken in the river, and tanks etc. No one should take bath against the time country or the traditions.

One should take a bath on Sunday, first of the month, on the Solar or Lunar eclipse, at the time of the performing of the charities, or on the day of the performing of the vrata, one should take bath facing the east with devotion. During the time of impurity one should not bathe in hot water.

One should apply oil over the body taking into consideration the particulars days. Those who apply the oil daily over their body daily should use the oil, because for them it is not prohibited.

Except the day of the eclipse, the mustard oil can be applied over the body.

Taking into consideration the time and the country, one should take bath facing north or the east appropriately.

A devotee of Siva should never take a bath using the clothes of others. Reciting the name of Siva, he should take bath wearing the pure costumes.

In case another man’s costumes are worn during the night, the same could not be taken as impure. One can take bath with them and then discard them.

The water libation should be performed for the gods, rsis and the manes, after the bath, for their pleasure. Thereafter sipping the water he should wear the pure and washed dhoti or lower garment.

Thereafter, Î Brahmanas, one should go to a place plastered with cow-dung and auspicious asana should be spread over it.

The seat should be made of wood or a cloth-cover. The variegated seat fulfils all the desires.

O Brahmanas, one should select the asana of deer skin, as might be considered appropriate by him. Seating over that asana an intelligent devotee should draw tripundra over his body.

With the marking of tripundra the japam, tapas and charities performed by a person are quite successful. In the absence of the holy ashes, one should draw tripundra with water.

In this way, after drawing the tripundra over the body, one should wear Rudraksa. After the daily rites are over, the worship of lord Siva should be started.

The performing acamana by sipping of water thrice, reciting the appropriate mantras, or saying that it was the drop of the water of Ganga, one should perform acamana.

Then a devotee should bring food and water for the adoration of Siva, besides other things which could be easily available.

Collecting all these things, one should be seated with patience. Then he should keep water vase pouring the water, fragrance and unbroken rice in it and keep it to his right for the purpose of worship. Then remembering his own preceptor, he should get his permission.

With the offering of a samkalpa appropriately, adding his desire with the same, one should adore Siva with devotion appropriately.

Then displaying Siva-mudra, offering vermilion and other things, Ganesa should be adored with Siddhi and Buddhi, his consorts.

Keeping in his mind a desire to have an audience with Siva, he should recite the mantra om namah Sivaya and several other names.

Then he should pray forgiveness, and then adore Ganesa with brother Karttikeya, offering his salutation to them again and again.

The gatekeeper Mahodara, who always guards the gate, should be adored, after which the chaste Parvati should be adored.

Sandal paste, saffron, incense,lamp, naivedya, should be offered to Siva.

Then offering his salutation, he should go to Siva. In case there be the Sivalinga of earth, gold, silver or of any other metal, then the same should be adored with devotion.

After the adoration of Sivalinga, all the gods are adored (or otherwise) one should consecrate the linga in clay appropriately.

Remaining in one’s own house, all the rule should be observed, then warding off the spirits and goblins, the image should be consecrated.

A dikpala (god of the quarters) should be adored after consecrating his image. Only Siva should be adored in the house-hold reciting the basic mantra.

As per rules the Dvarapala has not to be consecrated in the house. The Sivalinga which is adored in the house everything is lodged in the same.

At the time of adoration one should invoke Siva with his family and adore the same. There are no rules prescribed for the purpose.

One should be seated before Siva, facing north. The sipping of the water should be done thereafter.

Then salutation should be done washing the hands. Reciting the mulamantra, the ðranayaḍṁ should be performed ten times.

Then he should display five mudras and by doing this the adoration is done by hands.

Thereafter the lamp should be shown. Then the homage is to be paid to the preceptor who should be seated in the yogic postures like, padmasana, Bhadrasana, uttana or paryanka, whichever is convenient should be used for sitting and one should perform all the rites once again. After the worship, he shall float it along with the cake. These rules are not binding when the worship is done in a house.

Thereafter Sivalinga should be washed with the water of arghya then the material for the adoration should be collected carefully.

The god of gods should then be invoked, reciting the mantra and lord Siva is to be lodged over the peak of the mountain Kailasa, with the spouse of Parvati, the excellent one.
