He has the same form as explained earlier, who is Nirguna as well Saguna-Siva, having five faces, ten arms, three eyes, banner of the bull.

He has white complexion like the camphor. His limbs are divine, has the crescent moon over the head, wearing the matted locks of hair over the head, uses the tiger skin as the scarf.

Vasuki and other serpents are coiled over the limbs of his body. He holds the bow Pinaka and other attributes, the eight siddhis dance before him.

The crowds of devotees shout the slogans of victory, who is possessing the sharp lustre and served by the gods, crying loudly for his victory. He is of unbearable sight due to the excessive splendour.

He is the one, who protects all the jivas, has a smiling face, praised by the Vedas as well the sastras, besides Brahma and Visnu.

I invoke lord Siva, who is so blissful and to whom the devotees are quite deer. Thus meditating upon Samba Siva, he should offer him a seat.

The entire worship of Siva should be done with the names ending in the dative case. Then padya and arghya should be offered to Siva.

Then Siva the Supreme Soul, should be offered acaman, a devotee should bathe him, with each one of the components of pancamrta.

Thereafter the offering shall be made with utmost devotion, reciting the requisite Vedic mantras or the names ending in dative case.

Siva should be offered all the desired things and thereafter he should be bathed with water.

Making all the efforts, the fragrance, sandal paste and kasturi shall be applied to Siva. The water poured over the deity in a continuous current, shall be rendered fragrant.

The water ablution shall be made reciting the Vedic hymns or the six syllabled mantra eleven times in case that much of time could be spared. The deity should then be wiped with the cloth.

Thereafter acamana has to be offered, besides the cloth seeds of sesamum and barley grains, wheat, green gram or the black gram, shall then be offered to Siva with various mantras. The flowers have then to be offered to the five headed Siva.

Lotuses, rose flowers, samkha and kusa- flowers, thorn-apples, mandaras grown in wooden vases, holy basil leaves, or the wood- apple leave should be offered to each one of the faces, in accordance with the previous meditation or according to one’s own desire. By all means, Siva, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, should be worshipped with all devotion. In case other flowers are not available, the leaves of the wood-apple tree should be used for the exclusive worship of Siva.

By offering the leaves of the wood-apple tree, the entire adoration of Siva becomes successful. The fragrant powder and the oil has also to be offered.

Thus various sorts should be offered to Siva with great joy. Then the incense of guggulu (the fragrant gum resin) and aguru (Aloe wood) should be offered to Siva.

A lamp lighted in ghee, shall then be offered to Siva. Again you should offer Arghya by this mantra.

With great devotion the water should be sprinkled over the face of Siva, while praying, "O Siva, you bestow on me the beauty, fame, as well as pleasures, besides comforts and salvation. You please accept my argha. Salutation to you." Thereafter excellent type of naivedya should be offered to Siva. After sometime aṣṁḍṁñṁ should be offered. The betel leaf should then be offered with all the ingredients.

Lighting five wicks, the arati should be performed, which should reach the feet twice, twice upto the navel, once at the mouth, and seven times at all the limbs of the body. Then performing meditation one should recite the mantra.

The mantra should be used by a devotee according to his knowledge and the number. The mantra should be recited as per the direction of the preceptor.

One should offer prayer to Siva delightfully. Then lord Siva should be circumambulated quite slowly.

Then he should prostrate before Siva appropriately and reciting other mantras, offer the hand cup filled with flowers, saying, “O Lord Siva, whatever worship has been offered knowingly or unknowingly, let it be successful, Î Lord by your grace. I belong to you and so is my life. My mind is devoted to you.

Î Lord of Parvati, Î Lord of the spirits, be pleased with me, taking me to be your slave, because a person who feels slipped from the earth, the earth is the only support for him.

Therefore whatever sins have been committed by me in adoring you, you have to protect me for the same.” In this way the prayer should be offered.

Then offering the flowers, one should praise Siva again and again. “O Lord of the gods, Î Master, you now depart for your place with your family.” In this way, he should be sent off.

“O Lord you return again at the time of adoration, with respect.” In this way one should offer prayer to Siva, who is benevolent to the devotees.

He should be sent off, and one should lodge him in his own heart. The water of his feet should be sprinkled over the head. Î Sages, I have thus explained the method of the adoration of Siva; which bestows the devotion as well as the salvation. What else do you want to listen from me?”

## Chapter 14 - Directions for Siva’s worship

The Rsis said, “O Disciple of Vyasa, Î Fortunate one, you kindly speak out with examples as to which types of flowers offered to Siva yield which type of fruits which are bestowed by Siva?”

Suta said, “O Saunaka and other sages, you please listen to me quite respectfully. I am lovingly going to reveal the method of the offering of the flowers.

The divine sage Narada, had (in earlier times) asked Brahma about the same, who had lovingly explained the method of offering flowers to Siva.”

Brahma said, “By offering the lotus, wood- apple leave, Satapatra (variety of big lotus flower) and sankha-puspi, bestow riches to the devotees. A person desirous of wealth should offer these flowers to Siva.

In case a devotee offers Siva a lac of flowers, he surely achieves fortunes and his sins are all destroyed.

The bunch of twenty lotus flowers is called prastha and half of a thousand wood-apple leaves also make half a prastha.

A thousand lotus petals, make half a prastha, sixteen palas make a prastha, while ten tankas make a pala.

According to this calculation, flowers for adoration should be weighed. In case the adoration is thus performed, it would bestow all the desires. In case a devotees worships without any desire, he is sure to become like Siva himself.

Î Sages, the one who is desirous of achieving a kingdom, he should try to please Siva by adoring a crore of Parthiva-lingas.

The unbroken flowers and rice should be offered to Sivalinga. Application of the sandal paste, abhiseka of Siva should be performed with the drop of water.

The lotus flower and leaves of wood-apple should be offered to the Parthiva-linga.

The ancient sages have laid special emphasis for the offering of the flowers of samkha-puspi to Siva and by doing so all the presents as well as the future desires of a person are fulfilled.

After the offering of the flowers, incense, lamp, naivedya, argha, arati, pradaksina, salutation, begging of forgiveness should be prayed for and thereafter there should be the ceremonial send off. At the end, other devotees should be served with food.

The one who is desirous of an important position should worship with half the aforesaid number. A person desirous of his release from the prison, should adore a hundred thousand lingas of Siva.

A person suffering from ailment should adore, half of the aforesaid number of Siva- lingas (i.e. fifty thousand). The one who is desirous of a girl child, he should adore twenty five thousands of lingas with twenty five thousand flowers.

A person desirous of higher education should adore Siva with twelve thousand and five hundred lotus flowers. The person desirous of god speech, should worship Siva with ghee.

For the destruction of the enemies, an equal number of flowers should be offered to Siva. For the destruction of the enemies for one lac times, Siva should be adored and for enchantment, the number should be reduced to the half.

For subjugating of the vassal kings, worship of Siva, for a crore of times is recommended.

For earning fame, the same number has been prescribed. For obtaining a vehicle a thousand Parthivas should be adored. A person desirous of salvation should adore five crores of Parthivas with devotion.

The people desirous of higher education should adore a crore Parthiva-lingas of Siva, who is benevolent to all. Those who are desirous of having an audience with Siva, should adore half the above number.

For the fulfilment of the other desires, the Mrtyunjaya mantra should be recited. By performing japam of this mantra five lacs of time, Siva appears before the devotee.

In case a person recites the said mantra a lac of times and begins a second instalment, he would be born in a higher caste. By reciting the mantra three lacs of times, all the desires are fulfilled and by reciting the mantra four lacks of times, Siva himself appears before the devotee.

By performing the japam, five lacs of times, one undoubtedly gets the full reward. In case the said mantra is recited ten lacs of times, one receives further auspicious reward.

The persons desirous of salvation should adore Siva with kusa grass. Î Sages, in relation to the worship of Siva, the number everywhere is one lac.

The person desirous of long life should adore Siva with the durva grass. The person desirous of a son, should adore Siva with Dhattura flowers.

The wood-apple flower with red stalk is considered to be the best and is said to yield the best results. The offering of the flower of agastya tree (aeschynomena grandi flora) to Siva by a person, it would bestow great fame for him.

The worldly pleasures as well as the salvation could be achieved by a person, by offering Tulasi leaves (Holy basil) to Siva. Immense prowess could be achieved by offering of the of madara (calotrapis gigantea), kubjaka and kalhara flowers.

The adoration of Siva with Chinese rose, causes death for the enemies, while oleander flowers drive away all the ailments.

By worshipping Siva with bandhuka flowers, the devotee gets ornaments, jasmine flowers would yield good horses or vehicles, the linseed flowers, shall attain the favour of Visnu.

By offering Sami leaves, to Siva, the devotee achieves the devotion as well as salvation. The jasmine flowers, when offered to Siva, would yield a beautiful women to the devotee.

By offering the splendid yuthika (a kind of jasmine)flowers, the shortage of the cereals never occurs in the house of a devotee by offering the white rose to Siva, he will secure plenty of garments.

Using the flowers of Nirgundi (medicinal plant), the mind of the devotee gets purified in the world. By offering a lac of leaves of the wood-apple tree, all the desires of a devotee are fulfilled.

The flowers of the weeping nyctanthous (Harsigdra) when used in the adoration of Siva by a devotee increases the comforts and wealth of the devotee. In case the flowers of the season are offered to Siva, a devotee surely achieved salvation.

The offering of the mustard flowers to Siva, surely brings death to the enemies. By offering a lac of mustered flowers to Siva, would yield enormous reward.

Except the campaka and ketaka flowers, there is no other flower which is not liked by Siva, therefore these two types of flowers should not be offered to Siva.

Hereafter, I am going to speak out the reward of offering the grains and pulses in the adoration of Siva, which should be listened by you with devotion.

By offering rice to Siva, the riches of a devotee are increased, but they should be offered to Siva with utmost devotion.

There should be six prasthas of unbroken rice, or two palas in weight or one lac in counting.

Siva should be adored prominently. Thereafter a beautiful cloth should be offered to Siva. This is the excellent way of offering rice to Siva.

Thereafter a coconut should be offered with fragrance, unbroken rice flowers, besides the incense, lamp etc. by which full reward of the worship could be derived.

Two rupees of silver connected with Prajapati, besides the black gram should be given to the priest as daksina, for two ceremonies. Or daksina. according to one’s capacity should be given to the priest.

Thereafter food should be offered to twelve Brahmanas. The entire process then constitutes the completion of Laksapuja in detail with the requisite mantras.

The mantras are required to be repeated a hundred and eight times. Thereafter a lack of sesame seeds are required to be offered to Siva, and by doing so, all the sins are destroyed.

A lac of sesame seeds are eleven palas (or forty four tolas). A person who is desirous of his own welfare, should adore Siva, as has been done earlier.

On this occasion the food should be served to the Brahmana devotee of Siva and by doing so, all the miseries emanating from the sins disappear.

Î Parvati, similarly the adoration of Siva with a lac of barley has been prescribed. Eight and a half prasthas and two palas of barley grains constitute a hundred thousand in number, according to the ancient calculation. The sages ordain that the worship of Siva with the grains of barley, increases the divine pleasures.

The devotees desirous of reaping the best reward of their adoration should feed the Brahmanas to please Prajapati. Lord Siva is also pleased with he worship done with wheat.

In case Siva is adored with a lac of wheat grains, then there is an increase in the progeny of devotee. Half a drona has a lac of wheat grains. Rest of the process should be carried out appropriately.

In case Siva is adored with the green gram grains, he bestows all types of comforts over the devotee.

Seven prasthas or two palas, to seven and a half palas of green gram make a hundred thousand in number. This has been ordained by the ancient Brahmanas. Then eleven Brahmanas should served with food.

By adoring Siva, the supreme soul, with the Priyangu flowers (Panicum-Italicum), there is an increase in dharma, artha and kama. This type of adoration is always pleasant.

A lac of Priyangu make a prastha, according to the ancient people with wisdom. Thereafter twelve Brahmanas should be served with food.

The enemies are destroyed by adoring Siva with mustard seeds. Twenty palas of mustard seeds count for a lac of them.

By adoring Siva with them the enemies are destroyed. Decorating Siva with arahara pulses, (citisus cajam), his adoration should be done.

A cow and a bull should be given in charity for the sake of lord Siva. The adoration of Siva with black pepper results in the destruction of the enemies.

Siva should also be adored by colouring him with the colour of the arhara leaves. This type of adoration bestows all types of rewards besides the pleasures.

Î Sages, I have explained to you the adoration of Siva, done by means of cereals. Now listen to the calculation of a lac in the case of flowers.

A prastha of samkhapuspi flowers, make a lac, according to Vyasa, who is well aware of all the measurements and calculations.

The eleven prasthas make a lac of the jasmine flowers. The same is the number of the yuthika or juhi flowers. The flowers of mustard seed count half its number.

Twenty prasthas of Mallika flowers make a lac, while an equal number of sesamum flowers measure a little less then a prastha.

Oleander weighs double than the earlier ones. The people with wisdom describe the same number for Nirgundi flowers.

In the white rose bandhujiva and Siris flowers too have the same mode of calculation. Ten prasthas of bandhujiva flowers constitute a hundred thousand.

Thus taking into consideration the different measures, Siva should be adored for the fulfilment of all the desires. For achieving salvation Siva should be adored shedding away all the desires.

Hereafter I shall speak on the subject of dharapuja, listening to which, people face all the welfare.

Adoring Siva appropriately with devotion, then the stream of water should be poured over Siva.

When a person in high fever starts uttering useless words. In order to pacify such a person, water should be poured over Siva reciting the Satarudriya or Ekadasa-Rudra mantra. By doing so the patient is sure to get relief.

One should also recite the Sivanama and japam from Purusasukta, Sadanga-Rudri or Mahamrtyunjaya mantras.

Besides these mantras, the Gayatri mantra, om-namah-Sivaya or Pauranika mantras should be recited while pouring water over the Sivalinga.

For the increase in the comforts and the progeny dhara-worship has been prescribed to be the best. Making use of the excellent dravyas the holy ashes should lovingly be applied over the body.

By reciting a thousand mantras as stated above, Siva should be bathed with the dhara of ghee, which results in the development of the race. There is no doubt about it.

Thus Siva should be adored reciting the mantras spoken by me. Ultimately twelve Brahmanas connected with Prajapati, should be served with food.

In order to bestow wisdom over a person short of wisdom, the milk mixed with sugar should be poured over lord Siva.

By so doing, the concerned person achieves wisdom comparable to Brhaspati. The adoration with dhara of milk should be continued till the recitation of the ten thousand mantras is over.

In case, without any cause, there develops any crack or lactation in the body, or one develops love in proper or improper person, or there is an increase of love and misery anywhere.

Or the dispute arises in the house, or the miseries overpower the house, all of them would disappear in no time with the performing of the dhara-worship of Siva.

For causing miseries to the enemies, the dhara of oil should be poured over Siva and by doing so the job is done.

By pouring the dhara of the fragrant oil, there is an increase in the pleasures. With the pouring of the dhara of mustered oil, the enemy is surely destroyed.

By adoring Siva, with the pouring of the dhara of honey, the danger from Yaksa is warded off. By pouring the dhara of sugarcane juice, one gets all types of bliss.

By pouring the dhara of the water of the Ganga, one achieves salvation. One get success in the process of reciting the Mrtyunjaya mantra.

In this case the recitation should be done ten thousand times and at the end, eleven Brahmanas should be served with food.

Î Sage, I have spoken to you whatever had been asked by you. This process shall make all the efforts successful.

By adoring Siva appropriately together with Parvati and Karttikeya, the type of reward which is achieved by a devotee, is being spoken by me, whatever had been heard by me.

A devotee of Siva enjoying all the pleasures in this world with sons and grandsons, and after his death he achieves Sivaloka, which bestows all the comforts.

He boards the plane having the lustre of crores of suns, and which moves at will, he joins to singing and dancing of the Rudrakanyas.

He enjoys sports with the relatives of Siva, till the time of the dissolution. Thereafter he is redeemed by achieving the perfect knowledge.

## Chapter 15 - Manifestations of Rudra

Narada said, “Î Creator, Î Brahma- the fortunate one, foremost among the gods, you are graceful. You have recited today the extremely auspicious story of Siva, in which we learnt about the divine and surprising origin of Sivalinga, with the influence of which all the miseries in this world disappear.

Now you speak out the glory and what transpired thereafter, the grandeur of the created things and particularly the mode of creation. You kindly speak out the same.”

Brahma said, “You have put me a correct question, I had heard about the subsequent happenings which I shall relate to you briefly.

After the disappearing of the eternal lord, Î Brahmana, both myself and Visnu felt immensely comfortable.

Then myself and Visnu, in the form of the swan as well as boar, surrounded the earth for its protection.”

Narada said, “O Brahma, possessing enormous wisdom, I have developed a great doubt in my mind you kindly remove the same with great compassion.

Both of you took to the form of swan and the boar, but why did you do so? What had been the reason for it?”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the sage Narada, Brahma, concentrating his mind at the feet of Siva, spoke with respect.”

Brahma said, “The swan can fly upwards steadily and has the power to distinguish between falsehood and the truth. Because of this it can separate milk from the water.

Thus the swan can distinguish between ignorance and knowledge. Because of this, Brahma, the creator of the universe took to the form of a swan.

But Î Narada, I failed to find out the refulgent form of Siva and therefore it was absorbed in the same.

The one who is absorbed in the creation of the universe, how could he be blessed with the real knowledge? Because of thus, I even after taking to the form of swan, could not achieve the true knowledge.

A boar can steadily go down deep below, therefore lord Visnu took to the form of a wild boar.

Or in other words Visnu took to the form of a white boar in order to start sveta-varaha-kalpa.

The date from which Hari took to this form, Varaha-kalpa started from that time.

When he first desired to take to that Varaha form, since that time in every kalpa, the Varaha-kalpa was repeated.

Î Narada, in this way I have replied to your question. You listen to it. Î Sage now, I, concentrating my mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, shall narrate the sequence of the creation.

After the disappearing of lord Mahadeva, I, being the Grandsire of the lokas, in order to obey his command, sat in meditation reciting his name.

Offering my salutation to Siva and gaining wisdom from Visnu, and feeling blissful, I mentally decided to start creation of the universe.

Lord Visnu, offering his salutation to Siva and bestowing the appropriate enlightenment to me, disappeared, Î Dear one.

By achieving the grace of Siva, Visnu went to Vaikuntha, out of Brahmanda and started living there.

In order to resolve for creation, devoting my mind at Siva and Visnu, I created the water first of all and I poured a hand cup full of water in it.

O Brahmana, then out of that water an egg of twenty four tattvas was formed and it took to gigantic form.

Then I becoming doubtful, meditated upon Visnu for a period of twelve years.

O Dear one, at that point of time, lord Visnu himself appeared before me and touched my limbs and then delightfully said.”

Lord Visnu said, “O Brahma, ask for a boon. I am pleased with you. There is nothing in the world which cannot be given to you. By the grace of Siva, I can bestow everything on you.”

Brahma said, “O Visnu, the fortunate one, you have spoken truthful words that Siva has given me over to you. It is therefore proper that I should request you. Therefore you give me whatever Siva has desired to be given to me. I offer my salutation to you. You give me whatever has been desired by Siva to be given to me.

This gigantic egg in the form of virat comprises of twenty four tattvas. There is no life in it in the beginning. Therefore it looks lifeless.

O Visnu, you have appeared before me today by the grace of Siva. Therefore you activate this egg with the strength of Siva.”

At these words of Brahma, Visnu who is always ready to obey the command of Siva, took to the infinite form and entered the egg.

Then Visnu having a thousand heads, thousand eyes and a thousand feet, encompassed the cosmic egg, touching the earth everywhere.

Then Visnu was properly praised by me, who entered the cosmic egg comprising of the twenty four tattvas which got activated.

Lord Hari, who happens to be the preserver of all the seven lokas, himself appeared in his gigantic or virat form.

In these seven lokas, the charming Kailasa, was lodged at the top most position, which was made by Siva, his own dwelling place.

Î Divine Rsi, even if the whole cosmic egg is destroyed Kailasa and Vaikuntha would never be destroyed.

Î Sage, I am dwelling in the Satyaloka. Î Dear one, at the command of lord Mahadeva, I engaged myself in the task of creation.

When I started creation, the sin was created first of all in the form of five illusions. It was the nature of darkness endowed with knowledge.

Thereafter, I feeling delighted created the immobile beings. At the command of Siva, I continued my meditation in an unattached manner of the conscious beings.

Observing that creation, I, for the success of my efforts, started other type of creation, then the creatures moving in transverse manner appeared like the cows and others. They were the form of misery, which could not establish my basic desire.

Treating them to be of no consequence, I again meditated upon and then the creatures, which could move up and having Sattvaguna (or the divine creation) appeared.

The creation of the gods was extremely pleasant. But I again started thinking, taking them to be an obstruction in the achieving of my goal.

Then at the command of Siva, the creation with dominant rajoguna was made which moved downwards, like those of the human beings, who were the great aspirants.

Then at the command of Siva, the bhutas (goblins) were created. In this way five types of creation also called Vaikrta were set in motion.

In this way three types of creations from Prakrti, were made by Brahma. Of these the first was Mahatsarga, the second was subtle Bhautika.

The third was the vaikarika-sarga. Thus there are three Prakrti-sargas. Combining the Prakrti and Vaikarika-sargas, eight types of creations have been defined.

Kumara-sarga happens to be the ninth, which is the combination of Prakrt and vaikrta. Their further divisions are beyond my capacity to describe.

At the end, I shall now describe the Brahmanical creation, which is of very little consequence. It is in this sarga, that the great creation of Sanaka and other rsis referred to above as kumara-sarga has taken place.

Sanaka and others are my mind born sons, who resemble me. All the five of them were fully detached from the world and were great recluses.

They possessed enormous wisdom, and were detached from the world at my command and they always meditated upon Siva. They had declined to engage themselves in the task of the creation.

Î Sage Narada, listening to their refusal to get engaged in the task of creation, I was enraged and confused.

Î Sage, having been overpowered with the anger and confusion, two drops of tears fell from my eyes.

Then suddenly I remembered Visnu, who arrived there atonce, and advised me suitably saying.

“You meditate upon Siva.” Î Sage, at this advice of Visnu, I performed severe tapas.

While performing tapas for the sake of creation, from a point in between my eyebrows as well as the nose, called avimukta, he manifested himself as half man and half woman or Ardhanarisvara.

On seeing the unborn lord Siva, who was the heap of lustre, lord of Uma, omniscient, the creator of all, well known as Nilalohita, before me, I offered my salutation to lord Siva, I praised him with great devotion, which delighted me. Then I said to lord Siva, the god of gods, “You take up several types of creation yourself.”

Then Mahesvara- the god of gods, listening to my words, started creating several beings like himself and filled with rajoguna.

Then I said to Mahesvara- the Maharudra, “O Deva, you create the people who are afraid of birth and death.

“O Sage, Siva, the ocean of compassion then smiled and said.

Mahadeva said, “O Brahma, I shall not create people, who are afraid of the birth and death besides those who are ugly and remain drowned in the ocean of mercy because of their sins.

I, in fact, redeem the people drowned in the ocean of misery and as their preceptor I bestow knowledge on them.

O Prajapati, “You better create the people who have to suffer for their sins. At my command, you would not be bound in any illusion.”

Brahma said, “Saying this, the glorious lord Siva, in my full view, disappeared from that place with his attendants.

## Chapter 16 - The Creation- described

Brahma said, “Î Narada, I, after performing the pentuplication of the bhutas elements and other attributes like sound etc., also evolved the gross Ether, wind, fire, water and earth out of them and the created mountains, oceans, trees etc. and the period of time ending with Kali and other ages.

O Sage, I created many other things but I was still dissatisfied. Î Sage, then I meditated on Siva, and his consort Amba and the created aspirants.

I created the sage Marici from my eyes, Bhrgu from my heart, Angira from the head, and from Vyasa, the sage Pulaha.

Then Pulastya from the udana-vayu, Vasistha from Samana-vayu, Kratu from ṁðañṁ-vayu, Atri from the ears and Daksa Prajapati from Prana-vayu.

You (Narada) were created from my lap, Kardama from my shadow. Finally dharma was created out of my conception, which is meant for the achievement of everything. Î Foremost of the sages, by the grace of Siva these excellent sadhakas were created, after which I felt satisfied.

Then, Î Dear one, at my command, the Rsis who had been born of my sankalpa and were the followers of the excellent dharma were engaged in the following of dharma.

O Sage, then I created several sons, out of my body like the gods, demons and several others, and different types of bodies were assigned to them.

Î Sage, then at the inspiration of Siva, I divided my body into two parts and I became of two forms.

Î Sage, I was spread as male from the one half of my body and a female from the other part. Lord Siva then created mithuna.

Out of these the excellent sadhaka was the Svayambhu Manu and the yogini emerged in the form of the ascetic Satarupa.

The beautiful damsel was accepted by Manu. Î Dear one, thereafter the creation by sexual intercourse started.

He got two sons from her, known as Priyavrata and Uttanapada, besides the three daughters, who were known by the names of Akuti, Devahuti, and Prasuti. Ruci was married to Akuti, Devahuti was married to Kardama and Prasuti, the younger sister of Uttanapada was married to Daksa Prajapati. Out of these, the sons and progeny was spread in the mobile and immobile worlds.

With the union of Akuti and Ruci, yajna with daksina were born. With the union of yajna and daksina, twelve sons were born.

Î Sage, with the union of Devahuti and Kardama, several girls were born. Daksa Prajapati too had twenty four daughters.

Î Sage Daksa Prajapati, gave away thirteen daughters in marriage to Dharma, including Sraddha. You listen to the names of the thirteen wives of Dharma.

These included Sraddha, Laksmi, Dhrti, Kriya, Santi, Tusti, Pusti, Medha, Buddhi, Lajja, Vasu, Siddhi, and Kirti.

The eleven younger daughters were Khyati, Sati, Sambhuti, Smrti, Priti, Ksama, Sannati, Anurupa, Uraja, Svaha and Svadha who were respectively married to Bhrgu, Bhava (Siva), Marici, Angirasa, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu- the excellent one, Atri, Vasistha, fire-god and Pitrs (manes).

These girls were married with the progeny produced by them the entire mobile or immobile universe was filled.

Thus at the command of Siva the lord of Ambika, besides according to ones own karmas several best of the Brahmanas were born

According to another kalpa Daksa had sixty daughters, out of when ten were married to Dharma and twenty seven to the moon.

Thirteen of them were given to Kasyapa appropriately. Î Narada, four of the excellent forms were given to Garuda.

Besides, girls were given each to Bhrgu, Angira and Krsasva and many children were born to them in the mobile and immobile world.

Î Sage, the thirteen girls who were given to the sage Kasyapa appropriately, the mobile and immobile worlds were filled with their progeny, and there were no shortage at all.

Thereafter, the gods, the rsis, daityas, trees and plants, besides the mountains were created.

Thus with the progeny of the daughters of Daksa Prajapati, the entire mobile and immobile world was filled from Patala to Satyaloka.

The entire cosmic egg was filled and no place remained without creation. Thus at the command of Siva, Brahma created the universe.

Sati, the daughter of Daksa was always protected by Siva, because she had been created for the sake of performing tapas.

She was born from Daksa, for the benefit of the people. He performed several tapas for the redemption of his devotees.

Vaikuntha happens to be his left limb, I (Brahma) happens to be his right limb, while Rudra happens to be his heart. Thus Rudra is conceived to be of three types.

Myself, Visnu and Rudra possess the gunas, while Sadasiva himself is absolute- without gunas and is infallible.

Visnu represents- sattvaguna, Brahma- rajoguna and Siva has tamoguna within but of different nature outside.

Visnu is of tamasika nature within, but externally he is Satvika. Rudra is of Satvika nature within but Tamasika nature outside. I on the other hand am of Rajasika nature throughout.

The goddess of speech is of Rajasic nature, Sati is of Satvic nature, Laksmi is of tamoguna nature. The supreme Siva taking to the form of Sati, was married to lord Siva. In the yajna of her father, she ended her life and achieved her true place at the instance of Narada.

Then at the prayer of the gods, she was reborn as Parvati. After performing severe tapas, she again got Siva, as her husband.

Î Sage, the said Siva came to be known by several names like Kalika, Candika, Bhadra, Camunda, Vijaya, Jaya, Jayanti, Bhadrakali, Durga, Bhagavti, Kamaksa, Kamada, Amba, Mrdani, Sarvamangala, Parvati, possessing several qualities bestows pleasures as well as salvation.

Thus the three goddesses possessing all the virtues, and the three gods possessing all the virtues performed the best of activities on earth.

Î Sage, I have narrated to you the method of the creation of the world. At the command of Siva, I created the entire globe.

Siva is the supreme Brahman, Myself, Visnu and Rudra are his manifestation.

Sadasiva is free to take to the visible or invisible form. He enjoys all the sports with Siva in the Sivaloka.

Rudra happens to be his complete and perfect incarnation. Five faced Siva, has built a blissful abode at Kailasa, which is beyond destruction even after the destruction of the universe.

## Chapter 17 - The story of Gunanidhi

Suta said, “O Sages, listening to the words of Brahma, Narada offered his respectful salutation to him and asked him.”

Narada said, “When did Siva, who is benevolent to his devotees, go to Kailasa, and when did he develop friendship with Kubera?

What did Siva, who is the complete form of the universe, do there. You please narrate all this to me because I am too anxious to know about the same.

Brahma said, “O Narada, now I shall narrate the story of Candrasekhara Siva, the way he went to Kailasa and how did he develop friendship with Kubera? Your please listen to me.

In the city of Kampilya, there was a priest who was born in the Somyaji family known by the name of Yajnadatta.

He was well-versed in the Vedic and post- Vedic literature, honoured by the kings besides being an excellent orator.

Making all the efforts, he maintained the sacrificial fire, engaged himself in study of the Vedas, possessed beautiful temperament, had beautiful limbs, and his face resembled the moon.

He had a son named Gunanidhi, after his yajnopavita ceremony was performed, he studied the eight types of lores, pretty well. After sometime he started gambling stealthily from the father.

He brought enormous wealth from the mother and gave it to the gamblers to make friendship with them.

He discarded all the ways of the Brahmanas and became averse to the performing of the sandhya and the prescribed ablutions. He started denouncing the Vedas, the sacred texts, the gods as well as the Brahmanas.

He flouted the conventions and in functions, of the smrtis and indulged in singing and playing. The actors and the heretics were quite friendly to him.

Even at the inspiration of his mother, he never went to his father. Whenever his father, who always remained pre-occupied in the house-hold affairs asked his wife about his son, who could not be seen by him, for long, then she used to say, “He is taking bath, or is adoring the gods, has just gone out, or after completing his studies he has gone out with his friends. Since she had only one son, therefore, Gunanidhi’s mother always cheated her husband.

Diksita- his father was completely unaware of his son’s activities. Still in the sixteenth year he performed his hair-cutting ceremony.

Thereafter Yajnadatta Diksita married his son also according to the provisions of the Grhyasutras.

O Narada, the mother of Gunanidhi, made her son to sit by her side and advised him appropriately daily.

She said, “O Son, your father is of harsh temperament. In case he comes to know of your activities, he would surely beat you and me both.

I daily conceal your evil deeds from your father. Your father is respected because of his noble character and behaviour, but not due to his wealth.

Î Dear one, the wealth of the Brahmanas lies in the best of wisdom as well as the company of he noble people. Then how do you not feel interested in such things?

In the race of Diksita Brahmanas, the people performing the Soma-yajna, the best of scholars well-versed in the scriptures, are born. Your grand father too was well known for the same.

Leaving the company of the evil people, you make friends with people of nobility concentrate your mind in studies and perform the duties of the Brahmanas.

You earn grace, fame and honour according to your father and conduct yourself with humility. Don’t you feel ashamed by following the evil path? Shed away the evil path.

You have reached the age of nineteen and your wife is sixteen years of age. With your chaste wife, you engage yourself in the service of your father.

Î Son, your father-in-law also is adorable, because of his virtues and humility. Are you not ashamed of him? Therefore you discard the evil ways.

Î Son, you maternal uncle too is also excellent in studies, race and humility. Are you not afraid of him? You belong to spotless races on both sides (both paternal as well as maternal).

You should observe the Brahmana boys in your neighbourhood, and also the humble disciples of your father in your own home.

Î Son, when the king becomes aware of your misconduct, he would have no faith in your father and shall put an end to his livelihood.

The people dismiss your present day misbehaviours as simple childishness, thereafter they would snatch away your position of Diksita.

The people would denounce your father and find fault with him as well, denouncing me at the same time. They would also say that boy has adopted the evil ways of his mother.

Your father is a noble soul and conducts himself according to the Vedas and Smrtis. I also remain devoted at his feet. In this connection, lord Siva is my only witness.

I have never seen the face of any wicked person, after my menstrual bath. The destiny is always powerful, which has given me a son like you.”

Thus the mother always extended good advice to her son, but he never cared for her words being evil minded and was absorbed in vices.

Who is the person who is not shattered by indulging in hunting, drinking, back-biting, telling lie, stealing, gambling, visiting whores etc.

The evil minded and wicked son, whatever valuables like wealth, gold, silver, costumes etc. were found by him in the house, he forcibly carried then and gave them to the gamblers.

Once he took away the gem studded finger ring of his father and gave it to a gambler.

Fortunately Diksita found that ring in the hand of the gambler and asked him, “Where from did you get this ring?”

When so asked by the Brahmana again and again, then the gambler shouter, “O Brahmana, why are you blaming me? Have I stolen this ring?

I have purchased this ring from your son, by paying its price. On the earlier day he had won back the sari of his mother.

It is not that he has given me this ring, he has given to other gamblers, enormous amount of wealth.

He has also given gems, gold, silver, costumes, cosmetics, several types of bronzes, copper vases, which he lost in gambling.

The gamblers, make him stark naked and bind him. There is no other gambler in the world comparable to him.

Î Brahmana, could you not recognise your son truly, who is the foremost of the gamblers, and is evil-minded and follows the evil ways?”

On hearing this the head of Diksita was lowered in shame and covering his head with scarf, he left for his home.

Reaching his home, Yajnadatta, the sacrificer, well-versed in Vedic rites, spoke to his wife who happened to be quite a chaste lady.

Yajnadatta said, “O Mistress, where is your wicked son Gunanidhi or leave him, what have I to do with him? Where is my beautiful finger ring?

You had taken it out while applying paste over my body. You atonce bring that gem studded ring to me.”

On hearing the words of her husband, the wife of Diksita became panicky and said, “O Deva, I am engaged in taking bath at noon and also am collecting the material for adoration. The time for the arrival of the guests is fast approaching and you are quite fond of the guests.

I am engaged in cooking my food. I have kept it somewhere and I fail to remember the same.”

Diksita spoke in anger, “O Woman, giving birth to degraded son, whenever, I enquired about your son, you always told me that he had gone with his two or three friends; for studies outside.

Î wife, I had given you a silk sari of red colour, which used to hang down in the house always where is it? You speak out the truth. Don’t be afraid.

Now a days, I don’t find the golden vase studded with gems and the silken scarf given by me.

Where is bronze vase from south and where is the copper pot made in Bengal? Where is the ivory swing?

Where is the surprising type of puppet made in hilly region, shining like the moon. Where has it gone?

O Brahmana women born in a high family, I am uselessly getting angry with you at the moment. I shall take food only when I shall marry again.

I would have been better without the son who brought blemish to the race; get up and fetch me some water. Let me offer libations to him with sesamum seeds.

It is better to be issueless than to have a sinful son, therefore for preserving the sanctity of the family, I am disowning the wicked son.

The Brahmana then took his bath performed his daily prayers and he married a Brahmana girl on the same day.

## Chapter 18 - Gunanidhi’s salvation

Brahma said, “On hearing the news, Gunanidhi the son of Yajnadatta, denouncing his luck, left that place for an unknown direction.

Then after going at some distance, wicked Gunanidhi, the son of Yajnadatta, getting exhausted sat at a spot.

He felt extremely worried as to what should he do next? He thought, “ I am neither wealthy nor well-read.”

A person possessing enormous wealth could be happy in a foreign land, quite quickly. When one possesses wealth, there is always danger of its getting stolen. Such an obstruction could be caused from all the sides.

I having birth in the house of the performer of yajna, how was I entangled in this evil path? It is quite surprising. The destiny is quite powerful, controlling all our future activities.

I am unaware of begging. No known person is available here. I am deprived of money. With whom should I take refuge now.

My mother used to serve food to me well before the sun rise. From whom shall I beg food. My mother is also not here.”

Brahma said, “O Narada, in this way, variously thinking, Gunanidhi sat under the shade of a tree. In the meantime the sun was set.

In the meantime, a Siva’s devotee surrounded by the other devotees of Siva, carrying various types of the materials came out of the city, for the adoration of Siva, on the occasion of Sivaratri festival.

Overpowered with the devotion of Siva, he entered in the temple of Siva and started worshipping Siva appropriately with a careful mind.

Gunanidhi, smelt the fragrance of various types of preparations, having been disowned by the parents, being hungry, he went to the temple.

He thought, “The devotee has offered the naivedya to lord Siva, which could be consumed by me at night when all the devotees go to sleep.”

With this hope in this mind Gunanidhi, kept on sitting outside the Siva temple and observed the adoration performed by the devotees in honour of Siva.

When all the devotees went to sleep after the singing and dancing, he entered the temple for grabbing the naivedya which had been offered to Siva.

Finding the light of the lamp quite dim (and since he could not properly see inside) he made a wick of his cloth to improved the light of the lamp.

Then Gunanidhi, the son of Yajnadatta, suddenly lifted up sufficient quantity of Siva’s naivedya from the temple, while rushing back in a haste with the sweets in his hands, he struck with his foot against a devotee who had been sleeping there, who woke up at once.

He shouted, “Who is moving in a haste?” Who is he? Catch him.” Thus the sleeping devotee cried loudly.

When he fled in panic the city guards caught hold of him and be laboured him, as a result of which he was blinded.

O Sage, the son of Yajnadatta, then consumed naivedya by the grace of Siva and not by the future merit.

Thereafter he died. As soon as the messengers of Yama, holding club and noose in their hands, got ready to carry him to Yama, in bondage, at the same time, Siva’s attendants, boarding a divine plane, holding the spears in their hands, arrived there.”

The attendants of Siva said, “O Messengers of Yama, you leave this religious minded Brahmana, who is not to be punished, because all his sins have been washed out.

The messengers of Yama were surprised at these words of Siva’s attendants and said to them.

Getting afraid of the Attendants of Siva, the messengers of Yama, meekly said, “This Brahmana, had discarded his family traditions. He disregarded the words of his parents, and had forsaken truthfulness and purity. He never offered Sandhya prayers. He even does not take the ceremonious bath regularly.

What to speak of his other misdeeds, he has transgressed and outraged the naivedya offered to Siva. You can see this for yourself. He, infact is not fit enough to be touched by the auspicious people like you.”

Those who consume the Sivanirmalya (the offerings of Siva), or show disrespect to the same, they earn sin by touching such a person.

Even poison is not so dangerous when drunk. Never shall a person make use of Siva property even if he were to die.

You have been considered to be an authority on dharma, but we are not so. In case this Brahmana, has the slightest virtue in him, you kindly enlighten us for the same. We would like to hear the same.”

Thus listening to the words of the messengers of Yama, the Attendants of Siva offering salutation at the feet of Siva, said, Siva’s Attendants said, “O Messengers of Yama, the subtle dharma of Siva could be known to the people having the sharp vision."

“O Messengers of Yama, the deeds performed by the sinless son of Yajnadatta, you listen to the same."

He has removed the shadow of the lamp falling over the Sivalinga. By tearing out a piece of cloth from his scarf he put a wick in the lamp at night.

O Attendants, he also derived merit from by listening to the name of Siva, though casually.

He was also a witness to the worship of Siva being performed by the devotees. He also observed a fast and his mind was concentrated too.

He will surely go to Sivaloka with us today. Serving as a servant of Siva, he would enjoy great pleasures for some time.

Then he getting free from all the sins would become the king of Kalinga country because he is the best of the Brahmanas and is loved by Siva.

Don’t speak anything else, you better return to the place from where you had arrived.” Thereafter the messengers of Yama returned to their abode.

Brahma said, “O Sage, thus listening to the words of Siva’s Attendants, the messenger of Yama went back to Yamaloka.

O Sage, reaching there, he spoke everything to Yama including the words spoken by the Siva’s attendants to them.

Then Dharmaraja said, “O Messenger, listen to my words carefully and delightfully obey my command."

“O Messenger, all the people of the world, who apply white holy ashes making tripundra, over their bodies, should all be set free and should never be brought here."

“O Messengers, those who apply the white ashes over their bodies, they should also be left out and should not be brought here."

Whosoever takes to the form of Siva due to any reason, and wanders in the world, he should also not be brought here.

Those who wear Rudraksa and matted locks of hair, they are also not to be brought here.

Such of the people who take to the form of Siva for the sake of livelihood, should also not be brought here.

Those who take to the form of Siva, deceitfully, they should also be left out and should not be brought here.

Thus Yama commanded his servants. They also kept quiet smiling serenely.

Brahma said, “The Attendants of Siva, saved the Brahmana from the clutches of Yama and he at once proceeded on to the place of Siva.

He served Siva and Parvati there, while enjoying all the comforts and in his next birth be became the son of the king of the Kalinga country known as Arindama.

He was known as Dama who was devoted to Siva since his childhood and also made his childhood friends as the devotees of Siva.

After the death of his father, he accended to the throne at quite a tender age and started various activities dedicated to Siva.

The said king was beyond subjugation by other kings, and he did nothing else except lighting of lamps in Siva temples.

He called for the village heads in his country, and commanded them that they should light lamps in the Siva temples in their villages and that the defaulters would be punished.

Because by giving lamps in charity, lord Siva gets pleased, as per the provision of the Vedas.

In the Siva temples around the villages, the lamps should invariably be lighted.

The person disobeying the order of the king, he would be beheaded. The lamps then started burning in all the Siva temples of those times.

The king Dama, following the same dharma, became the follower of the great religion and ultimately met with his end.

He had great faith in burning of lamps in the temples, therefore, he burning several lamps, ultimately became the lord of Alkapuri where the lamps of gems were lighted.

Thus the slightest service rendered to Siva bestows enormous reward in due course of time. Thus realising, the people desirous of pleasures, should always adore Siva.

On the one hand was Gunanidhi the son of Diksita, who was deprived of all the dharmas, who accidentally went to the Siva temple for stealing the naivedya and the riches there, who lighted lamp for his selfish motive, and removed the darkness at the top of the linga.

For this petty thing, he became the king of the Kalinga country. With the rise of the earlier Samskaras he made the people to bum lamps in the Siva temples.

Look here, O Sage, he earned the position of a Dikpala and now he becoming Kubera, is ruling the kingdom of Alkapuri.

Thus the story of Gunanidhi, the son of Yajnadatta has been narrated, besides the patience of Siva. By listening to this all the desires of the people are fulfilled.

The way in which he became the foremost of the gods and the friend of Siva, O Dear one, you listen to the story carefully, which I am going to speak out.

## Chapter 19 - Friendship of Siva and Kubera

Earlier in the Padmakalpa from my mind- born son Pulastya, a son named Visrava was born. His son was named as Vaisravana.

They lived in Alkapuri built by Visvakarma. Then performing severe tapas they adored Siva.

After the expiry of that kalpa, the kalpa named Meghavahana arrived. Then Gunanidhi the son of Yajnadatta, performed severe tapas.

Realising the importance of Siva, by giving away lamp in charity, reaching the city of Kasi, which illumines the heart, under the lustre of the gem of the mind, he repeated the mantras of the eleven Rudras with great devotion and immense concentration of mind.

He could realise his oneness with Siva and his tapas had very much increased, free from the fire flies of Kama, Krodha or the grave obstructions, stopping the breath, and consecrating Sivalinga by stopping his breath, and spotless vision, he adored it with flowers of good ideas and feelings.

He continued his tapas till his body was reduced to skin and bones.

While he was so engaged in tapas, Lord Visvesvara, accompanied with Parvati, addressed the devotee himself, who was the lord of Alaka, with a pleasant mind.

He was concentrating his mind on Sivalinga and Siva, looking at him said, “O Lord of Alaka, you ask for a boon you desire.”

By the time the lord of Lanka opened his eyes, he found lord Siva, the moon crested lord of Uma, shining with lustre resembling a thousand suns in front of him.

His eyes dazzled with the lord’s lustre. Then closing his eyes, he said to lord Siva, the bestower of all the boons, and lord of all the gods, “The only boon I seek for is, to have a look at you.

O Lord, what shall I do with the boon. O Moon-crested lord, salutation to you.”

Then Mahadeva, the spouse of Uma, touched him with his hands and bestowed strength in him to have a look at him.

When he opened his eyes thereafter, then he first found Uma there. Then achieving the strength of Siva darsana, the son of Yajnadatta, thought, “who is the beautiful woman close to Siva? She must have performed tapas greater than that of mine.

Her beauty, love, fortune, and grace are all surprising.” These were the words repeated by the son of Yajnadatta again and again.

Thus uttering again and again, he started looking at her cruelly. As a result of this his left eye was burst out.

Then the goddess spoke to Siva, “Who is this wicked ascetic? Looking at me he says, “You make, my penance shine and seeing me with his right eye, with jealousy, why does he become enjoined at my beauty, love and good looks?”

Thus listening to the words of the goddess, Siva said laughingly, “O Uma, he happens to be your son. He does not look at you with an evil eye, but thinks that how great is the glory of your tapas?" Thus speaking to the goddess, Siva said to the son of Yajnadatta.

“O Son, getting pleased with your tapas, I want to give you a boon. You would be the lord of treasures and the Guhyakas.

You would be the king of the kings of Yaksas and Kinnaras. You will be the lord of auspicious people and will bestow riches on all the people.

You will always remain friendly with me. I shall always reside close to your city of Alaka, and shall keep on increasing your love for me.

Come on the son of Yajnadatta, this is Uma, your mother. You are a great devotee. You delightfully, touch her feet.

Brahma said, “Thus bestowing the boon to the Brahmana, Siva said to Uma, “O Goddess, be compassionate on your son.”

Thus listening to the words of lord Siva, Parvati, delightfully, spoke to Gunanidhi.

The goddess said, “O Son, let your spotless devotion in Siva continue forever. You will be deprived of your left eye.

The boons granted to you by Siva shall always be fructuous. You had become jealous of me because of my beauty and because of that you would be called Kubera.”

Thus pronouncing boons on him by Siva as well as Parvati, Kubera entered a place named Vaisvesvara.

This is how Kubera achieved the friendship of Siva. Alaka the abode of Kubera was close to Kailasa, the abode of Siva.

## Chapter 20 - Departure of Siva for Kailasa

Brahma said, “O Narada, you listen to the arrival of Siva at Kailasa because of the tapas of Kubera.

Siva, after bestowing the boon of Kubera’s becoming the lord of treasures, reaching his excellent place started thinking.

My form emerging out of the limb of vidhi, can cause destruction. In that form, I could reach the abode of Guhyaka at Kailasa?

Rudra born out of my heart is the only and complete Brahman, who is served by Brahma, Visnu and other gods. He is inseparable from me being invisible.

Therefore, I, in that form, becoming his friend, shall live at Kailasa close to Kubera and performs severe tapas."

Thus thinking, Rudra with the desire of carrying out the desire of Siva, played upon the small dram that produced the divine sound (nada).

Its encouraging sound was filled in the three worlds, heightening enthusiasm and was filled with deep sound.

Listening to that sound, all the gods like Brahma, Visnu and others besides the sages, personified agamas or Sastras, the Vedas, and the Siddhas also arrived there.

All the gods and demons, also arrived there with pleasure, besides the attendants of Siva also arrived from different places.

The leaders of ganas adored by the entire world, possessing the great fortunes, also arrived there. I am going to speak out their number. You listen to me attentively.

Samkhakarna, the leader of the ganas, arrived there with a crore of ganas, Kekaraksa arrived there with ten crores of ganas. Vikrta arrived with eight crores of ganas.

Visakha arrived with sixty four crores of ganas, Pariyatrika arrived with nine crores of ganas, Sarvantaka with six crores of ganas, Dundubhi with eight crores of ganas, Jalanka the best of the ganas, with twelve crores of ganas, Samda, with seven crores of ganas, while Vikrtanana also had the same member.

Kapali was accompanied with five crores of ganas, while auspicious Sandaraka had six crores of ganas, Kanduka and Kundaka had a crore of ganas, each, Vistambha and Candratapana, arrived there each with eight crores of ganas.

Mahakesa- the lord of the ganas, was accompanied with a thousand crores of ganas.

Kundivaha and Subhaparvataka went there with twelve crores of ganas each. Kala, Kalaka and Mahakala are the lord of ganas and they reached there with a hundred crores of ganas.

Agnika brought a hundred crores, Abhimukha brought one crores, Adityamurdha and Dhanavaha, brought hundred crore each of the ganas.

Sannaka and Kumuda brought a hundred crores each. Amogha, Kokila and Sumantraka brought one crore each.

Kakapada and Santanaka, brought sixty crores each, Mahabala, Madhupinga and Pingala brought nine crores each.

Purnabhadra and Nila brought ninety crores each and reached before lord Mahadeva. The great warrior Caturvaktra, arrived with seven crores of ganas.

The lord of all reached there ready to go to Kailasa surrounded by the groups of crores, thousands, hundreds and twenties.

Kasthagudha, Sukesa and Vrsabha, each arrived with sixty four crores; Citra, Nakulisa and Svayamprabhu reached each with seven crores.

Lokantaka, Diptatma, the lord Daityantaka, lord Bhringiriti and the glorious, Devadevapriya, Asani, Bhanuka, and Sanatana, each with sixty four crores; Nandisvara, the supreme chief of ganas and Mahabala were each with a hundred crores.

These and other leaders of ganas were all powerful and innumerable having thousand hands and matted locks of hair with crowns.

All of them had the crescent moon decorating their heads. They had blue necks, three eyes, adorned with necklaces, ear rings, crows and other ornaments.

The lords of ganas resembling Brahma, Indra and Visnu and having the lustre of crores of suns, surrounded by Anima and other ganas, reached there.

With their minds having been filled with the anxiety to meet Siva, other Gana-chiefs besides other noble souls reached there.

Visnu and other gods reached there and offering their salutation to Siva with folded hands, lowering their heads, offered excellent prayer to lord Siva.

Thus Siva accompanied with Visnu and others lovingly proceeded to the abode of Kubera at the Kailasa mountain.

Finding the arrival of Siva, Kubera, adored him with great respect with his family, offering many presents.

Thereafter, Kubera, in order to please Siva, also adored lord Visnu and other gods, the ganas and followes of Siva.

Thereafter Siva, with a delightful heart embraced Kubera, smelt his head and lived there with his ganas.

Then Siva commanded Visvakarma to construct houses for the dwelling of the gods and his devotees.

O Sage, at the command of Siva, Visvakarma reached there and built the asramas there.

Then Siva was delighted at the request of Visnu. Thus becoming compassionate over Kubera, he moved towards the Kailasa mountain. After blessing Kubera, he entered his abode in an auspicious time.

Lord Siva, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, graced Visnu and other gods lovingly, as a result of which all of them were immensely pleased. The ascetics and the Siddhas performed abhiseka for Siva.

All of them worshipped Siva presenting him several types of gifts and offerings. Then the arati was performed ceremoniously.

O Sage, at that point of time there had been an auspicious shower of flowers, while the apsras started singing and dancing.

At that point of time the words of victory and obeisance were heard everywhere. At that point of time all those present there felt enthusiastic having been filled with pleasure.

At that point of time Siva looked extremely graceful seated over his lion throne. Visnu and other gods served him appropriately again and again.

Siva was pleased with the prayer of Visnu and other gods and he fulfilled the desires of all of them. Then Siva, the lord of all bestowed boon desired by all of them.

O Sage, at the command of lord Siva, all of them getting pleased after having their desires fulfilled delightfully went back to their respective abode. I also left the place with Visnu.

Then myself and Visnu were seated over the asanas delightfully. Then sweet words were spoken to us and feeling compassionate on me, lord Siva said to me.

Siva said, “O Visnu and Brahma, both of you are quite dear to me. You are best of all the gods. You are creator and preserver of the three worlds.

At my command, both of you may now leave for your respective abodes. I bestow all the comforts on both of you. I continue to take special care of both of you.”

Listening to the words of Siva and offering salutation to him properly and with his permission both of us returned to our respective abodes.

At the same time, Siva, holding the hand of Kubera, made him sit beside him and spoke the pleasant words.

Siva said, “O Friend, getting charmed with your love, I have become your friend. Now you proceed on to your abode without fear. O True Friend, I shall always be helpful to you.”

Listening to the words of Siva, Kubera with his delightful heart, retired to his abode with the permission of Siva.

Thereafter Siva, stayed at Kailasa which is the best of the mountains with his ganas, practising yoga. Sometime he himself delivered discourses on ancient historical tales.

Sometimes Siva, being expert in divine sports roamed about at the pleasant places of Kailasa with his ganas.

Lord Siva, who had taken to the form of Rudra, was engaged, sometimes, in the divine sports with his ganas, being a great yogi.

Siva, thus spent his time at Kailasa without his consort. After sometime he married Sati, the daughter of Daksa Prajapati.

Then Siva started sporting with Sati, the daughter of Daksa, following the worldly traditions. O Divine sage, he became happy.

O Sage, thus I have explained to you the incarnation of Rudra, besides the episode of Siva’s arrival at Kailasa and his friendship with Kubera.

I have also narrated the sports of Siva which enhance the knowledge and fulfils all the daily desires of the people in this as well as in the future life.

Whosoever reads or listens to this story carefully, he, enjoying all the worldly pleasures on earth and achieves salvation in the other world.

SIVA-MAHAPURANAM

Rudra Samhita

## (2) Sati Khanda

## Chapter 1 - Brief Story of Sati

Narada said, “O Brahma, you know everything about Siva. You have narrated the auspicious stories of Siva and Parvati, which are surprising.

I do not feel satisfied by listening to the stories of Siva from your lotus like mouth.

You have stated that Rudra residing over Kailasa, is the complete form of Siva, having controlled all his senses.

Lord Siva, is adorable by Visnu and other gods. He is the final goal of the people of nobility and is free from all controversies. He is free from blemishes and movement of the ascetics. Such a great lord indulges in divine sports.

Accepting the request of Lord Visnu, he the bestower of welfare became a house-holder by marrying Parvati, who had been his wife in the earlier birth.

She was the daughter of Daksa Prajapati earlier and subsequently she was born as the daughter of Himalaya. How could there be two girls with a single body?

How was Sati turned as Parvati and married to Siva? This entire story and also the events connected therewith should be told to me, O Lord Brahma.”

Suta said, “Thus listening to the words of Narada- the divine saint, Brahma was pleased.

Brahma said, “O Son, O Best among the Sages, I shall narrate to you a beautiful story, listening to which your life would surely become successful.

In earlier times, on looking at my daughter Sandhya in the company of my sons, I became lustful and became upset.

Having been reminded of Dharma, Rudra the great yogi, denouncing me in the presence of my sons, and went back to Kailasa.

Having been influenced with Siva’s Maya, I had developed enmity with Siva, becoming foolish.

Inflicted with the same jealousy, I, in order to confuse him, overpowered with the Maya of Siva, made many efforts.

O Sage, all my efforts with sons, made against Siva were of no use.

When all my efforts together with my sons were of no avail, then I, remembered Visnu the lord of Rama, who on his arrival advised me appropriately.

At the advice of Visnu who is well-versed in Siva-tattvas, then I who had been overpowered with the Maya of Siva, shed away the jealousy with Siva but I could not discard my stubbornness.

Then adoring Sakti, in order influence Siva, I created her as the daughter of Daksa and Asikni (the wife of Daksa). Daksa, you know was my son.

The same daughter of Daksa Prajapati was born as Uma, and she, after performing severe penance, became the wife of Siva, for bestowing welfare on his devotees.

Now Rudra with the unblemished wisdom, during his married life deluded me and carried on several sports as a house-holder.

After his marriage with Uma, Siva reached at the Kailasa mountain, becoming independent, with the desire of getting progeny, started roaming about getting attracted towards each other.

With the pleasant company of her, much of the time of Siva, who was free from all the depraved feelings, was passed.

Thereafter at the desire of Siva, the feeling of rivalry between Rudra and Daksa started, as a result of which the latter had been overpowered with the Maya of Siva, which made him proud, and foolish.

With the effect of the Maya of Siva, the immensely proud and foolish Daksa, started denouncing the immensely peaceful and unblemished Siva.

Then the immensely proud Daksa, organised a yajna, in which Visnu, the lord of the universe, myself and all the gods were invited by him, but he totally ignored Siva.

Having been filled with anger, he did not invite Rudra, and overpowered with his enmity, he also failed to invite Sati his own daughter.

When overpowered with the Maya of Siva, Daksa failed to invite his own daughter, then the chaste Sati, performed her own sport.

Though the arrogant Daksa had not invited her, but Sati, at the command of Siva, went to the place of her father.

In the absence of the atma of Siva, having been insulted by her father, Sati denounced all those present there, and burnt her body in the fire of the yajna.

On hearing this, Siva was immensely enraged. Then he plucked one of the locks of his hair which was turned into Virabhadra.

Emerging out of Siva’s locks of hair with his ganas, he sought for the command of Siva. Siva said, “You destroy the yajna of Daksa, humiliating all those present there.

The immensely valorous and strong. Virabhadra- the lord of ganas, at the command of Siva, at once reached the place of yajna.

At the command of Virabhadra, his ganas created enormous disturbance in the yajna punishing all those present there, without any exception.

They overpowered all the gods including Visnu, and making all the efforts, they severed the head of Daksa and burnt it in the fire altar.

Virabhadra then after destroying the yajna creating enormous disturbance, went back to the Kailasa mountain and offered his salutation to Siva.

In full view of the gods, Virabhadra, the Attendant of Rudra, destroyed Daksa’s yajna.

O Sage, with excellent lord Rudra getting angry, no one could ever be comfortable. This has been ordained in the Vedas and the Smrtis.

Thereafter Rudra was pleased when he was praised by the gods. The lord who is always compassionate to the down trodden, made their prayer fractious.

Siva, who roamed about, performing several types of sports, because of his compassionate nature, restored everything to its original position.

Daksa Prajapati was brought back to life. All were honoured again. The merciful Siva, then had the yajna completed.

O sage, then Visnu and other gods present there, were immensely delighted and worshipped Rudra.

The flame emerging out of the body of Sati fell over the mountain, which bestows pleasure to the people.

The goddess Sati, has been known by the name of Jvalamukhi. A mere look at the same, destroys all the sins and fulfills all the desires.

Even today the flame is worshipped in several ways in the form of festivities for the fulfilling of all the desires.

Thereafter, the same Sati was reborn as the daughter of Himalaya and was known by the name of Parvati.

She again performed severe penance and got Siva as her husband.

O Sage, whatever you had asked me, the same has been spoken by me. By listening of this story, a person is freed from all the sins, there is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 2 - The appearing of Kamadeva

Suta said, “O Dwellers of Naimasarnya, after hearing his words, the excellent sage further asked about the auspicious story which destroys the sins.

Narada said, “O Brahma, O Excellent one, O Great lord, by listening to the story of Siva which bestows welfare, from your lotus like mouth, I do not feel satisfied.

O Creator of the universe, O Brahma, you better narrate the entire story of Siva, including the glory of Sati, I would like to listen to the same.

How was Sati born in the house of Daksa Prajapati? How did Siva consent to make her his own wife?

In the earlier time how did Sati end her life because of the anger of Daksa? Then how was she born as the daughter of Himalaya and risen in the sky?

How did Parvati perform the severe penance and how was she married with Siva. How could she share half the body of Siva?

O Immensely learned one, you kindly speak out all these facts in detail. There is none else comparable with you who could remove the doubt in this connection.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, you listen to the most secret and, auspicious glory.

O Sage, in earlier times, Visnu, for the welfare of the universe, once asked Siva about this, who replied to the former thus.

O Sage, thereafter, when I broached the subject with Visnu, then he explained to me in details.

I shall now narrate the ancient story of the glory of Siva and Parvati, which fulfills all the desires.

When Siva was absolute, without attributes, having no alternatives, devoid of forms, and beyond existent and non-existent, the greatest of the great, of changeless form when united with Sakti, was filled with attributes and had specific forms and divine features. O Brahmana, he was accompanied with Uma. Visnu emerged out his left limbs and I (Brahma) emerged out of his right side. O Sages, Rudra was born out of his heart.)

Inspite of his being one, he was multiplied into three. As Brahma, he became the creator, as Visnu he became the preserver of the universe and as Rudra he became the destroyer.

I, after adoring him, was known as Brahma, the grand sire of the world. I then created the gods, demons and the people.

By creating the gods, Daksa and Prajapatis, I felt quite happy and I thought myself to be the greatest of all.

I created from my mind the rsis like Marici, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Angirasa, Kratu, Vasistha, Narada, Daksa and Bhrgu.

O Sage, when I produced my mind-born sons, at the same time a beautiful damsel was also born from my mind.

She was quite charming and could win the beauty of the evening time and was quite beautiful, attracting the minds of all.

Such a virtuous woman, could not be found in the heaven, earth or the nether world in all the three times (past, present and future).

On looking at her, I thought in my mind together with Daksa and my other sons.

O best of sages, when I, Brahma was thus thinking an astonishing type of a person, emerged in my mind.

He had the lustre of the molten gold, vast chest, beautiful nose, thighs, waist, and legs. He had curly hair.

His both the eyebrows had joined. His face resembled the full moon. He had stout chest which was hairy.

He was of the size of a black elephant, and well built, wearing the blue garments. He had the hands, feet, face and the eyes of red colour.

He had the slander waist, charming teeth, resembling the intoxicated elephant. He had eyes resembling the petals of fully blown lotus flowers. His hair was fragrant.

He had the neck like the conch, embossed with the symbol of fish. He was tall and had makara-fish. as his vehicle. He carried a bow and five flowers for his arrows. When he rolled his eyes here and there his glance looked quite attractive. O Dear one, his breath was fragrant wind. He was accompanied with the feeling of love.

On seeing that Being, my sons Daksa etc. became very curious and were struck with wonder.

The minds of my sons were inflicted wit the arrows of Kama and they could not gain patience.

The said person then bowed in reverence to me- the creator of the universe and bowing down his head humbly said, that person said, “O Brahma, What should I do? You entrust such a task to me, by which I might be able to earn respect from all.

You bestow a place of pride for me. You tell me who is my wife? You are the creator of the universe and the lord of the three worlds.

Brahma said, “Listening to the worlds of the noble-souled person Kama, I (Brahma) surprised and kept quiet for some time”

Then convincing himself, and getting free from surprise Brahma called that person (kama) and said.

Brahma said, using your present form and with the arrows of five flowers, captivate the men and women and carry on the task of eternal creation.

No one of the mobile or immobile creatures in the three worlds, the gods or any other jiva would be able to stand before you.

Even Siva- the Purusottama and Visnu would be overpowered by you, what to speak of the other beings.

You would stealthily enter the minds of the people, and comforting them, you would indulge in the activities of the creation, which would last forever.

The aim of your lotus arrow would be pleasant and surprising for the mind. You would be the cause for their elation.

Thus I have defined you job for the creation of the universe. My sons shall spell out your real name.

Brahma said, “Thus speaking and looking towards the faces of his sons, Brahma occupied the lotus seat.

## Chapter 3 - Curse and blessing on Kama

Brahma said, “Thereafter, Marici and other sons of mine, who were well aware of my mind, gave him the appropriate names.

Daksa and others who were engaged in the creation, getting aware of his story and looking at his mouth, gave him the proper place and the appropriate wife.

O Brahmanas, then Marici and my other sons, gave that person the suitable names.

Rsis said, “Since you have churned the mind of Brahma, therefore you would be known in the world as Manmatha.

O Spiritual one, there would be no one more beautiful in the three worlds than you. Therefore you would be known by the name of Kama.

Since you would get others intoxicated, therefore you would be known by the name of Manmatha.

No god would be more powerful than you and you would be all pervading, since you would reside everywhere.

O best of men! as you please, first Prajapati Daksa himself will give the suitable wife to you.

The girl, having been mind-born of Brahma would be extremely beautiful in the world and would be known by the name of Sandhya.

This girl has been born of the mind of Brahma, like he jasmine flower and would be known as by the name of Sandhya.”

Brahma said, “Then he holding the five arrows of flowers, and secretly thought about the future course of action.

The five weapons of Kamadeva viz.: harsana (delight), rocana (appeasing), mohana (deluding), sosana (withering) and marana (killing) could delude and torment even the sages.

He thought, “Brahma has desired me to follow the eternal dharma and I shall do so here itself in the presence of the sages.

The sages and Prajapati himself are present here. My job would be accomplished in their very presence.

Sandhya, who has been described by Brahma, is also present here. Let her speak out her mind also. I shall test my power here and then carry it out elsewhere. Every one would be charmed by me.”

Brahma said, “Thus thinking and with a firm resolve in his mind, Kamadeva, placed all the five flow arrows over his bow.

Kamadeva- the great archer, standing in the posture of Alidha, turned his bow circular like a bangle and was ready to shoot.

As soon as he held the bow in that manner, at once the pleasant winds which delighted the minds of people started blowing.

Thereafter Kamadeva, charmed Brahma and all other ascetics separately with his flower arrows.

O Sage, thereafter, myself as well as all other ascetics came under the influence of Kama’s charm. The minds of all of them were infested with passion.

Because of the influence of the passions, all of them started looking (greedily) at Sandhya, because a woman is always the cause of the increase of the lust.

Kamadeva, charmed all with passion and he did not stop till all of us lost control over the sense-organs.

When on looking at her my vital elements were displaced, fortynine animal instincts Bhavas emerged out of my body.

Sandhya too after having been voluptuously gazed by all of then, also began to display her gestures like side glances, pretence of concealing the feelings etc. as a result of having been hit by the arrows of Kama.

Sandhya, who was beautiful by nature, displayed the sentiments sprouting in her mind, like a golden river with slow waves which appeared extremely beautiful.

Then Prajapati, whose body had been overpowered with dharma, looking at Sandhya became desirous of getting her.

O Dear one, thereafter, Marici, Atri and all other ascetics, besides Prajapati, were overpowered with the sensuous excitement

Kamadeva, on the other hand finding myself and other rsis having been infested with lust, considered himself to be successful in his task.

Kama thought that the task that had been assigned to him by Brahma, he was competent enough to perform the same.

Observing the sinful way of the father Brahma, his son Dharma remembered Siva, the protector of dharma.

Then Dharma, the son of Brahma mentally meditating on Siva, the protector of Dharma, offerd many prayers sadly.

Dharma said, “O God of gods, O Mahadeva, O Dharmapala, salutation to you. O Siva, you are the creator and the preserver of the universe.

You yourself function as Brahma, for the purpose of creation, Visnu for the purpose of preservation, and Siva at the time of dissolution. You are beyond the three gunas viz.: sattva, rajas and tamas.
