Suta said, “Listening to these words of Brahma, Narada then enquired about the greatness of Siva and Siva.”

Narada said, “O Disciple of Visnu, Î Brahma, Î Possessor of great fortunes, kindly speak out the details of the story of Siva and Siva who followed the worldly traditions.

Why did Siva abandon his wife who was dear to him than his life even. I consider this event to be unprecedented.

How was your son Siva humiliated? How did Sati end her life in the yajna of her father?

What happened thereafter? What did Siva do thereafter? You kindly speak out the same, I would like to listen to the same with utmost faith.”

Brahma said, “Î Narada, you are the best of the sons as well as the learned people. You lovingly listen to the story of Siva with other sages.

After bowing in reverence to other gods, as well as Visnu, who serve Siva, I am going to narrate the astonishing story of Siva- the Supreme Brahman.

This is all the sports of Siva. Because the lord is engaged in several sports. He is saguna as well as nirguna and same is the case with Sati.

Î Excellent sage, otherwise, who else is competent enough to do that act. He alone is the supreme soul, Supreme Brahman and the Supreme Isvara.

He is the one who is always adored by lord Visnu, myself, all the sages, gods, mendicants, Sanaka and other siddhas.

Even the serpent Sesa, always sings his glory but never feels exhausted. Î Dear one, he is the same lord Siva.

The visible expansion of tattva is because of his sports alone. No one is at fault in this case. He is all pervading and inspires all.

Once, Siva, who is well versed in sports, mounted over Nandi with Sati, was roaming about on earth. After roaming about on earth upto the seashore, he arrived in the Dandakaranya, where Siva- the lord of truthful means and actions, pointed to Sati, the beauty of the surroundings of the place.

Siva at that point of time, found Rama with Laksmana searching for his spouse Sita who had been stolen away by Ravana.

Sri Rama at that moment was desparately crying for Sita, looking here and there.

Searching for her, he was confused and devoid of shame was asking about Sita from the trees, and was filled with grief.

Having been born in the solar race, Rama the son of Dasaratha, elder brother of Bharata, filled with grief and gloom, was seen by them.

The immensely benevolent lord Siva, bowed in reverence to Rama, wandering in the forest with Laksmana.

Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees had an audience with Rama who was moving in the other side of the forest uttering the word jaya (victory) for him.

Then observing the sports of Siva, which captivates all, Sati, getting influenced with the illusion of Siva, felt surprised.

Sati said, “O God of gods, Î Supreme Brahman, Î Lord of all, all the gods including Hari and Brahma serve you.

They serve you as well meditate upon you. You are known through the science of metaphysics after making strenuous efforts. You are the undecaying great lord.

Î Lord, these two persons appear to be grief stricken, because of their separation who were wandering in the forest in a gloomy state of mind? They were looking miserable.

Out of the two, the one having the complexion of the blue lotus flowers, looking at him, why did you feel delighted like a devotee?

Î Siva, Î Master, you remove my doubt, because it would not be proper for the master to bow in reverence to the servant.”

Brahma said, “The goddess Sati is the eternal force, being Parames'vari. Having been overpowered with the illusion of Siva, she put up this question.

Listening to the words of Sati, lord Siva, who was well-versed in the divine sports replied to Sati smilingly.”

Paramesvara said, “O Goddess Sati, you listen to me lovingly. I am revealing before you the factual position. There is no trick in it. With the influence of the boon, I offered my salutation to him with respect.

Î Goddess, both of them were Rama and Laksmana, the sons of king Dasaratha, having been born in the solar race.

Out of them the fair complexioned one is the younger brother Laksmana- the incarnation of the serpent Sesa, while the elder one is Rama himself. He the complete form of Visnu and is incapable of being harassed.

They, for the protection of the noble people and for our benefit, have incarnated on earth.” Thus speaking, Siva, the creator of the universe kept quiet.

Listening to the words of Siva, Sati could not believe them because the illusion of Siva is quite powerful and captivates the three worlds.

On realising this, Siva, the eternal one, understood that Sati had not believed his words, then he, who was well-versed in the divine sports, said to her.

Siva said, “O Goddess, in case you have no belief in my words then you can test Rama with your own wisdom.

Î Sati, Î beloved one, you act in a way by which your confusion could be removed. In the meantime Siva went from that place and rested under the shade of a banyan tree.

Brahma said, “The great goddess Sati, at the command of Siva, started thinking as to how the forest dweller Rama could be put to test?

I shall take to the form of Sita and then go to Rama. In case Rama is lord himself then he would understand everything otherwise not.”

Thus thinking, she, under the influence of illusion, of Siva, took to the form of Sita and went to Rama.

Sri Rama said, “O Sati, salutation to you. You speak out lovingly, where has Siva gone today? How could you arrive in the forest alone?

Why have you taken to this form, discarding your own form? You kindly speak out the reason for the same.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the words of R3ma, Sati was taken aback at that moment and taking the words of Siva to be true felt shameful.

Taking Rama to be the form of Visnu and reverting to her original form of Sati, devoting her mind at the feet of lord Siva, she delightfully said.

“Lord Siva, accompanied with me and his attendants, roaming over the entire earth has reached in this forest.

He spotted you engaged in search of Sita. He found you and Laksmana painful, without Sita.

Offering his salutation to you and praising your Vaisnavi illusion, is delightfully resting under a banyan tree.

He felt pleased without looking at your four-armed form. He felt blissful at the sight of your spotless form.

Listening to the words of Siva, I felt confused. Î Rama, I therefore at his command, have tested you.

Î Rama, I have come to realise that you are Visnu. I have also witnessed your greatness. Though my doubt has been removed, still Î Intelligent one, you listen, what I intend to speak out to you.

How have you become adorable by Siva? You tell me correctly. You remove the doubt from me and by doing so, welfare would soon be bestowed on you.”

Brahma said, 'Thus listening to the words of Sati, the eyes of Rama were blossomed. He remembered lord Siva, which increased the devotion of Siva in his heart.

Î Sage, Sati also did not return to Siva, without the permission of Rama. Highlighting the glory of Siva, Rama said to Sati.

## Chapter 25 - Separation of Siva and Sati

Sri Rama said, “O Goddess, in earlier times lord Siva, the creator of the universe, once summoned Visvakarma, the best architect in the universe, and got a gigantic and charming building built near his cowshed. A beautiful lion throne was placed therein.

Lord Siva also got a beautiful and vast umbrella made which was hung over the lion throne, for the sake of Ganesa.

He also invited all the gods including Indra and others, besides siddhas, Gandharvas, Nagas and the acaryas, upadesas and Agamas, Brahma with his sons, the sages and the celestial goddesses and nymphs arrived there with various presents.

Sixteen virgins each of the devas, sages, siddhas and serpents were also brought for the auspicious ceremony.

Î Sages, different musical instruments like lute tabours, etc. were played, upon, and songs were sung. There was thus a great pomp and show at the festivities.

The articles and herbs which were considered necessary for the festivities were brought. Five pots were filled with the sacred water from all the flowing holy rivers.

The attendants made all other necessary arrangements. The Vedic hymns were recited loudly.

With the mind filled with delight, lord Siva, called Visnu from Vaikuntha. Î goddess, lord Siva was immensely pleased at the devotion of Visnu.

During the auspicious time, lord Visnu was made to occupy the unique throne and decorated him delightfully, in various ways.

A beautiful crown was placed over the head of Visnu an the abhiseka of Visnu was performed in the Brahmanda-mandapa by Siva himself.

Siva then conferred all his fortunes on Visnu, which could not be given to anyone else, by Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, offering prayer to Visnu.

Siva who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, displaying independent but subservient, to the boon granted by him, spoke these words to Brahma, the creator of the universe.

Siva said, “O Lord of the world, from today onwards, lord Visnu, what to speak of the entire universe, would be adorable by me even. All should listen to this.

Î Dear one, together with all the gods, you also offer your salutation to lord Hari. At my command the Vedas shall also excel him in the same way as they do for me.”

Sri Rama said, “Thus speaking, Siva himself offered his salutation to Visnu. Thereafter Siva, getting pleased with the devotion of Visnu, bestowed further boons on him.

Thereafter, Brahma and other gods, the sages, siddhas and others offered their salutation to Visnu.

Thereafter, Siva praised Visnu in the presence of all and getting pleased, he bestowed several other boons on him.

Siva said, “You at my command, henceforth, would become the creator, preserver and the destroyer of the world, you will chastise the evil people and become the bestower of dharma, artha and kama.

You will be the lord of the universe, adorable in the world, immensely valorous, besides being invincible in the battle, even by me.

You accept the three Saktis conferred by me on you. You will engage yourself in several types of sports and your glory would spread in all the three lokas.

Î Visnu, whosoever would be jealous of you, I shall punish him making, all the efforts. Î Visnu, I shall bestow the excellent moksa (liberation) to your devotees.

You accept this Maya from me which can hardly be withstood by the gods and others and by which the entire world can be captivated or made unconscious.

Î Hari, you are actually my form. This Brahma is my right arm. You are the creator of Brahma and would become his sustainer as well.

Of course, I happen to be Rudra, who would be adored by you and Brahma. There is no doubt about it.

Living here, you protect the entire world by incarnating on earth variously and in diverse ways of protection.

Your place in my loka would be of great prosperity and glory, which would be known as Goloka.”

Î Visnu! your incarnations for the protection of all beings on the earth, my devotees will behold these with pleasure through my blessings.

Sri Rama said, “In this way, lord Visnu, received from Siva, the imperishable fortunes. Siva, the lord of Uma, on the other hand getting free, started living over the Kailasa mountain with his attendants.

Since then, the lord of Laksmi, took to the form of a cowherd and lovingly going to the Goloka, became the lord of cows, cowherdesses and the cowherds, wandering there with pleasure.

Then Visnu, getting pleased, started protecting the entire world. He incarnated several times, at the command of Siva and became the protector of the world. At that point of time, Visnu at the command of Siva, incarnated four times on earth, viz.: as Rama, Laksmana, Bharata and Satrughna.

Î Goddess Sati, I had arrived in the forest with Sita and Laksmana, at the command of my father and had to face miseries here because of luck.

Some demon has stolen away my wife known as Sita. Getting separated from her, I, in the company of my brother, am searching for her. Î Mother Sati, I could have an audience with you and by your grace, I am sure to meet with welfare.

By having a meeting with you it would result into a boon in getting back Sita. By your grace, I am sure to kill the wicked demon. There is no doubt about it.

It is a matter of great fortune for me today, that I could have an audience with both of you. when both of you are graceful on someone, he is sure to become the excellent one.”

Thus speaking repeatedly offering his salutation to chaste Siva, with utmost devotion, and with her permission, Rama kept on wandering in the forest.

Then the goddess Sati, listening to the words of Rama who had controlled his sense organs, started praising Rama, who was engaged in the devotion of Siva and felt delighted at heart.

She felt painful at heart at her performance. With her gloomy and faded face, she returned to Siva.

While walking on the way back she was thinking again and again. "I did not believe in the words of Siva, and thought ill of Rama.

Now what reply shall I give to Siva?” Thus thinking, she felt extremely painful.

She was feeling painful and her appearance faded out and feeling depressed, she ultimately went to Siva and offered her salutation to him.

Finding her so depressed, Siva enquired about her welfare and asked her lovingly, “How did you put him to test?”

Listening to these words of Siva, she went to him and said, “I have not put him to test. Then she stood there having been depressed.

Thereafter, Siva the great yogi, well versed in the various types of sports, resorted to dhyanam or yogic power and learnt about the entire story of Sati.

He was reminded of his vow at the time of the anger of Hari, which was desired to be fulfilled by Rudra- the one who honoured the vow.

At that point of time Siva felt painful that he the creator, spokesperson and the protector of Dharma spoke like that.

Siva said, “In case I love Sati as I did earlier, then my vow would be shattered, since I happen to be the follower of the worldly traditions.”

Brahma said, “Thus thinking variously, Siva, the follower of the Vedic traditions, discarded Sati from his mind and saved his vow.

Thereafter, Paramesvara, disowning Sati from his mind, moved towards Himalaya. This secret was not revealed by Siva.

At the time of their departure, divine speech rose in the sky telling Siva with in the hearing of everyone, particularly Sati- the daughter of Daksa.

The divine voice said, “O Great lord, you are graceful no doubt. There is no other great yogi comparable with you. No one can fulfil the vow.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the divine voice, the goddess Sati, was extremely faded out and asked Siva, “Kindly tell me the vow undertaken by you?”

Inspite of the question raised by Sati, Siva, who had been benevolent to all, did not disclose the vow, undertaken by him at the time of marriage in presence of Visnu.

Î Excellent sage, then Sati, meditating for his beloved Siva, came to know everything, about her disowning by Siva.

Sati then, realising that she had been discarded by Siva, took deep sighs again and again and was plunged in grief.

Siva on the other hand realised that Sati had known about his vow, therefore in order to divert her attention, he started narrating several auspicious stories in order to appease her.

Thus narrating the auspicious story, Siva accompanied with Sati, went to the Kailasa mountain. Reaching there, Siva, sat in his real form in meditation in yogasana.

Thereafter Sati continued to live their with an extremely disturbed mind. But Î Sage, no one came to know about such performance of Siva and Siva.

Î Sage, in this way, Siva, who followed the worldly traditions, and maintained his body at well, spent some time.

Thereafter, Siva, who removes the miseries of others, finished his smadhir knowing about which Sati, the mother of the world arrived there.

She offered her salutation to lord Siva with a painful heart. The large hearted Siva then gave her a seat in front of himself.

Then he lovingly spoke out some charming stories. Then he relieved her of all the sufferings by his sports.

Sati thereafter enjoyed all the comforts as before, but Siva did not discard his vow. Î Dear one, this performance of Siva should be considered as an ordinary one.

Î Sage, the story of Siva and Siva is being narrated by the sages like this. But some foolish people take it to be the separation between Siva and Siva. But how could they be separated?

Who could actually know the performance of Siva and Siva? Both of them roam about at will while sporting and make their own lives forever.

Sati and Siva are always united together like the words and their meanings. Siva cannot be separated from Sati, without his wish.

## Chapter 26 - Cause of conflict between Daksa and Siva

Brahma said, “In the ancient times, the great sages collected in the holy place of Prayaga and performed an auspicious yajna there, appropriately.

The siddhas, Sanaka and other divine sages, besides Prajapati, the gods and the ascetics who had audience with Brahma also arrived there.

I also arrived there with my disciples, together with Agamas, Nigama in the shining embodied forms.

Several people participated in the festivities having diverse character. Discussions were carried out on different subjects enshrined in different sacred texts.

Î Sage, in the meantime, lord Siva together with his ganas and Sati arrived there. He was the creator of the three worlds, besides being bestower of the benefits to the three worlds.

With the arrival of Siva, the gods, the siddhas sages, and even myself offered there salutation to him, besides praising him.

All the people present there took their seats, at the indication of Siva and started praising their fortunes (for having a look at Siva).

At the same time, suddenly Daksa, the lord of the illustrious Prajapatis arrived there delightfully.

The arrogant and devoid of Daksa offered his salutation to me and took his seat at my indication.

All the gods, quite humbly, with folded hands offered their salutation to Daksa, eulogising him at the same time.

But lord Siva who engaged himself in diverse sports, freely, continued sitting over his seat. He failed to offer his salutation to Daksa Prajapati.

Then Daksa Prajapati- my son, when found this, he was suddenly enraged over Siva.

Daksa on the other hand, who was immensely arrogant and short of wisdom, cruelly looked at Siva and spoke words which could be heard by all.”

Daksa said, “All the gods, demons, rsis, and others are offering their salutation to me. How is it that this immensely arrogant person, surrounded by the goblins sand ghosts, behaves like a wicked person?

He always lives in the cremation ground, is shameless, inactive, always served by the ghosts and the goblins, intoxicated being ignorant of the correct practices, and spoiling the old tradition has not offered his salutation to me.

He is deceitful, wicked, sinful, denouncer of the Brahmanas and the one who has the lust for his wife alone. He is always interested in the love-sports and therefore I am going to pronounce a curse on him.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking the immensely wicked Daksa, started talking about Siva- Î gods and Brahmanas, listen, he is due to be killed by me now.”

Daksa said, “I expel Rudra from the yajna. He is an out-caste from all the varanas, having an ugly shape, dweller of the cremation ground. He is devoid of race and birth. From today onwards, he would not receive his part (of the yajna) with other gods.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the degraded words of Daksa, and considering Siva to be comparable with other gods, other sages and rsis like Bhrgu and others denounced Siva.

Listening to the words of Daksa, Nandisvara the attendant of Siva, felt enraged and became ready to pronounce a curse on Daksa.”

Nandisvara said, “O Deceitful one, immensely foolish, evil minded, Daksa, how could you expel my lord Mahesa from the yajna!

How could you pronounce a curse on Siva, who makes all the sacrifices fruitful and successful and even the holy places are purified by him?

Î Evil minded Daksa, you have cursed lord Siva, in vain, with your inconsiderate rashness, as a Brahmana and you have laughed at him.

Î Degraded Brahmana, he is the one who creates, preserves and ultimately destroys the universe, such a type of Siva has been made by you the target of your curse. Why have you done so?”

When Daksa was thus rebuked by Nandi as well then Daksa filled with anger, cursed Nandi also.

Daksa said, “You- all the attendants of Siva are also expelled from the Vedic rituals besides being discarded by the rsis.

You would be engaged in the deceitful or useless talk, devoid of good manners, engaged in drinking wine, wearing .the matted locks of hair, the ashes on the body, as well the bones as ornaments.”

Brahma said, “When Daksa so pronounced a curse over the attendants of Siva, Nandisvara- the dear attendant of Siva, was immensely enraged.

Then Nandisvara the son of Silada, who was quite illustrious said to the extremely arrogant Daksa.”

Nandisvara said, “O Evil minded and wicked Daksa, you have uselessly pronounced the curse, unaware of the importance of Siva- tattva, over the ganas of Siva, because of the rashness of your mind possessing petty knowledge.

Bhrgu and others having been filled with the pride of being Brahmanas and having evil minds laughed at Siva, the great lord.

Such of the degraded people present here who are against Siva, I pronounce a curse on them with the influence of Rudra.

“You would not be able to understand the meaning of the Vedas, even after deep discussion on the subject. You would always say that there is nothing else.

Having been overpowered with êīḍṁ (desires), krodha (anger), lobha (greed) and mada (arrogance), you would always be desirous of the heaven and become shameless beggars.

These Brahmanas will officiate in the sacrifices of the Sudras following the Vedic path. They would actually be paupers eager to receive money through any source.

Because of their receiving riches through the undeserving sources, they would fall in hell while some of them would turn as Brahmaraksasas.

A person, who, taking Siva to be an ordinary person, becomes inimical to him, such on evil-minded person, would be deprived of jnana-tattva.

Soon- this Daksa would become goat faced and would indulge in worldly vulgar and lustful pleasures besides the evil ways. He will lay down rules for rituals perpetually discussing the Vedic hymns. His bright face will fade out and he would be strayed away from his goal. He will fall from his holy place and indulge in wicked deeds.”

Filled with anger, when Nandisvara cursed the Brahmanas and Daksa, there was a huge uproar at the place.

Then I, (Brahma) the spokes-person of the Vedas, and well-versed in Siva-tattva, listening to the same, denounced several times Bhrgu and other Brahmanas present there.

Siva on his part, listening to the words of Nandi, spoke sweatly to him trying to convince him.

Sadasiva said, “O Nandi, the great intellect, don’t be angry. You have cursed the Brahmanas uselessly.

Vedas are composed in the form of syllables and are in the form of the Suktas, there lives the souls of all the living beings.

Therefore you do not pronounce any curse in anger. The Vedas lead to self realisation and as such, they should not be cursed.

Î wise Nandi, you have imparted knowledge to Sanaka etc. the sons of Brahma, be calm and quiet. I have not at all been cursed.

I am myself the yajna, the performer of the yajna besides being the part of yajna. I am also the soul of the yajna, the performance of the yajna, and an exterior to the same.

Who are they? Who are you? Who are all these? I represent them all in reality. You better think from this angle. You have cursed the Brahmanas in vain.

Î Immensely wise one, Î Nandi, you, shedding away the anger, realising the fundamental basis of the formation of the universe, through the factual position, get enlightened and re-assured.”

Brahma said, “When so advised by Siva, Nandisvara shed away the anger, achieving the supreme knowledge and he became calm.

Thus convincing Nandi who was the closest and dearest of Siva’s ganas and accompanied with all the ganas left for their own abode.

Daksa Prajapati, on the other hand was surrounded by the enraged Brahmanas, filled with rage and feeling inimical to Siva left for his abode.

At that point of time Daksa pronouncing the curse, and shedding away his devotion for Siva, started denouncing Siva.

I have narrated the crooked wisdom of Daksa in relation to Siva- the Supreme Soul. Î Dear one, now I shall narrate the humiliation extended to him by Siva.

## Chapter 27 - Start of Daksa’s sacrifice

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, once Daksa Prajapati, organised a huge sacrifice. Receiving the diksa for yajna he invited in that yajna all the divine sages.

Influenced with the illusion of Siva, the gods and rsis also arrived for the performing of the yajna.

The sages who arrived there in Daksa’s sacrifice included Agastya, Kasyapa, Atri, Vamadeva, Bhrgu, Dadhici, lord Vyasa, Bhardvaja, Gautama, Paila, Parasara, Garga, Bhargava, Kakubha, Sita, Sumantu, Trika and Vaisampayana and many others.

In this way several other sages together with their wives, arrived in the yajna of my son Daksa.

All the gods, Lokapalas and Ganadevatas arrived there with their respective vehicles and the ganas.

I, the creator of the universe, was also invited with prayers from Satyaloka. I also, together with my sons, family and the Vedas arrived there.

Lord Visnu was also invited respectfully from Vaikuntha with his family and attendants for participating in the yajna.

Thus the wicked Daksa, invited all and honoured them all appropriately.

Daksa allotted all of them the vast buildings built by Visvakarma- the divine architect for them.

All the places, the gods, myself and Visnu were lodged gracefully, who looked fine.

At the bank of the holy places of Kanakhala, the yajna, was organised in which Bhrgu and other great sages were appointed as priests.

Visnu, himself was the presiding deity along with the Maruts. I myself (Brahma) functioned as the chief priest for the Vedic rituals.

Similarly the Lokapalas (guardians of the quarters) functioned as the gate-keepers or the watchmen. They were well-equipped with arms and were assisted by their attendants who were quite enthusiastic.

The yajnadeva also appeared in that sacrifice The excellent sages held the Vedas.

The sacred fire of the yajna took to diverse forms in several ways, in order to receive the sacrificial offerings of Daksa.

Eighty six thousand (Rtviks) priests collectively made the offerings in the fire. Sixty four udgatrs participated in as Adhvaryus and Hotrs. Their number was the same. The seven sages recited jointly as well as severally, Saman hymns.

Daksa extended his invitation to participate in the sacrifice to Gandharvas, Vidyadharas, Siddhas, Adityas, the innumerable Nagas, along with their followers and the ritualists.

The Brahmanical, royal divine sages, besides the kings, their ministers, friends and army, the eight Vasus and the Ganadevatas, besides the security guards for the yajna were all invited by Daksa.

The yajna-mandapa was decorated, with proper initiative, Daksa with his wife after performing Svaslivacana, and receiving diksa for yajna looked quite graceful.

The wicked Daksa, taking Siva to be the carrier of skull, did not consider him fit for invitation.

Since Daksa had the faults-finding nature he did not invite, his dearest daughter Sati, because of her being the wife of Siva, in the yajna.

Thus with the start of the yajna of Daksa, all the people were engaged in their respective assignments.

In the meantime the sage Dadhici, finding Siva absent from the yajna became nervous and spoke.

Dadhici said, “O all the celestial sages and others, listen to my words. Why has Siva not arrived in the yajna?

Though the best of the gods, the sages, and the lokapalas have arrived but the yajna has no grace without Siva.

The people with wisdom are of the opinion, that the eternal Purusa, because of whom, all the works face success, the same Purana-purusa, Supreme lord, blue-throated one known as Bull-bannered one, is absent from here and is no more visible.

Î Daksa, with the presence of three eyed and five faced Siva, all the inauspicious things become auspicious.

Therefore, yourself, Brahma, and all competent Visnu, should at once summon Siva.

For the completion of the yajna, with Indra, Lokapala, Brahmanas and the Siddhas, Siva should be brought here.

All of you should go at once, where lord resides and bring here Siva and Sati.

Î Gods, with the arrival of Siva- the Supreme, Soul, with Sati, the yajna would be purified.

The one with the reciting of whose name, or by remembering whom, all the tasks are established, such a lord Siva should be brought here making all the efforts.

The yajna could be purified only on the arrival of Siva here, otherwise it would remain incomplete. I am speaking the truth.”

Brahma said, “Listening to these words, the foolish and evil-minded Daksa, at once spoke laughingly.

Visnu happens to be the base of the gods, in whom is enshrined the Eternal Dharma. I have invited him in the yajna. What is the deficiency now in the yajna.

Visnu in whom, all the Vedas, yajnas and all the noble deeds are enshrined, is already present here.

Brahma- the Grand Sire of all the lokas, Brahma from Satyaloka with the Vedas, Agamas Upanisads and other scriptures have already arrived here.

Besides Indra has also arrived here with all the gods. In addition to these, the sinless sages have also arrived here.

Such of the people who are suitable or all worthy of being included in the sacrifice and deserve honour have arrived. All of you are well aware of the Vedas and their interpretation and are steady in your rites.

Then what is the use of getting Rudra here? Î Brahmana, I had given my daughter to Siva at the advice of Brahma.

Î Brahmana, Siva does not belong to a noble race and his parents are unknown. He is the lord of goblins, ghosts and spirits and is incorrigible.

He is haughty, self-conceited, foolish with false prestige and is proud. He is unfit for this task, therefore he has not been invited by me.

Therefore you should not speak such words again. All of you should make my yajna a success.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Daksa in the presence of all the gods and rsis, supported with arguments, the sage Dadhici said.

Dadhici said, “With Siva, this yajna would be termed as a yajna. Particularly your destruction is sure to happen in this yajna ”

Thus speaking the sage Dadhici, left the place of yajna alone, and went to his asrama.

All other people devoted to Siva also left the place pronouncing curse on Daksa.

With the departure of Dadhici and other sages like this, the evil-minded Daksa laughed and said.

Daksa said, “The Brahmana Dadhici and similar types of sage have left my place of yajna.

This has been well-done and I desired the same. Î Gods and the sages, I am speaking the truth.

The people who are slow-witted, senseless, rogues, indulging in false deliberations and discussions, are considered to be out of the Vedic circle. Such people with evil conduct are not fit enough to participate in the sacrificial rites.

Î Brahmanas, sages and the gods, all of you with Visnu should make my yajna fruitful.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the words of Daksa, the divine sages overpowered with the Ṅīóī of Siva, worshipped the deities in sacrifice. Î Sage, I have this explained the event of the cursing of the sacrifice of Daksa. Now I shall speak about the destruction of the sacrifice.

## Chapter 28 - Satø’s Travel

Brahma said, “When the gods and rsis delightfully went to the Daksa’s yajna, Sati at the same time was surrounded by her handmaids in the fountain house, under a canopy over the Gandhamadana mountain.

She was engaged in several types of sports. At the same time, she saw Rohini with Moon who was proceeding to attend the yajna of Daksa.

Seeing thus couple (Rohini and Moon), Sati asked Vijaya her chief maiden and her beloved friend, wishing her all welfare.

Sati said, “O beloved friend Vijaya, where is this moon going in the company of Rohini in such hurry, after taking leave of us?

Brahma said, “At these words of Sati, Vijaya herself went to the moon and asked him appropriately.” Where are you going at the moment.

Listening to the words of Vijaya, the moon respectfully told her about the purpose of his journey as well as the festivities in the house of Daksa in the form of a yajna.

Listening to the words of the moon, Vijaya at once returned to the Sati and apprised her of the factual position, as ascertained by her from the moon

Î hearing this, Sati- the goddess Kalika was immensely surprised. Then failing to understand the reason for it, she started thinking.

“Both Daksa and Vlrinl are my parents. How is it that they have failed to invite me? Have they forgotten their dear daughter?

I shall ask the reason for it from Siva.” Thus thinking, Sati decided to go to Siva. Thereafter, Sati, making her friend Vijaya to wait at that place, at once went to Siva.

Reaching the court of Siva, she found him surrounded by several attendants, Nandi and other great warriors.

Thus finding her husband Siva, so seated in his court, the daughter of Daksa went to Siva, to know about the reason.

Siva took Sati, lovingly in his lap and with great respect, he pleased her with his words.

Thereafter Siva, who could perform several types of sports, was the lord of. all and who could bestow pleasure to all, spoke to Sati with honour in the presence of his ganas.

Siva said, “O Slender waisted one, feeling surprised, why have you arrived in my court? You tell me at once the reason for the same.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, at these words of Siva, Sati said to the lord Siva, offering her salutation to him with folded hands.”

Sati said, “I have come to know that a great yajna with festivities is being held in the house of my father, in which the gods and the rsis are present.

Î Lord of the Devas, why are you not attending the yajna in the house of my father? You tell me?

To meet the friends by the friends is the sacred dharma. Î Mahadeva, ' you also increase the practice mutual love (with friends).

Î Master, you accept my request, making all the efforts, you accompany me to the yajna of my parent’s house to day itself.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the aforesaid words of Sati, Mahesvara spoke out the words, which had pierced into his heart and spoken by Daksa.

Siva said, “Î Goddess, your father Daksa is particularly inimical to me.

Those who are present there today, those gods and the rsis are not my own and are ignorant.

Î Goddess, those who go to the house of others without invitation, they have to face humiliation worse than death.

In case when Indra goes to any one uninvited, he also gets humiliated, what to speak of the others? Therefore, such a journey should not be undertaken.

Î My beloved, therefore, both of us should not attend the yajfia of Daksa. I am speaking the truth.

A person troubled by the enemies does not feel so painful as he is hurt with the evil words.

Î Beloved, the noble people, possessing the six virtues like vidya and others, are humiliated by the wicked people, because they are themselves deprived of those virtues.”

Brahma said, “At these words spoken by Siva- the supreme soul, Sati felt enraged and spoke to Siva, who was foremost of the fluent speakers.

Sati said, “O Siva, lord of all, by your presence the sacrifice of my father would ha -e become successful. But my evil-minded fathe- has failed to invite you today.

Î Lord Siva, I would like to know the trend of thoughts of the evil minded people today as well as those of the divine sages and all other wicked persons assembled there.

Therefore, Î Lord, I would like to go to the sacrifice of my father. Î Lord Siva, kindly grant me permission to do so.”

Brahma said, “Then lord Siva, possessing the perfect wisdom, realising everything and foreseeing all, being the cause of protection, at the request of the goddess, spoke to her.”

Siva said, “O Goddess, in case this is what is desired by you and if you think it needful to go, Î Righteous one, you can immediately go to your father’s sacrifice with my permission.

You can proceed with royal grace mounting the bull Nandi which is profusely decorated.”

Sati was then commanded to mount the caparisoned bull, and proceeded on her journey towards the house of her father.

The great lord Siva also gave her the royal paraphernalia like umbrella, flywhisks, silken clothes and ornaments, for proceeding on journey.

Sixty thousand of Siva’s attendants, delightfully accompanied her enthusiastically.

At that point of time great festivities were being performed at the place, of yajna. The attendants of Vamadeva also celebrated the festivities of Sati, the spouse of Siva.

Singing the glory of Siva and Siva, th\< valorous warriors of Siva, started dancing anc jumping here and there.

The journey of the mother of the universe was looking extremely graceful. All the three worlds were filled with the sound of victory.

## Chapter 29 - Declaration of Sati

The influential yajna in which the gods and demons had participated delightfully, Sati suddenly reached there, being the daughter of Daksa.

She found her father’s abode, filled with people with various moods. Who were quite beautiful, illustrious, including the gods and the rsis.

The goddess Sati got down from her mount Nandi and stood at the gate. Then she went alone at the place of yajna.

At the arrival of Sati, her mother Asikn! as well as her sisters welcomed her properly. But her father Daksa, having been influenced with the illusion of Siva, ignored her even after spotting her there and showed no respect for her. Terrified from Daksa, others too did not extend any respect to her.

Î Excellent sage, thus, having been immensely insulted and surprised, Sati, offered her salutation to her parents.

She observed the shares of Hari and other gods having been displayed in the yajna. Finding that no part of yajna had been assigned for Siva, she could not control her anger.

Thus having been humiliated by all, burning Daksa with the fire of her looks, she started gazing at him quite cruelly.

Sati said, “Why have you not invited Siva who is highly auspicious and by whom the entire mobile and immobile universe is sanctified.

How can a yajna be performed, without Siva, who is the form of yajna himself, the best among those who know about the yajna, is the part of yajna, besides being the performer of yajna!

With the mere remembering of whom everything is purified, and without him the entire performance is polluted.

The articles of offerings, the mantras, besides the havya and kavya are identical with Siva. How is this yajna being performed without him?

Did you insult him taking him to be like other ordinary gods? You have lost your wisdom and you are quite mean inspite of your being my father.

You are not aware of the prowess of Siva, by whose grace, Brahma, Visnu and other gods have attained their present positions.

How could Brahma, Visnu, the gods as well as the sages arrive in your yajna without Siva- their master?”

Brahma said, “Paramesvarl, who was the form of Siva, thus speaking, even rebuked Visnu and other gods, separately.

Sati said, “O Visnu, Siva, whose nirguna and saguna forms are described by the Vedas, you are well aware of the same Mahadeva.

Î Visnu, though Siva, educated you, saving you several times from the attack of the king Saiva and others.

Î Evil minded one, still there had been no enlightenment in your heart and you participated in this yajna, of Daksa, without the presence of your master.

Do you know, Brahma had become arrogant because of his five heads, then Siva reduced his heads to four. Have you forgotten that incident?

Î Indra, you are well aware of the prowess of Siva. The lord- performer of the difficult tasks, reduced your Vajra to ashes.

Î Gods, you are not aware of the prowess of Siva. Î Atri, Î Vasistha, what is all this, that has been done by you?

When Siva was begging alms in the Darukavana, you people had pronounced a curse on him.

At the pronouncing of the curse, Siva reduced to ashes all the mobile and immobile living beings of the world. How could you forget that incident so easily?

Brahma, Visnu and other gods have turned as fools, to arrive here to participate in the yajna, without the presence of Siva.

Siva, by whose grace, all the Vedas with their parts were created and Siva, cannot be known even by the knowledge of Vedanta

Brahma said, “Thus feeling painful at heart, the mother of the universe, then calmly feeling free from anger spoke variously.

Listening to her furious words all the gods like Visnu and others, besides the sages kept quiet getting frightened.

Thereafter Daksa listening to the words of his daughter, looking at her cruelly spoke.

Daksa said, “Presently, you have no business to talk much. It is immaterial whether you stay or go away. What for have you arrived here?

Siva, your husband is inauspicious and devoid of the graceful lineage and has been discarded by the Vedas. He is the king of goblins, ghosts and spirits. This aspect is well known to the learned people.

Therefore, Î Daughter, knowing fully well about Rudra’s being shabily dressed and indecent features, I did not invite him to this sacrifice attended to by the gods and the sages.

At the advice of the foolish and sinfu Brahma, without any deep thought I marriec you with that evil person.

Therefore shedding away the anger, you be calm. Since you have arrived in the yajna, you better receive your share of the same.”

Brahma said, “At these words of Daksa, the daughter of Daksa, who is adorable in the three worlds, looking at her father with contempt, felt further enraged.

Then she thought in her mind, “How can I now return to Siva. I would like to meet Siva, but in case he asks me (about the events which took place here), what reply shall I give?”

Thereafter full of wrath and breathing hard Sati, the mother of the three worlds, spoke to her evil minded father.

Sati said, “The one who rebukes Siva and the one who listens to such rebukes, both of them fall in the hell and they remain there till the sun and the moon last.

Therefore, I shall get rid of this body, entering the fire. Î Dear one, listening to the contemptuous words about my husband, remaining alive would be of no consequence.

In case a person himself is powerful enough, then he should cut off the tongue of the person who rebukes Siva and then purify himself.

In case he is not so strong enough, then he should cover his both the ears with his hands and leave the place. This is what the people of learning speak.”

Brahma said, “Sati then started repenting, stating the dictum of virtue. Then with a painful heart she remembered the advices given to her by Siva her husband.

Then becoming furious, she spoke to Daksa- her father, Visnu as well as the sages quite frankly.”

Sati said, “O Dear one, by rebuking Siva now, you are sure to repent later. You will suffer in this world, you are bound to face further torture.

There is no other person in the world, who hates Siva or is not well-disposed towards him. Who else could be inimical to Siva, except you?

There is no doubt that the degraded people, always denounce the noble people, but the greatness lies in the fact, in case one is able to remove his ignorance, with the application of the dust of the feet of such noble people.

A person who recites the name of Siva comprising of two letters even once, all his sins are washed out.

It is surprising that though the dictum of Siva cannot be transgressed, who is the holiest of the holy persons, you have been so wicked as to preserve an ill feeling against him. you are surely the enemy of Siva.

The lotus like feet of Siva are served by the minds of the noble people like the bees. He is the one who bestows the appropriate rewards to his devotees quite gracefully.

He is the one who showers fulfilment of the desires of his devotees, including the realising of the self.

Except you no one else including Brahma, Sanaka and other sages consider him to be inauspicious.

He lives in the cremation ground, with dishevelled locks of hair, with ghosts and goblins, wearing the garland of skulls, applying ashes over his body.

But the gods and the sages, place the dust of his feet over their heads. This is the nature of lord Siva, the great god.

Two types of deeds have been prescribed in the Vedas- direct and renunciatory. The learned people, differentiate between the two and hold that they cannot be simultaneous and cannot occur in a single entity. But Siva is the great Brahman and these actions have no effect on him.

Î Father, the paths of egoism which has been selected by you for travelling, should not be followed by you let the smoke of your yajnas'dla is not way laid.

This is the path followed by the AvadhUtas. Î Evil minded father, you should not be arrogant and conceited.

What more should I speak with my tongue? You are wicked and evil minded. My body, which is born of you is of no use to me now.

Disgrace to the birth in which the great people are denounced and rebuked. A person with wisdom, should cut off such a relationship.

Siva calls me DaksyayanI, because of your gotra and hearing it, I would feel painful henceforth.

Therefore, discarding this corpse and despised body, produced from your body, I shall gain happiness.

Î Gods, Î Sages, all of you should listen to my words. All of you having evil minds have conducted yourself improperly.

All of you are fools, quarrel-some as well as re-approach Siva. All of you are surely to be punished by Siva.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking to Daksa, Sati kept quiet and started reciting the name of Siva in her heart.

## Chapter 30 - Sati ends her life in fire-altar

Narada said, “O Brahma, when Sati, the beloved of lord Siva, became silent, what happened thereafter? You please speak out the same.”

Brahma said, “Sati then remembered her husband respectfully and then kept silent. Then becoming calm, she sat in the northern direction on the ground.

Sipping the water appropriately, she clad herself in the auspicious clothes, closing her eyes, she entered the yogic trance.

She kept her face steady balancing the ðãīñṁ and ṁðṁñṁ winds. Then she raised up the wind udana from the umbilical region and established it in the cardiac region, then taking it through the throat, finally she fixed it in the centre of the eyebrows.

Then she desired to cast off her body because of her anger with Daksa. By yogic practices she desired to bum off her body and retain the pure wind. In this position she devoted her mind towards her lord and nothing else.

Her body, which was free from all the sins, fell in the yogic fire and was reduced to ashes. Î Excellent sage, she did so as per her own wish.

On observing this terrific disturbance was created on the earth as well as the sky, which frightened even the gods.

It is a pity, that having been antagonised by a wicked person, the beloved of Siva, cast off her life.

“The foolishness of Daksa is quite surprising, who happens to be the son of Brahma, having the mobile and immobile living beings as his subjects.

Alas! Sati, the noble beloved of the bull- bannered Siva, became dispirited and disgusted. She should have been appropriately honoured.

The wicked Daksa Prajapati, has an evil mind and is inimical to Brahman. His defame will surely spread in the entire universe.

Daksa is the one who humiliated the girl born of his own body simply for the sake of his enmity with Siva. He, after his death, would fall in the terrific hell.”

When the people indulged in such a type to talk, and observing the surprising end of Sati’s life, suddenly all the attendants of Siva, rose up holding their weapons.

All attendants of Siva filled with anger situated on the gate were great mighty and through the favour of Siva they became furious.

The attendants of Siva, shouted loudly ha, fie, no, no, repeatedly. The sound of the cries of Siva’s attendants was spread everywhere. The gods and the sages who collected there, were terror stricken who said repeatedly, “Disgrace to us.”

The tumultuous cries of those people echoed in all the four directions and all the gods and the sages gathered there were frightened.

The enraged attendants of Siva, after confabulations among themselves, took up their arms and creating the scene of the time of dissolution, raised tumultuous sound, which was spread in all the directions.

Î Narada, some of the ganas having been overpowered with grief, cut off their own limbs with sharp weapons.

In this way twenty thousand gunas of Siva died with Sati, which was a surprising event.

Such of the ganas of Siva, who escaped death, they got up to kill Daksa with their weapons.

Î Excellent sage, thus learning about attack by the ganas of Siva, some of the sages with the use of the mantras meant for the destruction of the obstacles in the yajna performed homo in the sacrificial fire.

Soon after the pouring of the offerings in the fire-altar by Bhrgu, thousands Rbhu warriors rose up from the fire of yajna.

Î Excellent sage, those warriors holding the fire as the weapon, fought a terrific war with the ganas of Siva.

The powerful Rbhus had the Brahmateja with them and with the application of the same the pramathas or Siva’s ganas were destroyed in large number.

In this way with the enormous force some of the attendants of Siva were killed and routed quickly, while others fled away from the scene. This was a great surprise.

Observing this, Indra and other gods, Maruta-ganas, rsis, Visvedevas, Asvini- kumaras and the lokapalas kept silent at that time.

Some of the people surrounded lord Visnu and started eulogising him. Feeling disturbed, they thought that no obstruction in any form should be caused.

The gods of noble wisdom like Visnu and others then started thinking, “What shall happen further? All of them became upset because they were unable to remove the misfortune.

Î Excellent sage, in this way a disturbance was created in the yajna of the wicked Daksa- the son of Brahma, who was inimical to Siva.

## Chapter 31 - The divine voice

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, at the same time, a divine voice was heard in presence of Daksa and the gods.

The divine voice declared, “O Wicked, evil-minded and immensely foolish Daksa, why have you committed the unfortunate misdeed?

Î Fool, you did not listen even to the blissful Dadhici, the Supreme follower of Siva.

The Brahmanas left your yajna, pronouncing the unbearable curse, still your foolish heart was unable to understand the factual position. Then you showed no respect to your own daughter, who arrived at your place of your own accord.

Î Ignorant one, you did not adore Siva and Sati. Î Fool, you have uselessly become arrogant, thinking yourself to be the son of Brahma.

Sati should always be adored, because she bestows reward for all the merits. She is the mother of the three worlds. She bestows welfare on all and is lodged to the left of Siva.

Sati, the bestower of the fortunes should always be worshipped, she is Mahesvarl, and brings fortunes on all her devotees.

With her daily adoration, she removes the fear of the universe. She fulfills all the desires, and removes all the disturbances.

With her adoration daily she bestows fame and riches. She is the great goddess, Paramesvarl who bestows pleasures as well as salvation.

Sati is the mother of universe and protects the same. She is the eternal force. She destroys the universe at the end of the kalpa.

The same Sati is the mother of the world, mother of Visnu, has the diverse shining features, besides being the mother of Brahma, Indra, the moon, the sun and the gods.

Sati alone is the bestower of the fruits of penance, dharma, charity etc. She is Siva’s Sakti, Mahadevi, destroyer of the wicked people besides being the Supreme deity.

Thus you have failed to offer the due share of Siva, who happens to be the husband of Sati. You are a fool and an evil minded one.

Siva is the supreme lord, is the master of all, the greatest of the great, worthy of being served by Visnu. He bestows welfare to all.

The Siddhas perform penance in order to have an audience with him. the yogis perform meditation and yogic exercises, in order to have a look at him.

With the mere audience with Siva, one achieves enormous fruits, endless wealth and cereals besides the reward for performing of yajna.

Siva happens to be the creator of the universe and is the possessor of all the vidyas (lores). He is the upholder of the primordial knowledge and is the most auspicious of all the auspicious beings.

Î Wicked person, you have disregarded his Sakti today. Therefore, your yajna is going to be destroyed.

By ignoring the adoration of the adorable people, one invites misfortune for himself. Was the most adorable Siva, not worthy of adoration?

The dust of whose feet is applied by the serpent Sesa over his thousand heads, Siva happens to be the Sakti of the same lord.

It is due to the meditation at the feet of Siva, that Visnu has achieved his exalted position. Sati had been the dear wife of the same Siva.

By meditating at whose lotus like feet, Brahma attained his present form, Sati was the beloved wife of the same Siva.

By adoring whose lotus like feet, Indra and other Lokapalas, achieved their respective positions, the same Siva is the creator of the universe and Sati is the mother of the universe. Î Foolish one, you could not welcome her. Then how could you gain welfare.

Because you failed to adore Siva and Sati, enormous misfortunes have befallen on you.

Your pride that would not achieve welfare without adoring Siva, has been shattered today.

By becoming inimical to Siva, the lord of all, which one of the gods would come to your rescue? I don’t find anyone in the world.

In case the gods would come to your rescue, they would meet with destruction in the same way as the fire fly is destroyed by the fire flame.

Let your face be burnt today. Let your yajna be destroyed. Whosoever comes to your rescue today, he would surely be burnt alive.

All the gods are placed under an oath, that they should cause misfortune for you because of your being wicked.

All the gods should leave for their respective abodes, keeping themselves away from the yajna, otherwise all of them are sure to meet with destruction.

The sages, Nagas and others-should leave the yajna-mandapa otherwise, they would also face destruction.

Î Lord Visnu, you also leave the place of yajna, otherwise you will also face destruction.

Î Brahma, you also leave the place of yajna at once, otherwise you will also perish today.”

Brahma said, “Thus addressing all the people present in the yajna the divine voice, which meant welfare for all, stopped.

Î Dear one, listening to the divine voice, Visnu and other gods, besides the sages, disappeared.

## Chapter 32 - Birth of Virabhadra and Siva’s advice to him

Narada said, “What did the foolish Daksa Prajapati do with other people (present there) after learning of the words of the divine voice.

After the defeat of the Siva’s ganas with the strength of the mantras of the sage Bhrgu, (all kept mum) and no one spoke a word to anyone else. All of them stood perplexed and stunned.

Some of the ganas of Siva, escaped the force of mantras of the sage Bhrgu and took refuge with Siva.

They apprised Siva of the factual position about the yajna of Daksa, with respect.”

The ganas said, “O Mahadeva, you are superior to the gods, therefore you kindly protect us since we have taken refuge with you. Î Lord, you kindly listen to the episode of Sati in detail.

Î Siva, the arrogant and wicked Daksa and the gods, insulted Sati. They did not display your share of the yajna, though they did so for the other gods. The same wicked Daksa abused you.

Finding your share absent in the yajna, Sati felt enraged and she burnt herself jumping in the fire alter.

Feeling shameful, then thousands of ganas ended their lives there itself, while many others severed their limbs there itself.

When we got ready to destroy the yajna, then Bhrgu, your enemy, drove us out from that place.

Î Lord of the universe, Î Master, now we have arrived here to take refuge with you, therefore you free us from the fear. We are grieved and stricken with terror.

Î Lord of Lord! the wicked Daksa and others showered enormous insults on you in that sacrifice.

Î Bestower of boons, in this way, we conveyed the entire news about Sati and ourselves to you. Now you can move against those fools as you deem fit.”

Brahma said, “Thus lord Siva, listened to the words of his ganas and he remembered Narada in order to know the factual position from him.

Then the divine sage arrived there at once and offering his salutation to Siva he stood there with his hands folded.

Then praising you, Siva asked you about the news of Sati, who had gone to the yajna of Daksa.

Î Son, when thus asked by Siva, then you, being the devotee of Siva, at once, revealed the true happenings in the yajna of Daksa.

Î sage! Listening to your words, the immensely valorous Siva was enraged.

Then Rudra, the destroyer of the universe, plucked a lock of hair from his head and threw it over the mountain.

Î Master, with the throwing of the lock of hair, it was turned into two pieces and the deafening sound resembling the sound of the time of dissolution was heard.

Î Divine sage, from the fore-part of the matted lock of hair, the immensely terrific and great warrior who was the leader of his force, known as Virabhadra was born.

He looked like the flames of the fire of the time of dissolution, having two thousand hands. He enveloped the world all around and towered over it ten inches more.

At that time with the enraged breathing of Siva, a hundred types of fevers, and thirteen types of mental humours came out.

From the other part of the matted lock of hair, Mahakali was born. Î Dear one, she was terrible to look at, and was surrounded by crores of goblins.

All the fevers were frightening to look at, cruel, and appeared like burning all round.

Thereafter Virabhadra, offered his salutation to Siva with folded hands and said.

Virabhadra said, “O Maharudra, Î Rudra of terrific appearance, having the sun, moon and the fire as your eyes, Î Lord, get me your command, what have I to do?

Î Lord, you tell me, should I dry up the ocean in the fraction of a moment, or reduce the mountain to powder.

Î Siva, tell me, should I reduce the entire globe into ashes in a moment'? I can reduce to ashes all gods and sages.

Î Siva, should I stop the breathing of the universe or should I kill all the living beings of the world?

Î Mahesvara, with your grace, nothing is impossible for me. A person more valorous than me has neither appeared on earth in the past, nor shall be appear in future.

Î Lord, what ever task is entrusted to me at any place, I shall perform it in no time by your grace.

Î Siva, by your grace even the degraded people cross the ocean of the universe, can I not cross the ocean of misfortunes?

Î Lord, even a blade of grass sent by you would accomplish enormous task, without any difficulty in moment. There is no doubt above it.”

Though all the tasks, Î Siva, get established by your grace only, but you still send me with your grace. Î Lord Siva. I possess this strength by your grace.

Î Lord Siva, I possess this strength by your grace only. None without your grace will have the same strength and enthusiasm.

This is true and there is no doubt about it that without your command and permission no one would be able to move even the blade of grass.

Î Siva, all the gods and others are under command. I am also subject to your command issued by you. You are the controller of all the living beings.

Î Siva, I offer my salutation to you again and again. You kindly depute me today for the success of your task.

Î Siva, my right limbs are throbbing repeatedly, therefore my victory is certain. Therefore, Î Lord, you please send me.

There is special types of delight and enthusiasm in my mind. My mind is devoted to your lotus like feet.

Therefore, auspicious thing are going to happen at every step.

Indeed, he alone is victorious forever, he alone meets with welfare as well, daily, who is firmly devoted to you and whose mind is immensely devoted to you.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of Virabhadra, Lord Siva, the spouse of Sati, felt delighted and said, “O Virabhadra, by victorious.”

You listen to me, whatever has to be done by you there, which would delight me.

Presently, Daksa Prajapati, the son of Brahma, is getting ready to perform a yajna. He is my adversary besides being a wicked, unwise and conceited person.

You reduce his yajna as well as those present there to ashes. Thereafter, Î VTrabhadra, the best of my gunas, you return to me quickly.

The gods, Gandharvas, Yaksas and others, whosoever be present there should be reduced to ashes. Even if Visnu, Brahma, Indra or Yama are present there, fell them to the ground making all the stremous efforts.

Disobeying the command of the sage Dadhici, whosoever is found in the yajna, should be burnt by you alone.

In case Visnu and other gods arrive with the pramathas, then reciting several types of the attractive mantras, burn them out.

Whosoever be present there disobeying my oath, feeling proud, would be inimical to me and you should burn them with fire flames.

The people present in the yajna of Daksa, should be reduced to ashes with their riches and wives as well. Then you return to me. Though on your arrival Visnu and other gods would praise you respectfully, but you should burn them all.

All the gods inimical to me be burnt in fire flames. Have no worry at that time of any sort.

Î Great warrior, you should bum Daksa, with his wife and relatives and thereafter delightfully drink water.”

Brahma said- Siva the slayer of Kala, the protector of the Vedic conventions, after thus speaking to Virabhadra, the great hero, stopped talking, with his eyes burning like the copper (in anger).

## Chapter 33 - The march of Vsrabhadra

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of Siva, respectfully, Virabhadra was pleased and he offered his salutation to the lord.

Accepting the command of Siva- the god of gods he marched towards the yajnamandapa of Daksa.

For the purpose of his grace, Siva made crores of his terrific ganas, who were terrific like the fire of the time of dissolution.

Thereafter the valorous ganas, anxiously marched on in front of and behind Virabhadra.

The ganas accompanying Virabhadra, were the warriors of Siva, who happened to be the death for the god of death.

The terrific Virabhadra, had the same dress as well as the features, besides the establishments like Siva and he moved ahead in a chariot. He had a thousand arms each one of which resembled the hood of the serpent king. He looked horrible and terrifying.

The chariot was four hundred hands in length and ten thousand lions were yoked in it.

His guards included several lions, tigers, crocodiles, fishes and the elephants in thousands.

At the start of Virabhadra for the destruction of Daksa, the flowers of kalpavrksa were showered at that time.

The goddesses like Kali, Katyayani, Isani, Camunda, MundamardinI, Bhadrakali, Bhadra, Tvarita, Vaisnavi, Mahakali, Bhairava, and Ksetrapalas, at the command of Siva, quickly marched on for the destruction of the yaina of Daksa.

Besides the Dakinis, Sakinis, pramathaganas, Guhyakas, Kusmandas, Parpatas, Catakas, Brahmardksas, Bhairvas and Ksetrapalas, obeying the command of Siva started for the destruction of Daksa’s sacrifice.

Similarly the sixty four yoginis marched on for the destructions of the yajna of Daksa.

Î Narada, listen to the number of the ganas of Siva of various groups.

The Ganadhisvaras named Sankukarna and Kekaraksa, had ten crores of ganas each, while Vikrta was accompanied by eight crore of gunas.

Visakha had sixty four crores, Pariyatraka had nine crores. Sarvankaka had six crores, Vira Vikrtana six crores, Jvalakesa, the best of the ganas had twelve crores, Dhiman, seven crores, Dudrabha eight crores, Kapallsa five crores, Sandaraka six crores, Kotikunta one crore, Vistambha, the best of ganas- eight crores, Sannad and Pippala with a thousand crores each, Avesana went with eight crores and Candratapana with the same number. Mahavesa the leader of ganas was surrounded by a thousand crores of gunas.

Î Excellent sage, Kundi and Pavataka- had twelve crores each. All of them accompanied with their respective ganas marched on for the destruction of the yajna of Daksa.

Kala, Kalaka and Mahakala accompanied with hundred crores of ganas each went to destroy the yajna of Daksa.

Agnikrta had a hundred crores, while Agnimukha with a crore, Adityamurdha and Ghanavaha had a hundred crores of gunas with them.

Sannaha had twenty five crores; Kumuda, Amogha and Kokila- the lords of the ganas, had a hundred crores with each one of them.

Kasthagudha, Sukesi, Vrsabha and Ganadhipa Sumantra were accompanied with sixty four crores of ganas each.

Kokapadodara and Santanaka, foremost among the ganas had sixty crore ganas each.

The Ganadhipa named Mahabala was accompanied with nine crores of ganas.

Madhupinga and Purnabhadra, the lords of the ganas marched with ninety crores of ganas each.

Caturvaktra had a hundred crore ganas, while Kasthagodha, Sukesa, Vrsabha, Virupaksa, Talaketu, Pancasya, Sadasya, were accompanied by sixty four crores each.

Samvartaka, Kulisa, Lokantaka, Diptatma, Daityantaka, Bhrgniriti, Devadeapriya, As'ani and Bhalaka arrived with sixty four crores of ganas each.

The Virabhadra the leader of the great warriors, at the command of Siva, surrounded by crores of ganas, reached there.

The hero was accompanied by thousand of crores of goblins and three crores of canine species born from the hair of Siva. He went ahead quite quickly.

Trumpets and drums were sounded aloud; The conches were blown in diverse ways, besides the horns of several kinds.

In such a pleasing atmosphere, several of the musical instruments were played upon delightfully.

While the march of Virabhadra was in progress, Î Great sage, several auspicious and pleasing omens occurred.

## Chapter 34 - Inauspicious omens witnessed by those present at the place of Daksa’s sacrifice

Brahma said, “Thus with the departure of Virabhadra with innumerable ganas, Daksa Prajapati as well as the gods, rsis, sages and the Brahmanas present at the place of óajna witnessed several inauspicious omens.

At the time of the start of Virabhadra with the ganas, three types of disturbances indicative of he destruction of the yajna appeared.

The left eye, arm and leg of Daksa started throbbing. Î Dear one, these symptoms were indicative of some evil and inauspiciousness, which caused harassment to him.

The place of the yajna of Daksa was shaken by earthquakes. Daksa also witnessed the astonishing types of constellations in the sky at noon.

The directions became dusty and the sun disc was faded out and spotted and thousands of horrible circles appeared around it.

The stars which were bright like the lightening or fire started falling from the sky. The constellations started moving on the opposite direction and downwards.

Hundreds of vultures started flying touching the head of Daksa. The yajna-mandapa was covered with shade of the wings spreaded by the vultures.

In the place of yajna of Daksa jackals and the owls started howling. The rain of white scorpions and comets started falling.

The winds carrying the dust or dust storms started blowing with great force, in which the locusts and the moths were carried in the whirlwind.

With the blowing of the forceful winds, the yajna-mandapa of Daksa started flying in t he air with the force of the wind. This was a new surprise in the yajna of Daksa, in which the gods were present.

Daksa and all others present at that site started vomiting blood, with pieces of flesh and bones, quite frequently.

All of them started shaking as the lamp flickers with the blowing of wind. All those present there felt painful like a person who is injured with a weapon.

Because of the crying and weeping the rain of tears started falling like the fall of frost in the morning over the forest of lotus flowers.

Sometimes the eyes of Daksa were shone like the blossoming lotus flowers during the day and sometimes like the flowers at night.

Showers of blood started falling from the sky. The directions were covered with darkness. All the directions went in flames, which disturbed all.

Observing the obstructions, Visnu and the gods, the sages, the Brahmanas and others felt extremely frightened.

All of them while fainting cried, “We are dead” and fell on the ground, as the trees standing at the bank of the river fall with the force of water.

All of them fell down over the ground like the one having been bitten by a snake like the ball and then again got up.

Then feeling miserable, they cried like the sparrow. Their groaning and cries got mingled with one another.

At that point of time the strength of all including Visnu, was faded out. All of them started rolling and dashing with one another like the tortoise.

In the meantime the divine voice from the sky was heard aiming at Daksa particularly besides the other gods.

The divine voice said, “O Daksa, you are foolish and sinful. Disgrace to your birth. You will have to face many painful situations, because of Siva.

It is pity that all the god present here will also have to face miseries, because of you. There is no doubt about it.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Akasavam (divine voice) and witnessing the disturbances in the yajna all the gods felt panicky.

With his body shaking and feeling nervous, Daksa took refuge with Visnu, the lord of Indra.

Feeling frightened, praising Visnu, he offered his salutation to Visnu, who is the god of gods and is merciful to all. He said to the lord.”

## Chapter 35 - Visnu’s speech

Daksa Prajapati said, “O Hari, the god of gods, Î Visnu, Î Friend of the poor, Î Ocean of mercy, you protect me as well as the yajna.

You are the form of yajna, performer of the yajna besides being the protector of yajna. Î Lord you shower your compassion over me in such a way that my yajna is not destroyed.”

Brahma said, “Thus Daksa Prajapati, respectfully offering prayer to lord Visnu, feeling frightened, fell at his feet.

The evil minded Daksa with painful heart, was lifted up by Visnu and listening to his words remembered lord Siva.

Remembering his lord Siva, Visnu being well-versed in the Siva-tattva, then spoke to Daksa.”

Lord Visnu said, “O Daksa, I, for the sake of your welfare, speak out a mantra.

Î Daksa, being unaware of the Siva-tattva, you have insulted Siva, the lord of all.

By showing disregard to Siva not only the task is spoilt, but one has to face misfortunes at every moment.

The place where the unadorable ones are worshipped, and those adorable are not adored, the poverty, fear and death are commonly found there. Therefore you should show honour to Siva in all respects. The present calamity has been due to your insulting him.

Presently because of your misconduct, all of us have lost our grace. This is the truth.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Visnu, Daksa felt worried. His face was faded out. He sat there keeping silent.

In the meantime Virabhadra- the leader of the ganas of Siva, who had been specifically deputed by Siva, arrived there at the place of yajna.

Some of the gunas followed him, some of them flew in the sky, while others arrived from the different directions and subdirections. At the instance of Siva, these innumerable valorous, fearless, gunas arrived roaring like the lions.

With the terrific sound which echoed in the three worlds, all the quarters were filled with darkness.

The earth containing the seven continents, was shaken with terror, the earth with mountains and forests, started shaking and all the oceans felt agitated.

In this way seeing that large army of Siva, ready for destruction, all the gods and others became surprised.

Finding the destructive efforts of the army of Virabhadra, Daksa, vomiting blood, fell at the feet of Visnu with his wife and said.

Daksa Prajapati said, “O Lord Visnu, I had started this yajna depending on you and the success of the same lies in your hands.

Î Visnu, you are the witness of all the deeds, besides being the protector of the yajnas. You are also the protector of Brahma as well as the Vedic religion.

Therefore, Î Lord, you protect my yajna. Who else except you, can protect this yajna, because you happen to be the lord of all.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the piteous words of Daksa, Visnu tried to enlighten him.

Lord Visnu said, “O Daksa, I shall protect your yajna because I have taken a truthful vow that I protect the dharma.

The words thus spoken by me are true and cannot be otherwise. Î Daksa, I tell you, that you shed away your cruel thoughts.

Î Evil minded Daksa, have you forgotten the surprising type of incident that occurred in the Naimisaranya forest?

Who is the person on earth to protect you from the wrath of Siva. Only an evil minded person would ever try to protect you.

What is beyond an evil minded person? He only becomes desirous of establishing his task.

You think it as your deed which is within the competence of a person. Without Siva no one else would be able to bestow on you the reward of your deeds.

The one who devotes his mind towards the lord with a peaceful mind, only he achieves reward for the same from Siva.

Those, who, depending on their learnings, insult the lord they have to live in the hell for hundreds of crores of kalpas in the hell.

Then, having been caught in the bondages of the deeds they are rotten in the hell for many births.

The lord of Rudra, born out of the fire of Siva’s anger, and destroyer of the enemies, is arriving in the place of the yajna.

He has surely arrived here for our destruction. Actually there is nothing beyond his capacity.

The immensely powerful (Virabhadra) would feel peaceful at heart after burning out all of us. There is no doubt about it.

In utter confusion I transgressed the oath of Mahadeva by siding with you. Because of that I also shall have to face the agony.

I am not at all competent to remove the calamity that has befallen on you. I have also revolted against Siva, by siding with you.

A person who is inimical to lord Siva, can never feel comfortable. Therefore I shall also have to face the misery with you today.

The Sudarsana-cakra will be ineffective on him because it is a weapon of Siva and a person not devoted to Siva can only be killed with it.

In case I use this Cakra against Virabhadra, it would return to Siva, without harming him in any way.

It is because of the grace of lord Siva that this Cakra still remains with me even after my violating the vow of Siva.

Thereafter, this Cakra cannot remain with me. With the flames of fire emerging out of it, it will leave me just now.

In case we adore Virabhadra respectfully but because of his being in angry mood, he would never protect us.

It is a matter of great pity that we are facing untimely destruction and I shall also be destroyed with you.

Presently, there is no one in the three worlds to save us. Who is the shelter of the enemy of Siva in this world?

Even after death, we shall have to face terrific torture of Yama. Who will be able to bear them?

Finding an enemy of Siva, Yama, grinding his teeth, throws such sinners in the pan filled with boiling oil.

I am prepared to go against the oath, but how shall I be absolved of the sin of siding with a wicked person?

Even in case we flee from this place Virabhadra, the devotee of Siva, will drag and pull us back with his tiller weapons.

Wherever we might stay in the heaven, earth and the nether world, the weapons of Virabhadra would surely reach there.

Such is the power of all the ganas (attendants) of the trident holder Rudra.

Kalabhairava at Kasi had cut off Brahma’s head even by scratching with the nails.”

Thus speaking, the extremely nervous Visnu, kept quiet. In the meantime Virabhadra also reached the yajncimandapa with his army. All the gods looked at Virabhadra.

## Chapter 36 - Talk between Visnu and Virabhadra

Brahma said, “Indra holding the Vajra in his hand laughed at Visnu listening to his talk, and got ready to wage a war on behalf of the gods.

At that point of time Indra was mounted over the elephant, Agni over the ram, Yama over the he-buffalo, Nirrti over the ghost, Varuna over crocodile, Vayu over the deer, Kubera over the Puspaka plane and got ready for waging a war.

Besides the glorious groups of gods, Yaksas, Caranas and Guhyakas, were mounted over their respective vehicles.

Observing the efforts of the gods, vomiting blood from his mouth, Daksa together with his wife went to those gods and spoke.

Daksa Prajapati said, “I had started this huge yajna with your strength. All of you possessing the immense prowess are competent to protect the same.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of Daksa, all the gods moved on for waging a war.

Then having been overpowered with the illusion of Siva, Indra, Lokapalas besides other valorous gods started fighting with the ganas of Siva.

Then the gods as well as the Siva ganas started fighting with one another using the sharp spears and arrows.

The war instruments like the conches were blown, drums were beaten, big and small battle drums were sounded.

Getting encouraged by that sound, the gods together with the lokapalas, hit and thrashed the ganas of Siva.

Î Excellent sage, on account of the incantations of Bhrgu, the ganas of Siva were driven out by Indra and other lokapalas.

The sacrificial priest Bhrgu caused the defeat of the ganas of Siva, to continue the proceedings of the yajna, besides pleasing Daksa.

Finding his gunas having been defeated, Virabhadra felt defeated. Therefore he set the goblins, ghosts and spirits after them.

Mounted over the bull, the ganas were deputed in the, front. Together with his forces Virabhadra holding a trident in his hand felled the god.

He killed all the gods, Yaksas, Sadhyas, Guhyakas, Caranas with his trident.

Some of then were cut off with his sword and the others with clubs. Rest of the devas were attacked with the other weapons.

The gods, thus having been defeated in the war, deserting their other associates fled away to the heaven.

Only mighty Indra and other Lokapalas stood there courageously in the great war.

All the gods then collectively went to Brhaspati- the preceptor of the gods and enquired of him.

The lokapalas said, “O Intelligent preceptor Brhaspati, you tell us the way to be victorious?

Brahma said, “On hearing these words of the Lokapalas, Brhaspati, remembering in his heart lord Siva, said to the foolish Indra.

Brhaspati said, “Whatever had been stated by lord Visnu earlier, it is happening today. Î Indra, I repeat his words again and you listen to me attentively.

The one who is Is'vara is the bestower of the reward of all the karmas. He does so with reference to the performer. He himself is unable to do anything.

Neither mantras nor the medicinal herbs, nor the black magic, nor the worldly activities, nor the Vedas, nor the two systems of mlmamsas nor other sacred texts, based on Vedic hymns, are able to know Siva. This has been declared by the ancient acaryas.
