Even a person well-versed in all the Vedas would not be able to know well about Siva. The Vedas declare that he could be known only to the people who are totally devoted to him.

Lord Siva could be known only by the peaceful and umblemished vision or by his grace alone.

Inspite of that, Î Indra, in the matter of what should be done and what not, I shall explain this aspect of the fulfilment of one’s desire. You listen to the same in your own interest.

Out of foolishness, Î Indra, you have participated in the yajna of Daksa with Lokapalas out of ignorance. What type of prowess are you going to display

These ganas with the help of Siva, getting enraged are participating in the war for the purpose of total destruction and they shall return after doing so.

No one’s efforts here for the protection of the yajna would prove successful.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of Brhaspati, Indra and other Lokapalas from the heaven felt worried.

Then Virabhadra who had been surrounded by the powerful ganas, remembering Siva said to Indra and other Lokapalas.

Virabhadra said, “All of you out of foolishness have arrived here for getting honoured. You come to me and I shall bestow honour on you, Î Indra, Agni, Sun, Moon, Kubera, Varuna, Vayu, Niriti, Yama, Serpent Sesa, groups of gods and demons.

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, Virabhadra, the best among the ganas of Siva getting enraged, shot arrows at all the gods, who getting injured, fled away to all the ten direction. After the fleeing of the Lokapalas and the gods Virabhadra went to the place of yajna with his ganas.

All the frightened sages then started praying to lord Visnu quickly bowing down repeatedly.

The Rsis said, “O God of gods, Î Lord of Rama, Î Lord of all, Î Supreme Lord, protect the yajna of Daksa, you are yourself the form of yajna.

You are the performer of yajna, the form of yajna, part of yajna. Protect it. Because none else can do so.

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of rsis, lord Visnu got ready to fight with Virabhadra.

Holding Cakra and other weapons in his four hands, he moved out of the yajna- mandapa with all the gods.

Virabhadra on the other hand holding a trident in his hand, accompanied with inriumerable gams found Visnu ready for waging a war.

Looking at Visnu, Virabhadra frowned at him in the same way as the lion frowns at the sight of the elephant or Yama gets enraged at the sight of a sinner.

Finding Visnu in that position, the enraged Virabhadra, the killer of the enemies, quickly said to Visnu.

Virabhadra, said, “O Visnu, how could you dare to disregard the pledge of lord Siva? Are you feeling proud at heart?

Have you strength enough to transgress the vow of Siva? Who are you? Who is your protector in the three worlds?

Why did you arrive here? Am I not aware of it? You tell me, how could you be the protector of the yajna of Daksa.

Did you not notice the performance of Sati? Did you not listen to the words of Dadhici? You have arrived in the yajna of Daksa in order to receive honour? Î Long armed one, I shall bestow reward on you (by cutting you to pieces).

Î Visnu, I shall tear out your chest with the attack of a trident. Who is there to protect you? Let him come to me.

I shall, after felling you on earth, bum you with fire and shall pound you thereafter.

Î Wicked, Visnu, the worst hater of Siva, are you unaware of the auspicious greatness of Siva? Î Long armed one, in case you are standing before me for a fight, then be steady, I shall despatch you to the place of no return.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Virabhadra, Visnu said, laughingly, “O Virabhadra, you listen from me today. I am the servant of Siva. Don’t call me ante-Rudra.

Daksa- the performer of the religious rites daily, requested me repeatedly for the performing of the yajna. But out of ignorance, he is unaware of the related secret.

I am subservient to my devotees and same is the case with Siva. Daksa is a devotee of mine. That is why I have arrived in the yajna.

Î Warrior, you have been born out of Siva’s anger, you listen to my vow. You are the form of the tejas of Rudra, therefore, Î Lord, you are quite glorious.

I shall withstand you. You can try to stop me. Whatever is destined, let it happen. I shall surely display my strength.’

Brahma said, “Hearing these words of Visnu, the long armed Virabhadra laughed and said, “I feel delighted to know that you are dear to my lord.”

Then laughing loudly Virabhadra, the best of the gunas, spoke humbly to Visnu, with delight.

Virabhadra said, “O Supreme lord, I had spoken the words in order to test your feelings. I shall now speak right earnestly. You listen to me attentively.

Virabhadra said, “As is Siva, so are you, Î Supreme lord, and as are you, so is Siva. Î Visnu, this has been ordained by the Vedas, at the command of Siva.

At the command of Siva, all happen to be his servants. We work at the command of Siva. Still out of respect we argue and speak like this.”

Brahma said, “Thus Sri Visnu listening to the words of Virabhadra, said to him smilingly.

Visnu said, “Î Valorous one, you can fight with me without any hesitation. Having been wounded by your arrows all over the body, I shall return to my place.

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, lord Visnu kept quiet, getting ready for the battle. The immensely powerful Virabhadra also got ready for the battle with the support of his ganas.

## Chapter 37 - Destruction of the yajna of Daksa

The immensely powerful Virabhadra, mentally adoring Siva, the remover of all the misfortunes, got ready to fight with Visnu.

Being the destroyer of all the enemies, he mounted over the excellent chariot, carrying the best of weapons, and started roaring like a lion.

Visnu on the other hand, blew the conch Pancajanya, which delighted the people on his side.

Listening to the sound of the conch, the gods who had fled away from the battle field returned to the same place.

Mighty Indra and other Lokapalas then started fighting with the ganas of Virabhadra roaring like a lion.

Roaring like the lion, the Sivaganas fought a terrific battle with Indra and Lokapalas.

Indra, Agni and Kubera fought with Nandi, Asman and Kubera with Kusmandapati, respectively.

Nandi was hit hard by Indra, with his thunderbolt having a hundred spikes. Indra was wounded in the middle of the chest, with the trident by Nandi.

In this way both the warriors started fighting enthusiastically with each other. They fought with each other variously with the desire of victory.

Then the fire god, getting immensely enraged, hit Asman with his spear, who in turn, having been filled with anger, attacked the fire god with a trident.

Mahaloka the chief of his ganas, meditating on Siva in his mind, delightfully fought a horrible battle with Yama.

The valorous Canda, attacking Nirrti with his astonishing types of weapons, fought with him.

The immensely strong Munda, carrying the divine weapons, fought with Varuna, carrying the huge spear.

Bhrngi the glorious one, attacked over the wind god, with his trident, while the wind god wounded Bhrngi with his weapons.

The valorous, Kusmandapati, with his mind devoted to Mahesvara, started fighting with Kubera.

The leader Bhairavi in association with the yoginis, tore out the bodies of the gods and drank their blood.

Ksetrapalas, devoured the gods. Mahakali on the other tore out several gods and drank their blood.

The exceedingly brilliant Visnu, then started fighting and shot his cakra on them, which could bum all the ten directions.

When Ksetrapala found the cakra fast approaching him he ran towards it and bravely caught hold of it and swallowed it.

Then Visnu- the conqueror of the enemy cities, finding his Cakra having been swallowed, caught hold of his neck and made him vomit out the cakra.

The valorous lord Visnu who is the sole protector of the world, carrying his cakra, started fighting with several of the Sivaganas.

Lord Visnu started fighting with demons, who were attacking him with several weapons.

Bhairava and other Sivaganas, on the other hand, started fighting, quite enthusiastically carrying several weapons, getting furious.

Thus witnessing the terrific war, Visnu, possessing enormous prowess, again started fighting with them.

Thereafter splendid lord Visnu, who was blinded in anger, holding his disc fought with Virabhadra.

Î sage, a terrible fight provoking harripilation took place between Mahavira and Varuna with various weapons.

With the yogic power of Visnu, innumerable four-armed warriors were created holding conch, Cakra and clubs in their hands.

All of them were as strong as Visnu himself, they started fighting with Virabhadra.

Virabhadra, on the other hand, with his mind devoted to Siva, he attacked them all with a trident, killing them at the same time.

Thereafter in the battlefield, the powerful Virabhadra, attacked Visnu at his chest with his trident.

With that attack Visnu, suddenly fell over the battle ground getting fainted.

Then a wonderful lustre, terrible like the fire, of the time of dissolution emerged at that place, which looked like burning all the three worlds. It was quite severe and frightened even the great warriors.

The glorious lord Visnu with his eyes becoming red in anger, got up again and started fighting again holding the Cakra.

His cakra, which had the lustre of the sun of the time of dissolution, was made inactive by Siva, which Visnu was about to shoot at Virabhadra.

The great sage Siva, the lord of illusion, because of his influence, the cakra held by Visnu in his hand, became totally inactive.

Then Visnu, stood before Virabhadra, the lord of the ganas like a mountain and started talking.

Î Narada when Virabhadra, made Visnu inactive and stunned, then the lord started reciting the mantra for his redemption from stupefaction.

Î Narada, after his stupefaction was removed, Visnu- the lord of Rama, took up his bow and arrow in rage.

Î Narada, Virabhadra, shooting three arrows, humiliated the Saranga bow by breaking it into three pieces.

Thereafter at the advice of the divine voice from the sky, Visnu took Virabhadra to be invincible, therefore he decided to disappear from the battlefield.

Having been reminded of the evil effect of the self-burning of Sati, besides the greatness of Siva, the lord of all, Visnu together with his ganas, went back to his own abode.

I, feeling, concerned about the condition of my son Daksa, feeling extremely painful, returned to Satyaloka and started thinking about the future course of action.

When myself and Visnu left the place, then the ganas of Siva conquered the gods as well as the sages.

They desecrated the yajna. Finding this, yajna-deva, taking to the form of a deer, fled away from that place.

Finding that the yajna taking to the form of a deer, flying towards the sky, Virabhadra caught hold of him and cut off its head.

Thereafter the heroic Mahagana Virabhadra caught hold of Prajapati, Dharma, Kasyapa, Aristanemi the sage with many sons, the sages Angira and Krsasva and the great sage Datta and kicked all of them on their heads.

The nose of Sarasvati the mother of the gods, was cut off by glorious Virabhadra with his own hands.

Thereafter, all other gods were thrown on the ground, and their bellies were torn out.

The anger of Virabhadra could not subside, even after the killing of the prominent gods and the sages and he kept on hissing like the snake.

Like the lion which kills the wild animals, Virabhadra, even after destroying his enemies, was looking on all the sides with anger to find out who was lodged where?

Thereafter the famous Manibhadra, pressing the sage Bhrgu under his feet, pulled his beard up.

Canda on the other hand quickly removed the teeth of Pusan, because when the curse was pronounced on Siva, he had been laughing showing his teeth.

Nandi on the other hand, removed the three eyes of Bhaga- because it was he who indicated with the winking of the eye.

The gana’s leaders then attacked over Svadha, Svaha, Daksina, mantra, tantra and all others who had been present there.

The ganas of Siva, getting enraged, showered filth and rubbish, over the sacrificial fire. The heroic ganas absolutely polluted the sacrifice.

The valorous Virabhadra, frightened Daksa, who had hid himself behind the fire altar. Finding this, Virabhadra forcibly dragged him.

He was caught by his cheeks and he tried to cut off his head with the sword, which could not be severed due to his yogic power.

Thinking that his head could not be severed with his weapons, Virabhadra jumped over his chest and tore out his chest with his hands.

Thereafter Virabhadra- the leader of the ganas, dropped the head of the inimical Daksa in the sacred fire of the fire-altar.

At that point of time Virabhadra, looked graceful wielding the trident in his hand. The Samvarta fire of the war, started burning with anger like the mountain of fire.

Thus Virabhadra, getting enraged, threw all of them in the burning flames, who were burnt like the fire flies.

When Virabhadra found that all including Daksa had been bum tout, then he laughed aloud, the sound of which echoed in the three worlds.

Thereafter, the flowers of he Nandanavana were showered over Virabhadra because of his prowess.

The cool, slow and fragrant winds started blowing and divine drums were beaten in the heaven.

As the darkness is removed by the sun, similarly Virabhadra, getting successful in his mission, went back to Kailasa.

Finding that Virabhadra, has performed his duty faithfully, Siva was delighted and he declared him the leader of the valorous ganas.”

## Chapter 38 - Conflict between Ksuva and Dadhica

Suta said, “After hearing the words of Brahma, of enormous wisdom, Narada- the Brahmana, felt surprised and he lovingly asked him.”

Narada said, “Please tell me the reason for Visnu’s participation in the yajna of Daksa along with the gods, because in the absence of Siva, a lot of discomfiture was in store for him?

Was it not known to Visnu, that Siva had the power of dissolution with him. Then why did he fight with Sivaganas, like a foolish person devoid of wisdom?

Î Merciful lord, this is the biggest doubt in my mind. Removing that doubt, you kindly continue to narrate the story of lord Siva, which is quite enthusiastic for the mind.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent Brahmana, you listen to the excellent story of lord Siva, quite lovingly, which removes all the doubts of the person putting the question.

In earlier times the wisdom of Visnu was once lost due to the curse of the sage Dadhica. He therefore went to the sacrifice of Daksa along with gods to help Ksuva.” Narada said, “There was a king named Ksema, who possessed great splendour, who was quite friendly to Dadhica- the great sage with enormous spiritual power.

In earlier times a great dispute arose between Ksuva and Dadhica, relating to the penance, which resulted in a great disaster.

Dadhica had been a great devotee of Siva, besides being well-versed in the Vedas, once observed that the Brahmana happened to be the best of all the varnas.

On hearing the words of Dadhica, the king Ksuva- who had been intoxicated because of his riches, spoke.

Ksuva said, “The king is born with the amsas (parts) of the eight Lokapalas, therefore, he indeed is the best.

It has been ordained in the Vedas that the king is the form of all the gods. Therefore, Î Excellent Sage, I happen to be the excellent one.

Therefore, the king happens to be nobler than the Brahmanas. Take the case of Cyavana. Therefore, I am not to be disrespected by you and am to be honoured always.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage listening to the words of Ksuva, which were contrary to the Vedas and the smrtis the sage Bhrgu was immensely enraged.

Thereafter, Î Sage, Dadhica getting enraged struck by the sage, Ksuva- the king, shot the vajra at the sage Dadhica. The lord of the universe then thundered aloud.

Dadhica- Bhargava, having been struck with vajra, fell down on the ground and then he remembered Sukra- one of his ancestors.

Sukra arrived there at once and with the application of his yogic knowledge, rejoined the limbs broken by the king Ksuva with the attack of vajra.

Sukra, who was the foremost of the devotees of Siva, with the use of Mrtyunjaya vidya, restored the body of Dadhica to his original position.”

Sukra said, “O Dear Dadhica, I, after worshipping Siva, shall speak out to you the highly potential Vedic hymn of Mahamrtyunjaya.

We worship lord Siva having three eyes, who is the lord of the three worlds and the master of the three gunas.

Siva is the essence and the fragrance of the three tattvas, three fires, three lokas, three arms and always has trimurti.

He is Mahadeva among the three gods. He has the trigunatmik form. He is the essence of the fragrance of flower and happens to be the lord of the devas.

As the fragrance is enshrined in the flowers, similarly he is found present in all the sense organs, the gods, gunas, in a very strong manner. Similarly he is the lord of the gods.

Î Suvrata, Î Dear Brahmana, he establishes the union of Purusa and Prakrti, besides Mahat to different sense organs.

Î Excellent sage, he happens to be Brahma, Visnu and other gods, who derive their nourishment from him.

Î Prajapati, you worship with sacred rites, penance, self-learning of the Vedas, yogic practices, meditation, remaining truthful and by other means and you will be surely freed from the noose of Yama. The lord is the cause of bondage and freedom.

In my opinion, this Mrtyunjaya mantra is the excellent of all. Repeat the mantra regularly with your mind devoted to Siva. After, japam, homa and recitation of the mantra, observe the fast but you can drink water during the day and night. In case the penance is done in the presence of Siva, there could be no danger from any quarter.

Nyasa and other ritualistic rites shall be observed daily worshipping Siva, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees. I shall also talk about meditation. It is only after the meditation that the mantra shall be repeated till the purpose for which the adoration is made.

I adore the three eyed lord Siva the conqueror of the death, accompanied with (Parvati), who pours water on his head from the two pitchers held in his lotus like hands, by means of the other pair of hands. He has placed the two hands with the pots over the lap. He usually holds the Rudraksa rosary and a deer in his hands, and whose body is rendered cool, wet with the nectar falling from the crescent adorning his head.

Brahma said, “Thus advising the sage Dadhica- the excellent sage, Sukra, reciting the name of Siva, returned to his abode.

Listening to his words, the great sage Dadhica, reciting the name with devotion of Siva, went to the forest.

Reaching there he started repeating the Mahamrtyunjaya mantra and continued to perform penance for Siva.

He continued reciting that mantra for a long time and performing penance for Siva, he pleased the lord in the form of Mahamrtyunjaya.

O Excellent sage, Siva who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, was pleased with his tapas and he appeared before him.

Finding the lord Siva appearing before him, the excellent sage was delighted, and he appropriately offered his prayer to him with folded hands.

O Excellent sage, thereafter, lord Siva, feeling pleased, asked Dadhica, the son of Cyavana for seeking a boon.

Thus listening to the words of Siva, Dadhica as the most excellent devotee of the lord, with folded hands offering his salutation to him.

Dadhica said, “O Great lord of the gods, kindly bestow three boons one me. First my bones should be strong like vajra. No one should be able to kill me I should never face distress.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Dadhica, Siva was pleased and he bestowed three boons on him.

Having been thus bestowed with the three boons from Siva, the great sage who always followed the path of bliss, at once reached at the place of the king Ksuva.

Having achieved the three boons of being indestructible, possessing of Vajra like bones and becoming free from distress, he kicked the king on his head with his foot.

Getting enraged, the king Ksuva, then with his mind devoted at the glory of Visnu, attacked Dadhica at his chest with vajra.

By the grace of Siva, the attack of vajra could cause no harm to Dadhica, which surprised the son of Brahma.

Ksuva, the son of Brahma, also finding that the attack of vajra had become infructuous, felt extremely surprised.

Then Ksuva, who had been defeated by Dadhici- the devotee of Mrtyunjaya, Brahma felt surprised.

Garuda- bannered Visnu, having been pleased with his tapas appeared before him, because of his tapas.

Looking at the lord Janardhana with his divine sight, he bowed in reverence to him and eulogised him.

After adoring and offering prayer to the invincible lord, praised by Indra and others, he bowed his head in reverence to him and submitted to him.”

The king Ksuva said, “O Lord, I had a great friend who was the noble soul and humble, known by the name of Dadhica, who is a famous Brahmana.

He worshipped Mrtyunjaya-Mahadeva, and became free from death and sickness.

The said sage Dadhica kicked me in my Court at the head with his right foot, showering an insult on me.

In arrogance he openly declared that he had achieved a boon from Mrtyunjaya and therefore he was not afraid of any one.”

Brahma said, Lord Visnu, then remembered the enormous prowess of Siva and realising the invincibility of Dadhica, said to Ksuva the son of Brahma. Î Best of the kings, the Brahmanas are least afraid of anyone.

Î King, the devotees of Siva are particularly free from any danger. I am myself suffering presently because of the curse from a Brahmana.

Because of that curse, I shall the destroyed and then brought back to life by Siva.

Therefore, Î Leader of the kings, I shall try to get you victorious over Dadhica. But the yajna can never be completed.”

Listening to the words of Visnu, king Ksuva accepted them. But he remained there to have his desire fulfilled.

## Chapter 39 - Fight between Visnu and Dadhica

Brahma said, “Lord Visnu, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, with the aim of doing some god to the king Ksuva, taking to the form of a Brahmana, arrived at the abode of the sage Dadhica.

Visnu said, “O sage Dadhica, engaged in the adoration of Siva, I have arrived to ask for a boon from you. Can you give it to me?

Brahma said, “In this way, Visnu, in order to establish the task of the king Ksuva, deceitfully asked for a boon from the sage who was a great devotee of Siva.

The sage Dadhica said, “O Visnu, you have changed your form with your illusion, in order to establish the task of the king Ksuva and have arrived here. I have known the purpose of your arrival here.

Î Visnu, by the grace of Siva, I am well aware of the happenings of the past, present and future.

I know you in the form of Hari or Visnu. You therefore shed away this form of a Brahmana. The evil minded king Ksuva had adored you. Discarding the deceitful form, you better recite the name of Siva. I am well aware of your devotion towards the lord.

You better speak out the truth to me. Can there be any danger to a devotee of Siva like me?

While reciting the name of Siva, I am the least afraid of the gods, demons or others. I am speaking the truth.”

Visnu said, “Î Dadhica, you are not afraid of anyone from any source, because you are a devotee of Siva and are omniscient.

I bow in reverence to you. At my command you first tell the king Ksuva once that you are afraid of him.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, Dadhica, the supreme devotee of Siva, listening to the words of Visnu, then fearlessly spoke while smiling.”

Dadhica said, “By the grace of Siva, the holder of the Pinaka bow, I am, the least afraid from anyone at any place.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of the sage, lord Visnu getting enraged, tried to reduce the sage to ashes with the use of his Cakra.

The Cakra shot at by lord Visnu, in the presence of the king Ksuva, became infructuous.

When Visnu found his Cakra becoming infructuous, then Dadhica the great sage, possessing the knowledge of the cause of discrimination between existent and nonexistent, smilingly said to Visnu.”

Dadhica said, “Î Lord Visnu, formerly, the great Cakra was obtained from Siva by you making great efforts. Thus is the auspicious cakra of Siva. Therefore, it cannot harm me at all.”

Then lord Visnu getting enraged used various other weapons (which were of no avail). Then Dadhica said, “You can attack me with Bahmastra as well.”

Brahma said, “Hearing these words of the sage Dadhica, and thinking him to be quite weak, Visnu, getting enraged, shot all the weapons at him.

Then all the foolish kings respectfully joining with Visnu, started fighting with the Brahmana.

Indra and other gods fighting on the side of Visnu, started shooting their weapons on Dadhica.

Then Dadhica, who had controlled all his senses, remembering the name of Siva in his mind, holding Kusa grass in his hand created the bones of vajra for all the gods.

O Excellent sage, with the influence of - Siva, the kusa-grass held by Ksuva in his hands was turned into tridents emitting fire of the time of dissolution.

Then the sharp-edged trident issuing burning the gods from all the sides.

All the weapons shot by the gods at the trident started offering their salutation to it.

All the gods were deprived of their strength and getting frightened, they fled away from the scene. Only the frightened lord Visnu, the illusory one stayed there.

Thereafter lord Visnu produced out of his body lakhs of valorous warriors.

Î Divine sage, the warriors of Visnu, started fighting with lonely Dadhica.

Dadhica the devotee of Siva, reduced all of them to ashes while fighting with them.

Thereafter, Visnu well-versed in illusion in order to surprise Dadhica, took to his universal form.

At this Dadhica then had a look in the body of Visnu, with thousands of mobiles and immobiles, besides the gods.

There were crores of bhutas, crores of ganas and crores of universes which could be seen in the body of the univeral form of Visnu.

Dadhica, the son of Cyavana, looking at all the things so spread there, spoke to the all universe.

Dadhica said, “O Long armed one, squeeze your illusion. In case one thinks it deeply, it is only a fallacy. Î Madhava I am also aware of thousands of such practices, which are unknown to others.

O Visnu, I bestow the divine sight on you and you carefully look at me and you will find thousands of Brahmas, Visnus, Mahesas besides the entire world. You look at me carefully.”

Brahma said, “The sage who had become fearless because of the brilliance of Siva, displayed the entire globe in his body.

Remembering Siva in his mind, Dadhica, the Supreme Saiva, becoming fearless antagonised Visnu.”

Dadhici said, “O Lord Visnu, why are you displaying the prowess of your illusion or the strength of the mantras. You better discard this illusion and fight straight away.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the words of the sage, spoken fearlessly, filled with the brilliance of Siva, Visnu was immensely enraged at him.

Finding that Visnu was sure to fight with Dadhica, all the gods fled away from the place.

In the meantime the king Ksuva came to me. Then I removed the fainted gods as well as from that place.

Learning from me that the Brahmana, could not be defeated, then lord Visnu went to him and offered his salutation to him.

The king Ksuva became more humble, and going to the sage offered prayer to him.

Ksuva said, “O Excellent sage, Î Foremost of the devotees of Siva, you are beyond the sight of the wicked people. Only the devotees of Siva can recognise you.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of gods. With the king, the ascetic Dadhica, became graceful on them.

Thereafter looking at Visnu and other gods and feeling enraged, the sage Dadhica, concentrating his mind on Siva, pronounced a curse on them.”

Dadhica said, “Let the gods, the ascetics, and Visnu with his attendants be destroyed in the fire of the anger of Siva.

Brahma said, “Thus pronouncing a curse on the gods, the sage then said to Ksuva, “O Best of the kings, Brahmana is more adorable than the gods and the kings.

Î Leader among the kings, only the Brahmanas are powerful and influential. Thus speaking Dadhica retired to his hermitage.

The king Ksuva too returned to his abode, offering his salutation the Dadhica, while Visnu, accompanied with the gods retired to his abode.

Since that time this place was known as Sthanesvara. Having an audience with Siva here, a person, who visits this place attains the Sayujya devotion of Siva.

Thus I have narrated the story of the conflict between Ksuva and Dadhica, in brief. Leaving Siva, Dadhica had cursed Brahma and Visnu.

A person who recites the story of Ksuva and Dadhica daily, he overcomes the untimely death and achieves Brahmaloka after his death.

The one who hearing this story, enters the battlefield, he becomes eternal and victorious.

## Chapter 40 - Audience of gods with Siva

Narada said, Î Brahma, the displayer of Siva-tattva, you have narrated the astonishing sports of Siva.

Now you tell me as to what happened after the return of Virabhadra to Kailasa, destroying the yajna of Daksa.

Brahma said, “All the gods at that time, besides the sages, having been wounded by the army of Siva and getting defeated, arrived at my place.

Offering their salutation to me, and several types of prayers to me, they started speaking their tales of suffering.

Learning about the news, I feeling painful at heart with the death of my son, started thinking in my mind, as to what should be done by me to relieve the gods of their sufferings? And also bring Daksa back to life, completing his yajna at the same time.

O Sage, I never felt comfortable while thus thinking. Then I remembered Visnu and was given the proper guideline.

Thereafter, I went to Visnuloka accompanied with the gods and the sages. Reaching there, I offered my salutation to the lord, and after praising him I narrated to him the tale of my agony.

I said to him, “Î Lord, you kindly make efforts, by which, yajna of Daksa could be completed, Daksa is brought back to life and the gods as well as the sages feel comfortable. You kindly do something.

Î Visnu, you always please the gods, Î Lord of Rama, all the gods and the sages have arrived here to take refuge under your feet.”

Listening to the words of Brahma, Visnu, remembering lord Siva in his mind, spoke with a painful heart.

Lord Visnu said, “In case a sin is committed against a powerful person, then the apology could be the only remedy.

Î Brahma, since the share of lord Siva in this yajna was not set aside, therefore all of us are the sinners before Siva.

You try to appease Siva with a spotless mind and offer salutation to him holding his feet.

At the command of the protector of the world, whose fury destroys everything and with his grace the resuscitation is sure and quick.

You with your wife, must apologise to Siva, for the evil words spoken by the wicked Daksa.

Î Brahma, this is the biggest remedy for the atoning of that sin. He would surely be pleased with it. I am speaking the truth.

Neither I, myself, nor the gods nor the sages with human bodies, could be aware of his tattva, his prowess, and the limitations.

By becoming inimical to the supreme independent soul, who can lay down a remedy to quell his delusion.

I also have antagonised Siva. I shall also come to the abode of Siva with you. Let us all beg forgiveness from him.

Brahma said, “With this command, of Visnu, Brahma and other gods, got ready to proceed on to Himalaya,.

At that point of time, lord Visnu, accompanied with other gods, the sages, and the Prajapatis, reached the Himalaya mountain.

The place is quite dear to Siva, which is inhabited by the Kinnaras, gods, apsaras, yogis, siddhas besides being the highest place. There were several types of springs.

The wives of the gods and the siddhas were also found there, who roamed about with their husbands in the mountain caves. The mountain of snow was decorated with several types of trees.

Several deer and birds roamed about there. There were numerous springs there. The wives of the gods and the siddhas used to visit the mountain caves with their husbands. The mountain of snow was decorated with several trees.

The lions and other creatures, shedding aside their natural enmity lived there. All sorts of the divine splendour could be found there.

The auspicious river Ganga, originating from the holy abode of Sati and also known as Visnu-padi, flowed there and as such the place was quite clean.

Thus looking at the Kailasa mountain which is dear to Siva, all the gods, the sages as well as lord Visnu felt surprised.

Close to the mount Himalaya, they also spotted the divine city of Alaka, the dwelling place of Kubera, a friend of Siva.

A forest of lotus flowers was also found by them close by, around which birds of several species were chirping.

Two rivers named Nanda and Alakananda were flowing around it, at the sight of which all the sins are washed out.

The divine damsels daily descended from the heaven and drank their waters. For the enjoyment of their sexual sports with their men folks, they entered in those waters.

After passing through the city of Alaka and the lotus forest, they found on the way the banyan tree of Siva.

The immobile shade surrounded it. It had a large number of suspended branches without hanging roots. It was a hundred yojanas in height and had no nests on it. It protected the people from the heat.

It was the place where Siva had been engaged in yogic exercises. It was excellent and quite gigantic. It was visible to the exceedingly meritorious people, besides being beautiful and auspicious.

It was the abode for the people desirous of moksa. Visnu and other gods found Siva seated in meditation under the shade of that tree.

Sanaka, Sanadana and other great yogis and the devotee of Siva, were found by them, serving the lord delightfully.

The Guhyakas, Kubera- the lord of demons and friend of Siva, besides the Sivaganas, were also serving him.

Siva had taken to the form of a yogi, with the ashes applied over his body. He was friendly to the entire world.

Î Narada, at your instance, when he was discoursing on the divine knowledge, then all the people present there listened to the same. He was seated over the kusa grass.

He had placed left foot over right thigh and the knee. The Rudraksa rosary was suspended from his wrist. He was displaying tarkamudra.

Looking at Siva, all the gods including Visnu, offered their salutation to him with folded hands.

Lord Siva- the refuge of the saintly persons, stood up and welcomed Visnu and myself and offered his salutation lowering his head.

Then Visnu and other gods, bowed in reference to Siva, touching his feet, while Visnu the goal of the world bowed to Kasyapa.

Visnu and the gods, performed obeisance to Siva and spoke to him, who was revered by the lords of the gods, Siddhas, ganas and the sages.

## Chapter 41 - The gods offer prayer to Siva

Visnu and other gods said, “O God of gods, Î Mahadeva, you are the one who prescribes the worldly conventions, by your grace, Î Lord, we know you as Isvara as well as the Supreme Brahman.

Î Lord Siva, why do you always confuse us with your divine and inscrutable illusion?

You are the Supreme Brahman or even beyond that. You are greater than Prakrti and Purusa. You are the material and activating cause the universe. You are beyond Parabrahman and imperceivable.

You alone can with your own influence create, sustain and destroy the universe. You sport about with your- your own manifestation like a spider weaving its web.

Î Siva, you, being merciful, have created the yajna and have protected Vedatrayi through Daksa.

The religious limitations which are followed by Brahmanas devoted to the path of the Vedas, have been created by you.

O Lord you bestow welfare on your own as well as the other people. The people having good and bad nature have good and bad results respectively.

You bestow the reward of all the good and the bad deeds. You are the lord of all the auspicious things. This has been prescribed by the Vedas.

The evil minded people who consider karmas to be supreme, talking of heart-rending things, having evil mind, speaking foolish and harsh words, inflict pain on others.

O Lord, let not the destruction of these gods be carried out by you since you are quite merciful.

Salutation to Siva, who is peaceful, Supreme Brahman, the highest soul, having matted locks of hair, the great lord, and the illustrious one.

You are the creator of the Prajapatis (creators) of the world. You are the preserver, the grand father and inspite of possessing the three gunas, you are nirguna or the one without attributes. You are beyond the primordial nature and the supreme being, salutation to you.

You are blue throated, the creator, the supreme soul, form of the universe, seed of the universe, and the cause of bliss of the universe, salutation to you.

You are omkṁrṁ, vasatkara, initiator of all the things, Hantakara, svadhakara and are the consumer of all the havya and kavya offering of yajna.

Î Religious minded one, how is it that the Daksa’s sacrifice has been destroyed by you? Î Lord, you are the benefactors of the Brahmanas. How is it that you have become the destroyer of the yajnas.

You happen to be the protector of the Brahmanas, cows, besides those who take shelter with you and are the protector of Dharma, you are to protector of all the living beings.

Salutation to you, Î Lord, having the splendour of innumerable suns; salutation to you, Î Bhava, Deva, and the lord in the form of fragrance and fluid.

Salutation to you, Î Siva, you are the form of earth, always fragrant, you have the form of Agni and are great splendour.

Salutation to Siva, who is wind in the subtle form of the principle of touch. Salutation to you, who are lord of animals, and the priest presiding over the yajna.

Salutation to you, the terrible one in the form of the sky, the principle of sound; salutation to the great lord of the moon or the one accompanied by Uma- the form of Prakrti.

Salutation to you in the form of ugra and the sun; salutation to you being a karmayogi (performer of actions), the slayer of the god of death, and the enraged Rudra.

Salutation to the one who is he the form of welfare, Bhima, Sankara and Siva. You control all the living beings and you bestow welfare on us.

Salutation to you, since you bestow pleasure on all, are the form of Universe, the Supreme Brahman, lord of Ambika, and Uma.

Salutation to the one who is form of mobile and immobile, the great soul which is free from the form of Sata and Asata. You are the cause of grandeur.

Salutation to the one who is born in the universe in several forms, and who is Nila, Nila-rudra, Kadrudra and Pracetus.

Salutation to the most bounteous lord who fulfills numerous Desires of the devotees, who is the greatest and is the destroyer of the enemies of the gods.

Salutation to you since you make people to cross the ocean of the universe with the reciting of the Taraka mantra, always young, the illustrious one, and the lord known as Hrsikesa.

You bestow welfare on gods, the great soul, the great one, having dark throat, salutation to you.

Salutation to the golden complexioned one, the supreme lord, having the complexion of the molten gold, Bhima, the form of Bhima and always engaged in horrible deeds.

Salutation to the one, whose body is smeared with ashes, adorned with Rudraksa, and who takes to long, short and dwarfish form.

Salutation to you, who can kill anyone at a distance, at front and in front, the one who carries the bow, a trident, a club and a plough share.

Salutation to the one who holds several types of weapons, destroyer of the daityas and the danavas; who is sadhya, sadyarupa and sadyojata.

Salutation to the one, who is beautiful, vamarupa, vamanetra, Aghora, the great lord and Vikata.

Salutation to Tatpurusa, Natha, Ðurañṁ- purusa, bestower of the four aims of life, vrati and Paramesthi.

Salutation to you as Isana, Brahman, form of Brahman, and the supreme soul.

You are horrible for the wicked people for us you are the bestower of welfare, consumer of the kalakuta poison, for the protection of the gods, salutation to you.

You are Vira, Virabhadra, protector of the warriors, holder of the trident, the great lord, the best among the Pasupatis, salutation to you.

Salutation to you possessing the best of knowledge, Srikantha, holder of the Pinaka bow, the endless one, the subtle one, besides the form of death and anger.

Salutation to you- the great lord who is grater than the greatest, the greatest of the great, all pervading and form of the universe.

For whom, Visnu happens to be the pelvic region, who has Visnu as his spouse, who is the sun, Bhairava, protector of all, Tryambaka and the sportive one, salutation to you.

Salutation to Mrtyunjaya, the cause of grief, Triguna, having the sun, moon and fire as his eyes and happens to be the bridge for every cause.

You pervade the entire universe, with your own brilliance, being unblemished consciousness, bliss and the light.

Î Mahesvara, Brahma, Visnu, Indra, moon and other prominent gods have been born of you.

Because, by dividing your body in eight parts, you are called as the compassionate Astamurti lord.

The wind blows getting afraid of you, the fire burns, the sun shines, and the deaths wanders on all the sides.

Î Ocean of mercy, Î Mahesana, Î Pramesvara, be pleased with us and always protect us, because we have been fainted.

Î Ocean of mercy, you have always saved us from several misfortunes, in the past. Similarly you protect us presently as well.

O Lord, you kindly complete the unfinished yajna of Daksa Prajapati.

Let Bhaga be bestowed with eyes, the performer should be brought back to life and Pusan should get back his teeth. Bhrgu should get back his beard and moustaches.

The gods whose limbs have been cut off should be restored to them. All should become hale and hearty.

Î Lord, you will surely receive the share of the yajna. Vasistha will officiate in the sacrifice, the sacrifice will have the share of Rudra, not otherwise.

Thus speaking both Brahma and Visnu with folded hands prostrated over the ground, and begged forgiveness.

## Chapter 42 - Showering of grace on Daksa

Brahma said, “On being conciliated by Visnu, Brahma and other sages, Lord Siva felt delighted.

Then Siva, the ocean of mercy, smilingly re-assured the gods and said to them.

Mahadeva said, “O Excellent gods, you listen to me attentively. Î Dear ones, I shall bear the anger of all of you. I am speaking correctly.

These foolish persons were overpowered with my illusion and therefore, I do not find them guilty, still I have punished them.

The yajna of Daksa was not destroyed by me in any way. The one who becomes jealous of others, he has to reap the reward.

Therefore, one should not cause pain to others. The type of feelings one has against others, the same will recoil on him alone.

Yajna is my head, therefore Daksa should now have the head of a he-goat. Let the god Bhaga, witness the yajna with the eyes of the sun.

Î Dear one, while performing the yajna, as usual. I speak the truth.

My opponent- the sage Bhrgu will have the beard resembling the he-goat. All the gods, whose limbs have been broken by Virabhadra, would be restored to them and they would appear quite beautiful as before.

Let Asvani Kumaras regain their arms and Pusan the performer of the yajna regain the hands. Let all the participants of the yajna become healthy. I have ordained this now.

Brahma said, “Thus speaking the merciful lord of the mobiles and immobiles, left for having rest.

Thereafter Brahma, Visnu and other gods listening to the words of Siva, felt delighted and uttered repeatedly, “Well done.”

Thereafter, Visnu, together with the divine sages, delightfully completed the yajna inviting Siva.

Thus according to the prayer of Visnu and other gods, Siva reached int he region of Kanakhala, where the yajna of Daksa was being performed.

Siva witnessed the destruction caused to the yajna, the gods and the sages.

The gods and goddesses like Svaha, Svadha, Pusan, Tusti, Dhrti, Sarasvati, the sages, the manes, Agnis, and several others like the Yaksas, Gandahrvas, and Raksasas, whose bodies had been mutilated and injured, or killed in the battlefield, were seen by Siva laughingly.

Finding the desecration of the yajna, he summoned the chief of the ganas- Virabhadra possessing immense prowess, and spoke to him.

Siva said, “What is all this that has been done by you. You have heavily punished the gods and the rsis.

You immediately are responsible for the performing of this evil deed and this happens to be the result of the same.”

Brahma said, “At these words of Siva, Virabhadra at once brought the headless body of Daksa and placed it before Siva.

Lord Siva, who bestows welfare on the people, looking at the headless body of Daksa, said to Virabhadra.

“Where is his head?” Virabhadra said, “I had burnt his head in the burning fire-altar.”

Listening to these words of Virabhadra, he lovingly reminded the gods about the word spoken by him earlier.

Then Virabhadra said, “After doing in accordance with the command of Siva, Visnu, the other gods and I acquainted Bhrgu with the same quickly. At the command of Siva, they at once rejoined the head of the sacrificial animal- the goat, with the body of Daksa.

After the joining of the head when Siva looked at it, Daksa, was brought back to life as if woken up from sleep.

On regaining life, he saw Siva, the merciful one, before him. Daksa stood there delightfully.

Earlier he was extremely inimical to Daksa but having an audience with him on that day, he became spotless like the moon of the winter season.

He delightfully intended to offer prayer to lord Siva, but having been reminded of the death of his daughter in the yajna, he could not do so.

Thereafter feeling shameful of his deeds, but having been delighted at the sight of Siva, he started offering prayer to lord Siva.”

Daksa said, “O Bestower of the boon, the store house of knowledge, the eternal one, I bow to Siva the great being and the chief of the gods and the sole relative of the universe. I bow in reverence to the great lord.

Salutation to the lord of the universe, having cosmic form, the primordial being, and the form of Brahman itself. I offer my salutation to Siva, who bestows happiness to the world and is greater than the greatest.

O Mahadeva, adorable by the gods, be merciful on me. Î Ocean of compassion, Î Siva, you kindly forgive me for my sin.

You have exercised you compassion on me by punishing me. Î Deva, I am quite foolish, I had not been able to understand your tattva.

I have understood your tattva today, you are the best of all and are to be served by Brahma and Visnu as well. You are Mahesvara to be known through the Vedas.

You are like the wishfulfilling tree for the noble people and always punish the wicked people. You are independent and the supreme soul, and bestow the desired boons to your devotees.

O Siva, It is you who created the Brahmanas who possessing divine knowledge perform penance as well as the vratas and are well-versed in the Atma-tattva.

As the cowherd protects his cows, similarly you protect all the living beings from all the misfortunes, holding a staff in your hand. You are the protector of all the limitations or the traditions.

I had injured you speaking harsh words, still you showered your compassion on me as well as the gods.

You are lord Sambhu, the friend of the poor, the Supreme one and well disposed towards your devotees, because you get pleased with your precious deeds.”

Brahma said, “By so eulogising Siva, who showers his blessings of all, the humble Daksa Prajapati then kept quiet.

Thereafter, Visnu with his voice choked with emotions, offering salutation to Siva, started eulogising him.”

Visnu said, “You are Mahadeva, Mahesan, compassionate to the universe, Supreme Brahman, friend of the poor, and the ocean of mercy.

You are all pervading, roam about freely, and are the lord with fame, to be known through the Vedas. You have been so gracious on us. This Yaksa had turned us sinful.

The foolish Daksa happens to be my devotee. He denounced you earlier very much but you are unblemished, therefore you kindly forgive him.

Î Siva, I have also committee a sin by foolishly fighting with Virabhadra- your gana.

Î Supreme Brahman, Î Sadasiva, you happen to be my lord and I happen to be your slave and have to be protected by you. You are our supporter.”

Brahma said, “O God of gods, Î Mahadeva, Î Ocean of mercy, Î Lord free from all the bondages, the supreme soul, Parmesvara, unchanging, Î Pearless one, you are indestructible, Î Isvara, you have protected the body of my son, without caring for the insult, he showered on you. Now you kindly redeem his yajna.

Î Lord of the gods, be pleased and relieve all the people of your curse, because by possessing the divine knowledge, it is you who can aspire and function as a restrainer.

Î Sage of excellence, lord Visnu praised lord Siva, quite humbly with folded hands.

Thereafter Indra and other gods besides the Lokapalas calmly but delightfully eulogised lord Siva.

After that all the gods, Prajapati, Siddhas, and the rsis also, eulogised lord Siva with a delighted heart.

Similarly the demi-gods, nagas, the Brahmana members of the assembly, bowed in devotion and eulogised lord Siva variously.

## Chapter 43 - Performance of Daksa’s yajna

Brahma said, “When I myself, Visnu , the divine saints, and all other people eulogised Siva, he felt pleased.

Thereafter with the compassionate sight of Siva, he consoled Brahma, Visnu, the sages and the gods with his benign glance, and then spoke to Daksa.

Siva said, “Though I am the independent lord of all, still Î Daksa Prajapati, you listen to my words which I am going to speak to you. I am always subservient to my devotees.

Î Daksa Prajapati, four types of devotees having auspicious souls always serve me. The latter are greater than the former.

They are the distressed, discoverers or the researchers, those desirous of riches, and the wise. In preference to them, the first three ordinary ones and the fourth type is of extra ordinary nature.

Out of them all, the wise people are more dear to me. No one else is dearer to me than them. I speak the truth.

I am the knower of self. People can know me by means of the divine knowledge. The people with little wisdom intend to achieve me by means of Vedas and Vedanta.

The people who are engrossed in the karmas can never find me through the Vedas, nor the yajnas, nor the charities, nor with the performing of the penance.

You intended to free yourself from the worldly bondages simply by means of the karmas. This was the reason for my becoming angry, resulting in the destruction of your yajna.

Hereafter, Î Daksa, taking me to be the supreme lord, becoming careful with your wisdom, now you perform the yajna.

O Prajapati, you listen to my words with noble wisdom. I, taking to a saguna form, reveal to you something secret, for the protection of dharma.

I happen to be Brahma, Visnu, the supreme soul being the sole cause of the universe. I am the soul, the witness and without attributes.

O Sage, I enter in my virtuous illusion, and then create the universe, besides preserving and destroying it. I earn my title according to my karmas.

The ignorant person finds different living beings, viz., Brahman, Isvara etc. in that supreme soul, the universal god, which is pure self.

Even as an ordinary person does not consider the limbs like the head, hands etc. separate from the body, similarly my devotee does not have the separation among the living beings.

The one who does not find any difference among the three deities viz. Brahma, Visnu and Siva, who represent the soul of all living beings, he becomes peaceful.

Such of the degraded person who differentiates in the three gods, he surely falls into the hell and remains there till the moon and the stars shine.

The person with wisdom should, having faith in me, adore other gods as well and by doing so, one attains knowledge resulting in the achieving of the everlasting salvation.

Without the devotion of Brahma, the devotion of Visnu cannot be achieved, while no one can worship me, without the devotion to Visnu.”

Thus speaking Siva, the lord of all, mercifully started speaking in the presence of all those assembled there.

“Whosoever denounces me being the devotee of Visnu , or being a devotee of Siva denounces Visnu , for both of them there is a curse that they can never achieve the knowledge of tattvas.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the pleasant words of Siva, all the sages, the gods, and others felt delighted.

Daksa with his family having been filled with delight, was engrossed in the devotion of Siva. Besides the gods also recognised Siva as the lord of the universe.

The way the people adored Siva, who getting delighted in his mind, granted the desired boons to all as he received reverence to his great self.

Then Daksa- the devotee of Siva, with the permission of the lord, completed his yajna.

He earmarked the full share for Siva, besides giving the other gods their respective shares. Then he secured the blessings of Siva, by giving away the due share of the Brahmanas and the other gods.

Thereafter, with the grace of Siva, Daksa, in association with the priests of the yajna, completed all the rites of the gods in accordance with the sacred traditions.

Î Excellent sage, thus the yajna of Daksa was completed by the grace of Siva.

Thereafter, all the gods and the sages, besides the other people, were delighted at the completion of the yajna, and praised Siva reciting his glory Thereafter feeling pleased, they returned to their respective abodes.

Getting immensely pleased, myself and Visnu , reciting the glory of Siva, returned to our abodes.

Then Daksa, lovingly honouring Siva, the abode of virtues, who returned to Kailasa, with his ganas, fully delighted.

Siva, after his return to Kailasa, remembered Sati too much and narrated her stories to the prominent ganas.

Lord Siva, possessing the supreme knowledge, displaying the worldly conduct, feeling painful at heart, spent a long time by narrating the stories of Sati.

How could the blemish of grief attract the mind of Siva, who was the protector of the noble people, the Supreme Brahman, the lord of all, who had never indulged in improperties.

Myself and Visnu can never be aware of his secrets then what to speak of the gods, the sages, the yogis as well the humans?

The glory of Siva is beyond limits, which is unknown even to the learned people. By his grace, the devotees, can know about him without much efforts.

Siva, the supreme lord is one and without blemish. He displays his sports to the people of the world appropriately.

O Sage, by reading or listening to the life stories of Siva, the people with wisdom achieve the unique divine position and also enjoy the best of comforts on earth.

Thus Sati, the daughter of Daksa, putting an end to her life was reborn from the womb of Menaka, the wife of Himalaya. This is well known.

She again performed the penance and had Siva as her husband. Then Gauri, after becoming the better half of Siva performed astonishing sports.

Thus I have narrated the surprising life story of Sati, which fulfills all the desires and bestows comforts as well as the salvation.

The story is auspicious by itself, which purifies others and bestows, heaven, fame, long-life, the sons and the grandsons.

A person, who getting devoted, reads it or teaches it, he after enjoying all the comforts on earth ultimately achieves moksa.

Siva-Mahapuranam

Rudra Samhita

## (3) Parvati Khanda

## Chapter 1 - Marriage of Himalaya

Narada said, “O Brahma, how was the daughter of Daksa Prajapati, known as Sati- the mother of the universe, putting an end to her body in the yajna of her father, was reborn as the daughter of Himalaya?

And how did she, after performing the severe penance, regain Siva, as her husband. You kindly narrate the story in detail.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, you listen to the auspicious and the excellent story of Parvati, which destroys the sins.

At the time when the Supreme goddess Sati was roaming about over Himalaya with her husband, at the same time Menaka, the wife of Himalaya was completely satisfied with all the rddhis and the siddhis, taking her to be her own daughter and she used to serve her.

But when Sati, having been humiliated by her father, burnt her body in the fire of yajna, the goddess Paramesvari achieved the abode of Siva.

Î Sage, Menaka, the wife of Himalaya at the same time adored Sati in the Sivaloka.

Then it came into the mind of Sati that she should be born as the daughter of Himalaya.

Sati who had ended her life in the yajna of Daksa, was reborn delightfully as the daughter of Menaka.

She was known by the name of Parvati. At the advice of Narada, she performed severe penance and she again got Siva as her husband.”

Narada said, “O Brahma, Î Destiny, Î Immensely intelligent one and best among the people with wisdom, you first tell me the story of the birth of Menaka and her marriage.

Graceful is the chaste Menaka, who gave birth to a daughter named Parvati. Therefore she the chaste lady is quite graceful and is adorable by all.”

Brahma said, “O Sage Narada, you listen from me the story of the birth of Parvati. How was she married and what was her conduct? All these auspicious details increase the devotion.

Out of all the mountains, in the north, Himalaya indeed is the highest one. Î Excellent sage, this mountain is extremely illustrious, filled with splendour and prosperity.

Because of his mobile and immobile nature, he has two aspects. I briefly describe about his subtle form

Extending from east to west, it serves as the measuring rod. It is the abode of several types of gems and serves as a measuring rod for the earth.

Several species of the trees are grown over it and it has many peaks. The animals like lions, tigers and others besides the ascetics surround the same.

This happens to be the largest abode of snow, having several surprises and is dear to the gods, sages siddhas, and ascetics serving as an abode for them.

He has the pure soul and happens to be the abode of austerities, besides being the treasure of several metals.

He has the divine form, is charming and beautiful in all forms, is the part of Visnu, unblemished and is dear to the noble people.

For the expansion of his race and the dharma the king of the mountains, desired to marry himself, by means of which the gods as well as the manes could be served.

For the establishment of their task, all the gods, Î Excellent sage, went to the manes living in the celestial places, and said to them.

The gods said, “Getting delighted, all of you should listen to our words. In case you intend to perform the task of the gods, then do as we pray to you.

You have a divine girl named Menaka. You lovingly marry that girl to Himalaya- the lord of the mountains.

By doing so, all would be immensely benefited and the miseries of the gods would also be removed.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of the gods, thinking deeply, keeping in view the curse of the daughter, the manes accepted the words of the gods.

Thereafter the manes gave away their daughter to Himalaya appropriately. In the auspicious occasion of the marriage enormous festivities were held.

All the gods including Visnu and others, reciting the name of Siva in their minds also participated in the same.

The manes gave away their daughter to Himalaya appropriately. They praised the manes as well as Himalaya.

Thereafter all the gods and the sages, delightfully, getting reminded of Siva and Parvati, returned to their respective abodes delightfully.

Thus observing the function and performing the marriage appropriately, Himalaya delightfully returned to his abode.”

Brahma said, “I have narrated the pleasant story of the marriage of Menaka with Himalaya, what more do you want to listen from me?

## Chapter 2 - Sanaka’s curse to Menaka and others

Narada said, “O Brahma, you kindly narrate the birth of Menaka and the curse on her, removing our doubt.

Brahma said, “O Narada, Î Excellent son possessing noble wisdom, you listen to the episode of the birth of Menaka, which I am going to narrate.

Î Sage, there is a son of mine named Daksa, about whom I have already stated. He had sixty daughters, for expanding the creation.

They were married to Kasyapa and other sages, and the related details are well-known to you. Now you listen to the story in detail.

Out of them, the daughter named Svadha was married to the manes, who produced from her three virtuous daughters.

Î Excellent sage, you listen to their auspicious names which remove the obstacles and bestow welfare.

The eldest daughter was known as Mena, the middle one was known as Dhanya, and the youngest one was known as Kalavati. All these three were the mind-born daughters of the manes.

All the three daughters were born as Ayonija and not from the womb of Svadha but are known to be her daughters. With the reciting of their names, all the desires of a person are fulfilled.

They are the mothers of the three worlds, and are adorable by all besides bestowing benevolence to all. They are the yoginis being the store house of knowledge and pervade the three worlds.

Î Excellent sage, once all the three sisters went to Svetadvipa- the abode of Visnu .

Offering their salutation to Lord Visnu, they started eulogising him with devotion. They took their seats at the instance of lord Visnu. In the mean time several people arrived there.

Î Sage, at that very moment, Siddhas the sons of Brahma- Sanaka and others also reached there and took their seats with the permission of Brahma.

On seeing those sages, Sanaka and others, and the people who had arrived there stood up. When the elders of the gods, respected by the people sat down, they all bowed down to them.

Î Sage, having been confused with the illusion of Siva, the three sisters did not stand up.

The illusion of Siva confuses every one, because the entire universe is controlled by the same.

It is also called the destiny. It has many names. It is activated with the will of Siva. There is no doubt about it.

Having been overpowered with the same illusion the girls did not bow his reverence. They looking at them, feeling surprised, kept on sitting.

Sanaka and other wise sages, were immensely enraged at their indiscreet behaviours.

Having been influenced with illusion of Siva, Sanatakumara and other sages, getting enraged, pronounced a curse on the girls.

Sanatakumara said, “All the three of you are the daughters of manes, but are still foolish, and are deprived of the noble knowledge, and the tattvas of the Vedas.

Because of your arrogance, you did not get up nor did you bow in reverence to us. You have been fascinated, witnessing the human form, leave the heaven at once.

Because of the ignorance of all the three of you, you will become the wives of the humans. You will reap the reward of your deeds.”

Brahma said, “Hearing this, all the three of them were terrified as well as surprised and lowering their heads they fell over the feet of the sages.

The daughters of the manes said, “O Best of the sages, Î Ocean of mercy, be pleased with us. Out of foolishness, we did not bow in reverence to you.

O Brahmana, Î Great sage, we have reaped the reward for the same. You are not at all to be blamed in this case. Now you be merciful on us to enable us to regain the heaven.”

Brahma said, “O Dear one, listening to their words, influenced with the illusion of Siva, the sage said, “I shall now speak out the way to free yourself of the effect of the curse.”

Sanatkumara said, “O three daughters of the manes, be pleased and listen to my words which will destroy the grief.

You will be born as Parvati, from Himalaya, as his eldest daughter.

The second daughter named Dhanya who is also called the yogini, would be the wife of the king Janaka. She will, (in due course of time) have Sita as her daughter, like Mahalaksmi.

The youngest one, at the end of Dvapara, shall be the wife of Vrsabhana- a merchant and will be known as Radha.

The yogini named Menaka, getting the boons from her husband and Parvati shall achieve the supreme position over Kailasa.

Dhanya, then giving birth to the daughter named Sita, shall take the king Siradhvaja to Vaikuntha.

Kalavati, on the other hand, after marrying Vrsabhana shall give birth to a girl named Radha, and shall undoubtedly proceed on to Goloka.

Who achieves the glory without suffering? When the sufferings of a noble person comes to an end, then he enjoys all the comforts in the heaven. Having an audience with Visnu, all your karmas will be washed out.”

Thus speaking and having been relieved of the anger, remembering Siva who bestows comforts as well as the salvation. He again said.

Sanatkumara said, “You listen to a few more words lovingly. My words always bestow comforts. With your minds devoted to Siva, you are repeatedly graceful, honourable, as well as adorable.

The goddess Jagdambika, the daughter of Menaka, known as Parvati, will perform severe tapas and become the wife of Siva.

The girl known as Dhanya will give birth to Sita who shall be the wife of Rama. Following the worldly traditions, she would marry Rama.

Radha, the daughter of Kalavati, would be the wife of Krsna, having been bound with the secret bondage of love and will dwell in Goloka.

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, the excellent sage Sanatkumara, disappeared with his brothers from that place.

Î Dear one, the three sisters- the daughters of manes, getting relieved of the sins, returned to their abodes.

## Chapter 3 - Visnu and other gods eulogise Siva

Narada said, “O Brahma, you are well- versed in all the scriptures. You tell me, what happened thereafter?

You have narrated to me the astonishing type of the story relating to the rebirth of Menaka. You have also narrated about her marriage, now you tell us about her story.

What did Himalaya do after his marriage with Menaka? How was Parvati, the mother of the universe born to her?

How did Parvati performed penance and how could she get Siva as her husband? You speak out all these details.

Brahma said, “O Sage, you lovingly listen to the auspicious glory of Siva, by listening to which even a person suffering from the sin of Brahmahatya is also redeemed, getting all his desires fulfilled.

When Himalaya, the lord of the mountains, reached his abode after his marriage, with Menaka, then Î Narada, great festivities were observed throughout the world.

Himalaya, possessing noble wisdom, invited the Brahmanas as well as the relatives and adequately welcomed them.

Thereafter, pleasing all the Brahmanas as well as the relatives, getting pleased blessed him in many ways before returning to their respective abodes.

Himalaya also quite delightfully, lived with Menaka at his home, besides roaming about in the Nandanavana and other forests.

Î Sage, at that point of time, lord Visnu and other gods also besides the sages went to the abode of Himalaya.

Finding the arrival of the gods, Himalaya was delighted and he offered his salutation to them, and praising his own fortunes honoured them.

Then he bowed his head in reverence to him with folded hands, eulogised them with devotion. The hair of Himacala stood at end, and tears of love fell from his eyes.

Î Sage, thereafter, Himacala, bowing himself in reverence, spoke to Visnu and other gods.

Himalaya said, “My birth has been successful today. The penance performed by me has also been successful. The knowledge possessed by me besides all the activities have been successful today.

Today my race, my land, and my wife feel graceful. There is no doubt about it.

Because all of you have arrived collectively in my abode. I am your humble servant anxious to have your command.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Himacala, Visnu and other gods, felt delighted, expecting the success of their mission and they spoke.

The gods said, “O immensely wise Himacala, listen to our benevolent words. We shall now reveal the purpose for which we have arrived here.

Sati, the daughter of Daksa and the wife of Siva in earlier times, had been enjoying sports on earth in the form of Uma.

Having been insulted by her father, remembering her pledge, getting rid of her human body, she achieved the supreme position.

The relevant story, Î Himacala is well known to you. The gods too will be under your control.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the words of Visnu and other gods, the delighted lord Himacala said, “Be it so.” Then he adored them with respect.

Thereafter all the gods quite respectfully, thus speaking to Himalaya, and then went to Uma, the beloved of Siva.

Having been seated at an appropriate place, they started reciting the name of Jagadamba in their minds. They offered their salutation to the goddess, and the gods with utmost devotion eulogised her.

The gods said, “O Goddess Uma. the mother of the universe, dweller of Sivaloka, beloved of Sadasiva, Mahesvari, Durga, all of us offer our salutation to you.

You are Srisakti, purifier, Santa, the form of holy nourishment, and the one having the form of Mahat and Avyakta, salutation to you.

Î Siva, cause of welfare, pure, gross, subtle, the great goal and the one who is delighted with the inner and auspicious learnings.

You are the faith, fortitude and prosperity; you alone control everything. You are the splendour and energy of the sun brightening your own universe.

We offer salutation to the goddess who pervades in the globe as well as in the living beings and who feeds from Brahma to the blade of gross, salutation to you.

You are Gayatri, mother of the Vedas, Savitri and Sarasvati. You are the only source of life of the universe and you are also Vedatrayi the form of dharma.

In all the living beings, you live as Nidra (sleep), ksudha (hunger), Trpti (satisfaction), Trsna (lust), kanti (lustre), chavi (reflection), and Tusti (contentment). You delight every one, forever.

Among the noble souls, you are the form of Laksmi and you are the foremost to punish the sinners. You are the form of calmness in all the living beings, you are the mother for the protection of all the people.

You remain as tattva in the Pancamahabhutas. You are justice among those who uphold justice and you are the personification of the efforts.

In the Samaveda you are the form of song, in Yajurveda you happen to be granthi (blending knot), in the Rgveda you are the invocation, in the Samaveda you are the song, while in the Atharvan you are the measure of time.

You are the force behind all the gods, you are Tamo-mayi sakti, you have the virtues of a mother, you are visible in the Rajasika quality of the creator, you are the benefactress of the form of Siva.

You are the protector from the miseries of the ocean of the universe. You are the boat without the sail. You are well-versed in the practices of Astangayoga, you are the dweller of the Vindhya mountain, salutation to you.

You bestow comforts in the nose, eyes, mouth, arms, chest and the mind, always with patience. For the welfare of the people. You appear in them as sleep. Let the same goddess Bhagvati, who is engaged in creation and preservation of the universe, be pleased with us.

Brahma said, “Thus eulogising Jagadamba, Uma, Mahesani, and Sati, all the gods stood there in order to have a look at the goddess.

## Chapter 4 - The assurance of the goddess to the gods

When the gods so eulogised the goddess, Durga, the mother of the universe, the destroyer of the distress and misfortunes, she appeared before them.

She was mounted over the divine chariot studded with gems, over which a soft cushion had been spread and decorated with shining ornaments.

Her limbs had the brilliance more then crores of suns. She had the best limbs on her body. She was surrounded by a halo, created by her own splendour. She had the astonishing type of shine.

She was away from the worldly comprehension. She was Mahamaya, the spouse of lord Sadasiva, possessing the three gunas for the performing of the worldly activities and deprived of the three gunas for the performance of the divine functions. She was everlasting, and dweller of the Sivaloka.

She was the mother of Brahma, Visnu and Mahesa, she was known as Candi and Siva, who removed the miseries of all, the mother of all Mahanidra, and the redeemer of all the noble people.

The goddess was sighted by the gods through the huge column of lustre. The gods desirous of having an audience with her, praised her.

Thereafter, Visnu and other gods desirous of having a look at her, witnessed the mother of the universe, by her grace.

Gods, the dwellers of the heaven, feeling delighted, offered their salutation to her, and then offered special prayer to her.

The gods said, “O Siva, Î Sarvani, Kalyani, Jagadamba, Mahesvari, remover of all the misfortunes, all the gods offer their salutation to you.

Î Goddess of the gods, your glory is unknown fully even to the Vedas, nor the other scriptures. Your glory is beyond comprehension, meditation or the mind or speech.

Being unable to describe your glory fully, the Vedatrayi, tremble at your name getting surprised, then what to speak of the other scriptures.

Your devotees can know fully about you by your grace. Such of the devotees who take refuge with you have to face no miseries.

Î Mother, you lovingly listen to the prayer of your devotees. Î Mahadevi, we are all your slaves forever. Listen to our prayer which we are going to explain.

You ended your life in the yajna of fire fulfilling your vow. Thereafter you proceeded to your loka. As a result of this, the pride and arrogance of Brahma and other gods was shattered.

Having been insulted by the father, you according to your own vow, ended your life in the fire. Thereafter you left for your abode. At that point of time Siva too felt painful at heart.

Î Mahesvari, the task of the gods therefore could not be fulfilled. Therefore we the gods and the sages have arrived here to take refuge with you.

Î Spouse of Siva, you fulfil the desire of the gods. Î Siva, make the words of Sanatkumara fruitful.

O Goddess, incarnating on earth, you again become the wife of Siva. Perform your divine plays in a befitting manner, and make the gods happy.

Make lord Siva, dwelling over Kailasa happy. Let all the living beings he happy and there should be the end of miseries.”

Brahma said, thus speaking Visnu and other gods, with their minds filled with loving devotion, waited there silently with humility.

Siva, also felt delighted at the god’s prayer, and ascertaining the course of the prayer, she remembered lord Siva, and then the merciful goddess Uma, smilingly addressed Visnu and other gods. The goddess favourably disposed towards her devotees spoke.”

Uma said, “O Visnu, Î Brahma, Î other gods, let all of you be comfortable. Listen to my words. I am undoubtedly pleased with all of you.

My performance always provides comforts to all the three worlds. The sport relating to the yajna of Daksa, was performed by me.

I shall surely appear on earth, with full incarnation. There are several reasons for the same, which I am going to highlight with respect.

Î Gods, earlier when I was born as Sati, then both Himalaya and Mena had severed me lovingly as parents.

Even presently both of them are serving me with utmost devotion. Out of both of them, Menaka, serves me particularly as a daughter.

All of you including Rudra can leave now. I shall incarnate in the house of Himacala, in order to relieve you of your sufferings.

All of you can now retire to your respective abodes, and be comfortable. On the other hand, I, incarnating as the daughter of Menaka, will make you all comfortable.

Thereafter, I shall become the wife of Siva. This my be a secret thought. The sports of Siva are always surprising, which can confuse even the minds of the people with wisdom.

Î Gods, when I, as the daughter of Daksa, witnessed the insult of my husband, then with grace of my husband, I ended my life there in the fire of the yajna.

Since that time, my husband, lord Rudra, getting relieved of all the costumes, taking to the form of Kalagni Rudra, is absorbed in thoughts about me.

Sati who had gone to the place of the yajna of her father, and witnessing the insult of her husband there, she ended her body because of her love for her husband.

Since then, Siva taking to the divine form, felt painful in separation from me, because Mahesvara could not tolerate his separation from Sati.

He witnessed my anger at the place of yajna. Thinking that the virtuous lady has cast off her body out of love for him, he became a yogin, discarding the domestic life.

Î Visnu, Î Brahma, Î gods and sages, you listen to me further, the divine sports of lord Siva, protect the universe.

Oppressed by the pangs of bereavement, he made the garland of my bones, and wore it around his neck, but still he could not be peaceful. He always remains lonely, without sleep.

Like a helpless person, he wanders here and there and cries loudly. He keeps on wandering and is unable to distinguish between good and bad.

Thus he behaves like a lustful or a lovelorn person. He behaves like a person, in despair due to separation.

But in reality, Akhilesvara, the lord of Maya, the complete Siva, and Paramesvara is without any blemish or misfortune. Therefore he is invincible.

Otherwise what has he to do with illusion, or of what avail are the illusion, love and other emotions for him.

Lord Siva is desirous of marrying me. Therefore, Î Gods, I shall incarnate on earth in the house of Menaka and Himacala.

Therefore, I in order to please Siva, shall be born from the womb of Menaka, the wife of Himacala.

I shall achieve Siva as my husband, by performing severe tapas and then undoubtedly perform the task of the gods.

Now you can revert to your respective abodes and adore Siva daily. By his grace, all the miseries will be removed. There is no doubt about it.

By the compassion of the merciful Siva, all shall gain comforts. In the form of the wife of Siva, I shall become adorable by all the three worlds, and shall be worshipped always.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking Siva, the mother of the universe, in full view of all the gods disappeared and left for her abode.

Visnu and other gods, besides the sages, offering their salutation towards that side, returned to their respective abodes.

Î Excellent sage, thus I have repeated the story of Durga, which bestows on the people, all the comforts, pleasure and the salvation.

The one who listens to this story or recites it to others, or reads it himself, he gets all his desires fulfilled.

## Chapter 5 - Menaka receives a boon

Narada said, “What happened after the disappearing of the goddess and the departure of the gods to their respective abodes?

How did Himacala and Menaka performed severe penance? Î Dear one, how was a girl born out of the womb of Menaka. You please speak out.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent Brahmana, listen to the great story. I, after bowing in reverence to Siva, narrated the story with utmost devotion.

Î Dear one, after delivering of the discourse, and departure of Visnu and other gods, Himacala and Mena, started performing the severe penance.
