Brahma said, “O Dear one, Î Immensely intelligent one, Candrasekhara Siva, who indulged in enormous sports, kindly listen to this story respectfully.

When the fire flames merging out of the third eye of Siva, burnt to death, the god of love, at that particular time an astonishing sound was heard, which echoed in the sky.

Listening to the great sound, and finding the god of love having been burnt, the frightened Parvati, accompanied with her maids returned to her abode.

Feeling surprised with that sound, all the kins of Himalaya, anticipating trouble for her daughter went to that place.

Finding his daughter distressed, Giriraja felt painful at heart and went to his daughter, who was crying in separation from Siva.

He, then holding her hands, wiping out tears from her eyes, said, “O Parvati, don’t cry. Don’t be afraid.” Thus speaking he pacified her.

He took distressed Parvati in his lap, Giriraja Himalaya consoled her variously and took her home atonce.

When Siva disappeared after the burning of Kamadeva, Parvati getting separated from Siva felt uneasy everywhere.

Parvati, after her return to the abode of her parents, felt as if she had been reborn.

Denouncing her beauty, she uttered, “I am unfortunate.” Parvati the daughter of the lord of mountain, could not be pacified by maids even.

She never felt the least comfortable, while sleeping, bathing, walking, or standing inspite the company of her maids.

She kept on thinking, “Disgrace to my beauty, dharma, activities,” and then always remained absorbed in the memories of Siva.

Thus Parvati felt painful at heart with the separation from Siva and finding no comfort anywhere, she always recited the name of Siva.

Inspite of her staying in her parental home, her mind remained devoted to Siva. Î Dear one, she reciting the name of Siva repeatedly fainted.

Himalaya, Mena, Mainaka and others kept on consoling Parvati and advising her to forget Siva, but she did not listen to anyone.

Î Narada, then Indra deputed you for the purpose and you roaming about at will reached the mountain Himalaya.

Himalaya, the great soul, adored you and enquired of our welfare, providing you a high seat to be seated.

Thereafter, Giriraja narrated the story of his daughter Parvati, right from the beginning and said, “In this way my daughter was engaged in service of Siva, but in the mean time Siva, burnt out Kamadeva.”

On hearing this, you said to the lord of mountains, that he should adore Siva, the lord of Kailasa. Thus speaking recalling the memories of Siva, you left the place.

Leaving that place, Î Sage, you again went to Kali, when she was alone.

Î Sage, you are the best of all the sages, you reached before Kali and advising her properly for her welfare, you spoke the beneficial words.

Narada said, “O Kali, you listen to my compassionate words, which will be beneficial for you, besides being unblemished and shall surely fulfill your desire.

You, without performing tapas, getting proud of your beauty, went to serve Siva, who is compassionate on the down-trodden people and has shattered your pride.

Siva, your lord is a recluse and a great yogi, Î Siva, the devotees are dear to the lord, and he has discarded you burning Kamadeva.

Therefore you perform tapas for him for a long time. When you are purified by performing tapas, Siva would surely accept you.

You cannot leave Siva, who is the cause of benevolence. Î Goddess, because of your stubbornness never accept anyone else as your husband, except Siva.”

Brahma said, “Î Sage, Listening to your words, the daughter Kali, of Giriraja, having a deep sigh spoke to you with folded hands.”

Siva said, “O Lord, you are omniscient, you do good to the world, therefore you give me mantra-diksa for the adoration of Siva.

Because no task can be established without a competent preceptor. I had earlier learnt about this eternal truth.”

Brahma said, “Listening to these words of Parvati, the sage Narada appropriately gave diksa of the Pancaksara-mantra to Parvati.

O Sage, developing her faith in the mantra, highlighting on the best influence of the great mantra, you said to her.

Narada said, “O Goddess, you listen to the astonishing effect of this mantra. With the mere listening of the same, lord Siva, would be pleased.

This mantra is the king of all the mantras, and is instrumental in fulfilling of all the desires. It bestows the pleasures as well as the salvation and is quite dear to Siva.

Î Beautiful one, with the appropriate recitation of this mantra, Siva, would appear before you without delay.

Concentrating your mind on his form, you recite the said mantra of Siva comprising of five letters, the lord would be pleased.

Thus Î Parvati, you perform penance because Siva could be achieved by tapas alone. This is true that all the devotees achieve the reward of tapas.”

Brahma said, “O Narada, dear to Siva, engaged for the welfare of the gods, you, thus speaking to Kali, left for the heaven.

Î Narada, listening to your words, receiving the Pancaksara mantra which indeed is the best of mantras, Parvati, at that time felt extremely happy.

## Chapter 22 - Penance of Parvati

Brahma said, “O Divine sage, after your departure, the delighted Parvati, thinking that Siva could be achieved only with the performing of penance, got ready for the performance of tapas.

Then accompanied with her maids named Jaya and Vijaya, she consulted her parents.

She, first of all went to the Giriraja Himalaya offered her salutation to him with all humility and then enquired of him.

The maids said, Î Himalaya, you please listen, we are speaking out the words of your daughter. She intends to purify her body, beauty and your race, which is possible only with the penance of Siva. Except this, it cannot be achieved by any other means.

Therefore, Î Lord of the mountains, you kindly permit Girija to proceed to the forest for the performing of tapas.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, when so asked by the maids of Parvati, Himalaya thought over the matter and said.

Himalaya said, “This is a good idea which I like you better consult Mena as well. What could be better than this, in case it is accomplished.

With this the success of myself any my race is established. What could be a better idea than this, in case her mother also likes it?”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of her father, Parvati then went to her mother.

Î Narada, when the maids, with Parvati went to her mother, then they, offering their respectful salutation to her, said to her.”

The maids said, “O Goddess, salutation to you. You better listen to the words of your daughter, listening to which you can do so accordingly.

Your daughter intends to perform tapas. She is now asking for your permission after having sought the permission of her father. She intends to perform tapas for achieving Siva.

Î Chaste lady, Parvati intends to purify her present form. In case she is permitted by your to do so, then she would start tapas.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, thus speaking, both the maids, kept quiet. Feeling painful, Mena did not agree to the request.

Then Parvati, folding her hands, meekly, remembering the lotus-feet of Siva in her mind, spoke to her mother.

Parvati said, “O mother, I shall go to the forest in the morning to perform tapas for Siva. You kindly permit me to go.”

Brahma said, “Listening to these words of her daughter, Mena felt painful at heart. Getting upset, she moved closer to the daughter and said to her.”

Mena said, “In case you intend to perform the tapas, you can do so in your house itself Î Parvati, don’t go out.

Where are you going for the performance of tapas? All the gods and the holy places are lodged in my own abode.

Î Daughter, don’t be stubborn. Don’t go out. What did you achieve by going out earlier? What are you going to achieve presently?

Î Daughter, your body is quite tender and the tapas is quite hard. Therefore you perform the tapas here itself and don’t go out.

We have not heard of a woman’s going to perform tapas in the forest for the achieving of her success. Therefore, Î Daughter, don’t go out for tapas.”

Brahma said, “Thus the mother of Parvati tried to stop Parvati from going to forest, variously, but she could not feel comfortable, without adoring Siva.’

Because of the preventing of Parvati’s departure to forest for the performing of the tapas by Mena, she is called Uma.

When Mena observed that Parvati had been feeling uncomfortable because of her preventing Parvati to do so, then she permitted her to do so.

Î Excellent sage, receiving the permission from her mother, the ascetic Parvati, recalling Siva in her mind felt comfortable.

Parvati then bowed in reverence to her parents delightfully and accompanied with her maids proceeded on for the performance of penance.

Leaving aside several thoughts and numerous garments, and wearing the bark garments and the girdle with munja rope, she removed the garland from her neck, she clad herself in the deer skin, went to the place where the Ganga had descended, for the performing of tapas.

With her mind devoted towards Siva, she reached the place, where Siva had burnt Kamadeva. The said peak of Himalaya Î Narada, was without Siva and the same was then occupied by Parvati or Kali, the mother of the universe who arrived there.

Siva had performed severe tapas here in earlier times. For sometime she sat there with the feeling of separation, getting upset.

The daughter of Himalaya, crying aloud for Íṁrṁ-Siva, lamented there sorrowfully, having been filled with anxiety.

After a long time, suppressing her anxiety with fortitude, Parvati, the daughter of Himvan, got herself initiated for the performing of the ritualistic activity.

She started performing penance in the - Srngi-tirtha, which subsequently came to be known as Gauri sikhara.

Î Sage, several beautiful and the auspicious plants were planted at that place by Parvati, for testing the success of her penance.

The exquisite beauty (Parvati) purifying the ground, preparing a pedestal (and sitting over it), started performing penance, which was beyond the reach of even the great sages.

Controlling her mind with all the organs of senses, Parvati started performing the excellent tapas over that place.

She, in the summer season, performed tapas by lighting fire all round, reciting the Pancaksara-mantra.

During the rainy season she performed tapas over the open ground (without any coverage) seated over the stone rock, and was drenched by the down pour of the rains.

During the winter season, she remained in water with great devotion throughout the day and night. During snowfall and in nights too she continued the penance, observing fast.

Thus Parvati, meditated upon Siva- the bestower of fruits of cherished desires, performing severe austerities, getting engrossed in the recitation of the Pancaksara-mantra.

During the leisure time, daily she used to water the trees and plants, which had been planted by her, herself. In this task her maids also helped her. She also extended hospitality to others, whenever she found time.

With a peaceful mind she could bear the severe cold, gusts of wind, cool showers of rain and unbearable heat of the summer season.

She was never worried even in extreme calamities. Î Sage, she always remained engrossed in the devotion of Siva.

Initially she consumed fruits for sometime, then she consumed the leaves while performing tapas. In this way she spent several years.

In due course of time Siva, the daughter of Himalaya, stopped consumption of leaves even and continued her tapas, by completely fasting without taking anything.

Since the daughter of Himalaya, stopped event the taking of leaves, she was called as Aparna by the gods.

Thereafter Parvati, uttering the name of Siva, performed tapas standing over one leg, reciting the Pancaksara-mantra.

Adorned with the bark garments, matted locks of hair, Siva was engaged in the penance, by which, she conquered even the great ascetics.

Thus by recalling Siva in her mind, Parvati, spent three thousand years in the tapovana.

The place where, Siva had performed penance for sixty thousand years, sitting over that place for a moment, Parvati, thought.

“Î Mahadeva, are you not still pleased with me, who is performing tapas since long? Because he has not appeared before me even after performing of my tapas for such a long time.

The Sastras and the Vedas, praise Siva, besides the sages, as the bestower of the welfare omniscient, all pervading and viewer of everything.

He bestows fortunes on all, the moulder of the five emotions, and fulfills the desires of all the devotees, besides removing the distress.

In case I am really devoted to the bull-horned lord, discarding all my desires, then, let him be pleased with me.

In case Pancaksra-mantra given to me by Narada, has been recited by me with devotion, then let Siva, be pleased with me.

I have adored Siva, by the method prescribed by the scriptures, then let Siva be pleased with me.”

Thus thinking, Parvati, lowering her head, becoming free from all the blemishes, performed tapas for long.

She performed tapas in a way, which was beyond the reach of even the great yogis. Observing the tapas of Parvati, all the people, got surprised.

All the sages reached there in order to observe the tapas performed by Parvati and by doing so they thought themselves to be graceful.”

The greatness lies in following the standards of the virtuous people. There is no delimitation in penance. Therefore the virtue should be honoured by the people with wisdom.

After observing or listening about the performing of the penance by this lady, what type of penance could be pursued by a man? A penance higher than this has never been seen before nor would it be seen in future.”

Thus saying the ascetics praised the penance of Parvati and then they returned to their respective places with delight.

Listen further to the influence of the tapas of Jagadamba- the mother of the universe, which, of course is surprising.

The living beings who were inimical to one on other; also reached there, and with the influence of her tapas they shed away their enmity.

The lions and the cows which are inimical by nature, also because of her tapas never tortured one an other.

Î Excellent sage, even the cat and mouse are traditionally inimical to each other, even they developed no blemish among themselves.

Î Excellent sage the trees were laden with fruits, and the land was decorated with various types of grass.

The place where Parvati had achieved success in tapas, the forest of the place had become as beautiful as the forest of Kailasa.

## Chapter 23 - Himavan dissuades Parvati but the gods go to meet Siva

Brahma said, “While thus propitiating so hard for Siva by Parvati, long time passed but Siva did not appear before her.

Parvati with a firm resolve, while still in the forest, was then visited by her parents with the courtiers and said to her.

Himalaya said, “Î Fortunate Parvati, why are you causing so much of pain to your body, when Siva is not appearing. He is indeed a recluse detached from the world.

You are quite slim with tender limbs and with this type of hard tapas undertaken by you, you would be fainted. I am speaking the truth to you.

Î Beautiful one, you better get up and go home. What have you now to do with Siva, who has actually burnt out Kamadeva.

Therefore the umblemished Siva shall never come to take you with himself. Why do you still feel fascinated to him?

Î Damsel with an auspicious conduct, as the moon in the sky cannot be caught, you think of Siva like that.

Brahma said, “Mena, Sahyadri, Meru mountain as well as Mainaka also advised her similarly.

Kraunca and other mountains, also spoke to her similarly with various types of arguments.

When all of them so spoke to Parvati, who was performing penance, smilingly said to Himalaya.

Parvati said, “O My mother, Î My father, I had earlier told you on the subject. Have you forgotten my words? Î My brother you also please listen.

Mahadeva is a recluse and detached who has even burnt Kamadeva. I shall surely bring round Siva who is dear to his devotees.

Now you can go delightfully to your respective abodes. He will surely be pleased. Don’t think it otherwise.

The one who burnt Kamadeva and also the mountain forest, I shall call him with the power of my tapas.

One can serve Siva with the great force of tapas. You must know this. I am speaking to you truthfully.”

Thus speaking to her mother Menaka and brothers Mainaka and Mandara and also her father Himalaya, the daughter of king of mountain kept quiet.

All of them, who were quite intelligent, felt surprised. Therefore, Himalaya, Sumeru and other mountains, listening to the words of Parvati and praising her, went back to their respective abodes.

After the departure of all of them, she, with the firm resolve, in the great truth, started performing more severe penance.

O Excellent sage, with the severe penance performed by Parvati, the gods, asuras humans, mobile and immobile beings started suffering.

Then the gods, the demons, Yaksas, Kinnaras, Caranas, siddhas, sadhyas, sages, Vidyadharas, Nagas, Prajapatis, Guhyakas and others started suffering immensely but no one could know the reason for the same.

All the gods, including Indra consulted Brhaspati, the preceptor of the gods and then came to me to take refuge.

The upset gods having lost their lustre, atonce arrived and offered their salutation to me. Then offering prayer to me, they spoke collectively.

The gods said, “O Lord, the whole of the universe including the mobile and immobile have been created by you. Then why is it suffering so much? We are unable to understand it.

O Brahma, O Lord, you tell us the reason for the same. Because it is you alone who can know about it. O Lord, no one else can protect these people with scorched bodies.”

Brahma said, “Listening to their words, I recalled Siva in my mind and found that it was the effect of the tapas of Parvati.

In this way the entire universe would be burnt out. Thus thinking, all of them went to the ocean of milk to apprise Visnu of the factual position of their sufferings.

Reaching there they found that lord Visnu was comfortably seated over the lion-throne. Finding him there, they bowed in reverence to him and offered prayer to the lord. Then all the spoke to him.

Î Mahavisnu, with the severe penance of Parvati, the gods have suffered and have arrived here to take refuge with you. You kindly protect us all.

Listening to the words of all the gods, Visnu- the lord of Laksmi, while seated over the serpent bed said to us.”

Visnu said, “I have today understood the cause of the tapas of Parvati. I shall go to Siva, with you today.

O Gods, let us pray to Siva, that for the welfare of the universe, he should go to Parvati and seek her hand in marriage.

All of us shall try that Mahadeva the holder of the Pinaka bow, should grant a boon to Parvati today itself.

Therefore, we shall all go there to the place where- Rudra- the great lord, the form of extreme benevolence, is performing penance.

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Visnu, all the gods said with one voice, “We are afraid of the angry, the burner Siva, who causes the dissolution.”

The gods said, “ Siva is like the terrific fire of the time of dissolution. He is full of anger and is Virupaksa (having three eyes). Therefore we shall not go to him.

The way he had earlier burnt the invincible Kamadeva, similarly he would also burn us out with his anger.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of the gods, Î Sage, Visnu spoke in order to console all the gods.

Lord Visnu said, “O Gods, you better listen to my words with respect. Siva is the lord of all of us. He makes all fearless. He will never burn you.

Therefore all of you people with wisdom, should get along with me to take refuge with him, because he (Siva) is compassionate to all.

Siva is the Purana-Purusa, the lord of all, has excellent features, a great ascetic, greater than the greatest, the supreme self, let us take refuge with him.”

Brahma said, “When the immensely influential Visnu, thus spoke to the gods, then all the gods followed him to meet Siva.

All the gods accompanying Visnu, first went to the hermitage of Parvati, since the road to Siva’s place was the same.

Observing the penance of Parvati, the illustrious gods bowed in reverence to the mother of the universe, who was engaged in tapas having brilliant features.

After praising the penance of Parvati, whose body was the personified tapas, the gods moved on to the place, where the bull- bannered lord was present.

After reaching there the gods sent you inside and they themselves stood at a distance from Siva, who had reduced Kama to ashes. They were just watching.

Î Narada, you are the devotee of Siva and fearless at the same time. You approached Siva who was extremely pleased.

Î Sage, then you making all the efforts, called for Visnu and other gods and took them to Siva.

Thereafter, reaching there, all the gods including Visnu, found Siva who is well disposed towards his devotees, comfortably seated there. He was seated on Yogapatta, surrounded by his ganas and was in the form of penance and Paramesvara.

Then Visnu alongwith gods, Siddhas and great Rsis, eulogised Siva, with the hymns from the Veda and Upanisads.

## Chapter 24 - Siva agrees to Marry Parvati

The gods said, “O Lord Siva, destroyer of Kama, worthy of eulogy, possessing enormous splendour, Î Three eyed lord, salutation to you.

Î Lord, clad in deer skin, Î Bhima, Bhimaksa, Mahadeva, and lord of the three worlds, salutation to you.

You are the lord of all the worlds, you are the father as well as the mother, you are Isvara, Sambhu, Isa, and are particularly compassionate.

You are the lord of the worlds, Î Lord you protect us. Î Mahesvara, who else is there to relieve us from the miseries?”

Brahma said, “Listening to such worlds, Nandisvara, (the vehicle of Siva) feeling extremely merciful, said.

Nandisvara said to Siva, “O Lord of all, Visnu and the crowd of the gods, the sages, groups of siddhas, are especially interested in having an audience with you. Having been disgraced by the demons, these gods, desirous of achieving protection, have arrived here to take refuge with you.

Therefore, you kindly arrange for the protection of the gods as well as the sages. You have been specially known as Kinsman of the down-trodden as well as compassionate on the devotees.”

Brahma said, “When the compassionate Nandi, thus submitted to Siva, then he slowly opened his eyes.

The lord possessing the supreme wisdom, the supreme soul, lord Siva, ended his samadhi and spoke to the gods.

Siva said, “O Gods like Brahma and Visnu, what for have all of you arrived here before me? You immediately speak out the reason for the same.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Siva, all the delightful gods, looked at Visnu for speaking to Siva, in reply to his words.

Then Visnu- the great devotee of Siva besides being beneficial for the gods, spoke to Siva, revealing the great purpose of the visit of the gods to that place.”

Visnu said, “Î Siva, Tarakasura, has been troubling the gods immensely, therefore they all have arrived here to narrate the extent of their sufferings.

O Siva, the demon can be killed by your son. I am speaking quite truthfully.

Î Mahadeva, thus thinking, you kindly extend your mercy on us. You kindly relieve the gods from the sufferings caused to them by Tarakasura.

And for that purpose, Î Lord, Parvati should be accepted by you in marriage, with your right hand. Giriraja also intends to give away Girija in marriage to you.”

Listening to these words of Visnu, Siva, who had been engaged in yogic practices indicating the auspicious movement, spoke with pleasure.”

Siva said, “The moment I accept the immensely beautiful Girija, then all the sages, rsis and munis, would be filled with passions or lust. No one would then proceed towards the path of moksa. Soon after, my accepting the hand of Girija, she would bring back Kamadeva to life.

Î Visnu, I had burnt Kamadeva, for the success of my mission, at the advice of Brahma. There is no doubt about it.

Î Lord of gods, Î Intelligent one, I, keeping in mind what was proper and what was improper, had done everything. You should therefore not at all be stubborn in your approach.

Î Visnu, by burning Kamadeva, I had done immense good to the gods. Therefore all of you should live with me, getting free from the desires.

You, endued with great penance should also perform hard tapas like me and all other gods.

Î Gods, getting free from Kama, you can be endowed with the supreme bliss, and be relieved from blemish by means of spiritual contemplation.

Î Gods like Brahma, Visnu, Indra besides the sages, whatever had been done by Kamadeva earlier, in case the said event had been forgotten by you, then it should again be remembered by you.

Î Gods, in earlier times Kamadeva, had spoiled the mediation of everyone, who was a good archer besides being stubborn.

Kama is the path to hell, it results in anger. From anger emerges delusion and delusions destroys the penance.

Î Best of the gods, all of you at my advice should get free from the lust and anger.”

At this Brahma said “The lord Vrsavahana, thus speaking, intended the sages and the gods to speak out something.

Thereafter lord Siva, keeping quiet was again engrossed in meditation and was then surrounded by his ganas.

Siva then thought within himself, his own soul, the form that was unsullied, free from blemish, aberrations and ailments. The said form was grater than the greatest, eternal, free from the sense of possession, free from obsession, beyond the sound and words, was devoid of attributes and which could be known by means of perfect wisdom. Thus thinking about his own features in his meditation, lord Siva, the cause of great pleasure and protection, then was engrossed in the supreme bliss.

On finding that Siva was again engrossed in meditation, all the gods of the heaven, besides Visnu, Indra and others spoke humbly to Nandi.

The gods said, “The detached Siva, has again been engrossed in tapas. You happen to be the friend of Siva, besides being the best of his servant and omniscient.

O Lord of the ganas, you kindly tell us the way by which lord Siva could be pleased. We take refuge in you.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, when the gods so spoke to Nandi with delight, then Nandi, the dear gana of Siva, spoke to the gods.”

Nandisvara said, “O Gods like Brahma, Visnu, Indra and others besides the sages, you listen to the words by which Siva could be pleased.

In case you today insist that Siva should marry, you should eulogise the lord with respect and piteous prayer.

Î Gods, Siva, ordinarily is subservient to the devotion. Finding the best of devotion, the lord, even does extraordinary things.

Brahma, Visnu and all other gods should perform in the same way, otherwise all of you can return by the same way by which you had arrived here.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, thus listening to the words of Nandi, which appealed to all, who started praising Siva, with utmost devotion.”

The gods said, “Î God of gods, Î Mahadeva, Î Ocean of mercy, we have arrived here to take refuge with you. You kindly redeem us from the misery.”

Brahma said, “In this way the gods eulogised Siva using piteous words. Getting upset with love, all of them started crying.

Visnu too speaking quite humble words, devoting his mind to Siva, submitted to the lord with devotion.”

Brahma said, “When so eulogised by lord Visnu and others, lord Siva, who was well disposed towards his devotees, put a stop to his meditation.

Feeling himself delighted, lord Siva pleased even the gods, looked at all of them with compassion.”

Siva said, “O Brahma, Visnu, Indra and other gods, why have you arrived here collectively? You speak out truthfully to me.”

Visnu said, “O Siva, you are omniscient, you are the immanent being and lord of all. Are you not aware of what is there in our minds? Still, I shall speak out at your command. Î Lord Siva, innumerable miseries have befallen on us due to the terror of the demon Ḍarṁêṁ. It is due to the same, that the gods have arrived here to eulogise you.

For achieving you Siva has been born as the daughter of Himalaya. He (Tarakasura) can be killed by your son born of Siva alone.

Brahma has given such a boon to Taraka. Since then unmindful of his death, he is torturing the entire universe.

Parvati, at the advice of Narada is performing hard tapas. With her refulgence, all the mobile and immobile beings, are sufferings.

Î Supreme lord, you go to Siva and grant her the desired boon to her. Î Lord, relieving the gods of all the miseries, make them comfortable.

Î Siva, we have developed a great desire in our minds to witness your marriage, let the same be performed in an appropriate manner.

Î Excellent one, the time for the fulfilment of the boon you had granted to Rati, has arrived. Therefore you kindly complete your pledge immediately.”

Brahma said, “Visnu and other gods, besides the sages, thus speaking, offered their salutation to lord Siva and eulogising him, with several stotras, they took their seats in front of Siva.

Listening to the words of the gods, Siva, the protector of the Vedic traditions and who was subservient to his devotees, smiled and spoke.

Siva said, “O Brahma, Visnu and other gods, all of you should listen to me with respect. I am going to speak out correct words in a suitable manner.

Marriage is not the appropriate thing for men, which is a great bondage, which binds family.

There are several type of the evil companies in the world, and the company of a woman is the worst of all. A person can shatter all other bondages of iron or wood, but he cannot be freed from the bondage of a woman.

The enjoyment of the worldly pleasures tighten the bondage. Salvation is beyond the reach of a person even in dream, who is involved in the enjoying of the worldly pleasures.

A person desirous of pleasure, should appropriately detach himself from the worldly pleasures, because the worldly pleasures have been equated with the poison, which serves as the killer of the human beings.

A person who talks to a person involved in the enjoyment of the worldly pleasures or a sensuous person, his down fall is imminent.

Though I am well aware of all these things, still I shall grant your prayer, making it a success.

I am always subservient to my devotees and act accordingly. Therefore I am known in the world as the one who performs ill-fitting things.

I made the vow of the king of Kamarupa a success. I saved the king Sudaksina, who had been taken prisoner by the king Bhimaraja.

(Sudaksina was the son of the king Paundraka and was related to Jarasandha. He had been entrusted with the responsibility of guarding the southern gate of the yajna. Bhimaraja had imprisoned him after defeating him (Bhagavata Purana 10.60). I am surely subservient to my devotees, therefore I may have to do everything. I am known the world over as the performer of ill fitting things.

Î Gods, I have relieved you of all the miseries. Because of my endearment towards my devotees, I drank poison, for the benefit of the gods. I have always been instrumental in the removing of the miseries of the gods.

On several occasions, I had to suffer variously for the sake of my devotees. Taking to the form of Grhapati, I removed the sufferings of the sage Visvanara.

O Brahma, Î Visnu, what more shall I speak, I am indeed speaking the truth. All of you are well aware of my pledge in a realistic manner.

Whenever my devotees are in trouble, then I always remove their sufferings.

I am fully aware of your sufferings at the hands of Tarakasura. Now I shall shortly remove your suffering caused by that demon.

Though I am least interested in the marriage, still I shall marry Girija for the sake of begetting a son.

Î Gods, now all of you should go happily to your abodes getting free from danger. I shall fulfil my task. There is no doubt about it.”

Brahma said, Thus speaking, keeping quiet, Siva was again absorbed in the tapas. Î Sage, Visnu and other gods, then proceeded on to their respective homes.

## Chapter 25 - Seven sages test the devotion of Parvati

Narada said, “After the departure of Brahma, Visnu and other gods from that place, what happened thereafter?

Î Dear one, what did Siva do? At what time Siva went to bestow boon on Parvati. You kindly speak out the story with pleasure.

Brahma said, “After the departure of the gods like Brahma and other, to their respective abodes, Siva in order to test the tapas of Parvati, who was engrossed in meditation, started thinking about the atma-tattva by means of his own soul. Who is greater than the greatest, free from illusion and obsessions, and lodged within itself.

The bull-bannered lord Siva, was then turned in the form which, no one could understand his movements, because he happened to be the creator and the Supreme Lord.

Brahma said, “Î Narada, at that point of time, Parvati was performing hard tapas, observing which even Siva felt surprised.

Being subservient to the devotee, he ended his samadhi. Then Siva- the creator, recalled Vasistha and other sages in his mind.

All the seven sages, delightfully praising Siva arrived there.

Feeling pleased, they offered their salutation to lord Siva, and started eulogising him with choked voice, folded hands and lowering their heads.

The seven sages said, “O Mahadeva, the lord of the gods, Î Ocean of mercy, Î Lord, we people feel graceful today, by your remembering us.

What is the purpose of your calling us here. Kindly get us the command. Be merciful on us like your own devotees. Salutation to you.”

Brahma said, “ Siva, the ocean of compassion, having been thus addressed by the sages, the lord with blossoming lotus like eyes said.

Mahesvara said, “O My dear seven sages, listen to my words urgently. You are my best well-wisher and are all knowledgeable.

Presently, Parvati, the daughter of Himalaya, is performing tapas with a concentrated mind.

Î Brahmanas, she, together with her maids, is engaged in tapas to achieve me as her husband, leaving all her other desires.

Î Sages, all of you at my command, go there and lovingly put to test her firmness in her resolve.

Î Ascetics, at my command you can utter deceitful words, shedding all the doubt.”

Brahma said, “Thus, at the command of Siva, all the seven sages went to the place where Parvati was performing tapas being the mother of the universe.

Reaching there, the sage found Parvati, the image incarnate of the penance and was illumining with her own glory.

All the seven ascetics then offered their hearty salutation to the goddess. Having been honoured by the goddess Bhagavati, they said.

The Rsis said, “O Daughter of Giriraja, what for are you performing the penance. Who is the god of your liking? You tell us.”

Brahma said, “When the sages so spoke to her, Siva, the daughter of Giriraja, inspite of being secret, she spoke truthfully before them.

Parvati said, “O Excellent sages, you listen to my words with your heart full of love. I am going to reveal the truth, whatever has been thought by me.

Listening to my impossible words, you people will laugh at me. Î Brahmanas, I am feeling shy to speak out. What should I do?

My stable mind is helplessly attempting at a great task and intends to raise a huge wall over the water.

I am performing tapas at the command of the divine sage Narada. The desire of my heart is that Lord Siva should be my husband.

The featherless bird in the form of my mind, is stubbornly flying in the sky. The hope of mine can be fulfilled only by Lord Siva and none else.”

Brahma said, “Listening to these words of Parvati, the sages smilingly honoured Girija, but spoke false and deceitful words.”

The Rsis said, “You are not aware of the cruel mind of Narada having a stone like heart, inspite of your possessing enormous learnings.

Narada also tells the falsehood, and indulges in the churning of others minds. By, listening to his words, one has to face all round misery.

With your noble wisdom you better listen to this beautiful story, which I am going to narrate quite lovingly. You better lodge it in your mind.

Daksa Prajapati, at the command of his father achieved ten thousand sons from his wife and made them to perform tapas.

All those sons went to the western ocean for the performing of the tapas. Narada also reached there.

He rendered them deceitful advice, as a result of which, they never returned to their abode.

On hearing thus, Daksa was annoyed. Brahma advised them properly, then he giving birth to another thousand sons, who were again sent for the performing of tapas.

At the command of their father, they also proceeded for tapas. Narada again went to them for rendering advice, who also followed the path of their brothers. They also became the Bhiksus, and never returned to their abode.

Î Parvati, this type of the behaviour of Narada is well known in the world. He makes the people like recluses.

There was a Vidyadhara named Citraketu, in earlier times. The sages advised him and he deserted his home.

By advising Prahlada, he made him suffer badly at the hands of his father. He is in the habit of spoiling the wisdom of others.

To whomsoever, advice was rendered by Narada, he deserting his house usually lived on begging.

Narada is deceitful at heart and is beautiful to look at. All of us know him pretty well being his companions.

The skylark is called to be a devotee or a gentle bird from a distance, but does he not eat the fish? In fact an associate knows the conduct of an associate.

You are respected by the people with wisdom and you also at his advice, becoming foolish are performing the hard tapas.

Î Girl, the one for whom you are performing the hard tapas is perpetually indifferent, unblemished and the enemy of Kamadeva. He has inauspicious body, is shameless has no home or the pedigree. He remains naked and is ill-featured. He is associated with ghosts and goblins. He remains naked and carries a trident.

The rogue of the sage Narada, has destroyed your wisdom with your illusion and confusing you has made you to perform the tapas.

What type of comfort are you going to enjoy by getting such a type of husband. Î Girija, you just think over it.

Earlier, he married the virtuous daughter of Daksa named Sati, and could not maintain her even for a few days.

Raising some blemish in her, he deserted her after sometime. The lord then went on meditating on his own form, free from stains, sorrows and sported happily.

He is single without a second and without attachment. He is after salvation, Î Gentle lady, how can a woman put up with him?

Even now, Î Fortunate one, leaving aside the evil ideas, you go home and you will surely meet welfare.

The groom suitable to you is the one possessing all the virtues, who lives in Vaikuntha, who is the lord of Laksmi and is well-versed in all the sports.

We shall arrange for your marriage with him. He can make you comfortable in all respects. You leave the stubbornness and Î Parvati, be comfortable.”

Brahma said, Parvati, the mother of the universe, listening to such types of words, she laughed and spoke to the omniscient sages thus.”

Parvati said, “O Sages, whatever has been spoken by you could be correct from your point of view, but Î Brahmanas, I am unable to discard my stubbornness.

I have been born of the mountain. Therefore, the hardness is quite natural with me. Therefore, you kindly don’t dissuade me from my path.

The words of the divine sage Narada are quite beneficial for me, which will never be neglected by me, because according to the people well-versed in the Vedas, the words of the preceptors are always beneficial.

The words of the preceptors are always beneficial and those who believe in them firmly, they never face misery in this as well as the future worlds.

Those who feel that the words of the preceptor are not true, they can never be comfortable in this world nor in the world after death. They always feel miserable.

Î Brahmanas, one should not neglect the words of the preceptors either in the house or in the forest. Therefore my stubbornness will surely provide comfort to me.

Î Sages, whatever has been spoken by you is improper. I shall point out in brief the real meaning of the same.

You have described Visnu as the above all and having all the noble virtues, who roams about everywhere, and that is true, and for the vices pointed out by you in Siva, I am going to give the reason for the same.

Siva is the Supreme Brahman, is the unblemished one. He takes to many forms for the sake of his devotees. He is not interested in displaying his worldly splendour.

Siva moves in the form of an Avadhut remains engrossed in the bliss and is the personified supreme bliss.

To adorn one’s body with the ornaments is a matter of illusion. He is Brahman, and he keeps himself away from the illusion. He is the lord, Nirguna, unborn, free from illusion, of invisible movement, and a cosmic Being.

Î Brahmanas, Siva does not shower his blessings on the ground of faith, caste etc. I know Siva only, through the blessings of the preceptor.

Î Brahmanas, in case Siva fails to marry me, I shall ever remain a virgin. I am speaking the truth.

In case the sun rises from the west, or the Meru mountain becomes mobile, even if the fire becomes cool, or the lotuses bloom over the rock at the top of the mountain, my stubbornness cannot be removed. I am speaking the truth.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking and then bowing to the sages, the daughter of the mountain kept quiet and remembered Siva with a devoted mind.

The sages on realising the firmness of Parvati, appreciated her and bestowed the excellent blessings on her.

The sages who had arrived to test the faith of Parvati, felt delighted after bowing to Parvati and at once returned to the place of Siva.

Reaching the place of Siva, they apprised him of the factual position and then taking leave of him with respect, went back to the heaven.

## Chapter 26 - Conversation between Jatila and Parvati

Brahma said, “After the departure of the sages, Siva the creator of the universe, himself resolved to put Parvati to test.

On the pretext of testing her, Siva took to a form with matted locks of hair, he proceeded on to the peak of Gauri Sankara.

Taking to the form of an old Brahmana, shining with brilliance, he was delighted in his mind. He carried an umbrella and a staff to support him.

He found the goddess seated over a pedestal surrounded by the maids. She looked like the digit of the moon.

Siva- who is well disposed towards his devotees, having the form of a Brahmacari, finding Uma there, lovingly went to her.

Finding a Brahmana’s arrival to her place, Siva called for the material and adored him.

She lovingly observing all the formalities, welcomed him, and respectfully enquired of his welfare.”

Parvati said, “Who are you arriving here in the form of a Brahmacari? Where from have you arrived? You are well-versed in the Vedas and the entire forest is illumining with your brilliance.”

Brahmana said, “I am an old Brahmana roaming about at will. I am intelligent ascetic who bestows happiness helping others.

Who are you? Who is your father? What for are you performing the hard tapas in this lonely forest, which is beyond the reach of even the sages.

You are neither a small girl nor an old woman, you are the beautiful damsel. What for are you performing the tapas without your husband.

Î Beautiful ascetic, are you the wife of some one, who does not take care of you? Or has he deserted you?

You tell me in which race are you born? Who is your father? What is your name? You seem to be extremely fortunate and are uselessly performing tapas.

Are your Savitri, who gave birth to the Vedas or are you Laksmi or Sarasvati, or either one of them? I would like to know about you.”

Parvati said, “O Brahmana, I am neither Savitri, nor Laksmi, nor Sarasvati. I am Parvati, the daughter of Himalaya.

In my earlier birth, I had been the daughter named Sati of Daksa Prajapati. My father denounced my husband then I burnt my body with the yogic fire.

As luck would have it, then I became the daughter of Himalaya and got Siva fortunately, but he burnt Kamadeva to ashes, then he left me and went away.

After his departure, due to my mental agony, I was upset and resolved to perform hard tapas and with that end in view. I reached over the bank of Svarganga.

After performing tapas for a long time, unable to find my husband, I thought to entering the fire, but in the mean time I found you and have stopped here for sometime.

You can go, because I intend to enter in the fire, because Siva has not accepted me. Wherever shall I take birth, I shall get Siva as my husband.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, Parvati in full view of Siva, entered the fire inspite of his preventing her from doing so.

But due to the influence of Siva, the fire, for Parvati, became cool like the sandal paste.

Remaining in the fire for sometime when she found that the fire was unable to burn her, she then got ready to leap towards the sky, then Siva- in the form of a Brahmana again asked her.

The Brahmana said, 'O Beautiful one, what type of tapas is being performed by you? Because of that you are unable to understand anything. Neither has the fire consumed your body, nor has your wish been fulfilled.

Therefore, you express your desire correctly before the blissful Brahmana like me.

Î Goddess, you express the thoughts of your mind before me, a Brahmana, appropriately. I have become friendly with you. Therefore do not conceal anything from me.

Î goddess, what type of boon is required by you. I want to ask you. Because it is in you that the fruit of the penance can be seen.

In case you are performing tapas for some one else, then you can do so. The gem is in your hand, leaving that, the collection of glass pieces is of no use.

Why have you covered your beauty with the bark garments or the animal hide instead of the costumes.

You speak out the real purpose of the tapas, hearing which a Brahmana like me could be pleased.

Brahma said, “When so asked by the Brahmana, then Parvati, indicated her maid, for giving an answer and he made her to speak out the factual position.

Then at the instance of Parvati, Vijaya- the dearest maid spoke to the Brahmacari.

The maid said, “O Ascetic, I shall narrate the excellent story of Parvati, together with the reason for her performing the tapas, in case you be interested in the listening of the same.

This friend of mine is the daughter of Giriraja Himalaya, known by the name of Parvati. Mena is the name of her mother. She has not yet been married. She does not desire anyone else except Siva to be her husband. For that purpose she has performed tapas for three thousand years.

My friend had started tapas for the same purpose. Î ascetic Î Brahmana, I shall speak out the reason for the same, which you please listen.

Parvati, in reference to Brahma, Visnu, Indra or other gods, would like to have Siva, in the form of a husband.

Î Brahmana, the trees which had been planted by Parvati earlier, are now sprouting and yielding fruits.

My friend has been performing severe penance at the advice of Narada, to make her beauty fruitful and to establish her father’s race, besides blessing Kama. She has directed her penance towards lord Siva. Î Holy ascetic, it is strange that her desire is not being fulfilled.

O Excellent Brahmana, I have first told you everything out of my love for her. What more do you want to ask.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the true words of Vijaya, Î Sage Narada, Siva, who had arrived there disguised as an ascetic laughingly said.”

The ascetic said, “The words spoken by the maid look like a big joke. In case it is true then she should speak out from her own mouth.”

Brahma said, “At these words of the Brahmana with the matted locks of hair, the goddess Parvati, repeated the words spoken by her maid, from her own mouth to the Brahmana.

## Chapter 27 - Talk between Parvati and Brahmacari

Parvati said, “O Excellent sage with the matted locks of hair, listen to my entire story. Whatever my friend has stated, the things are exactly like that, there is not an iota of falsehood in it.

Siva, has been accepted by me in my mind speech and action as well as by the means of my ascetic feelings.

I am well aware of the fact that it is quite an inaccessible object. How can I attain it? But still out of my anxiety I am performing this tapas.

Brahma said, “After thus speaking to the old Brahmana, Siva kept quiet. Listening to the words of Parvati the Brahmana said.

The Brahmana said, “For so long, I had desired that I should leave for my place after knowing from the goddess, the purpose for which she had been performing the tapas, and thereafter I could go to my place. You can do whatever you like.

Had you not spoken to me, the friendship would have become infructuous. As is the karma as well as the destiny, one should speak it out.”

Brahma said, “Speaking these words to her, as soon as the Brahmana intended to go, then Parvati offering her reverence spoke to the Brahmana again.”

Parvati said, “O Excellent Brahmana, where are you going? You stay here for some more time and talk of my welfare.” At these words of Parvati, the staff bearer stopped and said.

The Brahmana said, “By stopping me with devotion, do you want to listen something from me. I am therefore going to talk on the tattva, which would bestow the divine knowledge on you.

Mahadeva is quite well known to me. He is the preceptor of dharma. I am speaking out correctly. You listen to me attentively.

Mahadeva has a bull for his mount and applies ashes over his body. He has matted locks of hair over the head. The tiger or the deer skin is worn by him.

He holds a skull in his hand, the serpents crawl over his body. He consumes poison and the forbidden food. He has three eyes and is quite horrible to look at.

No one is aware about his birth. He has no home and is deprived of all the pleasures. He is without robes, having ten hands, and is always surrounded by the ghosts and goblins.

What for do you desire him as your husband? Where has your intelligence disappeared. Î Goddess, you just think over and tell me.

I had earlier learnt about his terrific vrata. I can speak out the same, in case you are really interested to listen to it.

Due to the move of destiny, Sati, the daughter of Daksa Prajapati, had married Siva. But what was the pleasure enjoyed her?

Learning that Sati was the wife of the skull-bearing Siva, Daksa discarded her. He deprived Siva of his share of the yajna.

Then Sati, realising her own insult as well as that of her husband, got enraged she deserted Siva by ending her own life.

You are the gem of the woman and your father happens to be the king of the mountains. Then why do you want to achieve such a husband by performing such a hard penance.

In exchange for a precious diamond you intend to get a piece of glass. You intend to apply the mud over your body, discarding the sandal-paste.

Discarding the sun-shine, you are desirous of the light of the fire-fly. Disowning the silken cloth, you intend to wear the leather.

Shedding away the comfortable living in the house, you intend to be a forest dweller. Discarding the excellent treasure, you intend to collect the iron.

Leaving aside Indra and other Lokapalas, you aspire to get Siva as your husband. This is not at all proper. It is also against the worldly conventions.

On the one hand, you have the eyes resembling the lotus petals, whereas Siva has three eyes while you are moon-faced, and on the other hand Siva has five faces.

On your head, you have a beautiful and divine plaited hair, resembling a she-serpent, while Siva wears the well-known matted locks of hair.

While the sandal paste has been applied over your body but the limbs of Siva have been plastered with ashes of the cremation ground. While you are clad in silken garments, but Siva is clad in elephant hide.

While your body is adorned with divine ornaments, on the other hand serpents are entwined over the body of Siva. While you are served by the gods, but Siva is served by the goblins and ghosts.

While cymbals are played in your home, and on the other hand Siva has the double drum damaru in his possession. You have the auspicious sound of the drums, while Siva has the inauspicious horn to serve as a sound.

On the one hand is the sound of double drum, and on the other is the sound of the throats ghosts and goblins. Therefore there is no matching beauty between the two of you.

In case he had possessed the riches he would never have remained naked. Bull is his vehicle. Therefore it appears that he possesses nothing.

The virtues of the grooms, who could provide comforts to the ladies have to be taken into consideration Virupaksa Siva, has no virtues absolutely.

On the other hand, Kamadeva, who is quite dear to you has also been burnt out by him. He after honouring you, left for some other place, deserting you at the same time.

No one is aware of his caste. He education is also unknown. The ghosts assist him and he has the poison in his throat.

He always remains alone and is particularly unattached. Therefore you do not get attracted towards Siva. You have the beautiful garland around your neck, while Siva wears the garland of skull. Your body has been applied with cosmetics of sandal wood, whereas the body of Siva is smeared with ashes of the cremation ground.

Î Goddess, the features and beauties of yourself as well as Siva, are of opposite direction. Atleast it does not appeal me. You may, however, do whatever you like.

All, whatever has to be discarded is now being desired by you. You may now detract your mind from him, otherwise you can do whatever you like.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of the Brahmana denouncing Siva, Parvati felt enraged and she spoke to him.

## Chapter 28 - Witnessing of the real form of Siva by Parvati

Parvati said, “For so long, I had thought that someone else had come. But now everything has become clear. You are a person who cannot be killed.

Î Lord, whatever has been spoken by you is false. In case you know him well, then how could you speak against his performance.

Have you ever found Mahesvara in this form? He happens to be the Supreme Brahman, and can take to any form due to his sports.

Taking to the form a Brahmacari, you intend to cheat me? Taking to the deceitful form, you are speaking foul words.

I am quite well aware of the form of Siva. Therefore I place before you the Siva-tattva quite thoughtfully.

In fact he is the nirguna Brahman. For specific reason he take to the Saguna form. How could there be some one who being of nirguna nature could take to saguna form at will? The said Sadasiva is the central place of all the lores. Then what has the Supreme soul to do with the ordinary lore.

At the beginning of the kalpa all the Vedas emerged from the breath of Siva, which were given to Visnu initially. Then who is the lord comparable with Visnu.

How could he be measured, in age, who is primordial to everything and in everyone? Even the primordial nature Prakrti, was born out of him. Therefore, how could that Sakti, be of any avail to him.

Such of the people who always adore Siva, the lord of the Saktis, he bestows on them three types of everlasting energies.

By adoring him, a person, overcomes the death fearlessly. His name as Mrtyunjaya is well known throughout the world.

By his favour Visnu retains his Visnuhood, Brahma the Brahmahood, and the gods their godhoods.

As Indra goes first of all to meet lord Siva, similarly the other living beings as well as the gatekeepers also go to him for the same purpose.

When the bottom of the Sivaganas falls over the crown of Indra, then it starts glittering. What else can I speak in his favour? He himself is the great lord.

What can a person not achieve by serving lord Siva who is the form of benevolence. There is no shortage with Sadasiva, that he would be desirous of me?

A person who had been a pauper for seven births, when serves Siva, he achieves he fortunes which last for long.

All the eight nidhis (treasures) dance before him daily lowering their heads. Therefore what is beyond him?

Though the costumes of Siva are not auspicious, but still his devotees meet with welfare, by adoring him.

He is the one, by adoring whom, all the desires of his devotees are fulfilled. How could a blemish appear in the unblemished Siva?

A person who always recites the name of Siva, all other people get purified simply by looking at him.

You have stated that the ashes of the cremation ground are inauspicious, in case this be true then why do the ashes from the body of Siva are applied by the gods over their heads?

The lord, who taking to the saguna form performs as a creator, sustainer and the destroyer, how could the same Siva be called as nirguna?

Siva- the supreme soul, has the form of Brahman, devoid of attributes. How can the people like you know him who speak against him?

The one who is wicked, sinful and opposes the Vedas, he is ignorant of the nirguna-tattva of Siva.

A person being ignorant of Siva-tattva, denounces the lord, all the merits earned by him throughout his life, get destroyed.

You have denounced here the illustrious Siva, and I have adored you- the denouncer of Siva, therefore, I have also earned the sin.

After having a look at the person who denounces Siva, one should take bath with clothes, performing repentance at the same time.

Î Wicked one, you told me that you knew Siva well. But surely you are unaware of the eternal Siva.

Whatever form might be possessed by Siva, and irrespective of his being of several forms, but he is surely dear to the noble people, and unblemished, besides being my beloved.

Even Brahma and Visnu could not be compared with him who is the great soul, then what to speak of the other gods who are subservient to the times.

Thus thinking with my truthful wisdom, I am performing the hard penance in order to achieve Siva.

He is the supreme lord, lord of all and dear to the devotees. He is compassionate over the down trodden people, and I am desirous of achieving him.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, thus speaking, Girija, the daughter of Giriraja, kept quiet and started adoring the unblemished Siva in her mind.

Listening to the words of Girija, as soon as the Brahmcari Brahmana, was about to say anything, Girija who was fully devoted to Siva, was averse to the denouncement of Siva, then spoke to her maid.

Girija said, “You better stop this wicked Brahmana, making all the efforts. He is about to speak out something more, denouncing and rebuking Siva.

It is not the one who denounces Siva, who earns the sin, but the one who listens to the rebuke of Siva, also earns the sin.

It is the duty with the devotees of Siva, that they should destroy those who rebuke Siva. In case he is a Brahmana, he should be spared or the hearer should leave that place without delay, at once.

The wicked man will again denounce Siva. Since he is a Brahmana, he is not to be killed and should be abandoned.

He should not be seen again at all. Let us leave this place and go else where. Let us not look at him.”

Brahma said, “Saying this, Î Sage, when Parvati was about to step forward, the Brahmana, held the hand of Parvati.

He then displayed his beautiful form, which was adored by Parvati. Siva then lowered her head with shyness.”

Siva then said to Parvati, “Where are you going leaving me alone here? Now I shall not leave you. I am pleased with you. Ask for a boon. You can be bestowed with everything.

From today onwards, I am your slave, you have indeed purchased me with your penance. I am attracted towards your beauty as well. Without you even a moment is like a yuga for me.

You better shed away your shyness. You had been my spouse since many births. Î Girija you better think yourself with your own noble wisdom.

Î Damsel with firm wisdom, I put you to test in many ways. You forgive me for my behaviour, which I displayed because of the worldly traditions.

No one in the three worlds is dearer to me them you are. I am subservient to you by all means. Î Siva, you fulfill my desire.

Î Dear, you come to me. You are my wife and I am your husband. Now I shall go to my abode in Himalaya with you.”

Brahma said, “At these word of Mahadeva, Parvati was pleased and she forgot all the pain she had to face during the time of tapas.

Î Excellent sage, all the sufferings of the chaste Parvati were over, because, the pain in the efforts performed is forgotten, after the receipt of the reward.

## Chapter 29 - Talk between Siva and Parvati

Narada said, “O Brahma, Î Fortunate one, what happened thereafter, I would like to hear everything.

Brahma said, “O Divine sage, you can listen from me what happened next. I shall start the story which destroys all the sins and enhances devotion towards Siva.

Î Brahmana, on hearing the words of Siva- the great soul, and witnessing his true and pleasant form, Parvati felt very much delighted.

The immensely chaste lady, goddess Parvati, replied to the lord, standing close to him with great delight with her face beaming with love.

Parvati said, “O Lord of the gods, you happen to be my master. Have you forgotten the one for whom you had destroyed the yajna of Daksa?

You are the same and I also happen to be the same. Presently I have been born of the womb of Mena, to make the task of the gods who have been terrified of Taraka, a success.

Î Master, in case you are really happy with me, and are kind to me, then you become my husband.

With your permission I shall now proceed to the abode of my parents and you display your glory in the form of your marriage.

Î Lord, you go to my father Himalaya and ask for my hand since you are clever in the divine sports.

By spreading you glory in the world, you make my father successful as a householder.

With the advice of the sages, my father, together with his kins, will accept your proposal delightfully.

Earlier, I had been the daughter of Daksa, when I was given over to you by my father, then did you not marry me appropriately?

Since my father Daksa did not adore the planets, therefore such type of hindrance was created in the married life.

Î Lord, Mahadeva, this time, for the establishment of the task of the gods, you get the marriage performed in an appropriate manner.

You therefore marry me surely observing all the rites of the marriage and in accordance with the rules, for the fulfilment of the task of the gods.

The traditional procedure of the marriage must be followed. Let Himavan realise that his daughter has well performed the auspicious penance” (for seeking Siva in marriage).

Siva said, “You better listen to my words. You move in such a way, which provides welfare and by which no obstruction of any kind is caused.

Î Beautiful one, all the moveable and immovable beings starting from Brahma, are all perishable.

The one who is standing before you (Siva) is one but takes to many forms. I become Saguna inspite of being nirguna. I am illumined with my own brilliance. Presently you own lustre has been added to it.

Î Goddess, though I had always been free, but I have been made subservient to you. You happen to be Prakrti, who performs everything, besides being the great illusion or Mahamaya.

Î Goddess, the entire universe has been made of the illusion. It is held by the supreme soul with great wisdom. It is united and covered by the ganas of nature of the Souls akin to the nature of the Supreme Soul.

Î Excellent godess, what have you spoken? For Siva, except you what else are the planets? What are the seasons, Î Fair complexioned lady?

With the difference of attributes and actions, because of our favourable disposition towards the devotees, the universe has been created.

You are indeed the subtle primordial nature comprising of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. You are capable of the perpetual activity. You possess the attributes and are also without them.

O Slender wasited Parvati, I happen to be the form of the soul for all the living beings of the world. Becoming unblemished and without having any desire, I take to different forms as per the desire of my devotees.

Î Parvati, daughter of the mountain, I shall not go to your father Himavat as a mendicant, begging for you.

Î Parvati, when the immensely noble people also, beg with spreading of palms, then they feel the inferiority complex.

After knowing all this Î Virtuous lady, what type of task do you intend to be performed by me. Î Beautiful one, you can do anything you like except this.”

Brahma said, Inspite of thus speaking the lotus eyed Parvati, bowed in reverence to Siva and spoke to him again and again.

Parvati said, “You are the soul, while I am Prakrti. There is no doubt about it. Inspite of our being independent, we are subservient to the devotees, whether we are with or without attributes. Î Lord, Î Sambhu, making all the efforts, you agree to my words, you ask for me from Himalaya, making me fortunate at the same time.

Î Siva, I am always your devoted servant. Be compassionate on me. I have been your wife in all the births.

You are Brahman, the supreme soul, without attributes, beyond Prakrti, unblemished, without desires, independent and Paramesvara.

Inspite of that taking to the Saguna form, you are engaged in the redeeming of your devotees. You sport about in your own soul, engrossed in it and you are quite familiar in all your sports.

Î Mahesvara, Î Mahadeva, I know you fully well. Î Omniscient one, what is the use of talking more. You kindly be compassionate on me.

Performing the astonishing sport, expand your glory in the universe, singing which appropriately, a person should cross the ocean of the universe.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking to Siva, Parvati offered her salutation to him lowering her head and with folded hands and then she stopped.”

At this prayer of Parvati, Siva, the great soul, in order to uphold the worldly tradition, agreed to do so and got ready for the purpose.

Thereafter, Siva, disappearing from the scene, went to Kailasa with the attraction for Kali preserved in his mind.

Reaching there, he conveyed the news to Nandi and others, who also felt delighted.

Thereafter, Bhairava and other ganas, also felt happy on learning the news and they celebrated huge festival.

Î Narada, everything went on in an auspicious manner. The miseries were ended and Siva himself was in a pleasant mood.

## Chapter 30 - Return of Parvati and the festivities

Narada said, “O Brahma, you are the bestower of the salvation, and are therefore graceful. I was able to listen to this astonishing story by your grace.

O Intelligent one after the departure of Siva to Himalaya, where did Parvati, the bestower of welfare, go and what did she do? You kindly tell me.”

Brahma said, “O Dear one, you listen to me attentively, what happened thereafter, with delight. After the proceeding of Siva to his abode, Parvati also, recalling his name in her mind, thinking her beauty to be successful, reciting the name of Mahadeva, returned to her parents’ place.

Listening to the news about the return of Parvati, Mena and Himalaya were filled with delight, they boarded the divine plane and proceeded towards that side.

He was accompanied by his family priest, the people of the place, several maids, and other kinsmen, who also went with him.

With their minds having been filled with delight, they shouted the slogans of victory including Mainaka and other brothers, who also went there.

The auspicious water pots, decorated with sandal paste, agaru, musk the branches of trees besides the fruits were placed on the both sides of the road.

The priests, Brahmanas, the auspicious sages, the female dancers and the sages reciting the Vedas went along, mounted over the elephants in order to welcome Parvati. The road was decorated with the trunks of the banana trees, the damsels with their husbands and sons, stood on the way carrying the burning lamps in their hands.

The Brahmanas were reciting the Vedic hymns, the conches were blown, and several types of musical instruments were being played upon.

In the meantime Durga, reached near the city and was spotted by her parents, while she was entering the city.

Becoming anxious with delight, Kali on the other hand, rushed towards them and she offered her salutation to her parents with her maids.

Bleating her, they said, “O Daughter.” Thus speaking they embraced her and becoming emotional with affection, they started crying.

Thereafter the other related women together with the wives of her brothers also embraced her.

They said, “You have performed the task for redemption of the entire family, pretty well. With your tapas all of us have been purified.

Praising her, all of them bowed in reverence to her. They offering the flowers, sandal paste, adored Siva.

At the same time the gods arrived in the sky, boarding their respective planes and showered the rain of flowers on her, besides eulogising her variously.

Then all the Brahmanas, made her mount over the decorated chariot and allowed her to enter the city.

At that point of time, the Brahmanas, the maids and several other damsels were of course present, who made her enter the house ceremoniously.

Î Excellent sage, the damsels, showered the fried paddy over as the ceremonial ablution. The Brahmanas showered their blessings on her, both Himalaya and Mena, were extremely happy at that time.

They felt that their household life to be quite fruitful, because a virtuous daughter is better than an evil son. Then Himalaya, praising Narada said, “You are graceful.”

Giriraja then distributed monetary gifts to the Brahmanas and the lords. He made the Brahmanas and others to recite auspicious hymns as the part of festivities.

Î Sage, thus the parents were quit happy with their daughter. All the brothers, daughters-in-law, close kinsmen and the woman, delightfully sat in the courtyard of Himalaya's house, with Parvati.

Then, Î Dear one, Himalaya honoured with pleasure, all the people who had arrived there and thereafter he left the place for taking a bath in the Ganga.

In the meantime, Siva, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, and well-versed in divine sports, assuming the guise of a dancer, reached before Menaka.

He held the blowing horn in the left hand and the small double drum in his right hand. He was wearing a red cloth and a sack was hanging behind his back. Disguised as a dancer, well-versed in dancing, Siva danced well and sang several sweet songs in sweet voice.

He blew the horns and played on the little drum in sweet tunes. Everything was quite pleasant.

To witness the performance of the dancer, all the men and women of the city besides all the children and old people collected there.

Î Sage, listening to his pleasant song and the charming dance, Mena and all others present there were filled with ecstasy.

Finding Siva in her heart holding trident etc. in his hand and extremely handsome, Durga was fainted. The ashes were applied over his body, wearing the garland of skulls, having three eyes over the face, wearing the yajnopavita of snake, Siva said, “Ask for the boon you desire.” Siva had the fair complexion, who was friendly to the poor, ocean of mercy and beautiful in all respects.”

Finding Siva in her heart in this form, Siva offered her salutation to him in reverence and asked for a boon from him to become her husband.

Lovingly, bestowing a boon to Siva, from his heart, Siva disappeared, while the mendicant continued to dance.

Then Mena feeling pleased with his fortunes carried the gems in a golden vase in order to give them to Siva.

He did not accept the gems but in place of the gems, he asked the hand of Parvati and then he started dancing and singing.

Mena was surprised and enraged at his words. She rebuked the mendicant and intended to drives him out.

At the same time Himalaya arrived there after having his bath in the Ganga. He found the mendicant in human form in his courtyard.

Learning of the news from the mouth of Mena, he was enraged and asked the servants to drive out the dancer.

Î Excellent sage, no one could drive out the dancer, who could not be touched like the burning fire and was filled with lustre. No one could drive him out.

Î Dear one, the mendicant who was well-versed in various types of sports, displayed before Himalaya, his endless great power.

Himalaya then found him in the form of Visnu, adorned with the Kirita crown, Kundalas, yellow garments, and four hands.

Whatever flowers had been offered by him to Visnu at the time of his worship, were all found in his body.

Thereafter, Giriraja found him in the form of four headed Brahma of red complexion, reciting the Vedic hymns.

Thereafter Giriraja saw him in the form of the sun which happens to be the eye of the universe, in a moment.

Î Dear one, thereafter, Himalaya, saw him in the form of Siva with Parvati, illumining at the same time.

Then he saw him as a mass of splendour without any specific form. It was unsullied, free from peculiar attributes, and desires. It was wonderful and formless.

Thus he found him in many forms and with many features, which surprised him pleasing him at the same time.

Thereafter the best of the mendicant, then begged for the hand of his daughter and he accepted nothing else.

Having been confused with the illusion of Siva Giriraja did not accept that proposal. Thereafter, the mendicant disappeared from that place, without accepting anything at all.

After his departure, both Mena and Giriraja came to realise that both of them had been cheated by Siva.

Thus thinking both of them developed in their minds devotion towards Siva, which bestowed moksa and bliss.

## Chapter 31 - Illusion of Siva

Brahma said, “O Narada, realising about the undisturbed and great devotion of both Himalaya and Mena, towards Siva, Indra and all other gods felt immensely concerned.

The gods said, “In case Himalaya gives away his daughter with utmost devotion to Siva, then surely he will achieve moksa, disappearing from Bharata.

The mountain is the abode of enormous gems. In case he leaves the earth, the name of the earth as the abode of gems would become infructuous.

He will assume his divine form casting off his immobile aspect and giving away his daughter to Siva, taking to the divine form, he will go to the place of Siva.

Reaching there he will surely merge into the form of Siva and enjoying the best of pleasures, he will surely achieve moksa.

Brahma said, “Thus consulting among themselves, all the gods, thought of deputing their preceptor to Himalaya.

Î Narada, Indra, who is of selfish nature, accompanied with other gods went to the place of his preceptor.

Indra and other gods, reaching the abode of his preceptor, respectfully narrated their feelings to him.

The gods said, “O Preceptor, for the success of our task, you kindly go to the abode of Himalaya and denounce Siva, making all the efforts.

Durga is not going to marry anyone else except Siva. By giving away his daughter half heartedly to Siva, he will not earn full merit.

Himalaya is presently lodged on earth. Since it is the abode of innumerable gems, therefore, you establish him on earth.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of the gods, the preceptor did not agree with them and reciting the name of Siva, he placed both his hands over his ears.

The preceptor, with a benevolent mind, recalling Siva in his mind, rebuked the gods again and again and said.

Brhaspati said, “All the gods are selfish in nature and sabotage the interest of others. By denouncing Siva, I shall surely fall in hell.

Let some one among you go to Himalaya, and do good to himself by advising him.

In case he gives the daughter unwillingly, he will remain on earth and in case he gives away the daughter with devotion, then he is sure to achieve moksa.

Afterwards the seven divine sages will advise Himalaya that Durga is not going, you accompanying Indra, go to Brahmaloka and convey the news to Brahma. He will be able to do your job.”

Brahma said, “Hearing this, all the gods made consultations among themselves and then they reached in my court and they discussed the matter with me quite respectfully.

Î Sage, listening to the words of the gods about denouncing of Siva, I, the reciter of the Vedas lamented and said.

Brahma said, “O My sons, I am unable to perform the task of the unbearable denouncing of the lord Siva, which is the cause of misfortunes and the destruction of fortunes.

Î Gods, you should go to Kailasa and please Siva and send him to the place of Himalaya.

Let him go and denounce himself before Himalaya, because the denouncement of others leads to destruction, while one’s own denouncement earns glory.”

Brahma said, “The gods listening to my words, offering their salutation to me, went to Kailasa- the chief of the mountains.

Finding Siva there, the gods, lowering their heads, bowed in reverence to him and started eulogising him with folded hands.”

The gods said, “O God of gods, Î Siva, all of us take refuge in you and you remove the miseries of your devotees.”

Î Lord, you are favourably disposed towards your devotees, always engaged in their tasks, you are the uplifter of the distressed and ocean of mercy. You remove our miseries and distress.

Brahma said, “Thus eulogising Siva, Indra and other gods, placed the entire news respectfully before Siva.”

Listening to the words of the gods, lord Siva, accepted their request with a smile.

All the gods, reaching their respective abodes thought that the task was done and started praising Sadasiva.

Thereafter Siva- the lord of illusion, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, being unblemished, went to Giriraja.

At that point of time Giriraja was seated over the lion throne, surrounded by his kinsmen and Parvati in the assembly.

At that every moment Sadasvia arrived there wearing the shining tilakam over the forehead, carrying a beautiful umbrella and a danda. He was clad in beautiful clothes.

He was holding a rosary of crystal beads, wearing Salagrama around his neck, reciting the name of Hari with devotion. Taking to the form of a Brahmana ascetic, arrived there.

Finding him there, Himalaya got up with his kinsmen. Finding a unique guest he prostrated before him.

Parvati also offered her salutation with devotion to the lord of her life. Recognising him Parvati, delightfully offered her prayer to him.

Siva in the form of a Brahmana, blessed all. Î Dear one, he praised heartly the goddess Siva, blessing her at the same time.

The king of mountains Himalaya respectfully offered him madhuparka etc. which was accepted by Brahmana with pleasure.

Then great mountain Himalaya adoring the Brahmana appropriately and enquired about his welfare delightfully.

Then Giriraja enquired the Brahmana about his identity with all respect. Brahmana also replied soon with due respect.

The Brahmana said, “O foremost among the mountains! I am a learned Vaisnava-Brahmana. I roam about on earth living on astrology and match making.

By the grace of my preceptor, I move like the speed of mind, can move everywhere, am omniscient, simple minded and help others. I have an auspicious soul, besides being the ocean of mercy and the remover of all the blemishes.

I am aware of the fact that you are inclined to give away this daughter with divine beauty to Siva.

He is helpless having no shelter, has no association, is ugly, devoid of virtues, dweller of the cremation ground, wearers of snakes.
