He remains naked; has a dirty body, is adorned with the ornaments of snakes. His pedigree is unknown. His conduct is bad and he always remains wandering.

His body is smeared with ashes, he remains furious always, he lacks wisdom, his age is unknown and always wears the crown of the matted locks of hair over his head.

He supports all those who roam about, he is adorned with the garlands of snakes, is a mendicant, is the follower of the wrong path and stubbornly discards the path of the Vedas.

O Mountain, your present inclination is not at all auspicious, Î Best of the learned people born in the race of Narayana, you should be sensible.

Siva is not at all the deserving person. On hearing this the people at large will laugh at you with disdain.

Î Giriraja, look here, he is devoid of kinsmen, you are the enormous abode of gems, while Siva is a pauper.

O lord of mountains! you, leaving Parvati, consult your other relatives like sons, wife and the wise courtiers.

O wise mountain, the patient does not like the medicine and on the contrary, he likes the harmful diet that increases the sickness, appeals him the most.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking the Brahmana stopped. Thereafter he took the food and left the place delightfully for his abode.

## Chapter 32 - Arrival of Sapta-Rsis

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of the Brahmana, feeling painful at heart and dropping tears, Mena, said to Himalaya.

Mena said, “O Giriraja, you listen to my words which are going to ultimately result in comfort. You better ask the opinion over the words of the Brahmana, from the devotees of Siva.

The Brahmana who had been the devotee of Visnu has denounced Siva. Î Lord of mountains, listening to the same, I feel extremely painful at heart.

O Lord of mountains, I shall not give my daughter to that Siva, because of his being ugly, devoid of humility and virtues, because my daughter is quite beautiful and possesses all the virtues.

In case you do not agree to my words, then I shall end my life or consume poison.

I shall bind a rope around the neck of Parvati and drag her to the forest and drown her in the ocean. But I shall never, give my daughter to Siva.”

Thus speaking, Mena, with her mind filled with grief, retired to the chamber of anger, discarding food and lay down over the bare floor.

Î Dear one, Siva on the other hand, who was upset with the pangs of separation, at once recalled the seven sages.

At the recalling of Siva, the Saptarsis, at once arrived there like the kalpavrksa.

Arundhati, also herself accompanied them. On the arrival of the seven sages illumining like the rays of the sun, Siva discarded performing the tapas.

Î Sage, the seven sages, offered their salutation to Siva, in reverence and standing before him they eulogised him, considering themselves to be quite fortunate and spoke to him.

Thereafter feeling surprised, they again offered their salutation to Siva the lord of the three lokas and then spoke.

The sages said, Î Best of all the lords, you are a Cakravarti among the gods, we consider ourselves to be extremely fortunate.

In earlier times we had performed the tapas thrice and had studied the Vedas, had performed homas offering the three types of oblations, had visited several holy places, and performed all the noble deeds.

Whatever was possible with our minds, speech and the body, we have been successful with your simply remembering us.

A person, who daily adores you, he gains success in his desires. What could be said about the merits of the people who are remembered by you.

O Sadasiva, with you remembering us today, we have become the best, usually, you never come across the path of desires and aspirations of the ordinary people.

As the fruit grown at height is beyond the reach of a dwarf, the one who is blind by birth, is deprived of eye-sight, the dumb person cannot gain speech, or a pauper can never have the sight of the treasures.

The lame person cannot reach the mountain top a barren woman cannot produce child.

Similarly, Î Lord, we could get an audience with you, which is beyond the reach of an ordinary person.

What more can we speak on the subject? Î God of gods, you are the lord of all the gods. By an audience with you we have become worthy of great respect.

You are complete in all respects. What are we required to do? In case you are really kind to us, then command as a task to be performed by the slaves like us.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of the sages, Siva, depending over the worldly traditions, spoke very pleasing words.

Siva said, “The rsis are always respectable, and out of the rsis you are more respectable Î Brahmanas, I have remembered you for a particular job.

My intentions are to do favour to others and you are well aware of the same. I have to be specially benevolent to the people.

The gods are frightened from the wicked Tarakasura. He has become invincible because of the boon granted to him by Brahma, what shall I do?

O Sages, the eight cosmic bodies possessed by me, are not for my self-interest, but are meant for the welfare of the others and this is well known

Still I would like to marry Siva. She on her part has performed very hard tapas which is beyond the reach of the sages, in order to achieve me.

I have also to bestow the desired reward to her for her benefit. This is my clear vow, which delights my devotees.

At the instance of Parvati, I had gone to the abode of Himalaya as a mendicant. I purified Kali with my divine sport.

Taking me to be the Supreme Brahman, both Mena and Himalaya, agreed to give their daughter to me with Vedic rites.

Then at the instance of the gods, I taking to the form of Visnu’s devotee went to the abode of Himavan and denouncing myself. I have shattered their devotion in me as a result of which they have become averse to me and do not feel like giving away their daughter to me.

Therefore, all of you should go to the abode of Himalaya and advise him appropriately.

Making all the efforts, you should speak to them the words as per the provision of the Vedas. You should establish this noble cause, by whatever means, it is possible to do so.

Î Best of the sages, I would like to marry their daughter and I have already granted her a boon for that purpose.

What more shall I speak on the subject? By visiting that place, you convince Himalaya and Mena in such a way that the task of the gods could be established.

In case you have to go beyond, then whatever method could be thought by you, it can be applied by you. This is your own task and has to be done to receive the credit for the same.”

Brahma said, “Listening to these words, the rsis with the spotless mind, having been thus graced by the lord, felt delighted.

We became opulent and felt successful in all respects. We became adorable among all creatures.

Who is adorable by Brahma and Visnu and bestows success in all the tasks, was entrusting the rsis for a particular task.

He happens to be the father and mother of the universe, let this relationship remain ever growing like the moon (of the bright fortnight).”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking the divine sages, offering there salutation to Siva, reached the capital of Himalaya through the sky way.

Reaching the divine city, the sages were immensely surprised and they started talking to one another about their merits.”

The Rsisi said, “We are very fortunate today, besides being auspicious that we have been able to visit the capital city of Himalaya and more so because Siva has deputed us himself for the purpose.

This is better than Alaka, the city of Kubera or of Bhagavati, the city of the Nagas or Amaravati of Indra.

There are beautiful houses for living here, which have the courtyards studded with crystals and gems.

The slabs of solar or moon stones are found in every house; different kinds of divine trees are also growing there.

There are toranas in every house. In the balconies over the roof-tops, the swans as well as the parrots are found carved on the walls of the palaces.

The beauty of the festoons is found in every house which are of different types and shapes. There are several lakes, step-wells and tanks spread everywhere.

The gardens and the parks are of various types and are visited by the people with pleasure. The men are like gods while the women resemble the apsaras.

The comforts which are achieved by the performers of the yajnas and the followers of the Puranas, the same comforts can be achieved in the Himalaya without much efforts.

The people preserve the desire of the heaven till such time they do not visit this place. Î Ascetics, after looking at this place, the desire for the heaven vanishes or the heaven looks of no consequence for them.”

Brahma said, “In this way the best of the sages, praising the beauty of the city, went to the abode of Himalaya, possessing enormous riches.

Finding the sages, with the resplendence of the sun, who were arriving by the sky way, Himavan felt surprised at the sight of the illustrious sages.”

Himalaya said, “The seven sages illumining like the sun are arriving here. I should therefore adore them.

Graceful are the house-holders like me, because the ascetics, who provide comforts to all are arriving here.”

Brahma said, “Soon after the descending of the sage on earth, Himalaya finding them before him respectfully went to honour them.

Lowering his head, folding his hands, he bowed in reverence to the seven sages and then adored them with great honours.

Accepting his adoration, the seven sages with delightful minds, spoke beneficial words to Himavan.”

Himalaya said, “O Sages, with your arrival here, my house-hold has been purified.” Thus speaking, he, with utmost devotion provided seats to them for sitting.

Making them occupy their seats, he, with their permission, himself took his seats and than spoke to the sages.

Himalaya said, “I have become fortunate, besides having all my desires fulfilled. My life is successful today. I am the best person worthy of being seen in the world, besides becoming like several sacred places.

This is because you in the form of Visnu have arrived in my abode. You are the perfect ones, what could be the special purpose of your visiting a poor person like me?

Still I am your servant. There might be some task with you to be entrusted to me. You kindly speak it out, to make my life a success.

## Chapter 33 - Pleasing of Himavan

The Rsis said, “Siva is called the father and Siva the mother of the universe. Therefore, you should give away your daughter to Siva.

Î Himalaya, by doing so, your life would be successful and in that case, you would become the preceptor of the preceptors of the world.” Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, then listening to the words of Saptarsis, Giriraja, with folded hands, spoke to them.

Himalaya said, “O Seven sages of great enlightenment, whatever has been spoken by you, has already been cherished by me by the grace of Siva.

Then a Brahmana, belonging to the Vaisnava cult arrived here and had spoken much against Siva quite lovingly.

Since then the mother of Siva, having been overpowered by ignorance, is not inclined for the marriage of her daughter with Siva.

Feeling painful, wearing dirty cloths stubbornly she retired to the chamber of anger. She remains unconvinced inspite of the repeated arguments.

I am speaking the truth, even I have been overpowered with ignorance. Therefore I am also not at all inclined to give away my daughter to a beggar.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, having been influenced with the illusion of Siva, Himalaya kept quiet and then sat among the sages.

Then all the rsis praising Sivamaya then sent Arundhati to Mena.

Thereafter Arundhati, the bestower of knowledge at the command of her husband, went to the place of Mena and Parvati at once.

Reaching there, she found Mena, sleeping, after getting fainted. Making her conscious, Arundhati spoke the sweet words to her.

Arundhati said, “O Chaste Mena, devoted to your husband, you get up because, I, Arundhati and the compassionate Saptarsis have arrived.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the voice of Arundhati, with her beaming face, Mena got up and offered her salutation to her.”

Mena said, “Which one of my merit has risen today, that the wife of Vasistha and the daughter-in-law of the creator of the universe has arrived here in our abode.

Î Goddess, what for have you arrived here. You tell me particularly. I happen to be your slave girl with my daughter. Be graceful on me.”

Brahma said, “At these words of Mena, Arundhati convinced her variously, she took Mena with her and arrived at the place where Saptarsis were seated.

Thereafter, the Saptarsis, who were well versed in speech, with their minds devoted in Siva, respectfully convinced Giriraja.”

The Rsis said, “O Giriraja, you listen to our benevolent worlds. By giving your daughter Parvati to Siva, you become the father-in-law of the destroyer of the world.

You should pray to the lord of all, making all the efforts. Brahma is desirous of uniting Siva and Parvati, for the destruction of Taraka.

Though Siva, the great yogin, is disinterested in marriage, but still he will marry your daughter at the request of Brahma.

Your daughter has performed tapas in order to achieve him for which Siva has bestowed a boon on Parvati. Siva will marry her because of these two reasons.

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of the sages, Himalaya, who had been feeling panicky, smiled and spoke quite humbly.

Himalaya said, 'I don’t find any property with Siva. He does not have any house or a relative.

He is detached besides being a mendicant. Therefore, I do not intend to give away my daughter to him. You are the sons of Brahma, you tell me the future course of action.

In case a father gives his daughter to an unsuitable person in marriage, out of love, delusion fear or covetousness, he is doomed and is sure to fall in hell.

At my own free will, I shall never give Parvati to Siva, the holder of a trident. Î Sages, whatever arrangement suits the occasion, should be carried out.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sages, on hearing the words of Himavan, Vasistha, the most eloquent in speech, among he sages, said.

Vasistha said, “O Lord of the mountains, listen to my words. An action which is according to the dharma, provides comfort in this as well as the other world.

Î Mountain, three types of words are stated to be in the world. A learned person knowing all the lores, can well understand them by means of his pure vision of knowledge.

Some of the words which are initially pleasing, but subsequently prove to be false and painful. Such words are spoken by the enemies alone.

There are some words, which appear harsh in the beginning but are found pleasant subsequently. Such words are spoken by the compassionate and religious minded kinsmen.

The words which are as sweet as the nectar and bestow pleasure being essence of the truth, besides being beneficial, are considered to be the best.

Î Mountain, these are the three types of words, which have been prescribed in the treatises on polity. You therefore tell me which type of behaviour should be adopted by me to please you.

Siva is no doubt devoid of the riches created by Brahma. But his mind is engrossed in the ocean of the true knowledge.

The one who is in possession of the blissful knowledge, how could he be desirous of the outward things. A house-holder gives his daughter away to the one having country, kingdom and the riches.

By giving away the daughter to a grieved husband, a father earns the sin of the killing of the daughter. Who says Siva is grieved, when Kubera happens to be his servant.

With the mere movement he can create or destroy the universe, he happens to be the nirguna supreme lord and is beyond Prakrti.

For creation etc. there are three types of images viz. Brahma for creation, Visnu for preservation and Siva for destruction.

Brahma is lodged in Brahmaloka, Visnu in the ocean of milk, and Siva lives in Kailasa. All the three are the Vibhutis of Siva.

The primordial Prakrti emerging out of Siva, takes to three forms in the creative activity partially out of support with diverse digits.

Sarasvati , born out of his mouth is the presiding deity of speech. Laksmi born out of his chest bestows all types of riches.

Parvati was manifested out of the lustre of the gods. Then after killing all the demons she bestows all the fortunes on the gods.

In another kalpa, she was born from the womb of the wife of Daksa and was known by the name of Sati, who was married to Siva by Daksa.

She, listening to the denouncement of her husband, ended her life in the fire of yoga. She has presently been born out of the womb of Mena.

Î Mountain, this Siva will remain the wife of Siva in all the birth and provide the best of wisdom to the best of the learned people.

She is always victorious, who bestows success being the form of success herself. Siva applies the ashes of the bones of Sati always on his body.

Therefore you give away Parvati- your beautiful daughter to Siva, otherwise, she herself would go to the abode of her husband.

Mahadeva observed that Parvati, after taking a pledge, had to bear many pains while performing the tapas. Siva, then taking to the form of a Brahmana, arrived at the place where she had been performing the tapas.

Assuring her and bestowing the desired boon on her, he returned to his place. Î Himalaya, being subservient to the prayer of Parvati, he is asking for her hand.

Î Giriraja, you had also accepted the same getting devoted to Siva. How have you changed your mind, you tell me?

Returning from there, Siva has sent us together with Arundhati and the Rsis to you with prayer.

Î Himalaya, we would like to convince you. You give away Parvati to Siva and by doing so you would earn enormous bliss.

Î Giriraja, in case you do not give Siva to Siva, of your own sweet will, then she would be married with him due to the moves of the destiny.

Î Dear one, Siva had bestowed a boon on Parvati at the time of her performing the penance and the words of Siva cannot be otherwise.

Î Himalaya, even the pledge of the devotees of Siva, cannot be broken, then what to speak of the pledge of Siva, taken by him himself.

Indra had once playfully cut off the wings of the mountains, while Parvati had destroyed the peak of the Sumeru mountain.

Î Lord of mountains, it would not be advisable to destroy your entire riches for the sake of one person. You better disown one, for the sake of one person. These are the eternal words of the Vedas.

The king Anaranya had protected his wealth, by giving away his daughter to a Brahmana, being afraid of him.

His preceptors and the kinsmen well-versed in the lores of polity had advised the king who had been panicky of the curse of the Brahmana.

Therefore, Î King of the mountains, you also protect your kinsmen besides ruling over the gods by giving away your daughter to Siva.

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of Vasistha, Himalaya, while painful at heart but smiling outwardly, enquired about the story of the king Anaranya.”

Himalaya said, “O Brahmana, in which race was the king Anaranya born. How did he save his property by giving away his daughter?”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Himalaya, Vasistha feeling delighted, narrated the relevant story to Himalaya.

## Chapter 34 - The story of Anaranya

Vasistha said, “The king Anaranya hailed from the race of Indrasavarni, the fourteenth Manu.

Anaranya was a great devotee of Siva and the son of Mangalaranya and he ruled the seven island of earth.

He appointed Bhrgu as his priest and performed a hundred Asvamedha sacrifices. Though he was offered the position of Indra by the gods, but he declined the offer.

Î Himalaya, the king had a hundred sons and a daughter named Padma, who was as beautiful as Laksmi.

Î Himalaya, as compared to the amount of love the king had with his hundred sons, he loved his daughter much more than all the sons.

The king had five chief queens, who were quite dear to him. They were therefore quite fortunate.

The daughter was grown up in the palace of her father. He sent letters in search of a suitable mach for her.

Once the sage Pippalada was about to move towards his hermitage, when he spotted a Gandharva in the secluded orchard.

He was well-versed in the science of erotics and in the company of his wife, he was completely engrossed in the ocean of passions and lust.

Finding the couple in that erotic position, his passions were aroused. Neglecting his penance, he thought of his marriage.

Thus suffering from the lustful passions, Pippalada the best of the sages spent much of his time (wandering uselessly).

Once the excellent sage was going to the river Puspabhadra for taking a bath when he suddenly spotted the princess Padma, resembling Laksmi in beauty.

The sage asked the people of the vicinity about the girl. The people who were afraid of a curse of the sage, told him.

The people said, “This girl is Padma, the daughter of the king Anaranya. She is extremely virtuous and is desired by several kings.”

Brahma said, “The sage who was desirous of that girl, listening to the truthful words of the people became upset.

O Himalaya, then the sage took hit bath, and then adored Siva, his family god.

Thereafter the lustful sage, went to the king who in panic bowed in reverence to him, offering madhuparka besides adoring him with devotion.

Accepting his adoration, the sage asked for the hand of his daughter. The king who was unable to speak out anything, kept quiet.

The sage said, “O King, you give your daughter to me, otherwise, I shall reduce you to ashes in no time.”

Î Sage, all the servants of the king felt disturbed with the brilliance of the sage. Looking at the old Brahmana, the king started crying with his kiths and kins.

The queens too, who were also unable to do so, started crying. The chief queen and the mother of the girl also became upset with grief.

Î Himalaya his sons too felt extremely painful. What more to speak, all the relatives of the king felt sad.

In the meantime, the learned Brahmanas, the excellent preceptor, and the priests came to the king.

The king offering his salutation to them adored them and started crying before them. He apprised them of the entire situation and enquired from them about the future course of action.

Thereafter, the preceptor of the king, the Brahmana, Pandita and the priest and two scholars well-versed in polity convinced the king.

The king, the queens, the boys, and the girl were all feeling painful at heart. Observing them, the preceptor as well as the priest spoke the words for the welfare of all.

The preceptor and the priest said, “O Intelligent king, you listen to the benevolent words of both of us. Don’t be grief stricken with your kiths and kins. You divert your wisdom towards the scriptures

O King, today or after sometime or a year, you have to give away the girl in marriage.

We do not find a groom better than the Brahmana. By giving away the girl in marriage to the sage, you protect your entire kingdom and the riches.

When the entire kingdom and riches are bound to the destroyed for the sake of one person, then giving her, you protect your kingdom unless it is an object which had taken refuge with you.”

Vasistha said, “On hearing the words of the wise people, the king lamented again and again, but ultimately offered his daughter, completely adorned with ornaments to the excellent sage.

Î Himalaya, the sage married the girl appropriately and he went home with Padma, who was as beautiful as Laksmi.

By giving away his daughter to the old Brahmana, and feeling painful at heart, deserting his kiths and kins, he went to the forest for the performing of the tapas.

Î Himalaya, after the departure of her husband, his wife also died in grief.

Without the king, the priest, and other respectable people were all fainted. All the other people were overpowered with grief and they were breathing heavily.

Anaranya on the other hand performed hard tapas in the forest and adoring Siva, he achieved the best place in Sivaloka.

Kirtiman was the eldest son of the king, who ruled the people like his own son?

Î Himalaya, at your instance, I have narrated the excellent story of Anaranya, who saved his entire kingdom by giving away his daughter.

Î Giriraja, you may similarly give away your daughter to Siva and protect your race. By doing so you will make the gods even subservient to yourself.

## Chapter 35 - The story of Padma and Pippalada

Narada said, “O Dear one, what did Giriraja do, after listening to the story of Anaranya? You please tell me.”

Brahma said, “Listen to the story of the king Anaranya including that of his kanyadana, Himalaya asked Vasistha with folded hands.”

Himalaya said, “O Excellent sage, Î Ocean of mercy and the son of Brahma, you have narrated the astonishing story of Anaranya.

What did the daughter of Anaranya, known as Padma do, after her marriage with Pippalada. It would be quite a blissful story.”

Vasistha said, “The sage Pippalada was too old but he went with his wife Padma, the daughter of Anaranya to his hermitage.

He started lovingly living there. He was not sensuous and he engaged himself daily in the performance of religious rites.

Padma, the daughter of Anaranya, served her husband with devotion, mentally, by speech and her actions, like Laksmi serving Visnu.

Once, when she was going for a bath in the divine river, wearing a serene smile on her face, she was spotted by Dharmaraja, who had taken to the form of a man.

He was mounted over the beautiful gem- studded chariot. He was adorned with various ornaments, was quite young, and was beaming like Kamadeva.

Looking at beautiful Padma, the wife of the sage, he intended to test her inner feelings.”

Dharmaraja said, “O Beautiful one, you are charming and youthful and are fit to be enjoyed by the king.

Î Slender waisted one, you are not at all suitable for the old sage Pippalada. I am speaking the truth.

The cruel Brahmana, always remains engaged in the performing the tapas and is on the death’s door. Leaving him, you look at me, who happens to be the king. I am well-versed in erotic exercises, besides, being lustful.

One attains beauty because of the merits of the earlier birth and with the passionate embrace of both of us, it would be successful.

Î Beautiful one, I am husband of thousands of beautiful damsels, and am well- versed in the science of love, Leaving that old husband, you take me as your servant.

You make your life successful by roaming about with me in the lonely forests, beautiful mountains and river banks.”

Vasistha said, “Thus speaking, he got down from the chariot and when he was about to catch hold of her, the chaste girl said to him.”

Padma said, “Away, Away you go, Î Sinful king. In case you cast your lustful eyes on me, you are sure to be destroyed in no time.

How can I resort to you since you are lecherous and mad after women, forsaking the sage Pippalada whose body has been sanctified by the penance?

With the mere touch of a person under the influence of women, all the merits are destroyed. Such a person is a great sinner and his sight alone earns sins.

Even when the holy rites are performed by a person who is lustful for women, he remains impure. The manes, the gods and all the people hate him.

A person whose has been overpowered by a woman, his divine wisdom, penance, recitation, performing of homa, worship, education and the charities are of no use to him.

I am like your mother and you are talking to me like a beloved. Because of this, in due time, you will have to face destruction because of my curse.”

Vasistha said, “At these words of Padma, Dharmaraja, the lord of the gods, shedding away the form of a king took to his original form of Dharmaraja, shaking at the same time.”

Dharmaraja said, “O Mother, I am Dharmaraja, the preceptor of the learned preceptors. Î Chaste lady, I always treat the others’ wives as mothers.

Though I had been fully aware of the feelings of your heart, still, I, in order to know your feelings, moved by the destiny had come to you.

Î Chaste lady, you have subjugated me and this has been quite appropriate. The lord has prescribed punishment for those who do not follow the path of righteousness.

I bow in reverence to Siva, who is competent enough, bestows pleasure and pain, besides fortunes and misfortunes.

He is competent enough to develop love with the friends and enmity with the enemies, who is competent enough for the creation and the destruction of the universe. Salutation to such a type of Siva.

He is the one who has bestowed whiteness to milk, made the water as a cool, and the fire has been given the power of burning, salutation to such a type of Siva.

He is the one who, with the performing of tapas, created Mahat and Prakrti and the one who created Brahma, Visnu, Siva and others, salutation to such Siva.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, Dharmaraja the preceptor of the universe, silently stood before her getting surprised by her chastity and devotion to her husband.

Î Himalaya, the princess being the wife of Pippalada, the chaste Padma looking at Dharmaraja felt surprised and spoke.”

Padma said, “O Dharmaraja, you happen to be the witness of all the people, why are you trying to test my mind?

Î Brahman, whatever was done by me, I am not at all at fault. Î Dharma, I had cursed you because of the nature of a woman, or by ignorance, how could it be removed? I feel concerned about it. Let me get that knowledge to enable me to feel peaceful.

The directions, the sky, the wind, could get destroyed, but the words of curse pronounced by a chaste woman can never be otherwise.

You were complete with all the four feet in Satyayuga, like the full moon. Similarly Î Dharmaraja you will always be there. With your destruction the entire creation would be destroyed and I am keeping on talking uselessly.

Î Best of the gods, in Tretayuga you will lose one foot, two feet in Dvapara, three feet in Kaliyuga, and at the arrival of Satyayuga, you would again be completed.

During the period of Satyayuga you would become all pervading, while in the rest of the yugas, your domination shall remain in selected pockets.

Let my words be pleasant for you. Now I shall leave to serve my husband. You also go to your abode.

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of Padma Dharmaraja felt pleased. Î Narada, he spoke to Padma, who had been so talking.

Dharmaraja said, “O Chaste lady. You are graceful, let you meet with welfare. Because of the protection from you, let your husband, be youthful and become powerful for the conjugal pleasure, besides being religious minded, virtuous, clever in speech, and let his youthfulness remain eternal.

Î Padma, he shall enjoy long life like Marakandeya, wealthy like Kubera, possess fortunes like Indra, devotee of Siva like Visnu besides possessing wisdom comparable to Brahma and Brhaspati.

You will always enjoy the fortune of your husband throughout your life and your youthfulness shall be everlasting.

You will be the mother of ten sons having long life, each one of whom would be more virtuous than your husband.

Your abode will remain filled with all types of riches and would be more illustrious then Kubera even.”

Vasistha said, “O Himalaya, thus speaking Dharmaraja kept quiet. Then Padma circumambulated him and returned to her abode.

Dharmaraja also left the place, showering blessing over Padma and since then he praised Padma in every gathering.

She used to enjoy the conjugal pleasures with her husband daily in a lonely place. In due course of time she gave birth to the sons who were more intelligent them their father.

Then her abode was filled with all types of riches, which increase the pleasures of the husband and wife, and the cause of comforts in both the lokas.

Î Giriraja, I have thus spoken out the ancient history of both of them, which you listen with respect.

Thinking on these lines, you better give away your daughter Parvati to Siva. Don’t be angry with Mena on this account.

An auspicious combination of planets is approaching after a week which is rarely found.

The presiding planet of the lagna is in lagna itself. The moon is in conjunction with his son, Mercury as well as the constellation Rohini. The moon and the stars occupy pure positions. The month is Margasirsa and the day is Monday free from all the blemishes. All the planets are in auspicious conjunction. They are not influenced by the evil planets. The Jupiter is in a position, which is conducive to the birth of a fortunate child and all the good fortunes to the groom. Î Lord of mountain, give away your daughter Parvati- the mother of the universe, the primordial being, to Siva- the father of the universe. Then you become peaceful and contented.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, then the sage Vasistha who was the foremost among the learned people, reciting the name of Siva in his mind, kept quiet.

## Chapter 36 - Advice of the seven sages

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Vasistha with his wife and the servants, Himalaya felt surprised and then spoke to his mountain relatives.

Himalaya said, “O Sumeru, Gandhamadana, Mandara, Mainaka, Vindhya and other mountains, you listen to my words. What should I do in view of the words of the sage Vasistha. You give the subject a hearty thought and then speak out to me.”

Brahma said, “All the mountains like Sumeru and others, decisively but lovingly said to Himalaya.

The mountains said, “O Adorable one, what have we to think about? The task has already been established. She has been born for the establishment of the task of the gods.

Therefore you give away Parvati to Siva. She has been born for the sake of Siva alone. She performed tapas to achieve Siva, who has already consulted for the same.

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Meru and other mountains, Himalaya felt delighted, while Girija started laughing in her mind.

Arundhati on the other hand narrated several types of historical events to Mena and convinced her.

Thereafter Mena, the wife of Himalaya felt pleased, and convinced over the cause of the marriage. Then she served food to the sages, Arundhati and Sailaraja and thereafter took the food herself.

Then the learned Sailaraja, serving well all the sages, spoke to them with folded hands, the appropriate words, which were free from confusion.”

Himalaya said, “O Saptarsis, you please listen to my words. I have been relieved of the confusion, listening to the story of Siva and Siva.

My body, wife, Mainaka and other sons, the daughter and all the rddhis as well as the siddhis belong to Siva. There is no doubt about it.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, he with great honour, adorning his daughter with all the ornaments, put her into the lap of the sage.

Then Sailaraja lovingly spoke to the sages, “I have taken a firm decision to marry Parvati to Siva.”

The sages said, “Î Giriraja, you are the donor, the goddess Parvati is the alms, while Siva happens to be a beggar. What could be the better combination than this?

Î Himalaya, the reason for which your peaks are adored is because of your being the lord of the mountains. Therefore you are quite graceful.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking the Saptarsis with a spotless heart, blessed the girl that she should provide the best of comforts to Siva.”

Touching her with their hands, they said, “You will earn fortunes and the virtues in you would increase like the moon of the bright fortnight.”

Thus speaking all the seven sages showered flowers over her, blessing her.

At that point of time Arundhati with her noble face, narrated the virtues of Siva.

The beard and the moustaches of Himalaya were smeared with the powder of turmeric and saffron, according to the worldly conventions, as an auspicious custom.

After settling about the auspicious time of lagna for the marriage, besides congratulating and complementing one another the sages returned to the abode of Siva on the fourth day.

Reaching Kailasa, the abode of Siva, Vasistha together with other sages, bowed in reverence to Siva and offered prayer to him reciting hymns. Thereafter they spoke to Siva.”

The sages said, “O God of gods, Î Mahadeva, Î Supreme Lord, you kindly listen to our performance (with Himalaya).

We narrated to Mena and Giriraja several types of statements and examples from the ancient scriptures, as a result of which they have been enlightened.

Parvati has been engaged with you by the lord of mountains. It is not otherwise. Now you please start with your attendants and the gods, for the marriage.

Î Great god, Î Lord, you should now go to the house of Himalaya and marry Parvati, for the birth of Kumara Karttikeya.”

Brahma said, “The delightful Siva, who was well-versed in the people’s tradition listened to the words of the sages quite delightfully and then spoke to them smilingly.

Siva said, “O Sages, I have neither heard nor seen a marriage. The way you have done earlier, you do it now similarly.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the auspicious common words of Siva they spoke smilingly to lord of lord Sadasiva.

The Rsis said, “You please invite, the entire community, besides Visnu with his retinue, Brahma with his sons, Indra- the lord of gods, all the sages, Yaksas Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Siddhas, Vidyadharas and apsaras.

Besides them, all others should be respectfully invited. All of them would establish your task. There is no doubt about it.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, all the Saptarsis at the command of Siva, praising the lord for his divine ways, returned to their abode.

## Chapter 37 - Despatch of the letter of engagement and other connected celebrations

Narada said, “O Dear wise father, what did Himalaya do after the departure of the seven sages. You kindly tell me.

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage after the departure of the sages with Arundhati, the performance of Himalaya is being stated by me.

Thereafter, Himalaya, inviting his sons and the brothers like Meru and others, felt delighted.

Delightfully he made his priest Garga to write down the lagna-patrika and sent the same to Siva together with fruits, fried eatables besides the sweets, with a pleasant heart.

The carriers of the sweets etc. reaching Kailasa met Siva and handed him over the letter of engagement, with fruits and sweets etc. performing the tilakam of Siva.

Siva also honoured them appropriately and then they all returned to Himalaya with pleasure.

When Himalaya came to know that his people, who went to Siva were immensely honoured, he was very much pleased.

Thereafter he sent the invitation letters pleasantly to his relatives in his country.

Then he collected several types of eatables suiting to the occasion of the marriage.

The mountainous masses of rice, beaten rice, jagarry, sugar candies, and salt were collected in heaps. He caused huge tanks and receptacles built for the storage of ghee, curd, as well as fried flour cakes of barley and other grains and the ball-like sweets. Big tanks and receptacles were made for the nectar, sugarcane juice, baked cakes and the sugar candies. Tanks were built for the storage of butter, spirituous beverages, sweet juice of various kinds, besides the various kinds of rice preparations.

In addition various types of pickles and side dishes were prepared, which might be to the likes of the ganas of Siva and the gods. Various types of valuable costumes purified in fire, were kept ready.

Gems and jewels of various kinds besides the gold, silver and other articles were also duly collected.

Himalaya started the auspicious rites during the auspicious muhurta. The mountain damsels then started decorating Parvati with cosmetics.

The damsels themselves, adorned with all the ornaments, started the welfare ceremonies. The wives of the Brahmanas also joined the welfare ceremonies.

Himalaya too joined the welfare ceremonies, according to the local traditions.

Himalaya was pleased at the arrival of his relations. In the meantime he also invited his other relations as well.

All of them arrived with their sons, wives, servants and others. Î celestial sage, listen to a detailed narration of the arrival of those mountains.

I am narrating the story in brief in order to please Siva. The great mountain known by the name of Devalaya, taking to a divine form, decorating the body with several of the precious gems, arrived with his wife and his people, carrying several of the jewels and the gems.

The graceful Mandaracala, clad in beautiful costumes, arrived in the house of Himalaya with his wife and sons.

Astacala, having divine wisdom and benevolent mind, carrying several types of the best of presents arrived there.

Udayacala, possessing enormous glory, arrived there carrying enormous gems and valuable jewels.

The highly comfortable mountain of Malaya, and having the best of kinsmen, reached there respectfully.

The mountain named Durdara, with a pleasant mind accompanied with the huge army and his wife, arrived there.

Î Dear one, the Nisada mountain, variously decorated, arrived there with a delightful heart, in the abode of Himalaya.

The lord Gandhamadana mountain also accompanied with his wife and sons, arrived in the abode of Himalaya.

The mountain, Karavira, carrying several types of riches, reached there. Besides Mahendra- the king of mountains, also arrived at the invitation of Himalaya.

The Pariyatra mountain accompanied with his wife, son and the servants, also arrived there.

Kraunca- the king of mountains, accompanied with his family the servants and army, also arrived in the abode of Himalaya.

A mountain named Purusottama, carrying several types of presents, respectfully arrived in the house of Himalaya.

The blue mountain, accompanied with his son and wife, carrying enormous riches, arrived in the house of Himalaya.

In addition to the above, the mountains Trikuta, Citrakuta, Venkata, Srigiri, Gokamukha also arrived in the house of Himalaya.

Vindyacala- the king of mountains, carrying delightfully, many presents, arrived there with his wife and sons.

The great mountain named Kalanjara feeling extremely pleased, arrived in the house of Himalaya with several of his ganas.

Kailasa the lord of mountains also, with a pleasant mind, showering his grace on all reached there. All of them were delighted. All of them were the family deities of those mountains.

Î Narada, such of the mountain which were located in other islands, all of them reached the abode of Himalaya.

Î Sage, all the mountains which had been invited by Himalaya, delightfully reached there to witness the marriage of Siva and Parvati.

At that point of time Sonabhadra and other rivers also arrived there lovingly in order to witness the marriage of Siva and Siva.

All the other rivers taking to the divine forms, arrived there to observe the marriage of Siva and Siva.

The rivers like Godavari, Yamuna, Brahmaputra, Triveni, also arrived there to witness the marriage of Siva and Siva, in the abode of Himalaya.

The river Ganga, having been adorned with all the ornaments, taking to an excellent form, arrived to participate in the marriage of Siva and Siva.

The rivers like Narmada, Mahamoda, Rudrakanya, Saridvara, adorning themselves with the best of ornaments, lovingly arrived to attend the marriage of Siva and Siva.

With the arrival of the invitees from all the four quarters, the graceful Himapuri was crowded from all the sides.

The enthusiasm prevailed all-round in the city, which was decorated with the flags and the toranas. Because of the pitching of tents, for the invitees, the sun shine had been faded out and the glamour of the city was increased.

Himalaya also on his part, honoured the guests and invitees who had arrived in his abode.

Separate arrangements had been made for the lodging of each one of them. They were fully satisfied with the supply of all the essential commodities.

## Chapter 38 - Description of the mandapa

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, thereafter Himalaya the lord of the mountains, celebrated a huge festival in the city.

The water was sprinkled over all the sides of the roads. The roads were decorated on both the sides with the trunks of the banana and other trees, decorating them at the same time.

The pillars were erected in the courtyard which were covered with the silken cloth. The mango leaves decorated all the sides.

The toranas were decorated with jasmine flowers beside other auspicious materials.

In this way the lord of the mountains, made all the arrangements for the pleasure of his daughter. Thereafter, the material for adoration was procured before the immensely influential Garga- the royal priest.

Then he summoned Visvakarma and made him build a beautiful and vast mandapa with a beautiful altar in the centre.

Î Narada, the divine sage, the canopy was spread in a area of ten thousand yojanas with numerous auspicious symbols, and looked astonishing.

The mandapa was equally pleasant both for the mobile and immobile beings and looked beautiful from all the sides.

The mobile objects displayed their excellent glory, while the immobile one surpassed the mobile one in excellence.

The watery places excelled the beauty of the solid ground. Even the experts could not distinguish between water and the ground.

At places the images of artificial lions were placed, at places, there were the lines of cranes, while at places the (artificial) peacocks attracted the minds of the people.

At places one could find artificial (images) of women dancers dancing with artificial men casting wistful glances at them and enchanting them.

In this way, the beautiful images of gate¬keepers had been installed at the entrance gates, carrying the bows in their hands. These images of the gate-keepers looked like the real ones.

The images of Mahalaksmi, possessing all the auspicious symbols, appeared as if she had just emerged out of the ocean of milk.

The images of elephants appeared attractive decorated with ornaments, like the real ones. Similarly the horses appeared charming with the horse-riders, while the elephants so appeared with the elephant riders.

The images of the chariots driven by the charioteers, looked quite surprising. The images of the foot soldiers had also been beautifully made.

O Sage, all these images had been made by Visvakarma, delightfully, in order to give a surprise to the gods and the sages.

Î Sage, the statue of Nandi, at the portals, of crystalline beauty and brilliance, appeared like a prototype of the real Nandi.

Above Nandi, was the divine Puspaka- plane decorated with sprouts and was shining with the flywhisks.

To the left were two elephants as if having been born in the country of Kashmere. They had four tusks each. They were of sixty years of age, possessing immense lustre and were intoxicated.

Similarly, the images of two horses decorated with flywhisks, having the resplendence of the sun, and adorned with ornaments were also made.

The Lokapalas were adorned with the best of Kavacas ands the gems. The gods too were shown in the images in a realistic manner.

The images of Bhrgu and other ascetics, besides the siddhas, gods, were also made.

The image of lord Visnu had been made in a surprising manner, together with his attendants and Garuda.

Narada was shown reciting the Vedas. My image also was there in the company of my sons.

Indra resembling the full moon was shown with his family, mounted over the elephant Airavata.

What else could be stated, Î Divine sage, with the inspiration of the Himalaya, Visvakarma had projected the entire community of gods in the paintings (and sculptures).

Thus Visvakarma built the divine mandapa, which attracted the minds of the gods, reflecting several acaryas as well.

Thereafter, Giriraja Himalaya commanded the competent architect-Visvakarma to build the houses for the dwelling of the gods, resembling their respective abodes in their own lokas.

Those houses were provided with the high, neat and clean beds by Visvakarma.

Visvakarma, built the seven lokas for the residence of Brahma in a moment, which were quite resplendent.

Similarly, he created a new Vaikuntha, a brilliant abode of Visnu with wonderful features.

Visvakarma also built the house for Indra with many surprises as well as the fortunes.

Similarly he also built beautiful and the vast houses for the Lokapalas.

He also built the mansions for others gods of various kinds which were quite beautiful.

Visvakarma who had achieved boon from - Siva, and who was immensely learned, made a beautiful house in order to please Siva, in a moment.

Similarly he also built an abode for Siva, which was quite surprising and had the symbols like small double drum, trident etc. in Sivaloka.

This type of the astonishing construction work, which was well illumined was undertaken by Visvakarma for the pleasure of Siva.

Thus observing all the worldly formalities, Himalaya delightfully waited for the arrival of Siva with the marriage party.

Î Divine sage, thus I have narrated the blissful story of Himalaya to you. Now you tell me what more do you intend to listen from me?

## Chapter 39 - Arrival of the gods at Kailasa and departure of the marriage party of Siva

Narada said, “O Dear one, Î Destiny, Î Immensely learned one, Î Disciple of Visnu, Î Ocean of mercy, you have narrated the astonishing story to me.

Now I would like to listen to the auspicious event of the marriage of Siva, which bestows welfare.

What did lord Siva, after receiving the lagna-patrika do? Now you narrate the same story.

Brahma said, “O Intelligent son, listen to the great fame of Siva. After receiving the letter of Himalaya, what did Siva do, you better listen from me.

Lord Siva, after receiving that letter, honoured all those persons, who had carried the letter to the lord.

After the letter was read, the date of marriage was appropriately accepted and those people were given a respectful and a hearty send off.

Then Siva prayed to the sages, “You have performed pretty well. All of you should attend my marriage, since I have accepted this marriage.” This is what Siva, told those sages (who had arrived with the letter).

Listening to these words of Siva, the sages were delighted. They, offering their salutation to Siva and circumambulating him returned praising their fortunes.

Î Sage, Siva, the lord of the gods, performs many sports, together with the gods, following the worldly traditions, and you yourself quite lovingly, praising your fortunes, arrived there, with all humility, lowering your head, you offered your salutation to the lord with folded hands.

Then you offered prayer to him shouting slogans of victory to the lord, Î Sage, thereafter, praising and eulogising the lord, you sought permission from Siva to return.

Displaying the worldly behaviour and heightening your pleasure with sweet speech, the delighted Siva, pleasantly said to you.

Siva said, “O Excellent sage, you listen from me today. I speak to you, because you are the foremost of my devotees and quite dear to me.

At your command, Parvati performed severe tapas for me. Getting delighted, I have promised to be her husband.

I am subservient to her devotion. Therefore I am going to marry her. The Saptarsis have fixed the date of marriage.

Î Narada, the marriage will the performed, just after a week. I shall celebrate the marriage, following the worldly tradition.”

Brahma said, “Î Dear one, listening to the words of Siva, the supreme soul, feeling delighted, you bowed in reverence to the lord and said.

Narada said, “This is your Vrata that you always remain subservient to your devotees. You have acted appropriately according to the desire of Parvati.

Î Lord, taking me as your humble servant, you kindly get me your command for any service, I am fit for.”

Brahma said, “Î Excellent sage, after you thus spoke to Siva, lord Siva, who is well- disposed towards his devotees, delightfully spoke to you with respect.”

Siva said, “O Sage, you, on my behalf invite, Visnu and other gods besides the sages, the siddhas, and all others, located in all the four quarters.

At my command all of them should arrive with their wives and children, well-decorated.

Those of the gods who would not attend my marriage ceremony, I shall not consider such gods as my own. This is sure.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the pleasing words of Siva, you accepted his command, moved at once and communicated the invitation to all.

O Narada, then, performing the function of a messenger, you delivered the message to all. Coming back you took your seat with his permission.

Siva too was anxiously waiting for the return of Narada, while dancing with his ganas.

At the same time lord Visnu, together with his entire family arrived there, suitably dressed.

He, together with Laksmi and his family members, offered his salutation to lord Siva. All of them took their seats with the permission of the lord.

I also reached Kailasa with my ganas. I took my seat bowing in reverence to Siva.

Indra and the other Lokapalas also arrived there with their wives and sons, well dressed.

The sages, the Nagas, siddhas, Gandharvas, and other people also arrived with pleasure, after receiving the invitation.

Siva welcomed delightfully, all the gods and others, severally.

A surprising type of festival was organised over Kailasa, in which the divine damsels performed the dance.

Î Sage, Visnu and other gods, who had arrived there, had come to participate in the marriage party of Siva.

All of them had been invited by Siva and inspired by me. All of them engaged themselves in the service of Siva.

The seven mothers (Sapta-matrikas) engaged themselves in decorating Siva appropriately.

Î Excellent sage, at the desire of Siva, he was decorated with his natural attire and ornaments.

The crescent moon decorated the head. His third eye looked like the tilakam.

Î sage! two snakes appeared as ear ornaments or as gem-studded kundalas.

The serpents coiled over the other limbs appeared like the ornaments studded with gems.

The ashes mixed with sandal paste were applied over his body like the cosmetic. The elephant skin as well as the tiger-skin were like the excellent silken garments for him.

At that point of time, Siva looked quite charming and his beauty was beyond description. At that time Siva appeared as possessing all the fortunes.

Then all the gods, Danavas, serpents, birds, apsaras, and the sages getting fully pleased and belonging to the side of the gods (bride), came close to Siva and said.

All of them said, “O Mahesvara, Î Mahadeva, you kindly show your grace on us, by marrying Girija.”

Then Visnu, bowing in reverence to Siva, delightfully spoke the words befitting the occasion.

Visnu said, “O God of gods, Î Mahadeva, dear to those taking refuge with you, you perform the tasks of your devotees. You listen to my words.

Î Siva, according to the method prescribed in the Grhyasutras you perform your marriage with the daughter of Himalaya.

Î Siva, when you perform this the marriage appropriately then this tradition would be established everywhere.

Î Lord, according to your own traditional dharma, you first established the mandapa, perform the Nandimukha-sraddha with devotion and establish your fame in the world.”

Brahma said, “When Siva- the Parmesvara was so addressed by Visnu, then Siva, who was the follower of the worldly traditions, did so. Siva entrusted the responsibility of performing all the rites to me, which I respectfully carried out with the help of the sages.

The sages like Kasyapa, Atri, Vasistha, Gautama, Bhaguri, Kanva, Brhaspati, Sakti, Jamadagni, Parasara, Marakandeya- the great sage, silapaka, Arunapala, Akrtasrama, Agastya, Cyavana, Garga, Silada, Dadhici, Upamanyu, Bhardvaja, Akrtvrana, Pippalada, Kusika, Kautsa and Vyasa with his disciples, having been aspired by me, besides other ascetics, reached before Siva and they performed all the ceremonies concerning the marriage.

The Rsis well-versed in the Vedas and other connected literature, following the Vedic traditions, performed the safety rites of Siva, and tied the safety thread around his wrist.

Reciting the hymns from the Rgveda, Samaveda and Yajurveda, besides various stotras from the Puranas, the sages, performed the auspicious rites.

To ward off the obstructions, the adoration of the planets was performed under my instructions. They worshipped the gods lodged in the altar.

After appropriately performing the social and Vedic rites, Siva was pleased and delightfully bowed in reverence to the Brahmanas.

The lord of all- Siva, started from the excellent mountain Kailasa, keeping the Brahmanas and the gods ahead.

Crossing the mountain Kailasa, Siva stopped for a while, along with the gods and the Brahmanas, receiving different ovations.

At that point of time, the gods, resorted to singing and dancing in order to please Siva.

## Chapter 40 - Siva’s marriage procession

Brahma said, “Siva then called Nandi and other ganas delightfully and commanded them to accompany the marriage party.

Siva said, “Leaving some of the ganas here, the rest of them should accompany me to the city of Himalaya.”

Brahma said, “At the command of Siva, the lords of the ganas leading their respective armies, marched on with pleasure. Some of them are described here.

Samkhakarna- the lord of the ganas marched on with a crore of ganas to accompany Siva towards the abode of Himalaya.

The delightful Kekaraksa was accompanied with ten crores of ganas, while Ganesvara named Vikrta had eight crores of ganas with him.

Visakha- the leader of the ganas had four crores of ganas with him, while the gana- leader named Parijata had nine crores of ganas with him.

Sarvantaka and Vikrtantaka had sixty crores each. The leader named Dundubha had eight crores of ganas with him.

Kapala- the lord of ganas had five crore ganas with him, the warrior named Sandaraka had six crores ganas with him.

Kanduka and Kunduka moved one with a crore of ganas each. Ganesvara and Vistambha on the other hand had seight crores each.

The leader named Pippalada was delightfully marching with a thousand crores of ganas. The Ganesvara, known as Saunadaka, moved with the similar number of ganas.

The Ganesvara, known as Avesana, had the army of eight crores of ganas, while Mahakesa was accompanied by a thousand crores of ganas.

O Sage, Kunda and Parbata had twelve crores each, the great warrior Candratapana had eight crores each.

Kala, kalaka, Mahakala and Agnika had a hundred crores each.

Agnimukha- the leader of ganas, was accompanied with a crore of ganas, while Adityamurdha and Ghanavaha each had a crore of ganas.

Sannaha and Kumuda, the leaders of the ganas had a hundred crores of ganas, while Amogha and Kokila had also the same number with them.

Sumantra had one crores, Kakapadodara and Santanaka had sixty crores each.

Mahabala had nine crores, while Madhupingala, Kokila, Nila and Purnabhadra were leading ninety crores of the ganas.

Caturvaktra had seven crores, Karana had twenty crores, Ahiromaka had ninety crores, of ganas marching with them.

Î Narada, Yajvaksa, Satamanyu, Meghamanyu, had ninety crores of ganas moving with them. Kasthangustha- the leader of the ganas, was accompanied with sixty four cores of ganas, while Virupaksa, Sukesa, Sanatana, Vrsabha, Talaketu, Sadasya, Pancamukha, Sanatana, Samvartaka, Caitra, Lakulisa, Svayamprabhu, Lokantaka, Diptatma, Daityantaka, Devabhrngariti, Devapriya- the great, Asani and Bhanuka moved with sixty four thousand ganas each moved with Siva to attend his marriage.

There were a thousand crores of goblins and three crores of Pramathas, sixty crores of Virabhadras, and three crores of Romajas.

Besides, the others ganas, like Nandi, joined the marriage procession of Siva by hundreds and twenties crores of ganas.

The Ksetrapala-Bhairava, arrived with crores of ganas, getting enthusiastic to join the marriage of Siva.

These as well as several other warriors delightfully arrived to joint he marriage of Siva.

Many of them had a thousand hands each, having the crowns of the matted locks of hair over the heads, besides the crescent moon, blue necks and three eyes.

They were wearing Rudraksa, garlands, kundalas, crowns and keyuras. Their bodies were plastered with ashes.

Many other Ganesvaras having the lustre of crores of suns, were present there.

Î Sage, some of them could move in the terrestrial world, some in the sky and some over the earth.

Î Divine sage, what more could be stated in this connection, all the ganas of Siva, living in all the lokas, arrived there well-pleased.

Thus Siva accompanied with the gods and others, marched towards the city of Himalaya, for his marriage.

When Siva departed for his marriage accompanied with the gods, then listen to their activities on the way.

The goddess Candi, officiating as the sister of Siva, arrived there well decorating herself, who frightened the opponents.

She was seated over the pretasana (seat of a ghost), adorned with the ornaments of snakes carrying in the gold pitcher filled with water and looked quite shining.

She was shining with her family, with a beaming face, looking jovial. Besides her, valorous other goddess also arrived there joyfully.

Î Sage, crores of the goblins in divine form, were present there.

Accompanied with all of them the goddess with deformed face moved ahead of all, quite joyfully. She could cause love as well as disturbance.

Candi- relegated all the Rudraganas to the background. All the Rudraganas were dear to Siva, who were eleven crore in number.

At that point of time, the sound of double drum, kettle-drums, and the blowing of the conches, echoed in the sky.

Huge turmoil was created with the beating of the big drums, which destroyed misfortunes and created welfare.

Î Sage, all the gods, siddhas, Lokapalas and others, followed the ganas.

O Sage, Visnu mounted over Garuda moved in the middle, who looked graceful with the chatra carried over his head.

He was surrounded by his attendants, who were moving the flywhisks over him and he was adorned with all the ornaments.

I also moving with them, following the path of Vedas and Agamas appeared graceful.

I had been engaged in the service of Siva, together with Sanaka and others, Mahasiddhas, sons of Prajapati and other kiths and kins.

Indra, adorned with all the ornaments, mounted over the elephant, looked quite graceful.

The Rsis having been filled with enthusiasm had joined the marriage procession.

Sakini, Yatudhan, Betalas, Brahmaraksasas, spirits, goblins, pisacas and pramathas, besides, Tumburu, Narada, Huha, Huhu, the best of the Gandharvas, and the Kinnaras were happy, playing on the musical instruments.

All the mothers of the universe, all the divine damsels, Gayatri, Laksmi, and the wives of the other gods (also joined the marriage procession).

The wives of the gods and the mothers of the universe, went to the marriage of Siva, quite delightfully.

Vrsabha, resembling the pure and beautiful crystal, which is believed by the Vedas, besides the sastras, siddhas and the great sages, as dharma, over which lord Mahadeva- to whom dharma is quite dear, was mounted, was moving in the marriage procession surrounded by the divine sages.

Accompanied with all the great sages, Siva, while moving for his marriage with Siva, looked quite graceful.

Thus the story of the grand marriage procession of Siva has been narrated to you. Now listen to the pleasant incidents happening in the city of Himavat.

## Chapter 41 - Beauty of the mandapa

Brahma aid, O Sage, thereafter, making consultations among themselves, at the command of Siva, lord Visnu, first of all sent you to the house of Himalaya.

O Narada, at the instance of Visnu, you bowing in reverence to Siva, moved towards the house of Himalaya.

O Sage, you by looking at your image made by Visvakarma, you felt shy and surprised.

O Excellent sage, by looking at your image, you felt tired and kept on looking at the proficiency of the art of Visvakarma.

Then you entered the *mandapa* of Himalaya which had been beautifully painted like the gems, which had the golden pitchers, and the *apsaras* like Rambha had been painted. The *mandapa* had a thousand pillars and was quite astonishing in nature. Finding the pedestal or altar made therein you were surprised.

O Sage Narada, you felt confused at that point of time and you lost your wisdom. Feeling surprised you spoke to Himalaya.

“Have Visnu and other gods, besides the *Siddhas,* and ascetics arrived already?

O Lord of mountains, you tell me truthfully, whether Mahadeva, mounted over his bull has already arrived with his *ganas.'’’*

Brahma said, “Listening to your words having been filled with surprise, Giriraja Himalaya spoke the truth to you.

Himalaya said, “O Wise Narada, Siva, together with the people of the marriage party has not yet arrived for marriage with Parvati.

O Narada, look carefully. These are the paintings made by Visvakarma. O divine sage, free yourself from the confusion, remember Siva, and be healthy. After eating something, you have some rest. Be graceful on me delightfully and you go back to Siva with Mainaka and other mountains.

O Immensely wise sage, going back to Siva, with the mountains, praying on my behalf, bring all the gods, *Rsis,* demons, besides Siva whose feet are adored by all, here.”

Brahma said, “Taking the food, and having some rest, in the abode of Himalaya, you returned to Siva, together with the sons of Himalaya.

Finding Siva having been surrounded by the gods, you and the sons of Himalaya offered your salutation at the feet of lord Siva.

Then O Sage, all the gods including Indra, Visnu and myself, besides the attendants asked you.

They had been struck with surprise, and suspicion, on finding the mountains Mainaka, Sakya, Meru and others, adorned with all types of ornaments.

The gods said, “O Narada, O Intelligent one, you appear to be bewildered. Have you been treated well by Himalaya or not? Speak out everything at length.

Why have the excellent mountains like Mainaka, Sakya and others richly adorned with ornaments, possessing immense strength arrived here?

O Narada, does Himalaya really intend to give away his daughter to Siva or not? What has taken place in the abode of Himavan now? Please speak out.

We are having doubts in our minds. Hence we, the heaven-dwellers, ask you to say everything, O righteous one, and rectify our doubts.

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of the gods and others, O Sage, you having been confused with the illusion of Visvakarma, spoke to them.

O Sage, you took me and Visnu aside you spoke these words to me to Visnu and also to Indra who is lord of gods and by the severing of the wings of the mountains, he was their earlier enemy.

Narada said, “In order to confuse all the gods, Visvakarma had made such images, by which he tends to confuse all the gods appropriately.

O Indra, earlier, you had defeated Himalaya. Have you forgotten it, therefore, he is sitting in his house in order to defeat you.

I, finding my false image, was confused. He has similarly made the images of Brahma, Visnu and Indra.

O God of gods, what more could be said in this connection. No one has been left out.

He had made the images for the enchanting of the gods and the spell has been made use of by means of this projection.”

Brahma said, “On hearing your words lord Indra, who was completely frightened at once spoke to Visnu.”

Indra said, “O Lord of Laksmi and the lord of gods, Tvastr who is agitated over the grief of his own, will surely kill me under this pretext and not otherwise.”

Brahma said, “Listening to his words, Janardana, the god of gods, spoke to Indra smilingly, assuring him at the same time.”

Visnu said, “Earlier Nivata- Kavaca, the *daityas,* on the basis of *Mahavidyas* had confused you, O Indra.

Then, O Indra, at my instance, you had cut off the wings of Himalaya and other mountains.

In case the mountain recalling the earlier enmity because of his illusion, would try to subjugate us, even then you should not be afraid of the enemy.

Lord Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, will surely protect us.”

Finding Indra thus talking getting panicky, Siva said, “O Visnu, Î Indra, what type of conversation is going on between the two of you?” Î Sage, Siva, while thus asking both of them spoke to you.

Î Narada, tell what had Himalaya told you? Speak out truthfully. Don’t conceal anything.

O Dear one, tell me whether Himalaya is ready to give away his daughter to me or not? Speak out quickly. What did you observe, after reaching there? What did you do? You lovingly speak out everything.”

Brahma said, “At these words of Siva, you revealed everything to him in seclusion.”

Narada said, Î God of gods, Î Mahadeva, Î Lord, you listen to my words. There is no danger or obstruction in the marriage.

Giriraja is sure to give away his daughter to you. In fact these mountains have arrived here to welcome you.

But in order to confuse the gods, astonishing types of paintings (or creations) have been made, O Omniscient one, they are only for the sake of curiosity. There is no possibility of any obstruction.

O Lord, at the command of Himalaya the illusory Visvakarma, had made a beautiful *mandapa* with many surprises.

The paintings of all the gods have been drawn, just to confuse them, looking at which I was confused and overpowered with illusion.”

Brahma said, “O Dear one, listening to the words of Narada, Siva, who was well-versed in the worldly sports, spoke to the gods smilingly.

Siva said, “O Visnu, in case Himalaya gives away his daughter to me, then what have we to do with his illusion.

O Brahma, O Indra, O Sages and O gods, you also tell me, in case Himalaya gives away his daughter to me, then what have we to do with his illusion.

The people well-versed in polity say, that the task should be established by any means, therefore, all of you making Visnu as your leader, move on for the establishment of the task.”

Brahma said, “When Siva was so talking with the gods, then, he like an ordinary person became lustful.

Thereafter at the command of Siva, the gods like Visnu and others, the *Rsis,* the sages and others were relieved of the confusion.

Then all them making you and the mountain as the leaders, went to the house of Himalaya and felt surprised.

Thereafter, accompanied with Visnu and other gods, besides the leaders of the *ganas,* as well as the army, the delightful Siva reached the city of Himalaya with the marriage party.

## Chapter 42 - Meeting between the lord and the mountain

Brahma said, “On coming to know that Siva (with the marriage party) has reached near the city, he felt pleased.

Then he carrying all the necessary material sent the Brahmanas to welcome them, with all his relatives.

Himalaya himself, praising his own fortunes, went towards that side with devotion.

I, finding the army of the gods there, feeling graceful and surprised, confronted them.

The gods, then observing the community of the lord of mountain- Himalaya, were extremely surprised. Actually both the communities of the gods as well as the mountain were please.

O Sage, the armies of the gods as well as the mountains were shining like the eastern as well as the western oceans.

With the mutual meeting of the gods and mountains, both of them felt delighted.

Placing Siva in the fore-front, Himalaya adored him offering his salutation to him. All the Brahmanas as well as the mountains followed him.

The lustre of Siva, mounted over the bull, with delightful face, adorned with all the ornaments, displaying heavenly beauty over his limbs, became resplendent on all the four sides.

He wore costumes of the fine silken yam, over the body, adorning his head with the gem-studded crown. He was smiling with bright resplendence.

The ornaments of snakes were found on all his limbs. He was being served by the gods, holding the flywhisks in their hands.

He was flanked by Visnu on the left and Brahma on the right. Indra the god of gods was at the back.

He was eulogised by Brahma and other gods. He looked kind to the people. He was the one having assumed different physical forms for his own reasons. He was Brahman himself, the lord of all and the bestower of the boons.

He was both with or without attributes, subservient to the devotees, merciful, greater than the primordial being and of the primordial nature, existence, knowledge and bliss itself.

Visnu appeared mounted over Garuda, to the right of the lord, who was adorned with all the ornaments.

O Sage, I with four heads was found with my kiths and kins to the right of Siva.

Finding both the lords, who were dear to Siva. Giriraja bowed in reverence to them also with his kiths and kins.

Then mountain-king bowed in reverence to the gods, who was standing at the back of lord Siva.

Then at the command of Siva, Giriraja, moving forward entered his city, followed by rest of the gods including, Hari, Sesa, Brahma, sages, and all other gods,

All the gods and the sages after entering the city after Siva, started praising the same very much.

The gods and others were lodged over a beautiful mountain peak, where all the arrangements had already been made. Thereafter, they went to the place of *mandapa,* which was square in shape, and was decorated with *torana* on all the sides. Himavan then performed the ceremonial ablusion, gave charitable gifts and inspected everything.

Giriraja Himalaya, then sent his sons to Siva, who was seated in the company of Visnu and other gods.

Himalaya- the lord of the mountains, delightfully, with great enthusiasm intended to welcome Siva, with all his relatives.

The sons of Himalaya, reaching there, offered the salutation to lord Siva, with his companions, and conveyed the request of his father.

Receiving his consent all the sons, returned to their abode and delightfully told his father, about the arrival of Siva.

On the other hand the gods listening to the request to Giriraja, O Sage, all gods, including Siva and Visnu, felt extremely delighted.

All the gods, clad in beautiful costumes, together with Siva and sages reached the abode of Himalaya.

O Sage, at that point of time, Mena desired to have a look at Siva and for that purpose she sent for you for the purpose.

O Sage, at the instance of Siva, you went there and you desired to fulfill the desire of Siva, mentally.

O Sage, Mena, with an astonishing mind, with a desire for looking at the form of Siva, who shattered the pride of all, said to you.”

## Chapter 43 - Wonderful sport of Siva

Mena said, “O Sage, first of fall I would like to see Siva, the lord of Girija, for achieving whom, she performed such a hard *tapas.”*

Brahma said, “O Sage, thus, having been confused with ignorance, she with a desire to have a look at Siva, reached the terrace along with you.

Siva on his part realising about the pride of her mind, thought of displaying an astonishing sport and then said to Visnu.”

Siva said, “At my command, both of you (Brahma and Visnu) should move to the entrance gate of Himalaya. We shall follow you.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of Siva, calling for all the gods asked them to move on.

O Sage, Mena who was seated over the terrace, you pointed out Siva to her in such a way, which could confuse her mind.

O Sage, at that time she looking at the beautiful army of the gods, was simply pleased.

There were the Gandharvas moving first of all with beautiful bodies, clad in the best of costumes and adorned with all the ornaments. They arrived mounted over the various types of vehicles, decorated with various types of flags, playing on various types of musical instruments and accompanied with the *apsaras.*

On seeing Vasu, the lord of Vasus, Mena felt delighted and uttered, “Is this Siva?”

O Excellent Sage, you told her, “These are only the attendants of Siva. This is not the groom Siva.”

On hearing this, Mena thought, “Siva could be a person greater then them! How will he look like?”

In the meantime she saw Manigriva- the lord of Yaksas, with other Yaksas and their vast army with double the splendour of a Vasus.

On looking at the resplendent Manigriva- the lord of Yaksas, Mena felt delighted and said, “Is he Siva- the bridegroom of Parvati?

Then you replied to Mena, “This is not Siva, but is an attendant of Siva only.” By about the same time the fire-god passed by that way.

On seeing the splendour double to that as compared with Yaksa, looking at him, Mena asked you whether he was Siva- the bridegroom of Parvati, but you said no to her.

In the meantime Yama passed having the splendour double than that of Agni. On seeing him the delighted Mena exclaimed, “This is Siva.”

But you said “no”. At the same time Nirriti the lord of *Punyajanas* arrived there. He looked more graceful.

Looking at him, Mena felt happy, taking him to be Siva. But you told her that he was not Siva. Then arrived Varuna.

Finding that he was more graceful than the others she asked, “Is he Rudra- the lord of Girija? But you said “no”. Then arrived Vasudeva, who had much more splendour that the earlier ones. But you replied in the negative.

Then arrived the wind god, having a splendour greater than others. Mena felt delighted taking him to Rudra.

You again negativated her assumption. Then arrived Kubera, the lord of Guhyakas, who was still more beautiful.

Looking at him Mena thought him to be Siva, but you told her that he was not Siva. By the same time Isana also arrived.

Mena finding him to be more beautiful than others said, “Is he Rudra, the groom of Girija? But your reply was in the negative.

Then arrived Indra, who happened to be much more beautiful than others, who was the most beautiful than all the gods, being the lord of heaven.

Looking at him, Mena enquired, “Is he Siva?” But you told her that he was Indra, the lord of the heaven but not Siva.

Then there arrived the moon, who was the most beautiful of all and Mena took him to be Rudra. But you told her that he was not Siva.

Then arrived the sun who was more illustrious than others. When Mena tried to ascertain whether he illustrious than others. When Mena tried to ascertain whether he was Siva, or not, your reply was no to her.

Thereafter Bhrgu and other illustrious sages arrived, accompanied with their disciples.

Finding Brhaspati among them, Mena asked whether he was the husband of Girija but your reply was in the negative.

Then arrived Brahma, having enormous resplendence with him, accompanied with his sons and the sages. They appeared like the group of Dharmas.

Looking at them, the delighted Mena asked whether he was the husband of Girija? But your replied in the negative. In the meantime, there arrived cloud complexioned, four armed, looking graceful, lord Visnu.

He had the resplendence comparable with the crores of the gods of love, and with clad in yellow costumes. He had the lotus like eyes and was mounted over Garuda.

In his hands, he held *Samkha, cakra, gada,* as attributes and was wearing a crown. He had Srivatsa over the chest. The immense lustre issued from the body of the lord of Laksmi.

Mena looking at him, felt surprised and delightfully said, “He is the lord of Siva incarnate on earth. There is no doubt about it.”

Listening to the curious words of Mena, you said, “He is not the lord of Siva, but is lord Visnu instead. He is incharge of all the marriage party of Siva, besides being his great favourite. The bride-groom Siva is far better than him and it is impossible to describe his beauty, O Mena. He is the lord of the entire universe and the lord of all.

Brahma said, “Listening to your words, Mena thought that her daughter was quite auspicious, rich, fortunate, abode of happiness, for the three families.
