After thus instructing the goddess Parvati in the conducting of a chaste lady, the Brahmana woman, while taking leave of Mena told her to make preparations for the journey of Parvati.

Accepting the command of the Brahmana woman, she was overpowered with the affection of her daughter getting upset at the same time, with the separation of Kali, she some how composed herself and called her.

Embracing her, she cried aloud, Parvati too speaking humble words started weeping.

Overpowered with the grief of separation both the mother and the daughter fainted. With the cries of Parvati, the wives of the gods too were fainted.

All the woman fainted while crying. What to speak of others even Yogesvara Siva also started crying.

In the meantime Himalaya also reached there with his sons, courtiers, Brahmanas and the relatives.

Pressing the daughter against his chest, while crying, he said, “Where are you going?” Thus speaking he kept on crying again and again.

Then the Brahmanas, together with the learned priest, delivering discourse on *atmavidya* appropriately advised everyone.

With utmost devotion, Parvati, bowed in reverence to her parents, following the worldly tradition, Mahamaya- Parvati, again started crying aloud.

At the cries of Parvati, all the woman, sisters and brothers, also started crying.

Then the mother of Siva, sisters, brother, father started crying out of affection.

At that point of time, the Brahmana arrived there and apprised them of the auspicious time for the departure on journey, cautioning them at the same time.

Then Mena and Himalaya some how composed themselves and got the palanquin for the seating of Parvati.

The wives of the Brahmanas, made Sita to be seated in the palanquin. At that point of time, the parents and the Brahmanas, blessed her.

The chief queen Mena and Himalaya presented to Parvati, such of the articles and ornaments, which were beyond the reach of the ordinary people.

O Sage, Parvati offered her salutation to her mother, her father, the preceptors, the Brahmanas, the priests, the sisters and other woman, and then departed from the house of Himalaya.

Having been overpowered with affection, Himalaya accompanied with his sons, went to the place where Siva was seated with the gods.

All of them then started celebrating the occasion. All of them offered their salutation with devotion to lord Siva, and then returned to Kailasa, the abode of Siva, praising him.

Then Siva spoke to Parvati, “I am going to remind you although, you are well aware of your previous birth. In case you remember it, then you should speak out the same. In my divine sports, you have always been my beloved.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the words of Siva, Parvati, the beloved of Siva, then spoke smilingly.”

Parvati said, “O Lord, I am silently remembering everything. But presently you perform all the essential duties today. I bow in reverence to you.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the nectar like words of Parvati, engaged in the worldly traditions, Siva was extremely pleased.

Making all the materials ready, Siva made several types of eatables and served them to Narayana and others for eating.

Those who had joined his marriage and the others, were served by Siva the delicious articles of food, quite lovingly.

All the gods with their spouses, getting adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments, bowed in reverence to Siva.

He eulogised him with the best of the *stotras.* Then circumambulating him, praising the marriage ceremony, they went back to their respective abodes.

O Sage, Siva, then according to the worldly tradition, bowed in reverence to me (Brahma) and Visnu as lord Visnu had offered his salutation to the sage Kasyapa.

I blessed Siva, embracing him at the same time and he in turn eulogised me as the Supreme Brahman.

Then both myself and Visnu, bowed in reverence to both Siva and Siva, and with their permission, praising the marriage returned to our abodes.

Siva too together with Parvati, engaged themselves in the divine sports, in the mountains delightfully. The *ganas* of Siva too were happy, who adored the married couple.

O Dear one, I have thus narrated the auspicious story of the marriage of Siva, which removes all the grief, bestows happiness and increases the life, and riches.

A person, who purifying himself and with a devoted mind will listen to this story, or regularly recites the same to others, he surely achieves Sivaloka.

This story is quite surprising, it bestows welfare, besides removing all the obstructions and ailments.

It bestows the glory, long life, sons and grandsons, fulfills all the desires, grants comforts as well as *moksa.*

It removes the danger of untimely death, is the cause of immense peace, is auspicious and the remover of all the sufferings.

In all the functions relating to the adoration of Siva, the person desirous of his welfare, should recite the same making all the efforts, because it pleases Siva.

Especially at the time of the consecration of the gods or at the time of the start of all the functions relating to Siva, recitation of this story should be made.

Getting purified, the story of Siva- Siva should be heard, because by listening to the same, all the desires of a person are fulfilled. There is no doubt about it.

Here ends the third Parvati Khanda of second Rudra Samhita of Siva Mahapurana.

A gem brought from the Himalaya and the Indus (being of four sorts- white, pale yellow red, and dark blue).  
One bowl approximately 250 grams.  
Jasminum Auriculatum.  
A particular attitude in shooting (the right knee advanced, the left leg drawn back).

## (4) Kumara Khanda

## Chapter 1 - Love sports of Siva and Parvati

I offer my salutation to Siva, who is pleased merely by offering a salutation to him, who loves his devotion, who bestows the complete devotion, who fulfills all the desires, who is the form of truth, truthful, who possesses the truth and the fortunes, at all the three times, who likes and speaks the truth, who is adored by Brahma and Visnu, and who takes to human form by his illusion alone.

Narada said, “Siva, who bestows welfare on all the three lokas, after his marriage with Parvati, reached the Kailasa mountain, and what did he do there? You tell me.

How could Atma-rama- the Supreme soul, Siva, get a son, the purpose for which he had married with Siva.

O Brahma, how was Tarakasura killed, which pleased the gods kindly narrate the entire story to me.”

Suta said, “Thus listening to the words of Narada, Brahma, happily, devoting his mind towards Siva delightfully, then replied to Narada.”

Brahma said, “O Narada, I am now going to narrate to you the story of Siva, relating to the birth of Kartikeya, and the killing of Tarakasura.

I am going to narrate to you the story, listening to which, a person is relieved of all the sins.

The relevant story destroys all the sins, is quite secret, quite surprising, remover of the sufferings from the sins, besides being the remover of all the obstructions.

The said story, bestows all the welfare, is quite important, pleasant in hearing, comfortable, cause of moksa and the destroyer of the evil or inauspicious deeds.

After his marriage with Siva, Siva, after reaching Kailasa, looked extremely graceful and then thought of performing the task of the gods.

On the arrival of Siva over the Kailasa mountain, enormous celebrations were held. The gods also felt delighted and then returned to their respective abodes.

On the arrival of Siva over the Kailasa mountain, enormous celebrations were held. The gods also felt delighted and then returned to their respective abodes.

Thereafter, Siva together with Parvati, went to the extremely pleasant lonely place.

There was a comfortable bed which had been made with flowers and sandal paste, where all the articles of comfort had been made available and was quite surprising.

Lord Siva, the bestower of honour, enjoyed love-sports with Parvati there for a thousand divine years.

With the mere touch of the limbs of Durga, Siva was fainted, while Siva was fainted with the touch of Siva. Both of them became unmindful of the days and nights.

O Sinless one, both of them were engaged in the love-sports to honour the worldly tradition as a result of which a long time was passed like a moment.

O Dear one, soon thereafter, all the gods including Indra, collected over the Sumeru mountain, started consultations amongst themselves.

The gods said, “O Great Yogi- resting in your ownself, unblemished Siva, you had married Parvati, for the accomplishment of our task.

A son has not yet been born, even after the lapse of such a long time. What is the reason for it? We are not aware of the reason, why, O Lord, such a delay is being caused.”

Brahma said, “In the meantime, Narada having the divine vision, came to know of their enjoying the conjugal pleasure for an unlimited period.

Then all the gods, making Brahma to lead them, reached the abode of Visnu.

Offering their salutation to him, I (Brahma), conveyed the news to him, hearing which all the gods stood there like a painting drawn on the wall.

For a thousand years, according to the calculation of the gods, Siva- the great yogi had been engaged in love-sports, and he was not disassociating from the same.”

Lord Visnu said, “O Brahma, don’t worry the least, everything will be well done. O God of gods, O Great lord, go and take refuge with Siva.

The one to takes refuge devotedly with Siva, such a devotee does not have to face the fear or danger.

O Brahma, the task would be established at the time of the interruption of the love-sport, and not now. Any task performed at the appropriate time, shall meet with success and not otherwise.

In case Siva is desirous of enjoyment, who can stop it? After the completion of another thousand years, he will stop it, at his own will.

The one who, by any means disturbs the couple enjoying the conjugal pleasures, he will have to face separation from his wife and sons, in every birth.

He will be deprived of the excellent wisdom, getting his glory destroyed. He will be deprived of his fortunes, such a sinner, after his death shall have to suffer from the torture, in the Kalasutra hell for a hundred thousand years.

Durvasa- the great sage, had got Indra separated, when he was engaged in love making with Rambha. Therefore he had to suffer from the separation of his wife.

Then Durvasa, married another woman and after enjoying the conjugal pleasures with her for divine thousand years, removed his pain of separation.

Brhaspati had prevented Kamadeva while he was united with Ghrtachi. As a result of this, the moon abducted the wife of his preceptor within a month.

Then he, after adoring Siva, got Tara as his wife and for that purpose, he had to fight with his own preceptor. He removed the pain of his separation by getting Tara pregnant.

The sage Gautama had the moon, while he was engaged in sex-play with Mohini. Therefore, he had to face the separation from his wife.

Though Hariscandra, made a sudra woman unconscious while she was having an intercourse with some one in a lonely place, but you just listen to the result of the same.

At the denouncement of Viswamitra, he was deprived of the kingdom, the wife and the son. Thereafter he adored Siva as a result of which he was relieved of the sin.

Though a noble Brahmana, was copulating with a Sudra woman, the gods did not interfere because of this fear.

Everything can be achieved with the discharge of the semen. O Brahma, the process of discharge is quite effective, which is fruitful and no one can withhold it.

O Gods, the activities of conjugal pleasures, of Siva was going to continue for a divine thousand years and the method of the dropping of the semen of Siva on the ground, had to be thought of. A son named Skanda would be born of the semen of Siva.

O Brahma, presently you should retire to your abode with the gods. Let Siva, enjoy the company of Parvati in the secluded place.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, thus speaking, Visnu, the lord of Laksmi, at once returned to his abode. The gods also retired to their respective places with me.

Because of the love-sports of Siva and Parvati, the earth became weighty and started shaking with the serpent Sesanaga and the tortoise.

When the tortoise could no more carry the burden, then the wind which is the life of all the creatures, was also shaken, as a result of which all the three lokas were frightened.

Then all the gods, along with me again took refuge with Visnu and feeling disgusted, conveyed the news to him.

The gods said, “O God of gods, O Protector of all, we have been frightened, and have arrived to take refuge with you. You kindly protect us.

We do not know the reason for which the breathing of the people of the three worlds has been stopped, as a result of this, all the gods, the sages, mobiles and immobiles, of the three worlds have been distressed.”

Brahma said, “O Great sage, thus speaking all the gods with me took their seats getting distressed.

On hearing this, lord Visnu, proceeded towards the Kailasa mountain, which was liked the most by Siva.

Visnu, dear to the gods, together with myself and the gods, went to Siva’s place in order to have an audience with him.

When Visnu together with the gods could not find Siva there, he felt surprised. He quite humbly enquired about Siva’s whereabouts from his ganas."

Lord Visnu said, “O Siva’s ganas, where is Siva, the lord of all? All of you are quite compassionate. Since we are immensely suffering, therefore you tell us about him.

Brahma said, “The ganas of Siva, on hearing the words of Visnu and the gods accompanying him, lovingly spoke to Visnu- the lord of Laksmi.”

The Siva’s ganas said, “O Visnu, you please listen with Brahma and the other gods. We speak truthfully, because of our devotion for Siva.

Sarvesvara Siva who is well-versed in the performing of several sports, has gone to the abode of Girija, leaving us here.

O Lord Visnu- the husband of Laksmi, we are unaware of the activities of Siva in that place. He left for that place- many years back.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, listening to the words of the ganas of Siva, Visnu felt surprised. Then he alongwith me and the gods went to the abode of Siva.

Visnu- who is loved by the gods, spoke with compassionate tone quite loudly.

O Excellent sage, then myself, Visnu, and all the gods offered prayer to Siva.”

Visnu said, “0 Paramesvara, 0 Mahadeva, what are you doing inside. You please protect the god who have arrived here having been frightened by Tarakasura.

O Excellent sage, I myself, Visnu and the gods having been frightened by Tarakasura, prayed to Siva, variously. Then they started crying there.

O Excellent sage, the gods having been troubled by the demon, started crying creating uproars.

## Chapter 2 - Birth of Kartikeya: the son of Siva

Brahma said, “Lord Mahadeva, who was well-versed in the knowledge of yoga, listening to the prayer and the uproar, intended to end the love-sport, but was unable to do so for fear of Parvati.

Then Siva who was well-disposed towards his devotees, arrived near the gods who had been frightened at the gate of the house.

Finding lord Siva there, myself (Brahma) besides the gods, were immensely pleased.

Listening to the words of the gods, Siva with a painful heart spoke to them.

O Sage, Brahma, Visnu and other gods, humbly lowering there heads, bowed in reverence to Siva, offering prayer at the same time.

The gods said, “O God of gods, O Mahadeva, O Ocean of mercy, O Lord, O Sankara, you are immanent, and as such you are well aware of everything.

O Lord, O Mahesvara. You kindly kill the most powerful demon Taraka and others, showing your mercy on the gods.”

Siva said, “O Visnu, O Brahma and other gods, I am well aware of the ideas in your mind. Whatever is destined, is destined to happen. No one can stop it.

Whatever has happened till now, was destined to happen. Now you listen what is going to happen now, who will receive the semen emerging from me?”

Thus speaking “Let him take who will- take up this discharged semen.” Thus speaking, he let it fall over the ground. At the instance of the gods, the fire god taking to the form of a dove, swallowed the semen of Siva through the beak. O Sage, in the meantime Parvati arrived there.

At the delay of the return of Siva, she found the gods there. Learning about the news, Parvati was enraged. Then getting enraged, she spoke to the gods like Visnu and other.”

The goddess said, “O Gods, you are particularly wicked, selfish and cause pain to others. O Gods for the accomplishment of the selfish motive, you, by adoring the supreme lord Siva, have obstructed my conjugal pleasures, making me barren at the same time.

O Gods, no one can feel comfortable by opposing me. Therefore, you the wicked gods will also have to suffer.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, the daughter of Himalaya, getting enraged, pronounced a curse on Visnu and other gods.

Parvati said, “From today onwards, the wives of the gods would remain barren. Such of the gods who opposed me shall have to suffer.”

Brahma said, “Jagadamba, thus pronouncing a curse on the gods, spoke in anger to Agni, who had swallowed the semen of Siva.” Parvati said, “O Agni, from today onwards, you shall become the consumer of all and you will always suffer from pain. The performer of the task of the gods, O Agni, you are a fool unaware of the Siva-tattva.

O Immensely wicked Agni, you bestow knowledge to others. But you have consumed the semen of Siva and by so doing, you have not done well.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, the daughter of Himalaya, thus pronouncing a curse on Agni, feeling dissatisfied, returned to her abode with Siva.

Reaching there, Siva, making all the efforts, spoke to her. O Excellent sage, thereafter Parvati gave birth to Ganesa as a son.

O Sage, I shall narrate that story later on. Presently I shall narrate the story of the birth of Guha (Kartikeya).

The cereals and other eatables which are consumed by the fire god are passed on to the gods as per the provision of the scriptures and the Vedas. Therefore all the gods became pregnant.

Then Visnu and other gods being unable to tolerate the semen of Siva, started suffering. Because of the curse of Siva, they also lost their wisdom.

Thereafter, Visnu and other gods getting confused, burning from the fire of semen, went to take refuge with the husband of Parvati.

Reaching the gate of the abode of Siva, started praying in a humble manner, with their hands folded to Siva and Parvati both.

The gods said, “O God of gods, O Mahadeva, O Lord of Giriraja, O Great Lord, what has happened to us at the moment. Your illusion is imperishable.

We have become pregnant, and are burning with your semen. O Siva, kindly remove our present suffering.

Brahma said, “O Sage, thus listening to the prayer of the gods, the lord of Parvati, arrived at the place, where gods were standing.

At the arrival of Siva at the gate, all the gods, lowering their heads, offered their salutation to Siva who is kindly disposed towards his devotees and then offered prayer to him.”

The gods said, “O Sambhu, O Siva, O Mahesan, we particularly offer our salutation to you. We are burning from your semen andhave arrived here to take refuge with you. You kindly save us.

O Siva, you kindly remove our sufferings, otherwise we will die soon. O Lord, who else is there except you, to relieve use from the sufferings.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the pathetic words of the gods, Siva, the lord of the gods, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, spoke to the gods smilingly.”

Siva said, “O Brahma, O Visnu and other gods, you better listen to my words and you will be comfortable thereafter. All of you should be alert.

O Gods, all of you should vomit out my semen. Thereafter with my command, all of you would be comfortable.

Brahma said, “Then Visnu and all other gods, honouring the command of Siva, the devoting their mind at the feet of the imperishable Siva, vomited out the semen of Siva,.

The semen of the gold complexion, after falling over the earth, was raised like an astonishing mountain and started shining, touching the heaven.

Then Visnu and other gods offered prayer to Siva who is well-disposed towards his devotees and became comfortable.

O Excellent sage, at that point of time the fire god could not be comfortable, because lord Siva had issued a hard command to him.

O Sage, then the fire god, getting upset, lowering his head, feeling painful, offering prayer to Siva, said.

The fire god said, “O God of gods, O Mahesan, I am a fool but a servant to you. Granting me pardon, you kindly remove my burning sensation.

O Lord, you are well-disposed towards the miserable people. Therefore, Paramesvara, getting pleased, said to Agni.”

Siva said, “By consuming my semen, you did an improper thing. Thus because of the enormity of the sin and at my command, your burning sensation has not stopped.

O Fire god, since you have arrived here and taken refuge with me, I feel pleased. Now you will be relieved of your suffering.

Now you drop my semen in the womb of a chaste woman, quite carefully. Thereafter you would be relieved of the burning sensation and be happy.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the words of Siva, (the fire god), slowly, with devotion, folding his hands, spoke to Siva, who bestows welfare to his devotees.

“O Lord, O Mahesvara, your semen is quite unbearable, which cannot be retained by any other woman in her womb, except Parvati.”

O Excellent sage, at these words of the fire god, then at the inspiration of Siva, you in order come to get you help. Agni then spoke to you.

Narada said, “O Fire god, you listen to my words, which are remover of fire, bestower of welfare besides the extreme bliss and remover of all the sufferings.

O Dear one, you burn all and are known as Agnideva, as desired by Siva, I am going to speak out a remedy, following which quite respectfully, you will be relieved of your suffering.

O Agni, in the month of Magha, the women who take bath early in the morning, you should deposit the semen in their bodies.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, at the same time, the wives of the same seven sages arrived there, who regularly took bath in the month of Magha.

O Sage, six of the seven women, after taking their bath, shivering with cold, went to the fire.

Finding them confused, the wise and the chaste Arundhati stopped them from doing so.

O Sage, six of the seven wives of the sages, becoming stubborn and confused with the illusion of Siva, went towards the fire to relive themselves of the cold.

O Sage, particles of the semen of Siva entered the bodies of those women through the pores of the hairs, O Sage. Thereafter, the fire god was relieved of the burning sensation.

Then the fire god at once disappeared from the scene, in the form of a flame and happily went to his abode, reciting the name of Siva in his mind.

O Saint, in turn the women became pregnant and felt distressed with the burning sensation. All of them then returned home, but Arundhati was annoyed with Agni.

O Dear one, the husbands of the women, realising the plight of their wives became furious. They consulted one another and discarded them.

O Dear, on seeing their own state the six ladies felt very miserable and distressed.

Then feeling disgusted, the six women of the sages, cast off their semen in the form of foetus over the peak of Himalaya and were thus relieved of their burning sensation.

O Excellent sage, Himalaya too was unable to bear the heat of the semen of Siva, Himalaya, getting scorched, while trembling, hurled the semen into the flowing water of the Ganga.

O Excellent sage, the Ganga too finding the semen of Siva to be unbearable, dropped it by her waves in the forest of the sara grass.

With the fall of the semen in the Sara forest it was turned into a handsome and a beautiful male child, having enough of glory and splendour, who delighted all.

O Sage, on the sixth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Margasirsa, the son of Siva was born in the world.

At that point of time, both Siva and Parvati the daughter of Himalaya, became extremely happy at the mountain.

Having been filled with motherly affection, the milk started oozing out of the breast of Parvati. The minds of all the people was delighted at that time.

O Dear one at that time the auspicious celebrations were held in all the three worlds, which provided comforts and delights to the sages obstructions were particularly created in the tasks of the wicked people and the demons.

Suddenly the drums were beaten in the sky and O Narada, the rain of flowers was showered over the child.

O Excellent sage, Visnu and all other gods suddenly felt delighted. There was a great jubilation everywhere.

## Chapter 3 - Childhood sports of Kartikeya

Narada said, “O God of gods, O Prajapati, O Brahma, O Creator of the universe, O Lord, you kindly tell me as to what happened thereafter.

Brahma said, “O Dear one, at that point of time, as a move of destiny, the sage Visvamitra arrived there of his own.

Observing the divine resplendence of the son of Siva, his desire was fulfilled and he bowed in reverence to him with delight.

Then Visvamitra, who was well aware of the influence of the child, eulogised him at the instance of Brahma.

Then the son of Siva, who indulged in several types of sports, feeling delighted, said to Visvamitra.”

The son of Siva said, “O Immensely wise one, how have you arrived here as per the desire of Siva? O Dear one, you better perform all the samskaras for me as prescribed in the Vedas.

From today onwards, you function as our priest. By loving me, you would surely become adorable by all.”

Brahma said, “Listening to these words, the son of Gadhi, was surprised and spoke to him in sweet words.”

Visvamitra said, “O Dear one, I am a Ksatriya son of Gadhi. I am not a Brahmana. I am known by the name of Visvamitra. I am a Ksatriya and the servant of the Brahmanas.

O Excellent child, I have given my acquaintance to you. You better give me your own introduction. Who are you. I feel surprised at your words.”

Brahma said, “On hearing these words, the divine child gave his introduction to the sage. Then the body who had been the cause of the great enjoyment, spoke to the son of Gadhi, quite lovingly.

Siva’s son said, “O Visvamitra, with my boon, you would become a Bramharsi. There is no doubt about it. The sages like Vasistha and others, would respectfully praise you.

Therefore, at may command, you can perform the samskaras. You keep this secret quite concealed and don’t reveal it to anyone.”

Brahma said, “O Narada, thereafter Visvamitra lovingly performed the samskara of Kartikeya according to the Vedic tradition.

Then Siva’s son who could perform several types of sports, delightfully, bestowed to the sage Visvamitra, the supreme and divine knowledge.

Since that moment, the son of Agni, who could indulge in several sports made Visvamitra his priest and he become a great Brahmana and an expert in the various divine sports.

O Sage, this happens to be his very first sport which had been performed by him and has been narrated by me to you. Now you listen to another wonderful sport of Siva’s son, which I am going to narrate to you.

O Dear one, at the same time a sage named Sveta arrived there and found a divine son.

Then arrived Agni, who after embracing him kissed him as well. Then calling him his son. he gave him a divine Sakti.

Guha (Kartikeya) then carrying that Sakti, climbed over the peak of the Kraunca mountain and attacking its peak with that Sakti, he threw it on the ground.

Observing this, initially ten demons arrived there to kill him. With the attack of the Sakti possessed by Kartikeya, all of them were destroyed.

A huge uproar was created there. The earth started shaking with the mountains. All the three lokas also started shaking. Indra the lord of gods too arrived there.

Then Indra attacked over the left arm of the boy, from where there emerged a Sakha, possessing great strength.

Indra again struck him with vajra, on the left side and there emerged another great warrior named Vaisakha.

Indra then attacked the child at his heart with vajra and a great warrior known as Naigama emerged from the same.

Thereafter Skanda and other three great warriors, at once proceeded for the killing of Indra, who took refuge with them.

O Sage, Indra then getting frightened returned to his abode with the gods, feeling surprised. But he could not realise the truth about the child.

O Dear one, the boy who indulged in such types of sports, firmly stayed there with delight without fear like before.

At the same time six Krttika women arrived their to take bath and they found the child who was a great lord.

All the Krttikas tried to catch hold of the boy, but all of them quarrelled among themselves over the possession of the boy.

In order to subside their quarrel, the child developed six faces. O Sage, thereafter all the six of them, made the child to drink milk from their individual breasts.

O Sage, all the six Krttikas, realising the mental condition of the child, carried him to their place.

The child who was desirous of drinking the breast milk, and was illustrious like the sun, was being brought up by the Krttika by means of breast feeding.

The child was dear to the Krttikas much more than their lives, and they never allowed him to be away from their sight even for a moment. In fact the son belongs to the one who brings him up.

Such of the costumes and ornaments which could rarely be found in the universe, were given to the child.

They specially fed the child with the delicious food daily and took special care to bring him up.

O Dear one, once, the son of the Krttikas, went to the royal court and displayed his wonderful feats.

The child who indulged in enormous sports, displayed his astonishing lustre before Visnu and other gods.

Looking at that resplendence, Visnu, together with all the gods and the sages feeling surprised and asked the child, “Who are you?” On hearing this he kept quiet and spoke nothing. Then returning home he lived there secretly.

## Chapter 4 - Search for Kartikeya and dialogue between Kartikeya and Nandi

Narada said, “O God of gods, O Lord of the people, O Brahma, what happened thereafter kindly narrate the story of Siva’s sports.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, when Krttikas took Kartikeya with them, but Parvati remained unaware of the birth of Kumara.

At that point of time, Parvati beaming with her lotus like face told her husband Siva, the lord of the gods.

Parvati said, “O Lord of the gods, O Mahadeva, listen to my pleasant words. O Lord, I have got you because of the auspicious deeds of my earlier birth.

Inspite of your being the best of the yogis, you became ready to enjoy the conjugal pleasures with me. O Siva, the gods disturbed the sexual pleasures between both of us.

O Lord, because of this, your semen was dropped over the ground instead of my womb. O Lord what has happened to that semen, and which one of the gods has concealed the same.

O Lord, your semen, could never become useless, then how could it become useless? Has the child been born out of it?

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, listening to the words of Parvati, Siva summoned the gods and the sages and the spoke to them smilingly.”

Siva said, “O Gods, have you heard the talk of Parvati (with me)? Now you listen to my words. Where has my unused semen gone? Who has hidden it?

Could it not be lifted by anyone in a haste? Whosoever has carried it, is he not liable for punishment? He could not be a competent king but a usurper and would be harassed by the people. He cannot be a protector.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Siva, the gods after consulting among themselves, started speaking gradually.

Visnu said, “Whosoever has concealed your semen let him not be entitled to your adoration in the land of Bharata.”

Brahma said, “Whosoever has concealed your semen, he would not be entitled to adore you in the auspicious land of Bharata.

Lokapalas said, “The sinful person, who has hidden you fallen semen, in confusion, he has earned the sin no doubt. He will suffer from that sin, without getting relieved of the same.”

The gods said, “A fool, who after making a promise does not fulfill it, he earns a sin. the same type of sin shall be earned by a person who has concealed the semen.”

The wives of the gods said, “The one who has hidden the semen should earn the sin, which is earned by a woman, who denounces her husband, enjoys love-sports with a person other than her husband, and getting separated from her parents and the brothers.

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of the gods, Mahadeva- the god of gods, feeling panicky spoke to Dharmaraja, who happened to be the witness of the deeds of all the people.

Siva said, “The gods have not hidden the semen. But it has been hidden by some one else. It is the infructuous semen of Mahesa- the great lord (like me).

You people are the witness of the deeds of the entire world. Have you hidden it? What do you know about it you tell me?”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Siva, all those present in the assembly started shaking and started talking to one another.

“Your solid semen at the time of your intercourse, had fallen on earth subsequently. I thought it to be infructuous because of your anger.”

The earth said, “I was unable to contain that semen and I transferred it to Agni. Therefore, O Lord Siva, you kindly forgive a helpless woman like me.”

Agni said, “O Lord Siva, I had been unable to contain that semen, therefore, I in the form of a pigeon dropped it over the Kailasa mountain.

The mountain said, “O Supreme lord, O Sankara, when the semen became intolerable for me, then I dropped it into the Ganga.

Ganga said, “O Siva- the lokapala, when I could not bear the semen in my waters, then I, through my waves, pushed it to the forest of Sara plants.

Then the wind god said, “With the fall of the semen in the forest of Sara plants, it was turned into a child. O Siva, at the bank of the Svargaganga, the child looked quite beautiful.”

Then the sun said, “O Lord, influenced with the wheel of time, finding the child crying, I moved towards Astacala. I could not stop during the night.”

The moon said, “O Siva, the child who wascrying was carried by the six Krttikas and took him to Badrikasrama.”

The water said, “The Krttikas, carrying your son, having the lustre of the sun and started bring him up like their own son.”

Sandhya said, “Those Krttikas are bringing up the child in the forest in Badrikasrama. Having been filled with curiosity, they have given him the name of Kartikeya.”

The night said, “The child is dearer to them than their own lives, and they never allow him to escape their sight even for a moment. The one who brings up a child, he is called the father.”

The day said, “They decorate him with the best of costumes and ornaments. They feed him with the best and the delicious food.”

Brahma said, “Listening to these words, Siva, the enemy of Tripura, felt immensely pleased and he gave away enormous daksina to the Brahmanas.

Learning about the news of her son, Parvati was pleased. She gave away enormous riches and crores of gems to the Brahmanas in charity.

At that point of time, Laksmi, Sarasvati, Savitri, Mena and other women, too, besides to gods like Visnu and others, gave away riches in charity.

At the instance of the gods, the sages and the mountains, Siva sent his ganas to the place, where his son was lodged.

They included Virabhadra, Visalaksa, Sankurkarna, Prakrama, Nandisvara, Vajradamstra, Mahanmada, Gokarnasya, Dadhimukha- resembling the fire flame, a lakhs of Ksetrapalas and three lakhs of goblins, Rudras who were as valorous as Siva himself in strength and Bhairavas, besides the innumerable ganas with the deformed faces. All of them were sent there.

The messengers of Siva, carrying various types of weapons in their hands, surrounded the Krttikas.

Finding the ganas of Siva, surrounding them, the Krttikas, spoke to Kartikeya, possessing the divine resplendence.

The Krttikas said, “O Son, the innumerable warriors have surrounded our house, what should be done? Where should we go? We are facing enormous danger.”

Kartikeya said, “O Auspicious ladies, don’t be afraid, why should you be afraid, when I am there? Though I am a child, I cannot be stopped by anyone. O Mothers, who can stop me?”

Brahma said, “At the same time, Nandisvara, the best of the army of Siva, sat before Kartikeya and said to him.”

Nandikesvara said, “O Brother and O mothers, you listen from me the auspicious cause of my arrival here. Lord Siva, the destroyer of the three worlds has sent me here.

O Dear one, all the gods like Brahma, Visnu and Siva, are present in an auspicious assembly.

At that time Parvati addressed Siva, the benefactor of all, in that assembly urging a search for you.

Siva, with a desire to get you called for and enquired from all the gods about you, who gave the appropriate reply.

Dharmaraja- the witness of the good and evil deeds, informed Siva about your presence with the Krttikas.

In earlier times Siva and Parvati indulged in amorous sports and the gods found that the semen of Siva had fallen on the ground.

The earth gave away the said semen to the fire god who passed it on to the mountain who dropped the said semen in the Ganga while Ganga placed the same semen in the forest of Sara plants.

In the forest of Sara plants the said semen took to the shape of a child who was picked up by the Krttikas. You should therefore descend on earth.

Siva is going to perform abhiseka for you in the presence of the gods, when you would receive all the weapons and kill Tarakasura.

You are the son of the destroyer of universal, Krttikas cannot keep you, because a dry tree cannot hide the fire flame in its cavity.

You are the most illustrious of all the people of the world. Therefore you cannot be graceful in such houses, in the same way as the reflection of the moon falling in the deep well cannot look decent.

The way you are issuing your lustre before us, appears like the sun shining having been covered with a cloud.

O Son of Siva, you are Visnu, the lord of the universe and none else. The all-pervading sky is not pervaded by anything else.

You being a Yogindra, cannot be involved with anyone else, but you are the participant in the preserving of the world. As the soul is not at all involved with the deeds of the living beings, you are like that.

You are Isvara- the creator of the world, you cannot fit in with them in the same way as the yogis are never desirous of the virtues or the lustre of the world.

Those who are unaware of you are surely foolish, O Brother; in the same way as the frog is totally unmindful of the lotus flowers.”

Kartikeya said, “O Brother, you are well aware of the knowledge of all the three times. You are a learned person; you are the attendant of Siva, therefore praising you would be of no consequence.

O Brother, the people get reconciled to whatever form of life in which they are born. Their own actions are responsible for their birth and they have to remain satisfied with the same.

The Krttikas are wise woman practising the yoga and are the digits of Prakrti. They have brought me up nurturing with their own breast milk.

I am their foster son. They are my own part. I am born of Prakrti, with the semen of Siva, who is the lord of Prakrti.

O Nandikesvara, I have not been separated from Parvati- the daughter of the mountain,

who is practically my mother like these ladies on the basis of virtuous rites.

You have been deputed by Siva since you are like a son to him. Therefore I have to get along with you and meet the gods.”

Thus speaking and taking leave of Krttikas hurriedly, Kartikeya moved on with the ganas of Siva.

## Chapter 5 - Crowning of Kartikeya

Brahma said, “In the meantime, there arrived an excellent chariot, which had been specially made by Visvakarma.

It had a hundred wheels, quite vast and could move with the speed of the mind. It was quite pleasant with courtiers seated in the same. It had been specifically been despatched by Parvati.

The immensely intelligent Kartikeya, born of the semen of Siva, mounted the chariot with a heavy heart.

At that point of time the Krttikas, unmaking their hair, started speaking like the mad person.”

Krttikas said, “O Ocean of mercy, you are going, leaving us like a merciless person. It is against dharma when the son leaves the mother.

You are our son by dharma. We have lovingly brought you up. What shall we do and where shall we go?”

Thus speaking, all the Krttikas, holding their son, tightly against their breasts, were fainted.

Kartikeya, advising his mothers with the divine discourse, entered the chariot with the courtiers.

Observing various types of auspicious signs, Kumara moved onto the abode of his father.

Nandikesvara was seated to the right of Kartikeya, in the chariot which moved withthe speed of the mind and reached over Kailasa near the banyan tree, which had the everlasting roots.

Kumara, son of Siva, delighted and expert in many divine sports, together with the Krttikas and courtiers, halted there.

Then Brahma and Visnu, together with all the gods, Rsis, Siddhas, and Caranas announced the arrival of Kumara.

Looking at the arrival of Kumara, of the son of Ganga, Siva, Brahma and Visnu besides the sages, were highly pleased.

At that point of time, the conches, kettle drums and other musical instruments were sounded. The delighted god held huge celebrations.

At that point of time Virabhadra and other ganas rhythmically started dancing.

The people eulogised him with sweet words and praised him delightfully, shouting the slogans of victory at the same time.

Shouting the cries of victory, and salutation, the delighted people, went forward to have a look at the son of Siva, bom in the grove of Sara plants.

Parvati arranged for the decoration of the outskirts of the city with dust of padmaraga (ruby) and other gems. The main royal road was made beautiful and auspicious.

The thirty goddesses like Laksmi and others stood in the front along with the chaste ladies whose husbands and sons were alive. Parvati stood ahead of them.

The divine dancers like Rambha and others, wearing serene smiles over their faces, and clad in the best of costumes, started dancing and singing at the instance of Parvati.

Those who sighted Kartikeya the son of Ganga, resembling Siva, found that his lustre was spreading in the three worlds.

All those present there, saw Kartikeya, who was resplendent like molten gold or the Sun, and all the people bowed

All of them lowering their heads, delightfully offered their salutation to the boy. Then they surrounded him on the right and the left.

I myself (Brahma), Visnu, Indra and other gods prostrated on the ground and went round Kumara.

In the meantime, Siva and Parvati delightfully arrived there and had a look at the blissful son.

Siva, who was the only friend of the universe, the lord of the universe, adorning his body with the snakes, together with Parvati, the mother of the universe, became happy by looking at the son.

Then Skanda- the carrier of Sakti, got down from the chariot and bowed to them in reverence.

The loveable, the supreme lord, carried the child in his lap and affectionately kissed his forehead.

Thereafter, the nervous Parvati, held Kumara in her lap and then covering him made him suck the breast milk, which was oozing out from the same.

Then the gods delightfully, shouting the slogans of victory, performed his arati. The sound of the slogans of victory echoed in the sky.

The Rsis honoured the child Kumara, who had arrived in the house, with the reciting of the Vedic hymns, while the musicians did so with playing on the musical instruments.

Kumara was illumining with his own lustre and he was carried by Siva in his lap. At that point of time, Siva looked extremely graceful and became the best among the people having sons.

Then Kumara, accompanied with his ganas, went to the place of Siva, who became delightful with the enthusiastic gods.

Both Siva and Parvati were surrounded by the gods, who offered their salutation to him, together with the Rsis, looking graceful at the same time.

Then Kumara started playing in the lap of Siva quite happily, pressing the serpent Vasuki with his hand.

Mercifully looking at Kumara, Siva smilingly spoke to Parvati about the sports of the child.

Then Siva, while smiling with Parvati, felt delighted. Siva had been the sole friend of the universe, omniscient and the protector of the universe, was overpowered with affection of his son and his voice was choked and he could not speak.

Thereafter Siva, the lord of the universe, who was well-versed in the worldly traditions made Kartikeya to sit over the gem-studded lion throne.

Hundreds of pitchers studded with gems and filled with water from various holy places, were sanctified with the reciting of the Vedic hymns. Then the ceremonies of ablution of the child were performed with the same auspicious water, with pleasure.

Visnu gave him, a crown, a coronet and bracelets studded with gems, besides his own Cakra and the Vaijayanti garland, with pleasure.

Siva gave him his trident, the battle-axe, the Pasupata weapon, the weapon of destruction besides the supreme knowledge to Kumara.

I, (as Brahma) gave Kumara a yajnopavita, all the four Vedas, Gayatri- the mother of the Vedas, Brahmastra, and the knowledge for the destruction of the enemies.

Then Indra, the lord of gods, gave him the great elephant Airavata, and Vajra, while Varuna gave him a noose and a white umbrella.

The sun gave him the Chariot, which could move with the speed of mind, besides a thick Kavaca. Yama gave him the yama-danda an the pitcher of nectar from the ocean of milk.

Agni gave the Mahasakti to his son Kumara, while Nirti gave him his weapon. The wind god gave him the Vayuvyastra.

Kubera gave him the gada, Isa- a sula or a trident, while other gods gave away their respective weapons quite lovingly.

Kamadeva gave away the treatises on love, the club and all his vidyas to him with a delightful heart.

The ocean of milk gave him the precious gem and a gem-studded anklet. Himalaya gavethe ornaments and costumes.

Garuda gave him the peacock- his son. Aruna gave him the cock which could fight with its talons.

Parvati felt happy at this, smilingly. She delightfully gave him all the fortunes and the long life.

Laksmi gave her the divine riches and a pleasant garland. The goddess Savitri, getting pleased, bestowed on him all the siddhis and vidyas.

O Sage, the goddesses who were present there, gave him the appropriate presents. The Krttikas also gave him the suitable presents.

O Sage, great function was held there at that time. All those present there were quite happy.

At that point of time, the glorious Siva feeling delighted, spoke to the gods like Brahma and others.

Siva said, “O Brahma, O Visnu and other gods, listen to my words. I am extremely happy today. All of you can ask for a boon.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, listening to the words of Siva, Visnu and other gods feeling happy said to lord Mahadeva.”

The Gods said, “O Lord, let Tarakasura be killed by Kumara. This story has been created because of the same.

Therefore, all of us should proceed for getting the demon killed. You kindly command Kumara, to kill Tarakasura.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the prayer of the gods, the compassionate Siva, gave away his son Kartikeya, they command for the killing of Taraka.

At the command of Siva, Brahma, Visnu and other gods, collectively made Kartikeya to lead them who moved towards the mountain.

Coming out of the Kailasa mountain, with the permission of Visnu, Visvakarma built a huge and astonishing city.

Then Visvakarma built a divine and beautiful palace for the sake of Kartikeya. A beautiful lion-throne was placed therein.

Then the intelligent Visnu, held a function there with devotion. In the meantime, the gods, performed the abhiseka of Kartikeya, with sacred water of all the holy places.

Kartikeya was then lovingly given the costumes, ornaments, besides all the articles of daily use in the house and lodged him there. Thereafter the celebration was made.

Then Visnu made Kartikeya, the lord of the universe and performed abhiseka for him. The gods adored him.

Then Kartikeya, who resembled lord Siva- the eternal one, was adored by the gods who offered their salutation to him reciting the stotras.

Then Kartikeya was seated over the excellent lion-throne, looking resplendent, because he had became the lord of the universe and he was the preserver of the three worlds.

## Chapter 6 - Kumara’s astonishing performance

Brahma said, “O Narada, thereafter Kartikeya performed astonishing feats which bestows devotion. You listen to the same from me.

At that point of time, a Brahmana arrived there to take refuge with Kartikeya, for the performing of a yajna.

The Brahmana, reaching before Kartikeya, feeling happy, offered his salutation to him besides eulogising him and then revealing the purpose of his visit.

The Brahmana said, “O Lord Kumara, presently you are the lord of the entire universe. You kindly remove my suffering after listening to my words. I take refuge in you.

I began goat a sacrifice, the goat was loosened and it fled away.

I do not know, where has it gone? I made an extensive search for it, which was of noavail. In the absence of the goat my yajna is being disrupted.

O Lord, how can my yajna be disrupted when you are there. O Lord of the entire universe, thus thinking you better fulfil my desire.

O Son of Siva, O Lord, with whom should I take refuge, leaving you? You happen to be the leader of the universe and are served by all the gods.

You are the friend of the destitute, friend of your devotees, and are fit enough to be served in every way. You are Paramesvara, who is being eulogised by Brahma, Visnu and other gods.

You are the son of Parvati, Skanda, the sole destroyer of the enemies, the great soul, the lord who bestows his own self for the noble people, seeking refuge in you.

O Lord, beloved of the Brahmanas O Lord of illusion, I have arrived to take refuge with you. You kindly protect me. You are the lord of all. Brahma and all other gods adore and eulogise you. You possess illusion and incarnate on earth with your illusion alone.

You provide comforts to your devotees and are always engaged in their protection.

You are the life of your devotees, are the mine of all the virtues. You are beyond the Sattva, rajas and tamas gunas. You are dear to Siva, the form of Siva, the son of Siva, you are pleasant, you are great being the form of sat and cit. You are omniscient, destroyer of Tripura, the son of Siva, and are subservient to your devotees. You are lord of all, destroyer of those who are inimical to the noble people and you treat Siva as your preceptor. You are the leader of the universe, the lord, adorable by all the gods, dear to all, you kindly protect me.

You are terrific and awful for the enemies, you bestow welfare to your devotees, and provide comforts of all. I, therefore, bow in reverence at you both your feet. O Skanda, you listen to my prayer. You spread your devotion in the minds of the people.

O Skanda, in case you are the protector with excellent honour, what harm can anopponent do inspite of his being so strong and efficient and protected on either side? What harm the serpent Taksaka or even the carnivorous animal cause to such a person?

Even the preceptor of the gods, (Brhaspati) cannot eulogise you properly. Then, tell me, how can I pray at the dust of your lotus like feet.

O Lord of all, O Ocean of mercy, favourably inclined to your devotees, I happen to be your own servant. You can forgive a hundred sins of your own servant, or let, the leader of the ganas should forgive me. O Lord you are well aware of even the slightest devotional deed performed by anyone anywhere. You remove the distress of your devotees. O Lord, except you, there is no protector for me. Moreover there could hardly be any degraded person than myself.

O Lord, you are the one who bestows welfare on all. You destroy the sins of the age of Kali, the friend of Kubera, having a merciful heart. You have eighteen eyes and six heads. You kindly get my yajna completed.

You are the protector of all the three lokas. You are dear to those who take refuge in you, are protector of the yajnas and are destroyer of those who create obstructions.

You remove the obstructions of the noble people and can indulge in all types of creations. O Prince of Siva, you kindly have my yajna completed. Salutation to you.

O Skanda, you are the protector of all, you are omniscient, lord of all, Sarvesvara, you establish firmness in all and you feed and preserve all.

You are well-versed in the Vedas, as well as the music, you make all firm in their resolve. You are the god of gods and are the rescuer of the noble people.

O Son of Siva, O Son of Parvati, O Knowledgeable one, O Self illumining one, you are the meditator as well as the meditation. You are the father of the fathers and the source of the noble souls.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the words of the Brahmana, the son of Siva- the emperor of the gods deputed Virabahu in search of the goat.

At the command of Kartikeya, Virabahu, at once offering his salutation to his lord, left in search of the goat.

He searched for the goat in the entire universe but could not find the yajna goat but he came to know about the disturbance created by it.

Thereafter, he went to Vaikuntha, where the goat was found by Virabahu, with the sacrificial stake tied to its neck.

The hero Virabahu caught hold of the goat by its horns, dragged it and brought it quickly before Kumara, though it was bleating loudly.

Finding the goat there, Kartikeya- the creator of the universe, at once rode on it carrying the burden of the universe.

O Sage, the goat went round the universe in a moment and returned to the same place getting tired.

Kartikeya got down from the goat and occupied his seat. The goat was also seated there. Then the Brahmana Narada said to Kartikeya.” Narada said, “O God of gods, O Ocean of mercy, you give the goat back to me, to enable me to complete my yajna, with delight. You kindly be friendly with me.”

Kartikeya said, “O Brahmana, this goat is not worthy of sacrifice. You better go to your place. By my grace your entire yajna would be completed.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the word of the lord, the Brahmana, feeling pleased returned to his abode, delightfully, blessing Kartikeya.

## Chapter 7 - The starting of the war

Brahma said, “ Observing the performance of Kartikeya, Visnu and others felt re-assured, getting pleased.

Influenced with the lustre of Siva, making Kumara to lead, they while singing, dancing and jumping, moved on for the killing of Tarakasura.

Learning about the war preparations of the gods, Tarakasura- the valorous one, accompanied with a vast army, marched on to fight with the gods.

Finding Tarakasura moving with a vast army, the gods, got surprised uttering the lion’s roar.

Then at the inspiration of Siva, a divine voice was heard addressing the gods like Visnu and other gods.

The divine voice said, “O Gods, placing Kumara in the forefront, you get ready to fight a war. You will surely be victorious.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the divine voice, all the gods were delighted, and thundering like the great warriors, became fearless at that time.

The fearless gods, desirous of the war, placing Kumara in the forefront, reached the confluence of the earth and the ocean.

O Gods, on the one hand was Kumara Kartikeya having been surrounded by the gods, and on the other hand Tarakasura had arrived with his vast army.

The big drums were beaten which produced the sound like the thundering of the clouds, in the battlefield and by playing of the other war bands.

At that time other daityas also started thundering together with Tarakasura; with the sound produced with the marching of the demon army, the earth started shaking.

Hearing the sound, all the gods becoming fearless, became attentive to fight with the warriors of Taraka.

Then Indra the god of gods, made Kumara to mount over the elephant Airavata, surrounded by the Lokapalas and the gods, and asked him to move ahead.

At that point of time, the war drums, kettle drums, bheris turvas, lutes, flutes and cymbals were sounded, while Gandharvas sang the war songs.

Leaving aside the elephant Airavata, Kumara boarded a divine chariot studded with various types of gems.

Then the son of Siva, having seated in a divine chariot, was endowed with enormous qualities and was shining with great splendour. The fly-whisks were moved over him.

The chatra of Varuna, studded with various types of gems, was held over the head of Kumara, which was illumined with innumerable moons.

The immensely powerful Indra, desirous of waging the war, and other gods, together with their respective armies, were present there.

Thus both the god and the daitya with their respective army formations, took their respective positions.

Both the armies of the gods and the daityas with the desire to destroy the opponent armies, were being praised by the respective bards, looking fine.

In the battle ground of the terrific forest, the warriors of both the sides, started thundering against each other. This thundering sound was frightening for the cowards and pleasant for the great warriors.

In the meantime, the gods intoxicated with their strength, besides the daityas, were engaged for the killing of the opponent army.

A terrific war started between the gods and the demons as a result of which the earth was littered with the heads and the headless trunks.

Having been wounded and killed with the striking of the sharp weapons, hundreds and thousands of great warriors fell on the ground.

With the fall of the hard swords, the arms of some of the soldiers were cut off. Besides some of the heroic warriors of great honour lost their legs.

With the strike of the clubs and mudgaras all the limbs of some of the warriors were shattered. Some of them were bound with nooses. Some of them fell with the strikes of the spears.

The backs of some of the warriors, were injured with spears, double edged swords, as well as the goads. The severed heads of some of them fell on the ground.

Many of the headless trunks of the warriors, holding the swords in their hands were dancing and jumping in the battle ground.

Hundreds of streams of blood started flowing. Several of the goblins and the ghosts arrived there.

The male jackals and vixens, started eating flesh. The flocks of vultures arrived, besides the eagles and the crows started eating flesh of those who were dead in the battle ground.

In the meantime Tarakasura, followed by vast army, marched on to fight the gods.

Finding the arrival of the arrogant Tarakasura for the waging of the war, Indra and other gods also marched towards him. The warriors of both the sides rted thundering.

The destructive mutual fighting between the gods and the demons started, observing which the warriors were delighted, while the cowards were frightened.

The valorous Tarakasura was engaged in fight with Indra. Samhrada fought with Agni, and Yama with Jambha.

Lord Varuna fought with Nirtti and Bala Suvira- the king Pavaman fought with Vayu.

Sambhu, expert in war fought with Sesa, Kumbhasura fought with the moon.

The valorous Kunjara, who was well- versed in various types of wars, fought with Mihira with several of the divine weapons.

Thus the armies of the gods and the demons, fought the duel fights with the warriors of both sides.

At that point of time the immensely valorous gods as well as the demons, tried to overpower one another. O Sage, in the said war between the gods and the demons, the demons became invincible.

Desirous of overpowering the opponent, both the gods and the demons fought a tumultuous battle, which was quite pleasant for the brave warriors and awful for the cowards.

With the fall of the gods and the demons in the battle ground, the ground had become awful besides being terrific. For the noble people, the land became comfortable and for others it became difficult to pass.

## Chapter 8 - Battle between the gods and the demons

Brahma said, “O Dear Narada, thus I have narrated to you about the war between the armies of the gods and the demons.

In this destructive war the demon Tarakasura attacked Indra, the god of gods, with the Supreme Sakti weapon.

As a result of this, he at once fell down from his elephant Airavata, on the ground and was fainted. Then Devendra, the holder of Vajra felt extremely painful.

The daityas, who were valorous and well-versed in the warfare, defeated even the Lokapalas.

The other gods fighting with the demons, were also defeated by the latter. The gods then unable to bear his attack started fleeing from the battle ground.

The successful demons started roaring like the lion and created huge disturbance and uproar.

In the meantime, getting enraged, Virabhadra arrived there with his ganas and moved towards Tarakasura, who thought himself to be invincible.

Virabhadra who was born of the anger of - Siva, who was the chief of the ganas of Siva, pushing behinds the gods, came forward to have a fight with Tarakasura.

Then the ganas of Siva and the demons started fighting with one another.

The warriors well-versed in the warfare, hit and smashed one another with tridents, double edged swords, nooses, axes and sharp edged spikes.

At once Virabhadra wounded Tarakasura with his trident, who fell down fainted on ground very soon.

But great demon Tarakasura got up at once and attacked Virabhadra with his Sakti.

The immensely illustrious and valorous, Virabhadra shot a terrific arrow called Trisikha at Tarakasura.

Then Tarakasura, the lord of the demons and adorable by the valorous warriors, again shot a Sakti at Virabhadra in the battlefield.

In this way both of them (Virabhadra and Tarakasura) who were well trained in the warfare, kept on attacking each other for a long time.

Then both the warriors fought an awful battle, which made the hair of the people to stand at ends with excitement.

Then the great warriors sounded the military bands and drums, besides playing on the kettle drums, cymbals, patakas, ankusas and gomukhas etc.

Both of them were attacking each other, variously and fought forcefully like Mercury and the Mars.

Finding them so fighting, being dear to Siva, you went there and spoke to Virabhadra.”

Narada said, “O Virabhadra- the great warrior, you are the foremost of the ganas of Siva, therefore, you better remove yourself from the battle. It would not be proper for you to kill Tarakasura.”

Listening to your words thus spoken to Virabhadra, he who had been the foremost of the ganas of Siva, spoke to you with folded hands.”

Virabhadra said, “O Intelligent and excellent sage, you kindly listen to my words. I shall kill Tarakasura today itself. You better witness my prowess.

Such of the warriors who force their masters to reach the battlefield, are sinners are no better than the eunuchs. Such warriors are doomed in the battlefield.

They would go the way of the wicked. They would surely fall in the hell. You should not think Virabhadra to be such a deplorable person.

Such of the warriors who keep on fighting fearlessly even when their limbs and the weapons are shattered, they get praised in this as well as the future world and attain the excellent pleasures.

O Lord Visnu and other gods, you please listen to my words, I shall relive the earth of the burden of Tarakasura.”

Thus speaking and reciting the name of Siva in his mind, accompanied with the pramathas, Virabhadra kept on fighting with Tarakasura.

Accompanied with several warriors having three eyes each and mounted over the bulls, Virabhadra kept on fighting but looked graceful in the battle ground.

Hundreds of fearless Sivaganas creating thunderous sound, making Virabhadra to lead, them, started fighting with the demons.

The demon soldiers of Tarakasura also, started trampling upon the ganas of Virabhadra.

The ganas of Virabhadra fought with the valorous daityas again and again. The ganas of Siva who were well-versed in the use of arms, were victorious over the demons.

The demons after their getting defeated at the hands of the ganas of Siva, started fleeing from the battlefield.

Then Tarakasura finding that his warriors were deserting the battlefield, was immensely enraged and he rushed towards the Sivaganas for the purpose of killing them.

Soon he developed ten thousand arms, mounting over a lion he killed several of the gods and their ganas.

Virabhadra- the foremost of the ganas of Siva, witnessed the performance of Tarakasura and he felt enraged, intending to kill him (Virabhadra).

Virabhadra, devoting his mind over the lotus like feet of Siva and holding the weapon named Trisikha, he marched forward. At that point of time all the directions were illumined with his lustre.

In the meantime the lord, desirous of witnessing a great fun, removed Virabhadra and others, at once from the battle ground.

At his command, Virabahu was removed from the battlefield, while Tarakasura, the leader of the demons was enraged.

Then demon who was expert in various weapons, tortured the gods variously with his prowess, raining the arrows on them.

Thus Tarakasura, the best among the warriors and protector of the demons, waging a great war, became out of control of the gods.

Finding the gods so frightened and the killing of the god at the hands of the demons, lord Visnu, getting enraged, got ready to fight with the demon king.

Then Visnu, holding his attributes like the Sudarsana-cakra, Saranga-bow, and other weapons, marched on for the killing of the demon.

O Sage, in full view of all the gods, an exciting battle was fought between Visnu and Tarakasura.

Visnu then attacked the demon with the club, but the valorous Tarakasura cut the club in two pieces, with his Trisikha weapon.

Then lord Visnu, who could make the gods fearless, getting enraged, shot the arrows at the demons from his Saranga bow.

Then the demon who always killed the enemy warriors, cut off the arrows of Visnu with the arrows shot by him.

Thereafter Tarakasura, attacked Visnu with his Sakti, as a result of which Hari was fainted and fell down on the ground.

He regained consciousness in a moment and created a lion’s roar and picked up the cakra issuing the fire flames.

He shot the cakra at the demon chief, who was fainted and fell down on the ground.

The immensely valorous demon king Tarakasura, got up again and he cut off the cakra with his Sakti.

Then he shot the same Sakti at Visnu, who made it infructuous with his sword called Nandaka.

O Sage, in this way, both the warriors, with the strength of gods and the demons, kept on fighting for long.

## Chapter 9 - Fight between Tarakasura and the gods

Brahma said, “O God of gods, O Guha (Kartikeya), O Son of Siva, O Son of Parvati, the useless fight between Visnu and Tarakasura, did not look nice.

Because the most powerful Tarakasura was not at all destined to be killed at the hands of Visnu. This is the truth which is being revealed by me.

O Son of Parvati, no one else except you, can kill him. O Great lord, therefore you accept my words.

O Son of Siva, O scorcher of the enemies, you have been born of Siva, simply for the killing of Tarakasura. Therefore, you at once get ready for the killing of Tarakasura.

O Valorous one, you kindly serve the gods suffering in the battlefield. You are neither a child nor a young boy, you are actually the lord yourself.

Look at Visnu, Indra, other gods and ganas who are agitated and feeling distressed. Slay this great demon and make happy the three worlds.

He, because of the strength of his tapas, has already conquered Indra- the god of gods, besides the Lokapalas and he has also humiliated lord Visnu.

The wicked demon has already conquered all the three lokas. Presently, the gods have fought with him again, in order to support you.

Therefore, you better kill this sinful person. O Son of Siva, none else except you, can kill him because of the boon granted by me to him.

Thus listening to my words, Kumara, the son of Siva, said, “All right, I shall do so.”

Then Kumara, the son of Siva, the great lord, having resolved for the killing of the demon, descended from the plane and stood over the ground.

The immensely valorous son of Siva, resplendent like the comet illumining with his own lustre, holding Sakti in his hands, running on foot appeared extremely graceful.

Tarakasura, finding Kumara- the in comprehensive six headed deity coming forward, looking fierce but imaginated, spoke to the gods decisively, “O this child will indeed slay the enemies.

I shall fight with him alive, and thereafter, I shall kill all the warriors, the gams of Siva, the gods, and the Lokapalas.”

Thus speaking, the valorous Tarakasura aiming at Kumara holding an astonishing type of Sakti, went to fight with him informing the gods.”

Tarakasura said, “Why have you produced Kumara before me? O Gods, you are shameless, particularly Indra and Visnu.

Even earlier both of them had acted against the Vedas, which I am going to reveal before you. You please listen to me.

O Gods, out of all of you, Visnu is much more deceitful. He is a culprit and is senseless. In earlier times had made Bali captive deceitfully.

Again he, in utter disregard to the Vedic provisions, had cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha cunningly.

At the time of the consumption of the nectar by the gods as well as the demons, he, by taking to the form of Mohini, denounced the path of the Vedas.

Then he incarnating as Rama, killed a woman named Tadaka and then killed innocent and sinless Bali. Then he killed Ravana who was a Brahmana and the son of Visrava. His this action was also against the polity as well as the Vedic traditions.

Behaving in a sinful manner, he exiled his own chaste and sinful wife Sita. Thus for his own selfish ends, he discarded the path of the Vedas.

In his sixth incarnation of Parasurama, he cut off the head of his own mother and humiliated, the son of his own preceptor.

Incarnating as Krsna, he enjoyed other’s wives, desecrating them. Leaving the path of the Vedas he married himself a number of times.

Then in the ninth incarnation of Buddha, he was opposing the path of the Vedas, and propounded the religion of atheists.

Thus he, disowning the path of the Vedas, committed a sin. How could he be victorious in the battles and how could he be adorable among the religious people?

Indra the elder-brother of Visnu, is a grave sinner. He committed several sins for his selfish ends.

To meet his own selfish ends, he destroyed the conception of Diti. He misbehaved with the wife of Gautama and killed Vrtra- the son of a Brahmana.

A Brahmana, named Visvarupa, who was the nephew of his preceptor Brhaspati, was beheaded by him, violating the path of the Vedas.

By repeating many sins one after the other, both Indra and Visnu, have particularly been deprived of the lustre and prowess.

Therefore you cannot be victorious on the basis of their strength. You have arrived here foolishly in order to lay down your lives.

Both of them are selfish. O gods, all the efforts without dharma become infructuous.

Both of them are impudent fellows and have placed an innocent child before me. In case I kill this child, then they both would earn the relative sin.

But let the child move away from this place in order to save his own life.” Thus pointing out to Visnu and Indra, he spoke to Virabhadra.

“In earlier times, you had also killed a large number of Brahmanas in the yajna ofDaksa Prajapati. O Sinless one, I shall make you reap the fruit of the same today.”

Brahma said, “Thus denouncing both Indra and Visnu, Tarakasura who was well-versed in the warfare, having lost all his merits, held an astonishing type of Sakti in his hand.

Then finding that Tarakasura was proceeding towards Kumara, Indra who was first standing behind Kumara, shot his Vajra at Tarakasura.

Then Tarakasura, who had been deprived of his strength because of his denouncement of the gods, fell on the ground getting shattered, with the striking of the Vajra, in a moment.

The demon then got up and shooting a Sakti at Indra, he made him fall from the elephant over the ground.

With the falling of Indra over the ground, huge disturbance was created in the enemies of the gods and they suffered mental pain.

At that point of time, the performance of Tarakasura, which was the cause of his destruction, was against dharma. You listen the relevant details from me.

He trampled over Indra, who had fallen over the ground and snatching the Vajra from Indra’s hand Tarakasura struck him with it.

Finding Indra, having been thus humiliated, Visnu, attached Tarakasura with his cakra.

With the strike of cakra Tarakasura, fell down on the ground. He got up again and then attacked Visnu with his Sakti.

With the attack of Sakti, Visnu fell down unconscious on the. ground. A terrible uproar was created at that time.

Visnu got up again in a moment, but in the meantime Virabhadra confronted Tarakasura. The glorious Virabhadra then attacked Tarakasura, with his trident with all his force.

Tarakasura, who was the lord of all the demons, in anger shot a sakti at the chest of Virabhadra.

With the attack of that enraged Sakti, Virabhadra fell down on the ground, for a moment and fainted.

All the gods with their ganas, Gandharvas, Nagas and Raksasas, created uproars and cries again and again.

Then Virabhadra, who was inimical to the opponents, got up after a moment like lightening and appeared graceful holding a trident in his hand.

The trident had a halo around like that of the sun, the moon and the fire, with its brilliance it lighted all the quarters and caused terror even in the hearts of the brave people. It had the deadly splendour.

When the powerful Virabhadra was about to strike the trident, he was prevented from doing so by Kumara.

## Chapter 10 - Killing of Tarakasura

Brahma said, “While stopping Virabhadra from fighting, then Kumara getting desirous of the killing of Taraka who was intending to kill his enemies, devoted his mind at lotus like feet of Siva.

On the other hand Kartikeya- the valorous one, having been surrounded by the huge army, getting enraged started thundering.

All the gods then shouted the slogans of victory, while the great sages, praised him with various speeches.

At that point of time, Tarakasura, who frightened all the living beings, started fighting with Kartikeya, an unbearable battle.

O Sage, both the warriors started fighting carrying the weapons in their hands. For the on-lookers, the battle was quite astonishing.

Both of them having been equipped with all the resources and wounded with the Saktis and other weapons, cheating each other, kept on fighting like the two lions.

While fighting, they hit each other’s spears taking recourse to mantras, Vaitalikas, Khecharkas, Praptikas and others.

Using these mantras the great warriors, possessed the magical powers. They fought with each other wonderfully well, making use of their entire strength and exploits.

With the desire of killing each other, using their entire strength, they skilled in battle, were shooting spears at each other.

They were fighting to cut or hit each other’s head, neck, thighs, knees, hips, heart, chest and the back.

Both of them, who were well-versed in fighting several types of battle, shouting aloud, started jumping.

While observing the battle, all the gods, Gandharvas, Kinnaras and others said to one another, “Who would win?”

At that point of time a divine voice from the sky was heard saying, “In this battle Tarakasura is sure to be killed at the hands of Kartikeya.

O gods, you be comfortable. Have no worry. For your sake, Siva himself is standing here in the form of his son.”

Listening to the auspicious divine voice, Kumara, who was surrounded by the pramathas got ready to kill Tarakasura.

Then the long armed Kumara, getting enraged, forcefully attacked the demon at his chest with a Sakti.

In utter disregard of this attack, the leading demon Tarakasura also hit a Sakti (spear) at Kumara.

With the strike of the spear, the son of Siva, fell fainted. In a moment, he got up again, with the prayer of the sages.

Then Kumara, who had been intoxicated like a lion, with the intention of killing Tarakasura, attacked the demon with a spear.

Thus Kumara who had been well-versed in the warfare with spears, kept on fighting with the demon for long.

Both of them had plenty of practice to their credit, therefore for the purpose of overpowering each other they were moving on foot.

They used various types of methods for the killing of each other. Then making several (deceitful) moves for killing each other, they fought thundering at the same time.

All the gods, Gandharvas, Kumaras and others started watching they war and feeling surprised the stood there silently.

The wind then stopped blowing, the sun lost its lustre, the earth started shaking with the forests and hills.

At that point of time, Himalaya and all other mountains, having been filled with affection, reached there at the place of Kumara.

Then Kumara, the son of Girija, finding them all extremely terrified, spoke enlightening them thereby.

Kumara said, “O Immensely fortunate mountains, have no worry at all. Today in your full view, I am going to kill this wicked demon.”

Thus assuring the mountains and the gods, Kumara bowed in reverence to Girija and Siva and held a powerful Sakti in his hands.

With the intention of killing Tarakasura, holding a Sakti in his hands, the powerful and the great lord Kumara looked graceful. Then Kumara, possessing the lustre of Siva, shot the Sakti over Tarakasura who had been the cause of the trouble for the world.

With the attack of that Sakti, Tarakasura, the lord of the demon army, was at once shattered and fell down on the ground.

With the attack of Kumara, Tarakasura, in full view of all, was wounded. Finding that the powerful Tarakasura, was lying wounded in the battle ground, Kumara did not attack him further.

With the defeat of the valorous Tarakasura, the gods killed several of the demons.

Getting frightened some of the asuras folded their hands (begging forgiveness), the limbs of many of them were severed, while many of them were killed.

Some of them shrieking "O save O save" with palms joined in reverence sought refuge in Kumara.

Some of them were killed Many of them fled away. The fleeing demons were belaboured by the gods.

Thousands of demons moved to Patala with the desire of remaining alive. While fleeing, they lost all hope and were distressed.

O Sage, the entire demon army was destroyed. No demon moved there for the fear of gods.

With the death of the wicked demon, the entire world became free from danger. All the gods became comfortable.

Thus at the victory of Kumara, all the gods were filled with joy and the three worlds were filled with pleasure.

Lord Kartikeya was victorious. Hearing this lord Siva, together with his spouse Parvati reached there.

Then Parvati, having been filled with affection, took Kumara in her lap and lovingly kissed him.

Himalaya also reached there surrounded by his sons and their kiths and kins and he adored Siva- Siva besides Kartikeya and his ganas.

All the divine ganas, the sages, siddhas, and the bards, offered prayers to Siva, Parvati, Kumara- son of Siva, and the ganas known as Tusita.
