Then the gods showered enough of flowers over them. The Gandharvas sang the songs, while the apsaras started dancing.

The musical instruments were specially played upon at that time. Frequent shouts of victory and salutation were raised.

Visnu, who was with me, also felt pleased. He too eulogised Siva with respect, besides Parvati and Kumara.

Keeping in front, Brahma, Indra and other gods, performed his arati lovingly, followed by the sages, who also did so.

Then there was jubilation with the playing of the vocal and instrumental music, besides the chanting of the Vedas as well as Kirtana.

The lord of the universe was eulogised, O Sage, by the delighted gods and ganas with the use of vocal an instrumental music.

Then lord Siva with Parvati, having been eulogised by all the gods, returned to their mountain abode, surrounded by his ganas.

## Chapter 11 - Kumara's victory and the killing of Bana and Pralamba

Brahma said, “O Sage, in the mean time the mountain Kraunca, having been tortured by Banasura arrived there to take refuge with Kumara.

Banasura having the strength of the ten crores of warriors, had troubled the mountain Kraunca- the maximum. Then Kraunca fleeing from the battle field rushed to Kumara, for his rescue. But he could not bear the lustre of Kumara.

He bowed in reverence at the feet of Kumara and started eulogizing him with devotion.”

Kraunca said, “O Kumara, O Skanda, O Lord of the gods and the destroyer of Tarakasura, I have rushed here to take refuge with you having been tortured by Banasura. O Lord of gods, you kindly be merciful on me and protect me.

O Kartikeya, he has fled away while fighting with you. O Compassionate lord. He is troubling me now.

O Lord, having been troubled by him and feeling miserable, I have arrived here to take refuge with you. O Lord be merciful on me.

O Fortunate one, you are self illumining, you kindly make me comfortable, after killing Banasura. You are the protector of the gods and the destroyer of the demons.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the prayer of Kraunca, Kartikeya, the protector of his devotees, carrying his astonishing Sakti in his hand, devoting his mind to Siva, (thought of waging the war).

Then the son of Siva, shot the Sakti over Banasura creating enormous sound, as a result of which the sky with all the ten directions started burning, creating the thundering sound.

O Sage, the Sakti shot by Kumara, reducing Banasura and his army to ashes in a moment, it then returned to Kumara.

Kumara then said to the excellent Kraunca, “Now you should go back to your home fearlessly, because the demon has been destroyed with his army.”

Listening to the words of Kumara, the excellent mountain Kraunca, feeling pleased, offering prayer to Kumara, (Guha) returned to his home peacefully.

Then Kumara, feeling pleased, consecrated three Sivalingas, which remove the sins.

They were known by the names of Pratijnesvara, Kapalesvara and Kumaresvara. These lingas bestow all types of success.

Then Guha (Kumara) the lord of all, consecrated a linga known as Stambhesvara, near the victory pillar.

Thereafter, Visnu and other gods, established a linga of Siva, collectively.

All of these lingas became exceedingly glorious, which fulfil all the desired and bestow salvation to the devotees.

Then all the gods delightfully proceeded towards Kailasa making Kumara as the leader.

At the same time Kumuda, the son of Sesanaga having been troubled by the demons, arrived to take refuge with Kumara.

The demon Pralamba who was the follower of Bana, had fled away from the same war and had started disturbance at the place of Kumuda.

Kumuda was the son of the great serpent Sesa, who arrived to take refuge with Kumara, the son of Girija and was offering prayer there.

Kumuda said, “O God of gods, O the best son of Mahadeva, O Great lord, I have arrived here to seek refuge from you, having been tortured from Pralambasura.

O Skanda, O Kumara, O Lord of the gods, O Enemy of Tarakasura, I have arrived here having been tortured by Pralamba, you kindly protect me.

You are friendly to the distressed, ocean of mercy, well-disposed towards the devotees, award punishment to the wicked persons. You protect those, who take refuge with you and are the protection of the noble people.”

Thus offering his prayer to Kumara, Kumuda prayed to him for the killing of Pralamba. Then Kumara, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, held his Sakti in his hand.

Then Kumar, was created thundering sound and all the ten directions, together with the sky started burning.

Pralambasura together with his ten thousand army was reduced to ashes in a moment, the Sakti returned to Kumara, without any obstruction whatsoever.

Then Kumara said to Kumuda- the son of the Naga, “Now you can go back fearlessly to your abode. The powerful demon has been killed already by me.”

Listening to the words of Kumara, then Kumuda the son of Nagaraja, delightfully, bowed in reverence to Kumara and the eulogising him, he returned to his abode.

O Sage, the killing of Tarakasura, and the victory of Kumara, has been narrated by me to you.

This is the divine story, which destroys the sins of the people and bestows all the desires. It is quite graceful and it also confers fame, long life, devotion as well as salvation.

The people who narrate the divine story of Kumara they become illustrious and fortunate and ultimately achieve Sivaloka.

A person, who, having been filled with devotion and faith, listens to the glory of the lord, he enjoying all the pleasures in this world, and ultimately achieves salvation.

## Chapter 12 - The story of Siva, Parvati and Kartikeya

Brahma said, “Finding Taraka having been killed, Visnu and all other gods besides the Rsis felt pleased and then started eulogising with devotion to the son of Siva.”

The gods said, “O Form of welfare, O Friend of the universe, salutation to you. Salutation to you, O Purifier of the universe.

Salutation to you having killed the chief of the demons. O Lord, salutation to the killer of the demon Bana. Salutation to the killer of Pralamba. Salutation to you possessing the auspicious features. Salutation to you, O Son of Siva.

You alone are the creator, sustainer and destroyer of the universe, you having been bom of the fire-god, be pleased with us. Your cosmic form compares with the universe. You are bom of fire, be pleased with us. O Son of Siva, you are friendly to the distressed, be pleased with us.

O Lord, you are the protector of the gods. O Lord, you protect us always. O merciful, you are the protector of gods, be pleased with us.

After the destruction of the demon Taraka together with his army, the gods have been freed from the sufferings by you. O Merciful one, be pleased.

Brahma said, “O Sage, when Kumara was so eulogised by Visnu and other gods, lord Kumara bestowed fresh boons on them, respectively.

Thereafter, finding the mountains lined up while praising, the son of Siva, spoke to them pronouncing also the boons on them.

Skanda said, “All the mountains shall be respected by the ascetics, the people engaged in rituals besides the people with wisdom.

O Mountains, all of you shall enjoy the privileged position like the Sivalinga. These are my words and there is no doubt about it.

Himalaya, who is my maternal grandfather, would bestow the reward to the ascetics for their tapas.”

The gods said, “Thus killing Tarakasura, bestowing the boons, you have made all the mobiles and immobiles comfortable on earth.

Now you can go back to the abode of your parents and can meet them.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, Visnu and all other gods, receiving permission, enormously celebrating the occasion, proceeded towards the Kailasa mountain.

As soon as Kumara was about to move towards Kailasa, the slogans of victory were shouted besides the cries of victory to Kumara.

Then Kumara boarded the gem-studded plane, which was an excellent one decorated from all the four sides.

Both myself and Visnu, moved the fly-whisks, holding them carefully in our hands.

Indra and all other gods started appropriately serving Kumara and moved around him with pleasure.

Shouting for the victory of Siva, all of them reached the abode of the lord of Kailasa raising auspicious sound.

Finding Siva and Parvati there, Visnu and all other gods offered their salutation to the lord with folded hands, lowering their heads.

The humble Kumara, descended from the plane, delightfully and bowed in reverence to Siva and Parvati- the mother of the universe who were seated over the lion- throne.

O Narada, looking at Kumara- her son, who was dear to her than her life, both Siva and Parvati were delighted.

Then Siva the great lord, lifted him up and carried him in his lap and lovingly smelt his head and touched him with his hand.

Then feeling delighted, Siva kissed the face of Kumara- the enemy of Tarakasura.

Then Parvati took him in her lap and smelling his head kissed his face.

O Narada, both the husband and wife, displaying the worldly traditions felt lovingly attracted towards him. At that point of time several types of celebrations were held in the abodes of Siva. The words of victory and salutations were heard from all the sides.

O Sage, thereafter, all the gods like Visnu and others, besides the sages, eulogised Kumara, bowing in reverence to Siva as well.”

The gods said, “O Mahadeva, the god of gods, you provide protection to your devotees, O Compassionate one, O Merciful one, salutation to you.

O Mahadeva, O Friend of the distressed, O Great lord, your illusion, which bestows welfare to all is really astonishing.

O Lord, we are ignorant, devoid of wisdom, and are unaware of the method of invoking you.

You retain the water of the Ganga with you, you are the support of everyone. You possess three attributes, lord of the three gods, therefore salutation to Siva.

O Bull-bannered one, O Mahesa, O Lord of the ganas, O Lord of all, you are the lord of the three worlds, Salutation to you.

O Lord, you are the destroyer of all the worlds, you are the protector, and the creator of the world, you are the lord of the three gunas, besides being eternal, salutation to you.

You are lonely and free from attachment, the supreme lord, Siva, the Supreme soul, spotless, the one beyond the world of matter and indestructible.

You are the form of time-holding a staff. You are referred to in the Vedic hymns, besides having hundreds of tongues, salutation to you.

The past, present and future, the mobiles and immobiles, O Lord have all emerged from your body.

O Lord, O Master, be pleased with us and protect us. O Paramesvara, we have taken refuge under you for all purposes.

O Blue necked Nilakantha, Rudra, you are with and without attributes, having all the forms of the world, salutation to you.

O Siva, O Nilakantha, you apply over your body the ashes from the pyres, you are eternal, Nilasikhanda and Srikantha, salutation to you.

You are adorable by all, humble and disciplined, Sarva and the one who is worshipped by all.

You are Brahma of all the gods, Nilalohita, out of Rudras, the soul of all the living beings. The followers of the Sankhya doctrine conceives you as Purus a.

You are Sumeru among the mountains, the moon out of the constellations, Vasistha among the Rsis, and Indra among the gods.

You pervade as Omkara in the Vedas, O Mahesvara, you protect us. You satisfy all the living beings for their welfare.

You are the witness of all the good and bad, O Supreme one, O Mahesvara, O Lord of the gods, let us expand, we are quite obedient to you.

O God of gods, you have thousands of crores of forms, we are unable to conceive about your end or limitations. Salutation to you.”

Brahma said, “In this way Visnu and other gods bowed in reverence to Siva again and again, who stood up with Skanda leading them in the forefront.

The self illumining lord Siva, who is quite compassionate, thus listening to the prayer of the gods, was pleased.

Then Siva, the great Isan, the friend of distressed, the goal of the noble people, felt delighted and spoke to Visnu and other important gods.”

Siva said, “O Visnu, O Brahma, O gods, listen to my words, attentively I am merciful. I shall protect all the gods by all means.

The lord of the three worlds is the destroyer of the wicked. He is well-disposed towards his devotees. He is the creator, preserver and the destroyer of all but is still free from all the blemish.

O Excellent gods, whenever you are placed in a miserable condition, you shall worship me for your welfare.”

Brahma said, “When so commanded by the lord, Visnu and other gods, besides the sages, bowed in reverence to Siva, Parvati and Kumara, delightfully and then returned to their respective abodes, with immense delight singing the pleasant glory of Siva, Parvati and their son.

Siva and Parvati stayed over the mountain quite happily, besides the ganas and Kumara. Lord Siva was immensely delighted.

In this way, O Sage, I have narrated to you the divine story of Kumara and Siva has been narrated to you. What else do you want to listen from me?”

## Chapter 13 - Birth of Ganesa

Suta said, “Listening to the astonishing type of the story of the enemy of Tarakasura, Narada delightfully asked Brahma.”

Narada said, “O Prajapati, O God of gods, well-versed in the Siva-tattva, I have listened to the story of Kartikeya, which is far better than the nectar.

Now I would like to listen to the story of the birth of Ganesa, who bestows welfare even to the welfare.”

Suta said, “Listening to these words of Narada, the delightful Brahma, devoting his mind at Siva’s feet said.”

Brahma said, “Because of the difference in the kalpas, there are several stories of the birth of Ganesa. Once, because of Saturn’s casting his gaze over Ganesa, the latter’s head was cut off and it was replaced with the head of an elephant.

Presently, the story of the birth of Ganesa in the Sveta kalpa is being narrated, wherein, the compassionate Siva, had himself cut off his head.

O Sage, there should be no doubt about the performance of Siva, the creator of the universe. The same Siva inspite of his being with and without attributes, happens to be the lord of all.

O Excellent sage, because of his divine sport there is the creation, preservation and the destruction in the world. You listen to the rest.

Long time after the marriage of Siva and his proceeding to Kailasa, Ganesa was born

Once the maids of Parvati, known as Jaya and Vijaya, entered into consultations with Parvati.

“The ganas of Siva, are always obedient to him, including Nandi, Bhrngi and others.  
The number of Pramathas is beyond counting, but none of them belongs to us. They also guard the gate at the command of Siva.  
They are ours no doubt, but we are not mentally akin to them. O Auspicious one, you should with the permission of Siva, patronise some one as your own.”

Brahma said, “The words spoken by the maids, were taken to be favourable by Parvati and started making efforts to materialise the proposal.

After sometime, Parvati was taking bath. Then Siva entered the house scolding Nandi.

When the mother of the world found Siva arriving, she felt shy and got up.

She was filled with curiosity and wonder, and she realised the proposal of her maid to be quite practicable.

Thus after the lapse of sometime, Paramesvari Siva thought in her mind.

“I should have a servant exclusive to myself, who should be extremely competent and efficient and who should not move even slightly, without my command.”

Thus thinking, she took some dirt out of her body and made a human figure

It was free of all the defects. All the limbs of the body were made beautiful and were of big size. It looked graceful and was immensely valorous.

It was clad with the best of costumes and adorned with the best of ornaments. She then pronounced the best of blessings for him

Then she said to him, “You are my son, you belong to me, there is no one else who could be called as mine, except you.” At these words of Parvati, the person, bowed in reverence to Parvati and praised her.

Ganesa said, “What is your task for me today, which should be performed by me at your command?” When he so asked Parvati, she replied.

Parvati said, “O Son, you listen to my words. You function as my gate-keeper today. You are my son. No one else, except you, belongs to me.

O Son, no one should enter my house without my command, even forcibly. I have spoken truthfully to you.”

Brahma said, “O Sage, thus speaking she gave him a strong staff. She got pleased at his beautiful form.

She kissed his face lovingly, embracing him she gave him a staff to be held by him in his hand and then placed him on duty at the gate to guard it.

O Dear one, the valorous Ganesa, holding a staff in his hand, was guarding the gate at the instance of Parvati.

Placing her son Ganesa, on duty at the gate, Parvati was taking bath with her maid.

At the same time, Siva, who was quite curious and well-versed in the divine sports, reached the gate.

Then Ganesa, without recognising Siva, said to him, “O Deva, you cannot enter the house without the permission of my mother.

My mother is taking her bath inside. Where are you going? You better leave this place at once.” Thus speaking, he raised the danda to stop the entry of Siva into the house.

Looking at him Siva said, “O Fool, whom are you obstructing? O Evil minded one, don’t you know me? I am Siva in reality.”

Then Ganesa, struck Siva with his danda. Then Siva who was well-versed in divine sports, said to the boy.

Siva said, “You are a fool Don’t you know me? I am Siva, the husband of Girija. O Boy, I am entering my own house. Why do you prevent me from doing so?

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, when Siva again tried to enter his house he was again beaten by Ganesa with the danda.

Then getting enraged, Siva commanded his ganas, “Who is he? What does he want to do? O Ganas, you look at him.”

Thus speaking Siva, following the worldly traditions and who performed several types of astonishing sports, sat outside the house getting annoyed.

## Chapter 14 - Controversy with the ganas

Brahma said, “At the command of Siva, the ganas said to the gatekeeper Ganesa.

Siva ganas said, “Who are you? Where from have you arrived? What do you want to do? You go away leaving this place, in case you are interested in remaining alive.”

Brahma said, “Listening to these words, the ganas of Siva, the son of Girija holding a fearless staff in his hand, spoke to the gatekeepers.

Ganesa said, “Who are you? Where from have you come? You are quite beautiful. Then why are you standing for picking up a fight? You leave this place.

Brahma said, “Thus listening to his words of Ganesa, the Siva ganas, getting free from pride, said.

The courtiers of Siva, after consulting among, themselves and getting enraged, said to Ganesa.

Siva’s ganas said, “We are the ganas of Siva, serving as the gatekeepers here, we have, at the command of Siva arrived here to remove you from this place.

We are not killing you treating you also to be a gana. Otherwise we would have killed you. You clear off from this place of your own. Why do you want to kill yourself?”

Brahma said, “Inspite of these words of the ganas of Siva, Ganesa, the son of Girija, admonished the ganas of Siva and stood there fearlessly at the gate.

All the Sivaganas then listening to his words, again went to Siva and conveyed the news to him.

O Sage, Siva, who is always engaged in the astonishing sports, hearing the words of Sivaganas scolding them spoke to them according to the worldly tradition.”

Siva said, “Who is he? The wicked one speaks like an enemy. What will the evil- minded one speak? Surely, he is desirous of his death.

Remove this new gatekeeper. You are conveying his news to me like eunuch's.”

Listening to the words of their master who is engaged in the several types of divine sports, they again went to the gate and spoke to gatekeeper.

Sivaganas said, “O Gatekeeper, who are you? How are you guarding this place, Who has put you on duty here? How can you remain alive ignoring us?

All of us are the gatekeepers. What are you doing, sitting here. Achieving the lion throne, how can a jackal, conceive of his welfare.

O Fool, you keep on thundering till such time, you have not witnessed the prowess of the ganas of Siva. You will meet your death soon after your having an experience of the same.

Thus listening to them and getting enraged, holding the danda in his hands, he started beating those who uttered foul words.

The fearless son of Parvati, admonishing the powerful ganas of Siva said to them.

The son of Siva said, “Keep yourself away from this place, otherwise I shall have to display my great prowess, by which you will the made a laughing stock.”

Listening to these words of the son of Girija, the Sivaganas, spoke among themselves.

Sivaganas said, “What should be done? Where should we go? What shall he do further? We have to save the bonds of decency, otherwise, what shall he think?”

Brahma said, “The Sivaganas, then went to Siva who was resting at a place a kosa away from his abode and said to him.

Then Siva, holding a trident in his hand, smilingly said to adorable and valorous ganas.

Siva said, “O ganas, you are eunuchs. You claim to be heroes but are never so. You are unfit to stand before me and speak. In case he has taunted you only, he would repeat in the same way.

Go and beat him. some one among you could perhaps be able to do so. Why should I speak more? He must be driven away.”

Brahma said, “O Great sage, when the ganas of Siva, were so rebuked by him, they went back and spoke to him (Ganesa).

Siva’s ganas said, “O Boy, why do you talk so arrogantly? You leave this place, otherwise your death is certain.”

Brahma said, “On hearing the words of the obedient ganas of Siva, Ganesa, the son of Parvati thought, “What should I do?” Thus thinking, he felt painful.

In the meantime the goddess overheard, the quarrel between the ganas and Ganesa who deputed her maid to find out what was happening at the gate.

The maid understood the situation in a moment and feeling delighted, went back to Siva.

O Sage, whatever the maid had observed at the gate, she returned and conveyed the same to Parvati.

The maid said, “O Mahesvari, our (Jana, standing at the gate, had rebuked the powerful ganas of Siva.

It would not be proper in case Siva and his ganas force their entry into the house without permission. It will not be good for you.

He has done well by not allowing their entry into the house, inspite of his facing the humiliation, which is quite painful.

Presently both the sides are engaged in the verbal duel and by so doing, it is evident that no one would be able to enter inside.

O Parvati, they can come in only by defeating him in the verbal duel, otherwise they would not be able to enter the house by any means.

Though, by rebuking this boy, all of them have rebuked us, still O Goddess, you should not lose your prestige.

O Chaste lady, all of them are now subservient to you like a monkey. How could they be arrogant? They would move according to your wishes.”

Brahma said, “Surprisingly, as per the desire of Siva, Parvati stood there for sometime. Feeling arrogant, then Parvati thought in her mind.

Parvati thought, “My son has not delayed for a while, when these people have started using the force. Now my humility would be of what use?

Whatever has been destined to happen let it happen, but no adversity would happen.” Thus thinking Parvati sent her maid to that place, who reaching there conveyed the words of Girija to Ganesa.

“O Noble one, you have done well by preventing their forced entry. What are these ganas before you. They can’t conquer you.

Irrespective of the right or wrong, you have to do your duty. You don’t have to be inimical inspite of your being victorious.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of his mother and her maid, the strength and wisdom of Ganesa were increased, besides he felt delighted.

Wearing a turban and girding his loins, pathing his chest and the thighs, he spoke to the ganas fearlessly.”

Ganesa said, “I am the son of Parvati, and you happen to be the ganas of Siva. Both of us are equals. You can do whatever you deem fit.

You are a gatekeeper and so am I. You are attentive and so am I, standing here.

You can obey the command of Siva, when you stand here.

Presently, I am obeying this command of the goddess Siva. O Valorous warriors, I speak out truthfully that I have taken a right decision.

Therefore, O all the Sivaganas, should respect my words. You cannot enter the house by force or by humility.”

Brahma said, “Hearing the words spoken by the son of Parvati, the Sivaganas then went back to Siva and offering their salutation to him, they quietly stood there before him.

Standing there, they conveyed the astonishing news to him. Then lowering their heads and with folded hands. They stood there while praising the lord.

Listening to the news, conveyed to Siva by his ganas, the lord following the worldly practices, said to them.

Siva said, “O Ganas, (under these circumstances) the waging of the war would not be proper. You are my ganas and he happens to be the gana of Parvati.

In case of our requesting him (in any form) then it would create a deplorable situation in the world and people would say that Siva is subservient to his wife.

You better indulge in the practice of tit for tat. You should behave with him in the same way as he does to you. What type of a prowess can a lonely child display before you?

You being my ganas are quite competent in the battle-field. How could my ganas be defeated in the battle?

A woman should not be obdurate particularly with her husband. Parvati will surely have to reap the reward of her actions.

Therefore, O my brave men, listen to my words attentively. The war has to be fought by all means. Whatever is destined let it happen.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, O Brahmana, thus speaking, Siva who had been well-versed in divine sports, became silent thinking about the ways of the world.

## Chapter 15 - Ganesa’s battle with Sivaganas

Brahma said, “At these words of Siva, his ganas, went to the abode of the lord, for the purpose of waging the war.

Ganesa also found that the ganas of Siva were arriving for the purpose of waging a war then he spoke.

Ganesa said, “You come here obeying the command of Siva. But I am the lonely boy obeying the command of Siva (Parvati).

Still you witness the prowess of the ganas of Siva, as well as that of mine. You also witness the war between the side of Bhavamas well as Siva, in which there is a valorous boy on the one side and on the other side are the great warriors like you well-versed in warfare, having fought such battles several times in the past.

I am of course a boy, who never fought a battle earlier, but have to do so now. Still let Siva and Parvati uphold your prestige.

I am of course least worried in this battle, because the result of this battle will surely go against me. The prestige of both of us would be of Siva and Parvati.

Therefore, O Ganesvaras, you fight the battle, keeping all these things in view. You fight on behalf of your master, while I shall fight for my mother.

Whatever type of battle would it be, let it be so. None in the three worlds would be able to stop it.”

Brahma said, “Ganesa thus admonished the Sivaganas who had arrived holding the rods and other weapons in their hands.

Grinding their teeth, uttering humkaras, looking at Ganesa again and again the Sivaganas left the place.

Then suddenly Nandi arrived and pulled his leg. Then rushed Bhrngi and he pulled his other leg.

While both of them were pulling the legs of Ganesa, he struck them with both his hands and freed himself.

Thereafter the son of Parvati, stood at the gate and holding an iron club he started striking the ganas.

As a result, some of the ganas broke their hands, backs, heads as well as the foreheads.

The legs of some of them were broken, others broke their shoulders. Those who came in the front, they were struck over the chests.

Some of them fell down on the ground, while some of them fled away. Some of them broke their feet and other went back to Siva.

In the battle, no one was able to face Ganesa, in the same way as the dear flee spotting a lion.

Similarly thousands of ganas, returned after the battle, but Ganesa kept on standing at the gate watching the Sivaganas.

As at the end of the kalpa, Kala looks awful, similarly the Sivaganas found him to be quite destructive.

At this time, urged by Narada, all the gods including Visnu and Indra came there.

All of them offered their salutation to Siva for the sake of his welfare, and spoke to him with his permission.

They said, “O Lord, You are the Supreme Brahman, besides being the lord of all. All of us are your servants. You are the creator of the universe besides being its preserver and the destroyer.

Because of your divine sports, you transform yourself in the Sattva, rajas and tamas forms, but actually you are without attributes. What type of the divine play has been enacted by you today? Tell us, O Lord.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, listening to the words of the gods, Siva, looking at his wounded ganas, started revealing everything to him.

Then, O Excellent sage, the Supreme lord, the husband of Girija, smiled and said to me.”

Siva said, “An immensely valorous boy is standing at the gate of my abode, holding a danda in his hand. He does not allow anyone to enter inside the house. He is powerful attacker. He has beaten my courtiers and defeated my ganas.

O Brahma, you can yourself go and advising him properly convince him and do whatever is favourable to me.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of the lord, and overpowered with ignorance, I accompanied with all the Rsis went to him.

The powerful Ganesa, finding my arrival there, got enraged, and coming near me, he pulled up my beard and moustaches.

(Then Brahma said,) “Forgive me O Lord, I have not arrived here for waging a war. I am a Brahmana, and be merciful on me. I believe in peace without disturbance.

O Narada, while I had been so speaking, then the immensely valorous child Ganesa, lifted up a parigha in his hand.

When the valorous one took parigha in his hand, I at once fled away from that place. Having been wounded with the parigha, all my companions, cried and ran away from that place. Some of them fell down, while others were killed by him.

Some of them at once went to Siva and conveyed to him all the news.

Thus looking at the killed and the wounded persons, and listening to the news, Siva was extremely enraged.

Then he commanded the gods like Indra and others, Kartikeya and other ganas, the goblins and ghosts, besides the pisacas.

At the command of Siva, all the ganas, holding their weapons in their hands, moved in all the directions for the killing of the gana (Ganesa).

Whatever weapon was available with anyone was shot by him at Ganesa quite forcefully.

Tumult was created in all the three lokas, besides the mobile and immobile living beings. All the people of the three worlds were filled with doubt.

They thought, “What is the cause of the destruction, when the life of Brahma has not come to the end till now? Has the untimely disturbance being created at the command of Siva?

Kartikeya and all other ganas arrived there and reported, “All our weapons have become infructuous on Ganesa.” On hearing this, all were surprised.

In the mean time, Jagadamba, who bestows knowledge to all, learning about this event, was, immensely enraged.

O Excellent sage, at that point of time, the goddess, in order to help her gana gave her two Sakti to help him.

O Great sage, one of them taking to a terrific form, stood their opening her mouth like the cave of a black mountain.

The other one had many hands like the lightening and could punish the wicked people. She was the awful great goddess.

All the weapons shot by the gods over Ganesa, were swallowed by these two goddesses with their mouths.

The gods were unable to find anyone of their weapons there. Of course the parigha of Ganesa could be seen everywhere. In this way both the goddesses displayed their astonishing performance there.

The lonely boy churned the entire army in the same way as the Mandaracala mountain had churned the Ocean.

The lonely child upset all the gods like Indra and others, besides the Sivaganas by beating them severely.

Thereafter, all of them having deep sighs, feeling disturbed with his attacks said.”

The gods aid, “What should we do? Where should we go? We are now unmindful of the directions even and he is wielding parigha to the right and left.”

Brahma said, “At that point of time, carrying the sandal paste as well as the flowers in their hands, the apsaras as well as Narada and other who were curious to witness the war, reached there.

O Excellent sage, at that point of time, all of them reached there through the sky way for witnessing the war as a result of which the entire sky was filled.

All of them felt surprised by looking at the war and they observed, that such a type of awful war had never been witnessed by them earlier.

The earth with the oceans started shaking. The mountains cracked and started falling, which were indicative of the war.

With the shaking of the sky, all planets and group of constellations, were upset. All the gods and the Sivaganas fled from that place.

Only the valorous Kartikeya stood there and did not flee. He stood there in front of all.

Parvati, with the creation of the two goddesses, made all the opponents unsuccessful in the war. All the weapons shot by the gods over Ganesa were made infructuous.

All those who were present there, rushed to Siva, while the gods and the Sivaganas fled from that place.

All the gods, bowing in reverence to Siva, asked him, “O Lord who is this gana?’

We had heard about the wars and had even witnessed them, but such a type of battle, has neither been seen nor heard of in the past.

O Lord, you kindly think over deeply otherwise the defeat is imminent. Undoubtedly, you are the protector of the universe.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to their words, the enraged Siva went to that place in anger.

The army of the gods, marched on with the lord Visnu, joyfully, following Siva.

At that time, O Narada, with his heart having been filled with devotion, you spoke to lord Mahesvara.”

Narada said, “O Mahadeva- the god of gods, you kindly listen to my words. You are all-pervading and perform all the divine sports.

O Siva, with the divine sport enacted by you, you have relieved the ganas of their pride and more so you have also shattered the pride of the gods as well.

O Siva, you have shattered the pride of all and have established the superiority of your force.

O Lord, well-disposed towards your devotees, you kindly do not display further the same divine sport. You kindly send back the gods and the ganas with respect.

O Lord, you are the bestower of the salvation, don’t play with him and rather kill him.” Thus speaking Narada disappeared from the scene.

## Chapter 16 - Severing of the head of Ganesa

Brahma said, “O Narada, lord Siva, who is compassionate over his devotees, listening to your words, got ready for a fight with that boy.

He called for Visnu and consulted him, he was accompanied with the soldiers of the gods. Then lord Siva appeared before Ganesa.

Because of the compassion of Siva, the valorous gods, then started fighting with enthusiasm, devoting their minds at the lotus like feet of Siva.

The valorous Visnu, having the great prowess, started fighting with Ganesa. On the other side was the great Ganesa possessing the weapons of the goddess.

Ganesa was beating the gods with a danda. The valorous Ganesa then shot a Sakti at Visnu.

O Sage, at that point of time the strength of all the gods was faded out. Observing Ganesa’s attack on Visnu, all the gods fled away from the battle ground.

Siva too, together with his army fought with the boy for long, but finding him awful, he felt surprised.

Siva then thought, “He can be killed deceitfully only. There is no other way out.” Thus thinking in his mind and standing firm in the army, he waged the war.

Finding the Nirguna Siva in his Saguna form, all the gods returned to the battle ground.

The ganas of Siva too, reaching there, collectively held celebrations there.

Thereafter, Ganesa- the valorous son of Sakti, raised his danda and struck Visnu, who bestows comforts to all.

Then Visnu said, “O Lord, this is an immensely tamasika boy and cannot be killed except in a deceitful manner. I shall try to confuse him and then you can kill him.

Thus thinking and in consultation with Siva, Visnu, after seeking permission from Siva, was himself confused.

Finding Visnu in that form, both the Saktis guarding Ganesa, disappeared. Both of them bestowed their strength on Ganesa.

With the disappearing of both the Saktis, Ganesa, shot a parigha at Visnu.

Then Visnu, devoting his mind to Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, making all the efforts, changed the direction of the parigha.

At the same time the enraged Siva, also holding a trident in his hand arrived there from another side.

The valorous son of Siva, found that Siva had arrived holding a trident in his hand, for the purpose of killing him.

Then Ganesa, who had become more powerful because of the Sakti of Siva, devoted his mind at the lotus like feet of his mother Parvati and shot his Sakti, at the hand of Siva.

Then Siva the soul of the universe, when found that his trident had fallen on the ground, he then took up the Pinaka bow in his hand.

Ganesa on his part dropped that bow also from the hand of Siva, with the striking of a parigha. With the shooting of the five parighas at Siva, Ganesa, made his five hands infructous. Then he picked up the trident.

Then Siva, who had been well-versed in the worldly traditions, said, “This is surprising. In case I have been placed in such an ugly position, then what would happens to my ganas?

Having been equipped with the strength of Sakti, Ganesvara, in the meantime also attacked the gods with parigha.

The gods having been struck with the parigha fled away to all the ten directions. No one could face Ganesa in the battle-field, who attacked others in a surprising manner.

Then observing the valorous, powerful, the great warrior gana, who liked the war, Visnu observed, “This boy is quite graceful.”

I have met with several gods, daityas, danavas, yaksas, Gandharvas and the Raksasas.

But the prowess and the virtues possessed by this gana can hardly be found in the three worlds.

While Visnu had been so thinking, Ganesa the son of Sakti, then shot the parigha at Visnu.

Then Visnu, devoting his mind at the feet of Siva, reduced the parigha to pieces with his disc.

When the pieces of parigha were again thrown by Ganesa, at Visnu , then Garuda, made them infructuous.

Thus for a long time, the two heroes Ganesa and Visnu fought with each other.

Then the valorous son of Sakti, devoting himself to Siva, attacked Visnu with his danda.

Unable to bear the attack of Ganesa, Visnu fell down on the ground. He got up at once and started fighting with the son of Siva.

In the meantime Siva, the trident bearer, arrived there and he cut off the head of Ganesa, with his trident.

O Narada, with the severing of the head of the gana of Parvati, the position of the gods as well as the ganas of Siva became stable.

O Narada then you went to goddess Parvati and revealed everything to her and also advised her that she should not compromise for her prestige.

O Quarrelsome Narada, thus speaking, you disappeared, because you always move according to the will of Siva.

## Chapter 17 - Ganesa brought back to life

Narada said, “O Brahma, the abode of wisdom, learning about the news, what was the reaction of Siva? I would like to listen to it correctly.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, I shall now narrate the relevant episode concerning the mother of the universe which occurred thereafter.

After the killing of Ganesa, the ganas of Siva started celebrating the occasion, playing on cymbals and other musical instruments.

O Excellent sage, Siva on the other hand was grieving after cutting off the head of the boy, then the goddess Girija was immensely enraged.

She thought within himself, “What should I do? Where should I go, alas! I feel extremely painful. How could I be relieved of the pain of his death?

My son has been killed by all the god and the ganas of Siva. Either I shall destroy them all or shall resort to dissolution.”

Thus feeling painful, Parvati then created hundreds and thousands of Saktis, who were spread in the entire universe.

All those Saktis possessed the lustre. The offered their salutation to the mother of the universe and said to her, “O Mother, get us your command.”

O Excellent sage, on hearing them, the basic Prakrti- the Sakti of Siva, felt enraged, and she spoke to all of them.

The goddess said, “O Goddesses, O Saktis, all of you at my command, start the dissolution of the world. You have nothing to think further about it.

You forcibly devour all the gods, Rsis, Yaksas, Raksasas, your own as well as the others should all the devoured by you.”

Brahma said, “At the command of Parvati, all the goddesses, getting enraged, started killing all including the gods.

As the straw is consumed by the fire, similarly the Saktis started devouring one and all.

Leaders of ganas, or Brahma, Visnu or Siva, Indra, Kubera, Skanda or the sun, the Saktis began to devour them. Wherever one looked, Saktis were found present there.

Karalis (the terrific ones), the Kubjikas (hunch backed), Khanjas (lame), Lambasirsas(those having long heads) and other innumerable Saktis lifted up the gods in their hands and put them in their own mouths.

Observing this Siva, Brahma, Visnu, Indra and other gods, besides the ganas and the sages, became doubtful about the further steps of Parvati, who could cause an untimely dissolution of the world. They lost all hopes, and aspirations for life.

All of them then collected together and discussed about the future course of action. Then they kept on discussing with one an other.

They thought, “Peace would be possible when the goddess Girija is pleased, otherwise, one cannot meet with welfare by making crores of efforts.

Siva, following the worldly practices, who performed several types of sports, cast his illusion on all.

The hopes of all the gods were dashed. The enraged Parvati did not want to get to the city.

No one of her own including the gods, Danavas, ganas, Dikpalas, Yaksas, Kinnaras, sages or Brahma, Visnu or Siva, could stand before Girija.

Observing her burning lustre, all of them were standing at a distance.

O Sage, you (Narada) arrived for the comfort of the gods.

You, offering your salutation to me (Brahma), Visnu and Siva, consulted them all about the future course of action.

Then all the god started consultations with you, to get rid of the painful sufferings.

All of them said, “Unless Girija showers her grace, no one could be comfortable. There is no doubt about it.

Thereafter all the Rsis accompanied with you went to Siva. All of them offered prayer to Siva, to calm her down and make her free from anger.

The gods offered their salutation to her again and again, and eulogised her variously. All of them then lovingly pleased her.”

The divine saints said, “O Mother of the universe, O Kalyani, we bow in reverence to you again and again.

O Mother, you are the creator of the universe, you are the eternal force, the sustainer of the world, besides being its destroyer.

O Supreme goddess of the gods, be peaceful. Salutation to you. O Goddess, the three worlds are agitated with your fury.”

Brahma said, “In this way all the gods eulogised the Supreme goddess with you. Because of her having been filled with furry, the goddess spoke nothing to them.

At that point of time, all the Rsis bowed in reverence at her lotus like feet. Then with folded hand, they slowly spoke to her.”

Rsis said, “O Goddess, you better stop the destruction. O Mother, look here, your lord is present here.

Who are we? Your people like Brahma, Visnu and the gods are present here with folded hands.

O Siva, O Paramesvari, you kindly forgive them all for their sins. All of them are upset today. Therefore you become peaceful.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking all the sages, with all humility at their command, folding their hands, were seated before the goddess.

Thus listening to their words, Candika was pleased. Then feeling merciful she spoke to the Rsis.

The goddess said, “There would be no destruction, in case my son is brought back to life and becomes adorable by all of you. In case you agree to make him the chief of all the gods, only then the world would be peaceful and enjoy comforts, otherwise not.”

Brahma said, “At these words of the goddess, all the sages, accompanied with you, conveyed the news to all the gods.

Indra and the other gods who were feeling painful at heart, conveyed the entire news to lord Siva.

Listening to the words of the gods, Siva said, “Everything should be done, to make the people comfortable.

You people should go to the northern direction and whosoever is met by you, his head should be cut off and fixed over the trunk of Ganesa.”

Brahma said, “Then the ganas, obeying the command of Siva, washed the body of Ganesa, appropriately and then adoring it, went to the northern side and they came across an elephant with a single tusk.

They brought its head and fixed it over the trunk of Ganesa, after which the gods conveyed to Siva, Visnu and Brahma, that the order of the lord had been executed and then they could carry on the job further.”

Brahma said, “Thereafter all the gods as well as the courtiers, obeying the command of Siva, became comfortable and looked graceful.

Then the gods like Brahma, Visnu and others, offered their salutation to the lord Siva- without attributes, and said to him.”

“As we possess the lustre emerging from you, similarly, Ganesa should also possess the same lustre from you, as also from the influence of the Vedas. Thereafter all the gods, together with Siva, sprinkled the sanctified water over Ganesa.

With the very touch of that water, the body of Ganesa was brought back to life, regaining consciousness. At the desire of Siva, the boy got up as if having been woken up from sleep.

He looked full of fortunes, having the head of an elephant, red complexion, extremely beautiful, smiling face, possessing beautiful lustre and pleasant figure.

O Excellent sage, all those present there felt delighted by looking at the living child of Siva. The miseries of all of hem were removed.

All the gods getting delighted, showed the child to Parvati, who was extremely delighted finding her son alive.

## Chapter 18 - Crowning of Ganesa as Chief of Sivaganas

Narada said, “O Brahma, when the son of the goddess was brought back to life, what happened thereafter? You kindly tell me.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent sage, when Girija found that her son was brought back to life, the event was celebrated, the details of which are being narrated by me.

O Sage, the son of Girija was brought back to life without any blemish whatsoever or nervousness. Thereafter the gods crowned him and consecrated him over the position of the chief of the ganas.

The goddess Parvati felt highly pleased at the sight of her son. She look him in her lap and kissed him.

The mother of the universe clad Ganesa with fresh costumes and adorned him with the best of ornaments.

The goddess then adored him offering all the siddhis to him. Then she touched her son who could remove all the sufferings, with her hand.

Then adoring her son, the goddess Girija, kissed his face, bestowing him with several boons. Then she said, “You had to suffer much.

You are quite graceful. You are successful in all your missions. You would be adored first of all the gods and those who would do so would always remain comfortable.

The vermilion is opening on our face, and as such you will be adored by the people with vermilion.

You will also be adored with the offering of flowers, sandal paste, auspicious fragrance, best of naivedya and performing your arati.

You will also be offered betel, daksina, and the people will offer their salutation to you after circumambulating you at the same time.

By doing so one would achieve all the siddhis. All his obstructions would be removed.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking, the goddess Mahesvari, adored her son again, offering the best of the padarthas.

O Narada, soon thereafter, all the gods and the ganas of Siva started recouping their health.

On that occasion, Indra and other gods, pleasing lord Siva, with their prayers and led him to Parvati.

Then all the gods collectively placed the son of Parvati, lovingly in the lap of Siva.

Then Siva, placing his hand over the head of the boy said to the gods, “This is my second son.

Ganesa then got up and offered his salutation to Siva, Parvati, Brahma and Visnu, besides the Rsis and Narada. Then sitting before all of them he prayed to them to forgive him for his sins. The humans were similarly filled with pride.

Then I myself, besides Siva and Visnu, bestowed on him the best of boons, and said to him collectively.

As we three are considered to be the best and most adorable among the gods, similarly, the leader of the ganas i.e. Ganesa would be adored in future.

Ganesa is the remover of the obstructions and bestows rewards of all the desires.

He would be adored first and then the people would adore us. In case the people adoring us and would not adore Ganesa, their adoration would be infructuous. There is no doubt about it. Brahma said, “Thus speaking, initially, Siva adored Ganesa, offering many things. Thereafter Visnu adored him.

Then I (Brahma) together with Parvati and other gods, adored him with utmost devotion.

In order to please Parvati, all the gods like Brahma, Visnu and Siva accepted Ganesa as the leader of the ganas.

Then Siva pronounced numerous boons on him, which could make him always comfortable in the world.”

Then Siva said, “O Son of Parvati, I am undoubtedly pleased with you, and when I am pleased, the entire universe feels pleased. No opponent is found.

You are the illustrious son of Sakti. You are extremely strong, inspite of being a boy. Therefore you would always remain comfortable.

You would be the foremost in the removing of the obstructions. Henceforth you would be the foremost of your ganas and would be adored the world over.”

Thus speaking, Siva, apprised him of several types of the methods for adoration and also blessed him variously.

Thereafter the gods played on musical instruments, besides singing. The apsaras resorted to dancing.

Then Lord Siva- the supreme soul, feeling delighted, bestowed the boons on Ganesa.

He said, “O Ganesa, on the fourth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Bhadrapada, you have been bom at the time of the moon rise.

Girija conceived your present form during the first prahara of the night. Therefore this would be observed as the best of vrata dedicated to you.

Therefore, all the people should perform this vrata for achieving all types of success.

When the same tithi arrives at the end of the year, then one should perform vrata on every Caturthi-tithi.

The people who are desirous of achieving all the comforts in the world, should adore you with devotion on the caturthi day.

A Caturthi called Ramea, comes in the month of Margasirsa and one should perform early morning ablution and entrust the vrata to the Brahmana.

He shall perform the vrata with Durva- grass and observe fast. After the elapse of a prahara in the night, the devotees shall take his bath and worship.

The image of Ganesa should be made of metal, coral, white arka flowers, or of clay. It should be installed and worshipped by a devotee, with all the purity and fragrance of various types, besides the divine sandal paste and flowers.

A handful of Durva grass with three knots, but without roots, should be used for the purpose of adoration. The shoots shall be hundred and one in number. The image should be worshipped with twenty-one of them Then Ganesa should be adored with lamps, and different kinds of food stuffs.

Then offering Ganesa the betel, argha and other best of articles, one should adore him, offering salutation and prayer to him. Thus after adoring Ganesa, the crescent should be worshipped.

The Brahmanas should be adored thereafter and feed them with sweet dishes.

Then the rites should be formally concluded, thereafter one should remember Ganesa. In this way the Vrata shall be concluded in an auspicious manner.

When the Vrata is so completed, in a year, a devotee shall perform the rite of the final conclusion of the Vrata.

At my instance twelve Brahmanas shall be fed. Then consecrating a kalasa the images should be worshipped.

An eight pitalled lotus should be drawn over the pedestal on the ground, the homa should be performed according to the Vedic rites, spending money according to one’s own capacity.

Food should be served to two chaste women whose husbands are alive and two boys in front of the images.

Remaining awake during the night one should perform worship in the morning. Thereafter, the rite of formal conclusion reciting the mantra “Ksemaya punaragamanaya-ca shall be performed.

The blessing should be received from the boys with the reciting of the Svasti-vacana. For the completion of the Vratas, the hand cup filled with flowers should be offered.

Finally, offering his salutation, one should engage himself in other works. A person who performs the vrata in this way, he receives the desired reward.

O Ganesa, to achieve success in all the jobs, one should adore you according to his capacity, offering vermilion sandal paste, rice and Ketaki flowers.

The one who worships you with all the required materials, all his works are successfully accomplished and the obstructions are removed.

This Vrata can be performed by the people of all the castes. This vrata can especially be performed by the ladies as well the kings desirous of their uplift.

Whosoever is desirous of something, he surely gets it. Therefore the person, desirous of something should always perform this Vrata."

Brahma said, “When Siva, thus spoke to Ganesa, the great soul, then ail the gods, the best of the Rsis, accepted his words, the people who were dear to Siva, adored Ganesa.

Thereafter all the ganas bowed in reverence to Ganesa and worshipped him, offering several articles.

O Excellent sage, I cannot describe the pleasure of Parvati, which she had at that time, with my four mouths.

The big drums were beaten by the gods then and the apsaras started dancing. The Gandharvas started singing and the rain of flowers was showered from the sky.

After the consecration of Ganesa as the lord of ganas, sufferings of all the people came to an end.

O Narada, Siva and Parvati were specially delightful. Bliss and plenty of welfare, that was conductive to happiness, was found everywhere.

The gods and the sages who had arrived there, retired to their respective abode at the instance of Siva, praising Parvati and Ganesa again and again, eulogising Siva at the same time. They uttered, “What a battle was it?”

After Parvati was relieved of her anger, Siva and Parvati, resorted to their natural way of life as before.

With the sole purpose of the benefit of the universe, Siva- the great lord, relaxing in his own soul, and engrossed in the activities for the welfare of the devotees, conferred on them, various kinds of grace.

Visnu and myself (Brahma) taking leave of Siva, serving both Siva and Parvati in many ways with devotion, returned to our respective abodes.

O Best of the sages, O Narada, you also singing the glory of Siva and Parvati and taking leave of him returned to your abode.

In this way I have related to you the auspicious story of Siva and Parvati, particularly concerning Vighnesa, quite respectfully as per your request.

A person who listens to this auspicious episode, which bestows welfare, he meets with all the welfare and finally becomes the abode of welfare.

A sonless person gets the son, a poor person gets the riches, a person desirous of a wife, gets a wife and a king desirous of the people gets the (good) people.

An ailing person is freed of the ailment, an unfortunate person gets the fortunes, a person having lost his son, get a son, a person who has lost his riches, gets back his riches and a lady whose husband had left for an other country, gets him back.

A person overpowered with grief, is relieved of the same, there is no doubt about it. A person in whose house the story of the birth of Ganesa is recited, the welfare, undoubtedly prevails there. The one who listens to the same on an auspicious day during the period of his journey, he by the grace of Sri Ganesa, achieves all the desires.

## Chapter 19 - Proposal for the marriage of Ganesa

Narada said, “0 Dear one, I have heard about the surprising birth of Ganesa, and also the story of his valorous performance.

O Dear one, O Lord of the gods, what happened thereafter? The auspicious story of Siva and Parvati, bestows immense delight.”

Brahma said, “O Excellent and compassionate sage, you have referred about an excellent matter, about which, O Best of the Rsis, I am going to speak. Therefore you please listen to me attentively.

O Narada, “Both Siva and Parvati, felt happy at the performance of both of them. With the loving care of the mother, both of them felt more and more comfortable. Both the brothers played together.

O Excellent sage, both the brothers served the parents with utmost devotion.

The affection of the mother, kept on increasing over both the sons as the crescent of the bright fortnight keeps on increasing.

O Divine sage, once both Siva and Parvati, seated in a secluded place were engaged in some important discussion.

Both Siva and Parvati said, “Both the sons have reached the marriageable age. How should we marry both of them?

“Kartikeya is quite loveable, and similar is the case of Ganesa.” Engaged in such thoughts, they were enjoying the sports of both of them.

O Sage, getting aware of the feelings of their parents, both the sons became desirous of getting married.

Both of them then started repeating before the parents, “I shall also marry.”

“Listening to the words of both the sons, both Siva and Parvati, following the worldly traditions, felt concerned about the issue.

They thought, “What should be done?” How should both of them be married?” Thus thinking, they thought out a solution of a surprising type.

Once both of the parents were seated, they called for their sons and said to them.

Siva and Parvati said, “Both of us have worked out a pleasant solution for you both. O Dear sons, you please listen to us.

Both of you are equal to us, without any difference. For the welfare of both the sons, we have thus resolved.

“Whosoever, shall return first after circumambulating the earth, he would be married first in an auspicious time.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of his parents Kartikeya, at once got out of the house for taking a round of the earth.

The intelligent Ganesa started thinking, again and again, using his brain.

He thought, “What should be done? Where should I go? I cannot cross the ocean. I cannot proceed, even after walking for a krosa. Then how could I take a round of such a vast ocean.” Thus thinking whatever was then done by Ganesa, you please listen from me.

After taking his bath appropriately, he came to his house and said to his parents.

Ganesa said, “I want to adore you by seating you over the asana. You kindly fulfil my desire.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Ganesa, accepting his worship, both of them were seated over the asanas.

He adored both his parents appropriately. He circumambulated them seven times offering seven salutations to them.

Then Ganesa, the ocean of wisdom, spoke to them with folded hands, when both the parents were overwhelmed; with affection.”

Ganesa said, “O Mother, O Father, you please listen to me. Now you should marry me at once.”

Brahma said, “In this way listening to the words of Ganesa, who had been the ocean of wisdom, and the great soul, his parents said to him.”

Siva-Parvati said, “You first go round the earth filled with forests. Kumara has already left for the purpose. Similarly you should also go and take a round of the earth.”

Brahma said, “Thus listening to the words of his parents, Ganesa getting enraged spoke the appropriate words.

Ganesa said, “O My Father, O My Mother, both of you are the form of dharma, you kindly weigh my words according to the provisions of dharma.

I have gone round the earth seven times, then how can both of you speak like that.”

Brahma said, “Taking shelter under the worldly traditions, both Siva and Parvati, listening to his words, said to Ganesa.”

The parents said, “O Son, when did you go round, seven times the earth with vast forests?”

Brahma said, “O Sage, listening to the words of Siva and Parvati, the great intellectual and the ocean of wisdom, replied to them.

Ganesa said, “By circumambulating you both- the father and the mother, I according to my wisdom, have gone round the earth up to the ocean.

This has been provided in the Vedas as well as in the other scriptures. Is it true or untrue? The one who by adoring the parents, circumambulates, the earns the reward of going round the entire earth.

The one who goes on pilgrimage, to the holy places, leaving his parents behind, he earns the sin of killing his parents.

The lotus like feet of the parents are the holiest place for a son. For reaching other holy places, one has to travel a lot, but (the lotus like feet of the parents) are always close by, easily approachable besides being the means to dharma. For the son and the wife, this is the best of holy place in the house itself.

This has been ordained by the Vedas and the holy scriptures, which should also be followed by you, otherwise they would prove as false together with the Vedas. There is no doubt about it.

In case you do not believe in this, your present form would be falsified and the Vedas would also be proved as false.

Now, the auspicious marriage ceremony should be performed at once, otherwise the Vedas and the holy scriptures would prove false.

O my religious minded parents, you kindly weigh both the aspects appropriately and move accordingly.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking the great intellectual, and best among the learned people, kept quiet.

Both Siva and Parvati, who were the master of the universe, felt surprised hearing the words of Ganesa.

Thereafter, both Siva and Parvati, started praising Ganesa who had spoken correctly.”

Siva and Parvati said, “O Son, you are a great personality, possessing the spotless wisdom. The words spoken by you are utterly true.

The one, whose wisdom remains stable even at the time of misfortune, his miseries vanish in the same way as the darkness is removed at sunrise.

The person who possesses wisdom, is quite powerful. How could a fool attain strength? A hare made an intoxicated lion to fall into the well.

The duties of a boy as prescribed in the Vedas, Sastras and the Puranas, have been performed by you.

No one has acted in the manner in which you have conducted yourself. We have accepted your words, which cannot be otherwise.

Brahma said, “Thus assuring Ganesa, the ocean of wisdom, (both Siva and Parvati) started thinking of performing his marriage.

## Chapter 20 - Marriage of Ganesa

In the meantime, Prajapati Visvarupa, had two daughters possessing the divine features, known as Siddhi and Buddhi. All the limbs of their body were extremely beautiful.

The marriage of Ganesa was fixed with them by Siva and Parvati holding the marriage ceremony.

All the gods joined the marriage party delightfully, in the same way as desired by Siva and Parvati.

The marriage ceremony was performed by Visvakarma, observing which all the gods, Rsis, sages and all others felt extremely delighted.

O Sage, Ganesa also achieved the best of pleasures from them, which would be beyond description.

After some time both the wives of Ganes'a the great soul, gave birth to a son each, who were quite beautiful.

A son named Ksema was bom to Ganesa’s wife named Siddhis while Labha a beautiful son was born to his second wife named Buddhi.

Thus while Ganesvara, was enjoying unthinkable pleasures, in the meantime, going round the entire earth, Kartikeya, the second son of Siva returned from his journey.

At the same time ahatma Narada also arrived there and he said, “I am not talking deceitfully, by falsehood or otherwise.

Whatever your parents have done in your absence, no one else in the world could ever do so.

They sent you out on the pretext of going round the earth, they performed the excellent marriage of Ganesa.

With the two daughters of Prajapati Visvarupa.

He has got a son each from both his wives. Siddhis gave birth to Ksema and Buddhi gave birth to Labha, both the sons cause comforts to all.

By getting two sons, from his two wives, Ganesa, with the permission of his parents is enjoying all the pleasures.

With the deceitful command of your parents, you went round the earth surrounded by the oceans and the forest. You have got the reward for the same.

O Dear one, you first think over, as to why your parents played this trick with you. In case a father can play such a trick with his own son, then what would be beyond him to be done to others.

According to my mind, whatever has been done by your parents, is highly improper. You also think over the same. At least, I have not liked it.

In case the mother gives the poison, or the father sells off, or in case the king might usurp everything, then what could be said about anyone.

O Dear one, an intelligent person, would never look at the face of such a person, who commits such harmful deeds.

This is the polity ordained in the Vedas, Sastras, as well as the Smrtis. Now you can do whatever you like.”

Brahma said, “O Narada, at the desire of Siva’s mind, you kept quiet, after thus speaking to Kumara.

Skanda too, offering his salutation to his parents, getting enraged, proceeded on towards the Kraunca mountain, much against the wishes of his parents.

They said, “Why are you going inspite of our asking you not to do so.” Kartikeya went away much against the wishes of his parents.

Kartikeya said, “O my parents, I shall not stay here even for a moment. Discarding love, both of you have played a trick with me.”

O Sage, Kartikeya, thus speaking to his parents left the place and has not returned till date. With a mere sight at him all the sins are washed out.

O Divine sage, since that date, Devarsi Kartikeya, the son of Siva remained unmarried.

His name bestows all the pleasures and is well known in the world. He destroys all the sins. He bestows the virtues besides being best of those bestowing brahmacarya.

On the full moon day of the month of Kartika, all the gods, Rsis together with their disciples, go to Kumara to have a look at him.

On the full moon day in the Krttika constellation, one who has an audience with Svami Kartikeya, all his sins are washed away and his desires are fulfilled.

Uma felt painful at the departure of Skanda. Then she said to Siva, feeling grieved at heart, “Let us go together to his place.”

In order to please Parvati, Siva went to the place of Kartika. He assumed the form of Jyotirlinga known as Mallikarjuna.

Even today, Siva is seen there with Parvati, fulfilling the desires of his devotees. He is the goal of the noble people.

When Kumara came to know about the arrival of Siva, he developed detachment and became eager to go elsewhere.

When the sages and the gods prayed him from a distance, still he continued to live at a place nearly three yojanas away.

Getting upset with the attraction of their son, both Siva and Parvati, O Narada, used to go to that place on every full moon day.

Siva used to go to that place on the moonless day alone, while Parvati used to go there on the full moon day.

O Narada, whatever episodes relating to Kartikeya and Ganesa, as asked by you have been narrated by me.

By listening to this story, the people are relieved of all the sins. He achieves all the best of desires, whosoever reads or teaches it to others, hears or makes others to hear it, all his desires are fulfilled. There is no doubt about it.

A Brahmana attains Brahmanical excellence, a Ksatriya becomes victorious, a Vais'ya becomes prosperous, and Sudra attains comparison with virtues.

An ailing person is freed from ailment, a frightened man is relieved of fear, and a person is freed from the danger of goblins ghosts etc.

This narrative is sinless, bestows glory and increases pleasures. It bestows long life and makes one achieve the heaven. It is beyond comparison and bestows sons and the grandsons.

It bestows salvation and enlightens one of the Sivatattva. It delights Siva and Parvati both, besides increasing devotion to Siva.

The devotees shall always listen to the same besides those who seek deliverance and are free from the worldly desires. It establishes identity with Siva. It is conducive to the welfare and is identical with Siva.

Here end the fourth Rumara Khanda of second Rudra Samhita of Siva

Mahapurana

## (5) Yuddha Khanda

## Chapter 1 - The demon Tripurasura

Narada said, “I have listened to the excellent story of Ganes'a, Skanda, as well as the blissful household life of Siva.

Now you narrate the story of the lord Siva, who had killed several demons while roaming about here and there.

How did lord Siva, kill a demon, inimical to the gods, with three cities, with the shooting of a single arrow, burning them at the same time.

O Lord, you also narrate the story of lord Candracuda who was free from illusion and bestowed comforts over the Rsis.”

Brahma said, “Once in the earlier times the sage Vyasa, had put a similar question to Sanat Kumara- the great sage, and the answer given by him is being narrated by me.

Sanat Kumara said, “O Immensely intelligent Vyasa, listen to the story of Candrasekhara Siva, who is the destroyer of the universe, had burnt Tripura with the shooting of a single arrow.

O Excellent sage, when Tarakasura, was killed by Skanda, the son of Siva, then all the three of his sons, started performing tapas.

They were known by the names of Taraka- the eldest one, Vidyunmali- the middle one, and Kamalaksa- the youngest one. All the three of them were equally strong.

They had controlled all the senses, were ready to undertake any assignment, having controlled all the senses, were truthful, firm in mind, immensely strong, besides being inimical to the gods.

All the three of them, discarding all the pleasant comforts, went to Sumeru mountain, and started performing penance in a cave there.

All the three sons of Tarakasura, disowning all the desires like singing, music 88 and dancing during the spring season, kept on performing the tapas delightfully.

They bore the heat of the sun during the summer season, lighting fire all round, sitting in the centre, used to perform the homa.

In the scorching heat, they used to fall and get fainted. During the rainy season they faced the heavy down pour of the rain over their bodies.

In the winter season, they controlled their hunger and thirst, discarding nice food stuffs, steady, wholesome and delicious fruits, and roots besides the beverages, they remained hungry. They remained themselves as stones.

In the early winter, they remained over the top of the mountain, with fortitude, without any support from anyone of the four quarters.

In the late winter, they stayed under the water, or wore wet silken cloth or were covered with the dew drops.

They were never perplexed or distressed under such conditions. Their penance became more and more severe gradually. In this way the three excellent sons of Taraka, continued to perform hard tapas, for Brahma.

The best of the danavas, following the hard rules, were engaged in hard tapas following severe austerities.

All of them performed tapas by standing on one leg for a hundred years, on earth.

The wicked demons lived on inhaling air only, for a thousand years, facing hard conditions.

For a thousand years they performed tapas standing upside down. For a hundred years, they kept on raising their one hand upwards.

With their evil intentions, they bore extreme distress. Thus all the three of them, spent day and nights quite carefully.

In this way a lot of time of those sons of Tarakasura, was spent following dharma. This is what I feel.

Then Brahma, the preceptor of all the gods and the demons, feeling pleased with their tapas appeared before them.

Accompanied with the sages, gods and ausras, the grandsire of all the living beings, spoke to them while appeasing them.

Brahma said, “O Great demon-sages, I am pleased with your tapas. I shall give you all whatever you would desires.

O Enemy of the gods, what for have you performed such a hard tapas. I am the one who bestows reward to all those who perform tapas."

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Brahma, all the three of them offered their salutation to him, slowly and then they revealed the desire of their heart.”, the grandsire of all the living beings, spoke to them while appeasing them.

The three demons said, “O lord of the gods, in case you are really pleased with us, and are desirous to bestow a boon on us, then grant us the boon that we should be indestructible of anyone or any living being.

O Lord of the universe, you kindly make us invincible from our enemies free from the old age, ailment and death.

We should be free from the old age and death. We should be able to cause death to all others in the three worlds.

Of what use are the enormous riches, vast earth, the best of cities, all means of excellent pleasure and other fortunes, in case, some one is swallowed by the death in a few days? Everything become useless for such a person. There is no doubt about it.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to these words of the demon ascetics, devoting his mind in favour of lord Siva, Brahma spoke to them.”

Brahma said, “O Demons, everyone cannot be immortal and everlasting. You don’t be desirous of the same and therefore ask for any other boon, which pleases your mind.

O Demons, whosoever has been bom is bound to die one day, whosoever he might be. No one is immortal on earth.

Except Hari and Siva, there is none immortal on earth. Both of them are beyond dharma and adharma and have both manifest and unmanifest forms.

In case the tapas is performed for creating trouble on earth, then the entire result of the same should be deemed to have vanished. Therefore you should ask for a boon quite thoughtfully.

O Sinless demons, you should not insist for immortality. Immortality is beyond the reach of even the gods and the demons and cannot be warded off. You better ask for another boon.

You taking the refuge in Sattvaguna and you better ask for some other boon, to save yourself from its cause.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to these words of Brahma, they kept on thinking for a while and then they spoke to Brahma, the grandsire of the universe.”

The daityas said, “O Lord, we do not have a place which could be beyond the reach of the valorous enemy, and make us live comfortably.

You give us three cities, which should be extremely beautiful, filled with all the riches, and are indestructible by the gods.

O Preceptor of the universe, Lord of the worlds, by your grace we shall move about on the earth occupying these cities.

Thereafter Tarakaksa said, “Such a beautiful city in gold should be made by Visvakarma, which should be impregnable by the gods.”

Then Kamalaksa said, “My city should be made of silver,” and Vajramali desired his city to be made of iron and steel.

O Brahma, all the three cities should be made at one place. They should be constructed during noon time, when the sun is in Abhijit constellation and the moon is in Pusya constellation.

When the clouds are overcast in the sky and the Puskaravarta clouds are dropping the rain.

We shall return after a thousand years and by that time, these cities should be complete 91 in all respects. There is no doubt about it.

O Brahma, when the three cities are joined together, the lord who is the abode of all the gods, seated in an astonishing type of vehicle, containing all the necessary requirements, may, in his distorted sport, shoot an amazing singly arrow and pierce our cities. Lord Siva is free from enmity with us, besides being worthy of our adoration and respect. Then how can he burn us? This is what we think in our minds. A person like him is difficult to get in the world.

Sanatkumara said, “Then Brahma, who happens to be the grandsire of the entire universe, listening to these words, remembering Siva, said, “Be it so.”

Mayadanava was then ordered to build three cities of gold, silver and iron.

After thus issuing a command to Mayadanava, in the presence of the sons of Taraka, Brahma- the creator, returned to his abode, in full view of all of them.

Then Maya who was filled with wisdom, making all the efforts, made the city of gold for Tarakaksa, a silver city for Kamalaksa and a city of iron, for Vidyunmali, together with three forts, which were located with heaven, the sky and the earth.

Bestowing the three cities to the Danavas, keeping in view their welfare, he himself also started living there.

After getting the possession of the three cities, the sons of Taraka, entered therein. The immensely valorous Danavas, started enjoying all the comforts there.

Numerous kalpavrksas were growing in those cities, besides numerous horses and the elephants. There were several places, with gem-studded windows.

There were several planes in which rubies were fixed in all the four sides, and illumined like the sun rays. Some of them resembled the moon, which decorated the city.

There were the huge royal places. The gates of the cities, resembled the peaks of the Kailasa mountain. There were numerous divine damsels, besides those of the Gandharvas, Siddhas and caranas.

Every house had a Siva temple, places for performing the homas, and the learned people well-versed in the scriptures, lived there.

There were enough of step-wells, wells, tanks, both big and small, besides the divine orchards with charming trees.

All the rivers, rivulets and canals were filled with water. The place was quite delightful with the trees which yielded useful fruits.

The place had the herds of elephants, horses, chariots and palanquins of different types.

During the evening time, besides the play grounds, the separate rooms were made for the study of the Vedas.

No sinful persons, could be found there who spoke evil words by speech or the mind. Everywhere only the noble people with good conduct could be seen.

The houses of the city were adored with the chaste women who were devoted to their husbands and served them well, and were averse to evil ways.

The immensely fortunate, daitya-warrior lived with their sons and wives, besides the Brahmana, who were well-versed in the smarta doctrine and were devoted to their dharma.

There were enough of dwarfs, having broad chests, high shoulders, well-versed in peace and war, who could get enraged at the appropriate time only and found everywhere.

There were enough of dwarfs, having broad chests, high shoulders, well-versed in peace and war, who could get enraged at the appropriate time only and found everywhere.
