Mayadanava, had kept on duty the warriors there, who had the complexion like the blue lotus flowers, having the curly hair resembling the black wasps and who were always anxious to fight.

The powerful warriors, who had become valorous because of their adoring Siva and Brahma, who could wage the best of wars and who could churn the powerful gods like the Sun, Marut, Indra and other valorous gods, could be found there.

O Gods, whatever faiths are described in the Vedas, Sastras and the Puranas, besides 93 those which were pleasing to Siva, could be found in those cities.

All the three sons of Tarakasura, after achieving the boons from Brahma, adoring Mayadanava, lived there.

Disowning all the three worlds, the sons of Taraka, entering their respective cities, devoting their minds in the worship of Siva, they continued to rule.

O Sage, in this way, they performing the noble deeds, while ruling their respective countries, quietly lived, with comforts for long.

## Chapter 2 - Prayer by the gods

Vyasa said, “O Son of Brahma possessing great intellect and most eloquent, please narrate as to what happened thereafter? How were the gods pleased?”

Brahma said, “On hearing the words of Vyasa of enormous wisdom, Sanatkumara spoke, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of lord Siva.”

Sanatkumara said, “Indra and other gods scorched by their brilliance and getting distressed, consulted one another and sought refuge in Brahma.

Bowing in reverence to Brahma, and circumambulating him, they placed their tales of sufferings before him, availing of the proper opportunity.”

The gods said, “O Brahma, the dwellers of the heaven are facing the enormous distress by Maya, the virtual ruler of the three cities, together with the sons of Taraka.

Therefore, O Brahma, we people have approached you, after suffering at the hands of the demons. You kindly think of ways and means to kill him, in order to relieve us from the sufferings.

Sanatkumara said, “At this prayer of the gods, Brahma- the creator, smilingly said to the gods who had been suffering at the hands of Mayadanava.”

Brahma said, “O Gods, Don’t be so much afraid of the daitya. I shall make arrangement for the destruction of the demon. Siva will do everything for you.

He had risen because of his achieving the boon from me. Therefore, I cannot kill him. Tne merits are always on the rise in the city of Tripurasura.

Therefore, all of you including Indra, should go to Siva and pray to him. He happens to be the lord of all and in case he is pleased, he would perform your task.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus listening to the words of Brahma, all the gods including Indra, feeling painful, went to the place of Siva.

They bowed in reverence to Siva, who bestows welfare on all the people of the universe, with folded hand and offered prayer to him.”

The gods said, “O Hiranyagarbha, sustainer of the entire universe, O All-pervading lord, salutation to you.

You are the form of Hara, destroyer of all the living beings, you are nirguna, possessing immense lustre; salutation to you.

You are above the age of childhood, youthful and old age, unblemished, illustrious atma-svarUpa of the great bhiitas, uninvolved, and a great soul, salutation to you.

You are the lord of all the living beings, you could shoulder the great burden, remover of the desires, having the form of un-inimical, and immensely, illustrious, salutation to you.

You are the destroyer of the huge forest of the Daityas like the forest fire, you are like the axe for the destruction of the trees in the form of the Daityas, O Holder of the trident, salutation to you.

You are the destroyer of the Mahadaityas, you carry all the weapons, you are lord of Ambika and are Paramesvara, salutation to you.

O Lord of Parvati, the Supreme Soul, Mahesvara, Nilakantha, Rudra as well as the form of Rudra, salutation to you.

You could be known by means of Vedanta, follower of the independent path, you take to the saguna form for the sake of your devotees, while remaining nirguna otherwise, salutation to you.

O Mahadeva, you bestow comforts to all the three lokas, besides being Pradyumna, Vasudeva, salutation to you.

You are Sankarsana, destroyer of Kansa and Canura, Damodara and are completely detached from the world, salutation to you.

O Hrsikesa, Acyuta, Vibhu, Mrda, Ssankara, Adhoksaja, killer of Gajasura, destroyer of Kama, salutation to you. O Consumer of the poison.

You are Narayanadeva, devoted to Narayana, form of Narayana and born of the body of Narayana.

You possess all the forms, you protect people from the terrific hell, destroys of the sins, having the bull as the vehicle, salutation to you.

You provide strength to your devotees, you can change your form in a moment, having several forms, as well as a single form and are the destroyer of the crowds of the demons.

You bestow welfare over the Brahmanas, and cows, you have a thousand forms and a thousand limbs salutation to you.

You are the form of dharma and can be known by means of the Vedas and the beloved of the Vedas, salutation to you.

You are the form of the Vedas, the face of the Vedas (or the reciter), you follow the path of noble conduct, and are approachable through the path of the good conduct.

You are the form of Brahma, form of truth, beloved of truthfulness, you are the truth and can be achieved by means of truth, salutation to you.

You possess illusion, lord of illusion, eager for meeting others, you are the form of Brahman, having emerged from Brahman, salutation to you.

You are the form of tapas of Isa, salutation to you. You bestow the reward of tapas, you are praiseworthy, form of prayer, and can be pleased by prayer, salutation to you.

You get pleased with the following of the 96 commands of the Vedas, you appreciate the prayers, you have the four types of forms (viz.: Sattva, rajas, tamas and nirguna) form of water, and the form of earth, salutation to you.

O Lord, the gods and all others, being excellent, represent your excellence. Among the gods. You are Indra and are the sun among the planets.

You are the Satyaloka, among the lokas, Devaganga among the sacred rivers, the white complexion among the varnas, and you are Manasarovara among the lakes.

You are Himalaya among the mountains. Kamadhenu among the cows, the ocean of milk among the oceans and the gold among the metals.

You are Brahmana among all the varnas, and the king among the people, O Lord Siva. You are Kasi, among the holy places which bestow salvation, and are Prayaga among the places of pilgrimage.

O Mahesvara, you are the crystal among all the stones, lotus out of flowers, and Himalaya among the mountains.

Among the activities, you are the speed, Bhargava among the poets; you are Sarabha among the birds, you are the lion among the ferocious animals.

O Bull-bannered Siva, you are Saligrama among the stones and Naramadalinga among the adorable stones.

O Paramesvara, you are the bull Nandisvara among the animals, Upanisads among the Vedas, the among the sacrificers, you are the cool-rayed moon.

Among the burning things, you are the fire, among the devotees of Siva, you are Visnu, among the Puranas, you are the Mahabharata, among the letters of the alphabets, you are Makar a or Ma.

You are omkara among the blja mantras. Among the killer elements, you are the poison and you are the sky among all-pervading things of all the souls, you are the Supreme souls.

You are the mind among the sense organs, among the charitable gifts, you are the gift of freedom from danger, among the sanctifying and the life giving agents, you are considered to be the waters.

Among all acquisitions, you are the acquisition of a son, among those possessing the force, you are the wind, among the daily routine sacred rites, you are the Sandhya worship.

Among all the yajnas, you are the Asvamedha yajna, of all the yugas, you are the satyayuga, among the constellations, you are the Pusya constellation. You are the Amavasya (moonless) among all the tithis.

Of all the seasons, you are the Vasanta (spring) season, among the holy occasions, you are Sankranti (the first day of each month), among the grasses, you are the Kusa grass, and among the trees, you are the Banyan trees.

Among the yugas you are the Vyatipata, among creepers, you are the Soma-creeper, among intellectual activities, you are the virtuous inclination, and among the intimate friends, you are the wife.

O Mahesvara, out of the auspicious activities of the aspirants, you are pranayama, of the twelve Jyotirlinga, you are Visvesvara.

Of all the Kiths and Kins, you are the dharma and of all the asramas, you happen to be the Sanyasa-asrama. You are the supreme liberation in all the vargas. You are Nilalohita among the Rudras.

You are Vasudeva among the gods and are Hanuman among the monkeys. Of all the yajnas, you are the Japa-yajha and are Rama among the carries of the weapons.

You are Citraratha among the Gandharvas, Pavaka or fire among the eight Vasus, among the months, you are the intercalary month, and among the holy rites, you are caturdasi.

Of all the royal elephants, you are Airavata, and the sage Kapila among the Siddhas. You are Ananta among the serpents, of all the manes, you are Aryamana.

You are Kala (time) among those who are the destroyers, Bali among the Daityas, O Lord of all, what is the use of prolonging the prayer, you preside over the entire universe, and remain partially stationed within and partially out of it.”

Sanatkumara said, “In this way all the gods, offered prayer to the Bull-bannered Siva, variously, reciting the divine prayers, which were relevant to the context. All of them including Indra and others were very 98 much distressed, but they were quite shrewd in expressing their selfish interest and therefore they mentioned them to Siva- the trident holder, with folded hands, bending their shoulders, in reverence.”

The gods said, O Lord Mahadeva, the three sons of Tarakasura, have collectively defeated Indra and other gods.

They have usurped the control of the three worlds with them. They have defeated the sages and the Siddhas in all respects, have desecrated the holy places and have destroyed the entire universe.

The terrific daityas usurp all the shares of thQ yajnas of gods, by themselves: obstructing the path of the sages, they have spread adharma or evil everywhere.

The sons of Tarakasura, are immune to death from all. O Lord, all the living beings are working at their command.

Before all the three of them are able to destroy the entire universe, you protect the universe by any means.”

Sanatkumara said, “When Indra and other gods were thus talking, lord Siva listened to them and then spoke.

## Chapter 4 - Receiving of Diksa by the lord of Tripura

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter, the immensely illustrious Visnu, made an illusory human to emerge from his body, who could 103 create obstructions in the religious activities of the Daityas.

His head was clean shaven, was clad in dirty clothes, a dirty sack was hanging from his shoulder and he carried a broom in his hand, which was moved by him at every step.

He carried a duster in his hand, the face was dried up, uttering the word dharma, with anxiety, he offered his salutation to Visnu and stood before him. Then with folded hands, he spoke to lord Hari, “O Hari, the destroyer of the enemies, you kindly get me a command, as to what should be done by me. O Lord, what would be my names, O Lord, what shall be my dwelling place. You kindly tell me?”

Then Lord Visnu, listening to his auspicious words, feeling pleased, said to him.

Visnu said, “O immensely intelligent one born of my body, you undoubtedly are my own form. The purpose for which you have been created, you should understand it, which I am going to speak out to you.

Since you are born out of my body, you can surely do my work. You would be adorable for me even. There is no doubt about it.

You would be known by the name of Arihant and several other names. I shall tell you about the place later. Presently you should listen to me with respect, whatever I speak to you.

O Illusory one, you compose a Sastra of sixteen thousand verses, which should be against the provisions of the Srutis, Smrtis and varnasrama-dharma. The s'dstra should be composed in the Apabhramsa language and there should be emphasis in actions. You shall strain yourself to extend it further.

I shall bestow on you the ability to create it and different kinds of magic arts shall be subservient to you.”

On hearing the words of Visnu, Maya¬purusa, the great soul, bowed to lord Visnu and replied to him.

The shaven head said, “O Lord, let me get your command quickly as to what has to be 104 done by me. By your grace all my efforts shall be fruitful.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, he recited the main tenet in the deceptive philosophy, “Heaven and hell are functioning here itself.”

Then remembering the lotus like feet of Siva, Visnu again said to him, “You better confuse, all the three Daityas living in the three cities.

Making strenuous efforts, you better educate them and then they should be initiated by you. O Great intellect, by doing so, you would not earn any sin whatsoever, at my command.

O Ascetic, undoubtedly, the Vedic and Smarta dhamas would shine and flourish as usual there. But these shall certainly be exploded through this Vidya.

O the one with shaven head, you should go there for the destruction of the people living in the three cities. You propagate the tamasika rites and cause the destruction of the three Cities.

Thereafter, O Great one, you should retire to the desert region and carry on your duties and activities there, till the arrival of the age of Kali.

At the advent of the Kali age, you should propagate your own dharma through your disciples and the grand disciples.

At my command your dharma would certainly spread and prosper. With the following of my command, you would surely achieve my place.

The all powerful lord Visnu, at the desire of lord Siva, issuing the command, then disappeared.

Thereafter the shaven head monk, as per the command of Visnu, made the clever disciples to get ready, the illusory Sastra was himself taught by him.

The four disciples were also like him. They took their seats offering their salutation to lord Hari.

O Sage, Hari too, in order to obey the command of Siva, lovingly spoke to the four 105 disciples.

“At my command, you should also become like your preceptor. You are graceful, you will surely attain the noble goal.

Then all the shaven headed monks followed the heretic cult carried the begging bowls in their hands and covered their mouths with a piece of cloth.

They developed the habit of wearing the dirty clothes and kept silent usually bul occasionally uttered, “Dharma is the immense gain, and is the true essence” or other similai words.

They carried a besom broom made of pieces of clothes in their hands and walked very slowly step by step because they were afraid of injuring living beings.

They, while offering their salutation to the lord delightfully, took their seats in front of their preceptor.

They were grasped by hand the lord, and then handed over to their preceptor and he lovingly uttered their names.

He said, “As you belong to me, similar is the case with these disciples undoubtedly. You happen to be the foremost of all, therefore you would be called with the prefix of Pujya or adorable with their names. They would be worthy of respect.

You people shall also be known by the name of Rsi, yati, and Upadhyaya.

You would be able to use my auspicious name with your own names. My name as Arihanta is the destroyer of sins.

All of you should engage yourself in the activities, which should bestow comforts to the people. You would achieve the excellent stage in case your activities are conducive to the welfare of the people.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter the (shaven head monk) accompanied with his illusofy disciples, delightfully went to Tripura who always acted at the command of Siva.

At the instance of the illusory monk, who had controlled his sense organs, taking to the form of an ascetic, he spreaded his illusion.

He reached an orchard in the city 106 accompanied with his disciples and camping there, he spreaded his illusion.

O Sage, since the people of the city were devoted to lord Siva, his efforts did not meet with success initially, as a result of which the Yati became somewhat disappointed.

Then he remembered lord Visnu, and offered prayer to him in his heart feeling painful at heart, he felt discouraged.

When he remembered Visnu, then Visnu remembered Siva. With his permission he remembered Narada.

With the remembering of lord Visnu, by the Yati, the sage Narada reached there. He offered his salutation to him and took his seat before the Visnu, with folded hands.

Then Visnu, who was the foremost among the intellectuals said to Narada, “You are always engaged in doing good to the people and perform the task of the gods.

O Excellent one, I am speaking on behalf of lord Siva. You at once go to Tripura, where a Rsi with his disciples has gone in order to confuse the people there.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of lord Visnu, Narada went to the place where the illusory saint had gone.

At the command of lord Visnu, the lord of illusion, Narada received diksa from that Rsi there.

Then Narada went to the lord of the city of Tripura, after enquiring about his welfare, said to him.”

Narada said, “A Yati, who is quite a religious one and well-versed in all the lores, besides the Vedas has arrived in your city.

I have come across several Dharmas, but has found none comparable to the one (propounded by him). Impressed with his Sanatana Dharma, I have myself received diksa from him.

O Lord of the Daityas, in case you be interested in that dharma you can also receive diksa from him.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to his important words, feeling surprised at heart, the king of the Daityas was confused.

He thought, “When Narada has received diksa, let me also do the same.” Thus thinking, he himself went to that place.

Observing the form of that Rsi he was confused with his illusion. Offering his salutation to the sage, he said to him”

The lord of Tripura said, “O Sage, with a spotless heart, you kindly bestow diksa on me. I really intend to be your disciple.”

Thus listening to the spotless words of the king of Daityas, the Sanatana Sage said.

I shall bestow diksa on you, in case you obey my command otherwise I would not do so even by making crores of efforts.”

Hearing these words, the king was overpowered with the illusion. He at once spoke to the Yati, folding his hands.”

The Daityas said, “I shall act as per your command and shall never disobey you.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the lord of Daityas, removing the cloth from his face, the excellent Rsi said.

“O Lord of the Daityas, you receive diksa which is the best of all the dhamas. Be successful by receiving diksa, appropriately.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking the illusory sage, gave him diksa according to the rules of his religion, appropriately.

After the receiving of diksa by the king of Daityas, as a natural process, all the people of Tripura were also initiated.

O Sage, thereafter the city was filled with the disciples and semi-disciples of the illusory sage.

## Chapter 5 - Fascination of Tripuras

Vyasa said, “When the lord of the demons was so initiated by the deceptive sage, well- versed in the magical art, what did the sage say and what did the Daitya ruler do?”

Sanatkumara said, “After bestowing diksa on the demon king, the Arihant ascetic, followed by his disciples, Narada and others, spoke to the Daitya king.”

The Arihant said, “O King of the Daityas, listen to my statement, which is filled with wisdom. It is the essence of the Vedanta and bears high esoteric importance.

The entire universe is eternal. It has no creator, nor is it the object of creation. It evolves by itself and is destroyed by itself.

There are several creatures right from Brahma to the blade of grass, which are gods on to themselves. There is no other god.

Brahma, Visnu, Rudra and others are merely the names of the embodied beings just as my name is Arihant etc.

When the time arrives the bodies perish, similarly the bodies of all others from Brahma to mosquito, perish at the appropriate time.

In case we think over deeply there is no special feature or the excess of merits in any particular body, because the food, conjugal pleasures, sleep and fear are common to all.

By consuming food and water of the required quantity, all the living beings derive the similar satisfaction, which is neither less nor more.

One is relieved of the thirst after the consuming of water. This is the case with all. There is hardly any difference at any stage.

Even if a person has thousands of women with him but at the time of the intercourse only one could be made use of.

Inspite of a person having hundreds of high breed horses, but only one could be used for the purpose of riding it.

A pleasure one gets by sleeping in a comfortable bed, the same comfort is derived by a person getting anxious for sleep by sleeping over the ground.

As the human beings are afraid of death, the same feeling pervades in all the living beings right from Brahma to an insect.

In case one considers with wisdom, then all the living beings are equal. With this resolve, no one should cause death to others by any means.

There is no other dharma better than to extend compassion on all the living beings. Therefore all the people should extend compassion on all the creatures.

With the protection of a Jiva the entire universe is protect and by killing a person, one earns the sin of killing all the three lokas. Therefore one should not kill but protect others.

Ahimsa (non-violence) is the supreme dharma. It is sinful to cause injury to the soul of others. Salvation lies in the fact that a person is not subservient to others. The heaven is reflected by enjoying all the desired pleasures.

This has been ordained by the ancient acaryasn, with examples. Therefore a person who is afraid of the sufferings in a hell, should not resort to killings.

Among the mobiles and immobiles of the three worlds, there is no sin worse than the killing of others. The one who resorts to killings surely falls in the hell, and the person who does not do so, achieves the heaven.

There are several types of charities, which yield little reward but a person who bestow safeguard to others, no charity could be comparable to it.

After deep thinking, the ancient Rsis have described four types of charities in the world, which provide comfort in the present as well as the future life.

These are to provide safeguard to be frightened person, to provide medicines to the ailing persons, to provide education to the students and food to the hungry person.

Whatever further charities have been prescribed by the sages they do not compare well with providing of the safeguard or protection to the needy person.

Without caring for the strength or influence of the mantras, gems and the medicines, for the earning of the name and artha (riches) one should practice for them making all the efforts.

By earning enormous riches, is useful only for the propitiation of the twelve organs of senses. The propitiation of other things is of no consequence.

The twelve organs of senses are the five organs of activity and the five organs of knowledge together with the mind and activity.

The heaven and the hell for the living beings exist here on earth alone and nowhere else. Happiness is the heaven and misery is the hell.

In case one meets with his end enjoying all the comforts, the philosophies well-versed in the tattvas call it the moksa or liberation.

The philosophers and the thinkers, consider that when the pain comes to an end, alongwith its impression, and in case the ignorance too disappears, it is considered to be the biggest salvation.

The persons well-versed in the Vedas, consider this statement as quite authentic that one should neither kill anyone himself nor should he be inclined to cause injury to others.

The learned people feel that the encouraging of the slaughter of animals in the Vedas, cannot beheld as authoritative. To say that violence is permissible in the yajnas is a faulty view of the wicked people.

It is really surprising that those desirous of achieving heaven have to resort to the felling of the trees, killing of the animals, making a muddy mess with blood and by pouring oil and ghee into the fire.”

Thus explaining his view to Tripura, educating thus all the people (in the new dharma), the Yati then again spoke with respect.

“One should believe in the elements, which apparently cause comforts to the body and have been contained in the Buddhistic theology and which are consistent with the Vedic hymns.

It is said in the Vedas that the bliss is an aspect of the Brahma and this statement of the Vedas is correct. It would not be proper to conceive of various other gods.

One should enjoy all the comforts upto the time the body is healthy, the sense organs are not deformed and the old age is at bay.

After becoming sick, when the sense organs are faded out, and on the arrival of the old age, one is deprived of all the comforts. Therefore the persons desirous of comforts should give away their own bodies to the beggars.

The one who after his birth is unable to please the beggars, he becomes the burden of the earth and the ocean the forests or the mountains.

The body is ready to go in a trice and with this belief, one should keep the body healthy.

The body is the food for the dogs, crows and the insects and gets vanished, when it is reduced to ashes. This has been ordained by the Vedas.

Whatever differences in castes are visible in the world, are all false. When all are man, then who is superior and who is inferior?

The ancient people declared that the creation was started with Brahma, who had the sons named Daksa and Marici.

Kasyapa, the son of Marici, married thirteen beautiful daughters of Daksa Prajapati, according to the Vedic rites.

But the people of the present times, whose intelligence and strength are but a truthful, unnecessarily struggle whether, it was proper or improper.

The ancient people believe that the four castes emerged out the face, arms thighs etc. of Brahma but when we think it deeply, this statement does not appeal.

Now the question is when four sons are born of the body of a person, could they be of different castes?

Therefore this caste system is beyond understanding. Therefore one should not make any difference among the humans.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, thus speaking to the king of the Daityas and the people, the sage, together with his disciples, desecrated quite respectfully, the Vedic dharma.

Then he denounced the womanly virtues of chastity and the manly virtues of controlling of the organs of senses.

Similarly he denounced the institution of gods, the systems of sraddhas, yajnas, vratas performing of sraddha at the holy places besides other such practices.

He also denounced, the appropriate worship of Siva, adoration of linga, Visnu, Surya, Ganesa and other gods.

Then the Yati, who was the foremost of the illusory people, also denounced particularly the taking of bath, giving of charities, celebration of festivals etc.

O Narada, what more shall I speak? The illusory Yati, denounced all the aspects of the Vedic dharma.

Taking shelter under the Yati dharma, all the women of Tripura siva disowned their devotion towards their husbands.

The fascinated men indulged in seduction and became successful in gaining access to the wives of others.

The maid-servants in the harems, the princes, the people of the city, and the ladies were perfectly enchanted by him.

In this way, when all the people of the city became averse to dharma, the adharma or evil started spreading quite speedily in the city with delight.

At the command of Visnu, the god of gods, the poverty itself entered the city of Tripura.

The riches which the people had achieved quite gracefully from the supreme lord, left the place, at the command of Brahma.

With the bestowing of the confusion of wisdom, created by lord Visnu by his illusion, over the demons, Narada felt successful.

Upto that stage Narada also remained in an .illusory form, but by the grace of lord Visnu, he remained free from blemish.

O Sage, at the desire of lord Siva, the king of Daityas together with his brothers and Maya, was deprived of his prowess.

## Chapter 6 - Prayer of Siva

Vyasa said, “O Illustrious Sanatkumara, when the king of Daityas was so deluded with his brothers and the people of the city, what happened thereafter, you kindly tell me.

Sanatkumara said, “When the demon Tripura was so deluded, leaving the adoration of Siva, he discarding the chastity and resorted to evil ways.

Lord Visnu, the spouse of Laksmi, felt successful, and went to Kailasa, accompanied with the gods.

On Visnu’s arrival at Kailasa with the gods, then Brahma, who had been engaged in meditation, mentally came to know of the happening there. Then Visnu-Purusottama, eulogised the lord, offering all the prayers.

Visnu said, “O Mahesvara, O Lord, O Supreme soul, O Lord, O Narayana, Rudra, Brahma and the Supreme Brahman, salutation to you.”

Thus praising him and prostrating before Mahadeva and he recited the name of Daksinamurti Siva five lakhs of times.

At that point of time the mind of all the gods had been attracted towards Siva.

The gods said, “You are the soul of all, O Siva, you relieve all of all the miseries, O Rudra, O Nilakantha, form of consciousness, Praceta, salutation to you.

You relieve people of all the misfortunes and are our protector. You destroy the enemies of the gods, and you are always adorable for us, salutation to you.

Your are eternal and the prime cause. You are blissful and indestructible. O Lord you are the creator of the Prakrti and Purusa, besides being the lord of the universe.

You are the creator of the entire universe besides being its sustainer as well as the destroyer. You are the form of Brahma, Visnu and Siva, besides those of Sattva, rajas and tamas.

You are the one who redeems the universe. You are the indestructible lord of all. You are the bestower of boons, you are the subject and out of the content of the speech.

You are the foremost in the Yogavidya, the best of the Yogis, adore you for salvation. You dwell in the lotus like hearts of the yogis.

The Vedas conceive you as the form of Brahman, you are a heaped mass of splendour, besides being greater than the greatest.

O Illustrious one, you are treated as the Supreme Soul in this world. O Lord Sarva, Lord of the three worlds.

O Preceptor of the universe, you are the smaller than the smallest and bigger than the biggest, who could be seen, heard and adored besides being known.

You have the limbs like hands, feet, eyes, heads, faces, ears and noses on all the sides, therefore we offer our salutation to you on all the sides.

You are omniscient, all-pervading one, lord of all, the blossoming one, form of the universe, O Virupaksa, I bow in reverence to you from all the sides.

You are the lord of all, lord of the universe, the truth, Siva, the best of all and possess the lustre of crores of suns. Salutation to you.

You are the god of the universe, you are without the beginning or the end, you are the possessor of the thirty six virtues (gunas) and activiser of everything. Salutation to you.

You activate Prakrti, the grand sire of all, the lord of all the bodies, salutation to you from all the sides.

You are the abode of the Vedas and those who are well-versed in the Vedas, you are the bestower of the boons, are self bom and know the essence of the Srutis.

We could never be a witness to all what has been done by you, but the gods, demons, Brahmanas, the mobiles and immobiles, describe you as the creator.

O Siva, you are dear to the gods, destroying the asuras in a moment, you relieve the gods of their sufferings, you save the gods who have been placed in a precarious condition.

O Paramesvara all of them have been overpowered with your delusion. With the method adopted by Visnu, they have fallen from dharma.

O Lord, well-disposed towards your devotees, presently, they, because of our good fortune, disowning the Saiva faith have embraced the Buddhist faith.

O Granter of refuge, you always perform the task of the gods. We have taken refuge with you. Now you do whatever you like.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus eulogising Siva, the gods humbly stood there with folded hands and lowering their heads.

Thus Indra and other gods offered prayer to Siva, who getting pleased with the adoration, arrived there mounted over the bull.

Getting down from Nandi, he embraced Visnu, and feeling delighted, Siva lovingly patted the back of Nandi and then looked at all the gods.

Casting a compassionate glance at them, Siva, the lord of Parvati, spoke to Visnu in a deep voice.

Siva said, “O Lord of gods, I have well understood about the task of the gods besides the delusion of Visnu and the intelligent Narada.

Best of the gods, I shall surely destroy Tripura the lord of the asuras who is quite an evil one.

But the great Daitya had been my firm devotee. The one who discarded the dharma would be killed at my hands.

Let Visnu or my one else kill him who has made him to leave his dharma. Presently all the people of Tripura, are averse to my devotion.”

Listening to these words of Siva, O Excellent sage, all the gods felt sad.

Finding Visnu and all other gods feeling so sad, Brahma, the creator of the world spoke to with folded hands.

Brahma said, “You are the foremost of the people well-versed in yoga-vidya. You are the supreme lord besides being the Supreme Brahman and the protector of the gods and the ascetics. Therefore no sin is involved in killing the demons.

They were actually deluded at your command. You in fact inspired them. They have discarded the dharma besides adoring you. Inspite of that no one else can kill them.

Therefore, O Mahadeva, protector of the lives of the gods and the ascetics, for the sake of the protection of the sages, you kindly kill those Mlecchas.

A king does not earn sin in case he acts in a religious manner. Therefore the thorns have to be removed for the protection of the noble people as well as the Brahmanas.

Even an ordinary king would do so in case he maintains his sway. You have the suzerainty of all the worlds, therefore you must protect them expeditiously.

O God of gods, lord Visnu, Rsis, sages, yajnas, Vedas and Sastras are all under your domain.

O Lord, you are the exclusive emperor of all besides being the lord of all. Hari and the entire universe is your own kiths and kins.

O Lord beyond birth, Hari happens to be your crown prince. I being Brahma happen to be your priest. Indra who always obeys your command is your royal servant.

O Lord of all, the gods are also bound by your role. All of them perform their duties daily. There is no doubt about it.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Brahma, Siva, the protector of the gods, delightfully, said to Brahma.”

“Siva said, “O Brahma, you have described me as the emperor of the gods, but I do not have any means to accept this position.

I do not have a divine chariot or a charioteer. I also do not have the divine bow and arrow for achieving victory in the battle.

I have no chariot, seated in which I could be able to kill the powerful Daityas.”

Sanatkumara said, “Then all the gods including Brahma, Visnu and others, collectively said to lord Mahesvara, offering their salutation to him.

The gods said, “O Lord Siva, we shall transform ourselves us as a chariot and get ready for the war.”

Thus speaking and receiving the consent of Siva, the gods felt delighted folding their hands and spoke to one another individually.

## Chapter 7 - Prayer of Siva by the gods

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the gods and others, Siva who is the well- wisher of the people and well-disposed towards his devotees, lovingly accepted their prayer.

O Sage, in the meantime, Parvati, accompanied with both her sons, arrived there, where Siva was seated.

At the arrival of Parvati, all the gods including Visnu, and others feeling surprised, humbly offered their salutation to her.

O Sage, all of them shouted the slogans of victory. Then they kept quiet being unaware of the cause of the arrival of Parvati.

Feeling surprised all of them praised Parvati. Then she spoke to her husband who was quite clever in the divine sports.

The goddess said, “O Lord, you are the best among those having the sons, look at Kartikeya, who is playing having been adorned with the best of ornaments.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus listening to the words of the mother of the universe, lord Siva was never satisfied by drinking the nectar of a gaze at the face of Kartikeya.

He paid no attention at the gods who had been suffering. Then he embraced Skanda and he felt delightful, by smelling his head.

Then Parvati, after consulting Siva on some important issues, stood up for returning.

Then Siva, the player of the divine sports, accompanied by Kartikeya, Nandi and Parvati, having been adored by all the gods returned to his abode.

Then all the gods becoming anxious, were seated at the gate of the abode of Siva, feeling disgusted.

They started thinking, “What should be done? Where should we go? Who would relieve us of our miseries. Oh! we are finished. What has happened now?

Indra and other gods were totally upset, looking at one another and started cursing their fate.

They thought, “We are sinful people and the Daityas are virtuous.”

In the meantime a great gana of Siva, known as Kumbhodara arrived there and he struck the gods with baton.

All the gods feeling panicky and uttering miserable words, fled from the place. The sages fell down, getting upset.

Indra, getting upset, crawled on his feet. The celestial sages fell down over the ground, getting upset.

Feeling equally painful, all the gods and the sages, collectively then went to Brahma and Visnu. Kasyapa and other sages went to Brahma and Visnu having compassionate temperament.

Kasyapa said, “This is all due to the luck.” Then all of them said to Visnu, who removes the sufferings of all.

Some of the Brahmarsis said, “The task could not be established because of our ill- luck.” Some of them felt surprised as to how could it happen?”

O Sage, listening to the words of Kasyapa and other sages, Visnu, assuring the gods and the sages, said, “O Gods and the sages, you listen to my words with respect. Why do you feel painful? You better get relieved of sorrows.

O God think over this, it is not an easy task to propitiate the great people. It is well-known that there is great difficulty at first in propitiating the great. The lord will certainly be pleased, after coming to know about your resolute nature.

Siva is the lord of all the gods. You carefully think in your mind as to how could the lord of the ganas be made favourable immediately.

O Intellectuals, the following mantra should be recited. Utter the syllable omkara first then repeat the word namah. Then Sivaya (Siva) is to be spoken. The Subham has to be uttered twice and then Kuru twice. Thereafter you say Sivaya namah orh.

In case you repeat this mantra a crore times devoting your mind to Siva, he will surely carry out your task.”

O Sage, at these words of the powerful Visnu, the gods started adoration of Siva in the same manner. All the gods including Brahma and Visnu, devoting their minds to Siva, adored him.

All the gods including Brahma and Visnu, devoting their minds towards Siva, and for the establishing of the task of the sages, started reciting the mantra.

O Excellent sage, all the gods, keeping patience, thus recited Siva-mantra a crore times.

In the meantime Siva came into direct view assuming his real form and said to them.

Lord Siva said, “O Visnu, O Brahma, O Gods, O Auspicious sages, I have been pleased with your recitation. You now ask for the desired boon.”

The gods said, “O Siva, the lord of gods, O Lord of the universe, O Sankara, in case you are really pleased with us, then finding the gods to be in a precarious condition, kill the demon Tripura.

O Lord Siva, O Merciful one, O Friend of the distressed, you kindly protect us. You have always and repeatedly protected us.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Brahma, Visnu and other gods, O Narada Siva spoke.

Siva said, “O Brahma, O Visnu, you better listen to my words with respect. The three cities have been as good as destroyed.

You first of all build the divine chariot, the charioteer and the arrow urgently, as already promised by you.

O Brahma, O Visnu, then you better decorate me as the emperor of the three worlds.

You are responsible for the creation and upkeep of the universe and as such, you help the gods keeping in mind that the Tripura or the three cities have already been destroyed.

The mantra which has been recited by you, bestows great merit, and pleases me the most. The same mantra, which fulfilling all the desires, bestows the pleasures and salvation, besides granting comforts to the devotees of Siva.

The mantra is quite graceful, bestows glory, increases the age. It bestows heaven to those desirous of heaven. Those who are free from desires, it bestows salvation to them.

A person, who purifying himself, would recite this mantra daily, listens to it, or narrates it to some one else, all his desires are fulfilled.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus listening to the words of lord Siva, Brahma, Visnu and other gods, were pleased.

Then at their command, Visvakarma, for the welfare of the world, made a splendid chariot of excellent nature, consisting of all the gods.

## Chapter 8 - Making of a divine chariot by Visvakarma

Vyasa said, “O Omniscient one, O Possessor of noble wisdom, O Best of the devotees of Siva, O Dear one, O Sanatkumara, you have narrated the astonishing story of Siva.

Now you please speak about the building of the divine chariot, which was made by Visvakarma, for the sake of Siva.

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the sage Vyasa, Sanatkumara- the excellent sage, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva said.

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, O Immensely wise Vyasa, I now according to my wisdom, remembering the lotus like feet of Siva, shall speak about the building of the chariot for lord Siva.

Visvakarma built a divine chariot for Siva, representing the entire universe, with devotion.

It was made of gold comprising of all the five elements. The sun served as the right wheel, while the moon served as the left wheel.

The right wheel had twelve spokes; while number of spokes in the left wheel was sixteen. O Narada the twelve spokes of the right wheel, represented the twelve suryas.

O Suvrata, the sixteen spokes in the left wheel represented the sixteen digits of the moon. The left wheel was also decorated with the constellations

O Narada, the six seasons, constituted the rims of the wheels of the chariot. The puskara of the chariot was the sky and the Mandara mountain was the inner side of the chariot.

The pole shafts of the chariot comprised of the mountains of the rising and the setting sun. Mahameru was the basic support and the Kesara mountains were the sharp sides.

Samvatsara (year) happened to be its force, the two Ayanas (both north and south) were the functions of the wheels and axles The muhurtas constituted the bondages of the chariot and the Kalas were the nails of the yoke.

The division of time kastha constituted the nose of the chariot and the ksanas were the axle shafts. The bottom of the chariot was comprised of the nemisas, while the poles comprised of the division of time.

The fender of the chariot was made of firmament. The heaven and the salvation were the flag staffs. Abhramu and Kamadhenu constituted its horrows at the ends of the shafts. The unmanifest principle, made their shafts and cosmic intellect were the chariot’s reeds. The cosmic ego cosmic corners and elements were its strength.

O Excellent sage, the cosmic sense organs constituted the embellishments of the chariot on all sides. Faith was its movements.

The six Vedangas represented the ornaments, O Great one of the good rites, the Puranas, Nyaya, Mimamsa and the Dharma- sastras constituted the small ornaments.

The excellent mantras forceful with their syllables were the feet, of all characteristic features and the stages, in life constituted the bells issuing the tinkling sound.

The serpent Ananta with possessing a thousand hoods, constituted its fittings and the main as well as the subsides quarters and the pedestals of the chariot.

The clouds like the Puskara and others represented the gem-studded banners of different colours. The four oceans were conceived as the bullocks of the chariot.

The Ganga and other rivers resplendent with excellent female forms, adorned with all the ornaments held the fly-whisks in their hands.

They took their respective positions in different parts of the chariot, illumining the same. The seven courses of the wind including Avaha and others, became the seven beautiful steps of the chariot

The lokaloka mountain served as the steps all round, which were quite bright as well as oblique.

The mountains surrounding it on all the sides were considered to be its bondages. The bottom surface of the chariot comprised of the people of the nether-world.

Lord Brahma served as the charioteer of the chariot, the gods were holding the reins, omkara served as a whip with Brahma. Brahma was also its god.

Akara served as an umbrella for him, while 123 Mandaracala moved on with a baton in his hand. Sumeru, the king of the mountain served as his bow, while the serpent of Siva served as the cord of the bow.

Sarasvati, the form as Vedas served as the bell for the chariot. The immensely illustrious Visnu, served as the bow, the tip of which was represented by the god Agni.

O Sage, all the four Vedas served as the steed of the chariot. The remaining planets became their embellishments.

His army emerged from the poison, the winds served as his feathers and the wings. Vyasa and other sages were the drivers of the vehicle.

O Great sage, why should I elaborate. Whatever things were available in the world were used in the chariot.

At the command of Brahma and Visnu, Visvakarma had built a beautiful chariot making all the efforts.

## Chapter 9 - Siva’s march for waging the war

Sanatkumara said, “Thus yoking the Vedas in the form of steed in the great and divine chariot with numerous surprises, the same was presented by Brahma to Siva.

Then Visnu and other gods making several types of prayers to Siva, seated him in the chariot.

Then lord Siva was mounted over the divine chariot representing all the gods, in which there were numerous scaffoldings attached.

At that point of time, all the gods including Brahma and Visnu, the lokapalas, the Rsis, Gandharvas, serpents, and others started eulogising Siva.

He was surrounded by the apsaras well- versed in dance and music. Then Siva, the bestower of boons, felt pleased looking at his charioteer.

When Siva was about to take his seat, the chariot in which all the lokas had been enshrined, at the same time the horses in the form of the Vedas had a head on fall on the ground.

The entire earth and the mountains were shaken. Unable to bear the weight even the serpent Sesa started shaking.

Then lord Dharma who carried the earth in the form of a bull, lifted up the chariot in a moment.

Being unable to bear the resplendence of Siva seated in the chariot, he also felt defeated.

Holding the rains in his hands, Brahma, delightfully, yoked again the steed in the form of the Vedas, in chariot at the command of lord Siva.

Then Brahma drove the horses who could move with the force of the mind and the wind.

After Siva was seated in the chariot, the chariot moved through the sky way, towards the city of the Danavas with great speed.

Then lord Siva, looking at the gods, said to them, “In case you declare me as the lord of the animals (Pasupati) then I shall surely kill the demons.

O Best of gods, and other people, by the excellent demons could be killed only after assigning separate separate animal-hood bi the gods and other and not otherwise»

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of the lord with wisdom, they became dispirited getting suspicious of the animalhood.

On knowing about the feelings of the gods, Siva, the lord of god and consort of Parvati, displayed his sympathy with the gods and laughingly said.

Siva said, “O Excellent gods, you will not fall even in your animal-hood. Let it be heard and let the process of animal-hood be practiced.

The one who performs the divine Pas'upata rites, he would surely be relieved of the animal-hood. I assure this to you. Be careful.

Even the people with other faith, if follow 125 the Pasupata-Vrata, then O Gods, they would also be relieved of the animalhood.

Those who would adore me for twelve, six, or three years continuously, they would be relieved of the animal-hood.

O Gods, therefore, you also perform the divine and excellent Pasupata-Vrata, as a result of which you would also be relieved of the animal-hood. There is no doubt about it.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Siva- the supreme soul, all the gods including Brahma and Visnu, accepted them.

O Lord, because of this, all the gods and the animals became the animals and Pasupati- Rudra became the remover of the noose or the bondages of the animals.

Since that date, Siva came to be known by the name of Pasupati, which bestows all the comforts.

Then Siva, the lord of gods, pleased all the gods including Brahma, Visnu, Rsis and others who started praising him, shouting the slogans of victory.

The grandeur of the form of Siva at that point of time can hardly be described even in hundred years.

Thus Akhilesvara Siva, who bestows pleasure on all, accompanied with Parvati, marched on for the killing of Parvati.

At the time of departure of Siva, for the killing of Tripura, he wras followed by the illustrious gods, the elephants, the horses, lions, chariots, and bulls etc.

They were equipped with the weapons like the ploughs, Sulas, musals, bhusindis (guns), stones and several other solid weapons. All the gods carrying such weapons, in their hands, marched towards the battle-field.

Indra, Brahma, Visnu and others, carrying several types of weapons, and illumining at the same time, celebrating variously, shouting the slogans for the victory of Siva, moved ahead.

At that point of time the Rsis decorating their heads with the matted locks of hair, holding the dandas in their hands, felt delighted, while the caranas showered flowers from the sky.

O Narada, while marching on towards Tripura, who was competent enough to count the number of the leaders of the ganas? Still I would like to speak out the same.

Bhrngi- the chief of the Siva-ganas surrounded by the lords of the ganas and the gods, went speedily to destroy the three cities like Mahendra seated in an aerial chariot.

The names of the important leaders were Kesa, Vigatavasa, Mahakesa, Mahajvara, Somavallisavarna, Somapa, Sanaka, Somadhrk, Suryavarcas, Suryapresanka, Suryaksa, SQrinaman, Sura, Sundara, Praskanda, Kundara, Canda, Kampana, Atikampana, Indra, Indrajava, Yantr, Himakara, Salaksa, Pancaksa, Saharaksa, Mahodara, Satijhru, Satasya, Ranka, Karapuraputana, Dvisikha, Trisikha, Ahamkarakaraka, Ajavaktra, Astavaktra, Hayakaraka and Ardhavaktra. These and other lords of ganas, who were innumerable, can hardly be characterised and classified. All of them marched on and surrounding Siva.

When they were so marching with Siva- the holder of the bow, they were mentally prepared to reduce to ashes, all the mobile and immobile living beings.

Siva, the carrier of the bow, was himself competent enough to reduce to ashes the entire universe, therefore the burning of Tripura was not at all a big thing for him. What is the use of the chariot, the bow, his own ganas as well as the Devaganas?

O Vyasa, still Siva, the holder of the bow, for the destruction of the three cities of Tripura, for the sake of the gods, himself marched on with his own as well as the Devaganas. This happens to be his astonishing sport.

O Excellent sage, I shall speak out the reason for the same. It was so done for the destruction of the sins of others and for spreading his glory in the universe.

Another reason was to assure the wicked people that Siva was supreme, of all the gods.

## Chapter 10 - Burning of Tripura

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter lord Siva, possessing all the equipments in the chariot, got ready for the performing of the task of the gods.

The lord stood there in pratyalidha posture for a hundred thousand years. The bow was well strung, and kept near the head. The arrow was fixed, the fingers were clenched firmly at the bow. The eyes were concentrated.

Ganesa was stationed at the thumb. During this time, the three cities, did not come within the target path of the trident holder Siva.

Then Siva, the holder of the bow, also known as Virupaksa, heard a pleasant divine voice from the sky.

The akasavani said, “O Siva, the lord of the universe, unless you adore Ganesa, you will not be able to destroy these cities.”

On hearing this Siva the destroyer of Andhakasura, summoned Bhadrakali and then adored Ganesa.

After adoring Ganesa appropriately, and pleasing him, lord Siva looked at the sky.

He found that three cities of the sons of Taraka, were stuck to one another.

It is said, that when the great lord Siva, the lord of gods, the Supreme Brahman, worshipped by all, is there, it would not be proper to say, that he achieved success by another god’s grace.

He is independent, the great Brahman, who possessed and was at the same time devoid of attributes. He is invisible the supreme soul and unblemished or spotless.

He himself is the form of Pancadevas and is adorable by the five gods. He is the Supreme lord and it is not necessary for him to adore anyone. On the contrary, he is adorable by all.

Or otherwise, O Sage, but everything is possible because of the sports of Siva- the god of gods and the bestower of the boons.

When the adoration of Ganesa was completed by Siva, then all the three cities of Tripura were joined together, which delighted all the gods and the sages.

Then all the gods, the Siddhas, and the sages, shouted the slogans of victory and adored Siva, who had eight cosmic bodies.

Then Brahma and Visnu the lords of the worlds, said, “The time for the killing of asuras has arrived, O Great god. The three cities of the sons of Taraka, have been united. Therefore, O Lord perform the task of the gods.

O Lord of the gods, kindly shoot the arrow, lest they are separated again.”

Then stringing the bow quite tightly, and fixing the arrow Pasupata, worthy of worship, he thought of Tripuras.

Then Mahadeva, who was well-versed in the performing of the excellent divine sport, looked at it contemptuously.

Virupaksa, was competent to destroy all the cities in a moment. He is protector of the noble people. This should be known to all.

O Lord of the gods, Siva is competent enough to reduce the entire universe to ashes with his mere look. You better use the arrow for the sake of our glory.”

Thus Brahma, Visnu and all the gods, prayed to Siva. Thereafter he desired for the destruction of Tripura, with the shooting of his arrow.

On the arrival of the long desired muhurta, stretching the cord the astonishing bow, he created the deafening sound.

Then challenging the great demon and announcing his name, Siva, shot an arrow having the lustre of the sun.

The arrow which was the destroyer of the sins, resembling Visnu, burnt the Daityas in their abodes in Tripura.

All the three cities, which had been spread upto the four oceans, fell on earth, after having been reduced to ashes.

Because of discarding the worship of Siva, hundreds of Daityas were burnt out with the fire of the arrow.

Then Tarakaksa, with his brothers while dying devoted his mind towards Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees.

With his heart having been filled with the immense devotion of Siva, he prayed to Siva, mentally.

Ḍrakṁksṁ said, “O Siva, I have realised that you are pleased with all our brothers. When will you bum us again like this?

Today we have witnessed your form which is beyond the imagination of the gods as well as the demons. Therefore (we pray) that we should remain devoted to you in all our future births.”

O Sage, thus speaking, the Danavas, at the command of Siva, were burnt in that fire.

O Vyasa, all the young and the old Danavas there, were also reduced to ashes at the command of Siva.

All the ladies, men and their vehicles, were burnt in fire as the universe is reduced to ashes at the time of dissolution.

Some of the best women were embracing their husbands, some of them were sleeping. Some of them had been tired after enjoying the sex play with their husbands.

Some of them were half burnt, but they were also fainted with delusion. With the fire of the burning of Tripura not even a slightest thing could escape destruction, irrespective of its being mobile or immobile. All were burnt out. Only the indestructible Visvakarma or Maya could escape death.

He was not the opponent of the gods, therefore, he escaped from the wrath of Siva. Actually Siva, protects his devotees taking refuge with him even in great danger.

Irrespective of anyone being a daitya or someone, else, whose collective performance was not destructive, he was saved, while others of the evil activities were burnt in the fire.

Therefore all efforts should be made by the noble people to avoid evil activities, by which the people have to face destruction.

No contact with the people of Tripura should be developed. This is the opinion of all. But by chance if it happens, let it happen.

Those who worshipped Siva, with their kiths and kins, attained the region of Ganapati subsequently.

## Chapter 11 - Prayer by gods after witnessing the awful form of Siva

Vyasa said, “O Great intellectual Sanatkumara, the devotee of Siva, son of Brahma, you are graceful. What did the gods do after the burning of Tripura?

Where did Mayadanava go? Where did the lords of Tripura go after they were burnt out. In case the story is related to Siva in any way, then narrate the same to me.

Suta said, “Thus listening to the words of Vyasa, Sanatkumara, the son of Brahma, remembering the lotus like feet of Siva, and spoke.

Sanatkumara said, “O Immensely intelligent Vyasa, the son of Parasara, Siva was engaged in worldly sports, listen to his story, which washes away all the sins.

When all the three cities of the Tripura were burnt out by Siva, then the gods felt extremely surprised.

The gods like Visnu, Indra and others, looking at the resplendent face of Siva and feeling nervous kept quiet.

Siva with Parvati, was looking extremely awful, having the terrific form, the lustre of whom put in blaze all the directions, resembling the lustre of crores of suns of the time of dissolution.

Finding Siva and Parvati in this state, all the gods were frightened, who stood there getting frightened lowering their heads.

The excellent sages finding the army of the gods having been frightened, he kept mum and stood quietly on all the four sides.

Looking at the terrific form ot Siva, the frightened Brahma, keeping alert, started offering prayer to Siva delightfully with the gods.

At that point of time, the frightened god of gods, lord Visnu, prayed to Mahesvara, Bhava, Hara, Tripurari, subservient to his devotees, together with Parvati.

Brahma said, O God of gods, O Mahadeva, O Compassionate over the devotees, you are the lord of the universe, blissful, O Lord Siva, O Parmesvara, O Siva, be pleased with us.

You are the form of omkara, you redeem all the jivas, you are destroyer of Tripura, O Mahesvara, salutation to you.

You are the lord with many names. You are favourite of the devotees, you are free from attributes; you are greater than Prakrti and Purusa, salutation to you.

You are unblemished, eternal, spotless, divine and possess the three gunas. Salutation to you.

You possess attributes, lord of the heaven, Sadasiva, peaceful, Mahesa, besides the holder of the bow. Salutation to you.

You are omniscient, well-disposed towards those who take refuge in you, besides being Sadyojata, salutation to you.

You are Aghora, well served by the gods, subservient to the devotees, Isan, Varenya, besides being the bestower of the bliss, salutation to you.

O Mahadeva, you better protect all the frightened gods. You have made us beholden to you with the burning of Tripura.”

Thus offering prayer to lord Siva, all the gods including Brahma and others, individually bowed in reverence to him.

Thereafter Brahma, with folded hands, lowering his head offered prayer to Siva.

Brahma said, “O Lord, O Lord of the gods, O Sankara, Mahadeva, let me develop the eternal devotion at your feet.

O Lord of the gods, let me always serve you as your charioteer. O Paramesvara, let you always remain graceful to me.

Sanatkumara said, “In this way Brahma praised Siva with folded hands lowering his head.

Thereafter Visnu also offered prayer to Siva, with folded hands, bowing in reverence to him.

Visnu said, “O Lord of the gods, O Mahesan, Kin of the down trodden, merciful, dear to the devotees, be graceful on us getting pleased.

You are both with and without attributes, salutation to you. You are the form of Prakrti as well as the Purusa. Therefore salutation to you.

You have the Saguna form, you are the soul of the universe, love the devotion, peaceful, Siva and the supreme soul, salutation to you.

O Sadasiva, you are Rudra, the lord of the universe,. salutation to you. Let my devotion towards you get firm and keep on increasing.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, Visnu, who has immensely devoted to Siva, kept quiet. Thereafter all the gods bowing in reverence to Siva, said to him.”

The gods said, “O Lord of the gods, O Mahadeva, O Merciful one, O Siva, the lord of the world, be pleased with us.

All of us delightfully bow in reverence to you let our firm devotion at your feet become everlasting.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus, when Siva was so eulogised by Brahma, Visnu and other gods, Siva, who bestows welfare on the universe, delightfully said.

Siva said, “O Brahma, Visnu and other gods, I am particularly happy today, you better ask for your desired boon.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to these words of Siva, all the gods spoke delightfully.”

All the gods said, “In case you are pleased with us, and intend to bestow a boon, then you considering all of us as your slaves, bestow the boon, that whenever your devotees are in trouble then you would appear on the scene and remove their miseries.

Sanatkumara said, “Thus feeling pleased at the words spoken by Brahma, Visnu and other gods, the delightful Siva said, “Be it so.”

O Gods, I am pleased with the stotras recited by you. Whosoever would read them or listen to them would be bestowed by me with his desired things.”

Thus speaking, Siva, the remover of all the miseries, fulfilled the desires of all (those present there).

## Chapter 12 - Maya’s taking refuge with Siva, bestowing of the Vitalaloka to him and assurance to shaven headed monk that his cult would prosper in Kali age

Sanatkumara said, “In the meantime Mayadanava, who escaped unhurt, by the grace of Siva, arrived there.

He bowed in reverence to Siva and all other gods with folded hands.

Then he got up looking at Siva. He with his voice having been choked he offered prayer to Siva.

Mayadanava said, “O Lord, well-disposed towards your devotees, O Sankara, you are the Kalpavrksa, devoid of any particular leaning towards any side.

O Splendour formed one, salutation to you, O Omniformed, O Auspicious soul, O Holy one, salutation to you.

You have many forms, you are eternal, and are of variegated form, salutation to you. You have the divine form, are yourself divine, salutation to you.

You are the remover the miseries of all your devotees, the noble soul, creator of the three worlds, besides being the sustainer as well as the destroyer. Salutation to you.

You can be achieved with the devotion of the devotees, are merciful, bestower of the reward of the tapas, O lord Siva, salutation to you.

O Paramesvara, you like prayers, but O Lord of all, I am ignorant about the offering of the prayers. I take refuge with you and therefore, you getting pleased on me protect me.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the prayer of Mayadanava, O Excellent Brahmana, lord Siva was pleased, and he eagerly spoke to Maya.”

Siva said, “O Mayadanava, I am pleased with you. O Excellent demon, speak out the boon you desire. I shall surely fulfil your desire. There is no doubt about it.

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the auspicious words of Siva, Maya, the foremost among the asuras, said, “O God of gods, O Mahadeva, in case you are pleased with me and in case I am of worthy of receiving of a boon, then bestow your eternal devotion to me.

O Paramesvara, you be friendly to your devotees always, compassionate on the miserable people and be indifferent towards the wicked and the evil beings.

O Mahesvara, my mind should never 135 develop any evil thoughts. Let me always remain free from danger and remain engrossed in your devotion.”

Sanatkumara said, “When so prayed by Mayadanava, the delightful Siva, who is well- disposed towards his devotees, said to Mayadanava.

Mahesvara said, “O Best of the Danavas, you are quite graceful being my devotee and unblemished. I have presently bestowed all the boons desired by you.

You should proceed to Vitalaloka at my command with your family. It is more charming than the heaven even.

With your mind devoted to me, live there quite happily. At my command no demonic ideas would ever emerge in your mind.”

Sanatkumara said, “Gracefully honouring the command of Siva, bowing in reverence to him as well as the other gods, Mayadanava, proceeded on to Vitalaloka.

Thereafter the monks with shaven heads also left the place. While so leaving, they offered their salutation to Brahma, Visnu and other gods and said to them.”

Where should we go? What should we do? You kindly issue your command to those who are obedient to you.

O Brahma, O Visnu, O gods, by removing the devotion from the minds of the demons, who were devoted to Siva, we have committed a grave sin.

With the opposing to the devotion of Siva, we shall have to dwell in the hell for crores of years. We can be redeemed thereafter.

But you kindly enlighten us to be free from the sin of this wrong doing. We take, refuge with you.”;

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words spoken by them, Brahma, Visnu and other gods, looked at the shaven headed monks.

Then Visnu and other gods said, “O Shaven head monks, don’t be afraid. All the 137 events have happened with the consent of Siva.

You will never have to face miserable condition, because you are devoted to Siva and well-wishers of the gods as well as the sages.

Siva has always been favourable to the gods and the Rsis and the one who does good to the gods and the Rsis is always dear to him. Therefore the one who does good to the divine sages never falls in evil times.

From today onwards, your cult would be meant for the people of the age of Kali, and will be faced with disastrous results. This is the truth and there is no doubt about it.

O Valorous shaven-headed monks, till the start of the age of Kali, you shall stay in the desert region at my behest.

At the start of the Kali age; you can propagate your cult, which will be followed by the deluded fools.”

O Great sage, thus advised by the great gods, the shaven headed monks, bowed in reverence to the gods and went to the place allotted to them.

Then lord Siva- the great yogi, after burning the abodes in the three cities, felt contented. He was appropriately adored by Brahma and others. Then the lord, after completing the task of the gods, suddenly disappeared from that place together with his ganas, his sons and the goddess Parvati.

After the disappearing of Siva from that place, with his ganas, the fortress also disappeared along with bow, arrows, the chariot and other things.

Then the gods like Brahma, Visnu, and others, besides the sages, Gandharvas, Nagas, Surya, apsras, and the human beings, felt delighted.

They reciting the glory of Siva, went to their respective places and started living there peacefully.

Thus I have narrated to you the excellent story of the sports of Siva, known as Candrasekhara relating to the killing of Tripura.

This episode bestows the best of glory increases the age, enhances the riches as well as the cereals, and is the bestower of the heaven as well as the moksa. Now what also do you want to listen from me?

Whosoever listens to this excellent story, he enjoying all the best of comforts in this world ultimately achieves moksa.

## Chapter 13 - The punishing of Indra by Siva and restoring him to his original position at the request of Brhaspati

Vyasa said, “O Brahma’s son Sanatkumara, I had heard that Siva the great lord had killed Jalandhara- the great Daitya.

O Immensely learned one, you kindly narrate the relevant story of Siva in detail. Who could feel satisfied by listening to the spotless story of Siva?

Suta said, “When so asked by the sage Vyasa, the son of Brahma, who was quite good in speech; the peaceful great sage said.

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, Once Indra and Brhaspati, went to Kailasa to have an audience with Siva.

In the meantime Siva came to know about the arrival of Indra and Brhaspati for the testing of his knowledge.

Siva, who always bestowed salvation to the noble people stood without robes, obstructing their path. He was delightful with the matted locks of hair over his head.

Thereafter both Brhaspati and Indra, found a person with an astonishing form on the way.

He was immensely resplendent, peaceful, having the matted locks of hair over his head, with long arms, broad chest, awful eyes, and fair complexion.

Then arrogant Indra, finding disguised Siva, obstructing his way, without recognising him, asked him.”

Indra said, “Who are you? Where from have you come? What is your name? Tell me correctly. Is Siva lodged in his asrama, or has he gone somewhere?”

Sanatkumara said, “When so enquired by Indra, the ascetic remained quiet. Indra again asked him, but he still kept quiet.

Then Indra the lord of the lokas again asked him but still the playful lord Siva the great yogi, kept quiet.

When Indra so asked Siva again and again, the latter in order to test his knowledge, kept quiet. Then Indra, feeling proud of possessing the entire riches of the three worlds, feeling angry, scolded him.”

Indra said, 'O Evil-minded one, you have given me no reply inspite of my asking you again and again. I strike my Vajra at you and shall see who comes to your rescue.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking Indra the lord of gods, getting enraged, finding some one with matted locks of hair standing before him naked, lifted his hand in order to strike him with Vajra.

Then Siva found Indra carrying Vajra in his hand, he stopped him.

Then Siva with horrible eyes, getting enraged, suddenly started burning with anger, as if he would bum himself.

On the other hand, Indra, because of his arm becoming inactive, started burning from within like a snake, whose prowess had been stopped with the use of mantra.

Then the naked ascetic who was none else than Siva himself, wearing the matted locks of hair over the head and was illumining with his own splendour, was recognised by Brhaspati who offered his salutation to him.

The extremely wise Brhaspati, offered his salutation to him while prostrating before him. Then he started praying him.

Brhaspati, the preceptor said, “O Lord of gods, O Mahadeva, you are the form of soul, O Mahesvara, O Lord, O Trayambaka, having 139 the lock of hair over your head, salutation to you.

You are the lord of the destitute, all pervading, killer of Andhakasura, O Siva, Brahma and Parmesthi, salutation to you.

O Virupaksa, Rudra, having many forms, having deformed body, having several bodies, you are beyond all the forms, salutation to you.

You are the destroyer of the yajna bestower of the reward for the yajnas, the form of yajna, you attract people towards the performing of the karmas. Salutation to you.

You are Kalantaka, the form of Kala, decorated with the serpents, the Supreme lord, omnipresent, salutation to you.

You use the weapon called Brahmasirsa, you are adored by Brahma as well the moon and work for the benefit of the Brahmanas. Salutation to you.

You are the fire, wind, sky water, earth, the sun, moon, constellations and the jyotiscakra.

You represent Brahma, Visnu, Paramesvara, Sanaka and the other sages, besides being the sage Narada.

You are the lord of all the worlds, the soul of the earth, related to all and are the different forms of all, besides being beyond Prakrti.

You resort to creation possessing rajoguna, as Brahma, with Sattvaguna you preserve the entire world as Visnu.

O Mahadeva, you alone, with the use of tamoguna with your divine sports, destroy the entire lokas comprising of the Pancabhutas (five elements).

O Creator of the universe, on the strength of your devotion the sun shines, the nectar rains, the wind blows constantly.

With the strength of your dhyanam, O Siva, the clouds drop the rain and with the strength of your meditation, Indra the lord of gods, brings up the universe like the son.

On the strength of your devotion and getting afraid of you all the gods, sages, clouds, perform their duties surprisingly.

By serving at your lotus like feet the people on earth, without serving other gods, enjoy all the comforts of the world.

By serving at your lotus like feet, a person achieves such a high position which is beyond the reach of even the great yogis.”

Sanatkumara said, Brhaspati, after thus eulogising Siva, who bestows welfare to the universe, pushed Indra, at his lotus like feet and then bowed in reverence to him.

In this way while placing the humble Indradeva, at the feet of Siva, Brhaspati spoke to the lord, with all humility.

Brhaspati said, “O Kin of the destitutes, O Mahadeva, Indra has fallen over your feet. Now you pacify your enraged eyes.

O Mahadeva, be pleased. Protect Indra, who takes refuge in you. Let the fire emerging from your third eye, be pacified.”

Sanatkumara said, “ Siva- the god of gods, the ocean of mercy, Mahesvara, on listening to these words of Brhaspati, spoke in deep voice.”

Siva said, “O Brhaspati, the fire of anger which has already emerged from my third eye, how could it be taken back. When the skin of the snake is removed, it cannot be replaced.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening the words of Siva, Brhaspati was frightened and feeling painful he said.

Brhaspati said, “O Lord, O Siva, you should always exercise your compassion over your devotees. You make your name as well- disposed towards the devotees as true.

O Lord of gods, you better place your scorching lustre somewhere else. You redeem all your devotees. Therefore you kindly redeem Indra as well.”

Sanatkumara said, “At these words of Brhaspati; lord Siva, who removes the miseries of his devotees, spoke to Brhaspati delightfully.

Siva said, “O Dear one I am pleased with your prayer and I therefore grant you an excellent boon. Because of restoring life to Indra, you would be known by the name of *jiva.*

The fire which had emerged from my third eye for the killing of Indra, I shall now throw it away at a long distance to save Indra from its harm.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, Siva threw the fire emerging from his third eye, into to the ocean of salt water.

Thereafter Siva who is at times engaged in gigantic sports, disappeared from the scene. On the other hand Indra and the preceptor Brhaspati, left for their respective abodes in horror.

## Chapter 14 - Birth of Jalandhara from the oceanic fire and his marriage with Brnda

Vyasa said, “O Son of Brahma, O Omniscient one, O Sanatkumara, salutation to you. I have listened to the astonishing story of lord Siva.

O Dear one, when Siva, threw away the fire of his third eye into the oceanic water, then what happened thereafter you tell me the same.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Immensely wise and dear one, listen to the astonishing divine play of lord Siva, hearing which his devotees are turned as the yogis.

The fire emerging from the third eye of Siva, when thrown in the oceanic water, took to the form of an infant.

At the confluence of the Ganga and the ocean, the terrific child started crying aloud.

Listening to his cries, the earth started shaking and with his cries the heaven and the Satyaloka became deaf.

With the cries of the infant, all the lokas were frightened. The lokapalas of all the four directions were also upset.

O Narada, what is the use of speaking more, with the listening to his cries, all the mobile and immobile beings started shaking.

Thereafter all the gods and the sages, getting disturbed went to Brahma, the grand sire.

Indra and all other gods offering their salutation to Brahma, praised him as well.”

The gods said, “O Mahayogi, lord of the lokas, lord of the gods, the astonishing type of sound which is being produced presently, should be stopped by you.”

Sanatkumara said, “Then Brahma the grand sire of all the lokas, heard the words spoken by the gods with surprise and in order to know the factual position, he desired to visit the place from where the sound was produced.

O Dear one, then Brahma, along with the gods, descending from the Satyaloka, in order to find out what was happening there, went to the seashore.

On the arrival of Brahma at the seashore, he found the infant there; seated in the lap of the ocean.

Finding the arrival of Brahma at the seashore, then the god-like ocean, offering his salutation to Brahma in human form, placed the child in his lap.

Then feeling surprised Brahma, enquired from the ocean, “Whose is this astonishing child? You tell me quickly.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Brahma, feeling delighted, the ocean spoke to Brahma, offering his salutation to him with folded hands. Then he offered prayer to him and said.

The Ocean said, “O Brahma, I know nothing about this child. O Lord of all the people, it emerged at the confluence of Gangasagara suddenly.

O Preceptor of the universe, you better perform the birth rites of this child. O Destiny, you perform the post-natal rites for the boy.”

Sanatkumara said, “At these words of the ocean, the child started shaking Brahma, holding him by the neck.

When Brahma, the creator of the universe was so shaken by the child, tears started flowing from the eyes of the creator of the world.

Brahma some how got his neck released from the hands of the child and then spoke to him with reverence.

Brahma said, O Ocean, I shall narrate the future as revealed by his horoscope completely. Listen to me attentively.

Since he made the tears to flow from my eyes, he will be known by the name of Jalandhara. He would become youthful just now and attain mastery over all the lores. He would be extremely valorous, courageous, heroic, invincible and majestic like you. He would win all the battles like Kartikeya and he would shine with all sorts of prosperity. He would become the emperor of the demons and will conquer even Visnu. No one would be able to defeat him.

He can be slain by none else except Siva himself. He will return to the place from which he sprang up.
