He will have a chaste wife who will multiply his fortunes. She wall be extremely beautiful in all the limbs. She will have a pleasant speech and shall be the ocean of the noble conduct.

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, he called Sukracarya, the preceptor of the Daityas, and his abhiseka was performed. Thereafter, Brahma disappeared with the permission of the ocean.

The ocean was pleased by looking at the child, and taking him as his son, he got him inside his abode.

Then he started bringing up the child feeling pleased. He was quite illustrious and beautiful as well.

Thereafter, the ocean, summoned a demon named Kalanemi and desired his daughter to be married with Jalandhara.

O Sage, Kalanemi, who was the best among the asuras, being valorous, accepted the demand of Brahma.

Then Kalanemi, gave away his daughter to Jalandhara, the brave son of the ocean, the marriage, was performed in Brahma style.

O Sage great festivities were held in the marriage. The rivers and the demons were happy.

The ocean also felt delighted at his son’s getting united with a wife. According to the prevailing practice, he made charitable gifts to the Brahmanas and others.

The asuras who had been defeated by the gods and had migrated to Patala to take shelter there, fearlessly returned to the earth and started living with him.

The demons like Kalanemi and others were pleased after giving his daughter to the son of the ocean. The demons then took refuge with him for the purpose of defeating the gods.

The immensely valorous son of the ocean, Jalandhara, after his marriage with Brnda, endeared himself among the people with the influence of Sukracarya- the preceptor of the demons.

## Chapter 15 - Finding the severed head of Rahu, Jalandhara attacks Indra and defeats him

Sanatkumara said, “Once Jalandhara- the son of the ocean with the spouse of Brnda, was seated in his court with his wife.

In the meantime, the powerful Sukracarya, illumining all the directions with his lustre, arrived there.

On his arrival there, all the demons as also Jalandhara, the son of ocean offered then salutation to him.

The illustrious Bhargava, took his charming seat blessing them. The other demons also took their seats.”

Jalandhara- the son of the ocean, who was a firm and the best ruler, felt delighted, lovingly looking at his court.

Then Jalandhara enquired about the headless Rahu from Bhargava (Sukracarya).

Jalandhara said, “O Lord, O Preceptor, who severed the head of Rahu? What was the reason for the same? You please tell me correctly.”

Sanatkumara said, Thus listening to the words of Jalandhara, the son of the ocean, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, narrated the correct episode.”

Sukra said, “O Valorous Jalandhara, benevolent to all the demons, you listen, I shall narrate, the entire story to you.

In ancient times, the great grand son of Hiranyakasipu and son of Virocana was the king Bali, who was quite powerful and religious minded.

After he defeated all the gods, then he accompanied with selfish Indra, went to take refuge with lord Visnu and spoke to him. At his command, the gods who were past master in deceitful ways, entered into a compromise with the demons, making an alliance.

For the achieving of the nectar, the gods dominated by Visnu, were engaged for the churning of the ocean.

Then the gods, who are inimical to demons, stole away the pearls extracted from the ocean besides consuming the entire nectar themselves, deceitfully.

Then Indra and other gods became powerful and they with the help of lord Visnu defeated the gods.

Then Visnu, who favoured Indra, cut off the head of Rahu, while he was consuming the nectar.”

Sanatkumara said, “In this way Sukra narrated the story of the severing of the head of Rahu as well as that of the churning of the ocean.

Listening to the story in detail of the theft of the gems, the defeat of the Daityas, and consuming of the nectar by the gods, the valorous Jalandhara- the son of the ocean, in addition to the churning of the ocean- his father, Jalandhara was immensely enraged.

Then he summoned his messenger named Ghasmara, repeated to him the story that was narrated to him by Sukra.

Then he lovingly honoured the messenger, assured him of all protection, and sent him to Indra as his messenger.

Ghasmara- the intelligent messenger of Jalandhara, then rushed to the heaven, where all the gods were lodged.

Reaching there he entered the assembly of the gods. Keeping his head straight as a token of haughtiness, he spoke to lord Indra.

Ghasmara said, “Jalandhara, the son of the ocean, is the lord as well as the emperor of the demons. He is exceedingly strong and valorous. He is supported and helped by Bhargava (Sukra).

I happen to be his messenger named Ghasmara, but I am not a devourer. I have arrived before you having been sent by him.

No one can disobey the command of the immensely learned Jalandhara. He has conquered all the enemies of the Daityas. Listen to his command.

Jalandhara has said, “O Degraded gods, you had churned my father with a mountain and stole away the gems of my father.

You have not done well by this. You better return the gems to me. Take my refuge with all the gods.

Otherwise O Wicked god, you will have to suffer a lot. I shall destroy your kingdom, I am speaking to you truthfully.”

Thus listening to the words of the messenger, Indra felt surprised. Remembering him with awe and anger, Indra said.

“The ocean had concealed the mountains frightened from me in its waters and he saved my enemies.

Therefore I usurped all his gems. The one who is inimical to me, can never remain peaceful. I am speaking to you truthfully.

Samkha, the son of the ocean, became inimical to me earlier. Because of his foolishness, he was deprived of the company of the noble people.

Visnu my younger brother killed that sinful person, because he was the killer of the sages and lived in the oceanic waters.

O Messenger, you return at once, and reveal to the son of the ocean the real cause of the churning of the ocean.

Sanatkumara said, “Thus the intelligent messenger Ghasmara was so returned by Indra, he went back to Jalandhara.

The intelligent messenger, repeated before Jalandhara, all whatever had been spoken to him by Indra.

On hearing this the lips of the demon king started fluttering and he started making efforts for defeating the gods.

With the efforts of the demon king, crores of Daityas arrived from all the directions as well as the nether world.

Then the valorous and glorious Jalandhara, the son of the ocean, accompanied by crores of demon commanders, including Sumbha and Nisumbha, marched on for the waging of war.

He soon arrived at Indraloka with his army, where he blew the conch, and all the warriors started thundering thereafter.

The demon king thundering with allthe warriors, camped in the Nandanavana.

The gods finding that the city had been surrounded by the demon army, marched on for waging the war, wearing the kavacas.

Thereafter the armies of the gods and the demons, started fighting with musalas, parighas, arrows, clubs, battle axes, saktis and other weapons.

They started running for killing one another. In a short time both the armies started moving through the streams of blood.

The elephants, horses, chariots, foot soldiers, which were killed or destroyed, decorated the battle-field as the red clouds appear in the evening.

The demons killed in the battle were brought back to life by Bhargava with the sprinkling of the water sanctified with the Sanjivini lore.

The sage Angira also, getting the divine medicine from the Drona mountain, brought back the gods to life.

Finding that the gods had also been brought back to life, Jalandhara, getting agitated said to Sukra.

Jalandhara said, “How could the gods, who have been killed by me, brought back to life? I have heard that no one else except you is aware of the secret of the Sanjivini lore.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the son of Sukra- the preceptor of the Daityas, delightfully spoke to Jalandhara.

Sukra said, “O Dear one, the sage Angira, is bringing back the demons to life be fetching the divine medicine from the Drona mountain. This is true.

O Dear one, in case you are desirous of being victorious, then lift up the Drona mountain and drown it in the ocean.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the preceptor Sukra, the Daitya king went to the Drona mountain.

He lifted up the Drona mountain with both his arms and consigned it in the oceanic waters. It was no surprise for the lustre of Siva.

The immensely valorous son of the ocean again arrived in the battle-field with enormous army and started killing the gods with various weapons.

Then finding the gods having been wounded, the preceptor of the gods went to the Drona mountain, but could not find it there.

When he came to realise that the Drona mountain had been carried away by the demon king, he felt frightened and returning to the gods, he said to them.

The preceptor said, “O Gods, you better run away. The demon son of the ocean has destroyed the Drona mountain.

The immensely valorous Daitya Jalandhara, bom out of the amsa of Siva, cannot be defeated.

O Gods, the way he was born, similar is his influence. I have come to realise that he was bom out of the insult by Indra, showered on Siva. All of you should remember it.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the preceptor of the gods, the frightened gods lost all hope for victory.

Having suffered at the hands of the demon king, Indra and all other gods, losing heart, fled to different directions.

Then the Daityas son of the ocean, finding the gods having fled the battle-field, sounding the war-bands, shouting the slogans of victory, entered the city of Amaravati.

Finding the arrival of the demon king in the city of Amaravati, all the gods, took refuge in a Cave in the Sumeru mountain.

Then Jalandhara established his own demons over the high positions in the heaven, and then started in search of the gods.

## Chapter 16 - Fleeing of the gods from the heaven and fight between Visnu and Jalandhara armies

Sanatkumara said, “Finding the arrival of the Daitya, Indra and ail other gods, trembling with fear, fled away collectively.

Then they making Brahma to lead them went to Vaikuntha. Reaching there, they eulogised Visnu together with Brahma.”

The gods said, “O Hrsikesa, Mahabahu, O Lord Madhusudana, O God of gods, the destroyer of all the Daityas, salutation to you.

O Lord Visnu, you salvaged the Vedas, taking to the form of Matsya incarnation, through Satyavrata, salutation to you. You sport about in the ocean of dissolution.

For the purpose of the churning of the ocean, you were the one who could carry the Mandaracala mountain taking to the form of tortoise.

Salutation to you. Salutation to you who redeemed the earth, the base of the human beings.

O Vamana, also having the form of a Upendra, and Visnu, salutation to you. Taking to the form of a beggar, you deceived Bali.

You incarnated as Parasurama, and destroyed the Ksatriyas. For the welfare of your mother you were enraged an the wicked people. Salutation to you.

Salutation to Rama who delighted the worlds and who set the maryada for the noble conduct. Salutation to you the destroyer of Ravana and the lord of Sita.

Lord Krsna, possessing the secret knowledge, being the Supreme soul, enjoying the company of Radha; indulging in several types of sports, salutation to you.

You take to invincible body, denouncer of the Vedas, Yogacarya, the one who takes to the form of Jaina and Buddha, O Lord of Laksmi, salutation to you.

You are the form of Kali, destroyer of the Mlecchas you establish the Dharma of truth, you are the form of the Sakti (prowess) beyond measure, salutation to you.

You are the form of Kapila, the great soul who expounded the doctrine of Samkhya and yoga to Devahuti. O Lord, salutation to you. You are the preceptor of Samkhya philosophy.

Salutation to you as a great yogi and a saint, who expounds the great wisdom. You are the creator of the form of knowledge, whereby the soul is delighted, salutation to you.

You are the form of Vedavyasa who classified the Vedas, salutation to you. You are the one who wrote the Puranas, for the welfare of the world. Salutation to you.

You are the one who performs the task of the devotees, through the incarnation of fish etc. Salutation to you. You are the form of Brahman, the cause of creation, sustenance and destruction, salutation to you.

You are like Vajra in order to remove the pain of your devotees, you bestow comforts, do good to others, wearer of Pitambara, sole performer of all the deeds, protector of those taking refuge in you, salutation to you.

You remove the pain of your devotees, taking to the form of Vajra. You sleep over the serpent bed, and have the sun as well as the moon as your eyes. Salutation to you.

O Lord of Laksmi, O Ocean of mercy, save us because we have taken refuge in you. All the gods have been driven out of the heaven by Jalandhara.

The sun has been dislodged from its place. Similarly the moon and the fire have also been removed. The serpent king has been dislodged from Patala.

The gods are wandering like the ordinary human beings and they no more look graceful as before. We have all arrived here to take refuge with you. You better think of ways and means for the killing of the demon.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the distressed words of the gods, lord Visnu, the ocean of mercy, spoke with the voice thundering like the clouds.

Visnu said, “O Gods, shed away the fear. I shall now measure strength with the demon Jalandhara in the battle ground.

Thus speaking with distressed mind, Visnu, the enemy of Asuras got up quickly. The god Visnu who is favourably disposed to his devotees mounted over his vehicle Garuda.

Laksmi finding her husband going with the gods, spoke with folded hands, dropping tears from her eyes.

Laksmi said, “O Lord, I am your beloved as well as your devotee. O Ocean of mercy, how would you kill my brother in the battlefield?”

Visnu said, “I shall fight with the Daitya Jalandhara, because of the prayer of the gods to kill him. Therefore I am proceeding at once for the waging of the war.

Because he has been born out of the amsa of Siva, at the request of Brahma and because of your love for him, he will not be killed at my hands.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking carrying the Samkha, cakra, gada, mounted over Garuda, Visnu went for a war, accompanied with Indra and other gods.

Soon he reached the place where Jalandhara was lodged. The gods at that point of time getting help from Visnu, started roaring like the lion.

At that point of time Garuda, the younger brother of Aruna, with wind produced with the wings encircled the demon Jalandhara. He was shaken as the clouds in the sky are flown with the flowing of the forceful winds.

Then Jalandhara found that the Daitya army was suffering because of the wind. Redeeming them, he at once approached Visnu getting enraged.

Gaining strength from the lustre of Visnu, the gods delightfully started the war.

Finding that the army of the gods was ready for a war, Jalandhara, then commanded the demon army to wage the war.

Jalandhara said, “O Daityas, you fight with these coward gods, quite strongly.

At my command, let all the warriors come out with their entire army, including Mauryasa hundred thousand, the Dhumras in hundreds, the Asuras and the Kalakeyas in crores, besides the Kalakas, the Daurhradas and the Kankas in lakhs.

All of you should come out at once equipped with several divisions of army and different kinds of weapons. Be fearless and have no hesitation at all.

O Sumbha, O Nisumbha, destroy in a moment the insignificant gods who are feeling nervous in the battle-field. You are extremely powerful.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus at the command of Jalandhara, the Daityas, who were well- versed in the battle-field, and the gods with their fourfold army, started fighting.

They started killing one another with the shooting of sharp arrows, clubs, tridents, pattisa, tomaras, the battle-axes as well as the spears.

All of them were quite strong and they started killing others using the best of arms.

The heroic gods supported and invigorated by Hrsikesa roared like lions and discharge sharp arrows.

With some sharp arrows, some with the clubs and spears, some with he battle axes, and some with tridents were attacking one another.

In this way a great war was fought between the gods and the Daityas, which was quite ferocious, observing which all the Siddhas and sages were frightened:

## Chapter 17 - With the asking of the boon by Jalandhara, Visnu starts living in the abode of Jalandhara, with Laksmi

Sanatkumara said, ‘Thereafter the immensely valorous demons, attacked the gods with spears, battle axes, pattisas, and other weapons, who had been nervous at heart.

Having been wounded with the weapons of the Daityas, Indra and other gods fled away from the battle-field, getting terrified.

Then Visnu looking at the fleeing gods, and he himself arrived in the battle-field mounted over Garuda.

Visnu was bestowing protection to his devotees and the lustre of his Sudarsana-cakra was spreading on all the directions, looked graceful.

The valorous lord Visnu, holding the conch, sword, mace and the Saranga bow, appeared quite furious. He conducted himself well in the battlefield.

O Sage, stringing the Saranga bow, he stretched its cord and created the deafening sound, which echoed in the three lokas.

The enraged Visnu, when shot an arrow, and the heads of crores of demons were chopped off. At that time with the wind produced by the wings of Garuda, the Daityas started flying like the flying of the clouds in the sky with the forceful wind.

When Jalandhara found that the demons was suffering with the wind's force, then the great Daitya who was horror for the gods got enraged. The Daitya then forcefully rushed to fight with Visnu.

He thundered aloud, frightening the gods and the demons alike and they became deaf.

With the terrific sound produced by Jalandhara, which echoed in the entire universe and all the creatures started shaking.

Then started a terrific war between Visnu and Jalandhara, as a result of which the sky was filled with the arrows.

O Sage, with the war waged by both of them, all the gods, asuras, Rsis and Siddhas were frightened and surprised.

With the shooting of an arrow Visnu injured the heart of Jalandhara. Then shooting other arrows, he cut off the demon's flag, chatra and bow.

Then the Daitya holding a club in his hand and taking a leap, attacked Garuda over its head, as a result of which he fell down on the earth.

Then the infuriated Asura with throbbing lips struck Visnu in his heart with his sharp shining trident diffusing its splendour.

Then Visnu, the destroyer of the Daityas, smilingly cut off demon's club with his sword. Visnu then pierced the body of the great Daitya with the arrows issued from the Saranga bow.

Then Visnu, the destroyer of asuras, getting enraged, shot a terrific arrow at Jalandhara.

Finding that the arrow of Visnu was targeting him, the Daitya intercepted the same, by shooting another arrow. Then the demon shot another arrow, which pierced the heart of Visnu.

The large armed Kesava- the valorous one, cut off the arrow of the Daitya and then he roared aloud.

Then the Daitya, shaking in anger, again placed an arrow at the bow. The immensely valorous Visnu, cut off the said arrow, with his own arrow.

Then Vasudeva, getting enraged, for the destruction of the Daitya, placed the arrow over the bow and started roaring like a lion.

The immensely valorous Daitya, Jalandhara, chewing his lips in anger, cut off the Saranga bow of Visnu with his arrow.

Then the immensely strong Daitya, the enemy of the gods, who frightened the powerful gods, shot a sharp arrow at Visnu.

Then Visnu the protector of the universe, after the cutting off his bow, shot a huge club at Jalandhara in order to kill him.

The club shot by Visnu, which was like the blazing flame, moved with unerring aim, and dashed against the demon's body.

Though the demon was hit by it, the great haughty Jalandhara, did not move even slightly as though he was hit by a flower garland.

Then the enraged Jalandhara, who was invincible in war, frightening the asuras, hurled a trident, resembling fire, at Visnu.

Lord Visnu at once remembered the lotus like feet of Siva, and cut into pieces the trident with his Nandaka sword.

When the asura's trident was split and made infructuous, the asura had a leap and he rushed towards Visnu and hit him in the chest with his Vajra like fist.

Visnu, unmindful of the pain caused with the striking of the fist struck hard Jalandhara with his powerful fist.

Thereafter both the warriors started fighting striking each other with arms, fists, knees, creating roaring sound on earth.

Thus the Daitya fought with Visnu for a long time. Then feeling surprised he felt painful at heart.

Then Visnu- the foremost among the makers of the illusion, assumed a delightful aspect. Then he addressed the asura king in a thundering voice.

Visnu said, “O Excellent demon, you are quite graceful. You indeed are invincible in war. Since you happen to be a great lord, therefore, you are not at all afraid of any weapons.

Many demons have been killed in the war by these weapons. The bodies of the wicked and the naughty people had been pierced through the killed by these weapons.

O Great demon, I am immensely pleased with this fight with you. You are really great. A valorous person like you has not been seen in the three worlds, including the mobile and immobile beings.

O Lord of demons, I am pleased with your prowess, I shall grant you anything even that which cannot be given; whatever is in your mind.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of Visnu, well-versed in illusion, the intelligent king of the demons said.”

Jalandhara said, “O Dear to the devotees, in case you are pleased with me, then give me the boon, that you live in my abode with my sister and your ganas.''

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the great Daitya, Visnu painfully said, “Be it so.”

Thereafter, Visnu, accompanied with Laksmi and the gods started living in the abode of Jalandhara.

Then Jalandhara- the Daitya finding Visnu with Laksmi living in his abode, was immensely pleased.

Thereafter Jalandhara, made the demons to hold all the positions of the gods and then returned to earth.

All the gems available with the gods, Gandharvas and the Siddhas were usurped by Jalandhara, the son of the ocean.

The immensely powerful Daitya was entrusted with the control of Patala, and the valorous Jalandhara brought Sesanaga and other serpents, on earth.

Making the gods, Gandharvas, Siddhas and the serpents, his own subjects, he started ruling the three worlds.

Thus Jalandhara exercised control over all the gods, and started ruling the people religiously like his own sons.

Then ruling the people with a religious mind, no one with ailment, miserable and destitute could be found in his domain.

## Chapter 18 - At the instance of the gods, Narada, highlights the beauty of Parvati to Jalandhara

Sanatkumara said, “O Excellent sage, inspite of the Daitya’s ruling the earth according to dharma, but all the gods felt painful because of his dominance.

Feeling painful at heart, all the gods mentally took refuge with Siva who was quite well-disposed towards his devotees and offered prayer to him.

For getting relieved of their sufferings, they offered prayer to the great lord, the bestower of everything, by means of pleasant words.

Then lord Siva who always granted the wishes of his devotees, summoned Narada in order to help the gods. Then he inspired him to go to the Daitya.

Then the immensely intelligent Narada- the devotee of Siva, the abode of rescue for the noble people, with the permission of the lord Siva, went to the gods in the city of Jalandhara.

On the arrival of the sage Narada, Indra and other gods, stood up to receive him.

Offering their salvation to Narada, Indra and the other gods, having been filled with anxiety, respectfully gave him the asana.

Having been comfortably lodged in his seat, the gods again offered their salutation to Narada and said to him.

The gods said, “O Compassionate one, O Excellent sage, you are quite dear to Siva, listening to our miseries, you relieve us from them.

The Daitya Jalandhara, has removed us from our respective places, we are fed up with his over lordship.

The sun, the moon, Agni, Dharmaraja, Lokapalas and all other gods have been dislodged from their respective positions.

The powerful Daitya has made the lives of all the gods miserable. Therefore all of us have arrived here to take refuge with you.

Jalandhara, the powerful daitya has overpowered even Visnu in the battle-field.

Because of the boon Visnu has become subservient to the Daitya, as a result of which he is living in the abode of Daitya with Laksmi.

O Intelligent one, try to put an end to Jalandhara by some way or the other. You have arrived here because of our good fortune. You have always been performing our task with success.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Excellent sage, listening to these words of the gods, the compassionate Narada assured them variously and spoke.

Narada said, “I am well aware of the fact that you have all been defeated by the Daitya, besides removing you from your respective positions making your destitutes.

I, on the basis of my strength, shall establish your task. Because of your sufferings, I am favourable to you.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, Narada, assuring the gods, then went to the court of Jalandhara.

Jalandhara possessing all the fortunes, finding the arrival of Narada, got up with devotion and offered him a high seat.

He adored Narada appropriately, the lord of the Daityas, getting surprised started laughing.

Jalandhara said, O Brahmana, O Sage, where from are you coming? Have you anything somewhere for which you have arrived here? You please tell me.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Daityaraja, the sage Narada feeling pleased, spoke Jalandhara.”

Narada said, “O Lord of all the Daitya and Danavas, O Intelligent Jalandhara, O Lord of all the lokas, you are quite graceful. You are the one making use of all the gems.

O Best of the Daityas, you listen to the cause of my arrival here. I shall reveal the same in the presence of all.

I went of my own accord to the mountain Kailasa which grows kalpctvrksa forest and is spread in an area of ten thousand yojanas,

There are hundreds of Kamadhenus there. The resplendence of cintamani is spread everywhere. There is gold everywhere there and it possesses the astonishing things.

I found there the fair complexioned Siva, who is immensely beautiful, having three eyes, with has head adorned with the crescent moon, seated with Parvati.

I felt surprised by looking at them and I thought whether such a type of splendour could be found anywhere else in the three worlds or not.

O Lord of the Daityas, then I was reminded of your own splendour. I have arrived here simply to witness the same.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus listening from Narada, the great Daitya Jalandhara, displayed his entire grandeur to Narada.

Then Narada, who always performed the task of the gods, being immensely wise, said to Jalandhara at the inspiration of lord Siva.

Narada said, “O Best of the great warriors, undoubtedly you possess enough of riches, you are also the lord of the three worlds. Therefore there is no surprise in it.

The gems, diamonds in heaps, elephants, and other things, besides all the precious things are no doubt with you presently.

You have usurped the elephant Airavata, which is the gem of the elephants, Uccaisrava the best horse of the horse of the sun is with you.

You have also brought the kalpavrksa. The nine treasures of Kubera are with you. The plane of Brahma, driven by the swans is already with you.

Thus all the best of gems from the heaven and the earth are all possessed by you.

O Immensely valorous one, I am quite pleased, with the best of elephants, horses etc. besides all the fortunes.

O Jalandhara, you do not have the gem of a woman in your abode. Therefore you make special efforts in order to achieve the same.

O Jalandhara, inspite of possessing all the gems, in case it is deprived of the gem of a woman, it does not look graceful.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to these words of high-souled Narada, the noble soul, Daityaraja with his mind excited by passion, said.”

Jalandhara said, “O Great lord, O Divine sage, where could the best of the gem of woman be available? You please tell me.

Wherever the gem of the woman would be available, O Brahmana, I would surely bring her here there is no doubt about it.”

Narada said, “Siva in the form of a naked yogi lives at Kailasa, which is quite beautiful and possesses all the riches.

His wife is extremely beautiful, charming and attractive to the mind, known as Parvati.

Such an exquisite beautiful form has never been seen anywhere. It incites the enthusiasm of everyone, being highly wonderful, her beauty fascinates even the yogis and is worthy of being seen. She is conducive to prosperity.

It comes to my mind, O Valorous Jalandhara, that there could be none more prosperous in the three worlds than Siva, possessing the most excellent of all the ladies of the universe.

Even the four faced Brahma was attracted towards her beauty and lost his mental control in earlier times. Such a lady could be beyond comparison.

Even Siva, well known to be free from attraction has been won over by her womanly sports. Siva inspite of his being independent, has been subjugated by her.

The prosperity which is enjoyed by Siva, besides his dalliance with the most excellent of all the ladies of the world, has not been enjoyed by you.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, the world renounced divine sage, who was well- versed in the performing of the task of the gods, returned through the skyway.

## Chapter 19 - Jalandhara’s sending a messegen to Siva for getting Parvati

Vyasa said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, after the departure of Narada through the skyway, what did the Daityaraja do? You speak out to me in detail.

Sanatkumara said, “Narada, thus speaking to the Daitya, left the place and after his 162 departure, Daityaraja listening nearly about the beauty of Parvati, was at once infested with passion.

Deprived of his wisdom, overpowered with the force of time, and with the desire of achieving a beautiful woman, the daitya then summoned the Simhikeya (Rahu) the messenger.

On his arrival, the passionate Jalandhara- the son of Sindhu, said to him.”

Jalandhara said, “O Simhikeya (Rahu) immensely intelligent one, you achieve success in all the tasks. You go to the Kailasa mountain.

There lives a yogi, who is completely detached and applies ashes over his body. He wears the matted locks of hair over his head and is known by the name of Sambhu.

Reaching there O Messenger, you speak to the ascetic with matted locks of hair on his head, who is completely detached.

O Yogi, O Ocean of mercy. You stay in the forest and are served by the goblins and the pretas. Of what use would be this gem of a woman with you?

It would not be proper for you to keep her with you when my master, who is the lord of the three worlds is there, therefore you hand over the gem of the woman with you to me for my use.

The best of gems of the three worlds are already with me. The entire mobile and immobile universe is already under my control.

Airavata the gem among elephants belonging to Indra, the horse named Uccaisrava, Parijata tree, have been forcibly usurped by me.

The plane of Brahma driven by the swans is already parked in my courtyard, which is the best form of a gem.

I have usurped the nine treasures of divine nature from Kubera forcibly. The chatra of Varuna, which showers gold is already with me.

The great garland named Kinjalkini, made of unfading flowers is already with me, which had been received by Varuna, from my father- the ocean. It is with me. The excellent Sakti possessed by Varuna, which saves from death has also been forcibly been taken by me from him. The fire god has given me two garments.

O Lord of the yogis, thus all the gems are with me. O Yogi, with matted locks, you give away your gem like woman to me.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Rahu, Nandi permitted him to go inside. On his arrival inside, Rahu felt surprised finding Siva there.

Reaching there he found that Siva- the great lord had applied ashes over his body and had driven away the darkness with the lustre issuing from his body.

He was being adored like the great kings. All his limbs were quite beautiful, adorned with all the divine ornaments who was seen by him.

Getting influenced with his lustre, the messenger offered his salutation to the lord. Then the messenger named Rahu, got himself seated before Siva and desired to speak out something to him. At the instance of Siva, he started speaking.

“I am the messenger of the Daityaraja, who is served by the Nagas and is the lord of the three worlds, I have arrived here when my master has specifically deputed me to your place.

Rahu said, “Jalandhara, the son of the ocean is the lord of all the Daityas. Presently he is the lord of the three worlds and the leader of all.

The powerful Daityaraja is like Yama from the ghosts. Taking you to be a yogi he has given a message, which you please listen from me.

The Daityaraja enjoys enormous divine influence, he is lord of all the gems, you listen O Siva, to the command of the lord of the Daityas.

You live in the cremation ground, wear the garland of bones. Then how can the best daughter of Himalaya be your wife?

I am the lord of the gems and she happens to be the gem of the woman. Therefore she is most suited for me and not for a beggar who lives on alms.

All the lokas are under my control. I also distribute the portions of the yajnas. All the gems found in the three worlds are available with me.

We make the best use of the gems. On the other hand, you are a yogi and remain naked. Therefore, you hand over this gem of a woman to me, because the subjects are meant for the pleasure of the king.”

Sanatkumara said, “Soon after Rahu spoke thus a terrfic human emerged from the place between the eyebrows of Siva, who thundered like Vajra.

He had the rolling tongue, resembling that of a lion. He had the eyes like the burning flames. He was gigantic to look at. His hair was raised upwards, having the dry body, resembling Narasimha.

His body was large and the arms and thighs were quite long. The terrific and awful person pounced upon Rahu- the messenger.

He rushed towards Rahu to devour him, Rahu fled away with great speed, but he caught hold of Rahu outside the place of Siva.

Rahu said, “O God of gods, O Mahesan, I take refuge with you. You kindly protect me. You are always adorable by the gods and the demons and you are the lord with all the fortunes. O Isan, O Mahadeva, your terrible gana is going to devour a Brahmana like me.

O Isan, O Mahadeva, your terrible gana is going to devour a Brahmana like me.

O Lord, you are well-disposed towards the people who take refuge with you, O Lord of gods, you kindly save me from being devoured by him. Salutation to you again and again.

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, Lord Mahadeva who is the beloved of the destitutes, listening to the words of the Brahmana spoke to his gana”

Mahadeva said, “O Best of the ganas, this Rahu is a messenger, besides being a Brahmana who has taken refuge with us. Therefore such people should be protected. Such people are not entitled to any punishment.”

Sanatkumara said, “At these words of the compassionate, lord he at once released him, finding him a Brahmana.

Leaving Rahu in the sky, the gana went to Siva and pleaded to the great lord in piteous words.”

The Purusa said, “O God of gods, O Mahadeva, you are kind to those taking refuge with you, O Compassionate Siva, you have deprived me of my food.

O Lord, I am hungry and thirsty in all respects. Hunger is causing pain to me. O Lord of gods, what should I eat. You give me a command.

Listening to the words of that person, the lord who performed wonderful sports, and for self benefit said.

Sanatkumara said, “In case you are extremely hungry, then you should consume the flesh of your own hand and feet.

Sanatkumara said, “Thus at the command of lord Siva, the gana ate up the flesh of his own hands and feet. Only the head was left out.

The gana- then performer of the terrific task, when left with his head only then surprisingly Sadasiva said to him.

“At my command, you did what I wanted you to do. Therefore you are graceful. I am pleased with you.

O Immensely valorous ganas, you frighten the wicked people. Therefore you will always serve as my gatekeeper.

You are quite dear to me. My devotees while adoring me shall also adore you as well. Those who do not adore you will not be dear to me.

Sanatkumara said, “Thus receiving a boon from Siva, the gana was immensely pleased. Since then Kirtimukha was always lodged over the abode or the temple of Siva.

This gana should always be worshipped in the course of adoration of Siva. Those who do not worship him at the outset will find their worship in vain.

## Chapter 20 - Battle between the armies of Siva and Jalandhara

Vyasa said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, you have narrated the auspicious story of lord Siva.

O Great sage, now being lovingly graceful to me, you please tell me as to where did the messenger Rahu go after getting free from the clutches of the gana of Siva.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of intelligent Vyasa, the delightful Brahma's sonthe great sage said.

Sanatkumara said, “He released the messenger Rahu in the Barabara country and he started stammering in his speech. This fact is well known in the world.

He considered himself to have been reborn and becoming humble and free from arrogance, went to the city of Jalandhara.

O Vyasa, reaching there, he narrated the treatment he received in presence of Siva, to the king of the demons.

On hearing it, the valorous son of the ocean, the excellent lord of Daityas, Jalandhara was enraged from head to foot.

Thus having been enraged, the Daitya king asked his demon warriors to be ready for a war.”

Jalandhara said, “O Kalanemi, Sumbha, Nisumbha and all other Daityas should get ready to march on for waging of the war. With their respective army contingents.

The descendants of Kambu family, Daurhradas, Kalakas, Kalakeyas, Mauryas and Dhaumras, should start for the fight.”

After thus issuing the command, the lord of the asuras, the valorous son of the ocean, marched on quickly in the company of crores of Daityas.

Then Sukra and headless Rahu, went ahead of him. In his quick jerky movement, the crown of the demon king fell down on earth.

At that point of time, the earth looked graceful, but the sky, was entirely enveloped by clouds as in the rainy season. Several of the evil omens occurred which were indicative of grave misfortune.

Observing his activities Indra and other gods secretly arrived in the abode of Siva at Kailasa.

Reaching there, they met Siva and all the gods with folded hands, lowering their heads, praised Siva.

The gods said, “O Mahadeva the god of gods, O Compassionate lord Siva, O Mahesan, salutation to you. We take refuge in you, therefore you protect us.

O Lord, we have been completely upset with the dangerous activities of Jalandhara. He has removed all the gods from their respective positions and driven them to earth.

O Lord, why are you ignoring the evil activities of Jalandhara. Therefore in order to save us, you please kill Jalandhara, the son of the ocean.

O Lord, you had earlier deputed Visnu for our protection, but he had not been able to do so.

Lord Visnu, presently becoming subservient to him is lodged in the abode of the demon king with Laksmi. All the gods are also lodged there under his command.

O Siva, we have arrived here secretly. The son of the ocean is forcefully arriving to wage a war against you.

O Omniscient one, O Lord, now you killing Jalandhara, should rescue all the gods, who have taken refuge in you.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, Indra and other gods, offered their salutation at his feet and took their seats quite humbly.

Thus listening to the words of the gods, Siva, summoned Visnu and smilingly said to him.

Siva said, “O Mahavisnu, the gods suffering at the hands of Jalandhara, have approached me taking refuge with me.

O Visnu, why did you not kill Jalandhara in the battle-field and why are you living with Jalandhara, leaving Vaikuntha?

I had deputed you for the protection of the noble people and for the killing of the wicked people.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Siva, then Garuda-bannered lord Visnu, humbly spoke with folded hands.

Lord Visnu said, “Because of the birth of Jalandhara from your own amsa, I could not kill him. Therefore, you kindly kill him yourself.

O Lord of gods, he is quite powerful, and can defeat all the gods. I am telling you the truth.

I fought with him together with the gods, for a long time. But I could not be successful against him by any means.

Feeling pleased with his prowess, I asked him to seek for a boon. Hearing my words, he asked for a boon that “With my sister and the gods, you live in my abode and O Mahavisnu, you should always be subservient to me.” Therefore, I left for his abode.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus listening to the words of Visnu, the compassionate lord Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, Mahesvara, feeling pleased, said.”

Siva said, “O Visnu, you are the best of all the gods, you please listen to my words with respect. I shall undoubtedly kill the demon Jalandhara.

Taking the demon Jalandhara as having been killed, all the gods should assume your respective positions.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to these words of Siva, Lord Visnu, getting relieved of the doubt, went back to his place.

O Vyasa, in the meantime, the powerful Daitya king, accompanied with the demons who were ready to wage a war, reached the Kailasa mountain.

He, similar to Kala surrounded the Kailasa mountain with his vast army and started roaring like a lion.

Listening to the thundering sound of the Daitya. Siva, the destroyer of the wicked people, felt immensely enraged.

The great lord of several sports, the enthusiastic Siva, commanded his powerful ganas including Nandi and other for waging the war.

Then Nandi, Ganesa, Kartikeya, and all other ganas were inspired for the war.

Then all the leaders of the ganas and also the ganas themselves, getting enraged and shouting the slogans for war, arrived for the waging of the war.

Then at the ridges, the valleys and the sides of Kailasa a terrible battle was fought between the leaders of the pramathas and the Daityas in which the weapons struck with the weapons.

The great war drums, mrdangas, and conches which inspired the heroes as well as the sounds of the trumpets of elephants, neighing of horses and the creaking sound of chariots, shook the whole earth.

The entire atmosphere was filled with javelin, iron clubs, huge pestles, iron rods, arrows, pikes etc. as if strewn with pearls.

The earth was littered with dead elephants, horses and the foot soldiers and it shone in the same way as it had earlier shone when the great mountains were scattered and smitten with the vajra of Indra.

The earth had become extremely marshy as it became impassable with the spread of the flesh and streams of blood, where the Daitya were killed with pramathas.

With the use of Sanjivani, Sukra brought the Daitya forces back to life who were killed by the pramathas again and again.

Observing them all the ganas, and the pramathas felt agitated and frightened. They reported the activities of Sukra to the lord.

On hearing this, lord Siva was greatly agitated. He took to blazing form burning all around.

Thereafter, the terrific Krtya emerged out of the mouth of Siva, whose thighs were as long as the tree trunks, the face was like the cave and she could fell the trees with the striking of her breasts.

O Excellent sage, the terrific krtya at once reached the battle-field. She roamed about in the battle ground devouring the demons.

Then she fearlessly approached the place where Jalandhara was lodged with Sukra.

O Sage, with the spread of her lustre from her body from earth to the sky she hid Sukra in her vagina (yoni) and then disappeared in the sky.

With the disappearing of Bhargava (Sukra) from the demon army, the demon warriors were faded out and having been deprived of their arrogance, they started fleeing from the battle-field.

Then getting terrified from the ganas of Siva, the demon army vanished in the same way as the straw disappears with the wind storm.

With the demon army having been disappeared with the terror of the Sivaganas, Sumbha, Nisumbha as well as Kalanemi, were immensely enraged.

All the three army commanders, started driving out the Sivaganas from the battle-field with the shooting of their arrows, like the clouds of the rainy season.

The arrows shot by the demon leaders, covered all the directions like the locusts and frightened the warriors of Siva.

Having been attacked with the hundreds of arrows, the Sivaganas shed stream of blood, resembling the red kimsuka flowers of the spring season. They were confused and could not decide about their next step.

Finding that their army had been so shattered, the enraged, Nandin, Ganesa, and Kartikeya, hurriedly stopped towards the rushing Daityas.

## Chapter 21 - Special war between the gods and the demons

Sanatkumara said, “Then finding Nandi, the leader of the devaganas, besides Ganesa and Kartikeya, got enraged and rushed for a wrestling fight.

Kalanemi was to fight with Nandi, Sumbha was to fight with Ganesa, Nisumbha with Kartikeya, with doubtful minds.

Nisumbha shot five arrows at the heart of peacock- the vehicle of Kartikeya, which wounded the peacock who fell down on the ground.

Then Kartikeya, getting enraged, shot five arrows at the chariot of Nisumbha, the horses and the charioteer, killing them all.

He shot another arrow at arrogant Sumbha, the enemy of the gods. Sumbha having been struck with the arrow, started thundering like the cloud.

The immensely strong Nisumbha, while roaring shot an arrow at Kartikeya, in the battle ground.

Kartikeya, then getting enraged picked up the Sakti weapon, but in the meantime Nisumbha short him with a Sakti; who fell down.

O Vyasa, thus roaring like a lion, both Kartikeya and Nisumbha, kept on fighting between themselves.

Thereafter Nandisvara shot at Kalanemi, seven arrows, which shattered the horses, chariot, the flags, and the charioteer.

Kalanemi on the other hand, getting enraged, with the issuing of the sharp arrows from his bow, cut off the bow of Nandi.

Then the valorous Nandisvara, disregarding the powerful Kalanemi, shot a powerful trident at his chest.

After the destruction of Kalanemi's horses, chariot and he himself getting wounded with the trident of Nandisvara, the demon picked a mountain top and hurled it Nandi.

On the other hand Sumbha mounted over a chariot and Ganesa mounted over the mouse- his vehicle, started wounding each other.

Ganesa shot an arrow at the heart of Sumbha and by shooting three arrows at his charioteer, he made him fall on the ground.

The enraged Sumbha then showered the rain of arrows at Ganesa and shooting three arrows at the mouse, he started thundering like the clouds.

Having been wounded with the arrows, the mouse felt painful and was upset. Ganesa on the other hand kept no waging the war without falling from the mouse.

Then Ganesa struck the heart of Sumbha with his battle-axe as a result of which he fell down on earth and he himself again rode over the mouse, his vehicle.

Lord Ganesa again got ready for a fight. Then he smilingly attacked the demon with anger and disdainfully, as if hitting a great elephant with a goad.

Then both Kalanemi and Sumbha attacked Ganesa together, mercilessly with the arrows as well as the serpents.

Finding him afflicted, the powerful Virabhadra, together with a crore to goblins rushed for his help.

The *Sivaganas,* like the *Kusmandas, Bhairavas, Vetalas, Yoginis, Pisacas, Dakinis*, and the *ganas* accompanied him.

The earth then started shaking with the noises of several types including shouts of joy, lion's roars and the sound of the damarukas.

The goblins then rushes towards the battle ground and started devouring the Daityas. They made them fall with high jumps and then started dancing in the battle-field.

O Vyasa, in the meantime Nandi and Kartikeya regained consciousness and they started roaring in the battle ground.

Both Nandi and Kartikeya reaching the battle ground started killing the Daityas, with the shooting of his arrows.

The soldiers of the demon army, getting killed, wounded, fallen and devoured, felt panicky and upset.

Thus the terrific and glorious Kartikeya, Ganesa, Virabhadra, Nanda and other Sigvaganas kept on roaring in the battle-field.

The warriors of Jalandhara- the son of the ocean, Sumbha, Nisumbha, Kalanemi and other demons were defeated.

The valorous Jalandhara, the son of the ocean, finding his army having been so shattered, pounced upon the Sivaganas mounting his chariot.

The defeated demons, finding their master there, got enthusiastic. O Vyasa, then they again started roaring for war finding their master.

O Sage, then the victorious Nandi, Kartikeya, Ganesa, Virabhadra, and other Sivaganas also started roaring.

From both the armies, the sound of trumpeting of the elephants, neighing of horses, moving of chariots, blowing of conches and the beating of the kettle-drums, was heard. All of them resorted to roaring like the lion.

The bunch of arrows shot by Jalandhara, covered the land as well as the sky like the fog.

Jalandhara then shot five arrows each over Nandi- the son of Silada and Ganesa, wounding them. He also wounded Virabhadra with twenty five arrows and then he started thundering like a lion.

Then the valorous Kartikeya, the son of Rubra, at once shot a Sakti at Jalandhara- the son of the ocean. Thereafter he kept on thundering.

With the striking of the Sakti, the eyes of the demon started rolling and he fell down on the ground. But he at once got up again.

Then Jalandhara, getting enraged shot a club at the chest of Kartikeya.

O Vyasa, the son of Siva, according to the boon, successfully displayed the effect of the club. As a result of this, the Kartikeya at once fell down on the ground.

Similarly the immensely valorous killer of the enemies, fell down on the ground getting a little upset.

Thus the enraged Ganesa, devoting his mind at the feet of Siva, and getting strength from the same, cut off the enemy's club with the battle axe.

Virabhadra then attacked the demon's chest, with the shooting of three arrows he wounded the heart of the demon. He also cut off seven times, his horses, flags, bow and the chatra.

Then the demon getting immensely angry, mounted over an other chariot and picking up a terrific Sakti, he hurled it over Ganesa.

Then the valorous demon, getting enraged, thinking about Virabhadra in his mind, rushed towards him.

The valorous Jalandhara then started shooting sharp arrows at Virabhadra and kept on roaring at the same time.

The enraged Virabhadra also cut off the arrow of the demon with his own arrow.

Both of them were illustrious like the sun, best of the warriors, and kept on fighting for long with the exchange of several weapons.

Then Virabhadra killed the horses of the demon's chariot with his arrows. After cutting of the bow of the demon warrior, Virabhadra also cut off his flag.

Then holding a parigha, the valorous demon took a high jump and reached near Virabhadra.

Then the powerful son of the ocean attacked with parigha over the head of Virabhadra. After this he roared.

With the attack of the parigha over the head Vlrabhadra, fell down on the ground and stream of blood started flowing from his head.

Finding the fall of Vlrabhadra, the Sivaganas reciting the name of Siva fled from the battle-field.

Listening to the turmoil of his ganas, Siva asked his ganas standing near him.”

Siva said, “O Valorous warriors, what is the cause of the turmoil among my ganas. You find out the reason for it. I shall bring the peace no doubt.”

When Siva so gracefully questioned his ganas, by the same time, the best of the ganas reached Siva.

With the anxiety writ large over their faces, Siva enquired of them about the welfare, then the ganas repeated the happenings in the battle-field.

On hearing this, lord with many sports, encouraged the ganas, assuring their safety.

## Chapter 22 - Jalandhara’s approaching Parvati in the form of Siva, and deputing of Visnu by Parvati to cheat Jalandhara’s wife Vrnda

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter Rudra- the great lord, taking to the awful form, mounted over the vehicle bull, smilingly reached the battle-field.

The Sivaganas, who had deserted the battle-field, on arrival of Siva, also returned and started roaring like a lion.

While uttering the lion’s roar, the Sivaganas, carrying their weapons, started showering the rain of arrows which killed the Daityas.

Sighting the awful Rudradeva, the Daityas fled away from the battle ground it the same way as the sins disappear at the sight of the devotees of Siva.

When Jalandhara found that the Daityas had fled from the battle-field, then showering thousands of arrows, he rushed towards Candisa (Siva).

Thereafter both Sumbha and Nisumbha, grinding their teeth, together with thousands of the demons, rushed towards Siva.

The valorous Kalanemi, Khadgaroma, Balahaka, Ghasmara and Pracanda, rushed towards Siva.

Soon he covered Siva with the showering of the arrows. O Sage, Sumbha and all other Daitya warriors, wounded all the limbs of Siva, with the shooting of the arrows.

When Siva found that all his ganas had been covered with the shooting of the arrows by the demons, then he cut off all the arrows of the demons and covered the sky with his own arrows.

Siva then injured all the demons with the shooting of his arrows, who felt painful. He felled all the Daityas, with the shooting of his arrows.

Then he removed the head of Khadgaroma with the striking of his battle axe. With the use of Khatvanga the head of Balahaka was cut into two pieces.

The demon named Ghasmara was bound with noose and thrown on the ground. The head of valorous Pracanda was removed with the trident.

Some of the Daityas were killed by Nandi- the vehicle of Siva, while some of them were killed with the arrows shot by Siva. The Daityas could not stand in the battle-field as the elephant cannot face the lions. The getting enraged, the great and patient Daitya Jalandhara, pushing aside other Daityas, smilingly spoke to them.

Jalandhara said, “You are like the refuse of the mother, because you are fleeing from the battle-field. In case you are killed while fleeing, then in that case you would neither be praised, nor would you achieve the heaven which the proud warriors usually achieve.

In case you are least interested in the war, or you possess even a little of courage in your heart, if you are not desirous to enjoy the conjugal pleasure with your wife, then you merely stand before me.

The death in the battle ground is considered to be supreme, as a result of which all the desires are fulfilled.

A warrior who meets with his death in the battle-field, he achieves salvation piercing through the solar region. He is then turned as an omniscient ascetic or a Sanyasi.

The people with wisdom should not be afraid of death, anywhere. The death is certain, inspite of making all the efforts against it.

O Valorous warriors, the death is always linked with birth, irrespective of whether it comes to day or after a hundred years. Death is certain.

Therefore shedding away the fear; keep on fighting with pleasure and by doing so one achieves pleasure during this world as well as in the next world.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking Jalandhara advised his warriors variously further, but, they getting terrified could not stay there and fled away from the battle-field.

Jalandhara, the heroic son of the ocean then looking at his fleeing army, was immensely enraged.

Then Jalandhara uttering the words harsh like Vajra, challenged Siva and said to him.

Jalandhara said, “What would you gain by killing these warriors, O Siva having the locks of hair over your head, in case you possess some strength, then display it before me, by fighting with me.”

Sanatkumara said, “Then the great Daitya Jalandhara, shot seventy arrows at the bull- bannered Siva, the performer of noble deeds.

Before the arrows shot by Jalandhara could reach Siva, the latter intercepted them midway and shooting arrows of his own cut off all of them, smilingly.

O Sage, then Siva, with shooting seven arrows, cut of the horses, flags, chatra and the bow. There was no surprise in it.

Then Daitya- the son of the ocean, with the destruction of his bow and chariot, rushed towards Siva, carrying a club in his hands.

O Vyasa, lord Mahesvara who engaged himself in all the divine sports, cut the Daitya's club into two pieces with the shooting of his arrow.

Then the asura getting immensely enraged, rushed towards Siva with a clinched fist.

Then Siva, quite easily, with the shooting of his arrows, drove Jalandhara at a distance of a *kos'a.*

The Daityas at this stage realised that Siva was more powerful than he himself was. Therefore, he in order to overpower Siva with delusion, spread his *Gandharva-maya.*

With the influence of the said delusion, several *ganas, apsaras* and the Gandharvas appeared on the scene in order to confuse Siva.

Then the Gandharvas started singing and the apsaras started dancing. The other people started playing on flutes, mrdangas and cymbals etc.

Witnessing the wonderful feat, Siva was fascinated with the ganas. He was not even aware of the costumes which had fallen from his body.

Finding that Siva had been absorbed in the dance, Jalandhara urged by lust, immediately went to the place where Gauri was lodged.

The conducting of war was left by him to both Sumbha and Nisumbha and Jalandhara, with a demonic illusion, assumed the form of Siva, with ten brawny arms, five faces, three eyes, and the matted hair. He was seated over the great bull. In every respect, O Vyasa, Jalandhara resembled Siva.

Finding that Siva was approaching her, Parvati came out from the midst of the female friends within the range of his vision.

On looking at the beautiful Parvati, by the lord of Daityas, his semen fell on the ground and all his limbs became benumbed.

Thereafter, when Gauri came to realise, the truth that he was a Daitya and not Siva, she disappeared from the site and went to northern shore of the lake Manasa.

When the Daitya was unable to find Parvati there, who had disappeared like lightening, the Daitya atonce went back to the place where the lord Siva stood in order to fight with him.

Then Parvati remembered lord Visnu mentally and she found atonce that the lord was seated before her.

Finding Visnu present before her, Parvati bowed in reverence to him with folded hands. Then Parvati, the beloved of Siva, and the mother of the universe spoke to Visnu delightfully.

Parvati said, “O Visnu, Jalandhara, the Daitya king, has performed an astonishing deed today. Are you not aware of the evil deed performed by him?”

Listening to these words of Jagadamba, Visnu, lowering his head and folding his hands said to Parvati.

Visnu said, “O Goddess, by your grace I have known about everything. O Mother, you tell me, now what should I do?”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of Visnu, Parvati, the mother of the universe, then desired to teach the policy based on dharma.” Parvati said, “He himself has shown the path, now that has to be the way and he should be paid in the same manner. At my command, destroy the chastity of his wife.

O Visnu, “the Daitya cannot be killed otherwise. There is no other virtue comparable to chastity in the world.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing this command, Visnu accepted it with all humility. Then Visnu atonce went to the city of Jalandhara.

## Chapter 23 - Cheating of Vrnda by Visnu who is cursed by her

Vyasa said, “O Sanatkumara, an excellent orator, you tell me, what did Visnu do, reaching the place of Jalandhara.

Sanatkumara said, “On reaching the city of Jalandhara, Visnu thought of desecrating the chastity of Vrnda.

Visnu, then who was the foremost of the illusory gods made Vrnda to witness a dream and he himself stayed in the beautiful orchard of the same city.

Then Vrnda the chaste wife of Jalandhara witnessed a bad dream during the night.

With the illusion of Visnu, Vrnda saw in dream her husband naked mounted over a buffalo, with the oil smeared over his body.

He was wearing the garland of black flowers and was surrounded by vultures, jackals, moving towards the southern direction, surrounded by darkness. His head had been completely shaven.

She found that she, together with her own city was drowning in the ocean, in the dream. Many such terrific dreams had been witnessed by her in the early morning.

Then the girl, kept on thinking about the bad dreams and in the meantime the sun rose, which was lustreless and pours.

Taking it to be unfortunate, she while crying, became upset. Then she went to the balcony of the top floor of his palace, but she remained restless.

Then she accompanied with to maids, went two the orchard of the city, but she remained uncomfortable there as well.

Then Vrnda, the wife of Jalandhara, feeling disturbed and painful, went from one orchard to the other. They could not understand anything.

While so wandering, Vrnda had an encounter with two demons having the lion's face, shining teeth and awful in appearance.

Looking at both of them, getting frightened and nervous, she found an ascetic keeping silence accompanied with a disciple, while fleeing in horror.

She then went to him, getting frightened, placed her arms around his neck and said, “O Sage, you protect me. I take refuge in you.”

Finding Vrnda having been frightened from the demons, he removed both the demons uttering a humkara.

Vrnda, then finding that the two demons had disappeared with the mere humkara of the ascetic, the wife of Daityaraja was immensely surprised.

Having been relieved of the fear, Vrnda, prostrated before the sage with folded hands and then spoke to him.”

Vrnda said, “O Ocean of mercy, you remove the sufferings of others, O Best of the ascetics, you have saved me from the danger of the wicked demons.

O Ocean of mercy, though you are omniscient and all competent, still, I would like to speak out something to you. You kindly listen to me.

Jalandhara my husband has gone to fight with Siva. O Suvrata, you kindly apprise me with the latest news of the battle-field.

Sanatkumara said, “The fake ascetic, listening to her words, and being well-versed in meeting his selfish ends, fixed his gaze upwards.

At the same time two monkeys arrived there and took their seats in front of the sage. With the indication of his eyebrow, they atonce disappeared in the sky again.

O Great sage, within a second, both the monkeys returned carrying with them the head, body and the limbs of the Daitya and stood in front of the sage.

Looking at the head, body and the limbs of her husband, Vrnda fell unconscious. She was extremely painful at the misery of her lord.

Vrnda said, “O Lord, earlier, you used to delight me with pleasant stories, then why are you not now talking to your innocent wife?

You are the one who had been victorious over Gandharvas, Visnu and all the gods, you are the conqueror of the three worlds, then how can an ascetic kill you?

You are the best of the Daityas, being unaware of the Rudra-tattva, you did not accept my words. I had told you that Siva is the Supreme Brahman.

I could know the secret of it only by serving you. Because of your arrogance and the evil company, you forgot everything.”

In this way Vrnda- the chaste wife of Jalandhara who was quite firm in her dharma, spoke much for long and started lamenting for long, which could break the heart.

Then she some how composing herself, taking deep sighs then spoke to the sage with folded hands.

Vrnda said, “O Ocean of mercy, doing good to others, becoming compassionate on me, bring my husband back to life.

O Excellent sage, as far as I believe, you are competent enough to bring my husband back to life. Therefore you restore the life to my husband.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, the chaste Vrnda, who was immensely devoted to her husband, heaving sighs of relief, fell over the feet of the sage.”

The sage said, “He has been killed by Siva in the battle-field, therefore he cannot be brought back to life. Those who are killed by Siva, cannot be brought back to life.

Still, being merciful, I shall bring him back to life, because following the Sanatana dharma, the person who takes refuge, should be protected.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, thus speaking, the sage disappeared, from the scene, bringing her husband back to life.

Then Jalandhara, who was brought back to life stood up. With a delightful mind, he embraced Vrnda who was also delighted.

Looking at her husband Vrnda too was pleased. She was freed from sorrow, considering everything to be a sheer dream.

Delighted at heart, and with his passions aroused, she sported with him for many days in the forest itself.

Once at the end of the intercourse, she realised that he was Visnu and not her husband. She rebuked him in anger and said.

Vrnda said, “Disgrace to you, O Visnu for outraging the modesty of another man’s wife. I have now come to realise that you are an illusory ascetic.

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, and getting enraged, she displayed her excessive brilliance as a chaste lady, she pronounced a curse on Kesava.

“O Immensely degraded enemy of the demons, you shatter the dharma of others. O Wicked one, you listen to my curse, which is greater than all poisons, and you should receive it.

By displaying the two Raksasas to me with your illusion, they would be turned as the demons in reality and shall kidnap your wife.

You, yourself, suffering from the separation of your wife, with the lord of serpents who is acting as your disciple, will wander in the forest with him.”

Thus speaking, Vrnda who was immensely devoted to her husband, much against the wishes of Visnu, reciting the name of her husband, entered the fire flames.

O Sage, at that point of time, all the gods with their wives, reached the sky in order to witness of redemption of Vrnda.

Then the excellent brilliance of the wife of the Daitya in full view of all disappeared from the scene.

The brilliance of Vrnda, then entered the body of Parvati and the gods assembled in the sky, started shouting the slogans of victory.

O Sage, in this way, Vrnda- the queen and the daughter of Kalanemi because of the influence of her chastity, was redeemed.

Then lord Visnu, remembering Vrnda, picked up the ashes of her funeral pyre, and plastered it over his body. Thereafter inspite of the advice of the gods and the Siddhas, he could achieve no peace.

## Chapter 24 - Killing of Jalandhara at the hands of Siva

Vyasa said, “O Son of Brahma, O Intelligent one, you have narrated thus astonishing story. What happened in the battle-field thereafter and tell me how was he Daityaraja killed?

Sanatkumara said, “When the Daityaraja could not find Parvati, he returned to earth and with the end of the illusion of Gandharva, Siva, regained his senses.

Finding the disappearing of his illusion and also realising about the secret connected therewith, following the worldly practices, Siva, the destroyer of the world, got immensely enraged.

Then Siva, getting surprised and enraged, got ready to wage a war with the Daitya. The Daitya too finding the arrival of Siva, shot arrows at him.

The valorous Jalandhara, when so showered the arrows over Siva, the latter atonce cut off the demon's arrows, with his own arrows. This was no surprise for Siva, the destroyer of Tripura.

The astonishingly valorous Jalandhara, making use of his illusion produced Gauri, in order to confuse Siva.

She was shown in captivity over the chariot, by Sumbha and Nisumbha, who was being beaten by them. Siva witnessed the sight.

Thus looking at Parvati, conducting himself in the worldly manner, Siva was upset.

Siva, the master of many sports, lowered his head, exhausted and forgetful of his own prowess.

Then Jalandhara, quickly attacked Siva in his chest, belly, head with three arrows which pierced down deep as far as their feathered tail.

Then Siva, the great god of illusion, took to a terrific form in an instant and took to horrible form blazing in all the sides.

With the appearing of Siva in that horrible form, many of the Daityas could not face him and were turned shaky. All of them fled to all the directions.

O Excellent sage, the well-known warriors Sumbha and Nisumbha, could not stand firmly in the battle-field. The illusion created by Jalandhara, then vanished instantaneously. All over the battle-field, there was a great hue and cry.

At the flight of Sumbha and Nisumbha, the angered Siva, rebuked them pronouncing a curse on them.”

Siva said, “Both of you are extremely wicked. You have angered me by harassing Parvati and now you are deserting the battle-field.

(According to the prevailing tradition) a person fleeing from the battle-field has not to be killed. Since you, having escaped from my hands, would now be killed at the hands of the goddess.”

At these words of Siva, Jalandhara, the son of Sindhu resembling the fire, became furious with Siva.

Then he started shooting the sharp arrows at Siva, with great force As a result of this, the earth was covered with darkness with the arrows shot the demon.

As soon as Siva cut off those arrows quickly, the demon then attacked the bull of Siva with parigha.

Feeling painful with the attack, the bull returned from the battle ground. Siva was dragging him to his side but the bull did not stop.

Thereafter Siva revealed his unbearable splendour before all in the battle field. O great sage, this is true.

Siva appearing in a horrible form, at once became furious and suddenly turned himself into fire of the time of dissolution.

Finding the Daitya standing before him like the peak of the Meru mountain, Siva then thought that he was invincible by others. Therefore he himself got ready to kill hem.

Siva- the protector of the entire universe, honouring the words of Brahma, spreading compassion from his heart, got ready for the killing of the demon.

Then Siva becoming immensely furious exercising his divine sport made a mysteriously terrible wheel in the great waters of the ocean with his big toe.

Creating a sharp wheel in the oceanic waters and remembering the three worlds, which had been troubled by Jalandhara, lord Siva, who had killed Daksa, Andhaka, Antaka and destroyed the Tripuras, besides the yajna of Daksa and annihilated the three worlds, laughingly said.

Siva said, “Jalandhara, in case you are powerful enough to lift the wheel created by me with the leg in oceanic waters, you will be competent to stand and fight with me and not otherwise.

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of Siva, the eyes of the Daitya became red in anger, and he appeared like burning Siva with his eyes. Then he spoke.

Jalandhara said, “After lifting up the wheel, I shall kill you with your ganas. I shall kill all the people and the gods in the world, like Garuda killing the snake. I can kill mobile and immobile in the world along with Indra. O Lord Siva, who is there, in the three worlds, who can escape unhurt from my arrows.

I had conquered Visnu with my tapas in my childhood. Brahma with the gods, the ascetics and the sages are lodged in my house.

O Rudra, you have in an instant reduced to ashes the three worlds including mobiles and immobiles. You have overpowered the lord with your tapas.

The gods like Indra, Agni, Yama, Kubera, Varuna and others can hardly bear my prowess in the same way as the Nagas cannot bear the smell of Garuda in any way.

O Siva, I could not get my vehicle, in the heaven and earth. Going to all the mountains, I have defeated Ganesvara.

I have smashed the mountains like Himalaya, auspicious blue mountain and beautiful Sumeru mountain, for the relief of my itching arms

Just for my sport, the river Ganga, was stopped by me at the Himalaya mountain itself. Even my warriors were victorious over the gods who happened to be my enemies.

I caught hold of the submarine fire and shut its mouth. In a moment at that time the entire world was submerged in water.

I drowned Airavata and the other elephants in the oceanic waters. I threw away Indra at a distance of a hundred yojanas.

Using the *Nagapasa* I bound Visnu with the same. I prisoned Urvasi and other *apsaras.*

O Rudra, you know nothing about Jalandahra, the conqueror of the three worlds, and is immensely strong, Supreme Daitya.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, the son of the ocean, the Daitya did not recall the Daitya warriors who had been killed in the battle, nor did he move this way or that way.

Then the wicked demon slighted and rebuked Siva uttering harsh words haughtily pulling his arms forcibly.

On hearing the inauspicious words of the demon, Mahadeva laughed and became furious.

Siva then held in his hand the Sudarasana cakra which he had made with his big toe and got ready to kill the demon.

Siva held the Sudarsana cakra in his hand, which resembled the lustre of crores of Suryas, or like the fire of the time of dissolution, and shot it at the Daitya.

Then the Sudarsana, putting in flame, the sky as well as the Patala, reached before Jalandhara with great force and cut off the demon's head having vast eyes.

Echoing the earth with the sound of the fall, the head as well as the headless body of the Daitya fell from the chariot on earth and an uproar was created at the time of the fall of the Daitya. His body resembled the collyrium, fell in two parts in such a way as the Vajra cuts a mountain in two parts.

His terrific blood splashed in the entire universe, making it red. O Excellent sage, thereafter, the entire earth was deformed.

At the instance of Siva, the entire flesh and blood was carried to Raurava hell, which caused a huge pit of blood, there.

The lustre emerging out of his body was absorbed into the body of Siva like the lustre emerging out of the body of Vrnda was absorbed into the body of Parvati.

The killing of Jalandhara delighted all the gods, the Gandharvas, besides the serpents, who uttered, “Well done, O Lord.”

The gods, Siddhas and the great ascetics were immensely pleased singing the glory of the lord, with the showering of the flowers.

Overpowered with joy the divine damsels lovingly danced, in the company of Kinnara, who sang in harmonious sweat voice.

With the fall of the husband of Vrnda, all the directions were filled with ecstasy. The cool breeze carrying the fragrance started blowing.

The moon became cool, the sun regained its lost lustre, the fires started burning peacefully and sky became clear.

O Sage, in this way all the three worlds of the universe regained health and normalcy, after the killing of the son of the ocean at the hand of Siva the form of Ananta.

## Chapter 25 - God’s prayer to Siva

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter, Brahma and other gods, besides the sages, eulogised Siva quite humbly with the pleasant words.”

The gods said, O Mahadeva- the god of gods, well-disposed with those taking refuge in you, you always bestow comforts to the noble people removing the miseries of your devotees at the same time.

Your divine sports are astonishing. You can be achieved with devotion alone, otherwise you are inaccessible.” The wicked people cannot adore you. O Lord, you always remain pleased with us.

Even the Vedas are unaware of your real form. The noble ascetics recite your glory according to their own wisdom.

Your glory is extremely secret, which is sung by serpent Sesa with a thousand hoods, quite lovingly, purifying their speech with the same.

O Lord of the gods, by your grace even the sluggish become face to face with Brahman. According to the Vedas, you can be achieved by devotion alone.

You are compassionate on the destitutes, all pervading, and you appear with devotion alone. You are unblemished and the protector of the noble people.

O Mahadeva, several of the devotees have achieved salvation, with your devotion. Those who adore you in Sahara form, enjoy all the pleasures and those who adore you in nirvikara form have to suffer in the long run.

O Lord, in earlier times your devotee Yadupati, the son of Dasaraha, and his wife Kalavati attained the Siddhi with your devotion.

O Devesa, the king Mitrasaha and his wife Madayanti, because of your devotion achieved salvation.

Saumini, the daughter of the king Kaikeya, enjoyed pleasures, because of her devotion to

you, which are beyond the reach of the *yogis.*

O Lord, the excellent king Vimarsana, enjoyed all the pleasures upto the seven births and finally achieved salvation.

Candrasena- the great king, because of his devotion for you, was relieved of all the miseries and became comfortable in this as well as in the future birth

Srikara- the son of a milkmaid, achieved salvation because of your devotion and becoming the disciple of Mahavira and achieved heaven.

You, removing all the miseries of Satyaratha, bestowed salvation on him. Making Rajagupta- the prince, comfortable in this world you redeemed him.

O Great lord, similarly, you also made the Brahmana Sucivrata quite wealthy. You also showered your grace over your devotees with little knowledge.

Citravarma, the great king, because of your devotion, achieved inaccessible pleasures in this world and also achieved the salvation.

The prince Candrangada together with his wife, getting relieved of all the miseries, enjoyed all the pleasures and achieved the salvation.

The Brahmana Mandara who visited the whore being a degraded person, by becoming your devotee, after adoring you achieved the high position with her.

The prince Bhadrayu, was your devotee and by your grace he was relieved of all the miseries and he ultimately achieved salvation.

O Mahesvara, whosoever is engaged in the enjoyment of the women, or a wicked or unholy person, consuming formidable things, he also achieves salvation with your devotion.

O Siva, your devotee named Sambara, who used to apply regularly the ashes of the pyre over his body, and with the following of this practice regularly, he achieved Sivaloka with his wife.

O Lord, the son of Bhadrasena and the son of his courtier, followed the noble path, and always wore Rudraksa.

By your grace, both of them enjoying all the pleasures in the world, achieved salvation by your grace. The two devotees who had been a monkey and a cock in previous births, became the ornaments of Rudra. O Lord, you are always engaged in uplifting the devotees. The two female devotees Pingala and Mahananda, the whores, achieves redemption.

Sarada- the daughter of a Brahmana, became widow during childhood. With the influence of your devotion she became virtuous and also got a son.

The Brahmana named Binduga, was attracted to a whore, and was Brahmana for name-sake alone. His wife, received the highest place, listening to your glory.
