O Lord, O Mahesan, O Kin of the distressed, abode of mercy, several people have been redeemed with your devotion.

O Lord, you are Mahesvara, beyond Prakrti and Purusa. Because of you yourself being Nirguna, you happen to be the base of the three gunas- Brahma, Visnu and Íṁrṁ.

O Mahesvara, you remain unblemished inspite of your numerous daily activities. You are the lord of all. All the gods including Brahma are your slaves.

O Lord, O Siva, O Devesa, be pleased with us. We have taken refuge with you. We are your subjects. You always protect us.

Sanatkumara said, “Thus Brahma and other gods together with the excellent sages, offered prayer to Siva, and then concentrating their minds at the feet of Siva, they kept quiet.

Listening to the pleasant prayer of the gods, Siva, pronounced boons on them and then disappeared from the scene.

After the killing of the enemies, Brahma and other gods, feeling delighted, singing the glory of Siva, returned to their respective places.

The story of the killing of Jalandhara, by Siva is the excellent one and destroys the sins.

The prayer offered to him by the gods, removes all the sins. He is the bestower of all the comforts and such prayer always please Siva.

Whosoever reads and recites them, he achieves all the comforts in this world.

## Chapter 26 - Visnu’s applying of Vrnda’s ashes over his body-removal of the delusion of Visnu

Vyasa said, “O Best of the devotees of Siva, son of Brahma, salutation to you. You are quite graceful for narrating the divine story of Siva.

O Sage, I would pray to you to lovingly narrate the story of Visnu. He deluded Vrnda, but what happened thereafter? What did Visnu do and where did he go?

Sanatkumara said, “O Intelligent devotee of Siva, O Excellent Vyasa, listen, the story of Visnu is linked with the story of Siva and is spotless.

After Brahma and other gods kept quiet, the lord- well-disposed towards those taking refuge in him.

Lord Siva said, “O Brahma and all other gods, Jalandhara had been bom of my amsa, still I killed him for your sake.

Tell me whether you are now comfortable or not. I am without blemish. All my divine sports are for your sake alone.”

Sanatkumara said, “Then the eyes of Brahma and other gods blossomed with delight. They lowering their heads offered their salutation to the lord and then narrated the story of Visnu.”

The gods said, “O Mahadeva- the god of gods, you have saved us from our enemy, but in the meantime something else has happened. What should we do about it?

Visnu deluded Vrnda, making great efforts, who embraced the fire flames and achieved the highest position.

Having been deluded with your illusion, Visnu applied the ashes of Vrnda’s pyre and is staying there.

Having been deluded with your illusion, inspite of the best advise of the gods, the Siddhas and the sages, rendered to him quite respectfully, he is unable to understand anything.

O Siva, you kindly advise Visnu appropriately. The Prakrti besides the mobiles and the immobiles are subservient to you.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the gods, the great performer of the divine sports, spoke to the gods with folded hands.”

Lord Siva said, “O Brahma and all other gods, you listen to my words with respect. My unlimited illusion casts its influence on all.

The gods, asuras, humans, and the entire universe are subservient to my illusion. Under the influence of the same, Visnu has become lustful.

The great goddess Uma produces all the three gods. She happens to be the Mula- Prakrti. She is none else than Girija herself.

O Gods, for the removal of the illusion of Visnu, you better approach goddess Parvati or Siva, also known as Maya, besides the protector and the fulfiller of all the desires.

All the gods sing the prayer which pleases my Sakti. In case she is pleased, she would carryout your task.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, thus speaking to the gods, the five faced lord Siva, suddenly disappeared with his ganas.

As per the command of Siva, Brahma, Indra and other gods mentally adored Bhagavati- Mula-Prakrti who was well- disposed towards the devotees.”

The gods said, “The one from whom the universe, the three attributes- Sattva, rajas and tamas, which cause creation, sustenance and destruction, have emerged, and by whose desire the universe is evolved and dissolved, we bow in reverence to the same primordial Prakrti.

May the great illusion save us, the great Prakrti which presides over the twenty three principles, well enunciated in the universe, we bow to the primordial Prakrti whose form and the activities are unknown to the three worlds.

We bow in reverence to the primordial Prakrti who is favourably disposed towards the devotees. The persons devoted to her are not overpowered by poverty, delusion and destruction.

O Great goddess, kindly perform our task. O Parvati, kindly remove the delusion of Visnu. O Goddess Durga, salutation to you.

O Siva, when the fight between Jalandhara and Siva started, for killing of the Daitya king, Vrnda was deluded by Visnu, at the instance of Gauri. She was made to shed away her virtue and she finally reduced herself to ashes in the fire; achieving salvation at the same time.

Jalandhara was killed at the hands of Siva and we were all freed from his terror. Then lord Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, mercifully commanded us to adore you.

At his command, we have arrived here to take refuge with you. O Goddess, you yourself as well Siva are engaged in redeeming your devotees.

Deluded with the beauty of Vrnda he is still wandering there. He has been deprived of the wisdom and applying the ashes of Vrnda’s pyre, Visnu has been deluded.

O Mahesvari, inspite of the best advice of the gods and the Siddhas, influenced with your illusion, Visnu is unable to free himself from the delusion.

O Great goddess, kindly bring Visnu back to consciousness to enable him to protect the Visnuloka and perform the task of the gods.”

After this prayer of the gods, they saw a sphere of refulgence pervading the entire sky with its flames.

O Vyasa, Brahma and other gods, including Indra, heard the divine voice from the sky bestowing their desire.”

The divine voice said, “O Gods, it is I, who stand in the three forms with the three attributes of Sattva, rajas and tamas, which represent Gauri, Laksmi and Sarasvati.

Therefore, you go to them at my instance with respect. In case they are pleased, they would fulfil your desire.”

Sanatkumara said, “While the gods were so listening to the divine voice with surprise, there refulgence suddenly disappeared from the sky.

Inspite of that all the gods, listening to the divine voice and inspired with the same, offered their salutation to Gauri, Laksmi and Sarasvati.

Then Brahma and other gods eulogised them lowering their heads, and with the reciting of several stotras.

O Vyasa, then all the goddesses, illumining all the directions with their lustre, appeared before them.

Then the gods offered their salutation to them with delightful hearts, and then they revealed their task before them.

Then the goddesses, who are well-disposed towards the devotees, found the gods eulogising them offering their salutation to them. Giving them the seeds they said to them.”

The goddesses said, “You take these seeds and sow them at the place where Visnu is lodged. Your task would be established, after doing so.

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, the Trigunatmika Saktis of Brahma, Visnu and Siva, disappeared, after speaking thus.

Then all the gods including Brahma and Indra, delightfully carried the seeds to the place where Visnu was seated.

Then the gods, devoting their minds at the Saktis who were the amsas of the three gods, sowed the seeds over the ground where Vrnda was reduced to ashes in the fire. O Sage, all of them stayed there. Out of the seeds three plants were grown known as Dhatri, Malati and Tulasi.

Out of the seed, Saktis of Brahma, Dhatri sprouted, out of the seed of Laksmi, Malati sprouted, and out of the seed of Gauri, Tulasi was grown.

O Sage, “Out of those female forms of the vegetations, and because of his immense love for them, Visnu woke up.

Having been overpowered with lust, he demanded out of delusion. On the other hand Dhatri and Tulasi too looked at Visnu quite lovingly.

The seed which was given earlier as representing Laksmi, the woman emerging out of it, became jealous.

Therefore, she earning the name of Barbari, was denounced in the world. Both Dhatri and Tulasi became dear to Visnu.

Thereafter Visnu forgetting all his sufferings, went with them to Vaikuntha, where all the gods offered their salutation to them.

O Narada, during the mouth of Kartika, Tulasi and myrobalan are dear to all the gods, but more so to Visnu.

O Excellent sage, out of these, Tulasi is more excellent and graceful. She is dear to all except Ganesa and fulfills all the desires.

At the arrival of Visnu in Vaikuntha, all the gods eulogised him and offering salutation to him retired to their respective abodes.

O Excellent sage, with the disappearing of the delusion, and regaining of the wisdom, lord Visnu, while living in Vaikuntha, started devoting his mind to Siva, as before.

This story destroys all the sins of the humans, fulfills all the desires, removes all blemishes of passions and increases wisdom.

Whosoever listens to this story, daily or makes others to read or listen to the same, he undoubtedly achieves the supreme position.

The intelligent and valorous warrior, who after reading this story enters the battle- field, he surely becomes victorious.

This story bestows Brahmavidya over Brahmanas, victory to the Ksatriyas, riches to the Vaisyas, and comforts to the Sudras.

O Vyasa, this story bestows the devotion of Siva, is the destroyer of all the sins, and bestows the best position in the present as well as the future births.

## Chapter 27 - Performing of a tapas by Sambhasura for getting a son and birth of Samkhacuda

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, now you listen to the further story of Siva, lovingly listening to which, the devotion of Siva is firmly established.

The story relates to the killing of valorous demon Samkhacuda with the striking of a trident by Siva, who harassed the gods.

O Vyasa, you listen to the story of Siva, which I am going to narrate to you lovingly.

Kasyapa, the son of Marici who was the son of Brahma, was quite obedient to Brahma.

Daksa Prajapati had given his thirteen daughters to him as wives. Several children were bom of them, details of which I am not going to spell out for fear of expansion.

Who can describe in detail in the three worlds out of whom the entire mobile and immobile universe, besides the gods were born?

You listen to the relevant story which is filled with the illusion of Siva, which I am going to narrate. I am going to speak out the same.

Out of the wives of Kasyapa, there was the one named Danu, who was quite simple, humble and virtuous at the same time.

Danu gave birth to several valorous sons. O Sage, I am not giving the names of them, for fear of escalation.

Vipracitti happened to be one of them who was quite strong, valorous, devoted to Visnu and had controlled all the senses.

He was issueless. Feeling anxious he went to Sukracarya. Taking him as his preceptor, he received the Krsna-mantra from him.

Receiving the mantra he went to the Puskara-tirtha, and performed tapas for a lakh of years. Spreading an asana he kept on reciting the Krsna- mantra.

While he was so performing tapas an unbearable lustre emerged out of his head and was spread in all the four directions.

The gods, Manu and the sages suffering from that lustre, went to Brahma making Indra as the leader, and took refuge with him.

Brahma, who bestowed all the riches, was adored by them all, who also offered salutation to him. Offering prayer to him, they getting upset, specifically apprised him to the news.

Listening to the news, Brahma with all the gods went to Visnu in order to communicate the news to him.

Reaching there, they started offering prayer to Visnu the lord of the three worlds and great protector.

The gods said, “O Mahadeva- the god of gods, we are totally unaware about the lustre from which we are suffering and what was the reason for the same.

O Kin of the destitutes, you are the protector of your suffering slaves. We have come to take refuge with you. You kindly protect us.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Brahma and other gods, Visnu who is well- disposed towards those who take refuge in him, said.

Visnu said, “O Gods, all of you should keep patience and be healthy. Don’t be afraid. This is not the time of dissolution. Dambha, my devotee is performing tapas for getting a son. I shall pacify him with the pronouncing of a boon.

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, at these words of lord Visnu, the gods were pacified with pleasant hearts, they went back to their respective places.

Visnu then went to the Puskara-ksetra in order to bestow the boon at the place where the Danava named Damba had been performing tapas.

Reaching there, he assured him variously and then with the sweet voice spoke to his devotee who was performing tapas for him, “Ask for a boon.”

Listening to these words of Visnu, who was standing before him, he offered him his salutation again and again and then he eulogised him.

You kindly bestow your devotee a son, who should be strong and valorous, conqueror of the three worlds, and should be invincible from the gods.

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, at these words of the lord of Danavas, Visnu, stopped him from his performing the hard tapas and bestowing the boon to him disappeared from the scene.

After the departure of Visnu, the Danava, who had been successful in his tapas and his desire having been fulfilled, he offered his salutation to the direction towards, which Visnu had gone and then he went back to his home.

After sometime his wife conceived. She possessed lustre inside her abode.

O Sage the Jiva of Sudama, the friend of Krsna, who was a cowherd and was cursed by Radha, entered her womb.

His wife in due course of time, gave birth to an illustrious son. His father summoned several sages and performed his birth ceremony.

O Narada, after his birth a huge festival was organised. On an auspicious day, the father gave him the name of Samkhacuda.

Thereafter the child kept on growing like the moon of the bright fortnight. Receiving education during his childhood, he became quite illustrious.

He delighted the minds of his parents, with his child like sports. In due course of time, he became the beloved of his kins and relatives.

## Chapter 28 - Performing to tapas by Samkhacuda and his marriage with Tulasi

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter, at the advice of the sage Jaigisavya, Samkhacuda performed tapas at Puskara in the region of Brahma.

Controlling all his senses with the knowledge of Brahmavidya by his preceptor, Samkhacuda, started performing tapas with the concentrated mind.

Finding that Samkhacuda- the demon was performing tapas, Brahma, the preceptor of the universe arrived there in order to bestow boon on him.

Reaching there he said to the Daityaraja, “Ask for a boon.” The Daitya offered his salutation to Brahma, and then started eulogising him lovingly.

He asked for a boon from Brahma, that he should be invincible from the gods. Brahma, getting pleased said to him, “Be it so.” For this purpose he gave him away the Krsna-kavaca which bestowed welfare on the universe and made the holder victorious everywhere.

Then he said to him to go to Badarikasrama, where Tulasi was performing tapas of her own will. “You therefore marry her.

She is the daughter of Dharmadhvaja.” Thus speaking, Brahma, in full view of all disappeared from the scene.

Then Samkhacuda, achieving success in his tapas at Puskara, binding the auspicious kavaca around his neck, being successful in his tapas, with the delighting face, at the command of Brahma, atonce proceeded on to Badrikasrama.

Samkhacuda reached of his own accord, where Tulasi, the daughter of Dharmadhvaja had been performing tapas.

Finding the smiling beautiful charming woman fully adorned with ornaments, cast a loving glance at the great man.

On looking at the charming, tender, beautiful and chaste damsel, he stopped near her and spoke sweet words to her.

Samkhacuda said, “Who are you? Whose daughter are you? What are you doing? Why do you stay here and observe silence? You consider me as your devoted slave.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing these words, she lovingly spoke to him.”

Tulasi said, “I happen to be the ascetic daughter of Dharmadhvaja and am performing tapas in the forest. But who are you? You better leave this place comfortably.

The damsels even delude Brahma. A woman is like poison, is to be denounced and is the cause of blemishes. She is the form of illusion and is like the chain for the thinkers.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking the pleasant words, she kept quiet. Finding her so smiling,

Samkhacuda said, “Whatever has been spoken by you is not at all false. Your words comprise of some truth as well as some falsehood therefore you please listen from me.

You happen to be the foremost of all the chaste women. I am also not sinful with a lustful eye and as far as I believe you would also not be like that.

Presently, I have reached here at the command of Brahma and I intend to own you by the Gandharva type of marriage.

I am Samkhacuda, who gives away the due share to the gods. O Beautiful one, you do not know me well, nor have you ever heard my name.

I am particularly the son of Dambha of the demon race. In earlier birth, I had been Sudama, the friend of Krsna.

I have become Daityaraja because of the curse from Radha. By the glory of Srikrsna, I happen to remember the events of my earlier birth.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, Samkhacuda kept quiet before Tulasi. At these words of the lord of Danavas, she gracefully said, “Your words are true.” Then Tulasi smiled and said.

Tulasi said, “You have defeated me with your satvik thoughts. A man who is not defeated by a woman is really graceful.

Even the performing of the noble deeds could be unclean. A person who is defeated by a woman, is denounced by the gods, the manes as well as the humans.

A Brahmana is purified from the impurity of birth or death in the family after ten days, a Ksatriya is purified in twelve days, a Vaisya in fifteen days and the Sudra in a month. This has been ordained in the Vedas, but a person who is defeated by woman cannot be purified before death.

His manes do not accept happily, the pindas of rice and the sacred water offered by him, besides the offerings of fruits and flowers.

Of what avail are the knowledge, tapas recitation, homas worship the lord as well as the charities of a person, whose mind has been overpowered by the woman.

I had put you to test in order know about the depth of you wisdom. A woman should accept a husband by putting him to test.

Sanatkumara said, “When Tulasi was so speaking to Samkhacuda, Brahma arrived there and spoke to them.

Brahma said, “O Samkhacuda, what are you talking to her. You perform the Gandharva type of marriage with her.

You are gem among the men and she is the gem among the women. The union of person with wisdom with a lady with wisdom is always virtuous.

O King, who would leave the chance of happiness, unless forced to do so. He who does so of course is a brute.

O Chaste woman, to which type of test, you are putting to such a virtuous husband, who can smash all the gods, asuras and the Daityas.

O Beautiful one, you roam about with him in all the places in all the lokas.

Ultimately you would again achieve your four armed Krsna in Vaikuntha and Goloka.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus blessing them Brahma returned to his own place, while both of them married in the Gandharva fashion. Samkhacuda then went to his father after his marriage with Tulasi and started enjoying the worldly pleasures in the pleasant palace.

## Chapter 29 - Previous birth of Samkhacuda

Sanatkumara said, “After performing tapas and getting married Samkhacuda, returned to his place, where all his relatives felt delighted,

Then coming out of their loka, all the Daityas together with Sukracarya, went to Samkhacuda, collectively.

Finding their lord to be quite an illustrious one, all the Daityas offered their salutation to him with all humility. Then they loving by adoring him took their seats.

Then the son of Dambha, finding the arrival of his family priest Sukracarya, respectfully prostrated before him.

Then the family priest Sukra, looking at him pronounced his blessings on him. Then he started narrating the stories of Devas and Danavas.

He started narrating of the natural enmity between the gods and the Danavas, the defeat of the Daityas, the role played by Brhaspati in the victory of the gods.

Then all the Danavas after consulting among themselves, declared Sukracarya as their preceptor.

The delightful asuras then celebrated the occasion with great pomp and show. All of them lovingly gave several presents to Sukra.

Thereafter abhiseka of Samkhacuda, the son of Dambha was performed, after which he looked illustrious like Indra.

Then he leading a vast army of Daityas, Danavas and Raksasas, himself mounting over a chariot, marched on towards the city of Indra, in order to conquer him.

The Daityaraja, accepting the services of the Danavas, kept on marching looking graceful like the moon surrounded by the constellations or the sun surrounded by the planets.

When the self-illumining moon came to know about the arrival of Samkhacuda, he himself, together with all the gods, became ready to fight with the demon king.

This resulted into a great war between the gods and asura warriors, which delighted the valorous people and frightening the eunuches, which was quite terrific.

With the thundering sound of the great warriors an uproar was created. The war bands were increasing the enthusiasm of the warriors.

The asuras were fighting with the gods getting angry. After their defeat the demons fled away from the battle-field getting frightened.

Finding that, Samkhacuda, the lord of the Daityas that the Daityas were fleeing from the battle-field, he intensified the war uttering the lion's roars.

Sportingly, he crushed all the gods. The gods, being unable to face Samkhacuda’s lustre, fled from the battle-field.

All the gods feeling painfully, hid themselves in the mountain caves. Losing their lustre, the gods became subservient to the asuras like Jalandhara- the son of the ocean.

Thereafter, the valorous Samkhacuda- the son of Dambha, conquered all the lokas and usurped all the privileges of the gods.

He conquered all the three lokas, usurped the shares of the yajnas and declaring himself to be Indra, started ruling over the entire universe.

He himself usurped the powers of Kubera, the moon, the sun, Agni, Yama, Vayu and others and ruled with his own might.

Thus Samkhacuda became the lord of all the gods, demons, Danavas, Raksasas, Gandharvas, Nagas, Kinnaras, as well as the lords of earth.

Thus Samkhacuda became the lord of the three worlds, and all others, being immensely valorous and powerful.

Thus Samkhacuda, the king of kings enjoyed pleasures and comforts of all the Bhuvanas for many years.

There was no draught in his kingdom, nor any epidemics. There were no obstructions in his country or inauspicious planets. There were no ailments. The subjects were always happy and comfortable.

The earth could yield various types of crops without sowing. The Osadhis were juicy and effective.

The mines produced the gems, while the oceans produced the jewels. The trees were always laden with the fruits and flowers and the rivers always remained filled with the clean water.

All the people felt comfortable without the gods, besides being unblemished. The people of all the four varnas were devoted to their respective duties.

During the rule of Samkhacuda, no one felt painful. Because of the traditional enmity only the gods remained uncomfortable.

The valorous Samkhacuda was an intimate friend of Krsna. He always remained devoted to Krsna, the dweller of Goloka.

Because of an earlier curse, he had been bom in the demon race. O Sage, inspite of his being a Danava, he did not possess the temperament of a demon.

After having been defeated by the Asuras and having been deprived of all their rights, all the gods confabulated amongst themselves and accompanied with the sages, reached the court of Brahma.

Meeting Brahma, they offered their salutation to him and especially offered their prayer to him.

Brahma assuring the gods and the sages, went to Vaikuntha to meet lord Visnu, who made the noble people comfortable.

Brahma then accompanied with other gods, had an audience with Visnu the lord of Laksmi adorned with the kundalas and the kirita crown.

In his four hands he held Samkha, cakra, gada and lotus. He was clad in yellow costumes, and was being served by Sanandana and other sages.

Looking at the grace of lord, Brahma with all the gods, Rsis, ascetics, offered their salutation to him with folded hands, besides eulogising him.

The gods said, “O God of gods, O Lord of the universe, O Lord of Vaikuntha, you are the master of the three worlds, O Sri Hari, we have arrived to take refuge with you. Kindly save us.

O Lord of the three worlds, O Acyuta, O Master, O Govinda, O Life of the devotees, you happen to be the protector of the universe.”

Thus eulogising Visnu all the gods started crying before Visnu. On hearing them Brahma was addressed by Visnu.

Visnu said, “What for have you arrived in this Vaikuntha, which is beyond the reach of even the yogis? What ails you? speak out truthfully before me.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Visnu, the gods, folding their hands offered their salutation to Visnu again and again.

Then they narrated the tale of sufferings of Devas at the hand of Samkhacuda before high-souled Visnu.

Then Visnu who was aware of all the happenings around, smiled and revealed the secret to Brahma.

The lord said, “O Brahma, the cowherd of my earlier birth is devoted to me. I am well aware of the news about Samkhacuda the illustrious one.

You better listen to the story of his earlier birth. Don't have any doubt in it. Lord Siva will shower welfare on you all.

Siva's loka is lodged above all, He is the Supreme Brahman and the lord of all being Paramesvara.

He is the presiding deity of Prakrti and Purusa. He possesses all the three Saktis. He is with and without attributes. He possesses the supreme lustre.

O Brahma, the three deities bringing about creation etc. are bom of him. They are Visnu, Brahma and Siva and are endowed with Sattvika, and other attributes. He alone is the Supreme soul. He sports there with Parvati. He is free from illusion. He is the formulator of the eternal and non-eternal.

The Goloka is near it. Siva's cows shed is situated there. Krsna having my form stays there at the behest of Siva.

It is to tend his cows and the bulls, that he has been so ordered by him. Deriving happiness from him, he sports there.

His wife Radha is the mother of the universe. She has the form greater than the Prakrti. It is the fifth sportive form.

There are several milkmaids and the cowherds who had been born out her limbs. Roaming there, they are the followers of Krsna.

Samkhacuda, having been overpowered with the illusion of Siva, uselessly achieved the birth in the demonic race.

It has earlier been started by Krsna that he would meet his death with the trident of Siva. Then he being relieved of his present body would become an attendant.

Realising this, O Lord of gods, don't be panicky. You go and take refuge with Siva, who would bestow welfare on you.

Let me, yourself and all the gods stay here feeling assured.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, together with Brahma, Visnu went to Siva, the lord of all and who was well-disposed towards his devotees, reciting his name in their minds.

## Chapter 30 - Gods’ prayer to Siva for the slaying of Samkhacuda

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, Brahma and Visnu the lord of Laksmi, proceeded on to the extremely divine and unearthly Sivaloka.

Feeling delightful at heart, Visnu's face was beaming. The region was illumining with the gems studded in the same.

The first entrance gate was guarded by the surprising type of ganas. It was quite high, extremely beautiful and looked quite charming.

He found that the gatekeepers were clad in white garments and seated over the gem- studded lion-thrones, adorned with all the ornaments.

They found them with five faces, three eyes, fair complexions', quite powerful, applying the ashes over the body and wearing Rudraksa.

Both Brahma and Visnu humbly offered their salutation to them and then spoke to them that they wanted to have an audience with the lord.

They permitted them to enter, after which they saw another door which was quite brilliant and variegated.

They informed the gate-keeper of their intention for meeting the lord and they then entered the gate with the permission of the gatekeepers.

In this way Brahma had to pass through fifteen gates and reached the main gate, which was guarded by Nandi.

Eulogising him properly, both of them were permitted by Nandi to enter the gate as was done earlier. Thereafter both of them entered inside.

Reaching inside, they found the raised assembly hall of Siva, which was lighted by itself. He was surrounded by his courtiers clad in five garments and adorned with all the ornaments.

All of them were five faced, ten arms, three eyed, blue necks, with beautiful lustre and fair complexion.

All the ganas were adorned with gem-studded Rudraksa and other ornaments. They had applied ashes over their bodies. The chamber was square in shape and was shining like the lunar disc.

The gems, necklaces, diamonds etc. added to the grace of the place. Valuable precious stones were used to stud them and was lighted with the lotus petals, quartz, rubies and other valuable were used for its decoration. It was really wonderful and was laid as per the desire of Siva.

It had hundreds of steps, leading to it, each one of which was made of Syamantaka gems and the knotted golden thread joined them. There were beautiful sprouts of sandal wood in it.

It was supported by the pillars of sapphire and was richly decorated. The fragrant wind blew everywhere.

The chamber was a thousand yojanas in width. Numerous servants stood in attendance there. Visnu the lord of gods saw Siva seated with Parvati.

Siva was surrounded by his attendants like the moon surrounded by the stars. He was seated over excellent throne studded with valuable gems.

His head was adorned with a crown, besides ear-rings in the ears. His neck was decorated with the gem-studded necklaces. He had smeared his body with the ashes and he held a lotus flower in his hand.

He was delightful wearing a smile over his face and witnessing the dance accompanied with the music.

The calm and delightful Parvati, offering a fragrant betel leaf to Siva, was seen by them.

The ganas on both the sides were moving the fly-whisks over them. The Siddhas were humbly offering prayer to them.

The great lord Siva, who was the progenitor of the three gunas, the lord, who was beyond the reach of attributes, who assumes and discards his forms as he likes, and is invariable, who is free from illusion, is unborn, the primordial being, the lord of illusion, he is greater than the greatest and even great then the Prakrti and Purusa.

Looking at Siva with the perfect features, both Brahma and Visnu eulogised him together bowing in reverence to him with folded hands.

Brahma and Visnu said, “O Mahadeva- the god of gods, the Supreme Brahman, O Akhilesvara, O Quiet one, you are beyond the three gunas, O Progenitor of the three gods, O Lord.

O Paramesvara, O Lord, we have been antagonised and are shelterless. We have been harassed by Samkhacuda and have arrived here to take refuge with you. You kindly save us.

The region which is close to this place is known as Goloka and Srikrsna is the lord of the same and you happen to be the presiding deity for him.

One of his leading attendants had been Sudama, who by the move of destiny has been born as a Daitya as a result of the curse pronounced on him by Radha.

O Lord Siva, he has driven away the gods from their positions. The gods having been deprived of their rights, feel painful and have become a wandering lot.

He cannot be killed by any other god, except you. O Siva, by killing him you make all the lokas quite comfortable.

You are Nirguna, the truth, beyond measure, and possess the prowess beyond measure. Even in your saguna form you are beyond Prakrti and Purusa.

At the time of the creation, because of rajoguna, you are the creator of the universe. With Sattvaguna you function as the sustainer of the universe in the form of Visnu, and during the time of dissolution you take to the form of Tamoguna- Rudra, for the destruction of the universe. Besides these three forms, you have the fourth form of Siva, which happens to be the brilliance.

Because of your diksa, you are yourself the protector of the cows in the Goloka. In your cowshed, Krsna roams about daily.

You are the basic cause of all and their lord. You are beyond Brahma, Visnu and Siva. You are unblemished, always a witness, the Supreme soul as well as Paramesvara.

You help the destitutes and those without support. You are the protector of the down-trodden and kin of the distressed. You are the lord of the three worlds, and you love those who come to take refuge with you.

O Lord of Gauri, O Paramesvara, be pleased with us, and uplift us. O Lord we are subservient to you. Now you do as you like.

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, thus speaking, both Brahma and Visnu, humbly offered their salutation to Siva and kept quiet.

## Chapter 31 - Siva’s discourse for gods

Sanatkumara said, “ Siva listening to the pathetic words of Brahma and Visnu, smiled and spoke the words rumbling like the clouds.”

Siva said, “O Brahma, O Visnu, you be free from the panic caused to you by Samkhacuda something nice would emerge from the activities of Samkhacuda.

I am well aware of the cowherd Sudama the devotee of Krsna, who has been reborn as Samkhacuda.

At my bidding, Visnu has assumed the form of Krsna and is living in the Goloka’s cowshed presided over by me.

Earlier he was overpowered with delusion, thinking himself to be free and started sporting independently.

Finding this, I increased his delusion with my illusion by removing his noble wisdom and got a cursed pronounced on him.

Thus sporting I suppressed the illusion. Regaining knowledge there, they were relieved of the delusion and they (Radha and Krsna) got back the nobel wisdom.

Feeling distressed they came to me and they offered salutation to me with folded hands. Then Radha and Krsna humbly eulogised me with their hands folded.

Feeling shameful they narrated their story. Feeling distressed they prayed for protection from me. Then I said to them delightfully. “O Krsna, you forget your fear at my behest.

I am the protector, always infused with love, something good will befall on you. Whatever has happened, has happened at my will. There is no doubt about it.

Go to your abode along with Radha and your associates. He will certainly become a Danava in the land of Bharata.

In due course of time you both will be redeemed of your curse. You accept my words with Radha quite gracefully.’’ Krsna with noble wisdom felt extremely delighted on hearing this and left for his abode and feeling frightened, he kept on adoring me.

Thinking that the entire world was subservient to me, and his was not independent, Sudama became the lord of the Danavas as a result of the curse of Radha.

The noble Samkhacuda who was inimical to the gods and was evil-minded, is presently causing pain to the gods.

He has been overpowered with my illusion and is receiving advice from his wicked courtier who says, “During my rule, you should be free from the danger from the gods.”

Sanatkumara said, “While Siva was so talking with Brahma and Visnu, another incident took place. You Listen about the same.

In the meantime Sri Krsna and Radha accompanied with the cowherds and his courtiers, arrived there in order to appease lord Siva.

They offered their salutation to lord Siva, with devotion, and meeting with him, they took their seats with his permission.

Again offering their salutation to Siva they again started eulogising him. Getting relieved of the delusion, they became aware of Sivatattva.

Sri Krsna said, “O Mahadeva, god of gods, O Supreme Brahman, you bestow the salvation to the noble people. O Paramesvara, you kindly forgive me for my fault and be pleased with me.

O Mahesvara, O Paramesvara, everything emerges from you. Everything is lodged in you and you happened to be the lord of all. Be pleased with us.

You are the greatest lustre, you are the eternal being directly pervading everything. O Lord of Gauri, we are well guided, with you being the leader.

I had been overpowered with delusion. I used to roam about thinking myself to be Supreme. As a result of which, I have received the curse of a woman.

O Master, Sudama- the best of my courtier was a cowherd. He has been born in the demon race because of the curse of Radha.

O Lord of Durga, O Paramesvara, we take refuge with you and you kindly redeem us.”

Thus talking, both Radha and Krsna stopped and Siva who is well-disposed towards those who take refuge in him, was pleased.

Siva said, “O Krsna- the lord of milkmaids, getting relieved of the fear, be comfortable whatever has been done by you was done at my behest.

You go to your place and you would meet with welfare. Remaining alert, you should remain within your limits.

Taking me to be better than the best you can roam about at your own will. You engage yourself in your duties with Radha and courtiers.

You shall undergo the effect of your curse with the young damsel Radha in Varaha kalpa and then attain your region.

O Krsna, your friend and the most beloved Sudama, has now been bom as a Danava and has caused pain to the universe.

Presently he is a Danava and an enemy of the gods and is known by the name of Samkhacuda, as a result of the curse of Radha. He supports the Daityas and is inimical to the gods.

He had driven out all the gods including Indra from their abodes and is causing pain to them. He has usurped all their prerogatives. Because of this the gods have been scattered in all the ten directions.

Both Brahma and Visnu have arrived here because of the same reason to take refuge with me. I shall surely relieve them of all their sufferings.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, Siva then apprised Krsna, about the suffering of the gods.”

Siva said, “O Brahma, O Visnu, hear my words with joy. Both of you can go back for the delight of the gods.

Rudra is my complete form who is the dweller of Kailasa. I have taken to that form for the performing of the task of the gods.

O Visnu, my complete form resides over Kailasa and is subservient to the devotees.

There is no difference between you and myself but my that form is meant to be served by both of you. That form is adorable by all the gods, the mobiles as well as the immobiles.

Whosoever conceives of any difference between two of us surely falls in the hell. He is deprived of the sons and the grandsons who suffers in this world.”

When the lord of Parvati was so talking Sri Krsna together with Radha, offered their salutation to lord Siva, again and again and left for their abodes with their cowherds.

O Vyasa, then Brahma and Visnu, getting relived of the fear, delightfully went to Vaikuntha, offering their salutation to Siva again and again.

Reaching there, they apprised the gods of the factual position and accompanied with the gods they both Brahma and Visnu, went to the Kailasa mountain.

They saw Siva, the lord of Parvati the Saguna leader of the gods had taken to human form for the protection of both of them. The lord of the gods, possessing the attributes was eulogised by them as before with devotion and with choked voice, folded hand and bending their shoulders with humility.

The gods said, “O Mahadeva, the god of gods, O Lord of Girija, O Sankara, all the gods getting frightened have arrived here to take refuge with you. You kindly protect us.

You destroy the demon Samkhacuda- the lord of the Danavas, who has been harassing the gods. He has defeated all the gods in the battle-field making them nervous.

Having been deprived of all the prerogatives, we are now wandering on earth like all the human beings. Terrified from him, we are presently cannot even look at the heaven.

O Ocean of compassion, you better redeem all the three gods from the misery. Killing the Daityaraja save Indra from fear.”

Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, after listening to the words of the gods, smiled and spoke the words resembling the rumbling tone of the clouds.

Siva said, “O Brahma, O Visnu and other gods, you better go back to your abodes. I shall surely kill Samkhacuda with his warriors.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the nectar like words of Siva, all the gods took the Danava as having been killed and were pleased.

Thereafter Brahma returned to Satyaloka, Visnu to Vaikuntha and the gods returned to their respective places.

## Chapter 32 - Siva’s deputing Puspadanta as a messenger to Samkhacuda

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter Isan, Maharudra, destroys of the evil forces, protector of the noble people, Siva, at the desire of the gods, resolved in his mind for the killing of Samkhacuda.

Siva then sent Citraratha the lord of the Gandharvas to Samkhacuda as his messenger.

He, at the command of Siva, reached the city of Samkhacuda, which was far more beautiful than the cities of Indra and Kubera.

He found there that the palace of Saihkhacūda was the best of all, having twelve gates which were guarded by the gatekeepers.

Spotting the best of gatekeepers, Puspadanta, fearlessly told him the purpose of his arrival.

Passing through that gate, he delightfully entered inside the palace. The place was extremely beautiful, charming, vast, and glamorous.

He found Samkhacuda, seated over the gem-studded lion-throne, surrounded by the warriors.

He was surrounded by three crores of the Daitya kings and a hundred crores of Daitya- warriors were patrolling around him, carrying the weapons.

Finding the Daitya king with such a glamour, Puspadanta was surprised, and he delivered the message of Siva to him.

Puspadanta said, “O Lord Rajendra, I am the messenger of Siva, known by the name of Puspadanta. I am going to deliver the message of Siva to you, which you please listen.

Siva has said, “You better return the kingdoms and the prerogatives of the gods, otherwise you fight with me.

The noble gods have taken refuge with me. I being Maharudra am annoyed with you. Therefore I would surely kill you.

I have assured full protection to the gods. I am well-disposed towards those who take refuge with me and punish the wicked people.

Are you going to return the kingdoms to the gods or are going to fight with me? O Lord of the Danavas, you think over and let me know either of the two alternatives.”

Puspadanta said, “This is the message of Siva to be conveyed to you and I have done that. O Lord of Danavas, the words of Siva cannot be otherwise.

I intend to return to my lord Siva atonce. What should I convey to him on my return? You please tell me.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus listening to the words of the messenger, the Daitya king laughed and said him”.

Samkhacuda said, “I shall never return the kingdoms of the gods to them because the land is to be ruled by the brave men. I shall face Rudra- the supporter of the gods in the battle-field.

The warrior who allows others to attack him is considered to be the basest in the world. Therefore, I shall surely attack Rudra first.

O Valorous one I shall start on victory march tomorrow morning. You better convey my message to Rudra.

Thus listening to the words of Samkhacuda, the messenger laughed and then spoke to the arrogant Daitya king.

Puspadanta said, “O Lord of kings, you cannot stand before Siva and his ganas. It is entirely different to face Siva.

Therefore you atonce return all the prerogatives of the gods to them and you yourself flee towards Patala, in case you intend to remain alive.

O Best of the Danavas, don’t treat Siva, as an ordinary god. He is the god of all the gods besides being Sankara- the Supreme soul.

All the gods like Indra and others, besides Prajapati, Siddhas, sages and Nagaraja are under his command.

He is the lord of Brahma and Visnu. He take to Saguna form inspite of his being nirguna. He is the one with the winking of whose eyebrow, the dissolution of the world is caused.

Siva is the destroyer of the universe, He is the protector of the noble people, destroyer of the wicked people. He is unblemished and better than the best.

He is the lord even of Brahma and Visnu. O Best of the Danavas, you should not insult his command.

O Rajendra, what is the use of speaking much more, thus thinking in your mind, you consider Mahesan as Supreme Brahman and the knowledge supreme.

Return the prerogatives and kingdoms of the gods and by doing so you would meet welfare. You will have to face danger, in case you act otherwise.”

Sanatkumara said, “Overpowered with the moves of destiny, the glorious Danava king, spoke to the messenger of Siva.

Samkhacuda said, “I shall not return the prerogatives and kingdoms to the gods of my own, without waging a war. I am speaking this truthfully.

The entire mobile and immobile world is subservient to the time. Everything is established according to the time and is destroyed in due time.

You better go and convey my words to Rudra. He would do whatever he thinks best. Don’t talk much.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, the messenger of Siva, returned to his master and reaching there he conveyed to him the factual position.

## Chapter 33 - Departure of Virabhadra, Nandi, Kali, Asta-Bhairavas, and other Sivaganas

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the messenger, Siva spoke to Virabhadra and other *ganas.*

Siva said, “O Virabhadra, O Nandi, Ksetrapala, Astabhairava, and all powerful *ganas,* get ready with all the weapons.

At my command, all of you should, under the leadership of the princes, march today itself, Bhadrakali should also proceed with her army. I am also starting for the killing of Samkhacuda.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus commanding the warriors, Siva marched forward with his army followed by the valorous warriors.

In the meantime Skanda and Ganesa, the leaders of the entire army, delightfully went to Siva carrying the weapons with them.

They included Vlrabhadra, Nandi, Mahakala, Subhadraka, Visalaksa, Bana, Pingalaksa, Vikampana, Virupa, Vikrti, Manibhadra, Vaskala, Kapila, Dirga-damstra, Vikara, Tamralocana, Kalankara, Balibhadra, Kalajihva,Kuticara, Balonmatta, Ranaslaghya, Durjaya, Durgana and several other ganas, besides the chiefs of the army the number of which I am going to tell you. You please listen to it carefully. Samkhakarna- the destroyer of the enemy force, was accompanied by a crore of warriors. Kakaraksa had ten crores, Vikrta had ten crores.

Visakha had sixty four crores of ganas, Sarvantaka had six crores of warriors, Sriman Sarvantaka had six crores, and an equal number was with Vikrtanana.

Jalaka- the leader of the ganas had twelve crores of warriors with him. Samada had seven crores, Sriman Dundubha had sixty crores, Vikrta had eight crores.

Karaksa had five crores, Sandaraka had six crores, Kanduka and Kundaka had a crore of warriors each.

Vistambha, who was the best of all the Ganadhipas, had eight crores, besides Pippala and Sannada had a thousand each.

Avesan and Candratapana had eight crores each, besides the Ganadhupa known as Mahakesa, was surrounded by a thousand crores of warriors.

Kindin and Parvataka had twelve crores of warriors each. Kala, Kalaka and Mahakala had a hundred crores each.

Agni had a hundred crores, Agnimukha had a crore; Aditya and Ghanavaha had half a crore each.

Sannaha and Kumuda had a hundred crores each; Amogha, Kokila, and Sumantraka had a hundred crores each.

Kakapada and Santanaka had sixty crores each. Mahabala had nine crores, while Madhupingala had five crores.

Nila, Devesa and Purnabhadra had ninety crores each, while Mahaball and Pancavaktra had seven crores each.

Accompanied with thousands, hundreds and twenties of ganas the warriors reached the battle ground, for celebrating the war-festival.

A thousand crores of goblins, thirty crores of Pramathas, three crores of lomajas, and sixty four crores of ganas accompanied Virabhadra, who also arrived there.

Kastharudha, Sukesa and Vrsabha, were sixty four crores in number. Virupaksa the ancient lord, arrived with his army of sixty four crores of ganas.

Talaketu, Sadasya, Pancasya, Samvartaka, Caitra, Larikulisa, Svayamprabhu, Lokantaka, Dipatma, Daityantaka, Prabhu, Devabhrngi, Srimana. The one dear to the god of gods, Asani and Bhanuka, sixty four thousand crores of Kahkalas (Skeletons) Kalaka, Kala, Nandi, Sarvantaka, these as well as several other great warriors, whose number was without counting, together with their *ganas* arrived there fearlessly in order to wage a war against Samkhacuda. All of them marched on for the purpose of fighting with Samkhacuda.

All of them had a thousand elephants, wearing the crowns of locks of hair, and had a crescent lodged over the heads. They were all having blue throats and three eyes each.

All of them had applied ashes over heir bodies and were wearing the garlands of Rudraksa. They were adorned with haras, kundalas, keyuras as well as the crowns.

Like Brahma, Visnu and Indra, they possessed several siddhis like anima and others. They possessed the lustre of crores of suns, and were well-versed in warfare.

O Sage, many of them could roam about on earth, sky, Patala as well as the seven heavens.

O Narada, what is the use of speaking much, all the Sivaganas who dwelt in all the lokas, arrived there for the purpose of fighting with the Danavas.

Eight Bhairavas, Ekadasa-Rudra, eight Vasus, Indra and the twelve Adityas arrived there rapidly.

Agni, the moon, Visvakarma, Asvani- Kumara, both the Kubera, Yama, Nirrti, Nala- Kubara, Vayu, Varuna, Buddha, Mangala and other planets, the powerful Kamadeva, arrived with lord Siva.

Ugradamstra, Ugradanda, Karata and Bhadrakali with a hundred arms, besides the goddess Mahesvari also arrived there who was seated over the best of the gem-studded lion- throne, clad in red garments, wearing the garland of red flowers, and applying the red sandal paste over the body.

She was dancing and singing in sweet tone. She was smiling and assuring protection to her own class of divinities, and frightening the enemies.

She had a long moving protruding tongue. She was holding a samkha, cakra, gada, padma, bow and the arrow in her hands.

She carried a round skull, besides a trident which was a skull, besides a trident which was a yojana in length and a sakti, of similar touching length the sky.

She also carried a mudgara, musala, a vajra, a sword, a shield, Vasrav-astra, Varunastra, Vayavyastra, Nagapusa, Narayanastra, Gandharvastra, Brahmastra, Garudastra, Parjanyastra, Pasupatastra, Jhimbhastra, Parvatastra, Mahavira, Saura, Kalakala, Mahanala, Mahesvarstra, Yamadanda, Sammohanastra, Divyasamarthastra, besides another two hundred divine and other weapons, were held by her in her hands.

Three crores of yoginis, besides three and a half crores of Dakinis also arrived there with Kali.

Skanda, who had been surrounded by goblins, pretas, pisacas, Kusmandas, Brahmaraksasas, Betalas, Yaksas and offered his salutation to lord Siva. With the permission of his father he sat besides him.

Thereafter, Siva, accompanied with his entire army, becoming fearless, marched on for waging a war with Samkhacuda.

Then Siva rested under the pleasant shade of a banyan tree which was grown over the bank of the river Candrabhaga (modem Chenab) in order to free himself from the fatigue of the journey.

## Chapter 34 - Samkhacuda proceeds for waging a war

Vyasa said, “O Son of Brahma, immensely wise sage, you live for long since you have narrated the great story of Siva.

What did the glorious Samkhacuda do, after the departure of the messenger of Siva. You please speak out the same in detail.

Sanatkumara said, “After the departure of the messenger, the glorious Samkhacuda, went inside the house and revealed the matter in its totality of his wife Tulasi.”

Samkhacuda said, “O Goddess, listening to the words of the messenger of Siva, I am getting ready for the war. Therefore you please permit me to do so.”

Thus speaking the intelligent Samkhacuda, convinced his wife variously. Insulting Siva, he enjoyed the pleasures with his wife.

Both the wife and husband, enjoyed several types of sports speaking sweet words and were absorbed in the ocean of pleasure.

Rising up in the early morning, getting free from the daily routine, he gave away enormous charities.

His son who was the best of all the Daityas, was crowned as the king who was entrusted with his entire riches and the wife.

He consoled his crying wife variously with noble words, assuring her at the same time.

Then he gracefully summoned his army commander and asked him to be ready for the war.”

Samkhacuda said, “O Army Commander, all the warriors should get ready today and march for waging the war.

All the Daityas, Danavas, and the valorous army of the Kankas, should fearlessly march on.

The fifty races of asuras, and a crore of asuras should march on to fight with Siva, the supporter of the gods.

A hundred races of the Daitya named Dhumra, should march on to fight with Siva, at my command.

The Kalakujas, Mauryas, Dauhrdas and Kalakas should get ready and march on at my command to fight with Siva.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus issuing the command, the immensely valorous king of the Danavas, followed by thousands of armies, marched on.

His army commander was well-versed in warfare and the use of arms, while the charioteer was well-versed in driving the chariot.

He was accompanied with three lakh aksauni army and formed horrible army formations, then marched out of the army camp and reached the battle ground.

Then he, having been infested with enormous pride, boarded the gem-studded plane and proceeded on for the waging of the war.

There is an Aksayavata (ever green banyan) tree over the bank of he river Puspabhadra and the Siddhasrama is located in the Siddhaksetra which bestows success to all.

There is the tapobhumi of the sage Kapila in the Punyaksetra of Bharata. The place is located to the east of the western ocean and to the west of the Malayacala mountain.

In the northern region of Srisaila and to the south of the Gandhamadana mountain the region is spread in the area of five hundred yojanas in length and five yojanas in width.

In the land of Bharata, there is the Punyabhadra river having the water clean like the crystal rock.

She happens to be the spouse of the ocean of salt water. (It falls into the western ocean) and is always meritorious. It originates from the Himalaya and joins the river Sarasvati.

Flowing from the left side of Gomanta, this river falls into the western ocean. Reaching there, Samkhacuda, found the army of Siva.

## Chapter 35 - Exchange of messengers from both the sides

Sanatkumara said, “Then Samkhacuda- the lord of the Danavas, sent an immensely intelligent person known as Danavesvara to Siva as his messenger.

Reaching there, he found Candrasekhara Siva having the lustre of a crore of suns and was seated under the tree of Vata.

He was seated in Yogasana in dhyanamudra, showing the mystic gesture with his eyes, with a smiling face and the body as pure as the crystal and blazing with transcendent splendour.

Siva had an iron gada and a trident as his attributes. He was wearing the tiger skin. The messenger saw the three eyed lord of Parvati, who destroyed the death of his devotees, the peaceful Siva, who bestowed the fruits of the penance, the creator of the fortunes and was quick to be propitiated, eager to bless the devotees. His face was beaming with pleasure. He saw the lord of the universe, identical with the universe, and of the universal form, bom of all, lord of all, creator of all, the cause of the destruction of the universe, the cause of the causes, the one who enables the devotees to cross the ocean of hell, the bestower of knowledge, besides being the seed of knowledge, blissful and eternal.

On seeing him, the messenger, the leader of the Danavas descended from his chariot and bowed in reverence to Siva as well as to Kumara.

He also saw Bhadrakali standing to his left and Kartikeya standing before him. Kali, Kartikeya and Siva offered him the customary blessings.

The messenger of Samkhacuda was well aware of the sacred texts. Bowing in reverence to Siva with his hands folded, he spoke the auspicious words.

The messenger said, “I am the messenger of Samkhacuda and have arrived before you. O Siva, what is there in your mind, you tell me truthfully.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus listening to the words of the messenger of Samkhacuda, lord Siva was pleased.

Lord Siva said, “O Intelligent messenger, you better listen to my pleasant words. You yourself thinking carefully, tell him in unambiguous terms.

Marici was the son of Brahma, who was well aware of all the dharmas. He had a son named Kasyapa.

Lovingly Daksa given in marriage to him his thirteen daughters. One of them was the daughter named Danu, who increased the fortunes of Kasyapa.

Danavas were the four sons of Danu who were quite illusions. One of them was Vipracutti. His son named Dambha, was immensely wise and a religious minded one. You are his son- being the lord of Danavas besides being immensely religious one and the best of all.

In your earlier birth you were a cowherd and immensely religious minded. Presently you have become the lord of Danavas, because of the curse of Radha.

Though you have been bom in the Danava race, but you are actually not a Danava. Realising the position of your earlier birth, you shed away the enmity with the gods.

Don’t be inimical to them. You enjoy your position quite gracefully. Do not try to expand your kingdom nor should you spoil it.

O Danava, getting devoted to me, you return the kingdoms to the gods. You remain in your kingdom with pleasure. Let the gods enjoy their own positions.

Don’t trouble the people and preserve no malice against the gods. The descendants of Kasyapa are the noble people, and followers of the noble path.

Whatever the sins like Brahma and other are there in the world, do not merit even one sixteenth part of sin emerging from the offence against the kinsmen.”

Sanatkumara said, “These as well as many other words of advice auspiciously based on the Srutis and Smrtis, were spoken by Siva to him enlightening him in an excellent way.

The messenger who had been well briefed by Samkhacuda, and who was well aware of his responsibility, but had been deluded by the destiny and as such he replied to Siva, quite humbly.

The messenger said, “O Deva, every word of your speech is totally correct, but still you kindly listen to my truthful and the factual words.

You have just now stated that it is a terrific sin to work against the kinsmen. Then O Lord, is it meant for asuras alone and is not applicable to the gods?

In case it is applicable to all of them, I, on deep thinking say something over which you kindly convey your decision in order to remove our doubt.

O Mahesvara, at the time of dissolution, why did Visnu cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha?

O Girisa, why did you destroy Tripurasura in the battle field taking the side of the gods?

Why was Bali forced to go to Patala after usurping his kingdom and fortunes? Why is Gadadhara getting ready to redeem Sutala and the other regions.

Why was Hiranyaksa killed by the girls with his brother? Why were Sumbha and other demons killed by the gods?

In ancient, times, why was the nectar that emerged from the churning of the ocean, totally consumed by the gods? The trouble was taken by us and the benefit was gained by the gods.

The entire universe is but an object of sport of Kala- the Supreme soul. Whomsoever and whenever, he pleases to bestow the fortunes, he gets them.

The enmity between the gods and the demons has been going on for some reason or the other. The victory and the defeat are subservient to the Kala.

In the enmity between the gods and the demons, the interference by the lord of the universe is of no consequence. Because the enmity suits the related parties.

You are the lord of the demons as well as the gods. (The interference by you) is quite shameful, since you are picking up a row with us.

This is because the winner gains much glory and after defeat one gets denouncement. Both the situations are opposite to your performance. You give this situation a thought in your mind.”

Sanatkumara said, "Thus listening to the words spoken by the messenger of Samkhacuda, Siva spoke, appropriate words to the messenger, which suited the occasion.

Siva said, “I am subservient to the devotees and have never been independent. I perform according to their desire. I never take sides.

In earlier times listening to the prayer of Brahma, there was a fight between Visnu and Madhukaitabha.

At the prayer of the gods, Visnu, who had been favourable to the devotees, killed Hiranyakasipu in order to save Prahlada.

My fighting with Tripura and reducing it to ashes was done at the request of the gods.

The other demons of the universe, killed Sumbha and other demons at the specific prayer of the gods.

Presently all the gods took refuge with Brahma. Then both Brahma and Visnu, took refuge with me.

O Messenger, at the prayer of Brahma and Visnu, I being the lord of the gods, have arrived in the battle-field.

You happen to be the foremost of the courtiers of Krsna. Out of the Daityas who have been killed till now, no one had been so religious minded as you are.

O King, why should I feel shy of fighting with you. I being Siva, has been specifically deputed by the gods with all humility.

You better go and tell Samkhacuda, all whatever has been spoken by me to you. Let him do whatever he likes. I am performing the task of the gods.”

After thus speaking, Siva kept quiet. Thereafter the messenger of Samkhacuda, got up and returned to his lord.

## Chapter 36 - Fight between the gods and the Danavas

Sanatkumara said, “The messenger on his return apprised the Samkhacuda of the factual position, quite correctly, besides conveying the message of Siva to the Daitya king.

Samkhacuda then commanded his courtiers, to get ready for fighting with Siva, mounted over the chariots. Then he commanded his army to get ready.

On the other hand, Siva inspired his own army and he himself got ready sportingly.

The battle started, several war bands started playing. The lion’s roars as well as the thundering sounds were created.

Then the Dharma-yuddha (battle based on religious principle) was started.

Mahendra himself fought with Vrsaparva, Bhaskara fought with a religious mind with Vipracitti.

A great war was fought by Visnu with Dambha. Kala fought with Kalasura, Kalakeya fought with Kubera, Yama fought with Visvakarma, Mrtyu fought with Bhayankara besides Yama with Samhara.

Varuna fought with Kalambika, Vayu fought with Cancela, Budha with Ghata-prstha, while Sani fought with Raksasa.

Ratnasara fought with Jayanta, Astavasus fought with Varcas-ganas, Asvanikumara with Diptimans, and Dhumra fought with Nalakubara.

Dhurandhara fought with Dharma, Ganakaksa fought with Mangala, Sabhakara with Vaisvana and Pipita fought with Kamadeva.

The twelve Adityas fought with Gokamukha, Curna, Khadga, Dhumra, Samhala, glorious Visva, and Plasa with Dharma. All the gods helping Siva, fought with the asuras.

The eleven great Rudras, fought with the valorous and glorious eleven asuras.

Mahamani fought with Ugradanda, Rahu fought with the moon, while Sukra fought with Brhaspati.

Nandisvara and others fought with the best of the Daityas. The great war has not been described extensively.

O Sage, Siva was seated under the banyan tree with Kali and his son. The groups of soldiers were fighting among themselves.

Samkhacuda, adorned with gem-studded ornaments was seated over the lion throne.

A terrific war was fought in which the gods as well as the demons were killed with several of the great weapons were used in the war.

The warriors gracefully carried the weapons like the clubs, rsti, pattisa, cakras, Bhusndis, prasasas, mudgaras, nistrimsas, spears, parighas, Saktis and the raised battle axes.

The arrows, the tomaras, swords, thousands of Satghnis, besides the bhindipalas were carried by the warriors.

Several of the elephants, horses, chariots, and the foot soldiers, were torn to pieces.

The arms, legs, hands, waists, the ears, both the feet of the warriors, had been cut off with swords, kavacas etc.

The battle field had been littered with the severed heads decorated with the kirita crowns, besides the severed trunks of the elephants.

The severed arms adorned with ornaments were scattered in the battle field, and appeared like the fallen bee-Rivers.

Observing the Kabandhas (headless trunks of humans) running here and there, the severed hands started dancing carrying the weapons.

The valorous warriors carrying the weapons kept on jumping, while fighting with one another.

The warriors, started cutting the heads of one an other quite enthusiastically, displaying their prowess.

Some of the warriors killing the enemies with the golden tipped arrows, were thundering aloud like the clouds thundering with the shower of rain.

Some warriors covered the enemy warriors and the charioteer seated in the chariots in the same way as the clouds cover the sun.

The warriors engaged in the wrestling duel were challenging one another, while fighting, and striking at the sensitive points.

The crows of valorous warriors, were uttering the lion’s roar. They were carrying the Banners in their hands.

The forcefully blew their conches. The valorous warriors, feeling delighted, started jumping in delight.

In this way a terrific battle was fought between the warriors of both the sides, which delighted the brave people.

This was just the divine sport of Siva- the great lord, which influenced the gods as well as the demons.

## Chapter 37 - Samkhacuda’s fight with Kartikeya and other warriors

Sanatkumara said, “At that point of time, the Daitya defeated the gods, who fled away having been wounded with the weapons of the demons.

After their deserting the battle field, they took refuge with lord Siva. Getting upset, they shouted the slogans of “Save, us, Save us.”

Finding that the gods had been defeated, and listening to their frightened words, Siva was immensely irritated.

Siva bestowed protection on the gods, by casting a compassionate look on them. He increased their prowess wit his own lustre.

At the command of Siva, the valorous Skanda, the son of the lord, started fighting with the demons fearlessly in the battle field.

Then Skanda- the killer of Tarakasura, getting enraged uttered the lion’s roar, an then killed a hundred aksauni army of the demons in the battle field.

Then the lotus eyed Kali, cut off the heads of the demons and with the flowing of the blood, she started devouring the demons.

She kept on drinking their blood at the same time. Then she waged the war which was quite terrific for the gods as well as the demons.

She put a hundred lakhs of elephants, and an equal number of Danavas in her mouth in the battle field, quite playfully.

Thousands of headless trunks were dancing in the battle ground. A terrific uproar was caused at that time, which frightened the cowards.

Then Skanda getting irritated, started shooting the arrows and in a moment killed crores of asuras in the battle ground.

The bodies of the Danavas were wounded with the arrows shot by Skanda. Those who could escape death fled away from the battle ground.

The demons named Vrsaparva, Vipracitti, Danda, Vikampana, fought with Skanda one after the other.

On the other hand the goddess Mahamari (epidemic) started fighting without having any respite. The Daityas were injured with the Sakti of Skanda.

At that point of time both Skanda and Mahamari became victorious. The musical instruments were sounded in the heaven besides the showering of the flowers.

Observing the horrible and surprising type of battle of Skanda, resembling the Prakrti- kalpa, and finding the terrific destruction of the demon army by Mahamari, the Daitya king himself got ready to wage a war.

Carrying the excellent weapons with him he boarded the best of the plane, bestowing protection to his warriors

Getting ready with the immensely brave warriors, Samkhacuda, mounted the chariot. Then he stretched the cord of the bow upto the ears, and started showering the arrows.

No one could stop the showering of the arrows by him. A terrible darkness spread in the battlefield.

The gods and others fled from the battle ground, deserting it, leaving Kartikeya alone.

The demon king, then started showering the rain of mountains, serpents, trees and stones which was quite awful, and could not be stopped by anyone else.

With the showering of he stones etc. by Samkhacuda, Kartikeya felt painful like the sun covered with the fog.

The demon king then resorted to the spreading of the illusion- created by Mayadanava, which, O Excellent sage, could not be detected by the gods as well as the ganas of Siva.

At the same time the illusory demon king who was quite valorous as well, cut off the arrow of Kartikeya with the shooting of an arrow.

By shooting a divan weapon, he killed his peacock, shattering to pieces, his chariot.

Then he shot a Sakti, shining like the sun over the chest of the king of Danavas. With the attack of the same, he lay unconscious for a long time.

Then Kartikeya the killer of the enemy warriors, regained consciousness in a moment and then mounted over his vehicle studded with precious gems.

Remembering Siva and Parvati in his mind, Kartikeya fought a terrific war with his weapons.

Then the son of Siva destroyed all the weapons like serpents, mountains, trees, stones etc. on great war using his divine weapon.

Shooting the Parjanya- arrow, the fire was extinguished and he sportingly destroyed the chariot of Samkhacuda, besides his bow.

Then he also destroyed his kavaca, horses, kundalas, the shining crown, uttering lion's roars again and again.

Then he shot at Kartikeya a destructive Sakti; shining like the sun, which made him unconscious for a moment.

The valorous demon, getting relieved of the pain, and regaining consciousness, got up and uttered a lion’s roar.

Then he shot a Sakti at the valorous Kartikeya, who fell down on earth making the Sakti given to the Brahma, successful.

Then Kali carried Kartikeya in her lap to Siva, who playfully brought Kartikeya back to life with his jnana-drsti.

Then immense strength was bestowed by the lord on him, as a result of which the glorious one got up. The son of Siva, then desired to return to the battle field.

In the meantime the immensely valorous Virabhadra, started fighting with the strong Samkhacuda.

Whatever weapons were shot by the demon in the battle field, were made infructuous by Vlrabhadra with his arrows.

The lord of Danavas then shot hundreds of divine weapons, which were made infructuous by the glorious Vlrabhadra.

Observing this, the glorious Samkhacuda was immensely annoyed. Then he shot a Sakti at the chest of Vlrabhadra, as a result of which he fell down unconscious on earth.

The leader of the ganas regained his consciousness in a moment and got up again. The leader of the Sivaganas, then lifted up his bow.

In the meantime, at the command of Kartikeya, Kali again started devouring the demons, and saving the Sivaganas at the same time, entering the battle ground.

All the gods, Yaksas, Gandharvas, Raksasas, the serpents, Nandisvara and others started following her. Many warriors, got ready for the carrying of the vases filled with wine and the wear bands.

## Chapter 38 - Battle between Mahakali and Samkhacuda

Sanatkumara said, “Reaching the battle ground, Bhadrakali uttered the lion’s roar, which made the Danavas unconscious.

She, uttering in auspicious cries, she started laughing and drinking wine, she started dancing in the battle field.

She had protruding fangs, she held a danda in her hand. The goddess was without robes and she drank wine. All other goddesses drinking wine started dancing in the battle field.

At the same time a thundering uproar was created among the gods and the demons. All the gods started thundering with delight.

Finding Kali in the battle field, Samkhacuda at once reached there. The Daityas were frightened finding her there, and the Daitya king assured them his protection.

Kali then threw at the demon king the fire of the time of dissolution, which was extinguished by the demon king with the use of Vaisnavastra.

The goddess then opening her mouth devoured a large number of demons there and started laughing aloud frightening the demonic forces.

Like the fire flames of the time of dissolution, the weapon struck the chest of Samkhacuda, who fell down over the ground like a danda and started eulogising it again and again.

At the humility of the demon, the weapon returned. The goddess then reciting the mantra shot Brahmastra at the demon.

Finding the Brahmastra in flames approaching him, the demon offering his salutation to it, sat down over the ground. In this way the demon king made even the Brahmastra to retreat.

Then the demon king getting enraged, lifted up the bow with force and reciting a mantra shot a divine weapons at the goddess.

The goddess then brought into use the Narayanastra. The Danava finding that the better weapons were being used, by the opposite party, he also started using the superior weapons.

The demon then shot a hundred yojana long Sakti at the goddess, which was turned into hundreds of pieces by the goddess with the use of a divine weapon.

Then he again shot a Vaisnavastra at the goddess, which was made infructuous by Kali with the use of the Mahesvarastra.

In this way the battle went on for a long time, between Kali and the demon in full view of the gods as well as the Danavas.

Thereafter the goddess was enraged like the god of death, who reciting the mantras was about to shoot the Pasupatastra.

But before the shooting of that arrow, a divine voice was heard, asking the goddess not to use the said weapon over the demon.

It said, “O Candika, Samkhacuda is not going to be killed even with the use of Pasupatastra. You better think of some other way out.”

On hearing this, Bhadrakali, did not shoot that weapon. But she devoured a hundred lakhs of demons in a moment.

When the awful goddess rushed to devour the demon Samkhacuda, then the horrible demon stopped her from doing so with the use of the Divyastra.

Then the enraged Danava king holding the sharp edged sword which was shining like the sun of the summer season, threw it at the goddess.

Finding the sword approaching her in anger, the goddess opening her mouth, swallowed the burning sword.

The demon king then mode use of several other divine weapons, without any success, because the goddess reduced them all to hundreds of pieces.

The goddess then rushed towards him with force in order to devour him, but the demon, who had been the lord of all the siddhis disappeared.

Finding him missing, the goddess in anger, with use of her fist killed his charioteer and also broke his chariot to pieces.

Samkhacuda then returned atonce and shot a flaming cakra at Bhadrakali resembling the flame of the fire of dissolution.

The goddess, easily caught hold of that cakra in her left hand and put it in her mouth swallowing it at the same time.

Becoming forceful and enraged, she administered a powerful Vajra-like fist at him as a result of which the Danava king felt giddy and fell down on earth.

The glorious demon regained his senses in a short while but taking her to be like mother he did not indulge into a physical fight with her.

But the goddess, catching hold of him, rotating him again in the air, tossed him off in the sky.

The glorious Samkhacuda flew away with great force and falling down he offered his salutation to the goddess and then got up.

Then he mounted over the gem-studded plane without any confusion, started fighting again delightfully.

Kali then drank the blood of the Danavas because of her hunger. In the meantime a divine voice from the sky was heard.

“There are only a lakh of thundering Danavas in the battle field. Therefore, O Isvari, you better devour them.

O Goddess, the king of the Danavas is not going to be killed at your hands. Therefore you don’t think of killing him.”

On hearing the divine voice, the goddess ate the flesh and drank the blood of a large number of demons and then she went back to Siva. Reaching there, she apprised the lord of the factual position of the battle.

## Chapter 39 - The war between Siva and Samkhacuda

Vyasa said, “What did Siva do after listening to the words of Kali? O Intelligent one, you tell me correctly. I feel quite anxious about it.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Bhadrakali, Siva, the performer of the great sports smiled and spoke to her assuring her at the same time.

Siva who was well aware of the secret of the divine voice from the sky, thought over the matter and accompanied with his ganas, he went towards the battle ground.

Finding the Bhairavas, Ksetrapalas, Virabhadra and others, who were equally valorous as compared to Siva himself, he accompanied with them, he marched riding on the bull as his vehicle.

Taking to the form of a warrior, Siva approached the battle-ground. At that point of time Siva appeared like the god of death.

At the arrival of Siva, Samkhacuda, descended from the plane and prostrated before him.

Offering his salutation to him, he boarded the plan by yogic means and then picked up his bow and arrows.

Both Siva and the demon kept on fighting for a hundred years, by showering arrows at each other.

Samkhacuda was showering the harsh and sharp arrows, while Siva was destroying them with his own arrows. Maharudra Siva also known as Virupaksa, who punished the wicked people, protector of the noble people, was injuring the limbs of the demon's body with his arrows.

Then Danava, holding the shield and the sharp edged sword attacked the bull of Siva. Soon after the demon's attack over the bull of Siva, the lord cut off has shield and the sword with his special weapon, reducing them in pieces.

Danava Samkhacuda, then getting enraged, attacked Siva with his Cakra, which was reduced by Siva into pieces with the striking of a fist.

Then he furiously shot a club at Siva, which was reduced to ashes by rapid splitting by the lord.

Taking a Parasu weapon (axe) in his hand Samkhacuda, the lord of Danavas, rushed towards Siva.

Siva dropped him also on the ground, with the shooting of his arrows, together with his battle-axe.

The demon regained his consciousness after some time, and mounting his chariot, holding the arrows and the divine weapons, rose to the sky and looked graceful.

Finding that the demon was approaching him, Siva created unbearable sound from his bow as well as the damaru (small drum).

With his lion's roar all the directions were filled. Then Siva himself started thundering frightening the demon.
