The thundering sound of the bull-bannered Siva, which shattered the pride of the elephants, echoed in all the directions, besides the earth and the sky.

Then Mahakala struck the sky and the earth with both his hands, the thundering sound of which made all the demons completely upset.

The Ksetrapalas also laughed aloud, which was indicative of the future evil. Bhairava too thundered in the battle ground.

The thunderous uproar was created in the battle ground. The sound of warriors was heard in all the directions.

With the sharp thunderous and frightening sound, all the Danavas became fearful. Hearing this, the valorous king of Danavas was irritated.

When Siva spoke, challenging him, “O Wicked demon, stop for a while,” then all the gods and their ganas shouted the slogans of victory.

Then coming again the valorous son of Dambha hurled at Rudra his spear terrible with shooting flames.

The Sakti which was issuing the fire flames, was intercepted by Ksetrapala who destroyed it with the fire flame emerging from his mouth.

Then an awful war was fought between the demon as well as Siva, which shook the earth, mountains, lakes, etc.

Then thousands of arrows shot by Siva, as well as the arrows shot by the son of Dambha, were being neutralised by each other.

Then getting enraged, Siva shot a trident at the demon, which was unbearable and with its strike Samkhacuda was fainted and fell down on the ground.

He regained consciousness after some time, and the asura again started shooting arrows at Siva.

Suddenly Samkhacuda developed ten thousand arms and holding ten thousand Cakras in them, he surrounded Siva with ten thousand Cakras.

Then the great Siva- the remover of enormous miseries and the husband of Durga, getting enraged, destroyed all the cakras with his arrows.

The demon then accompanied with a huge army, arrived to face Siva, holding a gada in his hand.

Then Siva who shatters the pride of all the wicked people, cut off the demon’s *gada* with his sharp edged sword.

With the destruction of his gada, the danavas was immensely enraged and he carried a shining trident in his hand.

Finding the Daitya king approaching with a trident in his hands, Siva shot his trident with great force aiming at his heart.

With the striking of the trident at Samkhacuda’s chest, it was burnt out and another person emerged from his body who started shouting, “You stop here” repeatedly.

With the emerging of that person from the body of Samkhacuda, Siva cut off his head with the sword, who fell down on earth.

The enraged Kali then spreading her mouth, cutting the necks with her fangs, devoured many of the asuras.

The Ksetrapala too, getting enraged devoured many of the demons. The bodies of the rest were shattered with the weapons of Bhairava.

The intelligent Virabhadra, then he destroyed several other warriors, Nandisvara killed several other demons who troubled the gods.

Thus captivating them with anger, several warriors, shot several weapons which killed the demons who troubled the gods.

In this way the maximum army of Samkhacuda was destroyed. The remaining warriors fled away in fright.

## Chapter 40 - Taking to the form of a Brahmana, Visnu begs for the kavaca from Samkhacuda

Sanatkumara said, “The Danavas was immensely enraged, finding the best of warriors who were dear to him than his own life, having been killed in the battle field, he said to Siva, “I am ready to fight a battle, then what is the use of killing the soldiers. You better fight with me.”

O Sage, thus speaking the demon king god ready with a firm resolve. Then for waging a war, he appeared before Siva.

The Danava then shot a Divyastra at Siva- Maharudra. Then he shot arrows at Siva in the same way as the clouds shower the rain.

Disappearing from the sight, he displayed several types of illusory sports, which could not been imagined by any one of the gods.

Observing this, Siva shot the Mahesvarastra which was quite divine and could destroy the illusion.

With the lustre issuing from that weapon, all the illusions created by the demon disappeared and all the weapons shot by the demon became lustreless and infructuous.

Thereafter, the immensely powerful Siva, picked up his trident, for killing the demon which was unbearable even by the most illustrious people.

Suddenly a voice from the sky was heard, which said, “O Siva, don’t use this trident at present. Listen to our prayer.

You are competent enough to destroy the entire universe in a moment, what to speak of the killing of Samkhacuda alone.

You happen to be the master of all, therefore don’t destroy the Vedic discipline, but rather you make it applicable and successful.

Till such time the demon carries in his hand the kavaca of Visnu, and till such time the chastity of his wife is preserved, Samkhacuda could neither become old no meet with his death. These are the truthful words of Brahma.

Thus listening to the words of *akasavani,* Siva accepted those words. As desired by Siva, Visnu, the protector of the noble people, arrived there.

Then Visnu who was the best among the people with illusion, took to the form of an old Brahmana, went to Samkhacuda and said to him.

The old Brahmana said, “O Danava king, I have come to you for begging alms. Give me the alms.

O Kin of the down trodden. I shall not spell out my demand just now, but shall speak it out later, and you will truthfully materialise it.”

The request of the Brahmana, was accepted by Samkhacuda. Then he said deceitfully, “I would like to have your *kavaca.”*

The Danava king who had a great faith in the truthful Brahmanas, on hearing this, gave away the divine *kavaca* to the Brahmana which was dear to him than his life even.

After thus receiving the *kavaca* from Samkhacuda deceitfully, Visnu then went to the beautiful wife of Sankhacuda, known as Tulasi.

Visnu, who was well-versed in illusion, in order to establish the task of the gods, discharged his semen into the vagina of Tulasi.

Thereafter Visnu inspired Siva to kill Samkhacuda. Thereafter Siva, took up the burning trident in his hand.

Lord Siva, the Supreme soul, then held the trident in his hand, which filled the sky and the earth with its lustre.

Its lustre resembled crores of suns, of the noon time. It issued the fire flames, was invincible, and could never be infructuous, besides being the killer of the enemies.

It happened to be the leader of all the weapons. It was horrible and unbearable by the gods and the demons.

Issuing flames, it stood there, in a composite form for the destruction of the universe.

It was a thousand bows in length, and a hundred hastas in width. It was in the form of an individual as well as universal. It was eternal and uncreated.

The same trident whirled around the head of Samkhacuda for sometime and then fell on the head of the Danava at the behest of Siva reducing the Danava king to ashes.

O Brahmana, then the trident after killing Samkhacuda, rapidly returned to Siva and after its having finished the assigned task, returned by the aerial way with the speed of the mind.

The big drums were sounded in the heaven while the Gandharvas and Kinnaras sang. The gods and the sages, eulogised the lord, while the divine damsels kept on dancing.

The flowers were showered over Siva continuously, while Brahma, Visnu, Indra and other gods, praised him, besides the sages.

The Danava king Samkhacuda, was released from his curse with grace of Siva, who regained his original form.

The conches in the world are formed with the bones of Samkhacuda. The holy water emerging out of the conches is considered to be auspicious for all, except for Siva.

O Great Sage, the water from the conch is particularly sacred to Visnu and Laksmi, besides all the people who are devoted to Visnu and Laksmi. But it is not the case with Siva.

Siva, after the slaying of Samkhacuda returned to Sivaloka, mounted over the bull- his vehicle delightfully with Parvati, Kartikeya as well as Ganesa.

Lord Visnu returned to Vaikuntha, while Krsna became mentally peaceful. All the god then returned to their respective abodes quite delightfully.

The entire universe became normal and peaceful. The earth became free from the obstacles. The sky was purified and the entire universe became auspicious.

Thus the delightful story of Siva has been narrated by me, who removes all the miseries, bestows riches and fulfills all the desires.

It (the story) is graceful, bestows glory, enhances life and is the remover of all the obstructions. It bestows the devotion as well as the salvation, and fulfills all the desires.

The one who listens to the story of Siva, daily or recites or narrates to others, he surely attains riches, grains, happiness and particularly- the devotion of Siva.

The story is unparallel and removes all the obstructions. It bestows the best of knowledge and enhances the devotion towards Siva.

By listening to it, the Brahmana achieves the glory of a Brahmana, a Ksatriya become victorious, the Vaisya achieves riches, and the Sudra becomes the most excellent of the men.

**Chapter 41 - Tulasi's curse to Visnu**

Vyasa said, “How did Narayana plant his semen into the vagina of Tulasi? You please tell me about it.

Sanatkumara said, “Narayana is the protector of the noble people and performs the tasks of the gods. He enjoyed the company of Tulasi- the wife of Samkhacuda.

You listen to the relevant episode about Visnu, who obeys the command of Siva and Parvati.

Listening to the divine voice of the battlefield, Siva desired Visnu to bring the kavaca of Samkhacuda.

Then Visnu exercising his illusion, took to the form of a Brahmana and at once went to the Daitya-king and got the kavaca from him. Then Visnu taking to the form of Samkhacuda went to the abode of Tulasi.

The slogans of victory were shouted over the gate of Tulasl’s palace, besides the drums were beaten, making Tulasi to wake up.

Listening to those words, she felt delighted and with respect she started looking at the road outside.

She atonce gave away charities to the Brahmanas she atonce started celebrating the occasion. Hoping the arrival of her husband, she atonce decorated herself.

Descending from the chariot, Visnu taking to the form of Samkhacuda, went to the place of Tulasi, for the performing of the task of the gods.

Finding the arrival of her husband, she delightfully washed his feet and then started crying.

Then she made him sit over the beautiful lion-throne and offered him the betel v/ith camphor as the sign of welfare.

Then she said, “My life has become a success to-days that I find my husband having returned from war, quite hale and hearty.”

Thus spiking, she smilingly looked at him with unstable eye and enquired about the news of the battle ground, with sweet voice.

Tulasi said, “Lord Mahadeva, is the destroyer of innumerable worlds and his command is always honoured by Brahma and other gods.

He is the producer of all the three gods. Inspite of his being *nirguna,* he is known as Trigunatmaka. At the instance of Brahma and Visnu, and at the desire of his devotees he takes to Saguna form.

Siva is the dweller of Kailasa, lord of ganas, the Supreme Brahman, the movement of the noble people, had at the request of Kubera, taken to the Saguna form.

He can in a moment destroy crores of globes and in whose minutest time many Visnus, Brahmas, and others pass away. It is with such a Siva, that you had gone to fight.

You have happily returned after defeating him- the great lord. How could you do it? Please tell me all about the same?”

On hearing these words of Tulasi, the lord of Laksmi, who had taken to the form of Samkhacuda, laughed and sweetly spoke to her.

Lord Visnu said, “When I, being fond of war, reached the battle-field, a great tumult was created, resulting in a great battle.

Then the war between the gods and the Danavas started. Both the sides were desirous of victory. Initially, the Daityas were defeated by the gods, who were proud of their strength.

Then I faced the powerful and valorous gods. Getting defeated by me, the gods took refuge in Siva.

Siva, in order to help them reached the battle ground to wage a war. Being proud of my prowess, I fought with him for a long time.

My dear wife, both of us fought continuously for a year. O Loving damsel, all the asuras were destroyed.

Then Brahma brokered peace between the two. At his bidding, the powers of authority was re-assigned to the gods.

I have returned home, Siva was returned to Kailasa. Now there is normalcy everywhere, and all are healthy. The trouble has been vanquished.

Sanatkumara said, “After thus speaking the lord of the world lay down over the bed. Feeling delightful, Visnu then indulged in sexual intercourse with Tulasi.

Tulasi, on observing a change in the sex behaviour, endearment and attraction, she asked him, “Who are you?” Tulasi said, “Who are you? tell me quickly. You have enjoyed me deceitfully. You have outraged my modestly. Therefore, I am going to pronounce a curse on you.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of Tulasi Visnu became nervous. O Brahmana, Visnu then resumed his own beautiful form.

Observing him minutely, she came to realise that it was Visnu and none else. Enraged at the outraging of her modesty, she said.

Tulasi said, “O Visnu, you are devoid of compassion. You are stone hearted. Desecrating my chastity, you have killed my husband.

Since you are merciless like a stone, therefore with my curse you would be turned into a stone.

Those who describe you as the ocean of mercy, they are surely, confused and mistaken, why did you kill your own devotee for the sake of others?” Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking the grieved chaste wife of Samkhacuda, started lamenting again and again

Finding her so crying, Visnu remembered Siva, with whose delusion the entire world gets confused.

Then Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees appeared on the scene. Visnu offered his salutation to him, eulogising him at the same time.

Finding that Visnu was feeling harassed, and the beloved of Samkhacuda lamenting, Siva who was kind to the poor tactfully enlightened both of them.

Siva said, “O Tulasi, do not lament. Everyone has to reap the reward of his actions. In the ocean of karmas in this world, there is nothing like the pleasure and the pain.

Now both you and Visnu, listen to the words being spoken by me, which will provide comfort to both of you.

O Tulasi, you discarding this body shall achieve the divine body. Then you taking to the form of Laksmi, would enjoy the company of Visnu daily.

Discarding this body, when you take to the divine form, then you would enjoy the company of Visnu, like Laksmi.

When your body comes to an end, then you would be known as the auspicious river Gandaki in Bharata.

O Great goddess, because of my boon, for a long time you would become the means for the adoration of the gods.

You would always keep the company of Visnu in the heaven, earth and Patala. O Beautiful one, among the flowering trees, you would become the beautiful Tulasi plant.

Being the presiding deity of the trees, you would always remain with Visnu in seclusion in Vaikuntha.

You will also remain on earth as the presiding deity of the rivers, the wife of the salt ocean and the bestower of all the merits.

Lord Visnu, because of your curse to him, would remain on your banks in the form of stone.

The crores of terrible sharp-toothed worms shall penetrate and erode the stones and carve rings on it.

Because of the difference in the cakras, those stone will be termed as representing Laksmi-Narayana etc. and will be treated as auspicious and the bestower of the merits.

The Salagrama-sila of Visnu, and the confluence of Tulasi there, the place will enhance the merits.

The one who removes the Tulasi-leaf (Holy basil) with Salagrama-sila, he will not face separation from his wife in the next birth.

Leaving aside the conch, whosoever would pluck the leaves of Tulasi without using the conch, he would become a widower and a chronic patient for seven births.

The one who keeps, Salagrama, Tulasi and the conch in one place, shall become wise and the favourite of Visnu.

You have been the beloved of Samkhacuda for a period of a Manvantara. Therefore, your separation from Samkhacuda, is really painful to you.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter Siva highlighted the auspicious glory of Salagrama-sila, and Tulasi.

Then pleasing Visnu and Tulasi- both, Siva- who bestowed comforts on the noble people, disappeared from the scene.

The words of Siva delighted Tulasi. Discarding her body, she took to the heavenly form.

Then Visnu, accompanied with Tulasi, went to Vaikuntha. Atonce she cast off body of Tulasi and was turned into the river Gandaki.

Visnu was also turned into Salagrama-sila which purified the people. O Sage, the worms made several types of holes.

The Salagrama-silas found in water are treated as extremely auspicious. Those which are found over the banks are called Pingala. They are considered as harmful.

Thus I have narrated at your instance, the story of Siva, in reply to your question, which fufills all the desires, and is quite auspicious.

The narrative which intermingles the glories of Siva and Visnu, has been spoken out by me in detail, which confers the worldly pleasures as well as salvation. What more do you want to listen from me?

## Chapter 42 - Slaying of Hiranyaksa

Narada said, “Listening to the episodes of the killing of Samkhacuda and the story of Siva, I do not feel satisfied in the same way as the people do not feel satisfied even after the consuming the nectar.

O Brahma, you please speak out the story of Siva and the illusion created by him to please his devotees, besides his sport.”

Brahma said, listening to the killing of Samkhacuda, Vyasa the son of Satyavati, again questioned Narada, the son of Brahma.

Sanatkumara narrated the auspicious and praiseworthy stories of Siva to Vyasa, the son of Satyavati.

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, you listen to the auspicious story of Siva and the way as to how one of the ganas of Siva was turned as Andhakasura.

O Excellent sage, initially, he fought a great wear with Siva and subsequently he repeatedly pleased Siva with his Satvika temperament.

Siva, who is well-disposed towards those who take refuge in him enjoys astonishing glory because he is well-disposed towards his devotees and indulges in several sports.

Realising the immense glory of Siva, Vyasa- the son of Satyavati, with his mind filled with decoction for Siva, bowing in reverence to the sage Narada, and then spoke to him.

Vyasa said, “O Lord, O Excellent sage, who was Andhaka? In whose race was he born on earth? What was the name of his father?

By the grace of Narada, you reveal the entire secret of this story. I have known about him from the intelligent Skanda the son of Siva.

How could he achieve the position of a Ranadhisvara from Siva? Andhakasura is extremely graceful, having achieved the position of a Ganesvara?

Brahma said, “Listening to the words of Vyasa, Narada- the son of Brahma said at that moment. The way the Daitya achieved the Supreme Laksmi from Siva, Vyasa the father Sukadeva, desired to listen about the same.

Sanatkumara said, “In the ancient times, once Siva who is well-disposed towards his devotees, the emperor of the gods, accompanied with Parvati and his ganas left Kailasa and reached Kasi, for the purpose of sporting.

He built his capital there and appointed a hero Bhairava as its protector. Then he performed many sports there which pleased the people, together with Parvati- the daughter of the mountain.

Once he went to the Mandara mountain, to witness its excellent beauty, where also he sported with Parvati and other ganas.

In the eastern region of the Mandaracala mountain, Parvati playfully, closed both the eyes of Siva.

Parvati closed the eyes of Siva, with her lotus like hands having the lustre of coral and the golden lotus. At the closing of the eyes of Siva, immense darkness spread everywhere.

With the touch of the eyes of lord Siva with the hands of Parvati, the rapturous rutting juice emerged from her hands which became hot with the fire of his eyes on the forehead and flowed out in copious drops.

A child emerged out of it. With an awful face, filled with rage, ungrateful, blind, crooked, black in colour, having a form different than a human, deformed and with many diseases.

He sang, laughed, danced, licked and started thundering like the cloud. Looking at the child, Siva smilingly said to Parvati.”

Siva said, “Whatever you did by closing my eyes, then why are you getting afraid of the same?” Listening to these words of Siva, Parvati removed her hands from the eyes of Siva.

During the light, the blind creature looked more awful. Finding such a type of person, Parvati asked Siva.

Gauri said, “Who is this horrible creature resembling us. You tell me. Who has produced him? What is the purpose of his birth? Who is his father?”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of his beloved, the mother of the three worlds, and the cause of the creation of the blind creature, lord Siva sportingly smiled and said.

Siva said, “O Parvati of mysterious activities, listen. When my eyes were closed by you this wonderful being of fierce might was born of my sweat and shall be named Andhaka.

You are the cause of his creation though not in a natural way. He will be guarded as well as by you and your friends. He well-being rests with you. O Noble damsel, you think over it intelligently and take care of him accordingly.”

Sanatkumara said, “The merciful Siva, listening to the words of the Daitya king, pleasantly said to him, “Though no son could be produced with your semen, but still I shall give you a son.

Then the winter season arrived. Inspired by Hiranyaksa- the great Daitya, with the desire of his having a son looked at his elder brother’s son, the son of Kasyapa, overcoming the mental blemishes including the anger, with the desire of having an audience with Siva, stood like a log and performed hard *tapas* in the forest.

O Narada, getting pleased with his tapas Siva arrived before the demon and said to the Daitya king.

Siva said, “O Daitya king, don’t trouble your sense organs any more. What for are your performing the *tapas*? I have arrived here to bestow a boon on you. You speak out your desire to me.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Siva, the demon Hiranyaksa was immensely pleased. He offered his salutation to Siva with folded hands, lowering his head and then eulogised him.”

Hiranyaksa said, “O Candrasekhara, there is no son in my luck. Therefore I have performed the tapas. Therefore, O God of gods, you give me a powerful son.

Because my brother has five valorous sons, like Prahlada and others, while I do not have son as a result of which my race is getting destroyed. Now who would take care of my kingdom?

The one who overpowers the others’ kingdom and enjoys it, or rules the kingdom of his father, he is called the son and by doing so, the father is called as possessing the son.

The intelligent people, well-versed in the *dharma*, say that only the people having the sons, are redeemed. Therefore all the people are desirous of sons, otherwise the *tejas* of a person is transferred to the animals.

A person without a son, cannot be redeemed. Because of this, the people become desirous of the sons.”

Sanatkumara said, “The merciful Siva, listening to the words of the Daitya king, pleasantly said to him, “Though no son could be produced with your semen, but still I shall give you a son.

My son named Andhaka is valorous and invincible like you. You accept him as your son and shed away the grief.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking and feeling delighted Tripurari Siva, handed over the boy to Hiranyaksa.

The demon, receiving a son from Siva, with all humility, going round him, adoring the lord offering prayers, and getting delighted returned to his abode.

Receiving the son from Siva, the immensely valorous demon, conquering the entire earth and the gods, took the child to Patala.

Then the gods, sages, and the Siddhas, adored lord Visnu in the form of Varaha who was enormously powerful.

He, tearing out the earth with his nostrils, entered the Patala loka, killed several Daityas with his unbroken fangs.

Then with the attack of his Vajra-like feet, he churned the demon army, he cut off the head of Hiranyaksa, with the Sudarsana-cakra issuing the lustre of astonishing type, burning the wicked Daitya. Then delightfully, he crowned Andhakasura as the king of Patala.

Then Varaha, carrying the earth over the tip of his trunk, delightfully established her at her proper place and started protecting her.

The delightful gods like Brahma and others, besides the sages, eulogised the lord Varaha, who had performed a noble deed. Thereafter all of them returned to their respective places.

## Chapter 43 - Killing of Hirnyakasipu in the form of Narasimha

Vyasa said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, after the killing of the violent enemy of the gods- Hiranyaksa, what did his elder brother- the great asura, do?

O Son of Brahma, O Munisvara, I am quite anxious to learn about it. You kindly tell me; salutation to you.

Brahma said, “Thus listening to his words, Sanatkumara, the great sage devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, spoke to him.”

Sanatkumara said, “Soon after the killing of his brother at the hands of Visnu in the form of Varaha, he was filled with anger and grief.

Then he commanded his valorous warriors who were the enemies of Visnu, that they should kill all the people.

The violent warriors, accepting the command of their lord, started destroying the gods.

The Daityas with a wicked mind, started destroying the gods as a result of which, they deserting the heaven started living on earth secretly.

Feeling painful at the death of his brother Hiranyaksa, Hiranyakasipu, performed the water oblation to the soul of his departed brother. The distressed Hiranyaksipu then consoled his wife and others.

Then the emperor of the Daityas, desired to make himself invincible, undying, unaging unrivalled and the sole ruler.

He performed a severe penance in the revine of the Mandara mountain. Keeping his arms lifted up he fixed his eyes in the sky. He stood on earth on his big toe alone.

While he was so engaged in his tapas, the gods, accompanied with their forces, defeated the Daityas and regained their lost seats.

The smoking fire of the penance springing from his head, spreading all around, scorched the entire world from above and below.

Feeling scorched with the same, they deserted the heaven and approached Brahma, with their faces having been turned pale deformed by the demon’s penance, and they apprised the creator of the world with the factual position.

O Vyasa, when so apprised by the gods, the self-born, creator of the universe, went to the hermitage of the Daitya in the company of Bhrgu, Daksa and others.

Having already scorched the three worlds, he found Brahma, having arrived there, who desired the demon to ask for a boon. Listening to the sweet words of Brahma, the intelligent Daitya said.

Hiranyakasipu said, “O Brahma, I have never been afraid of death nor was I ever afraid of the weapons, the noose, Vajra, the dry trees, mountains, water, fire, enemy, etc.

I had also not been afraid of the gods, Daityas, the sages, Siddhas, besides the humans so created by you. What more shall I say, O Lord of the people, the heaven, earth, day, night, the sky and the nether-world, had never been frightening for me.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to these worlds, Brahma, recalled Visnu in his mind and feeling merciful, said to him, “You get everything.

You stop performing tapas. You have already performed the tapas for ninety six thousand years. All your desires have been fulfilled. You better get up and rule over the Daityas.” On hearing this the Daitya king felt pleased.

After his having been crowned as the king, he thought of destroying the three worlds. He removed all the dharmas and getting intoxicated, he conquered even the gods.

Then Indra and other gods with the permission of Brahma, after having been tortured by the Daitya, went to the ocean of milk, where the lord of Visnu was sleeping.

All of them eulogised Visnu, with sweet words. Finding him delightful, each one of them narrated the tale of his suffering.

Learning about their suffering and miseries, lord Visnu got up from his bed and he pronounced a boon on all of them, which caused them the comfort variously, speaking favourable words.

Assuring the gods and the sages, Visnu, having the brilliance of fire, said to them, “O Gods, all of you should go back to your abodes with pleasure. I shall surely kill the demon.

O Excellent sage, listening to the words of Visnu, Indra and other gods took Hiranyakasipu as dead, and feeling pleased went back to their respective places.

Then Visnu- the noble soul, assumed the composite form of a lion and a man. His head was matted and full of manes. His sharp fangs served as his weapons. He had keen and pointed claws. The snout was beautifully shaped and the mouth was wide open. The body was terrible and refulgent with the lustre of crores of suns. He was blazing, immensely powerful, with flames issuing like the fire of dissolution. He resembled the universe. It is not necessary to describe him in more words. When the sun was about to set, then lord Narasimha went to the city of the asuras.

The Man-lion fought with the Daityas and killed many of the powerful ones. He held them upwards and rotated them. Exhibiting powerful prowess, he crushed and smashed the valorous asuras.

Finding the composite form of the man-lion, Prahlada the son of the Daitya lord, said to his father.

Prahalada said, “This is lord Narasimha- the universal one, who taking to the composite form, has arrived in your city. Now shedding away the war you better take refuge with him. I am observing the horrible face of the lion.

There is no great warrior in the three worlds comparable to him in strength. You better rule the country, bowing in reverence to him.” Listening to the words of his son, the Daitya king said, “O Son, you have been frightened.”

The lord of the Daityas after speaking to his son, then said to other powerful Daityas warriors, “Capture the lion with deformed face, the eyebrows as well as the eyes.”

At his command, when the Daitya warriors rushed towards him to capture the lion, all of them were burnt out like the fire flies in a moment.

When the Daityas were so burnt out, then the Daitya-king, fought with the man-lion, using all the weapons like the *Saktis,* noose, goad, pavaka and others.

While they were so fighting with these weapons roaring furiously at each other a day of Brahma passed by.

Then the Daitya suddenly assumed many arms, holding all the weapons in his hands. He furiously looked at the frightening man-lion and rushing towards him he pounced upon him.

The demon was then seized by the lord of beasts, with his hands as powerful as the beasts. The Daitya was seized by the lord of beasts with his hands as strong as the mountain, and placed him over his knees. Then he tore and scratched his chest by the claws, piercing every vulnerable joint of his body.

The Daitya’s heart was torn out with the claws. Then he lay there dead like the log of wood and his limbs were reduced to powder.

After the killing of the enemy of the gods, Prahlada offered his salutation to Visnu. Prahlada was then crowned as the king and the lord disappeared from the scene.

O Narada, all the gods were then pleased and they offered their salutation to lord Visnu who had accomplished his task. Then all the gods including Brahma, went back to their respective abodes.

Thus, I have narrated the birth of Andhakasura from Siva, the killing of Hiranyaksa by the Man-lion, besides the crowning of Prahlada.

O Narada, now you listen from me influence of Andhakasura, who emerged from Siva, his fight with Siva, and his becoming the lord of the ganas of Siva.

## Chapter 44 - Andhaka receives the kingship of his father and deputes a messenger to Siva demanding Parvati for himself

Sanatkumara said, “Once Andhaka, the son of Hiranyaksa, was jokingly asked by his cousin brothers who were quite arrogant, as to what would be done by him with the kingdom, during the course of their games. They said, “O Blind fellow, what will you do with your kingdom?

Hiranyaksa was a fool who adopted you being blind as a son. You are quarrelsome, ugly and hideous. He got you after adoring Siva by severe tapas.

You therefore, cannot lay your claim over the kingdom. Can a person, who is really not the son of a king ever aspire to rule the kingdom? You better think over it yourself. At the most you could be given some share of the kingdom.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of his brothers, Andhaka was distressed, he intelligently thought over the whole matter and appeased his brothers variously. During the night he went to a lonely forest and he performed tapas there for ten thousand years, reciting the mantras. He stood on one leg fasting and raising his arm at the same time, continuously. It may be said in brief that he performed such a severe tapas, which no other asura could do.

Daily he cut a piece of flesh and consigned it to the blazing fire alongwith his blood, repeating his mantras at the same time. The process went on for a year.

Then only the bones and the veins were left in his body which issued bad smell. The entire blood was lost and then he thought of burning himself in fire.

Then all the gods getting surprised and frightened, quickly started eulogising Brahma.

Then Brahma stopped Andhaka from indulging in the cruel activities and said, “O Danava, you ask for whatever is desired by you.

The miserable Daitya, listening to the words of Brahma, offering his salutation to him spoke to him. The cruel brothers like Prahlada and others, who have usurped my kingdom, should be my servants.

A blind person like me should gain the divine sight. The gods like Indra and others should pay taxes to me. I should be invincible from the gods, Daityas, Gandharvas, Yaksas, serpents, besides the humans. I should not be killed at their hands.

Even Indra, Visnu and Siva should not be able to kill me.” Thus listening to the awful words of the Daitya, becoming doubtful in his mind, the creator said.

Brahma said, “O Daitya king, everything would be done, but you have to accept the cause of your destruction as well. Because the one who is bom, has to meet with his end ultimately.

A noble person like you should not aspire for a long life.” Listening to the words of Brahma quite humbly, the Daitya said again to Brahma.”

Andhaka said, “The most excellent of the ladies whether of mature, middle or young age, shall be like mothers to me.

When I become desirous for a woman, who could be beyond the reach of the persons mentally, by speech, or by actions, in the form of an asura, then only I should meet destruction.”

Listening his words, Brahma feeling surprised, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, at his command, he said to Andhaka.

Brahma said, “O Daitya king, you may get whatever is desired by you. O Daitya king, you get up and enjoy your desires. You should always fight with the valorous warriors.”

O Excellent sage, listening to the words of Brahma, he offered his salutation to the lord with devotion. Then Hiranyaksa’s son said to Brahma.

Andhakasura said, “O Lord, how can I fight with my enemies with this type of the body. With the touch of your auspicious hands, you restore the flesh on my body.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the Daitya, Brahma then touched his body with his hand and getting adored by the gods, sages, Siddhas, he left for his abode.

With the very touch of the hand of Brahma, the body of the Daitya king was restored to its original position, gaining all the strength. With the eyes having been restored to him, he returned to his city.

His brothers, like Prahlada and others, finding Andhaka returning with boons, restored the entire kingdom to him and all of them became subservient to him.

Andhaka, then with the army and the attendants, went to the heaven to conquer it. He conquered the gods there, made Indra the carrier of Vajra, his tax payer.

Thereafter he conquered the nagas, birds, Raksasas, Gandharvas, Yaksas, humans, mountains, the trees besides the quadrupeds.

In this way he became victorious over all the mobiles and immobiles in the three worlds, and then enjoyed sexual pleasures with thousands of beautiful damsels.

Then collecting ail the beautiful girls from Patala, earth, and heaven, he enjoyed their company over the mountains, river banks, and the mountains valleys.

Then sporting among these damsels, joyfully, he consumed, the divine and super human beverages left over by them and became highly elated.

Besides other excellent things, he enjoyed the juices, fruits, fragrant flowers, charming vehicles, which were quite pleasant to drive, besides an excellent palace created by Maya.

Thus indulging in various types of sports, ten thousand years were passed, whichbeautified and made him pleasant, and mysteriously wonderful by means of flowers, incenses, unguents, and other eatables.

He was unaware of anything auspicious and beneficent to him in the other world. He was deluded, blinded by pride and spoiled by his association with the wicked.

The haughty fellow attacked leading scholars by using fallacious arguments. Filled with pride, he roamed about with his Daitya friends destroying Vedic rites.

Getting intoxicated with the riches, he disregarded the Vedas, the Brahmanas, the gods, and the preceptors. Overpowered by misfortunes, he spent his life following the evil ways.

Once he accompanied with his army, went to the earth, where he spent crores of years. Once he visited the Mandaracala mountain.

Observing the golden beauty of the place, he kept on wandering there for long. Out of delusion, he desired to stay there for long for the enjoying of the pleasure.

He built a wonderful stable and the best of city on the ridges of the Mandaracala mountain, and forced people to live there gradually.

Once his three courtiers named Duryodhana, Hasti and Vaidhasa, spotted a most beautiful damsel on the mountain.

The quick-moving Daitya courtiers hastened to their lord Andhaka and joyously apprised him of the factual position.

The courtiers said, “O Daitya king, we spotted an ascetic in a cave, who was seated in dhyanamudra closing his eyes. He was beautiful to look at and had a moon digit over his head. He had the elephant skin bound around his waist.

The serpents had been coiled around his body. He wore a garland of skulls around his neck and the crown of matted locks of hair over the head. He held a trident and bow and arrow in his hands, besides a rosary.

He held a sword, a staff, and a trident in his hands. He has locks of hair and four hands. He has the extremely fair complexion and his body is besmeared with ashes. He has an astonishing dress being an ascetic, who is quite illustrious.

Not far from him, another person, having simian features, very terrible and demeanour was seen. Equipped with weapons his hands are rough and brawny. He is the guard on duty. There is a white bull, too old but firm and steady.

Close to the beautiful ascetic, an extremely charming damsel, young and beautiful is seated, who happens to be the gem on earth among the heaven.

She is richly adored in corals, pearls, jewels, gold, gems and is neatly dressed. She wears fine and auspicious necklaces. The one who has seen her can be called a man of sight. The sight of anything else is of no avail.

O Lord of the Daityas, she happens to be the graceful divine wife of the auspicious Siva or the ascetic. O Daitya king you enjoy the best of the gems in the world. Therefore, you better call her here in order to observe her.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to their words, the entire body of the Daitya started shaking. He suddenly sent his courtiers named Duryodhana and others to the ascetic.

O Great sage, the courtiers who had been well-versed in polity, reaching there offered their salutation to the great sage and apprised him of the purpose of their visit. They also enlightened the ascetic about the royal order.

The courtiers said, “There is a Daitya king known as Andhakasura, the son of Hiranyaksa, who is the lord of the three lokas. At the command of Siva, he has arrived here for the purpose of sight seeing. We happen to be his valorous courtiers. We have arrived before you at his command. You listen to us attentively the word he has conveyed to you through us.

“O Excellent sage, O Intelligent one, who is your father? Why are you seated here? Who is the father of this beautiful damsel? You give her away to the lord of the Daityas.

Whereas your body is smeared with ashes, adorned with the garland of skulls and is dreadful in appearance, why do you keep the bow and the quiver, the arrows, the sword, the missile bhusundi, the trident, the Vajra and the iron club?

While you have the sacred Ganga, the crescent moon, the matted locks of hair, the pieces of bones from the dead bodies, the serpents with poisonous breath, and the protruding mouth, then what to speak of the close embrace of a lady of the developed breasts.

It is inauspicious to ride over an old bull. Besides, O Merciful one, it would not be proper for you to have a look at the gem like woman. It is quite religious to offer adoration to sandhya (evening), while the thorn apple and hemp are your favoured food, which are against the normal practices of the world.

You peacefully hand over this woman to me. O Foolish one, how can you perform the tapas with a woman? This is not proper for you, because I happen to be the lord of gems to the three worlds.

At my command, you disown all the weapons. Thereafter you perform tapas with a spotless mind. In case you disobey my command, you would be deprived of your life.”

Then lord Siva, who was well-versed in the worldly conduct, being lord of the universe, treating Andhakasura to be of evil wisdom, listening to his words, smiled and then spoke to the Daitya.

Siva said, “In case, I happen to be Rudra, then what have you to do with me. Why do you indulge in falsehood. Speaking of such words would not be proper for you. You better listen to my prowess.

I am unmindful of my parents. Remaining ugly and foolish, I perform the Pasupata-vrata in this caves, which could never be performed by any one else.

The world which has to be discarded like the wood without the base, has emerged from me alone. The damsel, who always remains young is quite beautiful, bears all the odds, is all pervading, and is the form of success being my wife.

O Raksasa, presently you can take away anything you like.” Thus speaking, Siva in the form of an ascetic, kept quiet.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening the these serious words, the Danava, offered his salutation, lowering his head left the place and for the destruction of the three worlds he proceeded on to the place of Andhakasura- the son of Hiranyaksa.

Whatever words Siva had spoken smilingly, were repeated by the valorous courtiers, to Andhaka- the lord of Daityas, offering their salutation to him, shouting the slogan of victory.

The courtiers said, “The demons are always, unstable and valorous. They are never miserly or devoid of tattvas. They are never afraid of the cruel, ungrateful, sinful or even the lord of Yama.

O King, you are the lord of all the Daityas, that illustrious ascetic and the best of the warriors, with a smile, treating all the three worlds like straw or is of no consequence, has conveyed a message for you.

Whereas I am a person who could frighten even the death, am equipped with terrific weapons, then where is the fight that terrifies even the death? Where is this Viraka of Simian facial features? Where is the demon, senile and rickety in limbs?

Where is this hideous man? Where is this unfortunate wretch? Where is your strength? Where are the spreading creeping plants? In case you are really so powerful, attempt to fight with him. Let us do something.

For the destruction of the wicked people like you, I possess enough of weapons, which are hard like Vajra, besides being awful, while you have a soft body resembling the lotus flower. Therefore, you do whatever you like.

O Lord of Danavas, many such words were spoken by the ascetic to be conveyed to you. Therefore would it not be proper for you to fight with him?

Getting deprived of the improper words, in case you become careful at our words, then it would be good otherwise we shall have to repent, reminded of the words of the ascetic subsequently.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter the foolish Daitya, disregarding the truthful, beneficial, harsh as well as the sharp words of the courtiers, he started burring in anger like the pouring of the ghee in the fire which make the flames to rise high.

Thereafter the Daitya having been intoxicated because of the boon, and under the spell of misfortune, having been hurt with the arrows of passion, holding a sword in his hand, rushed like the forceful wind for waging the war.

## Chapter 45 - Battle between Andhakasura and Siva’s army

Sanatkumara said, “Andhakasura-accompanied with excellent warriors, who was an excellent warrior himself, moving like an intoxicated elephant, the great demon, followed by his army, having the wavering his eyes, reached there.

With his mind having been overpowered with passions, he glanced at the cave, which was protected by Viraka as a fire fly looks at the fire flame quite lovingly.

Looking at it again and again, having been thrashed by Viraka and other ganas, the Daitya king Andhaka burning with passion, got confused.

On his arrival, Viraka attacked him with stones, trees, Vajra, water, fire, serpents and tortured him with sharp weapons, which remained ineffective on him and then he asked him, “Who are you. What for have you arrived here.”

On hearing the words of Viraka, Andhaka remained silent, but began to fight with Viraka and surprisingly, in the battle, he was defeated by Viraka, which was incredible.

When the sword of Andhaka was shattered to pieces, he fled from the battle field, having last all his pride. His throat dried up with hunger and thirst and he felt aggrieved.

Then Prahlada and other prominent Daityas fought with Viraka. Though the Daityas were all terrible, but still they were defeated by Viraka using hundreds of weapons. The Daityas having been attacked with numerous weapons, which wounded them, they felt defeated and ashamed.

Then the most powerful Daityas like Virocana, Bali, Banasura, Sahasrabahu, Bhaji, Kujambha, Sambara, Vrtrasura and others collectively fought the battle.

While they were so fighting, they were overpowered by Viraka alone, the gana of Siva. The bodies of some of the Daityas were cut into two pieces; only a few Danavas were left alive. Then the Siddhas shouted the slogans of victory.

When the packs of jackals, began to dance in the midst of blood fat, flesh, etc., when beasts of prey, ghosts, and spirits, roamed in the terrible field of blood. When the Daityas were so smashed, Siva, the carrier of trident, assured Parvati variously.

Siva said, “O Dear Parvati, in earlier times, I had performed great Vrata called Mahapasupata. The strength, I derived from the same, is exhausted.” Then Siva again said, “O Siva, assuring the daughter of Daksa, I had made a forecast.”

Siva said, “O Goddess, because of you, my immortal army has been destroyed at the hands of the mortal Daityas, which is due to the effect of evil planet.

O Beautiful one, you rest assured, now, I retiring to the forest, intend to perform the extremely divine and hard vrata for the achieving of the astonishing boon.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, Siva, the great soul, slowly reciting the word om, retired to the auspicious and thick forest. He proclaimed loudly his intention and perform penance highly illuminated.

The vrata which could not be performed by the gods and the asuras such a PAsupata-vrata was performed by Siva for thousands of years, white Parvati lodged over the Mandaracala mountain kept on waiting for him.

Parvati who was quite chaste, humble, alone, free from danger was protected in the cave by her son Viraka, but still she felt painful.

The Daitya then getting intoxicated with the boons, followed by his strong warriors, losing patience because of the arrows of the passion, again arrived at the mouth of the cave.

The Daitya then, getting irritated, accompanied with his strong soldiers, discarding his food, drinks, sleep and kept on fighting with Viraka, for five hundred and five days.

In the battle, the swords, daggers, bhindipalas, gadas, bhusundis, sharp arrows, crescent arrows, besides those having the face of a tortoise were used.

The Daityas also used the prominent arrows, sharp spears, battle-axes, tomaras, mudgaras, khadgas, balls, mountains, trees, besides the divine weapons.

With the attack of those weapons by the Daityas, the valorous Viraka was fainted. The Daityas covered the dark cave completely.

Parvati then found that Viraka had been surrounded with the terrific net of the weapons of the enemy, and that he was unable to remove them.

The goddess Parvati was afraid at the sight. From within the cave, she remembered the powerful warriors of Brahma, Visnu as well as those of Siva.

With the mere remembering of the divine army, Brahma, Lord Visnu in the form of woman and Indra with all army, taking to the female form, reached there.

All the gods, sages, Siddhas, nagas and Guhyakas, taking to female form, entered the cave of Parvati- the daughter of the lord of mountain.

Because during the rule of an excellent king, the entry to his inner apartment is prohibited, therefore, the Daitya could not enter the cave, where innumerable women were found. The damsels who were to fight for the sake of Gauri, were extremely delightful which were hundreds and thousands in number. They had taken to the astonishing and divine forms and were feeling quite happy. Parvati on the other was also happy in the cave.

Thundering sound of clouds as at the end of a kalpa, were produced by these thousands of women. They played on trumpets and conches which make the soldiers victorious.

Regaining his consciousness, the powerful Viraka, he stood in the front, he snatched the weapons from the Daityas and used them against the enemies, killing them at the same time.

Then Brahma carried a danda in her hand, the enraged Gauri, Narayani holding the conch, gada, cakra and bow as the weapons in her hands.

Vyamalaku holding a danda and a plough, was having the complexion of gold and had a great force with her. Indrani hold Vajra in thousand hands.

Vaisvanari sakti had a thousand eyes, who remained stable in the war, while she was invincible by even hundreds of the Daityas. Vikrali had a large face and Yamya sakti held a danda in her hand.

The goddess Nairrti, held a sharp sword and the horrible bow in her hands. Toyalika arrived carrying the pasa (noose) of Varuna for the waging of the war.

The goddess of the forceful wind arrived holding a good in her hand. The Sakti of kubera held a club in her hand resembling the fire of the time of dissolution.

The awful goddess having the sharp face terrific form, having the nails as the weapons, and frightful like the poisonous serpent too arrived there. In this way hundreds of goddess marched on to the battle field.

Finding the vast vary of Andhaka, all the goddesses became frightful at heart. Their faces were faded out and they felt distressed losing all the enthusiasm.

All the Brahmanci and divine saktis convincing in their minds then went to Parvati at the advice of whom, they declared Viraka as their chief commander.

Equipped with the power of the boon, the Daitya king started waging a great war thinking that either he would meet with his end or become victorious.

The Parvati, declaring the intelligent Viraka as the army Commander, she fought as astonishing battle together with her friends.

Then Andhaka, the Son of Hiranyaksa, also made the great army formations. Anticipating the participation of Visnu, finding the sakti of Yama, he deployed a terrific Daitya named Gila

Because of his fight with Brahman, his face had turned horrible, and therefore lord Visnu had arrived. In the meantime, spreading the lustre of thousands of suns, the enraged Krttiivasa-Siva also arrived there.

Finding the arrival of Siva after a thousand years, all the Saktis, feeling delighted in the company of Viraka fought a fierce battle.

Parvati, displaying her valour, offered her salutation to Siva, lowering her head and then she continued fighting. Then Siva embracing Parvati and entered the cave. Gauri then relieved Brahmani and other goddesses quite gracefully and entrusted Viraka the responsibility of guarding the entrance of the gate.

When the demon could neither find Gauri nor Siva, then Andhaka, who was well-versed in polity sent a messenger named Vighasa to Siva.

The messenger, whose body had been shattered by the weapons hurled by the gods. He entered into cave and offered his salutation to Siva, and spoke quite arrogantly.

The messenger said, “I am the messenger who has been sent by Andhaka and have arrived in the cave. He has desired that you should have no concern with this lady who should be given to him.

You are an ascetic. You perform tapas. I had thought that I should not pick up a row with an ascetic. But actually you are not an ascetic but my enemy. Then fight with me, with animosity. O Wicked ascetic, I shall despatch you to the hell comparable with Patala.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to these words from the mouth of the messenger, the three eye Siva who makes the noble people comfortable, and shatters the pride of the wicked people, Siva, started burning in anger spoke to him.

Siva said, “Since you have spoken very harsh words to me therefore you leave atonce and tell your master that in case he possessed enough of strength, then let him fight with me.

The one who is incompetent, the woman, the pleasant things and the riches are of no consequence for him. Let your Daitya who is intoxicated with strength, fight with me. This is my firm decision.

The incompetent person cannot manage his life. Therefore, you do whatever has been thought by you and whatever has been thought by us will be done by us.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words spoken by Siva from his mouth, Vighasa felt delighted. Then thundering aloud he reached the place of the Daitya king Andhaka.

## Chapter 46 - Defeat of Virabhadra in the battle

Sanatkumara said, “The Daitya king, who was well aware of the indication of lord Siva, carrying a club in his hand together with his army, keeping the invincible Gila in the forefront, went to the cave of Siva and shot hard weapons at Siva, Viraka as well as Parvati.

Some of the Daityas broke the outer gate of the cave. Some of them destroyed the flowers and the leaves. They also destroyed the fruitsand roots besides the tanks, the gardens as well as the approach roads. Some of them trampled the sunny peaks of the Himalaya mountain.

Then Siva getting enraged, remembered his army and called them there. Besides that he also summoned his goblins, his army, as well as Visnu and other gods, who arrived there with their armies, chariots horses, bulls and the cows, besides the camels, donkeys, birds, lions, tigers, deer, boars, small fish, crocodiles, and other creatures. Several other beings and the groups of creatures, which could sting also arrived. Immediately after having been called, the gods arrived and stood before Siva with hands folded with reverence. They arrived with camels, chariots, elephants, horses, bulls, cows, mules, excellent birds, lions, bhutas tigers, deer, boars, cranes, fishes, crocodiles, other living beings scattered lies, serpents of the cremation grounds, together with ghosts and spirits, divine chariots lakes, river, and mountains.

When the gods had taken proper rest and were free from the fatigue of the journey and even the tiresomeness of the horses was also removed, Siva deployed the gods for waging the war. In order to ensure victory, Siva also deployed the army commander.

The Daitya army, led by Gila, fought the terrible war like the time of dissolution and beyond any limit of yugas, swallowing the gods in the battle ground angrily.

Then Vighasa swallowed Brahma, Visnu, Indra, Surya, the moon and others. Then Viraka, deserting the battle ground, entered the cave, and offering his salutation to lord Siva, the enemy of cupid, apprised the lord of the happenings in the battle ground.

He said, “0 Lord, your army has been swallowed by Vighasa. Lord Visnu, the destroyer of the Daityas has also been swallowed by the Daitya, besides the sun, the moon, Indra, Yama, Varuna, Vayu, Kubera, and others.

I have been left alone. What should I do now? The undefeatable Daitya king is quite happy with his daitya army.

Feeling frightened, I have arrived here with the speed of the wind. Lord Visnu, being subservient to his devotees, had killed Hiranyakasipu, the son of Kasyapa, with his sharp nails, and had opened his mouth to devour all the three lokas.

Then all the sages like Vasistha and others had pronounced a curse on him, that he would fight with the Daityas for a long time.

For his own benefit, Visnu then said to the sages, “O Excellent sages, “When shall I be free from this terrific curse? Then the angered sages said, “You would feel enough painful with the arrows and fists of Vighasa, you would enter his mouth.

Then you establishing yourself in the sacred place of Badrikasrama and getting relieved of the curse, would proceed to your place. Since that time the hungry Gila, getting pleased at war, wanders here and there.

As Rahu tortures the rising sun and the moon, as Sukra is extremely inimical to the gods, because he, with the application of the Sanjivini medicine frees the demons of all the wounds.

Even if we might have to lay down our lives, but you kindly be a witness for a moment to enable us to accomplish the task.

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing this from his excellent son, Siva, the lord of Pramathas, the lord of the three worlds meditated for a long time. Then he performed a unique miracle with the chanting of the Samana mantras. He then taking to the form, as resplendent as the sun, laughed and dispelled darkness.

Observing the light the sage Viraka after consuming the rock powder, fought with the Daityas with the deformed faces. By consuming the same rock powder, he had earlier conquered the demon named Pura.

Then the said Daitya swallowed the Maharudra. Then the virtuous Nandisvara, the best of the warriors, and the foremost of the sages, held the sharp arrows, the spear and the sword.

When he looked behind, he found Siva mounted over the bull Nandi, was getting ready to fight with Vighasa and to force him to vomit out the gods who had already been swallowed by him, holding the bow and arrows in his hands.

The sage Viraka came out of the mouth of Vighasa, with Visnu and all other gods. In this way, Vighasa vomited out all the gods including Brahma, Indra, sun, the moon and all others. Thereafter the army of the gods, delightfully fought again a great war.

When the gods won the battle, Sukra, with the use of Sanjivani lore, brought all the dead demons back to life. Then the ganas of Siva made Sukra captive and carried him to Siva, who swallowed the preceptor of the Daityas.

The gods after the destruction of Sukra, also destroyed the entire community of the Daityas. Several of the Bhutas who were eager to consume the flesh of the demons, together with the headless trunks of the Daityas, started dancing in the battle field.

The intoxicated Betalas, the birds with sharp claws and the beaks, besides the jackals with their mouths filled with flesh of the dead demons, after the end of the war, the Daitya born in the race of Hiranyakasipu was then defeated by Visnu, Siva and Indra.

After the defeat of the Daitya, the soldiers,carried him through the ocean to Patala. In this way with the destruction of the demon army, Andhaka who troubled the gods, and who was the destroyer of the world, his pride was shattered with the attack of gada by Visnu.

Since he had achieved the boon, he was not inclined to give up fighting. Then Indra badly injured him with his severe attacks. Then he, with the use of weapons, destroyed all the tree, mountains, water reservoirs and others. Then thundering aloud he summoned Siva with an indication.

Still he continued fighting with weapons, which had fallen in the battle ground. When the stalk of even the used weapons was exhausted, then he started throwing at Siva and Parvati, the trees, serpents, Vajra like hard weapons, with his illusion. Using hundreds of deceitful means, he kept on fighting.

He had been immensely valorous like Tripurasura and the valorous one having been blessed with hundreds of boons, he had achieved earlier, becoming arrogant, resorted to several deceitful ways, but still his body was shattered with the attack of several weapons.

With his illusion, the world was filled with the warriors of his form. Thereafter, Siva, the enemy of Tripura, taking to the form resembling the fire of the time of dissolution, attacked the Daitya with his trident.

When his warriors were badly wounded by the ganas of Siva and enough of flesh and blood from their bodies was lost, then several Daityas emerged from the same. Then the intelligent Visnu, with the use of his yogasakti summoned Siva, the lord of the pramathas who took to a horrible form, with a horrible face, and who could not be over powered by those who had the lust for women.

That form of Visnu had a dreadful face, dry body, several arms, was furious and he appeared from the ear of lord Siva.

Taking to the form of a goddess, she graced the earth with her lotus like feet. All the gods praised her. Thereafter the goddess having been inspired by the lord, started drinking the warm blood of the demon army. Enough of mud was created with the blood.

When the blood dried up, the lonely daitya, with his hands and feet as hard as Vajra, besides the legs, nails etc., he attacked Siva reciting his name according to the dharma of Ksatriya.

Then Siva, at the end of the war, shot an arrow at his chest with which he was hung in the sky. With the sunrays his body started drying up, besides getting decomposed with the wind and the rain.

The body of the daitya was scorched with the sun rays, with the fall of snow over it, the body got shattered, but his life did not depart out of it. Thereafter the compassionate Siva, bestowed the position of his gana on him.

Then at the end of the war, Visnu the lord of the three worlds, accompanied with Brahma and other gods, went to Siva. They adored him adequately, lowering their heads, and shouting the slogans of victory they became delightful.

Siva, then having been adored by them variously with several types of materials, sent them off quite gracefully. Thereafter Siva and Parvati achieving a son like Viraka who had come back out of the mouth of Vighasa, felt delighted. Then establishing his amsa in the Cave, Siva, started sporting with Parvati.

## Chapter 47 - Bringing back of Daitya to life

Vyasa said, “It has been reliably heard by me, that in the great terrific battle, that caused horror, Sukra, the intelligent lord of the Daityas was swallowed by Siva- the enemy of the Tripuras. Please tell me precisely, what the great ascetic Sukra lodged in the stomach of the trident bearing lord, Siva did?

How was it that the terrible fire of Siva, resembling the fire of dissolution did no harm Sukra? How could the wise Sukra possessing the immense lustre emerge from the stomach of Siva? For how long and in which way did Sukra eulogise him?

How could he get the lore which could defeat death? O Excellent one what is that excellent lore, by which one could overcome the death?

How could Andhaka achieve the position of Ganapati, getting released from the tip of the trident of Siva?

O Intelligent one, you kindly narrate the entire episode exhaustively, because I intend to drink the nectar of the sports of Siva.”

Brahma said, “Listening to the extremely illustrious words of the sage Vyasa, devoted his mind at the lotus like feet of lord Siva.

Sanatkumara spoke, “O Vyasa- the great intellect, listen to the excellent sports of Siva. You are a great Saiva and bestow bliss. Therefore, you are quite graceful.

With the start of the battle between Siva- the lord of mountains- Vyuha, with Andhaka the lord of impregnable vajra-vyuha.

O Sage, though the valorous Daityas were victorious, but subsequently, with the influence of Siva, the pramathas were victorious.

On hearing this, Andhakasura, felt extremely painful at heart. Then he thought of the method of achieving victory for himself.

The immensely wise Andhaka, withdrew himself from the battle-field and he alone, rapidly rushed to Sukra.

Descending from his chariot, he offered his salutation to the excellent preceptor with folded hands. Then Andhaka who was well- versed in polity thought for a while and said to Sukra.

Andhaka said, “Taking you to be my preceptor I have arrived here. Since we have always been victorious, we can never be defeated.

Because of your influence, we consider all the gods and their followers including Siva and Visnu as insignificant as the useless blades of grass.

By your grace, the gods feel afraid of us as an elephant is afraid of the lion or the serpents from Garuda.

By your grace, the Daityas have fearlessly entered the impregnable thunderbolt vyuha- the Daityas and Danavas have frightened the armies of the gods.

O Bhargava, by taking refuge under your feet, we have become carefree like the earth and roam about fearlessly even in the battle ground. O Brahmana, you kindly save the asuras who have been killed by the enemies.

You kindly have a look at the terribly strong Daityas, who could even destroy the death, are suffering at the hands of the gods. Hunda and other warriors have been terrorised by the gods. You kindly look at them.

The lore which you had achieved thousands of years ago by inhaling the smoke, the time has arrived to make use of it.

O Bhargava, let the pramathas see for themselves, the result of the lore which was achieved by you by bringing the Daityas back to life.”

Sanatkumara said, “The patient Bhargava, thus listening to the words of Andhaka, started thinking with a painful heart.

“What should I do today? What would be proper for me? What would be beneficial for me. to bring the Daityas back to life would be a troublesome job, which would be totally improper for me to do.

The lore has been achieved by me from Siva. Then should I make use of the same, by bringing the Daityas who were killed by Siva’s ganas, back to life?”

Then he thought, “The best path is to save a person who has taken refuge with us. This is the best of dharma.” Thus thinking Sukra, accepted the words of Andhaka.

Then Bhargava, smilingly drew his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva and then with a pleasant mind spoke to the Danava king.”

Sukra said, “O Dearest one, whatever has been spoken by you is true. I had achieved this lore for the protection of the Danavas.

Inhaling the smoke for a thousand years, I achieved this vidya, which bestowed welfare to my kiths and kins, from Siva.

I shall bring back to life, the Daityas killed by the pramathas in the same way as the raining clouds revive the drying crops.

Within a moment, you would find the warriors as if they wake up from the sleep, healed from wounds and free of pain and very healthy.

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking to Andhaka, Sukra, reciting the name of Siva, in order to bring each and every demon back to life, made use of the Sanjivani-vidya.

Immediately after the use of the lore, all the Daityas and Danavas got up as if having been woken up from sleep, holding the weapons in their hands.

They rose up like the merit of the men, who gave water to the thirsty or like the charity given to the Brahmanas, at the time of distress in the spirit of faith.

On seeing Hunda and other asuras having been brought back to life, the asuras shouted aloud like the clouds thundering having been filled with water.

Thundering with terrible sounds, the fearless and valorous asuras got ready to fight again with the pramathas.

The Sivaganas finding that the killed Daitya and Danava warriors had been brought back to life by Sukra, they felt surprised.

They apprised Siva of the performance of Sukra after pondering intelligently and consulting one another.

In the war -yajna (sacrifice of the war) of the pramathas, observing the performance of Sukra, Nandisvara, the son of Silada, who was infuriated on seeing the work of Bhargava went to lord Siva.

Shouting the slogans of victory, Nandisvara narrated to Siva having the white complexion like the flower of the wood-apple plant the valorous deeds performed by Indra and other gods, besides those of the Sivaganas.

He further said, “O Lord Siva, the enemy Daityas who had been killed by the pramathas were brought back to life by Sukra, with the use of the Sanjivini lore quite playfully.

The demons named Tuhunda, Hunda, Kumbha, Jambha, Vipaka, Paka and other great Daitya kings were made to return from the abode of Yama. They are driving out now the pramathas from the battle-field wandering freely there.

In case Sukracarya continues to bring back to life all the killed Daityas to life, then O Siva, how could the Ganesvaras be victorious? How could they be peaceful?”

Sanatkumara said, “At these words of Nandi, the leader of the pramathas, then Siva, the lord of the pramathas said to Nandi smilingly.

Siva said, “O Nandi, you atonce leave this place and tell Sukra- the preceptor of the Daityas. You catch hold of Sukra from that place and bring him here as the eagle catches hold of a bird.”

Sanatkumara said, “At this command of Siva, Nandi started behaving like the bull. Tearing through the army he reached the place where Sukracarya was seated.

All the Daityas holding the noose, swords, trees, mountains, were guarding him. Nandi then removed all the Daityas kidnapped Sukra in the same way as Sarabha carried away the elephant.

He was clad in lose garments, without ornaments, dishevelled hair, and was held by the valorous Nandi. In order to get him freed, the Daityas holding Vajra, spear, swords, battle-axes, sharp cakras, and kept on showering the stones like the clouds with storm.

Keeping Sukra in hostage, Nandi, the leader of the ganas vomited fire from his mouth, as a result of which it caused harm on the enemy soldiers. Then he carried Sukra to Siva.

Then he said, “O Lord, here is Sukra (Bhargava) and he handed him over to Siva immediately.” Mahadeva accepted Sukra as if some present received from a devotee.

Without saying anything, Siva, the protector of the creatures thrust Sukra into his mouth like a fruit. The Asuras shouted "Alas! Alas."

## Chapter 48 - Swallowing of Sukra by Siva

Vyasa said, “When Siva swallowed Sukra, then what did the warriors of Andhaka do? O Great sage tell me the same.

Sanatkumara said, “After Sukra was swallowed by Siva, the Daityas lost hope for victory. They appeared like the elephant without the trunk or the bull without the horns, or the gods without the heads, or a Brahmana without the Vedic studies, or the Sattvaguna without the enthusiasm, or the unlucky person with great enthusiasm.

They appeared like the wife without a husband, flock of birds without the wings, life without merits, knowledge of Sastras without Vratas.

They were as powerless as innumerable activities rendered fruitless without the support of fortunes, or a ksatriya devoid of heroism, or the gathering of the virtues without the truth.

When Bhargava was carried by Nandi, and then swallowed by Siva, as he had swallowed poison, the Daityas were grieved who had been anxious to wage the war.

Finding them disappointed, Tuhunda, Hunda and other Daityas, were deprived of enthusiasm, then the courageous and valorous Andhaka replied.

Andhaka said, “With the abduction of Sukra perforce, Nandi has cheated us. Surely our bodies have been deprived of life today.

With the abduction of Sukra alone, our patience, strength movement, glory, sattva, lustre and prowess have all been snatched away.

Therefore disgrace to all of us because we have been unable to save all competent, protector of our race, and adorable by our race, could not be saved by us at the time of his facing the misery.

Therefore all of us should fight with the pramathas, devoting your mind at the feet of the preceptor.

Devoting my mind at the pleasant feel of the preceptor, I shall destroy all the pramathas together with Nandi.

I shall force them by killing Indra and other gods, and shall get Sukra released from them forcibly as a yogi frees the jiva with his karmas.

Sukra is the protector of all, and in case, he himself is all powerful, in that case, he himself would comes out of the body of Siva, then all of us will be saved.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of Andhaka, the powerful Danavas, roaring like the thundering clouds, spoke after deciding to do what was then to be thought of.”

The Danavas said, “In case we are destined to live, the pramathas cannot over power us. In case things be otherwise, then what is the use of running away from the battle ground, leaving the master behind.

Out of arrogance a warrior, who in the battle field deserting the lord flees, he after death, surely falls in the Andhatamisra hell.

Their blemish their fame with the darkness of defame, can never be comfortable, in this as well as the future world.

What is the use of charities, tapas or the bath at the holy places, unless some one does not take bath in the battle like tirtha on earth.”

Thus listening to his word, the Daityas sounded the war drums and pounded the pramathas in the battle.

They created great havoc, by fighting with arrows, swords, vajras, hard rocks, bhusundis, bhindipalas, and other missiles besides spears, javelins, axes, skull headed clubs, tridents, maces, staffs, and other weapons.

There was a huge noise, everywhere, produced by the drawn bows, flying arrows, the shooting of missiles, bhusundis, bhindipalas, and the lion’s roars.

Huge tumult was created with playing of the war bands, trumpeting of the elephants and neighing of the horses.

The sound which echoed between the earth and the sky, caused horripilation to the cowards and the braves alike.

At that point of time, the sound of the trumpeting of the elephants and the neighing of the horses was heard. The flags and banners had been shattered, besides the weapons of the war.

The fountains of blood were flowing. The elephants and the horses had been killed and the thirsty warriors had been fainted.

O Sage, thereafter, Nandi and other pramatha warriors, killed the asuras with their own strength and became victorious.

Then Andhakasura finding that his army was being destroyed at the hands of the pramathas, mounted over the chariot and started driving out the pramathas.

The demons on the other hand started destroying the pramathas in such a way, with the use of their weapons, and the shooting of the arrows, as the mountains are destroyedwith the fall of Vajra, or like the clouds without water are sunk low.

Glancing at the incoming and the outgoing pramathas, far off or at close quarters, Andhaka hit them severely, with as many arrows as the hair on their bodies.

Then Skanda, Vinayaka, Nandi, Somanandi and other pramathas finding that the army of pramathas had been severely and badly smashed by Andhaka, the ganas of Siva, became, furious and all of them started fighting the battle astonishingly.

The terrific Sivaganas, like Vinayaka, Skanda, Nandi, Somanandi, Naigameya, and powerful Vaisakha, showering the arrows and the Saktis, blinded Andhaka.

Then the tumultuous uproar was created in the armies of the Daityas and the gods. With that uproar Sukra, who had been lodged in the stomach of Siva, while rotating like the wind desirous of getting an exist, found the seven lokas together with Patala.

He witnessed Brahma, Visnu, Indra, Adityas, the apsrasa, astonishing lokas, besides the battle between the god and the Danavas.

He kept on wandering in the belly of Siva for a hundred years, but could find no exit, in the same way as a wicked person can find no fault in a noble person.

Then Sukra, making use of the yoga he had learnt from Siva, recited the mantra and emerged out of his stomach with the semen of Siva. Then he offered his salutation to Siva. Parvati then accepted him as her son and freed him from all the obstructions.

Finding Bhargava’s emerging out of the belly of Siva through his (Siva’s) semen, the merciful Siva smiled and said to him.

Mahesvara said, “O Son of Bhrgu, since you have emerged out of my linga as the semen, therefore you would be known as my son Sukra.”

Sanatkumara said, “At these words of Mahadeva, Sukra, having the lustre of the sun, eulogised Siva, with his hands folded, offering his salutation to him at his feet.

Sukra said, “O Siva, you have innumerable hands and feet, innumerable heads, innumerable forms, and innumerable arms. I offer my salutation to you. How can I eulogise you?

You have the form of Astamurti, Anantamurti. You are the well-wisher of the gods as well as the Daityas. You are the destroyer of those having the cruel sight. O Lord, you are really adorable, how can I eulogise you?”

Sanatkumara said, “In this way Sukra. adoring and eulogising Siva, at the command of the lord, went back to the Danavas as the moon is absorbed in the clouds.

Thus the swallowing of Sukra by Siva in the battle field has been narrated. Now you listen to the mantra which Sukra had recited in the belly of Siva, for emerging out of it.

## Chapter 49 - Andhaka performs tapas lodged at the tip of Siva’s trident

Sanatkumara then spoke out the mantra :- Om salutation to the God of the gods, towhom Devas and asuras bow, the great lord of past and future, one who has green and tawny eyes, the mighty, one in the form of intellect, one having the tiger hide as his covering cloths, the one springing from the flint sticks of sacred fire, the lord of the three worlds, Isvara, Hara, the bay-eyed, the cause of the dissolution of the Yugas, the fire, the lord of Ganas, the protector of the worlds, the one of great arms, of great hands, the trident-bearing, of great fangs, the Kala, Mahesvara, the imperishable, the time-formed, the bluenecked, the one of huge belly, the presiding deity of ganas, the soul of all, the purifier of fall, the all-pervading, the destroyer of the death, the one observing sacred rites on the Pariyatra mountain, the Brahmacari, the one knowable through Vedanta, the one reaching the limits of austerities, Pasupati, the bodiless, the one armed with trident, the bull-bannered, Hari, the one with matted locks hair, the tufted one, the staff-bearing, the one of great fame, the lord of Bhutas, the dweller in a mountain- cave, the one beating time of Vina and Panava, the deathless, the comely, the one like the early morning sun, the dweller in the cremation ground, the lord consort of Parvati, the suppresser of enemies, the one who felled the eyes of Bhaga, the one who broke the tooth of Pusan, the one who cuts the cruel ones, the one armed with noose, the hour of dissolution, the meteor-mouthed, the fire bannered, the sage, the blazing, the lord of subjects,
