the leader, the father, the fourth one, the most excellent one in the world, Vamadeva, the chivalrous in speech, the Bhiksu of the left wing, the Bhiksu-formed, the one with matted locks hair, the complicated, the one who benumbed the hand of Indra, the one who benumbed the Vasus, the sacrifice, the performer of sacrifice, Kala, the intelligent, the bee, the moving one, the one originating from the hedges of the trees, the one adored by the name Vajasana by the people of all stages of life, the creator of the universe, the sustainer of the universe, the eternal Purusa, the stable one, the presiding deity of Dharma, the one of three-fold paths, the conceiver of all living beings, the three-eyed, the multi-formed, the one as refulgent as ten thousand suns, the lord, the one sounding all musical instruments, the one who releases from all hindrances, the binding one, the supporter of all, the most excellent of all virtuous ones, the Puspadanta, the part, the face, the destroyer of all, the golden-eared, the deity at the door, the terrible, the one of terrible exploit, om, Obeisance, Obeisance. Reciting then excellent mantra Sukra emerged from the linga of Siva like the semen.

Parvati accepted him like a son. Lord Visvesvara then turned him eternal like the second Siva.

After the lapse of three thousand years, Sukra the great sage, who was well-versed in the Vedas, was reborn on earth.

He found that the ascetic patient Danava king, was hanging from the trident of Siva devoting his mind to Siva.

He was meditating on hundred and eight forms of the great atman as under :-“the great god, of misformed eyes, the moon-crested, the nectar like, the permanent, the stable, the blue-necked, the trident-bearing, the bull-eyed, the great unknowable, the Purusa, the bestower of all desires, the enemy of Kama, the destroyer of Kama, assuming forms at his own will, wearing matted locks of hair, the hideous, the Girisa, the terrible, long-lipped, the red-robed, the Yogi, the destroyer of Kala, the destroyer of Tripuras, the bearer of skull, the performer of secret rites, the one-of secret formulas, the grave, the conceivable, the support of Anima and other qualities, the bestower of riches to the three worlds, the heroic, the destroyer of the heroes, the terrible, the awful, the fleshy, the clever, the consumer of great flesh, the mad, the awful, the great Isvara, the founder of the three worlds, the miserly, the hunter, the destroyer of sacrifice, the one with Kartikeya, the highly elated, clad in elephant’s hide, covered with hide, the agitated, wearing serpents as ornaments, the lender of support the spirit, the heroic, worshipped by Sakini, the Aghora (the gentle), the destroyer of terrible Daityas, sounding awfully, the vegetation-formed, smearing ashes on the body, with matted hair, the pure, served by hundreds of Bherundas, the lord of bhutas, the ruler of bhutas, the refuge of the five elements, the sky-sojourning, the furious, the ruthless, the fierce, the lord of Candi, the beloved of Candika, the fearful, the lofty, the Garutman (the winged one), the permanent, the partaker of spirituous liquor, the serpent-formed, the extremely terrible, the death, deathless, death of death, of great army, residing in the forest of the cremation ground, the attached, the unattached, blind with passion, adored by hundreds of passionless devotees, possessed of the Sattva, Rajas, Tamas attributes, as also of the Dharma and Adharma, younger brother of Indra, the truth, the untruth, the existent, the non-existent, the uncaused, the lord with half-female form, the sun, as refulgent as crores and hundreds of suns, the sacrifice, the lord of sacrifice, Rudra, Isan the bestower of boons and Siva. The Danava Andhaka meditating on these hundred and eight forms of the supreme soul became free from that great fear.

Lord Siva, feeling pleased, showering the divine nectar, removed Andhaka from the tip of the trident.

Then Siva peacefully spoke to the demon Andhaka, The great lord forgave what the demon had done before.

Siva said, “On Suvrata, Daitya king, I am pleased with your patient, discipline and prowess. You better ask for a boon.

O Excellent Daitya king, because of your adoring me daily, you have been freed from all the sins. You are entitled to receive a boon. Therefore, I want to bestow a boon on you.

As a result of the merits for three thousand years since your birth you have been redeemed.

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing this, Andhaka knelt down on the ground with folded hands and spoke to the lord of Uma, while shaking.”

Andhakasura said, “O Lord, whatever had been spoken by me earlier were the words choked with extreme pleasure. You are greater than the greatest and were addressed by me as an ordinary poor person. Whatever I did in the battle ground was all due to the delusion, and was the most deplorable in the world. It was due to the fact that I was not aware about your greatness earlier. O Lord please do not keep those words in mind.

Out of lust whatever, I expressed about Parvati, (was deplorable): Therefore O Lord I deserve compassion from you. I feel painful. Therefore, you kindly forgive me.

I am always depressed, devoted to you and worthy for compassion. Be merciful on me.

I am a destitute, full of devotion for you, and have arrived to take refuge with you. I adore you with folded hands, you kindly save me.

Let the goddess who is the mother of the universe delightfully glance at me.

O Candrasekhara the anger of the goddess is on one side while I- a daitya, worthy of compassion on the other side. O Candracuda, Sambhu, O Mahesvara, I will not be able to tolerate her.

On the one hand you are extremely large hearted and on the other hand am I, with all the blemishes like lust, anger, and other sins besides compelled with the old age and death.

Let the competent warrior Viraka not be enraged on seeing me the miserable creature.

Let me always look at Parvati as a mother with reverence due to elders. O Lord, you are as white as the snow, necklace, moon, conch and jasmine flowers.

Let me always be devoted to you both. Let me be free from the enmity from the gods. Let me be peaceful at heart and engage myself in the yogic practices. Let me stay with your ganas.

O Siva, by your grace, because of my birth in a daitya family, I should never indulge myself in evil ways. This the excellent boon, I seek from you.

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking and looking at the mother Parvati, and devoting his mind towards Siva, the Daitya king kept quiet.

When Siva looked at him with the delightful eyes, then he was remind of the story of his earlier birth.

Having been reminded of the said story, he looking at both Siva and Parvati, became successful in his life.

Then both Siva and Parvati, kissed his head, and the delightful Siva, bestowed all his desires.

This is the story of the earlier birth of Andhakasura. Thereafter, be by the grace of Siva, achieved the pleasant position of Ganapati.

Then Siva bestowed the Mrtyunjaya mantra to him, which fulfills all the desires and as such it should be recited carefully.

## Chapter 50 - Learning of Mrtasanjivani lore by Sukra

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, you please listen how did Sukra, the great sage, achieved the lore concerning the destruction of death.

In earlier times the family of Bhrgu, had performed tapas meditating upon, lord Visvesvara for a long time at Varanasi.

O Vedavyasa, he dug a pleasant well and consecrated an auspicious linga (phallic emblem) of high-souled Siva is lodged at Kasi.

He bathed Siva a lakh of times assiduously with pancamrta using a drona measure each time. He also used fragrant materials with them for ablutions.

He applied the sandal paste as well as the paste of Yaksakardama to Siva- the lord of gods, thousands of times. Thereafter he applied the fragrant ointment over the lord.

With utmost regard and devotion, he offered flowers and leaves, while adoring the lord, the Raja-Campaka, wood apple, Karavira, Kusesaya, jasmine, the white rose, kadamba (Neulea orientalis) Bakula (Mimusops dengi), blue lotus, a kind of jasmine (Mallika), a big variety of lotus flowers (Satapatri), Sindura (medicinal plant), Kimsuka (Butea frondosa), Bandhuka, (a flower blooming at mid-day) Purnaga, Nagakesara (Messya ferrea), saffron, Navamalli (double tree) Bilva leaves (wood apple) Maruvaka, Vrka, Granthiparna, Damanaka (a fragrant plant), the charming mango sprouts, Tulasi (holy basil) leaves, Divagandhari leaves, Brhatpatri leaves, Darbha-grass, Nandyavratas, Agastyas, sala, Devadaru, Kancanara, Kuravaka, Durva- grass, Kuruntaka and lotus petals of various auspicious kinds.

He eulogised Siva, with various mantras and repeated them a thousand times. He sang songs of Siva’s glory, with dancing and making various types of offerings.

In this way, Sukra eulogised Siva for five thousand years and adored Siva in various ways.

When he realised that Siva was the least inclined to bestow a boon on him, then he resorted to another hard means for worship of the lord.

He washed the blemish of unstability of his heart with the water of his feelings, and controlled the organs of senses.

Making his gem like mind clean and spotless, and offered it to Siva, Sukra then spent time inhaling only the smoke.

Thus becoming firm in his mind, Sukra engaged himself in performing tapas, observing which Siva was pleased with Sukra.

Then Siva the husband of Sati, also known as Virapaksa, having the lustre of a thousand of sons, then spoke to Sukra, who had been bom out of his linga.

Mahesvara said, “O Great sage, O son of Bhrgu, O Excellent one, I am particularly pleased with your tapas.

O Bhargava, you better ask for your desired boon, which would be lovingly bestowed by me on you. There is nothing which cannot be given to you.”

Sanatkumara said, “Hearing the pleasant words of Siva, Sukra felt pleased, and was drowned in the ocean of bliss.

The Brahmana bowed to Siva, with his eyes, blooming like a lotus with pleasure and his body excited with thrill and with surging waves of joy.

With the bliss overflowing, the hair of his body stood at ends. The lotus eyed Brahmana, offering his salutation to Siva, folding his hands over his head, feeling delighted, shouting the slogans of victory, offered prayers to Astamurti Siva.

Sukra said, O Jagadisvara, you removing the entire darkness with your resplendence, destroy all the demonic ideas, O Gem of the heaven, you make the sun to shine for the benefit of all the lokas.

You, becoming the sun as the eye of the universe, illumine the sky and the earth, daily. Removing the entire darkness, you shine as the moon having been filled with nectar. Salutation to you.

You are the form of wind, flowing for the sake of adoration. You are like the life of the three worlds. No one can remain alive without you. You delight the race of the serpent. You spread the stopped wind of all the creatures, salutation to you.

You are the only one to purify the world, you have the enormous strength like the fire. There is none except you to bestow divine moksa to the perishable beings. You are the inner soul of the living beings. You are the one who keeps this world alive. You purify them at every moment and bestow peace on them. Salutation to you.

O Form of the sky, O Isvara, the world had developed as auspicious. You made it variegated. O Lord of the universe, the universe is free from dirt by diving it into the water. Therefore, I bow in reverence to you.

O Sky formed one, because you give peace within and outwardly, the universe evolves and expands, O Merciful one, it always breaths in you and naturally merges in you. Therefore I bow in reverence to you.

O Lord having the form of the earth, you support and hold the universe, O Lord of the universe, who else can be the enemy of the darkness and destroy it. O Lord, you have serpents for ornaments, you are beyond all that and deserve eulogy. Therefore, I bow in reverence to you. You are greater than the greatest.

O Self formed one, O Hara, you are the abode of all the souls. You are the reflection of all, you are Astamurti, because of the tradition of your form, the mobile and immobile world has been spread. Therefore I offer my salutation to you.

O Lord, you possess the form which is beneficial to the universe. You are protector of the devotees, Sarvartha, Sartha and paramartha. You are equipped in eight forms. I offer my salutation in reverence to you having the vast form.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus eulogising the eight formed Siva, with the reciting of eight verses, Bhargava touched the ground, with his head and bowed again and again.

When Siva was so eulogised by the illustrious Sukra and offered his salutation prostrating on earth, Siva, raised him holding him with his arms.

Then Siva spoke the sweet words which were deep like the rumbling sound of the clouds, with his shining teeth, illumining the directions.

Siva said, “O Dear one, O Best of the Brahmanas, O Poet, you are my auspicious devotee with the performing of the tapas with this body, with the consecrating of the lingas and adoring the same, with your stable and purified heart, with the offering of the gifts and the merits derived therefrom, your unshaken purity, and holy conduct in this Avimukta-ksetra, I visualise you as my other son. There is nothing that cannot be given to you.

With this body, you enter in the cavity of my belly and then returned through the passage of my linga and appeared in the form of my son.

Therefore, I bestow a boon on you, which is beyond the reach of even the attendants of Visnu and which had been kept a secret from Brahma and Visnu.

My spotless lore known by the name of Mrtasanjivani had been created by me with the strength of my tapas.

O Immensely auspicious one, I shall bestow that lore, in the form of a mantra to you. O Ocean of the ascetics; you arc competent enough to receive that lore.

Aiming at whomsoever person you would make use of the same, you would surely be able to bring back to life the same person.

Your resplendence would become greater than the sun and the fire. You would shine like a star in the sky and would become the best of the planets.

Such of the men and women who would travel before you, all their obstructions would be removed with your compassionate look.

O Brahmana with noble Vrata, with your rise, in the sky, the marriages and other auspicious activities would be successful.

With your combination all the tithis, would be delightful. Your devotees would be valorous as well as bear progeny.

The linga consecrated by you would be known as Sukresa. Those who will adore this linga all their tasks would meet with success.

Those who, during the whole year, through every night, perform Vratas for Sukra and offer oblation in the Sukra well, on your day, and adore Sukresa, shall derive these fruits. They will have unfailing semen and profuse the secretion and will have sons.

O Vyasa, the way Sukra achieved the Mrtyunjaya lore with the performance of his tapas, the same has been narrated by me. Now what else do you want to listen from me.

## Chapter 51 - The story of Usa the daughter of Banasura

Vyasa said, “O Omniscient one, O Sanatkumara, you have lovingly narrated the astonishing story of the grace of Siva.

Now you kindly narrate to me the story in which Siva had bestowed the position of a gana over Banasura.

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, now I shall narrate to you, quite respectfully, the story of Siva in which he had bestowed the position of a gana to Banasura.

In this context, the episode of Krsna’s war with Siva, when the latter blessed Bana should also be stated.

The story which comforts the mind and the ears, besides being auspicious, should be listened by you. This story of Siva relating to his auspicious sports is a historical one, which you please listen.

There was an excellent mind-born eldestson of Brahma, known by the name of Marici who was a sage of great intellect. He was a Prajapati too.

The eldest wife Diti had two powerful sons. The elder one was known as Hiranyakasipu, and the younger one was Hiranyaksa.

He had a son named Kasyapa, who expounded the creation. He was devoted to Marici and Brahma.

The eldest of the wives was Diti. The demons were her sons. The gods and others including the mobile and immobile beings were born to others.

The eldest out of them was known as Diti, whose sons came to be known as the Daityas. The rest of the daughters produced the gods as well as the other mobile and immobile beings.

Hiranyakasipu had four sons named Hrada, Anuhrada, Samhrada and Prahlada.

Out of those brothers, Prahlada had been a great devotee of Visnu and he had controlled all his senses. None of the Daitya was strong enough to kill him.

Virocana the son of Prahlada had been a great donor, who gave away his own head, after cutting it, to Indra who begged for the same.

He had a son named Bali, who too was a great donor and devoted to Siva. It is he, who gave away in charity the entire earth to Visnu in the form of Vamana.

He had a son named Bana, who was devoted to Siva. He was highly respected and intelligent. He was truthful and a liberal donor, besides had made thousands of charitable gifts.

He stayed in the Sonita town, he ruled over the three worlds. He defeated all the rulers forcefully.

Because of the grace of Siva, the gods became subservient to Bana, who was devoted to Siva.

Inspite of Bana’s being highly virtuous, the gods were distressed because of his enmity towards them. With the playing of his instrumental music, with his thousand arms, in the Tandava dance, he propitiated Siva.

Siva, who was favourably disposed to his devotees, was immensely pleased with his dance and he looked at him with pleasing eyes.

The lord of the three worlds who gave protection to the people, well-disposed towards his devotees, desired to bestow a boon on Banasura.

Siva said, “O Excellent devotee, you are intelligent son of Bali. Then Banasura- the great Daitya, bowing in reverence at the feet of Siva, started eulogising him.

Banasura said, “O Mahadeva- the god of gods, well-disposed towards the devotees, O Mahesan, O Excellent one, in case you are pleased with me, then.

O Lord, you live in my city with your sons and the ganas, for my benefit, showering your grace on me.”

Sanatkumara said, “Banasura- the son of Bali, having been overpowered with the delusion of Siva, begged for the boon from Siva, the bestower of salvation, difficult to be propitiated and the stable one.

Siva who is well-disposed towards his devotees, after giving away those boons, started living lovingly with his Sivaganas in the city of Banasura.

Once Siva, in the city of Banasura, known as Sonitapura enjoyed sports in the river of that city with the gods and the demons.

At that point of time, the Gandharvas and apsaras delightfully performed dance and musical concert. The sages offered their salutation to Siva eulogising him at the same time.

The pramathas started dancing the ascetics performed the homa. Siddhas also arrived there in order to witness the divine sports of Siva.

The enemies and those indulging in controversies, besides the degraded people fled away from that place. The goddesses became closer and were free from fear.

All the worldly blemishes of the devotees of Siva, were removed. All the people were pleased by having a look at lord Siva.

The sages and the Siddhas were delighted at the conduct of the ladies. All the seasons displayed their influence.

The cool breeze carrying the flower dust started blowing. The birds perched in the tree branches, started issuing sweet notes.

The tree branches laden with fruits, were bending with their weights. The Cuckoos started issuing the cooing sound in the trees as well as in the gardens, increasing the passions.

Thereafter Candrasekhara Siva, observed the victorious god of love and then he said to Nandi.

Siva said, “You atonce move from here and go to Kailasa and bring my wife Gauri, adorned with all the ornaments.”

Sanatkumara said, “Nandi accepting the command of Siva, went to Parvati, and as a messenger of Siva, he conveyed the message of the lord to her in seclusion, bowing in reverence to her.

Nandisvara said, “Lord Siva, Mahesvara- the god of gods wants to see you in well decorated form. I have spoken to you at his command.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Excellent sage, at the command of Siva, the chaste Gauri started decorating herself respectfully.

Then she said to Nandi, “I shall reach before Siva.” You convey my message to Siva at my command.” On hearing this, Nandi reached before Siva with the speed of the mind.

Then Siva who was extremely agitated said to Nandi- “O Dear one, you go atonce and bring Parvati from there.”

Nandi said, “All right” and then he went to pleasant eyed Gauri and he said to her, “ Siva intends to see you in the best of costumes.”

O Goddess, Siva intends to roam about with you. When the husband has become so passionate, you should atonce go to him.

Then all the apsaras consulted among themselves. “ Siva is anxious to meet Parvatipresently.

Lord Siva is the enemy of the god of love, therefore the woman whoever is selected by him would be treated as the best of all.

Let us roam about with the ganas of Kamadeva taking to the form of Parvati. Presently Siva has been overpowered by the passion.” All of them thus consulted among themselves.

“Whosoever is in a position to touch Siva except Parvati, should go there and should try to attract lord Siva towards herself.

Citralekha - the daughter of Kusmanda said, “I taking to the form of Gauri, can touch Siva.”

Citralekha said, “Receiving the support of the real Vaisnava-yoga, Visnu in earlier times had taken to the form of Mohini.

At that time Urvasi too had changed her form. Ghrtaci had taken to the form of Kali and Visvaci had taken to the form of Candika.

Rambha too had taken to the form of Savitri and Menaka had dressed herself as Gayatri, Sahjaniya had disguised herself as Jaya, and Punjakasthali had taken to the form of Vijaya.

Subsequently, several of the apsaras had disguised themselves in several forms, with the use of the Vidyas possessed by them.

The daughter of Kumbhanda looking at their forms, with the application of the Vaisnava yoga, knowing their secrets, had concealed her form.

The daughter of Banasura, known as Usa was well-versed in the divine yoga and took to the beautiful form of Parvati.

Her feet resembled the best of the red lotus flowers and were also embossed with the best of the auspicious symbols.

Parvati on the other hand became aware of their plan to enjoy the company of Siva, since she was well aware of the inner feelings of others.

Parvati said, O chaste and honourable with self-respect, you have adopted my form out of passion.

Therefore you during the present month of Kartika shall start menses. During the bright Dvadasi of the month of Vaisakha during mid¬night, whosoever would cohabit with you when you are asleep, in the inner apartment observing the fast, he would become your husband.

You have adored Visnu since your childhood, quite carefully.” She accepted the words of Parvati and felt ashamed in her mind.

Thereafter Parvati wore all the ornaments, arrived before Siva and started sporting with him.

O Sage, while so enjoying the sport, lord Siva, with Parvati and all the ganas suddenly disappeared from the place.

## Chapter 52 - The story of Usa- her meeting with Aniruddha

Sanatkumara said, “Now you listen to the second story of lord Siva- the Supreme soul, which bestows bliss, and reflecting his love on his devotees.

In the ancient times Banasura, overpowered with misfortune, pleased Siva with the Tandava dance.

Finding that Siva- the husband of Parvati had been pleased, he lowering his head with folded hands, spoke to him.

Banasura said, “O Mahadeva- the god of gods, the foremost of all the gods, I am powerful by your grace. You kindly listen to my words. You have bestowed me with a thousand arms which are a burden for me. Except you, there is no other warrior comparable to me in strength.

O Lord what shall I do with the thousand arms. O Lord Siva, what is the use of the mountain like arms, without a war.

With the itching for a war, I intend to fight with the elephants of the directions. When I got ready to fight with the towns and the mountains, they disappeared.

I made Yama a great combatant and the great fire-god too, similarly. Varuna has been made a cowherd looking after my cows.

I made Kubera, the lord of elephants, made Niriti a maid servant, overpowering Indra, I made him my tax-payer.

Now you kindly let me know about the war in which my hands fall shattered with the weapons of the enemy or cause them fall in thousands of pieces. O Lord Siva, you kindly fulfil my desire.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing this, Siva, who removed the obstructions of his devotees, felt enraged and laughing aloud spoke to him.

Siva said, “O arrogant one, the most degraded one in the Daitya race, disgrace to you in all respects. You are the son of Bali and my devotee. You should not have spoken like this.

Your arrogance would be removed shortly. You will shortly have to fight with a valorous person like me.

In that battle, your mountain like arms shall fall on earth like the trunks of the banana trees.

In your armoury, O Wicked soul, when your flag staff with the figure of peacock, which is installed in your armoury, falls without being blown off with the strong wind, you should then be clear in your mind that a terrible battle is in the offering. You should then go to that terrible war with your army generals. Now return to your abode where Siva is present.”

O Wicked one, you will face the enormous evil times.” After saying this, the lord, well- disposed towards his devotees and dispeller of the pride, stopped.

Sanatkumara said, “Banasura, on hearing all this, adoring Siva with the flowers carried in his hands, offering his salutation to the lord, Mahadeva, returned to his abode.

On an enquiry by Kumbhanda, he getting pleased, narrated to him all that had happened. Banasura then started anxiously waiting for the event.

As luck would have it, once he himself witnessed his broken flagstaff, after which Banasura, himself marched on for waging a war.

He summoned his army with eight ganas and performing the ynddha-yajna. He surveyed and inspected the wine used in the war, then he observed the auspicious signs in the quarters and set off. He the son of Bali, the horrible warrior capable of fighting with ten thousand persons, felt extremely enthusiastic.

Then be thought on to himself, who could be the great warrior well-versed in the use of arms, who would arrive to fight with me, and would cut off a thousand arms of mine like the Mandara-wood. By that time, I with the use of sharp weapons shall cut him off, a hundred times.

In the meantime Kala- the god of death arrived there, who had been sent by Siva, at the place where the daughter of Banasura had been seated, decorating herself.

She adored lord Visnu in the month of Vaisakha and at the dead of night she was sleeping in the inner quarters, after her monthly course, who was accepted in the women form.

Then overpowered by the divine maya, weeping like an orphan, she was enjoyed by the grandson of Krsna, who had been sent there by Parvati.

Thereafter with the help of the attendants of Parvati, he at once returned to Dvaraka by means of their divine Yogic power.

When she was so enjoyed (by the grandson of Krsna), she talking so much, started crying and lamenting and got ready to kill herself informing her handmaids.

O Vyasa, when she was reminded by her handmaid of her own fault, then she started recollecting the earlier events.

O Sage, then the daughter of Banasura named Usa, spoke to Citralekha, the daughter of Kumbhanda in sweet words.”

Usa said, “O Handmaid, the person who had already been settled by Parvati, how can I get him appropriately?

In which race has he been born? He has captivated my mind.” Thus listening to the words of Usa, Citralekha said to her.”

Citralekha said, “O Goddess, how can I produce the person seen by you in a dream and is unknown to me.

The daughter of the Daitya was blinded in love and was getting ready to kill herself. On the first day, she was somehow saved.

O Excellent sage, Citralekha the intelligent daughter of Kumbhanda, then spoke to the daughter of Bana.

In case the lover who was captivated your mind, is available in the three worlds, then I shall bring that man in order to remove your misery. You just tell me about him.

Sanatkumara said, “At these words of Citralekha, she drew the portraits of the gods, the Daityas, the Danavas, Gandharvas, Siddhas, nagas, Yaksas and others on a cloth.

Among the humans, she drew the portraits of Yadavas of Vrsnivamsa, Surasenas, Rama, Krsna, besides Pradyumna, the best of the humans.

Looking at the portrait of Aniruddha the son of Pradyumna, Usa felt delighted and lowering her head in shyness she spoke to Citralekha.

Usa said, “O Handmaid, I have found out the thief who stole away my mind, reaching at night.

With the very touch of his body, I felt attracted towards him. I want to know more about him, you please tell me about him.

In which race, was he born? What is his name?” On hearing this, the Yogini Citralekha, started explaining about his race and his name.

O Excellent sage, on hearing everything about his race, the passionate daughter of Bana, said to her maid.

Usa said, O Friend, you make arrangement to get him, so that I could be able to get my beloved husband.

O Friend, I cannot live without him even for a moment. You make me comfortable, by bringing him gracefully here.

Sanatkumara said, “O Excellent sage, when the daughter of Banasura thus spoke to her friend, she the daughter of the minister, feeling surprised, thought.

Then Citralekha, who could move with the speed of the wind, informing Usa, got ready to move to Dvaraka, taking him to be the grandson of Krsna.

On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Jyestha, she reached the city of Dvaraka after travelling for three days.

The divine yogini, travelling through the skyway, arrived there in a moment and found Aniruddha in the orchard of the inner apartments.

He was sporting with the damsels and drinking wine. All his limbs were beautiful, had dark complexion, wore a serene smile over his face, and was quite youthful.

The yogini Citralekha covered Aniruddha, the grandson of Krsna, who was seated over the bed, with the black cloth and with the strength of the Tamasa-yogic strength.

Carrying the bed over her head, she reached Sonitapura in a moment, where the daughter of Aniruddha was lodged.

Having been overpowered with passion and lust she was behaving like a mad person. On the arrival of Aniruddha, she was frightened a bit.

When both of them were united in the inner apartment at a secured place, and they enjoyed the sexual pleasure, then all the gatekeepers of the inner-apartment were woken up.

The guards appointed at the doorway to the harem with canesticks in their old and emaciated hands, under the impression that someone with a divine body having an illegitimate affairs with a virgin, found out that man by means of gestures and inferences. But when they found that some immensely strong person of youthful age, who was courageous and quite anxious for war, was inside, then the valorous guards, of the inner apartment of Banasura, the son of Bali, informed the monarch of the factual position.

The guards said, “O King, in the secret inner apartment, some one who has forcibly arrived there and is forcibly enjoying your daughter?

O Lord of Daityas, having large arms, you better go and see for yourself and do whatever you think best. We are not at all at fault in this case.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Excellent sage, the Daitya king, was surprised listening to the blemish of his girl.

## Chapter 53 - Fight between Banasura and Aniruddha who was bound by the Nagapasa- Shattering of Nagapasa by Kali

Sanatkumara said, “Thereafter, the enraged Banasura, went to the abode of his daughter and found there a young boy of youthful age.

Finding him there, Banasura, who had been well-versed in the warfare, feeling surprised, asked him the cause of his arrival there saying, “Who is this beautiful, courageous, patient, unfortunate and a foolish person whose death is nearing, arrived here?”

He has blemished my race, character and my dear daughter. Better kill him with hard weapons.

O Warriors, capture this wicked person of evil conduct and throw him in a harsh prison for a long time.

Who is this immensely valorous and fearless person?” Thus thinking, the intelligent Banasura, was overpowered with doubt.

Then the sinful and evil-minded Banasura, commanded the thousand soldiers to kill him.

At his command, the valorous warriors surrounded the inner apartment and shouted to kill and cut him off. Then the Yadava, thundering at the sight of the enemy soldiers, stood at the entrance gate of the inner apartment carrying an unparallel parigha.

Then he moved out of that house, like Yama, carrying a Vajra in his hand. After killing all the soldiers, he again returned to the same house.

O Excellent sage, getting enraged, and having been filled with lustre of Siva, he killed all the ten thousand warriors.

When a hundred thousand soldiers had been killed, Banasura, then getting enraged called for Kumbhanda, who was well-versed in warfare. Aniruddha was protected with the lustre of Siva, his body was resplendent, but the intelligent son of Pradyumna was challenged for a duel fight. Thereafter Aniruddha, with the use of the sword of the demon king, killed the ten thousand warriors as well the horses, shattering their chariots at the same time.

Aniruddha, using the Sakti, which resembled the fire of the time of dissolution, attacked the great Daitya.

With the attack of the Sakti (spear). Banasura, seated in his chariot vanished along with his horses.

Finding the disappearing of the Daitya king, with the strike of the Sakti, Aniruddha glanced on all the directions and stood there like a rock.

The deceitful Daitya king, after his disappearing, started attacking Aniruddha stealthily again and again.

Then the immensely valorous, Banasura, the devotee of Siva, deceitfully shot a nagapasa, which captured Aniruddha.

After enslaving Aniruddha, he was imprisoned in a cage, who enjoyed respite from the war. Then the valorous Banasura spoke to the valorous son of the charioteer.

Banasura said, “O Son of the charioteer, you atonce cut off the head of this person, who has showered blemish over my spotless Daitya race.

Cutting of all his limbs distribute them to the Daityas. Let the kites and crows eat his flesh and bones.

O Son of the charioteer, then you kill him by throwing him in the well filled with enormous grass and water. What more should I speak. Destroy him in all respects.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Banasura, the religious minded demon Kumbhanda said to him.

Kumbhanda said, “O Deva, you first think over. It would not be proper for us to do so. By killing him it would amount to the killing of the soul. This is what I feel.

He is no ordinary a person, but appears quite valorous like Visnu. Besides is bestowed with the resplendence of Siva.

Moreover in courage, he appears to be equal to the moon-crested lord. Inspite of his having been reduced to the miserable plight, he maintains his courage.

This grandson of lord Krsna, even after having been bitten by the serpents like Daityas, he thinks all like the straw and of no consequence.”

Sanatkumara said, “The Danava who was well-versed in polity, after thus speaking to Banasura, addressed Aniruddha.”

Kumbhanda said, “O Valorous one, who are you? Who is your father. Speak out truthfully before me. O Wicked and degraded person, who brought you here?

You offer your salutation to Daitya king with folded hands and eulogise him repeatedly that “You have overpowered a destitute like me.

By so doing, you can get yourself released, otherwise you are sure to rot in captivity and tortures.”

Aniruddha said, “O Degraded friend of the Daitya, you live on the food provided by him. O Degraded demon, you are not aware of the dharma of an enemy.

What I feel is that becoming a destitute, and to flee, is like the death for a valorous warrior. Such a behaviours is against the conduct of a warrior, and happens to be like a thorn. The only welfare for a valorous Ksatriya warrior is to face the enemy in the battle field and not to beg mercy like a miserable destitute.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus he spoke the words, which were best suited for a great warrior. Hearing these word, both Kumbhanda as well as Banasura felt surprised and were enraged.

At that point of time, in order to assure Banasura, his courtier as well as Aniruddha, a divine voice from the sky was heard.

The divine voice said, “O Siva’s devotee, immensely valorous, intelligent Bana- the son of Bali, you first think over.

Lord Siva, is the lord of all, the supreme lord, and is as well the witness of all the deeds. This mobile and immobile world is subservient to him.

He is the creator of the universe, sustainer as well as its destroyer. Both Brahma, Visnu and Siva are representing Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. They are the form of Siva.

He pervades in all. He is the lord and inspirator of all. He is beyond all, unblemished, indestructible, eternal, and the lord of illusion besides being Nirguna.

O Intelligent son of Bali, with the desire of lord Siva even the weak become valorous. Thus thinking in your mind be pleasant.

The lord who is well-disposed towards his devotees, the performer of several sports, shatters the pride of all. He will also shatter your pride.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Great sage, the aerial voice stopped after speaking thus. Banasura, then at the advice of the aerial voice, did not kill Aniruddha.

But he going to his inner apartment, consumed the best of wine and forgetting the words, enjoyed the sexual pleasure, since he had been adversely affected.

But Aniruddha, who had been in bondages of the serpents, feeling disturbed without his beloved, remembered Durga.”

Aniruddha said, “O Goddess possessing enormous anger, O Yasoda, the one who affords protection, I have been bound with Nagapasa. You kindly protect me.

You are devoted to Siva, the great goddess, you create, preserve and destroy the universe, there is no one else, except you to protect me. Therefore O Siva you kindly protect me.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus eulogising Kali having the complexion of collyrium, and pleasing her by offering prayer to her, at the dead of night in the month Jyestha, on the fourteenth day of the black fortnight, the goddess appeared before him.

Then she with the Vajra- like fists, broke the cage and reduced the serpentine arrows to ashes.

She released Aniruddha, and making him enter the inner apartments, she disappeared from the scene.

O Excellent sage, in this way, the goddess Siva- the form of the Sakti of Siva, making Aniruddha comfortable by releasing him, disappeared from the scene.

With the influence of Siva-sakti, Aniruddha- the son of Pradyumna, becoming victorious and getting the daughter of Bana, felt extremely comfortable.

Because of excessive drinking his eyes were red and he continued enjoying the sexual pleasures with the daughter of Banasura as before.

## Chapter 54 - Departure of Krsna to Patala in order to get back Aniruddha and his fight with Banasura

Vyasa said, “O Excellent sage, the daughter of Kumbhanda when abducted Aniruddha- the grandson of Krsna, then what did Krsna do? You tell me.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Excellent sage, after the departure of Aniruddha, Sri Krsna felt painful at the crying of the ladies of the harem.

Krsna and his wives felt worried in the absence of Aniruddha. In this way four months of the rainy season passed.

Learning of his capture of his grandson from Narada, Sri Krsna, the lord of Yadavas, felt concerned.

Sri Krsna, listening to the news, summoned gracefully atonce marched towards Sonitapura.

At that point of time, Balarama and Krsna were followed by Pradyumna, Yuyudhana, Sama, Sarana, Nanda, Upananda, Bhadra and others.

The Yadavas accompanied with twelve aksaucehini's of army, surrounded the city of Banasura from all the four sides.

They destroyed the city, orchards, boundary wall; fortresses, ceilings besides the minarets, of the city. With this destruction, Bana was infuriated and set forth with an equal number of army.

Siva mounted over his Nandi and accompanied with his sons and the pramathas arrived there for fighting.

Krsna and his warriors fought with Siva the protector of Banasura, and his ganas a terrific battle. Krsna fought with Siva, Pradyumna with Kartikeya, besides Kusmanda with Kupakarna fierce battles.

Samba fought with the son of Banasura, Satyaki with Banasura, Nandi with Garuda, while the other fighters fought with other warriors.

At that point of time, Brahma and other gods, the sages, Siddhas, Caranas, Gandharvas, apsaras arrived there to witness the war boarding their respective vehicles.

O Best of the Brahmanas, the Yadavas fought an awful battle with the pramathas including Revati and others.

Krsna with the brother Balarama accompanied with his son, fought a fierce battle with pramathas.

The fight continued with Agni, Yama, Varuna, Vimukha, Tripada, Jvara and Kartikeya, besides the groups of pramathas fought with Vrsnis. It was a horrible battle causing horripilation.

There was the fight with naked and shameless women too. Several groups of horrible kotaris fought at every step from one another.

The goblins, pramathas Guhyakas and other ganas of Siva, were driven out by Krsna, with the arrows shot from his bow.

In this way Pradyumna and others, who were delighted at the war, destroyed enormous army of the enemy.

Lord Siva, finding the destruction of his army, was infuriated and started thundering aloud.

Thereafter the ganas of Siva, having been invigorated with the resplendence of Siva, started thundering killing the

Then Krsna shot several types of arrows at Siva from his Saranga bow which were made infructuous by Siva.

Siva then neutralised Brahmastra with Brahmastra, Vayavyastra with Punatastra and Agnyastra with Parajanyastra.

The army of the side of Krsna, fled away with the attack of Siva. O Vyasa, no one could stand the battle field because of the resplendence of Siva.

O Sage, after the fleeing of the army of Krsna, the destroyer of the enemies, created terrible fever missile called cold.

O Sage, when the army of Krsna was so routed the cold fever missile of Krsna, rushed at Rudra blazing the ten quarters.

Finding the arrival of the fever missile of Krsna, lord Siva thrust his own fever missile. The two fevers fought with each other.

The fever missile of lord Krsna was oppressed by the one issued by Siva, as a result of which the former started crying aloud, unable to receive respite anywhere else, it eulogised the lord Siva having the bull banner.

Lord Siva was then delighted and since he is favourably disposed towards his devotees, who take refuge in him, having been eulogised by the fever missile of lord Visnu.

Siva said, “O Cold fever, I am happy with you, don’t be afraid of my fever missile any more, whosoever listens to our conversation, he would be no more afraid of the fever.

Sanatkumara said, “At these words of Siva, Narayana- fever missile left the place offering his salutation to Siva. Observing this episode, Sri Krsna was surprised feeling panicky at the same time.

Having been injured with the arrows of Pradyumna, and getting infuriated Skanda the leader of Daityas shot a Sakti at the former.

With the shooting of the Sakti by Skanda, blood started gushing from the body of Pradyumna, who disappeared from the battle ground.

With the use of various weapons by Kumbhanda and Kupakarna the valorous Balabhadra also deserted the battle ground.

Garuda on his part, taking to a thousand forms, drank the oceanic water and raining it like the clouds, killed several of the Daityas

Thereafter the powerful Nandi, the vehicle of Siva, getting infuriated started striking the enemies with his horns.

With the striking of the horns, Garuda was surprised getting injured and he also fled away from the battle ground, leaving his lord behind.

Under these circumstances, the lord, son of Devaki, getting astonished with the resplendence of Siva, spoke to his charioteer.

Sri Krsna said, “You at my command drive the chariot straight to lord Siva, to enable me to talk to him.”

Sanatkumara said, “At these words of lordKrsna, the charioteer named Daruka, drove the chariot close to Siva.

Then he humbly folding his hands, submitted to Siva- who is well-disposed towards his devotees.”

Sri Krsna said, “O Mahadeva, the god of gods, you are well-disposed towards those who take refuge in you, you are the soul of all and Paramesvara.

You are the creator of the universe besides being its preserver and the destroyer ultimately. You are the only form of the perfect knowledge, the symbol of Brahman, extremely peaceful and the supreme lord.

The time, divinity, the actions, the individual soul, the nature, the solid objects, the vital airs, the souls, the created beings, the numerous seeds, sprout everything with your illusion. O Lord of the universe, I take refuge in you being the cause of those things, you are the great lord.

You assume different forms playfully, you are the lord of the three worlds, you support the gods and others while destroying those who prefer the evil path.

You are the great Brahman, the great light hidden in the Sabda-Brahman which is seen by the purified souls, like the sole firmament.

You are the primordial Purusa, without a second. You are the fourth being and the vision of the soul. You appear like changing, though you are the lord, the cause without another cause unto you.

O Lord, O Mahesvara, you with your illusion for the popularity of your gunas, you are merged as well as separated from them.

O Lord as the sun is free from the shadow, gets resplendent with its own light, similarly you possess the spotless vision.

O Great one, O Self illuminated one, O Lord Siva, you getting free from the Sattva, Rajas and Tamas gunas brighten the attributes by means of attribute itself.

The people where intellects are deluded with your illusion get attached to their wives, sons, abodes etc. and sail and float the ocean of sin.

A person who is unable to control hissenses, and considers the worldly pleasures as having been achieved by luck alone, and does not respect at your feet, he is to be pitied since he actually deceives himself.

O Lord it is at your command, that I have arrived here to cut off the arms of Banasura. It is actually you, the destroyer of the pride, who had pronounced a curse over Banasura.

O Deva, you better leave the battle field lest your curse becomes infructuous. O Lord, kindly permit me to cut off the arms of Banasura.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Excellent sage, listening to these words and the prayer of Sri Krsna, lord Siva was pleased.”

Siva said, “O Dear one, you have spoken the truth. I had pronounced a curse on the Daitya king. Actually you have arrived here to cut off the arms of Banasura at my command.

O Hari, O Lord of Rama, I am always subservient to my devotee. How can you cut off the arms of Banasura in my presence.

Therefore at my command, you shoot Jrmbhastra on me and make me benumbed. Thereafter you can do whatever you like and be happy.”

Sanatkumara said, “These words of Siva surprised Sri Krsna immensely. Siva too felt pleased having reached the battle ground.

O Vyasa, Krsna was well-versed in the use of various arms, then he shot the Jrmbhastra at Siva.

After shooting of the Jrmbhastra, by Sri Krsna, Siva felt enchanting. In the meantime Krsna slew the army of Bana with swords, daggers and clubs.

## Chapter 55 - Krsna’s cutting of the arms of Banasura, by the grace of Siva and marriage of Usa and Aniruddha

Vyasa said, “O Sage Sanatkumara, the omniscient one, O Dear one, the son of Brahma, salutation to you. You have narrated this astonishing story.

When Krsna shot the Jrmbhastra at Siva, killing the army of Bana at the same time, then what did Banasura do? You tell me.

Suta said, “Thus listening to the immensely illustrious Vyasa’s words, the great sage who was the son of Brahma said to him.

Sanatkumara said, “O Intelligent Vyasa, you listen to the stories of Sri Krsna and Siva, who indulge in several type of sports.

When Siva was overpowered with sleep with his sons and the ganas, then Banasura arrived there for waging a war with Krsna.

He took the horse from Kumbhanda and carrying various types of weapons, the valorous son of Bali started fighting an astonishing war.

Finding the destruction of his army, the Daitya king was immensely infuriated. Then the son of Bali fought a terrific war.

Having been invigorated by Siva, the valorous Krsna also considered Banasura like the straw and started thundering aloud.

O Excellent sage, Sri Krsna, with the issuing of the deafening sound from his bow, Saranga, frightened the army of Daitya- Banasura.

The great sound originating from the twang of his bow echoed in the intervening space between heaven and earth.

Then he stretched the cord of the bow upto the ears and shot the sharp arrows resembling the nagas getting infuriated, at Banasura.

Banasura the son of Bali on his part, finding the arrows approaching him, cut of those arrows with the arrows shot by him, in the mid-way.

Then the killer of the enemies lord Krsna, started roaring. All the Yadavas, at that point of time, were fainted remembering Krsna.

Then the valorous Banasura devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, shot arrows at the immensely valorous Krsna.

The valorous Krsna, the enemy of the Daityas, also devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of lord Siva, cut off all the arrows of the enemy.

The Yadavas like Balarama and others, killed several of the enemy warriors, getting irritated.

In this way the battle between both Krsna and Banasura continued for long, which surprised all the onlookers, who felt surprised.

At that point of time Garuda smashed a large number of the enemy warriors, by crushing them with his wings.

Daitya king - the son of Bali, finding that his warriors had been crushed he was enormously infuriated.

Then Bana with a thousand hands, remembering Siva, displayed the prowess which was unbearable for the enemy.

He simultaneously shot arrows at Krsna, the killers of the Daitya warriors, and other soldiers of Yadava army, besides Garuda.

He shot an arrow each at Garuda, Krsna, Balarama and several other warriors of the enemy.

Then Sri Krsna, the destroyer of the enemy of the gods, Mahesvara, valorous, form of Visnu was enraged in the battle ground and he started thundering.

Devoting his mind at Siva, he shot several arrows at valorous Bana and many of his warriors.

Then Hari, becoming carefree, cut off the bow and the chatra of Bana, besides killing his horses as well.

The valorous Banasura, also roared getting enraged, and he attacked Krsna with a club, who fell down on the ground.

O Divine sage, Krsna got up at once and fought with the Daitya according to the worldly sport, who was also a devotee of Siva.

Thus Siva in the form of Krsna and the Daitya a devotee of Siva kept on fighting for a long time.

O Excellent sage, the powerful lord Krsna kept on fighting with Banasura for a long time. Then getting invigorated with the command and prowess of Siva, he felt immensely enraged.

Then lord Krsna, the destroyer of heroic armies, at the bidding of Siva, suddenly cut off many arms of Banasura, with the Sudarsana cakra.

By the grace of Siva, only four beautiful arms were left out and soon his misery was over.

Forgetting Siva’s command, when Krsna was about the sever the head of Banasura, then Rudra stood before Krsna

Siva said- O Lord, O Son of Devala, O Visnu, what was ordained by me formerly has been accomplished by you who always follow my dictates.

Now you get back the Sudarsana-cakra. Let this cakra not exercise its wroth over my devotee. Therefore do not severe the head of Banasura.

O Govinda, this is essential Cakra, which had been given by me to you for waging wars. Now you ask it to return to you.

At my command, you did not use this Cakra over Dadhici, Ravana, valorous Tarakasura and the others.

You are in fact, yogisvara, the supreme soul and Janardana, therefore, you think in your mind.

You are not at all afraid of death. Therefore my word always comes to be true. I am pleased with you.

In earlier times, Banasura, scratching his arms and getting filled with arrogance, had arrived before me and had demanded an opportunity for waging a war. Then O Hari, he had forgotten his position.

Then I had pronounced a curse on him, “Some one would arrive for the cutting of your arms, and would shatter your pride.

At my command, the lord has arrived for the severing of your arms, therefore now you return to your abode with your spouse.”

Thus speaking, and negotiating friendship between the two of them, Siva accompanied with his son and Parvati, returned to his abode.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Siva, getting back the Sudarsana cakra, the victorious Krsna returned to his inner apartment.

Assuring Aniruddha, he accepted his grandson with his wife Usa and thus graced Banasura.

Sri Krsna felt pleased by receiving Yogini Citralekha- the handmaid of Usa, Sri Krsna was successful in his mission by the grace of Siva, and felt delighted.

Receiving permission from Banasura, the son of Bali, offering mentally, the salutation to Siva, Lord Krsna, retreated to his abode in Dvaraka.

On the way he overpowered the inimical Varuna. All of them then reached the city of Dvaraka well pleased.

Garuda was then sent off to his abode, and meeting their kins, all of them started living in Dvaraka, quite happily.

## Chapter 56 - Bestowing the position of Ganapati on Banasura by Siva

Narada said, “After the departure of Sri Krsna and Aniruddha with his wife Usa to Dvaraka, O Great Sage, what did Banasura, do?”

Sanatkumara said, “ Banasura, after the departure of Krsna and Aniruddha with his wife, getting reminded of his foolishness, felt quite painful at heart.

Then finding Banasura, having been soaked in blood. Nandi said to him.

Nandi said, “O Devotee of Siva, O Banasura, don’t repent. Siva is well-disposed towards his devotees and showers his grace on them.

Whatever he desired has happened. O best of the devotees of Siva, now you devote your mind towards Siva, again and again.

Siva the eternal lord is always kind to his devotees. Therefore you, devoting your mind to Siva, remain happy daily.”

Then Banasura, clearing his mind of all the jealousies, felt encouraged with the words of Nandi, and went to the place of Siva.

Reaching there, he felt anxious, shedding away the arrogance, infested with love, he started crying.

With his hands and the feet floundering, offering his salutation, he started eulogising Siva.

Then he performed Tandava dance displaying pratyalidha and other postures

He started playing on thousands of mouth organs. With the shaking of his hands, he made his eyebrows also to dance.

Gradually he displayed several types of dances, he made the streams of blood to flow over the ground.

Banasura, the great devotee pleased Siva- Candrasekhara, the holder of a trident, forgetting his movements.

In this way he danced with several poses. Then lord Siva, who loves the dance and music, spoke to Banasura.

Siva said, “O Dear one, Daitya king, O Son of Bali, I feel pleased with your dance. Therefore you ask for any boon you desire.

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, on hearing these words of Siva, the Daitya king, desired for the healing of his wounds as the boon.

Then he begged forgiveness for his deceitfulness in the battle of arms, infallible position of Ganapati, the kingship for the son of Usa at Sonitapura.

Friendliness with the gods and particularly Visnu, free of enmity and that he should not have the feeling of demon-hood comprising of Rajas and Tamas.

O Sage, he desired of the spotless devotion towards Siva, love towards the devotees of Siva, and a feeling of compassion towards all the living beings.

With folded hands and tears flowing from his eyes, eulogising him, the great ausra, the son of Bali, begged for these boons from Siva.”

Bana said, “O Mahadeva, the god of gods, well-disposed towards those who takes refuge in you, Mahesan, kin of the destitutes, Ocean of mercy, I offer my salutation to you.

O Ocean of mercy, O Siva, O Lord, by getting delightful, you have shattered my pride.

You are the Brahman, the supreme soul, all pervading, Lord of the universe, the form of the globe, ugra, Isvara, Virat, all pervading and the supreme one.

O Lord, you have the sky as your navel, fire is your mouth, water is your semen, the dhyuloka as your head, and the earth as your feet besides the moon is your mind.

The sun is your eyes, rddhi is your belly, Indra your arms, Brahma is your intelligence, Prajapati is the charity and the dharma happens to be your heart.

O Lord, the osadhis represent your hair on the body, the hair of the head is the cloud, the three eyes represent your three gunas. Therefore, you are the Purusa representing the souls of all.

Your face represents the Brahmana, the arms Ksatriyas, the thighs as Vaisyas and the feet as the Sudras. In other words, all the four varnas have emerged out of you.

O Mahesvara, you are always adorable by all the living beings, because the people achieve salvation by adoring you.

O Isvara, the one who neglects you, it amounts to neglecting one’s own soul and he consumes poison, in the form of the pleasure of senses, discarding the nectar.

Brahma, Visnu and other gods, the sages with the spotless mind, have taken refuge with lord Siva.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking, Banasura, the son of Bali, kept quiet and felt delighted, offering his salutation to Siva.

Thus listening to the prayer of Banasura, lord Siva said, “You will be benefited enormously.” Thus speaking he disappeared from the scene.

Then with the grace of lord Siva, Bana attained the immortality of the eternal times and became one of the gana of Siva, with delight.

Thus I have narrated by means of words pleasing to the ears, the excellent story of lord Siva, the carrier of the trident, who is the preceptor of the preceptors, and who always sports in the middle of the worlds. His story includes his activities in relation to Bana.

## Chapter 57 - Killing of Gajasura, the son of demon Mahisa by Siva

Sanatkumara said, "O Vyasa, now you listen to the story of Siva, who killed Gajasura with his trident.

After the killing of Mahisasura by the goddess, the gods were pleased.

O Excellent sage, Gajasura was his excellent son, who, remembered the killing of his father at the hands of the gods.

Then he keeping in mind, the killing of his father, aiming at Brahma, went to the forest, and started performing hard tapas, there.

He started performing the severe penance with the sole purpose that he should be free from lustful passions and should be invincible from the men or women.

He then started performing tapas in a Himalayan cave resting over two big toe of the feet raising one of his hands towards the sky.

The son of Mahisasura, named Gajasura was quite an intelligent one having matted locks of hair over the head and was resplendent like the shining sun.

The fire in the form of the penance originating from his head and filled with smoke spread in the worlds above, below and on the sides, scorching them.

The rivers and the oceans were agitated with the fire emerging out of his head. The stars fell along with the planets. All the ten quarters were in a blaze.

All the gods including Indra, getting scorched from the heat, left the heaven and reached Brahmaloka and said, “The earth is shaking.”

The gods said, “O Brahma, we are suffering because of the tapas of Gajasura, besides being upset. Now we cannot live in the heaven. Therefore we have arrived here to take refuge with you.

You better pacify him and arrange for bringing others back to life. Otherwise all the lokas would be destroyed.”

At this prayer of Indra and other gods, the self-born Brahma, accompanied with Daksa, Bhrgu and others went to the place where the Daityaraja was performing tapas.

The Daitya king appeared to be scorching the lokas with his tapas like the clouds covering the sky. Observing him the surprised Brahma spoke smilingly.

Brahma said, “O Son of Mahisa, the Demon king. Your tapas has met with success. O Dear one, I have arrived here to bestow the boon on you. You better ask for a boon.

Sanatkumara said, “Then Daityaraja, the son of Mahisasura, got up and speaking in choked voice, he asked for the boon.

Gajasura said, “O God of gods, salutation to you. In case you are interested in giving me the boon, then I should always unattacked and invincible either by the men or the women.

I, possessing all the strength and prowess, should be invincible from the gods even. I should be able to enjoy the fortunes of all the lokapalas.”

Sanatkumara said, “In this way the Danava, asked for a unique boon fromBrahma, which was given to him by the creator, having been pleased with his tapas.”

Then the son of Mahisasura, getting pleased, returned to his abode.

The great asura then subjugated all the ten directions, the three worlds, the gods, the asuras, humans, Indra, Gandharvas, Garuda and the serpents.

Then bringing them under this control, he usurped the resplendence of the lokapalas.

He started living in the abode of Indra, to which Nandanavana was attached and was built by Visvakarma.

In the palace of Devaraja Indra, the valorous Daityaraja having conquered all the lokas, the Cakravarti Gajasura, made the gods to adore his feet and he kept on living there.

The invincible asura, thus conquering all the directions, enjoying all the pleasures of his liking, never felt satisfied.

In this way he felt intoxicated with the fortunes and started moving contrary to the provision of the scriptures and in short time he lost the balance of his mind.

Then the son of Mahisasura started troubling the gods.

The evil minded Danavas, started troubling the gods, humans, and pramathas getting reminded of his earlier enmity. He particularly caused pain to the religious minded people.

O Dear one, once the immensely powerful Danava Gajasura reached the capital city of Siva.

O Sage, on the arrival of the Danava there, all the residents of the place cried for shelter and safety, which created a turmoil.

Getting intoxicated, due to his prowess, the demon entered the city trampling over Siva.

At that point of time all the gods including Indra, getting defeated at the hands of Daityaraja, took refuge with Siva, offering their salutation to him. Then they started offering prayer to him.

They also informed Siva about the arrival of Gajasura in the city of Kasi and also that the demon was causing trouble to the noble people.

The gods said, “O Mahadeva - the god of gods, the demon has arrived in your city. O Merciful one, he is causing harm to your devotees. Therefore, you should destroy him.

Wherever he places his foot on earth, the ground starts shaking with his weight.

With his force, the trees of the peaks fall and the mountains are turned to pieces with the striking of his arms.

With the touch of his crown, the clouds disappear from the sky. The sky has turned blue with the touch of the locks of his hair.

With his breathing high waves are produced in the rivers and the oceans, with timi fish.

With his delusion the height of his body is raised to nine thousand yojanas. The body develops breadth of equal dimensions.

The yellowness and the moisture in his eyes is hardly found in the lightning even, the same asura has arrived here.

Wherever the Danava of unbearable prowess reaches, declares that he cannot be killed by the unattached men or women. Therefore you kindly protect your devotees.

O Lord of the gods, you are the protector of the city of Kasi and as such we have apprised you about the conduct of the Daitya. Therefore you kindly protect your devotees.

Sanatkumara said, “The gods thus eulogised Siva who being the protector of his devotees rushed for protecting them by killing the asura.

Finding that Siva, who was well-disposed towards his devotees was holding a trident in his hand, Gajasura started thundering.

Then both of them waged a great war, shooting several weapons at each other roaring like a lion at the same time.

The immensely illustrious, immensely valorous and powerful Gajasura, injured Siva, the destroyer of the Danavas, with sharp arrows.

O Sage, then Siva, assuming the horrible form reduced the arrows of the demon into pieces, shooting his own arrows intercepting them in the middle.

The enraged Gajasura, then, rushed towards Siva carrying a sword in his hand and shouting “I have killed you.”

Finding that Gajasura invincible by others was approaching with the trident and the sword in his hands. Siva shot a trident at him.

Gajasura, then having been wounded with the trident of Siva started eulogising the lord.”

Gajasura said, “O Mahadeva, the god of gods, holder of the trident, lord of the three worlds, destroyer of Kamadeva, I happen to be your devotee.

O Mahesan, enemy of Andhaka, killer of Tripura, omniscient one, my death at your hand would bestow enormous welfare on me.

O Merciful one, I beg to submit something, you kindly listen to me. O Mrtyunjaya, I am speaking the truth and not the falsehood. You kindly think over the same.

You are the only one adorable in the world and rule the same. All have to meet with their end in due course to time. But the death (at your hands) bestows welfare.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to his words, Siva, the ocean of mercy, smiled and spoke to Gajasura, the son of Mahisasura.

Siva said, “O Treasure of the enormous strength, best of the Danavas, possessing excellent wisdom, O Gajasura, I am pleased with you. You better ask for a boon you desire.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Siva, the bestower of the boon, the delighted king of Danavas, replied.”

Gajasura said, “O Digambara Siva, O Mahesan, in case, you are really happy with me, then you should wear always my skin which has been purified with the tip of your trident.

The elephant skin is of your own size, which has been defeated by me at your hands in the battle field. Its touch is quite pleasant, besides being pleasant to look at. This is the divine skin, which would make you comfortable.

It would never issue any bad smell. It would always remain soft, graceful and spotless.

O Lord, this hide, even after getting scorched with the flames of fire of tapas for a long time, would not be burnt. Therefore it is the abode of the auspicious fragrance.

O Digambara (without robes) in case my skin is not auspicious, then how could it come in contact with your limbs in the battle-field?

O Siva, in case you are satisfied, and pleased, then grant me another boon, that from today onwards, you should also be known as Krttivasa or the clad in elephant hide.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of Gajasura, Siva, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, was pleased and he replied to Gajasura- the son of Mahisasura, “Be it so.”

Lord Siva, who is the favourite of his devotees, granted the boon to Gajasura and again said to him.

Siva said, “Let your auspicious body become my linga in the region bestowing salvation.

It would be known by the name of Krttivasesvara. It would be the best of all the lingas. It would remove all the sins, being the bestower of salvation.

After thus speaking, the Digambara Siva, the lord of the gods, then wore the skin of Gajasura accepting the hide of it.

O Best of sages, on that particular day, pramathas in Kasi as well as all other people felt pleased celebrating the occasion.

Brahma, Visnu and all other gods, feeling delighted, eulogised Siva with their hands folded.

At the death of Gajasura the son of Mahisasura, the gods left for their respective abodes and the entire universe felt rejoiced.

I have thus narrated to you the auspicious story of Siva, which displays his love for his devotees, which bestows heaven, fame, longevity of life and increases riches and cereals.

The one who listens to this episode with devotion, or narrates the same, to others observing the spotless rites, he enjoys all the pleasures and attains salvation and the greatest bliss.

## Chapter 58 - Killing of Dundubhi, Nirhrada by Siva in the form of Vyaghresvara

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, I am now going to narrate to you the way, how the demons named Dundubhi and Nirhrada were killed by Candrasekhara Siva.

With the killing of valorous Hiranyaksa- the son of Diti, by lord Visnu, his mother felt extremely painful. The demon Nirhrada, the maternal uncle of Prahlada, tried to console Diti with various pleasing words, assuring her at the same time.

Then the illusory demon- king, assured Diti, thought of the way and means to overpower the gods with ease.

When gods the enemies of the Daityas, with the help of Visnu, deceitfully killed Hiranyaksa with his brother, he thought, “What is the strength of the gods? What do they eat? What is their base? How could I conquer them?” In this way he started thinking of the ways and means to subjugate the gods.

The demon, after considerable thinking came to the conclusion, that, “the Brahmanas are the main reason for the same.”

Then the enormously foolish Dundubhi and Demon Nirhrada rushed again and again for the killing of the Brahmanas.

Because according to him the gods enjoyed the share of the yajnas which were performed with the reciting of the Vedic hymns. TheBrahmanas were the base of the Vedas. Therefore Brahmanas were the strength of the gods. There is no doubt about it.

In case the Brahmanas are destroyed, the Vedas will perish and with the destruction of the Vedas, the gods will perish, as well.

With the destruction of the sacrifices, the gods would be deprived of their food. They would grow weaker and would become easily vulnerable. When the gods are overpowered, I shall become the sole and honourable lord of the three worlds. In that case I shall usurp all the fortunes of the gods.

I shall enjoy pleasures in my kingdom, free from thorns.” After thus thinking, the wicked Daitya further thought.

“Which is the dwelling place of the Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas, having the strength of tapas, mainly lodged?

Surely most of the Brahmanas are dwelling in Varanasi. Initially the Brahmanas of Kasi should be killed and thereafter I should go to other places of pilgrimage.

I shall devour all the Brahmanas in whichever holy place or in whichever asrama they are found.”

In this way the illusory Nirhrada, thinking, according to his race, reached Kasi and started killing the Brahmanas.

In whichever forest, the Brahmanas went for the collection of the wood and Kusa grass, he, the evil-minded one, devoured all of them.

In order to conceal his identity he used to change his form as a wild animal in the forest and as an aquatic creature in the water, hiding himself there.

The illusory demon even escaped the sight of the gods. During the day time he remained among the sages seated in dhyanamudra.

During the nights whosoever Brahmanas moved through the hermitages, then he taking to the form of a tiger devoured them all.

He devoured them fearlessly leaving no trace of them, even the bones. In this way he devoured many of the Brahmanas.

Once on the day of Sivaratri, a devotee of Siva, was seated in dhyanamudra in his cottage in meditating posture

Then the Daitya Dundubhi Nirhrada, under the pride of his strength, taking to the form of a tiger attempted to devour him.

But since the Brahmana, before sitting for meditation with a concentrated mind, using the mantra-kavaca had safeguarded the place the demon failed to attack him.

On the other hand the omnipresent Siva came to know of the evil design of the demon and he decided to kill him.

When the Daitya, in the form of the tiger was about to attack the devotee, the lord appeared before him.

The linga, having been adored by the devotee, Siva came out of it, the Demon expanded his size like a mountain.

Siva being the abode of intelligence, is always anxious to save his devotees as well as the universe. The Danava contemptuously looked at Siva, but the lord caught hold of the demon and pressed him under his armpit.

The five faced Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, hit the tiger over the head with his Vajra like fist.

With the striking of the fist, and the force used by the lord under the armpit the tiger groaned aloud in great pain and roared filling heaven and earth with the same and fell down dead.

Following the tract of the sound the ascetics were agitated in their minds and reached the place of incident during the night itself.

Finding the lord Siva there with the lord of the beasts, pressed in his armpit, they bowed in reverence to him. They eulogised him shouting the slogans of victory.

The Brahmanas said, “You have saved us from this terrific misery. O Preceptor of the universe, O Isa. You kindly be merciful on us.

O Mahadeva, in this self-same form in the name of the lord of the tiger offer protection. Let this place remain sacred always.

You also protect us from other dangers. O Lord of Gauri, you bestow protection to your devotees removing the wicked demons.”

Sanatkumara said, “On hearing the words of his devotees, Candrasekhara Siva said, “It would be done accordingly.” Thus speaking the lord addressed his devotees again.”

Siva said, “Whosoever shall glance at me in this form, all his terror shall be removed by me.

Listening to this episode concerning me, remembering that linga in his mind, whosoever would enter the battlefield, would be surely victorious in the battle.”

In the meantime all the gods celebrating festivities and shouting the slogans of victory reached there.

All the gods lovingly folded their hands, to Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, eulogised Siva, offering their salutation to him.

The gods said, “O Sankara, O Lord of the gods, remover of the miseries of the devotees, O Lord, you have protected us by killing Dundubhi Nirhrada.

O Lord, well-disposed towards the devotees, you kindly protect us. O God of gods, O Lord of all, O Master, you always destroy the wicked people.”

Thus listening to the words of the gods, the lord accepted their prayer and merged into the linga.

The Brahmanas also left the place getting pleased. One should listen, narrate and teach the excellent episode of the emerging of Vyaghresvara and by doing so a person has all his desired fulfilled. In the life after death, he achieves moksa without misery.

This episode of the sport of Siva is full of the nectar like words. It bestows the heaven, glory, long life, sons and grandsons.

It bestows the supreme type of devotion, makes one graceful, is the bestower of welfare, pleasant, destroyer of the worldly blemishes and makes one achieve the devotion of Siva.

## Chapter 59 - Killing of the Daityas, named Vidala and Utpala by Gauri

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, you lovingly listen to the story of the lord Siva, the way he got a Daitya killed by indication, from his spouse- Gauri.

In the ancient times there were two powerful Daityas known as Vidala and Utpala. Both of them had turned arrogant, because of the boons they had received from Brahma that they could never be killed by any human being.

O Brahmana, both the Daityas, on the basis of the strength of their arms, reduced all the three lokas to be of no consequence and defeated all the gods in the battle ground.

All the gods, after their defeat went to Brahma. They offering their salutation appropriately to him, submitted to him with respect.

Then Brahma said to him, “All of you should keep patience and adore Siva with Parvati. Both of them are bound to be killed at the hands of the goddess.

Siva is auspicious, benevolent favourably disposed to his devotees. Together with Parvati he would bestow grace on all the gods.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus speaking to the gods, Brahma, devoting his mind at the feet of Siva, kept quiet. The gods also feeling pleased returned to their respective abodes.

Thereafter, Narada, at the instance of Siva, went to the abode of the Daityas and praised the beauty of Parvati.

Listening to his words, both the Daityas were influenced by delusion and overpowered with the lust, they thought of kidnapping the goddess.

They started thinking, that how could with the rise of their fortunes, they get the goddess and at which place?

Once lord Siva because of his divine sport, started roaming about, while Parvati started playing the ball with her handmaids, quite close to Siva.

She moved her limbs with ease up and down. She was caught by the black wasps because of the fragrance merging from her breath.

At times the black wasps made her eyes agitated. Suddenly the tresses of the flowers fell on the ground in front of her. Drops of sweating appeared over her cheeks. Drops of sweat dripping from the paintings on her cheeks brightened up.

The resplendence of her body spread all round, through the parting of her gown. By exerting herself too much in beating the ball, her red hand became redder than the red lotus.

When the ball bounced, her eyes too followed it making the brows to dance thereafter. As the goddess Parvati, the mother of the universe was so playing, she was spotted by the Daityas who were passing through the sky way, as if the death had taken them in its lap.

With the influence of the boon they had received from Brahma, both the demon named Vidala and Utpala, having been overpowered with pride had conquered the three lokas with the strength of their arms.

Having been overpowered with lust, they with the intention of abducting Parvati, making use of Sambari-Maya, descended from the sky.

Both of them were extremely wicked with unstable minds, taking to the form of messenger, descended on earth.

Lord Siva, observing from their unstable eyes, in a moment recognised them with contempt.

The lord shot a significant glance at Parvati, the destroyer of the miseries, devoting that they were the Daityas and not his ganas. They could assume any form.

O Dear one, Parvati, well understood the indication of Siva who had been great sportsman.

Understanding the indication with the winking of the eye by Siva, Parvati struck the ball at both of them killing them instantaneously.

Both the valorous and wicked Daityas, with the strike of the ball, whirled and whirled and fell down on the ground.

They fell down like the ripe fruits of palm tree or the two peaks of the Sumeru mountain with the strike of Vajra, falling down on the ground, with the blowing of the wind.

The ball, after killing the two Daityas indulging in the improper activity was turned into a linga.

The said linga which was lodged near Jyesthesvara came to be known as Kandukesvara, in due course of time.

Brahma, Visnu and Siva besides other gods arrived there at the same time, together with the sages.

Thereafter all the dwellers of KasI, delightfully receiving the boon from the same, went back to their respective abode.

Finding Siva accompanied with Parvati there, they folded their hands with devotion and offering salutation to them, eulogised them as well.
