O Vyasa, Siva, who had been well-versed in roaming about the well-disposed towards his devotees, kept on sporting there for sometime, delightfully and then he returned to his abode with Parvati and his ganas.

The linga lodged in KasI, is the destroyer of the wicked people and fulfills all the desires of the wicked people bestowing all the worldly pleasures and moksa ultimately.

Whosoever listens to this episode delightfully, recites it or himself reads it, he can have no fear from the misery.

He enjoying all the comforts in this world, attains the unique divine place after death which is rare to gods.

O Dear one, you have listened to the extremely astonishing episode of Siva and Parvati, which develops the feeling like the son towards the devotees and bestows welfare on the noble people.”

Brahma said, “In this way narrating the stories of Siva, enquiring from Vyasa and with his inspiration my son Sanatkumara, went to KasI, through the aerial way.

O Excellent sage, I have narrated the whole of Yuddha Khanda as part of Rudra Samhita, to you, which fulfills all the desires.

In this way the whole of Rudra Samhita has been narrated by me, which is extremely liked by Siva, which bestows all the pleasures as well as the salvation.

It removes the obstructions emanating from the enemies. Whosoever recites it daily, all his desires are fulfilled and he ultimately achieves salvation.”

Suta said, “In this way Narada, the son of Brahma and a devotee of Siva, listening from his father, the glory of Siva, besides his hundred names, became successful in his efforts.

In the form of the conversation between Brahma and Narada, I have narrated the entire story of Siva, the foremost of all the gods. Now what else do you want to listen from me?

Here ends the fifth Yuddha Khanda of second Rudra Samhita of Siva Mahapurana

## Satarudra-Samhita

## Chapter 1 - Saunaka describes the difference in Sadyojat Vamadeva, Tatpurusa, Adyoresa and Isan forms of Siva

I bow in reverence to lord Siva, who is blissful, performer of the endless sports, Mahesvara, all pervading, the Great, beloved of Gauri, the father of Kartikeya and Ganesa and the eternal lord.

Saunaka said, “O Disciple of Vyasa, O Great personality, ocean of the knowledge and mercy, you kindly define the incarnations of Siva, by which the noble people were bestowed with warfare.

Suta said, “O Sage, in earlier times the same question was asked by Sanatkumara from Nandi, the form of Siva, as well as the support of the noble people. He, devoting his mind at Siva, replied to him.”

Nandisvara said, “In the different kalpas, there had been innumerable incarnation of Siva. Still I shall speak about them according to my wisdom.

In the nineteenth kalpa of Svetalohita, Siva incarnated for the first time as Sadyojata.

In the said kalpa, Brahma, meditating upon the Supreme Brahman, produced a prince named Svetalohita.

Brahma, looking at that Purusa, taking him to be Isvara in the form of Brahman, offered his salutation to him with folded hands.

Knowing about Siva in Sadyojata form, Brahma was pleased and he started meditating upon the Supreme Purusa with devotion.

As he thus meditated, several sons, white in colour and well-known for their strength were born to him. All of them possessed great wisdom, having the form of the Supreme Brahman.

They were known as Sunandana, Nandana, Visvanandana and Upanandana, who were the disciples of the noble soul. The Brahman was surrounded by them.

The delightful great lord, known as Sadyojata incarnation of Siva, bestowed on Brahma, lovingly the perfect wisdom and the creative power.

During the next kalpa i.e. the twentieth one, which was named and glorified as Rakta (red) Brahma assumed the red splendour.

Brahma again meditated getting desirous of sons, as a result of which, a son appeared before him, clad in red costumes and garlands. His eyes and ornaments were red in colour.

Finding the son with a noble soul, he kept on meditating and being incarnation of Siva, he was given the name of Vamadeva. Brahma therefore bowed in reverence to him with folded hands.

Then he had four sons clad in red garments, who were know as Viraja, viveka, Visoka and Visvabharana.

During the twentieth Kalpa, Vamadeva Siva, getting pleased, bestowed the knowledge and the power for creation.

(In this way this was the second incarnation of Siva known as Vamadeva.) The twenty-first kalpa was known as the Pitavasakalpa during which Brahma was clad in the yellow garments.

During this kalpa when Brahma was meditating for a son, he attained a young son, who was enormously resplendent and had long arms.

When he carefully looked at him, he found him to be the incarnation of Siva. Therefore he started the muttering of Sivagayatri.

With the muttering of Sivagayatri, mantra, which was adorable by all, Siva was pleased with Brahma.

Thereafter, several of the divine Yogakumaras clad in bellow garments, and were the instigators of the path of yoga.

(This was the third incarnation of Tatpurusa). After the expiry of the Pitavarna- kalpa of Brahma, another kalpa named after Siva started.

During those times, there was water everywhere. Then after the expiry of a hundred years of Brahma, he felt painful about the creation of the universe and he started thinking.

Then he found before him, an illustrious, black complexioned, immensely powerful boy who was resplendent with his own lustre.

He was clad in black costumes, black turban, black yajnopavita, and black-agaru was pasted over his body.

Finding the noble soul of terrible exploits-known as Aghora, (non-terrible), he adored him. He was the lord of gods and had wonderful black and tawny colour.

Brahma then adored Aghora, in the form of Brahma. He worshipped the unperishing being, who was favourable disposed towards his devotees and spoke pleasing words.

Thereafter, four black complexioned princes, with their bodies having been plastered with agaru after the bath, appeared before him.

They had the resplendent form of Siva and were known by the name of Krsna, Krsnasikha, Krsnasya and Krsnakanthadhrk.

They were noble souls, who initiated the great and wonderful yoga called Ghora for the use of the creation by Brahma.

O Great sage, then another wonderful kalpa of Brahma known as Visvarupa came in Vogue.

(This is the fourth incarnation of Ghora). As Brahma desirous of sons, meditated on Siva, mentally, Sarasvati, (the goddess of speech) of great sound, manifested herself. She was Visvarupa- the universal form.

Then Isana- with much renowned features- the supreme lord of crystal like pure brilliance, and adorned with all the ornaments, appeared before Brahma.

Isan was the unborn lord, all pervading, all bestowing, all in all, having fine form and the formless one. Brahma therefore bowed in reverence to him.

Lord Tsana, after enlightening Brahma, about the noble path, created four auspicious sons together with his Energy.

Who were known as Jatin, Mundin, Sikhandin, and Ardhaminda. They all imparted the knowledge of great virtues and attained the goal of yogic practices.

Thus I have narrated elaborately the genesis of Sadyojata and others, O Sanatkumara, O Omniscient one, with the sole purpose of the welfare of the three worlds. Then they attained the eternal bliss.

(This is the fifth incarnation known as Isan). O Great intellectual, their benevolent conduct has been spread in all the three worlds.

In fact Isan Purusa is called Ghora, who is also known as Vamadeva, besides being Brahman and Mahesa. His images are well-known.

The first and the best form of Siva is Isana being the principal one. It directly occupies and presides over the individual soul and enjoys Prakrti.

Tatpurusa is the second form of Siva which occupies and presides over the object of enjoyment or the support of the attributes.

The third form known as Aghora has the limbs of Siva, having the form of dharma representing the buddhi-tattva of Siva.

The fourth form of Siva is Vamadeva which is the place of ahamkara (pride) and performs multifarious activities.

The fifth form of Siva, known as Tsana, is the permanent lord of the organ of hearing, speech and the all pervading sky.

The people with wisdom and intelligence conceive Tatpurusa as the lord of tvac (the organ of touch perception), hand, sense of touch and the element of wind.

The form of Aghora is conceived by the people of wisdom, as the support for the physical body, the sense of taste, colour and the fire.

The lord Vamadeva is conceived as the lord of the organ of taste, the excretion, of taste itself as well as the water.

The Sadyojata form of the lord is known as the sense of smell, of smell itself, of the earth and the generative organ.

The people desirous of welfare should bow in reverence before these forms of Siva, because they happen to be the sole cause of welfare.

Whosoever with devotion will recite the forms of Sadyojata and others, he would achieve salvation, enjoying all the pleasures.

## Chapter 2 - Eight forms of Siva- like Bhava, Sarva and others

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, O Dear one, you listen to the discussion about the excellent incarnations of Siva, who bestows comforts of all, and fulfills all the desires.

The entire world comprises of the eight forms of Siva. Pervading that the universe subsists like the pearls in the string.

The well-known eight presiding deities are Sarva, Bhava, Rudra, Ugra, Bhima, Pasupati, Isana and Mahadeva.

These eight deities preside over the earth, water, fire, wind, sky, the soul, the sun and the moon.

The essence of the entire lore is that the form of lord Siva, comprising of the earth, that holds the entire earth of mobile and immobile beings is known as Sarva.

The water that enlivens the universe is called Bhava.

O Master, the one who preserves the entire universe, pervading inside and out, and who makes the wind to blow, is known by the ugra form of Siva. This has been ordained by the noble people.

The all-pervading lord, who provides all the opportunities, having the gigantic form of Siva like the sky. It splits and differentiates the groups of elements.

The one who is the presiding deity of all the souls, who is the abode of all the souls, that form of Siva is known as Pasupati. He has been conceived as the one who shatters all the worldly bondages.

The one, who brightens the universe in the form of the sun, he is called the Isana form of Siva, which pervades in the sky.

The moon which pervades the earth with the nectar like rays, is known as Mahadeva form of Siva.

The eighth form of Siva- the Supreme soul represents Atman, which is more pervasive than the others. This form pervades the universe.

As with the watering of the roots of the trees, the branches sprout, similarly with the adoration of Siva, the universe as the body of Siva develops.

As the father feels happy when his sons and grandsons are comfortable, similarly, when the entire universe feels happy, Siva also feels delighted.

In case some damage or bondage is caused by anyone to some other person, then he surely does harm through Astamurti who is the presiding form of Siva, who should always be adored because Siva happens to be the primordial cause of all.

O Sanatkumara, I have described the eight forms of Siva, who is engaged in the welfare of all and are well-known in the world. The people desirous of their own welfare should always serve them.

## Chapter 3 - Appearing of Siva in Ardhanarisvara form, before Brahma, desirous of creation of the world by sexual exercise

Nandisvara said, “O Great intellectual one, O Dear one, you kindly describe the excellent Siva’s form of Ardhanarisvara which fulfilled the desires of Brahma.

When there had been little evolution of the people created by Brahma, he felt extremely painful.

Then there was a divine sound from the sky said, “Carry on the creation produced by the couples” (i.e. the male and the female). Then Brahma thought of the creation based on the sexual relations.

Earlier to that the race had not appeared out of the sexual intercourse with the females. Therefore Brahma could not create the world based on sexual relationship earlier.

Brahma thought that the creation cannot be progressed without the influence of Siva. Therefore he started performing tapas.

Then he meditated upon Siva united with the great Sakti called Siva in a combined way performing severe tapas.

Observing the severe austerities of Brahma, lord Siva was rapidly pleased with him within no time.

Then Isvara- the form of complete consciousness, entered into the Ardhanarisvara form, representing half male and half female and he appeared before Brahma.

Brahma, finding before himself lord Siva, combined with Sakti, offered his salutation to the lord with folded hands and eulogised him.

Then Mahesvara, the creator of the universe, getting pleased with the work of creation, spoke in the thundering voice like the clouds.

Siva said, “O Son of great fortune, O Grand-father, I have well understood all what you have in your mind.

You have performed this tapas for the sole purpose of the increase in the creation. I am pleased with your tapas and I bestow upon you the desired boon.”

Thus Siva extremely large hearted, and sweet tempered one, separated his body from that of Siva.

Looking at the Supreme Sakti, having been separated from the body of Siva, Brahma offered his salutation to her and then eulogised her.

Brahma said, “O Siva, your husband Siva, initially produced me. Thereafter the same Siva, the supreme soul, created the rest of the universe.

O Siva, I mentally created the universe again and again, which could not progress.

Thereafter, I intend to increase the universe by means of the sexual intercourse, because they are all my subjects.

Earlier, you could not create the imperishable race of the females. Therefore the race of the females is an excellent one.

All the Saktis emerge from you. Therefore, O Akhilesvari- the form of the Supreme Sakti, I offer prayer to you.

O Siva, bestow on me the strength for the creation of the race of females. Salutation to you. O Beloved of Siva, O Mother, Siva is the cause of all the mobile and immobile world.

O Isvari, the bestower of the boon, I seek for a boon from you which you kindly give me, O Mother of the universe. Salutation to you.

O Mother, for the increase of the mobiles and immobiles in the world, you be the daughter of my son Daksa Prajapati.”

In this way, Brahma, prayed to Paramesvari, His prayer was granted by the goddess and she bestowed the desired Sakti to Brahma.

Then Siva of the universal form, produced a powerful Sakti out of her eyebrows.

Looking at that Sakti, lord Siva, the ocean of mercy, the best among Devas, skilled in divine sport, smilingly said to Parvati.

Siva said, “Brahma has adored you performing the tapas. Therefore getting pleased, you better fulfil his desires.”

The goddess Paramesvari, accepting his command, according to the words of Brahma, she became the daughter of Daksa Prajapati.

O Sage, then Siva, giving the unique Sakti to Brahma, entered the body of Siva, who disappeared from the scene.

From that day onwards the share of the woman, started to be given separately. Brahma then felt delighted and the creation based on sexual union started

O Dear one, in this way I have describes the Ardhanarisvara form of Siva, which bestows welfare on the noble people.

Whosoever recites or reads this episode, he after enjoying all the comforts in the world, ultimately achieves the highest position.

## Chapter 4 - Incarnation of Siva as Svetamuni or Rsabhadeva

Nandisvara said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, the story of Siva as narrated by Rudra would always benefit Brahma.

Siva said, “During the seventh Manvantara, in Varahakalpa, the lord Kalpesvara would bestow the knowledge to all.

When the great grandson would be born to Vaivasvata Manu, O Brahma, then there would be four yugas in the said Manvantara.

O Vidhi, O Brahma, for the benefit of the Brahmanas as well as the lokas, at the end of Dvapara-yuga I shall incarnate.

O Brahma, then with the processing of the yuga, on the arrival of the first yuga in Dvapara, then Vyasa himself would become the lord.

During the period, for the benefit of the Brahmanas, at the end of Kaliyuga, I shall appear as Sveta-muni together with Siva on earth.

O Brahma, four of the best of my disciples would be born over the peak named Chagala over the pleasant mountain Himalaya.

They would be known as Sveta, Svetasikha, Svetasva, and Svetalohita. All the four of them on the basis of the dhyana-yoga would achieve my loka.

Then, they understanding me as imperishable, would become my devotees and meditating in the Supreme Brahman, they would be free from the birth, death and old age.

O Brahma, the humans can never have an audience with me without meditating upon me. O Son, the giving of charities, practising of dharma are the only means to achieve the same.

During the second Dvapara-yuga, when the patriarch Satya becomes Vyasa, I shall be born as Sutara and continue to live in Kali age.

There too my disciples will be the four Brahmanas well-versed in Vedic lore. They would be known by the names of Dundubhi, Satarupa, Hrsika and Ketuman.

With the practicing of the dhyanayoga, all of them would achieve my loka. Thereafter, they well realising the truth about me would be liberated.

During the third Dvapara when Bhargava would become Vyasa, then I shall be known by the name of Damana.

Then also I shall have four sons viz.: Visoka Visesa, Vipapa and Papanasana.

O four-faced Brahma, I shall help Vyasa and will propagate firmly the path of renunciation in the Kali age.

During the fourth Dvapara, Angira would become Vyasa and I would be known by the name of Suhotra.

During that period also I shall have four sons who would be the great yogis. O Brahma, I shall tell you their names also.

They would be known by the names of Sumukha, Durmukha, Durdarbha and Duratikrama. O Brahma, even then, I shall help Vyasa with my disciples.

During the fifth Dvapara, there would be Vyasa known as Savit. During that period I would be born as a great yogi and would be known by the name of Kanka.

During that period also, I shall have four disciples who would follow the path of yoga. You listen about their names from me.

They would be known as Sanaka, Sanatana, Sanandana and Sanatkumara, who shall have the spotless mind and will be devoid of pride. These would be my four sons.

O Brahma, during that yuga, I with the name of Kanka, popularise the nirvrtti-marga and shall help Vyasa known by the name of Savitr.

On the arrival of the sixth Dvapara yuga, then Vyasa would be known by the name of Mrtyu who would be classify the Vedas.

Then I, the supporter of the nirvrtti-marga shall help Vyasa, and shall known by Lokaksi.

During that period also, I shall have four sons, who would be quite firm in their resolve. They would be known by the name of Sudharma, Viraja, Sanjaya and Vijaya.

With the start of the seventh Dvapara Indra would become Vyasa. O Brahma, during that period, I would be known by the name of Jaigisavya.

Then I, becoming a great yogi, shall meditate in a cave in Kasi, seated over a Kusa seat and concentrate firmly over the Yogic practices.

O Brahma, during that period I shall help Vyasa, known by the name of Satakratu, besides redeeming the devotees from the fear of the universe.

I shall even then have four sons, known by the names of Sarasvata, Yogisa, Meghavaha, and Suvahana.

During the period of the eighth Dvapara, the sage Vasistha would officiate as Vyasa and divide the Vedas.

During that period I shall incarnate as Dadhivahana and shall help Vyasa.

During that period as well, I as a yogi shall have four sons known by the names, Kapila, Asuri, Pancasikha, and Salvala.

O Brahma, on the arrival of the ninth Dvapara, then the sage of Sarasvata, would become Vyasa.

While the said Vyasa would be engaged in meditation, for the development of the nirvrtti-marga, I shall appear in the form of Rsabha.

During that period, I shall have four great Yogins as my disciples, viz.: Parasara, Garga, Bhargava and Girisa.

O Sage, with them, I shall firmly establish the path of yoga, helping Veda-Vyasa at the same time.

O Brahma, in that form, I shall be extremely merciful and redeem you as well as the people who would be caught up in the worldly bondages.

O Brahma, such is my incarnation named Rsabha. It causes yogic practices and fulfills the desire of Vyasa, in the guise of Sarasvata and it comprises of several of the divine sports.

There had been a prince known by the name of Bhadrayu, who had been discarded by his father and he died of the poison infection. He was brought back to life by me during that incarnation.

When that prince reached the age of sixteen years, I as Rsabha went to his place all of a sudden.

O Brahma, being duly worshipped by him, that sage of good form, instructed him in virtues in connection with the running of his kingdom.

Becoming immensely delighted, he gave him a divine conch and a lustrous sword which could destroy his enemies.

Then the merciful sage, who had been compassionate over the down-trodden, applying the ashes over his body, infused in his body the strength of twelve thousand elephants.

Thus assuring Bhadrayu variously with his mother, Rsabhadeva, who had been adored by the king, he left the place to move at will.

O Brahma, thus the Royal sage, subjugating all the enemies, married Kirtimalini and started ruling the country with a religious mind.

This was the performance of Rsabha incarnation of Siva. He bestowed protection to the noble people, the kin of the people in misery and this had been the ninth incarnation of Siva, about whom I have spoken to you.

The story of Rsabhadeva is quite auspicious, which bestows heaven, glory and long life. It should be listened with great attention.

## Chapter 5 - Incarnations of Siva during the tenth to twenty eight Dvaparas

Siva said, “During the tenth Dvapara yuga, over the Bhrgutunga peak of the Himalaya mountain, there would be a Vyasa named Tridhama.

I shall have my sons named Bhrgu, Balabandhu, Naramitra, Ketusrnga, Tapodhana and others, who would be well-versed in the Vedic lore.

In the eleventh Dvapara, Trivrta-muni, would be the Vyasa and I shall appear as Kali at Gangadvara.

During that period also I shall have four religious minded sons, known as Lambodara, Lambaksa, Kesalambha as well as Pralambaka.

During the twelfth Dvapara, the sage Satateja who would be able to well define the Vedas who would be Vyasa. Then I shall be born at the end and of Dvapara and at the end of Kali-age.

In order to help the sage Atri adorned with the golden kavaca, functioning as Vyasa, I shall propagate the nirvrtti-marga in order to help him.

O Great sage, during that period I shall have the sons named Sarvajna, Samaboddhi, Sadhya, Sarva.

During the thirteen Dvapara yuga, Narayana shall be Vyasa and I shall be named as Bali- the great sage, near Darmaranya.

Then in Balakhilya’s asrama, over the Gandhamadana mountain, I shall have excellent four sons viz., Sudama, Kasyapa, Vasistha, Virajas.

During the fourteenth kalpa when Raksa would function as Vyasa, then I shall be born in the Angiras race, in the form of Gautama.

Then at the start of the age of Kali, I shall have four sons known as Atri, Davasada, Sravana, Sraviskata.

When during the fifteenth Dvapara, Trayyaruni would become Vyasa, then I shall appear in the name of Vedasira. Then I shall produce a great weapon named Vedasira, which would be quite powerful one, and would be lodged over the bank of the river Sarasvati, emerging from northern range of the Himalaya mountain.

During that period too I shall have four powerful sons, known by the names of Kuni, Kunibahu, Kusarira and Kunetra.

During the sixteenth Dvapara, the sage Deva would function as Vyasa. In order to cooperate with him I would be born in the name of Gokarna.

There is an auspicious forest named Gokarna. There I shall have four sons who would be known by the names of Kasyapa, Usana, Cyavana and Brhaspati. They by performing tapas would achieve my abode.

During the seventeenth Dvapara, Devakrtanjaya would officiate as Vyasa. Then I, would appear over the excellent peak of Himalaya as Grhasvami.

The said snow clad mountain has a considerable height and is known as Sivaksetra. I shall also have four sons there known as Utathya, Vamadeva, Mahayoga and Mahabala.

When during eighteenth Dvapara, Rtanjaya would officiate as Vyasa, then I would appear as Sikhandi over the snow clad mountain peak.

In the great and auspicious Siddha-ksetra, there is a mountain named Sikhandi. In the forest of the similar name, there live the Siddhas.

There I would have four ascetic sons viz.: Vajasrava, Rucika, Syavasya and Yatisvara.

During the nineteenth Dvapara, the sage Bhardvaja would function as Vyasa, when I would appear as Jatimali. Then I shall have four sons over the peak of the Himalaya known as Hiranya, Kausalya, Lokaksi and Praghimi.

During the twentieth Dvapara, Gautama would become Vyasa, while I would be known as Attahasa. During that period the people would like to laugh.

There is hill named Attahasa over the Attahasa mountain, which serves as the dwelling place for the gods, humans, Yaksaraja, Siddhas besides the caranas.

There also I would have four sons viz., Sumanta, Varvari, Kabandha and Kusikandhara.

During the twenty first Dvapara, Vacaksrava would be Vyasa, then I shall appear in the Darukavana as Daruka.

There also I shall have four sons named Plaksa, Darbhayini, Ketuman, and Gautama.

During the twenty second Dvapara, when Susmayana would officiate as Vyasa, then I would become a great sage in Varanasi.

I shall be known by the name of Languli Bhima. Indra and all other gods, during the start of kali-age, in the world find me in the form of Halayudha.

During that period also I shall have four sons viz. Bhallava, Madhu, Pinga, and Svetaketu, who would be quite religious ones.

During the twenty-third Dvapara the sage Trnabindu would officiate as Vyasa. Then I shall appear over the mountain Kalanjara as Sveta.

There also I would have four sons, named Usika, Brhadsva, Devala and Kavi.

During the twenty fourth Dvapara when Yaksa would officiate as Vyasa, then I, in the Naimasarnya ksetra, shall appear as a yogi named Suli.

There also I shall have the great ascetics as my disciples and would be known by the name of Salihotra, Agnivesa, Yuvanasva and Saradavasu.

During the twenty fifth Dvapara, Sakti would officiate as Vyasa. Then I would appear as a great ascetic named Dandi.

There would be four great ascetics as my disciples as would be known by the names of Chagala, Kundakarna, Kumbhanda and Pravahaka.

During the twenty sixth Dvapara, Parasara- the great yogi would be officiating as Vyasa, while I would appear in Bhadravatapura, by the name of Sahisnu.

There I shall have four ascetic disciples, viz.: Uluka, Vidyuta, Sambuka and Asvalayana.

During the twenty seventh Dvapara, during the period of Jatukarna Vyasa, then I shall appear in the Prabhasa region, as Somasarma.

I shall have four ascetic disciples there known by the names of Aksapada, Kumara, Uluka and Vatsa.

During the twenty eighth Dvapara I shall appear in the form of Dvaipayana Vyasa- the son of the sage Parasara.

Then out of the sixth amsa Krsna- the best of humans and the son of Vasudeva, would become Vasudeva.

At the same time, I shall also appear with the influence of yogamaya which surprises the universe, in the form of a Brahmacari named Yogatma.

For the benefit of the Brahmanas, discarding this body in the cremation ground like dead one, I with the power of yogamaya, accompanied without, enter the divine and auspicious cave of the Sumeru mountain together with Visnu. At that point of time I would be known by the name of Lakuli.

Then I shall bodily incarnate in the auspicious Siddha-ksetra, and would remain popular till the earth lasts.

At that point of time also, I shall have the ascetic disciples, who would be known by the names of Kusika, Garga, Mitra and Taurusya.

All those yogis, would be well-versed in the Vedas, and Brahmacaris. All of them achieving Mahesvara yoga, would proceed on to the place of Sivapura.

In the Vaivasvata Manantara in each one of the Dvaparas, several incarnation of Siva occurred which have been described here.

O Excellent one, these are the twenty-eight incarnations of Vyasa which are relevant to each one of the Dvapara yugas. Besides these, the incarnation of Yogesvara has been defined at the beginning of each Kaliyuga.

During the incarnation of each one of Yogesvara, four sons or disciples are conceived, who develop the path of yoga, great disciples of Siva and are stated to be eternal.

These disciples of Siva plaster the ashes over their bodies, wear the rosary of Rudraksa and paint tripundra over the forehead.

All these disciples were always engaged in religious activities, were well-versed in the Vedic and post-Vedic literature, always mentally and bodily devoted to Siva.

All of them were devoted towards me, engaged in meditation towards me and had controlled all the senses. The people with wisdom have described their number as a hundred and twelve during the twenty eight Dvaparas.

Thus I have described the details of the incarnations of twenty eight Yugas starting from Manu to Lord Krsna.

When Krsna- Dvaipayana incarnates during this kalpa, he would discuss about the Vedas and the Vedanta-sastras.

Then lord Siva, showering his grace over Brahma and thus speaking to him, casting a compassionate glance on him, disappeared from the scene.

The description of forty two incarnations of Siva, ends here.

## Chapter 6 - Performing of tapas by sage Silada for getting a son, achieving of Nandi, who proceeded for performing tapas

Now the other incarnations of Nandisvara are described. Sanatkumara said, “How were you born of the amsa of Mahadeva and how could you achieve access to Siva. I would like to hear about the same in detail.

Nandisvara said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, listen to me quite carefully. O Sage, the way I was born of Siva and achieved the Sivatattva, you listen from me.

When the sage Silada became desirous of having a son, then his manes spoke to him with the intention of his redemption. For that the powerful and quite religious Silada, performed a penance with his drooping eyes and went to Sivaloka as an ascetic.

Then making Indra as a target, the sage Silada, with a firm resolve, performed hard tapas for a long time.

Indra was delighted at his penance. He, the lord of gods went to him, in order to grant him the boon.

The delightful Indra said to him, “O Sinless and excellent sage, I feel pleased with you. You better ask for a boon.”

The excellent sage Silada, then offered his salutation with folded hands and eulogising him with holy hymns.

Silada said, “O Indra the lord of gods, in case you are pleased with me, then give me a son, born without the human contact.”

O Great sage, are ayonija son not born of womb and devoid of death cannot be given even by Brahma, Visnu or any other god.

Even those two born of Siva, the destroyer of Tripura, die. The extent of the longevity of their age has been separately mentioned in the sacred texts.

Therefore, O Great Brahmana, shed away your desire of a deathless son, who is not born of human contact and accept a son suited to your mortal form.

But in case Siva, the lord of gods is pleased even an immortal son not born of a human touch, though difficult to get, could be obtained.

Neither I nor lord Visnu, nor Brahma, O Great sage, can make you achieve an immortal son not born of the human touch.

You should therefore worship Siva for the fulfilment of your desire for achieving a son. Siva is the greatest of the gods and is all powerful. The son desired by you could be achieved through him alone.”

Nandisvara said, “After thus speaking to the great Brahmana Silada, and showering his blessing on him, the compassionate lord of the gods, returned to his abode surrounded by the gods.

After Indra, the thousand eyed lord had left the place, Silada meditated upon Siva and pleased him with his tapas.

While the Brahmana was so engaged in the tapas throughout the day and night, a thousand divine years passed like a moment.

His body was surrounded by the anthill, thousands of worms, with pointed beaks, as hard as the thorns. Other types of blood sucking insects also gathered around him. In this cavity with the flesh and blood having been dried up. He was practically reduced to a skeleton. Thus the excellent sage Silada was reduced to such a (miserable) condition.

Then the delighted lord Siva appeared before Silada which could not be seen by the people with wicked wisdom.

Silada who had performed tapas for a thousand divine years, Siva appeared before him and desired him to ask for a boon.

Silada, who had been engaged in great meditation and had concentrated his mind in tapas with utmost devotion, did not hear the words of the lord, who is subservient to his devotees.

When Siva, the killer of Tripura, touched the sage with his hand, the tapas of the latter was disturbed.

O Sage, then the sage Silada, opened his eyes, and he (to his utter surprise), found Siva and Parvati both standing before him. Then he offered his salutation to both of them at their feet.

Overwhelmed with the delight, in choked voice, lowering his shoulders, and his hands folded, filled with joy, he eulogised Siva.

Feeling pleased the three eyed Siva said to Silada, the excellent sage, “I have arrived here to bestow a boon on you.

O Great intellect, what have you to do with this tapas? I give you a son who would be well-versed in scriptures besides being omniscient.”

Then Silada listening to the words of Siva, offering his salutation to him spoke to Candrasekhara Siva.

The sage Silada said, “O Lord Siva, in case you are really pleased with me, or you intend to bestow a boon on me, then give me a son not born of human contact and free from death.”

Nandisvara said, “When he thus spoke to Nandisvara Siva, then the lord feeling pleased said to Silada.

Siva said, “O Ascetic Brahmana, in earlier times Brahma, the gods and the sages had adored me to incarnate on earth.

I shall therefore appear in your house as ayonija son known by the name of Nandi. In that case you would become the father of the father of the three worlds.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, looking at the sage, Siva, together with Parvati disappeared from the scene.

After the disappearing of Siva, the excellent sage Silada, went back to his abode and spoke to the ascetics.

After a short while, my father, the foremost of Brahmanas, who were well aware of the sacrificial rites, commanded for the construction of an altar for the performing of a yajna.

But before the start of the sacrifice, I was born as the son of Siva at his instance, with the resplendence as brilliant as the fire of the time of dissolution.

Then the rain was showered by the clouds like Puskaravarta and others. At my birth as the son of Silada, the Kinnaras, Siddhas, Sadhyas and other beings, travelled through the sky and showered flowers all round.

Then Brahma and other gods together with their spouses, Visnu, Siva and Parvati, lovingly arrived there.

The occasion was celebrated and the asparas started dancing. All of them joyfully adored linga.

All the god who had arrived there praised Silada immensely and eulogising Siva and Parvati, returned to their respective places. Siva and Parvati also returned to their abode.

Silada also found me like Surya of the time of the dissolution having three eyes, in the form of a boy with the crown of the matted locks of hair over the head.

Silada was highly delighted. I was in the form of Rudra in every respect holding the trident and other attributes; lovingly he bowed before me.

Silada said, “O Lord of gods, since I have been pleased by you, you will be known by name of Nandi, the lord of the universe.

Nandisvara said, “My delighted father, after, offering his salutation to Mahesvara, returned to his leaf hut in the same way as a pauper returns after receiving riches.

O Excellent sage, when I reached the cottage of Silada, then I took to the human form, discarding the earlier one.

My father, who had been respected by the world at large, finding me in human form, then he, who had been surrounded by the people, started lamenting.

Silada, the son of Salankayana, who loved his son the most, performed all the birth rites for me.

During the fifth year, my father, taught me all the Vedas and other related literature.

After the completion of the seventh year, at the command of Siva, two ascetics named Mitra and Varuna arrived to our hermitage at the instance of the lord, in order to see me.

The sage Silada honoured them both. They were seated comfortably and looking at me they said again and again.

Mitravaruna said, “O Excellent one, this Nandi is well-versed in all the scriptures. We have not come across anyone like him. Only one more year of his life has been left.

Silada, who was extremely attached to his son, listening to the words of the Brahmanas, started crying, embracing his son.

Finding my father as dead and fallen, devoting my mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, I spoke delightedly.

“O Dear one, for what reason, are you crying while shaking? What ails you? I would like to know the correct reason for the same.

The father said, “O Son, your short life only is the cause of my pain. Who will remove my misery? With whom shall I take refuge?”

The son said, “Even if the gods, Danavas, Yama, Kala or anyone else, intend to kill me, even then I cannot have a short life. Therefore, don’t be grieved. I am speaking this swearing on you.”

The father said, “What is your tapas, knowledge, and yoga? Who is your lord? Whereby O Son, you propose to ward off my terrible misery?”

The son said, “O Father, I shall cheat death by means of my tapas and not learning. I shall conquer death by means of my tapas and not learning. I shall conquer death by worshipping the lord and not otherwise.”

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, after saying this, I bowed at feet of my father and circumambulating him, I went to the excellent forest.”

## Chapter 7 - Bestowing of the position of a gana by Siva to Nandi

Nandisvara said, “Reaching a secluded place, I performed such a severe tapas which was beyond the reach of great ascetics even.

I adored the three eyed Siva having ten arms, five heads engaged in the peaceful tapas.

In the auspicious northern region of the river I took to samadhi with a concentrated mind.

Siva and Parvati became pleased founding me engaged in the tapas (penance) and both of them bedecked with the crescent moon, said.”

Siva said, “O Son of Silada, I am pleased with your tapas and would like to bestow a boon on you. You have performed an excellent tapas. On Intelligent one, you ask for anything you have in your mind.”

At these words of Siva, I placed my head at his feet. Then I prayed him to relieve me of the grief and old age.

Thereafter, Siva, lifted me up with his own hands since I had been overpowered by devotion, with tears flown from my eyes.

Getting up he held me with his own hands, touching me at the same time, because he is always engaged in the removal of the miseries of others.

The lord of the universe, looking at Parvati and other ganas and casting his compassionate glance on me, said.

“O Son, Nandi you possess enormous wisdom, therefore you should be the least afraid of the death. In fact, I had sent the two Brahmanas to you. You are undoubtedly like me.

You, together with your father and the friends are eternal, free from old age, free from sufferings, imperishable, and are Ganapati, getting all your desires fulfilled.

You are my strength and shall always remain with me besides being dear to me. Because of my grace, you would never have to face the old age. You would neither face death, nor would you be reborn.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, the compassionate Siva, taking out the garland of skulls, resembling the lotus flowers, placed it around my neck.

With placing of the auspicious garland of skulls around my neck, I attained three eyes and ten arms, resembling Siva.

Then the Paramesvara Siva, holding me with his hands said, “What an excellent boon should I bestow on you today?”

Then Siva, took out the spotless water from the locks of his hair and sprinkling over me declared, “Let you become Nandi.”

Five spotless streams known as Jatodaka, Trisrota, Vrsabhadhvani, Svaranodaka and Jambu started flowing with clean and forceful water.

O Sage, all these rivers still exists at this basin called Pancananda which is very auspicious spot of Siva, in the Japesvara region.

Those who take bath in the five rivers- Pancanadas, and adore him reciting his name, they certainly achieve the Sivasayujya type of salvation.”

Thereafter Siva said to Parvati, “O Parvati, after performing abhiseka of Nandi, I intend to establish him as the chief of my ganas. What have you to say about this?”

Uma said, “O Lord of gods, O Supreme lord, you give over Nandi, the son of Silada to me. He will be my loving son.”

Nandisvara said, “Then the independent, the Supreme Isana, viewer of all, well- disposed towards all, remembered all the best of the leaders of his ganas.

With the mere remembering of Siva innumerable Ganesvaras of Siva having the appearances resembling the lord, arrived there.

All the Ganesvaras, offered their salutation to both Siva and Parvati with folded hands, lowering their heads, and then spoke the auspicious words.

Ganesvaras said, “O Deva, the great lord, destroyer of Tripura, and Kamadeva, what for have you remembered us? We have arrived here.

Should we dry up the oceans? Or should we kill Yama with his attendants? Or should we kill the old Brahma, besides the death?

Should we bring Indra and Visnu in bondage? Or shall we bring the ferocious Daityas and Danavas?

On whom should we inflict severe punishment at your command? O Lord, for whose success should we celebrate?”

Nandisvara said, “Then Siva started praising his valorous ganas, listening to their courageous words.”

Siva said, “This Nandisvara is my dearest son, therefore, at my command all of you should accept him as the chief of the Ganesvaras.

All of you should lovingly perform the abhiseka of Nandisvara, the chief of all the ganas. He would be the lord of all of you.”

Nandisvara said, “All the leaders of the ganas accepted the words spoken by lord Siva and collected the material for performing of the abhiseka.

Then the gods like Brahma, Visnu, Indra, Lokapalas, besides the ascetics arrived there delightfully.

At the command of Siva, Brahma, performed abhiseka of Nandi quite carefully and appropriately.

Then the gods like Brahma, Visnu, Indra alongwith Lokapalas and the ascetics eulogised delightfully.

After completion of the prayer by all the gods, Visnu, the lord of the three worlds then himself offered prayer to Siva.

Then the gods, like Visnu and others, the Ganesvaras and the Daityas, shouted the slogans of victory.

O Excellent Brahmanas, at the command of Siva, my abhiseka was thus performed by Brahma and others since then I am known as Nandisvara.

Then at the command of Siva, there Visnu, Brahma and other gods married me with enormous festivities.

Suyasa the divine daughter of Marut, who delighted the mind and the heart became my spouse.

Suyasa received a chatra which was clean like the moon over which the damsels moved the flywhisks.

I occupied the lion thrown with her. Mahalaksmi, adorned me with all the ornaments besides the crown.

The goddess then gave me the divine garland of gems, which had been worn by her around her neck, besides that I was also given a white bull, a lion, a flag, chariot, and a divine garland, resembling the moon. O Sage several other articles were also given to me.

Thus soon after the marriage, I bowed in reverence with my spouse to Siva, Parvati, Brahma and Visnu.

Then lord Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees said to me and my spouse.

Isvara said, “O Son, you listen, now Suyasa is your wife. I shall therefore delightfully bestow the boon, whatever is there in your mind.

O Ganesvara, O Nandisa, I am always pleased with you. You listen to my graceful words with your wife.

You will always be my favourite and will be endowed with all the prosperity. You will be a grand yogi and a fine archer along with your father and grandfather, who would never be defeated by anyone. You will be always victorious and worthy of adoration. You would possess enormous prowess. You shall be there wherever I shall be and I shall be there wherever you shall be.

On Son, your father will be endowed with all the prosperity. He will be the presiding officer of the ganas, quite powerful and a great devotee of mine.

O Dear son, your grandfather also will be like the same. This is the rule with me that whosoever approaches me, is surely endowed with a boon.”

Nandisvara said, “Then the great goddess spoke with the intention of bestowing a boon on Nandi, “O Son, you better ask for a boon you desire to have.”

Listening to the words of the goddess, Nandisvara spoke with folded hands, “Let my mind always remain devoted at your feet.”

Listening to my words, the goddess said, “Be it so”. Then the goddess addressed Suyasa, the wife of Nandi.

The goddess said, “O Daughter, you better receive your desired boon. You will have three eyes and shall be free from the bondages of birth and death. You will always remain devoted to me besides your husband with your sons and grand sons.”

Nandisvara said, “Then at the command of Siva, Brahma, Visnu and other gods, getting pleased, also bestowed boons on us.

Then Siva, accompanied with me and the goddess, besides all the relatives, mounted over the bull and proceeded to his abode.

All the gods like Visnu and others eulogising both of them left for their respective abodes.

O Son, O Great sage, I have thus narrated the stories of my incarnations to you, which bestow delight to the people always, besides increasing devotion in Siva.

A person who listens to the story of the birth, abhiseka, his marriage and my bestowing of the boons on him, or listens to it with devotion or recites it, he enjoying all the pleasures in this world, ultimately he achieves the salvation.

## Chapter 8 - Incarnation of Bhairava

Now the incarnation of Bhairava is being described, Nandisvara said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, now you listen to the story of Bhairava, by listening to which the devotion in Siva is firmly established,

Bhairava happens to be the complete form of Siva. The people overpowered with the illusion of Siva, remain ignorant about the same.

O Sanatkumara, in fact the four faced. Brahma and the four-armed Visnu also remain ignorant about the illusion of Siva.

There is no surprise in the same because all the people cannot be aware of the illusion of Siva and overpowered with the same, they do not adore the lord.

In case the same Paramesvara, bestows on anyone the knowledge about himself, only then someone can know about him. No one can know him of his own accord.

The foolish people devoid of wisdom, are unable to visualise the all pervading Siva. He is known as a mere lord, who is beyond the reach of the mind and words.

O Excellent sage, I am going to narrate an ancient historical episode. O Dear one, you listen to that ancient story with utmost faith.”

“Once the gods and the sages went to Siva and Brahma who had been seated over the peak of the pleasant Sumeru mount in order to learn about the supreme tattva.

Reaching there, offering their salutation to Brahma, lowering their shoulders and the hands folded, they respectfully prayed to the lord.

The gods and the sages said, “O God of gods, lord of the subjects, creator of the universe, leader of the people, tell us correctly about the undecaying supreme tattva.”

Nandisvara said, “Brahma had been overpowered with the delusion of Siva and forgetting about the supreme tattva started talking about the common matters.

Brahma said, “O Gods and the sages, you listen to me with respect and noble wisdom. I would like to discuss about the reality of the imperishable tattva.

I happen to be the cause of the creation of the universe. I am the creator, the self born, the unborn, the lord, the primordial being, the Brahman, and the sole unsullied soul.

O Excellent gods, I happen to be the instigator of the worlds, and the deterrent as well. There is no one greater than I, or anyone else who could cause the revolution.”

Nandisvara said, “While the creator was thus speaking, Visnu, who had been present there got irritated, since he also was overpowered by Maya. Getting enraged, he spoke these words.

O Brahma, this is not proper. It is a sheer foolishment on the part of a person practicing the yoga. Unaware of the reality, you are uselessly speaking like this.

I am the creator of the worlds, the great soul, the greatest Purusa, the sacrifice, lord Narayana, the master of Ṅṁóa and the greatest goal.

O Brahma, the creation is carried out by you at my command. By disregarding me, the life of no one can be saved on earth.”

In this way having been overpowered with the illusion of Siva, there started a controversy between Brahma and Visnu, who being desirous of their respective victory, quoted the Vedas as well as the Sastras in support of their individual arguments.

They further argued that all the four Vedas should be consulted, who are present in human form.

Brahma and Visnu said, “Vedas have always been treated as authentic. Therefore you speak out the truth about the matter. What is the sole unchanging entity?”

Nandisvara said, “Thus listening to the words of both of them, Rgveda and others spoke, devoting their mind towards Siva.”

O Gods, in case we are honoured, O Deities as the causes of creation and maintenance, we shall spell out the authorities which will remove your doubts.”

Nandisvara said, “On hearing the conditions mentioned by the Vedas, the two deities told the Vedas, “Whatever is mentioned by you, shall be acceptable to us as an authority. What is that entity? Please enlighten us about the same.”

Rgveda said, “The one is whom all the bhutas have been absorbed, and from which everything comes out, who is called the greatest entity, is called Rudra alone.”

Yajurveda said, “The lord who is adored by all the yajnas, besides the yogic practices, and the one who testified, he happens to be Siva, the viewer of all.”

Samaveda said, “By whose Maya all the beings wander in the world, who happens to be the matter of search for the ascetics, whose resplendence illuminates the entire universe, he happens to be the supreme tattva known as Trayambaka.”

Atharvaveda said, “Mahadeva with whom the devotees have an audience with utmost devotion, he happens to be the supreme tattva, who is beyond the miseries.”

Nandisvara said, “Listening to these words of the Vedas, both Brahma and Visnu overpowered with the Maya of Siva, smilingly spoke to the Vedas.

Brahma and Visnu said, “O Vedas, what is all this being talked by you in unconsciousness? What has happened to you today? You appear to have lost your wisdom. Is it so?”

This Siva, the lord of the Pramatha remains with his body smeared with ashes. He is of white complexion, remains naked and enjoys the company of Siva throughout the day and night. Then how could he be the supreme tattva?

He remains in ugly form, wears the matted locks of hair over the head, rides a bull, has the snakes as ornaments, and is devoid of company. How could, therefore, Siva be a Supreme Brahman?”

Listening to the words of both of them, the all pervading, formless as well as with form Omkara spoke.

Omkarṁ said, “Lord Rudra, does not enjoy the company of others except his own spouse playfully.

The same Paramesvara Siva, is eternal, and self-luminous. Siva is his Sakti, in the form of the Bliss and is not a chance occurrence.”

Nandisvara said, “Even after this argument, both Brahma and Visnu could not be freed from the ignorance. It was caused by the Maya of Siva alone.

Then the great flame infested itself before them. It filled the space between the heaven and earth with its splendour.

O Sage, then Brahma and Visnu found a human image, with an astonishing form in that splendour.

Then the fifth head of Brahma started burning in anger, unable to understand the identity of the third person among them, taking to the human form.

while Brahma was thus thinking, then the great personality appeared in a moment with three eyes- Nilalohita with a trident in his hand, the serpents and the crescent moon served as his ornaments. Then Brahma , under the influence of Maya laughingly spoke.

Brahma said, “O Nilalohita, I know you Don’t be afraid, O Moon crested one, You are Rudra, who emerged in earlier times out of my forehead. Because of your cries, the name Rudra was given to you by me. O Son, you seek refuge in me alone. I shall protect you.”

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, listening to the naughty words of Brahma - born of louts, Siva felt irritated as if he was about to cause destruction.

Getting enraged he created Bhairava, illumining with great lustre. Siva then spoke to him lovingly.

Siva said, “O Kalabhairava, initially, you punish this Brahma. You would possess the lustre of the god of death and shall be known as Kalaraja.

You are known as Bhairava because you possess horrible features and are capable of supporting the earth. Because even Kala is afraid of you, therefore, you are known as Bhairava. Even Kala will be afraid of you. Therefore you would be known as Kalabhairava.

Getting enraged, you will destroy the wicked people. Therefore you will be popularly known as Amardaka.

Since you will atonce consume the sins of the devotees, therefore you would also be known as Papabhaksana.

Of all my places, Kasi happens to be the best of the city, therefore O Kalaraja, you would always be the lord of the same.

All the sinful people there, would be ruled by you. Citragupta would maintain the account of all their good and bad deeds.”

Nandisvara said, “Accepting these boons, Kalabhairava, atonce, severed the fifth head of Brahma, with the nail of his left finger.

The limb which commits a crime, is punished. Therefore, the fifth head of Brahma, which denounced Siva, was cut off.

Thereafter Visnu finding the severed head of Brahma, got panicky and then started adoring Siva, reciting the Sataurdriya mantras.

Brahma too, getting afraid, also started reciting the mantra of Satarudriya. O Sage, in this way, both of them were relieved of the arrogance.

Then they came to realise that Siva was the Supreme Brahman, with sat (existence), Cita (knowledge), and ananda (bliss) as his characteristics. He is the great soul and transcends the attributes.

Omniscient Sanatkumara, you please listen to my words. Till such time a person is filled with arrogance, the wisdom remain invisible.

By shedding away the arrogance a person can well realise the supreme soul. Siva is the destroyer of the pride, and as such he relieved both of them of the arrogance.

When Siva came to know that both Brahma and Visnu have been freed from their arrogance, the great lord Siva, assured them of his protection.

Then lord Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, consoled them both and then spoke to Bhairava, his own form.

Lord Siva said, “Visnu shall be honoured by you always as also Brahma. O Nilalohita carry the skull of Brahma, yourself.

In order to educate the people, you take on the vrata of Brahmahatya. Holding the skull in your hand, you always keep on begging alms.”

Thus speaking and in full view of all, Siva produced a small girl named Brahmahatya. Then Siva in the form of mass flame spoke.

“Until she goes to the divine city of Varanasi, you too shall follow her, for a long period.

You can freely move to any place, except the city of Varanasi. On reaching Varanasi, you would be freed from Brahmahatya.

Nandisvara said, “Thus great lord Siva, who indulges in astonishing divine sports, thus inspiring Brahmahatya, disappeared from the place at once.

## Chapter 9 - Relieving of the sin of Brahmahatya at Kapalamocana Tirtha-Varanasi

Nandisvara said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, thus listen lovingly to another story of Bhairava, which destroys all the blemishes and increases devotion.

Due to the presence of Brahmahatya, Bhairava kept on calculating the time of his release. At the words of the lord of the gods, he kept on performing the vrata of a kapalika.

He, the soul of the universe, holding a skull in his hand, wandered in all the three lokas, but the harsh Brahmahatya, did not leave him.

Wandering in each and every tirtha, he could not be relieved of the Brahmahatya. This is the reason, why the illusion of Siva is believed to be an astonishing one.

Once having been served by the Pramathas, Siva taking to the form of a Kapalika, went to the place of Narayana alone.

Thereafter the three eyed Siva, having the serpents as the earrings, Bhairava, the amsa of Siva, lord Visnu, the other gods and their spouses prostrated before him, together with the sages.

Thereafter, Visnu, the lord of Laksmi eulogised him reciting various stotras.

O Excellent sage, thereafter, lord Visnu, getting pleased, addressed Laksmi, who had emerged out of the ocean.

Visnu said, “O Beloved, O Lotus eyed one, O Spotless and Sinless one, O Fortunate one, look here, both of us have become graceful today, since we are having an audience with lord of the universe.

He is the creator the preserver, besides being the lord of the world. He is the primordial being, the lord and the refuge of all. He is calm and greater than the twenty six principles.

He is the omniscient, lord of the yogis, the sole leader of all the beings, the internal soul of all the living beings and he always bestows everything to everyone.

O Laksmi, look, he is the lord whom the conscious people, are engaged in yogic practices, visualise in their hearts, discarding their sleep, stopping their breathing, concentrating their minds. He happens to be the same. You better visualise him with the vision of your knowledge, in your own heart.

He is the one who is known to the yogis who are well-versed in the Vedic tattvas. He is the one, who being formless, is at times visible in some definite form. The one who is all pervading is arriving here.

The conduct of Brahma is quite surprising because the one who describes his conduct daily, he inspite of his possessing a body becomes without body or is turned into an invisible form.

At the mere sight of the lord, the people are never reborn on earth. Such a type of lord Tryambaka who has the crescent as an ornament, is arriving here.

O Laksmi, my eyes resembling a lotus leaf, have become graceful today because I would have an opportunity to have a look with these eyes, Mahesvara, the great lord.

Disgrace to the position of the gods, who have not seen lord Siva so far, who bestows salvation, and who is the remover of all the miseries.

What is use of becoming a god in the heaven, in case, we people are unable to achieve salvation by looking at Mahadeva.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, lord Visnu bowed in reverence to lord with the thrill of delight, having been filled with pleasure and spoke to Siva, having the banner embossed with the bull.”

Visnu said, “O Lord, having no change, O Destroyer of the sins, what is all this being done by you? You are the omniscient lord of the gods as well as the creator of the three worlds?

O Lord of the gods, having three eyes, O Intelligent one, this is only your sport. O Virupaksa, O Destroyer of Kama, what is the cause of this motivation?

O Lord Siva, O Lord of Sakti, why do you keep on begging? O Lord of the universe, I am doubtful about this, O bestower of the kingdom of the three worlds.

Nandisvara said, “When so questioned by Visnu to Siva- the Bhairava, then the lord, who performed the astonishing types of sports, smilingly said to Visnu.”

Bhairava said, “I severed the fifth head of Brahma with the forepart of my finger nail. I am performing this Vrata for atoning that sin.”

Nandisvara said, “These were the words spoken by Mahesvara to Visnu. Then Visnu, getting reminded of something lowering his head said to Siva.

Visnu said, “You are the destroyer of all the sins, therefore, you do whatever is liked by you, but don’t allow your Maya to exercise her influence on me.

O Excellent one, because of the strength of my yogic practices, crores of Brahmas emerge from my naval, in each every kalpa.

O Deva, you better discard your Ṅaóṁ, which is quite difficult for the undisciplined people to face it. O Great lord, Brahma or no other gods are presently under the influence of your Maya.

O Lord of all, you happen to be the movement of the noble people, O Lord of Parvati, in case I am well aware of your sports, it is all by your grace.

O Siva, at the time of destruction, you would destroy all the gods, sages, all living beings as well as those following various Varnasrama.

O Mahadeva, even then would you attract the sin of Brahmahatya? O Siva you are not subservient to others. You enjoy your sports independently.

Like Siva, you have the garland of the skulls of the heads of Brahma, then, O Siva, how could the Brahmahatya attract you.

O Lord of the universe, a person, who after committing a heinous crime, recites your name, he is atonce relieved of the sin.

As the darkness cannot remain in face of the sun, similarly all the sins of your devotees are washed out.

The auspicious soul, who, often, adores your lotus like feet, all his the sins including Brahmahatya disappear in no time.

O Lord of the universe, a person whose speech recites your name, even the sins, as big as the mountain, can do no harm to him.

O Supreme soul, bestower of the salvation you take to any form at will. This is only your fancy besides the miserliness and dependence.

O Lord of the gods, I feel graceful today because I am having an audience with Paramesvara the indestructible one, who is beyond the reach of the great Yogesvaras.

Today, I have been extremely benefited. I have been bestowed with extreme welfare, because, having an audience with you, it appears like having consumed the nectar and even the heaven appears to be of no consequence.”

At these words of lord Visnu, Laksmi, with spotless mind dropped the alms into the begging bowl of the lord.

Bhairava Mahadeva also getting immensely pleased proceeded on to some other place for begging alms.

Finding the Brahmahatya following him, lord Visnu called her and prayed to her,” you better disown Bhairava, the carrier of the trident.”

Brahmahatya said, “By serving Siva, in this way, I am purifying myself for the purpose of achieving salvation.”

Nandisvara said, “Inspite of the request of Visnu, Brahmahatya, did not disassociate herself from Bhairava. Then Bhairava smilingly said to Visnu.”

Bhairava said, “O Lord of Laksmi, you bestow grace and honour on others. I feel pleased with your nectar like words which are like the nature of the noble people.

O Sinless Visnu, you better ask for a boon. I shall bestow a boon on you. You will be the foremost of your devotees becoming unblemished.

The ascetics who are used to getting alms, do not feel happy after receiving the alms so much, as they get pleased by receiving the alms quite respectfully.”

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of Bhairava, Visnu was pleased and then he spoke to Mahesvara.”

Visnu said, “The only praiseworthy boon for me would be that I should always adore you by my mind and the speech.

O Siva, this is like the shower of the nectar without clouds, I feel delighted over this, your benign glance, is as good as is a treasure so easily acquired by me.

O Lord Siva, let me never be detached from your feet. This is the only favour I seek and nothing else.”

Lord Bhairava said, “O Dear, O Intelligent one, let it be so. You will grant the boons to all the gods.”

Nandisvara said, “Then blessing Visnu, moving in the central mountain Meru, and the world, the lord went to the city of the liberated souls known as Varanasi.

As soon as Bhairava with awful features entered the city of Varanasi, Brahmahatya felt aggrieved and she entered the nether world.

The skull of Brahma fell on the ground, suddenly from the lotus like hand of Bhairava. The holy place then came to be known as êṁðalamoṣṁñṁ.

Observing the skull of Brahma falling from his hand, in full view of all, Rudra danced with delight.

The unbearable skull of Brahma did not leave his hand while he was roaming elsewhere in the world, but it dropped in a moment when he reached Kasi.

The Brahmahatya committed by Bhairava which could not be removed elsewhere, it was removed at Kasi in a moment. Therefore one should adore Kasi.

One who remembers the kapalamocana, present the holy place, all his sins of as well as the future world are washed out,

By taking the bath appropriately in this holy place, offering oblation to the gods as well as the manes, a person is relieved even of the sin of Brahmahatya.

Lord Bhairava, establishing the holy place of kapalamocana-tirtha removed the sins of the devotees.

In the month of Margasirsa, on the dark eighth day of the black fortnight, Mahesvara had appeared in the form of Bhairava.

On the bright eighth day of the fortnight of Margasirsa, one who performs Vrata seated before Kalabhairava, remaining awake during the night, he is relieved of all the grave sins.

The one who will perform the same Vrata, remaining at some other place, with devotion, remaining awake during the night, he will achieve salvation, after getting relieved of all the grave sins.

All the great sins committed by the people in the course of countless millions of births, vanish, with the mere sight of Kalabhairava.

The people, who trouble the devotees of Kalabhairava, the foolish fellows, have to suffer and they ultimately achieve the degraded position.

Those who are devoted to Visvesvara, but are averse to Kalabhairava, they particularly suffer while living in Kasi.

Observing fast in Kasi, those who do not adore Bhairava, their sins keep on increasing as the moon keeps on growing in the bright fortnight.

A person, who living in Kasi, does not eulogise Kalabhairava on each dark eighth day of the black fortnight, or on every Tuesday, all his merits disappear like the moon of the dark fortnight.

A person, who listens auspicious episode of the birth of Kalabhairava, he is relieved of all the sins.

In case, a person who is imprisoned, or is placed in a miserable condition, listens to the story of the birth of Kalabhairava, he is surely relieved of all the miseries.

## Chapter 10 - Lord Siva’s assurance to the gods

Nandisvara said, “O Lord, Virabhadra, who created obstructions in the yajna of Daksa Prajapati, had been the incarnation of Siva, the great soul.

His entire story has been narrated in the story of Sati. You have also listened to the same, several times. Therefore it is not being narrated here in detail.

O Great sage, presently, I am now narrating the story of Siva, connected with his incarnation as Sardula. For the benefit of the gods, lord Siva, had once taken to the form of Sarabha, possessing the divine lustre assumed the form of Sarabha.

O Excellent sages, Siva, who moves for the welfare of his devotees, is said to have incarnated on earth, several times, the number of which is beyond counting

One could count the stars in the sky, the particles of the dust on earth, or the streams of the rain fall, but, an intelligent person taking to many births, cannot count the incarnations of Siva. The words now spoken by me are correct.

Still, according to my wisdom, whatever has been heard by me, I shall narrate, the divine story of Sarabha, portending great prosperity.

O Sage, when Jaya and Vijaya were cursed by you, they were reborn as the sons of Diti and Kasyapa.

They were known as Hiranyakasipu and Hiranyaksa, who became the courtiers of the divine sages.

In earlier times, Brahma, for the redemption of the earth had prayed to lord Visnu. Then the lord Visnu, taking to the form of Varaha, killed Hiranyaksa and redeemed the earth.

Then learning of the death of his dear brother at the hands of Visnu, Hiranyakasipu was immensely enraged.

Performing tapas for ten thousand years, he achieved a boon to remain invincible on earth.

Then he proceeded to the city of Sonitapura, called the gods from all the four directions, subjugating the entire world he started ruling without any obstruction.

Wiping out all the dharmas torturing all the gods and the sages, the sinful Hiranyakasipu, started destroying even the Brahmanas.

Hiranyakasipu, who had been inimical to Visnu, also developed enmity with Prahlada his own son and the devotee of Visnu.

O Sage, then Visnu, in the form of Nrsimha suddenly appeared from the column of the assembly hall in the evening time.

O Excellent sage, the awful body of Nrsimha, with the flames emerging out of the same, started frightening the best of the Daityas.

Nrsimha killed all the Daityas in a moment and Hiranyakasipu fought a fierce battle with him.

O Excellent sages, for a moment they fought a fierce battle observing which the onlookers were thrilled.

At the evening time, the lord of gods, lord of Laksmi, Nrsimha (man-lion) dragged Hiranyakasipu to the threshold even as the gods were watching in the sky.

Then he atonce placed the Daitya king over his lap and tore out his belly, in full view of the gods.

When Hiranyakasipu was killed by Visnu in the form of Nrsimha, all the gods as well as the universe felt relieved and comfortable.

The gods played on the musical instruments. Prahlada felt surprised. Laksmi too felt surprised at the sight of the astonishing form of the lord.

Though the Daitya king was killed, and the gods retired to their respective abodes, but since the flames of anger of Nrsimha were not subsided, therefore, the people of the city could not be comfortable.

The entire universe, was upset with the fire flames. The gods too felt uncomfortable, getting apprehensive of the future happenings.

Thus speaking, they kept themselves at a safe distance out of fear, the lotus born deity and others were excited by the fury of the man-lion.

In order to subside the same, they sent Prahlada to him, requesting him collectively.

The compassionate Nrsimha, embraced Prahlada, as a result of which his heart became calm, but the fire of his anger could not be subsided.

Even when the anger of Nrsimha could not be subsided, all the gods went to Siva to take refuge with him.

Reaching there, all the gods and Brahma, in order to make the people of the universe comfortable, started praising Siva.

The gods said, “O Mahadeva, the god of gods, you are well-disposed towards those who take refuge in you. All the gods have arrived to take refuge with you. You kindly protect their lives. O Sadasiva, salutation to you again and again. During misery in earlier times, you had saved us.

The gods churned the ocean. The gems were distributed, but on the emerging of the poison, it was consumed by you and none else.

You saved us but you yourself became the blue-throated one. Had you not consumed the poison, then the entire universe would have been perished.

O Lord, it is well-known, all the miseries when engulf a person, get removed with the mere reciting of your name.

Presently we are suffering from the fire flames of Narasimha. O Sadasiva you are surely competent enough to subside the same.”

Nandisvara said,“When the gods so prayed to lord Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotee, the supreme lord bestowing protection to all, delightfully said.

Siva said, “O Brahma and other gods, all of you should fearlessly retire to your respective abodes. I Shall remove all your miseries surely.

The one who takes refuge with me, all his sufferings are removed. A person who takes refuge with me is dearer to me than my life.”

Nandisvara said, “Hearing this all the gods were rejoiced and reciting the name of Siva, they returned to their respective abodes.

## Chapter 11 - Removal of Narasimha’s pride by Virabhadra

Nandisvara said, “Thus having been praised by the gods, the immensely illustrious Siva- the ocean of mercy, got ready to extinguish the fire of anger of Narasimha.

Prior to that Siva remembered the powerful Virabhadra and spoke to Bhairava, the creator of dissolution.

Bhairava on the other hand accompanied with his ganas, smiling and laughing about, jumping and dancing arrived there.

He had with him crores of intoxicated warriors resembling Nrsimha, with terrific temperament who were dancing delightfully.

They were engaged in sports with the dancing warriors with Brahma and others like a ball and who had never been seen before. Such warriors offered their salutation to Bhairava.

Like the fire flame of the time of dissolution, his three eyes looked quite graceful. He was without weapons, wearing the matted locks of hair, was resplendent, and his head was decorated with the digit of the crescent moon.

He had the eyebrows like the broken pieces of Indra's bow and had two sharp fangs curved like the crescent moon.

With the powerful roar, he could deafen the directions. He had the complexion like the blue clouds, possessing the terrific beard and moustaches.

A musical instrument like Trisikha, was being played upon by Virabhadra, who with his Virasakti, arrived there.

He said to Siva- “What for have you summoned me, the lord of the universe? You get me your command delightfully.”

Nandisvara said, “Lord Siva, who punished the evil people, listening to the words of Virabhadra, with grace, looking at him, said to him lovingly.”

Siva said, “The gods are facing a grave danger untimely. The fire of anger of Nrsimha is burning people. You have to pacify the same.

Initially you should try to convince him to be peaceful. In case, he does not listen then you display the Bhairava form before him.

O Virabhadra, you at my command, overpower the small lustre with the smaller one and the big lustre with the bigger one.”

Nandisvara said, “In this way Virabhadra - the leader of ganas was commanded by Siva, thereafter he left for the place, where lord Nrsimha was lodged.

Virabhadra, having the universal form, lovingly spoke to Nrsimha, in the same way as a father addresses a son.”

Virabhadra said, “O Madhava, you have incarnated on earth for providing comfort to the people. Besides Parmesthi-Brahma has entrusted the protection of the people to you.

In earlier times incarnating as Matsya (Fish) you rescued Manu, tying his boat with your tail from the ocean.

Being the form of karma, you maintain all the beings, you rescued the earth. Then in the form of Hari, you killed Hiranyakasipu.

Then taking to the form of a dwarf, you captivated Bali, the Daitya king. You happen to be the lord of all the living beings, being eternal.

Whenever the people of the world are in danger then you incarnating on earth, remove their miseries and make them comfortable.

O Visnu, there is no one else devoted to Siva more than or even equal to you. You have led the Vedic dharma (sacred rites) to the noble path.

The purpose for which you had incarnated in earth in this form, it has been well served, with the killing of Hiranyakasipu and saving Prahlada. O Lord, there is no other devotee of Siva bigger than you.

O Lord, this Narasimha form of yours is quite a terrific one, therefore you remove the form from my sight.”

Nandisvara said, “In this way Virabhadra spoke to Nrsimha in a pleasing and peaceful way. But the immensely proud Nrsimha, displayed more anger than he did earlier.

O Sage, frightening him with his awful fangs, he spoke to mighty and terrible Virabhadra with harsh words.

Nrsimha said, “You better leave for the place from where have you come. Don’t talk to me about the welfare of the universe. Now I shall destroy the mobile as well as the immobile worlds.

I am myself the destroyer, but no one else can destroy me. I rule everywhere. There is no one else to exercise his control over me.

By my grace, all the mobile and the immobile worlds, remain fearless. I happen to be the operator and controller of all the Saktis.

O Lord of the ganas, a person possessing grace and the resplendence, possess indeed my lustre.

The gods well-versed in paramartha conceive me as the best The parts of my Sakti could be visualised in Brahma, Indra and other gods, who remain delighted with the same.

Brahma, the creator of the universe, was born out of the lotus emerging from my navel. I am the most independent of all the gods. I preserve and destroy the universe.

This is the height of my resplendence. What more do you want to listen from me? Therefore, you taking refuge in me, and then leave, feeling carefree.

O Ganesvara, you take me as the best of the gods. The entire universe comprising of the gods and the humans, belongs to me.

O Virabhadra, I am the form of Kala, for the destruction of the universe. Presently I am getting ready to destroy the people. Even the death can be destroyed by me. All the gods remain alive by my grace alone.”

Nandisvara said, “The immensely strong Virabhadra listening to the arrogant words of Nrsimha, then contemptuously laughed at him saying.”

Virabhadra said, “Are you not aware of Visvesvara- the carrier of the bow? You are concentrating your discussion on the false ideology of your own. Now only the destruction is left.

How many more incarnations are still due to you? The entire story as to who has done what, would come to an end.

You please tell me the blemish by which you have faced this precarious condition. Now you have to receive daksina from Siva, who is well-versed in destruction.

You are Prakrti while Siva is Purusa. You possess the strength by the grace of Siva. No doubt, the fire faced Brahma had been born out of your navel.

For the creator of the three lokas, Brahma and performed severe tapas concentrating his mind at Siva, the blue throated one.

At that point of time, Siva had emerged out of his forehead. Therefore, Bhairava, the god of gods had deputed me for your destruction.

I have been deputed to subjugate you amicably or by force. O Nrsimhadeva, Siva, the lord of the three worlds, has entrusted me the task of your destruction.

With the strength derived from him, you have been able to destroy a demon, which has made you arrogant and you are now roaring aloud carelessly.

The good done by the noble people, is really comfortable and the good done by the evil people is always painful.

O Nrsimha, in case your consider yourself to be the creator of Siva, then there would be no other person, more ignorant or arrogant than you.

O Nrsimha, you are neither a creator nor a preserver, nor the destroyer. You are subservient and a fool. You are in no way independent.

Siva has operated upon you like the potter's wheel, with his own force. O Hari, in each and every one of your incarnations, you were subservient to him and function accordingly.

Even today by burnt skull of the form of karma still adorns the neck of Siva among the garland of skulls, which cannot be worn by anyone else.

Have you forgotten that during the incarnation of Varaha, your horn had been removed by the gana of Siva, the enemy of Tarakasura, forcing you to cry.

Because of the trick of Visvaksena, you had been burnt with the fire flames of trident of Siva and I had severed your head during the yajna of Daksa.

Even today, I have severed the fifth head of Brahma- your son, which could not be restored till date. Have you forgotten all this?
