Dadhici had overpowered you while scratching your head in the battle-field. Have you forgotten it?

O Holder of Cakra, have you ever thought about the source from which you received the Cakra? Who did good to you? You have forgotten all this.

Because of my bearing the entire burden of the universe, you remain carefree in the oceanic bed. How could you be called Sattvika.

From you to Stambha, the prowess of Siva is pervading. With that, you even after becoming powerful are deluded with the lustre on all the sides.

The glory of the resplendence of Siva, which remains invisible. Only the people with sharp intelligence can visualise the same which is all pervading.

The Paramesvara after pervading the sky, earth, Indra, fire, Yama, and Varuna, the darkness as well as the moon, the said Paramesvara, pervades therein.

In case you are Kala, then Mahesvara is Mahakala. Therefore being the form of death, you would meet with death with his terrific digit.

Íṛ is stable, indestructible, valorous, protector of the universe, lord, remover of the pain, grand, the deer, the bird, having golden complexion, and happens to be the ruler of the entire universe. Brahma and other gods have no existence. Only Siva, is the ruler of the entire universe. There is no doubt about it.

Realising this, you end yourself with your own splendour. O Foolish Narasimha, don’t force yourself to proceed towards destruction.

Otherwise the great Vajra of Siva, having the form of Mahabhairava would fall on you like the death.

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking Virabhadra, the form of the rage of Siva, fearlessly waited for the intentions of Nrsimha.

## Chapter 12 - Incarnation of Siva as Sarbha

Sanatkumara said, “O Great intellectual Nandisvara, do you know, what happened thereafter? Being merciful on me, you kindly narrate the same.

Nandisvara said, “At these words of Virabhadra Nrsimha became upset in anger. Then he applying great force, tried to capture him roaring aloud.

At that point of time the enormous resplendence of Siva in the form of a column appeared spreading from the earth to the sky.

The form of Virabhadra disappeared from the scene, for a moment and it did not remain like the gold in appearance nor the sun, or the fire.

It also did not resemble the lightening, nor the moon. The resplendence of Siva was of a unique type. At that times all the lustres was merged in that resplendence.

The great resplendence could not be accommodated even in the sky. It was the ordinary sign of Siva in a deformed manner.

He had thousands of arms, locks of hair with the crescent over the head, possessing well developed body, with the beak and the wings, he appeared like a bird.

He had the sharp fangs. The talons were as sharp and strong at the Vajra which served as his weapons. He had long arms, four feet and he resembled the fire, in appearance.

He was ready to cause dissolution, creating horrible and deep sound. He was in great anger, and his eyes emitted the fire of Krtyas.

His fangs and the lips were visible creating a thundering sound, Siva appeared before Nrsimha in a horrible form.

At the sight of the horrible form of Siva, the prowess of Nrsimha, faded out, in the same way as the light of the fire fly disappears with the sun shine.

Fluttering with his wings, and tearing the navel and legs of the Man-lion with his tail, and with his two hands, he struck his chest, holding Visnu. It expanded in the sky with the gods and the sages.

Like a vulture capturing a serpent, he fearlessly caught hold of Visnu, lifted him up and fell him on the ground. At the time of fight, he was excessively oppressed being hit with the wings. Then lord Siva carried Visnu and flew up.

All the gods followed him praising him at the same time. Brahma and other sages bowed to him, in reverence with love.

Having been so held by Siva, Visnu was helpless. His face was grief-stricken. With his hands folded, he eulogised lord Siva, speaking simple words.

After eulogising Mrda with a hundred and eight names of the lord, Narasimha requested lord Sarabha again.

“O Great lord, whenever my ignorant mind, becomes defiled by arrogance, it shall be removed by you only.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus lovingly speaking to Siva, the Man-lion turned submissive, bowing in reverence to him. Visnu was completely defeated and faced the end of his life.

Within a second, Virabhadra made his powerful body powerless and dead.

Nandisvara said, “Thereafter, Brahma and other gods, adored lord Siva in the form of Sarabha, for the welfare of the three lokas, offering prayer to him at the same time.

The gods said, “O Lord Mahesvara, Brahma, Visnu, Indra, the moon and other gods, besides the rsis, Daityas, have been born out of you.

In fact, you produce Brahma, Visnu, Indra, Surya, and other gods, you preserve them, and as such, you are called Sakalesvara.

Because of the destruction of the universe, you are called as Íṁrṁ by the people with wisdom. Since you have placed Hari in bondage, therefore, you are also called Íṁrṁ.

Because you dividing your body in eight parts, maintain the entire universe, therefore, O Lord, you save the gods like us bestowing the desired boons.

You are the supreme Purusa, Sambhu, Sarvesa, Suranayaka, Nil-svatma, spotless soul, the Supreme Brahman, and the refuge of the noble people.

You are friendly towards the distressed, the ocean of mercy, of wonderful sports, the vision of the great soul, the intelligent one, the enormous cosmic being, the all pervasive, the truth, the existence, knowledge and bliss are your characteristics.”

Nandisvara said, “On hearing these words of the gods, Siva- the great lord, spoke to the gods as well as the great ancient sages.

As the water poured into the water or the milk poured into the milk or the ghee poured into the ghee becomes one with those things, so also Visnu is merged in Siva and not otherwise.

It was Visnu alone, in the form of Nrsimha, who was arrogant and strong, engaged in annihilating the universe.

He shall be bowed and adored by my devotees, aspiring achievements. He is the foremost of my devotees, and the bestower of the boons.

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking the powerful lord- the king of birds, (Sarabha) in full view of the gods disappeared from the same.

Then Virabhadra, the powerful leader of the ganas, carried the body of Nrsimha to a mountain peak.

Since that time, he wears the skin of Nrsimha and his head is prominently inbeded in the garland of skulls worn by him.

All the gods becoming fearful, narrating the story, went to their respective abodes with a feeling of surprise. A person who reads or listens to the episode filled with the nectar of Vedas, all his desires are fulfilled.

This episode is quite graceful, bestower of glory, enhances the age and good health, and removes all types of obstructions.

It removes the miseries, fulfills all the desires, bestows welfare, is the remover of untimely death, destroyer of enemies besides is enhancing wisdom.

Sarabha is the excellent form of Siva. Its story should be narrated among the devotees of Siva.

The devotees of Siva should read and listen to the same. It bestows nine types of devotion, besides purifying the mind.

In the festivities concerning Siva, on the eight and fourteenth days of the moon or at the time of the consecrating of the images of Siva, its recitation bestows Sayujya devotion of Siva.

During the danger from the thieves, tigers, lions, and the humans, or in the crimes which are self commited, in the royal court, in other disturbances, in earthquakes, the dust storms and other natural calamities, fall of comets, terrible storms, excess fall of rains and the draught, whosoever recites this episode, such a person with a firm resolve, is termed as the devotee of Siva.

One who, listens to it with a selfless mind, performing the Vrata of Siva, he reaching the Rudraloka, becomes an attendant of Siva.

Reaching Rudraloka, he enjoys life in the company of Rudra. O Sage, thereafter, he, by the grace of Siva, achieves the Sayujya devotion of Siva.

## Chapter 13 - Performing of tapas by Visvanara and his wife for getting a son

Nandisvara said, “O Son of Brahma, lovingly listen to the story of Siva, relating to his incarnating in the house of Visvanara.

O Sage, Grhapati the lord of Agniloka, was illustrious like the fire and was the best among the worldly beings.

The sage Visvanara dwelt over the pleasant bank of the Naramada, in the city of Narmopara. He was an auspicious soul and was devoted to Siva.

He was born in Sandilya gotra and lived in the auspicious Brahmacarya-asrama, performing the Brahma-yajna daily.

He well understood the meaning of all the scriptures, possessed the noble conduct and was well aware of the performance of the devotees of Siva, besides the worldly behaviour.

He, taking into consideration the qualities of a virtuous wife married a girl of a spotless family according to the provision of the scriptures.

He daily performed the homa or fire sacrifice, fie yajnas, and the six practices. He used to adore the manes as well as the guests.

In this way a lot of time of the Brahmana was passed, after which his wife Sucismati said to her husband.

“O Lord, I have enjoyed all the womanly pleasures with you for a long time, by your grace.

O Lord, I have a desire longing in my mind for some time in the past, which can be fulfilled by you.”

Visvanara said, “O Beloved one, which is that think, which is dear to you and can bestow welfare? You ask for the same and I shall surely provide it to you.

O Auspicious one, by the grace of Siva, who does good to all, nothing is beyond my reach.”

Nandisvara said, “The wife who treated the husband like a god, then she said delightfully with folded hands.”

Sucismati said, “In case I am worthy of achieving a boon, and in case you intend to bestow a boon on me, then you grant me a son resembling Siva. I seek for no other boon.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus listening to her words, the Brahmana- performer of the auspicious Vrata, meditated for a while thinking in his mind at the same time.

He thought, “It is quite surprising, that my wife, has desired for an extremely inaccessible thing, which is beyond the reach of the human desire. Let it be so. It is the lord only who does everything.

It is by Siva himself dwelling in her tongue, in the form of speech, that these words have been uttered. This is quite possible. Who else would have endeavoured to do so?”

After thus thinking, the sage Visvanara- the large hearted one, who strictly believed in the principle of monogamy, spoke to her.

After consoling his wife, the sage set out for the performance of tapas in the city of Varanasi, where lord Siva was himself living.

Soon after his reaching Varanasi and at the sight of Manikarnika, he was freed from the distresses acquired in the course of the hundreds of past births.

He saw Visvesvara and other Sivalingas. He performed ablutions in all holy well, tanks, and the lakes.

Íṛ offered his salutation to Vinayakas and Sarva Gauri. He adored Kalaraja Bhairava- the destroyer of the sins.

Making all the best efforts, he eulogised Dandanayaka and other ganas, Adikesava, and others. He also adored Kesava.

He worshipped Lolarka and other suns again and again and offered pindadana at all the holy places quite carefully.

He pleased the sages and the Brahmanas by serving thousand types of dishes and also adored the Mahalingas with devotion.

Then he started thinking again and again, as to which one of the Sivalinga would bestow, quick success, to enable him to achieve a son.

After thinking for a while, the wise sage Visvanara praised a linga named Viresa which confers the blessings of a son immediately.

Innumerable thousands of Siddhas had met with the success by adoring it. Because of that it came to be known as Viresvara linga of success.

One who adores Viresvara linga for a year with devotion, he attains long life, has all his desires fulfilled, besides getting a son.

Therefore, I also adoring Viresa during all the three times, shall shortly achieve a son as desired by my wife.”

In this way immensely auspicious soul, the Brahmana Visvanara, with a firm resolve in his mind, taking a bath with the water of Candrakupa, took a samkalpa.

For a month he took meals once a day, then for a month he took food during the night alone, then for a month he lived on the food, he received without seeking for the same and ultimately he discarded taking the food altogether.

Then he took milk alone for a month, then he remained vegetarian for a month; he took for a month the gingerly seeds daily a fist full of them. For another month he took only Pancagavya. For another month, he took liquid food. For another month, he performed the Candrayana Vratas. For another month he drank water from the tip of the kusa grass and for another month, he lived on inhaling air alone as his food.

In this way he performed a wonderful tapas. He adored Viresa thrice a day.

Thereafter, on the thirteenth month, the Brahmana was returning, after having his bath in the Ganga river, very early in the morning, the sage saw a child of eight years, with ashes smeared over his body in the centre of the linga.

He had the eyes stretching to the ears, had red gums, having the crown of the yellow locks of hair, naked and with a delightful face. His form was like the child who was quite conscious. He was reciting the Suktas, and was smiling playfully.

By looking at the boy, the sage was thrilled and he offered his salutation to him mentally. He was reciting hymns from the Vedas and was laughing sportily.

Then Visvanara, adored the child form of Siva, reciting the eight passages which fulfil the desires.

Visvanara said, “Brahman is one and because of that he is called unique. This is true, there is nothing else here, except that. Therefore I take refuge with you.

O Siva, inspite of your being formless, you possess many forms. You are the creator and the destroyer of all. As the Sanatana-dharma is one with many forms, you resemble the same. Therefore, I take refuge with you.

One visualises a snake in a rope, silver in the conch shell, the flowing of water in the mirage- like that when he is known, the whole world vanishes leaving behind Sat alone. I, therefore, take refuge in you, O Lord.

As there is coolness in the water, the power of burning in fire, warmth in the sunshine, pleasing gentleness in the moon, fragrance in the flower, and ghee in the milk, just in the same way, O Siva you are essence of the world. Therefore, I take refuge in you.

You being earless, but still perceive the sound, you are noseless but still perceive fragrance, you are footless having come from far off place, you are eyeless but still you can see. You are tongueless but still perceive the taste. Who can know about your reality? Therefore I take refuge in you.

O Lord, you are directly unknown to the Vedas, nor to Visnu, nor the creator of everything, nor the leading yogins, nor Indra nor the other gods. You are known only to a devotee. Therefore I take refuge with you.

You have no spiritual lineage or a gotra, nor a body, neither destruction nor form, no humility, no country and inspite of all this, you happen to be the lord of the universe and you fulfil the desires of all. Therefore, I adore you.

O Enemy of the cupid, you pervade in all and all are lodged in you. You are the lord of Parvati. You are without robes and are peaceful. You are a boy, a youth and an old man. There is no element in the world which is separated from you. Therefore, I offer my salutation to you.”

Nandisvara said, “By the time the Brahmana, thus praising the boy, fell prostrate on earth, then the boy was transformed into a old man and he spoke to the Brahmana.

The boy said, “O Excellent sage, O Visvanara, you have pleased me- a Brahmana, therefore feeling delighted you better ask for a boon.”

Thereafter the delighted and competent sage Visvanara, stood up and said to lord Siva who was in the form of a boy.

Visvanara said, “O Lord, O Mahesvara, nothing is hidden from you. You are omniscient, the soul of all, you are Siva and bestow everything to all.

Why do you want me to speak out something to you placing a demand before you? You are the lord of all and you may do as you like.

Nandisvara said, “Listening to word of Visvanara, who had been performing auspicious Vratas, Siva in the form of a boy smiled and said to him.

“O Holy one, the desire of Sucismati being carried by you, shall undoubtedly be carried out and fulfilled.

O Mahamati, I shall emerge from Sucismati as your son and shall be known as Grhapati, pure and loved by all gods.

The eight passage stotra recited by you when recited by anyone for a years before Siva, thrice, daily, all his desires would be fulfilled.

With the reciting of this stotra one achieves sons, grandsons besides the riches. It provides peace in all respects and removes all the obstructions.

This stotra undoubtedly bestows the heaven as well as the salvation, besides the riches. Like other stotras, this stotra too fulfills all the desires.

A person who rising early in the morning, taking bath, adores Sivalinga for a year daily, he gets a son.

This stotra of fulfilling desires should not be imparted to all and it should be protected making all the efforts. It bestows sons to the barren ladies.

A man or a woman, should regularly sit besides the Sivalinga for a year and recite this stotra, then he or she surely gets a son.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking Siva in the form of a boy, and who provides refuge to the noble people, disappeared from the scene. The Brahmana Visvanara too delightfully went back to his abode.

## Chapter 14 - Incarnation of Siva as Grhapati

Nandisvara said, “The Brahmana delightfully returned to his place and narrated the news of his visit to Varanasi to his wife.

Then Sucismati, the wife of the Brahmana, started praising her fortunes lovingly.

She became pregnant in due course of time and the Brahmana performed the rites of impregnation duly.

Before the stir of the throb of the child in the mother’s womb was felt, the Brahmana performed the holy rite of pumsvana in the manner ordained in the Grhyasutras for the growth of the embryo’s manliness.

In the eighth month of the pregnancy, he performed the auspicious rite of Simanta which is conducive to the growth of the embryo and results in the comfortable birth of the child.

Then at the conjunction of the stars, when the Jupiter was in the centre, the lagna was auspicious when the favourable planets stood in pairs, Siva, the bestower of pleasures to all, was born as the son of Sucismati. His face resembled the moon. The light of the lamps in the labour room was faded out with the lustre emerging out of the body of the child. The lord who is the destroyer of the misfortunes, and the bestower of happiness to all the earthly people, besides those of the nether worlds, and the heaven, was born as a son to Sucismati. The smoke emerging therefrom was turned as the perfume, in order to sweeten the breath of the quarters. The rain of flowers with pleasing fragrance was showered from the sky. The celestials sounded the divine drums, and all the quarters were illuminated.

The minds of the people as well as the waters of the rivers were purified. The darkness was removed, and the dust was subsided.

All the people were filled with sattvaguna. The rain of nectar was dropped. The words of welfare of the people were liked by all.

Thousands of the divine damsels, besides Rambha and other apsaras, Vidyadharis, and Kinnaris, carried the welfare material.

The damsels of Gandharvas, Nagas and the Yaksas, arrived singing the many types of auspicious songs.

The sages like Marici, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Kratu, Vasistha, Kasyapa, Agastya, Vibhanda, Lomasa- the son of Mandavi, Romacarana, Bhardvaja, Gautama, Bhrgu, Galava, Garga, Jatukarna, Parasara, Apastamba, Yajnavalkya, Daksa, Valmiki, Mudgala, Satatapa, Likhikta, Silada, Samkha, Unchabhuk, Bharata, Jamadagni, Samvarta, Matanga, Amsumari, Vyasa, Katyayana, Kutsa, Saunaka, Susruta, Suka, Rsyasrnga, Durvasa, Suci, Narada, Tumburu, Uttanka, Vamadeva, Pavana, Asita, Devala, Salankayana, Harita, Visvamitra and Bhargava, Mrkandu with his son, Parvata, Daruka, Dhaumya, Upamanyu, Vatsa and other sages, together with the daughters of the sages arrived there for the celebrations. Therefore the abode of Vaisvanara on that date was filled with grace.

Visnu with the mount Garuda, Brahma accompanied with Brhaspati and Siva was accompanied with Parvati and Bhrngi.

Indra and other gods, Nagas from the Patalaloka carrying enormous gems, the ocean with treasures.

Thousands of creatures taking to the mobile and immobile forms, reached the place for attending the festivities, where the moonlight had been spread.

Brahma in a humble way, performed all the birth ceremonies and gave him the name of Grhapati, consulting the Vedas.

Reciting the Vedic hymns, the name was given appropriately on the eleventh day of the birth.

After bestowing blessings on everyone with the reciting of the hymns of the Vedas, Brahma left the place mounted over the swan.

After providing proper safety for the child, in accordance with the worldly practices, Siva returned to his place, riding his vehicle, alongwith Visnu.

All the people praised the fortunes of Sucismati as if Siva had appeared in their own houses.” “How beautiful is the boy, how grand is his resplendence and all his limbs have the auspicious marks.

Or otherwise, it is not a surprise for the devotees of Siva, because he adored Siva and Rudra himself appeared in his house.

All of them praising individually, feeling thrilled, returned to their abodes getting permission from Visvanara.

The parents are bestowed with salvation with the birth of a son and as such the householders desire to get a son. This has been ordained by the Vedas.

A house without a son is treated as a deserted one. The worship of the householder becomes of no consequence. His tapas is never completed and without a son a person is never purified.

There is no gain better than getting a son. There is no comfort better than a son, and there is no friend better than a soon in this as well as the future world.

During the fourth month the father performed the ceremony of crossing the threshold, by the father. At the close of six months, the rite of tasting the food was performed and at the end of a year, the rite of shaving or cutting the hair of the child was performed.

A priest well-versed in the performing of the rites, performed the karnavedha ceremony of the child during the Sravana constellation. Thereafter in the fifth year, in order to increase Brahmateja, the thread ceremony (yajnopavita) was performed.

Then performing the upanavana samskara, he was taught the Vedas by an intelligent sage. The boy learnt the Vedas with the other related literature for a year.

He learnt by heart, the pada-patha and the kramapatha of the Vedas. He learnt all the lores from the mouth of his preceptor. Then the all powerful boy, learnt the qualities of humility and others.

Thus the boy started serving his parents at the age of nine years. At that point of time Narada arrived in the abode of Visvanara in order to meet Grhapati.

Narada- the divine sage, reaching the courtyard of Visvanara, occupying a seat, enquired about his welfare.

Devoting his mind at the feet of Siva, Narada, revealed about his future, in presence of Grhapati and also explained the duties of a son.

Nandisvara said, “Thus the sage spoke to the child. The parents then asked Grhapati to offer salutation to Narada. He did so and quietly took his seat with humility.”

Narada said, “O Visvanara, you come here. Be seated close to me. I would like to examine your symptoms. Show me your right hand.

Thereafter at the inspiration of Siva, the intelligent Narada, examined his palate, tongue etc. of the boy.”

Narada said, “O Sage Visvanara, listen, reading the symptoms of your son, I am going to speak out which you should listen with respect. Your son possesses all the auspicious symptoms and marks.

He possess all the virtues and the auspicious characteristics. He possesses all the spotless digits. Therefore you should bring him up as Brahma brings up the moon.

Therefore, you should protect this child making all the efforts, because when the destiny is on the opposite even the virtues turn as vices.

In the twelfth month from now, he has to face danger from fire or the lightening.” Thus speaking, the divine sage Narada, returned to his abode.

## Chapter 15 - Performing of tapas by Grhapati to ward off untimely death

Nandisvara said, “Visvanara, listening to the words of Narada, with his wife, then he felt like the falling of the hard Vajra.

Beating his breast he lamented and was fainted because of the grief of his son.

His mother Sucismati also feeling grieved started crying, aloud and became completely upset.

Listening to the lamenting, Visvanara, regaining consciousness, uttered, “What is all this happening here?” Crying thus aloud, he further uttered, “Where is Grhapati, the lord of my inner organs of senses?”

Then finding his parents excessively grieved, the boy Grhapati, a part of Siva, smiled and said to his parents.”

Grhapati said, “O Mother, O Father, what has happened? What for are you crying so much? Where from have you got this pain.

I am protected with the dust of your feet and as such I am beyond the reach of even the god of death, then what to speak of the poor lightening?

O Mother, O Father, both of you should listen to my firm resolve. In case I happen to be your son, then I would move in such a way that even the death gets terrified from me.

O Mother, O Father, I am speaking the truth. I shall recite the mantra of Mahakala-Mrtyunjaya who is omniscient and is the bestower of everything to the noble people.

Nandisvara said, “Listening the words of their son, both husband and wife felt like having regained their lives with the fall of the rain of nectar, getting relieved of their mental agony.

The Brahmana couple said, “O Son, you repeat your words, repeat them. You speak out about the form of Mahakala and that the time and pitiable fickle existence will not affect you?

A great way out has been proposed by you for the removal of our distress, by that of the worship of lord Siva, the conqueror of the death.

The same is the result of those who seek refuge in Siva, who removes sins and does everything beyond the path of our desire. There could be nothing better than this.

O Dear, have you not heard about the slayer of Tripuras who were protected in earlier times or Svetaketu who was bound with noose by Kala.

Silada, the son of Nandi, under threat from death in the eighth year of his life, became the devotee of Siva, who delights the world, saved his life.

The poison- Halahala, emerging out of the churning of the ocean, and resembling the fire of the time of dissolution, was consumed by Siva, saving all the three worlds.

Siva caused the death of the immensely arrogant Jalandhara, who had usurped the riches of others, with the Cakra produced with the big toe of his foot.

He, shooting a single arrow, produced the fire out of it and dried up Tripurasura, who had plundered all the riches of the universe.

Siva is the one who reduced the arrogant Kamadeva, who had conquered the three worlds, with the mere casting of a glance on him.

O Son, Siva is the only creator of Brahma who is the sole creator of the universe. He is Meghavahana, Acyuta, protector of the universe, therefore you should take refuge with Siva.”

Nandisvara said, “Receiving the permission from the parents, and bowing in reverence at their feet, circumambulating them at the same time, besides assuring them variously, he left his house.

Then he reached the city of Kasi, which is beyond the reach of Brahma, Visnu and other gods, and removes the three types of sufferings.

The city of Kasi, in which the Ganga, looks graceful like the garland of creepers, and in which the goddess. Annapurna possessing her divine virtues, is lodged.

Reaching there the Brahmana boy, initially went to Manikarnika and taking bath there appropriately, he adored lord Visvesvara with folded hands, lowering his head, with spotless mind, and then he felt delighted. He offered his salutation to lord Siva, who saves the lives of the three worlds.

Looking again and again at the auspicious linga there, he felt delighted in his mind. There is no doubt about it.

He thought, “There is no one more fortunate than myself in the three worlds, who could have an audience with lord Visvesvara.

In earlier times, Narada had told about me, because of the rise of my fortunes and I have now become successful.

Thus he consumed the nectar of bliss, on an auspicious day, he consecrated a Sivalinga which bestows good to all.

He adopted austere practices which were difficult to be performed by those who have no control over their senses. He filled pots with the water of Ganga purified with a cloth. He daily bathed the Sivalinga with hundred and eight pitchers filled with water. Then he put a garland of blue lotus flowers around the deity.

The garland was made of a thousand and eight lotus flowers. He consumed the roots and fruits once in a fortnight or a month.

He lived on dry leaves, which had fallen of their own for a period of six months. For six months he lived on inhaling the air alone and for another six months he lived on consuming the drops of water.

O Narada, with the image of lord Siva enshrined in his heart, the period of one year passed.

On the twelfth year from birth, the thunderbolt-armed Indra arrived before the boy as if fulfilling the utterance of Narada.

Indra said, “I am Indra and am pleased with your penance. You ask for a boon desired by you. I shall give it to you.”

Thus listening to the words of Indra, the son of the sage, patiently replied in sweet voice.”

Grhapati said, “O Enemy of Vrtra, O Holder of Vajra, O Indra, you are very well known to me. I do not seek for a boon from you. It is Siva alone, who could grant a boon to me.

Indra said, “ Siva is not at all separate from me. I am the god of gods. Shed away the childishness and you ask for a boon.

Grhapati said, “O Spouse of Ahalya, O Evil one, enemy of the mountains, O Indra, you can go back. This is absolutely clear that I, except Siva, will seek boon from no one else.

Nandisvara said, “Thus listening to the words of Grhapati, the eyes of Indra were turned red in anger and he frightened the boy with the awful Vajra.

Like the lustre of the lightening emerging from the Vajra, the boy was reminded of the words of Narada and getting frightened he was fainted.

Then Siva the lord of Gauri, the remover of darkness, appeared on the scene. Touching the boy with his hand, he said, “Let you meet with all the welfare, you better get up.”

Grhapati opened his eyes as if having been woken up after the sleep in the night. Opening his eyes he found Siva standing before him.

He found lord Siva with three eyes, with Parvati lodged to the left, having blue throat, bull-bannered, and having the crescent moon as the crown. He had the matted locks of hair over the head, carrying the trident and a bow. His body was white like the white camphor and was wearing the elephant skin.

Realising him to be Mahadeva, on the authority of the Sastra and because of the words of the preceptor, that he was Siva, he felt thrilled and the tears of joy started flowing from his eyes.

For a moment he became immobile like the mountain Citrakuta or Triputraka, because he had lost his senses. Therefore, he could neither offer any prayer, nor salutation and was unable to express any request even. Finding him in such a precarious condition, Siva smilingly said to him.

Isvara said, “O Boy, Grhapati, are you afraid of Indra, carrying Vajra in his hand. It appears like that. Don’t be afraid. I have actually put you to test.

Indra or his Vajra or even the Yama can cause no harm to a devotee of mine. It is actually I who had frightened you.

I bestow on you the best of the boon. You take to the form of Agni, bestowing boon on the gods.

Let you be turned as the fire dwelling in the bodies of all the creatures. You rule the region between the regions of Dharmaraja and Indra.

The linga which has been consecrated by you, will be known by your name and will be known by the name of Agnisvara and would enhance all the resplendence.

The devotees of Agnisvara would not be afraid of fire or the lightening. They would never face indigestion nor would they have to face the untimely death.

They shall not have to face the untimely death. A person who adores Agnisvara- the bestower of all the wealth, while living in Kasi, in case he meets with his death at a place other than Kasi, he reaches Agniloka.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, summoning the parents, and kins of Grhapati, he was bestowed with the position of a Dikpala, performing his abhiseka. Then lord Siva, absorbed himself in the said linga.

Thus I have narrated the story of Grhapati form of Siva and his incarnation as Agni.

There is, an illustrious one comfortable and the pleasant city of Citrahotra. The people who are devoted to Agni, reside there.

Those who have controlled their senses, or the ladies prominently possessing Sattvaguna are all illustrious like the fire.

A person who performs the homa daily, or the Brahmana, who is devoted to the five types of fires, he, being a Brahmacari, becoming resplendent like the fire resides in Agniloka.

A devotee, who gives wood to a Brahmana, for removing cold, or builds fire altar with bricks, he dwells in the Agniloka.

The one who cremates an unknown dead body, performing Sraddha at the same time, or he himself being incapable, makes others to do so, he is honoured in the Agniloka.

The god Agni is the best well-wisher of the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and Vaisyas. Agni is the god for them, besides being the tirtha.

All the inauspicious things coming in contact with the fire are purified and because of the same, Agni is known as Pavaka as well.

The fire is surely the immanent soul of a man. Even the morsel of flesh will be digested in the stomach by the same, but not the muscles of a woman.

The fiery form of Siva is in the form of the visible fire. Except this, what else is seen as creative, protective or destructive?

Fire is the eye of Siva- the lord of the three worlds. In the world filled with pitch darkness, what else than this, becomes the illuminator?

The incense, the lights, the food offerings, milk, curd, ghee and sugarcane juice, all these go unto the dwellers of the heaven, when offered into the fire here.

## Chapter 16 - Siva’s incarnation as Yakses'vara at the time of the churning of the ocean

Nandisvara said, “O Excellent sage, now you listen to the Yakses'vara incarnation of Siva who shatters the pride of the arrogant people and bestows devotion on the noble people.

In earlier times the immensely strong gods and the Daityas entered into a contract, churned the ocean for getting the nectar.

After churning of the ocean by the demons and the gods, initially emerged the terrific poison, which was as awful as the fire of the time of dissolution.

Finding that all the gods and the demons were frightened. All of them left the place and reached before Siva and took refuge with him.

Having an audience with Siva, the foremost of all the gods, Visnu and other gods, offered their salutation to him lowering their heads.

Then lord Siva, who is graceful to his devotees consumed the terrific poison, who could destroy the gods and the demons.

Consuming the terrific poison, he held it in the throat, which made him graceful and he came to be known as NUakantha.

Then by the grace of Siva, feeling free from the destruction due to the poison, the gods and the demons again churned the ocean.

Then numerous gems emerged out of it, which were distributed among the gods and the demons.

By the grace of Visnu the entire nectar was consumed by the gods and the demons could not have any taste of it. Because of this, the gem like nectar, became the cause of conflict between the demons and the gods.

Then there started a conflict between the demons and the gods. The moon getting fearful from Rahu took refuge with Siva and offering his salutation to him prayed for safety.

Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees and provides shelter to the noble people, placed the moon, who had taken refuge with him, over his head.

Thereafter Rahu, arrived before Siva- the lord of mobile and immobile creatures offering his salutation to him he offered prayers to Siva. With sweet voice.

Well understanding his intention, Siva placed the skull of Rahu in the garland of skulls worm by him.

Thereafter, all the gods defeated the demons and the valorous gods became victorious because of their having consumed the nectar.

Then Visnu and all other gods having been influenced with the Maya of Siva, became proud of their prowess.

O Sage, then Siva who happens to be the lord of all and shattered pride of all, took to the form of Yaksesvara and reached the place where the gods had assembled.

Looking at Visnu and all other gods, Siva who shatters the pride of all, Mahes'a- the lord of Yaksas said to them.

Yaksesvara said, “O Gods, why have you all assembled here? I would like to know the reason for the same. You give me the reply.

The gods said, “O Deva, a great war was fought here, in which several of the Daityas were killed and the remaining ones fled away.

We, the valorous people, are the destroyer of the Daityas and each one of us is quite strong. These Daitya were of no consequence before us.”

Nandlsvara said, “Thus listening to the arrogant words of the gods, then Mahadeva in the form of Yaksa, and remover of the pride of all said.

Yaksesvara said, “O Gods, now you listen to my words with respect. I am speaking to you the words which shatter the pride of all and are correct.

None of you should be so arrogant. There is some other god who happens to be the performer as well as the destroyer. In your pride, you have forgotten Siva.

O Gods, in case you are really proud of your strength, then you should cut off the blade of grass just placed by me before you.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, Siva in the form of Yaksa, placed a blade of grass before them and accordingly shattered the pride of all the gods.

Thereafter all the gods including Visnu, who considered themselves to be quite strong, displayed their individual strength using all their weapons.

Because of the influence of Siva, who shattered the pride of all the gods, the efforts made by them were of no avail.

Then there was a divine voice from the sky, which relieved the gods of the surprise, that Yaksesvara was none else but Siva himself, who shatters the pride of all.

He is the Paramesvara- the performer, the real preserver as well as the destroyer. All are valorous because of his strength. Otheiwise no one is quite strong.

Having been influenced with his Maya, you have not been able to recognise Siva, your own lord, nor could you know about the reality of your own lord who is the form of knowledge.”

In this way, listening to the words of the divine voice from the sky, the pride of all gods disappeared in a moment. Then the gods, offered their salutation to Siva in the form of Yaksesvara, eulogising him at the same time.

The gods said, “O Mahadeva- the god o: gods, you are the destroyer of the pride of all O Yaksesvara, performer of the great sports, C Lord, your Maya is quite astonishing.

Having been influenced with your Maya in the form of Yaksa, even today we treat ourselves separate, because of our pride.

O Lord, O Sankara, by your grace, we have attained the knowledge of truth that you are the creator, the preserver and the destroyer as well.

You are the operator of all the Saktis and withdraw them also. You are the lord of all, the supreme soul, indestructible and unique.

O Merciful one, you, in the form of Yaksesvara, have shattered the pride of all of us. Therefore, we accept your grace.”

Therefore the Yaksesvara, bestowing his grace on all the gods, rendering several types of advice to them disappeared from the scene.

Thus the incarnation of the pleasant form of Yakses'vara has been described. When pleased, he makes the devotees fearless. This is the spotless episode, is the remover of the pride of all, and bestows daily to the noble people, peace, pleasure and salvation.

A satvika person, who listens to this story with devotion, he achieving all his desires, ultimately attains salvation.

## Chapter 17 - The ten incarnations of Siva with Sakti

Nandisvara said, “Now you listen to the ten incarnations of Siva including that of Mahakala, as found in the Upasana Kanda.

Mahakala happens to be one of them, who provides devotion as well as the salvation to the noble people. Mahakali happens to be his Sakti, who fulfills the desires of the devotees.

The second incarnation is that of Tara having Tara as his Sakti. Both of them bestow comfort to their devotees.

The third incarnation is that of Bhuvanesa and his Sakti is called as Bala. Both of them bestow comforts to the noble people.

The fourth incarnation is that of Srividyesa and his Srividya is known as sodasT. Both of them provide devotion and salvation to their devotees.

Bhairava happens to be the fifth incarnation of Siva and Bhairavi in his Sakti. They fulfill the desires of their devotees.

The sixth incarnation is that of Chinnamastaka, and his Sakti is known as Chinamusta. Both of them fulfil the desire of his devotees.

The seventh incarnation is that of Dhumavan. Dhumavati happens to be his Sakti. Both of them fulfil the desire of their devotees.

The eighth incarnation of Siva, is that of Bagalamukha. Bagalamukhi, happens to be his Sakti.

The ninth incarnation is that of Matanga and Matangi is the wife of Siva, who happens to be his Sakti. She fulfills all the desires.

Kamala happens to be the tenth incarnation of Siva, which bestows the devotion as well as the salvation. Kamala or Girija happens to be his Sakti. She protects her devotees.

These ten incarnations of Siva, provide always the worldly pleasure and salvation to their devotees.

The one who adores the ten forms of Siva with an umblemished and spotless mind, daily, he achieved several types of comforts.

In the Tantra literature these ten incarnations of Siva have been described. By adoring them, all the desires are fulfilled.

O Sage, the astonishing type, of glory of these eternal Saktis, has been highlighted in the Tantra-literature, who fulfil all the desires.

In the activities like the killing of the enemies, the aforesaid Saktis are taken to be the best. They punish the wicked people and increase the Brahmateja.

O Brahman, Mahakala, and other Saktis of Siva, have been described by me with his ten incarnations.

During all the festivities relating to Siva, whosoever recites this episode, or listen to it, he becomes immensely dear to Siva.

In case a Brahmana recites the same, he achieves the Brahmateja, a Ksatriya becomes victorious, the Vaisya achieves the wealth, while the Sfldra becomes comfortable.

The followers of Siva, while listening to this episode, become more comfortable and get more devoted to Siva.

## Chapter 18 - Eleven incarnations of Siva for the protection of the gods

Nandisvara said, “Now you listen to the eleven incarnations of Siva listening to which the sins earned out of the telling of lie, do not trouble a person.

In earlier times, once Indra getting defeated from the Daityas, fled away from Amravatl, deserting his abode.

Terrified from the Daityas, all the gods went to the great sage Kasyapa, and with folded hands, lowering their shoulders, getting upset, they offered their salutation the sage.

The gods then submitted to the sage with respect, the way they had been defeated by the Daityas. They narrated the tale of their sufferings to him.

O Dear one, the father of the Daityas (Kasyapa) listening to the prayer of the gods was not much moved.

O Sage, Kasyapa with a peaceful mind, assured the gods to keep patience, went to Kasi, the city of Visvesvara.

Taking the appropriate bath in the Ganga, he adored Siva, with Parvati.

Then he consecrated a Sivalinga, with welfare of the gods in his mind, he performed severe tapas for Siva.

O Sage, then devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, Kasyapa kept on performing penance for long.

Then Siva, who was the friend of the distressed and abode of the noble people, appeared before Kasyapa in order to bestow a boon to him.

Then Siva, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees said to Kas'yapa, the best of his devotees, “Ask for a boon”.

Then the sage Kasyapa the grandson of Brahma, delightfully looking at Siva, started offering prayer to the lord, with his hand folded.

Kasyapa said, “You are always engaged in meditation, are indestructible, unique, lord of all, the supreme soul, well-disposed towards those who take refuge in you.

You are the form of Sakti, protector of the noble people, kin of the distressed, protector of the devotees.

O Lord, all the gods are devoted to you and are feeling painful at their defeat at the hands of the Daityas. You kindly protect them.

Lord Visnu is unable to do so, therefore I am troubling you. They have approached me for redress of their grief and in turn, I have meditated on you for the purpose.

O Mahes'vara, I have taken refuge with you for all purpose. Granting my wish you remove the miseries of the gods.

O Lord of gods, I feel particularly painful because of the misery of my sons. You provide comfort to me, because you happen to be the helper of the gods.

O Lord, you better please the gods by killing the Daitya, who happen to be my son and have defeated the gods and the Yaksas.

O Lord Siva, kindly help the gods always because the demons cause injury to them.

Nandisvara said, “At the words thus spoken by Kas'yapa, Siva- the lord of all, disappeared in full view of all saying, “Be it so”.

The sage Kasyapa too was immensely delighted and reverted to his abode and communicated the news, gracefully to the gods.

Thereafter, Siva in order to be true to his words was born from the womb of Surabhi in eleven forms.

At that point of time the entire atmosphere was turned like Siva alone besides being blissful. All the gods felt delighted together with the sage Kasyapa.

The eleven Rudras viz.: Kapali, Pingala, Bhima, Virupaksa, Vilohita, Sasta, Ajapada, Ahirbudniya, Canda and Bhava, are said to be the sons of Surabhi.

They appeared in the form of Siva in order to establish the task of the gods and to provide comfort to all. The valorous sons of Surabhi, were meant for the help of the gods and they killed the Daityas in the war.

By the grace of Rudra, Indra and other gods defeated the Daityas. The gods then became carefree and started ruling with pleasure.

Even today, all the Rudras, remain present in the heaven for the protection of the gods.

They are well-disposed towards the devotees, well-versed in performing various types of sports and comfortably live in the city of Tsana.

Crores of Rudras are said to be their attendants, who surround all the three lokas.

O Dear one, thus I have spelt out the eleven incarnations of Siva as Rudra, who bestow pleasure on all.

This is the spotless episode which removes all the sins, besides being graceful, glorious, bestower of long life and fulfills all the desires.

O Dear one, whosoever, carefully listens to this story, or recites it, he enjoying all the pleasures in this world, and achieves salvation ultimately.

## Chapter 19 - The tapas of Atri and birth of Candra, Dattatreya and Durvasa

Nandisvara said, “O Excellent sage, now you lovingly listen to another episode of Siva, in which, for the protection of dharma, he took to the form of Durvasa.

Atri had been a great ascetic and the husband of Anusuya and obeyed the command of Brahma, who happened to be his father.

At the command of Brahma, Atri went with his wife Anusuya for performing tapas for getting a son over the peak of the Tryaksakuta mountain.

They meditating over the bank of the Nirvindhya river, with the application of pranayama, controlled their breath, becoming carefree, performed tapas for a hundred years.

He made a firm resolve in his mind. “That whosoever was the sole and unblepiished lord, would bestow a son to me.”

He spent a lot of time in performing tapas. One day suddenly fire flames emerged out of their bodies.

O Sage, the fire flames scorched all the *lokas,* Indra and other gods, besides the sages.

Thereafter Indra and all other gods suffering from the flames of fire, proceeded on to the abode of Brahma.

O Dear one, offering their salutation to Brahma, they eulogised him and then revealed to him the tale of their sufferings. Then all the gods accompanied with Brahma, went to Visnuloka.

O Sage, reaching there, Brahma and all the gods, offered their salutation to Visnu. After praising him they narrate the tale of their suffering.

Then Brahma and Visnu with all the gods went to the place of Siva. Reaching there, they offering their salutation to him and eulogised him as well.

After eulogising for long, Visnu narrated the tale of the suffering of the gods, saying, “O Siva, the tapas performed by Atri, has produced huge fire flames.”

O Sages there after all the gods present there, besides Brahma, Visnu and Mahes'vara, started consultations among themselves, for the welfare of the world.

Then Brahma, Visnu and Siva, who were the best for the bestowing of the boons, went to the tapobhiimi of Atri.

The sage Atri offered his salutation to all the gods recognising them. On the basis of their attributes, and offered prayers to them.

Then the humble son of Brahma, feeling surprised, spoke to all the three gods- Brahma, Visnu and Siva.

Atri said, “O Brahma, Visnu and Siva, you are adorable in all the lokas. You are the lords and are the creator, preserver as well as the destroyers of the universe.

I, with my wife have been performing tapas for getting a son concentrating on one lord, who is well known in the world.

How have you three- the best in bestowing of the boon, arrived here? You bestow the boon to me, removing my doubt?”

Thus listening to the words of the sage Atri, all the three gods said, “O Best of sages, whatever had you resolved, it would be done in the same manner.

All of us Brahma, Visnu and Siva, bestow similar types of boons. You will have three sons born of the amsas of each one of us.

All the three of them would enhance the glory of the parents besides being themselves quite popular in the world.” Thus speaking all the gods left to their respective places feeling delightful.

The sage Atri also delightfully returned to his abode, receiving the boon. O Sage, after meeting Anusuya, he became blissful.

Thereafter Brahma, Visnu and Siva, were born as sons from the womb of Anusuya, who were delightful at heart and performed several sports.

Moon was bom of the womb of Anusuya from the ams'a of Brahma, but since the gods threw him in the ocean, he emerged out of the same (at the time of the churning of the ocean).

From the amsa of Visnu, Datta was bom from the womb of Anusuya. O Sage, he propagated the best method of Sannyasa.

O Excellent sage, from the amsa of Siva, Durvasa, the propounder of dharma and the best of the sages was born.

Siva, who enhanced the Brahmateja was bom in the form of Durvasa, he tested several people in dharma.

O Excellent sage, there was a king named Ambrisa in the solar race who was tested in dharma by Durvasa. You better listen to the relevant story.

Ambrisa had been the king of the earth surrounded by seven islands.

The king had taken a firm vow that fasting on the eleventh day of a fortnight, he would break his fast on the twelfth day of the same fortnight.

Hearing about the firm resolve of the king, Durvasa once went to him with his disciples.

The king realising that at the time of breaking the fast the Dvadasi was for a short duration and as soon as the became ready to take his food, Durvasa arrived there at the same time. The king invited him for taking food.

Thereafter the sage Durvasa, accompanied with his pupils, went for taking his bath and the sage delayed his return deliberately in order to test the king’s resolve.

Realising the obstruction in the performance of *dharma,* the king with permission of the *Sastras,* only sipped some water and then he kept on waiting for the return of Durvasa.

In the mean time the sage Durvasa also arrived there and apprehending that the king might have taken food, the sage, born of the *amsa* of Siva, who has assumed that form for the testing of piety, became furious with the king. He uttered extremely harsh words for testing his piety.

Durvasa said, “O Base king, after inviting me and without feeding me, you have consumed water. I shall display the fruit thereof, because I punish the evil people.”

After thus speaking, he stood up and his eyes were turned red due to anger. Durvasa then tried to burn him. At once the Sudarsana cakra of Visnu, blazed forth to protect the king and burn the sage, unmindful of the fact that he was an amsa of Siva. It had been deluded by the Maya of Siva.

In the mean time the divine voice spoke to Ambrisa- the noble soul and the devotee of Brahma and Visnu.

The divine voice said, “This Sudarsan cakra was given by Siva to Visnu, therefore, O King, don’t use this cakra for the killing of Durvasa.

Durvasa happens to be the gigantic form of Siva and the cakra was given by Siva to Vi§nu. O King don’t take him to be an ordinary sage.

This ascetic had arrived here to test your dharma. You better take refuge in him otherwise there would be the dissolution of the earth.”

Nandisvara said, “O Excellent sage, the divine voice was quiet after thus speaking. Then the king Ambrisa adored the sage Durvasa, with respect, who had been bom out of the ams'a of Siva praising him at the same time.

Ambrisa said, “In case I had been bestowed with the boon, I had faithfully followed the dharma. In case our race is devoted to the gods and the Brahmanas, then let the cakra of Visnu be peaceful.

In case lord Siva who is well-disposed towards his devotees, then the Sudarsana cakra should particularly be peaceful and harmless.”

Nandisvara said, “When the intelligent Ambrisa, so prayed to Siva, the Sudarsana cakra taking Durvasa to be the ams'a of Siva, was completely subsided.

Then the king Arhbrl?a, bowed in reverence to the sage Durvasa, who had arrived for the test of the king, taking him to be the form of Siva.

The sage having been born of the amsa of Siva, felt pleased with the king and returned to his abode after taking the food.

I have highlighted the story of Durvasa in relation to the test of dharma of Ambrisa. Now sage listen to the other story.

O Sage, then Siva in the form of the sage, tested the promise of Rama, which he had given to Kala.

In the meantime, Durvasa because of his stubbornness sent Laksmana inside the chamber of Rama. O Sage, Sri Rama, because of his promise, disowned his brother Laksmana. This story is quite well known to the people at large and because of the same, I have not repeated the same here.

He, by remaining firm in his dharma, delighted Durvasa, who blessed Rama with a boon.

Then he in the Dvaparayuga, tested the performance of Krsna, as well. O Excellent sage, I am going to narrate the story which you should listen with attention.

At the request of Brahma, Krsna, in order to remove the burden of the earth and for the protection of the noble people, was born on earth as the son of Vasudeva, and was known by the name of Krsna. He killed the evil minded people, the sinful persons, the wicked and saved the Brahmanas and the noble people.

Krsna the son of Vasudeva, also served the Brahmanas variously. He used to serve food to various Brahmanas daily.

When it became well known that Krsna was well-disposed towards the Brahmanas then the sage Durvasa arrived there to meet him.

He then joined the chariot of Krsna and Rukmini, with the chariot of his own started driving the same.

The sage then descended the chariot and finding the firmness of Kr§na, he was pleased with him and bestowed a boon on him to have his body as hard as Vajra.

O Sage, once the auspicious sage Durvasa was taking bath in Devagaiiga. But suddenly he felt shameful because of his becoming nude.

Realising this, Draupadi, tore out a part of her sari and gave it the Durvasa, which could remove the shame of Durvasa.

Finding the piece of cloth floating with the flow of water towards the sage, he covered his private parts and felt delighted.

Thereafter he pronounced a boon on Draupadi for the increasing the length of her cloth. This boon helped the Pandavas at the time of need.

There were two wicked kings named Hamsa and Dimba. They once insulted the sage Durvasa, who destroyed him at the command of lord Visnu.

Durvasa the great sage, particularly established Sannyasa-vidhi appropriately on earth, besides the Brahmateja.

By delivering excellent discourses, he redeemed several worldly beings and several of them were bestowed with salvation.

In this way, the sage Durvasa, displayed several sports, discussing about which the humans feel graceful. Their age and glory are enhanced. This story fulfills all the desires.

The one who listens to the story of Durvasa with devotion, or recites it to others, he becomes comfortable in this as well as the future world.

## Chapter 20 - Incarnation of Hanuman and the related story

Nandisvara said, “ O Sage, now you listen to the story of Hanuman and the way in which lord Siva taking to the form of Hanuman indulged in various types of sports.

O Brahmana, the way in which lord . Siva did good to Sri Rama and the story which bestows welfare to all may pleased be listened from me.

The virtuous Siva, who is engaged in various types of sports, once witnessed the Mohini form of Siva.

Like a person suffering from lust, Siva at the instance, the saptarsis, (the swan sages) carried the semen of Siva, for the purpose of Sri Rama, with respect, over the tree leaf and inserted the same in the ear of AnjanI the daughter of Gautama, through ear to her womb.

Then after some time, Siva appeared in the form of a monkey by name of Hanuman who was quite valorous.

The excellent monkey Hanuman, was quite powerful ever since his birth. He is the early morning taking the solar disc to be a ripe fruit, swallowed it.

At the prayer of the gods, he released the sun. The valorous monkey, the incarnation of Siva, was bestowed with boons by all the gods and the ascetics.

Hanuman, getting pleased, went to his mother and narrated all the happenings to her with respect.

At the command of his mother, the intelligent Hanuman, went to the sun and learnt all the lores, without much efforts.

Then Hanuman, who was born of the amsa of Siva at the command of his mother, went to Sugriva, who was born of the amsa of the sun.

Bali, the elder brother of Sugriva, who was having relationship with Sugriva's wife, turned him out of his house.

The he became the courtier of Sugriva. Having been born out of the amsa of Siva, he did good to Sugriva.

After the abduction of Sita, Hanuman made Rama who had arrived with his younger brother, a friend of Sugriva.

Sri Rama killed Bali, who has been enjoying the company of his younger brother's wife, and when he considered himself to be immensely powerful,

O Dear one, then at the command of Rama, Hanuman in the company of several monkeys, searched for Sita.

Learning about the presence of Sita in Lanka, the monkey king Hanuman crossed the in accessible ocean, which could not be crossed by others.

Reaching there he performed enormous astonishing feats, and handed over he finger ring to Sita which had been given to him by Rama.

Hanuman, the great warrior, narrated to Sita, the story of Rama, which saved her life and removed her grief.

Destroying the garden of Ravana, Hanuman killed the demons, carrying the mudrika given by Sita to him, Hanuman returned to Rama.

Then Hanuman, the performer of the enormous divine sports, created enormous disturbances in Lanka besides killing Aksaya kumara, the son of Ravana quite fearlessly.

O Sage, then Ravana, firmly coiled the clothes soaked in oil around his tail, capturing him, and ignited the fire.

Then Hanuman, bom out of the amsa of Siva, jumped from one place to another and burnt the entire Lanka.

The king among the monkeys, then burnt out the entire Lanka, leaving the house of Vibhlsana. Hanuman then himself jumped into the ocean.

Extinguishing the fire flames of his tail, he went to the other shore of the ocean, Hanuman, the amsa of Siva, then, delightfully went to Sri Rama.

The forceful Hanuman rapidly went to Rama, and handed over the cudamani of Sita to him.

Thereafter at the command of Rama, the monkey warriors, built a bridge over the ocean with stones and the mountains.

Then Rama with the desire of crossing the ocean, for becoming victorious over Ravana, consecrated a Sivalinga over the seashore, adoring it at the same time.

Receiving boon from the ocean, crossing the ocean, Rama surrounded the entire Lanka, Rama fought with the demons with the help of the monkeys.

He brought Laksmana back to life who had been hurt with the attack of a Sakti, by brining Sanjivani.

Then Hanuman, the son of Mahadeva on the other hand, killing the demons, protecting the army of Rama, pleased both Rama and Laksmana and saved their entire army.

The immensely valorous Hanuman destroyed Ravana with his relatives, without much efforts, making the gods quite comfortable.

Then Hanuman, killed Mahiravana and safely brought back Rama and Laksmana from his place.

In this way the excellent monkey, expeditiously performed the task of Rama. He also shattered the pride of the demons and indulged in various types of the divine sports.

He established the adoration of Rama on earth and himself becoming an excellent devotee of Rama, made Rama and Sita quite comfortably.

He was the destroyer of the pride of all the gods, redeemed the devotee, and was the incarnation of Rudra.

Hanuman was immensely valorous, a great warrior and was always engaged in the task of Rama. He acted as the messenger of Rama, killed the Daityas, and was well-disposed towards his devotees.

O Dear one, thus I have narrated to you the excellent story of Hanuman, which bestows riches and cereals, besides fulfilling all the desires.

A person, who listens to it attentively, he enjoying all the pleasures achieves moksa ultimately.

## Chapter 21- Curse of Parvati to Bhairava to be born as a human

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, O Son of Brahma, now listen to the excellent incarnation of Siva, which removes all the desires.

O Great sage, once, Siva and the great goddess Parvati, became desirous of enjoying sports.

They kept Bhairava as the guard, they went inside the forest and behaving like ordinary human beings, they were served by many attendants lovingly.

O Sage, both of them were engaged in various types of sports of their own liking for long. Both of them were highly delighted.

The independent goddess Parvati, sportily took to the form of mad woman and with the permission of lord Siva, came near the door in that form itself.

Fascinated with her attractive form, Bhairava glanced at her as an ordinary woman and stopped her from going out.

O Sage, when Bhairava glanced at her like an ordinary woman, then she got enraged and then she pronounced a curse on him.

Siva said, “O Degraded person, you are looking at me like an ordinary woman, therefore O Bhairava, you go to the earth and became a Bhairava in human form.”

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, there was a commotion when the curse was pronounced on Bhairava by Parvati. Bhairava on the other hand felt extremely painful.

O Excellent sage, then Siva atonce went to Bhairava, tried to appease him variously reassuring him at the same time.

O Sage, because of the curse of the goddess, and with the desire of Siva, the said Bhairava was reborn as Vaitala in human form.

Because of their love for him, both Siva and Parvati, behaving as humans also incarnated on earth.

O Sage, Siva in the form of Mahesa and Sarada in the form of Girija indulged in various types of sports on earth.

O Dear one, in this way I have described the excellent story of Mahesa before you. This story bestows people with riches, the cereals, the auspicious glory, and long life. It also fulfils all the desires.

Whosoever listens or recites the same with devotion, he enjoying all the pleasures on earth, ultimately achieves moksa.

## Chapter 22 - Visnu’s enjoying the company of divine damsels born out the ocean

Nandisvara said, “O Intelligent son of Brahma, O Excellent sage, now you listen to the incarnation of Siva as Vrsa, in which form he shattered the pride of Visnu.

In earlier times, the gods as well as the demons were afraid of the old age as well as the death. Both the gods and demons entered into an agreement and started making endeavours for achieving the gems.

O Son of the sage, the gods and the demons, got ready for the churning of the ocean of milk.

With the serene smiles worn on their faces, the gods as well as the demons, started thinking as to how to meet with the success.

Then at the command of lord Siva, the divine voice declared, assuring the gods as well as the demons.

The divine voice said, “O Gods an the Daityas, you churn the ocean of milk in which your prowess as well as the intelligence would be helpful.

Mandaracala should be made the churning rod, let the serpent Vasuki serve as a churning rope. You should collectively and gracefully chum it.

NandlsVara said, “O Excellent sage”, both the gods as well as the demons, listening to the divine voice, started making efforts for the completion of the task.

The gods as well as the demons, then collectively went to the Mandracala mountain, possessing enormous beauty.

Pleasing him and receiving his approval, they uprooted it with their arms.

O sage, uprooting and lifting it by means of their arms they went to the milk-ocean. Because of the lack of strength, they could not carry it to the ocean of milk.

The heavy Mandaracala mountain slipped out of their hands and fell over the gods and the Daityas.

Losing courage, all the gods and the Daityas fell down then and there. After sometime, they regained their consciousness and started offering prayer.

Still with their strength and will power, they again carried the mountain Mandaracala and brought it at the northern shore of the ocean and placed in the oceanic waters.

Then the gods and the demons, used the serpent Vasuki as the rope and started churning the ocean for achieving the gems.

At the start of the churning of the ocean, the goddess of the heaven, the daughter of Bhrgu, Laksmi, the beloved of Hari, emerged out of the ocean.

Thereafter Dhanvantri the physician, the moon, Kalpavrksa, the horse known as Uccaisrava, the elephant Airavata, the wine, the Saranga bow of Visnu, the conch, Kamadhenu, Kaustabha gem as well as the nectar emerged out of the ocean.

When churned again, Kalakuta- the terrific poison, resembling the fire of the time of dissolution, emerged from the ocean of milk.

The drops of the nectar, which fell outside, while it emerging out of the ocean, gave birth to the damsels with heavenly beauty.

They had the faces resembling the full moon of the winter season, the lustre like the lightening, adorned with garlands, êṛóīãṁ, kataka and the divine gems.

These damsels were spreading their nectar like beauty in all the ten directions and intoxicating the entire universe with their sharp and carved looks.

Crores of such damsels emerged out of the drops of nectar. Thereafter, emerged nectar which removed the death and the old age.

Laksmi, samkha (conch), the kaustabha- gem, and the sword was taken by lord Visnu. The horse- Uccaisrava was owned gracefully by the sun.

The Parijata tree and Airavata- the king of the elephants were accepted gracefully by Indra, the husband of Saci.

Lord Siva, at his own sweet will, lodged the poison Kalakuta in his throat, for the protection of the gods. He also placed the crescent moon over his head.

O Vyasa, overpowered with the delusion of Siva, the Daityas owned the wine. Rest of the people accepted Dhanvantri.

O Sages, the cow Kamadhenu was also owned by the ascetics. The other damsels taking to the form of Mohini, remained unmoved.

There had been a great war between the gods and the Danavas, over the possession of the nectar and for becoming victorious.

O Vyasa, Bali and other Daityas, having the lustre like the sun and the fire of the time of dissolution, were victorious over the gods and usurped the nectar from them.

Because of the illusion of Siva, the gods like Indra and others, getting terrified from the demons, took refuge with lord Siva, getting upset.

O Sage, thereafter, the nectar, at the command of Siva, was snatched away from the Daityas by Visnu in the form of Mohini.

Visnu who was the foremost of the illusory people, taking to the form of Mohini, cast a spell on all the asuras and made the gods to consume the entire nectar.

Approaching the damsel Mohini, the Daitya kings said, “Serve us the nectar as well. Don’t indulge in discrimination.

Thus speaking all the Daityas and Danavas, deluded by the Maya of Siva, gave the nectar to Visnu in disguise.

In the meantime looking at the damsels born out of the nectar drops, the leading Danavas took them to their abodes according to their convenience.

Maya built the cities for those damsels which were hundred times more beautiful than the heaven. They were well fortified mechanically.

The cities thus built were well guarded by the Daityas and then they all set out for fighting with the gods taking the pledge to fight, even without embracing the damsels.

Then the Daityas, getting anxious for war, they declared, “In case we are unable to be victorious over the gods, then we shall not touch these damsels.”

They started filling the sky uttering the lion’s roar individually and with the sound of the blowing of the conches, they started pleasing the clouds.

Then the Daityas and the gods fought such a terrific war which became famous in the three worlds.

With the protection provided by Visnu, the gods were victorious. The gods led by Visnu killed many demons and the rest fled away from the battle ground.

The Daitya who had been overpowered with the illusion of Visnu, were killed by the gods, and those who escaped death retired to the nether world.

The valorous Visnu also holding the cakra in his hand, followed them. Those Dahyas felt frightened while living there.

At the same time Visnu spotted the damsels born out of the drops of nectar.

Fascinated by the cupid's arrows Visnu attained highest pleasure only there. He began to indulge in sexual dalliance with those women of exquisite beauty.

Visnu produced from those damsels extremely valorous sons who were well- versed in the warfare, who started shaking the entire world

Those sons of Visnu, having great strength and prowess, created great havoc both in the heaven and earth causing misery to all.

Observing the great harm done to the world at large, the gods and sages approached Brahma and apprised him of the factual position, bowing in reverence to him.

O hearing them, Brahma led them to the mountain Kailasa. Meeting Siva, he bowed in reverence to him again and again, together with the gods.

With their hands folded, lowering their shoulders, reciting several stotras they eulogised to Siva, the supreme lord who is always victorious.

Brahma said, “O Mahadeva, the god of gods, O Lord, you better save the entire world from the blemished sons of Visnu.

O Lord, Visnu getting attracted towards the damsels emerging out of the nectar drops, has become lustful and lives in the nether world.”

Nandisvara said, “In order to call back Visnu for the protection of the universe, Brahma together with the god and the ascetics, prayed to Siva for long.

Then, the ocean of mercy, Mahesvara, lord Siva, understanding the trouble, took to the form of a bull.

## Chapter 23 - Visnu’s fight with the Bull form of Siva

Nandisvara said, “Then Siva taking to the form of a bull, holding a bow named Pinaka ir his hand, entered Patalaloka while thundering.

With the thundering sound of Siva, several of the cities were razed to the ground. All the dwellers of the cities, started shaking.

Then the bull faced the sons of Visnu who had been under the illusion of Siva.

O Excellent sage, the sons of Visnu, finding the bull bellowing aloud rushed to face him, thundering aloud.

Then Siva in the form of a bull getting enraged, moved forward, and tore out the sons of Visnu with his horns and the hoofs.

All the sons of Visnu, after having been tom by the bull- Siva, died on the spot.

Then Visnu, the foremost of the valorous people, finding his sons having been killed, came out of his abode and rushed to face Siva, thundering aloud.

Visnu, finding that Rudra in the form of a bull was leaving the place, he attacked him shooting several of his arrows.

Then immensely valorous Siva in the form of the hug mountain like bull swallowed all the weapons of Visnu.

O Sage, then, Siva in the form of a bull, getting furious, shaking all the three lokas, thundered aloud.

Then the lord Vrsa atonce jumped disregarding the enraged Visnu, tore him out with his horns and hoofs.

Thereafter, having been overpowered with the Maya of Siva, feeling fatigued, Visnu, getting injured, could not bear the attack.

He fainted and his pride was shattered. On regaining consciousness, he realised that it was Siva in the form of a bull who was roaming about.

When Visnu came to realise about the truth of Siva the husband of Parvati having arrived in the form of a bull, then he, with his hands folded, lowering his shoulders, spoke to him.

Visnu said, “O Lord, O Mahadeva, the god of gods, ocean of mercy, having been overpowered with your Maya, I had lost my wisdom.

O Lord, you are my lord in the form of Vrsa, and entering into a conflict with you, I would like to be pardoned for that sin.”

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, listening to the humble words of Visnu, lord Siva spoke to the lord of Laksmi. “O immensely intelligent Visnu, how could you not recognise me? You fought with me. How could your entire wisdom fade out?

Though you are subservient to me, still you are unaware of yourself. Don’t enjoy the company of these damsels. You better detract yourself from this misconduct.

O Lord of gods, you are enjoying the company of these women having been overpowered with lust, which is improper for you because the lustful person is deprived of all the knowledge, whereas your name redeems a person.”

Listening to the knowledgeable words of Siva, feeling ashamed in his mind, Visnu spoke to Siva. Visnu said, “My Cakra is here. I shall carry the discus and return to my place respecting your words with reverence.”

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of Visnu, Siva in the form of the bull, again spoke to Visnu.

“O Visnu, at my command, don’t delay any further. You leave this place atonce, leaving your cakra here.

I shall give you another cakra which would be more terrible than the sun of the time of dissolution and more efficacious than the words of Siva.

After thus speaking, Siva created another cakra as illumining as the Kala or fire, for the destruction of the wicked.

He gave the cakra as resplendent as the ten thousand fierce suns, to Visnu the supreme soul, the preceptors of the gods and the prominent sages.

After receiving another Sudarsana cakra containing more lustre, Visnu the foremost of the intelligent gods, spoke to the gods, “O Gods, you listen to my words anxiously and act rapidly and atonce. It will be to your advantage.

There are divine young girls in the nether world. Anyone can enjoy their company at will.”

Listening to these words of Visnu, all the valorous gods got ready to enter the nether world with Visnu.

Lord Siva, realising the truth about the bent of mind of the gods, pronounced a terrific curse on the eight type of gods.

Siva said, “Whosoever, except the Daityas and the sages bom of my athsa would go to Patala, he would meet with his death instantaneously.

Listening to the words of Siva, who does good to the people, all the gods retired to their respective abodes.

O Vyasa, in this way Siva punished Visnu who had turned lustful for women. Thereafter he returned to the heaven and the people of the world became comfortable.

Then Siva who had taken to the form of a bull, who is well-disposed towards the devotees, thus disciplining Visnu, establishing the task of the gods, went back to Kailasa.

Siva is the destroyer of the illusion of Visnu, who bestows comforts to all the three worlds, and his incarnation as the bull has been described by me.

This is the auspicious story which destroys the enemy’s obstructions, bestows heaven, glory, long life, pleasures and salvation.

A person, who listens or recites the same with pleasure and alertness, or reads or makes others to read the same, he enjoying all the pleasures on earth and attains liberation ultimately.

## Chapter 24 - Siva’s incarnation as Pippalada

Nandisvara said, “O Intelligent are, I, now with my heart filled with devotion, narrate the incarnation of Siva as Pippalada, which should be lovingly listened by you.

This story was initially told by Dadhici, who was a great Saiva Brahmana, belonging to the glorious Bhrgu race and son of the excellent sage Cyavana. He had defeated Visnu while fighting with the sage Ksava and with the help of Siva, Visnu was cursed.

Suvarca the wife of Dadhici was an extremely chaste woman, who had cursed the gods.

Lord Siva appeared from her womb as Pippalada who was well-versed in performing various divine sports.

Suta said, “Thus listening to the astonishing words of Nandisvara, the excellent sage Sanatkumara spoke with folded hands.

Sanatkumara said, “O Immensely intelligent one, O Nandisvara, Brahma had earlier told me the story of the curse as well.

Now I would like to listen to the episode of Suvaraca’s pronouncing a curse on Visnu. I shall listen to the story of Pippalada later.

Suta said, “Thus the son of Silada, listening to the auspicious words of Brahma’s son, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, spoke delightfully.

Nandisvara said, “O Excellent sage, Once Indra and all other gods were defeated at the hands of Vrtrasura and his Daitya army.

In the cottage of the sage Dadhici, all the gods were seated getting disgusted after their defeat at the hands of Daityas, throwing away their weapons.

Then Indra and other gods, and the sages suffering at the hands of the Daityas, reached the Brahmaloka and started narrating to Brahma, the tale of their sufferings.

Listening to the words of the gods and those of Visvakarma, Brahma said, “O Gods, Vrtrasura the lord of all the Daityas is quite powerful. Visvakarma has got him for the purpose of the killing of the gods.

O Intelligent one, now you should move in a way in which he could be killed. I am speaking the way out for the protection of dharma which you please listen attentively.

Dadhici- the great sage, is great ascetic who lias controlled all his senses. In the ancient times, he had received a boon frc.n Siva, that his bones should be turned as hard like the Vajra.

You should go to Dadhici and ask for his bones. He will surely give them to you.”
