Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of Brahma, Indra- the lord of gods, together with Brhaspati and other gods, went to the abode of the sage Dadhici.

Indra, found Dadhici with Suvarca in the asrama. Brhaspati and other gods offered their salutation to the sage with folded hands.

The learned sage, well understanding the intentions of the gods, sent Suvarca inside the as'rama.

Then the selfish Indra, accompanied by the gods bent upon achieving his own object, and most efficient in polity said to the great sage.

Indra said, “All of us- the gods and the sages, having been fed up with the misbehaviour of Vrtra, have arrived here. You are a great devotee of Siva, as well as the great donor. We have arrived here to take refuge with you.

O Brahmana, you kindly give us your bones to enable us make Vajra for the killing of the treacherous Daitya.”

At these words of Indra, the sage who always believed in doing good to others, devoting his mind to lord Siva, ended his life.

Then the sage having been relieved of all the bondages, proceeded on to Brahmaloka, where the rain of flowers on him, was showered, which surprised all.

Thereafter, he called for the Matrika Surabhi on earth asked her to consume the flesh of the sage. Then he commanded Vis'varkarma to make a Vajra out of the bones of the sage.

At the command of Visvakarma, with the power of Siva, he made Vajra from the bones.

The Vajra that was made of the back-bone of the sage, it was given the name of Brahmasirasara, other weapons were made of the other bones of the sage. O Sage, with the combination of the valour of Siva, Indra, holding that Vajra, getting enraged rushed towards Vrtrasura, as Rudra rushes towards Yama.

Then Indra, getting ready, cut off the head of Vrtrasura like the mountain peak with the Vajra.

O Dear one, then the dwellers of the heaven rejoiced in their minds. The delightful gods showered the rain of flowers over Indra.

O Dear one, this story has been narrated to you with reference to the context. Now you listen from me about the Pippalada incarnation of Siva.

Suvarca- the dutiful and the chaste wife of Dadhici entered inside the asrama at the command of the sage Dadhici.

When she completing all the household jobs, came out of her abode then she did not find her husband there.

O Excellent sage, she was taken aback witnessing the grave act performed by the gods.

Observing this evil deed of the gods, Suvarca was enraged and she pronounced a curse on the gods

Suvarca said, “O Wicked gods, all of you are too selfish and greedy. All of you should become animals from today onwards.”

Thus Suvarca, a woman sage and the beloved wife of the sage, cursed the gods including Indra.

The chaste lady, made a pyre, collecting the wood in order to end her life with her husband, which was put to flames.

At the same time the divine voice from the sky was heard at the instance of Siva, which provided comforts, and assuring her at the same time.

The aerial divine voice declared, “O Intelligent one, don’t indulge in killing yourself. The tejas of the sage is enshrined in your womb. You should give birth to the child making all the efforts.

Thereafter, you can do whatever you like, because it has been ordained by Brahma, that a pregnant wife should never enter the fire flames.”

Nandisvara said, “O Excellent sage, the divine voice stopped after thus speaking, listening to which the wife of the sage was surprised for a moment.

The chaste lady who was anxious to follow her husband and in order to abort the child she tore out her belly with a stone.

From her womb, a child the tejas of the sage, having enormous lustre, illuminating the ten directions appeared in the form of a male child.

O Dear one, from the tejas of Dadhici the child born resembled the incarnation of Rudra, who could indulge in his own lovely sports.

Suvarca looking at the divine child the incarnation of Rudra, felt delighted. Then she offered her salutation to the child and praised him, O Excellent sage. Then she lodged that form of Siva in her heart.

Then Suvarca having the spotless mind, and desirous of joining her husband in the heaven, smilingly spoke to the child.

Suvarca said, “O Dear one, O Supreme Isan, you stay under the pipal tree for long, and make all the people comfortable.

You allow me to go to the abode of my husband. Living there with my husband, I shall take care of you- the form of Rudra.”

Nandisvara said, “Suvarca thus spoke to her son. Thereafter, she entering the samadhi, proceeded on to her husband.

O Sage, in this way, the wife of Dadhici, reaching her husband, in Sivaloka, started serving Siva.

In the meantime, Indra and other gods, besides the sages, delightfully arrived, at the invitation.

Then Brahma and Visnu, knowing about the incarnating of Siva with the union of Dadhici and Suvarca, on earth, reached there on earth with their ganas.

Finding that Siva had been incarnated in the form of the son of the sage Dadhici, they eulogised him with folded hands.

O Excellent sage, the gods then celebrated the occasion delightfully. The big drums were beaten, and the dancers started dancing.

The Gandharvas and Kirnaras started playing over the musical instruments, while singing.

Pippalada the illustrious son of Dadhici, was appropriately consecrated. Then Brahma, Visnu and other gods eulogised him again.

The delighted Brahma, gave him the name of Pippalada. Then Visnu and other gods said, “O Lord of the gods, be pleased.”

Alter saying this, and celebrating great jubilation, Brahma, Visnu and the other gods, reverted to their respective abodes.

Then Rudra, the great lord in the form of Pippalada, performed tapas for a long time at the foot of the fig tree with the sole desire of bestowing welfare on the worlds.

While Pippalada was so performing the tapas as per the earlier conventions of the universe, a long time elapsed.

## Chapter 25 - The story of the Pippalada incarnation of Siva

Nandisvara said, “O Excellent sage, with the desire of establishing of the dharma, on earth, Pippalada- the form of Siva indulged in the several types of sports. You listen to the same with grace.

Once the sage Pippalada, went to take bath in the Puspabhadra river, where he met with a damsel named Padma, who was also born of the amsa of Siva.

With a desire of get her, Pippalada, who had been well-versed in all the tattvas and who could roam about in the three worlds freely, went to the king Anaranya- the father of the girl.

The king was frightened at the sight of the sage, who offered his salutation to the sage. Offering the madhuparka, he adored him with devotion.

Accepting his worship and the devotion, the sage asked for the hand of his daughter.

The sage said to the king, “You give away your daughter to me, otherwise, I shall reduce to ashes yourself and all others in no time.”

O Great sage, with the lustre of Pippalada, the son of Dadhici, all the kins of the king were upset.

Thereafter the frightened king, lamenting again and again, decorating his daughter Padma, gave her away to the old sage Pippalada.

The delightful sage Pippalada after marrying the princess, went back to his hermitage.

Reaching there, the ascetic with simple temperament though pretty old started living with his wife Padma.

Thereafter the said daughter of the king Anaranya, started serving the sage, with her actions, thought and behaviour as Laksmi serves Visnu.

Thus Pippalada having been born of the amsa of Siva, becoming young, started enjoying the company of his wife.

The recluse sage, begot ten sons from Padma, who was a worthy as their own father and who increased the delight of Padma.

Thus Pippalada the incarnation of great lord Siva, indulged in various types of sports.

Observing the harassment caused by the planet Saturn, which had no remedy, Pippalada lovingly, granted a boon to the entire world.

From sixteenth years from birth, none will have that affliction. Similarly the devotees of Siva, will remain unaffected by the influence of Sani. These words of mine will be true.”

In case Saturn disregards my words, and still harasses men, he will surely be reduced to ashes.

O Dear, thus, getting afraid of Pippalada, the excellent planet, Saturn, inspite of living in the cruel place, because of the fear of Pippalada, does not cause any harm to the devotees of Siva.

O Excellent sage, the story of the excellent sports of Pippalada the humari form of Siva, has been narrated by me.

By remembering the three ascetics like Visvamitra, Kausika, and Pippalada, the pain caused by the influence of Saturn is subsided.

A person, on earth should read or listen to the story of Padma and Pippalada, which is the best for the pacifying the pain or harassment caused by Saturn. By reading or listening to the same, all the desires are fulfilled.

Graceful is the great intellectual Dadhici, who was dear to Siva and Pippalada was born to him from the amsa of Siva.

O Dear one, this episode bestows the auspicious heaven and the merits and also removes the pain of the harsh planets. It fulfills all the desires and enhances devotion towards Siva.

## Chapter 26 - Vaisyanatha incarnation of Siva

Nandisvara said, “O Dear one, O Sage, I am now going to narrate about the incarnation of Siva as Vaisyanatha which bestows delight to all. You better listen to the same attentively.

In earlier times, there lived a whore in the village of Nandlgrama. She was quite beautiful, popular and the devotee of Siva.

She possessed many fortunes, wealth and was immensely beautiful, besides being charming and attractive.

She was well-versed in all the musical lores and pleasant to look at; listening to her song and music all the people including the king and the queen felt delighted.

The whose daily adored Siva and Parvati. She muttered the name of Siva and also wore the ashes and Rudraksa over her body.

Adoring Siva, the lord of the world, she used to serve both of them. She sang the auspicious glory of Siva, she danced before him.

She decorating a monkey and a cock, with Rudraksa made them dance daily, clapping her hands.

Observing them both dancing, and overwhelmed with the devotion of Siva, the whore, laughed aloud with her maids.

The trained monkey having been adorned with the ear ornaments and the armlets of Rudrdksa danced before her like a child.

The tuft of the cock was adorned with Rudraksa which used to dance with the monkey, and pleased the onlookers.

Thus she who was respectfully engaged in the adoration of Siva and remained happy enjoying the fun.

O Excellent sage, thus while the whore was so comfortably engaged in the worship of Siva, a long time passed.

Once Siva himself taking to the form of a Vaisya, in order to test her mental feelings, arrived at the abode of the whore.

Decorating his head with tripundra, wearing the rosary of Rudraksa, reciting the name of Siva, taking to the form of a devotee of Siva, applying ashes over the body, adorning the arms with the best of armlets, wearing the best of gems, looking cheerful, he arrived there.

Finding the arrival of the adorable person, the beautiful whore, delightfully, gave him her own seat with respect.

Finding an extremely beautiful armlet around his arm, she developing the desire to possess the same, spoke to him with surprise.

Mahananda said, “The armlet worn by you around your arm, is attracting my mind. It is best suited for a beautiful woman.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus, finding that the whore was attracted towards the armlet studded with nine types of gems, the large hearted Vaisya said to the whore.” Vaisyanatha said, “In case you desire to receive this divine armlet, then you tell me the price you can offer for the same.

The whore said, “I belong to the class of whores who flirt here and there. I am not a chaste lady. Undoubtedly the usual practice followed in our family is the prostitution.

In case I take this armlet from you, then I shall be your wife for three full days and nights.

The Vaisya said, “O beloved whore, in case your words are true, then let it be as you say. I shall give you the bangle studded with gems. Be my wife for three days and three nights.

In this deal the witnesses are the moon and the sun. Repeat the word “true” thrice and touch my heart, O Beloved.”

The whore said, “O Lord, I shall be your wife for three days and carryout the duties of a wife for that period. This is true. This is true undoubtedly.”

Nandisvara said, “After repeating this three times, Mahananda touched the heart of the Vaisya with pleasure.

The Vaisya, after giving the gems-set armlet, also handed over a linga made of gems, to her said thus -

The Vaisya said, “O My beloved, this gem- set linga is quite dear to me. It should be kept secretly by you making all the efforts.

Nandisvara said, “Well, it will be done accordingly.” Thus speaking the linga of gem, was received by the whore who placed it in the centre of the dancing hall and then entered her home.

The whole night she had the sexual union with the Vaisya who behaved like a libertine. She then went to sleep over the brilliant soft couch.

O Sage, then at midnight, at the desire of the merchant, O Sage, suddenly some noise was heard in the dancing hall.

O Dear one, the flames of fire, with the help of the wind, spread further. The fire burnt out the dancing platform.

Finding the dancing chamber burning, the whore was upset and she released the monkey from the bondage.

The monkey together with the cock fled away escaping from the fire flames to a distant place.

The Sivalinga which the Vais'ya had given to the whore was also burnt out with the pillar and was broken. Both the Vaisya and the whore, felt extremely painful at the destruction of the Sivalinga.

Finding the linga having been burnt, which resembled him, the Vais'ya, in order to know the mental inclination of the whore, got ready to end his life.

Then the Vaisyanatha who had playfully taken to human form, but was none else them Siva himself, declared that he would end his life.

Vaisyanatha said, “O My beloved, with the breaking of the linga, I cannot remain alive. I speak out this truthfully.

O Beautiful one, you ask your servants to prepare a pyre for me. With my mind devoted to Siva, I shall enter the fire.

Even in case Brahma, Visnu, Indra and other gods arrive to stop me from doing so, but I, disregarding them shall enter the fire flames ending my life.

Nandisvara said, “Observing his firm resolve, the whore felt extremely painful. Her servants made a pyre outside the house.

Then the playful Siva in the form of Vaisyanatha, in order to test the association of the whore, in full view of all, he circumambulated the burning pyre and then entered the fire flames.

O Excellent sage, the damsel Mahananda, was taken aback at his performance and started repenting.

Then the miserable whore, getting reminded of the auspicious dharma, spoke in presence of all the relatives.

Mahananda said, “Receiving the armlet of gems from him I had taken vow that for three days, I shall remain wife of this Vaisya according to the dharma.

The Vaisya has lost his life because of my deed. Therefore, I shall also enter the pyre with him.

The Acaryas speaking the truth had declared that I shall becomes a woman following the dharma. In case I do so, my truth will be protected.

To take refuge of the truth is the best of dharma. One achieves salvation by following the truth. Therefore everything is enshrined in the truth.

Nandisvara said, “Inspite of her relatives trying their best to stop her from entering the fire flames, the woman terrified for the loss of truthfulness, with the firm resolve, got ready to bum herself in the fire flames.

She donated all her property to the Brahmanas, concentrating her mind at the feet of Sadasiva, she circumambulated the fire thrice and she got ready to jump into the fire flames of the pyre.

Devoting her mind at the feet of Siva, the whore was about to jump into the fire flames, when Siva- the soul of the universe himself prevented her from doing so.

The whore then looked at the three eyed Siva- Candrasekhara, having the lustre of crores of suns and the moons. Getting frightened, she stopped for a moment.'

She was upset, disturbed, and shaking with the tears flowing from her eyes. Holding her hand the lord assured her.

Siva said, “I have arrived here in order to test your truthfulness, dharma, patience, besides your devotion towards me taking to the form of a Vaisya.

With the help of my Maya, I put to flames your dance platform, besides the linga of gems and then I entered the fire flames.

In order to uphold the truth, you got ready to enter the fire flames with me. Therefore, I would bestow pleasures to you which are inaccessible to others.

O Beautiful one, I shall give you whatever is desired by you. I am pleased with your devotion. There is nothing in the universe, which cannot be given to you.”

Nandisvara said, “At these words of Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees and is the lord of Gauri, the whore Mahananda said to Siva.”

Mahananda said, “I am not desirous of the pleasures of the earth, heaven as well as the nether world. I need nothing else except the touch of your lotus like feet.

All my male and female servants, besides the kiths and kins, are desirous of having an audience with you, being devoted to you.

You should bestow salvation to them with me so as to enable them to be freed from the bondages of the birth and death, salutation to you.”

Nandisvara said, “Honouring the words of the whore, Mahesvara, accompanied with all of them proceeded on to the heaven.

I have narrated the excellent story of the incarnation of Vaisyanatha, who comforted Mahananda. This story also bestows comforts to the devotees of Siva.

This story of the Vaisyanatha incarnation of Siva is extremely auspicious, bestower of the comfort of Mahananda besides being divine. It bestows everything over the noble people.

A person, who, carefully listens or recites this story, he never falls from dharma in this world, achieves salvation after his death.”

## Chapter 27 - Dvijesvara incarnation of Siva

Nandisvara said, “O Dear, listen to me. I shall narrate to you about the incarnation of Siva, the great soul, as Dvijesvara. It is quite pleasing and bestows comfort to the noble people.

O Dear one, I have already narrated to you the story of the king Bhadrayu, who was blessed by Siva in the form of a bull.

In order to test his patience as well as piety, the lord manifested himself again in the form of a leading Brahmana. The relevant story is being told by me.

O Dear one, the king Bhadrayu, with strength of Rsabhadeva, conquering the enemies in the battle field, occupied the throne.

O Brahma, he was married to the daughter named Klrtimalini, of the king Candrangada and his wife Slmantinl.

O Sage, once the king Bhadrayu, went for a pleasure trip with his wife in a thick forest.

In that beautiful forest, the king sported about along with his beloved queen, who protected those who took refuge with her.

At the same time lord Siva with Parvati arrived in the same forest, started sporting in order to test their dharma.

Both Siva and Parvati, took to the form of a male and female Brahmana couple, and produced a tiger with their Maya.

The tiger rushed towards the Brahmana couple chased by the tiger, and took refuge with the king and the queen. Both of them started crying.

O Dear one, the king Bhadrayu, who was the best among the Ksatriyas, and well- disposed towards those who took refuge with him, found the Brahmana couple crying.

O Excellent sage, the Brahmana couple, who was turned as such because of the Maya of Siva, spoke to the king Bhadrayu getting frightened.

The Brahmana couple said, “O Noble king, you better protect us from this tiger. O Great lord, the tiger has arrived here to devour us both.

It is terrific like the death, frightens all the creatures, and therefore, O Noble king you kindly protect us before he devours us both.

Nandisvara said, “When the king heard the cries of the Brahmana couple, and as soon as he lifted his bow and arrow, by that time the tiger captured the wife of Brahmana.

The Brahmana woman was caught by the tiger who started crying, “O Lord, O My husband, O Siva the preceptor of the world, and so on.” She was caught by the tiger.

By about the same time, the king attacked the tiger with his arrow. The arrows shot by the king over the tiger could do no harm to the beast, as the mountain remains unaffected with fall of the torrential rains.

The powerful tiger, paving been hurt with the arrows of the king, fled away carrying the wife of the Brahmana.

Finding that his wife had been carried away by the tiger, the Brahmana felt surprised and started crying as per the prevailing practice.

With his own illusion, Siva in the form of a Brahmana, cried for long, he spoke words which shattered the pride of the king Bhadrayu.

The Brahmana said, “O King, where are your powerful weapons? Where is the huge bow which protects the people? Where is your strength of the twelve thousand elephants?

What is the use of your sword, conch, mantras and the knowledge for the use of the weapons? What could be the use of your satvik virtues, the great weapons?

All the virtues which you possess, have become infructuous today, because you could not save the dwellers of the forest

This is the supreme duty of a Ksatriya that he protects the people from misery. This quality of your race is no more found in you. Then what is the use of your remaining alive.

The king well-versed in dharma, protects the miserable people who take refuge in them, sacrificing their own lives as well as the riches. Without this, they are as good as dead.

The kings who do not came to the rescue of the miserable people, it would be better for the rich householders offering no donations, to be beggars.

Such of the learned persons who are quite miserly in helping the destitues and the poor, it would be better for them to consume the poison or enter the fire flames. This has been ordained.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus listening to his lamenting and the denouncement of his strength and prowess, the king feeling painful at heart started thinking.

Because of my ill-luck today, my prowess and the glory both have been destroyed. I have also attracted the grave sin.

The traditional dharma of my family has been destroyed because of my evil wisdom, therefore all my riches the kingdom and the age would come to an end.

Today, I shall relieve this Brahmana suffering from the separation of his wife who has been seized by the tiger, by surrendering my own life.”

With his resolve in his mind the excellent king Bhadrayu, falling at the feet of the Brahmana, assured him variously.

Bhadrayu said, “O Learned Brahmana, shed away the grief and be merciful on a ksatriya who has lost his strength. I shall give you whatever you desire from me

This entire kingdom, the queen, and my body is subservient to you. What more than this can you expect from me?

The Brahmana said, “What is the use of a mirror to a blind man? What is the use of a house to a beggar? Of What use is the book to a foolish person? And of what use are the riches to a person without a wife?

Thus having been deprived of the wife, I am no more interested in any other enjoyments. You better give away your chief queen to me. This, is exactly what I want.”

Bhadrayu said, “A donor person can donate the sugarcane balls {guda) ghee and other rasas, besides the riches, his own country, elephants, horses, and even his own body, but he cannot donate his own wife.

A person earns a sin by uniting with other's wife and he cannot be absolved of the same sin after repenting for the same repeatedly.

The Brahmana said, “With the performing of the tapas by me, I can get myself absolved of the sins like Brahmahatya and other terrible sins. In comparison to this, enjoying of other's wife is no greater a sin.

Therefore, you give away your wife to me. I need nothing else. Because of your failing to save a frightened person, you would surely be lodged in the hell.”

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of the Brahmana, the panicky king thought.” It is a grave sin to neglect the protection of a frightened person. It is better to give away the wife.

Therefore, by giving away my wife to the Brahmana, getting absolved of the sin, I shall atonce enter the fire flames and earn the glory.”

Having thus resolved in his mind, igniting the fire, he called for the Brahmana and performing the oblation, he gave away his wife in charity.

The king, taking his bath, getting purified, bowing in reverence to the gods and Brahmanas, circumambulating the fire, becoming alert he devoted his mind to Siva.

Then Siva in the form of Dvijesvara. appeared on the scene and stopped his devotee from falling into the fire.

Siva in the form of Candrasekhara, had five faces, three eyes, having the long and yellow locks of hair over the heads, and was resplendent with crores of the Suns of the noon time.

He had the fair complexion resembling the lotus flowers, clad in the elephant hide, served by the waves of the river Ganga over the head, wearing the garland of serpents, around the neck, and adorned with the crown, armlets and wristlets.

He held the trident, Khatvanga, battle axe, dear skin, astariga yoga and the bow called Pinaka as attributes. He was mounted over the bull. This neck was blue like the neck of the peacock. The king saw Siva in that form.

Then the rain of flowers started falling from the sky. The gods started beating the drums in the sky and the apsaras started dancing.

Eulogising Siva, the gods like Brahma, Visnu and other gods besides the sages arrived there.

A huge congregation was held there which enhanced devotion and the king kept on watching the same with folded hands.

The king's heart having been purified at the sight of Siva, felt thrilled and his body was soaked in perspiration. He, with folded hands, and the voice choked, started offering prayer.

Having been so eulogised by the king, the lord Siva- ocean of mercy, with Parvati said delightfully to the king.

“O King, I am extremely pleased with your devotion and dharma. Let you and your wife ask for a boon, which will surely be granted to you.

Indeed, I had taken to the form of a Brahmana in order to test your devotion and the dharma. The woman who was devoured by the lion was none other than Parvati.

This tiger emerged out of my Maya which was immune to the attack of your arrows. I had asked for your wife first in order to test your dharma.”

Listening to these words of Siva, Bhadrayu, bowed in reverence to him, eulogising him at the same time. Then he spoke to him quite humbly.

Bhadrayu said, “O Lord, I only want to seek a single boon. I had been overpowered with the worldly grief and you have appeared before me.

O Lord, O Master, in case you intend to bestow a boon on me, then I intend to seek a single boon from you- the granter of the boons.

O Mahesvara, let my father Vajrabahu with his wife and I with my wife should always remain devoted at your feet and serve you always.

O Mahes'an, you make the Vais'ya named Padmakara, and his son Sanaya to take refuge with you.”

Nandisvara said, “Thereafter his queen Kirtimalini, also felt delighted. She also pleasing Siva, asked for an excellent boon.

The queen said, “O Lord Mahadeva, let my father Citrangada and my mother Slmantanl, dwell always at your feet.”

Nandisvara said, “The lord Siva, who is well-disposed towards his devotees, delightfully said, “Be it so.” Thereafter he disappeared from the scene in a moment.

The king Citrangada and his wife Slmantani, achieved the place of Siva, after achieving the lord.

For ten thousand years, he ruled the country with great prowess, then he entrusting the kingship to his son, proceeded on to the Sivaloka.

The king Bhadrayu having been bestowed with the boon by Siva, enjoyed all the pleasures with his queen Kirtimalini for long.

O Master, I have narrated to you about the excellent story of the Dvijasvara incarnation of Siva, who bestowed the best of his grace on the king Bhadrayu.

This is the description of the auspicious glory of the incarnation of Dvijesvara. By reading or listening to the same, one achieves the Sivapada.

A person who listens or narrates this episode to others, he can never fall from his dharma and achieves salvation ultimately.

## Chapter 28 - Yatinatha incarnation of Siva

Nandisvara said, “O Learned sage, listen, I am going to narrate the blissful story of the Yatinatha incarnation of Siva.

O Munlsvara, over the mountain Arbudacala, there lived a Bhila named Ahuka.

His wife named Ahuka was quite a chaste lady. Both of them were the followers of Siva and used to adore the lord daily.

O Sage, once, the Bhila, in order to get food for his wife penetrated deep into the forest.

In the meantime, at evening Siva reached in the form of an ascetic in order to test her chastity.

In the meantime the Bhila- the owner of the house also arrived. The Bhila having the noble wisdom, adored the ascetic quite lovingly.

In order to know about his intentions, Siva in the form of an ascetic spoke quite pathetic words to the Bhila.

Yatinatha said, “You give me some place in your house to live in. I shall leave this place in the morning. You shall always meet with welfare.”

The Bhila said, “You have spoken the truth. O Master, you listen to my words. There is very little space in my house, how shall you be able to stay here?”

Nandisvara said, “At these words of the Bhila, the ascetic thought of leaving the place. Then the Bhilini thought for a while and said to her husband.

Bhilini said, “O Master, keeping in view the duty of a householder, you provide space to this ascetic. Don’t disappoint the guest. Otherwise there would be the loss of dharma

You sleep with the ascetic comfortably inside, while I shall sleep outside with the weapons.

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the noble words which could bestow merits, the Bhila thought in his mind.

“How can I sleep inside driving the wife out? It would be a sin to send Yatinatha elsewhere. Whatever might happen, I shall sleep outside today.

Thus insisting, the ascetic and the Bhilini, were lodged inside the house, while the Bhila slept outside.

During the night the Bhila was troubled by the cruel animals and he did his best to save himself.

Inspite of all the efforts of the Bhila the wild animals of the forest devoured him.

After rising in the morning the Yati found that the Bhila had been devoured by the wild animals. He felt extremely painful.

Although distressed, the Bhilini suppressing her grief and keeping patience, spoke to the grieved Yatinatha.

The Bhilini said, “O Yatinatha, why are you feeling grieved? Graceful is my husband who met with his end, being successful by serving the guest and doing good to others.

O Yati, I shall also end my life by burning my body with him. You don't bother for me This is the traditional dharma of a woman.”

Listening to her words Yatinatha made the pyre and she, following her dharma entered the pyre.

In the meantime Siva himself appeared on the scene and lovingly spoke, “You are graceful, you are graceful.” These were the words spoken by Siva.

Then Siva said, “O Auspicious soul, I am pleased with your conduct. You better seek a boon. I am subservient to you. There is nothing in the world, which cannot be granted to you.

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the delightful words of Siva, she was pleased and she could remember nothing at that time.

Siva was pleased at his condition and he asked her to seek for a boon.

Siva said, “The ascetic who appeared in my form, would reunite you both in the next birth taking to the form of a swan.

This Bhila would be born as Nala in the Nisada city as son to the immensely glorious king Virasena. There is no doubt about it.

O Auspicious soul, you will be born as the virtuous daughter of the king Bhima of Vidarbha and will be known by the name of Damayanti.

Both of you enjoying the royal pleasures for long, ultimately will achieve a position which is beyond the reach of even the great yogis.

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, Siva himself, because of his dharma, was turned into the form of an immobile linga and for this reason, the linga came to be known as Achalesa.

O Dear one, the Bhila name Ahuka, in his next birth was bom as the prince Nala to the king Virasena of Nisada.

Ahuka, the wife of the Bhila on the other hand, was also bom as daughter of the king Bhima of the Vidarbha country and was known as Damayanti.

The Yatinatha form of Siva was also born as the swan who arranged the marriage of Nala with Damayanti.

Because of the devotion of the earlier birth and the merit accmed therefrom Siva took to the form of a swan, made the lives of both of them quite pleasant.

Siva incarnating as a swan, who was well versed in various types of conversation, made Nala and Damayanti comfortable variously.

This is the story of Siva incarnating as Yatinatha as well as the swan, which is quite an astonishing one, besides being auspicious. It bestows salvation.

Whosoever listens or recites the auspicious story of the incarnation of Siva as Yatisa and Brahma-hamsa he achieves the supreme position (salvation).

This is the excellent episode which bestows, merits, fulfills all the desires, grants, the heaven, noble glory, long life and enhances devotion.

Listening to the story of Yatisa and Hamsa form of Siva, a person enjoying all the types of pleasures on earth, ultimately achieves the Sayujya devotion of Siva.

## Chapter 29 - The story of Nabhaga and Krsna-darsana incarnation of Siva

Nandisvara said, “O Sanatkumara, now you listen to the excellent story of Krsna- darsana who imparted the best of knowledge to Nabhaga.

Sradhadeva had Iksavaku and other sons. In the ninth generation of that race, Nabhaga was born. His son was known as Nabhaga.

Ambrisa his son was a great devotee of Visnu. The sage Durvasa was pleased with him because of his Brahmasakti.

Nabhaga was the grandfather of Ambrisa. O Sage, you listen to his story, who was imparted knowledge by Siva.

Nabhaga who was the intelligent son of Vaivarvata Manu, stayed in the abode of the preceptor for long. He had controlled all his senses.

By about the same the sons named Iksavaku and others, distributed the properly, without giving anything to Nabhaga.

Getting their respective shares, all of them at the command of the father, started enjoying the best of pleasures in the world.

Thereafter the Brahmacari Nabhaga, learning all the Vedas and the post-vedic literature returned to his abode. O Sage, Nabhaga found that the property had been distributed among all his brothers, who were enjoying the same. Then in order to get his share, he lovingly spoke to his brothers Iksavaku and others. Nabhaga said, “O Brothers, you please get me my share of the property which you have not so far distributed. I have arrived here for the same purpose.

They said, “We had forgotten about you at the time of the distribution of the property. Now we shall return your share to the father, which you should receive from him undoubtedly.”

Listening to these words of the brothers, Nabhaga felt immensely surprised. Then he went to his father and said, “O Father, I had gone to Gurukula for studies as a Brahmacari. You distributed the entire property to all the brothers, except me.

On my return when I respectfully demanded my share, then they have sent me to you. I have therefore arrived here for that purpose.

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, listening to his words, his father Sraddhadeva was surprised and assuring the noble Nabhaga, he said to him.”

Manu said, “Don’t believe in their words which are deceitful. In case they have asked me to give you the share from my property, then I shall give you the best of the share of the property.

Those cheats have entrusted you to me in the form of the share of the property. Therefore, I make appropriate arrangement for your livelihood. You listen to me carefully.

From today onwards the Brahmanas of Angirasa gotra, while performing the yajna would forget on every sixth day the mantras to be recited by them.

O Learned Nabhaga, you go there and recite the mantras of two Suktas before them; as a result of which the yajna would be completed.

At the conclusion of the yajna, the Brahmana, while returning to the heaven, feeling delighted collect the money which remained unspent in the yajna, which would be handed over them to you.”

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of his father, Nabhaga with whom only the truth was the strength, lovingly went to the place of the yajna.

O Sage, on the yajna of that day, Nabhaga- the highly learned one, recited two Vaisvadeva Suktas quite clearly.

At the close of the yajna, the Brahmanas of Anglrasa-gotra collected the wealth that had been saved from the yajna and it was given to him and then they left for heaven.

After accepting of the wealth that was saved from the yajna by Nabhaga, Siva appeared on the scene.

All the limbs of Siva were beautiful, graceful, having black complexion, and he intended to know the feelings of Nabhaga after his appearing on the scene.

Then Siva, for the purpose of testing, appeared before Nabhaga and said to him.

Isvara said, “Who are you to carry away my wealth and the assets. Who has sent you here. You tell me the whole truth?”

Nandisvara said, “On hearing his words, O Dear, the poet Nabhaga, son of Manu, humbly replied to Krsna-darsana.”

Nabhaga said, “The wealth of the yajna has been given to me by the sages. Therefore, why, O Krsna-darsana, you stop me from taking it?

Nandisvara said, “On hearing the truthful words of Nabhaga, the delighted Krsna- darsana spoke to him.

Krsna-darsana said, “O Dear one, in the controversy between two of us, your father is an authority. You better go and ask him. His words would serve as an authority in this case.

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, listening to the words of Krsna-darsana, the learned Nabhaga went to his father and asked him accordingly.

Sraddhadeva Manu, listening to the words of his son, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, said to his son.”

Manu said, “O Dear one, you listen to my words. The ascetic in the form of Krsna- darsana is Siva himself. Everything belongs to him including the remnants of the yajna. The remnant part of the yajna also belongs to him.

The remnant part of the yajna goes to Siva. There is nothing beyond his desire. This is what is spoken by the learned people.

Undoubtedly lord Siva has the right to own everything. There is nothing beyond his desire. Siva has arrived in that form to shower his grace on you. Therefore, O Nabhaga, you go there and please him with your truthfulness.

Beg from him forgiveness for your sin and eulogise him bowing in reverence to him. He is not only the lord of the yajna, but also the lord of the world.

O Dear one, all the gods like Brahma, Visnu and others, besides the siddhas and the sages, move over the path of righteousness by his grace.

O My best son, what is the use of speaking more, you go there atonce and please Mahadeva, the lord of all.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, Manu Sraddhadeva, atonce sent back his son, to Siva and he himself also went there.

The immensely intelligent Nabhaga, offered his salutation to Siva, with his hands folded lowering his head and delightfully spoke to him in a humble voice.

Nabhaga said, “O Isvara, all the things in the three worlds belong to you. This is what my father has told me, then what to speak of the remnant of the yajna.

O Lord, whatever I spoke innocently and unknowingly earlier, I beg forgiveness for the same. I am bowing in reverence to please you.”

Thus speaking, Nabhaga with dejected mind, started eulogising lord Siva Krsnadarsana quite humbly with palms joined in reverence.

The immensely learned Sraddhadeva, also sought forgiveness for his sin, offering his salutation to Siva with folded hands, eulogising him at the same time.

In the meantime Brahma, Visnu, Indra and other gods, besides the siddhas and the sages arrived there.

All the gods and others possessing the noble souls, celebrated the occasion and all of them offered their salutation to him with folded hands, individually.

Then Siva in the form of Krsna-darsana, feeling pleased, looked at all the them with a compassionate glance. Then he smilingly addressed Nabhaga with a compassionate look.

Krsna-darsana said, “Whatever has been spoken by your father is true and based on dharma. Because of your noble conduct, you also spoke the truth. There is no doubt about it.

Therefore, I am happy with your truthfulness, therefore, mercifully I bestow the knowledge of Brahman to you.

O Nabhaga, you become great and wise, along with the Brahmanas atonce. You take all this wealth as well, which I grant you with compassion.

O Intelligent one, you enjoy all the pleasures on earth without any hesitation. By my grace, you will achieve the auspicious goal, alongwith the Brahmana sacrificers. Nandisvara said, “O Dear, after thus speaking, lord Siva, who is favourably inclined towards the truth, disappeared from the scene, in full view of all those who were present there.

Thereafter Brahma, Visnu and other gods, O Excellent sage, returned to their respective abodes after delightfully, bowing towards that direction.

Sraddhadeva also, returned to his abode with his son. After enjoying all the pleasures, he went to the city of Siva at the end.

Thus O Brahmana, the story of the appearing of Siva as Krsna-darsana, who bestowed his grace on Nabhaga, has been narrated to you.

This episode is quite auspicious, and conducive to the worldly enjoyments. It bestows salvation to the noble people. Those who read or listen to it, all their desires are fulfilled.

The learned people who remember this episode in the morning as well as in the evening, they attain wisdom and the knowledge of the mantras besides the excellent goal ultimately.

## Chapter 30 - Manifestation of Siva as Avadhutesvara

Nandisvara said, “O Son of Brahma, listen to the Avadhutesvara incarnation of Siva, who shattered the pride of Indra.

In the earlier times, Indra, together with Brhaspati and other gods, went to the mount Kailasa in order to have an audience with Siva.

Thereafter, Siva realising that the preceptor Brhaspati and Indra were coming to meet him, in order to test their mental condition, took to the form of a naked Avadhuta and appeared like the burning fire, because he could indulge in various types of sports. He became awful to look at.

Siva in the form of Avadhuta, protected the noble people, had the beautiful form, whose costumes was hanging. Siva in this form stood obstructing their way.

While going to Siva, both Indra and the preceptor found an awful personality obstructing the way.

O Sage, Indra, because of his pride in his authority, failed to understand that the strange personality was none else than Siva himself and asked him.

Indra said, “You are naked Avadhuta, but who are you? Where from have you arrived? What is your name? Tell us correctly atonce.

Is Siva available at his place or has he gone somewhere? I, with the preceptor and the gods have arrived here to meet him.”

Nandisvara said, “When so asked by Indra, Siva who shattered the pride of others, playfully taking to a different form, kept quiet.

Indra asked him again, but the naked Siva sportily, in order to shatter his pride, and creator of the forceful things, again spoke nothing.

Again, Indra the lord of heaven and the master of the three worlds, asked him, but the great yogi of the great sports, kept silent.

Thus when Indra asked him again and again the strange person kept mum, in order to quell the arrogance of Indra.

Thereafter Indra, who had the pride of the three worlds, getting enraged denounced the person with locks of hair and said.

Indra said, “O you fool, you are not giving answer to what I am asking. Therefore, I air going to kill you with my thunderbolt and \] shall see who will save you?”

Thus thinking, Indra feeling irritated, looked at him and raised his Vajra to attack him.

Sadasiva found Indra carrying Vajra in his hand and he stunned his hand.

Thereafter Siva getting enraged, turning eyes quite awful, and the flames of fire started issuing from his body.

With his unmoving arm, Indra too was engaged and started burning within himself like the snake having been overpowered with the use of the mantras.

Brhaspati then found that Siva was engulfed in flames with his own lustre. Then he took that person to be none else them Siva himself and he atonce offered his salutation to him.

The large hearted Brhaspati then prostrated before lord Siva with folded hands. Then he eulogised him with devotion.

The preceptor said, “O Mahadeva, the god of gods, well disposed towards those who took refuge with you, O Lord of Gauri, O Lord of all, salutation to you. You kindly be pleased with us.

Brahma, Visnu and all other gods are influenced with your Ṅīóṁ can know you correctly, by your grace alone.

Nandisvara said, “Thus lord Siva was eulogised by Brhaspati, who also made Indra to prostrate before him at his feet.

O Dear one, then the large hearted Brhaspati, humbly folding his hand, said.

Brhaspati said, “O Lord of the destitutes, O Mahadeva, I bow in reverence at your feet. You kindly redeem me. Shedding away the anger, speak to me lovingly.

O Mahadeva, you kindly save Indra, who has taken refuge with you getting terrified from your fire flames.

Nandisvara said, “Lord Siva, in the form of an Avadhuta, appearing in an astonishing form, the ocean of mercy, lightening to the words of Brhaspati, smilingly spoke.

Avadhuta said, “The tejas that has emerged out of the eyes due to the anger, how could it be taken back? Can a serpent wear again, the skin, which is once removed from his body?” Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of Siva, feeling upset with terror, Brhaspati again spoke.

Brhaspati said, “O Deva, O Lord, O Sankara, you should be merciful over your devotees, you make your name as Bhaktavatsala to be true.

O Lord of the gods, it behoves you to cast off the fire elsewhere. Please life up Indra, since you are the uplifter of your devotees. Nandisvara said, “Thus requested by Brhaspati, Siva who was known as Bhaktavatsala- the delighted soul and the dispeller of the distress of those, who bow in reverence to him.

Siva said, “O Preceptor of gods, I am pleased with you and shall grant you an excellent boon. You will be famous as jiva because you have gifted life to Indra. I shall throw away the fire emerging from my eye in the forehead which is unbearable to the gods so that it does not cause any harm to Indra.

Nandisvara said, “After thus speaking, he picked up the wonderful fire that originated from his eye, in the forehead in his hand and cast it off in the ocean of salt. As soon as he threw it, a child emerged out of it.

The son of the ocean in due course of time came to be known as Jalandhara, the lord of the demons. The said demon king Jalandhara was killed by Siva himself at the request of the gods.

Thus Siva- Loka Sankara, displayed his astonishing story, appearing as Avadhuta and thereafter he disappeared from the scene.

Thereafter all the gods, becoming fearless, became comfortable. Brhaspati- the preceptor of the gods, and Indra the lord of gods, also became fearless and lived comfortably.

Siva to whom Indra and Brhaspati had gone to meet, both of them felt beholden to him after having an audience with him. All of them then returned to their respective places.

The narration about the Avadhuta incarnation of Siva, delights the noble people very much, punishing he wicked at the same time.

This auspicious episode is quite divine and while bestowing excellent glory, heaven, enjoyment of all the pleasures, besides the salvation, fulfills all the desires.

Whosoever listens to this episode quite carefully, or narrates it to others, he enjoying all the pleasures in this world, ultimately achieves the sayujya type of the devotion of Siva.

## Chapter 31 - Incarnation of Siva as Bhiksuvarya

Nandisvara said, “O Brahmana, O Excellent sage, you please listen to me. Now I shall mention abut the incarnation of Visnu, who with the compassion of the devotees, removed the doubt about a women.

In the city of Vidarbha, there was a king named Satyaratha. who was quite religious minded, truthful, loved by the people, and a great devotee of Siva.

O Sage, he ruled the country with a religious mind, getting devoted to Siva, a long time was passed.

Once Satyaratha had a great war with Saiva king who had surrounded his city.

The king of the Vidarbha country fought with the enemy king and his forces. Unfortunately a large army of the king Satyaratha was killed by the warriors of Sala king

In the war at the killing of Satyaratha by the Salvas, the warriors of the former were frightened and they fled away from the battle field.

O Sage, when the city was so surrounded by the enemy forces the pregnant queen of Satyaratha king somehow escaped and went out of the city.

The grieved wife of the king Satyaratha, devoting her mind at the feet of lord Siva, fled towards the east.

Thereafter the queen found a spotless lake in the morning by the grace of Siva, she reached a far off place.

Then reaching there, the young and tender limbed wife of the king sat under shade of a tree for having some rest.

Luckily the queen, in an auspicious moment, gave birth to a son with all the auspicious symbols.

The mother of that infant felt extremely thirsty. She entered the lake to drink water, but was swallowed by a crocodile.

Soon after his birth the infant’s position became miserable. He suffered from hunger and thirst and was deprived of his parents and started crying over the bank of the lake.

O Sage, lord Siva, who knew everything, showered his grace on the infant who was weeping and wailing in the forest.

Lord Siva , who removed the miseries of all, then inspired a female beggar, who while wandering reached there, with her child who was a month old.

The widow beggar was carrying a year old child in her lap, while wandering and she found a shelterless infant crying in the forest.

O Sage, in the lonely forest finding the infant there, she felt surprised and she thought.

“I have met with a great surprise today, which can not be conceived by the mind and is beyond description.

This is the infant, whose umbilical cord has not been cut, is lying on the ground. He is deprived of his mother. He is weeping but is quite brilliant.

He is without parents, or any other person to help him. What could be the reason for it? Alas! How powerful are the moves of the fate?

I am not aware of his parents, no one here knows about him. How can I know about his birth? But I surely feel attracted towards him.

I shall not touch him without knowing about his birth and his parents, though I would like to bring him up and nourish him, as my own child.”

Nandisvara said, “As soon as the Brahmana lady thus thought about the infant, lord Siva showered his grace on her, since he is well disposed towards his devotees.

Lord Siva then, taking to the form of a beggar, who is the performer of great sports and bestower of pleasures on his devotees, in all respects, without any condition and forever, assumed the form of a mendicant.

Lord Siva suddenly arrived in the form of a mendicant to the place where, the Brahmana lady stood with her mind filled with doubt and was desirous of knowing about the truth.

The lord whose ways are beyond description, and is the abode of mercy, assuming the form of a great mendicant, laughed and told the Brahmana lady. The Brahmana said, “O Brahmana lady, don’t have any doubt in your mind. Don’t be sorry. Protect this auspicious infant, lovingly as your adopted son.

By bringing up this child, you will shortly meet with enormous welfare. Bring u this illustrious infant by all means.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking Siva, the ocean of mercy appearing in the form of mendicant, was asked by the Brahmana lady, with resnect.

The Brahmana lady said, “You have arrived here because of my good luck. I, at your command, shall bring of this boy like my own son. But still I particularly want to know as to who is he? Whose son is he, and who are you present here?

O Lord, O Excellent mendicant, it comes to my mind that you are none else them Siva himself, while this infant must have been your devotee in the earlier birth.

Because of some sin, he has been rendered helpless like this. Facing the reward for that sin, he, by your grace would enjoy an exalted position.

It is because of your Maya that I have lost my way and have been sent by you here in order to save him.”

Nanisvara said, “Then Siva in the form of a mendicant spoke to the Brahmana lady who had attained perfect knowledge by looking at him and who evinced the desire to know the details about the infant.

The mendicant said, “You listen with delight, about the parentage of the body. O Sinless one, I shall narrate all the details about him to you.

This infant is the son of the king Satyaratha, the king of Vidarbha and a great devotee of Siva. He was truthful and a devotee of Siva.

Listen, the king Satyaratha had been killed by Salvas in the battle ground. His upset wife fled from her home during the night.

She gave birth to this boy. When thirsty, she went to the lake to drink water, when unluckily she was swallowed by a crocodile.”

Nanarsvara said, “In this way Siva revealed the truth about the birth of the child, the death of his father in the battle ground, and the death of his mother who was swallowed by a crocodile. All these facts were related by Siva to the Brahmana lady.

O Excellent sage the Brahmana lady felt extremely surprised. Then she questioned the mendicant in the form of a Siddha.

The Brahmana lady said, “O mendicant, the king, the father of this infant, enjoying all the pleasures of his life, but what for was he killed by the Salvas for petty gains.

Why did the crocodile swallowed his mother and why was the infant orphaned at birth?

O Mendicant you please tell me. You tell me how would my poor son of a mendicant and the infant who is a prince would happily be brought up together?

Nandisvara said, “Thus listening to the words of the Brahmana lady, the delightful lord in the form of a mendicant spoke wearing a smile over his face.

The Mendicant said, O Brahmana lady, with this excellent story, I would reply your all the questions. You better listen to me carefully. The king of the Vidarbha country an the father of this infant, was the king of the Pandya country in his earlier birth.

The said king was devoted to Siva and ruled his country with a religious mind. Removing all the disturbances, he always pleased his people.

Once the king on the day of *Trayodasi* fasted completely for the day and night adored Siva- the lord of all, at the time of dusk.

When the king was so engaged in the worship of Siva, a terrific sound was heard in the city.

Listening to the terrific sound, the king, discarding the worship of Siva, with the expectation of the arrival of the enemy, marched out of his house.

His powerful courtier at the same time accompanied with the weapons and subordinate rulers, joined the king.

Apprehending him to be the enemy courtier, the king getting enraged, and upset, taking him to be the warrior of the enemy, got his head cut off.

The king without finishing the worship of Siva, also consumed delightfully, the unclean food during the night.

The said devotee of Siva became the king of the Vidarbha country during his present birth. Because of the obstruction in the adoration of Siva, he was attacked by the enemy and was killed during the time of his enjoying the pleasures.

His father in the earlier birth, became his son in the present birth. But he was deprived of the riches due to the obstruction caused by him the worship of Siva.

The mother of this infant had killed her ṣO-wife in the earlier birth and because of the same sin, she was devoured by he crocodile in the present birth.

Thus I have narrated to you their activities in the previous as well as the present births. People having no devotion to Siva, and those who do not worship him, have to face poverty.

Your present son had been an excellent Brahmana in the previous birth. He spent his life in receiving gifts, but failed to perform the auspicious rites like yajnas etc.

O Brahmana lady, your son has incurred poverty. You better seek refuge in Siva in order to word off the sins.

You should adore Siva with these two children. Siva will do good to you after these upanayana-samskara (thread ceremony is performed).

Nandisvara said, “Thus advising her, Siva in the form of a mendicant, who is quite well disposed towards his devotees, appeared before her in his true form.

Thereafter the Brahmana lady, taking him to be Siva, lovingly offered her salutation to him eulogising him in the choked voice.

Thereafter, lord Siva in the form of a mendicant, in full view' of her, disappeared from the place.

After the departure of the mendicant, the Brahmana lady, having been relieved of the worries, returned to her home, with her own child as well as the infant.

Then she living in the Ekacakra city started bringing up her own as will as the prince- son of the king, serving food to both of them.

After the thread ceremony was performed for both of them by the Brahmanas, both the boys went on growing up adoring Siva.

O Dear one, both the boys at the command of the sage Sandilya, appropriately performing the Vratas used to adore Siva during dusk time.

Once the son of the king alone went to the river for taking a bath, where he found pitcher filled with wealth.

Thus performing the adoration of Siva a period of four months passed for both the son of the Brahmana as well as the prince.

Adoring Siva with great delight, he kept on living in the same house for a year.

O Sage, after the expiry of one year, the prince, by the grace of Siva, went to the forest with the Brahmana boy.

A Gandharva girl suddenly arrived there who was married by prince and thereafter he started ruling the country without any obstruction. The Brahmana lady who had brought him up like her own son, became his mother and the Brahmana became his brother.

Thus adoring Siva, Dharmagupta, ruled Vidarbha, enjoying all the comforts.

The incarnation of the Bhiksuvarya of Siva, appeared on earth to bestow pleasure to the prince and the story of the same has been narrated by me.

This auspicious story is extremely important and is the best means for achieving dharma, artha, kama and moksa. It fulfills other desires as well.

A person who listens or narrates this story daily, quite carefully, he enjoying ail the pleasures in his life ultimately proceeds on the place of Siva.

## Chapter 32 - Incarnation of Siva as Suresvara

Nandisvara said, “O Dear one, now, I am going to narrate about the Sures'vara incarnation of Siva, who had made the elder brother of Dhaumya quite comfortable. You please listen to it.

Upamanyu the dear son of Vyaghrapada, who was dear to the learned people, because of his auspicious performance in his earlier birth was born as the son of the sage.

Since childhood he lived with his maternal uncle, with his mother. As a move of destiny, Upamanyu, the son of Vyagrapada was quite poor.

Once he got a little of milk to drink in his maternal uncle's home. Then he asked his mother to give him more milk.

Listening to the words of her son, he ascetic mother went inside and adopted an excellent method.

She grounded some seeds and grains she got by gleaning, into the paste with water and the artificial water was given to the boy as milk, after fondling and coaxing him.

After drinking the false milk, given by his mother, the boy cried, “This is not the milk.” Then he cried again.

On hearing the cries of her son, the mother wiped off the tears of his lotus like eyes and said to him painfully.

The mother said, “How can the forest dwellers like us have milk. We can never have milk without the grace of Siva.

O Son, only that can be attained what we had dedicated to Siva in our previous birth. Therefore we should not worry like thus.”

He said, “O Mother, don’t grieve, in case Siva is the bestower of welfare, then O Auspicious one don’t grieve we shall meet with welfare.

The loving son of Vyaghra-pada, listening to the words of his mother, getting relieved of the grief said to his mother.

“O Mother, you listen to my words. In case Mahadeva is present somewhere, then sooner or later I shall achieve he ocean of milk.

Nandisvara said, “The boy after saying this with pleasure and repeating that “let there be welfare”, he bowed to his mother and left her and then began to perform the penance.

Reaching the Himalaya mountain, inhaling air alone preparing a hermitage of eight bricks, he made a Sivalinga of clay.

Invoking Samba-Sadasiva, reciting the Pancaksara-mantra he started adoring it, offering the wild flowers and the leaves,

Adoring Siva and Parvati together, and devoting his mind towards them, reciting the ÐṁñṣīŪṁãṁ mantra, he performed penance for a long time.

Upamanyu- the great soul, while performing his tapas all the mobiles, immobiles in were scorched.

At the same time, listening to the prayer of Visnu and other gods, lord Siva, in order to test the depth of the devotion of Upamanyu, took to the form of Indra.

Parvati turned herself as Indrani. All the ganas of Siva were turned as gods. Nandi was turned into Airavata.

All of them collectively went to the hermitage of Upamanyu, in order to grace him.

O Excellent sage, Siva in the form of Indra, in order to test his devotion, addressed the boy in deep voice.

Suresvara said, “O Mendicant, I am pleased with your penance. You better seek for a boon. I shall fulfil all your desires. There is no doubt about it.”

At these words of Siva spoken in the form of Indra, the boy spoke with folded hands, “I desire boon from Siva at whose feet I am devoted to. I intend to receive a boon from him.”

On hearing this Indra said, “Are you not aware of Indra, who happens to be the lord of the three worlds, and is adored by all the gods?

O BrahmarsI, you happen to me my devotee. You can go and remain always devoted to me. I bestow everything on you. Discard adoring Siva- the nirguna one.

Don’t have any relation with the nirguna form of Siva. What purpose, is his adoration going to serve to you? He becoming pisaca has separated himself from the gods.”

Nandisvara said, “On hearing this, the son of the sage, reciting the Pancaksara mantra, thought him to be a person having arrived to cause obstruction in his tapas.

Upamanyu said, “You in your anxiety to denounce Siva have called him nirguna (devoid of merits) and a pisaca who is the lord of all the gods.

You are unaware of Rudra, who happens to be the lord of all the gods. He happens to be the creator of Brahma, Visnu and the other god and is beyond Prakrti.

I would like to have the boon from the deity whom the learned people call eternal, the single, the multitude, separate from the existent and non-existent besides being unmanifest.

I would like to seek a boon from the deity whom the omniscient sages, consider free from causations, controversies, and is the bestower of the principle of Sankhya and yoga.

There is no entity greater than lord Siva, who is beyond attributes. He is the cause of the causes, and the most excellent of Brahma, Visnu and other gods.

I deny to take a boon from you and neither from Brahma or Visnu. Nor do I want any boon from any other god. Let Siva alone bestow a boon on me.

What is the use of speaking much? I tell you the truth and my firm resolve. I do not request any other god, except Siva.

O Indra, listen to my words I have a feeling that in my earlier birth, I must have committed some sin, that I have been able hear to the denouncement of Siva presently.

A person, who listening to the denouncement of Siva, ends his life then and there, he ultimately achieves Sivaloka.

O Degraded one of all the gods, though I had a desire to drink milk only, but now, killing you with the weapon of Siva, I am going to end my life.”

Nandisvara said, “Then Upamanyu, who got ready to end his life, discarding his desire for the drinking of milk, got ready to kill Indra.

He picked up the ashes from the fire altar, sanctifying the Aghora-weapon he threw it towards Indra, thundering at the same time.

Then remembering both the feet of Siva, Upamanyu, devoting his mind towards the fire, got ready to burn his body.

At these activities of the Brahmana, Siva in the form of Indra, changed his thoughts in a benevolent way.

The terrific Aghora-weapon shot by Upamanyu, was caught by Nandisvara at the command of Siva in the midway.

At the same time lord Siva, assuming his own form with the moon for his crest, revealed it before the boy.

The lord displayed before the boy thousands of oceans of milk and curd, besides the edible food items.

Thus he witnessed Siva and Parvati seated with his ganas, holding the trident and other divine weapons as attributes.

At that time the divine musical instruments were played upon in the sky and the rain of flowers started falling. All the ten directions were covered with the presence of Brahma, Vi?nu and other gods.

Thereafter Upamanyu was drowned in the waves of the blissful ocean. Then with his heart having been filled with devotion, he prostrated before them.

In the meantime, Siva taking to his true form smilingly said, “Come on, Come on”, and then kissing his forehead, he bestowed boons on him.

Siva said, “O Son Upamanyu I am pleased with the best of your conduct. O Brahmarsi, I put you to test. You happen to be my staunch devotee.

Getting devoted to me, you live comfortably with your kiths and kins. Having been relieved of your miseries, you remain blissful always.

O Upamanyu, O Excellent one, I have accepted you as my son today. Parvati is now your mother. You will always remain a boy.

Thousands of oceans of milk, curd, honey and other edible things have been given by me to you quite lovingly, O Sage. You please accept them. Besides that, I have bestowed upon you the eternalship and the permanent position of a Ganapati as well.

I am Mahadeva- your father and Jagadambika (Parvati) is your mother. Choose your boons whatever you desire.

Getting relieved of all the miseries, you will be unaging, undying. You will be famous, brilliant and endowed with the divine knowledge. You will be a great lord.

Thereafter, lord Siva taking into consideration the great penance of Upamanyu, gave him ten boons. He bestowed on him the knowledge of Siva and his rites. He was enlightened about the vows of Siva, bestowing the fluency of speech, and efficiency and the stay in his own region, on him.

Thus granting him the boons, Mahadeva, held him with both the hands and kissed his forehead saying, “You are my son.” Thus speaking he handed him over to Parvati.

Then Parvati observing all this lovingly, placed her lotus like hand over his head and bestowed on him the eternal position of unaging.

Then the ocean of milk which had an eternal taste in the form of a pinda was given to him.

They also bestowed on him the prosperity, and the power of yoga besides the undying knowledge of Brahman and the great assets.

After receiving the excellent boons from Siva and Siva, and the eternal status of their son, he was extremely rejoiced.

Then Upamanyu, feeling delighted, offering salutation to them with folded hands, sought for a boon with devotion.

Upamanyu said, “O Lord of the gods, O Parames'vara, you getting delighted, bestow on me your divine, eternal and everlasting devotion.

O Mahadeva, let me have faith in my kiths and kins, besides your devotion, excessive love and closeness to you.”

Nandisvara said, 'Thus speaking, Upamanyu, the excellent Brahmana, feeling pleased offered prayer to Siva with a choked voice.

When Upamanyu so eulogised Siva and Parvati in the presence of all, then the delightful Siva said.

Siva said, O Son, O Sinless one, you are blessed. You are especially devoted to me. Whatever has been desired by you has been given to you.

You will be un-aging, undying, and free from misery. You must be respectable, to all, free from blemish and the foremost among my devotees.

O Excellent Brahmana, your uiths and kins, and the gotva would be everlasting and you will remain devoted to me for all times to come.

O Sage, I shall always reside in your asrama. You will there comfortably. Don’t get anxious ever.”

Nandøsvara said, “Thus lord Siva, bestowing the excellent boons on Upamanyu, disappeared from that place with Parvati and his ganas.

Receiving the excellent boons from Siva, Upamanyu went to his mother and conveyed the entire news to her.

Hearing this, his mother was extremely delighted. Upamanyu also was also respected by all, and he enjoyed all the pleasures.

O Dear one, I have thus described Suresvara incarnation of Siva, which bestows all the comforts to the noble people.

This auspicious story, fulfills all the desires of the noble people, besides granting them the heaven, long life, enjoyment of pleasures and the salvation ultimately.

Whosoever listens to this with concentrated mind, or recites it, he enjoying all the pleasures on earth, ultimately achieves Sivaloka.

## Chapter 33 - Siva's incarnation as Brahmacari

Nandisvara said, “O Sanatkumara, now you listen to the extremely auspicious incarnation of Siva, as Brahmacari, quite lovingly.

In ancient times, Sati, the daughter of Daksa, having been insulted by her father ended her life in the fire altar, and was reborn in the house of Himalaya from the womb of Mena as her daughter.

She went to the thick forest with her maids to perform severe tapas for achieving Siva as her husband.

Siva then sent Saptarsis in order to test the depth of her devotion, since he was well versed in various types of sports.

The ascetics went there and put Parvati to test, but they could not be completely successful.

Returning from that place, offering their salutation to Siva, enlightening him of all the happenings there, getting permission of Siva, they retired to the heaven.

After the return of the ascetics to their respective places, the playful lord Siva, himself desired to test the devotion of Parvati.

Then the delightful lord Siva, at his own will took to the form of a peaceful Brahmacari.

He appeared as an extremely old Brahmana, resplendent with his own lustre, with a delightful mind, carried the danda and a chatra.

Disguised as a Brahmacari, Siva who is kindly disposed towards his devotees, and form of welfare, appeared before Parvati in the forest of penance.

Parvati was surrounded by her maids seated over a pedestal like the digit of the moon, having a spotless heart, who was spotted by Siva.

Disguised as Brahmacari, Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, went to the goddess Parvati.

Parvati finding the astonishing, illusions, having hair in all the limbs, peaceful Brahmana carrying a danda and the dear skin, having arrived there.

The old Brahmana, appearing as the Brahmacari, having matted locks of hair as well as Kamandalu, when reached before Parvati, she, lovingly adored the Brahmana with all the material for worship.

Then the goddess Parvati, adored him with devotion and faith, and enquired about his welfare.

She said, “Who are you the best among those possessing the knowledge of the Vedas? Where from have you arrived in the form of a Brahmacari. You have made the forest resplendent with your lustre.

Nandisvara said, “When so questioned by Parvati, the Brahmacari Brahmana, in order to test the mind of Parvati lovingly spoke atonce.

Brahmacari said, “I am a mendicant Brahmacari Brahmana, who wanders about here and there at will. I make the people comfortable, doing good to them.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking Siva who is well disposed towards his devotees, as a Brahmacari, concealing his true form, stood before Parvati.

Brahmacari said, “O MahadevI, what shall I say? There is nothing appropriate to be spoken. It appears to me that a great calamity seems to have happened which would be extremely confusing.

The young age is meant for enjoyment of all the pleasures which are available at home. You are performing tapas for nothing.

Who are you? Whose daughter are you? You are performing tapas in this lonely forest, which is beyond the reach of even the great yogis.

Nandisvara said, “Thus listening to the words of the Brahmacari, Parvati smiled and spoke loving words to him.

Parvati said, “O Sage, O Brahmacari, O Brahmana, listen to my introduction. Presently, I have been bom in the house of Himalaya as his daughter.

I had earlier been bom in the house of Daksa Prajapati, when I had been known as Sati, the wife of lord Siva. Listening to the denouncement of my husband from my father I burnt out my body in the fire of yoga.

O Brahmana, because of my merits, I have achieved this birth. Then Siva, burning Kamadeva, deserted me and left the place.

After the departure of Siva, felt painful and ashamed. Then having been inspired by the words of the preceptor, I arrived here for performing of tapas.

I am speaking the truth. I have selected Siva as my groom by action, thought and behaviour.

Though I am fully aware of the fact that it is difficult to get him, still because of the anxiety of my mind, I am performing the tapas.

Leaving aside Brahma, Visnu, Indra and other gods, I truthfully desire Siva to be my husband.

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, listening to the firm words of Parvati, the Brahmacari Rudra spoke smilingly.

The ascetic with matted locks of hair said, “O Daughter of Himalaya, O Goddess, what type of decision have you made? Leaving aside Indra and other gods you are performing tapas for achieving Rudra as your husband?

I know Rudra very well and am going to speak to you about him. He uses a bull as his vehicle. He is full of blemishes and wears the locks of hair over the head.

He avoids company and always lives alone. He is particularly a detached fellow. Therefore, don’t devote your mind to him.

O Goddess, the form and habits of Siva are quite different as compared to you. I don’t like it. You may do as you like.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking Rudra disguised as a Brahmacari, denounced himself variously in order to test Parvati.

Listening to the unbearable words of the Brahmana denouncing Siva, the goddess Parvati then said to him.

“I have come to realise that you are a person to be killed. But taking into consideration all the things, I feel that you cannot be killed.

You are a wicked person who was arrived here in the form of Brahmacari. O Foolish one, you have denounced Siva, therefore, I feel enraged.

You are not at all aware of Siva. Your are opposite to him. I feel painful for having adored you. I feel miserable.

A person who being ignorant of Sivatattva denounced the same without knowing the reality, all his merits are reduced to ashes.

By touching the enemy of Siva, one should perform repentance.

O Wicked person, you claimed that you were well aware of Siva. But you are actually ignorant of him. He is the Supreme lord in reality.

He might take to any form by his Maya, but he is the one who would bestow the desired reward. He is unblemished and is dear to the noble people.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, the goddess Parvati discussed on the Sivatattva (Siva’s principle) where Siva has been concerned as the one without attributes, unchanging, performer of the penance of Brahman.

ON hearing her words, the Brahmana was about to speak out something, but by that time, Parvati whose mind had been devoted to Siva, and was averse at the Siva denouncing of Siva, immediately spoke to her friend Viajya.

Parvati said, “O Friend, this wicked Brahmana must be prevented. He is going to speak again. He is sure to insult Siva.

He is not only the denouncer of Siva, but also the one who is interested in such insult of Siva.

A denouncer of Siva, shall be slain by the attendants of Siva by all means. In case he happens to be a Brahmana he should be abandoned. Let him leave this place atonce.

The wicked person would again denounce Siva. He cannot be killed because of his being a Brahmana. He should therefore be discarded and one should not look at him.

Leaving this place, let us move to some other place so that we do not have to talk to this person.

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, thus speaking as soon as Uma raised her foot for departing, lord Siva, held the edge of her cloth, revealing himself.

Siva appeared in the same form to Parvati, in which she usually adored Siva. Siva then felt that it was Siva who had spoken to her.

Siva said, “O Parvati, where are you going leaving me alone. I cannot leave you. O Auspicious soul, you are my staunch devotee. I have tested you for the same.

Taking to the form of a Brahmacari, in order to know your ideas, I talked to you like this.

O Parvati, because of your firm devotion towards me, I feet immensely pleases. You seek for from me whatever desire is there in your mind. There is nothing that cannot be given to you.

O Beloved Parvati, from today onwards, I have been enslaved by your beauty and now even a moment appears like a yuga without you.

You better shed away shyness, you are my eternal wife. O Beloved, come on, I shall go with you to the Himalaya.”

At these words of Siva, Siva was extremely pleased and all her sufferings due to the performing of the penance were removed.

Looking at the divine from of Siva, lowering her head with shyness, she spoke lovingly.

Siva said, “O Lord of gods, in case you are pleased with me, then you agree to be my husband. These were the words spoken by Parvati to Siva.

Nandisvara said, “Accepting the hand of Parvati in marriage appropriately, Siva went with her to Kailasa. Parvati established the task of the gods by accepting Siva as her husband.

O Dear one, I have narrated the Brahmacari incarnation of Siva, in which form he appeared in order to test the mind of Parvati.

I have narrated to you the excellent and auspicious story to you. Whosoever will listen to it with devotion, he would achieve salvation.

## Chapter 34 - Siva’s incarnation as Sunartaka-nata

Nandisvara said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, now I shall narrate the story of the incarnation of Siva as Sunartaka-nata.

When Parvati, in the form of Kalika, went to the forest for the performance of the penance to achieve Siva as her husband. She started performing severe penance.

O Sage, Siva was pleased with her severe penance. Then Siva in order to test her ideas and to bestow her with the boon went to her.

O Sage, feeling pleased, he appeared before her. Siva then asked Siva to ask for a boon.

Finding Siva in that excellent form, and listening to his words, Parvati was immensely pleased and she offered her salutation to him.

Parvati said, “O Lord of gods, in case you are pleased with me, and intend to bestow a boon to me, them being compassionate on me you become my husband.

O Master, O Lord, I with your permission return to the home of my father appropriately. You should also go to my father.

In the form of a mendicant and revealing your spotless fame, you beg me from father and make the life of the householder fruitful.

O Lord Siva, it behoves you to marry me with all the prescribed rites for the establishment of the task of the gods.

O Lord, you are unblemished, therefore, fulfil my desire. You are favourably disposed towards your devotees while I always remain devoted to you.”
