Nandisvara said, “At this request of Parvati, Siva who is well disposed towards his devotees said, “Be it so.” Then he disappeared from the scene and reached his mountain abode.

Thereafter Parvati with hr handmaids, making her beauty fruitful, returned to her parental home.

Learning about the return of Parvati, Himalaya with Mena went to receive her daughter, with delight.

Finding her with smiling face, both of them received her suitably within the house and glad at heart celebrated the event with pleasure.

Both Mena and Himalaya, gave charities to the Brahmanas and others performing the welfare ceremony with the reciting of the Vedic mantras.

Then after he sat with his daughter delightfully in the courtyard for sometime. Thereafter, Mena and Himalaya both went for a bath in the Ganga.

At the same time, Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, and the performer of beautiful sports, disguised as dancer went to Mena, the mother of Parvati.

He held the horn is his left hand and a damaru in the right hand. He had a red sack hanging at the back. He was well versed in dancing and singing.

Siva in the form of a dancer, started performing various dances joyously in the courtyard of Menaka and sang sweetly.

He played on the horn as well as the damaru pretty well and started dancing. He displayed various types of sports.

In order to enjoy the dancing and the songs, all the people of the city, including the women, men, boys, young and old, atonce reached there.

O Sage, observing the dance and listening to the songs, the people were fascinated and Mena too felt delighted.

Influenced with the sports of Siva, Mena, atonce got up and brought a gold vase filled with gems, to offer the same to Siva.

The offering of the gems was not accepted by Siva, who said, “I want Siva in charity.” Thereafter he again started dancing and singing.

Hearing these words of the dancer, Mena was surprised as well as enraged. She denounced the mendicant and desired him to be driven out.

At the same time Himalaya returned after having his bath in the waters of the Ganga and found a male mendicant in the courtyard.

Listening to the news from the mouth of Mena, he was much more enraged and he commanded the mendicant to be driven out.

O Excellent sage, no one could drive out the mendicant or touch him since he had been resplendent like the fire.

O Dear one, the mendicant, who was well-versed in various types of sports, then displayed his unlimited influence.

Himalaya atonce visualised him in the form of Visnu and then Lin the form of Brahma. In a moment then he found him in the form of the sun.

O Dear one, then he was found with an astonishing lustre as Rudra with Parvati delightfully.

Then he feeling blissful and surprised, found him in various forms there.

Then he playful mendicant, again asked for Parvati as his alms, and accepted nothing else.

Then Paramesvara, inspired by the words of Durga, disappeared from the place and retired to his abode.

Only then both Himalaya and Mena came to realise that cheating both them, Lord Siva had returned to his abode.

Then thinking that they have to give away their ascetic daughter to Siva, both of them developed extreme devotion towards Siva.

Thereafter the playful Siva, married Parvati appropriately, and the marriage delighted his devotees.

O Dear one, the dancer who honoured the words of Parvati, was the incarnation of Siva and the relevant story has been narrated by me.

I have narrated the auspicious and excellent story to you. One who lovingly listens to it, he achieves salvation.

## Chapter 35 - Incarnation of Siva as a Brahmana

Nandisvara said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, O Excellent one, now I am going to narrate the incarnation of Siva as an ascetic Brahmana. You please listen to the same.

Realising about the extreme devotion towards Siva and Parvati by Himalaya and Mena, all the gods felt extremely concerned and started consultations among themselves.

They thought, “In case Himalaya alone gives his daughter Parvati to Siva, then they could active the nirvanapada of Siva.

Himalaya is the store house of all the gems, beyond measure. In case it achieves salvation, then the name of earth as Ratnagarbha (enshrining gems in her womb) would become infructuous.

Himalaya leaving his immobile form and taking to a divine form, after giving away his daughter to Siva, will proceed to the Sivaloka.

By the grace of Siva he will attain identity with the great god and will enjoy all the bless of comforts there finally attaining liberation.

O Sage, after this type of discussion, the gods went to the abode of their preceptor. For achieving their self interest they spoke to their preceptor thus.

The god said, “O Preceptor, you go to the abode of Himavat, for the accomplishment of our task. Reproach lord Siva and stop the mountain’s devotion to lord Siva.

O Preceptor, in case the mountain gives away his daughter to Siva with great devotion, he will surely attain salvation. Let him stay on earth itself.

Thus listening tot heir words and deeply thinking over the subject.

The preceptor said, “Let anyone of you go to Himavat and place this proposal before him. I am not going to oblige you on the issue.

Otherwise, O Gods, all of you with Indra should go to Brahmaloka and apprise Brahma about your apprehensions. He will surely do your job.

Nandisvara said, “Hearing this and thinking over the subject, all the gods went to the place of Brahma and apprised him of the factual position.

Listening their words and thinking over the matter, Brahma said, “I shall not denounce Siva, because it would be painful for all times to come.

O Gods, all of you should go to Kailas'a, please Siva and send him to the abode of Himavat.

Let him go to Himalaya and denounce himself, because by denouncing others one has to face destruction.

Nandisvara said, “Then all the gods collectively went to Kailasa. Reaching there they offered their salutation to Siva with devotion and then apprised him of the factual position.

Listening to the words of the gods, he accepted them and assuring them he sent them off smilingly.

Then Siva, without blemish, lord of Maya, well disposed towards his devotees, thought of going to the abode of Himalaya.

He was clad in divine garments held the danda and kamandalu in his hands, applying the spotless tilakam, holding the rosary of crystal beads, and carrying Salagrama around his neck, he got ready to leave.

He then taking to the form of an ascetic Brahmana, accompanied with the group of Brahmanas, quickly went to the abode of Himalaya.

Finding him there, Himalaya got up with his ganas and appropriately prostrated before them.

Then the lord of mountain asked them, “Who are you?” On hearing this the excellent Brahmana, respectfully spoke to the lord of mountain.

The ascetic Brahmana said, “O Mountain, I am a Vaisnava ascetic Brahmana. By the grace of my preceptor I possess true vision. I am omniscient and can go anywhere.

O Excellent mountain, I happen to be a devotee of Visnu, and by my divine knowledge, I have known something while I had been in my abode. Listen, I shall mention the same to you with pleasure to you without any haughtiness.

You intend to give your comely daughter resembling Laksmi to Siva, whose race as well as the parentage is unknown.

O King of the mountains, your this idea is not going to bestow welfare. You are born in the race of Narayana, and are foremost of the learned people. You first think over.

O King mountains, you keep in mind that Siva has no kith and kin of his own. You better ask your brothers as well as your wife Mena in this regard.

Leaving Parvati, you better make enquiries from all. O Mountain, a patient never likes the medicine but would prefer the unsuitable diet.

Siva is not a proper person to whom the daughter should be given. The entire world would laugh at you.

He is devoid of home, always lonely, had a deformed body, devoid of gunas, indestructible dweller of the cremation ground, carries the terrific serpents with him and remains naked always.

He applies ashes over his body, carries snakes over the head, devoid of all the dsramas, and his movements are unknown.”

Brahma said, “Thus speaking all the truthful words denouncing Siva, the lord who indulged in several sports, returned to his abode.

Listening to the words of the Brahmana, both Mena and Himalaya, became ready to do unholy things. They thought, “What could be done for the one, who is engaged in the adverse things?”

Then Siva, with the activities which delighted his devotees, married Parvati and performed the jobs of the gods.

O Dear one, O Lord, I have narrated the story of the ascetic Brahmana of Siva which was meant for the establishment of the task of the gods.

The story is quite auspicious, bestower of heaven, enhances life, which has been narrated by me. Whosoever reads it or recites it, he, enjoying all the comforts and achieves salvation.

## Chapter 36 - Siva’s incarnation as Asvatthama

Nandisvara said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, now you listen to Asvatthama incarnation of Siva.

O Sage, from the amsa of immensely intelligent divine sage Brhaspati, an ayonija (born without human contact) son was born known as Drona.

He was the foremost of all the archers, valorous, Brahmarsi, well-versed in all the scriptures, immensely glorious, extremely illustrious and knew pretty well all the Sastras.

The learned people knew him as well versed in the Vedic literature as well as the archery. The excellent Drona, performed astonishing feats had been the promoter of his race.

O Brahmana, he had been the acarya of the Kauravas on the basis of his own strength and was famous as one of the six, prestigious warriors.

In order to help the Kauravas, he performed tapas for Siva for a long time for achieving a son for the purpose.

O Excellent sage, having been pleased with the hard tapas of Drona, lord Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, appeared before Drona.

Finding Siva before him, the Brahmana Drona, delightfully with folded hands, offered his salutation to the lord and started eulogising him.

Getting pleased with his prayer and the penance, Siva- who is well disposed towards his devotees, asked him to seek for a boon.”

Listening to the words of Siva, the humble Drona said, “You bestow a son from your amsa who should be invincible.”

Listening to the words of Drona Siva said, “It will be done accordingly.” O Dear one, O Sage, Siva, the performer of sports, bestower of comforts, then disappeared from the scene.

Thereafter, Drona, feeling delighted and doubtless, went to his abode. Delightfully, he conveyed the news to his wife.

In due course of time lord Siva, destroyer of all, and extremely powerful one, was born as the son of Drona, as his own amsa.

O Sage, he was well known as Asvatthama on earth. He was a great hero having lotus like eyes, and had the power to reduce the power and strength of the enemy.

The valorous Asvatthama at the command of his father, became famous for helping the Kauravas.

The great warrior, with the help of whom Bhisma and other Kaurvas became the great warriors and became invincible even from the gods.

With the terror of whom the Pandavas were unable to be victorious over the Kauravas, and all of them had been defeated inspite of their being the great warriors.

With the performance of the hard tapas for Siva, and at the discourse of Sri Krsna, Arjuna, receiving the weapon from Siva, became victorious over the Kauravas.

O Sage, the immensely valorous Asvatthama, because of his birth from the amsa of Mahadeva, becoming subservient to his devotion, displayed his glory.

Asvatthama, having been well trained in the methods of waging the war, killing the sons of Pandavas, (he remained invincible) and Krsna and other warriors could not stand to his prowess.

Having been grieved with the death of his son, finding Arjuna, arriving mounted over the chariot Asvatthama fled away.

While fleeing, Asvatthama shot a Brahmasira weapon at Arjuna, as a result of all the direction were filled with its lustre.

Finding his life in danger, the frightened Arjuna, loosing all his brilliance said to Krsna becoming utterly exhausted.

Arjuna said, “O Krsna, I am unable to understand anything, this unbearable lustre is approaching me from all the directions.

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of Arjuna, Krsna the devotee of Siva, devoting his mind to Siva and Parvati both, said to Arjuna.

Sri Krsna said, “This is the invincible Brahmastra which has been used by Asvatthama, the son of Drona, which cannot be prevented in any way.

You remember Siva your master atonce, who has given you the fully competent weapon.

With the use of Saivastra by you, reduce the striking powers of his weapon.” Thus speaking, Sri Krsna, for the protection of Arjuna, himself devoted his mind at the feet of Siva, for the protection of Arjuna.

O Sage, listening to the words of Sri Krsna, Arjuna, reciting the name of Siva by hearty, touching the water, shot the Saivastra. Though the weapon named Brahmasira was invincible, and could not be made infructuous in any way, still with the shooting of Saivastra by Arjuna, the former weapon was neutralised.

This is no surprise for Siva having the astonishing type of conduct, because the unborn one, with his prowess, could create, sustain and destroy the universe.

O Sage, Asvatthama, born of the amsa of Siva, was not surprised and maintained his calm by the grace of Siva and did not feel painful.

Thereafter Asvatthama, in order to rid the earth of the Pandavas, decided to kill Abhimanyu- the son of Uttara.

With this end in view, Asvatthama shot a weapon with immense lustre, named Brahmastra which could not be stopped by anyone, at the womb of Uttara.

Then Uttara- the wife of Abhimanyu getting upset with the attack of the weapon and getting inflames with the same, eulogised lord Krsna.

Then Krsna devoting his mind at Siva, offering from his heart, salutation to the lord, realised that the weapon shot by Asvatthama was destroyer of the Pandavas.

Krsna then shot the Sudarsana-cakra which he had received from Indra for his own protection, at the command of Siva, and saved the descendant of the Pandavas.

Knowing about this story, Krsna, the devotee of Siva, painfully bestowed his own form to the foetus.

Then Krsna- a great devotee of Siva, feeling delightful, made all the Pandavas to fall at the feet of Asvatthama.

Then Asvatthama, the son of Drona, feeling delighted, bestowed boons on Pandavas and Krsna lovingly.

O Excellent sage, thus Siva, in the form of the son of Drona, incarnated on earth and enjoyed several sports.

The incarnation of Siva as Asvatthama, was immensely strong and valorous. He showered comforts on all the three lokas. Even today he is lodged at the bank of the Ganga.

I have narrated to you the story about Asvatthama incarnation of Siva. It bestows all success and fulfills the desire of the devotees of Siva.

A person who listens to the story of this incarnation or recites the same, he achieving all success in this world ultimately goes on to Sivapura.

## Chapter 37 - Arjuna deputed to Indrakila mountain by Vyasa

Nandisvara said, “O Learned one, now you listen to the story of the Kirata incarnation of Siva, who getting pleased bestowed a boon on Arjuna for the killing of the demon Muka.

Having been defeated by Arjuna in the gambling game, the excellent Pandavas then proceeded on to the forest of Daivtavana.

Reaching there they spent a lot of time comfortably with the use of the divine vase provided by the sun.

O Excellent Brahmana, Duryodhana, deceitfully sent the sage Durvasa with evil intentions, to the Pandavas.

He went there with his ten thousand pupils and asked the Pandavas to serve them with their desired food.

The Pandavas accepted their demand but asked Durvasa to have a bath at the river with his pupils.

O Excellent sage, after the departure of Durvasa, all the Pandavas got ready to end their lives because they had no food to serve the sage as well as his disciples.

Then Draupadi remembered lord Krsna, who arrived there at the same time, who was satisfied by serving him with a piece of vegetation.

Durvasa the great sage finding himself with his pupils with their bellies filled, left the place.

Then the Pandavas asked Srikrsna, “A powerful enemy has been born. What should we do my lord. You tell us.”

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, when so asked by the Pandavas, Srikrsna, devoting his mind at the feet of Siva, spoke to them.

Srikrsna said, “O Excellent Pandavas, it is my firm belief that all of you should adore Siva.

I myself, reaching Dvaraka, in order to overpower my enemies and keeping in view the advice of the sage Upamanyu, adored lord Siva for seven months at the Batuka mountains.

He fulfilled all my desires. With his influence I received all the best of Saktis.

Even now I serve him. You should also serve Siva, who bestows all the comforts as well as the salvation.

Nandisvara said, “Thus Srikrsna, assuring the Pandavas, disappeared from the place and reached Dvaraka, with his mind devoted at the lotus like feet of Siva.

Then the Pandavas sent a Bhila in order to assess the prowess of Duryodhana.

The Bhila reaching there adequately assessed the strength of Duryodhana and returned to the Pandavas.

O Excellent sage, listening to the words of the Bhila, Pandavas felt painful and spoke among themselves.

“Though we are all fully competent, but still we are bound with fetters of truthfulness. Therefore, what should we do and where should we go?”

Nandisvara said, “At that very moment Vedavyasa, with his body plastered with ashes, wearing the matted locks of hair over the head, and Rudraksa, reached there.

Having been influenced with the devotion of Siva, he was reciting the Pancaksara mantra. He was quite resplendent and appeared like the form of Dharma.

At the arrival of the sage Vyasa, the Pandavas welcomed him while standing and gave him a seat of the deer skin covered by the Kusa-grass. Then they waited in front of him.

After the sage Vyasa was seated comfortably, all the Pandavas adored him with delight, eulogising him at the same time. Then they said to the sage that they felt graceful with his arrival.

They said, “We have performed enormous tapas and given charities as well. All of them have now become successful with your arrival here.”

O Grandfather, by having an audience with you, all over miseries are over. The wicked people with evil intentions have made our lives painful.

By having an audience with you, all over miseries have vanished, about which we had thought that they were beyond removal.

In case one is not relieved of the miseries even after reaching the asramas of the great sages, then it could be the fault of the destiny.

Our poverty- the cause of our grief would also be removed. The nature of the great people is like the kalpavrksa.

O Lord, their merits should always be considered as important, with the coming in touch of whom, or with the taking of refuge with whom, one derives merits.

No one should think of the big or small, because the great people protect the noble people by nature itself.

The characteristic of the degraded and the miserable people, are conducive to their glory, because they have an opportunity to serve the good people, making strenuous efforts.

Thereafter, it is one’s own destiny. No one can be blamed for the same. Therefore, O Lord, on meeting you, everything auspicious takes place.

Your very presence here has delighted our minds. Now you render us the suitable advise to remove our miseries.”

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of the Pandavas, the sage Vyasa felt delighted and spoke to them.

O Pandavas don’t feel painful at heart. You are graceful and successful. You have not deserted the path of truth.

The noble people by nature do not disown the excellent dharma and the truthfulness even at the cost of their lives, because that could be the way to success.

For us people like as you as well as they (Duryodhana and others) are equal. But still one has to favour the truth.

The blind Dhrtarastra, overpowered with greed, discarding dharma, has usurped your kingdom.

For him undoubtedly both Kauravas and Pandavas are his sons. The elders, should be merciful on the younger after the death of their father.

Thereafter he (Dhrtarastra) did not prevent Duryodhana, from misbehaving with you. Had he done so, this calamity would not have befallen today.

Now whatever has been done, has been done and cannot be removed. Duryodhana is indeed wicked. All of you are virtuous and truthful.

Therefore, he has to face the miseries ultimately. The seed which is sown germinates into a plant.

Therefore, you people should not feel painful at all, because you are ultimately going to face the welfare. There could be no second opinion about it.

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, Vyasa, pleased Yudhisthira and the other Pandavas who again said.

The Pandavas said, “O Master, you have spoken the truth, but those wicked people are troubling us even during over staying in the forest.

O Excellent one, you kindly relive us of our miseries. Srikrsna had earlier said, that we should always adore Siva.

We had been lethargic about his advice. Therefore you discourse us over the adoration of Siva.

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of the Pandavas, the sage Vyasa, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, spoke to the Pandavas.” Vyasa said, “O Religious minded Pandavas, you listen to my words. Srikrsna spoke the truth to you, because I myself adore lord Siva.

You also adore him lovingly, which would bestow enormous comforts on you. One faces all the miseries by neglecting Siva.

Nandisvara said, “Thereafter the sage Vyasa, asked Arjuna, of the five Pandavas to particularly adore Siva, explaining to him the details thereof.

The excellent sage then considered Arjuna fit enough for the performing of the penance. Then he spoke to the noble Pandavas.

Vyasa said, “O Pandavas, I speak for your benefit. Siva is the rescue of the noble people. He is the best of all the form of the Supreme Brahman.

Starting with Brahma and ending with infinity whatever is visible in the universe, is the form of Siva alone, which should be adored and respected.

Siva is the remover of all the miseries and should be served by all. Siva is pleased in a short time with his devotion.

When Siva is pleased, he bestows on his devotees all the pleasures besides the salvation.

Therefore the people desirous of pleasures and salvation should adore lord Siva. He destroying all the wicked people, bestows salvation.

But first of all, a Ksatriya should recite the lore of Indra with a firm mind. For a ksatriya possessing enormous resplendence, this alone is conducive to his welfare.

Therefore, let Arjuna, with a firm mind recite the lore of Indra. Initially he will put him to test and then Indra the lord of the gods would be pleased.

Then Indradeva, getting pleased, will remove the obstructions and will guide him about the excellent mantra of Siva.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, the sage, made Arjuna to take his bath first, then making him to face east, advised him on the lore of Indra, which was well received by Arjuna having the sharp wisdom.

The excellent sage, then also enlightened Arjuna listened to the method of worship of Parthiva. Then the sage Vyasa with excellent wisdom, spoke to Arjuna.

Vyasa said, “O Arjuna, now you leave this place and go to the bank of the Ganga over the Indrakila mountain and perform tapas appropriately.

This invisible lore is going to be of immense use for you. Thus blessing Arjuna, Vyasa said to the Pandavas.

O Kings, all of you should remain firm in your dharma. You will meet with excellent success. There is no doubt about it.

Nandisvara said, “The excellent sage then blessed the Pandavas thus and devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, disappeared from that place.

## Chapter 38 - Arjuna’s penance

Nandisvara said, “Arjuna, at that point of time, receiving the mantra became immensely resplendent.

Observing the resplendence of Arjuna, they came to the conclusion that they were bound to be victorious.

It appeared from the words of Vyasa that the task was to be established by Arjuna and none else. They said to him, “O Arjuna, you make our lives a success.”

Thus speaking, the Pandavas feeling painful due to separation from him, sent him, much against their wishes.

The chaste Draupadi, stopping the flow of the tears emerging out of her separation from Arjuna, bade goodbye to him and said, to Arjuna.

Draupadi said, “O King you shall strenuously follow the instructions of the sage Vyasa. Let your path be auspicious and let Siva be your benefactor.”

Thereafter the Pandavas bade farewell to Arjuna and feeling painful thing continued to stay there.

Listen, O Excellent sage, then they observed that a person does not feel painful with his near and dear ones.

In case of separation the pain of separation is doubled daily. Therefore how could a patient person maintain patience?”

Nandisvara said, “O Excellent sage, when the Pandavas were feeling so painful, the sage Vyasa again reached there,

The painful Pandavas gave him a seat with respect and offering their salutation to him, adored him with folded hands.

Pandavas said, “O Lord, we have been burnt out with the painful situation. Your presence has delighted us all.

O BrahmarsI, O Lord, you kindly stay here for sometime in order relieve us from the sufferings. At your mere sight our mental agony is removed.”

Nandisvara said, “At these words of the Pandavas the great sage Vyasa lived there for sometime in order to appease them and made them comfortable. He narrated several types of auspicious stories to them in order to remove their sufferings. O Excellent sage, the humble Dharmaraja, offering his salutation to Vyasa, said to him.

Dharmaraja Yudhisthira said, “O Excellent sage, O Lord, you kindly listen, with the hearing of your words, I feel peaceful. O Immensely learned one, you please tell me whatever I am going to ask you.

Have these types of miseries been faced by anyone else in the world or it is we people who have suffered such types of miseries for the first time?”

Vyasa said, “In earlier times Nala the king of the Nisada country had to face misfortunes far greater then those faced by you.

The king Hariscandra too had to face enormous miseries, which are beyond description, hearing which others also feel painful.

O Pandavas, similar type of misfortune had to be faced by Rama as well, listening to which even today, the men and the women feel painful.

It is beyond my capacity to narrate the same. The human body is the abode of miseries and taking this fact into consideration, you better stop such discussion.

The one who has held this body, he has surely to face the miseries. Initially to enter into the womb of the mother itself is the cause of pain.

During the childhood one has to face trouble suiting to the tender age of childhood. Then in the youthful age, one has to face the pain of desires.

With the passage of time, a person, spends the time of his life, facing many responsibilities, quite unconsciously.

Ultimately, there is the enormous pain of death. Thereafter the learned people have to face several types of hells.

Therefore all this is false and you better behave in a truthful manner, in order to please Siva.

Nandisvara said, “In this way, the brothers, in order to pass time, entered into the several types of discussions.

Arjuna with a firm mind, dwelling in the mountain Caves, where he met with a Yaksa. Thereafter, he killed the decoits.

Feeling delighted he proceeded towards the best of the mountain and reaching there he found a beautiful spot at the bank of the Ganga.

He found Asokavana like the excellent heaven, there. Taking his bath there, offering his salutation to his preceptor, he sat there in meditation.

He was clad in the costumes as advised to him. Accordingly, he controlled all his senses, making his mind stable, he sat there in meditation for performing the penance.

He made a clay idol of Siva, which was quite beautiful. He then stood in front of it in meditation on the excellent heap of splendour.

He used to take bath thrice a day, and worshipped Siva variously. He performed the upasati form of worship of Siva, repeatedly.

Indra’s spies noticed the column of splendour coming out of his head; which frightened them. They thought within themselves, “When did he come here? Indra must be informed." Thus thinking they went to Indra and apprised him of the factual position.

The spies of Indra said, “O God of gods, we know not who is there in the forest, whether he is a god, an ascetic, Surya or the fire, performing the tapas?

Having been scorched with the unbearable lustre issuing from his body, we have arrived here before you. We have apprised you of the factual position, now you may do whatever like.”

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the news of the spies and getting aware of the desire of his son, and leaving the guarding of his family there, he started thinking of going there to text him.

“O Leading Brahmana, Indra, the lord of Saci, assumed the form of an elderly Brahmana bachelor and went to test him.

On his arrival there Arjuna adored him, offering prayer at the same time and sitting before him he asked, “Where from have you arrived. You tell me.”

The lord of gods, Indra thus requested by him spoke with a hint at testing his courage, out of love.

The Brahmana said, “O Excellent one, what for are you performing tapas in this young age? Is it for achieving salvation? Or are you doing so for being victorious?”

Nandisvara said, “When so questioned by the Brahmana, Arjuna apprised him of the entire situation. On hearing which the Brahmana again asked him.

The Brahmana said, “O Warrior, the tapas that is performed for the achieving of the pleasures, that could hardly be appreciated. O Excellent one, a Ksatriya, should perform tapas for salvation alone

Indra is the bestower of the comforts. He cannot bestow salvation. Therefore, O Excellent one, you perform the best of tapas in all respects.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus listening to his words, the ascetic Arjuna was enraged, and spoke disregarding the words of the Brahmana.”

Arjuna said, “Why did you put me a question relating to the kingship or salvation? I am performing this tapas at the command of the sage Vyasa.

O Brahmacari, you can leave this place. You want me to fall from my goal? What is the purpose of your arrival here?”

Nandisvara said, “At these words of Arjuna, Indra, getting pleased appeared before him in his true form with all the splendour.

At that point of time, looking to the form of Indra, Arjuna was ashamed. Indra spoke to him again after consoling him.

Indra said, “O Dear one, O Dhananjaya, O Immensely learned one, you ask for the boon you desire. There is nothing in the world which cannot be given to you.”

Listening to these words of Indra, Arjuna said, “O Dear, you kindly bestow victory on me, since I have been harassed by the enemy.”

Indra said, “Your enemies like Drona, Bhisma- the grand sire, Kama, Duryodhana and others are quite powerful. You will not be able to be victorious over them. It would be difficult even for me to defeat them. Therefore you listen to the words which would be beneficial to you.

O Excellent warrior, except Siva, no one else has the power to grant you the desired victory. Therefore you recite the name of Siva.

Siva happens to be the lord of all the lokas with their mobile and immobile creatures. He is all powerful. He can bestow the pleasures as well as the salvation, beside the other rewards.

I, (Indra), Brahma, Visnu and other gods, bestow the boon, but those desirous of victory should adore Siva alone.

From today onwards, leaving aside my devotion, you should appropriately resort to the adoration of Siva including the one in the form of the clay symbol. You should meditate upon Siva.

By all the means, you should adore Siva with devotion. O Bharata you would surely achieve the everlasting success. Don’t be doubtful in your mind.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus thinking, Indra called all his attendants and said to them, “All of you should protect Arjuna, quite carefully.”

Indra commanded his attendants to guard Arjuna. Indra with his mind filled with love and again said to him.

O Noble one, O terrifier of enemies, never rale the country carelessly. This lore is going to be beneficial to your glory.”

Indra said, “O Excellent one, an aspirant should always keep calm, because Siva protects in all the ways. He will certainly bestow the rewards of wealth and others on you.

Nandisvara said, “In this way, Devaraja Indra, bestowing boon on Arjuna, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, returned to his place.

The immensely great warrior, controlling his senses Arjuna, offered his salutation to Indra. Thereafter he started the severe tapas for Siva.

## Chapter 39 - Killing of the demon Muka and the appearing of Siva in the form of Kirata

Nandisvara said, “According to the directions of Vyasa, Arjuna took his bath, adored Siva appropriately.

The excellent sage standing on one leg, adored Siva appropriately gazing at the sun, started reciting the Siva-mantra.

With his mind devoted at Siva, he kept on muttering the Pancaksara-mantra of Siva.

Observing his splendour achieved by Arjuna, with the performing of penance, the gods felt surprised. They went to Siva and they carefully spoke to him.

The gods said, “O Lord of all, a human is performing tapas to achieve you O Lord, why don’t you give him whatever he wants?”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, the god variously eulogised Siva. Devoting their minds at the feet of lord Siva, all of them sat there, with their mental agony.

The great lord Siva with a large heart, listening to the words of the gods, spoke to them delightfully.

Lord Siva said, “O Gods, your words are true. You better go back to your respective places. I shall surely perform this task of yours. There is no doubt about it.

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of Siva, they felt rest assured. Therefore all the gods went back to their respective places.

At the same time a demon who had been sent by Duryodhana for the killing of Arjuna, arrived there in the form of a boar.

O Foremost of the Brahmana, the deceitful Duryodhana had sent the demon at the same place where Arjuna was lodged.

The demon, tearing out the mountain peaks, as well as the trees, creating various types of sounds, arrived there with great force.

Then Arjuna, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, started thinking.

Arjuna thought, “Who is the one, having arrived with the intention of violence? Who is he? Where from has he come here? Surely he has arrived to kill me.

I am developing a feeling in my mind that he is my enemy. Even earlier I have killed several of the Daityas and Danavas. He is possibly related to some one of them who has arrived here to take revenge, or otherwise, he could be a friend of Duryodhana and devoted to him.

The one by meeting whom the mind feels delighted, he would be a friend and the one by meeting whom the mind feels painful, he is taken to be an enemy.

The conduct reveals the family, the body reveals the diet, the mode of speech reveals the extent of learning and the eye indicates the affection.

The concealed mind is revealed by the general appearance, the mode of walking- the activities, the speech reveals the features of the eyes and the face.

The eye is of four sorts- the resplendent, then impassioned, the squinted and the ruddy. The features are different likewise, O Learned men.

It is resplendent, when the friends meet. It is impassioned at the sight of the son. It is squinted while coming in contact with the beloved and it is ruddy at the sight of an enemy.

At the sight of him my sense organs feel excited. Therefore, he is surely an enemy and should be killed surely.

My preceptor has also advised me that a trouble shooter should be killed without much thinking.

Surely, my weapons are meant for the purpose.” Thus thinking he strung the bow and got ready.

In the meantime, for the protection of Arjuna, and in order to test his devotion, lord Siva, taking to an awful and clever Bhila or a hunter, arrived there with his ganas in order to kill the Daitya.

The hunter had tucked his loin cloth and held the banner of Siva. His body was decorated with white lines made with ashes and carried the bow and arrow.

The quivers of the bow were carried by him at his back and he looked like the king of the hunters or the Bhilas.

The chief commander Bhila, creating several types of sounds, which echoed in all the ten directions, started following the boar.

With the sound thus created in the forest Arjuna was excited, with all the mountains even agitated by these sounds.

Arjuna uttered, “What is all this happening? Let Siva do good to all. I had earlier listened from the month of Srikrsna.

Vyasa had said earlier which was repeated by the gods, “That Siva does good to all bestowing comforts at the same time.

Because of his bestowing salvation, he is called the granter of redemption. With the mere reciting of his name, the people meet with welfare.

Those who adore Siva by action thought and behaviour, they do not have to face the miseries even in dream. If it so happens, it could be due to the activities of the earlier birth.

The force of the powerful destiny is also reduced. There is no doubt about it. Or otherwise it could be the fault of the destiny.

Or otherwise Siva, of his own accord, removes the sufferings of a person to some extent and undoubtedly frees his devotees from the painful situations.

He is all powerful, and can turn at his own will the poison as the nectar or the nectar as the poison.”

Thus thinking the new as well as the old devotees should firmly devote their minds towards Siva.

Irrespective of the coming and going of the wealth, even if one has to face the death, irrespective of the praise or the denouncement, but the miseries could be removed by Siva alone.

It is Siva alone who could save the people form the merits or the sins. He is the only bestower of the eternal pleasure. But sometimes he causes miseries for his devotees as well in order to test his devotion.

Because of his being a compassionate one, he bestows comforts ultimately, in the same way as the dirty gold, after putting in fire, and heating it up, it becomes spotless.

This is what I had heard from Vyasa earlier. Therefore, I can enjoy the best of comforts by adoring Siva.”

While Arjuna was so thinking, by the same time, the boar arrived there for the purpose of killing.

It was being followed by Siva. The astonishing boar started looking like a mountain between Siva and Arjuna.

Arjuna recited the glory of Siva, therefore, Siva, who was well disposed towards his devotees also reached there quite quickly.

At that time both of them shot arrows at the boar. The arrow of Arjuna struck the boar in the mouth, while that Siva, injured the boar at its tail.

The arrow of Siva entered the boar’s body through the tail and emerged out through its mouth, while the arrow of Arjuna entered the body of the boar through its mouth and came out through the hind quarters.

The arrow of Arjuna came out touching the arrow of Siva and fell down. The boar demon was killed and fell down on the ground.

The gods were pleased and showered the rain of flowers. Shouting the slogans of victory they started offering prayers.

Observing the terrific form of the Daitya, Siva was pleased, while Arjuna felt comfortable.

Arjuna with a delightful heart then uttered, “This demon has an astonishing form.

Turning to this form he had arrived for killing me. Undoubtedly lord Siva inspired me to kill him.”

Thus thinking, eulogising Siva Arjuna then went back to the place of his meditation and eulogising Siva he offered his salutation to him.

## Chapter 40 - Quarrel between Arjuna and Siva, at the killing of the boar

Nandisvara said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, listen to the divine sports of Siva which is dubbed with the immense love and devotion of his devotees.

Siva sent his attendant to extract the arrow (from the demon’s body) when Arjuna was also present there.

The ganas of Siva and Arjuna reached simultaneously to pick up the arrows. Arjuna scolding the ganas then took out his own arrow.

The ganas said to him, “O Excellent sage, this arrow belongs to us, therefore you better leave the same.

When the attendants of the Bhila so spoke, Arjuna, remembering the name of Siva, said to them.

Arjuna said, “O Foolish forest dwellers, what are you doing thoughtlessly? I had shot this arrow, then how could it belong to you?

My name has been engraved in many lines over the feathers in the rear of it. Then how could it belong to you? You cannot be free from the temperament of being a plunderer.”

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of Arjuna, the Bhila- the lord of the ganas, laughingly, said to Arjuna who was in the form of an ascetic.

O Ascetic, you are not performing the tapas, but you have deceitfully taken to the form of an ascetic.

How can an ascetic tell a lie? I am an army commander. Don’t think me to be alone here.

Our lord is present here with many of the Bhilas of the forest. He is fully competent to punish or to shower his grace on anyone.

The arrow belongs to him, and you have just picked it up. This arrow cannot remain with you.

O Ascetic, why do you want to discard the tapas stealthily, deceitfully or in a surprising manner?

I have heard that the penance is marred and wasted by indulging in theft, pride, deceitfulness and the breaking of the promise. Therefore, O Sage, how can you derive the benefit of the penance?

In case you do not give me this arrow, you will be an ungrateful person. It was surely for saving your life that my master shot this arrow. This is true.

Your enemy has been killed by him while you in return have grabbed his arrow. You are an extremely ungrateful person and are going to spoil the fruits of the tapas.

In case you are not truthful, then how could you meet with success? In case you are in need of this arrow, then go to our master and beg for the same from him.

He can give you several of such arrows. He is our king. Why don’t you ask from him for an arrow?

Without your asking for his help, he has rendered his help to you, you intend to do harm to him. This is not at all proper. You better free yourself today of your fickle mindedness.”

Thus listening to his words, Arjuna, the son of Prtha, devoting his mind at Siva, spoke the arrogant words.

Arjuna said, “O Bhila, you better listen to what have to be spoken by me. Your words are devoid of truthfulness. I am well aware of the forest race to which you belong.

While I am a king, you are a thief. How can there be a fight between you and me. I fight with equals, and not with the people who are lower to me in status.

Therefore your master would also be like you. We have always been called as the donors, but you forest dwellers are thieves.

O Forest dweller, now you tell me, how can I ask anything from your master? Why don’t you ask for my arrow from me?

I have a number of such arrows, which I can give you. You yourself can also have the arrows from me. But I cannot part with the arrow like this?

O Forest dweller, in case your master so desires, then I can give him many such arrows. Why does he not come forward and ask for the same.

You are simply talking. Let your master arrive here and be victorious over me in the battle.

O Bhila commander, let your master have this arrow from me and comfortably go back to his home. Why is he delaying?

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of Arjuna, who achieved prowess by the grace of Mahesvara, the Bhila spoke.”

Bhila said, “You are a fool but not an omniscient ascetic. Why do you want to die. Give me the arrow and be comfortable, otherwise you will have to face ugly situation.

Nandisvara said, “At these words of the Bhila who was blessed with the Sakti of Siva, Arjuna, devoting his mind towards Siva, said to him.

Arjuna said, “O Forest dweller, you carefully listen to my words. On the arrival of your master, I shall show him the reward.

To fight with you would be like a lion fighting with a jackal, which would be laughable. I shall fight with your master.

You have listened to my words. Now you will witness my great prowess. Therefore you go to your master, or you do whatever you like.”

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, at these words of Arjuna, the Bhila went (to his master) Siva in the form of a Kirata- the chief commander.

Thereafter the Bhila apprised his master of the details of all the conversation he had with Arjuna.

The lord of Kiratas listening to the words of his gana felt delighted. Then Siva, in the form of a Bhila arrived (at the place of Arjuna) with his army.

The Pandava Arjuna also looking at the army of Kirata arrived there with his bow and arrows.

Thereafter the Kirata again sent a messenger to Arjuna, the great soul, to deliver him the message.

Kirata said, “O Ascetic, at the sight of the army, you better return the arrow. Why do you intend to kill yourself for a petty thing?

Your brothers and wife will feel painful and the kingship of the earth would slip out of your hands. This is what I feel.”

Nandisvara said, “Siva taking to the deceitful form for the protection of Arjuna intended to test the firmness of his mind and said.

Then Siva accompanied with his gana went to Arjuna and tried to convince him explaining the entire situation.

On hearing this, Arjuna spoke to the messenger who has arrived before him that he should go and inform the army commander, “In case I follow your words, everything would become topsy-turvy.

In case I return my arrow to you, it would be the cause of ignominy to my entire race.

My brothers would feel painful and all my lores would prove infructuous. Therefore let us fight out.

The fight of lion with a jackal is unheard of similarly a king is never arraid of a forest dweller.”

Listening to the words of Pandava, again returning to his master, he spoke to Siva, the form of the universe.

Thereafter Mahadeva in the form of a Kirata, listening to the words of the messenger, went to Arjuna with his army.

## Chapter 41 - Battle between Siva and Arjuna, Siva bestows boon to Arjuna, meeting of Arjuna with Sri Krsna in Dvaitavana

Nandisvara said, “At the arrival of Kirata, Arjuna devoting his mind towards Siva, fought a terrific battle. The ganas of Siva, also caused pain to Arjuna, with the various types of sharp arrows. Having been injured by them, Arjuna remembered his lore.

Then Arjuna also destroyed the arrows of the ganas of Siva. When they again shot the arrows at Arjuna, he remembered Siva.

With the shooting of the arrows by Arjuna, the ganas of Siva fled away in all the ten directions and never returned to their master.

Then Siva and Arjuna possessing enormous strength and prowess, kept on fighting with various types of weapons.

Then Siva feeling compassionate towards Arjuna, went to him but Arjuna hit hard on him.

Then Siva snatched away all the weapons and kavacas of Arjuna, leaving only his body with him.

Though frightened within himself, Arjuna kept on courage and patience, devoting his mind at Siva and engaged himself in a wrestling with Siva.

During the battle, the ocean as well as the earth started shaking and the gods were perplexed about the future sequence of events.

By the same time lord Siva started fighting remaining in the sky, Arjuna also followed the same.

Both the king and the god were fighting while flying in a surprising manner. Observing that battle the gods felt astonished.

Thereafter, Arjuna, finding the opponent to be a stronger than him, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, and deriving the strength therefrom, he held his feet.

Catching hold of Siva’s feet he whirled him. But lord Siva, favourably disposed towards his devotees, laughed, indulging in divine sports

O Sage, it was surely done by Siva himself, who is subservient to his devotees and it could not be otherwise as he was going to bestow his devotion on him.

Then Siva smiled and revealed his wonderful, auspicious and true form as an absolute supreme being as brought out in the Vedas, Sastras, and the Puranas. It was the form, which Vyasa had advised him to meditate upon. It was the form, which bestowed all the siddhis. It was the form of Siva, looking at which Arjuna was surprised.

He uttered, “Alas! A calamity has occurred. It is none else than Siva himself, who had been accepted by me as my lord. He himself is the lord of the three worlds. What is all that has been done by me?

The Maya of the lord is quite powerful, which overpowers even those who possess Maya. Concealing his true form, what has the lord done? He has cheated me.

Thus thinking in his mind, folding his hands, lowering his head, he offered his salutation to the lord quite lovingly and feeling painful, he spoke.

Arjuna said, “O Mahadeva, the god of gods, you kindly forgive me for my sins.

You, concealing your form have cheated me. What has been done by you? O Lord, disgrace to me for fighting with you.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus the Pandava, while repenting fell down at the feet of Siva the great lord.

Thereafter Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, feeling pleased, variously assuring Arjuna, said to him.

Siva said, “O Arjuna, don’t feel sorry, you are a great devotee of mine. All what I did was to test your devotion towards me. Therefore be relieved of the grief.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, Siva lifted up Arjuna with his own hands and rid him of his bashfulness by means of his own qualities of being the lord of the universe.

Then pleasing Arjuna, the son of Pandu- honoured by the great warriors, Siva, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees, spoke to him quite pleasantly.”

Siva said, “O Arjuna, the foremost of the sons of Pandava, whatever weapons had been shot by you during the battle were treated by me as my adoration by you with flowers. I feel pleased with you. You seek for a boon.

All this has been done by me with my own sweet will. You are not at all at fault. There is nothing with me which cannot be given to you. Therefore you ask for anything you like.

I have performed this auspicious task in order to spread your glory among your enemies and to stabilise your kingdom. Don’t feel painful and free yourself from the anxiety.

Nandisvara said, “At these words spoken by Siva to Arjuna, then the latter, getting careful spoke to Siva.

Arjuna said, “O Lord, O Sadasiva, O God, you are quite compassionate. You love your devotees. How can one describe about your desires?”

Thus speaking the Pandava started adoring lord Siva. Arjuna then eulogised the lord according to the provisions of the Vedas.

He said, O God of gods, O Dweller of Kailasa, O Sadasiva, having five faces, salutation to you.

O Lord having the locks of hair over the head, having three eyes, having the pleasing appearance, you are thousand faced, salutation to you.

O Blue throated one, O Sodyojata, Bull bannered, lord of Girija, salutation to you.

You have ten arms, the supreme soul, holder of a damaru, holder of a skull, wearer of the garland of skulls, salutation to you.

Your body is resplendent like the crystal or the camphor, you are the holder of a trident and a bow. Salutation to you.

You are clad in the tiger skin as well as the elephant hide. You also carry the serpents as well as the Ganga. Salutation to you.

You have beautiful red feet and are served by Nandi and other ganas. You are the lord of ganas. Salutation to you.

You are the form of Ganesa, salutation to you. Kartikeya is your follower, therefore salutation to you. You bestow the devotion and salvation to the devotees. Salutation to you.

You are without attributes as well with them, salutation to you. You are formless as well as with form. You are having the digits, as well as you are devoid of digits. Salutation to you.

Salutation to you since you took to the form of a Kirata in order to bestow your grace on me. You are fond of battle, and follower of the sports of the battle of the great warriors. Salutation to you.

Whatever form is visible represents your lustre. You are the form of pure consciousness. You sport about in different forms in the three worlds.

Your excellence is beyond limit, like the particles of dust or the stars in the sky or the drops of rain.

Even the Vedas are unable to highlight your good qualities. O Lord, how can I, with little intelligence, speak about them.

O Mahesan, O Mahesvara, you are what you are. You can bestow your grace over a slave like me, because you happen to be my lord.”

Nandisvara said, “Listening to the words of Arjuna, the delightful Siva spoke to Arjuna, smilingly.

Siva said, “What is the use of talking much. You better listen to my words. I can give you everything.”

Nandisvara said, “At these words of Siva, Arjuna offered his salutation to the lord with folded hands and spoke in miserable tone.

Arjuna said, “O Excellent one, what should I say, you are yourself all knowledgeable. Still you kindly listen to me what I have to say.

The danger from the enemy has been subsided by having an audience with you. You kindly do something by which I may be able to achieve success in the present as well as the future world.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking, with folded hands, lowering his shoulders, offering his salutation to Siva, Arjuna stood before Siva.

Siva also felt extremely pleased and satisfied finding Arjuna, the son of Pandu, the foremost of his devotees.

Siva then gave to Arjuna, his invincible Pasupata weapon. Then he said to him.

Siva said, “This is the greatest weapon with me, which I am giving to you. Now no one can defeat you. Now you will be victorious over the enemies.

I shall also speak to Sri Krsna to help you. He happens to be my soul and is devoted to me. Therefore he will establish your task.

O Bharata, with my influence, you with your brothers should always follow the dharma and rule the country without obstruction.”

Nandisvara said, “Thus speaking Siva placed his hand over the head of Arjuna and disappeared.

Thereafter, Arjuna, after achieving the boon and the divine weapon, getting delighted, remembering Siva- his preceptor and returned to his abode.

All the brothers, after meeting Arjuna, felt immensely pleased as the body comes back to life. With this the chaste Draupadi also felt comfortable.

The delighted Pandavas, were not satiated by hearing the details from Arjuna and knowing that Siva was quite satisfied. There was a shower of flowers and the sandal paste in the hermitage for honouring Arjuna, the enemy of the boar.

Feeling delighted, they offered their salutation to Siva while thanking him. Keeping in view that the period of exile is coming to an end, a ray of hope for victory kindled in them.

In the mean time Sri Krsna came to know about the arrival of Arjuna and he arrived in the forest to meet him. Learning of the entire news, he was pleased.

I have therefore stated that lord Siva, relieves all of their miseries. Therefore, I also adore him. You should also do so.

Thus I have narrated the story of the Kirata incarnation of Siva. By listening to it or reciting it to others, a person gets his desires fulfilled.

## Chapter 42 - Siva’s incarnations as twelve Jyotirlingas

Nandisvara said, “O Sage, now you listen to the incarnation of Siva as twelve Jyotirlingas of Siva, who indulges in various types of the divine sports.

These Jyotirlingas include (i) Somanatha in Saurastra, (ii) Mallikarjuna over Srisaila, (iii) Mahakala in Ujjain, (iv) Amaresvara in Omkaresvara, (v) Kedara in Himalaya, (vi) Bhimasankara in Dakini, (vii) Visvesara in Varanasi, (viii) Trayambaka over the bank of the river Gautami, (ix) Vaidyanatha at Citabhumi, (x) Nagesa in Darukavana, (xi) Ramesvara at Setubandha and (xii) Ghusmesa at Sivalaya.

O Sage, these are the twelve incarnations of Siva- the Supreme soul, which bestow the pleasure by a gaze at them or with the touch of the same.

O Sage, in first incarnation of Somanatha, the lord had removed the miseries of the moon. One is relieved of the ailments like consumption, leprosy and others by adoring Siva in this form.

Siva in the form of Somanatha incarnated in Saurastra. Siva in this form was adored by the moon for the first time.

There is a moon altar there which washes out all the sins. By bathing in this kunda one is relieved of all the ailments.

By looking at the Somanatha-linga, which happens to be the soul of Siva, a person getting relieved of the sins, enjoys pleasures and the salvation.

O Dear one, the second Mallikarjuna incarnation of Siva, is located over the Srigiri mountain, which bestows the desired reward to the devotees.

O Sage, this linga was initially adored for achieving of a son, as a result of which Siva had arrived there from Himalaya.

O Sage, the second Jyotirlinga, by its adoration and looking at it, bestows comforts and its bestows salvation ultimately.

O Dear one, the Mahakala incarnation of Siva, appeared in the city of Ujjain. He protects his devotees.

This is the Jyotirlinga, which had reduced to ashes the demon named Dusana, who had arrived there to kill the son of the Brahmana Vedapriya. On being eulogised, Siva had arrived there and destroyed demon, the enemy of the Brahmanas, and destroyer of the Vedic dharma by merely uttering the humkara, reducing him to ashes.

Killing him, Siva in the form of Mahakala Jyotirlinga, got himself established there itself at the request of the gods, for the protection of his devotees.

Looking at the Mahakala Jyotirlinga, adoring it by making all the efforts, a person has all his desires fulfilled and he achieves salvation ultimately.

The fourth incarnation of Siva- the supreme soul, happens to be the linga named Omkaresvara, which fulfills the desires of his devotees.

O Sage, lord Mahadeva had appeared from his Parthiva-linga which had been appropriately established, to fulfil the desires of the Vindhyagiri mountain.

At the prayer of the gods, Siva, the bestower of the pleasures and the salvation, took to two forms and lodged himself there, being the one who is well disposed towards his devotees.

O Lord of the sages, the excellent phallic image abides in the syllable Omkara. It also abides in the earthen phallic image in Omkaresvara-Mandhata.

O Sage, O Great sage, whatever is adored in the extremely divine phallic image described to you bestows the desire of all the devotees.

The fifth great incarnation of Siva is the Kedaresa enshrined at Kedaranatha mountain in the form of a Jyotirlinga.

It is lodged at Visnu’s Nara-Narayana incarnation at the Kedara peak of the Himalaya.

The linga of Siva, known as Kedaresvara was adored by Nara-Narayana. It fulfills the desires of his devotees who adore it or have a look at it.

Inspite of his being the lord of all, he is particularly the lord of Kedara-khanda. O Dear one, this incarnation of Siva, fulfills all the desires of his devotees.

The sixth incarnation of Siva- the great lord is called Bhimasankara. During this incarnation, Siva had playfully killed the demon Bhimasena.

Siva, in this incarnation, killed an awful demon who caused terror for the devotees of Siva and protected the king Sudaksina of Kamarupa.

Siva himself is lodged in the form of linga at the well known place of Dakini. The king Sudaksina eulogised him.

The seventh incarnation of Siva in the form of a linga was held at Kasi. O Sage, it is the form of the entire universe which bestows the pleasure and devotion.

Visnu and all other gods, as well as Kubera and Bhairava are also lodged there.

Siva is lodged there in the form of a Jyotirlinga there. In his own city, the lord is found in the form of a siddha, who confers salvation.

Such of the people, who recite the names of Kasi and Visvesvara, and keep on muttering his name with devotion remain un¬influenced by the karmas and ultimately achieve the state of Kevalya.

The eighth incarnation of Siva- the moon crested one as Tryambaka, who appeared on the bank of the river Gautami at the prayer of the sage Gautama.

When requested by the sage Gautama, and in order to delight the sage, the lord stood there, motionless in the form of a Jyotirlinga.

It is quite surprising that with look and touch of the lord, all the tasks of the people get established and they achieve salvation ultimately.

By the grace of lord Siva the river GautamI happens to be the beloved of Siva there, which delights the sage Gautama.

The ninth incarnation in phallic form of Siva is known as Vaidyanatha, who emerged for the sake of Ravana, who indulged in various types of sports.

(It is said that) Ravana was carrying (Siva under the pretext of fetching him, but he was installed in the form of a Jyotirlinga in a cremation ground.

The lord than came to be known as Vaidyanatha in the three worlds. In case one looks at the lord or worships him with devotion, he attains pleasure as well as salvation.

O Sage, the prayers highlighting the greatness of Vaidyanathesvara, earns the devotees the worldly pleasures as well as the devotion, who read or listen to the same.

The incarnation of Nagesvara is glorified as the tenth one. He incarnated himself for the protection of his devotees and for the punishing of the wicked people.

He killing the Daruka demon, who was the destroyer of dharma, saved his devotee named Supriya Vaisya.

Siva, who is always engaged in the welfare of the universe absorbed himself as Jyotirlinga of Samba- Sadasiva.

O Sage, by looking at the phallic image of Nagesvara, and by adoring him, the terrific sins are washed out.

The eleventh phallic incarnation of Siva is known as Ramesvara, which was consecrated by Rama himself. This Jyotirlinga had helped Rama.

Lord Siva, having been pleased with the devotion of Rama, had blessed him to be victorious. This Sivalinga appeared at that point of time, since Siva is known to be well disposed towards his devotees.

O Sage, Rama, adored and eulogised lord Siva immensely in phallic form, after which the Setubandha was built.

Since that date the Ramesvara Jyotirlinga is being held in high esteem. This linga fulfilling all the desires of the devotees, bestows the salvation.

A person who bathes the Ramesvara linga with the water of the Ganga, becomes the living liberated soul.

He enjoys all the divine pleasures on earth, which are beyond the reach of the gods and ultimately achieves moksa.

Ghusmesvara is the twelfth phallic incarnation of Siva, who performing several sports, delights Ghusma.

O Sage, in the southern region near Devasaila, lord Siva had appeared in a tank to please Ghusma his devotee.

O Sage, Siva who is well disposed towards his devotees, saved the son of Ghusma from the terror of the demon Sudehya, feeling pleased with devotion of Ghusma’s son.

Feeling pleased with his prayer, Ghusmesvara who fulfills all the desires, took to the form of a Jyotirlinga, over the bank of the tank.

One who looks at the Sivalinga with devotion, and adoring it, a devotee enjoying all the worldly pleasures attains salvation ultimately.

Thus I have narrated the glory of all the twelve Jyotirlingas, which bestow devotion as well as the salvation.

Whosoever listens to the story of these Jyotirlingas or reads it, he getting free from all the sins, achieves Satarudriya Samhita in which the details of a hundred incarnations of Siva have been spelt out who fulfills all the desires.

Whosoever will recite this Samhita carefully or listen to it, all his desires will be fulfilled. He will achieve salvation ultimately.

Thus ends the third Satarudra Samhita of Siva Mahapurana

## Koti-Rudra Samhita

## Chapter 1 - Greatness of Jyotirlinga and Upalingas

The one who is free from all the blemishes and enshrines all the fourteen *Bhuvanas* in himself, with the slightest compassion of whom a person achieves all the fortunes as well as the *moksa,* whom the *yogis* blissfully meditate upon in their hearts, such an illustrious Siva, always has Parvati lodged to his left, I offer my salutation to such a great lord.

He is full of compassion and as such he has the pleasant sight, wears a serene smile over the face, resplendent with the digit of the moon, he is remover of all the three types of distress, (*adhidevik*, *adhibhautika,* as well as *adhyatmik),* whose existence and knowledge sheds brightness and who is encircled with the arms of the daughter of the mountain i.e. Parvati.

The sages said, “O Suta, you have well narrated the glory of the Siva’s incarnations, keeping in view the welfare of the people of the world.

O Excellent one, O Supreme Mahesvara, you are indeed graceful, therefore you speak out further the glory and greatness of the *Sivalingas* in detail. In every region of the earth, the auspicious *lingas* are found. Besides, there are the *Sivalingas* at some other auspicious places.

O Disciple of Vyasa, you better describe such *lingas* (phallic images of the great lord) in detail whether they be on the earth in the different holy centres or in the places glorified by men, keeping in view the welfare of the people.

Suta said, “O Excellent sage, you have put me an excellent question, keeping in view the good of the people. O Brahmanas, I shall describe these *lingas* in brief.

O Sage, there are innumerable *Sivalingas* in the world. The entire earth is full of *lingas,* besides the entire earth has the form of *linga.*

All the holy places have the form of *lingas,* which are lodged in the mobile and immobile world. Though they are numberless, still, I would like to speak out something.

Whatever is visible in the world, or is talked about, or is remembered, is all in the form of Siva. There is nothing else except him.

Still, O Sages, whatever has been heard by me, and whatever is found on earth, I shall lovingly narrate the same.

There are *Sivalingas* in the heaven as well as in the nether world, because Siva is worshipped by the gods, demons, as well as the humans. Therefore the *Sivalingas* are found in all the three worlds.

O Sages, as the gods, the demons and the humans are found in all the three worlds, similarly the *Sivalingas* which shower their grace on all are similarly found in the world in the form of *lingas.*

For the showering of the grace on the human beings, the *Sivalingas* were consecrated in holy as well as the other places.

Wherever Siva was remembered with devotion by the devotees, he appeared at such places and after performing the task of his devotees, he established himself there.

In order to do good to the people, he created the *linga* and by adoring the *lingas,* the devotees meet with success.

O Brahmanas, all the *lingas* of Siva found on earth, are beyond counting, still I would like to describe the prominent *lingas.*

I shall speak out the main *linga* at prominent places, listening to which a person is relieved of all the sins in a moment.

O Excellent one, all the prominent *Jyotirlinga* are being described by me. By listening to their names all the sins are washed out in a moment.

There is Somanatha in Saurastra, Mallikarjuna at Srisaila, Mahakala at Ujjaini, Paramesvara or Amalesvara in the Omkara- ksetra, Kedaresvara is in Himalaya, Bhimasankara in Dakini, Visvanatha in Varanasi, Tryambakesvara at the bank of Gautami, Baidyanatha at the cremation ground, Nagesvara at Darukavana, Ramesvara at Setubandha, while Ghusmesvara or Ghusanesvara at Sivalaya.

A person who recites the name of these twelve *Jyotirlinga* daily in the early morning, he is relieved of all the sins, and he meets with all the success.

O Excellent sage, whosoever will recite the names of these *Jyotirlinga* with any particular desire in his mind, he will achieve success in that particular field in the present as well as in the future world.

Such of the large hearted people who would recite their names in a selfless manner, they shall never have to enter again the wombs of their mothers.

With their adoration, the miseries of the people of all the *varnas* shall disappear in this world and they ultimately would achieve salvation.

The offerings of these *Jyotirlingas* shall be taken and others shall be fed with the same. Such a performance, reduces the sins to ashes atonce.

O Brahmanas, the result of the worship of the *Jyotirlinga* cannot be described by Brahma and others.

Even if one of them is adored, continuously for six months, the pain of rebirth in mother’s womb will never recur.

O Great sage, even if a person of a base birth happens to see the *Jyotirlinga,* he would in future be born in a pure and a good family.

After having been bom in a good family, he will become rich and the master of the Vedas. Then after performing the auspicious rites, he shall attain salvation, without any obstruction.

O Great sage, whosoever he might be, whether he is an outcaste, a slave or a person of lowest caste, by looking at the *Jyotirlinga,* he is reborn in the Brahmana race. Therefore, one should always have an audience with the *Jyotirlinga.*

I have described the fruits of these *Jyotirlingas* only slightly, O Excellent sages, now you listen about the *upa-Jyotirlingas.*

At the meeting point of the earth and the ocean, there is an *upalinga* of Somesvara. It is also known as Antakesa.

Besides the Mallikarjuna in Bhrgu-kaksa, there is an *upalinga* called Rudresvara, which bestows comforts of its devotees.

At the bank of Narmada, besides the Mahakala *Jyotirlinga,* there is an *upalinga* called Dugdhesa, which removes all the sins.

Besides the *Jyotirlinga* of Omkaresvara, there is an *upalinga* known by the name of Kardamesa. It is lodged over the bank of the Bindu lake and fulfills all the desires of the people.

An *upalinga* named Bhutesa is found close to Kedaresvara, which is lodged over the bank of the Yamuna. It relieves his devotees of all the sins.

An *upalinga* known as Bhimesa, is found near Bhimasankara, which is lodged in Sahyacala. I bestows the strength of the body as well as of the mind.

*Jyotirlinga* Nagesvara is lodged over the bank of the river Sarasvati-Mallika, close by there is an *upalinga* named Bhutesvara. All the sins get destroyed by devoting at it.

The *upalinga* Guptesvara is found near Ramesvara, while *upalinga* Vyaghresvara is found near Ghusmesa.

O Brahmanas, I have described the *Jyotirlingas* as well as the *upalingas,* which remove the sins and fulfill all the desires.

O Sages, there are the prominent *lingas.* Besides them, whatever the important *lingas* are there, you listen their description from me.

## Chapter 2 - Sivalingas and their greatness

Suta said, “The city of Kasi is located at the bank of the river Bhagirathi or the Ganga, which bestows salvation and is the dwelling place of Siva.

A *linga* known as Avimukta is lodged there. There is an other *linga* known as Krttivasesvara, because of which all the residents of the place, irrespective of their being young or old, have been equated with Siva.

There are two more *lingas* at Kasi, known as Tilabhandesvara as well as Dasasvamedha. At the confluence of the Ganga-sagara, there is a *Sivalinga* known by the name of Samgamesvara.

The *lingas* named Bhutesvara as well as Narisvara, are lodged over the bank of the Kausiki river.

Batukesvara *linga* has been lodged over the bank of the river Gandaki and the *linga* known as Purisvara, which bestows comforts on all, is consecrated over the bank of the Phalgun river.

Towards the north from that place, there are two *lingas* known as Siddhanathesvara as well as Duresvara, with bestow success to the people, with merely having a look at them.

Srngesvara is lodged in the battle ground of Dadhici. Besides these, Vaidyanathesvara and Japyesvara *lingas* of that place are also well known.

Besides the *lingas* named Gopesvara, Rangesvara, Vamesvara, Nagesvara, Kamesvara, Vimalesvara, Vyasesvara, Sukesvara, Bhandesvara, Humkaresvara, Surocanesvara, Bhutesvara, Sangamesvara, remove all the great sins.

Over the bank of the Taptika river, Kumaresvara *linga* is lodged. Besides the Siddhesvara and Sanesvara *lingas* are also found there.

The *lingas* named Ramesvara, Kumbhesvara, Nandisvara, Punjesvara, and Pumakesvara are lodged over the banks of the river Purna.

At the Dasasvamedha *ghata* of the holy place of Prayaga, the Brahmesvara *linga* was consecrated by the lord Brahma in earlier times which bestows *dharma, artha, kama* and *moksa.*

The Somesvara *linga* is also lodged which removes all the obstructions. Then there is the Bhardvajesvara *linga* which enhances the *Brahmateja.*

The linga called Sulakantesvara, which fulfills all the desires, is also there, besides Madhavesvara *linga* is the protector of his devotees.

O Brahmanas, the *linga* named Nagesvara, which particularly bestows its grace over the kings of the solar face, has also been established in Saket (Ayodhya).

The *linga* named Bhuvanesvara is lodged in Purusottamapuri, which is quite famous. The *Mahalinga* named Lokesvara, bestows all types of bliss.

The *Sivalinga* known as Kamesvara and Gangesa, bestow extreme purification. There is a *linga* known as Sukresvara, which is adored by Indra, or the benefit of the people.

Batesvara *linga* fulfills all the desires. Two *lingas* named Kapalesvara and Vattresvara, which remove all the sins are lodged over the bank of the Sindhu river.

The Sivalingas known as Dhautapapesvara as well as Bhimesvara and Suryesvara are said to have emerged out of the *amsas* of Siva.

Nandisvara which is adored by the people of the three worlds bestows knowledge, while Nakesvara and Ramesvara bestow high merits.

The *lingas* known as Vimalesvara, Kantakesvara and Dhartukesa are lodged close to the confluence of Ganga-sagara.

The *linga* known as Candresvara, bestows peace like the moon, while Siddhesvara *linga* fulfills all the desires.

The spot where Siva had killed Andhakasura, has two *lingas* known as Bilvesvara and Andhakesvara.

Siva from his own *amsa* took to Saranesvara and he established himself there for the comforts of the people.

There is a *linga* named Kardamesa, while the Kotisvara *linga* is lodged over the Arbuda mountain. The Acalesa *linga* which bestows comforts to the people is also quite well- known.

Over the bank of the river Kausiki, there is a *linga* lodged there, which is known as Nagesvara. Antesvara *linga* bestows welfare and grants benefit to the people.

The *lingas* known as Yogesvara, Kotisvara, Saptesvara and Vaidyanathesvara are also quite well-known.

Siva’s *linga* known as Bhadra, is famous as Bhadraesvara. The *lingas* known as Candesvara, Sangamesvara are also connected with them.

In the eastern direction, there are some ordinary *lingas,* which have been mentioned by me to you.

O Munisvara, Now I shall describe the *lingas* of the southern region.

## Chapter 3 - Tapas performed by the sage Atri and emerging of Atrisvara linga

Suta said, “In Brahmapuri over the Citrakuta mountain, is a *linga* known as Mattagajendra which was established by Brahma himself in the earlier times. It fulfills all the desires.

To the east of it, there is an other *linga* known as Kotisa. To the west of Godavari, there is a *linga* known as Pasupati.

In the southern direction, Siva himself is lodged in the form of Atrisvara *linga* for the benefit of Anusuya and the other lokas. Lord Siva appearing in the form of *linga* had removed the sufferings of the people due to draught and failing of the rains.”

The *rsis* said, “O Excellent *rsi,* O Suta, how did Siva appear there in the form of Atrisvara?”

Suta said, “O *rsis,* you have questioned me correctly. In this connection I shall tell you the best of a story, listening to which, one is relieved of all the sins.

In the southern region, there is a forest named Kamada, located close to Citrakuta. It makes the ascetics and the noble people quite happy.

Atri, the son of Brahma accompanied with his wife performed hard *tapas* there.

O Sage, once there was draught for a hundred years and there was no rain fall at all, as a result of which the people were suffering.

O Excellent sages, during those times all the trees and the fruits had dried up. No water could be found even for daily use.

No moisture could be found anywhere. Hot wind kept on blowing everywhere. There was a turmoil among the people.

Observing the destruction of the people, the chaste wife of the sage Atri spoke to her husband, that she could no more look to the miseries of the people.

Thereafter, the excellent sage, seated in meditation, performing *pranayama* thrice.

He devoted his mind to the spotless Siva having the extreme lustre.

Finding her husband and the preceptor- the sage Atri, thus engaged in meditation, his disciples deserted him due to the shortage of food. They went to far off places.

Then the chaste lady Anusuya was left all alone.

She daily used to perform the adoration of the *Parthiva linga* as well as the sage Atri reciting the *mantras* appropriately. After serving Siva repeatedly, she eulogised him with devotion.

Anusuya, the well behaved wife of the sage Atri, circumumbulated her lord as well as Siva. After prostration, she went round in the reverse manner too. Observing the beautiful lady, the Daityas and Danavas were extremely agitated by her brilliance. But they kept themselves away as the people do from the blazing fire.

O Excellent Brahmanas, Anusuya’s service to Siva, was performed mentally with devotion through mind, speech and body, which surpassed even the penance of the sage Atri.

Till such time the sage was engaged in *pranayama,* both the husband and wife remained engaged in their respective duties.

O Excellent sage, till such time, no one was there, the sage Atri remained engaged in his *tapas* without any obstruction. The chaste Anusuya also kept herself engaged in the service of her lord and Siva.

Having been engrossed in service of her husband and Siva, she knew nothing. As a result of the *tapas* of Atri as well as the service of Anusuya, the gods, *rsis,* besides the Ganga and other rivers, arrived there delightfully to have an audience with them.

Observing the *tapas* and service, they felt surprised with their astonishing devotion, they had observed.

“The penance of which one of the two- or the service is greater?” They themselves replied, “Atri’s penance is good but the service of Anusuya is better.”

Looking at the performance of both of them, some of them, said, “Her service is better.” Others said, “The sage has performed difficult penances of course, but nothing could be compared with the penance of Dadhici.

The sage is blessed, Anusuya is also blessed, since the great penance is pursued by these with great pleasure. If there be any other person, performing such an auspicious, difficult and excellent penance, anywhere in the three worlds, we are not aware of the same.” Thus praising them, they left the place, leaving Ganga and Siva.

Feeling delighted with the adoration of Siva and fascinated with the *dharma,* she (Ganga) stayed there.

O Ascetics, Ganga said, “I shall do good to Anusuya, before my departure. Siva on the other hand, was fascinated with the *tapas* of Atri and stayed there.

O Excellent sages, Siva, after getting lodged there in his full *amsas,* then retreater to Kailasa. In the meantime, fifty four years passed, but there were no rains. Then as the sage Atri was meditating, Anusuya resolved to keep on fasting even without water.
