Thereafter what happened after the *tapas* of the sage Atri and the devotion of Anusuya, you listen to the same.

## Chapter 4 - Appearing of Atrisvara linga

Suta said, “O Foremost among those having the knowledge of Brahman, the sage Atri, then woke up from his penance and asked his wife Anusuya, for water.

The chaste Anusuya, holding a *kamandalu,* went deep into the forest, thinking, where to go? Where from to get water?

She thought, “What should I do, where should I go? Where from shall I get the water?” At the same time she looked at Ganga with surprise.

By the time she went over to her, Ganga, the most auspicious river, assumed a beautiful form and said to her.

Ganga said, “O Goddess, you are graceful, tell me, where are you going? I am pleased with you, therefore, I have to obey your command.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, listening to his words, feeling surprised, she said.

Anusuya said, “O Lotus eyed one, who are you? Where from have you come? You kindly tell me truthfully.”

Suta said, “O Excellent sage, at these words of the wife of the sage, the divine Ganga spoke to her.

Ganga said, “Observing your devotion towards Siva as well as your husband. I have stayed on here.

O Damsel with a serene smile, I am Ganga and I am fascinated by you because of your devotion. You better ask for whatever you need.”

Suta said, “At these words of the Ganga, the chaste lady offering her salutation to her, spoke standing before her. “In case you are pleased with me, then give me some water.”

Thus listening to her words, Ganga asked Anusuya to dig up a pit there. She did so atonce, and in a moment the Ganga entered into it.

Soon after her entry into the pit, she was transformed into water. Anusuya then took water, getting surprised.

Then Anusuya, the wife of the sage, spoke to Ganga for the benefit of the people.

Anusuya said, “O Compassionate one, in case you are pleased with me, you remain here till the arrival of my husband.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of Anusuya, which make the noble people comfortable, Ganga said, “O Auspicious soul, you give me over the sage Atri.” Thus speaking, Ganga made her water stable and everlasting there. Anusuya then giving water to her husband, stood before him.

The sage drank the divine water appropriately. He was pleased and felt comfortable.

Atri then uttered, “This is not the water which we drink daily.” Thus thinking the sage looked all around.

Observing the dry trees all round and finding the directions more dry, the great sage said to his wife, “Had there been no rains again?

Listening to the words of the sage, Anusuya said, “No”. Then he asked, “Then where from have you brought the water?”

O Excellent sages, at these words of the sage Atri, she felt surprised and she thought in her mind.

“In case I speak out the truth, it would exhibit my greatness and in case I do otherwise, my chastity would be lost.

Both the things cannot be done. Therefore, I have to speak out the truth.” In the meantime the sage asked her again and again.

Then by the grace of Siva, wisdom dawned over the chaste lady and she said, “O Master, I shall speak out the relevant story to you.

Anusuya said, “By the glory of Siva, and because of your merits, the Ganga has arrived here and this is the water of Ganga.”

Suta said, “The sage was surprised listening to the talk of his wife. Then he devoting his mind to Siva said to her.

The sage Atri said, “O Dear one, are your words true or false? In case you are speaking the truth, then it is impossible or difficult to get.

O Chaste lady, how has it happened, which is beyond the reach of the gods and the *yogis* even? I feel immensely surprised.

In case it is so (as has been spoken by you) then I would like to see the things for myself. I shall believe only thereafter.” Hearing the words of the sage, his wife replied to him.

Anusuya said, “O Master, O Great sage, in case you intend to have a look at Ganga, then come alongwith me.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking, reciting the name of Siva in his heart, the sage accompanied with his chaste wife reached the place where Ganga was lodged.

Then the chaste lady arranged for the audience of her husband with the Ganga lodged in the pit.

Reaching there the excellent sage found that, the pit was filled with water to the top. Then he said, “Ganga is quite graceful.

Is it the fruit of my own *tapas* or of some one else?” Thus speaking he started eulogising Ganga.

Then the sage took a bath with that sacred water. Then sipping it, he praised Ganga again and again.

The Chaste Anusuya also took a bath in that water, and then started performing *tapas* daily.

Then Ganga said to Anusuya, now I shall return to my place.” At this, the chaste Anusuya spoke to Ganga.

Anusuya said, “O Mistress of the gods, in case you are pleased with me, then you kindly stay on in this *tapovana* forever.

The great people, by nature, when they once except something, they do not back out of it.” Thus speaking, Anusuya, prayed to Ganga, again and again.

The sage Atri also did so; praying Ganga to stay on to that place to make them feel having a master.

Listening his beautiful words, Devaganga was pleased and then she spoke to Anusuya.

Ganga said, “You first of all bestow the reward of the merits performed by your husband for a year, then I shall stay here for doing good to the gods.

I do not feel happy with the charities, the holy places, or yogic practices, as much, as I do with the *dharma* of chastity.

I am speaking the truth. The delight I gain with the sight of a chaste woman, the same amount of delight is not found by any other means.

Looking at a chaste woman, I feel purified and am absolved of the sins, because a chaste woman is like Parvati herself.

In case you give me the fruit of the merits for a year, then I shall stay here.”

Suta said, “The chaste Anusuya, listening to the words of Ganga, gave away a year’s fruit of the merits of her husband to Ganga.

The great people by nature do good to others. The gold, sandalwood, the sugarcane, etc. can be quoted as examples.

Observing the auspicious performance of the chaste Anusuya, Siva too was immensely pleased and he emerged out of the *Parthiva-linga* there.

Siva said, O Chaste lady, I feel pleased with your performance. You better ask for a boon from me because you are quite dear to me.”

Thereafter, both the husband and wife, looking at the beautiful five-faced body of Siva, felt surprised.

They offered their salutation with folded hands to Siva- the bestower of welfare, then adored and eulogised him and then said to him.

Both the husband and wife said, “O Lord of the gods, in case, you and the mother of the world are pleased with us, let both of you stay in this forest, showering your pleasure over the world.”

Since that time Ganga, Siva and Parvati delightfully kept on living in the hermitage of the sage.

Then Siva, who removed the miseries of all, came to be known as Atresvara, and Ganga started dwelling in that pit, with their *maya.*

Since that date, the Ganga dwelling in the pit which was a hand in depth with everlasting water and came to be known as Mandakini.

Such of the sages who had left that place earlier, returned to that place from all the *tirthas* with their wives and started living there.

The people interested in the performing of *yajna,* performed the *yajna* with the sages using the barley and other food grains.

O Great sage, having been pleased with these rites, the clouds showered plenty of rain. There was a great bliss in the world.

The greatness of Atrisvara has thus been explained to you. It is pleasing and conducive to the worldly pleasures and salvation. It fulfills all the desires and increase devotion.

## Chapter 5 - Death of a Brahmana woman and the glory of Nandikesvara

Suta said, “Lord Mahesvara is lodged over the peak of the divine Kalinjara mountain, in the form of *linga* known as Kalanjara.

The Vedas and other scriptures speak of its divine glory. A holy place called Nilakantha is also located there. Taking a bath there, one is relieved of all the sins.

O Excellent sages, innumerable *lingas* are found at the back of the Reva river and all of them bestow the bliss.

The river Reva has the form of Rudra and removes all the sins at the mere sight of it. All the stones found there, have the form of Siva with them.

O Excellent sages, still I would like to describe the most prominent of all the *lingas,* which bestows pleasures and salvation.

There is a *linga* called Artisvara there, which is also called as Parmesvara as well as Simhesvara.

The *linga* known as Sarmesvara, Kumaresvara, Pundarikesvara and also Mandapesvara, are found there.

Tiksnesa is there which removes all the sins at the very sight. Dhundhuresvara is located over the banks of the Narmada river, which also removes the sins.

Sulesvara, Kumbesvara, Kuberesvara, and Somesvara are quite famous.

Hanuman had consecrated the *linga* called Nilakantha, Mangalesa, Mangalayatana and Mahakapisvara were also consecrated by Hanuman there.

Besides there, the *linga* called Nandikesvara, which is the destroyers of the crores of killings and it fulfills all the desires, is also lodged there.

A person who adores Nandikesvara with devotion, all his tasks are successfully established daily. There is no doubt about it.

O Excellent sages, whosoever takes a bath over the bank of the Reva river, all his sins are washed out and all his desires are fulfilled.

The ascetics said, “Why is the Nandikesvara *linga* so graceful? You kindly enlighten us on the subject.”

Suta said, “You have asked me a good question. Whatever I had heard about it earlier, I repeat the same, O Saunaka, and other sages, now you listen to me with respect.

In earlier times, Yudhisthira asked the sage Vyasa about the same and I am going to repeat his words to you lovingly.

Over the western bank of the Reva river, there is a city named Karniki in which the people of all the four *varnas* dwelt.

A Brahmanas belonging to a high race, living there, once leaving the care of his two sons, to his wife went to Kasi.

The said Brahmana met with his death there. On receiving the news of their father’s death, his sons, performed all the last rites of their father.

The mother who was desirous of the welfare of her sons, brought up the boys and keeping some money with her, she distributed the rest of the riches to both her sons.

Some money was kept by her with herself, to be used at the time of his death. After the lapse of sometime, the Brahmana lady performed some auspicious deeds, but she as a matter of chance did not die.

When the sons found that their mother had not met with her death, and observing her pain, they said to her.

The sons said, “O Mother, what is the task which remains undone by you, because of the suffering devotion he does not meet with untimely death. You kindly speak out lovingly. We shall surely do the needful.

Suta said, “Listening to the words of her sons, she told them that there was enough of shortage (of money) but you should do only that much to enable me to earn the comfortable death.

Her elder son said, “You kindly speak out. I shall do whatever is required.” The Brahmana lady said, “O Son, listen to me lovingly. Earlier, I desired to go to Kasi, but presently I have to die here.

O Son, you carefully drop my bones in the water of the Ganga. You will meet with welfare.”

Suta said, “At these words of the religious minded mother, the elder son, who was devoted to his mother who was on the death bed, told her, “O Mother, you meet with your death comfortably. I shall do your job first and thereafter I shall attend to my job.

Carrying the water in his hand, when the son reached his house, his mother died reciting the name of Siva.

After performing her obsequies and the monthly *Sraddha*, he started on his journey.

The elder son, who was famous as *Suvada* carried her bones and started on pilgrimage.

He engaged a servant to accompany him, consoled his wife and son, performed the *Sraddha,* charities and other rites. Then he set out from his house after *mangala-smarana,* accompanied with his servant.

He covered a distance of twenty *yojanas* on that particular day and at the sun set, he halted in the house of a Brahmana.

The Brahmana performed the *Sandhya* and worship besides performed the *kirtana* of Siva.

In the meantime half of the night was spent by the Brahmana and his servant.

O Sages, you listen to me. At the same time an astonishing event occurred there, which I am going to narrate to you.

## Chapter 6 - Change of the black colour of a Cow to that of white at Nandikesvara

Suta said, “The Brahmana, who had gone out, returned to his home in the night, he found that a Cow had been tied up in the courtyard of his house.

O Excellent sages, looking at the cow in the courtyard, the Brahmana said to his wife that he wanted to milk the Cow. But she had no milk as a result of which he felt painful.

Then he said, “The Cow is yielding no milk.” Thus speaking, he immediately brought the calf.

He tried to tie up the calf with the peg. O Sage, the master of the household intended to drink milk.

O Sages, when the Brahmana pulled the calf, it struck the Brahmana at his foot with its hoof, which caused pain to the Brahmana.

With the strike of the calf Brahmana was angered, who struck the calf with his elbow.

The calf too felt painful with the striking of the Brahmana. The Brahmana milked the cow no doubt, but he did not release the calf at which the cow started crying. Listening to which the calf said.

“O Mother, why are you weeping? What ails you? You tell me lovingly.” At this the Cow spoke to the calf.

“O Son, I cannot speak out, the type of pain, I am suffering from which is beyond description. The wicked Brahmana has beaten you. This is what pains me.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of his mother, the calf said, trying to convince her, “that it was all due to the moves of the destiny.

What should we do, where should we go? We are bound here with the *karmas.* We are reaping the reward of the deeds performed by us earlier.

The task is established smilingly and we have to face the result while crying. There is no one to cause any pleasure or the pain.

To think that the pleasure or the pain is caused by some one is sheer foolishness. To think that “I am doing” is a false idea.

One achieves the pleasure or the pain due to the deeds performed by the people earlier. This is why the deeds are adored. Everything is enshrined in the *karmas.*

Yourself, myself and all other creatures are bound with their *karmas.* Therefore you should not think like this.”

Suta said, “Thus listening to the words of wisdom from her son, the cow, who felt painful for her son, she said to the calf.

The cow said, “I am well aware of the fact, O Son, that all the creatures are subservient to their deeds, but, I, having been over-powered with *Maya,* am feeling painful.

Inspite of my crying for long, my grief could not be removed.” Listening to the words of his mother, the calf said, “In case you are well aware of this, then why are you weeping. Can anything be gained by weeping? Therefore, you better rid yourself of your sorrow.”

Suta said, on hearing the words of her son, the cow feeling painful heaved a deep sigh and then spoke to the calf.

The Cow said, “My distress will disappear only when a similar misery befalls on the Brahmana. I am speaking out the truth. Tomorrow morning I shall hit him with my horns. Undoubtedly, he will meet with his death with that strike.

The calf said, “We have to face the fruits of the previous deeds presently. What type of the reward, are you going to reap with the killing of a Brahmana.

One gets birth in the land of Bharata when the merits and the demerits are equal when the deeds are wiped out by enjoyment or by suffering, one achieves liberation.

Sometimes the action is destroyed, but sometimes the actions bestow results. This is the reason for your intention to perform the evil deed.

Where from have I been your son. Where from have you been my mother? You first think over, the pride of sonhood or the motherhood is extremely useless.

Who is the mother? Who is the father? Who is the husband, and who is the wife? In fact no one belongs to anyone here. All have to reap the fruits of their own deeds.

O Mother, thus thinking, you should shed away your misery, making all the efforts. In case you are desirous of pleasure, you should perform noble deeds on earth.

The cow said, “O Son, I am well aware of everything, but I cannot free myself from *Maya.* I shall surely cause him the injury, which he had caused to you. Thereafter I shall go to the place, where *Brahmahatya* could be removed. I am quite well aware of that place.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, thus listening to the words of his mother cow, the calf observed silence and didn't say anything more.

O Excellent sages, listening tot he surprising story of the cow and the calf, the traveller Brahmana felt astonished in his mind.

Then he thought, that I shall leave this place only after watching the incident in the morning and also finding out the place which relives one of the *Brahmahatya*.”

Thus thinking in his mind, the said Brahmana, feeling surprised, slept with other Brahmanas, as well as his servant feeling surprised, near the calf who was devoted'to his mother.

When the day dawned, the house holder got up in the morning and woke up the traveller, saying.

The Brahmana said, “It is time of dawn. Why are you sleeping? You proceed on journey, wherever you want to go.

He said, “O Brahmana, the body of my servant is ailing. Therefore, we shall leave after sometime.”

Suta said, “Creating such a pretext, the man continued to sleep with the intention of knowing the details of the wonderful incident, by which he had felt so much surprised.

At the time of the milking of the cow, the Brahmana, who intended to go somewhere, at the time of the milking of the cow, spoke to his son.

The father said, “O Son, I am leaving on some urgent business, you should milk your cow appropriately.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking the excellent Brahmana left for some place. His son got up and he untied the calf.

Then the wife of the Brahmana arrived for the milking of the cow. The son of the Brahmana tied the calf with a peg and beat it.

In order to get milk, he took the calf to the cow. Then the enraged cow struck the boy with her horns.

Having been struck at the sensitive spot, the boy became unconscious and fell down on the ground. The cow killed the boy. Hearing the news, the people arrived there. All the relatives while crying, were engaged in saving the life of the boy but in the meantime, he breathed out his last.

There was a huge commotion at the death of the boy. Feeling grieved his mother started crying again and again.

She cried, “What should I do? Where should I do? Who would relieve me of the misery? While thus crying, the cow was beaten and left free.

The white colour of the Cow was atonce turned black observing this, the people felt surprised.

The traveller Brahmana, observing this left the place. Thereafter he followed the cow.

The cow raising her tail, went to the place near Nandikesvara *linga* over the bank of the river Narmada.

She entering the river water dipped herself in the water thrice and she regained her white complexion. Then she returned to the place, from where she had come. The traveller Brahmana stood there feeling astonished.

Then the Brahmana and his servant took bath at the *tirtha* which could wash out the sin of *Brahmahatya.*

Then both of them praising the river Narmada, moved on and on the way they met with a damsel adorned with all the ornaments.

She said to the Brahmana, “Where are you going feeling surprised. O Brahmana, speak truthfully before me, shedding away deceitfulness.”

Suta said, “The Brahmana revealed everything truthfully then the woman said, “You stop for a while.”

At this, the Brahmana stopped, and humbly said, “You tell me, what is your command for me.

She said, “You drop the bones of your mother at the place, which you have first seen. Why are you wandering here and there.

O Best of the travellers, your mother, will taking to a divine form and reaching Sivaloka, she would achieve salvation.

O Excellent Brahmana, the Ganga arrives there on the seventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaisakha, and that seventh day falls to day.” Thus speaking the goddess Ganga, disappeared from that place.

Returning to the prescribed spot, as soon as the Brahmana consigned some of the bones of his mother in the water there, an astonishing scene was visible at that particular holy place.

The Brahmana found his mother in a divine form who said to him, “You are graceful and quite successful in your endeavours, you have purified your entire race.

Let there be always an increase in your riches, cereals, age and your progeny.” Thus blessing her son, she proceeded on to the heaven.

She enjoyed best of the comforts in the heaven for a long time by the grace of Siva, then she attained the excellent place.

Her Brahmana son, with noble soul, after consigning the bones in the water, returned to his home.

## Chapter 7 - Killing of the lustful demon Mudha

Rsis said, “O Lord, O Suta, how does the Ganga arrive in Narmada on the seventh bright day of the month of Vaisakha? You please tell me.

O Learned one, how was Nandikesa transformed as Siva? You lovingly narrate the relevant episode.”

Suta said, “O Excellent *Rsis,* you have enquired about an excellent episode concerning Nandikesa, which I am going to tell you, listening to which, there is an increase in the merits.

A Brahmana had a daughter named Rsika was appropriately married to another Brahmana boy.

O Excellent Brahmana, the wife of the Brahmana inspite of her being an extremely chaste lady, because of the deeds of her earlier birth, became a widow while still young.

The said wife of the Brahmana observing the *Brahmacarya-vrata* performed hard *tapas* resorting to the *Parthiva-puja.*

At the same time an illusory demon named Mudha possessing enormous prowess, feeling lustful went to that Brahmana girl.

Finding the beautiful damsel engaged in *tapas,* he in order to unite with her, started enticing her.

O Ascetics, the chaste lady had been engaged in meditating Siva and she did not look at him with a lustful eye.

Having been engaged in *tapas,* she did not welcome the demon, because she was devoting her mind towards Siva engrossed in his worship.

Having been disgraced by the beautiful damsel, the foolish demon king, getting enraged, appeared in his horrible form before her.

The wicked demon then spoke extremely harsh words and frightened the Brahmana woman.

Then the Brahmana lady, who was engaged in the adoration, cried for Siva, again and again with devotion.

The lady was extremely upset, for the protection of her *dharma* and took refuge with Siva, uttering his name.

Siva who had taken the *vrata* to protect those who took refuge with him, appeared there in order to delight her.

Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, reduced to ashes, the passionate demon.

Thereafter Siva, who is well-versed in protecting his devotees, cast a compassionate glance on her and asked her to seek for a boon.

The chaste Brahmana lady, listening to the words of Siva and witnessing his blissful form, bowed in reverence to the lord. Then the excellent lady with noble thoughts, lowered her head and with folded hands, eulogised Siva.

Rsika said, “O Mahadeva, god of gods, well disposed towards those who take refuge in you, you are the protector of your devotees and the down trodden people.

By killing the demon Mudha, for my sake, you have actually protected the entire world.

You kindly bestow on me, your everlasting devotion. This is the only boon I seek from you. What more is needed by me?

O Lord, O Mahesvara, you kindly listen to another prayer of mine. You better stay here for the benefit of the people.”

Suta said, “The chaste Rsika, thus praying to Siva, kept quiet. Then the compassionate Siva said.

The compassionate Siva said, “O Rsika, you are devoted to me besides possessing noble character. Whatever boons have been sought for by you, have been granted by me to you.

At that point of time the gods like Brahma, Visnu and others, learning about the appearing of Siva, delightfully arrived there.

They lovingly offered their salutation to Siva and they adored him. Then folding their hands, lowering their heads, they eulogised him.

At that very moment, Ganga also arrived there and started praying Rsika. She praised her fortunes as well.

Ganga said, “You give me a word to remain with me for a day in the month of Vaisakha.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of Ganga the chaste Rsika, accepted the words of Ganga, for the welfare of the people.

Then Siva, for the pleasure of Rsika established himself in the *Parthiva-linga* made by Rsika with his full *amsas.*

All the gods delightfully praised Rsika and Siva. Thereafter, Brahma, Visnu and Devaganga, retreated to their respective places.

Since that date, this excellent *tirtha,* became the remover of all the sins and came to be known by the name of Nandikesa *linga* of Siva.

O Brahmanas, since that date, for the removal of the sins of the people, every year, Ganga for the welfare of all, arrives here once in a year.

Having a bath in the holy place, adequately adoring the Nandikesvara *linga,* a person is relieved of all the sins including *Brahmahatya.*

## Chapter 8 - The glory of Mahakala

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, you better listen with devotion. I am going to describe about the *lingas* found on earth in the Western region.

There is an extremely divine *Sivalinga* called Kalaramesvara in the city of Kapila on earth. One is relieved of his sins by merely having a look at it.

On the Western seashore there is *Sivalinga* known as Mahasiddhesvara, which bestows *dharma, artha, kama* and *moksa.*

At the western seashore, there is a region known by the name of Gokarna, which relieves one of all the sins like *Brahmahatya* and others, besides granting the fulfilment of all the desires.

There are crores of *Sivalingas* at the holy place of Gokarna, which represent crores of *tirthas* at every step.

What is the use of speaking much, all the *lingas* at Gokarna, besides the water there, are the form of Siva.

O Dear one, the glory of the Gokarna region as well as the *Sivalingas* there, has been highlighted by the great sages in the *Puranas.*

The *linga* will be of white colour in the *Satyayuga,* extremely red in the *Tretayuga,* of yellow colour in the *Dvapara* and of black colour in the age of Kali.

The immensely valorous Gokarna, would become soft on the arrival of Kaliyuga.

Even the extremely sinful persons, by adoring the valorous Gokarna *Sivalinga* would achieve the place of Siva.

Such of the sages who would adore Siva in the Gokarna region, in the auspicious day and the constellation, they undoubtedly achieve the form of Siva.

Whenever a person adores the *Sivalinga* at Gokarna, he achieves the position of the supreme Brahman.

Lord Siva, for the benefit of Brahma, Visnu and other gods, resides in the Gokarna region in the form of the Mahabala *linga.*

The demon Ravana, had consecrated the Gananayaka *Sivalinga* at Gokarna, after performing severe *tapas.*

The gods like Brahma, Visnu, Indra, Visvedeva, Marudgana, Vasu, Asvinikumara, the moon with the stars, the gods who move in planes, together with their courtiers, live at the eastern gate in order to please lord Siva.

Yama, the death, Citragupta, fire god, the manes besides the Rudras, attend the lord at the southern gate.

Varuna, the lord of the rivers, associated with great rivers like Ganga and others, guard the western gate and serve Mahabala.

The gods like Vayu, Kubera, the goddess Devesi, Bhadrakali, Candika, along with other Matrikas, live at the northern gate.

All the gods in association with the Gandharvas, the manes, Siddhas- Caranas, Kimpurusas, Vidyadharas, Kinnaras, Guhyakas, the birds, several *Pisacas, Betalas,* valorous Daityas, Sesa and other serpents, besides Siddhas with all the sages, offer their salutation to the *linga* named Mahabala and having all their desires fulfilled they enjoy all the pleasures.

Several people, by performing the *tapas* and worship there have attained extreme success, relating to the present as well as the future world.

The *Sivalinga* at Gokarna is called the door to salvation. O Brahmanas, the Mahabala *linga* has been adored by several people, who also eulogised the same.

On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Magha, even if the sinner adore the Mahabala-linga, he earns salvation by the same.

On the occasion of the celebrating the occasion, people of all the *varnas* arrive even from other countries.

All the women, children old people of all the four *asramas* meet with success by arriving here.

With the influence of Mahabala, by adoring that *Sivalinga,* even the wife of a *Candala* attained the region of Sivaloka.

## Chapter 9 - Liberation of a Candala woman with the unmindful dropping of the leaves of wood-apple tree

Rsis said, “O Excellent one, you are the Supreme devotee of Siva, therefore you are quite graceful. O Lord, who was the Candala woman? You kindly narrate her story.

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, you better listen to the astonishing story with devotion. With the influence of Siva, the story enhances faith of the listeners in Siva.

The Candala woman, was a Brahmana girl in her earlier birth, having the beautiful face resembling the moon and possessed all the auspicious symptoms.

O Brahmanas, she after attaining the youthful age, was appropriately married by her father to a Brahmana boy.

O Brahmanas, because of her youthful age, she spent sometime in the company of her husband.

O brahmins, after sometime, the youthful husband of Saumini became distressed and died of some ailment. Due to the misfortune of Saumini he died.

After the death of her husband, she felt extremely painful and for sometime she spent the life of chastity in her home.

Thereafter, because of her youthful age, inspite of being a widow, she could not bear the pain of passions and took to evil path.

Learning her misdeeds defiling the family, her relatives gathered together, caught hold of her hair, took her far off and abandoned her.

Finding a lonely damsel in the forest, a Sudra, took her to his home and made her his wife.

Thereafter, she living with him, consuming meat and wine, started enjoying the worldly pleasures with that Sudra. In due course of time she gave birth to a daughter.

Then the unchaste Saumini, consumed the wine in the absence of her husband, and tried to consume the meat.

Holding a sword in her hand she went to the cow-pen, in the darkness of the night, where the sheep were also kept with the cows.

The unchaste woman, getting intoxicated with wine, without thinking, slaughtered a calf which was crying.

The women brought the dead Calf in her house, getting afraid of the evil deed she started muttering the name of Siva.

For sometime she meditated upon Siva. Thereafter with her desire to consume flesh, she ate up the calf of the cow.

O Brahmanas, after a long time, Saumini, after her death, went to Yamaloka.

Yama on his part, keeping in view the deeds of her earlier birth, and the religious performance, removed her from the hell and allowed her to be bom in the family of a Candala.

Returning from the place of Yama, she entered the womb of a Candala woman. She was as a girl born blind at birth.

Her parents had died when she was still a child. Because of her suffering from leprosy, on one married her.

Then she, suffering from hunger, felt miserable and walked holding a stick in her hand and fed herself at the left-overs of the *Candalas.*

In this way she spent her life quite miserably. Even at her old age, she suffered miserably.

Once the said *candala* woman some how came to know that many people were going to the Gokarna *tirtha.*

Then she, with the expectation that by reaching there she could get some more food and clothes from the rich people, by begging, walked on slowly towards Gokarna.

The *Candala* woman reaching there spreading her hands speaking miserable words, begged for food wandering here and there.

Thus when she was so begging from the people, a meritorious pilgrim placed a bunch of wood apple leaves in the hands of the blind woman.

She thinking again and again and finding that the leaves cannot be consumed, she threw them aside.

The tree leaves thrown at night by her, fell at *Sivalinga* perchance as the move of the destiny.

In this way luckily it was *Siva-caturdasi* and inspite of her begging again and again from the pilgrims, she could not get anything to eat.

As such she had to observe fast remaining awake throughout the night unmindfully, which bestows pleasure.

In the morning, feeling alone and extremely painful she slowly moved on her return journey to her country, quite slowly.

Because of her observing fast for long, she was falling at every step she covered some distance and then was fainted. She fell down on the ground and then met with her end.

By the grace of Siva, the *Sivaganas* arrived and lodging her in a plane they carried her to the supreme place.

The unchaste woman, had earlier recited the name of Siva unmindfully. O Brahmanas, with the merit of the same, she achieved the place of Mahabala Siva.

On the day of *Siva-caturdasi,* at Sri Gokarna, offering the leaves of wood apple tree, she adored Siva keeping the fast.

This was the reward for performing a deed in a selfless manner, that by the grace of Mahabala, she is enjoying the comforts even today.

Thus is the great image of Mahabala *Sivalinga,* destroying all the sins and the bestower of pleasure instantaneously.

O Brahmanas, I have narrated the highest glory of the excellent Mahabala *Sivalinga.*

Besides that, I shall also narrate the astonishing type of greatness of the same, listening to which the devotion towards Siva is firmly established.

## Chapter 10 - Relieving of the curse by the king Mitrasaha, at Gokrana-tirtha

Suta said, “There was an Iksvaku king known by the name of Mitrasaha, who was quite a religious minded one.

He had a beautiful queen named Madayanti who was quite beautiful and chaste, like the queen Damayanti of Nala, who was famous for her virtues.

The king Mitrasaha, who was fond of hunting, once went to the thick forest with his army.

While roaming about in the forest, he came across a wicked demon named Kamatha, who was inimical to the sages and killed him.

Thereafter the younger brother of Kamatha tried his best to overpower the king deceitfully. For this purpose he went to the king. Finding him so humble and desirous of serving him, the monarch made him in charge of the kitchen.

Thereafter, the king roamed about in the forest for the purpose of hunting, and ultimately returned to his home leaving the hunting.

On the day of *Sraddha* of his father, he invited his preceptor Vasistha at home and served him food with devotion.

The demon cook served human flesh with the food, finding which, the preceptor said, “Disgrace to you, O king, you are wicked, you have deceitfully served me the human flesh. Therefore, you become *Raksasa* at once.

But when the preceptor subsequently came to realise that it was the cook and not the king who was at fault, he restricted the period of the curse to twelve years.

Then the king realising that the curse was improper fainted. Then filling water in his hand he was about to pronounce a curse on his preceptor.

Then his chaste queen Madyanti, fell at the feet of the king and stopped him from the pronouncing of the curse.

At her insistence he was dissuaded from the pronouncing of the curse. The water carried by the king in his hand for the pronouncing of the curse, fell at the monarch’s feet which were turned black and subsequently he came to be known by the name of Kalmasapada.

Then the king because of the curse of the sage Vasistha became a terrific demon who kept on wandering in the forest.

He taking to an awful form, became horrible like Yama. He while wandering in the forest devoured humans as well as the animals.

Like the messenger of Yama, he once spotted an ascetic couple enjoying the conjugal pleasures.

The demon, to whom, the humans served as food, and suffering from the curse, the Raksasa caught the ascetic’s son for devouring him a as lion captures a fawn.

The wife of the ascetic finding her husband having been caught by the demon, felt grieved and started praying to the Raksasa in pathetic voice.

The extremely cruel Raksasa, inspite of the prayer by the ascetic’s wife, devoured the head of the Brahmana ascetic.

Then the chaste lady lamented variously and she burnt herself with her husband’s bones.

The Brahmana girl while following her husband, by entering into the fire flames, cursed the *Raksasa.*

She said, “From today onwards, whenever you would have desire to unite with a woman, you would meet with your end.” Thus cursing the demon, she entered the fire flames.

The king, after period of the curse of the preceptor was over, taking to his original form, returned to his kingdom quite delightfully.

When the king was anxious to unite with Madayanti his queen, she stopped him from doing so reminding him of the curse of the wife of the ascetic, because, otherwise she would have become the widow.

Inspite of his having no son, he was deprived of the worldly pleasures, and feeling detached, he discarded his throne and went to the forest.

At the same time, he spotted the terrific *Brahmahatya* in terrific form, which caused pain, following him.

The king in order to get rid of the *Brahmahatya,* feeling sad, adopted several means like the performing of *Vratas, japam, yajnas* and other methods.

But when he could not get rid himself of the *Brahmahatya* inspite of his using several methods, then he went to the city of Mithila.

He seated himself on the outer orchard of the city, when he was engrossed in enormous worries, he found the sage Gautama arriving there.

The king then went to the sage Gautama with a spotless mind, which earned him some peace of mind. Then he offered his salutation at the feet of the sage.

The sage asked him about his welfare. Then the king heaving a deep sigh, feeling a bit comfortable at the sight of the sage and said to him.

The king said, “O Sage, the *Brahmahatya* which is invisible to others is troubling me. It scolds me at every step.

Because of the curse I ate the Brahmana, as a Raksasa. In order to free myself of the sin, I performed thousands of repentances, But I could not get rid of her.

O Sage, I, while wandering here and there, have adopted several methods to pacify her, but a sinful person like me could not be relieved of the *Brahmahatya.*

By having an audience with you, my life has met with a success and I presently feel delighted.

O Excellent one, I take refuge under your feet. Bestow peace on me to enable me to become comfortable.”

Suta said, “At these words of the king, the compassionate sage Gautama, revealed to him the method of getting relived of the terrific sins.

Gautama said, “O Great king, you can rid yourself of the fear of the grave sins. Can there be any fear for the devotees of Siva in the domain of the lord.

O Fortunate king you listen. There is a famous region known for the destruction of the sins which is known as Gokarna- the Sivalaya or the abode of Siva.

By visiting that place even the grave sins are washed out. Siva in the form of Mahabala lives there.

As the Cakravarti is supreme of all the kings, similarly Mahabala is the best of all the *lingas,* which destroys all the sins of all the *varnas* in all the *yugas.*

There is a holy place known as Gokarna on the western seashore. The *Sivalinga* established there removes all the sins.

Going there, even the condemned sinner, taking bath in sacred places, and adoring Mahabala achieves the place of Siva.

O Excellent king, you should therefore go to Gokarna, the place of Siva and adore the *Sivalinga* there and all your desires would be fulfilled. Taking bath in all the *tirthas* there and after adoring Siva there, you would achieve the *Sivaloka.”*

Suta said, “At the command of Gautama- the great sage, the king delightfully went to the Gokarna *tirtha.*

Taking bath in all the *tirthas* there, he adored Mahabala, getting free from all the sins, he achieved the supreme place of Siva.

The one who listens to the loving story of Mahabala, he enjoys comforts in Sivaloka upto twenty one generations of his race.

Thus I have narrated the greatness of the astonishing Sivalinga of Mahabala which removes all types of sins.

## Chapter 11 - Description of the lingas known as Candrabhala, Pasupati and others in the northern direction

The *Rsis* said, “O Suta, the devotee of Siva, you are indeed graceful. You have narrated to us the astonishing story of Mahabala *linga.*

Now you speak out the details about the *Sivalingas* in the north as well as their glory relating to the removal of the sins.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, now you respectfully listen from me, in brief the description about the *Sivalingas* lodged in the northern direction.

The Gokarna is another shrine which removes the grave sins. There is a huge forest there.

A *Sivalinga* named Candrasekhara is lodged there. It bestows all the success, which was brought by Ravana with devotion.

O Best of the sages, the *Sivalinga* there is the ocean of compassion, bestows welfare to all and has the same importance as the Baidyanatha *Jyotirlinga.*

Taking a bath in the Gokarna *tirtha,* adoring Candresvara, a person really goes to *Sivaloka,* there is no doubt about it.

The greatness of Candrasekhara *Sivalinga* is really surprising. Even Vyasa, always earning respect from his devotees, is unable to explain its glory.

Thus I have some how narrated the glory of Candrasekhara *Sivalinga.* Now you listen to the glory of the other *lingas.*

In the *Rsi-tirtha* known as Misra, there is a *Sivalinga* named Dadhici, which was adored by the sage Dadhici with devotion.

Reaching there, taking the bath appropriately one should adore the *Sivalinga* there.

The people desirous of the fruit of the pilgrimage should appropriately adore the *Dadhica-linga,* which pleases Siva.

O Excellent sages, by doing so all the desires of a person are fulfilled. He, enjoying all the pleasures in this world, ultimately achieves salvation.

The *Rsivara-linga* at Naimasaranya was consecrated by the seven sages, which bestows comforts of all.

O Excellent sages, by having a look at it and adoring it, even the sinful people enjoy all the comforts in this world and achieve salvation after death.

There is a *Papanasika-Sivalinga* at *Hatyaharana* place of pilgrim. It should be adored by a special method and by doing so sins for killing crores of creatures are washed out.

In the *Devaprayaga tirtha,* there is a *Sivalinga* which destroys all the sins, which should always by adored.

Pasupatesvara *Sivalinga* has been established in the Nepala country which fulfills all the desires.

This *linga* as the form of the head and its story would be narrated with the greatness of Kedaresvara.

There is a wonderful *linga* known as Muktinatha, close to it, with its adoration, one achieves devotion as well as salvation.

O Sages, I have described the *Sivalingas* in all the four directions, what more do you desire to listen from me?

## Chapter 12 - Reasons for Siva’s taking to the form of linga

The *Rsis* said, “O Suta, you are omniscient by the grace of Vyasa. Nothing is unknown to you. Therefore we ask you.

Is there any other reason in the world for the worship of *linga,* than what you have already spoken to us?

O Suta, Parvati, the beloved of Siva has been said to be the form of a *bana* or an arrow. You kindly tell me the reason for the same.

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, I heard from Vyasa the stories of the change of the *kalpas,* which I am going to narrate to you. All of you should listen to me.

In the ancient times an incident happened with the Brahmanas in the Daruvana, which is going to be narrated by me, as I had heard earlier.

In the forest named Daru, there lived the devotees of Siva, who was always engaged in the worship of Siva.

O *Rsis,* he adored Siva thrice a day eulogising him with the best of the *stotras.*

All the Brahmanas remained engaged in the worship of Siva. Once they went to the forest to collect fire wood for *yajna.*

In the meantime Nilalohita Siva with a deformed appearance arrived there in order to test them.

He was naked, immensely illustrious applying ashes over the body. Standing there. Holding his *linga* he displayed all sorts of vicious tricks.

Siva moved with a mind to do some good to the forest dwellers. He who was the favourite of the devotees, arrived in the forest of his own will.

The wives of the sages, were extremely frightened at the appearing of Siva. Some of the women got excited and getting surprised approached the lord.

Some of them embraced him, others held his hands. These women were engrossed in struggling with one another.

At the same time the foremost *rsis* arrived there. The felt painful and enraged at the sight.

Then feeling painful and having been overpowered with the *Maya* of Siva, they uttered, “Who is he? Who is he?”

When the naked *Avadhuta* kept quiet, then the terrific persons (Sages) spoke to him.

The *Rsis* said, “Since you are following the evil path, which is contrary to the Vedic practices, therefore let your *linga* fall on earth.”

Suta said, “At these words of the sages, the astonishing type of the *linga* of *Avadhuta,* fell on earth.

Wherever the *linga* resembling the fire moved, it burnt that place.

It went to heaven, *Patala* and earth, but could not remain stationary.

All the people, the *rsis,* and the gods felt extremely painful. No one was happy at that time.

Such of the divine sages who could not realise him to be Siva, they felt painful and they collectively went to Brahma and took refuge with him.

Reaching there all the Brahmanas offered there salutation to Brahma, then eulogised him and narrated the entire incident to Brahma, the creator of the universe.

Listening to the words of the *Rsis,* who had been overpowered by Siva’s *Maya,* offering his salutation to Siva, Brahma spoke to the *Rsis.”*

Brahma said, “All of you are well aware of everything and still you indulge in deplorable activities. O Brahmanas, in case the ignorant people speak like this, then what could be said about them?

Thus picking up a row with Siva, who can save himself. Does a person not welcome a guest who arrives at the house at noon time?

He carrying his merits and giving away his sins, leaves the place, irrespective of his being Siva himself.

I am speaking the truth unless the *linga* is established somewhere in the three worlds, there could be no peace anywhere. Therefore O Sages you should think about the *Sivalinga* in your minds.”

Suta said, “At these words of Brahma, they offered their salutation to the creator and said, “What should we do? You kindly tell us.”

At these words of the excellent sages, Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, himself spoke to them.

Brahma said, “You adore Girija that she should take the form of a *yoni.* Then pray to Siva to make his *linga* steady there.

Listen O Excellent sages, I shall tell you the mode of procedure. Act accordingly with love and devotion. She will thus be pleased.

Make an eight petalled mystic diagram of lotus and place a pot over it. Then the water from holy places should be poured into the pot, alongwith the sprouts of *Durva* and barley.

The pot should be invoked reciting the Vedic *mantras.* It should be worshipped according to the Vedic rituals, reciting the name of Siva.

The *linga* shall be put in that water. O Sages, when the sprinkling is made with the *Satarudriya mantras,* it would then stabilise.

Parvati in the form of the *yoni* and an auspicious arrow shall form the pedestal, wherein, the phallus shall be installed with the reciting of the Vedic hymns.

Lord Siva should be adored with the offerings of sweets and scents, sandal-paste, fragrant flowers, incense and other things, as well as by food and other offerings besides other form of worship.

After prostrating before the lord, chanting of the holy hymns, accompanied with the playing of the musical instruments, besides the singing, he shall be further adored. The *Svasti-vacana mantras* should be repeated and the devotees should shout slogans of the victory of the lord.

Thereafter, the following prayer should be recited, “O Lord, you are the one, who delights the world. Be pleased with me. You are the creator of the universe, preserver and destroyer. You yourself are eternal.

You represent the beginning of the universe, the cause of the creation and the form of the souls of all. O Lord Siva, you protect the entire world becoming peaceful.

With the performing in this manner, all would be happy leaving no blemish, all the three *lokas* would be peaceful and happy.”

Suta said, “At these worlds of Brahma, the Brahmanas offered their salutation to Brahma and went to take refuge with Siva for the benefit of the universe.

They worshipped Siva with great devotion, they offered prayer to him. Then Siva getting delighted, spoke to them.

Mahesvara said, “O Gods, O Sages, you listen to my words with reverence. If my *linga* (penis) is supported in a vaginal passage there will be happiness.

Except Parvati, no other woman can hold my *linga.* There would be peace everywhere, when she holds my *linga."*

Suta said, “O Excellent sages, on hearing this, all the gods and the sages prayed the Parvati, with Brahma.

After propitiating Girija (Parvati) and the bull-bannered lord and performing the rites mentioned before, the excellent *linga* became static.

The gods and the sages, for the establishment of *Dharma,* pleased both Siva and Parvati.

Brahma, Visnu and other gods, besides the sages, in addition to the mobile and immobile creatures of the universe, worshipped lord Siva.

Both Siva and Parvati, the mother of the universe were pleased. Then that *linga* was held by Parvati in that form.

With the establishment of the *linga,* all the people met with welfare. O Brahmanas, that particular *linga,* became famous in three worlds.

The establishment thus of Siva and Siva came to be known as Hatesa. All the people enjoy all the pleasures, by adoring it.

By worshipping this *linga,* one achieves all the pleasures and the riches on earth besides the best of salvation after death.

## Chapter 13 - Origin of Batuka

Suta said, “I have explained to you the way Siva transformed himself into *linga* in the three worlds. Now O Brahmanas what more to you intend to listen from me.”

The *Rsis* said, “O Lord, you describe the greatness of Andhakesvara and other *lingas* with devotion.”

Suta said, “In earlier times, Andhakasura, living in a pit of the ocean had controlled the entire universe.

The immensely valorous demon, came out of the pit, troubled the people and then again reverted to the pit.

O Excellent sages, getting fed up with the atrocities of the demon, the gods went to Siva and narrated the tales of their sufferings to the lord again and again.

Suta said, “Listening to their words, Siva- the destroyer of the wicked people and being the refuge of the noble people, delightfully said to the gods.

Siva said, “I shall kill Andhakasura, who is the cause of trouble for the gods. You better come with your army. I shall also arrive with my *ganas.*

When Andhakasura, who was the cause of trouble for all, came out of the pit, the gods usurped in the same.

The gods and the daityas then fought a terrific battle. By the grace of Siva, the gods became more powerful.

On the arrival of Andhakasura, the gods also thrashed him. By about the same time Siva too struck at Andhakasura with his trident.

Then the *asura* devoting his mind to Siva, saying that “at the end of one’s life by looking at you, one becomes like you.”

At this prayer of the demon, Siva desired him to ask for a boon, which could be give him.

On hearing those words, the Daitya taking refuge in truth, offering his salutation to Siva, then spoke.

Andhaka said, “O Lord of the gods, in case, you are happy with me, then grant me your auspicious devotion and you stay here forever.”

Suta said, “At these words of the demon, lord Siva, removed him out of the pit and he himself occupied the pit for the welfare of the people.

In case the said Andhakesa *linga* is worshipped for six months continuously, all the desires of a person are fulfilled.

A person who adores the *linga* for his livelihood for six months becomes a *Devaloka.*

As a person has been called *Devaloka* is not authorised to perform the ordinary rites of a Brahmana.”

The sages said, “Who is a *Devaloka,* what are his functions? O intelligent one, you tell us the same for guidance of the people.

Suta said, “There was a religious minded Brahmana, who was well-versed in the Vedas. He was quite learned in the Saiva literature besides being devoted to Siva.

He had a son named Sudarsana. He had a wife who had been born in wicked family.

She exercised full control over her husband. He had four sons. He used to adore Siva daily.

As a matter of chance, the sage Dadhici had to stay in another village for a few days. His stay there was extended at the instance of some other relatives.

Dadhici, the excellent devotee left his place saying to his son, that he should daily worship Siva.

Sudarsana- his son also continued to adore Siva for sometime. O Excellent sages, in this way long time passed.

In the meantime the occasion of Sivaratri arrived. As a matter of chance, all of them observed fast.

Sudarsana returned home, after performing the adoration, where he uniting with his wife, returned again.

He without taking bath in the night, worshipped Siva. Siva felt enraged at his sin and he said to him.

Siva said, “You had sexual intercourse with your wife on the occasion of Sivaratri. Without taking bath you performed the worship. You are an indiscreet fellow.

Because you have done this knowingly, you be sluggish and insensible. For me you are an untouchable person. Don’t touch me.”

Suta said, “When thus cursed by Siva, Sudarsana, the son of Dadhici, atonce became insensible, deluded by the *Maya* of Siva.

O Brahmana, Dadhici, the excellent devotee of Siva, heard about the incident on his return from the other village.

He too was rebuked by Siva, therefore he felt extremely distressed. He cried, “Oh, I am doomed by the foolish deed of my son.”

Dadhici then repeated again and again, this sinful son has destroyed the best of my race.”

The unfortunate son made his wife as an unchaste woman. Feeling repented, the father rebuked his son.

The father then with the intention of making his son comfortable, made all the grand efforts, besides adoring Girija with devotion.

Sudarsana too adored Girija according to the *Candipujavidhi* and recited many *stotras.*

In this way both the father and the son, adored Girija who was well disposed towards her devotees in many ways.

When the goddess found that lord Siva had been pleased, them she offering her salutation to him, placed him in the lap of lord Siva.

For the sake of his adopted son, she herself implored Siva, who was angry. But he became calm and the son too was delighted.

The bull bannered Siva was delighted, she bowed to him herself and placed the son in his lap.

Girija abluted the son with *ghee* and handed over to her son Sudarsana, the three-stringed sacred thread with a single knot and made him wear a *yajnopavita.* Then Ambika initiated his son Sudarsana in Siva-gayatri of sixteen syllables.

Then the Brahmana boy performed the *samkalpa-puja* (mental worship) sixteen times with the five syllabled *mantra* prefixing the word *sri* with the name of Siva.

Starting from the bathing to the offering of the salutation, seated alongwith the *rsis,* he adored Siva. With the playing of the musical instruments.

Then Candika getting pleased, made him recite several *mantras.* After this, Siva and the goddess were both pleased who said, “Whatever the riches or the cereals have been offered to me, should be taken by you and by doing so, you would not attract any sin.

You are the foremost in the task of the goddess like me. You also accept the *ghee* and the oil and whatever else has been offered to me.

In the *Prajapatya-vrata* you alone are enough. Only then the adoration would be complete, otherwise all of it would go waste.

You should always apply a round *tilakam* over your forehead taking your bath and recite *Siva-Gayatri* while performing *Siva-sandhya.*

Initially, you adore me and then the *Kulacara* should be performed and while doing so, you would meet with welfare. I have forgiven you for all your blemishes.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking, turning all his four sons in the form of *Batus* she established them in all the four quarters. After keeping Sudarsana as her son with herself, she granted boons to his sons, showering blessings on them in several ways.

The goddess said, “Between you two, whosoever becomes my *Batuka,* he shall be victorious. There should be no doubt about it.

The one who adores you, adores me as well. O Son, you will perform your duties always.

Suta said, “In this way the boons were bestowed over Sudarsana and his sons, by Siva and Parvati for the welfare of the world.

Both Siva and Parvati established them and because of that they were called as *Batuka.* Those who neglected the penance were known as *Tapodhanas.*

Because of the grace of Siva and Parvati, they met with the enormous development. The all adored Siva.

Till such time, a person does not perform the adoration of Siva, one should not adore the other gods. In case a person does so, it is not treated as auspicious.

One should not neglect the worship of *Batuka* inspite of auspicious or inauspicious situations, because in the *Prajapatya* rites and the connected feast, *Batuka* is considered to be the excellent one.

In the rites relating to Siva and Parvati, the importance of *Batuka* is quite conspicuous. I am going to speak about the same and you please listen to me.

I shall narrate the surprising event that happened, as I heard earlier, in the city of Bhadra, near the shrine of Andhakesa, during the daily of feasting in the Prajapatya rites.

Siva had given a banner to the king, since the lord was pleased with the devotion of the monarch. The lord also mercifully addressed the king.

Lord Siva said, “At the completion of the *Prajapatya-yajna* during the night, this banner would fall and at the dawn it would rise up.

Otherwise, this banner remains raised during the night as well.” Thus speaking, and feeling pleased with the king, Siva disappeared from the scene.

O Great sage, the king performed similarly as desired. According to the rules of the adoration of Siva, he served food daily to the Brahmanas.

When the entire task was completed then the banner was automatically raised in the morning and fell in the evening.

Once the adoration of *Batuka* was performed earlier, then the banner fell without serving food to the Brahmanas.

Observing the incident, the king asked the priest, “While the Brahmanas are consuming their food, but the banner remains unraised.

O Brahmanas, you tell me truthfully, the cause of the banner remaining unraised.” Then the learned Brahmanas said, “O King, in the present feast, you have served food to *Batuka,* first of all which pleased Siva and the banner has fallen.”

On hearing this, the king and the other people were wonder struck and started praising them.

With this Siva has increased the glory of *Batuka.* Because of this the ancient seers have taken *Âṁtuka* to be the excellent one.

In fact the adoration of Siva should be started with the adoration of *Batuka.* According to the words of Siva, no one else has the right to be adored like this.

For the purpose of the completion of the worship, let it be remarked, “Let the worship be completed.” This is their work and nothing else.

O Great Sages, “Thus whatever had been asked by you, has been narrated by me, listening to which a man achieves the fruits of the worship of Siva.

## Chapter 14 - Origin of the Jyotrilinga of Somanatha

The *Rsis* said, “Now you narrate about the glory of the *Jyotirlinga,* whatever has been heard by you.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas the genesis of the *Jyotirlinga* and their glory, had been heard by me from my preceptor and I shall repeat the same quite briefly.

O Excellent sages, the glory of the *Jyotirlinga* cannot be explained even in hundreds of years, still I shall speak out the same for your satisfaction.

Somanatha happens to be the first *Jyotirlinga.* O Sage you initially listen to its glory quite attentively.

O great sage, his daughters, twenty-seven in number, Asvini and others, were given in marriage to the moon by Daksa, the great soul.

Achieving the moon as their lord, all the girls felt graceful. The moon also felt graceful with them.

The gold looks graceful with the gem and same is the case of gems with the gold. Now you listen to what happened thereafter.

Of all the twenty-seven wives, he did not love any one so much at anytime as he loved Rohini.

The rest of the wives of the moon went to their father, feeling painful and took refuge with him. They explained the tale of their sufferings to their father.

O Brahmana, Daksa felt painful at this and spoke to the moon approaching him to pacify them.

Daksa said, “O Moon, you have been bom in a spotless race why are you extending different kind of behaviour towards those who are dependant upon you.

Whatever has been done by you is enough, but don’t repeat the same in future. Enjoying of the worldly passions leads one to hell.”

Suta said, “Thus requesting to moon, his son-in-law, Daksa returned to his place feeling satisfied.

The moon on the other hand, having been over-powered with the delusion of Siva, did not bother about the advice of Daksa.

Only he meets with welfare, whosoever is destined to do so, but the one who is destined to face misfortune, how could he meet with welfare.

The moon too due to the moves of destiny, did not listen to the words of Daksa. Since he was attracted towards Rohini, he did not honour his other wives.

Hearing this Daksa again arrived the abode of the moon and prayed to the moon, speaking the appropriate words.

Daksa said, “O Moon, you listen, I have made several requests to you which remain unheaded. Therefore you will suffer from the disease of consumption.”

Suta said, “At these words of Daksa, the moon atonce attracted the consumption disease, with the moon’s attracting the ailment of consumption, there was a turmoil everywhere.

O Sage, all the sages and the gods uttered, “What has happened? Now what should be done,” Thus thinking all of them were upset.

At the instance of the moon, Indra and other gods besides the ascetics like Vasistha and others, went to Brahma to take refuge with him.

O Sage, reaching there, the gods and the *rsis* offered their salutation to Brahma eulogising him at the same time. Then getting upset, they revealed the entire news to him.

Listening to their words, Brahma was wonder struck. Praising the *Maya* of Siva, he said, to them.

Brahma said, “Oh, this is the painful news for all that Daksa has pronounced a curse on the moon to suffer from the disease of consumption.

Of course, the moon is at fault. O Gods and the sages, you listen to the deeds of misconduct in which the moon indulged earlier.

The wicked moon, going to the place of Brhaspati, kidnapped his wife Tara. Then he went to the Daityas.

Then he made the gods and the demons to fight. Then at the instance of Atri, he returned Tara to Brhaspati.

Finding Tara pregnant, Brhaspati refused to accept her. At our insistence, Brhaspati somehow accepted her with great difficulty.

O Excellent sages, Brhaspati then said, “In case she rids herself of the pregnancy, I shall accept Tara again. Then I got her free from the pregnancy.

After the birth of the child, I asked, “Whose child was he?” Then she said that it belonged to the moon. Thereafter, at my instance Brhaspati accepted his wife Tara back to his fold.

In this way the moon has several earlier misdeeds to his credit. He is misbehaving even now.

Whatever has happened is quite good, otherwise he would have continued to indulge into misconduct. Now I shall speak out to you the remedy for his getting relieved of his misery. You better listen to me with respect.

In case the moon goes to Prabhasa-ksetra and worships Siva according to the method of *Mrtyunjaya-puja* and keeping Siva before himself, and worships him daily, then Siva getting pleased shall rid him of the ailment of consumption.

Suta said, “All the gods and the sages, listening to the words of Brahma, went to the places of Daksa and the moon.

They went to the moon and reassured him, all the gods, the *Rsis* and the moon them went to the Prabhasa-ksetra.

Invoking all the holy places there, including Sarasvati, they started adoring Siva by *Mrtyunjaya-pujan-vidhi.* The gods and the ascetics, with the spotless intentions, seated the moon at the Prabhasa-ksetra, and went back to their respective places.

The moon performed the adoration of Siva reciting the *Mrtyunjaya-mantra* and performed *tapas* continuously for six months.

Reciting the *Mrtyunjaya-mantra* for ten crores of times, and meditating upon Siva, the moon stayed there.

Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, felt delighted finding the moon there. Then he, appearing before the moon said to him.

Siva said, “O Moon, you ask for a boon you desire, I am happy with you. I shall bestow the best of boon to you.”

The moon said, “O Lord of the gods, in case you are pleased with me, then no task of mine can remain unsuccessful. Still you kindly rid me of the ailment of consumption.

Kindly forgive me for my sins and bestow welfare on me always.” At these words of the moon, Siva said to him.

Siva said, “In a fortnight, you will get reduced by a digit daily and in the next fortnight, it would go on increasing in the same sequence.” Suta said, “O Brahmana, listening to such a boon, the gods and the sages feeling delighted reached there.

Thereafter coming there, all they blessed the moon. Then they offered their salutation to Siva, with folded hands.

The gods said, “O Mahadeva- the god of gods, O Supreme lord, salutation to you. O Master, you stay her with Parvati.”

Suta said, “Then the moon having been filled with devotion, eulogised him though was in *Nirguna* form, but transformed himself in the *Saguna* form.

Siva then felt happy with the gods. In order to enhance the glory and greatness of the region, besides that of the moon, Siva established himself there in the form of Somesvara and became famous in the three worlds. O Brahmanas, by his worship, Siva becomes the destroyer of the ailments like consumption, leprosy and others.

Successful is the moon in his desires, besides being graceful, with the name of whom, Siva, the lord of the universe purifying the earth is lodged here.

All the gods established a *Kunda* of water there, which was patronised both by Brahma and Siva.

It came to be known by the name of *Candrakunda.* A person who takes a bath there, is freed of all the sins.

By taking a bath in that *Kunda,* continuously for six months, the incurable diseases like the consumption and others are removed.

By circumambulating the Prabhasa-ksetra, one earns the fruit of going round the earth. The mind is purified and one achieves heaven after his death.

A person at the sight of the *Somanatha- linga* is relieved of all the sins. He has his desires fulfilled and achieves heaven after death.

One who visits this place of pilgrims undoubtedly achieves the appropriate fruits.

The ascetics and the gods observing the reward of the *Somanatha-linga,* felt delighted, then offering salutation to *Sivalinga* took the moon with them who had been relieved of the ailment of consumption.

They praised the place of pilgrimage, besides taking a round of the same. The moon also engaged himself in his earlier task.

O Excellent sages, thus I have narrated to you the history of the *Somanatha-linga.*

A person who listens to the story of the creation of the *Somanatha-linga* or recites it to others, he getting relieved of his sins, achieves success in all his desires.

## Chapter 15 - Discussion on Mallikarjuna- the second Jyotirlinga

Suta said, “Hereafter, I shall narrate the origin of Mallikarjuna *linga,* listening to which a person with wisdom, is relieved of all the sins.

I have already detailed the divine Kumaracarita, destroyer of all sins, which is being repeated by me.

When the son of Siva, after going round the entire earth, the killer of Tarakasura, reached Kailasa, then Narada communicated to him about the marriage of Ganesa and further told him, that Siva, using his intelligence, had sent him out for taking a round of the earth.

On hearing this, Kumara, offering his salutation to his parents, proceeded on to the Kraunca mountain for living there, much against the advice of his parents.

After the departure of Kumara, his mother Girija felt extremely painful at heart. Then Siva advised her appropriately.

He said, “O Beloved Parvati, why do you feel anxious? O Damsel with beautiful eyebrows, your son would return, you better get relieved of the mental agony.”

When Parvati was so suffering from the mental agony, she did not listen to Siva, then Siva sent the divine sages to Skanda’s place.

The gods having the spotless wisdom, besides the sages, accompanied with their *ganas* delightfully went to Kumara to get him back.

Reaching there all of them offered their salutation to Kumara, conveyed the message of Siva and Parvati and further prayed to him.

Kumara who was suffering from enormous arrogance, refused to accept the command of Siva, as well as the prayer of the gods.

All of them, then returned to the place of Siva and offering their salutation to him, went back to their respective abodes with the permission of Siva.

Because of their separation from Kumara and his refusal to return to them, both Siva and Parvati felt agonised.

Then both of them feeling painful, displaying the worldly traditions, because of their love for their son, went to the place where their son was lodged.

Kumara, on the other hand, knowing about the arrival of his parents, discarding his attraction for the Kraunca mountain went to a place located at a distance of three *yojanas.*

After the departure of their son from the Kraunca mountain, both of them taking to the form of *Jyoti* (flame) established themselves at the Kraunca mountain.

Because of their love for their son, both Siva and Parvati used to go to the place of their son, in order to have a look at him.

Siva used to go to that place on the moonless day while Parvati went there on the full-moon day.

Since that date *Mallikarjuna-linga* earned popularity in the three worlds.

Whosoever, has a look at that *linga,* he, undoubtedly getting relieved of all the sins, has all his desires fulfilled.

All his miseries are removed and he ultimately enjoys extreme pleasure. He is further freed from entering the womb of his mother.

He undoubtedly achieves enough of riches, food grains, health free from diseases, glory and his wishes are fulfilled.

I have described the second *Jyotirlinga* named Mallikarjuna for the welfare of the people. One gets the best of pleasures by having a look at it.

## Chapter 16 - The glory of Mahakala Jyotirlinga

The *Rsis* said, “O Suta, you know everything by the grace of Vyasa. We don’t feel satisfied by listening to the stories of *Jyotirlinga.*

O holy Lord, be kind to us and describe the third *Jyotirlinga* to us now.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, I, with the association of you people, feel graceful and successful, because the association with the noble people bestows grace.

Thus feeling myself to be fortunate enough, I narrate the auspicious and divine story, which removes the sins. You please listen to it with respect.

There is a city named Avanti, which bestows salvation to all the people, is liked by Siva. It purifies the *lokas,* besides bestowing enormous merits.

There lived a Brahmana there, who was the performer of noble deeds, studied the Vedas, and was the performer of the deeds according to the Vedas.

The Brahmana performed the *yajnas* and daily adored Siva, making a *Parthiva-linga.*

After enjoying the fruits of all the deeds, the Brahmana studied the Vedas. Becoming a learned person, he attained the position of a noble person.

O Excellent sages, he had four sons, devoted to Siva besides being obedient to the parents.

The eldest of them was known as Devapriya, the next was Paramapriya, the third was Sukrta, and the fourth was the religious minded Suvrata.

Because of his merits, there had been an increase in his glory and pleasures of the Brahmana, as the digit of the moon increases during the bright fortnight.

Thereafter, there was an increase in the noble qualities, as a result of which the entire city was filled with *Brahmateja.*

O Brahmanas, now you listen to the excellent even that happened in the meantime. You listen from me, as I had heard earlier. I shall narrate the same to you.

A great demon king named Dusana, who was envious of *dharma* lived over the Ratnamala mountain.

Receiving the boon from Brahma, he treated the worlds as insignificant. He had driven out the gods from their abodes defeating them.

He destroyed the religion of the Vedas and the *Smrtis* in the same way as a lion destroys a rabbit.

He destroyed all the *dharmas* based on the Vedas. He wiped out *dharma* from each and every holy place or the region.

At that point of time, the city of Avanti looked quite charming. Thus thinking, whatever he did there, you listen from me.

Dusana- the demon king arrived in that city accompanied with a huge army.

The immensely wicked and enemy of the Brahmanas, summoned four demons and told them.

The Daitya king said, “The wicked Brahmana, following the Vedic *dharma* do not listen to me. Therefore you punish them all.

O Demons, I have defeated all the gods and the kings. Can I not overpower these Brahmanas?

In case they should be desirous of remaining alive, they should discard adoration of Siva and the Vedic *dharma.*

Otherwise their lives would be in danger. I am speaking the truth. You better carryout this job without any doubt.”

Suta said, “Thus taking a decision, all the four Daityas started burning like the fire on all the four quarters.

The Brahmanas, observing the activities of the *daityas,* did not care for the same, since they were engaged in meditating Siva. They did not feel panicky.

Keeping patience, the Brahmanas did not feel disturbed at all, because the demons were of no consequence before Siva.

In the meantime, the city was surrounded by the demons and they terrified the people, who reached before the Brahmanas.

The people said, “O Lord, what should we do? The wicked demons have arrived in the city and have killed many people.

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the people, all the four sons of Vedavrata, having the firm belief in Sadasiva, said to them.

The Brahmanas said, “Listen, we have neither the weapons nor the strength, to frighten or to face them or drive them out.

Even an ordinary person cannot be disgraced before Siva. We have taken refuge with Siva, and in case we are disgraced, it would indeed be the disgrace of Siva.

Let Siva protect us from the danger of the *asuras.* Who is to protect us today, except Siva who is well disposed towards his devotees.”

Suta said, “Thus keeping patience, worshipping Siva, the Brahmanas were engaged in the meditation of Siva. Then the powerful, Daitya looked at the Brahmanas.

Dusana- the demon king said, “Bind them and beat them.” Listening to the words of the Daitya king, the sons of Vedapriya, did not bother for them.

When the wicked demons, tried to beat the Brahmanas, then in place of the *Parthiva- linga,* a huge pit was formed.

Out of the pit, Siva in the form of Mahakala, for the protection of the noble people and for the destruction of the wicked people, appeared.

He declared, “I am Mahakala, for the destruction of the wicked people like you. O Wicked one, you better move away from the Brahmanas.

Thus speaking Mahakala uttered a *humkara,* which reduced the demon king Dusana and his army to ashes.

Dusana and a part of his army, also were killed by Siva the great soul. A part of the army fled from the battle.

As the darkness is removed with the appearing of the sun, similarly, the demon army was destroyed with the appearing of Siva-Mahakala.

The musical instruments started playing in the heaven. There was the rain of flowers. Brahma, Visnu and other gods arrived there.

The Brahmanas, offered their salutation to lord Siva, with devotion who bestowed welfare. Then they all eulogised Siva.

Then Mahakala Siva getting delighted, assured the Brahmanas and asked them to seek for a boon.

On hearing this all the Brahmanas with devotion offered their salutation to the lord, lowering their heads and said.

Brahmanas said, “O Mahakala, O Mahadeva, O Lord, you punish the wicked people, you redeem us from the ocean of the universe.

O Lord Siva, you kindly stay on here, for the welfare of the people. O Lord, you better redeem your devotees.

Suta said, “At these words of the Brahmanas, lord Siva, bestowed salvation to them, and he himself stayed in that pit for the protection of his devotees.

The Brahmanas who were lodged in all the four directions, achieved the *Sayujya* liberation of Siva. Within a radium of one *kosa* he established himself in the form of a *linga.*

Since that date, Siva in the name of Mahakalesvara became famous on earth. O Brahmanas, By having a look at him, at person does not have to face the misery even in dream.

A person who adores the *linga* with whatever desire in his mind, his desire is fulfilled and he ultimately achieves *moksa.*

O Brahmanas, I have thus narrated the origin of Mahakala. What else do you want to listen from me?”

## Chapter 17 - Greatness of the Mahakala Jyotirlinga

The *Rsis* said, “O Sage with excellent wisdom, the *Jyotirlinga* named Mahakala, is the protector of the devotees. You kindly highlight its glory.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, Mahajara-linga, the protector of the devotees, increases the devotion. Therefore, you listen to its glory with respect.

Once in the city of Ujjaini, there lived Candrasena, the devotee of Siva who had controlled all his senses and was also well versed in the *Sastras.*

O Brahmanas, there was a friend of the king, who was known by the name of Manibhadra besides being the foremost of the Ganas of Siva, besides being adorable by all the people.

Once the large hearted Manibhadra, feeling delighted gave away a *cintamani* to the king.

The gem *cintamani* resembling the *Kaustabha* gem, bestows welfare while one in engaged in devotion, by looking at it or even by listening to its name.

With the mere touch of the auspicious gem, the bronze, copper, lead, stone or any other metal turned into the gold.

The king Candrasura, a devotee of Siva, by wearing that *cintamani* around his neck, became graceful as the sun shines among the other gods.

All other kings became greedy knowing about the possessing of *cintamani* by the king Candrasena.
