Then all the deceitful kings demanded the divine gem from Candrasena, on some pretext or the other.

O Brahmanas, Candrasena was immensely devoted to Siva, who dismissed the demands of the kings.

When the king Candrasena rejected the demons of the other kings, then they started creating disturbances.

Thereafter, all the kings, with the fourfold army, got ready to defeat the king Candrasena in war.

They joined together and conspired with one an other. With their vast armies, they surrounded the four gates of Ujjaini.

Finding that the city had been surrounded from all the sides, the king took refuge with Mahakalesvara.

The king having no alternative left with him, fasted without taking anything, with a firm resolve, and started adoring Mahakala, throughout the day and night.

Lord Mahakalesvara was pleased with him and made arrangements for his protection, which you should listen with respect.

At the same time a milkmaid, wandering with her children, arrived before Mahakala.

The widow accompanied with a five year old son, observed with the devotion, the adoration being performed by the king for lord Mahakala.

Observing the surprising type of worship by the king, she returned to her abode.

Observing the worship of Siva, quite carefully, the son of the milkmaid, out of curiosity thought of performing the same adoration himself.

He brought a beautiful stone, placed it in the form of a *Sivalinga,* in a corner of the hut with utmost devotion. Then he offered the fake fragrance, unbroken rice, ornaments, costumes, incense, besides the eatables to it.

The boy adored the *Sivalinga* again and again offering the flowers and leaves. Then he, dancing before the *linga* offered his salutation to it again and again.

As his mind was engrossed in the worship of Siva the cowherdess, his mother called him to take his meals.

When the boy did not respond to the repeated calls of the mother, being engaged in the worship of *Sivalinga,* she herself went to that place.

She found that her son was seated before Siva, with his eyes closed. She then caught hold of him and belaboured him in anger.

When the son did not move even after having been belaboured and dragged. The destroyed articles of his worship, were thrown away with the *linga* at a distance.

The milkmaid, then feeling miserable, rebuking her son and with her mind filled with rage, returned to her abode.

At the destruction of his worship of Siva, by his mother, the boy fell on the ground, crying for the lord.

He was fainted because of the grief. He regained consciousness after sometime and opened the eyes.

By the grace of Siva, the place was turned into a beautiful abode of Siva known as Mahakala, which was observed by the boy.

It had huge doors of gold, the excellent festoons at the doorsteps. The temple had a resplendent dais set with valuable diamonds.

There were many pot-like domes in the temple, shining columns, studded with gems, besides the crystal bricks decorated the floor. The son of the milkmaid then saw a *linga* of gems, dedicated to Siva who is the abode of mercy together with the articles used for daily worship.

Looking at the place, the mind of the boy was filled with surprise. He got up at once and it appeared to him as if he had been drowned in the ocean of bliss.

He eulogised Siva, offering his salutation to him again and again. The boy came out of the Siva temple at sunset and found his own abode as beautiful as the city of Indra. It was also transformed suddenly like the one of gold, issuing enormous lustre of different nature.

Then he entered his house which was brilliant and glittering in the night, with gold and jewels, which were found spread everywhere. He felt immensely delighted.

He found that his mother was sleeping like a divine damsel. Her limbs were shining and she wore all the ornaments over her body.

O Brahmana, the child on whom Siva had been graceful, feeling pleased woke up his mother.

When she got up, she found everything surprising. With a joyful heart she embraced her son.

Listening to the grace of lord Siva, the husband of Parvati, showered on him, from the mouth of the boy, she uttered, “The one who adores Siva, he enjoys all the pleasures.

The king who had finished the performance of the rites during the night arrived there atonce and found the grandeur of cowherd’s son in the adoring of Siva.

Observing everything in the company of his courtiers, besides the chief priest, the king was absorbed in the ocean of joy and felt emboldened at the same time.

Dropping the tears of reverence and devotion, and reciting the name of Siva, delightfully, the king Candrasena embraced the boy.

O Brahmanas, the wonderful and enormous festivities were arranged. The glorious songs of Siva were sung with joy and excitement.

Because of the wonderful occasion, due to the appearing of the greatness of lord Siva, besides the thrill caused among the people of the city, the night passed like a moment.

In the early morning, the kings, who had surrounded the city from all the sides, for the purpose of the waging of the war, learnt about the event from their spies.

All the kings had arrived collectively for the waging of the war, but were wonder struck with learning of the news.

The kings said, “The king with a peaceful mind, known as Candrasena, being the lord of Ujjaini is a great devotee of Siva. Therefore he is invincible.

The city in which, such a small child too is so much devoted to Siva, what could be said about the king Candrasena who is a great devotee of Siva.

By becoming inimical to him, Siva would surely be displeased on us and because of his anger, all of us would face destruction.

Therefore, we should make friends with such a king and by doing so lord Siva would be graceful on us.”

Suta said, “With this resolve, all the kings leaving aside enmity, discarding the weapons, felt pleased.

With the permission of the king Candrasena, all the kings entered the city and performed adoration of Mahakala.

Thereafter, all the kings visited the house of the milkmaid and praised her fortunes.

The king Candrasena too arrived there and welcomed them offering the precious seats to them. Then he praised them getting surprised.

Looking at the Siva temple which had emerged by the grace and devotion of the son of the cowherdess, besides the *Sivalinga* consecrated therein, their minds were filled with devotion.

Then all the kings also felt pleased with the cowherd boy and they gave him several presents getting delighted.

The kings made him the chieftain of cowherds in all their different lands.

On that very occasion, Hanuman, the lord of the monkeys, who is adored by all the gods, also appeared on the scene.

Finding Hanuman there, all the kings got up suddenly and offered their salutation to the monkey-god with devotion.

The cowherd boy seated among them, was embraced by Hanuman and looking towards the kings , he spoke, Hanuman said, “O Kings, listen, all the human beings can meet with welfare with the adoration of Siva.

Similarly, the cowherd boy, by luck after adoring Siva, without reciting of any *mantras* has achieved pleasure and grace of Siva.

The boy belonging to the cowherd’s race, will increase the glory of his family besides being the best of the devotee of Siva. He, after enjoying all the pleasures in the world, would ultimately achieve *moksa.*

In the eighth generation of his family, there will be a famous cowherd Nanda and Visnu himself will be born as his son named Krsna.

From today onwards, this cowherd boy will achieve great glory, the world over and will be known as Srlkara.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking Siva as Hanuman- the lord of monkeys and son of Anjani, cast his compassionate gaze over the boy as well as the kings present there.

Thereafter, Hanuman revealed to Srikara- the cowherd boy, the method of adoring Siva.

O Brahmanas, thereafter, Hanuman, getting delighted, looking at Srikara and Candransena, besides looking at all others, disappeared from the site in full view of all.

All the kings felt pleased with their welcome and returned to their respective abodes with the permission of the king Candrasena.

The immensely illustrious Srikara, having been thus advised by Hanuman, started adoring Siva, with other learned Brahmanas.

The king Candrasena, as well as the cowherd boy kept on adoring Siva with devotion.

After sometime, both the king Candrasena as well as Srikara- the cowherd boy, while adoring Mahakala, achieved salvation.

Thus Mahakala- *Sivalinga* of Siva- who is graceful on his devotees, bestows his kindness on the noble people and destroys the wicked people.

This is the great secret, the sanctifying narrative that bestows all the happiness, is conducive to the heaven and enhancing devotion to Siva, has been narrated to you.

## Chapter 18 - The glory of Omkaresvara Jyotirlinga

The sages said, “O Fortunate Suta, you have narrated the wonderful story of Mahakalesvara *linga,* the protector of his devotees.

O Best of the learned people, now you please narrate the auspicious story of the fourth *Jyotirlinga* named Omkaresvara, which relieves one of all the sins.

Suta said, “O Brahmanas and the auspicious *Rsis,* I shall narrate the story of Paramesa *linga* of Omkaresvara for your pleasure. All of you should please listen to me.

Sometimes the immensely devoted sage Narada, served the *Sivalinga* at the place near Gokarna.

Thereafter, Narada, the great sage, reached the Vindhya mountain, where he also adored Siva with respect.

Then the Vindhya mountain appeared before Narada, feeling that he possessed everything and there was no deficiency with him.

Then Narada the remover of the pride feeling painful of the pride of Vindhya stayed there.

Then the Vindhya mountain said, “What type of the deficiency has been noted by you in me, which makes you sad?” Hearing this, the sage Narada said, “You possess everything no doubt, but the Sumeru mountain is higher than you and he is classified as the god, but not you.

Suta said, “Thus speaking, Narada left the place, while the Vindhya mountain, blaming his fate, felt painful.

Then the mountain Vindhya thought, “I shall now adore lord Siva.” Thus thinking, he went to Siva to take refuge with him.

He reached the place where Omkaresvara - *Sivalinga* had been consecrated. Reaching there he made another *linga* in clay.

He continued adoring Siva for six months seated at one and the same place.

Observing the performance of hard *tapas* by the Vindhya mountain with devotion, Lord Siva felt pleased, who appeared before him in his true form, which was beyond the reach of even the great *yogis.*

Then Siva, who granted the desires of his devotees, said to him, “You ask for anything you desire. I feel happy with your *tapas.”*

The Vindhya said, “O Lord of the gods, well disposed towards the devotees, in case you are pleased with me, then you bestow wisdom on me, in order to establish my task.”

Suta said, “On hearing this, Siva thought in his mind, that the wicked Vindhya, who cause pain to others, was seeking a boon from him.

Then what should I do so that my boon should become beneficial to him, because the boon given by him should not cause pain to others.”

Suta said, “Still, Siva gave him the best of the boon, saying to Vindhya the lord of the mountain, that he could do as he liked.

In this way all the gods with a spotless mind, prayed to Siva to keep on staying there.

On hearing the words of gods, Siva then accepted the request of the gods, for the welfare of the universe.

The earlier *linga* named Omkara was then turned into two forms. Then Siva lodged in Omkara, and earned the name of Omkara, the one lodged in Parthiva came to be known as Paramesvara. O Brahmanas, both the *lingas* there fulfil the desires of their devotees and are the bestowers of the devotion as well as the salvation.

Then the lord Rsabhadhvaja was adored by several gods, who bestowed several boons on them, getting pleased.

Thereafter all the gods returned to their respective abodes. O Brahmanas, Vindhya too was immensely pleased and after having his task established he freed himself of the pain.

In this way, whosoever, adores Siva, he does not have to take the trouble of entering the womb of his mother, besides enjoying the desired fruit.

Thus I have narrated to you the entire greatness of Omkaresvara *linga.* Now I shall describe the Kedara *linga.*

## Chapter 19 - Kedaresvara Jyotirlinga’s glory

Suta said, “Nara-Narayana, the two incarnations of Visnu, are performing penance at Badrikasrama Khanda in Bharata-varsa. Siva, in order to accept their worship of the *Parthiva-linga* arrives there daily. This is because Siva is always subservient to his devotees arrives there daily. This is because Siva is always subservient to his devotees.

Those two incarnations of Visnu, and spiritual sons of Siva, adored Siva there for a long time.

Once the delightful Siva told them, “I am pleased with you. You better ask for your desired boon.”

At these words of Siva, Nara-Narayana, spoke to Siva, keeping in view the welfare of the world.

Nara-Narayana said, “O Lord of gods, in case you are pleased with us and intend to bestow a boon, then you stay here forever for our adoration.

Suta said, “When both of them thus spoke, Siva got himself established over the snow clad Kedara mountain, in the form of *Jyotirlinga.*

The *linga,* having been adored by both of them (Nara-Narayana) the *linga,* which removed all types of dangers and pains, for the benefit of the people and for the devotees to have a look at it, was lodged, there, which could be seen even today.

Siva is found present there in the form of Kedaresvara. The lord fulfills the desires of all who have an audience with the *linga* or worship it.

This *linga* is adored by the gods as well as the ancient *Rsis.* Siva is also getting pleased bestows the desired boons.

Those who adore *linga* at Badrikasrama, achieve the desired boons daily, because Siva bestows the desired boons to his devotees.

Whosoever adored Kedara Siva in the past never came across any suffering or grief even in the dreams.

He is the one, who on seeing the Pandavas, assumed the form of a he-buffalo, using his magical powers and tried to run away.

But when he was caught by Pandavas by the tail, he stood there lowering his neck. They held his tail, who prayed them again and again.

Then Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, established himself there in the same form. The portion of his head appeared in Nepal.

Pandavas were asked by him to adore him in the same trunkless form. After having been worshipped by them, he stayed on to that place and granted several boons to them.

The Pandavas delightfully left the place after adoring Siva. Then they were relieved of their sufferings after receiving the boons desired by them.

Siva in the temple of Kedara is directly adored by the people of Bharata daily.

Those of the devotees of Siva, who staying there, offer bracelets, they achieve closeness to Siva and take to his form.

The one who observes his forms in the Badari forest, he getting relieved of all the sins and becomes a liberated soul.

Having an audience with Nara-Narayana and Kedaresvara Siva in Badrikasrama a person undoubtedly becomes a liberated soul.

Such of the devotees of Kedaresvara, who meet with their end while on journey, they surely achieve salvation.

One who adores Kedaresvara with devotion, sipping the sacred water of the place, he is never reborn.

O Brahmanas, one should adore Nara- Narayana and Kedaresvara in the Bharata Khanda gets redeemed.

He happens to be the lord of this place. He is particularly the lord of all. Siva in the form of Kedaresvara, fulfills the desires of all.

O *Rsis,* I have narrated everything whatever had been asked by you. With the hearing of this story all the sins are washed out. There is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 20 - The disturbance created by Bhimasura

Suta said, “Now I shall speak out the greatness of Bhima-sankara *Jyotirlinga* with the mere listening of which, a person achieves his desired things.

In the country of Kamarupa, once Siva, the receptacle of welfare and happiness, incarnated for the welfare of the universe.

O Sages, the reason for which Siva incarnated on earth for the welfare of the people, you listen from me.

O Brahmanas, in earlier times a Raksasa named Bhima was born on earth, who caused unbearable pain to all the living beings. He was immensely powerful and was the destroyer of *dharma.*

He was born at Sakya mountain from Kumbhakarna and Karkati, and was living always with his mother.

When Kumbhakarna who frightened the entire universe, was killed at the hands of Rama, then the demoness lived with her son at Saya mountain.

O Brahmanas, once the demon Bhima, who was the source of terror to the entire universe, asked his mother.

Bhima said, “O Mother, who is my father? How do you live here alone? I would like to know. You tell me truthfully.”

Suta said, “When so questioned by her son, whatever the wicked demoness told her son Bhima, I speak out to you.”

Karkati said, “Your father had been the immensely valorous Kumbhakarna, who was killed by Rama with his brother.

O Son, the valorous Raksasa- Kumbhakama, once arrived here and united with me long time back.

The valorous Kumbhakarna, leaving me here, returned to Lanka. I have not seen Lanka. Therefore I live here. Karkata is the name of my father and Puskasi is the name of my mother. Viradha had actually been my husband, who had already been killed at the hands of Rama.

At the death of my beloved husband, I lived with my parents. My parents were also reduced to ashes by an ascetic and they were killed.

Both of them had gone to devour the pupils of the sage Agastya, but the sage Sutiksana, the disciple of the sage Agastya reduced both of them to ashes.

Thus I was left alone suffering variously and helpless, and now I live over this mountain.

In the meantime Kumbhakarna, the brother of Ravana arrived here and united with me and leaving me, he left the place.

As a result of the same, you, the valorous one, were bom to me. Now I live here under your protection.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the mother, the immensely strong Bhima, getting enraged, thought, “What should I do to Hari?

He has killed my father Viradha, besides my maternal grandfather, causing sufferings to my mother.

In case I happen to be his son, then I shall surely cause trouble to Hari.” Thus thinking Bhima started performing severe *tapas.*

Devoting his mind towards Brahma, he performed *tapas* for thousands of years.

Raising his arm upwards, standing on one leg, fixing his gaze at the sun, Bhima, the son of Raksasa started performing *tapas.*

Then a brilliant lustre emerged out of his head which scorched the gods who rushed for taking refuge with Brahma.

Indra and other gods, eulogising Brahma, variously reciting several *stotra* adored him. Then after offering their salutation to him they revealed to him the tale of their sufferings. ”

The gods said, “O Brahma, the lustre of the Raksasa, is scorching the entire universe. You better give away all whatever is desired by the wicked demon.

Otherwise all of us would be reduced to ashes with his lustre. Therefore, you give him whatever is desired by him.

Suta said, “Brahma- the grand sire of the universe, listening to the words of the gods, got ready to pronounce a boon on the demon”.

Brahma said, “I am pleased with your penance, you ask for the boon desired by you.” Listening to the words of Brahma, the Raksasa said.

Bhima said, “O God of gods, O Brahma, in case, you are really pleased with me, and intend to grant me a boon then you kindly grant me the strength beyond measure.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking, the Raksasa offered his salutation to Brahma. Brahma also returned to his abode, pronouncing a boon on him.

Having been filled with pride, the demon too returned to his abode and offering his salutation to his mother he said.

Bhima said, “O Mother, you look at my strength. I shall destroy Indra and other gods, besides their helpers like Visnu and others.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking the immensely valorous Bhima, initially overpowered Indra and other gods, removing them from their positions.

Thereafter he defeated Visnu who is adored by the gods, several times. There after the demon conquered the nether world.

Initially he went to king Sudaksina to conquer the Kamarupa country, where he fought a terrific battle.

With the influence of the boon of Brahma, becoming valorous, he conquered the king of that place who was a devotee of Siva.

Then Bhima having the enormous influence, defeating the king of Kamarupa, put him in fetters and belaboured him.

O Brahmanas, the wicked demon Bhima plundered the kingdom, riches, food grains, gems and other valuables of Kamesvara king, who was the devotee of Siva.

Putting the noble king of Kamesvara, fond of sacred rites and favourite of Siva, in fetters, he was dumped in an isolated place.

The king somehow made a *Parthiva-linga* there and started adoring it, for his own protection.

He eulogised the Ganga several times. Then having the bath mentally, he adored Siva.

He then meditated upon Siva in accordance with the rules prescribed for the worship of earthen idols.

He offered his salutation, recited *stotras,* displayed *mudras, asanas,* adoring Siva by several other means.

Then he repeated the *mantra om namah sivaya* several times. Because of his helplessness, he could do nothing more.

The chaste queen Daksina too lovingly arranged for the adoration of Siva in her home, including the *Parthiva-puja.*

Both the husband and wife kept on adoring Siva with their devoted minds, serving the lord at the same time.

Having been deluded with the achieving of the boon, the demon Bhima, put a stop to the performing of the *yajnas* and other religious rites. He declared that whatever was meant for the gods should be give to him.

O Sages, the wicked demon overpowered the entire earth with his vast army.

Being himself powerful, he wiped out the reciting of the Vedas *sastras, smrtis, Purana* and other literature connected *dharmas,* and he himself usurped all the religious adorations.

O Brahmanas, he tortured Indra and other gods, besides the sages and drove them out from their respective abodes.

Indra and other gods, besides all the sages, getting upset, making Brahma and Visnu to lead them, went to Siva to take refuge with him.

Sitting over the bank of the Mahakosi river, the gods adored and pleased Siva, who bestowed welfare on all the worlds. They offered their salutation to him.

They consecrated the *Parthiva-linga* of Siva there, appropriately, eulogised him reciting several *stotras.* Then offering several prayers to the lord, they pleased him.

When so eulogised by the gods, Siva, getting pleased, then spoke to the gods.

Siva said, “O Brahma, O Visnu and O Sages, I am pleased with you. You ask for the boon. What should I do for you?

Suta said, “At these words of Siva, the gods offered their salutation to the lord and then spoke to him.

The god said, “O God of gods, you are aware of everything in the minds of others, nothing is unknown to you.

O Master, still you kindly listen. We narrate the tale of our sufferings at your command. You kindly cast a compassionate look at us.

The valorous demon- the son of Kumbhakarna and Karkati, is causing trouble to us throughout the day and night.

O Mahesan, O Lord, you kindly kill this extremely troublesome demon Bhima. O lord, be merciful, do not delay.

Suta said, “At these words of the gods, Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees said to the gods.

Siva said, “The king of Kamarupa is the best of my devotees. O Gods, you go to him and tell him that the desired task would be done in no time.

The king Sudaksina, The Lord, Kamarupa happens to be my devotee. Let him worship me with immense devotion.

The demon who has insulted you had achieved boon from Brahma, and who is quite a wicked one, I shall surely kill the wicked demon named Bhima.

Suta said, “Thereafter all the gods delightfully went to the king and repeated to him the words spoken by Siva.

Conveying the message of Siva to the king all the gods and the sages, returned to their respective abodes.

## Chapter 21 - Showering of the grace of Kamarupesvara

Suta said, “In order to shower his grace over his devotee, Siva stayed with him, together with his *ganas.* He concealed himself in order to protect him.

In the meantime, the lord of Kamarupa initiated a great meditation in front of the *Parthiva-linga* of Siva.

Thereafter the Raksasa was informed by some one that the king was making some black magic against him.

Suta said, “On hearing the news, the enraged Raksasa, held a sword in order to kill the king and rushed towards him.

Reaching there, the demon found the *Parthiva-linga* being adored and thinking that he was doing something against him (the king), he started thinking.

“I shall kill him today, with his weapons.” Thus thinking, the enraged Raksasa said to the king.

Bhima said, “O Wicked king, what is all this being done by you? I shall pardon you in case you speak out the truth, otherwise your death is certain.”

Suta said, “Listening to his words, the king of Kamarupa, started thinking with his mind, firmly devoted to Siva.

Whatever has to happen in future is destined to happen. Everything is controlled by the moves of the destiny. Fate is the second name of Siva.

The compassionate Siva, is present in this *Parthiva-linga*; shall he not do anything for me? Then this Raksasa is of no consequence.

Siva would surely uphold his words. The Vedas have claimed Siva to be extremely truthful.

According to him, “When a harsh person troubles my devotee, then I kill him surely in order to save my devotee.”

Thus holding patience and meditating Siva in his mind, the king reminded him of the promise, mentally and devotedly.

He said, “O Lord, I belong to you. You do whatever you like. I am speaking the truth. You take care of my welfare.

The king who was bound with fetters of truth, devoting his mind at the feet of Siva, spoke the truth, getting unmindful of the Raksasa.

The king said, “The one who is the lord of mobile and immobile and is unblemished, such a lord Siva is being adored by me.”

Suta said, “On hearing these words of the king of Kamarupa, Bhima spoke thunderingly, his body shaking with anger.

Bhima said, “I am well aware of your Siva. What harm can be cause to me? He is the one who was established by Ravana, the brother of my father.

You intend to remain alive on his strength? Then you have won everything. There is no doubt about it.

Till such time, I have not seen Sankara- your protector, you can serve him as your protector but not subsequently.

O King, by my having a look at him, everything would be clear. Therefore you remove this form of Siva from here, otherwise you would surely be in danger today. I, possessing the horrible strength, shall give your lord a surprising gift.”

Suta said, “Listening to such words of the Raksasa, but with a firm faith in Siva, the king said to the demon.

The king said, “I am a degraded and a wicked person, but I shall not disown the adoration of Siva. My lord is the best of all who shall never desert me.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the king, who happened to be the devotee of Siva, Bhima- the Raksasa, smilingly spoke to the king.”

Bhima said, “Intoxicated Siva, daily begs for alms. He is unaware of himself. How can a yogi protect his devotees?

Thus thinking, you remove yourself from him. Both myself and your lord shall be engaged in a fight.”

Suta said, “At these words of the demon, the king who was devoted to Siva, fearlessly spoke to Bhima, who always troubled the world.

The king said, “O Wicked demon, I cannot indulge into such wicked activities, but you can do so being all powerful.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking, rebuking the king, the Raksasa, threw his sword in anger at the king.

Then the Raksasa, who had arrived with his strong warriors, smilingly, said, “Now you observe the strength of your master, who bestows comforts over his devotees.”

O Brahmanas, before the sword could touch the body of the king, Siva reached there and declared.”

“Look here, I am Bhimesvara, and have appeared for the protection of my devotee. It is my firm resolve to always protect my devotee.

Now you witness my strength, by which I make my devotees comfortable. Thus speaking he cut off the demon’s sword with his bow into two pieces.

Then the wicked demon shot a trident, which was reduced to a hundred pieces by Siva.

Thereafter, the demon shot a *Sakti* at Siva, which was reduced to a lakh of pieces with the arrows of the lord.

Then he shot a dagger (huge iron club) at Siva, which was again reduced to small pieces like gingelly seeds by the lord with his trident.

A fierce fight between the demons and the *Siva ganas* followed, which was painful for the onlookers.

Thereafter, the entire earth became upset, in a moment. Then the ocean as well as the mountains started shaking.

All the gods and the sages were disturbed and they spoke, “We uselessly prayed to Siva.”

Then arrived Narada, who with folded hands, lowering his head, prayed to Siva-the remover of the miseries.

Narada said, “O Cause of the illusion, O Master, you kindly forgive me. Is it necessary to raise the battle-axe to destroy a straw?” You better kill the demon without delay.

When so eulogised by the gods, Siva reduced the Raksasa to ashes using the weapon of *humkara.*

O Sage, even as all the gods were watching, Siva, in full view of the gods burnt all the Raksasas in a moment.

As the conflagration burns the forest in a moment, similarly the enraged Siva burnt out the demon army.

46\. No one could know about the ashes of the demon Bhima, who was burnt with his entire family and thereafter his name could not be heard anywhere.

Thereafter with the grace of Siva, Indra and other gods, the ascetics besides the entire world became healthy.

The fire of the anger of Siva was spread from one forest to the other, together with the ashes of the demons.

Thereafter several *osadhis* were grown there. Then the excellent humans felt delighted.

There was no task in the world which could not be established with these ashes. The spirits, goblins, *pisacas* could be removed with those ashes.

Then the gods and the sages, prayed to lord Siva, to get established there for the pleasure of the people.

This is the degraded country, which caused trouble to those who are not interested in war. By finding you present here, the people would face welfare.

You will stay here as Bhima-sankara, who fulfills all the desires. This *linga* is the destroyer of all the calamities, and shall always be adored.”

Suta said, “At the prayer of the gods and the ascetics, Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, got himself established there in the form of *linga.*

## Chapter 22 - The glory of Visvesvara at Kasi

Suta said, “Now I shall narrate the greatness of Visvesvara- the remover of the grave sins. You please listen to the same.

Whatever things are visible on earth as substantive, as an entity in the form of knowledge or bliss, are eternal, free from blemish, desired for a second. That second, of the tree of salvation, was possessed of attributes and is called Siva.

It splits into two- the male and the female forms. The male is known as Siva, while the female is shown as Sakti or Parvati.

O Excellent ascetics, the invisible *Cita* and *Ananda* created *Purusa* and *Prakrti.* O Brahmanas, on seeing their parents, both *Purusa* and *Prakrti* developed a doubt.

Thereafter a divine voice emerged out from the great *Atman* free from attributes, “You perform penance, for the generation of the excellent creation.”

Then *Prakrti* and *Purusa* said, “O Lord Siva, there is no place for the performing of *tapas.* Where shall we perform *tapas* at your command.

Thereafter a beautiful city was built, which was the essence of the lustre and was spread in five *kosas* and was quite beautiful in which all the amenities could be found. Siva built the city while remaining in the sky in the firmament near the *Purusa.*

Visnu having been lodged in that city, became desirous of starting creation. He performed *tapas* sitting in meditation.

Because of his efforts, several streams of water emerged from that place. At that point of time, nothing was visible there.

Then Visnu saw as to what was the surprising thing found there? Then he shook his head.

Then a gem emerging out of his ear fell on the ground, which was turned into a great place of pilgrimage known as Manikarnika.

When the said Manikarnika in the form of water kept on flowing upto five *kosas* (Pancakosi), then Siva held it over the tip of his trident.

Then lord Visnu slept there with his wife *Prakrti.* At the command of Siva, Brahma was born out of the navel of Visnu, seated over a lotus.

At the command of Siva, he indulged into a surprising type of creation. He created fourteen *lokas* around the globe.

The size of the globe has been described by the sages to be fifty crores of *yojanas.*

The living beings in the globe are bound by their *karmas* and as such, how could they achieve me?” Thus thinking he separated Pancakosi.

The region of Pancakosi, bestows welfare and is the destroyer of the evil *karmas,* Kasi, illuminates the path of *moksa,* bestower of the divine knowledge, and is quite dear to me.

Lord Siva, the supreme soul, there, had been consecrated as a *Sivalinga* known by the name of Avimukta and spoke, “You have been formed of my *amsa* as *Jyotirlinga* and therefore, you never leave this place.”

Thus speaking lord Siva, grounded Kasi, with the tip of his trident and established it on earth.

Even after the completion of a divine day of Brahma, the city of Kasi does not get destroyed. O Sages, at that point of time, Siva holds it over the tip of his trident.

O Brahmanas, then Brahma again recreates the universe, then he again establishes Kasi. Because of the bondages of the *karmas* and their attraction thereto, it is called Kasi.

The Avimuktesvara *linga* of Kasi, always remains stable. It bestows salvation to the grave sinners.

O Excellent sages, in other regions one achieves *Sarupya* salvation, while at Kasi, one gets *Sayujya* salvation.

Those who cannot get redeemed elsewhere, they also get redeemed at Kasi. The region of Pancakosi, bestows enormous merits, therefore it redeems one of the crores of the killings.

Even the gods living here are desirous of their death here, what to speak of the others? This is because, Kasi, the beloved of Siva, always bestows pleasures and salvation.

The glory of Kasi is praised by Brahma, Visnu, *Siddhas, yogis,* ascetics, sages besides the living beings of the three worlds.

I cannot narrate the glory of Kasi in hundreds of years. Still I would do so according to my capacity.

Then Kalagni Rudra with *sattvaguna*inside, and *tamasika* outside, is well known in the world, and is the supreme being, with and without attributes, spoke, making several obeisances.

Rudra said, “O Lord of universe, O Great lord, I undoubtedly belong to you. Be merciful on me. I am your son and am accompanied with Parvati.

O Lord of the universe, you shall stay here for the welfare of the universe. I pray to you, O Lord of the universe, to save the worlds.”

Suta said, “Avimukta too, getting ready for the benefit of others, praising them, dropping the tears spoke to Siva.

Avimukta said, O God of gods, O Mahadeva, you are the *Osadhi* (medicine) of ailment of time (*kalaraja*) you are the lord of the three Osadhis and are also served by Brahma, Visnu and other gods.

O Deva, you kindly accept the capital city of Kasi and I (Avimukta), meditating up you shall stay here.

You are the bestower of the salvation, and fulfil the desires of all. Therefore you for the benefit of the world, stay here with Parvati.

O Sadasiva, you redeem all the living beings of the world. I pray to you again and again. You establish the tasks of your devotees.”

Suta said, In this way Visvanatha prayed to Siva. Since then he was lodged there for the benefit of the devotees.

Since the time, Siva started living in Kasi, the city looked better as compared to the earlier times.

## Chapter 23 - The greatness of the Jyotirlinga of Kasi Visvesvara

The *Rsis* said, “O Suta, O Lord, in case the city of Kasi is so auspicious, then you kindly reveal before us the glory of Kasi as well as *Avimukta.*

Suta said, “O Excellent sages, I shall narrate the greatness of Varanasi as well as that of Visvesvara, in brief. All of you should listen.

Once the goddess Parvati, for the welfare of the universe enquired about the glory of Kasi as well as *Avimukta."*

Parvati said, “You can speak out the glory of this region completely. Therefore, being compassionate on me and from the view of the welfare of the people, you please speak out the same to me.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the goddess, the lord of the universe, for purpose of the welfare of the universe, said to Bhavan!.”

Paramesvara said, “O Beautiful one, you have started an excellent discussion which bestows welfare on the universe. I shall therefore speak out the greatness of Kasi and Avimukta.

The region of Varanasi has always been my secret place and is the source of salvation for all the people of the world.

The *siddhas* of this region always take refuge under my *Vratas.* They adore several *lingas* for the achievement of my *loka.*

Those who have enquired about their own souls and have also controlled their own sense organs, follow the great *Pasupatayoga* as explained in the Vedas; which yields worldly pleasures besides salvation.

O Great goddess, my abode in Varanasi, is always appealing to me. Discarding everything else, you better listen to the reason for its greatness.

The learned person as well as the one who is devoted to me are both entitled to liberation irrespective of whether they take bath at the places of the pilgrimage or not, have an audience with the deity or not, both are the same.

Wherever they meet with their end, they become the liberated souls. They achieve *moksa* soon. This is my firm opinion.

O Goddess, O Supreme Sakti, you listen to the excellent glory of Avimukta place of pilgrimage, which you should listen attentively.

The people of all the *varnas* and the *asramas* irrespective of their being young, youthful, and old, surely achieve salvation, after their death in this city.

O Brahmanas, a woman, irrespective of her being clean or unclean, a girl, married, widow, barren, suffering from menstrual disorder or defects, one who dies during pregnancy or delivery or of whatever nature she might be, if she dies in this region, she attains salvation. There is no doubt about it.

The sweat born (lice, bugs etc.) the egg born, (birds and reptiles), the germinating ones, (trees and plants, and those born of embryo-born mammals), these living beings do not achieve the type of salvation elsewhere which they achieve here.

O Goddess, there is no need of perfect knowledge here, nor the devotion, nor the holy rites, nor the charitable gifts.

There is no need of any *samskaras,* meditation, reciting of the *mantras,* or adoration or the birth in the high family (to achieve salvation here).

Whosoever stays in this region of mine which bestows salvation, irrespective of the type of death he might have met with, he surely achieves *moksa.*

O Beloved, this divine city of mine is extremely sacred. O Parvati, Brahma and other gods are unaware of the glory of this place.

The great region is called *Avimukta.* Even after death, this region is better than Naimisaranya and others.

The learned people consider the Avimukta region as the place of *dharma, moksa* and pilgrimage.

Irrespective of a person meeting with his end while eating, sleeping, playing etc. or getting engaged in any other work here, he attains *moksa.*

It is better to become a *pisaca* after committing enormous sins, but to perform thousand of *yojanas* to achieve heaven, without the city of Kasi would not be worth while.

Therefore the people resort to Kasi with every strenuous effort and all the sages, serving Kasi, adore *Avyakta-linga* of Kasi.

O beloved, I distribute the various fruits among the various people who perform *tapas* with these ends in view.

Those who cast of their bodies here, no entanglement of any sort, binds them, the one who ends his life here is never bound in the bondages of the *karmas.*

Brahma, Visnu, Surya, divine sages, ascetics and other people adore me here at Kasi.

A person, involved in the worldly pleasures, who is unmindful of the *dharma,* in case of his death in this region, he does not have to face the re-birth.

Then what about the people, free of arrogance, patient, those having *sattvagunas,* free from deceitfulness, the auspicious souls and those who refrain from committing the sins.

A *yogi* is born here after thousands of years and achieves *moksa* (salvation), after his death here.

O Parvati, there are several *Sivalinga* here which have been consecrated by the devotees, which fulfil the desires of all, besides bestowing of *moksa.*

This region is spread up to five *kosas* in all the directions. One who dies in this region, he achieves nectar.

When a person with an auspicious soul dies here, he achieves *moksa* at once. But when a sinner dies, then he reaping the reward for the sins in several births, achieves *moksa* ultimately. The one who commits sins in this *Avimukta* region, he suffering pain of the Bhairavi type, achieves *moksa* after ten thousand years.

In this way, the course of the fate in regard to the one who commits sins, has been narrated by me to you. Realising this, one should serve the *Avimukta* region accordingly.

The deeds performed by a person can never be destroyed even in crores of years and as such one has to reap the reward of the auspicious and inauspicious deeds performed by him in his life.

With the performing of the inauspicious deeds one achieves hell and by performing of the noble deeds, one achieves the heaven.

O Parvati, the birth or life irrespective of being good or bad, long or short, one achieves salvation after spending of the same.

O Mahesvari, in the *karmakanda* section of the Vedas, the action that causes bondage, is said to be three fold which include collected (*sancita*), *kriyaman* (present) and *Prarabda* those which have already started yielding results.

The deeds of the earlier births are called as hoarded (*Sancita).* The deeds, the fruits of which are being experienced in the present birth, is called as *Prarabdha.* O Goddess the deeds (good or bad) performed during this birth are called as *Kriyaman* or activated.

The *prarabdha* deeds can be finished by facing them (in practical life) and by no other means. The deeds falling under the categories of *sancita* and *kriyaman* could be destroyed by means of adoration etc.

All the types of deeds cannot be destroyed without the city of Kasi. All other places of pilgrimage, are easily available, but the city of Kasi is difficult to achieve. It could be achieved by the noble souls alone.

In case some one had visited Kasi in his earlier birth with grace, only then one can meet his end at Kasi, otherwise death here is impossible.

A person, who takes a bath in the Ganga, arriving here, then all his *Sancita* and *Kriyaman* deeds get destroyed.

The *prarabdha* deeds can never be destroyed, except by enjoyment. This is certain. They can be destroyed in case one dies in Kasi.

In case one commits sins after having lived at Kasi, then because of the same, he has to be bom at Kasi again.

As a result of this all his sins get destroyed. Therefore a person should live in Kasi for the shattering of the bondages of the *karmas.*

O Beloved, a person who makes a Brahmana to live in Kasi at his own expense, he gets entitled to salvation with the stay of the Brahmana at Kasi.

A person who dies in Kasi, is never reborn. A person being desirous of a reward, when he dies at Prayaga, is also never reborn.

In case both (the desire and the achieving of the reward) are combined, then the reward of the stay at Kasi becomes useless. In case the combination is not there, the greatness of the *Tirtharaja* is of no consequence.

Therefore, with this end in view, lord Visnu resorted to the new creation at my command and he achieved his desired *siddhis.*

Suta said, “O Excellent sages, thus, there is the height of glory of Kasi and Visvesvara, which bestows pleasure and salvation to the sages.

Thereafter, I shall narrate about the glory of Tryambakesvara, listening to which, a person is relieved of all the sins in a moment.

## Chapter 24 - Gautama’s greatness in relation to Tryambakesvara

Suta said, O Excellent sage, now you listen to the story which removes the sins, as I heard from my preceptor Vyasa. I narrate the same.

In ancient times there was a famous sage Gautama. He had a chaste wife named Ahalya.

He performed tapas in the southern region at Brahmagiri mountain (near Nasik region) for ten thousand years.

O Ascetics, once there was no rainfall for a hundred years, which made all the living beings to suffer badly.

Not a single green leaf could be seen. Under these circumstances how could a drop of water which saves the life of the people be found there?

Then all the sages, humans, animals, birds, the deer were scattered in all the ten directions.

Finding such a type of draught the ascetic Brahmana, resorting to ðãṁñīóīḍṁ performed hard tapas while meditating.

The sage Gautama also performing ðãṁñīóīḍṁ performed tapas for six months in order to please god Varuna.

Then Varunadeva, in order to bestow a boon on him, arrived there. He said, “I am pleased. You ask for a boon. I shall grant you the desired boon.

Then the sage Gautama prayed to him for the fall of the rain O Brahmanas, then the lord Varuna, spoke to the sage.

Varuna said, “How could I make the rain to fall against the command of the gods. You are a learned sage. I can provide you in case you ask for something else.”

Suta said, “Thus listening to the words of noble Varuna, Gautama, eager to help others said to him.”

Gautama said, “In case you are pleased with me and in case you intend to give me the boon, then you do as per my request.

O Lord of all the gods, since you are the lord of the abode of water, then you give us the water in charity which should be beyond destruction and should be ever rewarding.”

Suta said- At this request of Gautama, Varuna spoke to him- You better dig up a pit.

At these words of Varuna, Gautama dug a pit which was a hand in depth, and was filled by Varuna with the divine water.

Thereafter Varuna, the lord of the waters said to the excellent sage Gautama, kind to help others.

Varuna said, “O Great sage, this ever lasting water shall be known on earth as a place of pilgrimage in your name.

The reward of performing tapas, charities, homa, adoration of gods, tapas, sraddha for the manes, would produce the everlasting reward.”

Suta said- Thus speaking lord Varuna, disappeared from the scene, while the sage Gautama who did good to others felt pleased.

The refuge of the great people is meant for the bestowing of importance, therefore the noble souls get an audience with the gods in divine form, which is beyond the reach of the degraded people.

One reaps the reward of the type of a person one serves. By serving the great people, one achieves greatness, while by serving the mean people, one becomes mean.

While serving a lion one achieves pearls, while serving a jackal one gets the pieces of bones.

The noble person by nature, cannot bear the pain of others, they remove the sufferings of others by facing the pain themselves.

The trees, gold, sandal wood as well as the sugarcane are excellent for doing good to others. The people possessing such qualities are rare in. the world.

The compassionate people, who are free from arrogance, those who do good to others, or those having controlled all the senses, (are Supreme) and the earth is stable by their grace.

Gautama, the great sage by achieving the inaccessible water started performing all the religious duties regularly.

The excellent sage then served several types of food grains like barley, rice and others for the performing of the yajnas.

The asrama of the sage Gautama was filled with various types of food grains, trees, flowers and the fruits.

Learning about them, thousand of sages arrived there, besides the animals, birds and the other living beings.

It was a unique type of forest in the world. Because of the everlasting water no one suffered due to draught.

Several of the Rsis, engaged in auspicious rites, started living there in the forest with their disciples, wives and the sons.

The crops were grown for the livelihood. Thus, with the influence of the sage Gautama the forest became blissful.

## Chapter 25 - False allegation on Gautama for killing a cow

Suta said- O Brahmanas, once the sage Gautama, sent his disciples with kamandalas for fetching water (at the kunda of water), where several other wives of the sages had also arrived, who stopped the disciples of Gautama from collecting the water saying, “We are the wives of the sages therefore we shall first fill the water.” Thus speaking, they rebuked them.

The disciples returned to the asrama and complained to the wife of Gautama. She consoled them somehow. Then she herself went with the pupils and got them the water herself, which was in turn supplied to the sage Gautama. The sage some how managed with that water.

Then the wives of the Rsis, getting enraged rebuked the wife of Gautama, after which the women with evil intentions returned to their respective abodes.

The wicked women incited their husbands differently by telling the concocted news.

Due to the move of the destiny, the rsis were influenced with the words of their wives.

The ascetics went to the sage Gautama getting infuriated.

In order to create obstructions in the meditation of Gautama, the evil minded and infuriated Rsis started adoring Ganesvara offering several presents.

Then Ganesa, who was subservient to his devotees, appeared before them, and the Brahmanas desired reward from him.

Ganesa said, I am pleased with you. You ask for a boon. What should I do for you.” On hearing his words,

The Rsis said- In case you intend to grant us a boon, then drive Gautama out of the hermitage, getting him humiliated by the ascetics.

Suta said- Thus listening to their prayer, Gajanana (elephant-faced deity) tried to convince them saying.

Ganesa said, “O Rsis, all of you should listen. The words spoken by you are not proper. Those who get enraged against him without any reason, shall have to face distress.

It is he who did good to all at the time of draught. It would not be proper to cause pain to him. In case you cause trouble to him, you are sure to face destruction.

By performing similar type of tapas, you should seek for the fruit of the same. Instead of auspicious fruit, you are aspiring for misfortune.”

Suta said- Listening to the words of Ganesa, the Rsis, because of their confused wisdom, spoke to Ganesa.

The Rsis said- O Lord, this is the only thing which you have to do for us and nothing else. At these words of the Rsis, Ganesa said, “A wicked person cannot achieve nobility, while a noble person cannot move on the evil path. This has been ordained by Brahma.

When you had been suffering for want of water then the sage Gautama relieved you of the miseries, making you comfortable.

But presently, you people are bent upon causing trouble to him. This is not proper in the world. You first think over.

All of your have been overpowered with the illusion of your wives and are neglecting my words. But this would indeed be beneficial for the sage Gautama.

Ultimately the same sage shall make you comfortable. It would not be proper to remove him. Therefore, you better ask for another boon.”

Suta said- Inspite of these words of Ganes'a, the Rsis failed to accept his advice.

Because of his being subservient to the devotees Ganesa, the son of Siva, with a painful heart, spoke to the degraded ascetics.

Ganesa, “I bestow a boon as prayed by you. Then whatever has to happen shall happen.” Thus speaking, he disappeared from the place.

Gautama, however, was unaware of the conspiracy hatched by the ascetics. He delightfully engaged himself in his daily prayers with his wife.

Thereafter, O Excellent sages, you listen the miseries which the wicked ascetics had to face because of the boon of Ganesa.

The paddy and barley had been grown in the fields of Gautama, which were filled with water. Ganesa reached there in the form of a skeleton cow.

O excellent sages, staggering and faltering, tne cow, because of the boon grazed fields of barley and paddy.

In the meantime, the merciful Gautama also arrived there as a matter of chance. He drove out the cow with the use of straw.

With the mere touch of the straw, the cow fell on earth and died in full view of the sage.

Then the wicked ascetics as well as their wives said, “What has this that Gautama has done?”

O Brahmanas, the surprised Gautama, called for Ahalya and spoke to her with a painful heart.

Gautama said, “O Goddess, what has happened here? How has it happened? The lord is annoyed with us? What should be done? Where should we go? This is the killing of a cow.”

Suta said- In the meantime the Brahmanas and their wives started teasing Gautama and Ahalya with harsh words.

Their evil-minded disciples as well as the sons also started rebuking Gautama, showering disgrace on him.

The Rsis said, “Your face is not worth looking at. You leave this place, O Killer of the cow and by looking at your face, one should have a bath with clothes on.

Till such time you remain in the asrama, the gods and the manes would not accept anyone of our offering.

O Killer of the cow and sinful one, you leave this place with your family and go elsewhere. Don’t delay.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking, the sages pelted stone at Gautama, while the woman abused him. Ahalya was also rebuked.

Having been insulted and tortured by the wicked Brahmanas, Gautama said, O Sages, I shall leave this place and go somewhere else.”

Thus speaking, Gautama the great sage, went at a distance of a Kosa from that place and rebuilt an asrama there again, as advised by them.

He thought, Till such time I am under the influence of the curse, I cannot perform the adoration of the gods, the sraddha of the manes, or any other Vedic rites.

Spending a fortnight there, the excellent sage Gautama, feeling painful, prayed to the ascetics.

Gautama said, “You being graceful, kindly tell me as to what else should I do, in order to get myself relieved of the sin.”

Suta said- When so asked by Gautama, the Brahmanas gave no reply to him. Then standing at one place, the sage Gautama again asked them with devotion.

Standing at a distance Gautama offered his salutation to them and humbly asked them again as to what should be done by him.

At these word of the sage Gautama, the sages who had conspired against the sage Gautama, said to him.

The sages said, “The human body cannot be purified without repentance therefore you perform repentance for the purification of your body.

Revealing your sin, you go round the earth. Then returning here, perform fasting for a month.

You should go round the Brahma mountain, a hundred and eight times in order to get yourself purified, or otherwise, you bring the Ganga on earth and have a bath in the same or making a crore of earthen lingas adore Siva.

Thereafter, taking a bath in the Ganga again, you should go round the mountain eleven times.

Bathe the Parthiva-linga with the water of Ganga, a hundred times, to achieve purification.” These words of the sages were accepted by Gautama.

Saying that, “As per your command I shall resort to the adoration of Parthiva-linga and shall go round the mountain.”

Thus speaking the excellent sage, after going round the mountain, made a Pdrthiva- linga and adored it.

Ahalya also did so. At that point of time, the disciples of Gautama served them both appropriately.

## Chapter 26 - Siva’s grace on Gautama by appearing of Tryambakesvara and Ganga

Suta said- O Brahmanas, at this performance of the sage Gautama, the delighted Siva, appeared there with his ganas before Gautama.

The compassionate Siva getting pleased said- O Sage, I am pleased with your adoration. You better ask for some boon.

Observing the divine form of Siva, the great yogi, the delighted Gautama, offered his salutation to him.

Gautama offered his salutation to Siva with folded hands and then said to the lord, “O God, you kindly relieve me of the sins.”

Suta said- Listening to the words of Gautama in this way, the immensely delighted Siva, then spoke to the sage Gautama.

Siva said, “O Sage, you are quite graceful, successful, unblemished and sinless. The wicked sages have cheated you, they are sinful, wicked and killers.

Even the sinful people are relieved of the sins by having a look at you. You always remain engaged in my tapas. Then how could you be a sinner?

O Sage, the wicked people, who have betrayed you, are degraded and the sinners and the people by a mere look at them become sinful and ungrateful, for which no repentance has been prescribed.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking, Siva who punishes the wicked and bestows grace on the noble people, O Brahmanas, highlighted the evil ways of those wicked ascetics, severally.

Listening to the words of Siva, the sage Gautama was taken aback. Then he offered his salutation to Siva with devotion and said to him.

Gautama said, “Those Rsis had showered enormous good on me. In fact had they not done so, I could never have an audience with you.

Graceful are those ascetics their wickedness and evil ways which have yielded enormous good for me.”

Suta said, “Thus listening to his words, Siva was pleased and casting his compassionate look on him the lord said to Gautama.

Siva said, “O Dear one, you are the best among the sages. Finding me pleased, you better ask for a boon, you desire.”

Suta said , “Gautama also thought over and said, “The news of my sin has been spread the world over, therefore, whatever has been spoken by me in the presence of all should indeed be accomplished.”

Thus thinking, the excellent sage Gautama, spoke to Siva, with his hands folded and lowering his shoulders.

Gautama said, “O Lord, you have spoken the truth, but the decision of the five leading persons, cannot be otherwise or reversed. Therefore, whatever has to happen, let it happen.

O Lord of the gods, in case you are pleased with me then let Ganga be given to me to do good to the universe. I offer my salutation to you again and again.”

Suta said, “Thus revealing the feelings of his mind, holding on to the lotus like feet of Siva, with the intention of doing good to the people, Gautama bowed in reverence to Siva.

Then Siva, took out the essence of the heaven and earth, which had been extracted earlier, and was given by Brahma to Siva in the marriage of the latter, besides the remaining water of the Ganga, was given away to Gautama by lord Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees.

The water of the Ganga, then took to the form of a damsel. The sage Gautama, then eulogising her, bowed in reverence to her.

Gautama said, “You are graceful, blessed and successful. You have purified the earth. O Ganga, you purify me since I am falling in the hell.

Suta said- Then Siva, who benefits all, also said, “O Ganga, you at my command, purify the sage Gautama.”

Thus listening to the words of Siva and the sage Gautama, Ganga said, “The devotion of Siva, purifies all.”

Ganga said, “O Lord, I purifying the sage with his family, shall return to my abode. These are my truthful words.”

Suta said- When Ganga so spoke to Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, then Siva again spoke to her for the welfare of the world.

Siva said, “O Goddess, till the advent of Kaliyuga, when the son of Vaivasvata shall be the twenty-eighth Manu, you stay here alone.”

Suta said, “On hearing the words of Siva, Ganga, the purifying leading river said.”

Ganga said, “O Mahesvara, O Tripurantaka, O Lord, in case I earn enough of glory and greatness, then I would like to stay on earth.

O Lord, please abide with me with this beautiful body of yours along with your consort and the ganas.

Suta said- Thus listening to the words of Ganga, Siva who is dear to his devotees, spoke to Ganga, for the welfare of the universe.

Siva said, “O Ganga, you are graceful, listen, I am in no way separated from you. Still you stay here and I shall also do so.”

Suta said, “Thus listening to the words of lord Parmesvara, Ganga was pleased and she accepted his command.

In the meantime all the gods, the ancient sages, the excellent tirthas, and other auspicious regions arrived there and shouted the slogans of victory in favour of the Ganga, Siva, besides Gautama- the great sage, adoring them with respect at the same time.

Thereafter all the gods including Brahma and Visnu, feeling delighted eulogised them with hands folded lowering their heads.

Both Ganga and Siva were pleased with them and they said to them, “O Excellent gods, you ask for the boon, which shall be granted by us for the welfare of all.

The gods said, “O Siva and Ganga, the best of the rivers, in case both of you are pleased, then you stay here for the benefit of the people.

Ganga said, “Why don’t all of you stay here for the benefit of all. I shall return after purifying the sage Gautama.

O Gods, I can stay here, in case you give me special honour and extend me a special treatment. In case you accept my words only then I shall stay here and not otherwise.”

All the gods said, “When the Jupiter, the most friendly to all, comes to the zodiac of Leo, then all of us will arrive here. There is no doubt about it.

O Leading river, we will ourselves become unclean, by washing out the sins of the people for eleven years. O Beloved, O Great goddess, we shall come to you for cleaning ourselves in every respect. We speak out this truth with great respect.

In order to shower your grace over the people, O auspicious river, and to do something which pleases us, Siva shall also stay here with you.

We shall stay here as long as the Jupiter is in Leo. \\ye shall bathe here thrice daily and also visit Siva. Then we shall get sins washed out and seeking permission from you shall return to our respective abodes.”

Suta said, “Thus at the request of the gods as well as the sage Gautama, Ganga and Siva established themselves there.

Then Ganga came to be known by the name of Gautami, while the Sivalinga was known by the name of Tryambakesvara. Both of them wash out the grave sins.

Since that date, at the time of Jupiter’s entry into the zodiac Leo, all the tirthas, ksetras, and the gods visit the place.

The places of pilgrimage like Puskara and the rivers like Ganga and others besides the gods like Visnu and others arrive at the bank of the river Gautami. While they stay there, they are deprived of the sanctity of their original places, which they get back on their return to their respective abodes.

The Jyotirlinga there is known by the name of Tryambakesvara, which is stationed at the bank of the river Gautami and destroys the grave sins.

One who has a look at the Tryambakesvara Jyotirlinga with devotion, and adores it with great reverence, after worshipping it, is freed from all the sins.

The same Tryambakesvara Jyotirlinga was adored by Gautama. By adoring it yields all the desires in this world while bestowing salvation after death.

O Great sages, in this way, I have narrated, whatever had been asked to me. What else do you want to listen further? I shall speak out the same to you. You should have no doubt in your mind in this regard.

## Chapter 27 - Humiliation of the ascetics envious to Gautama- curse of Gautama on them

The Rsis said, “O Lord, where from did the Ganga originate in the form of water and where did she achieve greatness? You please tell us.

The wicked Brahmanas who caused pain to the sage Gautama, what happened to them, O Sage Vyasa, afterwards?

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, listening to the prayer of the sage Gautama at that time, Ganga atonce originated from Brahmagiri.

The flow of Ganga started from the udumbara branches and Gautama- the well known sage took his bath in the same.

All the great ascetics as well as the disciples of the sage Gautama, took their bath delightfully in the sacred water of the Ganga.

The place is known as Gangadvara. O Excellent sage, that attractive place washes out all the sins.

The ascetics who had been inimical to Gautama, arrived there for taking bath. At the sight of those sages, the Ganga disappeared.

Then the sage Gautama with folded hands and lowering his head, prayed to Ganga, not to disappear like that.

The sage Gautama said, “These ascetics have been blinded with arrogance, irrespective of their being good or evil, you kindly appear before them because of my auspicious merits.

Suta said- Then the voice of Ganga was heard from the sky. “O Excellent sage, listen to the excellent words of Ganga.

These ascetics are extremely wicked, are ungrateful, and can betray their lord. They are wicked and deceitful. No one should look at them.”

The sage Gautama said- O Mother, you kindly listen, the words of the great lord, which should be made truthful by you.

The lord has said, that “I get sanctified by the person, who helps those who harm him in this world.”

Suta said-On hearing the words of the sage Gautama, the supreme soul, the voice rose again from above Ganga.

“O Sage Gautama, the words spoken by you are true and auspicious. Still, let them perform the repentance for their sins.

At your command, let all of them circumambulate this mountain a hundred and one times.

These wicked ascetics would be entitled to have a look at me only thereafter. I have spoke this truthfully.”

Thus listening to the words of Ganga those sages spoke to Ganga. “You kindly forgive us for our fault.” Thereafter they performed the repentance.

After the performing of the repentance by the sages the sage Gautama gave the lower part of Gangadvara, as kusavarta at the instance of Ganga.

The river Ganga appeared there again in order to please the sage Gautama. Since that date the place was known by the name ol Kusavarta.

A person who takes a bath there, is relieved of all the sins, achieves the inaccessible knowledge and then becomes entitled to achieving of moksa.

Gautama and other ascetics, becoming shameful of their wickedness met with one another.

The Rsis said, “O Suta, we had heard this story contrary to the one spoken by you. We narrate the same. (According to the second version of the story, the sage Gautama had pronounced a curse on the Rsis.) It should be understood like this.

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, that is also true, because it happened in a different kalpa. O Ascetics, I shall narrate that story as well.

Gautama finding the ascetics distressed by the famine, performed sever tapas for god Varuna.

Because of the illusion of Varuna, they got perennial supply of water there. Thereafter he made them sow enough of food grains and barley.

O Excellent sages, the sage Gautama thus did good to others. With the strength of his tapas the sage arranged for their food.

Sometimes, the wicked wives of the sages, were insulted by someone. In turn those wicked women spoke some uncharitable words against Gautama to their husbands.

Thereafter the evil-minded ascetic made an artificial cow and it started grazing the fields of the sage Gautama.

Gautama the great sage, finding his field being grazed by the cow, while driving it out beat it.

The cow with the mere touch of the blade of grass fell down on the ground. O Sages, as luck would have it, the cow died at once.

The evil-minded sages dwelling at that place collected there and announced the killing of the cow by Gautama.

At the death of the cow, Gautama, the devotee of Siva, felt surprised with his wife and the disciples.

Soon he realised the truth about the cow and getting enraged, he pronounced a curse on the ages.

Gautama said, “All of you are evil-minded and always cause pain to me- a devotee of Siva. Therefore you will become averse to the Vedas.

From today onwards, you will never be interested in the Vedic path, which bestows salvation or the path of Siva.

From today onwards you will have no faith in the path of the Vedas, or the path of moksa. On the other hand, you will follow the evil path.

From today onwards, your foreheads would be adorned with mud or dust. O Brahmanas, with the use of the dust, all of you will proceed to the hell.

Henceforth, you would no more be devoted to Siva. You would consider the worship of Siva like the worship of other gods.

You would no more be interested in the adoration of Siva or the rites connected therewith, or the devotees of Siva, or the days of the festivities auspicious to Siva.

Whatever painful curses have been pronounced by me today, they would be applicable to your off-shoots as well.

O Brahmanas, your sons and grandsons, shall never be devoted to Siva and shall proceed to the hell.

Thereafter, all of you becoming Candalas, will suffer from poverty and pain. You will be wicked, back biters, denouncers of others and march with red hot seals.”

Suta said, “Thus Gautama, pronouncing curses on all the sages, returned to his asrama. The same Gautama was purified with the devotion of Siva.

Then the cursed Brahmanas, having been ex-communicated from Siva-dharma, started living at Kanci.

their sons became averse to the following of Siva’s religion. Their future generations in the age of Kali, would also be wicked. O Excellent sages, thus I have spoken about that episode. The earlier story has already been heard by you with respect.

Thus the origin of the Gautami-Ganga, has been narrated by me. Its glory is also destroyer of all the sins.

I have also narrated the glory of the Tryambakesvara Jyotirlinga to you, on hearing of which a person is freed of all the sins. There is no doubt it.

Now I shall narrate the glory of the Vaidyanatha Jyotirlinga which removes all the sins, which you should listen.

## Chapter 28 - The glory of Vaidyanathesvara Jyotirlinga

Suta said, “The arrogant Ravana, the excellent one among the Raksasas, being prestige minded, once adored lord Siva at the Kailasa mountain.

When he could not please Siva even after the lapse of long time, then he performed more severe tapas to please the lord.

Then he performed tapas over the southern peaks of the Himalaya mountain in the cluster of trees at Siddhasthana.

O Brahmanas, he dug up a pit in the earth, consecrated the fire there, besides the Sivalinga close by. Then he kept on performing the homa there.

In the summer season, he sat with five types of fire burning around him. He sat on earth with five types of fire burning around him. He sat on earth in the rainy season, during the winter standing in water, he performed tapas of three types.

Thus he performed severe tapas. But Mahesan Siva, never gets pleased with the evil people so easily.

Thereafter Ravana becoming the noble soul, started adoring, offering each one of his heads daily.

While performing adequate worship of Siva, he cut off one of the heads daily and in this way he offered nine of his heads to Siva.

When only one of his head was left out, Siva who is well disposed towards his devotees appeared before him, getting delighted.

The heads which had been cut off earlier, were rejoined together appropriately, the lord bestowed on him the immense prowess as well as the desired boon.

The Raksasa, then receiving the grace of Siva in the form of the boon spoke to Siva, who bestows welfare, with folded hands, lowering his head.

Ravana, said, O Siva, you kindly be pleased. I shall carry you to Lanka. I have taken refuge with you today. You kindly fulfil my desire.”

Suta said, “When Ravana thus spoke to Siva then the lord felt disturbed in his mind and found himself lodged in a difficult situation.

Then Siva said, “O Excellent Raksasa, you better listen to my important words. You better carry Sivalinga with devotion to your abode.

When you place linga at whichever place on earth, it will get fixed there. There is no doubt about it. Therefore you may do as you like.”

Suta said, “At these words of Siva, Ravana, the king of the Raksasas, moved towards his abode carrying the linga.

On the way, because of the delusion of Siva, he developed a desire to ease himself. Then Ravana, the grandson of Pulastya, could not stop the urge.

Suddenly, he found a cowherd there and requesting him he handed over the linga to the cowherd, who was upset with weight of the linga in a moment.

Unable to carry the burden for long the cowherd placed the linga on earth. The linga made of the essence of diamonds, got fixed there. The linga could bestow all the desires and could remove the sins, with a mere look at it.

O Sage, this particular linga is known by the name of Vaidyanathesvara and is well known in the three worlds. It bestows devotion as well as salvation.

This excellent and the divine Jyotirlinga is an excellent one and removes all the sins by adoring it or having a mere look at him.

It is beneficial to all the lokas. After the fixing of the linga there, Ravana, the great Raksasa, reached his abode with the best of boons from Siva.

Hearing this, Indra having the spotless wisdom, and getting devoted to Siva, the gods an the sages thought among themselves.

O Sage, at that point of time, Brahma, Visnu and all other gods, arrived there and lovingly adored Siva.

The gods found the deity physically present there and after consecrating the image, they gave the name of Vaidyanatha. Then they bowed in reverence to the image eulogising it at the same time, after which they returned to their respective abodes.”

Rsis said, “After the consecration of the Sivalinga there and after the moving of Ravana to his abode, what happened thereafter? You kindly speak out in detail.”

Suta said, “After the return of Ravana to his abode after receiving the excellent boon and he narrated the news to his wife.

O Excellent sages, learning about the news, Indra and other gods, besides the sages, felt distressed and started talking among themselves.”

The gods and others said, “The wicked Ravana is inimical to gods, evil-minded and is a degraded one. Receiving the boons from Siva, he is sure to create trouble for us.

What should be done, where should we go. What will happen? The wicked Ravana, after gaining strength can do much harm to us.”

Thus feeling painful, Indra and other gods, besides the sages, called for Narada and becoming distressed asked him.

The gods said, “O. Excellent divine sage, you are competent to perform all the tasks, therefore you do something to remove the pain of the gods.

Ravana is quite a wicked person. No one knows about his future step. Having suffered at his hands, where shall we go?”

Narada said, “Get free from anxiety. I am going to do something. I shall work for the gods, by the grace of Siva.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking Narada went to the abode of Ravana. After he was well received there he said.

Narada said, “O Devotee of Siva, O Excellent Raksasa, O tapodhana, you are really graceful. O Ravana, I feel immensely delighted, meeting you today.

You better speak out completely the way you performed tapas for Siva.” When so asked by Narada.

Ravana said, “O Great sage, reaching Kailasa for performing penance, I performed hard tapas there for a long time.

When Siva could not be pleased, then I changed the routine. O Sage, returning from there I performed tapas then in the vrksa- khanda.

I performed tapas in five types of fires in the summer season, over the open ground during the rainy season, and in the water during the winter season. I performed three types of tapas.

O Excellent sage, thus I performed the hare tapas. Inspite of that, Siva was least pleasec with me.

Then I dug up a pit and invoked the consecrated fire in the same, besides a Parthiva-linga close to it.

Offering the fragrance, sandal paste, incense, lamp and naivedya to it, I also performed the arati for the same, adoring Siva at the same time.

Offering scents, obeisances, prayers, songs, dance, playing of the musical instruments, besides the mystic gestures of faces and fingers, were made.

O Sage, by these, as well as by several other means, based on the provisions of the scriptures, I worshipped Siva.

When inspite of my doing all these adorations, Siva failed to appear before me, then I felt miserable having been unable to reap the reward of the tapas performed by me.

Then I thought, “Disgrace to my tapas, my body and my prowess.” Then I continued homa in the burning fire, in the pit.

Thereafter, I thought, “Let me sacrifice my body in the fire altar. Then I cut off my heads and dropped them in the burning fire of the altar.

Then I cut off my nine heads and dropped them one by one in the burning fire altar purifying them, to lord Siva.

O Excellent sage, as soon as I got ready to cut off my tenth head, then lord Siva, himself appeared on the scene.

Lord Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, prevented me from cutting the tenth head, and delightfully said, “You ask for the desired boon which will be given to you.

At these words of Siva, I looked at him and offered my salutation to him with folded hands with devotion. Then I eulogised him.

Then I said to him, “In case you are pleased with me, then nothing is beyond my reach.

Getting pleased, the compassionate Siva, fulfilled all my desires saying “Be it so.”

He then rejoined all my heads like a physician with a mere cast of a benign glance at me

When this was done, my body regained its former grace. Then all the benefits were derived by me by the graces of Siva.

Then at my prayer, Siva arrived on earth and he came to be known as Baidyanathesvara in the three worlds.

With adoration and a look at this Jyotirlinga one is bestowed with devotion as well as salvation. He benefits all.

After adoring and eulogising that Jyotirlinga, especially, I have arrived here. Now I am going to conquer the three worlds.”

Suta said, “Listening to these words of Ravana, Narada- the divine sage, with his heart filled with surprise, said to Ravana smilingly.

Narada said, “O Best of the demons, I am going to speak out something which would benefit you. You should act, as I desire you to do.

Whatever has been spoken to you by Siva, not all of it would be truthful. I am giving you a beneficial advice.

What does the intoxicated Siva, not speak? All that he speaks is not always true. How could you take all his words to be true.

Therefore, you go there again, and try to uproot the Kailasa mountain for your own benefit.

In case you uproot the Kailasa mountain then you would undoubtedly be successful.

Restoring the Kailasa mountain as before, you can return comfortably here. Thereafter you can do as you like.

Suta said, “As a move of the destiny, Ravana was overpowered with delusion and treated the words of the sage Narada to be beneficial and true. Therefore, he went to Kailasa.

Reaching there he shook Kailasa mountain, as a result of which all the things lodged over the mountain were disturbed and fell down here and there.

Siva also uttered, “What is all that has happened?” Then Parvati smilingly said to Siva.
