Girija said, “You had bestowed enormous strength to a peaceful warrior you have got a good reward for making a good person as your disciple.”

Suta said, “Listening to the meaningful words of Parvati, Siva pronounced a curse on the arrogant and ungrateful Ravana.

Mahadeva said, “O Evil-minded, degraded, Ravana- a devotee, don’t be proud. Soon a person who would remove the arrogance of the strength of your arms, would be born on earth.”

Suta said, “Thus Narada, heard about the happenings as Kailasa”. Ravana on the other hand delightfully returned to his abode.

Then Ravana, who was himself proud of his strength and who shattered the pride of others, then conquered the entire world.

By the grace of Siva, Ravana, who had procured the divine weapons were unparalleled in the world.

Thus I have narrated the greatness of Vaidyanathesvara, by listening to which, all the sins get destroyed.

## Chapter 29 - Disturbance created by the Raksasas of Darukavana

Suta said, “Now I shall describe in detail about Nagesvara Jyotirlinga which has been conceived to be the best.

There was a demoness named Daruka and her husband was known as the powerful Daruka. The demoness had become quite proud because of her getting a boon from Parvati.

Daruka on the other hand, killed several of the noble people in the company of the other Raksasas, obstructing the performance of the yajnas and other religious activities.

He had a gigantic and vast forest over the western coast of the ocean, which had been spread over an area of sixteen yojanas (or sixty four miles).

The demoness Daruka wherever she went for roaming about in the forest, for the purpose of sporting, the land in that spot acquired all the requisites and was filled with trees.

The supervision of the forest had been entrusted to Daruka by the goddess. She visited the forest only casually alongwith her husband.

Staying there, the demon Daruka and his wife terrorised the people.

The terrorised people because of the fear of the demon, went to the sage Aurava to take refuge with him. Bowing in reverence to him, they prayed to him, lowering their heads.

The people said, “O Great sage, you are competent to do everything. You illumine with your own lustre. You kindly protect us, otherwise the wicked demon would surely kill us all.

There is no other protector for us on earth, taking refuge with whom we could be comfortable.

At your mere sight, all the demons flee out of fear. The burning flames of Siva always remain enshrined in you.”

Suta said, “The excellent sage Aurava, when so eulogised by the people, thought over and assured protection to them.

The sage Aurava said, “In case the demons try to kill the people of earth they would themselves be killed inspite of their being quite strong.

Wherever the people are killed, the Raksasa too would die. I am speaking the trutl to you.”

Suta said, “Thus assuring the people, who had taken refuge with the sage, who was well disposed towards his devotees, he performed tapas for the welfare of the people.

Then the gods, coming to know of the cause of the curse, thought of waging the war with the Raksasas.

Indra and other gods, making all the preparations collected, carrying all the weapons.

Finding that the gods were preparing for the war, all the wicked demons collected there and made consultations with one an other.”

The Raksasas said, “What should be done? Where should we go? We are facing a terrific situation. In case of fighting, we perish and in case we don’t do so, even then our destruction is imminent.

In case we stay as we are, then what shall we eat? Thus we have been placed in a difficult situation. Who can prevent it?”

Suta said, “Thus thinking, Daruka and other demons, when could not find any escape, then they felt miserable.

Apprehending the calamity, when observed by the demoness Daruka, then she said, “I have received a boon from Parvati.”

Daruka said, “In earlier times, I had performed tapas for Parvati, who had bestowed a boon on me that I could carry the forest with demons anywhere I liked.

When this boon has been received by me, then why are you feeling miserable. You remain with me with water and the forest.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the demoness, all the demons were pleased. Becoming fearless, the demons spoke among themselves.

The queen Daruka is quite graceful and successful, she has made us regain our lives. All the demons then offered their salutation to her and spoke to her.”

In case we can go, let us go. Why to think over this? O Gentle lady, we shall go and stay there permanently in the waters.

In the meantime, the people together with the gods arrived there for waging of the war, who had been tortured by the demons earlier.

Taking advantage of the boon of Parvati, the demoness, moved on with land and the water as a whole.

She adored the goddess shouting the slogans of victory. The demoness then started flying like Himalaya.

Daruka who was devoted to Parvati, accompanied with all her family besides the kiths and kins, lodged herself in the ocean, and became comfortable there.

The demons lived beneath the oceanic waters and then started roaming about comfortably.

Since that time the demons never returned on earth feeling terrified from the curse of the sage. They kept on roaming about over the surface of the water.

Thereafter, the demons made the sailors captive and lodged then in the jails beneath the water, occasionally killing some of them.

With the influence of the boon of Parvati, staying there fearlessly, the demons created havoc as before.

O Excellent sages, the people then felt terrorised in the water as they were earlier terrorised on earth.

Sometimes the demoness, getting out of the city, entered the oceanic waters and in order to torture the people, she obstructed the path between the earth and the water.

In the meantime, several beautiful boats arrived in which the people had boarded.

The demons felt delighted with the arrival of boats filled with humans. The demons entered the boats and started capturing the humans.

The valorous demons, making the humans captive brought them to their own city and imprisoned them binding them with fetters and hand cuffs.

Thereafter the humans, having been captivated with fetters, were humiliated by the enemies again and again. They felt miserable.

Their master was known as Supriya, who was a noble soul, besides being the devotee of Siva, following the Saiva faith.

He could never miss the adoration of Siva. He always applied ashes over his body and Rudraksa-rosary around his neck.

At times when he perchance failed to worship Siva, then he took no food on that particular day. Therefore, he (in bondage) also worshipped Siva.

O Ascetics, reaching the jail, he educated many people. He also explained to others the use of Siva-mantra and the method of adoring the Parthiva-linga.

All of them also started the worship of Siva, which fulfilled all the desires, in the same way as they had found and observed.

Some of them were seated in excellent postures, while some of them were mentally adoring Siva with delight.

O Excellent sages, their lord performed t worship appropriately according to Parthiv pUjana.

Such of the people who were unaware of the method of adoration, they simply remembered Siva, while others recited the mantra Oḍ namah Sivaya.

Supriya, the devotee of Siva was a Vaisya who performed the worship of Siva appropriately.

The form in which Supriya had adored Siva, the lord appeared before him in the same form. Supriya was unaware of the fact that his prasada had then been accepted by Siva.

O Excellent sages, thus adoring Siva, by the Vaisya, six months passed by without hindrance.

O Excellent Rsis, now you listen to the event thereafter, the story of the moon-crested lord.

## Chapter 30 - Greatness of Nagesvara Jyotirlinga

Suta said, “Once, the servant of the wicked demon witnessed the beautiful form of Siva in front of him.

He explained the true form of Siva as seen by him to the king of the demons which surprised the demon. He also narrated to him the astonishing story of Siva.

Feeling disturbed the demon king Daruka reaching before Vaisya enquired about Siva, getting upset.

Daruka said, “O Vaisya for whom, are you meditating upon? You tell me truthfully in case you intend to save your life, otherwise you are sure to be killed.”

Suta said, “The Vaisya replied, “I know nothing.” On hearing this the demon was infuriated and he spoke to the Raksasas, “You kill him.”

At the command of the demon, the Raksasas, arrived carrying arms in order to kill the Vais'ya.

Finding the arrival of the demons, the Vaisya closed his eyes and started reciting the names of Siva, meditating upon him.

The lord of Vaisyas said, “O Sankara, O Lord of the gods, O Sambhu, O Siva, destroyer of the wicked people, well disposed towards your devotees, lord of the three worlds, you kindly save me from the wicked demon.

O Lord, “You are all in all for me today. O Lord, I am subservient to you. You are always the protector of my life.”

Suta said, “At this prayer of Vaisya in favour of Siva, the lord appeared from a pit in a building having four doors.

In the meantime, Siva- the form of flame appeared with his family there. Witnessing the astonishing form of Siva, the Vaisya adored him.

With the worship of the Vais'ya, lord Siva was pleased, lord Siva, gave the Pasupata weapon, using which the Vaisya, killed all the Raksasas, destroying all the weapons with them. Thus lord Siva, the destroyer of the wicked people, saved his devotee.

After killing all of them, Siva the creator of the astonishing events and who assumes several bodies, during the course of his sports, granted a boon to the forest.”

The people of all the four castes viz. Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras, shall always flourish in this forest.

There would be no people here with tamasika qualities. The excellent sages, the propounders and devotees of Siva, following the Saiva faith will live here.”

In the meantime, the demoness Daruka eulogised goddess Parvati in her mind.

The goddess was pleased and she asked her, “What shall I do for you?” The demoness replied, “Let my race be protected by you.

Parvati said, “I shall protect your race. This is the truth that has been spoken to you.” Thus speaking the goddess Parvati had a quarrel with Siva.

Siva, because of his boon lovingly looked at Parvati and said, “You do whatever you like.”

Thus listening to the words of her husband, Parvati was pleased and she smilingly said.

Parvati said, “Your words would become true at the end of the present yuga. Then there would be the tamasik creation according to my opinion.

Otherwise, O Siva there would be a dissolution. I am speaking the truth, O Lord, you kindly take it for granted. I live in your asrama and belong to you.

The demoness Daruka is in fact my own - Sakti. She is the most powerful of all the demonesses and as such, she would rule over the demons. She would produce her sons from the wombs of other demonesses, who would live in this forest at my command, collectively.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words O Parvati, his spouse, lord Siva delightfully spoke to her.

Siva said, “O Beloved one, because of these words, just spoken by you, you listen to what have I to say in this regard. I shall lovingly stay in this forest for the protection of my devotees.

Whosoever will follow the varnas'rama dharma while living here and shall have an audience with me, with devotion, he would become a Cakravarti emperor in the universe.

Otherwise at the end of Kaliyuga and the start of Satyayuga, there would be a powerful king named Virasena, having a vast army.

Becoming great with my strength, he would become a Cakravarti emperor because of his devotion in me.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, thus talking between themselves, both the husband and wife, started joyfully sporting.

Then Siva was transformed as Jyotirlinga, while Siva (Parvati) became popular as Nagesvarl.

The Rsis said, “O Intelligent one, how7 will Vlrasiva go to Daruka-vana and worship Siva. You please tell me.

In the beautiful country of Nisodra, Mahasena was bom as the son, in the race of the Rsis.

Virasena made a Parthiva-linga and adored it for twelve years, performing tapas at the same time.

Then Siva the lord of the gods was pleased and he said, “Make a fish like image of wood, coat it with tin and other metal. O Virasena, then I shall create Yogamaya and give it to you and your men. Thereafter you proceed to the island in the western ocean and enter crevice made by me and worship Nagesvara. Then secure the weapon Pasupata and slay the demoness and others. When I appear before you, there would be no shortage of any sort with you.

By that time the strength provided by Parvati to the people there would get exhausted. The Mlecchas living in the forest would turn to noble ways.”

Siva, who removes the sufferings of all, thus speaking to the king Virasena, showering his enormous grace on the king, disappeared from the scene.

Thus showering a boon on the king Virasena by Siva, he became all powerful.

In this way the jyotirlinga Nagesvara was originated, which fulfills all the desires of the people.

Whosoever listens to the origin of Nagesvara Jyotirlinga, he is relieved of all the sins and is also relieved of grave sins, getting all his desires fulfilled.

## Chapter 31 - Origin of Ramesvara Jyotirlinga

Suta said, “O Sages, hereafter, I shall narrate the origin of Ramesvara Jyotirlinga, which you please listen with respect.

In earlier time, lord Visnu, who is dear to the noble people, incarnated on earth in the form of Rama.

O Brahmanas, Ravana, the wielder of great Maya, who was the ruler of Lanka, kidnapped Sita the daughter of Janaka and the wife of Rama.

Searching for her, Rama reached the city of Kiskindha. Reaching there, Rama, joining his friend Sugriva, killed Bali- his brother.

While searching for Sita, he stayed there for sometime, Sri Rama made consultations with Sugriva and Laksmana.

Then Sri Rama, the son of the king Dasaratha, sent monkeys under the leadership of Hanuman and other monkey chiefs in all the directions in search of Sita.

Lord Rama was immensely delighted after learning of the presence of Sita in Lanka from Hanuman, who also handed over her Ciidamani to Rama.

O Brahmanas, accompanied by Hanuman, Sugriva, the king of the monkeys, with Sri Rama and Laksmana marched on with monkey army, comprising of eighteen thousand billions and reached the shores of the southern salt ocean.

Reaching there, Rama, the favourite of Siva, stayed at the seashore, getting served by the monkeys and his brother Laksmana.

Sri Rama thought, O Sita, where have you gone? When shall I meet you? The vast, monkey army, is unable to cross the huge ocean.

Ravana, the uplifter of Kailasa, is immensely powerful. Lanka has an impregnable fort. Ravana’s son Indrajita is quite powerful.”

Thus thinking, he was seated over the seashore, with Laksmana. He was however, consulted and assured by the wild monkeys and the bears.

In the meantime Rama, the great devotee of Siva, asked his brother lovingly to bring auspicious water.

Sri Rama said, “O Brother Laksmana, the lord of the valorous warriors, I feel thirsty, you better get me some water through a monkey.”

Suta said, “On hearing this the monkeys rushed to all the ten directions and bringing the water, bowing in reverence to the lord Rama, they stood before him.

The monkeys said, “O Master, at your command, we have brought the excellent, tasteful and cool water which satisfies thirst and is refreshing. Please take it.”

Suta said, “On hearing this, Rama, feeling pleased, cast a compassionate look at the monkeys and took the water.

As soon as Rama, the devotee of Siva, was about to drink the water, then because of the will of Siva, he was reminded of something.

He thought, “How is it that I am drinking water, without having a look at lord Siva, who is bestower of all the bliss?”

Thus speaking the lord of the race of Raghu, took the water. Thereafter he made a Parthiva-linga and adored it.

He worshipped Siva with all the sixteen types of ancillary services like invocation etc. and with devotion according to the established practice.

After propitiating him with devotion, offering divine prayers, quite strenuously, Rama joyfully prayed to Siva, with utmost devotion.

Rama said, “O Siva, O Mahadeva, well disposed towards your devotees, I, with a pitiable mind take refuge with you. Therefore, you kindly protect me.

You make the universe to cross the water of the ocean which is beyond measure. Ravana- the enemy is quite powerful.

The strength of these unstable monkeys is my only strength. Let my aim of getting back my wife be established.

O Lord of good rites, you help me in this task, without your help, the task would be beyond our reach.

Your (devotee) Ravana is also infallible by others. By achieving the boons from you, he has become arrogant and proud. The valorous Ravana, is the conqueror of the three worlds.

I also happen to be your slave and I solely depend on you in all respects. O Siva, thus thinking you kindly bestow your favour on me.”

Suta said, “Thus offering prayer to Siva, Rama bowed in reverence to Siva again and again and said, “O Lord Siva, let you be always be victorious.”

Thus adoring Siva, reciting the mantras, and meditating upon him, he adored him again and again, dancing before the lord at the same time.

With his hearts overwhelmed with devotional love, he produced the throat sound. Lord Siva was extremely delighted with this.

Lord Siva, of brilliant form along with all his ganas, then appeared before Rama immediately.

Having been pleased with the devotion of Rama, Siva said, “Let you meet with welfare. O Rama, you better ask for a boon.

Finding Siva in that form, all those present there, got purified. Thereafter Rama, who was devoted to Siva, adored the lord.

Then Rama, eulogising Siva variously, offering his salutation to him, prayed for his victory over Ravana in the battle-field.

Observing the devotion of Rama, Siva with a delightful heart, said, “O Great king, let you be victorious.

Thereafter Rama, receiving the boon from Siva for victory, at his command, he again folded his hands and lowering his head prayed to him.

Sri Rama said, “O Master, O Siva, in case you are pleased with me then you kindly reside in this linga for the purification and welfare of the people.”

Suta said, “At these words of Sri Rama, Siva transformed himself into a linga and came to be known as Ramesvara on earth.

By the grace of Siva, Rama expeditiously crossed the ocean, killing Ravana and other Raksasas, them got back Sita his wife.

Since that date the glory of Ramesvara linga became wide-spread in the world. This linga fulfills the desires of all the devotees, besides the bestower of devotion and salvation.

Whosoever would adore Ramesvara linga with the water of Ganga daily, he becomes the liberated soul while living on earth.

He enjoys all the pleasures in this world which are beyond the reach of even the gods, and ultimately achieving the divine knowledge, surely attains moksa.

Thus I have narrated the glory of Ramesvara Sivalinga which removes all the sins. What more do you want to listen from me.

## Chapter 32 - The story of Ghusamesvara- the twelfth Jyotirlinga

Suta said, “O Excellent sages, after this, you listen to the glory of Ghusmesvara Jyotirlinga.

There is an excellent mountain Devagiri in the northern region which it looks quite charming.

Close to that, there lives a Brahmana, born in Bhardvaja race, known by the name of Sudharma and who was well-versed in all the four Vedas.

His wife named Sudeha was immensely devoted to Siva. She was also devoted to her husband and was well-versed in her household duties.

The Brahmana Sudharma, performed the homas prescribed in the Vedas, besides worshipping the gods and the guests.

He performed Sandhya thrice a day, was illustrious like the sun, well-read in the Vedic and post-Vedic literature and taught his pupils well.

He was wealthy and the abode of nobility, was always engaged in the adoration of Siva. He was devoted to Siva besides being the favourite of the devotees of Siva.

After following dhama for a long time, he was not blessed with a son. Because of that the menstruation period of his wife always remained fruitless.

Inspite of that, having realised about the reality of things, he did not grieve over this. He was aware of the fact that soul is the uplifter of the soul and the soul is the sanctifier of the soul at the same time.

Thus thinking he remained free from mental grief. But Sudeha, his wife felt distressed for being unable to produce a son.

Everyday she implored her learned husband to strive for the acquisition of a son.

He reproached his wife saying, “What shall your son do? Who is the mother? Who is the father? Who are the kins, father, son and the relatives?

O Goddess, all of them serve the selfish purpose in all the three lokas. There is no doubt about it. Thus thinking, using your wisdom, don’t feel sorrowful.

O Chaste lady, misery shall be eschewed by you, certainly. You shall not pester me like this everyday.”

Thus consoling her, he engaged himself in the adoration of the lord, forgetting about the pain of the man and a woman, he was extremely peaceful and contented.

Once Sudeha, went with her maids to the abode of her neighbour, where the marriage was being performed.

There, Sudharma’s wife was rebuked by the ladies of the neighbourhood calling her as a neutral woman. At these words, Sudeha felt painful at heart.

The neighbouring women said, “O Sonless woman, why are you arrogant? I am the mother of a son who would inherit my wealth, but you have none to inherit your riches.

Of course the king will surely confiscate your entire property. You are a barren woman, disgrace to you, your wealth, your honour as well as your prestige.”

Suta said, “Having been thus scolded by her neighbour, she was depressed and she returned home. Then she narrated to her husband all that happened in the neighborhood and the harsh words spoken by the ladies there.

The intelligent Brahmana remained unmoved with the incident on hearing the same. He said, “Let her speak as she likes. O Beloved, whatever is destined to happen shall happen.”

The Brahmana thus pacified and reassured his wife again and again, as a result of which she was free of worries. But she again spoke to her husband.”

Sudeha said, “You are my husband an\< you will beget a son some how. O Excellen among the humans, otherwise, I shall end nr life.”

Suta said, “On hearing the words of his wife, Sudharma, the excellent Brahmana, because of the persistent demands of his wife for a son, devoted his mind to Siva.

The conscious Brahmana then offered two flowers in the sacrificial fire, thinking in his mind that the right side flower would yield a son.

With this resolve, the Brahmana told his wife. You shall take one of these two flowers to decide about your getting a son.

She thought, “I shall surely have a son. Let the insignia flower come to me.” Then she bowed in reverence to Siva and the yajna- fire.” After eulogising again, she picked up one of the two flowers.

The insignia flower was missed by her due to delusion caused by the desire of Siva.

Observing this, the husband had a deep sigh. Devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, the Brahmana spoke to his wife

Sudharma said, “O Beloved, how could anything happen against the will of the lord? Shed away your false hope and serve the lord with devotion.”

After saying this, and he feeling defeated the Brahmana engaged himself in the performing of the sacrificial rites, meditating upon Siva at the same time.

But desirous of getting a son, Sudeha did not discard her desire for having a son. Folding her hands in reverence, and bending her head, she lovingly spoke to her husband.

Sudeha said, “Let me have no son bom to me. At my request you take another wife, who would surely bear a son to you.”

Suta said, “At this prayer of his beloved wife, the Brahmana, who had been an excellent devotee of Siva, and fond of performing the sacred rites, said to her.”

Sudharma said, our miseries are over, do not create obstacles in my religious performance now.”

Suta said, “Although, the husband thus prevented her from doing so, but she atonce brought the younger daughter of her mother (sister) and asked her husband to take her.

Sudharma said, “Now you declare her to be my beloved wife. But the moment she gives birth to a son, you would become jealous of her.”

Suta said, “At this warning of her husband, Sudeha, folded her hands in reverence and spoke to him.

“O Excellent Brahmana, I shall never be jealous of my own sister. You may marry her and beget a son. I insist on this.”

At the insistence of his wife, the Brahmana Sudharma, married the girl Ghusma with all the due ceremonies.

After the marriage was performed the Brahmana requested Sudeha, “O Auspicious beloved, she is your younger sister, therefore you should bring her up.”

Thus speaking, Sudharma, the most excellent devotee of Siva, continued to perform the sacred rites as before.

Sudeha, on the other hand served her sister like a slave, shedding away all the jealousy and opposition, quite lovingly.

The younger wife with the approval of his sister, made hundred and one lingas of Siva daily.

According to the auspicious religious provisions, Ghusma, rendered devotional worship to these lingas and consigned them daily in the lake nearby.

In this way she performed the wish- fulfilling adoration of Siva daily making them and then consigning them in the nearby lake as per the existing tradition with devotion.

Thus performing the worship of Siva regularly she completed the adoration of a hundred thousand lingas, which could yield the benefits of all the desires.

By the grace of Siva, a son was bom to her, who was quite beautiful, fortunate, and possessed all the auspicious virtues.

He possessed the divine knowledge and followed the dharma. The Brahmana, inspite of his being unattached, felt extremely delighted.

Since then Sudeha, became envious of her. Earlier her heart was quite cool and then it became blazing like the fire.

Since then Sudeha, became envious of her. Earlier her heart was quite cool and then it became blazing like the fire. Thereafter the painful event that occurred, you listen to it, O Sages with an attentive mind.

## Chapter 33 - Regaining of life of the Son of Ghusma by Siva’s grace and establishment of Ghusamesvara Sivalinga

Suta said, “The elder sister felt painful at the birth of a son to the younger sister and she could not tolerate the delight of her younger sister. She therefore started opposing the younger sister.

All the people praised the birth of the son, but she was unable to tolerate the felicitations received by her due to birth of a son to her sister.

The child happened to be the abode of the auspicious virtues of his parents, but her heart started burning like the fire flames.

After a few days, a Brahmana arrived there in order to give his daughter to the son in marriage and the father of the boy appropriately married the boy with the girl.

Sudharma was quite happy with his second wife Ghusma and because of this, all the relatives, honoured Ghus'ma, enormously.

In fact Sudeha felt burning in heart by observing her sister Ghusma. She felt that she was quite unfortunate and thus remained defeated.

Reaching his abode, the Brahmanas finding his son and the bride- just married, felt delighted and encouraged them.

Ghusma too was pleased but Sudeha felt painful. Being unable to absorb the pleasure, she fell down on earth.

But Ghusmii said, “Both the boy and the bride belong to you. The son and the bride take you as the mother and the mother-in-law respectively.”

The amount of the honour the husband gave to the elder wife, was not given to the younger one. Still the elder wife became deceitful at heart.

Once the senior wife Sudeha, extremely distressed, thought in her mind, “How could my mind be at peace.”

Sudeha said, “The flames burning in my heart could subside with the tears of Ghusma and not otherwise. This is true.

Therefore, I shall kill her son having the loving speech. This is my firm resolve. Whatever would happen thereafter, let it happen.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, the inimical nature among the co-wives is extremely ruthless and suicidal. The wicked people dc not bother as to what is to be done and wha1 not.

Once during the night, as the son was sleeping with his wife, she took out a big knife and cut off his limbs.

Thus the elder wife cut off the limbs ol Ghusma’s son, during the night. Since she was quite strong, she carried the limbs to the lake, where the earthen lingas of Siva were daily consigned into the water by Ghusma. After consigning the son’s limbs in the lake water, she returned home and slept.

Ghusma got up early in the morning and busied herself in the household jobs with delight. Sudharma was also engaged in the routine business.

Sudeha also, after having the burning of her heart subsided, started attending to the daily routine of the household.

When the bride got up in the morning, she found the bed was soaked in blood. She also found the pieces of flesh there. She therefore felt painful.

Then she asked her mother-in-law, “Where has your son gone? The bed is soaked in blood and the limbs of the body can be found there.

The bride who was fond of her husband, started lamenting, “Oh, I am doomed. O My mother of holy rites, who has committed this heinous crime?”

The senior wife, though was internally delighted, but outwardly displayed the pitiable condition, saying, “Oh, I am doomed.

Ghusma, heard the miserable lamentation of the bride, but did not discard the performing of the sacred rites, besides the daily adoration of Siva in the form of earthen lingas.

Her mind was free from disturbance. The husband also did not shed away his calm, till the completion of the daily worship.

The worship of Siva was ended at noon, then she looked at the terrible bed but inspite of that Ghus'ma did not feel painful at all.

She uttered, “The one who has given the boy shall protect him too. He is the destroyer of Kala, the goal of the noble people. He is well known as the favourite of his devotees. He is ours protector, the sole lord, and resembles a gardener. He can separate those who are united by him. What shall I gain by worrying over (the death of the son)? Thus realising the truth and getting enthusiastic in dedicating herself to Siva, she did not grieve much.

Carrying the earthen lingas she proceeded towards the bank of the lake, reciting Siva’s name. She kept herself well-composed as usual.

When the earthen lingas were consigned by her, thereafter she found her son standing on the bank of the lake.

The son said, “I would like to see my mother. After my death, I have been brought back to life by lord Siva because of the grace of my mother and the grace of lord Siva.”

Suta said, “O Brahmanas, finding that her son had been brought back to life, the mother did not feel so delightful, since she did not feel so painful even at his death earlier.

Lord Siva appeared before her at the same time in the form of a mass of lustre who spoke to her delightfully.

Lord Siva said, “O Lady with a beautiful face, I am pleased with you. You better ask for the boon you desire. The boy had been killed by the wicked woman, who is going to be killed with my trident.”

Suta said, “Ghusma bowed in reverence to Siva and prayed to him for the boon saying, “O Lord, you save my sister Sudeha.”

Siva said, “Sudeha did immense harm to you, then why should you save her. Since she indulged in the evil deeds, she deserves to be killed.

Ghusma said, “At your auspicious sight all the sins disappear and as such after having an audience with you all her sins have been reduced to ashes.

In fact the sins are washed out at the mere look at a person who helps those who harm him.

These are the wonderful words spoken by the lord himself, which have been heard by me. Therefore O Lord Sadasiva, let these words not be falsified.

Suta said, “At the request of Ghusma, lord Siva, who happens to be the ocean of compassion and favourably disposed towards his devotees, was immensely pleased with his devotee and with delight spoke to her.”

Siva said, “O Ghusma, you better ask for another boon that could be beneficial to you which will be granted by me. I am immensely please with your devotion and your nature of being free from attachment.” Suta said, “Hearing these words of Siva Ghusma said, “In case the lord is desirous of granting a boon to me, then you stay here in my name, for the protection of the universe.”

At this Siva felt delighted and he said, “I shall be lodged here in your name and shall be known as Ghusmesvara in order to bestow comforts over the people.

The Sivalinga of mine shall be known as Ghusmesvara besides being sacred and famous. This lake too (would be auspicious as well) being the store house of the Sivalingas for all times to come.

This place would be popular in the three worlds and shall be known as Sivalaya (the abode of Siva). This lake too will fulfil all the desires of the people at its mere sight.

O Auspicious lady, upto a hundred and one generations of your family, the illustrious sons of great excellence like this will be bom. There is no doubt about it.

They will have pleasant wives, will possess enormous wealth, long life and shall also possess skill in everything. They will be learned and liberal and shall attain all the worldly pleasures.

Upto a hundred and one generations, the sons will be endowed with many qualities. Therefore, there would be an all-round expansion of your family.

Suta said, “Thus speaking, Siva was then transformed as Ghusmesa linga and the lake came to be known as Sivalaya.

Then Ghusma, Sudeha and Sudharma arrived there and circumambulated Siva a hundred and one times.

Thereafter adoring Siva, getting relieved of the pollution of the mind, they moved collectively feeling comfortable.

O Excellent sages, this is story of the emerging of Ghusmes'vara Jyotirlinga. By looking at it or adoring it, there is an increase in the human comforts.

Sudeha felt ashamed finding the son became alive. O Brahmanas, then she begged forgiveness from both the husband and wife and she performed vrata in order to rid herself of the sin.

Thus I have discussed about the importance of twelve Jyotirlingas. All of them fulfil all the desires besides bestowing the devotion as well as the salvation.

Whosoever will read or listen to the story of these Jyotirlingas, he would be relieve of all the sins and achieve devotion as well as the salvation.

Once the demons became more powerful than the gods and they started troubling all the lokas, making the dharma to disappear from the earth.

## Chapter 34 - Siva bestows Sudarsana Cakra to Visnu

Vyasa said, “Listening to the words of Suta, the excellent sages praising him said to him.

The Rsis said, “O Suta, you are omniscient, therefore we ask you. O Lord, you kindly speak out the glory of Haridvara lingo..

It is said that lord Visnu had received Sudarsana, by adoring Haridvara linga. O Dear one, you therefore, kindly narrate the relevant story.” Suta said, “O Sages, you listen to the auspicious story of Harisvara, by which Vi§nu had received Sudarsana cakra from Siva.

Once the demons became more powerful than the gods and they started troubling all the *lokas,* making the *dharma* to disappear from the earth.

The strong and valorous demons when so troubled the gods, the latter went to lord Visnu, the protector of the gods, for rescue and narrated to him the tale of their sufferings.

The gods said, “O Lord we have been tortured by the demons. Be graceful on us. Where should we go? You are the protector of all and therefore we have approached you.”

Suta said, “With the words spoken by the gods, feeling miserable, Visnu, devoting his mind at the feet of Siva, spoke to them.”

Visnu said, “O Gods, I shall perform your job, after adoring Siva. The enemies are quite powerful and they have to be conquered making all the efforts.

Suta said, “At these words of the all powerful Visnu, the gods, thinking the demons having been dead, returned to their respective abodes.

Then lord Visnu, meditated upon the eternal Siva- the witness of all, besides being the lord of all, for the victory of the gods.

Reaching close to Kailasa, Visnu made an altar in the front, consecrated the fire and himself performed the tap as.

According to the procedure for performing the ParthivapUja, he recited several mantras and strotras. Visnu then adored Siva.

O Excellent sages, Visnu performed the worship of Siva, making a seat from the lotuses of the Manasarovara lake.

Visnu resolved then that till such time, Siva is pleased with me, I shall remain seated over this seat.” With this resolve, Visnu adored Siva.

O Brahmanas, when Siva was not pleased with Visnu, then he thought in his mind anxiously.

Thus thinking in his mind, he adored Siva, variously, but the sportive Siva, even then was not pleased.

Then Visnu feeling surprised having been filled with utmost devotion, offered prayer to the lord reciting a thousand names for him.

Reciting the name of Siva- who is well disposed towards those who take refuge in him, Visnu, reciting every name, adored Siva, with the offering of a lotus flower.

In order to test the devotion of Visnu, one of the thousand flowers was taken away by Siva (stealthily).

The wonderful Ṅīóṁ of Siva remained invisible to Visnu. But when he found a lotus flower missing, he started search for the same.

Visnu roamed over the earth in search of the lotus flower, quickly maintaining his sacred fire. When he was unable to find the lotus flower he was about to offer one of his eyes in place of lotus (since he was known to have the lotus eyes).

Observing this, Siva, who happens to be the destroyer of the miseries was pleased and he appeared before Visnu and addressed him thus.

Siva said, “O Visnu, I am pleased with you. You ask for the desired boon, which will be given to you. I can grant you everything.”

Suta said, “At these words of Siva, Visnu feeling delightful said, with folded hands in reverence.

Visnu said, “O Lord, what shall I speak to you. You are aware of the inner feelings of all, still I speak out at your command.

O Lord, the demons have troubled the entire world. None of my weapons is able to destroy the same.

What should I do? Where should I go? There is no protector for me on earth better than you. Therefore I have arrived here to take refuge with you.”

Suta said, “Thus speaking, offering his salutation to lord Siva, feeling extremely painful, Visnu sat before Siva.

Listening to the words of lord Visnu, Siva, the lord of gods, handed over his Sudarsana Cakra shining with the mass of splendour to Visnu.

Receiving the cakra, Visnu, killed all the powerful demons without much efforts.

Then the gods were delighted and the living beings of the world became comfortable. Lord Visnu, on the other hand, after receiving the weapon, felt extremely pleased.

Rsis said, “What are the thousand names of Siva, which pleased the lord and he gave away his own cakra to Visnu.

You kindly speak out their greatness together with conversation with Siva, as a result of which Siva became compassionate on Visnu.

Vyasa said, “Listening to the words of the sages with attentive mind, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, Suta spoke.

## Chapter 36 - Reward for reciting a thousand names of Siva

Suta said, “Listening to the divine Siva-sahasrandma-stotra recited by Visnu, lord Siva was pleased.

Siva also known as Bhuvanesvara, in order to test the devotion of Visnu, concealed a lotus flower.

When a lotus flower went short of a thousand lotuses, the adoration by Visnu could not be completed. Because of this, he was upset.

Then he thought in his mind, “Where has the lotus flower gone? In case the lotus flower is lost, let it be lost. I am usually conceived to have lotus like eyes.

Thus realising, taking refuge of Sattvaguna, he took out his one eye and offered it into the worship of Siva, offering his prayer with devotion at the same time.

On finding Visnu in such a form, Siva, the preceptor of the universe, appeared on the scene and said, “Don’t do like this.”

Mahesvara incarnated on earth out of the Parthiva-linga that had been consecrated by Visnu.

Finding the resplendent Siva having appeared on earth, Visnu, who was seated in the front offered his salutation to him eulogising him at the same time.

Finding Visnu with his hands folded, the smiling Siva said, “O Hari, I have fully known the feelings of your mind. You were engaged in performing the task of the gods. Today, it was the task of the gods alone.

For the establishment ot the task ot the gods, for the destruction of the demons without much efforts, I grant you the Sudarsana-cakra.

The form which bestows welfare to all has been witnessed by you, you take it for granted, that I have taken to this form for your benefit alone.

By recalling it in the battle field, and with the reciting of my thousand names, besides the use of this cakra the gods shall be relieved of their miseries.

O Suvrata, those who will listen to the Sivasahasranama stotra, they will surely achieve the indestructible success besides the fulfilment of their desires.”

Suta said “Thus speaking Siva took out the Sudarsanacakra which emerged out of his feet, which destroyed the enemies and handed it over to Visnu.

Visnu also, facing north, accepted the sam\< from Siva. After making obeisance to Siva Visnu said.

Visnu said, “O Lord, O Lokasankara, you tell me, what should I do for the removal of miseries and what should I recite?”

Suta said, When so asked by Visnu the helper of the gods, Siva, delighted and satisfied spoke to him.”

Siva said, “O Visnu, for the removal of all the misfortunes, one should adore my form. For the removal of several miseries, one should recite my thousand names.

O Visnu for achieving success of all the desires, one should carry my excellent cakra with him, making all the efforts.

These thousand names of mine, when read or taught by others, they will never face the miseries even in dreams. There is no doubt about it.

When a king finding himself in danger shall recite this sahasramma appropriately a hundred times, he is sure to meet with welfare.

It removes the ailments, bestows lores and riches, fulfills all the desires besides bestowing the devotion of Siva and the auspicious merits.

A person when reciting it with any desire in mind, he would reap the best reward for the same. There is no doubt it. This is the excellent truth.

A person who getting up in the early morning, adores me reciting the Sivasahasranama before me, he surely achieves success in no time.

Achieving all the siddhis in this world, he ultimately achieves Sayujya salvation at the end”

Suta said, “ Siva with a delightful mind, thus spoke to Visnu and when he was so offering salutation to him, Siva again spoke.”

Siva said, “O Suvrata, O Best of the gods, I bestow a boon on you. You better ask for a desired boon. You have made me subservient to you with the reciting of this stotra and your devotion towards me.”

Suta said, “At these words of Siva, Visnu, feeling delighted spoke to him with his hands folded.

Visnu said, “O Master, O Lord, the way in which you are extending your grace on me, you may continue to do so even in future.

O Great god, O Lord, this is the excellent boon desired by me that I should remain devoted at your feet in future, in order to remove the sufferings of the devotees. I desire

Suta said, “Listening to these words of Visnu, Siva felt compassionate on him. Touching his limbs Candrasekhara Siva said to him.

Siva said, “O Visnu, you possess the unending devotion in your heart which will always continue with you. You will be adorable by all the gods and the lokas.

By my grace, O Best of the gods, henceforth, you would be known by the name of Visvambhara.

Suta said, “O Excellent sages, Siva, the lord of all the gods, then in full view of all those present there, disappeared.

Lord Visnu too, as per the command of Siva, felt delighted on receiving the auspicious cakra (discus).

Recalling the name of Siva in his mind, he kept on reciting the stotra regularly and also read out the same to his devotees.

O Brahmanas, thus the story which you had enquired of me, which destroys the sins, has been narrated by me.

## Chapter 37 - Adoration of Siva through the sages

Rsis said, “O Suvrata, O Fortunate one, you are quite learned, you repeat the story of lord Siva again exhaustively.

Did the gods, the Rsis and the ancient kings also adore the excellent lord Siva?

Suta said, “O Excellent sages, you have asked me a good question. Listen, I shall speak to you in reply thereto. Lord Siva bestows his devotion and salvation to those who listen to this beautiful story.

The same story was asked by Narada from Brahma who in turn delightfully replied to Narada.

Brahma said, “O Narada, you listen to the auspicious story of Siva, which relieves one of all the grave sins. I am going to repeat it to you lovingly.

Visnu with Laksmi had once adored Siva. Then by the grace of Siva, all their desires were fulfilled.

I (Brahma) too adore Siva. O Dear one, I get myself engaged in the work of creation by the grace of Siva alone, in the universe.

Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatkumara and others besides the great Rsis, daily adore Siva All other Rsis also adore Siva.

O Narada, you are particularly devoted to Siva. Vasistha and the Saptarsis also adore Siva.

The chaste Arundhati, Lopamudra and Ahalya- the wife of Gautama also adore Siva.

The Rsis like Durvasa, Visvamitra, Sakti, Dadhici, Gautama, Kanada, Bhargava, Brhaspati, Vaisarnpayana also were devoted to Siva. Besides the sages named Parasara and Vyasa always adored Siva.

Upamanyu had been a great devotee of Siva. Besides JaiminI, Garga and Yajnavalkya were the great devotees of Siva.

The sages like Sukasaunika and others also adored Siva. O Excellent sages, besides those many other sages also worshipped Siva.

Aditi, the mother of the gods, together with her daughter-in-law, used to worship Pdrthiva-linga.

Indra and other Lokapalas, eight Vasus, the gods, Muherajikadeva, Sadhyaganas, were all devoted to Siva.

Gandharvas, Kinnaras, semigods, also worshipped Siva. The asuras (demons) and Mahatmas (the great souls) were also devotees of Siva.

O Sage, the Daitya king Hiranyakasipu, adored Siva with his brother and the son, Virocana, the father of Bali were all the devotees of Siva.

O Dear one, Banasura was a great devotee of Siva. Vrsaparva the son of Hiranyaksa, Danu and other Danava were all the devotees of Siva.

The great serpents like Sesa, Vasuki, Taksaka, besides Garuda and other birds were also devoted to Siva.

O Excellent sages, the two gods, the sun and the moon who started two lines of kings, on earth were devoted to the service of Siva always with their descendants.

O Sage, the self born Brahma, and other Manus, performed the worship of Siva and they were in the guise of Siva also.

Priyavrata and his son Uttanapada, besides his sons and successors were the kings adoring Siva.

Dhruva, Bharata, Rsabha, Bharata, his brothers, the nine yogins, and others too adored Siva.

The son of Vaivasvata Manu, Tarkhya, the kings like Iksavaku and others, who enjoyed all the worldly pleasures were devoted to Siva.

Kakustha, Mandhata, Sagara, Mucukunda, Hariscandra and Kalmasapada were the kings who were all devoted to Siva.

Bhagiratha, taking to the form of Siva, besides the other kings, used to worship Siva.

Khatvanga- the great king and associates of the gods, used to worship Parthiva-linga form of Siva daily.

His son named Dilip and his son Raghu, also used to worship Siva with devotion and pleasure.

His son Aja, who fought the battle of dhama and his son Dasaratha were specially devoted to Siva.

At the command of the sage Vasistha the king Dasaratha, getting the Pdrthiva-linga made, specially for him adored Siva.

At the command of the sage Rsyasrnga, Dasaratha- the devotee of Siva, performed the Putresthi- Yajna.

At the advice of the sage Rsyasrnga, Kausalya the queen of Dasaratha, adored Parthiva Sivalinga for achieving a son.

O Excellent sage, Kaikeyi and Sumitra- the queens of Dasaratha, for achieving the noble sons, had worshipped Siva.

All the three queens, got virtuous sons who could bestow welfare by the grace of Siva. O Sage, all the four sons were immensely glorious and followers of the noble path.

Thereafter at the command of Siva, lord Visnu appeared from the wombs of the four queens, in the form of four sons.

Rama was the son of Kausalya, Laksmana was the son of Sumitra, while Kaikeyi had two sons Bharata and Satrughna.

Rama wore the ashes and Rudraksa over his body, was free from all the attachments and worshipped the Parthiva form of Sivalinga daily.

O Sage, all the subsequent kings of the race, used to worship Siva in the form of Parthiva-linga.

O Sage, Sudumna- the great king and son of a sage, became a woman with his attendants as a result of the curse of Siva, for the sake of his beloved.

Thanks to the worship by him of the Parthiva-linga of Siva, he regained his excellent manhood. He remained a man for a month and a woman for a month, his womanhood disappeared.

Then he disowned his kingship, taking to the form of Siva, he devoted himself to the worship of Siva with utmost devotion and attained moksa which is inaccessible to others.

Pururava- the great king, worshipper of lord Siva and his son adored Siva with devotion.

Thereafter his son, named Bharata, always adored Siva with utmost devotion. The king Nahusa- the great Saiva was always engaged in the adoration of Siva.

With influence of the worship of Siva the king Yayati, had all his desire fulfilled and all his five sons were devoted to Siva.

Yadu and other five sons of Yayati were the worshippers of Siva. As a result of their devotion to Siva, they had all their desires fulfilled.

The other fortunate people of his race and of other races, worshipped Siva and ultimately enjoyed all the worldly pleasures besides achieving salvation.

Krsna himself adored Siva on the excellent mountain of Badari for seven months.

Lord Krsna, receiving several divine boons from Siva, felt delighted and brought the entire universe under his control.

O Dear one, his son Pradyumna, too always worshipped Siva, Samba and other illustrious descendants of Krsna were also the great worshippers of Siva.

Jarasandha was also a great devotee of Siva, besides the people of his race. The king Nimi, Janaka and their descendants were all the worshippers of Siva.

Nala who in earlier birth was born as a Bhila who guarded the roads, was bom as a son to the king Virasena in his second birth and was a worshipper of Siva.

The said Bhila protected an ascetic who was adoring Siva, but was himself killed by a tiger as a move of destiny.

As a result of the same merit, the Bhila became a Cakravarti king the husband of Damyanti.

O Sinless one, O Dear one, I have narrated to you the divine story of Siva, as desired by you. What more to do you want to ask me?”

## Chapter 38 - The glory of Sivaratri

The Rsis said, “O Dear one, you are blessed and successful, your life has met with success, because you are narrating the story of Siva to us.

O Suta, though I have heard the same story from several other Rsis, but the doubt of my mind could not be cleared, therefore I am speaking to you.

You tell me the Vrata, by performing which, Siva getting pleased bestows the best of the reward? You are well-versed in the interpretation of the rites of Siva, therefore we are asking you.

You kindly speak out the Vrata, with the performing of which one specially achieves devotion as well the salvation. O Disciple of Vyasa, salutation to you.”

Suta said, “O Excellent Rsis, you have put me a good question, being compassionate. Now I devoting my mind at the lotus like feet of lord Siva, am going to repeat the same whatever had been heard by me on the subject.

As all of you have asked, the similar type of information as was sought by Brahma, Visnu and Parvati from Siva.

Once all of them, asked Siva to spell out the Vrata, you getting pleased from your devotees, grant them devotion and salvation?”

When thus questioned by Visnu and other gods, I repeat the same whatever had been spoken by me at that point of time, by listening to which all the sins of the listeners are washed out.”

Siva said, “Several of my Vratas bestow devotion and salvation. But ten out of them are quite important.

Jabali and other sages well-versed in the Vedas have prescribed the ten Siva-vratas to be quite important, which should be performed by the Brahmanas appropriately.

O Visnu, on each eighth day of the moon, one should take food during the night making all the efforts. One should particularly keep fast on the dark eighth day of the moon.

O Visnu, one should perform vrata on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight. On the Ekadasi of the dark fortnight one should take food during the night after adoring me.

On the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight, the devotee of Siva should take food during the night.

The devotees of Siva should take food during the night on all the Mondays during both the fortnights.

During all these Vratas, food should be offered to the Brahmanas who are devoted to Siva. O Brahmanas, the vrata is completed by so doing.

The Brahmanas should perform thus Vrata appropriately. Failure in performing these Vratas, makes a Brahmana a thief.

Those traversing the path of salvation, should perform these Vratas appropriately and regularly, because, the following four instructions lead to salvation.

Adoration of Siva, reciting of japam for Rudra, keeping fast living in the Siva temple, and to face death while living in Kasi. The following of these methods lead one to achieve the eternal salvation.

The festivities comprising of Monday and the eighth day of the fortnight, besides the fourteenth day of the fortnight falling on Monday, please Siva. There is no doubt about it.

O Visnu, out of these the Sivaratri vrata is quite meritorious and should be performed by the people desirous of devotion and salvation.

There is no other Vrata more beneficial for the people, as compared to these Vratas. Of all the religious activities, this Vrata is the best.

O Visnu, people of all castes and asramas, with or without desire, the women, children, can derive the best benefit out of it

This Vrata is the best and most beneficial to the gods, the slaves and the slave-girls, and all the human beings.

The fourteenth moonless night in the month of Magha (at midnight), is considered to be of special importance. By adoring Siva on that occasion one is relieved of the sins of crores of killings.

O Visnu, you listen to the daily performance of that particular day since morning which I am going to speak to you. Let a learned person, discarding laziness get up early in the morning, then he should free himself from the daily routine and have a bath delightfully.

He should then go to the Siva temple in the morning after daily routine of bath, perform the worship of Siva appropriately and offer his salutation to the lord and then perform Samkalpa according to the prescribed course saying.

“O Lord of gods, O Mahadeva, O NUakantha, salutation to you. O Lord, I intend to perform the Sivaratri Vrata.

O Lord of gods, let my Vrata be successfully completed by your grace, without any obstruction. Let the enemies like passion, anger and greed not trouble me.

Thus performing the sathkalpa, collecting the material for worship, one should adore the linga lodged in the excellent place and well known in the Sastra.

During the first night he should go himself and place the material for worship on the right or the western side of Siva. Thereafter the performer of the Vrata reciting Samkalpa, should take his bath.

He should clad himself with the auspicious costumes including the underwears, and sipping the water thrice, he should start the worship.

He should adore Siva offering the same articles reciting the mantra prescribed for the purpose. He should not worship Siva without reciting of the relevant mantra.

Having been filled with the feeling of devotion, he should resort to songs, accompanied with music and dance during the first prahara. Then he should perform japam for the mantra Oḍ namah Sivyaya.

Reciting this mantra, a devotee should make an earthen Sivalinga. Getting free from daily routine, then he should worship the earthen linga.

Initially making the clay linga, it should be consecrated. Then he should please Mahadeva, reciting several types of stotras.

A learned person should narrate the glory of this Vrata, while the devotees should listen to the same with the intention of completing the Vrata.

During the four praharas of the night, all the four forms of Siva should be invoked and then sent off appropriately.

One should keep himself awake during the festivities. Thereafter in the early morning taking his bath, he should worship Siva.

Then he should offer prayer to Siva with his hands folded and lowering his head, besides offering his salutation to the lord.

He should then pray, O Mahadeva, O Master, the Vrata which I had resolved to perform, has since been completed. Now I am consigning it in water with your permission.

O Lord, Siva, I have performed this Vrata according to my means. Therefore, you be pleased with me.”

Thus speaking, he should offer bunch of flowers to lord Siva, besides making donations appropriately. Then offering salutation to Sivalinga, he should consign it.

The devotee of Siva should then give food to the Brahmanas as well as the ascetics, to their satisfaction and then he should take food himself.

O Visnu, in each one of the praharas of the night, the method of the worship to be performed by a devotee of Siva is being spoken by me.

During the first prahara the consecrated Sivalinga should be adored with all the suitable material with devotion.

Initially one should offer each one of the five padarthas of pancamrta, separately, reciting separate mantra for each one of them.

Thereafter the water should be poured over the linga to enable the offered dravyas to be washed out.

Reciting a hundred and eight namah- mantras the water should be poured over the linga. In this way one should adore Nirguna Siva in a Saguna form.

One should adore Siva using the mantra awarded by the preceptor or alternatively one should adore repeating the namah-mantra.

Siva should also be adored by offering the best of the sandal-paste, unbroken rice, and black gingerly seeds.

The hundred petalled, lotus flowers with and Karavira flowers should be offered to Siva reciting his eight names.

The eight names of Siva are- Bhava, Sarva, Rudra, Pasupati, Ugra, Mahan, Bhima and Tsana.

The word ’Sri’ should be prefixed to each one of these names which should put in the dative case. The incense and the lamps should be used. The food offering should be made thereafter.

During the first prahara (three hours), period, the learned devotee should make cooked rice as the food offering. Half a coconut and a betel should be offered thereafter.

Salutation, meditation, reciting of the mantra given by the guru, one should resort to repeating the Pancaksra-mantra (Oḍ namah Sivaya) for Siva to be pleased.

Displaying the Dhenumudra the spotless water should be sprinkled. One should then serve food as per one’s capacity to the five Brahmanas.

Till the completion of a prahara (three hours), the festivities should continue. Thereafter the fruits should be offered as part of puja and then the ritualistic send off should propound.

Then the Samkalpa should be performed in the second prahara or performing a single Samkalpa for the worship during all the four praharas, the same process of adoration should be carried out.

After performing the worship with five types of dravyas (materials), as before the stream of water should be poured. Double the number of mantras as compared to the earlier ones, should be recited while adoring Siva.

The devotee should adore Siva offering the gingerly seeds, barley, lotus flowers but particularly with the wood-apple leaves.

Argha should be performed with citron fruit and naivedya should consist of pdyasam, O Janardana, repetition of the mantras shall be twice and compared to that of the previous one.

Then one should resolve for the sumptuous feeding of the Brahmana and the process of worship during the second prahara should resemble the same as in the first prahara.

In the third prahara the process of worship as in the first prahara should be repeated. The offering of the barley should be replaced with wheat, and the flowers of the sun plant should be used in the offering to the lord.

Incense and lamps of various types should be used in adoration. O Visnu, the naivedya should comprise of the fried pieces besides the various vegetables dishes.

The performing of arati with the waving of lights using camphor shall be of various types, forming the part of worship. The arghya should comprise of pomegranate. The repetition of japath should be thrice as compared to the previous one.

The Brahmanas should then be served with food accompanied with daksina (monetary offerings). The festivities of dance, accompanied with music should continue till the end of the third prahara.

On the arrival of the fourth prahara, the ritualistic dismissal of the worship of the third prahara should be done. Till the end of that prahara, the performance of the adoration shall continue as before.

Lord Parmesvara should be worshipped offering black gram, green gram, Priyahgu grains or any of the seven cereals, the flowers of Samkhapuspi and the leaves of the wood- apple tree.

For the pleasing of Siva, naivedya (food offering) of sweet dishes, or the cooked rice with black gram or other fried food stuffs should be offered.

O Visnu, at the end of the fourth prahara, arghya should be given with different types of fruits.

O Excellent Purusa, the recitation of the mantras should be double than the earlier one, then the food offerings should be made to the Brahmanas.

Thereafter accompanied with the devotees singing and dancing accompanied with music should be performed for the spending of the time of festivities. The process should continue till the sunrise.

After the sunrise, the devotee shall take the bath and then adore Siva offering several types of presents. Thereafter a devotee should get his own abhiseka performed.

Based on the number of the praharas various types of charities and gifts should be given to the Brahmanas and the ascetics together with eatables.

The devotee offering his salutation to Siva, also offer the bunch of flowers to the lord. Eulogising the lord, he should offer prayers to Siva reciting the mantras.

“O Siva, I belong to you, my mind and life are dedicated to you. O Ocean of compassion, thus realising, you do whatever you think best.

O Lord of the bhutas, whatever the japath or the adoration has been performed by me knowingly or unknowingly, you should be pleased with me being the ocean of mercy.

As a reward from this fast and rite, let lord Siva, the bestower of happiness be pleased with me.

O Mahadeva, let the entire race of mine remain devoted to you. I should not be born in a race in which you do not happen to be the family deity.”

Thus speaking, a bunch of flowers should be offered, a devotee should seek blessings from the Brahmanas. Thereafter the invoked Siva should be sent off.

In case one performs this Vrata without much effort, the seed of salvation will stand planted in his heart. There is no doubt about it.

The people should perform this vrata every month. Thereafter performing the concluding rites, the devotee shall get the reward with other benefits.

One who performs this Vrata with devotion, I (Siva) remove all his miseries and bestowing the desired boon on also him, shower on him all the pleasures besides the salvation.”

Suta said, ‘Thus listening to the beneficial words of lord Siva, all of them became immensely illustrious. Thereafter lord Visnu, in the company of his associates, performed the excellent Vrata appropriately.

At some stage, lord Visnu enlightened Narada about this Vrata which bestows worldly pleasures as well as the salvation.

Thus, one who performs the Vrata in this manner, Siva maintains no distance from him. The merit of the same is beyond description and for such a devotee, there is nothing which cannot be given to him.

## Chapter 39 - Completion of Sivaratri Vrata

The Rsis said, “Now you tell me the concluding rites of the Sivaratri vrata, with the performing of which, Siva surely is pleased.

Suta said, “O Sages, you better listen to me with devotion, with the performing of which the Vrata surely comes to conclusion.

This Vrata of Sivaratri should be performed continuously for fourteen years. Taking food once on the day of Trayodasi, and fasting on the day of Caturdasi should be done.

On the day of Sivaratri, the morning rites should be performed appropriately. One should go to the Siva temple and perform puja there as prescribed in the scriptures.

Then one should have the well known Gauri-mandala made with much efforts, which is well known.

The Lingatobhadra mandala should be made or Sarvatobhadra should be made in the centre of it.

In the name of Prajapatya the costumes, fruits, and daksina should be offered to the kalasas after consecrating them.

These should be kept around the mandala. The kalasa of gold should be lodged in the centre quite carefully.

An image of Umamahesvara should be made by the performer of Vrata as per his means weighing a pala or half of it.

Parvati should be lodged carefully to the left and Siva should be seated to the right. This image should be adored in the night.

Getting purified the acarya and the priests should be selected and with their permission, one should perform puja with devotion.

The performer of the Vrata should remain awake during the night, performing puja in each one of the praharas. He should spend the night, by singing, dancing accompanied with music.

In this way performing the worship appropriately, pleasing Siva, one should perform the puja again in the morning, performing the homa as well.

According to one’s means, one should perform the Prajapatya rites, serving food lovingly to the Brahmanas offering charities to them with devotion.

The priests should be given the costumes with their wives, adorning them with ornaments with devotion, individually.

A well decorated cow with calf, should be given to the acarya saying, “Let lord Siva be pleased with me.

Thereafter the image of Siva seated over the bull, adorned with all the ornaments should be given in charity to the acarya.

Then with folded hands, lowering his head, one should pray to lord Mahesana in choked voice.

“O God of gods, O Great god, well disposed towards those who take refuge in you. O Lord of the gods, you shower your grace on me with this Vrata.

O Siva, O Sankara I have performed this Vrata with devotion. Any shortcoming in the same should be supplied by your grace.

Let the japam and worship performed by me knowingly or unknowingly be fruitful by your grace.

Offering the bunch of flowers to lord Siva, one should offer his salutation to him offering prayer at the same time.

One who performs the Vrata in this way he achieves the desired success, there is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 40 - The glory of Sivaratri

The Rsis said, “O Suta, listening to your words, we feel delighted. Now you describe the same Vrata in detail.

O Suta, who performed this Vrata first of all which was caused by performing the same in ignorance, what was the reward received by him?

Suta said, “O Rsis, all of you should listen. I shall narrate the ancient story of a hunter which destroys the sins.

In ancient times, in a forest, a hunter known by the name of Garudroha, lived with a large family. He was quite powerful, truthless and was engaged in cruel ways.

Daily he went to the forest and killed the deer, besides committing thefts in the forest in many ways.

He never engaged himself in any one of the religious activities, ever since his childhood. Thus the wicked hunter spent time in forest following the sinful ways.

Once the festival of Sivaratri arrived. The gigantic wild and wicked person was totally unaware of the importance of Sivaratri.

His hungry parents and wife said to him, “O Forest dweller, you give us something to eat.”

At these words spoken by his parents and the wife, he carrying the bow and arrow atonce moved out for the killing of the deer and for this purpose he wandered in the forest.

As a matter of chance, he could find no living being for hunting on that particular day. The sun was set in the meantime as a result of which he felt painful.

Then he thought, “what should I do, where should I go, I have got nothing today. What shall happen to my parents and the children?

My wife is pregnant, what shall happen to her when I should return home, carrying something. Otherwise, I shall not return to my abode.”

Thus thinking, the hunter went to a lake and seated himself over the bank of the lake with water.

He thought, “Some one would surely arrive here for taking water and I shall become successful by killing the same and then return to my abode.”

Thus thinking the hunter climbed a Bilva (wood apple tree) taking some water with him and sat on its branch.

The hungry and thirsty hunter kept on thinking as to when shall any living being arrive to be killed by him.

Then suddenly in the first prahara of the night, a thirsty hind arrived springing and filled with surprise.

O Visnu, finding the arrival of the hind, the hunter was delighted and he lifted up his bow and arrow in order to kill her.

Soon after he did so the leaves of the wood apple tree fell with water over the Sivalinga lying down below on earth.

With this, the adoration of Siva for the first prahara was completed, washing out his sins.

On hearing the noise of falling the water, the hind looked at the hunter and said to him getting upset.

The Doe said, “O Hunter, what do you want to do? You speak out truthfully to me.” Hearing the words of the doe, the hunter said, “My family is hungry and for that purpose, I shall feed them, by killing you.” Listening to the harsh words of the hunter.

The doe thought, “What should I do? Where should I go? What means should be adopted by me?”

The doe said, “O Malevolent one, in case my flesh could appease you then I would feel graceful. Because in that case, I am sure to earn merit.

A person who does good, earns, enormous merit in return, which cannot be described in hundreds of years.

But let me entrust the care of my young ones in my abode, to my sister. Then I shall return to you here.

O Forest dweller, Don’t take my words as false. I shall undoubtedly return to you.

The earth remains stable with the truth. The oceans remain with the power of the truth, the streams of water flow because of the truth. All of them are based on truth.”

Suta said, “When the hunter failed to agree to the words spoken by the doe, then the surprised and panic stricken doe said, again.

The Doe said, “O Hunter, Listen, I speak on oath. In case I do not return to you after visiting my abode,

Then I should earn the sin, a Brahmana earns a sin by failing to perform sandhya thrice a day, or the sin earned by a Brahmana by selling the Vedas or a woman who acts contrary to the command of her husband,

Or a sin earned by an ungrateful person, or a sin earned by some one by moving against lord Hari, or the sin earned by becoming inimical to the Guru or the preceptor or the sin earned by some one by moving against dharma.

Or the sin earned by a person betraying one’s faith. In case I do not return, I shall earn all these sins.

In this way taking several oaths, the doe kept on standing there. The hunter then developing faith in her, allowed her to go home.

The doe felt pleased and drinking water from the lake returned to her abode. By that time the first prahara was over.

The sister of the doe, feeling anxious, searching for her sister also arrived at the same spot, for drinking water.

Spotting her, the Bhila strung the bow aiming an arrow at the doe. As soon as he did so the water and the leaves of the wood-apple tree fell over the Sivalinga below.

With this, lord Siva achieved the puja of the second prahara without much efforts, quite pleasantly.

Looking at the hunter, the doe said, “O Forest dweller, what are you doing?” The hunter replied as before. The doe on hearing him said.

The doe said, “Listen, O Hunter, I am indeed graceful. In case this body could be made use of by some one, then his life becomes successful.

But my young ones are at my home. I shall return, entrusting their care to my husband.”

The hunter said, “I do not believe in your words. I shall undoubtedly kill you.” O Visnu, then the doe taking an oath said to the hunter.

The Doe said, “O Hunter, you listen to me whatever I have to speak to you. In case I do not return as assured by me, then I should earn the sin which a person earns by backing out of his words.

Or the sin a person earns by enjoying other woman, in preference to his own wife or the sin earned by a person who follows other dharma leaving the Vedic dharma.

Or the sin earned by the devotee of Visnu, by denouncing Siva, or a person who does not feed the Brahmanas on the day of the death of his parents.

Or the one who after repenting commits the same sin. In case I do not return as promised then I should earn all these sins.”

Suta said, “At these words of the doe, the hunter permitted her to go. She also feeling delighted and drinking water at the pool, left the place for her abode.

By that time, the second prahara also was over in which he remained awake. Then there started the third prahara.

Finding the delay in the return of the hinds, the hunter started searching for them, when in the third prahara, he found a buck moving towards the path leading to the pool of water.

Finding a strong and well built buck, he placed the arrow over the bow and was about to kill it.

O Visnu, when, while placing the arrow over the bow some water fell together with the leaves of the wood apple tree accidentally over the Siva-linga below as a matter of luck.

With this the adoration of Siva for the third prahara was performed, per chance and Siva displayed his compassion on the hunter.

Listening to the sound, the buck said, “What are you doing?” The hunter then said, “I am going to kill you for feeding my family.”

Listening to the words of the hunter, the buck getting pleased, spoke to the hunter.

The buck said, “I am graceful, besides being well-built and well nourished. You will derive the best satisfaction from me. A person’s body if not be used for the welfare of others, it is of no avail.

One who being competent enough, fails to do good to others, his ability is of no use and he falls in the hell.

But I shall come back by entrusting the care of my young ones to their mother and then return to you again.”

At these words of the buck the hunter felt surprised. His mind felt some what purified and was freed from the sins a little.

Then the hunter said, “All those who arrived here, went back speaking like you, never to return again. The cheats have not returned so far.

O Buck, you are also going, leaving me in trouble. How shall I carry on my livelihood?

The buck said, “O Hunter, I don’t tell a lie. The entire globe besides the mobile and immobile are sustained on truth.

One who tells a lie, all his merits are washed out in a moment. Still, O Bhila, you listen to my firm resolve for speaking the truth.

The sin one earns by cohabiting in the evening, or by taking food on the Sivaratri day. or by giving false witness, or misappropriation of a trust or a Brahmana, deprived of Sandhya,

Or a mouth without the reciting of the name of Siva, or one who fails to do good inspite of his being competent to do so, or the plucking of the wood apple fruit on the day sacred to Siva, or eating of the forbidden food,

Or to adore Siva, without applying ashes on the body, or to take food without adoring Siva, all the sins should be earned by me in case I do not return to you.”

Suta said, “Thus listening to the words of the buck, the hunter said, “You go and return rapidly.” Thereafter the buck left the place after drinking the water.

All of them the bucks and the hinds met at their abode hearing the news of one another in entirety.

All of them were bound with the oaths of truth. Then they decided to return to the hunter. All of them assuring the young ones, got ready to return.

The elder hind said to her husband, “How can the young ones remain here without you?

O Lord the oath had been taken first by me. Therefore, I should go first.” Both of you stay here.

On hearing this the junior doe said, “I happen to be your servant. I shall go today and you remain here.”

On hearing this the buck said, “I shall go, let both of you remain here, the young ones are well looked after by the mothers.”

On hearing the words of the buck, they did not agree on the basis of dharma and lovingly said, “Disgraceful is the life of a widow.”

Then entrusting the care of the fawns to the neighbours, all the three of them went to the place of the hunter.

The fawns too followed them, thinking they would meet the same fate as would be met by their parents.

Finding their arrival, the hunter felt pleased and as soon as he strung the bow, the water and the leaves of wood apple tree fell over Siva.

With which the puja of the fourth prahara was completed, as a result of which all his sins were washed out in a moment.

Both the senior and junior hinds and the buck said, “O Hunter, kindly make our bodies successful.”

Thus listening their words the hunter felt surprised. With influence of the worship of Siva, he achieved the inaccessible knowledge.

The hunter thought, “Blessed are the deer devoid of wisdom, who are ready to do good to others with their bodies.

I, inspite of having a human body, what have I done till date. Causing pain to the bodies of others, I maintained my body.

I maintained my family committing several types of sins. Alas! what shall happen to me by committing the sins in this way?

What shall be the fate of a person like me who had been indulging in sinful ways since birth. Presently I am thinking that disgrace to my life.”

With the achieving of this type of enlightenment, the hunter strung the bow and spoke to the deer, “O Deer, you return to your home.

At these words of the hunter, Siva, getting pleased, accepted his worship and displayed before him, his true form.

Then touching the hunter with his hands, Siva said to him, “O Bhila, you ask for a boon. I am pleased with your Vrata ”

The hunter, looking at the form of Siva, was atonce freed from sins and he uttered, “I have got everything.” Thus speaking, he fell at the feet of Siva.

Then Siva feeling pleased, gave the hunter the name of Guha. Then casting his compassionate look on him he granted him several divine boons.

Siva said, “O Hunter, listen to me. You after enjoying all the desired pleasures, reside in the capital city of Srngaverpura.

Your imperishable race will expand. You would be praised by the gods even. O Hunter, Sri Rama would arrive at your abode.
