He will make friendship with you, because he loves my devotees. Because of your devotion to me you would achieve the type of salvation, which is rarely achieved by others.”

Suta said, “At the same time, the deer, having an audience with Siva were relieved of their animal birth, after bowing in reverence to the lord.

Achieving the divine bodies, the deer, having been relieved of the curse, went to the heaven, boarding the divine plane.

Since that date Siva came to be known as Vyaghresvara over the Arbudacala mountain. By adoring and looking at him, one achieves the devotion and salvation at the same time.

O Best of the gods, the hunter also enjoying all the worldly pleasures since that date, by the grace of Rama achieved the Sdyujya devotion of Siva.

He performed the Vrata unknowingly but still he achieved the Sayujya type of salvation. Those who worship Siva whole heartedly, they attain complete identity with the lord.

After study of the Sastras and other religious scriptures, the Sivaratri Vrata has been treated as the best.

Several of the Vratas, the places of pilgrimage charities and the yajnas have been described.

There is a mention of the penance and japath as well, but they do not have the reverence comparable with Sivaratri.

Therefore, those who wish well of themselves, should perform the Vrata of Sivaratri which bestows the worldly pleasures, besides the salvation.

All this has been narrated relating to the Vrata of Sivaratri which is known as the foremost of the sacred rites. What more do you want to listen from me?”

## Chapter 41 - Types of Salvation

The Rsis said, “You tell me the position of mukti- the salvation as has been described by you.

Suta said, “I am going to tell you that salvation, which relieves one of all the worldly sufferings and is quite blissful, is of four types.

They are Sarupya (identity in form), Salokya (within the view of the lord), Sanidhya (closeness to the lord) and Sayujya (complete identity with the lord). The fourth one arises on Virata form and can be achieved with the performing of the Sivaratri Vrata.

O Excellent sages, Siva alone is the bestower of the salvation. Brahma and other gods can bestow worldly pleasures like dharma, artha and kama.

Brahma and other gods are the lord, of Trigunas (viz. sattva, rajas and tamas), while Siva is beyond the three gunas. He is unblemished, Supreme Brahman, the turya deity and is beyond Prakrti.

Besides, he is also the form of knowledge, indestructible, could be known by learnings, who is non-dual himself, bestower of the absolute salvation besides the Trivarga (dharma, artha and kama).

The fifth salvation named Kaivalya is ordinarily beyond the reach of the humans. O Rsis, I shall explain the details thereof, which should be listened by you.

The source from which everything originates, the one who maintains the universe and the source in which everything is absorbed and because of which everything exists,

O Sages, the same is called the form of Siva. The same source has been termed Sakala (with form) and Niskala (without form).

That form remains unknown to Brahma, Visnu, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatkumara, Narada and other sages.

Vyasa, Sukadeva- the son of Vyasa, excellent sages, the gods living prior to them, besides the Vedas, sastras, are also unaware of that form.

This knowledge is full of truth and i beyond limits which is called Saccidananda O blissful. He is devoid of gunas (attributes Nirvvadha (limitless). It is imperishable, pur and unsullied or spotless.

It is neither red nor yellow, nor white, nor blue, nor big nor small, nor gross and nor subtle.

The spot from where the speech return from the power of thinking of the mind, it i called Siva- the Supreme Brahman.

As the sky pervades everywhere, similarly it also pervades everywhere. It is beyond Maya. The supreme soul is beyond mutual conflict and rivalry.

O Brahmanas, its achievement in this world, can be made with the rise of the knowledge about Siva, or with the adoration of Siva or the subtle wisdom of the noble people.

It is quite difficult to achieve knowledge in the world though it is easier to adore him. Therefore O Brahmanas, one should adore Siva to achieve salvation.

Siva is subservient to devotion. It is he who bestows the divine knowledge as well as the moksa. Several of the siddhas have achieved salvation by means of devotion.

The worship of Siva is the mother of knowledge and it always bestows the pleasure and the salvation. By his grace the devotion becomes easy to access, the symptom of which is the sprouting of love for Siva in the mind of a person.

O Brahmanas, the devotion is of several types in the Nirguna and Saguna forms. Whatever is legitimate and natural, is most excellent and greatest. It is again two-fold Nisthika (permanent) and Anisthika (nonpermanent). The Nisthika is of six types and the other is a solitary one.

The people with learnings consider devotion to be of different types like ordained and n on-ordained. Since they are of various types, they are not explained individually.

Separated by the differences in those who resort to sravana (listening) etc. both are of nine sub-divisions each. Without the grace of the Ion , they are of difficult performance and with his favour their performance becomes easier.

O Brahmanas, devotion and knowledge are treated as one and the same by Siva. Therefore they should not be treated as separate. The one who observes both of them, he attains happiness.

O Brahmana, a person who is devoid c devotion will never attain perfect knowledge The one who is devoted to Siva, he attain knowledge automatically.

Therefore O Great sage, devotion to lore Siva must be maintained. There is absolutely no doubt that one can realise everything by means of devotion.

Thus I have explained to you whatever had been asked by you. On hearing this a person is relieved of all his sins and there is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 42 - The difference between Siva’s Nirguna and Saguna forms

The Rsis said, “Who are Siva, Rudra, Brahma and Visnu, which one of them has the Nirguna form. You kindly remove our doubt.

Suta said, “The one who emerged of the Nirguna supreme soul happens to be Siva. This has been described by the Vedas the post-Vedic literature besides Vedanta.

O Learned ones, from him Purusa and Prakrti were bom. Both of them staying in the jalatattva performed tapas.

The said place, in due course of time came to be known as Pancakosi in Kasi, which is immensely liked by Siva. The water of that place was spread in the entire world.

Finding this, Lord Visnu together with his Maya slept in the oceanic waters and subsequently came to be known as Narayana. His Prakrti came to be known as Narayani.

The one who emerged from the lotus flower grown from his navel, came to be known as Brahma- the grand sire. The one who was found by Brahma, after performing the tapas, came to be known as Visnu.

O Brahmanas, in order to remove the controversy between Brahma and Visnu, the form in which Siva appeared, came to be known as Mahadeva.

He said, “I shall appear from the head of Brahma in the form of Sambhu. The same Sambhu, the bestower of welfare came to be known as Rudra in due course of time.

Since that date for the meditation of the devotees of the lord, Siva, took the Sakara (with form) for the benefit of his devotees. He therefore likes the devotees of Siva.

There is absolutely no difference between Siva who is beyond the three gunas (sattva, rajas and tamas) and Rudra, possessing all the gunas, in the same way as there is no difference between the gold and the gold ornaments.

Both of them perform their activities similarly, bestow salvation to their devotees similarly. Both of them are served by the people equally well and they roam about indulging in several types of divine sports.

The immensely valorous Rudra is the form of Siva. He takes to different forms, for the sake of this devotees and also helps Brahma and Visnu.

His other forms in which he appears often, they get absorbed in the same. But he never gets absorbed anywhere else. He in fact gets absorbed in Siva alone.

The other gods get absorbed in Rudra but Rudra never gets absorbed in Visnu or other gods inspite getting an opportunity for the same. This has been ordained by the Vedas.

The universe adores Rudra, but Rudra adores no one else. Sometimes, however, showering his grace over the devotees, he himself adores himself.

O Learned people, those who worship others, get dissolved in them. Because of this, they attain Rudra in due course of time.

The people devoted to Rudra attain the state of Siva in no time. They do not have to depend on anyone else. This is the eternal voice of the Vedas.

O Brahmanas, ignorance is of various types. But this is not the case with the perfect knowledge. I shall explain their modes and you listen to me with respect.

Whatever is witnessed in the universe right from Brahma is Siva himself. The concept of manifestation is not real.

Siva was there before the creation of the universe, it was there in the midst of the creation and shall remain at the ends of the creation as well. Even when there nothing exists, Siva remains always. In other words, Siva is omnipresent.

O Excellent sages, because of this, Siva has been conceived to possess four gunas. He inspite of his being all powerful, has been conceived to be of two types.

It is he who has delivered the eternal Vedas, syllables, syllabic instants, his meditation and his worship to Visnu.

The eternal Sruti says “Isanah Sarvavidyanam. Therefore Siva is the creator of the Vedas besides being the lord of the Vedas.

He alone is Siva himself who blesses all. He happens to be the creator, sustainer as well as the destroyer. He is the cosmic witness and Nirguna.

Restrictions of time are for others and not for Rudra. He is Mahakala himself associated with Mahakali.

The Brahmanas claim Rudra and Kali to be the cause of all. Both of them have achieved everything because of their truthful plays.

No one produced Rudra, nor is there any lord for him nor the destroyer. But he happens to be the cause of Visnu and others.

Siva himself is the form though single, he takes to many forms. Apparently he appears in many forms but is unified into one ultimately.

A single seed growing into a tree becomes the cause of producing many seeds. Even in their multiplying, they remain the product of one and the same tree. Mahesvara in the form of Siva, symbolises the same.

O Sages, this is the excellent knowledge concerning Siva, which has been explained by me. Only the learned people are aware of the same and none else can know about it.”

The sages said, “You describe the type of knowledge, attaining which a person is in a position to achieve Siva. How is it that Siva is all in all and how is it that all the things visible in the world are the forms of Siva.

Vyasa said, “Listening to these words, Suta, who was well aware of the secrets of the Puranas spoke to the sages, devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva.

## Chapter 43 - The perfect knowledge of Siva

Suta said, “O Sages, I have heard about the extremely secret knowledge of Siva which is the form of salvation. I am going to narrate the same. All of you should listen to the same.

This question had been discussed in the gathering of the sages like Saunaka, Narada, Kartikeya, Vyasa and Kapila, who came to the conclusion saying.

“The universe is the form of Siva and all the articles contained therein are also the form of Siva. This should be admitted by the learned people.

From Brahma to the blade of grass, whatever is visible in the world is the form of Siva. The same could be called as lord Siva.

The universe is created at his will. He is omniscient, but no one exactly knows about him.

After creating the universe, he himself enters into it he remain aloof and unattached besides being the form of knowledge.

As the association of the light with the water appears in the form of the reflection, but in reality it never enters the water, similar is the case of Siva.

In reality Siva alone, being auspicious one, manifests himself. The ignorance of this reality is the defect of their mind. Indeed there is no second entity.

There is a difference of opinion in the different schools of philosophy, but still the followers of the Veddnta system of philosophy, believe the lord as eternal and of non-duality.

The jivatma of the same amsa getting deluded with Maya and thinks that he is different. After his release from ignorance, he becomes Siva.

Lord Siva is all pervading and remains present in all the living beings. He bestows welfare on all being the lord of sentients and insentients.

Following the path of Vedanta, the learned people, who try to have an audience with him, they achieve the fruits of the sight

As the fire being all pervading resides in the wood, but one who chums it, finds it surely manifested.

A learned person who brings in use, the devotion or other means, he surely has an audience with Siva. There is no doubt about it.

Siva pervades everywhere, and there is nothing else in the world. But because of the illusion his several forms are visualised by the peoples.

As the ocean, the clay and gold are conceived in several ways, due to the change of names, similarly Siva is visualised in many forms due to different names.

In reality there is no material difference between the cause and its effect. The visible difference is due to the illusory perceptions. With the removal of ignorance, all the differences are also removed.

Sprouting from the seed is variously seen. But is becomes the seed, after the perishing of the shoot.

The intelligence is the form of seed and sprouting is the form of deformity. At the disappearing of the deformity one regains his wisdom again. There is no doubt about it.

Everything in the universe represents Si' who is everything. Therefore there is: difference between the two. Then how can t manifestation be seen or the unity regained?

As the reflection of one and the same sun can be visualised in several forms in the water, though in reality it remains one only, or as the sky is all pervading but it cannot be touched, similarly, the all pervading supreme spirit also, cannot be put in any bondage.

The jiva is full of arrogance, and getting relieved of the same, it becomes Siva. The individual jiva because of its being the karmabhogi is quite insignificant, but after becoming unattached, it turns into the great Sankara

As with the mixing of silver with gold, the price of gold gets reduced, similarly the Jiva overpowered with the arrogance, its grace is reduced.

As the gold with its heating in the fire is purified, regaining its original value, similarly with the auspicious Samskaras, the jlva attains godhood.

By achieving a noble preceptor in the first instance, taking him to be the form of Siva, with devotion, one should worship him and should recall Siva loudly.

By so doing, all the blemishes and the sins earned by the body are removed. Then the ignorance too is lost and a person is bestowed with knowledge.

Then the Jiva, getting deprived of the arrogance attains the spotless wisdom. Then with grace of Siva he transforms himself as Siva.

As one looks to his own form in the clear mirror, similarly, a devotee while roaming about everywhere, can have an audience with Siva,

He becoming the living liberated soul, after the destruction of the body, gets absorbed in Siva. The human body is achieved by great fortunes. A learned person is treated to living without a body.

Only a person, who is not delighted by getting the best of things and does not feel painful in evil situations. In case he maintains perfect equanimity in all situations, he could be treated as the perfectly wise person.

A person desirous of salvation, with his linking with the soul, or with the transfer of the tattvas from one body to the other, on the basis of the idea of sat and asat,

The one who is absorbed in the body of Siva, he, getting free from the worldly tales, achieves spiritually based divine knowledge. Thereafter he achieves the devotion of Siva.

The devotion generates love, love generates Sravana, Sravana creates Satsanga after which a noble preceptor is found.

Thus with the achieving of the knowledge, the person is freed, one who becomes wise, he always adores Siva.

A person who adores Siva with unblemished devotion, he ultimately achieves salvation at the end. There is no doubt about it.

There is no other god better than Siva, to grant salvation and by taking refuge with him, a person is liberated from the universe.

O Brahmanas, thus I have repeated to you the advisory nature of words, of the Rsis which should be accepted by you making all the efforts.

Initially, this knowledge was imparted by Siva to Visnu in front of a Sivalinga. Visnu passed on the knowledge to Brahma, who in turn passed on the same to Sanaka and other great sages.

Sanaka and others revealed the knowledge to Narada who repeated the same to the sage Vyasa and he spoke it to me.

I have repeated the same to you for the welfare of the people and you should preserve this knowledge which helps in achieving Siva, making all the efforts.

O Excellent sages, I have thus spoken to you all that had been desired by you. You keep it secret making all the efforts. What more do you want to listen from me?

Vyasa said, “On hearing this, the ascetics were immensely delighted and offering their salutation, they prayed to him with choked voice.

The Rsis said, “O Disciple of Vyasa, salutation to you. You are blessed and are an excellent devotee of Siva. You have bestowed on us the best knowledge of Siva.

By your grace, all the doubts of our minds have been removed. We feel blessed by receiving the excellent knowledge about Siva, which bestows salvation. We are indeed blessed.

Suta said, “This knowledge should not be imparted to an atheist, an unfaithful person, or a rogue. Nor should it be imparted to the one who is not devoted to Siva or the one who does not want to hear it.

After studying the historical treatises, the Puranas, Vedas and the Sastras, a number of times, Vyasa collected this essence and imparted it to me.

After once listening to it, all the sins are removed. An atheist becomes a devotee, besides enhancing the devotion of a devotee.

By hearing it repeatedly, one attains good devotion. By its repeated hearing, the liberation is achieved. Therefore this should be heard repeatedly by the devotees desirous of achieving the benefit of the worldly pleasures besides the salvation.

For the achieving of the enormous benefits it should be repeated at least five times.” Vyast said, by doing so, he would attain Salvador and there is no doubt about it.

Nothing is beyond the reach of this knowledge. Whosoever has heard of this excellent glory, by reciting it five times, one comes face to face with Siva.

Several of the Brahmanas, kings and the Vaisyas, achieved the supreme success by listening to this five times.

Even today, whosoever, having been filled with devotion, would listen to the discourse on Siva, he would also achieve devotion as well as salvation.”

Vyasa said, “Thus listening to his words all the Rsis respectfully offered several of the things and adored Suta.

The offered their salutation to Suta reciting Svastivacana and several other stotras, praised him, and feeling free from all the doubts, they blessed him.

O Suta, all of them possessing the noble wisdom, feeling pleased, conceiving Siva to be Paramesvara, adored him, eulogising him at the same time.

This story of Siva is quite dear to him. Enhancing one’s devotion to Siva, it bestows devotion as well as the salvation.

This Koti-Rudra Samhita is the fourth one besides being blissful which has been described by me.

Whosoever listens to it carefully with devotion or recites it, he enjoying all the pleasures in this world, achieves salvation ultimately.

Thus ends the forth Koti-rudra Samhita of Siva Mahapurana

## Uma Samhita

## Chapter 1 - Krsna’s meeting with Upamanyu

The Supreme soul, who supports the seven worlds, with the use of *Sattvaguna,* and sustains them as well, the one who resorts to creation with the application of *rajoguna,* and resorting to *tamoguna* destroys the same, the one who is far away from the *Maya* (illusion) of the *gunas,* we meditate upon such a blissful, lord possessing spotless knowledge, who is truth, bliss infinite, pure consciousness, who assumes the names of Brahma, Visnu etc. and who is attained only with the application of eternal *Sattvaguna*.

The *Rsis* said, “O Suta, O Intelligent one, the disciple of Vyasa, salutation to you. You have narrated the fourth Koti-Rudra Samhita to us.

Now you kindly narrate the story of Siva, the supreme soul and Uma or Parvati comprising of several incidents.”

Suta said, “O Saunaka and other great sages, you listen to the story of Siva which bestows the devotion and salvation, quite lovingly.

The same auspicious question was similarly put by Vyasa *to* Sanatkumara, who then narrated the story of Siva.

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, the great sage Upamanyu had narrated the said story to lord Krsna, the same story of Siva is being repeated by me to you.

In earlier times, Sri Krsna, the son of Vasudeva, intended to adore Siva for the getting of a son and for that purpose he went to Kailasa- the abode of Siva.

He found the sage Upamanyu performing the *tapas* to whom Krsna offered his salutation with folded hands.

Lord Krsna said, “O Great devotee of Siva, having noble wisdom, O Sage Upamanyu, I have arrived here to perform *tapas* near the abode of Siva, for getting a son.

O Sage, you kindly enlighten me about the blissful glory of Siva, listening to which I may be able to perform the penance for Siva with devotion.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of learned Sri Krsna, the sage Upamanyu, recalling the name of Siva, spoke to him.

Upamanyu said, “O Krsna, the great devotee of Siva, I shall narrate to you the enormous glory of Siva, which has been witnessed by me.

While performing *tapas* I had seen Siva, his literature, his family besides Visnu and other gods.

All the three gods including Brahma and others were shining with him. He was of permanent happiness besides being imperishable. He had one foot, and huge feet with mouths with blazing flames.

He was illumining with a thousand rays, holding all the excellent weapons, having several eyes and a thousand feet.

He is the one who at the end of the *kalpa* surely destroys the world. There is none in the three worlds among the mobiles and the immobiles, who can escape death from him.

Lord Mahadeva, had reduced to ashes in a moment, all the mobiles and immobiles emerging from his arms together with the three worlds.

While I was engaged in *tapas* I found the eternal Siva, quite close to me together with his secret weapon. There is no other weapon comparable to it in the world.

The trident bearer has the weapon of victory which is known as the trident in the world. It is the destroyer of all the weapons.

It can undoubtedly tear out the entire earth, can dry out the ocean, and can make all the star to fall on earth. It is the same weapon.

It is the same trident which killed Yauvanasva, which had killed the great king Mandhata who was quite powerful, illustrious, conqueror of the three worlds, besides being a Cakravarti king.

With the same trident Haihaya and Lavanasura kings were killed. Lavanasura was killed by inviting Satrughna.

After the death of the demon when the trident reached the hands of Siva its top portion was sharpened and became frightening.

It stood as if threatening all with its three spikes for its knit eyebrows. It resembled the blazing fire without smoke, and the rising sun.

I also saw the battle-axe with sharp edges decorated with the serpents. It looked awful like, the god of death holding the noose in his hand. It resembled the ray of the sun which was beyond description or the features of the sun at the end of the *kalpas.* It was of the size of a fully grown man. Bhargava Rama has used it in the battle of killing the Ksatriyas.

It was given to Rama by Siva in earlier times. With the strength of this battle axe, the delighted sage burnt the Ksatriyas, twenty one times.

I saw the Sudarsana Cakra in the shape of a human being with a thousand heads and two thousand hands. It was divine and lordly.

It was illustrious, with two thousand eyes, a thousand feet and having the brilliance resembling the crores of suns, which was competent enough to bum all the three worlds at a time.

It had the extremely brilliant lustre, had a hundred knots, the best of *Vajra.* He had the great bow named Pinaka besides the quiver with arrows.

I also saw the weapons like Sakti, sword, noose, illustrious goad, the divine club besides several other weapons.

I saw the weapons possessed by the Lokapalas of the quarters on either side of lord Rudra..

To the right of Mahadeva, the grand sire of all the *lokas,* with his vehicle- the Swan, and the plan which moved at will, was also there.

To his left Narayana holding the *Samkha, cakra* and *gada* was lodged mounted over Garuda- the divine bird.

Indra, Svayambhuva Manus, Bhrgu and other *Rsis,* all went with him.

Skanda holding a *Sakti* and the bell, mounted over the peacock, Parvati like the second Agni, arrived and took their seats close to Siva. Then Nandi holding a trident in his hand, was seated in front of the lord.

All the Ganas, mothers and the goblins were present there.

All the gods offering their salutation to Siva, started offering prayer to him, surrounding him.

Whatever is visible or heard in the universe, was found possessed by Siva, which surprised me.

O Sri Krsna, in the said *yajna,* I becoming extremely peaceful, recited *stotras* with folded hands, and was drowned in the eternal bliss.

Finding Siva in front, with tears flowing from my eyes and choked voice, I worshipped Siva with great devotion.

Then feeling delighted, Lord Siva, lovingly spoke to me with his sweet voice with great pleasure;

O Brahmana, I put you to test several times. You cannot be separated from me. Let you meet with welfare and your devotion in me should stabilise.

O *Suvrata,* I am pleased with you. You ask for a boon you desire. A boon which is beyond the reach of other gods the same could be granted to you.”

Listening to the words from the mouth of Siva, I then spoke to Siva, who is compassionate on his devotees.

O Lord, in case you are pleased with me, in case I am fully devoted to you, then I should be aware of the truth, relating to all the three times (present, past and future).

I should have an unfailing devotion in you and all the people of my race should get enough of milk and rice.

O Lord, I should always reside close to your abode, and should always remain friendly with your devotees.

O Best of Yadus, when the words were thus spoken by me, Siva, the Paramesvara, cast a compassionate glance at me and said to me.

Lord Siva said, “O Upamanyu, O Sage, O Dear one, you shall be free from the blemishes of the old age and death. All your desires shall be fulfilled.

Being glorious you will be adorable among the *Rsis.* By my grace, you will possess humility, beauty, virtues, and all the. fortunes.

O Sage, you will remain close to the ocean of milk and you can reach anywhere you desire to do so.

Till such time the nectar like ocean of milk will remain, you will find all the kiths and kins with you in the Vaivasvata *kalpa.*

O Great sage, because of my compassion on you, your race will be everlasting and I shall be easily available to you in your abode.

O Son, my devotion will always remain lodged in your mind. I shall appear before you whenever you call me.

You can enjoy all the pleasures on earth at will. There is no cause of worry. Whatever you desire, it would be granted.”

Upamanyu said, “Thus speaking, lord Siva whose lustre resembled crores of suns, disappeared, bestowing the boon on me.

O Krsna, I have thus witnessed Siva with his entire family, who bestows devotion as well as salvation.

Whatever, the learned Siva, the supreme lord had spoken to me, had been achieved by me because of the adoration of Siva.

I myself witnessed there the Gandharvas, the *apsaras, Rsis*, Vidyadharas, and the Siddhas.

I had a look at the beautiful trees endowed with glossy leaves, fragrant with seasonal flowers, besides flowering trees and laden with fruits.

O Mighty hero, all what I got was due to the grace of Siva, the great soul, and the lord of gods.

The divine knowledge is possessed by me due to the grace of Siva, as a result of which, I remain aware of the happening in the past, present and future.

O Deva, Suresvara, I have seen the lord, who is beyond the reach of even the great gods, without propitiating. Who could be more graceful than I?

The eternal principles are known to be twenty six, which are well-known. Thus the learned people, adore the Aksara-Brahman.

The great lord alone is aware of the well- ordained principles and directs knower of all the true objects, besides being the lord of *Purusa* and *Prakrti.*

It was Siva alone, who created Brahma from his right side and Visnu from his left side for the protection or sustenance of the world

At the ends of the *kalpa* Siva created Rudra from his heart who destroyed the entire mobile and immobile creatures of the world.

At the end of the dissolution, the same Mahadeva, after destruction of the mobile and immobile creatures or devouring them, remains stable.

He is Sadasiva, omniscient, cause of all the living beings, all pervading, and visible to all the gods.

Therefore, you for the purpose of getting a son, adore Siva, who being well disposed towards his devotees, would soon be pleased with you.

## Chapter 2 - Upamayu’s instructions to Krsna, for adoring Siva

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the great sage Upamanyu, and developing of the devotion for Siva in his heart, Krsna then said to the great sage.

Sri Krsna said, “O Dear one, O Sage Upamanyu, being graceful on me, you enlighten me on the subject as to who were the people, who became successful by adoring Siva, getting their desires fulfilled.

Sanatkumara said, “Then Upamanyu- the foremost of the devotees of Siva, listening to the words of Sri Krsna, praised him. Thereafter the sage who was the ocean of compassion said to Sri Krsna.”

Upamanyu said, “Those of the devotees of Siva, who, after adoring Siva, got the desired rewards, the stories of such devotees are being related by me in brief, which should be listened by you. O Best of the Yadavas.

Hiranyakasipu, first of all, gained the glory and the suzerainty over all the gods for a period of a million years by adoring the Candrasekhara Siva.

His excellent son Nandana had been quite popular. By achieving a boon from Siva, he subjugated Indra and ruled over him for ten thousand years.

O Krsna, the awful discus of Visnu, and the *Vajra* of Indra were shattered against their enemy Nandana in the battle with the mere touch of his body.

In the body of the immensely valorous Rahu, because of his performing *tapas* for Siva, none of the weapons like *cakra, vajra* or other weapons, could be effective.

The gods were being tortured by that cruel planet. The Raksasas getting boon from the gods tortured them immensely.

Siva, the lord of the three worlds, getting pleased with the *tapas* of the demon for a hundred thousand years, bestowed the lordship of the three worlds to the demon possessing the lustre of the lightning.

Besides this, Siva also gave him a thousand powerful sons, and declared that he would always remain his servant.

Lord Siva then gave him the prosperous kingdom in the Kusadvipa. O Sri Krsna, thus lord Siva was pleased with him.

A hundred years earlier, Brahma, had created that particular demon with the name of Satamakha. After adoring Siva, he got a boon for having a hundred powerful sons.

The sage Yajnavalkya who is well known in the Vedas, received the best of knowledge by adoring Siva.

Adoring Siva, Vedavyasa, achieved the divine knowledge of three times, besides enormous glory.

The Balakhilya sages who had been humiliated by Indra, achieved Garuda who had brought nectar.

In earlier time there developed the scarcity of water because of Siva getting annoyed. Then the gods performed a *Yajna* relating to Siva through *Samkalpa,* and made the water to flow again.

Anusuya, the chaste wife of the sage Atri, observed fast for three hundred years, sleeping only on the reeds. She then achieved the three sons Dattatreya, the moon and the sage Durvasa and her sanctity made the Ganga to flow in Chitrakuta.

O Madhusudana, you please lord Siva, who makes his devotees comfortable and by doing so Vikrama achieved great success.

Citrasena, with his firm devotion towards Siva, pleasing Siva, became free from the danger of all the kings and achieved unparalled comforts.

Srikara, the son of a Gopi (milkmaid), by observing the *Siva puja* performed by a king had his mind filled with the devotion of Siva as a result of which he achieved the supreme success.

O Sri Krsna, Citrangada- the prince, had his wife known as Simantini, over whom lord Siva had been quite graceful, as a result of which he could not die even after his drowning in the river Yamuna.

He, reaching the abode of Taksakaraja in the nether world, made friends with him and carrying enormous riches he returned to his abode.

O Srikrsna, his wife Simantini was observing a fast on a Monday, therefore, she, by the grace of Siva achieved the best of fortunes.

In earlier times, the son of a Brahmana, overpowered with greed, deceitfully took to the form of a woman and because of the influence of the same, he was turned as a woman for all times to come.

In earlier times, the wicked and the fallen woman Cancuka, listened to the religious story of Siva from the son of a Brahmana, with devotion, after which she achieved salvation.

Because of the grace of his wife Cancuka, known as a Brahmana Binduga achieved Sivaloka listening to Siva Purana.

Pingala the whore and the degraded Brahmana named Madara, after adoring Siva Mahadeva achieved salvation.

A whore named Mahananda, because of her firm devotion at the feet of Siva, pleased the lord, and achieved salvation.

Kaikeyi and Sadara, the daughters of a Brahmana, enjoyed all the pleasures by performing the *vratas* of Siva.

O Sri Krsna, in earlier times a king named Vimarsana devoting himself towards Siva, and by the grace of the lord, achieved the supreme position (salvation).

A sinful king named Durjana, who had fallen for many women, he also getting detached from his deeds, attained the place of Siva, by adoring the lord.

Sabara- the Bhila, with his wife and Sankara, applying ashes over their bodies, used to perform the *Vratas* of Siva. Because of that they achieved salvation.

O Sri Krsna, a Candala woman named Saumini adored Siva unmindfully as a result of which, she by the grace of Siva, achieved the place of Siva.

A hunter named Mahakala who lived on killing others, achieved the best of place, by adoring Siva.

Durvasa- the great sage, in earlier times had propagated the devotion of Siva which bestowed salvation according to his faith.

A Ksatriya who was none else than Visvamitra himself, was turned into Brahmana in this very life like Brahma by adoring Siva the bestower of welfare to the world.

O Sri Krsna, Brahma- the grand sire of the universe, became the creator in the world, by adoring Siva with devotion.

O Hari, the excellent sage and devotee of Siva, Markandeya- the great lord, enjoyed the long life by the grace of Siva.

O Sri Krsna, Devaraja Indra, the excellent devotee of Siva, became the lord of all the gods due to the grace of lord Siva.

Bana- the son of Bali was a great devotee of Siva, who had controlled all his senses. He became the leader of the universe, because of grace of lord Siva.

Hari, Dadhici, Sakti, Mahesvara and Rama- all of them because of their devotion became the devotees of Siva. Further due to the devotion to Siva, Kanada, Bhargava, Guru and Gautama, became powerful and all competent.

O Krsna, the great *Rsi* Sakalya having the praiseworthy soul, adored Siva, mentally for nine hundred years.

Feeling pleased with his *tapas,* lord Siva said, “O Son, you would be the composer of the literature and your infallible glory will spread in the world.

Your race would produce the great sages, and become everlasting. You will yourself compose the Sutra-literature.”

The excellent sage thus received the boon from lord Siva. O Son of the race of Yadus, the said *Rsi* became popular and adorable in the world.

He became Savarni *Rsi* of the Satayuga. He performed *tapas* in this world for eight hundred years.

O Sinless one, I am pleased with you. You shall be the composer of literature (books), and remain eternal and indestructible.

In this way only those people worship Siva, who have to their credit the accumulated merits of the earlier births. Lord Siva also bestows boons for granting their wishes, when adored by such devotees.

In fact, the merits and qualities of Siva cannot be described by me from my mouth even in a hundred years.

## Chapter 3 - The glory of Siva

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the sage Upamanyu, Sri Krsna felt surprised and then he spoke to the sage with a peaceful mind.

Vasudeva said, “O great Brahmana, you are indeed graceful, close to whose abode, there resides Siva, the lord of gods. Then who can adore a person like you?

O Excellent sage, will the lord Siva grant me his vision? Will he do me this favour?

Upamanyu said, “O Best of the humans, you will soon have an audience with him, by his grace.

O Hari, on the sixteenth month from now, you will receive boon from Siva and Parvati. How shall the lord not grant you the boon?

O Acyuta, because of your praiseworthy virtues, you will be respected by all the gods. I shall tell you a *mantra* for reciting, O Adorable one.

With the influence of the muttering of that *mantra.* You will really have an audience with Siva and will get a son resembling you by the grace of Siva.

O Hari, *“Om namah Sivaya”* is the suitable and the best of the *mantras.* This divine *mantra* fulfills all the desires, besides bestowing the worldly pleasures as well as salvation.”

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, thus, narrating the stories relating to lord Mahadeva, eight days were passed like a *muhurta (2 &frac12; gharis*) .

On the ninth day, he was initiated and was instructed in Siva's mantra, the great one mentioned in the Atharvaveda.

Immediately he grew matted locks of hair and then he got himself clean shaven. With his immensely pure mind, he started performing *tapas* standing on the big toes of the feet, lifting his hands upwards at the same time.

On the arrival of the sixteenth months, lord Siva was pleased, who accompanied with Parvati appeared before him and granted him the divine vision.

Sri Krsna found Siva with Parvati, having three eyes, in the form of Candrasekhara and being eulogised by Brahma and other gods, besides the crores of siddhas.

He was wearing a divine garland and the divine garments. He was adorned with all the ornaments and being eulogised by the gods and demons offering their salutation to the lord with all humility.

He was full of all the surprises, unborn and imperishable lord. He was accompanied with various *ganas* and his two sons.

Sri Krsna looked at him with his hands folded in surprise, and he felt delightful, by looking at him.

Sri Krsna adored Siva reciting several of the *stotras.* Thereafter, he lowering his head recited the *Sivasahasranama stotra.*

Then the gods, Gandharvas, Vidyadharas, the great serpents, showered flowers and praised him with delight.

Lord Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, feeling pleased and looking at Parvati, spoke to Sri Krsna.

Mahadeva said, “O Krsna, I know you well, you are immensely devoted towards me. You ask for the boons which are beyond the reach of anyone in the three worlds.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of lord Siva, Sri Krsna, offered his salutation to him again and again, and then spoke to him.

Sri Krsna said, “O God of gods, O Mahadeva, O Lord, I seek the boons, from you about which I have already thought over.

Let my mind always remain devoted towards you. I should have everlasting glory, closeness to you, and my everlasting devotion towards you should always remain.

Let me have ten sons from my ten chief queens, who should kill the enemies in the battle field who should be proud of their strength.

O Lord, my enemies should never be able to humiliate me anywhere. I should be respected by the *yogis* as well.

O God of gods, salutation to you. You bestow these eight excellent boons on me. You are the lord of all and you are particularly my lord.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to these words of Sri Krsna, lord Siva spoke to him, “All what has been desired by you shall be done.” Siva again said.

“Your son named Samba, will be extremely powerful. He shall be cursed by the illustrious sage Samvartakaditya.

He will be your son in human form. Whatever has been asked for by you will be achieved.”

Sanatkumara said, “Thus receiving all the boons from Siva Sri Krsna, pleased Siva with various *stotras.*

Parvati too who also loved her devotees, feeling pleased, spoke to Vasudeva, the devotee of Siva, feeling delighted.”

Parvati said, “O Sinless one, O learned one, O Vasudeva Krsna I am pleased with you. You also receive the divine boons from me.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to these words of Parvati, Sri Krsna, the best of the race of Yadus, spoke to her with devotion.”

Sri Krsna said, “In case, O Goddess. You are pleased with me, and are ready to bestow boons on me, then the Brahmanas should never be envious of me because of my *tapas* and I should always adore the Brahmanas. Let my parents always remain happy with me.

Wherever I go, all the living beings should remain favourable to me. Let me always be born in a noble family, because of my having an audience with you.

Let me please Indra and other gods, the ascetics besides thousands of guests by performing a hundred *yajnas.*

Let me be able to serve them auspicious food in my house and I should love all my kiths and kins.

O Goddess, let me be loveable to a thousand damsels and O Sankari, I should always remain devoted to your grace.

O Parvati, let their parents be the speakers of truth, in the world. O Parvati, thanks to your grace, let these as well as the other boons take effect.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Sri Krsna, the eternal goddess, who fulfills all the desires feeling wonderful said, “Be it so.”

Thus showering his noble grace over Sri Krsna, Parvati and Paramesvara Siva, bestowing all types of boons, disappeared from the scenes.

O Great sage, “Thereafter Sri Krsna considered himself to have been blessed. Thereafter, he went back to the hermitage of the sage Upamanyu.

Reaching there the killer of Kesin (Sri Krsna), offered his salutation to the sage Upamanyu lowering his head and apprised him of the factual position (relating to his audience) with Siva and Parvati.

Upamanyu said, “O Janardana, there is no god comparable to Siva in bestowing of the great gifts and unbearable when infuriated.

O Krsna of great fame, listen to the lordly glory of Siva and his perfect knowledge, austerity, bravery and fortitude in dangers.

On hearing thus the devotion of Sri Krsna towards Siva was enhanced. Then he asked him about Siva’s glory and the great sage thus spoke to him.

Upamanyu said, “In earlier times in Brahmaloka, Siva was eulogised by reciting his thousand names by the noble soul Brahma bearing the staff.

Those well-versed in the *samkhya* philosophy recite the song of prayer as if it were a big lexicon The hymns bestows all the desires on me though inscrutable to them.

O Krsna, now you return to your abode recalling the name of Siva regularly. O Dear one, you would always be the foremost of the devotees of Siva.”

When so allowed by the sage Upamanyu, Krsna, the son of Vasudeva made salutation to the sage and returned to Dvaraka, reciting the name of Siva, mentally.

Sanatkumara said, “O Great Krsna sage, was then quite satisfied and invincible after worshipping Siva who benefits the whole world

O Excellent sage, Rama, the son of Dasaratha, because of his devotion towards Siva, also became successful in his enterprises and was victorious always.

O Sage, Sri Rama, performing severe *tapas* over the mountain top, received the divine knowledge from Siva together with the bow and arrow as boons.

Then he crossing the ocean, after building a bridge over it, killed Ravana with his family and getting back Sita, he returned to his abode. Thereafter, he ruled the entire world.

Similarly, Parasurama, finding that his father had been killed by the Ksatriyas. Feeling painful he adored Siva.

He pleased the lord and receiving a sharp edged battle-axe from Siva, he exterminated the Ksatriyas from the earth, twenty one times.

Parasurama- the ascetic is invincible and eternal even today. He adores Siva daily even today and can be seen by the Siddhas and the *Carana.*

Sri Rama is performing *tapas* at the Mahendra mountain. At the end of the *kalpa* he shall again achieve the position of an ascetic.

The ascetic Devala the brother of Asita, performed hard *tapas* to win the grace of lord Siva- the root of the universe.

He had been cursed by Indra, but he by adored *Sivalinga,* who fulfils the desires of all, and removes the past evils.

Ghrtsamada- the son of Caksusamanu became a deer in the forest as a result of a curse pronounced on him by the sage Vasistha. He used to wander lonely in the forest.

He always used to recall the name of Siva in his mind with the *Pranava mantra.* After his death, he became a *gana* having the face of a deer.

By so reciting the *japam*, he was ultimately freed from the curse and becoming imperishable and eternal, he became the follower of Ganesa.

Siva, who always roamed about at will, bestowed on the sage Garga a boon which was rare in the world, besides the ability to visit the holy places as he liked. He was also bestowed the knowledge of all the times besides the prosperity and the eternal mastery of the words of the four Vedas. He was also granted a hundred peerless sons as well.

Parasara was also granted a boon by Siva, who was pleased with him and he got a powerful yogi as the son, who was free from old age and death. He was known as Vedavyasa.

The sage Mandavya, who had been fixed to the top of the trident (for crucification) for a million of years, was released by Siva, bestowing his life back to him.

Once a poor householder Brahmana placed his son Galava in the house of his preceptor.

He hid himself in the house of the sage. Whenever a beggar arrived in his house, then he said to his wife, “He is surely a poor man.

You tell him that your husband is not visible in the house. What shall I give him remaining in the house?

Thereafter a hungry and thirsty guest arrived in the house of the Brahmana and asked the lady about her husband.

She replied, “My husband is not visible in the house.” The sage found out the truth with his divine sight he said to the lady, “The Brahmana is hiding in the house and has met with his death.”

Then at the instance of Visvamitra, his son Galava returned home and heard from his mother.

Galava, the son of the Brahmana reached his home and listening to the harsh curse of his mother, he adored Siva.

Reciting the name of Siva in his heart, he came out of the house. Finding his son coming, the father said with folded hands.

“I have been successful by the grace of Siva. I have regained my life after death and have been bestowed with the son and riches.”

I have narrated the qualities of Siva in brief, the exhaustive discussion of which cannot be narrated by Sesanaga with all its hoods.

## Chapter 4 - Display of Siva’s Maya

The sages said, “O Dear one, O Great sage, O Immensely learned one, you are indeed blessed. You have narrated the excellent and wonderful story of lord Siva.

According to the questions of Vyasa, you kindly repeat the story of Siva again. You are well aware of the *Sivatattva,* besides being omniscient and the disciple of the sage Vyasa.

Suta said, “In this way my preceptor Vyasa had asked Sanatkumara who was omniscient, devoted to Siva and an excellent sage besides being the son of Brahma.

Vyasa said, “O Omniscient one, O Sanatkumara, you have narrated the auspicious story of lord Mahadeva who indulges in many sports.

O Dear one, you again speak out the glory of Siva particularly. The faith in my mind to listen to the same is ever on increase.

Lord Siva who performs various type of sports, whose *Maya* deprived the people of wisdom, deluding them at the same time, you kindly narrate that episode.

Sanatkumara said, “O Immensely intelligent Vyasa, you listen to the pleasing story of Siva, with the mere listening to which the devotion towards Siva enhances.

Siva is the lord of all the gods. He is the soul of all besides being the vision of all. His glory pervades in the entire world.

Brahma and Visnu are the other forms of Siva. He happens to be the soul of all the living beings. He is represented in the form of *linga* besides being the form of *Sattva, Rajas* and *Tamas.*

The gods have eight types of *yonis.* The ninth one is the *yoni* of the humans. There are five *yonis* of animals and the birds. Then there are fourteen *yonis* in all. All the living being in the past, present and future are born of Siva and they ultimately get absorbed in him.

Brahma, Visnu, Indra, moon, the gods, Danavas, serpents, Gandharvas, the humans, besides all the kiths and kins, friends, *acaryas,* guards, the leaders, the preceptors, *kalpavrksa,* brothers, father, besides the mother have all the form of Siva.

Siva is all pervading, he is to be known by the people, or self manifest to all the sins. He is greater than the greatest. Nothing could be spoken abut him, and there is nothing greater than him in the world.

His *Maya* is divine and supreme. O Sage, he is all pervading. All the gods, demons, humans and others in the world are subservient to him.

Associating himself with the powerful desires of the mind, Siva had made subservient Visnu and other powerful gods.

O Excellent sage, with influence of the *Maya* of Siva, Visnu, having been overpowered with the *Maya* of Siva enjoyed the company of others wives

Indra, inspite of being the king of the gods fell for the beauty of Ahalya, the wife of Gautama and the wicked person committed a sin. Sage Gautama then pronounced a curse on Indra.

Agni, the best god in the world, because of the influence of *Sivamaya* was overpowered by the passion. Thanks to Siva who ultimately redeemed him.

O Vyasa, Vayu the life of the universe, also having been overpowered with the *Maya* of Siva, became subservient to Kamadeva and enjoyed the company of other’s wife.

The sun god too because of the influence of the *Maya* of Siva, becoming lustful, transformed himself into a horse for the sake of a mare.

Having been influenced with the *Maya* of Siva, the moon enjoyed the company of the wife of the preceptor ultimately, it was Siva alone, who redeemed the moon.

In earlier times two sages known as Mitra and Varuna, too were overpowered by the *Maya* of Siva.

At the sight of Urvasi, both of them became lustful. Then Mitra dropped his semen in a pitcher and Varuna did so in the water.

Thereafter Mitra’s son Vasistha was born of the pitcher and the sage Agastya resplendent like the oceanic fire was born from the ocean.

Daksaprajapati- the son of Brahma, under the influence of *Sivamaya,* got ready to enjoy the company of his own sister with his brothers.

Brahma several times under the influence of the *Maya* of Siva developed the desire to enjoy the company of his own daughter as well as with other’s daughters.

Cyavana- the great *yogi* too, under the influence of Siva *Maya,* enjoyed the company of Sukanya.

Under the influence of the *Maya* of Siva, Kasyapa, getting lustful, begged for the daughter of the king Sudhama.

Garuda, under delusion, desired the girl Sandili, as a result of which his feathers were scorched.

The sage Vibhandaka too was felled with passion at the sight of a woman. His son Rsyasrnga was born as per the desire of Siva from a doe.

Under the influence of the *Maya* of Siva, sage Gautama at the sight of naked Saradavati, enjoyed her company. He was excited and enjoyed the sexual intercourse with her.

The sage then deposited his semen in a wooden bowl from which Dronacarya, the best among the archers was born.

The sage Parasara, under the influence of the *Maya* of Siva, enjoyed sexual pleasures with Matsyodari, a damsel born of a fisherman’s family.

O Vyasa, Visvamitra, the great sage also under the influence of *Sivamaya* had a sexual exercise with Menaka in the forest.

It was due to ignorance that Visvamitra became inimical to the sage Vasistha. He was then transformed into a Brahmana, by the grace of Siva.

Under the influence of the delusion of Siva, the evil-minded Ravana- the son of Visrava, becoming lustful, abducted Sita and ultimately he had to face death because of the same.

Brhaspati- the excellent sage too with the delusion of Siva enjoyed the company of the wife of his brother as a result of which Bharavaja was born.

O Vyasa, thus I have narrated the influence of the *Maya* of Siva. What else do you want to listen from me?

## Chapter 5 - The grave sins

Vyasa said, “O Son of Brahma, O Lord, salutation to you. Now you spell out the sinful *jivas* who are destined to fall in hell.”

Sanatkumara said, “Those who indulge in performing sinful deeds, as a result of which they have to fall in the hell, are being described now. You listen to me attentively.

The mental sins comprise of having a desire in mind for usurping the riches and the wives of others, to wish evil of others, to get inclined towards performing of evil deeds mentally. These are the four mental sins.

Keeping of evil company, indulging in falsehood, and speaking of evil words and indulging in back-biting are the four types of sins of speech.

To eat forbidden food, to indulge in terror, to insist on evil doing, to usurp the riches of others, are the sins committed by the body.

Thus there are twelve types of sins committed by body, speech and the mind. Now I shall speak on their divisions, besides the reward of each one of them.

Those who are inimical to Siva who make people to cross the ocean of the universe, they are liable to go to hell, earning the grave sins.

Those who denounce the ascetic narrating *Sivakatha,* the preceptor and the parents, such foolish people fall in the hell.

Those who denounce Siva, the preceptor, find fault in the knowledge of Siva, steal the riches of the gods, and destroy the wealth of the Brahmanas.

Those fools who steal away *Siva Purana* and other scriptures, attract the six grave sins which are painful upto the last moment.

Those who do not feel happy at the *Sivapuja* performed by others, who do not offer salutation to Siva nor eulogise Siva, and indulge in their usual activities as before with pleasure, who do not bow in reverence to the preceptor and Siva, those who while engaged in *karmayoga,* do not scrub, clean and sanctify the spot of worship during the days of worshiper festivities, or adore the preceptors, or do not co-operate with them in the performance of their religious rites, those who misbehave as they please, become jealous of the devotees of Siva, who write or recite the literature on Siva, without adoring it, those who donate without justification, those who listen or recite indiscriminately, those who sport about covetously or those who pursue the false knowledge and lodge the lord at unclean spots, those who interpolate in the scriptures of Siva and narrate something else, those who do not speak the truth, do not give charities, the one who being himself unclean, sitting in an unclean place narrates the auspicious stories of the lord, the one who tries to listen to the Puranas without adoring the preceptor, who do not serve the preceptor with devotion or does not serve or obeys his command, who showing disrespect to the orator of the scriptures, raises useless controversies showing disrespect to him, who disowns the sinful, ailing, helpless, or the one surrounded by the enemies or the preceptor who has left for some other place.

Who disobeys the preceptor, his son, or the friends, or refuses to obey the words of the narrator of the scriptures, the preceptor discoursing on *dharma.*

O best of the sages, all these activities have been equated with the denouncing of Siva and said the greatest sins.

Besides killing of a Brahmana, drinking of wine, having illicit relations with the wife of the preceptor, a thief or his associate have been described as the grave sinners.

A person who believes that there is no sin in killing a Brahmana in anger, out of greed, fear or because of enmity, earns the sin of killing a Brahmana.

A person who first gives charities to a Brahmana, after inviting him and them gets them back, or finds fault with a faultless Brahmana, he too earn the sin of killing a Brahmana.

A person because of his arrogance of being learned humiliates a learned as and unattached Brahmana, in the assembly, he is treated to be the killer of the Brahmana.

The one who thinks his son’s false merits as great and under estimates the good qualities of others, he is treated to be the killer of the Brahmana.

The one who causes obstruction when the cow and the bull are mating, or the Brahmanas when they seek protection, is called the slayer of the Brahmana.

A person who usurps the land given to the gods, Brahmanas or for the use of the cows, even after the expiry of the date of lease, is called the slayer of Brahmana.

The misappropriation of wealth, of the deity or a Brahmana and the wealth earned by improper means, is no less than the killing of a Brahmana and there is no doubt about it.

In case a Brahmana, even after acquiring the knowledge of Vedic literature, besides of a Brahmana and Siva, and then being desirous of the same, indulges in sinful ways, he earns the sin equal the drinking of wine.

The discarding of any of the *Vrata, yajna* rules or regulations, besides discarding of *Brahmayajna* makes one earn a sin equivalent to the drinking of wine.

To disown the parents, give false evidence, to tell a lie before a Brahmana, eating of meat, to eat something which is forbidden for consumption by the devotees of Siva, to kill the innocent beings in the forest, or refusing to lay down ones life for the sake of a Brahmana, an ascetic or *dharma,* or to put on fire the path used by the movement of cows, the forest or the village makes; one earn the sin of *Brahmahatya.*

The usurping of the property of a poor person, and selling it by a Brahmana knowingly (done except in grave emergency) a man, woman, elephant, horse, cow, land silver, cloth, medicinal herbs, juices, sandal paste, *Agaru* camphor, musk, silk garments etc., and misappropriation of the deposit kept in trust, are the sins equal to the theft of gold. Not to marry the daughter of marriageable age to a suitable groom, to cohabit with daughter- in-law, friends’ wife, sister, maiden and a drunkard woman, and the, woman of high caste, amount to cohabiting with wife of the preceptor. These are the grave sins which have been highlighted by me. Now you listen about the minor sins.

## Chapter 6 - The minor sins

Sanatkumara said, “To usurp the wealth of a Brahmana, or to misappropriate the share of others, to be infested with extreme arrogance, cheating, ungratefulness, or to become lustful, to indulge in miserliness, to be envious of the noble people, cohabiting with other’s wife, to find fault with gentle girls.

Parivitti (the situation in which the younger brother marries, when the elder brother is still unmarried) or Parivetr (the younger brother who thus marries), by giving daughter to these two or to allow them to perform *yajnas,* the spoiling of trees and flowers around the temple of Siva, or even the slightest injury to the hermits, the theft of cattle, grain, wealth etc., of the family of one’s own servants, theft of base metals, food grains, and milch cattle, besides making the water dirty, selling of the places of performing *yajnas,* or tanks, wives and children, pilgrimages or fasts, sacred rites and investiture with sacred thread.

Depending on dowry, servitude to women, failure to save the women, developing illicit affairs with woman by illicit means, failing to return the debt in time, receiving grain as interest to loans, accepting of monetary gifts from the degraded people, adopting unfair means in business, using bullock constantly as a vehicle through the wild forest, resort to *uccatana* (exercising) an *abhicara* (black magic), accepting of grains as gifts, or working as a physician, engagement in sacred rites to satisfy the palate or the sexual urge, teaching only the text of the Vedas and not its meaning,

Discarding the *Sanatana dharma* and converting to other religion, study of improper literature, taking refuge under useless arguments,

To denounce the gods, fire, preceptor, ascetics, Brahmana and the Cakravarti monarch in their presence or absence,

To abandon sacrifice to gods and manes, to abandon their duties and rites, persons of evil conduct, atheists, sinners and habitual liars,

Indulging of intercourse during the new moon or the full moon during the day time or the vaginal passage of animals, or by other means or emitting the semen in water, or to cohabit with a woman during the period of menstruation,

Or those shatter the hopes of obtaining wives, sons and friends, speaking of displeasing words, the ruthless persons or those who break agreements,

Those who destroy the wells or the tanks, sellers of juices, or the one who differentiates among the people seated for food,

Such types of persons or those who indulge in such practices are called semi-sinners. The one who indulges in such types of sins or incites others (to do so), I shall mention about them, you listen the same.

Those who injure the cow, the Brahmana, the girls and their lords, or spoil the activities of the friends and the ascetics, they are sinful person, entitled to fall in hell.

Those who feel agonised by looking at the wives of others, or aspire to steal riches of others, or commit thefts, those who weigh less, those who cause pain to the Brahmanas, by kicking and blows, or the Brahmanas who serve the *Sudras* women (and drink wine with them due to passion), or distil wine, those who are cruel, and the terrorist people, who indulge *dana-yajna* or other rites for the sake of livelihood,

Those who drop their refuse or ease themselves in cowpen, place of *yajna,* a lake, streets, under the trees, in the orchards or in the houses (at places other than those meant for the purpose), those who drink wine in the palaces meant for the safeguard of one’ shame, those who are in search of weak points in others, or those who are in league with others, those who obstruct the way or the road by creating barriers with bamboos, bricks, rocks, or stone slabs, wood, horns and the thorns, and transgress the boundaries of others,

Those who rule deceitfully besides do business, indulge in trade in food stuffs in exchange for the cloth, those who trade in bow, weapons and darts, those who are cruel to the servants and the animals, those who behave treacherously with their lords, friends and the preceptor, such persons are treated to be illusory and wicked, who listen only to the words spoken slowly by those indulging in falsehood,

Those who themselves leaving the wife, friend, children, old, weak, ailing persons, servants, relatives, guests and others hungry without food, those who enjoy sweets, without giving them to the Brahmanas, their cooking is of no consequence. The Brahmanas denounce them.

Those who have not controlled their senses, break the laws which had been made by them, themselves, who reside in their abodes even after accepting *Sannyasa,* they infact are the destroyers of the images of Siva.

The cruel who beat the cow repeatedly, who instead of feeding the poor and weak, leave them alone, those who yoking the bulls in the carts, make them carry the unbearable burden, without feeding them well, nor do they free the bullocks for grazing,

Those who do not take good care of the sick and hungry bullocks without making any efforts, such people are called the killers of the cows and fall in the hell.

Such of the sinful people who castrate the bulls, squeezing out their scrotum, and those who force barren cows or heifers draw carts, are great sinners sure to fall in the hell.

Those who do not shower their grace on the guests besides others who arrive hungry and thirsty, expecting to get the food, at the house, and do not serve food to the destitutes, children, aged people, weak and ailing persons, such fools surely fall in the ocean of hell.

The riches remain in the house, the relatives return from the cremation ground, but the sins and the merits accompany a dead person.

A person trading in the sale and purchase of the cows and the goats, the husband of a Sudra woman and a Brahmana behaving as a Ksatriya, are bound to fall in the hell.

All the artisans, carpenters, physicians, goldsmiths, carriers of flags of the kings and rendering service deceitfully, are all bound to fall in the hell.

The one without thinking of the good or bad (consequences) and moves according to his own will, besides intending to punish, he is sure to fall in the hell.

The king in whose reign, the people are made to suffer by those taking bribes, those who purchase at will and by the decoits, the king surely falls in the hell.

When the Brahmanas accept the riches from an unjust king, they surely proceed to hell.

A king, who by earning wealth by unfair means, gives it to the Brahmanas, he surely falls in the hell.

The cruel people, by stealing other’s wives earn the sin. Even if the king, enjoys the company of other’s wife, he earns the sin.

A king when thinks some one as a thief, who is actually not so, and thoughtlessly punishes him, he falls in the hell.

In case the people steal even the small quantity of ghee, oil, food and drinks, honey, flesh, wine, toddy, jaggery, sugarcane, vegetables, milk-curd, roots, fruits, grass, firewood, leaves, flowers, medicines, shoes, umbrella, cord, seats, waterpot, copper, tin, lead weapon, conch, besides the aquatic products, medicinal concotions, bamboo, house hold articles, they fall into the hell. Those who steal coarse or fins cloths, out of greed, fall into the hell.

There are other similar things, by stealing even the small quantity of which makes one to fall in the hell.

There is no doubt that if a person steals other’s *possessions even* of the size of the mustard seed, he surely falls into the hell.

By committing these sins, a person after his death, is born as a snake and suffers torture.

At the command of Yama such persons held by the messenger of Yama, are carried to the place of Yama getting tortured.

Such of the gods, humans, animals and birds, who are engaged in *adharma* or sinful ways, they are ruled by Dharmaraja, who awards horrible punishments.

In case some one commits a mistake, then the preceptor makes him repent. In such cases the rule of Yamaraja does not operate.

The king awards punishment to the chastiser of other’s wives, thieves and injust persons, but for those who are hidden, Yama is the one to award them the punishment.

Therefore one should perform the expiatory rites to rid himself of the sins committed by him.

The one who commits the sin physically, mentally or by speech, or makes others to do so, or permits others to do so, he surely earns the sin.

## Chapter 7 - Path to Yamaloka and form of the messengers of Yama

Sanatkumara said, “As a result of the committing of the four types of sins the persons under compulsion fall in the awful hell.

It should be known to all the living beings whether they are in the womb of the mother, in the process of birth, children, youth, in the middle age or old age, whether they are women or eunuchs, that the auspicious or inauspicious activities of all the living beings are being watched by Citragupta, Vasistha and others.

There is hardly any living being, who does not reach the abode of Yama and reaching there he will necessarily have to undergo the result of his activities. It should be kept in view.

Those of the people who have to their credit, the noble deeds, having an auspicious mind, besides being compassionate, they enter the abode of Yama from the pleasant door on the east.

Those who are sinful, who are averse to charities, they enter from the troublesome southern gate in the abode of Yama.

After traversing the distance of eighty six *yojanas* the abode of Yama is found established in various forms.

For the noble souls the distance seems to be quite short, but for the sinful people, it is quite long and troublesome.

The path is full of sharp thorns, and is filled with sand and the stones as sharp as the sharp edged daggers.

At the places the path is enough of marshy or muddy; at places it is filled with long or short *Durva* grass like iron pins which pierce through the legs.

At places it is bank like tracks with uneven surfaces, there are mountains surrounded by the trees, at places one has to pass through roads burning like the fire flames, and the people become restless passing through those paths.

At some places there are deep pits, at places there are hard pebbles, the scorching sand besides the sharp thorns.

Sometimes one has to pass through the Bamboo forests with sharp branches, scorching slabs troublesome dark roads, and at places one has to get support by various means.

Somewhere the roads are full of sharp iron pieces at places one comes across the fieriest fire, while at places, there are hard rocks and at places there are peaks covered with snow.

At places there is scorching sand rising upto the neck at places, there is the dirty water, and some places are covered with the burning cowdung.

Some places are infested with the wild animals like lions, wolves, tigers, large mosquitoes, leeches and pythons.

At places there are terrible flies, poisonous snakes, besides the intoxicated elephants.

The boars which dig the earth with their sharp snouts, the he-buffaloes with sharp horns, and other wild animals are found in abundance there.

The persons who go by that way are harassed by awful and terrific Raksasas, Dakinis, and attract several types of ailments.

The dust storm shower pebbles and the unprotected people have to suffer on the way.

At places the people have to face flames with the fall of lightning and sometimes they get drenched with the rain water while moving on.

At places there is the horrible fall of *Vajra,* the fall of stars and the shower of burning coal.

At places, they cry because of the fall of dust or the horrible thunder of the clouds, getting frightened again and again.

Because of the shower of the sharp weapons, they get wounded on all the sides. The rain of acid currents falls on them from all the sides.

They dry up because the dry and cold winds which blow from all the sides, make them restless, getting squeezed at the same time.

Such people have thus to traverse the road without any water or eatables with them.

They have to pass through the difficult, deserted, shelterless, dark and troublesome paths.

The foolish and sinful people are forcibly dragged by the messengers of Yama.

They are lonely, helpless, devoid of relatives and friends, and cry thinking about their evil deeds again and again.

Becoming goblins, they are deprived of the clothes, and their throats, lips and palates are parched. They are frightened of the terror. They feel hunger and have a burning sensation all over the body.

Some of them are bound with chains hanging upside down and are dragged by the powerful messengers of Yama.

Even those who lower their heads, and feel tortured are dragged by the messengers of Yama. Some of them are dragged by pulling their hair, some of them are dragged bound with the ropes.

Some of them are made to suffer with the striking of the goad. Men in supine are dragged along the thorny path, or covered with the burning coal.

The hands of some of them are tied behind, and are hit in the belly, others are bound with the iron chains, still others are nailed in their hands.

Some one is bound by throat, piercing an *ankusa* in the tongue and is dragged with the rope.

Some of them are dragged by piercing a rope through their nose. Some of them are dragged with piercing of the ropes through their cheeks or lips.

The limbs of some of them, like the hands, feet, ears, lips, noses, *lingas* and the scrotum are cut besides other joints of the body.

Some of them are being tortured with the spears and the arrows. Being helpless, they rush for protection here and there, while crying.

Some of them are being beaten with iron rods and *mudgaras* again and again. They are pierced and scorched with fire and they keep on burning like the sun.

With the attack of the spears the puss and the blood start flowing from their bodies. Their bodies are filled with insects refuse and the helpless people are driven towards the place of Yama.

Because of hunger they repeatedly beg for food and water. They feel cold and desire to be warmed up with fire.

But since they had never given charities, therefore they have to move without food and water. Those who had given charities, they getting food and water move towards the place of Yama quite comfortably.

Having thus covered the path, they finally reach the city of the dead with utmost hardship. Then they are produced before Yama by the messengers after making the announcement.

To such of those people, who are quite auspicious souls, Yama welcomes them, offering p*adya* and *arghya.*

He says, “You have performed the deeds prescribed in the Vedas. You are blessed, because you have performed noble deeds for attaining the divine pleasures.

You better board the plane, enjoying the company of the divine damsels, and move on towards the spotless heaven which fulfills all the desires.

Enjoying the great pleasures there, and when the stock of merits is exhausted, you will have to suffer for the sins committed by you.

The people who are the followers of *dharma* have their own friends, therefore, they looking at Dharmaraja, enjoy the best of comforts.

Those who perform the evil deeds, find Yama in a terrible form. For them, his face is terrible, with curved fangs, cruel eyes with knit eyebrows, the hair on his head is lifted up, the face has large moustaches the lips are thick and they throb. He has eighteen hands, a furious face, has the complexion of the black collyrium. In his uplifted hands he carries all the attributes, threatening for punishment. The great buffalo serves as his vehicle. His eyes emit the flames of fire. He is adorned with red garlands and is clad in red costumes. His height is as much as the Mahameru mountain. His voice resembles the thundering sound of the clouds of the time of dissolution. He looks like getting ready to drink the oceanic water, or about to swallow the mountains, or vomiting the fire, or close to whom the death in the form of the fire of the time of dissolution was seated.

Yamaraja had been awful like the mountain of black collyrium and was holding various attributes in his hands like *Sakti, Sula, ankusa, cakra,* and the sword representing several disease, terrific epidemics, Kalaratri, several types of horrible ailments like the leprosy.

He also held in his hands, weapons with horrible mouths, the daggers, the bow, quivers, besides several other types of weapons. He looked terrific and immensely strong.

The attendants of Yama are also of black complexion like collyrium, hold innumerable weapons in their hands.

Thus Yama is surrounded by his innumerable attendants, looks horrible is seen by the wicked people, with Citragupta.

Yamaraja rebukes the sinful people who is advised by lord Citragupta with appropriate words.

## Chapter 8 - Description of the hell

Citragupta said, “O Sinners, stealing the riches of others, you enjoyed the company of others wives feeling proud of your enormous riches and strength.

For the deeds committed by you, the reward of the same shall have to be reaped by you. Why did you committed the sins for your own destruction?

With the suffering caused to you by your own evil deeds, why are you crying now. Now you face the consequences of your own deeds. No one is at fault.”

Sanatkumara said, “In this way the kings who were arrogant for their prowess and the performers of the evil deeds went to Citragupta.

Then Citragupta the great lord at the instance of Yama advised the sinful people.

Citragupta said, “O Destroyers of your own people, O Wicked kings, why did you commit the sins for ruling the country for a short time?

O Kings, with the attraction of the enjoying of royal pleasures, you forcibly did injustice to the people, punishing them at the same time. Now you reap the reward of the same.

Where is your kingdom, where are the women for the sake of whom, you committed the sins, leaving all of them, you are presently standing here alone.

I find that strength on which you destroyed the people has disappeared. Presently you are the prisoners of the messengers of Yama. What shall happen now?”

Sanatkumara said, “In this way the kings who are punished, by Yama, lament over their own lot and keep on standing silently.

After thus declaring the deeds of the kings, Yama, in order to purify them from the mud of sins, spoke to his messengers.

Yama said, “O Canda, O Mahacanda, you forcibly catch hold of these kings and gradually throw them in fires of hell, in order to purify them.”

Sanatkumara said, “Then he caught hold of the kings by their feet immediately and whirl them with great force up and when they fall he caught them again and dashed them against the heated rock. They are thus felled like the huge trees, struck with *Vajra.*

Because of their striking against a stone, the blood starts blowing through their ears and get motionless and fainted.

When they regained consciousness after blowing of the air, then they were thrown in the hell to get them relieved of their sins.

This hell is located at the end of the seventh nether world- Tala, where there are twenty eight Narakakotis lodged in complete darkness.

Its first cell is Ghora, the second one Sughora, the third Atighora, the fourth Mahaghora and the fifth is Ghorarupa.

The sixth one is Talatala, the seventh is Bhayanaka, the eighth is Kalaratri and the ninth is Bhayotkata.

Below them is the tenth cell named Canda and then Mahacanda, thereafter there is Candakalahala, Pracanda, Candanayika, Padma, Padmavati, Bhita, Bhima, Bhisananayika, Karala, Vikarala, and the twentieth is Vajra.

Then there are Trikona, Pancakona, Sudirgha, Akhilartida, Sama, Bhimabala, ugra while Diptapraya is the last one.

Thus the names of the cells of *Naraka* have been mentioned to you. Each one of them is meant for the torture of a particular type of sin. Thus there are twenty eight cells for twenty eight type of sins.

Each one of these cells is placed under the charge of a Nayaka. Each one of these cells is named after the each hell. You listen to the name of each one of them according to each cell.
