The first one is Raurava, with torture of the Maharaurava, even the great people start crying.

Then there are the five chief Nayakas including Sita and Usna, besides Sughora, Sumahatiksna, Sanjivana, Mahatama, Viloma, Vilopa, Kantaka, Tivravega, Karala, Vikarala, Prakampana.

Mahavaktra, Kala, Kalasutra, Pragarjana, Suneti, Khadaka, Suprapidana, Kumbhi-paka, Supaka, Krakaca, Atidaruna, Angara- rasibhavana, Meda, Asrkprahita.

Tiksnatunda, Sakuni, Mahasamvartaka, Kratu, Taptajantu, Pankalepa, Pratimansa, Trapudrava.

Ucchvasa, Sunir-ucchvasa, Sudirgha, Kutasalmali, Durista, Sumahavada, Pravaha, Supratapana.

Mesa (ram), Vrsa, Salma, Simha Vyaghranana, Gajanana, Svanana, Sukranana, Ajanana, Mahesanana, Ghukanana, Kokanana, Vrkanana, Grahakhya, Kumbhinakhya, Nakrakhya, Sarpaksya, Kurmaksya, Vayasakhya, Grdhraksya, Ulukaksya, Jalakaksya, Sardula, Kratha, Karkata.

Manduka, Putivaktra, Raktaksa, Putimrttika, Kanadhumra, Agni, Krmigandhivapus, Agnidhra, Apratistha, Rudhirabha, Svabhojana, Lalabhaksa, Antrabhaksa, Sarvabhaksa, Sudaruna, Kantaka, Suvisala, Vikata, Kataputana, Ambarisa, Kutaka, Vaitarini (the grievous river), Sutaptalohasayana, Ekapada, Prapurana, Asitalavana, Asthibhanga, Suparna, Vilatasa, Asuyantra, Kutapasa, Pramardana, Mahacurna, Asucurna, Taptalokamaya, Parvata, Ksuradhara, Yamalaparvata, Mutrakupa, Visthakupa, Asrukupa, Ksarakupa, Sitala, Musalolukhala, Yantra, Sila, Sakutalangala, Talapatrasigahana, Mahasakata, Mandapa, Sammoha, Asthibhanga, Tapta, Cala, Ayoguda, Bahudukkha, Mahaklesa, Kasmala, Samala, Mala. Halahala, Virupa, Svarupa, Yamanuga, Ekapada, Tripada, Tivra, Acivara, Tama.

These are the twenty eight cells, which are put incharge of each one of the Nayakas. In the sequence of a crore of hells, there are five Nayakas.

There are a hundred hells or so including Raurava, *Mahanarakamanda* comprises of four thousand hells.

O Vyasa, in this way I have spoken to you about the position of the hells. Now you listen to the tendency of detachment from sin and the suffering of the sinners.

## Chapter 9 - Sufferings in the hell

Sanatkumara said, “The sinful people are lodged in these hells. They are tortured variously to rid them of the effect of sins by causing various types of injuries to them. Till their sins are dried out, they are dried out in the fires of the hells.

As the metals are put in fire till they are cleared of the dirt, similarly the human beings are made to suffer (till they are relieved of their evil deeds effects).

The hand of the people, and the messengers of the Yamaraja hang them in the tree branches.

As a result of this, the sinners get afraid of the messengers of Yama and get fainted. Under these conditions, they drive the sinners upto a long distance.

The messengers of Yama fix two thousand *palas* of iron to the hanging feet of the sinners.

Feeling painful of the weight, the sinners suffer very much, recall their evil deeds and bear the terrific pain silently.

Then the sinners are beaten with the goads as well as the iron rods heated in fire.

Then they smear the acid over their bodies which is more painful than the fire even.

With the smearing of the paste, their limbs are tom out. Thereafter all their limbs right from the head are tom out.

Then they are roasted like brinjal in an iron pan. Then they are thrown in the wells filled with filths, swarms or worms, or in the tanks filled with puss and blood. They are then eaten by worms and crows, having the beaks as strong as the iron.

The dogs, mosquitoes, wolves, and tigers eat them up. At times they are roasted in the fire like the fish.

Because of their own evil deeds the people are sometimes wounded with sharp spears, sometimes they are crushed like the gingerly seeds in the oil mills and then turned into pulp.

Sometimes they are grinded like the gingerly seeds, an sometimes they are roasted in the pans or heated and roasted with the sun rays.

They are fried in the pans filled with boiling oil, again and again pressing their hearts and tongues.

Their bodies are carried to several types of hells and tortured there respectively.

O Vyasa, the messengers of Yama, torture variously all the sinners in different hells, which are quite agonising.

The mouths of the sinners are filled with the burning coals, and are beaten. Then they are burnt with acid and hot burning copper, hot clarified butter, and oil.

The hot *ghee* and oil are poured into their mouths and they are beaten very harshly to impart pain.

At places, the sinners are filled with filth and worms, and are forced to embrace the red hot fierce iron-silk tree.

Then they are beaten at the back with the heated hammers. Then they are sawn with the saws having the sharp teeth.

Because of their own evil deeds, they are agonised from head to foot. Under these conditions the sinners eat their own flesh and drink their own blood.

Those who always fed themselves, and never offered food or betel to anyone, they are beaten with clubs, and are crushed like the sugarcanes.

Then they are driven to the forest of *asitala* trees and their limbs are cut into pieces. The needles are pierced into all their limbs. Then they are stoked over the spear-heads.

With this torture, they feel agonised, but they do not die. In this way their body starts bearing the pleasure and pain.

The messengers of Yama, with protruding fangs, looking awful, take out flesh from their bodies and beat them with clubs.

The sinners have to live in Nirucchvasa hell without breathing. In case they breath, they are carried to a room with sand and beaten there.

In the hell named Raurava, the crying people are agonised variously. The types of agonies are inflicted in the Maharaurava hell, make even the extremely patient people to cry.

The sinners are beaten with the barbed iron clubs over the feet, face, anus and head as well as the eyes.

They are thrown again and again in the burning sand. When thrown in the burning marsh of creatures and they make shrieking sounds.

O Sage, in the Kumbhipaka hells, the sinners committing evil deeds are thrown the unbearable hot oil.

In the hells known as Lalabhaksa the sinners are roasted again and again.

The sinners devoid of merits are thrown in the Sucimukha hell, where, they are beaten by the messengers of Yama.

The sinners thrown in the Lokakumbha hell, are roasted in the great fire because of their own sins.

The sinners are tied with robes and are then thrashed over the rocks. In the Andhakupa hells when the sinners are thrown, then their bodies are cast into deep gloomy wells and are subjected to bee-bites.

When the bodies of the sinners are eaten up by the worms, they are hurled into the wells of the pungent acid.

The sinners in the Mahajvala hell cry in agony. Scorched with the heat of the hell, they rush up here and there.

The people are clubbed and tied together with mouths resting over the shoulders, the hands are brought through the hallow and tied, with nooses and ropes to the back. Such bundles of bodies undergo torture in the Mahajvala hell.

They are tied with ropes, soaked with mud, and are roasted in the fire of husk and cowdung, but they do not perish.

The people with ruthless character, are thrown over the hard rocks and are burnt like the straw.

Several of the worms which enter the bodies of the sinners, eat them from within.

Agonised by the hell called Parvata, the sinners move through the heaps of flesh and bones and the worms eat- them up with their sharp teeth, as a result of which they remain upset.

Their bodies are smeared with blood and are hung up side down in the fire.

Holding them, a burning iron club is inserted in their mouths and they are asked to chew the same. They are then beaten by the subservient and sinful messengers of Yama.

Thus the sinners are agonised in the hell. Now, I shall speak out their various modes of undergoing the torture in the hell.

## Chapter 10 - Agonies of the hell

Sanatkumara said, “The people making use of the prohibited scriptures, fall in the hell called *Dvijihva.* They are tortured there with ploughshares resembling half the tongue.

The cruel person who rebukes his parents, his mouth is filled with refuse and worms and is then beaten.

The men who destroy the temples of Siva, or the orchard surrounding the same, the step- well, well, tank, the house of a Brahmana, and lakes in Siva temple or play there, or those who getting intoxicated and carefree, apply oil besides unguents over the body, take bath, besides consuming betel, or having food, water, indulge in gambling or enjoying the sexual pleasures, they are tortured in several ways including the crushing in the oil mills and they have to suffer in the fires of the time of dissolution till the time of dissolution.

Then they are made to embrace the iron image of woman, heated in fire, who enjoy other’s wives are then dragged and beaten.

Such people, by embracing the aforesaid types of women, are scorched and they cry aloud.

Those who listen to the rebuking of the noble people, the burning iron rod is inserted in their ears and nailed with the metals like copper and others.

Then melting the tin, lead and brass, or with the hot iron, and adamantine liquid their ears are filled. The tortures in the hell are inflicted by filling the ear with these and other things, one after the other.

After causing paint in their ears with these things, other agonies of the hell are also caused on them.

Similarly for the sins committed with the organs of senses as well as the body the sinners have to face many agonies.

Such of the foolish people, who embrace others’ wives for the sake of conjugal pleasures, the heated and scorched sand is filled in their hands again and again.

Their bodies are applied with corrosive substances, like acid and others. The types of tortures inflicted on the sinners are quite painful in all the hells.

Such of the people who frown at the parents, with knit eyebrows, are scratched and the nails are inserted in their limbs.

Whosoever defiles the other’s wives, with which ever limb, the same organs of the body is tortured.

Those who stare at other’s wives with voluptuous intentions, the red hot needles are pierced in their eyes.

The alkaline substances are poured in their eyes. O Excellent sage, such types of agonies are caused to the sinners. This is true, there is no doubt about it.

Those who take food, without offering to the gods, fire, preceptors and the Brahmanas, their mouths are filled with hundreds of heated iron nails.

Such of the people pluck flowers out of greed from the orchards meant for the divinities, with their hand and then smelling them, place them over their heads, hot iron nails are hammered into their mouths and their noses are filled with alkaline substances.

Such of the people, who rebuke the noble people, the gods, the preceptors, devotees, and scriptures on *Sanatana dharma,* the burning hot nails with three fangs are hammered out in all the joints of the limbs, including the chest, throat, tongue, gums, palates, lips, nose etc., with *mudgaras.*

Thereafter alkaline is poured at all these joints. In this way the body has to undergo several type of agonies.

In the same process, all the sinners are sent to all the hells. Those who usurp the riches of others, and touch the Brahmanas with the feet, or touch them with hand or feet, the material to be used for the worship of Siva, the cow, or the Vedic or post-Vedic literature, their hands and feet are pierces with the red hot nails.

They also have to face several types of agonies relating to the hands and feet in all the hells.

Such of the sinful persons, who ease themselves or drop stools with in the boundaries of the Siva temple, orchards of the gods, their *lingas* as well as the scrotum are pounded into powder with the iron thrashing rods. Red hot needles are pierced into their anus and penis. The alkaline acid or molten metals are poured into them.

All the sense organs, move at the command of the mind which result into the mental agony. Inspite of having enough of wealth with him, in case he does not give charities, because of greed, or showers disgrace on the guests arriving in their abodes, they earning sins because of their deeds, fall into the inauspicious hell.

Those who take food without feeding the crows, and dogs, their mouths are kept open hammering two nails in it.

They are tortured with the beaks of the crows, sharp iron or the insects. They also feel agonised by means of several other reasons.

There are two dogs named Syama and Sabala, which obstruct the path of Yama. To these dogs I am offering the oblation. Let them take the same. Let the auspicious crows of west, or north-west, or south, and south-west, accept this oblation of mine.” Those who offer the *bali* reciting the *mantras* of Siva, and after adoring Siva, with devotion, performing *homa* at the same time appropriately, they do not have to face Yama. They proceed straight to the heaven. Therefore the oblation should be offered daily.

They proceed on to the heaven. Therefore a square mystery diagram should be made daily, which should be worshipped offering the fragrance and unbroken rice.

The oblation to Dhanvantari should be made in the north-east comer, to Indra in the east, to Yama in the south, besides to Siva with Uma and Daksa in the west. The same oblation should be offered to the manes in the south, to Aryamana in the east, besides Dhatr and Vidhatr at the entrance.

The offerings to the dogs and their masters, besides the birds, should be placed over the earth. The offerings for gods, manes, humans, goblins, ghosts, the Guhayakas, birds, all sorts of living beings, worms, and insects, live over the offerings from the humans. *Svahakara, Svadhakara* and *Vasatkara*, the third, in addition to *Hantakara* is known to be the four nipples of the cow. The *Svadhakara* nipple is sucked by the gods, the *Svadhakara* by manes, the *Vasatkara* by other gods as well as the lords of the *bhutas,* and the *Hantakara* nipple is sucked by the human beings.

A person, who with devotion, serves offering to the cow with devotion, he earns merit of performing a *homa* daily.

Or otherwise the one who neglects the same, he attracting an ailment and falls in the Tamisra hell. Thus giving them the *bali* at the door, the householder should meditate for a short while.

A house holder should serve food to the hungry guest from the same village with the same types of dishes, he himself takes, and according to his means.

The house from which the guest, returns, he gives away this sins to the householder and carries back his merits in return.

A person, enjoying all the delicious dishes of food stays in the hell for a long time with fetters on the body and the tongue pierced with force.

Pieces of flesh as big as the seed of the gingerly are cut off from his tongue and are given to him for eating. Similarly piercing through his tongue, the blood is extracted which is given to him for drinking.

Then he is beaten with canes and he is made to suffer due to the hunger and thirst.

The sinners thus have to face various agonies. Now you briefly listen to what he achieves in the last.

The one who commits the grave sins performs the religious rites also to some extent, or remains religious minded mostly, you listen to the position of both of them.

Because of the grave sins, the petty merits became of no consequence. Because of the involvement of a person in grave sins, he never feels comfortable.

Therefore, he becoming upset, does not drive any comfort from the good eatables as well, because of his involvement. Therefore he feels agonised before others daily because of the shortage.

A person who is excessively devoted towards *dharma,* he also like the fasting householder inspite of being rich, is not distressed by hunger even for a day.

There are several grave sins in the world, committing which, a persons is shattered as a mountain is shattered into pieces with the fall of a thunderbolt.

## Chapter 11 - The glory of giving away the food in charity

Vyasa said, “O Lord, the sinful people go to the place of Yama with great difficulty. You better speak out the means by which their journey could become comfortable.

Sanatkumara said, “For all the good or the bad deeds performed by a person, he shall have to reap the fruits of the same. Now I shall spell out the auspicious rites which yield good reward.

Those who perform the noble deeds in this world, have auspicious hearts besides being compassionate, they traverse the path to the place of Yama with comfort.

The one who donates on pair of shoes or a pair of sandals to a Brahmana, he goes to the place of Yama, mounted over a white horse. The one who gives an umbrella, he goes there under the shadow of an umbrella. One who gives a palanquin goes in a palanquin sitting comfortably in it.

Those who give a seat or an *asana* or a bed, move resting in between, quite comfortably. Those who set up orchards or provide shade or plant trees on the roads, proceed on to Yama’s abode without the sun or any other trouble.

Those who set up a garden, move on boarding the Puspaka plane. Those who build the temples of the gods enjoy all the sports in the home itself.

Those who build the hermitages for the ascetics or the homes for the destitutes, enjoy all the sports in the home.

Those who adore the goes, fire, preceptor, Brahmanas and the parents, move on to the place of Yama of their own accord, with respect.

Those who donate the lamps, illuminating all the ten directions move on to the place of Yama. Those who provide shelter remain healthy and move on comfortably.

Those who serve the preceptors move on to Yama’s abode resting on the way. Those who give away charities to the destitute Brahmanas, enjoy the homely comforts.

Those who donate cow, move by the way which fulfills all the desires. Whatever food and drinks they daily consume, they get the same on way to the abode of Yama.

Those who give water to the Brahmanas for washing their feet, they move by the water ways. The one who rubs oil over the feet of a Brahmana, he covers the journey mounted over a horse.

O Vyasa, a person, who provides water for washing feet, or paste for the body, lamp, food and shelter, the messengers of Yama never visit him.

By donating gold and gems, a person getting free from all the troubles, moves on to Yamaloka. By donating silver, or bull, be reaches the abode of Yama, quite comfortably.

By giving away such charities, a person reaches the place of Yama with comfort and enjoys several types of comforts in the heaven.

The donating of the food is considered to be the best of all the charities, because the food provides comforts instantaneously. It is pleasing besides enhancing the strength and wisdom.

O Excellent sage, there is no charity comparable with the giving away of the good The food makes a person to remain alive and die in the absence of it.

The food produces blood, flesh, fat and semen. The semen is the cause of the production of the human race. Therefore, the universe has its own importance of food.

The hungry never feel satisfied even after getting gold, gems, elephants, horses, women, garland sandalwood.

The child in the womb, or a newly born child, young, old, gods, Danavas, Raksas, all have the requirement of food.

Of all the ailments, hunger is the biggest disease, which is removed with the medicine like the food.

There is no trouble worse than the hunger. There is no comfort better than remaining healthy and there is no enemy worse than the hunger.

Similarly there is no other merit better than the giving away of the food, because all the living beings die getting scorched of the fire of hunger.

The donor of food is called the giver of life, and when he gives the life he gives everything. Therefore one achieves reward of all the merits by donating the food.

When a man performs the holy rites of the having been fed with the food gifted by some one, the merit of the sacred rites is shared half and half by the giver as well as the performer of the rites. There is no doubt about it.

All the gems like the worldly pleasures, women, vehicles and other are received by the giver of the food in charity to such a person in this as well as in the future world.

*Dharma, artha, kama* and *moksa* are the best means of the body. Therefore one should protect the human body by food and the drinks.

They praise food only, because it happens to be the base of all. There have never been a donation comparable with the food, nor shall it be there in future.

O Sage, the entire universe is based on the food. The food provides strength and the life is maintained by food alone.

The one who desires of the welfare of his family, putting himself in trouble, should always give food to the Brahmana as well as the Bhiksu.

One who gives food to the Brahmana, a beggar or some one who is in distress, he donates the best of riches for the next world.

A householder desirous of the welfare of his family should adore the Brahmana who arrives at the time of taking food or the one who arrives after long journey.

O Vyasa, getting free from jealousy, if a noble person, shedding away the anger, adores the guest, he enjoys enormous comforts on earth as well as in the heave.

One should not rebuke a person who arrives (to take shelter), nor should he be challenged, because the food served to a dog or even a *Candala* does not go waste.

When on gives food to an unknown and tried traveller, without causing any pain to him, he always achieves enough of riches and the food grains.

O Great sage, a person, who citifies the goes, manes, Brahmana and the guests, by serving food to them, he earns the enormous merit.

The giving of food in charity is quite important for the Brahmana as well as the - Sudra. One should not enquire about the country, *gotra, pravara,* education or other details.

Whosoever gives the food to the Brahmana on his asking for it, he resides in the heaven upto the time of dissolution.

The garden of the giver of a food achieves the fruits of the cherished desire as the Brahmanas do in the highest heaven,

O Sage, you listen to the names of the heavens which have been built for the sake of the givers of food.

The abodes of such great personalities are of different shade and are furnished with things of several types of comforts.

In the courtyards of those abodes the wish fulfilling trees are found planted. They provide all the comforts. There are the *step-* wells of gold besides beautiful wells and the step-wells.

The spotless water flows issuing pleasing sound, the eatable things, the costumes and the ornaments are stocked in mountain like heaps.

The milk flows in the streams. There are mountains of *ghee,* the palaces are white in which the golden beds have been made available.

The givers of the food go to those *lokas.* Those who are interested in their welfare in this as well as the future world, should give away food in charity.

These *lokas* full of lustre can be achieved by the noble souls who have given food in charity. Therefore the people should particularly give away food in charity.

The food has infact the form of Brahma, Visnu and Siva, there is no other charity comparable with the giving of food, nor shall it be in future.

A person who after committing a grave sin, gives away food in charity, he getting relieved of all the sins, goes to the heaven.

In the *Pretaloka,* eight types of charities have been described to be of immense importance which include the food, the water, horse, cow, umbrella and the seat.

By giving away such types of special charities, a man reached the abode of Yama by means of a plane. Therefore we should give food in charity.

Because of the glory of donating of the food, its *mahatmya* is quite auspicious. Whosoever reads it or narrates it he flourishes in all respects

O Great sage, whoever will listen to this episode or shall repeat it to the Brahmanas, his manes will enjoy the never ending gift of food.

## Chapter 12 - Penance and its greatness

Sanatkumara said, “Of all the charities, the gift of water is the best, because all the living being are satisfied with water alone. The water is conceived as the life.

Therefore one should lovingly build the water sheds or water tanks, which provide the bliss.

In the present worlds as well as the one which has to come, these indeed provide delight. Therefore, the people should build, the step-wells, wells, tanks, etc.

Half of the sins committed by a sinner are removed by digging a well filled with the water.

The one, who construct the water tanks and its water is drunk by the cows, Brahmanas, the ascetics and the humans his entire race is redeemed.

The one in whose tank enough of water remains in the summer season, he never has to face grave calamities.

I am going to speak out the gratitudes of tanks dug for water. A person who digs the tank is adored the world over.

In case a tank is dug in the house of a friend, it enhances friendship. It removes his sufferings and increases his glory.

A person who digs the tank, he achieving the reward of *dharma, artha* and *kama,* gets entitled to huge merits.

The tank for all the four types of the living beings is a great support. The building of a tank bestows the best of riches.

The gods, humans, Gandharvas, goblins, manes, Nagas, Raksasas, the trees and plants have all to depend upon the water or tanks.

The one in whose tank the water is contained till the start of the rainy season, he earns the merit of performing *homa.* This has been ordained by Brahma.

The one in whose tank, the water remains upto the winter season, he undoubtedly earns the merit of giving away a hundred cows in charity.

In case the water in plenty remains in the early and late winter, the person who digs it, drives the benefit in which plenty of gold is given as the *daksina* of the sacrifice.

In case enough of water remains in a tank dug during the seasons of spring and summer, the people with wisdom say; that he drives the benefit of the holy rites of Atiratra and Asvamedha sacrifices.

O Sage Vyasa, the merits occurring from the digging of the tanks etc. which are excellent and pleasing to all the living beings have been narrated to you. Now you listen to the merits of planting of the trees.

A person who plants a tree in the forest, he redeems the past as well as the future manes.

The trees so planted are undoubtedly born to him as *sons in* the next birth and after his death he achieves the indestructible *lokas.*

The trees adore the gods with their flowers, the manes with their fruits, and the travellers with their shade.

The Kinnaras, serpents, Raksasas, the gods, Gandharvas, humans and the ascetics, all take shelter under the trees.

The flowering trees, satisfy the people in this as well as in the future world. This is the reason that they are called as Dharmaputras

Those who dig up wells, plant trees, perform the *yajnas,* and adore the truthful Brahmanas, never fall from the heaven.

Truth is the Supreme Brahman, truth is the supreme *tapas, satya* is the supreme *yajna,* and truth is the best of scriptures.

It is the truth alone which wakes up the sleeping people, truth is the supreme place, truth is holding on to the earth. Therefore, everything is established in truth.

The penance, *yajna,* the gods, *Rsis,* adoration of manes, water and the knowledge is enshrined in the truth.

Truth is *yajna, tapas*, charities, *mantras,* Sarasvati- the goddess and *Brahmacarya* besides being *omkara.*

The water flows with the truth, the sun shines with truth, the fire has the burning capacity because of the truth, while the heaven remains established because of the truth.

The protection of the Vedas, and the bath in all the holy places is taken because of the truth. One achieves all the *padarthas* in the world by truth alone.

When weighed against the truth in the balance, a thousand horse sacrifices, and a hundred thousand other sacrifices cannot be equal to it. Truth is all supreme.

It is only with the truth that the gods, manes, humans, serpents, Raksasas, mobiles and immobiles and other *lokas* get pleased.

Truthfulness has been conceived to be the supreme *dharma.* Truth is the supreme position, truth is the Supreme Brahman, therefore one shown always speak the truth.

The truthful sages, after performing of the hard *tapas,* after being successful in the truthful ways, proceeded on to the heaven.

The people surrounded by the *apsaras* or seated in the planes, should always speak the truth, because there is nothing beyond the truth.

With a devoted mind one should take a bath in the deep and vast water of auspicious stream of the place of pilgrimage. It is called to be the best place.

Such of the people, who for the sake of their sons and others do not tell a lie, they indeed proceed on to the heaven.

The Vedas, the *mantras* and the *yajnas* are associated with the Brahmanas but they do not seem graceful in the people with falsehood. Therefore one should speak the truth.

Vyasa said, “O Ascetic, you please speak out the result of the *tapas* performed by the Brahmanas and people of all other *varanas."*

Sanatkumara said, “I shall speak about the *tapas* to be performed by the Brahmanas, which fulfills all the desires. I now speak on the *tapas.* You will please listen to it.

*Tapas* has been termed as the best fruit is yielded by means of *tapas.* Those who perform the *tapas* daily they enjoy pleasures with the gods.

With the performing of the penance, one achieves the heaven and auspicious glory. Besides all the desires too are fulfilled with the same.

With the. performing of the *tapas* one achieves the great knowledge, salvation, perfect wisdom, good fortunes and beauty.

By penance a person achieves several things and all the desire of a person performing the *tapas* are fulfilled.

No one reaches Brahmaloka without performing *tapas.* Even lord Siva cannot be achieved without the performing of *tapas.*

When a person performs *tapas* for achieving of a particular thing, he attains it in this world as well as in future as well.

A drunkard ascetic, or womaniser, killer of Brahmana, and the one who enjoys the wife of the preceptor, is also relieved of his sins, with the performing of the *tapas* and ultimately gets redeemed.

Siva, the lord of all, Visnu- the eternal one. Brahma, Agni and Indra performs *tapas.*

The eighty eight thousand ascetics of the sublimated semen, rejoice in the heaven, with the performing of the penance, along with the gods.

One can achieve kingship with the performing of the penance. Indra, the lord of god and the killer of Vrtra, protects everything daily with the performing of the *tapas.*

The sun and the moon, besides all the constellations who do good to others, illuminate because of their *tapas.*

No one can enjoy any types of pleasure in the world without the performing of the *tapas.* The people who are well-versed in the Vedasproclaim that it is with the performing of *tapas* that one achieves all types of pleasures.

The knowledge, the perfect knowledge, health, beauty and fortunes could be achieved by means of *tapas* alone.

It is because of the *tapas* that Brahma, engage himself in creation of the universe without much effort, or Visnu preserves it or Siva destroys it or the serpent sesa, carries it over its hood.

O Great sages, it is with the performing of the *tapas,* that Visvamitra a ksatriya, the son of Gadhi, was transformed into a Brahmana. This episode’s well known in the three worlds.

O Immensely intelligent one, I have narrated the excellent glory of the penance to you. Now listen to the glory of the study of the Vedas, which is much more excellent than the penance.

## Chapter 13 - The glory of the Puranas

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, the one performs *tapas* in a forest living on roots and fruits, and the merit he earns for the same would be equivalent to the reciting of a *rca* of the Vedas.

The best of the Brahmanas who earns the merit by reciting the hymns of the Veda he earns the double of the merit by teaching the same to his disciples.

O Sage, as the universe remains without light in the absence of the sun and the moon, similarly the same situation prevails without the Puranas. Therefore, one should study the Puranas as well.

A person well-versed in the Puranas is always adorable because he understands the person who suffer in the hell because of his ignorance of the Puranas.

Of all the competent people, the person who is well-versed in the Puranas, is considered to be the best because he saves the people from falling (in the hell).

A person well-versed in the Puranas should not be considered to be an ordinary person because he happens to be omniscient and as such he can be equated with Brahma, Visnu, Siva and the preceptor.

In order to enjoy comforts in both the worlds, the wealth, cereals, grains gold and costumes of several types should be given to the learned person, well-versed in the Puranas.

The one who respectfully gifts away the best of things, he achieves the highest position (salvation).

The one who gives away, the earth, cow, vehicle, the best of elephant, and horses to the person well-versed in the Puranas, listen to the merit which is earned by him for the same.

All his desires are fulfilled in the present as well as the future world and he earns the merit of performing the *Asvamedha* sacrifice.

The one who gives away the land with the fully grown crops over it, he redeems his ten past as well as the future generations.

He enjoying all the pleasures in this world, ultimately attaining the divine body, boards the plan and leaves for the place of Siva.

The sacrifices do not please the gods as much or *proksanakas* (animal sacrifice) oblation or floral offerings as with the reciting of the Puranas.

Listen to the meritorious benefits of a person who provides the sacred books I the temple of Siva, Visnu, the sun or anyone else.

Such a person achieving the merit of *Rajasuya* and *Asvamedha* sacrifices, piercing through solar region, moves on to Brahmaloka.

He lives there for hundreds of *kalpas*, then he becomes a king on earth. He indeed enjoys all the comforts without any obstructions.

He earns the merit of a thousand *Asvamedha* sacrifice, who recites the Purana in the temple of Siva. Nothing is dearer to the gods and Siva than this.

Therefore making all the efforts, one should recite *Siva Purana* or listen to it, because it fulfills all the desires.

By listening to the *Siva Purana* a person is relieved of all the sins and after enjoying several comforts he attains Sivaloka.

The merit one gets by performing of *Agnistoma* or the *Rajasuya* sacrifices, the same merit is gained by a person by listening to the story of Siva.

The merit one earns by taking a bath in all the holy places, giving in charity crores of cows, O Sage, same merit one earns by listening to the story of Siva.

One, who listens to the story of Siva, which purifies the three worlds, he should be treated as Siva and not an ordinary human being.

The dust of the lotus like feet of those who recite or listen to the story of Siva, have been conceived to be sacred place.

The people, who intend to visit the places which bestow welfare, should always listen to the *Siva Purana* with devotion.

In case some one is unable to listen to *Siva Purana,* then one should listen to it for a short while daily.

O Sage, in case a person is unable to listen to the story of Siva, daily, then he should listen to the same in the auspicious months.

O Excellent sage, with listening to the story of Siva, a person burning the forest of *karmas* crosses the ocean of the universe.

A person listens to the story of Siva for a *muhurta* or half of it, or even for a moment, he never has to face the misfortune.

O Sage, the merit one earns by giving away the charities, or the performing of the *yajnas,* it gets stabilised with the listening of the *Siva Purana.*

O Vyasa, particularly, the persons who are engaged in the *mukta-dhyana* there is no better *dharma* in Kaliyuga, than to the listening of the *Siva Purana.*

The listening *Siva Purana* and the holy recitation of his names yields, fruits in reality like the *kalpavrksa* tree to the human beings.

*Siva Purana* has been created like the nectarine juice for the men who are not so intelligent in the age of Kali and are deprived of virtue and noble conduct.

By drinking nectar only one person becomes free from old age. But by drinking the nectar of Siva’s story the entire family is freed from death and old age.

O Dear one, the position achieved by meritorious ascetics, and the performers of the *yajnas*, the same position is achieved by listeners of the Puranas.

When one is unable to achieve knowledge, then he should study the *yogasastras.* One should listen to the Puranas making all the efforts.

By this way, the sins are washed away and there is an increase in the *dharma.* With the listening of the Puranas, one achieves knowledge and cannot be bound in the worldly fetters.

Therefore the Purana should be listened to making all the efforts and by so doing, one achieves, *dharma, artha* and *kama,* besides the road to *moksa.*

The merit one achieves by performing charities, *yajnas, tapas* and performing pilgrimage to the holy places, the same merit is achieved by listening to the Purana.

Had there been no Puranas to serve as guides to *Dharma* then the ascetics to narrate the stories of the present as well as the future world would not have been found.

Even if a single Purana, out of the thirty six Puranas, is read or listened by some one with devotion he is relieved of all the doubts.

There is no path more comfortable than the listening of the Puranas. Without the *Sastras,* the world does not look graceful, in the same way as the world is filled with darkness without the sun.

## Chapter 14 - The glory of charities

Sanatkumara said, “All the big charities, which have been described as such, should be daily offered to the able persons and only then they bestow welfare on the donates.

O Excellent Brahmana, the gift of gold, gift of cow, the gift of land, when received by an auspicious person, result in the redemption of the donors.

With the giving away of gold and the cow, a person is relieved of al the sins.

The gift of gold, land, education and *tuladana* are highly praised. Of these the first two gifts are equal, but the giving of education is the best of all.

The milch cow, the umbrella, the costumes, shoes and food should be given daily to the beggars.

The stuff which is given to the Brahmanas or the beggars performing the *samkalpa* rites, besides the people in distress, makes the donor more humane.

The great charities include gold, gingerly seeds, elephant, girl, slave girl, house, chariot gem and the white cow are the great charities.

The learned Brahmana, after receiving all these gifts redeems himself as well as the donor undoubtedly.

The people who gift away the gold with a spotless mind, the gods shower the riches on them from all sides. This is what has been heard by me.

The fire represents all the gods and the gold is the form of Agni. Therefore by giving away gold in charity, it amounts to giving the same to all the gods.

The donation of land I also considered to be the best of all and fulfills all the desires. The gift of land with gold is also excellent and it was made by the king Prthu in earlier times.

Those who witness the land with gold being given in charity, they getting relieved of all the sins achieve salvation.

O Sage, now I speak on other excellent charities, as a result of which the people do not have to witness the painful *Asipatra* forest.

One should purchase a forest with the wealth earned lawfully, and donate it without being miserly, in an appropriate manner.

With a *prastha* measure of the gingerly seeds, an image of cow with calf endowed with all the qualities should be made in gold. It should possess all the characteristics, being divine in shape. The eight petalled mystic diagram should be made with vermilion and the unbroken rice grains. The devotee should adore Rudra and other gods there with utmost devotion. The cow and the calf after having been adored should be given to a Brahmana together with gold and gems according to the competence of the donor. They should be bedecked with all the ornaments. The devotee has to take the food during the night alone, and then give away lamps an gifts. This has to be done on the full moon day of the month of Kartika making all the efforts. One who performs according to his means, and observing all the rules, has not to fall in the terrible hell or the path of Yama.

O Vyasa, a person who performs accordingly, he, inspite his indulging in all the sins, enjoys the comforts of Indra with his relatives and friends for the period of the duration of fourteen Indras.

O Vyasa, the giving away of a cow in charity in an appropriate manner, is considered to be the excellent one. No charity could be compared with the same.

In case a person donates a white cow with her horns decorated with gold, the hoofs with silver and a bell metal vase, the said cow, O Vyasa, returns to the donor as the wishful-filling cow in this birth as well as in the heaven.

A virtuous Brahmana should be given away the things in charity, whatever things are liked by us in the world in order to make them indestructible.

*Tuladana* is considered to be the best of all the charities. A person who is desirous of his own welfare, he should perform *tuladana.*

The weighing balance is highly meritorious and it eliminate all the sins, by making a gift of it one gets rid of the sins and the bondage. In fact the *tuladana* is immensely meritorious and destroyer of all the sins

A person, who after committing all the sins performs *tuladana,* he getting relieved of all the sins, surely achieves the heaven.

“The sin committed by me with my body, mind, speech, during the noon, night, evenings, end of night or during any of the three times, let the same be removed by the presiding duty of the weighing scale- lord Siva, enemy of Kama and remove all the sins, done as a boy or as a youth, as an old man wakefully and consciously. The riches have been given by me to a deserving person. It has been placed in the balance comparable to my weight, with this let me earn the merit.” These *mantras* should be recited before making the gift.

Sanatkumara said, “A donor, being desirous of his own welfare, thus speaking, should distribute the wealth to different Brahmanas only then he will be freed from the sins.

O Vyasa, a person who donates *tulapurusa* he after destroying all his sins enjoys his stay in the heaven upto the period of the rule of fourteen Indras in the heaven.

## Chapter 15 - Description of Patalaloka

Vyasa said, “You tell me a single charity by giving which a person can derive the benefit of all the charities, for the benefit of all people.

Sanatkumara said, “With the giving away of the single charity timely, a person derives the benefit of all the charities, the same is being spoken out by me. You please listen.

A person desirous of achieving salvation after the crossing the ocean of the universe, should give away the whole universe as gift.

A man becomes the lord of the seven worlds with a fraction of the benefit that he obtains when the whole universe is gifts away.

A person who donates the universe, sports in the abode of the gods, with his relatives as long as the sun and the moon remain in the sky or the earth is steady or every one in the heavenly abode is favourable. Thereafter for rejoicing he achieves the place of Visnu, which is beyond the reach of even the gods.

Vyasa said, “O Lord, you tell me the details about the universe, its extent and its main soul and its structure to enable me to have a complete idea of the subject.

Sanatkumara said, “O Sage, you listen, I speak on the subject. I shall reveal its height and width in brief, listening to which, a person is relieved of all the sins.

That which is unmanifest and ultimate cause, becomes manifest as Siva, who is free from ailments. Because of the difference in the periods, he emerges out of them in due course of time.

O Dear one, the way Brahma created the globe with fourteen *bhuvanas,* I am going to narrate the same in brief, which you please listen.

The nether worlds are seven (Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Rasatala, Tala, Talatala and Patala). The upper worlds are also seven (Bhu, Bhuvah, Svah, Janah, Tapah, Satyam and Muhuh). As it stands in the middle of water, its height (globe) is double.

Sesa is the base of the globe, who is also called Visnu, who according to Brahma preserves the universe.

Even the gods and the Danavas are unable to speak out the qualities of Sesa. He is beyond measure and is adorable by the gods, *Rsis,* and the *siddhas.*

Sesa has a thousand hoods each one of which is studded with gems, which collectively illuminate the universe. He is also adorned with the spotless Svastika ornament.

He is lodged there with his waving eyes like the intoxicated fire, resembling the white mountain, adorned with a garland and crown.

He is like the Kailasa mountain, which shines white with the flow of the Ganga. He wears a blue cloth and is found intoxicated.

He touches the tail with his hands, holds a club as an attribute. The Naga girls of golden colour are adoring him with respect.

He is Rudra in the form of Samkarsana, looks brilliant with the fire flames. The flames of fire come out of his mouth at the time of dissolution, which subside after the destruction of the world.

He is lodged at the base of *Patala* and is adored with innumerable virtues. He is lord of all the living beings. Such a type of serpent Sesa carries the earth over his back.

The gods are unable to describe his prowess, though they are desirous to do so. His real form also cannot be known.

The earth is lodged over his hoods with red complexion, like the garland. Therefore who can describe his strength?

Getting intoxicated when he rolls his eyes, yawning at the same time then the earth with mountains, oceans and forests, shakes.

O Excellent sage, every *Patala* has an area of ten thousand *yojanas* and are known by the names of Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Rasatala, Tala, Talatala and Patala is the last one These are the seven *lokas* below the earth. This should be known by the learned people.

Their height is double (or twenty thousand *yojanas).* The land of all the *lokas* as well as the palaces there are of gold studded with gems.

The Danavas, Nagas, the great serpents, Daityas and Raksasas of the Daitya origin reside there.

Narada who had arrived in the heaven from the nether world, had described about them in the divine assembly, which were more charming even than the heaven.

All the ornaments there are studded with gems which are white and delightful. No other place is comparable with *Patalaloka.*

With the presence of the daughters of the gods and Danavas, there who does not like *Patalaloka*?

The rays of sun and moon do not reach there and the gems alone illuminate the area. The summer and winter are not to be found there.

O Excellent sage, the times that passes by is not known there and all sorts of eatables and drinks are consumed by immensely delighted people.

The cooing of the male Cuckoo is heard there. The lotuses blossom in the tanks. There are pleasant rivers and the likes. Each one of them is more attractive than the other.

O Brahmana, beautiful ornaments are found there, besides the fragrant pastes. The sound of the *Vina,* flutes and the cymbals are constantly heard there. There are songs everywhere.

The Daityas and the serpents remain delightful and enjoy all the pleasures by performing *tapas.*

## Chapter 16 - Achieving the hell and the repentance

Sanatkumara said, “The hells lodged above those *lokas* in which the sinners have to suffer the agonises, you listen from me.

These hells include. Raurava, Sukara, Rodha, Tala, Vivasana, Mahajvala, Taptakumbha, Lavana, Vilohita.

The river Vaitarini, Puyavaha, Krmibhojana, Ghora-Asipatravana, Daruna, Lalabhaksa, Puyavaha, Bhahirjvala, Adhahsira, Samdamsa, Kalasutra, Tama, Avicirodhana, Suvabhojana, Rusta, Mahasaurava, Salmali, which are quite painful.

O Vyasa, the people who are thrown in these hells, I describe about them in a sequence. You listen to the same with attention.

A person who gives a false evidence against the humans, the gods, Brahmanas and the cows, he falls in the Raurava hell.

The one who causes abortion, indulges in the theft of gold, or a cow, is the betrayer of other’s faith, the drunkard, killer of the Brahmana and the one who steals the belongings of others.

O Vyasa, those who associate themselves with them, or kill the preceptor, mother, sister or daughter, fall in the Taptakumbha.

One who sells out the chaste wife, collector of the interest, one who sells his hair, and the deserter of the devotees, falls in the Taptaloka hell.

The one who insults the preceptors the degraded person who eats last of all, the one who denounce of the gods, and their seller.

O Brahmana, one who enjoys the company of an unchaste woman, he reached the seven- tala hell. The their the killer of the cow, the fallen man, one who desecrates the limitations (*Maryada).*

The one who is envious of the Brahmanas, the gods, and the manes, one who pollutes the gems, is fallen in the krmi-bhaksaka hell, where he is eaten by the germs.

A degraded person, who eats food, without giving it to the manes, and the gods who acts deceitfully in the compassing of the scriptures, such a foolish person falls in the Lalabhaksa hell.

Those who serve the Sudras, perform *yajnas* for the undeserving persons, eat the forbidden things or food, and the sellers of the *soma* juice, fall in the Rudhiraugha hell. The destroyers of honey and the villages are thrown in the river Vaitarani.

Those who get intoxicated in the youthful age, those who cross the limits, those who are unclean and earn their livelihood by means of the fallen women, they fall in the hell named Krmi.

The one who cuts the trees uselessly, moves towards the Asipatra forest. Those who hunt the deer with an arrow having the shape of a horse shoe, fall into the *Vanhijvala* hell.

O Brahmana, the Brahmana, Ksatriya and Vaisya who falls from the path of good conduct, falls into the hell meant for the dog eating *candalas.*

Those who discard the *vratas,* those who fall from their *asramas,* have to face the agony of the terrific hell.

The Brahmacari, who has a night fall during the night, and those who do not educate their sons, they fall into the hell named *Svabhojana.*

Besides these, there are hundreds and thousands of the hells, where the sinners have to face the agonising pains.

Besides these, there are thousands of sins, which the people falling in the hell have to face.

A person, who, by his action thought and behaviour acts contrary to the *Varnasrana dharma,* he also falls in the hell.

The gods look at the sinners from the heaven and find then hanging upside down and they also find the gods lowering their heads.

The immovable beings, humans, insects, birds, animals, dear, religious minded people as well as the gods, always are desirous of *moksa.*

The number of the living beings in the heaven and the hell are the same. Those who do not perform the repentance rites for their sins go to hell.

The repentance rites for the grave sins are great while those of the petty sins are small, which have been prescribed by the Svayambhuva Manu.

In all the repentance rites, the name of Siva should be always recited which is the best.

A person after performing the repentance for his sin, in remorse thereof, the reciting of the name of Siva is the best.

The one who recites the name of Siva in the morning, noon and evening, he is relieved of all the sins.

With the mere reciting of the name of Siva, the lord of Uma, getting free from all the sufferings, one achieves the heaven and moksa.

O Excellent sage, O Best of the Brahmanas, the recitations, *homas* worship etc. obstacles in the path of sins. O Excellent sage, they do not occur anywhere in the three worlds.

The achieving the status of Indra- the lord of the gods, is the fruit of the merits which accrue from the merits of the adoration of Siva.

O Sage, the one who adores Siva with devotion throughout the day and night, never goes to hell because his sins are washed out without any effort.

O Excellent Brahmana, one achieves the hell by committing sins and the heaven by performing of the good deeds. One has to face agony in the hell and the comforts in the heaven.

When the merits are exhausted after sometime, it becomes the cause for the fall in the hell. Therefore there is no cause of pleasure or the pain.

The pleasures and the pain are only supreme Brahma, who enlightens on the reality.

The entire mobile and immobile world requires enlightenment as its soul. O Sage, there is nothing greater than the perfect knowledge nor is there any reality comparable to the same.

Thus I have described the details about the hells. Now I shall speak about the globe.

## Chapter 17 - Description of Jambudvipa

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, the globe which is spread over the seven continents, you listen from me the description of the same, which I am going to speak out in brief.

The seven continents comprise of Jambu, Plaksa, Salmali, Kusa, Kraunca, Saka and Puskara. All the seven of them are surrounded by the oceans.

Jambudvipa is surrounded by the oceans of salt (or saline water), sugarcane juice, *ghee,* curd, milk.

O Vyasa, the Meru mountain of gold is located in the centre. Below the earth it is spread to sixteen *yojanas* (sixty four miles), and its height is eighty four *yojanas* (336 miles).

Its peak is thirty two *yojanas* (128 miles) in breadth. The mountain is lodged over the back of the earth and it spreads on all the sides, in the shape of a pericarp.

The mountains like Himalaya, Hemakuta and Nisadha are lodged to its south.

The Nila, Sveta and Srngi mountains are lodge to the north of it. All the mountains are en thousand in number have the colour of sunshine and are filled with gems.

They have the height of a thousand *yojanas* and are spread in the same area. Bharatavarsa is the first subcontinent and thereafter there is kimpurusavarsa.

O Sage, then to the south of the Sumeru mountain, there is the Harivarsa, Ramyaka is to the north of it. Hirana-mayavarsa is its part.

O Excellent sage, Kuru country is located to the north. The extent of each one of these, is nine thousand *yojanas,* as in the case of Bharata.

In between them is the Sumeru mountain, spread in an area of nine thousand *yojanas* around the Sumeru mountain is Ilavrta mountain.

O Great sage, there are four mountains here like Ilavrta which look like supporting beams of the Meru mountain which are joined to it rising above.

The Mandaracala mountain is to the east, Gandhamadana is to the south, Vipula on the west and Suparsva mountain is lodged to the north.

Over the peaks of the same mountain, trees like Kadamba, Jambu, Pippala and banyan are grown which serve as the flagstaff are spread in an area of eleven hundred *yojanas.*

O Great sage, now you listen to the cause of the name of Jambudvipa. Several trees are grown there shining brightly. I shall speak out this mature to you.

There are a large number of rose-apple trees. The fruits of these trees are black like the elephants being of the same size. Getting ripe they fall from the mountain, and spread everywhere.

The river Jambu there is quite well known in which the juice of the rose apple fruits flow. The said juice is consumed by the people there.

The people living over the banks of the said river do not perspire, nor does the odour emerge from their bodies. No defects develop in the limbs of their bodies. They also do not have to face the old age.

The earth of the banks of the river is dried up with the breathing and the gold ornaments are made out of it, which are called Jambunada.

The Bhadrasvavarsa is to the east of the Sumeru Ketumalavarsa is on the west and Ilavrta is located between the two of them.

To the east is the Chaitraratha forest, Gandhamadana is to the south, Vibhraja is on the west and Nandanavana is on the north.

The four lakes known as Arunoda, Mahabhadra, Sitoda and Manasa are worthy of being used by the gods in all respects.

Four prominent mountains known as Sitanjana, Kurunga, Kurara and Malyavan, are lodged to the east of the Sumeru mountain.

The mountains known as Trikuta, Sisira, Patanga, Rucaka, Nisadha, Kapila and others are lodged to the south.

The mountains like Sinivasa, Kusumbha, Kapila, Narada, Naga and others are lodged in the western direction.

The filament-mountains like Sankacuda, Rsabha, Hamsa and Kalanjara are lodged to the north.

Over the Sumeru mountain, in the middle, the city of Brahma called Satakumbha is lodged, which is spread over an area of fourteen thousand *yojanas.*

Around the said city there are the houses of eight lokapalas, which have been built according to their status.

In the city of Brahma, the Ganga issuing from the feet of Visnu, is flowing throw the sphere of the moon.

The rivers like Sita, Alakananda, Caksu and Bhadra also flow from there and are spread in all the directions.

The river Sita flows to east of the Sumeru mountain, Alakananda to the south, Caksa on the west and Bhadra to the north.

The river Ganga flowing through the three paths, after crossing all the mountains joins the great ocean in four quarters.

The Sumeru mountain surrounded by the Sunila, Nisadha, Malyavan and Gandhamadana mountain looks like the bud

The four *varsas* viz. Bharata, Ketumala, Bhadrasva, and Kurus, are the petals of the world lotus.

Devakuta serves as the belly, which is spread from the south to north. Gandhamadana and Kailasa are lodged from east to west.

The Nisadha and the Nila mountains, located to the east of Meru mountain, move to the south as well as north and terminate within the pericarp.

The Kesara mountains like Sveta and others, appear like belly of the Meru in two mountains and look quite charming.

To the north of the mountains are the small boats used by siddhas and caranas as their resorts. There are fascinating forests and towns beyond them.

These towns belong to the gods, Yaksas, Gandharvas and Raksasas. The gods and the demons indulge in sports there throughout the day and night.

These places are meant for the noble souls like heavens on earth. They are beyond the reach of the sinners, who are unable to see anything there.

O Great sage in the eight *varsas* starting from Kimpurusa and others, there is no grief, no obstruction, hunger or thirst nor is there any confusion.

The people of that place are healthy, free of ailments, all free from miseries, and enjoy the long life of ten to twelve thousand years.

Only the *Satya, Dvapara* and *Treta yugas* alone prevail there. The waters for the irrigation of the land are always available there. There are no rains from the sky.

In all the seven continents, the water is spotless, the rivers have golden sand. There are hundreds of small rivulets in which the humans sport.

## Chapter 18 - The seven continents

Sanatkumara said, “Now I shall talk about Bharatavarsa which is located to the south of Himalaya and north of the ocean.

O Great sage, the continent is spread in an area of nine thousand *yojanas.* The learned people call it the land of heaven as well as the place for achieving *moksa.*

The people living here attain the heaven as well as the hell. I describe to you the nine regions of Bharata, which include Indradyumna, Kaseru, Tamravarna, Gabhastiman, Nagadvipa, Saumya, Gandharva and Varuna.

The ninth is land Sagarasambhrta which has emerged from the ocean. It is spread in thousands of *yojanas* from south to north.

Kirata is located to its east, and the country Yavanas in the south. The ascetics live in the north as well as in the west.

The Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and the Vaisyas besides the Sudras also live there. All the four *varnas* are engaged in the performing of the *yajnas*, waging of war, trade and service to others.

There are seven mountains like Malaya, Sahya, Sudama, Rksu, Vindhya and Pariyatra.

O Sage, the Vedas, *Smrtis,* Puranas and other scriptures have emerged from Pariyatra- the Kulaparvata. With the sight or the touch of the same, all the sins are washed out.

The seven rivers like Narmada, Surasa and others, besides the thousands of rivers starting from the Vindhya mountains are all auspicious and remove all the sins.

The rivers like Godavari, Bhimarathi, Tapti and others originate from the Rksa mountain, which destroy the fear of sins in no time.

The river Krsna, starts from the Sahya mountain, together with the river Veni and others. Krtamala and Tamrapani rivers originates from the Malaya mountain.

The rivers like Triyama, Rsikulya and others have their source in the Mahendra mountain. Kumari and other rivers originate from the mountain Suktiman.

Several cities are found established in these regions. They consume the water of these rivers and lakes.

O Great sage, there had been four yugas like Satyayuga and others in Bharatavarsa. This type of arrangement is hardly found in other islands or continents.

The charities were given here through the auspicious priests. The ascetics here used to perform *tapas* for the welfare of all, with respect.

O God sage, the land of Jambudvipa is indeed *Karmabhumi.* Out of that, the land of Bharata is the best, the rest are the *Bhoga- bhumis.*

O Sage, the *jiva* after earning of the merits for thousands of births, is born as a human being.

O land of Bharata, you are indeed blessed and graceful. You happen to be the path for achieving the heaven and the *moksa.* Therefore, even the gods adore you. This is the reason that the gods incarnate here in the form of humans.

The gods, sometimes emerging in human forms and sometimes they warn about in the supreme soul form of Siva and achieve the reward of this *karmas.* They desire that by attaining the human form they should achieve *moksa.*

The people who are enjoying the comforts and those engaged in performing the noble deeds are indeed blessed, since they are born in the land of Bharata and they are entitled to the heaven as well as *moksa.*

Bharata which is spread in an area of a lakh of *yojanas*, which has been described by the name of Jambudvipa, is surrounded by the ocean of milk.

O Brahmanas, Plaksa-dvipa is of double the size of Jambudvipa surrounded by the salt ocean and is spread over an area of a hundred thousand *yojanas.*

It has the excellent mountains named Gomanta, Rodha, Narada, Durdura, Somaka, Sumana and Vaibhrajaka.

On all these *varsa* mountains the gods as well as the Gandharvas reside there with the people.

The people there are free from ailments, agonies or other types of dangers. The people of this place have the life span of ten thousand years each.

There are seven holy rivers here known by the names of Anutapta, Sikhi, Papaghni, Tridiva, Krpa, Amrta and Sukrta.

There are thousand of small mountains or rivulets. The people therefore feel delighted by drinking the water of these rivers.

O great sage, there is difference in the four *yugas* in the seven mountains. O great sage, the time there resembles the Treta yuga forever.

O excellent sage, the Brahmanas, Ksatriya, Vaisya and the Sudras live there. There is a huge tree comparable to the *Kalpavrksa.*

O best of the Brahmanas, the said tree is the Plaksa tree, therefore the country is called Plaksadvipa. Lord Siva, who showers benefits on all is adored there.

Brahma and Visnu are also adored there with the reciting of the Vedic *mantras.* Now listen to the description of the Salmali country in brief.

There are seven sub-continents and you please listen to them. They are Sveta, Harita, Jimuta, Rohita, Vaikala, Manasa and Suprabha, which is the seventh. The continent draws its name from Salmali tree.

It is surrounded by the ocean which is twice its existence. There are seven rivers which are of the indications of the continent. You lease listen to their names.

They are known as Sukla, Rakta, Hiranya, Raudra, Subhra, Virocana and Nairta which is the seventh one. The water of these rivers is cool and auspicious.

There are seven continents here and the people of four *varnas* live here, who always adore lord Siva with various kinds of *yajnas.*

Close to this pleasant continent live the gods. The continent is always surrounded with the ocean of wine.

Kusadvipa is the double of its size, which is inhabited by the gods and the demons besides the humans.

Similarly the gods, Gandharvas, Yaksas and Kimpurusas also live there. The people of all the four *dharmas* are devoted to their respective dharmas.

In Kusadvipa also besides Brahma and Visnu. Siva too is adored for the fulfilment of the desires by the people.

There are seven mountains in Kusadvipa viz. : Kusesaya, Hari, Dyutiman, Puspavan, Manidrumam Haimasaila and Mandaracala- the seventh one.

There are seven rivers namely- Dhutapapa, Siva, Pavitra, Sammati, Vidya, Dambha and Mahi. All these rivers are the destroyers of the sins. Besides them there are thousands of rivulets having the spotless water and golden sand.

There is the stump of Kusa- grass in the Kusadvipa and is surrounded by the ocean of clarified butter. O Fortunate one, now you listen to the description of the other great continent of Kraunca-dvipa.

It is surrounded by the ocean of curd, which is of double in size. O learned one, you listen to the names of the mountains located close to this *dvipa.*

They are Kraunca, Vamana, Andhakaraka, Divavrtti, Mana, Pundarika and Dundubhi.

These mountains are golden in colour and the people live there free of danger, accompanied with their friends and the gods.

The Brahmanas, Ksatriya, Vaisya and Sudras live there in complete harmony. There are seven great rivers besides thousands of small rivulets.

These rivers are Gauri, Kukudvati, Sandhya, Rasi, Manojava, Santi, Pundarika and the people drink their auspicious water.

Siva in the form of *Yogarudra* is adored there. Sakadvipa is surrounded by the oceans of curds and whey.

There are seven mountains here and you listen their names from me. Udayagiri is to the east of it, while the Jaladhara mountain is located to the west.

Astagiri is at the back, besides Avikesa, Kesari, Saka, the great tree is worshipped by Siddhas and Gandharvas.

These countries are quite sacred and are inhabited by the people of the four *varnas.* The rivers are also quite auspicious, which remove all the sins as well as the miseries.

These rivers are Sukumari, Kumari, Nalini, Venuka, Iksu, Renuka and Gabhasti.

O Sage, thousands of small rivulets are also there, besides the small mountains which are in hundreds and thousands in number.

There is no question of the loss of virtues in them. People from heaven arrive in those varsas on earth for the purpose of sporting with one another.

In the land of Sakadvipa, the sun is lovingly worshipped by the people of all countries pious in mind and activities as mentioned before.

The Saka is surrounded by the ocean of milk on all the sides, which is twice as large. O Vyasa, the ocean of milk is surrounded by Puskara, twice as large.

There is a Mahavarsa, far greater then that, where Manasarovara is quite famous. It has the height of five thousand *yojanas.*

There is a great ring round it which is five thousand *yojanas* in length. The ring of Puskara-dvipa divides it into two.

The *dvipa* and the varsa are of similar shapes i.e. round. The life span of the people there is ten thousand years.

O Sage, they are free from ailments, grief, attachment, jealousy, and do not indulge into passion and hatred. The do not follow the evil ways nor do they kill or imprison anyone.

There is neither the truth nor the falsehood found there. The people have the golden complexion there and are clad in the similar types of costumes.

O sage, this varsa is called Bhauma, resembling the heaven on earth, and the life here is pleasing to all. They are free from ailments and sickness.

O Sage, the holy fig tree is the excellent abode of Brahma in the Dhataki-khanda and Mahavita in the Puskara-dvipa.

Brahma while living there is adored by the gods and the Daityas. The Puskara-dvipa is surrounded by the sweet water.

Thus the seven dvipas are surrounded by the seven oceans. The number of the dvipas and oceans are the same, but each one is twice as large as the one within.

The prominent feature of the oceans is that their water always remains the same and there is hardly any decline in the same.

O Excellent sage, in case the water in a pot is heated, it boils and evaporates, similarly when the moon rises, there is fermentation in the oceanic water, which rises up.

At the time of the rising and setting of the moon, the oceanic waters flow and ebb. Therefore in the bright and the dark fortnights, the waters in the ocean vary increasing and decreasing respectively.

O Excellent sage, thus I have explained the rise and the decline of the water of all the oceans.

O Sage, the people living in the Puskara- dvipa Khanda consume the food self acquired by them.

This dvipa is good for health and the element of greed is absent there. The wild people cannot reach there. The land is golden and is devoid of living creative. Its rise is double than the other dvipas.

The Lokaloka mountain is a thousand *yojanas* in height and in vastness, it is an equal number of yojanas, in extent.

O great sage, the earth which had emerged out of the egg of Brahma, has an area of fifty crores of *yojanas* together with its mountains.

The world is the base of all the living beings and has more attributes than any other elements here.

## Chapter 19 - Position of the planets like Sun and others

Sanatkumara said, “The part of earth over which the rays of the sun and the moon fall is called *Bhuloka* (or Universe).

The solar disc is situated at a distance of a hundred thousand *yojanas* from the earth, while the moon is located at a distance of a thousand *yojanas* from earth and a hundred thousand *yojanas* from the sun.

The sphere of the planets from all the constellations and stars ten thousand *yojanas* above the other.

Mercury (Budha), Venus and Mars are located one above the other. Brhaspati (Jupiter) is above all of them, while Saturn is above that.

The sphere of the seven sages is lodged still higher than that by a lakh of *yojanas* above it. Above the seven sages Dhruva the pole star is situated at a distance of a hundred thousand *yojanas.*

All the planets are lodged above the earth but below the pole star. The pole star of course is the prop of the circle of luminary bodies.

Maharloka is situated a crore of *yojanas* above the pole star, where the seven sons of Brahma are lodged. They live there even during the time of Kalpa.

The names of the seven sons of Brahma are Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Kapila, Asuri, Vodhu and Pancasikha.

The planet Sukra (Venus) is lodged at a distance of two lakhs of *yojanas* from Maharloka. At a distance of two lakh *yojanas* from Venus, Budha (Mercury) the son of the moon is lodged.

O Sage, two lakh *yojanas* above that is the planet Mars. Still two lakhs *yojanas* higher one finds Jupiter.

The planet Saturn is lodged at a distance of two lakhs of yojanas. All the seven planets stay in their respective Zodiacs.

Eleven lakh *yojanas* above them is the place of the seven sages. The Dhruva is said to be situated at a distance of fourteen hundred thousand *yojanas,* above the pole star.

Tapaloka is situated at a distance of sixty three hundred thousand *yojanas* from Janaloka, which happens to be the abode of the gods known as Vairajas, who cannot be burnt by fire.

Satyaloka is situated at a distance of four thousand *yojanas* from Tapaloka. This also known as Brahmaloka, where the people with spotless mind live, besides the Brahmacarins engaged in truthful ways. They move from Bhuloka to Brahmaloka.

In the Bhuvarloka, live the sages, gods and the Siddhas. In the Svargaloka, there live the gods, the twelve Adityas, Marut, eight Vasus and Asvinikumaras.

The Visvedevas, Rudras, Sadhyas, Nagas, Khagas also live there, besides the nine planets as well as the auspicious *Rsis.*

O Vyasa, There are the seven Mahalokas and the seven nether worlds, which have been described by me to you. This is how the globe has been spread.

As the wood apple is both above and beneath the earth, similarly the globe is enveloped by the caldron of the cosmic egg.

This cosmic egg is surrounded by ten times with water, fire, wind, sky, darkness, from all the four sides. It is further surrounded by *Mahattatva* (The second of the twenty five elements recognized by Samkhya) by ten times. The Pradhana-Mahattatva is established in Purusa,

The supreme soul is infinite, eternal and beyond measure, because of that he is called limitless.

He is eternal and the cause of all. It is his *Prakrti* (natural form, material cause of world). From the same infinite of unmanifest origin, thousands and lakhs of cosmic eggs are born. As the fire is enshrined in the wood, oil in the gingerly seeds, besides *ghee* in the milk.

Similarly the supreme souls, getting manifest in the entire globe starts from Mahat and ending with Visesa. He produces the eternal seed and the egg is born out of the same. (The birds are born out of the same).

Then the sons are born to them and their progenies further grow from them by which *tattvas* from *Mahat* to *Visesa* (the eternal distiguishing nature) and then the gods are born out of them.

A tree grows from the seed, while the seed emerges from the tree, because of that no harm is caused to the tree. Suryakanta gem emerges from the sun and the fire emerges from the same.

Similarly creation is caused by Brahma, Siva has no desire for the same. Because of the union of Siva and Sakti, the gods and others are born in a natural way.

They emerge out of the *Karmas,* and thereafter they are known as Brahma, Visnu, Rudra, Siva and other names.

The entire universe emerges out of them and are ultimately absorbed in them. Siva is said to be the cause of all the actions.”

Vyasa said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, I have a great doubt in my mind, you kindly remove it. Are there any *lokas* above and below the globe?

Sanatkumara said, “O Excellent Sage, there are lokas above the globe as well. I have arrived here and you please listen to me. I shall describe them briefly.

Vaikunthaloka is better then the Brahmaloka, which is resplendent and happens to be the abode of Visnu.

The wonderful Kumaraloka is above it which is the abode of Kartikeya- the son of Siva.

The extremely divine Umaloka is beyond it, where Sakti-Siva, the mother of the three deities resides.

The form of Siva- Prakrti who is greater than the greatest having the attributes of *sattva, rajas* and *tamas.* She is *nirguna* (having no epithet) and unblemished as well.

Above that is the eternal Sivaloka where resides Siva, who is eternal, beyond destruction, highly divine, extremely graceful, lord of the three gods, where supreme Brahman, Mahesvara Siva lives.

There is no loka beyond that. The Golaka is close to it which is the abode of humble cow.

Sri Krsna, at the command of Siva and Sakti, was deputed there to take care of the cows.

O Vyasa the Siva loka is wonderful, beautiful and without support. It shines with different objects.

Lord Siva, the spotless one, who is supreme soul is the lord of *that* place and is served by Brahma, Visnu and Hara.

O dear one, in this way I have described to you the position of the entire universe. What more do you want to hear about other worlds?

## Chapter 20 - Achieving of Sivaloka with the performing of tapas

Vyasa said, “O Omniscient Sanatkumara, now you kindly speak about the *loka* from where the devotees of Siva do not return after reaching there.

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, the son of Parasara, you lovingly listen about the devotees of Siva and the ascetics, who achieve the auspicious salvation and their *vratas.*

The performers of the auspicious *karmas* besides the penance, adore Siva, daily, and are always adorable.

O great sage, one gets inclined towards performing *tapas* and adoration of Siva by the grace of lord alone. One cannot achieve the pleasant Sivaloka without performing the *tapas.*

The groups of gods, *Rsis* besides the sages spend the time delightfully in the heaven. My words are correct.

The one who is difficult to achieve, who cannot be pleased, who is located far away, who cannot be overcome, can be achieved by means of *tapas.* Infact the *tapas* is not be disturbed.

Even Brahma, Visnu and Siva are engaged in the performing of *tapas*, because all the rare things have been achieved by the gods and the goddesses, by means of *tapas* alone.

The intentions with which one performs the *tapas,* the same is achieved in this world by means of *tapas.* There is no doubt about it.

O Vyasa, the *tapas* is of three types viz. *sattva, rajas* and *tamas.* All the tasks are established by means of *tapas.*

The *tapas* performed by the gods, Sanyasis or recluses and Brahmacaris is treated to be *Sattva.* The *tapas* performed by the demons and the humans is known to be of *rajoguna.*

The *tapas* performed by the Raksasas and other cruel people is treated to be *tamsic.* Such of the learned sages well versed in *tattvas* have described the reward of the same to be of three types.

The recitation by the gods with devotion, meditation and adoration are auspicious. They are treated as *Satvik,* which bestows all the rewards.

It fulfils the desires in this as well as the future world. The *tapas* that is performed with a particular purpose, is treated as *rajas.*

The *tapas* that is performed by severely agonising the body for the fulfilment of the desires is treated as *tamas.*

The Sattvika *tapas* is considered to be the best and the mind is established in *dharma* by the same and the wisdom remains stable. The performing of *puja,* taking bath, performing of *japam, homa,* purification, cleanliness, non-violence, *Vratas,* fasting, keeping silent, controlling of sense organs, maintaining of wisdom, knowledge, truthfulness, not to become angry, giving of charities, forgiveness, suppression of sense organs, compassion, digging of stepwells, wells, tanks, building of houses, performing of *Krcchra* and *Candrayana* vratas, performing of *yoga,* going on pilgrimage, building of *asrama* and *Dharmasala,* cause comforts to the men with wisdom. O Vyasa, these are the best of *dharmas* and enhance devotion towards Siva.

Celebrating of Siva's day of transit, conjunction of equinoxes the Nadamukta, *dhyana* or meditation shall be in all the three occasions. It retains he brilliance of the mind.

Pranayama is of three types viz. *Recaka, Puraka* and *Kumbhaka.* This with the knowledge of the cause of the veins, withdrawal or the obstruction of the senses, are the means of perfect knowledge and the achievements of the eight *Siddhis* like *anima* etc., remaining without pride even after the achieving of these *Siddhas.* This has been treated to be the best path for the gaining of the divine knowledge.

There are three stages in the state of trance, such as the stage of the log of wood, the stage of dead and the stage of *Harita.* All these stages are destructive of all the sins.

The five elements of prosperity of the royal futures are: the woman, bed, drinks, costumes, unguent paste and the betel.
