The forms of various pleasures are block of gold, copper, house, gems, cows, proficiency in the Vedic and post Vedic literature, singing, dance and ornaments.

The conches, *Vina,* cymbals, elephants, *chatras*, fly-whisks, are the things for delight.

O Sage, the man devoid of wisdom, is crushed like the gingelly seeds and rotates like the wheel of the vehicles like spokes.

Inspite of his possessing all the knowledge feeling painful one roams about in the mobile and immobile *yonis* like the watch.

Thus moving through all the *yonis,* he achieves the rare human body, after a long time.

Sometimes because of the glory of his merits, he achieves the human body, because the movements of the *karmas* are wonderful.

The human body is the means for achieving of the heaven and *moksa* and even after achieving the same, he does not do good to himself. After death he keeps on thinking for a long time.

It is difficult for even the gods and the demons to achieve the human body. Therefore after achieving the human body, one should act in a way that he has not to face the agonies of the hell.

In case after getting the human body, if one does not try to achieve heaven or *moksa* then his rare human birth is of no consequence.

The cause of having the human birth is to perform the *Caturvarga* (i.e. *dharma, artha, kama* and *moksa).* O Vyasa, therefore, a person should, as a human being attend to *dharma, artha, kama* and *moksa.*

The human birth is the root of *dharma* and is the cause of achieving all the *Siddhis.* In case one intends to gain, he must protect the roots.

Among the human beings, it is difficult to be a Brahmana, in case he still does not there would be no other fool greater than him, in case he still does not attend to his own welfare.

The land of Bharata is treated to be the *Karmabhumi* as compared to all the continents. One achieves the heaven and *moksa* by making all the efforts here.

A person who does not strive for his own welfare inspite of his attaining the human form in the land of Bharatavarsa, he has indeed deceived his soul.

O Brahmana, this is the land of sacred sites and that is the land of enjoyment. The fruit of the sacred rites performed are enjoyed in the heaven.

One should continue to perform the virtuous deeds as long as his body is healthy and normal. An ailing person is unable to perform anything by others even when he is asked to do so by others.

A person who does not achieve the everlasting *moksa* by means of his impermanent body, his gain of *moksa* lost, because the body is indeed perishable.

Every moment of his life is spent in his full view in the form of the day and night. Then does he not become consciousness then.

When the time of death of anyone is not certain, then who can maintain patience by meeting with sudden death.

When a person leaving everything is about to leave the world (after death), then nobody gives him money to be spent on the way.

But the wealth of virtue earned by him during his life time accompanies him as food packet and his journey is made comfortable. In the absence of such a food packet, one has to face agonies on the way.

Those who have timely collected the merits, they proceed on to the heaven and they gain at every step.

Realising this, a person should perform the noble deeds, discarding the evil ways. With the merits performed by him a person achieves godhood and the sins lead him to the hell.

Even the insignificant people who have taken refuge with Siva, they do not have to visit the hell nor do they have to face Yama.

But because of the sins, at the command of Siva, after living in the hell for a short duration, they return to Sivaloka.

Those who are fully devoted to Siva, they are always free from sins like the lotus flower which is free from mud.

O excellent sage, those reciting the name of Siva- Siva or Hara- Hara, are never afraid of Yama or the hell.

To achieve *moksa* without any agony, one should have the food packed for *paraloka,* collection of merits and the reciting of the name of Siva.

It is only the name of Siva, which removes the ailment of the universe and have not seen anyone else comparable to the same.

In earlier times Pulkasa, who was involved in or number of *Brahmahatyas* achieved salvation with the reciting of the spotless name of Siva.

Therefore a person with wisdom should keep on increasing his devotion for Siva. O Intelligent one, the devotion of Siva bestows devotion as well as the pleasure and *moksa.*

## Chapter 21 - Righteous war and its fruits

Vyasa said, “Brahmanhood is rare by nature. Brahmana has been born out of the face of Siva, Ksatriyas from the arms and Vaisya from the thighs.

Sudras were born out of the feet. This has been ordained by the Vedas. What happens to the places below the same. You please tell me.

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, with the following of the evil path the people fall from the highest place. A Brahmana should protect the highest place, after achieving the same.

Those who are born as Ksatriyas in place of the Brahmanas, they falling from Brahmanhood achievc the position of a Ksatriya.

By following the evil path, a foolish person, wanders in the cycle of birth and death for thousands of births and falls in darkness.

Therefore even after attaining the highest position, one should not became arrogant, nor should be destroy the same, even if he has to face enormous sufferings. Therefore one should always protect his position.

A person who after attaining the auspicious Brahmanhood disrespects the same, and disregards as to what is to be eaten and what not, he becomes a Ksatriyas.

I shall now explain to you as to how an intelligent Sudra achieve the *varna* of a Vaisya.

The duties of a Sudra have to be performed by him as provided in the *Sastras.* The people of all the *varnas* should perform their respective prescribed *dharmas* daily.

A Sudra desirous of becoming Vaisya attains that position. A Vaisya who, using his own money, performs the *Yajnas* appropriately, and perform the *homa* consumes the remnant food as his meals, he is undoubtedly is born in a Ksatriya race.

A Ksatriya, who possessing the *Samskaras* performs the *yajnas* giving *daksina,* with the intention of achieving the heaven, besides engaging himself in studies, before who washing his hands and feet daily entering the shrines, and who enjoys the company of his wife in the period, gives reaches in charities of the people, and fights for the protecting of the cows and the Brahmanas, he by performing these activities as well as with the performing of the *homa* with the reciting of the *mantras,* the Ksatriya becomes a Brahmana. Similarly, being a Brahmana, he becomes entitled to perform the *yajna.*

One who remains devoted to his duties, besides being truthful and controls his sense organs, he becomes dear to the gods in the heaven.

O excellent sage, the Brahmanhood is extremely difficult to achieve, which the humans achieve with great difficulty. With the achieving of the Brahmanhood, one achieves everything upto *moksa.* Therefore, a Brahmana should always be virtuous.

He should preserve his excellent Brahmanhood making all the efforts which is the excellent one of all the aims of life.

Vyasa said, “O excellent sage, you have mentioned about the glory. O foremost of the learned people, I would like to hear the same. You please speak out the same.

Sanatkumara said, “One does not get the type of benefits with the performing of the *homas* and giving away the daksina, as one achieves in the battle ground.

This is what has been ordained by the priests well-versed in the performing of the *yajnas.* Therefore, I shall speak out the fruit of the soldiers holding the weapons.

A valorous warrior who intends to crush the enemy army, he earns *dharma,* glory and the riches.

A person (warrior) who giving away charities, moves the chariot for waging of the war, he achieves the fruit of a *yajna,* performed with the giving of *daksina.*

Such a warrior getting valorous achieves the reward of performing of four *Asvamedha* sacrifices and ultimately proceeds on to Visnuloka.

One who dies in the battleground, holding a weapon, such a warrior never returns from the heaven.

A king, a prince or an army commander or any other Ksatriya warrior who dies in the battleground, he achieves the eternal heaven.

The number of the hair of a warrior which are split in the battleground, with the arrows, he attains the equivalent number of the worlds, which will be wish-yielding and eternal.

O Vyasa, he will have heroic seat, heroic bed, heroic status and heroic stability always both in the present as well as the future worlds.

Those who lay down their lives for the protection of the cows, Brahmanas and the master, they happily achieve the place like the virtuous persons.

One who killing a Brahmana, for the sake of his master, is himself killed in the battle, he also does not return from the heaven.

A person who dies for the sake of a Brahmana, the cows and his master, with the attack of a wild animal, or a beast or a tusked beast, he is treated as an excellent one and earns extensive and never ending benefits.

A worthy, person can perform hundreds of *yajnas* but it is difficult to lay down one's life in the battlefield.

For all the *varnas* and more so for a Ksatriya, all types of wars bestow merits and beautiful forms.

Now I shall speak about the *Sanatana dharma* as to which one of the persons should be killed or saved.

In case a Vedanta Brahmana becomes violent, and rushes to attack you, then he should be killed and by doing so, one does not earn the sin of *Brahmahatya.*

O Vyasa, in case a person who is fit to be killed but asks for water, then he should not be killed. A person who kills a such person in the battle he earns the sin of *Brahmahatya.*

A person who kills a sick person, a weak, a child, woman, orphan, miserly person, one standing erect, one with a broken bow or whose bowstring is broken should not be killed and the one who does so earns the sin of *Brahmahatya.*

An intelligent person who fights keeping all these things in view his life becomes successful and he feels delighted in the present as well as the future world.

## Chapter 22 - Genesis and evolution of the body

Vyasa said, “O excellent sage, how does the living being remain in the mother's womb in the process of birth. You kindly mention with purpose of achievement of the vairagya or detachment.

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, I shall now speak out in brief the essence of all the scriptures, which bestows detachment and removes the worldly bondages.

The grains left in the water vase, remains separate from it. The water's placed above the fire and the grains are kept above the same.

The fire kindled below the water, with the help of the wind, gets ignited and with the burning fire, the water gets heated.

The grain starts cooking with hot water around it. The food eaten by a person separates in two parts viz. the thick sediment or the element and the juicy one.

(In the body, the similar process is noticed). The thick element in the body comprises of the twelve forms of the sediment waste, which get split and are forced out of the body, while the juicy element gets circulated in the body. This provides nourishment to the body.

The dirt element of the body is emitted through the twelve exist points viz. the ears, the nose, the teeth, anus, penis, cough, sweating, stools and urine.

O Sage, O Sage, all the veins spread over the entire body are joined at heart like a lotus. These veins carry the juices of the body and the methodology used in the same is being spoken by me.

The subtle juice is carried in the mouth by the Prana-Vayu or vital air. The vital air then fills the entire veins with the said juice or colourless liquid.

Then the colourless liquid gets cooked inside the veins with the fire in the body. There are two possible modes of cooking i.e. the separation of the sediment or the liquid part of it. Initially the skin is formed which covers the entire body. Thereafter the blood is formed.

The blood produces the hair, flesh on the body, hair on the head and sinew (or the cord connecting the muscle with bone), the marrow and the nails are produced from bones.

From the marrow also emerges the semen which is the cause of conception. In this way the food consumed has twelve types of effects. Thus the twelve fold chemical processing of food in the body has been explained.

The semen is extracted from food, consumed by a person. It is by the semen that birth of another body is made possible with the consumption of food, the semen is formed. By cohabiting with a woman during the prescribed period, the semen enters the vaginal passage. Then the semen blown with the vital wind merges with the blood of the woman. At the time when the semen is discharged, the individual soul with the casual body, or the unit of sense organs etc. enters the vaginal passage fully covered and urged by its past conduct. The semen and the blood in the unified state becomes foetus in a day, and becomes Kalila in a week. In five nights, it takes the form of bubbles, which take to the form of foetus in seven nights.

In two months, the neck, the head, the shoulders, the backbone, the belly, hands, lips and feet of the foetus are formed. In three months time, the join are formed.

In the fourth month, the fingers are formed. In the fifth month, the face, nose and ears are formed.

In the sixth month, the gums, nails, holes in the ears, are formed.

In the seventh month anus, penis of the vaginal passage, yoni and the navel are formulated. Within the seventh month, all the limb-joints are formed.

O excellent sage, the jiva with all its limbs remains covered with embryo-skin in the womb of his mother.

The infant in the womb keeps on developing day by day, stealthily deriving food from the mother, of all the six tastes through the umbilical cord.

With the completion of the body, the memory is received in the body. Then it is reminded of the pleasures and pains of its earlier births, besides the sleep and the dreams.

Then it realises that it died, reborn, again dead, reborn and thus having reborn and died thousands of times, passing through the several yonis.

Presently soon after my birth, achieving the auspicious Samskaras shall perform noble deeds with this body to avoid my re-entry in the womb.

I had been then thinking in the womb, when I came out of the womb. I shall now aspire for the search of the knowledge of Siva, which bestows salvation from the universe.

Thus feeling painful in the womb because of the distress as a result of his past actions, the jiva (individual soul) thinks of the means for achieving moksa.

As a person surrounded by the mountains (slanting lands), feels miserable, similarly the jiva having been surrounded by the membrane in the womb, feels miserable.

As a person feels disturbed with a fall in the ocean, similarly the creature, during the period of pregnancy, having been drowned in the water of the womb feels painful.

As a person is roasted in an iron vase with the fire, similarly the creature placed in the vase like womb is heated with the gastric fire.

As the pains are felt with the continuous piercing of red needles, staying in the womb of the mother is equally painful.

All the creatures having bodies have to face horrible miseries, but the painful situation one has to face in the womb of the mother has no parallel.

The creatures with noble souls are born in the seventh month, but the sinners have to face immense pain.

O Vyasa, one does not feel pain more than that in the womb of the mother. At the time of birth, the sinners have to face enormous pain at the time of his emerging from the vaginal passage of the mother, but the noble souls do not have to suffer from such a pain.

The position of the body becomes like the crushing of the sugarcane in the mill, similarly the sinner gets tortured at the time of his birth like the beating with mudgara.

As the gingelly oil seeds after having been crushed in the oil mill are produced without substances, in a moment, the condition of the body at the time of birth, becomes similar.

The body lies in the womb in an unenviable condition. It is bound with the veins, plastered with the clay of flesh and blood, like a vase of refuse and urine.

It has hair on the head and the body, besides the nails. It is the abode of ailments, the main gate in the form of a mouth, with eight windows.

There are two doors in the form of lips, argala in the form of tongue. The body is sick because of the lust for pleasure. It is subservient to attachment and hatred.

All its limbs are covered with membrane. Facing painful situation, it emerges out of the vaginal passage.

It is soaked in filth, urine and blood. It is the ball of bones, born in open condition comes out the sheath.

It has three hundred and sixty bones, five hundred muscles, and is covered with thirty five million hair.

The vessels which are three and a half crores in number are visible as well as invisible, besides being gross and subtle.

The internal secretions move within the body and come out through these veins. The number of teeth is thirty two and twenty nails.

In the body, the measure of the bile content is a quarter of the measure, cough is four seers, fat is two seers and half of it is the tawny matters.

The weight of solid fat is 2'A tulas and the palas. Blood is three palas and is four times the marrow.

The semen is half a kudava, the strength of a person depends on the same. The flesh content in the body weighs a thousand palas.

O excellent sage, the blood is a hundred palas according to which the human waste and urine form four handfulls each.

Thus the unholy and perishable abode of the auspicious and eternal soul, which is bound with the bondages of the actions.

## Chapter 23 - The impurity of the body and sufferings in childhood

Sanatkumara said, “O Immensely intelligent sage, Vyasa, you listen, I am going to speak about the impurities in the body and their importance, in brief.

The body is considered to be impure, because it is formed of the semen and blood and is filled with filth as well as urine.

It is like a vase filled with filth and as such, though it outwardly looks pure, but in reality it is impure. Similarly, the body though is purified outwardly, but inwardly it is not so.

The extremely auspicious pancagavya as well as the havidravyas also get polluted with the mere touch of the body in a moment. What more impurity could be these.

The fragrant food items as well as the beverages, which delight the mind become impure, in a moment, with the touch of the body. What could be more impurity than this?

O humans, do you not observe that the filth and urine, which daily emerges from the body, (which are impure) then how could the body, which is the source of the same could be pure?

Even when the body is purified with pancagavya and the water of the kusa grass, it cannot be purified or become spotless like the coal powder.

How could the body be pure, which is the source of cough, urine, filth and other things?

The body indeed is the store house of impurities, even a single part of which is not pure like a bag of filth and urine.

After the flowing out of the filth and other types of dirt from the body the hands are washed and purified with the use of dust and water, but still the same (impurities) can never be separated from the body.

Even when you decorate the body with the fragrant materials, but still its nature does not change like the dog's tail.

As a thing which is originally black cannot be made white, similarly the body even after its purification can never be spotless.

Smelling the odour, observing his own filth, pressing the nose, one never feels detached.

Wonderful is the glory of this delusion, which has covered the entire universe. Even after observing the blemishes of his own body, he never feels detached.

One who does not feel detached from the filth of his own body, what more cause of detachment could be taught to him?

The bodies of all the humans are impure in this world. With the touch of the impure limbs of the body, even the auspicious things become inauspicious.

Purification of the body has been prescribed for the removal of its odour or the pastes. By removing both of them and with the application of the pure elements, the body is purified.

Even when a body is cleaned with the heaps of sand resembling a mountain, using the water of the auspicious Ganga performing the purificatory rites till death, a man with wicked feelings and emotions, can hardly be purified.

The evil soul can hardly be purified by having a bath at a holy place. Can the skin of a dog be purified by washing it at a holy place?

A person who se mind is polluted and even if he enters the fire, he can achieve nothing else beyond the burning of his body, and the benefit of earning the heaven or the moksa would be out of question for him.

Even when a person with an evil mind takes bath in the holy water of the Ganga for the entire life with the application of the dust or the sand resembling a mountain, even then be can never be purified. We declare this.

A person who is evil by nature, in case he enters the burning fire in which the ghee and oil has been poured, with its flames flowing towards the south, he can neither achieve dharma nor any other auspicious reward.

The fish live in the Ganga, while the birds live in several other holy places including the temples, but they drive no special benefit from the ceremonial ablutions and charitable gifts, in the absence of any holy or devotional feelings.

The purity of mind is the sole criterion for the performing of the deeds. A person embraces his wife with a different feeling and the daughter with a different feelings. This is the best example in this regard.

Feelings in the mind are different even if the objects are not different the same woman is looked at by the son by different feeling and by the husband by the different feelings.

Look at the great fortunes of the feelings. A person having no feelings, even when embraced by a woman, has no desire for her.

When a person is overpowered with the feelings of kama, krodha and lobha, then he cannot enjoy the tasteful and fragrant food served to him.

Because of the emotions a person is caught and he can rid himself of the emotions. The pure emotions can purify a person who achieves heaven and salvation with the same.

A person with the purified emotions when performs japam, sacrifices and prayers, attains the perfect knowledge and after his death he attains the place of the people perform mg yajnas.

Using the spotless water of the divine knowledge, besides the dust of Vairagya (detachment) the odour of a person arising out of filth and urine is removed.

In this way the body is impure by nature and is worthless. It has only the outer skin as Substantial like the minor stump of a plantain tree.

An intelligent person should understand that the body is faulty and defective. He shall therefore be disinterested in the emotions of the body, remaining peaceful.

Getting free from the worldly bondages, be becomes a living liberated soul and considers the world to be of no consequence, like the minor stump of the banana tree.

I have described the extremely painful birth caused because of the ignorance or the evil deeds of the human beings.

I shall explain the idea in half a verse, which has been discussed in the crores of scriptures. To say that “This is mine”, is the cause of pain and to say that “nothing belongs to me” is the cause of comfort.

Many of the kings devoid of attraction, achieved salvation and hundreds and thousands of the kings remained caught in the bondages of attraction.

The memory which is preserved by a jiva in the womb is destroyed with the bearing of the agony of the birth on coming out of the womb.

With the touch of the worldly wind, or because of delusion, a great fever overwhelms him.

Due to the said fever, he is overpowered with a great fascination which deludes him and he suffers from the loss of memory.

Because of the loss of memory, he does not remember the events of his earlier births, and as such he gets attached to the present life.

Having been overpowered by the attraction, the foolish jiva, does not get attracted to the noble deeds in this world. Because of this, he is unable to realise, either himself nor even the god.

O excellent sage, inspite of his having the ears, he is unable to listen to the things of his own welfare.

On walking over the even surface, he slips quite often and inspite of his having wisdom and well advised by the learned people, he is unable to understand anything.

He feels agonised in the world for his re¬entry into the womb. Having been reminded of the sins in womb, his wisdom is lost.

Thus lord Siva has composed this Sastra which is immensely divine, and relates to the tapas for achieving heaven and the salvation.

It is really surprising that inspite of the availability of the Sastra which fulfils all the desires, people do not think of their own welfare.

A child in his childhood, is unable to control his sense organs, nor can he speak anything. This is extremely painful.

At the time of cutting the teeth, it is quite painful. Several of the ailments of infancy besides the planets also cause trouble.

Sometimes the infant cries when he is thirsty. Because of ignorance the infant consumes even the filth and the urine.

During the childhood, the child has to bear pain, when he ears are bored, or when a medicine is to be taken or at the time of learning, a child has to face difficult situations.

The foolish follow does not think of his welfare, even after facing these miseries. It is quits surprising.

In the youthful age, when he develops a desire to enjoy the pleasures of sense organs and when they are not fulfilled, there shall be no question of comfort.

For a person overpowered with delusion, the jealousy is quite painful. His eyes are indication of pain like or person who is infuriated.

Because of his passions, he is unable to sleep during the night, while during the day time he is worried for of earning the livelihood.

The drops of semen of a person who is lustful with his mind engaged in women when dropped, they cannot make him comfortable like the drops of sweat.

A leprous monkey, when it scratches itself having been afflicted with worms, the same pleasure is derived by cohabiting with a woman.

The pleasure one derives from the company of a woman, is equal to the pleasure derived from a boil by removing the puss. There is nothing more to it.

The comfort one get with the release of the filth and the urine, the same type of pleasure is achieved from the woman. The fools interpret the same differently.

The women possess the improper things, besides the blemishes and there is no comfort with them. This has been declared by the Pancacuda (having five tufts).

The youthful age is overpowered with grace, disgrace, meeting and separation. It is followed by old age. Therefore there is disturbance in the old age.

The love between a man and a woman which had been mutually pleasurable in the young age declines during the old age because the body becomes weak, the skin develops wrinkles, the hairs become grey and no strength is left in the body to perform any serious task.

The one who remains attracted to the body even after its reaching the old age, who would be more foolish or unconscious than him.

In the old age, a person is disgraced by daughters, sons, relatives and even the servants who cannot be kept under control because they are not attached to him.

An old man becomes incapable of achieving dharma, artha, kama and moksa therefore, these could be achieved in the youthful age.

## Chapter 24 - Nature of women as described by the apsara Pancacuda

Vyasa said, “The apsara Pancacuda denounced the women, therefore, O Sage, in ease you are happy with me, then you speak out the same in brief.

Sanatkumara said, “O Brahmana, I shall speak out correctly the nature of women (as defined by Pancacuda) listening to which a person develops detachment.

O Sage, light minded women are the roots of all the blemishes, therefore, a person desirous of moksa, should be careful and should not be attracted towards them.

In this connection the story of conversation between the apsara Pancacuda and Narada is frequently quoted, which I am going to repeat.

Narada, after roaming about in all the places met for the first time the beautiful apsara Pancacuda.

Then the sage Narada asked the apsara with the curved eyebrows. “O slander waisted one, I have a doubt in my mind, which you please remove.”

At these words of Narada the excellent apsara said, “In case you consider me competent enough then you speak out your doubt to me.”

Narada said, “O beautiful and slander waisted one, I shall enquire an improper thing from you. I shall like to know about the nature of the women from you.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the divine sage, the excellent apsara spoke to the sage Narada.

Pancacuda said, “O Sage, a chaste woman should not be denounced by the women. All the people know about their nature.

O divine sage, do not force me to answer such type of question.” Thus speaking the apsara Pancacuda kept quiet.

Narada on the other hand listening to her pleasing words, keeping in view the welfare of the people, spoke to her again.

Narada said, “To make a false statement could be wrong and earns blemish. But there is no fault in speaking the truth. O slander waisted one, therefore you speak out the truth.”

Sanatkumara said, “At these words of Narada, the nymph with a smiling face started speaking out the common faults of the women.

Pancacuda said, “O Narada, this is the defect in the women that even the women of noble families, the women, whose husbands are live and are quite beautiful sometime do not stand within the limits of decency.

No one is more sinner than the women. The women are the roots of the sins. You should well understand this.

The women inspite of their having good husbands, good knowledge, ample wealth, great comeliness, and are quite pleasing, but when they get an opportunity with well known persons, and even for erring they going near them do not wait.

O lord this is the sinful way of we the women. We shedding away the shame, serve even the sinful people.

A person who desires a woman, approaches her, and serves her a little, the women start looting him.

When the men are not lustful, or because of the fear of the husbands, the women remain within the limits.

They do not disgrace anyone nor do they desire for the person of any particular age. They can serve even the beautiful as well as the ugly people.

It is not due to the fear, or by shouting or taunts, by riches the caste, or the relationship of the race, that the women remain faithful to their husbands.

Even the women of the noble families, desire to associates themselves with fallen women clad in the best of garments and adorned with the best of ornaments.

Such of the women who are lovingly kept in the house, with respect, they also get attraction towards the blind, hunch-back and dwarf, men.

O great sage, O divine sage, there are also other degraded people in the world and the women sometimes accept them as well.

O Brahman, in case the women do not get man live to some reason, then they without caring for their husbands, get attracted with other women and indulge into unnatural second activity.

The woman get disappointed in the absence of their husbands, for fear of their husbands, or due to the fear of death or captivity.

The fickle minded woman, those with evil desires, cannot be overpowered otherwise. An intelligent person can overpower her at the time of sexual intercourse.

As the fire never feels satisfied with the burning of the wood, the ocean is not satisfied by getting the water of the river, or Yama is not satisfied by the death of the people, similarly the women do not get satisfied by getting the men.

O divine saint\* there is only one secret with the woman that at the very sight of the men their vaginal passage starts emitting secretions.

On seeing a man fresh and clean from his bath with his body, perfumed with fragrance, the vaginal passage of the women starts dropping secretion as the water drops oozing from the leather-water-bag.

She does not allow or tolerate her husband who fulfils all her desires, protects her, giving her honour or consolation.

The women do not consider their welfare as much with the enjoying of the pleasures, nor with the ornaments nor with the collection of the riches as compared to the pleasure desired by them from the sexual intercourse.

The woman can well be compared with the god of death, Yama, Antaka, Patala, submarine fire, the sharp edge of a sword, poison, serpents and fire, all put together.

O Narada, the source from which Brahma created the Panca mahabhutas (five great elements), the worlds, and the source from which the men and women were created, the woman was created with blemishes.”

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of the nymph, and taking them to be true, Narada felt detached.

O Vyasa, I have narrated about the nature of the woman, as was explained by the apsara Pancacuda, which is the cause of my getting detached. Now what else do you intend to listen from me.

## Chapter 25 - Awareness about the time of death

Vyasa said, “O omniscient sage, Sanatkumara, I have learnt from you about the nature of the women. Now you enlighten me on the knowledge of Kala pleasantly.

Sanatkumara said, “The same question had been asked by Parvati, who had been feeling pleased with the listening to the various stories, from Siva in earlier times.

Parvati said, “O lord, O Deva, by your grace, I have learnst from you all the means of your devotion including the relevant mantras and the related methodology.

O lord, even now, I have a doubt about Kalacakra. Therefore, you kindly speak out the sign of death and the extent of life.

O lord, in case I am dear to you, then you speak out in the way, by which, I may be able to understand the same.” When so asked by the goddess.

The lord said, “O beloved, I shall narrate to you the opinion of the best of scriptures, by which the humans will be able to understand the kalacakra.

The days, fortnights, months, seasons, the ayanas (transit of sun) year and other are outer, inner, gross and the subtle signs.

O beautiful one, O Uma, I am going to speak on the subject more clearly, which will benefit the people who will develop detachment.

O dear, in case the body becomes pale from all the sides, quite suddenly, and the upper limbs become read, then one should understand that the concerned person would die in six months.

When the face, ears, eyes or the tongue are paralysed, the death would occur in six months.

O beautiful one, when a person does not hear the sound of a shrill cry, the person understanding Kala, can declare the person to die in six months time.

In case a person is unable to visualise the lustre of the sun, moon or the fire he will remain alive for six months and no more.

O beloved, in case the left hand throbs for a month, then it is certain that the man shall live for a month only.

When the limbs of a person fold and expand and the palate dries up, then the person will undoubtedly live for a month alone.

In the fever of mental aberration, when the nose starts emitting water, the concerned person will live for a fortnight. The one, whose face and throat, dry up, he will die after six months.

O beautiful one, a person whose tongue is swollen, and dirt accumulates in the teeth, such a person with the sign of death shall live for six months alone.

O beautiful one, a person who is unable to see to his own reflection in the water, oil, ghee or the mirror or finds no figure or a deformed figure, the people well aware of the kalacakra shall think that he will live for six months alone. O goddess, there are other means also to know about the time of death.

A person who looks at his shade without a head, he cannot remain alive even for a month.

O Parvati, these signs of death were linked with the limbs of the body. O beautiful one, I shall now speak of the outer signs. You listen to them.

When the solar or moon disc becomes visible without the rays, or is seen with red colour, then the person dies in a fortnight.

A person who visualises the star Arundhati, or the moon with black spot, or if the stars are not visible to anyone, he lives only for a month.

When a man gets confused about the directions, utathya or the polar star, or the solar zone, on looking at the planet, he dies within six months.

When a man find the rainbow in the sky during the night or the fall of comet at noon, or is surrounded by crows and the vultures, he dies in six moths.

In case one is unable to see the seven stars (saptarsis) and the Akasaganga or the milky way in the sky, he can live for six more months. This has been declared by the experts.

In case one sees the sun or the moon suddenly being eclipsed by Rahu, finds the directions rotating, then the said person is sure to die in six months.

A person who is suddenly surrounded by the blue flies, he surely dies in a month's time.

In case a vulture, crow or a pigeon suddenly pushes over the head of a person, he surely dies in a month's time.

Thus I have named the outer inauspicious signs about the death of a person for the benefit of the people. Now I shall speak out something quite briefly.

O goddess, one can see kala in both the right and left hands, which has been directly narrated.

In fact, O beautiful goddess, these are two fortnights, in which one has to take bath and be clear and remember the lord with his sense organs under control.

He shall wash his hands with red lac and milk. Then taking the fragrant flowers in hand he should think of good and bad.

O beloved, starting from the little finger, and ending at the thumb, the nyasa has to be made of each one of the tithis on each knot. Thus the two hands together will cover the mouth, which should be kept in a cup to be form and sit facing the east.

Then he should recite the Navatmaka mantra (om namo bhagavate rudraya) a hundred and eight times looking at the same time each and every knot of the fingers of both the hands.

O beloved one, in case in east a live looks like the bee, the death shall occur on the same tithi which could be of the bright or dark fortnight.

O beloved, I shall now speak out the sings of kala emerging out of the nada which has to be taken into account with the process of breathing (inhaling or exhaling).

O lady of slender waist, the service of the soul should be well understood, including the day of the week, the moment, truti, lava, nimesa, kastha muhurta, day and night, dark or bright fortnight, month, season, ayana (movement of sin), yuga, kalpa and mahakalpa.

Sadasiva calculates the time by three paths, viz., left, right and middle.

Starting from the fifth and ending with twenty fifth are the calculative of sound recording to the vamacara or left hand practises which are called nadapramana and have been told to you.

O beautiful one, bhutarandhra, disa (the quarters), the banner are the sounds of the left hand practices.

O fair complexioned lady, in case the attributes and the aberrations are added to it, it forms the right hand practices or daksina- nada.

When Ida and several other nadis, respire for five days continuously, then a person surely dies in a year's time.

In case they respire for ten days, he lives for a year. If they respire for fifteen days, he will die after a year.

When they respire for twenty days, he will live for six months. In case the left vein respires for twenty five days, then he will die within three months. In case its respires for twenty six days, his end will come in two months.

In case the nadis (veins) respire incessantly for twenty seven days, then he will live for a month.

This has been known in accordance with the left hand practices. In case the respiration is on the right side, then he will meet with his and in four days.

O goddess, these sixteen veins are lodged in four places. This three are sixteen veins in all. I shall now describe their extent factually.

Beginning with six days and calculating duly it happens as mentioned in the left path.

When the nada moves over the pranavayu for six days, then the personalities live for two years, eight months and eight days.

In case the pranavayu respirates for seventeen days, the person shall live for a year, seven months and six days undoubtedly.

With the respiration of the pranavayu continuously for eight days, the person will meet with his end in two years, four months and twenty four days.

When the pranavayu respires for nine days, a person can live for five or two months and twelve days.

The period of the previous days has been mentioned before, but the intervening days of the month should thus be calculated.

In case the pranavayu respirates for a year, a person lives for nine months and eight days.

In case it respirates for twelve days, he lives for a year, seven months and six days.

In case the vein respirates for thirteen days, then a person lives for a year and four months and twenty four days. Where the prana flows in the left side, for fourteen days, a person lives for a year, six months and twenty four days.

The people well-versed in the knowledge of Kala, believe that when the pranavayu respirates for fifteen days, a person lives for nine months and twenty four days.

According to the people well-versed in the source of kala, when the pranavayu respirates for sixteen days, a person lives for ten months and twenty four days.

O goddess of the devotees, in case the pranavayu respirates for seventeen days, then a person dies in nine months and eighteen days.

O goddess, with the flowing of the pranavayu for eighteen days on the left side, one dies in eight months and twelve days.

O goddess when the pranavayu respires for twenty three days, he certainly lives for five months i.e. four months and twenty four + six days = five months. If for twenty four days, he lives for three months and eighteen days. This has all been narrated to you in brief.

This is in accordance with *vamacara* or left hand practices. Now listen to the similar provision of the right hand practices. When the pranavayu respirates for twenty eight days, a person lives for fifteen days.

With the respiration for ten days, he dies in the similar number of days. With the respiration of thirty days, he dies in five days.

O goddess in case the pranavayu respirates for thirty one days continuously, then he surely dies in the three days.

When the Surya-nadli respires for thirty two times, then he can undoubtedly live for two days only.

I have thus explained to you the condition of the right hand pranas. Now I speak to you about the middle pranas. When the flow of the wind is on one side in the mouth, then with the flow of that breath, a person lives for a day only. The ancient people well-versed in kalacakra have described accordingly.

O goddess, I have narrated to you the kalacakra relating to the people concerning death for the benefit of the people. Now you tell me what more do you want to listen from me.

## Chapter 26 - Competence of the Yogis to avert the death

The goddess said, “O lord, you have spoken about kala in an ordinary way. Now you tell me to how the Yogis face the kala.

As the kala approaches all the living beings. O lord merciful on one, you tell me as to how the approaching kala can be deceived. O bestower of the happiness you please tell me for the benefit of the Yogis.”

Siva said, “I am going to answer all whatever has been desired by you for the benefit of the humans.

The body has been formed with the five elements like the earth, water, tejas (Agni), Vayu (wind) and the sky.

The sky is all pervading and is lodged in all. All are absorbed in the same and then again they emerge out of the same.

O charming lady, when the ether is disintegrated the elements resort to their causes. The conglomeration of the Parambhutas never remains stationary.

The learned people are well aware of every thing because of the strength of this tapas and mantras undoubtedly.

The goddess said, “Kala of the terrible form, the horrible and the only lord of the gods was reduced to ashes by you and then you were eulogised with the reciting of the stotras. You restored him to the charming position getting delighted.

You by mean of the stay of the Kala, told him that he world move about in the world in an invisible form and then you found the kala with enormous influence. Therefore that kala, as the result of the promising of the boon from you got up at once.

O Kala, is there anything here, with which you could be killed? You tell me. O Mahesa, you are the best and excellent among the Yogis. You are the lord, you are independent. You have taken to this body for the welfare of all.”

Siva said, “The kala cannot be killed by the gods, Daityas, Yaksas, Raksasas, serpents and even the humans, but can be bodily killed by the Yogis engaged in meditation, quite comfortably.

Sanatkumara said, “Listening to the words of Siva, the lord of the three worlds, Parvati smiled and said O Master, you tell me truthfully, the way of killing the Kala.” Then Siva replied to her at once, “O moon faced one, the way, the sinless yogis kill the serpent like kala, you listen from one.

Siva said, “O beautiful one, the body with five elements, is born with its own merits and ultimately it gets absorbed in the same tattvas.

The Vayu (wind) is formed out of the sky, from Vayu the tejas (or Agni) is born, the water emerges from the tejas are formed the water and the earth tattvas.

Each one of the element merges with the other in a sequence. Out of them, the earth has five attributes, the waters has four, attributes. The five has three, the wind has two, while the sky has only one. The attributes of the earth and other elements, are thus mentioned.

The five attributes are sound (Sabda), sparsa (touch), rupa (colour), rasa (taste) and gandha (the smell). When the body is relieved of its attributes, it perishes.

When all the elements resume their own attributes, the jiva is said to have been born. O goddess, thus you should recognise all the five bhutas appropriately.

O goddess, the Yogis, desirous of overcoming the kala, should making all the efforts, think of the partial attributes.”

The goddess said, “O lord well-versed in the yoga, how is kala desired to be overpowered by the Yogis? Can it be done by the reciting of the mantras or by meditation. You better explain the same to me.

Siva said, “O goddess, listen, I shall explain the topic to you for benefit of the Yogis. This knowledge should not be imparted to ordinary people.

O fair complexioned lady, this knowledge should be imparted to the faithful, the religious minded, people endowed with devotion, and the persons with spotless mind and those who are virtuous.

One should perform the practice of yoga, seated over an auspicious seat and take to pranayama, stopping breathing, in darkness without lighting a lamp, when all the people go to sleep.

One should close both his ears by pressing with the index finger, one hears a sound emerging from his stomach like the blocking of the fire.

Meditating on that sound, when it vanishes in a moment, then it destroys fever and other ailments.

A person who daily visualises that form for two ghatikas, he overpowers the death at will and roams about in the world freely as per his own desire.

He becomes omniscient and omniseer, attaining all the siddhis. The sound resembles the thunder sound of the clouds in the sky.

Listening to that sound, a yogi is atonce relieved of the worldly bondages. Then he becomes the subties of all the Yogis.

O goddess, I have narrated to you the sequence of method of Sabda-brahma. As a person desirous of paddy, discard the husk, similarly, a yogi should rid himself of all the bondages of the world.

Achieving the knowledge of Sabda- Brahma, a person who is desirous of other things, they behave like attacking the sky with the fist and want hunger and thirst.

Getting aware of the supreme Brahman which is the cause of salvation, is indestructible, free from all the limitations, nothing else should be aspired thereafter since it make the people comfortable.

Those who are entangled in the noose of kala, and are caught in the jaws of death, those are unaware of Sabda-brahma.

They roam about in this world till thing achieve the supreme place. After realising about the supreme reality, he is relieved of the worldly bondage.

Seated over a comfortable asana devoting himself at Sabdabrahman, overcoming the enemies like the sleep and laziness.

A person having the age of a hundred years, should devote himself to this practice for the whole life, as a result of which he will gain health, virility and the power to present the decay of the body besides the conquering of the death. The practice can be continued for the whole life.

Even the old people have developed faith in this, what to speak of the youthful people. In this method omkara or mantras have not to be followed, nor the bijaksara or seed syllables.

O beloved goddess, the Sabda brahman is not to be uttered, but it bestows enormous welfare.

Thus the Sabdas are nine-fold, as have been declared by the people well-versed in the secrets of breath. I shall speak them out in a proper sequence according tot he Siddhi of nada.

The nine Sabdas comprise of Ghosa (sound of soft consonant) Kansya (sound of bell metal), Sringa (sound of horn), ghanta (the bell), vina (lute), vamsaja (flute), dundubhi (drum) Samkha (conch) and Meghagarjita (thundering of the cloud).

Discarding all these sounds, one should practice tunkara. Thus a yogi, engaged in meditation is never involved in merits or the sins.

O goddess, when a person engaged in yogic practices is unable to hear making all his efforts to do so, a yog! should keep himself engaged in the yogic practices throughout the day and night.

While he is so engaged in his meditation, the sound of the conquest of the death rises from his body in seven days, which O goddess, is of nine types, details of which are being mentioned by me.

The fast sound is ghosa, which destroys all the ailments, purifies the soul. It is excellent besides being attractive and exercises its control.

The second one is kamsyanada. It stops the free movements of the living beings and undoubtedly seizes the effect of the planets and poisonous elements.

The third one is the sound of the horn which is used in black magic for overpowering the enemies and for killing them.

The fourth one is the sound of the bell. According to Siva, it attracts all the gods, then what to speak of the humans on earth.

Attracted with this sound, the virgins of Yaksas and the Gandharvas, bestow great siddhis on him as per his desire or of their own accord.

Vina is the fifth sound, by which arises the power of distance from great distance. This sound is heard by the Yogis.

A person mediating on vamsa-nada is enlightened on all the principles. The one who meditates on dundubhi is freed from old age and death.

Sankhanada is the eighth sound, O goddess, on hearing its sound, the Yogis can assume, form at will. The ninth sound is Meghanada with the influence of which a yogi is freed from all the miseries.

O pretty faced lady, the one who meditates tunkara, the form of Brahman with devotion he achieves success in all his efforts. He becomes omniscient and visualiser. He moves at his will and does not attract any blemishes. He is to be taken as Siva himself. There is no doubt about it.

O goddess, thus the form of Sabda brahman with its nine aspects has been fully explained to you. What more do you want to hear?

## Chapter 27 - Achieving Siva by escaping from death

The goddess said, “O lord, in case you are pleased with me, then you tell me as to how a yogi attains the region of wind arising from yogic sky.

Siva said, “I have already spoken much for the benefit of the Yogis including the way, overpowering kala, turn to the form of wind.

O beautiful one, getting aware of the particular day through that means, the yogi performs pranayama. O beautiful lady, in a fortnight's time he overpowers kala that has already come upon him.

The wind in the heart ignites the fire. The great wind which follows the fire remains pervading inside and outside everywhere.

The knowledge, science, enthusiasm and everything else is activated by the wind. The one who controls the wind, he controls everything in the world.

The Yogis absorb themselves in yogic practices for the purpose of eliminating the old age and death.

O Sage, as the blacksmith blows into the bellows and performs his job with the use of wind, the yogi has to perform in the same manner.

The lord having a thousand hands, eyes and feet, encompasses the universe and measure ten fingers beyond that.

Performing the pranayama, one should upward hold the breath, recite the Gayatri-mantra thrice affixing om to it besides Vyahrti. This is called pranayama.

The planets like the sun and the moon keep on coming and going, but a yogi engaged in meditation, never returns till date.

O goddess, for a hundred years, when a Brahmana consumes the water equivalent to a drop of water found over the tip of the kusa grass, he earns the fruit equivalent to the performing of the pranayama once.

A Brahmana, who getting up early in the morning, getting purified performs pranayama, he having been freed from all the sins proceeds on to Brahmaloka.

The one who shedding away the laziness, performs pranayama in a secluded place, he, overpowering the old age and death, roams in the sky.

Such a person like the siddha-purusa, achieving lustre, wisdom, strength and valour and the speed of the wind, enjoys all the praiseworthy comforts.

O goddess, the way a yogi attains a Siddhi, has been explained by me. Now I shall tell you the lustre and the Siddhi achieved by him.

A yogi is seated in the comfortable posture in a secluded place free from noise. In the middle place he displays brilliance together with the lustre of the sun and the moon.

The yogi devoid of lethargy, develops the light in between the two eyebrows, which is visible in darkness even in the absence of a lamp.

The yogi rubbing their eyes with their fingers should look at the stars and he should meditate on it for a muhurta or a half of it with concentration.

While observing the brilliance comparable with the rising sun, between the eyebrows, he also visualises in darkness the lustre resembling the rainbow colours like white, red, yellow and black. This is the lustre of Siva.

Finding the lustre like the rising sun, between the two eyebrows, the yogi who moves at will, sports independently.

By constant yogic practices, a yogi, gains several powers like the control of senses, entry into the body of others, achieving of eight siddhis like anima and others, mental vision, hearing from distant places, Vijnana or the knowledge of science, becoming invisible or assuming many forms, and the strength to fly in the sky.

Because of the deeds of the previous birth, the people well versed in the scriptures, sometimes get deluded.

The sinful people do not see even when they gaze it. Even while hearing they are as good as deaf, they behave like blind persons.

I am aware of the supreme soul, who is beyond the sun and the darkness. By knowing about him, a human being is freed from the jaws of death. There is no other path beyond this for the achieving of moksa.

I have thus narrated the best way of the resplendence, with the application of which the yogi overpowering Kala, achieves eternalship.

O goddess, now I speak on the subject by which a person escapes death. You listen to it carefully.

O goddess, the yogis, form the fourth part the other three are the bhutas, the yogis and meditators. The devotee practicing the fourth method is seated in comfortable posture at a convenient place with a spotless mind keeping his body straight. His hands are joined like a cap. The shape of his mouth is like the beak and he inhales the air slowly. The water drops clinging to his palate begin to exude, which are the gains of life, which he inhales through the air. By drinking his nectarine cool water, daily, he will never be overpowered by the death. He gets a divine body free from hunger and thirst.

In strength he equates with an elephant, he has the speed of a horse, the sharp vision like Garuda, can hear from a distance, having the black curly hair, beautiful like the Gandharvas or Vidyadharas, intelligent like Brhaspati, and he lives for a hundred divine years. Behaving in this manner, he comfortably roams about in the sky moving at will.

O damsel with a beautiful face, I shall speak out again about an other topic which was kept secret by me even from the gods. You listen to it with delight.

A yogi should practice the turning of the tongue towards the palate. After sometime the tongue would touch the uvula.

When so touched by the tongue, it starts exuding cool nectar, drinking which the yogis attain immortality.

The tip of the tongue touches the tip of uvula. The hands are clasped like the white lotus. The nectar then falls drop by drop on attaining the great region, he delights even the gods. This essential substance enables one to cross the ocean of worldly existence, remove all sins, cross the Kala along with the star. Then the yogi is freed from the hunger and thirst.

O Parvati, daughter of the mountain, with these four types of yogis on earth, they can bestow happiness over the entire universe. The yogi can create it in the heaven, what a man creates in the dream. This is only a fraction of what the four can perform.

Because of this reason, with the use of mantras, tapas, Vratas, discipline, Osadhis, polity, humility and dharma, the people getting attachment and following of the yogic practices, the earth yields the best of fruits. Siva, the primordial lord, even with the association of all the four types of yogis, does not feel disturbed. Therefore, I describe Siva- the shadowy Purusa appropriately.

## Chapter 28 - The shadowy person

The goddess said, “O Mahadeva- the god of gods, you have spoken about the signs of yoga for the achieving of the excellent Sabdabrahman.

Then for the benefit of the yogis you better speak about the excellent knowledge of the Chaya-purusa exhaustively.

Siva said, “O goddess, now I speak about the signs of chaya-purusa. You listen to the same. By getting an awareness of this topic a person is relieved of all the sins.

O fair lady, a person clad in white costumes, applying fragrance and the scent over the body, should be seated placing the back towards the sun or the moon and recite the mine syllable mantra of mine (i.e. om namo bhagavate rudraya). Then he should look at his shadow.

(It may be recalled here that the performer has not to be seated facing the sun and the moon, because in that case he would not be able to observe his shade. It is only by his sitting with his back towards the sun or the moon, that he would be able to have a look at his shadow). By looking at the shade of white colour then he should look at the sky then with a devoted mind he should look at Siva the creator of the universe.

By doing so, he would achieve Brahman. This has been pointed by the people well- versed in the science of kala. The person who does so is surely relieved of the sin of Brahmahatya.

In case the shadow seen by him is headless, then he will die in six months. This has been clearly defined in the Yogasastra.

When the shadow is of white complexion, there would be an increase in the dharma, with the black colour of the shadow, the sins would increase with the red coloured shadow, there would be a bondage and in case the same is found of yellow colour, there would be a destruction from the enemy.

In case the shade is without nose, it would result into the loss of kins, if it is devoid of mouth, there would be the danger of hunger, in case it is without the waist, the -loss of the wife could be expected and in case it is without the thighs, the loss of riches could be expected.

In the absence of the feet, one could travel to the foreign land. O Mahesvari, I have thus spoke the reward of the shadow-man. A person should carefully think over it.

Looking carefully at the chaya-purusa, remembering him in the heart, O Mahesvara, one should recite the Navatmaka-mantra.

A person who thus recites the mantra there would be no task which could be beyond his capacity to do after the lapse of the period of one year. He after achieving the siddhis like anima and others, he is able to roam about in the sky.

I shall also now speak of the rare Sakti possessed by such a person, by with the learned people are able to visualise everything in the world.

There is a coiling serpent conceived in the world, which is difficult to be known easily. It stands uppermost in the universe and is eulogised by the Vedas and has been described as a secret lore being the mother of all the lores.

It pervades in all the living beings and is also called as Khecara or the one which flies in the sky. She is visible, invisible, mobile, immobile, eternal, apparent, unapparent, eternal, colourless or without colour, besides being Bindumalini. By looking at it the yogis feel successful in their desires.

The merit one desires by taking bath at all the holy places, or giving away all types of charities and performing of all types of yajnas, the same merit is derived by a person by looking at Bindumalini.

The merit one earns by bathing at all the places of pilgrimage, or giving away the charities, is surely achieved on earth.

O Mahesani, receiving the fruit of all the yajnas, all the desires of a person are fulfilled.

Therefore a person with wisdom, should practice always the yoga-prana. By its constant practice, a yogi achieves expansion and success.

One attains wisdom and moksa by means of practice. A person desirous of moksa should resort to yogic practices.

O goddess, upto now, I have discussed about yoga, which bestows devotion and salvation. What more do you want to ask me, you tell me, I shall enlighten you on the subject.”

Suta said, “O excellent sages, listening to the words of Sanatkumara the son of Brahma, Vyasa, the son of Parasara was pleased.

Then Vyasa offered his salutation to omniscient son of Brahma known as Sanatkumara, again and again.

Then the sages and sage Vyasa, offered prayer to Sanatkumara, who was the ocean of the divine knowledge. ”

Vyasa said, “O excellent sage, I feel beholden to you. You have bestowed me with Brahman. You are graceful salutation to you again and again.

Suta said, “Thus Vyasa, after eulogising Sanatkumara, the son of Brahma, feeling delighted, kept quiet.

O Saunaka, then Sanatkumara, the son of Brahma, extended an invitation to Vyasa, and adored him. Thereafter both of them retired to their respective places.

O Brahmanas, I have narrated the pleasant conversation between Sanatkumara and Vyasa, which causes good to others. It is truthful, pleasing and achieves knowledge.

## Chapter 29 - Description of primeval creation

Saunaka said, “I have listened to great historical dialogue of Sanatkumara and Vyasa, which bestows the supreme tattva.

Now I would like to listen, to the way the world was created by Brahma, you tell me whatever Vyasa had spoken to you.

Suta said, “O Sage, you listen to the lores which is going to be narrated by me. It is divine, destroyer of sins, wonderful, is with several interpretations, besides exposing the words of scriptures.

Whosoever reads it, listens to it from beginning to end, or narrates it, he proceeds to the heaven with his race.

The one who is eternal and has sat and asat form is Pradhana and Purusa. The creator of the lokas created Pradhana after becoming Purusa.

O excellent sage, the creator of all the living beings, is devoted to Narayana. O great sage, you take him to be Brahma having the strength beyond measure.

O leading sage, salutation to the self born being who had been the cause of the origin of the kalpas and all other beings.

After offering my salutation to the Purusa called Hiranyagarbha, I shall resort to the best of the narration of the creation of the universe.

Whenever there had been the creation, Brahma had always been the creator, Visnu- the preserver while Mahesvara had been the destroyer. Except them there had been none else.

The self born Brahma when thought of creating several types of people, then he first of all created the water and the seed was planted in the same.

Water is called as Nara. Water happens to be the son of Nara. The one having his abode in waters s called Narayana.

Brahma had dropped the seed in waters it had the golden complexion. Brahma is popularly known as Svayambhu or self born, performed a yajna there.

Lord Hiranyagarbha stayed there for the year. He broke the egg into two parts resulting in the creation of the heaven and earth.

Thereafter fourteen worlds were created in the heaven above and below the earth. The lord created the sky in between the two parts of the egg.

The earth that was floating in the water, was created with ten directions in the sky and the earth. At the sametime, the mind, speech, kama, krodha and the sexual delight were created.

Then the seven Rsis like Marici, Atri, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasistha were produced, who were quite illustrious.

The Puranas also call these Rsis as the seven Brahmas. Thereafter Brahma, in anger created the eleven Rudras.

Prior to them, and earliest of all, the sage Sanatkumara, the Saptarsis, and Ekadasa Rudras were created.

Therefore Sanatkumara lives collecting his entire brilliance with him. Seven great families originated from the Saptarsis who were all divine and adored by the sages.

They are graced by the active great sages. Thereafter the lightning vajra, clouds, fire, rainbow, were created.

Initially the water was created and thereafter were created the clouds, which dropped the rain water. The Vedas like Rk, Yajuh and Saman were composed.

The gods were then adored with the reciting of the Vedas. This is what we hear. The gods were created from the mouth, the manes and humans from the chest and men through impregnation and the asuras from the thighs, from the limbs of their bodies, the tall and low living beings were created as the Apava created aquatic creatures.

When there was no expansion with the created beings, then the lord manifested his body with two halves of male and female.

Then he pervading in the entire universe with his Maya, creating the entire living beings, also created Virat. Ultimately Visnu was known as Virat.

He should be understood as the second Manu. After Manu, the said Virat-Purusa created he entire living beings.

The creations of Visnu were not born of womb. They had long life were famous, blessed and possessed of progeny.

O excellent sage, I have narrated to you the primeval creation, getting knowledge about which one attains his cherished heaven.

## Chapter 30 - The Creation

Suta said, “Thus with the creation of the people Apava the Prajapati, got Satarupa as wife, who had been born without any human contact.

With the glory of Apava, which pervaded the sky, both Prajapati and Satarupa were born.

Satarupa performed hard tapas for a hundred years and got the Purusa, who had been resplendent with brilliance, as a husband.

The said Purusa was none else then Svayambhuva Manu. His age is said to be seventy one Manvantaras.

From the said Virat-Purusa, Vairaja Satarupa was born. She gave birth to two sons named Priyavrata and Uttanapada.

From Prajapati Kardama, a woman named Kamya was born. Kamya had three sons named Samrat, Saksi and Avitprabhu.

The lord Uttanapada produced several sons. One of them was illustrious, divine and delighted all, who was known as Dhruva. Suniti the well known daughter of Dharma, having beautiful shoulders, was the mother of Dhruva.

The child Dhruva, performed tapas in a forest, for three thousand years in order to achieve the infallible position.

Having been pleased with his tapas, Brahma bestowed him an exalted position beyond the Saptarsis, resembling himself.

Then Dhruva had two sons named Push and Dhanya. Push got from Samuttha, pious and sinless five sons named Ripu, Ripunjaya, Vipra, Vrkala and Vrsatejas. The wife of Ripu gave birth to Caksusa as son, who was well known in all the directions.

Caksusa Manu produced a son named Varuna from his wife Puskarini. Ten illustrious sons were born to Manu from the wife named Nadalaya, who were quite illustrious.

O excellent sage, from Manu of great prowess, in Nadalaya the daughter of patriarch Vaisyajanma were born ten sons, viz., Puru, Masa, Satadyumna, Tapasvin, Satyavit, Kavi, Agnistoma, Atiratra, Atimanyu and Suyasa. From Agneyi, Puru produced six immensely illustrious sons named Anga, Sumanas, Khyati, Srti, Angiras, and Gaya. Sunitha- the wife of Anga produced a son named Vena to him.

Because of the evil conduct of Vena, the noble Rsis killed him in anger with a humkara.

Then Sunitha, prayed to the Rsis for getting a son. Then the Rsis churned his right hand.

With the churning of Vena's hand Prthu was born, holding a kavaca and a bow, having the lustre of the sun.

That incarnation of Visnu appeared for the sustaining the people, protection of dharma and for the punishing of the wicked people.

In that point of time Prthu- the ancestor of Ksatriyas protected the earth. He was the foremost of the kings who performed the Rajasuya yajna.

O excellent sage, two learned sons named Suta and Magadha were born to him. The said king milked the earth like a cow for the benefit of the people.

The said king provided the livelihood to the gods, Rsis, Daityas, Raksasas, humans and others. He performed a hundred yajnas.

The king Prthu had two sons named Vivitasva and Haryaksa, who were noble, well known and were well-versed in the study of the scriptures.

Sikhandini gave birth to a son named Pracinabarhisa, who had a son who could move in the entire world.

He married the daughter of the ocean appropriately, after which the great lord became graceful.

The king Pracinabarhisa performed several yajnas and produced ten sons from the daughter of the ocean Samudratanaya.

All of them were well-versed in the archery. They performed hard tapas, following their dharma. They were known as Pracetasas.

Remaining under the oceanic water for ten thousand years, reciting Rudragita, they meditated for Siva.

When they were performing tapas then the trees were grown everywhere on earth. Because of the neglect in the protection of the earth, the people faced destruction.

Finding the wild growth of the trees and after receiving the boons, O excellent sage, they were enraged. Then they intended to bum the trees with the strength of their tapas.

Then the Pracetasas emitting wind and fire from their months uprooted the trees and burnt them.

Thus some trees were destroyed while others were saved, therefore the king Soma approached them and said.

The moon said, “O Pracinabarhisa kings, do not be angry. Marry the excellent daughter of the trees known by the name of Anubhuta.

I am well-versed in the knowledge of future. She has been conceived by me in my womb. Let her be you wife and let the race of the moon flourish.

Daksa Prajapati will be born of her. He being the ancient son of Brahma, will be the creator of the great brilliance.

With the half of your brilliance and half my brilliance, the king full of the brilliance of Brahma, will make the people to flourish.”

Then listening to the words of the moon, the Pracetasas accepted the daughter of the trees, as their wife appropriately.

O Sage, Daksa Prajapati, was born to her through them, O Sage the immensely brilliant boy was born to her of the moon's part as well.

After creating mentally, the mobile and immobile beings, the bipeds and quadrupeds, Daksa began creation by sexual process.

As per the provisions of the sastras, Daksa virtuously married the daughter of Virana known as Virini.

He produced from Virini, ten thousand noble sons, named Haryasvas. They became detached at the advice of Narada.

On hearing this, he again produced from his wife a thousand sons named Subalasvas.

They also followed the foot steps of their brothers, at the advice of Narada. Becoming detached they became the mendicants, and they never went back to their father.

On hearing this Daksa, getting enraged, pronounced an unbearable cure over Narada saying, “O quarrelsome Narada, you will never remain stable at one place.”

O excellent sage, at the advice of Brahma, Daksa then erected virtuous maidens having the form of flames.

He gave away in marriage, ten maidens to Dharmaraja, thirteen to sage Kasyapa, two to the son of Brahma and two to Angira.

O excellent sage, he gave to gods to the sage Krsasva and all the rest of the girls were given away in marriage to the moon.

From the daughters of Daksa several sons like asuras and others were born, filling the entire universe.

O best of the Brahmanas, thereafter, the people were born by means of sexual union, who were earlier created by means of mental wish, Sankalpa, look or even the touch.

Saunaka said, “You had earlier said that Daksa was born by the thumb of Brahma, then was he transformed into Pracetas the great ascetic?

O Suta, you can alone remove my doubt. This is quite surprising as to how could be became the father-in-law of the moon?

Suta said, “The birth and death is quite common amongst the mortals. Daksa and others appear in every kalpa.

A person who is aware of the mobile and immobile creation of Daksa, he living the full span of his life, earns glory in the heaven.

## Chapter 31 - Daksa pronounces a curse on Narada

Saunaka said, “O Son of Suta, you kindly describe at length about the creation of the gods, Daityas, Gandharvas, serpents and Raksasas.

Suta said, “When there was no increase in the creation of the people with the efforts of Prajapati Virana, then the maiden engaged in tapas was summoned.

O immensely intelligent one, then she resorted to creation with intercourse with Dharma. You listen to the details of the same, which I am going to speak out in brief.

Daksa Prajapati, the powerful patriarch produced five thousand sons from his wife Virini, uniting with her.

At the birth of those sons, Narada said, “All of them had been born in the Srsti-yajna of Brahma.

Kasyapa alone would be the cause of the creation. This is what had been heard by Narada. Then the creation of the sons, at sage Narada spoke to them.

“You are unaware of the direction of the world and without knowing that what can you do? You are quite childish. You be aware of the world and only them proceed.”

At these words of Narada, all of them went on for knowing about the directions. Being unable to know the end of the earth, they returned to the parental home.

Learning about this, Yaksa again produced five thousand sons. The omniscient Narada spoke to them as well.

Narada said, “O fools, how could you resort to the creation without knowing the extent of the world? All of your are childish. What creation do you propose to make?

Suta said, “They too listening to the words of Narada, also followed the path of Haryasvas and proceeded to all the directions.

After crossing the limit of the ocean, they were defeated and have not returned to date, as they did not return from the ocean.

From that day onwards, a brother went in search of the brother, who was lost there and the task of creation could not be completed.

Realising that the son had perished, Daksa cursed Narada- the noble soul in anger.

Daksa Prajapati felt enraged at the lose of these sons too pronounced a curse on Narada. “You will always be surrounded by the controversies.”

Thereafter Brahma pacified Daksa Prajapati. Thereafter Daksa produced sixty girls from Virini. This is what has been heard by me.

Ten out of them were given to Dharmaraja, thirteen to Kasyapa, twenty seven to the moon, and four to Aristanemi.

Two were given to Brahmaputra, two of there to Angira and two were given to the learned Krsasva. You listen to their names.

O Sage, the wives of Dharma are Arundhati, Vasu, Yami, Lamba, Bhanu, Marutvati, Samkalpa, Sumuhurta, Sandhya and Visva.

O Sage, these are the wives. Now you listen to the names of their children. Visvedevas were born of Visva and Sadhyaganas were born of Sadhya.

Marutvana was born of Marutvati, Astavasus were born of Vasu, the twelve Adityas were born of Bhanu and Muhurtaja were born of Muhurta.

Lamba gave birth to Ghosa, Yami to Nagavithi and Arundhati gave birth to Prthvi visama.

Samkalpa gave birth to truthful Samkalpa as the son, O Saunaka eight sons were born to Vasu including Aya. Now you listen to their names.

They were known as Aya, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Pratyusa and Prabhasa. These are the names of eight Vasus.

The sons of Aya were named as Vaitanda, Srama and Santa, Lord Kala was the popular son of Dhruva.

Lord Varcas was the son of Soma, who imported lustre to others. The sons of Dhara were known as Dravina and Hutahavyavaha.

Sisira and Prana were born of Manohara, Siva, the wife of Anala gave birth to a son named Purojava.

Anila had other two sons, who were born of Avijnatagati, were known as Kumara and Agniputra. Both of them were born in the forest of Sara grass.

He had Sakha, Visakha, and Naigameya as his sons. The son of Krttika, was known as Krttika.

The sage Devala was born of Pratyusa. Devala also had two sons, who had the intelligent subjects.

Brahmacarini was the sister of Brhaspati who was well-versed in yogic practices besides being beautiful. She started wandering on all the four sides in the universe.

O fortunate one, the wife of Prabhasa- the eighth Vasu, gave birth Visvakarma Prajapati.

He was the master of various arts, was the architect of the gods, who could make all types of ornaments and was the best of artisans.

He build planes for all the gods, because of whose artistic skill, the people earned their livelihood.

The other opinion is being stated- His wife Sarupa gave birth to crores of Rudras, such as Raivata, Aja, Bhava, Bhima, Vama, Ugra, Vrsakapi, Ajaikapada, Abirbudhnya, Bahurupa, Mahat and others. Eleven of them are quite important. O Sage, you listen to there names.

They include Ajaikapada, Ahirbudhnaya, Tvastr, the powerful Rudrahara of may forms- Trayambaka, Aparajita, Vrsakapi, Sambhu, Kapardi and Raivata.

Thus a hundred Rudras have been mentioned to you. Now you listen to the names of the wives of Kasyapa.

## Chapter 32 - Kasyapa and his family

Suta said, “O Brahmana, Aditi, Surasa, Aristeta, Danu, Surabhi, Vinata, Ila, Tamra, Krodhavasa, Kadru and Muni were the wives of Kasyapa. Now listen to the names of their sons. In the earlier Manvantra, there were twelve excellent gods.

They were known by the names of Tusita. They confabulated among themselves and resolved that during the intervening period of Vaivasvata and Caksusa Manvantara, we shall be born from the womb of Aditi, entering the same, for the benefit of the people to provide welfare to the noble people.” Thus thinking, all of them were born from the womb of Aditi the wife of Kasyapa- the son of Marici. Then Visnu, Indra and others were born from the daughter of Daksa Prajapati. Besides there were the twelve illustrious sons, known as Aryama, Dhata, Tvasta, Pusa, Vivasvan, Savita, Mitravaruna, Amsa, Bhaga and Atitejas; in the Caksusa Manvantara.
