These are the twelve Adityas of the Caksusa Manvantara, who were born of Aditi.

The twenty seven chaste wives of the moon have been mentioned, they produced immensely illustrious sons.

The wives of Aristanemi, produced sixteen sons. The learned Bahuputra had four daughters.

O divine sage, O ascetic, Devaprahara is said to be the son of Krsava. His wife Arcisi also gave birth to a son named Dhumrakesa.

He had two wives named Svadha and Sati. Of these two, Svadha was the elder while Sati was the younger. Svadha produced the manes, Sati the Vedas and Angira.

At the end of a thousand yugas, they will be reborn. There are thirty three groups of gods.

As the sun rises and sets daily, similarly the groups of gods are born in each one of the yugas an then they vanish.

It was heard by us that two powerful demon sons were born to Kasyapa from the womb of Diti and were known by the names of Hiranyakasipu and Hiranyaksa.

Vipracitti gave birth to a daughter named Simhika. Four immensely illustrious and valorous sons were born to Hiranyakasipu.

They were known by the names of Anuhrada, Hrada, Samhrada and Prahlada. The last one was immensely devoted to Visnu.

Surya the wife of Anuhrada gave birth to two sons named Puloma and Mahisa. Dhamani the wife of Hrada, gave birth to Vatapi and Ilvil.

Krti, the wife of Samhrada gave birth to a son named Pancajana, Virocana was the son of Prahlada and the latter's son was Bali. O excellent sage, a hundred sons were born to Bali from his wife Asana. The king Bali was immensely devoted to Siva and always remained devoted to the worship of Siva.

He was a great donor, large hearted, possessed the auspicious glory and performed great tapas. Banasura was the eldest son of Bali, who was also devoted to Siva and possessed enormous wisdom. He achieved the position of Ganapati, by pleasing Siva.

You have already heard the story of Bana- the great soul. The said valorous Bana had pleased lord Krsna in the battlefield.

Hiranyaksa had five powerful sons viz. Kukura, Sakuni, Bhuta, Santapana, Mahanada and the valorous Kalanabha. They were the sons of Diti. O Sage, now you listen to the sons of Danu.

The immensely valorous Danu had a hundred sons. The names of the son of Kasyapa born from Danu were, Ayomukha, Sambara, Kapola, Vamana, Vaisvanara, Puloma, Vidravana, Mahasira, Svarabhanu, Vrsaparva and powerful Vipracitti.

O sage, all of them were the sons of Kasyapa and Danu. In this connection you listen tot he names of their daughters.

Svarabhanu had a daughter named Prabha. Puloma had the daughter named Saci and Upadanavi, Vrsaparva had two daughters named Hayasira and Vrsaparva.

Vaisvanara had two daughters named Puloma and Pulomika. They were the wives of Kasyapa and son of Marici and had many valorous sons.

Kasyapa the son of Marici was endowed with great penance and then got sixty thousand sons, who delighted the Danavas.

The valorous Puloma and Kalakhanja, who lived in Hiranyapura, were infallible even from the gods, but were killed by Arjuna by the grace of Brahma. Then Simhika the wife of Vipracitti also gave birth to several sons.

With the union of the Daityas and Danavas, thirteen powerful demons known as Simhakeyas were born.

The valorous Rahu, Salya, Bala, Mahabala, Vatapi, Namuci, Ilvala, Svasrpa, Ajika, Naraka, Kalanabha, Saramana, and Sarakalpa prolonged the race.

Several of the sons and the grandsons were born to them. They have not been spelt out in order to avoid the spreading of the topic, but they expanded the race of Danavas.

In the race of Samhrada, the daityas known as Nivata and Kavaca were born. Marutas were also born in the same race from Tapasya.

Tamra gave birth to Sanmukha and other sons possessing the Sattvaguna. The daughters of Tamra included Kaki, Syeni, Bhasi, Sugrivi, Suki, Grdhrika, Asvi and Uluki. Kaki gave birth to the crows, and Uluki to owls, Syeni gave birth to eagles, Bhasi to Bhasas, Grdhri to vultures and Suki to the parrots, while Sugrivi gave birth to other auspicious birds.

Tamra, the wife of Kasyapa, gave birth to horses, camels, as well as the donkeys. Thus the race of Tamra has been defined.

Vinata had two sons named Aruna and Garuda. Of these Garuda was the king of birds, but Aruna, because of his deeds could not achieve excellence.

Surasa had a thousand illustrious sons which could move in the sky and had many hoods.

Prominent among the serpents were Sesa, Taksaka, Airavata, Mahapadma, Kambala and Asvatara. All of them were the kings of the serpents.

Aila had the sons named Padma, Karakotaka, Dhananjaya, Mahanila, Mahakarna, Dhrtarastra, Balahaka, Kuhara, Puspadanta, Durmukha, Sumukha, Bahusa, Khararoma, Pani and others.

Krodhavasa gave birth to several sons in the form of ganas. All of them had the fangs, born of eggs i.e. the birds as well as the aquatic animals. The animals were born to Varahi.

Anayusa had the valorous fifty sons who were very strong. Bala, Vrtta, Viksara and Brhana were the foremost of them.

Surabhi produced rabbits and the buffaloes. Ila produced trees, creepers, spreading vines, and all kinds of grass. Khasa gave birth to Yaksas and Raksasas, while Muni gave birth to celestial nymphs. Arista gave birth to the serpents which were better in excellence than the human beings in process.

Thus sage, the progeny of Kasyapa has been narrated to you, who had hundreds of sons and the grandsons.

## Chapter 33 - Creation of Maruts and distribution of kingdoms

Suta said, “O dear one, you have described the creating of the Svarocisa Manvantara. When the great Varuna yajna was developed in the Vaivasvata Manvantara, the creation was evolved by Brahman while performing the same. I shall speak about the same now. All the seven Rsis initially created by Brahma as his mental sons; then O Sage, when the sons of Diti were destroyed in conflict with the gods, she went to Kasyapa and pleased him adoring him adequately.

He cheated her on the pretext of granting a boon to her. Then Diti asked for a boon to powerful son, who would be able to kill Indra.

Kasyapa, the great ascetic, granted her the boon and advised her to perform brahmcarya (or chastity) for a hundred years.

Then the excellent and auspicious Aditi (?) (Should be Diti) conceived and faithfully observed all the rules for celibacy.

Thereafter the praiseworthy and disciplined Kasyapa, made Diti to conceive and then proceeded on for the performing of tapas.

Then Indra observed a short coming in ninety nine years, when Diti, went to sleep without washing her feet, lowering her head and thinking about the birth of her son.

In the meantime, Indra holding the Vajra, in his hand, entered her womb and cut the embryo in seven pieces.

Having been cut with Vajra the embryo started crying. Then Indra spoke to the pieces of embryo, “Do not cry”. But the pieces could not be destroyed even after having been cut off with Vajra.

Then the pieces of embryo addressed Indra, “Why are you killing us? We are Maruts you brothers.”

O Brahmarsi, at the Desire of Siva they discarded the enmity and accepted Indra as their brother.

These forty nine Maruts, who could move to the sky at will, were turned as the associates of Indra.

After Prthu and other Maruts were grown up, who came to be known as Aristha, Purusa, Vira, Krsna, Visnu, Prajapati, Parjanya, Dhanadhyaksa, who happens to be the lord of the Universe, offered kingdoms to them.

O great sage, I have narrated to you the details about the creation of the living beings. Now you listen to the divisions of the countries. I shall speak out to you in a sequence.

The grand sire Brahma established Prthu- the son of Vena in the kingdom and then he started allotting the kingdoms.

Soma was declared as the king of the Brahmanas, constellations, planets, yajnas, tapas and the trees.

Varuna was declared as the lord of waters. Vaisravana was bestowed the suzerainty of the kings, the kingdom of Adityas was given to Visnu, Vasu was made the king of fires.

Daksa became the king of Prajapatis, Indra was made the king of Maruts, while Prahlada was made the king of Daityas and Danavas.

Yama and Vaivasvata were made the kings of manes. Siva holding the trident was made the king of Matrikas, Vratas, cows, Yaksas, Raksasas, all the spirits and goblins, besides the Parthivas.

Himalaya was declared as the king of mountains, ocean was declared as the king of rivers, bull the king of the cows, and the banyan tree was declared as the king of trees, greenery and ausadhis. In this way the kingdoms were distributed by Prajapati to all.

Then the all pervading Visvapati, who knew the inner feelings of all, declared Vairaja the son of Prajapati as the lord of east.

Similarly, O great king, he established Sudhanvan, son of Kardama, the patriarch in the kingdom of south.

Ketumat, the unfailing noble-minded son of Rajas was established as the king of the kingdom in the west.

O excellent sage, Hiranyaroma, the son of Parjanya Prajapati was also bestowed with a kingdom of the northern direction.

O Saunaka, I have spoken about the expansion of the kingdom of Prthu. This ancient place is said to be bestower of great rddhis.

## Chapter 34 - The fourteen Manvantras

Saunaka said, “O Suta, you kindly speak out in detail about the Manvantras because I am quite eager to listen about them.”

Suta said, “There are six Manus of the past known by the names of Svayambhuva, Svarocisa, Uttama, Tamasa, Raivata and Caksusa. The present Manu is called Vaivasvata.

The future Manus are Savarni, Raucya, Brahmasavarni, Dharmasavarni, Rudrasavarni, Devasavarni and Indrasavarni. All of them are the Manus of the past, present and future about which I have spoken as have been heard by me.

O sage, these fourteen Manvantras of the past, present and future have been spoken out by me. All these combined constitute a kalpa.

Now, O Saunaka, I shall speak about the sages, their sons and the gods, who are quite well known. You please listen to me with pleasure.

The Rsis named Marici, Atri, lord Angira, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya and Vasistha are the seven sons of Brahma.

O sage, in the Svayambhuva Manvantra, there were the Saptarsis the earth and the god named Yama was there.

The noble Agridhra, Agnibahu, Medha, Medhatithi, Vasu, Jyotisman, Dhrtiman, Havya, Savana, and Sabhra were the ten sons of the noble Svyambhu Manu. O excellent sage, at that point of time, the yajna was known as Indra.

O dear one, the first was known as the divine Manvantra. Now I shall speak about the second Manvantra. You listen to me correctly.

The contemporary Rsis of the period had been Urjastambha, Parastambha, Rsabha, Vasuman, Jyotisman, Dyutiman and Rocisman. At that point of time Rocana was known as Indra and the gods were known as Tvsitas.

Harighna, Sukrti, Jyoti, Ayomurti, Aya, Samaya, Prathita, Manasyu, Nabha and Surya had been the ten sons of Svarocis Manu, who were immensely valorous and strong.

O sage, I have thus spoken about the second Manvantra and you listen to the same quite carefully.

The seven sons of Vasistha were known as Vasistha uttama Manu had ten sons. Hiranyagarbha had the illustrious son named Urja.

I shall now speak out the names of the contemporary Rsis, which you please listen. O excellent sage, Manu named Uttama had ten sons known by the names of Isa, Urjita, Urja, Madhu, Madhava, Suci, Sukravaha, Nabhas, Nabha and Rsabha. At that point of time, Satyadeva, Sruta, and others were the gods. O sage, Satyajit happened to be Indra of that period.

This is the third Manvantra about which I have spoken. O sage, I now speak about the fourth Manvantra and you please listen to it attentively.

The seven Rsis were known as Gargya, Prthu, Vagmin, Janya, Dhata, Kapinaka and Kapivan. The name of the contemporary group of gods was Satya, while Indra was known as Trisikha. O sage now you listen about the sons of Manu, who were known as Dyutapoti, Sautapasya, Tapa, Sala, Tapana.

Taporati, Akalmasa, Dhanvi, Khadgi and Mahanrsi. These were the ten names of the Mahavrata Manu named Tamasa.

This is the fourth Manvantra, known as Tamasa, which has been described by me. O dear one, now you listen to the details about the fifth Manvantra.

The seven sages of this Manvantra are Devabahu, Jaya, Vedasira, Hiranyaroma, Parjanya, Urdhvabahu and Somapa, who were quite truthful. The gods of that period had been Bhutarajasas who were of the nature of performing penances.

At that point of time Vibhu functioned as Indra- the lord of the three worlds. Manu named Raivata was the real brother of Manu- Tamasa.

O sage, Arjuna and Panktivindhya besides others will be known as his sons. They performed severe tapas staying at the peak of the Meru mountain.

During the sixth Manvantra Raucya- the son of Prajapati Ruci, was Manu and Bhuti was known to be his wife. A son named Bhautya was born to them.

There will be seven Manus of the future Kalpa. The future sages will also be seven in each one of the Manvantras, in the heaven.

These seven Rsis are known by the name of Kasyapa, Atri, Vasistha, Visvamitra, Gautama, Jamadgni and Bhardvaja.

Parasrama, Vyasa, Bhardvaja, Asvatthama, the son of Drona, Saradvan, son of Gautama, Krpacarya, Galava of Kausika race, Ruru of Kasyapa race, will be he future seven sages. As mentioned by Svayambhu, the future gods will be three in number. The are the sons of the noble soul Kasyapa the son of Marici. The contemporary Indra will be Virocana the son of Bali.

Savarni Manu shall have ten sons named Visanga, Avanivan, Sumanta, Dhrtiman, Vasu, Suri, Surakhya, Visnu, Raja and Sumati.

O Saunaka, this will be the eighth Manvantara. Now you listen about the ninth one.

First of all I shall speak about Daksa Savarni Manu. You please listen. The seven Rsis named Medhatithi of the Pulastya race, Vasu of Kasyapa race, the illustrious and learned Angira of the Bhrgu race, Savana of the race of Vasistha, Havya of the race of Atri and Pulaha. These seven Rsis will function in the middle of the Manvantra. O great sage, the gods here are three.

All of them shall be the sons of Rohita the son of Prajapati, Daksaputra and will be known by the names of Dhrstaketu, Diptiketu, Paucahasta, Nirakrti, Prthusrava, Bhuridyumna, Rcika, Brhat and Gaya. These will be quite illustrious.

During the time of Manu of second Savarni, there will be the ten sages viz. Havisman of Pulaha race, Prakrti of Bhrgu race, Ayomukti of Atri race, Avyayaghti race of Vasistha, Prayati of the race of Pulastya, Bhamara of the race of Kasyapa, and Ananes and Satya of the race of Angira will be the seven sages. These known as Dvisimant are the groups of gods.

Mahesvara Siva shall function as Indra during the period. Manu will have ten sons named Aksatvana, Uttamauja, Bhurisena, Viryavan, Satanika, Niramitra, Vrsasena, Jayadratha, Bhuridyumna, Suvarca and Aci. In the eleventh Manvantra of the third Savarni, there will be seven sages. You listen to their glory from me.

The seven sages include Havisman of Kasyapa race, Vapuman of Varun's race, Vasistha of the race of Atri, Anaya of the race of Angira, Carudrsya of the race of Pulastya, Nirvara, Agni and Tejas. There will be the seven Rsis the three gods.

There are the sons of Brahma known as Vaidhrtas. The grandsons of Savarna and the sons of the third Savarni are- Sarvaga, Susarman, Devanika, Ksemaka, Drdhesu, Khandaka, Darsa, Kuhu and Baha, nine in all. These sons of Brahma will be called Vaidhrtas who will be known by the names of Sarvaga, Susarma, Devanika, Ksemaka, Drdhesu, Khanlaka, Darsa, Kuhu who will be called the sons of Manu. They will be the three grand sons of the third Manu.

Now you listen to the Rsis of the fourth Savarni who are Dyuti the son of Vasistha Sutapa of the race of Atri, Angira-the great tapas, Kasyapa the ascetic, the sage Pulastya, the mendicant Pulaha while the seventh ascetic was Bhargava. They will be the seven sages. The god will comprise of the five mind born sons of Brahma.

The name of the contemporary Indra shall be Rtadhama who will make the people conformable. O sage, then in the twelfth Manvantra named Raucya, the seven Rsis will be known by the name of Dhrtiman, Angira, Pulastya, Havyavan, Pulaha well-versed in tattvas, Bhargava, the noble Atreya, Kasyapa without body, Sutapa of the race of Vasistha.

Svayambhu has described the gods having three merits. Indra of the contemporary period will be known as Divaspati. The names of the sons of Aucya Manu, shall be Vicitra, Citra, Naya, Dharma, Dhrtondra, Sunetra, Ksatraka Vrddhaka, Nirbhaya, Drona, and Satapa.

During the time of Satya- the fourteenth and last Manu, the names of the seven Rsis will be Agnidhra of the Kasyapa race, Magadha of Pulastya race, Ativalya of Bhrgu race, Suci of Angiras race, Atri of Vasistha race, besides Ajita and Pulaha. Pavitra and others will be the Caksusa gods. Indra of the contemporary period will be known as Suci.

One who recites their names, getting up early in the morning, one finds an increase in the comforts. Therefore the people should narrate the name of the past great sages always.

O great sage, in this fourteenth Manvantra, the gods will have five ganas and ten sons known as Turangabhiru, Budhna, Tanugra, Anugra, Abhimani, Pravina, Visnu, Samkrandana, Tejasvi and Sabala. These will be the sons of Satya Manu.

During the rule of Manu known as Bhauma, the Purvakalpa comes to an end. I have spoken to you about the past as well as the future Manus.

Then the immensely illustrious Sanatkumara- the divine sage, had narrated the story of Manvantras to the sage Vyasa. All these Manus, are read the people with a religious mind for a thousand years.

Then they proceed on to Brahmaloka with their people on the strength of their tapas. A Manvantra comprises of seventy one fourfold yugas.

These are the fourteen Manus who increase the grace. At the destruction of each Manvantra, the universe is recreated.

No one can describe the Manvantras in a hundred years even. After the lapse of a hundred thousand yugas, there ends a kalpa.

All the living beings start burning with the sun rays. At that point of time, O Sage, Sat and others make Brahma to lead, reaching Visnuloka enter the same who happens to be the cause of the creation of all, at the time of the end of the Kalpa.

Still lord Siva the form of Kala will resort to destruction at the end of the kalpas. Now I shall describe the Vaivasvata, Manvantra.

Thus I have narrated the auspicious and graceful story of the genesis of the Manvantras, and with its recitation there is an increase in the race.

## Chapter 35 - The description of Vaivasvata

Suta said, “Daksayajini was the wife of Kasyapa- the great sage, who gave birth to Vivasvan- sun, who was married to Samjna, the daughter of Tvasta and Surenuka.

She was not pleased with the youthfulness and beauty of her husband because of his unbearable lustre.

She could not bear the lustre of her illustrious husband. Thus getting scorched with the exquisite beauty of her husband, she started feeling nervous.

O Sage, three sons named known as Manu- Prajapati and Sraddhadeva were produced from his wife. Then Yama and Yamuna were born twins.

Then Sanjna finding the lustre of the son unbearable, created an auspicious being known as Chaya of her own body.

Then Chaya, spoke with devotion to Sanjna, O auspicious one, with a sweet smile, what should I do for you.”

Sanjna said, “I am going to the abode of my father, you remain here in an unblemished manner.

I have these two sons who are quite simple, besides a beautiful daughter. In case you wish well of me, then bring them up carefully.”

Chaya said, “I shall not talk about you to the sun and shall bear all his tortures unless he pulls up my hair. You can leave the place comfortably.”

Suta aid, “Thus speaking, the goddess Sanjna feeling ashamed left for the abode of her father. The father rebuked her and insisted for her return to the sun.

Then she, changing her form, became a mare, and going to the Uttara Kura country, started roaming about among the humans.

On the other hand, the sun, taking Chaya to be his own wife produced Savarni Manu from her.

Even at the request of Sanjna, Chaya started loving more to his own son, than the children of Sanjna.

Yama the younger of the two sons of Sanjna, could not tolerate it and he did not forgive her. Ever since his childhood, he was of furious temperament, as a result of the gravity what was sure to happen in future. When Vaisvasvata Yama, rebuked Chaya rage, then the sinful Chaya pronounced a curse on him.

She said due to her immense rage, “Let you leg fall off.” Then Yama approached his father with his hands folded in reverence.

He said feeling painful of the curse and inspired by the words of Sanjna, “For the mother, all the sons should be equal.

Depriving us of the love, she takes only care of the youngest one. Only then I raised my foot. I beg forgiveness from you.

O best of the illustrious people, you are foremost of al the refulgent ones, I have been cursed by my mother. O lord of rays, by your grace, let my leg not fall from my body.

The Sun said, “O Son, there must be some reason for this, which has enraged a noble and truthful person like you.

I cannot falsify the words of your mother. The worms will eat away flesh from your body and fall on earth roaming about here and there.

These words will be true and you will be protected as well. O dear one, therefore, you should reassure your mind.”

Suta said, “O excellent sage, the sun consoled his son with these words. Then in anger Surya said to Chaya.

The Sun said, “O evil minded and enraged beloved, what is all this done by you? Do I love them more? Can you say so?”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of Surya, Chaya then spoke out the truth and then she became lustful, but the sun pacified her.

On hearing the words of Chaya, Surya went to Brahma and asked him, “Where has Sanjna gone?

Brahma said, “She feels scorched with your illustrious body. Therefore, she does not like your present form. She, therefore, being unable to bear the heat of your body lives in the grassy forest.

O lord of the rays, O lord of gods, Sanjna, possessing the yogic powers is quite praiseworthy. You better be peaceful speaking out your mind.

Now, I shall change your scorching form to a pleasant form.” Suta said, “In this way the sun was relieved of his anger.

The sage. Tvastr then put him over the turner's lathe, and sharpened him further. His blazing brilliance was reduced a little as a result of this. Then with the use of his yogic power, he found his wife Sanjna.

When the beautiful form was bestowed by Brahma to the sun, then he appeared more graceful. Then he found his wife Sanjna with his yogic power and found that she was unconquerable because of her lustre and the rules followed by her. The sun took to the form of a horse and went to her to have union with her.

She on her part, did not allow him to have union with her apprehensive of his being some stranger. Then the sun dropped the semen in her nostrils.

As a result of this the two Asvinikumaras were born. They were also known as Nasatyas and Dasras.

Then the sun showed his splendid form to both of them, finding her husband, there Sanjna too was extremely delighted.

The chaste lady then returned to her abode with her husband with a delightful face. Both of them were more delighted than earlier.

Yama felt painful with the earlier incident, but still he delighted the people following the *dharma.*

Because of his strict following of the Dharma, he was bestowed the position of Dharmaraja, besides being the lord of the manes and the achieving of lokapala as well.

The ascetic who had been Savarni Manu earlier because of this situation will be Manu in the Savarni Manvantra.

He is presently performing severe *tapas* over the Sumeru mountain. The youngest child of Surya was known by the name of Yami, who was turned as Yamuna in order to purify the people. He is called Savarni Manu in the world.

The one who listens to the birth story of these gods, or retains it in his memory, he is freed from all the approaching misfortunes and earns enough of glory.

## Chapter 36 - The nine sons of the race of Manu

Suta said, “Vaivasvata Manu, had nine sons of the gigantic, like him who were quite patient and devoted to the Ksatriya dharma.

They were known by the names of Iksavaku, Sibi, Dhrsta, Kurusa, Saryati, Narisyanta, Nabhaga, Kurusa and Priyavrata.

O Excellent Sage, Prajapati Manu, performed a yajna for achieving a son. But he could not get a son even with the performing of that yajna, and instead a young damsel adorned with divine ornaments and clad in beautiful costumes, known as famous Ila emerged from the same.

Then the ruler Manu said to Ila, “You do not come after me.” At this Ila said, “O best of the orators, your words are quite religious. I have been born in the abode of Prajapati, who had been desirous of a son from the amsas of Mitravaruna. I shall go to them since I am not at all inclined towards dharma.” Thus speaking the chaste lady went to Mitravaruna.

Reaching there, she said to them “O great sages, I have been born from your amsas in the yajna of Manu.

Therefore I have arrived before you. Speak out the future course of action for me. O fortunate ones, you better produce five more sons, to enable your race to continue.”

Suta said, “At these words of Ila born of the yajna of Manu, the sages named Mitravaruna, spoke to her with respect.

Mitravaruna said, “O well-versed in dharma, virtuous and beautiful lady of fair complexion, both of us are pleased with your self control humility and truthfulness.

O blessed lady, you will attain our glory, besides a son who will alone continue the race of Manu.

You will be known as Sudyumna in the universe, you will be the beloved of the world, quite auspicious and shall prolong the race of Manu.”

Suta said, “On hearing this, when she was returning to the abode of her father, then availing an opportunity, Budha cohabited with her.

Then Budha the son of the moon, produced the king Pururava from her. The son was quite beautiful and bestowed with wisdom, who became the husband of Urvasi.

By the grace of Siva, she after lovingly giving birth to a son was transformed as Sudyumna.

The three kins of Sudyumna were extremely religious who were known as Utkala, Gaya and the powerful Vinatasva.

O excellent sage, the sons of Utkala were the Brahmanas of Utkalaprada, Vinatasva's sons were the sons of the western direction and the sons of Gaya were the Gayavala Brahmanas of the east.

O dear one, when Manu entered the body of Divakara, then he divided the earth in ten parts.

The eldest king named Iksavaku inherited the central region. At the instance of Vasistha, Sudyumna the auspicious region of Pratisthana to Pururavas.

Then Sudyumna bestowed on him the position of Dharmaraja besides the kingdom. By getting the same, the universally glorious, Narisyanta, who had both the characters of both man and woman, gave birth to Sakas.

Then Nabhaga the son of Bahleya, got the region of Bahlaka. Mithuna was born of Saryati and came to be known as Anarta.

Sukanya who married to the sage Cyavana. The kins of Anarta came to be known as Raivata or Ramuja.

In the region of Anarta, he got the city of Kusasthali which was quite resplendent and was the last of the seven cities.

He had a hundred sons, out of whom, Kukudmi was the eldest one besides being the most excellent one, besides being brilliant, strong virtuous and the protector of the Brahmanas.

Kukudmni had a daughter named Revati, who was endowed with enormous beauty and resembled Laksmi in beauty.

At that point of time the programme of the Gandharva's dance and music was going on Availing of the opportunity, Kukudmi also started observing the dance and music there.

While so doing several of the yugas were passed but the sages and Kukudmi could not realise this aspect of the change.

Kukudmi them offered his salutation to Brahma with folded hands. Then he humbly revealed to Brahma, the purpose of his visit.

Listening to his words, Prajapati (the patriarch) Brahma, smiled and addressing the great king Kukudmi said.

Brahma said, “O son of Raibhya, O king . Kukudmi, you lovingly listen to my words. I am speaking to you truthfully.

Kukudmi- the lord of. all, once went to Brahma in order to consult him about her groom.

The grooms you had in mind have all perished. Even their descendants are also no more there, who have been devoured by the time, which is the devourer of all.

O king, the demons have destroyed your kingdom. The present is the twenty-eighth Dvapara and Sri Krsna had rebuilt the kingdom again.

The name of the city with many doors is Dvaravati, having many gates. It is protected by Vasudeva, Bhoja, Vrsni, Andhaka and others.

O king, you return delightfully and reaching there, you give away your daughter to Baladeva-the son of Vasudeva, in marriage.”

Suta said, “Thus at command of Brahma, the king returned, bowing in reverence to Brahma. He with his daughter, he felt extremely surprised due to the lapse of many yugas.

Then he, gave away his youthful daughter Revati appropriately to Baladeva- the brother of Krsna.

Thereafter the great king, reaching the peak of the Sumeru mountain engaged himself in the performing of tapas for Siva.

The Rsis said, “When Raivata stayed in Brahmaloka for many yugas, then how could be return on earth with his daughter. We have developed a great doubt about it.

Suta said, “The blemishes like the hunger, thirst, old age etc. are not to be found there. O sages, in the heaven, no one can face premature death.

Therefore, the king neither attracted old age nor the death. The girl also by seeking advice about her groom remained youthful.

The king then reached the divine city of Dvaravati built by Sri Krsna and married his daughter with Balarama.

The noble and great lord Balarama produced a hundred sons from Revati. Sri Krsna also had several sons from his several wives.

There had been enough of the expansion of their race with the progeny of both Balarama and Sri Krsna. As a result of this the auspicious Ksatriyas were spread in all the directions.

O Brahmanas, thus I have spoken about the race of Saryati. Now I shall speak about the races of other people in brief. You better listen to the same.

Dista had Nabhaga as the son. He after establishing his race of Ksatriyas, he himself performing the duties of a Brahmana ultimately achieved the Brahmanahood.

Dhastra was born of Dhrst, who was also a Ksatriya but the talent of a Ksatriya was lesser in him as compared to Brahmanahood. The arrogant Ksatriya was born from Kamsa.

Nrga, the son of Mana had been a great donor, who gave away in charity the riches as well as the cows to the Brahmanas.

He was turned as a chameleon, because of a mistake in his charitable gift of a cow prompted by his own sins and evil mind. He was ultimately redeemed by Sri Krsna.

Prayati an excellent son was born to him, who possessed enormous virtue. The relevant story was heard by me from the sage Vyasa, which has now been repeated to you.

Prsadhra was the son of Manu who was made a cowherd by the preceptor. He used to guard and serve the cows seated in Virasana at night.

Once the valorous person went to the cowpen, where he found a tiger which had arrived there to kill the cows. Cows finding the tiger among them started braiding in terror. Then the son of Manu, holding a sword cut-off the head of a calf instead of the tiger. The tiger on the other hand finding him approaching with a sword in his hand, was terrified and fled away.

The wicked tiger met with its end due to the rain and storm. Understanding the fact he returned to his place during the night.

At the end of the night at dawn he went back to the cowshed and found the dead calf and not the tiger. He felt immensely remorseful.

The preceptor, hearing about the killing of the calf, thoughtlessly, taking his pupil to be a sinner, pronounced a cursed on him saying that he should become a Sudra, instead of a Ksatriya.

The preceptor of the race, thus pronounced the curse thoughtlessly. Prsadhra then left the home and went to a forest.

With this painful situation he felt detached from the world and he achieved salvation by burning himself in fire.

Kavi- the son of Manu became a learned person by the grace of Siva. Enjoying all the pleasures in the world, he achieved to trace salvation.

## Chapter 37 - The race of Iksavaku

Suta said, “A son named Iksavaku was born out of the nose of Manu. He had nine sons who distributed enormous gifts in charity.

O Brahmanas, after him there had been several rulers in Aryavarta Vikuksi was the foremost of all who was the king of Ayodhya.

You better listen to his deeds, who belonged to the race of Brahma. He decided to perform a Sraddha, but he actually did not do so.

Out of the rabbits which had been brought for Sraddha he consumed one of them he became a sasada (an eagle or a hunter). Iksavaku was also deserted by the people as a result of which he went to the forest.

During the life time of Iksavaku, he by the grace of Vasistha became a king and had fifteen sons including Sakuni.

They became rulers of Uttarapatha, while the son of the king of Ayodhya, became the powerful king, who was known as Kakustha. Arinabha was the son of Kakustha. Prthu's son was Vistrasva, from whom Indra Prajapati was born.

Yuvanasva was the son of Indra and Srava had been his Prajapati. The intelligent Sravastaka was the son of Srava, who founded the city of Sravasti. Sravasti's kin was Brhadasva- the great ascetic.

Kuvalasva was the son of Yuvanasva who came to be known as virtuous Dhudhumara, after killing Dhundhu.

Kuvalasva had a hundred sons who were great archers. The father crowned Kuvalasva the king.

Entrusting the burden of the kingdom to his son, the king desired to return to the forest but was prevented to do so by the sage Uttanka.

Uttanka said, “Listen, you protect the earth with the religious mind. O great Purusa, the earth protected by you, would free be from controversy, excitement or pain. Therefore, you should not retire to the forest. In my hermitage there is region without water or over the mountain peaks covered with snow, where the sand of the seashore is widely spread, there lives a demon who is enormously arrogant, having a gigantic body. He is invincible by the gods even.

He lives under the ground covered with the sand. He is quite awful and is known by the name of Dhundhu. He is the son of the demon Madhu.

After performing the hard tapas fort destruction of the lokas, he goes to sleep. When he breaths after a year, then the earth shakes with all the mountain and trees, showering the red fire balls as well the sparks besides the smoke.

O king, because of him I can never remain stable in my cottage. O king with long arms, you better stop him for the welfare of the universe.

By your killing him the entire universe would feel at ease. O king, you alone are competent enough to kill him. O sinless one, you are competent enough to kill him.

O great king, lord Visnu had bestowed a boon on you in earlier times, according to which lord Visnu will regenerate his strength in you.

The sustaining of the people is an auspicious dharma. You cannot earn such merit by going to the forest.

O lord of kings, there is one dharma which could be more auspicious than the protection of the subjects as has been propounded by the ancient Rsis. ”

At these words of the sage Uttanka, the noble royal sage, gave away his son Kuvalasva to the sage, for the purpose of the killing of the demon.

O lord, O best of the Brahmanas, I have discarded the use of weapons. My son will surely kill Dhundhu.”

Thus speaking to the sage and advising his son appropriately, the king proceeded on for the performing of tapas. On the other hand Kuvalasva accompanied with the sage Uttanka, proceeded on forth killing of the demon.

At the same time, lord Visnu, at the inspiration of Uttanka and keeping the welfare of the people in view, entered the body of Kuvalasva, with his lustre.

Kuvalasva then became invincible from all, a huge sound appeared in the sky, declaring that, “The glorious prince will surely destroy Dhundhu.

The gods decorated him with the garlands of flowers from all the sides and praised him saying, “Enjoy long life and be victorious”

The king Kuvalasva, who had been the best among the victorious kings, accompanied with his sons, then dug up on ocean below the sand.

O Brahmarsi, the king who was resplendent with lustre of lord Visnu, possessed enormous prowess.

O Brahmana, the king and his sons, while digging the sand spotted the demon Dhundhu.

With the fire emerging from his mouth, and destroying the *lokas* with his anger, the demon started raining water all round the forest was disturbed with the appearing of the full moon.

O excellent sage, with the fire emerging of the demon’s mouth only three of the hundred sons of the king could be saved and the rest were destroyed.

O foremost of the Brahmanas, then the king Kuvalasva came face to face with the valorous and illustrious demon Dhundhu- the killer of the Brahmanas.

The king on his part neutralised the force of the water issued by the demon with the strength of the fire arrow as the fire is subsided with water.

After killing the demon Dhundhu, the king's performance was witnessed by the sage Uttanka.

The great sage Uttanka then bestowed the following boons over the king Kuvalasva: “you will have unending riches and you will never be defeated by the enemies.

You will always remain devoted to dharma, and you have an infallible abode in the heaven, your sons who have been killed in the battle shall achieve the infallible heaven.

Out of his three remaining sons, Drdhasva had been the eldest, while the remaining named Hamsasva and Kapilas'va were the younger ones.

Dhudhumara’s son was Drdhasva who has a son named Haryasva and Haryasva has a noble son named Nikumbha.

Nikumbha had the son named Samhatasva, who was quite well-versed in the warfare. Samhatasva had two sons named Aksasva and Krtasva.

He had two daughters, who were known as Vrsadvati and Hemavati, who were respected by the people, and were well known the world over because of their virtues. Prasenajit had been the name of his son.

Prasenajit got a chaste wife known by the name of Gauri. But her husband made her a stream, known by the name of Bahuda.

His son Yuvanasva, had been a great king, while Mandhatta, the of Yuvanasva was famous the world over.

Caitrarathi the daughter of Sasabindu, was his most chaste wife, who was the eldest of her ten thousand brothers.

Two auspicious sons were born to Mandhata from her who were known by the names of Purukutsa and Mucukunda.

The son of Purukutsa was known as Traiyaruni who was quite learned besides being a poet. His son named Satyavrata was quite powerful.

He was evil-minded and always caused disturbance in the reciting of the sacred mantras. He abducted the brides of others after marriage forcibly out of the lust, delusion or arrogance and fun. He abducted the virgins to satisfy his lust. The king Traiyaruni forsook him for his grave misconduct. Getting infuriated, he called him a degraded wretch.

Then the wicked son asked his father, where to go. The king then asked him to go to the place of the Candalas.

When he was so discarded by his religious minded father, Satyavrata started living in the colony of the Candalas.

The king Traiyarani, getting fed up because of the deeds of his son, forsook the throne and went to the forest for performing tapas.

O Brahmarsi, because of the misdeeds of his son, there was no rainfall in kingdom for twelve years.

Then Visvamitra the great ascetic, leaving his wife behind, went to the seashore and performed sever austerities.

His wife tied his middle son around her neck and offered him for sake for a hundred icons, in order to sustain the other children.

Finding the mother selling her own son, tied round her neck, for sale, Satyavrata released him.

The mighty Satyavrata, just to satisfy Visvamitra out of human sympathy, sustained him.

Thereafter, the son of Visvamitra came to be known as Galava because, he was tied round the neck of his mother. He also performed great tapas.

## Chapter 38 - The birth of Satyavrata, Trisunka, Sagara and others besides the related stories

Suta said, “Then Satyavrata started protecting the wife of Visvamitra because of his devotion, grace and the resolve of Visvamitra.

O Sage, Satyavrata killed the deer, pigs, buffaloes, and other living beings, which had been wandering in the forest and kept their meat in the hermitage of Visvamitra.

While the sage Vasistha used to protect the inner apartments with the co-operation of the priests, Upadhyayas and others, besides the tirtha, cows and the bodies etc.

Because of the words of Satyavrata or due to the moves of the destiny, Vasistha preserved the anger in his mind alone.

When the father removed his son from the kingship, at that time also Vasistha did not stop him from doing so due to some reason.

Satyavrata could not understand the importance of the mantras of the seventh pada of the marrige rites.

Then he presented himself for the pleasure and satisfaction of his father for the redemption of the race.

Even after the disowning of his father, Vasistha did not stop him. When the sage described his son to be crowned as the king even then Satyavrata kept quite.

The valorous person maintained the duties of his vow for twelve years. When he could not procure meat from any other place, then the prince found the wish fulfilling cow of Vasistha. Then because of his anger against Vasistha, out of greed, delusion and hunger, O sage, accepting the duties of a Candalas, he killed the cow and he consumed the beef of the cow himself and also served the same to the son of Visvamitra. On hearing this Vasistha expressed his rage on him and he said to him.”

Vasistha said, “You have committed three crimes. In case two iron stakes fail to cause injury to you I shall use another which would be more sharp then the earlier two.

You have committed threefold crime, by displeasing your father, by killing the auspicious cow of you preceptor and used things without sprinkling the holy water on them.

Then he gave him the name of Trisanku. Ever since that time he came to be known by the said name. On his return from his tapas, Visvamitra was pleased with Trisanku for the upkeep of his family in his absence. When he was pressed to ask for a boon then asked for the same.

After the end of draught lasting for twelve years, Visvamitra crowned him as the king of father’s kingdom and made Trisanku perform a yajna.

In full view of Vasistha and the gods, Visvamitra bodily transported him to the heaven.

His wife named Satyaratha who was born in the Kekaya race gave birth to Hariscandra who had been a noble soul.

Hariscandra the well-known Cakravarti king came to be known as Trisankava, who performed the Rajasuya yajna. His son was Rohita, who had a son named Vrka, while Vrka had a son named Bahu.

The said king was dethroned by the king Talajanga of the Haihayas country. He was a religious minded Brahmana, who did not perform the religious exercises for himself alone.

Bahu begot a son Sagara who was born with poison, Reaching the hermitage of the sage Aurava, he was saved by Bhargava.

Receiving the fire weapon from Bhargava, the king Sagara, killed Talajangas and other Haihayas.

Thereafter he after killing the Sakas, Bahudakas, Paradas and Khagas, with their armies, he established the excellent dharma and rule of the country.

Saunaka said, “O Suta, how was he born of a Ksatriya mother, with poison? Then how could he conquer all? You please speak out in detail.” O Sage, when so questioned by Pariksata, the reply that was given by the sage Vaisampayana, I am going to repeat the same to you. You please listen.”

Pariksata said, “O sage, how was the king Sagara born with poison, and how could be kill many kings, you please tell me.

Vaisampayana said, “O Lord of the people, O dear one, the king Bahu was infested with all the vices, therefore he was deprived of his kingdom by Talajangha born in the Haihayas dynasty.

There are five ganas of the Raksasas known as Yavanas, Paradas, Kamboja, Pahlavas and Bahudakas.

O king the armies of all the five Raksasas deprived Bahu of his kingdom and gave it to Haihayas.

O Brahmanas, after having been deprived of the kingdom, Bahu retired to the forest, with his wife, where he met with his end.

Yadani was his wife who had been pregnant at that time. Her co-wife, out of jealousy had poisoned her earlier.

She then for the sake of her husband resolved to enter the fire, when Aurava of the Bhargava race saved her.

The queen then for the protection of her child in the womb lived in the hermitage of the sage and started serving the sage, with her mind devoted to Siva.

Once when the muhurta and the lagna were good, when the five planets were favourable, the child was born with the poison administered to the queen.

In the powerful lagna Sagara having long arms was born.

The sage Aurava, performed the birth ceremony and other rites of the child. When he was grown up, he was taught the Vedas and other scriptures besides imparting the knowledge of the use of arms.

Then the valorous king started learning the use of the unbearable fire weapons.

Thereafter, he, on the basis of his strength and the fire weapons started killing the Haihayas.

Then the glorious king spread his fame in all the lokas and established the noble dharma on earth.

Then he subjugated the Sakas, Yavanas, Kambojas, Pahlavas who rushed to take refuge with the sage Vasistha.

The glorious Vasistha, made deceitfully to enter into an agreement offered them freedom from fear and produced them to the king Sagara.

At the instance of his priest, Sagara kept up his resolve by destroying their mode of worship and changing their hair style.

Half of the heads of the Sakas were shaven, and they were them set free. The heads of Yavanas and the Kambojas were completely shaven.

The king Sagara then had the complete heads of Paradas, while the beards and the moustaches of Pahlavas were shaved.

O dear, O dear one, the king became victorious on earth by means of dharma. The opponent Ksatriya kings were also deprived of the dharma.

The king establishing the victory of dharma, decorated a horse for performing an Asvamedha sacrifice.

O sage, Sagara entrusted the protection of the horse to his sixty thousand sons. The horse then moved towards the south eastern ocean.

The selfish Indra, stole away the horse and sent it in the nether world.

The king Sagara had the entire region dug in search of the horse.

With the digging up of the great ocean, the sons of Sagara found the great sage Kapila- the eternal Purusa and form of the universe.

As he woke up the fire emerged from his eyes, and sixty four thousand sons of Sagara lost their lives. Only four could be saved.

They were known by the names of Harsaketu, Suketu, Dharmaratha and Pancajana. These were the princes who carried over the race of Sagara.

Then the lord Hari bestowed five boons to the king Sagara for the increase of his progeny, wisdom, glory, beautiful sons and the riches.

With this performance he became the father of the ocean besides getting back the sacrificial horse from the ocean.

The immensely glorious Sagara then completed a hundred Asvamedha sacrifices. He also adored the Vibhutis of Siva as well as the other gods.

## Chapter 39 - The king Sagara and the expansion of his family

Saunaka said, “How could Sagara get valorous and strong sixty thousand sons? You kindly narrate the relevant story.

Suta said, “The king Sagara had two wives, who had been purified by his tapas. He pleased the sage Aurava with his tapas, who bestowed a boon on him.

One of them hurriedly desired to have sixty thousand sons and the other one desired only one son, who could prolong the race.

The senior queen on her arrival in her abode, produced a sack filled with the seeds. On emptying the sack the infants emerged out of the same.

The mid-wives brought them up. They were nourished in the pitchers filled with ghee (butter).

The prince Pancajana, who escaped the fire of anger of the sage Kapila became the king.

The powerful Amsuman was born out of him, who had a son named Dilip. The king Bhagiratha had been born in the same race.

It was Bhagiratha, who made river Ganga the best of the rivers to flow on earth. The ocean respectfully declared her as his daughter.

Srutasena had been the son of Bhagiratha. Nabhaga, his son had been as noble soul.

Ambarisa was the son of Nabhaga, who had a son named Sindhudvipa, whose kin happened to be the powerful Ayutajit.

The glorious Rtuparva had been the illustrious son of Ayutajit. He was an expert in the game of dice and was the friend of the king Nala.

The immensely illustrious Anuparva had been the son of Rtuparva. His son was Mitrasaha, who was known as Kalmasapada, as well.

The well-known Sarvakarma had been he son of Kalmasapada. His son was Anaranya.

The learned king Mundidruha was the son of Anaranya. He had the sons named Nisadha, Rati and Khatvanga.

O sinless one, Khatvanga returned from heaven, lay on earth for a muhurta and attained all the three worlds, by means of his intelligence and truthfulness.

Dirghabahu was his son. He had a son named Raghu. Aja was his son and Dasaratha was born to him.

Rama was born to Dasaratha who had been quite a pious person. Rama was quite popular as the amsa of lord Visnu and the devotee of Siva. He killed the demon king Ravana.

His story has been narrated in several Puranas as well as in the Ramayana. Therefore the relevant details have not been included here.

Rama had Kusa as his son, who was also quite well known. Atithi was the son of Kusa, while Nisadha had been the son of Atithi.

Nala was the son of Nisadha, Nabha was the son of Nala, while Pundarika was the son of Nabha. Ksemadhanva was the son of Pundarika.

Ahinagu's kin was valorous Sahasvan and his son was Virasena, who belonged to the Iksvaku dynasty.

The kin of Virasena was Pariyatra, whose son was Bala and he had the son named Sthala.

He had an illustrious son of the solar race and he had a glorious son named Yaksa. His son was Aguna and from him Vidhrti was born.

He had a son named Hiranyanabha, whose son was Yogacarya, who had been the disciple of Jaimini an expert in the spiritual science.

It was from him that the great king Kausalya Yajnavalkya studied the spiritual science of Yoga which reveals the problematic mysteries of the heart.

Pusyanaman had been his son and his son was Dhruva. His son was Agnivarna, and his son was Sighra.

Ksemadhanva had the son named Devanika, who had a son named Ahinagu.

His son was Marut, who became well- versed in Yoga doctrine. This king is still alive in a village of Kalapa.

At the end of Kaliyuga, he was destroyed there together with the people of that place. He will particularly redeem the solar race.

His son was Prthusruta, his son was Sandhi, his son was Amarsana and his son was Marutvan.

His son was Visvasa, his son was Prasenajit, his son was Taksaka, and his son was Brhadbala.

These are the names of the past Iksvaku kings. Now you listen to their future of noble kings.

Brhadrana will be the son of Brhadbala, who will have a son named Urukriya.

His son will be Vatsavrddha. His son will be Prativyoman, his son will be the Bhanu- divaka, who will be commander of army.

The great mighty Sahadeva will be his son and his son will be Brhadasva, whose son will be mighty Bhanuman.

The mighty Pratikasva will be the son of Bhanumat, whose son will be the best of the kings, Supratika.

O Brahmanas, his son will be Marudeva, his son will be Sunaksatra, his son will be Puskara and his son will be Antariksa.

His son will be valorous Sutapa, his son will be Mitracit, his son will be Brhadbhaja, and his son will be Barhi by name.

His son will be Krtanjaya, his son will be Rananjaya, his son will be Sanjaya and his son will be Sakya.

His son will be Suddhodana, his son will be Langala, his son will be Prasenajit, his son will be Sudraka.

Sudraka's son will be known as Runaka, his son will be Suratha, his son will be Sumitra, who will destroy the prestige of the race.

The Iksvaku race which was performing the noble deeds, had religious minded monarchs and possessing wonderful prowess, will come to an end of the end of Sumitra.

The auspicious race will disappear from the earth after the king Sumitra. It will further develop in the Brahma-Satyayuga.

Thus I have narrated the details of auspicious, Iksvaku kings who gave enough of charities.

I have also spoken about the creation of Aditya- Vivasvan and Sraddhadeva, who took good care of the people.

The one who listens or reads the story of the solar race, becomes an excellent ruler, enjoying all the pleasures achieves the Sayujya type of salvation.

## Chapter 40 - Influence of Sraddha for the manes

Vyasa said, “Thus listening about the glory of the excellent Sraddhadeva solar dynasty, Saunaka asked the excellent sage Suta.

Saunaka said, “O disciple of Vyasa having long life, Suta, the divine story of Sraddhadeva, which increases the race, I have some doubt about it which I am going to place before you.

How could lord sun earn the position of Sraddhadeva? I would like to listen to the same with respect. You kindly remove my doubt.

O lord, the glory of Sraddha and the fruit of the same may also kindly be narrated, by which the manes as well as the performer of the Sraddha could meet welfare.

I would like to know the origin of the Pitrs or manes. You kindly speak out the same to me.

Suta said, “O Saunaka, I shall narrate to you the entire story of the origin of the manes, which had been narrated by the sage Markandeya, at the instance of Bhisma- the grandsire, which had been told to Markandeya by the learned sage Sanatkumara. I am going to repeat the same story to you which fulfills all the desires.

Bhisma pitamaha, lying over the bed of arrows had said to Yudhisthira and the same is being repeated by me. You please listen.

Yudhisthira said, “How is nourishment achieved by the people who are desirous of getting nourishment which are the type of activations which cause him no pain? I would like to know about the same.

Suta said, “When so asked by Yudhisthira, Bhismapitamaha the noble soul said, quite lovingly.

Bhisma said, “O Yudhisthira, a person who with utmost faith, performs the Sraddha, remains delighted in that house by the grace of the manes.

For achieving the best reward, the people perform the Sraddha of the father, the grandfather and the great grandfather, because the manes bestow the persons desirous of dharma and progeny to the people who are desirous for the same. They also bestow riches to those desirous of nourishment besides the good health.

Yudhisthira said, “The manes of some of the people go to the heaven and the others to the hell and the living beings have to reap the reward of their deeds.

Then how the manes receive the material given to them in the Sraddha? How can a person falling in the hell get the reward for the same?

I have heard that even the gods adore the manes while they are lodged in the heaven. I would like to know more details about them therefore you kindly speak about them exhaustively.”

Bhismapitamaha said, “O destroyer of the enemy, I have heard from my father who had met this his death and then achieved heaven. I shall repeat the same to you.

I was about to give the pindas to my father at the time of his day of Sraddha. He desired me to place the kusa grass over the earth.

The performing of the Sraddha by means of Kalpa was not known to me earlier. Therefore, I thoughtlessly placed the pindas over the Kusa grass.

Then my father was pleased with my performance and then he spoke in sweet voice, “O best of the race of Bharata, I am pleased with the performing of the Sraddha by you.

You are well-versed in dharma, besides being the learned one. By you I claim to have the kins. O best of the humans, you have in fact redeemed me.

What the king does by virtuous or authoriatative rites, the subjects too emulate, taking them to be backed by precedent.

O best of the descendants of Bharata, you listen to the ancient dharma of the Vedas. Your performance is supported by the provisions of the Vedas.

Therefore, I am quite pleased with you. I, therefore bestow boon on you which can rarely be achieved in the universe.

You will not die unless you desire for the same. The death shall exercise its influence on you, only with your permission.

O best of the race of Bharata, what do you want? What is there in your mind? You ask for the best of boon.”

When they thus spoke to the grandsire, I spoke with my hands folded offering my salutation to them. In case you are pleased I have met with success. I intend to ask you a question you kindly answer the same.”

Then he said, “You can ask for whatever is desired by you. I shall surely reply to you.” When so desired by him, I asked him.

Santanu said, “O dear one, listen, I shall explain to you the reality about your question. The entire Pitr-kalpa has been heard by me from the sage Markandeya.

O dear one, whatever you ask me now, I had asked the sage Markandeya, the same questions. Then he who was well-versed in the sacred rites told me.

O king listen, once I looked up into the sky and found a great aerial chariot coming over the mountain.

The chariot appeared to me like a huge blazing mass of splendour, brilliant like the glowing coal which was quite pleasing to the mind and there was nothing parallel to it. A man of the size of a thumb was found by me lying therein. He was quite brilliant as if the fire had been placed over the fire.

I bowed to him, lowering my head. I asked the auspicious lord, “How may we know you.

The noble soul then said to me, “You do not have the strength of *tapas,* by which you could be able to now about me, the son of Brahma.

I am Sanatkumara. You tell me, what should I do for you? All other sons of Brahma are smaller than me.

We are in all seven invincible brothers, whose races are well established. All of us establish the soul in the soul and follow the *Yati-dharma.*

O sage, soon after my birth, I came to be known by the name of Kumara. Therefore people call me Sanatkumara.

The devotion with which you performed the tapas to have audience with me, I have appeared before you because of the same. Let you meet with welfare. Tell me what should I do for you?

When he was thus speaking, I spoke to him, “Listen, O lord, you kindly tell me the early history of the manes, correctly.

At these words of mine, he then told me, “Listen O dear one, I shall speak to you quite pleasantly the entire Pitrsarga.

Sanatkumara said, “Brahma initially created the gods and asked them to adore him. Then the gods who were desirous of the reward, started adoring the soul.

Then Brahma pronounced a curse on them that since “You have insulted me, therefore you will lose consciousness.

Then all the gods spoke to the grandsire, lowering their heads, “Kindly be merciful on us.” When they thus spoke, he asked them to perform repentance.

Then Brahma asked them, “You should ask from your sons, after which you will get enlightened.” On hearing this, they getting devoid of consciousness, started asking their sons.

O sinless one, they said to their sons, O sons, all of you should go for repentance.

Then the cursed gods, as per the desire of the sons, asked Brahma, as to why the sons have thus addressed us?

Then Brahma spoke to the gods, who were in doubt, “O gods you have no more to be treated as Brahmavadis.

Therefore what has been mentioned by the sons, the most excellent of the perfectly wise shall be followed without hesitation and not otherwise.

All of you should collectively adore the gods and the manes who fulfil all the desires.

Sanatkumara said, “O excellent sage, then all of them getting relieved of the doubt with the words spoken by Brahma starting living lovingly collectively.

Then the gods said to them, “Since you have addressed us as sons, therefore all of you should became Pitaras. There is no doubt about it.

The performance of Pitr-sraddha can be done by anybody now. The moon having been pleased with the performance of the Sraddhas will satisfy all the lokas.

They will delight the ocean, the mountains, the forest, besides all the mobile and immobile beings. Those desirous of nourishment from Sraddha rites, are given nourishment by the Pitrs when propitiated. Those giving three pindas in the Sraddha mentioning the names and the gotras, delight the pitrs wherever they be and are well looked after by them.

These words are truthful, whether gods or pitrs we are father and son successively. Thus the pitrs, who became the sons became famous in the world as mutual beneficiaries.

## Chapter 41 - The story of seven hunters

Sanatkumara said, “O best of the ascetics, there are seven pitrs in the heaven out of them, four have the definite form, and the three are without form.

Initially, they were adored by the gods and then the Brahmanas- they used to satisfy the moon with their yogic exercises.

Because of this, the charities for the *Sraddha* should be given to the *yogis* in the silver vase or the vases with silver.

The Svadha given to the priest in the Sraddha pleases the pitrs. Invoking the fire, the moon and Yama, the one who offers the pitrs by means of Agnaukarma Sraddha- viddhi, with devotion, the pitrs get pleased with the same.

The pitrs when pleased, fulfil the desire of the performer for nourishment, the progeny, heaven, health and other desired objects.

O sage, the adoration of the manes is better than the adoration of the gods. O Brahmarsi, you are eternal and free from the old age.

O sage even the yogic practices do not have the powers as are possessed by the devotion of the pitrs. Therefore, O sage, one should adore the pitrs particularly.

Markandeya said, “Thus speaking, the lord of the gods, bestowing the divine sight which is beyond the reach of the gods even, achieved the position of a yogi.

O Bhisma, listen, in earlier times the Brahmana- Bhardvaja's sons achieving the yogic dharma had fallen because of his evil deeds.

Their names which speak of their evil ways are- vagdusta (foul mouthed), krodhana (filled with anger), himsa (violent), Pisuna (back biter), kavi (poet), Svasrsa (self created) and Pitrvartin (worshipper of Pitrs).

O dear one, the sons of Kausika became the followers of Garga, after the death of their father, they went to the forest.

At the command their preceptor, they took away his milching cow and the calf. All of them were united in their activities.

O Bharata, they felt hungry on the way and they developed the evil wisdom due to childishness or foolishness and they thought of killing the cow.

Kavi and Svasrsa asked for the cow, which the others did not part with. They also could not stop the violence.

One who, out of them all, performed the religious practices daily, was known by the name of Pitrvarti. As being devoted to his parents said to them, getting enraged.

“Never mind in case you cannot do any good, but perform the Sraddha only for the manes, quite carefully.”

By doing so, the cow will attain piety undoubtedly. You will adore the pitrs with devotion and as such you will be free from the sin.

O Bharata, as advised by him, they bathed the cow and gifted it to the manes. As such their task was established.

All of them then said to the preceptor, that “A lion killed the cow in the forest. You kindly have this calf.”

The Brahmana, feeling painful accepted the calf. Because of their misconduct, they earned the sin of go-hatya.

O dear one, after some time, all the seven brothers died at the expiry of their term of life.

All the seven brothers, because of their treachery with the preceptor, killing of the cow, wickedness and violence were reborn as the sons of a hunter in the Dasarna country. They were strong and well-versed in dharma.

They were devoted to dharma, free from delusion, with nervous temperament, started living over the Kalanjara mountain like the deer.

Thereafter having been reminded of the cause of their death, like the lonely wild beasts, they started living in the forest fearlessly becoming peaceful.

All the seven hunters, were engaged in the auspicious deeds, free from evil deeds, and were well aware of their caste.

They had listened to dharma in their earlier birth from the preceptor which was retained in their minds, including the desire for non¬return to the world.

They performed the tapa at the mountain peak, consumed their food and finally ended their lives over that mountains. O descendent of Bharata, O king, over the mountain Kalanjara, they fall dead at seven different places are still found over that mountain still. Because of their activities which were neither inauspicious nor auspicious, they were reborn in the life which was neither auspicious nor in auspicious.

All of them were then re-born as Cakravaka (sheldrake) bird, which was auspicious and inauspicious. Then they were born as aquatic animal in the auspicious Saraddvipa.

They discarded their association with their mates and they conducted themselves like saints, were devoid of association, peaceful and free from the company of the women.

Getting free from the worldly bondages, conducting themselves as a brahmacaris following the path of dharma, they became auspicious birds.

They recollected their castes well. They were quite healthy and all of them being brahmacaris died at one place. All of them were spotless and noble souls.

In the form of Brahmana, they misbehaved with their preceptor, as a result of which they were born as animals and birds. Thereafter, with the performing of Sraddha, they achieved the knowledge about reality.

Getting well established they performed the Sraddha, as a result of which they achieved knowledge, gained, memory and the increase in merits.

The memory of the discourses on the sacred knowledge which they had heard in their earlier births, the was still preserved in them. Therefore they practiced the same.

Then they were known by the spotless names of a noble race viz. Sumana, Suvak, Suddha, Pancama, Chidradarsaka, Svatantra and Suyajna.

O great sage, the auspicious birds which moved round up the forests, had a wonderful character and you listen to the same.

The king of the Nipa country who was quite influential once arrived in that forest with the ladies of his herm.

The sheldrake bird observing the pomp and show of the king enjoying all the pleasures, desired, in his mind, “I have been shattered with the observing of fasts and hard tapas. In case the tapas yields some merits, or observing of the another life, let me become like him- the abode of fortune and bliss.”

Markandeya said, “Then two of his fellow birds said, “We shall be your countiers, your delighters and the well-wishers.

After saying, “Be it so.” The yogic soul attained the goal. The two sheldrake birds thus replied to him.

The deeds denouncing which you achieved the yoga-dharma. You are asking for the same in the boon. Now you listen to my words.

O dear, you will be crowned as the king of the kingdom of Kampilya and shall rule the country. Those who have been turned as the sheldrake birds, they will be your ministers.

When all the three of them did not speak about the kingdom, then their fourth companion spoke out while Sumana expressed his happiness over the same.

At the end of the period of your curse, you will again be turned as a yogi Sarvasattva, Suyajna and Svatantra too will attain yogic powers.

Because of these blessings, you will gain merit. You have sprinkled the cow and offered it to the pitrs.

We shall achieve wisdom which shall work as the cause of yogic practices for all. The bold words spoken by me are quite spirited and are quoted as the verse.

After achieving the human life you will attain yoga.” After thus speaking the bird Sumana became silent.

Markandeya said, “Thus speaking, O dear, son of Santanu, I have narrated the story for the welfare of the people. Now what else do you want to listen?

## Chapter 42 - Redemption of Seven hunters

Bhisma pitamaha said, “O immensely wise Markandeya, you are the best of those devoted to the *pitrs* (or parents). O excellent sage, what happened thereafter, you kindly tell me.

Markandeya said, “Then all the three birds dwelling around the lake Manasarovara, consuming the water and inhaling the air, started drying up their body.

As Indra roams about in the Nandanavana, the king together with the queens, returned to his kingdom after roaming in the forest.

He had an auspicious son named Anuha. Vaibhraja crowned his son as the king and moved to the forest.

He also started performing *tapas* with his associates. He also kept on performing *tapas* inhaling air alone, having no food.

The said king with the influence of his penance made the forest look wonderful which could bestow the yogic practices. The four birds who followed the yogic practices as well as the other three who had fallen from the yogic path, also met with their end in the same forest.

Then the seven auspicious souls were born in the city of Kampilya including Brahmadatta and others and were from sins.

Four out of the seven, remembered the events of their earlier life. The other three had been overpowered with the delusion. The immensely illustrious Brahmadatta was completely independent.

Chitradarsi and Sunetra were well-versed in Vedas and allied literature. Because of their association of the earlier birth, they became the kins of *Srotris.*

Since Pancala was conversant with Rgveda *mantras* became a preceptor, while Pundarika became master of the two Vedas. He was a Chandogya and the priest of the sacrifice.

Finding that his son was sinless, the king crowned him as the king and he finally attained the supreme god.

Pancala and Pundarika of Pingala entrusted the care of their house holds to their respective sons and returned to the forest where they gained their supreme path.

O descendant of Bharata, Sannati the wife of Brahmadatta, sported with her husband with utmost devotion.

The other three sheldrake birds, were born as Brahmanas in the family of a poor man.

Chidradarsin's four sons were well-versed in Vedic knowledge and were known as Dhrtiman Sumahatman, Tattvadarsin and Nirutsuka.

They performed the yogic exercises. Then they took leave of one another, bowing at the feet of lord Siva and then departed.

They at the time of their departure, again informed their father, that they were going to arrange for his livelihood so that he could pass his time comfortably.

O sage, you narrate this great meaningful *mantra* with devotion to the sinless king Brahmadatta alongwith his minister. Getting pleased, he will surely give you enough of villages and the food grains.” Thus speaking they adored the preceptor and then resorting to the yogic practices achieved *moksa.* The father of the four Brahmanas, after reciting the *mantra* was successful in his goal.

The said verse was narrated by him to the king as well as the minister. There were the seven obstructions in the Dasarna country, which were born as the tigers over the mountain Kalanjara.

They were born a shaldrake birds in Saraddvipa and then at the Kuruksetra ultimately they became the Brahmanas- well- versed in the Vedas.

His courtiers Pundarika and Pancala were also overpowered with delusion and they got confused. Then all of them were reminded of their dwelling at Manasarovara. Then they gave away enough of riches and eatables. Then the king entrusted the kingship to his son Visvaksena, crowning him as the king.

Then Brahmadatta returned to the forest with his wife. Achieving the strength of the *yoga*, he achieved the supreme position.

The noble courtier Pundarika on the other hand with the strength of *Samkhya yoga* got himself purified and attained the final position in *yoga,*

In the same sequence, Pancala- the great ascetic, achieving the excellent lore and the glory, achieved the position of yogacarya.

Such of the great warriors who adore Siva for the purpose of achieving *moksa* they surely achieve the highest position of Siva.

O sage, by listening to this chapter with faith and devotion all the sins committed mentally by speech or with the body are washed out.

With the performing of the *kirtana* of the name of Siva, all the sins disappear, therefore the name of Siva- the god of gods should always be recited, in the same way as the vase of clay vanishes in the water.

O great sage, for the pacifying of the sins, and for the fulfilment of all the desires, the faithful people should recite the name of Siva again and again.

For achieving nourishment, one should read this chapter or should listen to the same and by so doing he will undoubtedly achieve *moksa.*

## Chapter 43 - Method of Vyasa puja

Saunaka said, “O Suta, the disciple of Vyasa, now you listen to the method of adoring Acarya. What should be done after listening to the Siva Purana?

Suta said, “Listening to the excellent story of the Siva Purana the Acarya should be adored with devotion and faith, giving daksina (monetary gift) at the some time.

Then the learned creator of the Purana should be offered the salutation, the ornaments for hands, beside the best of costumes should be offered to him.

At the end of the worship of Siva, a cow with calf should be given to the Brahmana and an book seat made of a pala of gold together with cloth should also be given to him.

The Purana written in beautiful hand should be given to the Acarya and by doing so, the donor is freed from all the worldly bondages.

O Sage, the narrator of the auspicious story, should be given an elephant, a horse and other things according to the means of a person.

O Sage Saunaka, when the Purana is heard appropriately, the listener meets with success. I have spoken the truth.

Therefore O sage, one should listen to the Purana appropriately with devotion, expanded with the quotations from the Vedas, which is meritorious because the Puranas are the hearts of the Vedas.

## Chapter 44 - Birth of Vyasa from Satyavati and establishing of Vyasesvara linga at Kasi

The sages said, “O learned ocean of mercy, O lord, O master, O Suta, you bestow your grace on us and speak out the story of the birth of Vyasa.

Satyavati was the name of the mother of Vyasa, who had been married with king Santanu.

Then how was Vyasa, the son of Parasara, born to her? I have a doubt in this regard. You kingly remove the same.

Suta said, “Once the sage Parasara had been moving on a pilgrimage and suddenly he reached the charming bank of the river Yamuna.

The noble soul while taking food, said to Nisada, “You at once carry me across the Yamuna in your boat.”

At these words of the sage, Nisadha said to his daughter Matsyagandha, “O girl, you at once carry the sage across the river Yamuna.

O fortunate one, the ascetic Parasara was born of the womb of Drsyanti. He is well- versed in all the four Vedas and can cross the ocean of dharma.”

At these words of the father, the girl, attempted to carry the sage who was illustrious like the sun.

As a matter of chance the great yogi was attracted towards girl, who had never fallen to the beauty of even the apsaras.

With the lustful mind towards the beautiful daughter of the fisherman, the sage held the right hand of the girl with his right hand.

AT this the vast eyed damsel smilingly said, “O little spoken sage, why are you indulging in this deplorable deed?

O Intelligent one, you have been born in the best race of Vasistha. O Brahmana, I am the daughter of a Nisada (boatsmen), then how can both of us unite?

The human birth can rarely be achieved and to be Brahmana is the best. O excellent sage, among the Brahmanas, it is difficult to be an ascetic.

In spite of your possessing all the lores, healthy body, auspicious speech, noble race and humility, you have been overpowered by the lust, which is quite surprising.

In this improper deed, no one on earth can stop you from indulging in this misdeed, because of the fear of your pronouncing a curse.”

Thus thinking in her mind, she spoke to the sage, you keep patience till I carry you across the river.

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the damsel, the Parasara the great sage, left her hand and they reached across the river.

Reaching across the river having been overpowered with passions, the sage caught hold of her. Then the shaking damsel spoke to the ocean of mercy.

“O excellent sage, I am the daughter of a Nisadha having enough of odour, issuing from my body. You are quite broad minded and the best of the yogis.

The union of both of us would not be proper like the glass and the gold. The union is always pleasant between those having similar race and appearances.”

At these words of the damsel, the sage turned the girl with charming beauty issuing fragrance upto a yojana.

The lustful sage, then again hold her. At this Vasavi said to the sage, “It has been ordained in the Vedas that one should resort to the several intercourse at night and not during the day. It is quite sinful to enjoy sexual pleasure during the day time which is denounced by all.

Therefore you wait for the night fall. (Because presently) all will look at us and my parents are also standing at the river bank.”

On hearing this the great sage with use of his yogic power create the dark time spreading fog everywhere creating darkness. Then the damsel getting nervous of the physical union again said to the sage.

O great yogi, you have the semen which cannot go waste. You will leave after the sexual intercourse and I shall become pregnant. Then what will be my position?

O possessor of great wisdom, my virginity would be lost. The people will laugh at me. How shall I face my parents?”

Parasara said, “O girl, you freely enjoy all the sexual pleasures with me. You speak out whatever is desired by you. I shall fulfil the same.

In order to make my command truthful, you will be known as Satyavati and will be admirable by the yogis as well and the gods.”

Satyavati said, “In case (my union with you) remains unknown on earth to the people as well as my parents and if my virginity is not lost, only then you can accept me.

O master, my son should resemble you and should possess the prowess like you. The fragrance should always remain in my limbs and I should regain fresh youthfulness daily.”

Parasara said, “O beloved, all your desires will be fulfilled. Your illustrious son will be born of the *amsa* of Visnu.

You also listen to the reason of my turning lustful. My mind had never fallen even at the beauty of the *apsaras.*

O girl, the writing on the forehead by Brahma, can never be falsified, but I have been attracted towards a girl with the smell of the fish.

O beautiful one, your son, will be well- versed in the Vedas, composer of the Puranas and will be glorious the world over.”

Thus speaking the great yogi, enjoying the sexual pleasure with the girl, left the place quickly, after taking a bath in the Yamuna.

The girl also was conceived bearing the child illustrious like the sun. She gave birth to a son in an island by the yamuna who was quite beautiful.

He looked quite graceful holding a Kamandalu in the left hand and a danda in the right hand. He had yellow locks of hair over the head issuing resplendence from his body.

The illustrious boy soon after his birth spoke to his mother, “O mother, you can move out at will as you please and I shall also leave the place.
