O mother, whenever you need me then remember me and I shall fulfil your desire reaching before you.”

Thus speaking, the child, offering his salutation at the feet of the mother left for the place of pilgrimage, which destroyed the sins.

Having been overpowered with the love of her son, and remembering him brooding own her fate, she went back to her father.

Having been overpowered with the love of her son, and remembering him brooding own her fate, she went back to her father.

The child was born in an island therefore he was given the name of Vyasa. Because he separated the Vedas from the Sastras he came to be known as Vedavyasa.

He visited the holy places on pilgrimage which bestow dharma, artha, kama and moksa. These included Prayaga, the foremost of the places of pilgrimage, Naimisaranya, Kuruksetra, Gangadvara (or Haridvara), Avantika, Ayodhya, Mathura, Dvaraka, Amaravati, Sarasvati, Sindhuganga, Gangasagara, Kalanjara, Prabhasa, Badrikasrama, Mahalaya, Omkaraksetra, Purusottama-ksetra (Puri), Gokarna, Bhrgukaccha, Bhrgutunga, Puskara, Sriparvata and after visiting the sacred places of Dhara, he took bath at all the sacred places.

Thus by visiting at many holy places in many countries, Vyasa, the son of Kalika reached Varanasi, which happens to be the abode of merciful Visvesvara and the goddess Mahesvari- Annapurna, who lives there in order to bestow the eternal position to their devotees.

Reaching Varanasi, he visited the sacred place of Manikarnika, he was relieved of the sins of crores of births.

Then he took bath at all the Kundas, step- wells, wells and the tanks and also adored the prominent lingas including Visvesvara.

He offered his salutation to all Gauris, after worshipping Kalaraja and Bhairava; the devourer of all sins.

He also adored Dandanayaka and others ganas of Siva with devotion and also pleased all the Kesavas, making all the efforts.

He worshipped Lolarka and other suns, and he carefully offered the pindas at all the holy places.

The noble soul established the linga of Vyagresvara, by having a look at which a person attains the position of Brhaspati learning all the lores.

Worshipping the lingas like Visvesa and others with devotion, he thought of again and again as to which one of the lingas should be adored to achieve quick success.

A linga by adoring which he could achieve all the lores and by whose grace he could develop the capability for the composing of the Puranas.

Whether he should adore Sriman Omkaranatha, Krttivasesvara, Kedaresvara, Kamesvara, Candresvara, Trilocana, Kalesa, Vrddhakalesa, Jyesthesa, Jambukesa, Jaigisavyesvara,

Dasasvamedhesvara, Drumacandesa, Drkkesa, Garudesa, Gokarnesa, Ganesvara, Prasannavadanesa, Dharmesa, Tarakesvara, Nandikesa, Nivasesa, Patrisa, Pritikesvara, Parvatesa,

Pasupati, Hatakesvara, Brhaspatisvara, Tilabhandesvara, Bharabhutesvara, Mahalaksmisvara, Marutesa, Moksesa, Gangesa, Narmadesvara,

Krsnesa, Paramesana, Ratnesvara, Yamunesvara, Langulisa, Srimadvisvesvara, Prabhu, Avimuktesvara, Visalaksisa, Vyaghresvara, Varahesa, Vidyesvara, Varunesa, Vidhisa, Harikesesvara, Bhavanisa, Kapardisa, Kandukesa, Ajesvara, Visvakarmesvara, Viresvara, Nadesa, Kapilesa, Bhuvanesvara, Vaskulisa, Mahadeva, Siddhisvara, Visvedevesvara, Virabhadresa, Amrtesa, Satisa, Parvatisvara, Siddhesvara, Matangesvara, Bhutisvara, Asadhisa, Prakasesa, Kotirudresvara, Madalesvara, Tilaparnesvara, Hiranyagarbhesa, Srimadhyesvara and several others *lingas* are there which one of the linga should be adored by me?

Vyasa was thus worried about the adoration of Siva and suddenly with a concentrated mind he thought, “I have well realised the truth, which had been forgotten by me, my desire has been established. It is the Madhyesvara *linga* which fulfills all the desires and bestows *dharma*, *artha, kama* and *moksa*, with the worship of which or with the touch of which, the doors of the heaven get opened.

Therefore one should serve Madhyesvara Mahadeva. O Brahmanas, several of the people met with the success by adoring this *Sivalinga,*

Siva is called Madhyamesvara since he is stationed mainly in the centre of Kasi for bestowing happiness on the people.

The Gandharva named Tumburu besides Narada the celestial sage, became ...ficient in the art of music.

With the worship of the same lord, Visnu had gained the position of the bestower of *moksa,* besides Brahma became the creator Visnu the preserver and Rudra became the destroyer of the world.

Kubera became the god of wealth, Vamadeva became the devotee of Siva, Khatvanga became the king and those having no sons got the sons by the grace of lord Siva.

Candrabhama the *apsara* having the voice and sweet as the cuckoo, while dancing was absorbed in the *linga.*

Srikara, the son of a milkman, achieved the position of Ganapati, after adoring the compassionate Siva.

Brhaspati and Sukra who are respectively adored by the gods and the demons, achieved excellence in their learning only by the grace of Siva.

Therefore, I shall also adore Madhyesvara Siva and shall achieve the wisdom for the composing of the Puranas.

Thus speaking the learned Vyasa, the son of Satyavati, took his bath in the water of Bhagirathi and took a *Vrata.*

Sometime he consumed the dry leaves, fruit, vegetation, air, water and sometimes he lived without them.

Thus the auspicious soul adored lord Siva, Madhyesvara, thrice a day, consuming the tree leaves.

In this way a long time was passed, when once Vyasa, the son of Kalika, after his taking bath in the Ganga in the early morning, had an audience with Madhyesvara Siva, on whose left Uma was lodged, was clad in the tiger skin as the upper garment, and his matted locks of air was floating in the water of Ganga. He had a beautiful body.

He looked graceful and his hair resembled the moon rays of the winter season. His entire body had been plastered with ashes. His body was as bright as the camphor.

His eyes extended upto the ears. His lips were red like coral. His body resembled the child of five years’ age. He was adorned with ornaments suited to the children.

Finding such a lord Siva who was beyond the reach of the yogis, the form of consciousness, kin of the destitutes, lovingly offered prayer to him with choked voice.

Vedavyasa said, “O great lord, O god of gods, you are beyond the mind, speed and deeds and are beyond the reach of the yogis and cannot be visualised by them.

O lord of Uma, even the Vedas are unaware of your glory. You are the creator, preserver and destroyer of the universe. You are the foremost of all the gods.

You alone are the blissful lord, you are omniscient Sadasiva and you are beyond the name and the gotra.

You are the supreme Brahman the remover of the noose of Maya. You are free from the three ganas in the same way, as the lotus leaf is free from water.

You are beyond the birth, conduct, country or even the race. Inspite of this you are the great lord who fulfills the desires of the universe.

Even Brahma, Visnu, Indra and other great yogis are unaware of your tattvas. Then how can one adore you.

All are from you and you pervade in all. You are the lord of Gauri and the killer of Tripura. You are the child, young and the old. I hold you in my heart.

O Mahesa, you are adored by the devotees, O Siva, Puranapurusa, Sambhu and the supreme soul, salutation to you.”

Thus praising lord Siva, as soon as Vyasa was about to prostrate before, him, then Balasiva, getting pleased said to Vyasa.

“O yogi, you ask for the boon whatever is there in your mind. I am subservient to my devotees. Therefore, there is nothing which cannot be given to you.

Then Vyasa, the great ascetic, got up and said, “0 lord, you are omniscient, nothing is unknown to you.

You are great soul and bestow everything. Why should then the lord force me for begging which is the cause of misery.”

On hearing the words of Vyasa, with auspicious mind, lord Siva, having assumed the form of a boy, smiled and said.

The boy said, “O most excellent of those who are aware of Brahmana, the desire of your heart will undoubtedly fulfilled before long.

I the great lord shall dwell in your throat and shall make you compose, efficiently, O Brahmana the history of the Puranas.

The holy hymn abhilasastaka (the eight verses of desire) that you have now uttered shall fulfill the desire of the men who read and recite it in the temple of Siva thrice a day for a year.

The reciting of this hymn is conducive to the increase of learning and intellect. It is the cause of all the recites and is the bestower of virtues and salvation to the people.

In case a person getting up in the early morning, after taking his bath, adores Sivalinga for a year, reciting this stotra he becomes Brhaspati, inspite of his being a fools.

In case a man or a woman, recites this stotra before a Sivalinga daily for a year, his wisdom and education is increased.”

Thus speaking Balasiva was absorbed in the linga and disappeared Vyasa also became emotional dropping the tears of love.

In this way getting a boon from Madhyamesvara Siva, Vyasa playfully composed the eighteen Puranas, which included Brahma, Padma, Vaisnava, Saiva, Bhagavata, Bhavisya, Narada, Markandeya, Agneya, Brahmavaivarta, Linga, Varaha, Vamana, Kurma, Matsya, Garuda, Skanda and Brahmanda. These were the eighteen Puranas, which bestow glory and merit to the devotees of Siva.

Suta said, you are the best among those who posses the knowledge of the Vedas, you have given the names of the eighteen Puranas. You please speak out their description to me.

Vyasa said, “The same question was put by Tandi the son of Brahma to Nandikesvara. The reply he gave in this connection, you listen from me.

Nandikesvara said, “O sage Tandi, Brahmanda Purana is considered to be the foremost in which the four faced Brahma himself is the speaker.

The glory of the Padmakalpa has been described in the second Purana called Padma Purana named after the greatness of Padmakalpa.

The sage Parasara composed a Purana, revealing the thoughts of the father and the son, the same was spoken by Brahma. It is the third one known as Visnu Purana.

The Purana in the Purva and Uttara khandas of which, the story of Siva has been described in detail, it has been given the name of Siva Purana.

The Purana in which the story of the goddess Durga has been enshrined, it is called the Devi Bhagavata or the Devi Purana.

The sixth Purana has been spoken by Narada and is known by the title of Narada Purana. The Purana in which Tandi Markandeya, the great sage had been the speaker is known as Markandeya Purana, which is the seventh one.

The Agni Purana was composed with the combination of Agni. Since it deals with the events of future, the ninth Purana is known as the Bhavisya Purana.

Since the transformation of Brahma is narrated in the Purana, it is called Brahmavaivarta Purana. Because the subject of linga has been discussed in the Purana, it is title as Linga Purana.

O sage, the sports of lord Varaha have been, contained in the twelfth Purana, which is known as Varaha Purana. The Purana in which Skanda is the listener and Mahesvara is the speaker, it is called Skanda Purana which is the tenth one. The fourteenth is the Vamana Purana which deals with the story of Vamana. The fifteenth Purana is the Kurma Purana which deals with the Kurma or the tortoise incarnation of Visnu. The fifteenth Purana has been narrated by the fish incarnation of Visnu as such it is known as Matsya Purana.

The Purana, the speaker of which is Garuda himself, it the seventeenth one and is known as Garuda Purana. Since the topics of the globe are desired in the eighteenth Purana, it is called the Brahmanda Purana.

Suta said- The same question was put by me to the intelligent Vyasa and I had heard the story of all the Puranas then.

In this way Vyasa was born of Satyavati by Parasara. It is he who composed the Mahabharata as well as the Samhitas of the Puranas.

O Brahmana this Parasara and Santanu were united with Satyavati. Therefore there is no scope of doubt.

Because of this reason, the birth of Vyasa is quite surprising. The learned should follow the virtues of the elderly people.

Whosoever reads or narrates the mysterious story it, he getting relieved of the sins, goes to the Rsiloka.

## Chapter 45 - The story of the goddess and the killing of Madhu and Kaitabha

The sages said, we have listened to the story of Siva, comprising of the several events of different incarnations of the lord, which bestow devotion and salvation.

O best of those aware about the Brahmana, now we would like to listen to the pleasant story of the goddess who happens to be the mother of the universe.

Parvati happens to be the primordial Sakti of lord Mahesvara, who is the supreme Brahman. She is the mother of the three worlds.

She incarnated twice. Firstly as Sati and secondly as Hemavati. O immensely learned Suta, you speak out about her other incarnations.

Which one of the intelligent and learned, person would feel satisfied, listening to the stories of the mother, because the learned people surely listen to that story.

Suta said, “You the auspicious souls are graceful because you have desired to know about the story of the great mother.

The sages have declared that those who listen, narrate or recite these stories the dust of their feet is no less then the place of pilgrimage.

Graceful are those besides being successful, whose minds have been devoted to the stories of Sri Devi. Even their children and the race are graceful.

The people who do not adore the goddess who is the cause of all the causes, they are unfortunate and overpowered with the delusion.

Those who do not adore the goddess who is the ocean of mercy, they fall in the blind well of the universe.

As a thirsty person wanders in the desert in search of water, similar is the case of the one who leaving aside the goddess, takes refuge with some other god.

Who would be the person to discard the goddess who bestows her grace on the people, without much effort.

In earlier times the same question was asked by Suratha the noble soul, from the sage Medha. I am repeating to you the reply which the sage gave to Suratha. You please listen to it.

In the Svarocis Manvantara in earlier times, there had been a king named Suratha who was quite strong and valorous.

He was a great donor, truthful, well devoted to dharma, successful, devoted to the goddess and ruled his people well.

He was resplendent like Indra, but the other kings conspired to usurp the kingdom of the said king which was well looked after by him.

All the kings surrounded the capital city of the said king from all the sides. This resulted in a terrific war.

The group of the rulers defeated the king in the battlefield. They usurped his entire kingdom. Then they usurped his entire kingdom and drove him out of the city of Kola.

Thus king then returned to his own city and started ruling there with his courtiers. The opponents defeated him there as well.

As luck world save it, his own courtiers also becoming inimical to the king usurped the entire wealth of his treasure themselves.

Then the king on the pretext of hunting mounting the horse without any guard, proceeded on to the forest.

While so moving towards the forest, the king found an asrama of a Rsi there, surrounded with the flower garden on all sides.

The echo sound of the reciting of the Vedas was heard, all the living beings were peaceful there. The *asrama* was filled with his disciples as well as the grand disciples.

O learned one, because of the influence of the *Rsi,* the powerful lions and other animals did not frighten the weak living beings.

The learned and compassionate king, started living there. The great sage extended his hospitality to him with sweet words offering the seat and food to him.

Once the king feeling extremely worried thought, “It a pity, that I have lost fortune, resplendence, intelligence.

My entire kingdom has been usurped by the enemies. The kingdom which had been well-looked after by me, is now being enjoyed by the enemies.

There had been and king parallel in weakness to me in my race. Now where should I go? How can I get back my kingdom.

My permanent courtiers and the ministers have left me. I do not know which king they serve now.

I know not, in which position would they be after the destruction of the kingdom? My well known, warriors who were enthusiastic in killing the enemy in the battlefield, will now be serving the other king. Whether mountain like elephants, fast galloping horses, the well protected treasure since the time of my ancestors would be well looked after by them or not? Thus thinking noble king fainted.

In the meantime a Vaisya (a trader) also arrived there. The king asked him, “Who are you? What for have you arrived here.

What for are you feeling painful? You tell me.” Listening to the sweet words of the king, with tears flowing from his eyes, the trader spoke in humble voice.

Vaisya said, “I am a trader known by the name of Samadhi and have been born in a wealthy family. O king, because of the greed for wealth, my wife and son have driven me out.

O king, feeling painful of my deeds, I have arrived in the forest. Presently, I am unaware of the welfare of my wife, son, grandson, brother and nephew, besides the other friends, O compassionate king.”

Then the king said, “With the greed for wealth, the son and others have driven you out then why do you have so much of love for them like the fools?

The trader said, O king, you have spoken the purposeful words, but still my mind is bound with the great delusion.”

O excellent sage, then both the king and the trader having been overpowered with the delusion, went to the sage Sumedha.

The glorious king together with the trader offered his salutation to the Rsi who was a great yogi.

With folded hands, king spoke these words to the Rsi, O holy lord, it behoves you now to dispel our delusion.

I, having been deprived of the Rajlaksmi (kingship) have arrived in the forest, but still I am not at ease.

This trader too has been driven out by his son, wife and others, still attraction for them is still preserved in his mind.

What is the reason for it? We are well informed, but still but our minds are still upset with delusion. This is a great foolishness.”

The Rsi said, “The eternal Sakti Mahamaya, is the great goddess who deludes the minds of the people, attracting them.

O Lord Brahma and other gods getting influenced by the Maya remain unaware of the supreme tattva, then what to speak of the humans.

She alone, Paramesvari of three attributes, is the creator, sustainer and the destroyer of the universe at the proper time.

O king person with whom the goddess Bhagavati who is Kamarupini so well, gets pleased, he alone is relieved of the delusion and none else.

The king said, “O sage, who is the goddess Mahamaya, who deludes the entire universe? How was she born you tell me.”

The Rsi said, “The entire universe was turned like an ocean. Then Narayana the great yogi, taking refuge with Yoganidra slept over the serpent bed.

Then from the was of both the ears of Visnu two Daityas known as Mahdu and Kaitabha emerged. They were well known on earth.

They had resplendence like the sun of the time of dissolution, were quite terrific having gigantic bodies, fangs, chins and awful mouths. They appeared as if they would devour the world.

Both of them found Brahma seated over the lotus flower which emerged from the navel of Visnu. Getting ready to killing him they spoke, “Who are you?”

Brahma, then finding Visnu having been absorbed in sleep in the ocean of milk started praying to Paramesvari.

Brahma said, “You are the one who protects those who take refuge in you. You are the goddess Mahamaya, Jagadamba, you save me from these two terrific Daityas. Save me.

I bow in reverence to you who are Mahamaya, Yoganidra, Uma, Sati, Kalaratri, Maharatri, Moharatri greater then the greatest.

You are the mother of the three gods, eternal, bestower of the desired boons to your devotees, preserver of all the gods, and ocean of compassion.

Because of your influence, the gods like Brahma, Visnu and Siva, exercise themselves. You create, sustain and destroy the universe.

O mother, you are Svaha, lajja, spotless wisdom, Tusti, Pusti, Ksanti (forgiveness) and mercy or compassion.

O mother, you are Visnu Maya, Cetana (consciousness), the supreme Sakti, Lajja (shyness) and Trsna (lust).

O mother, you shower your delusion over the invincible asramas and then wake up lord Narayana who is the cause of the creation of the universe.”

Rsi said, “Oh the prayer of the Rsi, then Mahavidya, Jagaddhatri, the great goddess of all the gods, on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Phalguna, possessing the power to delude all the lokas, known as Mahakali emerged, who became well known in the world.

At that point of time a divine voice was heard in the sky saying, “O Brahma, don't be afraid, I shall surely destroy the. demons Madhu Kaitabha today.

Thus speaking, the Mahamaya emerging from the eyes and the face of lord Visnu, appeared before Brahma having invisible birth.

Thereafter, lord Janardana woke up and found the demons, Madhu and Kaitabha before him.

Then there started a war between Visnu and the demons, which continued for five thousand years.

With the influence of Mahamaya, both the demons having been filled with arrogance asked the lord of Rama to ask for a boon.

Narayana said, ‘‘In case both of you are pleased with me, then you grant me the boon that I should be able to kill you both. I need no other boon.”

The Rsi said, “Finding that the entire earth was covered with water, they said to Krsna, “kill us at a spot where the earth is not coyered with water.”

After agreeing to their words, the lord lifted up his dazzling discuss, placed their heads over his thighs and cut them off.

O learned one, thus I have narrated to you the story of the origin of Kalika. Now you listen to the origin of Mahalaksmi.

Inspite of being free from blemishes and devoid of forms and features, Uma manifested herself in various yogas to remove the distress of the gods assuming different forms and features.

Thus her manifestation has been spoken by me who appeared in the bodily form. This is her grandeur. The devotees adore her in this form. This is her sport.

## Chapter 46 - The killing of Mahisasura by the goddess

Rsi said, “There had been an excellent Daitya Rambhasura known by the name of Mahisasura, who had been quite powerful.

The said Daitya king, overpowering all the gods in the battlefield, occupied the throne of Indra in the heaven and started ruling the world over.

The god who had been defeated by the Daitya king, took refuge with Brahma, who together with Visnu went to lord Siva.

Reaching there all the gods offered their salutation of Siva as well as Visnu and narrated all the happenings in a sequence.

They said, “O lord, Mahisasura, defeating all of us, in the battle, driving out from the heaven has ruined us all.

Wandering in the universe we could get no comfort anywhere. What are the miseries which Indra and other gods had not to face?

The duties of the sun, the moon, Kubera, Yama, Agni, wind god, Gandharvas, Vidyadhara, Caranas, and other gods are performed by Mahisasura himself.

Therefore you have to protect the gods like us who seek your protection. Both of you should do something to kill the demon.”

Thus listening to the words of the gods, both Visnu and Siva were extremely enraged as a result of which their eyes became red.

Then the lustre emerged out of the mouths and the bodies of the gods, which was spreading in all the directions. Observing the said lustre, all the gods started adoring Durga.

Similar lustre also appeared from the bodies of the other gods and the terrible lustre merged together and was transformed into the form of a female and came to be known as Mahisasuramardini.

The face of the goddess who emerged out of the lustre of Siva, was quite resplendent. Her hair on the head were formed of the lustre of Yama, her arms were formed of the lustre of Visnu, both the breasts were formed of lustre of the moon, her waist was formed of the lustre of Indra and both the thighs were formed of the lustre of Varuna.

Her buttocks were forms of the lustre of the earth, both the feet were formed of the lustre of Brahma, the toes of the feet and the fingers of the hands were formed with the lustre of the sun.

The nose was formed of the lustre of Kubera, the teeth with the lustre of Brahma, the three eyes from the lustre of the fire god, the eyebrows were formed of the lustre of Sandhya, both the ears were formed of the lustre of the wind god with the lustre of the other gods, Paramesvari emerged, who was lodged over a lotus.

Then finding the goddess Bhagavati, having emerged out of the lustre of all the gods. Looking her all the gods were pleased.

Then Brahma and other gods found Siva, without weapons or attributes. Then all of them resolved to give her the weapons.

Siva then gave a trident to Mahesani Lord Visnu gave her the Cakra and a conch. Then Varuna gave her a Pasa.

Agni gave her the Sakti, the wind god gave her the bow and a quiver filled with arrows. Indra gave her a Vajra and a bell.

Yama gave her the Kaladanda, Prajapati gave her the aksamala, while Brahma gave her the Kamandalu. The sun gave her the innumerable rays.

Kala gave her the shining sword. The ocean of milk gave her a charming hara (necklace) and two unfading costumes, besides Cudamani kataka, kundala, crescent, armlets, beautiful armlets, the throat ornaments and the finger rings. Visvakarma gave her the pleasant battle axe.

The ocean gave her many weapons, an impregnable kavaca, beautiful garland, besides the lotus flower.

The Himalaya gave her a lion as a vehicle, besides several ganas. Kubera gave her a sack filled with Sura.

Sesa, the king of the serpents, gave her a nagahara of wonderful workmanship, studded with precious gems.

With these as well as offering other ornaments, the gods welcomed the goddess. Then the goddess laughed about again and again.

The terrific sound created by her echoed tremendously in the sky, which made the three worlds agitated.

The earth and all the four oceans were disturbed and were shaken. The gods who had been threatened by Mahisasura, shouted the slogans of victory.

The gods then prayed to the supreme goddess, Sakti, Ambika in the form of Mahalaksmi with choked voice in devotion.

Finding all the three worlds having been disturbed, enemies of the god became attentive holding their weapons.

Mahisasura too rushed towards that sound, in anger and found the goddess pervading in the three worlds with her lustre.

At that point of time crores of demon warriors surrounding the demon-king, arrived there holding the swords.

They included Ciksura, Camara, Vidala, Andhaka, Durdura, Durmukha, Trinetra, Mahahanu. These and several other warriors well-versed in warfare arrived there.

Several warriors carrying their weapons started fighting with the goddess in the battlefield and while doing so a lot of time was passed.

All the weapons shot by the demon army were made infructuous by the Mahamaya with her prowess.

Then the goddess attacked the demons like Caksura and other with club, arrows, *Sakti* and *Parasu.*

Then at the killing of his warriors, demon Mahisa tried to kill the enemy warriors, who had emerged out of the breath of the goddess.

He hit some of them with his hoofs, some with his horns, some with his tail and some with his mouth again and again.

After thus killing the warriors of the goddess, the demon king rushed towards the lion- the vehicle of the goddess, as a result of which the goddess was enraged.

The immensely powerful demon king also, trampling and scratching the earth with his hoofs, uprooted a mountain with his horns and threw it towards the goddess, after which he started thundering.

O king, rushing with force on all the sides, he threw many of the mountains on the earth from the sky.

The hills which had been uprooted by the demon king with his horns, were scattered like the parts of rocks and kept on falling on the earth. The ocean which had been shaken with his tail started overflowing.

Then Ambika, who frees the gods from danger, found the enraged demon king and she started thinking of ways to kill him.

The goddess Isvari then cough hold of a noose and with which he was captivated. Then he discarded his buffalo form, and was turned into the form of a lion. Before Ambika severed his head, he transformed himself into a human holding a sword in his hand.

When he was holding the sword and the shield, the goddess shot arrows at him. The demon then transformed himself as an elephant and started dragging the lion with his trunk.

The goddess then using her big sword, cut off his trunk, The demon again took to the form of Mahisasura.

He then agitated three worlds including the mobile and immobile beings. Then, Candika of great honour and exploit became infuriated.

Then after consuming the honey, rolling her eyes, she laughed. The demon king also having been intoxicated with strength and prowess, started thundering.

The demon king then uprooted the mountains and threw them at her, who with the shooting of her arrows reduced them to dust.

Having been intoxicated with the drinks and red face, with unstable sense organs, feeling upset, she spoke with deep voice.

The goddess said, “O fool, devoid of wisdom, why are you getting stubborn uselessly? No demon of the three worlds can ever face me.”

The Rsi said, “Thus speaking, the goddess, who possessed all the rays, jumped over him and pressing him under her foot, then pierced a trident in his throat.

With the pressing of the body of Mahisasura, under the foot of the goddess only half of the demon's body (in human form) could emerge out of the buffalo's neck, because he had been overpowered with the prowess of the goddess.

The immensely degraded demon had only half emerged from the neck of the buffalo, when the goddess cut off his head with the strike of a sword, who fell on the floor.

Crying aloud, his followers, getting afraid of the battle fled away from the scene of the battlefield crying for help.

The gods including Indra and others, eulogised the goddess, the divine damsels danced while Gandharvas sang songs.

O king, in this way the origin of Mahalaksmi has been spoken to you. Now with a cool mind, you listen to the origin of Sarasvati.

## Chapter 47 - Killing of Dhumralocana, Canda, Munda and Raktabija

Rsi said, “There were two illustrious demons known as Sumbha and Nisimbha. Their lustre had been spread among all the mobile and immobile creatures of the three worlds.

The gods troubled by them went to the Himalaya and then offered their salutation to the goddess Bhavani, who happened to be the mother of all the living beings fulfilling their desires.

The gods said, “O Durga, Mahesani, beloved of the kins, victory to you, victory to you. You protect the three worlds. O Parvati, salutation to you.

You are the bestower of the devotion, as well as salvation, O Supreme goddess, salutation to you. O Bhagavati, you are the creator, preserver and the destroyer of the universe, salutation to you.

You have the forms of Kalika, Tara, Chinnamasta and Sri-vidya, salutation to you.

O goddess of universe, I salute you. salutation to you the form of Bhairavi, salutation to Bagalamukhi and Dhumavati.

Salutation to Tripurasundari, salutation to Matangi, salutation to Ajita and Vijaya again and again.

You are Jaya, Mangala, Vilasini, Dogdhri and Ghorakrti, salutation to you.

You are Aparajita, Nityakara and Rudrani, who protects those who take refuge in you.

You can be known by means of Vedanta, the supreme soul and the leader of the innumerable globes, salutation to you again and again.”

The gods thus prayed to Siva, Gauri, the bestower of the boons. The goddess then getting pleased then to the gods, “What for are you eulogising me?”

Then a girl appeared from the body of the goddess Gauri, who in full view of all, spoke to the Sakti of Siva with respect.

“O mother, all the dwellers of the heaven are praying to you because we are being harassed by the demons Sumbha and Nisumbha.

The goddess who emerged out of the inner vestures of the body was known as Kausiki, who was to destroy Sumbha and Nisumbha.

She is also known by the names of Ugra Tara or Mahaugratarika. Since she emerged out of the body of Parvati, therefore she is also called Matangi.

Then she spoke to all the gods, “you live without danger, I shall surely establish your task. Even without base, I am independent.”

Thus speaking, the goddess atonce disappeared. The warriors of the demons Canda and Munda also had on look at the goddess.

Looking at her beautiful face, pleasing to the eyes, they fainted and fell down on the ground.

Reaching the king, they narrated the entire news from the beginning to end. They said, “O king we have seen an astonishingly beautiful damsel.

At the charming peak of the Himalaya mountain, she is mounted over a lion and surrounded by numerous divine girls with folded hands.

Some one was pressing her feet, some one was combing her hair, some one was rubbing her heads, while some one was applying the collyrium in her eyes.

Some one was showing the mirror held in her hand to the goddess. Some one was offering the betel leaf with cloves and cardamom.

Some one was standing holding a spittoon in her hand. Some one was decorating her body with costumes and ornaments.

Her thighs resemble the trunk of the Banana tree. Her nose resembles the beak of the parrot and her arms are like the serpents. Her feet are adorned with jingling nupuras and she wears a beautiful waist band.

The pearl necklaces adorns her breast which is rendered fragrant with deer-musk. The necklaces shine around the neck, she was sporting bedecked in chaplets.

Her forehead is decorated with a crescent moon and she wears gem studded earrings, her plaited hair is fine. Her face is bedecked with three wide eyes.

She is imperishable and wears the garlands. She has bangles on her hands. Her fingers are decorated with gold rings. There are dazzling bracelets decorating her wrists.

She is clad in white costumes and is seated over a lotus. She has applied the saffron tilakam. Her head is decorated with the crescent moon.

She issues the lustre of lightening and is clad in valuable costumes. She has raised breasts and long arms which are decorated with the best of ornaments.

Such a type of beauty could neither be seen among the Daityas or the Danavas. She is the best beauty and is charming in the three worlds.

You are the only one to enjoy love sports with her. By getting you she would feel graceful. She is the gem of the damsels while you are the gem of the men.”

Listening to the words of Canda and Munda the Mahasura summoned a messenger named Sugriva and sent him to her saying.

He said, “O messenger, you go to Himalaya, where there is a beautiful damsel, you bring her here giving my message to her.”

At these words of the demon king, Sugriva, the excellent demon went to Himacala and spoke to Mahesvari- the mother of the world.

The messenger said, “O goddess, there is Sumbhasura and his younger brother Nisumbha. Because of their prowess and strength, they are well known the world over.

I happen to be their messenger and they have deputed me to you. O Mistress of the gods, you listen whatever they have spoken for you.

After conquering Indra and other gods in the war, I have snatched away their gems. The part meant for them in the yajnas has been usurped by me.

I consider you to be the best of the gems among the women. Therefore, you enjoy all the pleasures owing me or my brother.”

Listening to the words of Sumbha, spoken by the messenger Sugriva, then Mahamaya, the beloved of Siva replied.

The goddess said, “O messenger, you are speaking truthfully. There is no falsehood in it. But you listen the vow which I had taken in the earlier times.

Whosoever defeats me in war, shattering my pride, can be his wife alone and of none else.

Then convey my words to Sumbha and Nisumbha and let them do whatever they deem fit.”

On listening to the words spoken by the goddess, the messenger Sugriva returned to his master and communicated the message to him in detail.

Listening to the words of the messenger, Sumbha the harsh ruler getting infuriated said to the army commander Dhumraksa.

“O Dhumraksa, there is a beautiful damsel over the Himalaya mountain. You move quickly and get her here by any means.

O Daitya king, don’t be afraid in getting her here. In case she be desirous of a fight, then you can fight also.”

At these words of Sumbha, the demon Dhumralocana went to Himalaya and spoke to the damsel born of the amsa of Uma, the mistress of the three worlds.

You get along with me to my master, you move to my lord, otherwise you will be killed by me since I have an army of sixty thousand asuras."

The goddess said, “O hero, you have been deputed by the king of the Daityas. In case you kill me, then what can I do for you? But I shall never go without a fight.”

At these words of the goddess, demon Dhumraksa rushed at her, but was burnt alive with the simple humkara of the goddess.

This feat of the goddess, earned her the title of Dhumavati in the world. When so adored by her devotees, she destroys the roots of enemies of her devotees.

After the end of Dhumraksa, his army was devoured by the infuriated lion of the goddess. Those who escaped death, they fled away.

When the Daitya king came to know about the end of Dhumraksa at the hands of the goddess, the valorous Sumbha was enraged biting his lips.

Thereafter he sent Canda, Munda Raktabija and other Daityas one after the other, who went to the place where Ambika was lodged.

The goddess with *anima* and other Siddhis, was riding a lion and was spreading her lustre in all the directions. Looking at her the demon kings said.

“O goddess, you atonce move to the abode of Sumbha and Nisumbha, failing which we shall kill your army as well as the vehicle.

You accept him as your husband, since he is adored even by the Lokapalas. By doing so you would enjoy all the divine pleasures.”

Thus listening to their words, Paramesvari the mother of the universe, smilingly spoke the simple, true and sweet words.

The goddess said, “Lord Sadasiva is parallel and the supreme Brahmana. The secrets about him are unknown to the Vedas. Then what to speak of Visnu and other gods.

I happen to be his subtle Prakrti, then how could I accept the second husband. Can the lustful lioness ever accept a jackal as her husband?

Or can a cow elephant accept a donkey, can a leopardess take a hare? O Daitya, you have been bound with the serpent of death as a movel of destiny. Therefore you are telling a lie.

In case you possess the strength, then fight otherwise proceed on to *Patala.”* Thus listening to the enraged words of the goddess they spoke among themselves.

We are not killing you because you are a woman. O goddess with a vehicle as a lion, in case you are desirous of a war, then come face to face.”

At these words of the demons, there was an increase in the conflict and the arrows were shot in the battlefield from both the sides.

Thus the goddess Paramesvari, fought a battle with the Daityas quite playfully and killed Canda, Munda as well as great demon Raktabija.

Inspite of their being inimical to the gods, they proceeded to the loka of the goddess Bhagavati, where her devotees are lodged.

## Chapter 48 - Manifestation of Sarasvati

The king said, “O lord, all the Daityas like Dhumraksa, Canda, Munda and Raktabija were killed and on hearing this what did Sumbha the demon, who had been troublesome to the gods, do?

O Brahmana, what transpired thereafter. Now you speak out the story of the manifestation of the goddess Bhagavati which is the remover of the Sins.”

The Rsi said, “O king, the powerful Daitya, on learning about the killing of the demon chiefs, commanded the infuriated and intoxicated warriors.

He said, “At my command, with the desire of being victorious, all the asuras, born in the race of Kaleya, together with the demons of Maurya and Daurhrda races should march on for fighting the war.

Both Sumbha and Nisumbha mounted over the chariots, issuing command to the demon warriors marched on. Both the army commanders ‘ were so followed by their warriors, as the swarm of moths emerges from the earth to face destruction.

At that point of time the war bands including the mrdangas (cymbals), mardalas, bherikas, dimdimas, jhajharas and anakas were sounded. The war managers rejoiced in the battle ground. The cowards fled away from the battlefield for their lives.

Clad in the marshal uniform the warriors came in quite enthusiastic style in the battlefield. They held various types of weapons and missiles and marched on teasing one another with an eagerness for victory.

The warriors mounted over the elephants, looked unmindful of the grave situation in the battle, where they rejoiced with their lord- the asura-king.

Even the gods were agitated listening to the sound of the shooting of the guns. The sky was covered with darkness and as such the sun became invisible.

Crores of the foot soldiers, charioteers, soldiers on the horsebacks, elephant riders and others, desirous of victory delightfully marched on.

The huge mountain like black elephants, started trumpeting in the battlefield and even the camels looking like the hills, produced hoarse sound from their throats.

The horses of excellent costumes with their head, decorated with garlands, who could move with great speed, started neighing. They moved in the sky galloping over the elephants, like the sun.

Observing the strength of the enemy Ambika strung the bow and sounded the bell which troubled the enemy. The lion also started roaring raising its manes.

Then Nisumbha, finding the goddess bedecked in fine ornaments, holding weapons and staying over the Himalaya, spoke words which were dubbed in sentiments like a man who is clever enough to understand the feelings for beautiful damsel.

Then he spoke with sweet voice, “Even a petal of the jasmine flower fallen on the beautiful damsels like you causes pain. Therefore O Mahesi, why are you waging a terrific war with your beautiful body?

Thus speaking the great asura kept quiet. Then Candika said to him, “O foolish Daitya, what are you talking uselessly. Either you start the war or go to the Patalaloka.

Then the great warrior, getting enraged, started shooting astonishing type of arrows as the clouds drop incessant rain during the rainy season.

The infuriated valorous demon, along with his arrogant warriors, fought with several sharp weapons like spears, axes, iron clubs, parighas, bows, bhindipalas, javelins, crescent arrows, and the long swords.

The huge elephants looked like the black mountains, with foreheads pierced and ran here and there. The flags of Sumbha and Nisumbha, were like the flying cranes, fluttered here and there.

Kalika cut off the Daityas like the fish. The necks of the huge horses were severed. They were thus killed and the rest of the Daityas were devoured by the lion.

With the killing of Daityas, elephants and horses, streams of blood started flowing. Their tresses of hair resembled the moss and their upper garments looked like the foam.

The cavalry men fought with their equals, the dephandridus with the elephant riders, the charioteers with charioteers and the foot soldiers with a foot soldiers.

Then it come to the mind of Nisumbha, that the terrific and the cool time had arrived in which a pauper becomes rich and a rich becomes a pauper,

The foolish becomes wise while the wise becomes foolish, a killer is praised by several self respected people. The great and valorous people get defeated and the weak become victorious in the battle ground.

A man becomes victorious or defeated at the will of the lord without much effort. None of Brahma, Visnu or Siva can remain alone by the transgression of the time.

The excellent warriors do not think it proper to flee from the battlefield. How could I be victorious over her because she has already destroyed my entire army.

She has surely arrived for destroying the demons and to help the gods. She is indeed the figure of the Puranas and eternal Prakrti of Siva. She is not a damsel of the world.

It is a disgrace to meet with ones end at the hands of a woman. This has been observed by the people well-versed in the warfare. But still how could I face the demon king without fighting her.

Thus thinking, the great charioteer, mounted over his huge chariot. Having been driven by his charioteer, he soon reached the battlefield, where the goddess Parvati was there being served by the other goddesses.

Then the Daitya spoke to the goddess, “O Mahesi, what is the use of killing of these mercenary soldiers. In case you are desirous of waging the war, then remove the Kavaca and then let us fight together.

Then Kausika said to Kali, “Look at the stubbornness of both of them. On the arrival of the misfortune, the destiny bestowing the evil wisdom, makes one move in the opposite direction.”

Then Nisumbha shot a thousand arrows at Candika and Kali. Parvati on the other hand reduced the arrows of the demon in thousand of pieces with his arrows.

Nisumbha then attacked the lion over his head with his shining sword, which was cut into two pieces by Ambika, like the log of wood.

With the breaking of the sword, he shot an arrow over the breast of Ambika, which was also made infructuous by her. Then he shot a trident with his hand at her heart which was destroyed by her with her feet.

Then the great warrior rushed towards the goddess holding a club in his hand, which was also reduced to pieces with the shooting of a spear by her. The demon cut off the spear of the goddess with another sword.

Ambika then shot the serpent like arrows dipped in poison, as a result of which he fell down on the ground dead.

Sumbha, the arrogant demon king, then getting irritated, mounted his chariot and having eight hands, approached the goddess Siva.

At that point of time, the goddess, blew a conch for the subjugation of the demon army. Then she produced the sound from the stringing the cord of the bow. The lion also roared at that time raising the manes of his neck. These sounds were echoed in the sky.

The goddess then resorted to a loud laugh frightening all the demons. The goddess then asked him, “Be attentive in the battle ground.” The gods then shouted the slogans of victory.

Then the demon king, shot a Sakti with burning flames which was cut off by the goddess. The Daitya also cut off the arrows shot by the goddess.

Candika then attacked him with a trident as a result of which he fell down fainted in the same way as a mountain falls into the ocean having been struck with vajra, shaking it at the same time.

The immensely valorous demon, facing boldly the attack of the trident, creating ten thousand arms, shot various cakras the killers of the gods and tried to kill Mahesvari mounted over a lion.

The goddess destroyed the cakras quite playfully picked up a terrific trident and shot it at the demon king, which killed him. Meeting their end at the auspicious lands of the goddess Siva, both the brothers then achieved salvation.

At the killing of the immensely valorous Sumbha and Nisumbha, the rest of the Daityas retired to Patala.

The Daityas who escaped death were devoured by Kali as well as the lion. The rest disappeared in all the ten directions, getting terrified.

The rivers started flowing with spotless clean water thereafter. The pleasant breeze started blowing. The directions became spotless.

The gods and the Brahmarsis again started performing of the tapas. Mahendra and other gods again became comfortable.

O lord, the story of Uma is extremely auspicious and bestows merits whosoever goes through this story with faith and devotion, he, after enjoying the unique pleasures in this world, by the grace of Mahamaya, achieves the proximity of Uma, after his death.

The Rsi said, “This is how the goddess who destroyed Sumbhasura, was born. She was born out of the amsa of Parvati and is called Sarasvati.

## Chapter 49 - Manifestation of Uma

The sages said, “O Suta, well-versed in all the scriptures, the goddess Parvati happens be the mistress of all the three lokas, from whom Sarasvati emerged.

She is conceived as the supreme Brahmana, the Mula Prakrti (natural form), Isvari, formless with form, eternal, blissful besides Sati.”

Suta said, “O ascetics, this is the best and the great story which you listen from me lovingly, with the mere knowledge of which a person achieves the supreme position.

Once there had been a war, between the demons and the gods and the gods became victorious because of the prowess of the great Mahamaya.

Then the gods arrogated the victory to themselves and started praising themselves as well.” We are blessed what harm can the demons do to us?

Witnessing our impressive prowess, the demons are afraid and have fled away to Patala shouting to flee.

It is really wonderful that the prowess of the gods has been responsible for the destruction of the demon race. Graceful are the gods.” These were the words spoken by all the gods.

Thereafter unprecedented the mass of lustre appeared them finding which all the gods felt surprised.

The lustre which was extremely black, and destroyer of the pride, was unknown to the gods, and with the choked voice they uttered, “what is this? what is this?”

Then the lord of the gods said to them, “you go over and carefully find out what it is?

At the instance of Indra, the wind god went to the lustre, and it asked him, “who are you?” When so asked the lustre the wind god said, arrogantly, “I am the wind and the life of the universe.” This is how the wind god replied.

The mobile or immobile things in the world are woven like warp and woof into me. I am the support of everything and move the entire universe.

Then the great lustre said, “In case you have strength enough to move the world, then you better move this blade of grass.”

Then the wind god, used all his force but the straw could not be moved even slightly. This made him feel ashamed and he returned to the place of Indra, quite silently and communicated to him his defeat.

He further said, “We infact think ourselves to be great falsely, where as we are unable to do even the smallest of the job.

There after the wind god sent all the gods to the lustre, one by one but none of then could know the truth about the lustre. Indra then himself went there.

Finding that Indra was himself approaching, the lustre suddenly disappeared from the place and the incident surprised Indra. In the meantime, Parvati- an image of compassion appeared there in order to grace them as well as to shatter their pride.

On the ninth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Caitra, at noon time, the blissful Uma appeared there.

She was lodged inside the lustre. She was resplendent spreading her lustre on all the sides. She clearly indicated to the gods that she was Brahma herself.

In her four hands, she held the noose, ankusa, abhayamudra (A gesture indicating free from fear) and was being served by the Vedas. She was youthful and extremely charming.

She was clad in red garments, wearing a red garland, and the red sandal paste had been applied over her body. Her form resembled crores of Kamadeva, and had the lustre of crores of moons.

She could read the minds of all. She was the witness of all the deeds, being the form of supreme Brahmana. Then the Mahamaya said.

Uma spoke, “None of the gods like Brahma, Visnu and Siva, can boast before me, what to speak of the other gods.

I am the supreme Brahman, the great lustre in the form of two Pranavas. I am all. There is none other besides me.

Though I am devoted of any form, I also posses other forms. I constitute all the principles. I am eternal and my attributes are beyond dispute. I represent both the cause and the effect.

Sometimes, I appear as a damsel and sometimes as a man, while at times both of them. I can assume all the forms.

I am the creator, the protector as well as the destroyer of the universe besides being the enchantress of the same.

All the Saktis like Kali, Laksmi and Sarasvati besides others emerge out of my body. All the arts also originate from me.

The demons could be conquered due to my strength. Without knowing my true nature you arrogate to yourselves as the lords of all.

As a magician makes a wooden puppet to dance, similarly, I also make the people to do so.

The wind blows getting afraid of me and the guardian of the quarters perform their duties for the same reasons.

Since I am independent, I bestow victory to all the gods at times and at times to the Daityas.

The Vedas describe my form which is beyond destruction and is the great abode, the one beyond illusion and happens to be greater than the greatest.

Nirguna and Saguna are my two forms one is mixed with Maya and the other is devoid of the same.

O gods, with your minds filled with devotion, you should adore me shedding away your arrogance since I happen to be the eternal Prakrti.

When the gods heard the compassionate words of the goddess, they worshipped her lowering their shoulders in devotion.

They said, O universal goddess, forgive us and be pleased with us. O mother, let us not become arrogant again. Kindly be compassionate.

From that time onwards, the gods started worshipping the goddess as they did earlier. Their arrogance disappeared and they were turned pure at heart.

O Brahmana, I have this narrated to you the details about the manifestations of Uma. By simply hearing this story, the people achieve the supreme region.

## Chapter 50 - The origin of Mahavidyas

The sage said, “O Intelligent one, all of us would like to listen to the story of Durga, daily. Now you please describe the other wonderful tattva of the same.

Suta you are the best interpreter of all the scriptures, and after listening to the several nectar like stories from your lotus like face, our minds do not feel satisfied.

Suta said, “The powerful Ruru had a well known son called Durgama, who attained the knowledge of all the Vedas because of a boon from Brahma.

He also got a boon from the lord of creation, for remaining invincible from the gods. Thereafter he created several disturbances on earth, shaking even the gods in the heaven.

With the destruction of the Vedas all the religious activities came to a standstill. The gods as well as the Brahmana fell from the noble path becoming wicked.

There were no charities nor did anyone perform hard tapas, what to speak of the yajnas or the homas. As a result of this, there were no rains on earth for a hundred years.

There was a huge hue and cry in the three worlds and all the people were extremely suffered with hunger and thirst.

All the tanks, wells, step-wells, rivers and oceans dried up including the trees, plants and the creepers.

All the gods then finding the people so disturbed went to Yogamaya Mahesvari, and took refuge with her.”

The gods said, “O Mahamaya, you save the entire people. You better subside your anger, otherwise all the people will vanish.

As you have already killed the demons like powerful Sumbha, Nisumbha, Dhumraksa, Canda, Munda and Raktabija, besides Madhu Kaitabha and Mahisasura, similarly, O ocean of mercy, you also kill the demon Durgama.

The children commit mistakes at every step, who else in the world forgives except the mother.

Whenever the gods and the Brahmanas face misfortune, you incarnate on earth remove the sufferings of the people, making them comfortable.”

Listening to the pathetic words of the gods, the compassionate goddess Bhagavati, revealed to them her form possessing innumerable eyes.

She held in her four hands attributes like bow and arrow, lotus and several fruits, she had a smiling face.

Finding the people suffering, then Parvati, with compassionate look, kept on weeping for nine days and nine nights.

Streams of tears started flowing from her eyes, which like the water, which delighted the worlds, plants and the medicinal herbs.

To the learned people the fruits and roots were made available the tender grass for cows and other animals, while arrangements were made for feeding other creatures as well.

All the gods, Brahmanas and humans felt pleased. Then the goddess said, “What else should I do for you?”

The gods said collectively, “You have pleased the humans, now you get us back the Vedas from Durgama.”

She replied, “All right.” Thus speaking she said, “All of you should get back to your homes. I shall soon get you back the Vedas.

Then all the gods, offering their salutation to the lotus eyed great goddess, having the lotus like eyes, returned to their respective abodes.

Thereafter there was a disturbance in the heaven as well as on the earth and in space, hearing which Raurava, surrounded his city from all the sides.

Then Siva for the protection of the gods, made a huge circle of splendour but she herself came out of it.

A great battle was then fought between the demons and the goddess. Both of them showered arrows at each other which pierced the armour of each other.

In the meantime, ten beauty forms emerged out of the body of the goddess which were known as Kali, Tara, Chinnamasta, Srividya, Bhuvanesvari Bhairavi, Bagala, Dhumra, Srimat-Tripurasundari, Matangi and Mahavidya holding the weapons in their hands. Thereafter emerged innumerable mothers of divine forms adorned with the crescent moon, and having the lustre resembling the lightning.

Then started a terrible combat between the demons and the mothers. A hundred aksaunis of the army of the son of Ruru was killed in the battle.

Durgama was then struck by the goddess with the edge of her trident, as a result of which he fell down on earth like an uprooted tree.

Thus after killing the demon, the goddess rescued the four Vedas, and returned them to the gods.

The gods said, “O Ambika, you took to the form of a goddess with innumerable eyes, therefore you will be remembered by the gods with the name of Sataksi.

You fed the universe with grow of the vegetation from your body, therefore you would be known by the name of Sakambhari.

O Siva, because of you killing the demon Durgama, the people will remember you by the name of Durga or Bhadra.

O Yoganidra, Mahabala, Jnanaprada, Jaganmata, salutation to you again and again.

O Paramesvari you are known by the name of Tattvanasi, you represent the innumerable crores of Brahmandas, salutation to you again and again.

O mother, we are ignorant about your power and the greatness, therefore we cannot eulogies you appropriately, because you are inaccessible through words, mind or body, having the eyes of the sun and the moon.

Looking at the gods like us, who else could be thus compassionate on us except goddess Sataksi the mother.

You destroy our enemies in such a way, that they are unable to defeat the three worlds in future.

The goddess said, “As the upset cows run after their calves, similarly finding you in difficulty, I becoming upset, and rush for your help.

Since I consider you as my children, when I do not find you, then even a moment is spent like a yuga by me.

All of you are my devotees, therefore, when I am there to remove your sufferings, you should not worry the least when I am there.

As I killed the Daityas earlier, I shall do so again. There is no doubt about it. I speak the truth.

When the other demons like Kumbha and Nisumbha are born, then I shall be born out of the womb of the illustrious Yasoda in Gokula. I shall then kill these demons. Then I shall be known as the one born of Nanda.

Taking the form of a bee, I shall kill a Daitya named Aruna, earning the name of Bhramari in the world.

When I, taking to an awful form shall kill the demons, then I shall be known by the name of the goddess Bhima.

Whenever the humans will be tortured by the Danavas, on earth, on every such time, I shall incarnate myself on earth and ensure their welfare.

The goddess who has been known as Sataksi, the same goddess is also known as Sakambhari as well as Durga.

There is no god more compassionate then Sataksi on earth who made the dry and suffering earth quite comfortable. We offer salutation to the same Mahesvari.

## Chapter 51 - Consecration of the image of the goddess

The sage said, “O disciple of Vyasa, O Suta, the best in Puranic lores, we are interested in further listening to the stories of Siva.

You kindly recite about the kriyayoga of Jagadamba, as was propounded by the sage Sanatkumara to Vyasa.

Suta said, “You are firmly devoted to the adoration of the goddess quite firmly and as such you are quite graceful. Therefore, you listen tot he secrets of the supreme Sakti with respect.”

Vyasa said, “O Omniscient, Immensely intelligent, Sanatkumara, the son of Brahma, I would like to listen to the wonderful kriyayoga of the goddess Uma.

What are its symptoms, how is the reward yielded? Whatever is dear to the supreme goddess, you kindly reveal the same to me completely.

Sanatkumara said, “O Vyasa, the secret which you desire me to be revealed to you, I am going to reveal the same to you. O immensely wise one, you listen to the same.

There are three paths, called- Jhanayoga, Kriyayoga and Bhaktiyoga which bestow the devotion and salvation by the mother.

Jnanayoga is the union of mind with the Atman. And when the mind is united with the outer arthas it is called the Kriyayoga.

The combination of the goddess with soul is called the Bhaktiyoga. The combination of the three is called Kriyayoga.

The karmas generate the devotion. Jnana is achieved by devotion and one achieves the liberation from Jnana. This has been resolved by the scriptures.

O excellent sage, yoga is the main cause of the salvation. Kriyayoga is the main means of liberation.

One shall know the Maya as Prakrti and the wielder of Maya as the eternal. After realising the identity of the two one is freed from the worldly bondages.

O Vyasa, a person who builds a temple of the goddess in stone, wood or mud, you listen to the merit he earns for the same. Great merit is achieved by adoring the goddess daily.

The same merit is achieved with the construction of a temple dedicated to the goddess. With the building of a temple dedicated to the goddess, he redeems thousand past as well as the future races.

Whatever sins are committed by him in the crores of his past births, they disappear the laying of the foundation of the while laying the foundation of the temple of the mother.

Ganga is the best of rivers, Sona is the best of great rivers, Earth is the best in forgiveness, the ocean in depth, or as the sun is best in all the planets, similarly the supreme mother is the foremost of all the deities.

The person who builds her temple, is considered to be the best and he earns grace in each one of his births.

A person who builds a temple of the goddess at Varanasi, Kuruksetra, Prayaga, Puskara, bank of Ganga, seashore, Naimasaranya, Amarakantaka, Sriparvata, Gokarna, Jnanaparvata, Mathura, Ayodhya or Dvaraka or any other place of sanctity, he is freed from all the worldly bondages.

The person who builds a temple remains in the Manidvipa for as many thousands of years, till the brick foundation of the temple lasts.

The one who makes the sculpture of the goddess, with all the prescribed characteristics, fearlessly he achieves the great place of Uma.

After the image of the goddess is installed when the auspicious stars are favourable, besides the planets and the season, they getting please with the devotee Yogamaya bestows her grace on him.

After the image of the goddess is installed, the devotee redeems the people of both the families of past and the future.

O great sage, foremost of all, the merit earned by a person after the installation of the image of the goddess, is crores of times more beneficial than the one the derived by setting up of the three worlds.

A person who installs the images of Pancatayana (Sun, Ganesa, Durga, Rudra and Visnu) with Ambika in the centre and other four in the four quarters, his merit cannot be calculated

One earns merits by reciting the name of Visnu during lunar or solar eclipse, a crores of times, (the merit of installation of the image of the goddess in Pancatayana) its merit would be a hundred crores of times greater than the same.

The merit one earns with the muttering of the name of Siva, a crore of times but bigger would be the merit, for reciting the name of Sridevi.

The one who consecrates the image of the Trigunatmika mother of the universe, by the grace of the adorable mother nothing becomes beyond his reach. His all the sins are washed out and his sons and grand sons always flourish.

Those who think of consecrating the excellent image of Uma, such type of saints achieve the unique place in the Paraloka.

When a person observing the temples under construction thinks that he would also build a temple himself when he gains money,” with this type of thinking, his race surely goes to the heaven. There is nothing beyond the reach of a person by the grace of Mahamaya.

Such of the people who take refuge under the supreme mother, the cause of creation of all, they should not be treated as humans, because they happen to be the ganas of the goddess.

Those who recite the name of Uma, while walking, sleeping, standing during the day or night, they are transformed as the ganas of Uma.

Such of the people who adore the goddess Siva offering flowers, incense, or lamps as a daily routine or on a specific occasions due to some reason, ultimately attain the abode of Uma.

Those who clean scrub, or smear the place of the goddess with cowdung, they attain the place of Uma.

The mother goddess, bestows her blessings over the family of a person, who builds a beautiful temple for her.

The glorious one through out the day and night repeats, “Let me devotees live for a hundred years and should not face miseries.”

The one who makes an excellent and unique image of the goddess, the people of his race stay with respect in the Manidvipa for ten thousand years.

After consecrating the image of Mahamaya and adoring the same appropriately, whatever is desired by the devotee, his desires are fulfilled.

A person who consecrating the image of the adorable mother, the bathes it with ghee and honey, who can describe the merit earned by him (with the process)?

The goddess Paramesvari should be bathed with fragrant sandal, aguru, marusi, musta etc. or the milk of the single coloured cow and the scented water.

He should make incense with excellent offering comprising of eighteen fragrant materials, and pour it in the fire flames. Then the arati of the goddess should be performed with the waving of the lights using camphor or the wicks soaked in ghee.

On the fifth, eighth, ninth and tenth day of the dark fortnight, and on new moon days, the devotee should worship the mother of the universe with fragrant flowers.

Then the Janakisukta, Srisukta or Devisukta should be recited or alternatively mula-mantras should be muttered.

All flowers, except Visnukranta, and Tulasi, delight the goddess. The lotus flower is very much liked by her.

Whosoever offers to the goddess the golden flowers or silver flowers, he achieves the supreme place with the crores of Siddhas.

At the end of the puja, a devotee should beg forgiveness saying, “O mother goddess the bestower of the happiness and bliss, be pleased.

The person should perform japam of mantras adoring the goddess with these words, getting absorbed in the devotion of the goddess, and meditate upon the four armed goddess mounted over a lion and displaying Varada and abhaya mudras.

Thus the goddess who bestows the desired boons to her devotees, should be offered various types of ripe fruits for the purpose naivedya.

A person who consumes the naivedya of the goddess, he washing out all the dirt, becomes spotless.

A person who observes a fast on the bright third day of the month of Caitra, he getting free from the worldly bondages, achieves the supreme place.

A person with wisdom should celebrate the Dolotsava (the festival of the swing) on the third days of the bright fortnight of the month of Caitra. On that particular day placing the mother of the universe with Siva in a swing, one should adore them.

One should worship them offering the vermilions, flowers, garments, camphor, aguru, sandal paste, incense, lights, naivedyas, garlands, scents and other articles.

He should then serve the goddess Amba the bestower of all welfare along with Siva.

Siva bestows all the desires on a person who performs his puja observing all the rites and the festival of swings of the goddess yearly.

The Aksaya Trtiya in the bright fortnight of the month of Vaisakha, should be observed as a fast and one who does so carefully, and also adores Siva and Gauri, with the offering of the flowers like mallika, jasmine, campaka, japa, banduka and lotus, his sins accumulated during the crores of births, mentally, physically or verbally, will be vanished. His life shall become purposeful and he will enjoy all the four arms of life i.e. dharma, artha, kama and moksa.

One should observe fast on the bright third day of the month of Jyestha and worship the goddess Mahesvari and whosoever does so, nothing would be beyond the reach for him.

On the bright third day of the month of Asadha one should celebrate the Rathoksana which is quite dear to the goddess, according to his means.

In the said celebration, the earth should be made as the chariot, the sun and the moon should serve as wheels, the Vedas should be the horses, while Brahma should serve as a charioteer.

The chariot made with such an imagination, should be decorated with the garland and the flower garlands. The goddess Siva should be lodged therein, thereafter.

An intelligent person should think in his mind, that the supreme mother goddess was lodged in the chariot for the observing as well as the protection of the people.

With the moving of the chariot quite slowly, the slogans of victory should be shouted and also say, “O goddess, you bestow your grace on the down trodden and destitutes, we are your devotees, therefore, you save us.”

With such types of words and with the playing of several types of musical instruments, the goddess should be pleased. The chariot should be driven to the boundaries where she should be worshipped.

After eulogising the goddess with several types of stotras the goddess should be brought back to her abode. After offering hundreds of salutations, one should pray to Ambika.

In this way if a person performing the Rathotsva-vrata adores the goddess, he enjoying all the pleasures in the world and ultimately achieves the place of the goddess.

Similarly one who performs the vrata on the bright third days of the months of Sravana and Bhadrapada, he always remains delightful with sons and grandsons, having enough of riches. He ultimately achieves the abode of Uma, which is lodged above all the lokas.

During the bright fortnight of the month of Asvin, one should perform the navaratra- vrata and by doing so all the desires are undoubtedly fulfilled.

No one even Brahma, Siva, Kartikeya or any other god is competent enough to describe the glory of the said vrata.

O sages, performing this Vrata, Suratha, the son of Viratha, had been restored his lost kingdom.

With the performing of the same Vrata, the intelligent king Sudarsana, the son of the wise king Dhruvasandhi, regained his lost kingdom.

With the performing of the same excellent Vrata and after adoring Mahesvari, the merchant named Samadhi, was freed from the bondage.

A person who performs all the rites appropriately in the bright half of the month of Asvin, on the third, fifth, seventh, eighth, ninth or the fourteenth day, Siva, fulfils all his mental desires.

The one who performs the auspicious rites on the third day in the bright half of the month of Kartika, Margasirsa, Pausa, Magha and Phalguna, and worships the great goddess, with red flowers, Karavira and others, offering her the incense, scents etc. all his auspicious desires are fulfilled.

This great Vrata should be performed by the woman for achieving of the blissful conjugal pleasures, while the men should perform the same for the gaining of the learning, wealth and sons.

The persons desirous of salvation should perform the Vrata prescribed for Siva and Parvati or those which are liked by the goddess.

Uma Samhita, bestows merits, enhances one's devotion in Siva, and comprises of the several events and short stories. It is blissful and bestows the devotion and salvation.

Whosoever listens to it with devotion or recites the same, reads it or makes others to read the same, he achieves the supreme position.

A person who keeps in his house the beautifully written Samhita, and if the same is adored with devotion, all his desires are fulfilled.

He can never be troubled by the goblins, pretas, pisacas and other wicked creatures. He surely attains sons, grandsons as well as the enormous riches.

The persons desirous of the devotion of Siva, should always listen to this auspicious Samhita.

Thus ends the fifth Uma Samhita of Siva Mahapurana.

Siva-Mahapuranam

## Kailasa Samhita

## Chapter 1 - Conversation among Vyasa and other sages over the importance of Omkara

Salutation to Siva, who is the cause of creation, preservation and destruction, besides (Ganesa) the son of Parvati.

Rsi said, “We have listened from you the excellent Uma Samhita, besides the other stories. Now I narrate the Kailasa Samhita, which increases knowledge of the Siva tattva. You better listen from me with devotion.

In earlier times, the illustrious sages were performing penance over Himalaya. Then they thought of going to Varanasi.

Starting from that mountain, they arrived at Kasi and reached the Manikarnika-ghata for the purpose of taking a bath.

Taking a bath there, they performed oblations for the gods as well as the manes. Then taking a bath in the Ganga again, they offered their salutation to the master of the sages and the adored the sages well-versed in the Vedas with devotion and eulogised the lord reciting the Satarudriya mantras.

They felt that they had became graceful with blessings of Siva. All of them were the devotees of Siva.

Then they met Suta, who had arrived there to visit Pancakrosi. Getting delighted, they offered their salutation to him.

Then Suta as well, accompanied with the sages, offering his salutation to lord Visesvara, reached the Mukti mandapa accompanied with the sages.

When Suta who was well-versed in the Puranas, and was seated there, the sages welcomed him offering the ardhya-padhya etc.

Meeting the great ascetics, Suta feeling delighted, enquired of their welfare, and also apprised them of his own welfare.

The sages finding Suta in a delightful mood, enquired of him the interpretation of omkara.

The sages said, “O great sage, disciple of Vyasa and well-versed in the Puranas, O Suta, you are indeed blessed. You happen to be the ocean of knowledge besides being the devotee of Siva.

Then Vyasa, the preceptor of the universe, had consecrated you as Purana-guru.

Therefore the knowledge of the Puranas is enshrined in your heart. You explain with case the interpretation of the Vedas as well as the Puranas.

All the Vedas emerged from omkara while omkara is another form of Siva. Therefore Mahesvara is lodged in your heart firmly.

We shall be free from ailments, after drinking the nectar of pranaya which is quite sweet and pleasing like the honey, emerging out of your lotus like face.

O intelligent one, except you none else can claim to be a preceptor, therefore nar te the nature of Siva out of compassion.”

On hearing their words, the intelligent Suta, the dear disciple of Vyasa, offered his salutation to Ganesa, Kartikeya, Siva and Parvati.

He also offered his salutation to Nandi, the son of Silada, Pariksita the husband of Suyasa, Sanatkumara and Vyasa, the great sage.

Suta said, “O virtuous and sinless sages, blessed are you, to possess such a firm wisdom, which can never be possessed by the sinful people.

The discourse that was delivered by the sage Vyasa, my preceptor to the sages of the Naimisaranya, the same words. O sages are going to be repeated by me to you.

With the listening of the same the devotion for Siva is inculcated. Therefore you listen to it with delight and care.

In the earlier times in the Svarocis-Manvantara a great sage named Drdhavrata had been performing tapas in the Naimisaranya region, along with other sages.

They conducted a sacrifice which lasted for a long time, adoring Rudra- the lord of the yajna. They intended to know the supreme nature of the lord and waited for the sage Vyasa. All of them were devoted to Siva and wore Rudraksa besides smearing the ashes over their bodies.

Observing their devotion, the sage Vyasa, who had been the reward of the tapas of the sage Parasara, appeared there.

At the sight of the sage Vyasa, the faces and the eyes of all those present there, were delighted. Welcoming the sage Vyasa, they adored him as well.

Honouring him they gave him a golden seat studded with gems. Getting comfortably seated over the throne, the sage Vyasa, spoke in deep voice.

Vyasa said, “Are all of you perfectly well in this great yajna. Why have you adored the lord of yajna appropriately? What for have you adored lord Siva as well as Parvati, who frees a person from the worldly bondages.

You by nature serve others. The worship that has been done for Siva seems to be with a desire to hear more about the great nature of the lord, which is the cause of salvation.”

When thus desired by the immensely brilliant sage Vyasa of the Naimisa forest, they first bowed to the lord, the noble soul, whose mind was delighted with his devotion to Siva.

The sages said, “O lord, O excellent sage, born of the amsa of Narayana, the abode of mercy, the immensely wise one, you are the master of all the lores.

You are the ocean of the grace of the lord Siva of the entire universe besides his Mayasakti.

A the sight of the dust of your lotus like feet, we feel delighted as a bee delights by getting the dust of lotus flowers.

The sight of your lotus like feet are beyond the reach of the wicked people. Since we could have a sight of them today, therefore we feel quite blessed.

O immensely learned one, in the Naimisaranya region the omkara's interpretation has to be highlighted and for purpose, a long term yajna is being organised.

Taking into account the supreme positron of Siva, we have decided that the glory of the lord should be heard.

O lord, we are unaware of the glory of Siva. Therefore you kindly remove the doubts of the ignorant people like us.

There is none else in the three worlds, who could remove the doubts. Because of this you are drowned in the immensely deep ocean of knowledge.

O ocean of mercy, you kindly make us sail the boat of the name of Siva (beyond the ocean of the universe). We are eager to know about the tattva of the devotion of Siva.”

Thus when so prayed by the ages well-versed in the Vedas, then the sage Vyasa, the father of Sukadeva, meditated within the pericarp of his heart on lord Siva who releases from the worldly bondages, and who happens to be Pranava, the essential substance of Vedanta, spoke, feeling delighted in his heart.

## Chapter 2 - Siva enlightens Parvati over the secret subjects

Vyasa said, “O Brahmanas, you are the lord since you have put me a good question.
