Lord Siva, the holder of the trident, when gets pleased with a person, he is enlightened about the meaning of Pranava.

Besides the persons who are deprived of the devotion of Siva, this particular knowledge cannot be achieved by them. This has been ordained by the Vedas.

You have adored Siva with the performing of the long time yajna, which has definitely been observed by me.

Therefore, O believers, I am going to repeat before you a dialogue between Uma and Mahesvara.

In ancient times, Sati the daughter of Daksa, in the context of the denouncement of Siva, ended her life in the yajna of Daksa.

With the influence of the said performance, she became the daughter of Himalaya in the next birth. At the advice of Narada, she performed tapas for Siva to achieve him as her husband.

Then Himalaya according to the costume of svayamvara married Parvati to Siva as a result of which she felt comfortable.

Once Mahadeva, while seated over the mountain Himalaya, with her husband Siva, put him a question.

Mahadevi said, “O lord, O supreme Isan, performer of the five krtyas, omniscient one, easily available with devotion, having the supreme nectai like form.

I listening to your denouncement I discarded the body of Sati and presently, I happen to be the daughter of Himalaya.

O Mahesan, O Mahesvara, you bestowing mantra-diksa on me, enlighten me over the spotless tattva.”

At this request of the goddess, Mahadeva, having the moon as ornament, feeling delighted at heart, spoke to the goddess.

Mahadeva said, “O goddess you are graceful because of developing this type of wisdom. Reaching over the peak of the mountain Kailasa, I shall establish you in the snotless tattva.”

Thereafter moving from the Himalaya the Kailasa mountain, bestowing diksa on Parvati she was made to recite the essential mantras.

Bestowing the mantra-diksa on the goddess, establishing her in the auspicious soul, Mahadeva together with the Mahadevi, went to the divine orchard.

Siva bedecked the goddess with the full- blown kalpataru tree flowers with the help of dearest friends of the goddess headed by Sumalini and made her sit in his lap feeling delightful having a look at her face. Then ensued the delightful discourse conformable to the Vedas between Parvati and Siva which was meant for the welfare of the world.

O ascetic, thereafter between Siva and Parvati, there started the narration of the auspicious stories.

Then the Sridevi said, “O lord, you advise me over the omkara mantra and others. But before that I would like to know the correct interpretation of omkara.

What was the origin of Pranava and why is it so called? What is the number of its matras or digits? Why is it called the intial mantra of the Vedas?

How many gods are there with it? What is the concept of the Vedas in relation to it? What types of rites are prescribed? What is their cause and what is the result?

How are the five Brahmanas lodged in this mantra in the regular order? How many kalas are mention? How could it be the soul of the universe?

O Siva, what is the link between the syllabus and their meanings? What are the means of understanding them? Who is authorized in this? What is the theme of the same?

What is the link between the knower and the known and what is the purpose? What shall be the nature of the practicing devotee? At which place the meditation should be done?

What is the form of the object to be adored? How is the devotee benefited with the same? What the method of performing the anusthana, O lord, which on should be the place of worship.

O Hara, what is the method the mandala of worship, the Rsi, the god, metre, nyasa and the method of adoration.

O Mahesan, in case you are kind to me, then I would especially like to listen to the same. You kindly speak out.”

In the way the goddess enquired of the lord Candrasekhara, who started speaking praising Parvati.

## Chapter 3 - Description of the form of Omkara and Virajahoma

Isvara said, “I am going to reply to you whatever has been asked by you, by listening to which, a jiva becomes Siva himself.

To know the meaning of Pranava is to understand me. Pranava is the seed of all the lores.

It is subtle like the seed of the Banyan tree and has the interpretation of great importance. It is the fore runner of the Vedas, it is the gist of the Vedas. It also represents my form.

I am beyond the three gunas, omniscient, creator of everything besides being the lord. Though I pervade everywhere, still I reside in the word om as Siva.

It is said that whatever object is there, whether it is synthesized into one of analysed in fragments, means pranava because of the combination and importance of the attributes.

In the way the goddess enquired of the lord Candrasekhara, who started speaking praising Parvati.

It is the indestructible Brahman besides being the means of attaining all the objects. The universe is created by Siva wit the reciting of the word om.

Since there is hardly any difference in the sense and the sound om this is thus explained. Siva is pranava or vice versa.

The Brahmanical sages, the learned people, who are aware of the identity between the sense and the sound conceive me as a single syllabled om.

Therefore a person who aspires for salvation, and is free from blemish, can well understand pranava as the cause of all and myself as the Nirguna Parmesvara.

O goddess the crest jewel of mantras will be given by me, at Kasi, for the liberation of all individual souls.

O Amba, I shall now describe the Pranavoddhara first of all, by knowing which one achieves supreme success.

Initially the devotee shall extricate Nivrtti then the fuel, time, staff and the lord.

In this way the pranava of five syllables, is explained by extricating the three matras, bindu and nada. It yields liberation to those who perform the japam in this way.

Pranava happens to be the vital breath of all the living beings right from Brahma to unmobile beings. This is the reason that it is called pranava.

It comprises of A, U and M is the middle, while bindu and nada are not the end. Om is formed with the combination of the same.

O excellent sage, the first letter A is like water, in the south, the second letter u is in the north, while the letter M is in the middle, before nada and bindu.

A, U and M are the three matras. There is half a matra more besides them.

O Mahesani, this half of the matra has the form of bindu-nada, which is beyond description and is known to the learned people alone.

O dear, the Vedas have declared that Isanah Sarvadevanam and the Vedas emerge out of my body. The statement of the Vedas is truthful.

Because of this, I happen to be the fore runner of the Vedas and pranava happens to express me and because of that pranava is mentioned as Vedadi.

A is the great seed of the same. From the rajoguna of the same, Brahma is born. U is its yoni or Prakrti and Hari possessing the sattvaguna is the protector of the universe.

M is the bija-purusa and represents the tamoguna and stands for Hara or Siva, who is the destroyer of the universe. Bindu represents Mahesvara, the creator of the tirobhava (or the sense of disappearing).

Nada is attributed to Sadasiva, who is compassionate to all. On the top of nada, there is Siva who happens to be greater than the greatest.

He is omniscient, creator of all, the lord of all, beyond destruction free from blemish, imperishable, beyond expression, the supreme Brahman besides being beyond existent and non-existent.

A as compared to the other consonants or vowels is more commonly used and is more pervasive. You think over it always.

The five Brahmanas starting with Saciva and ending with Tsana, are lodged in five letters like A etc., which happen to be my forms in due order.

There are eight kalas of Siva emerging from Sadyas, while in u there are thirteen kalas of the form of Vamadeva.

M has eight kalas of the form of Aghora. The bindu has four kalas which are visible to the people.

There are five kalas in the nada form of Tsana. With the combination of the six padarthas the six fold identity of pranava is established.

O dear, you listen to the interpretation of the six padarthas viz. mantra, yantra, deity, universe, preceptor, and the disciple.

It has already been pointed out that the pranava-mantra five letters, which takes to the form of a yantra. Now I shall speak the process of its mandala.

Yantra is the form of the deity, deity has the universal form. The preceptor has the universal form, while the disciple is the body of the preceptor.

All of them have the form of omkara and all of them represent Brahma. This has been ordained by the Vedas. (om itidam sarvam iti sarvam Brahma). Thus the Vedic text establishes the link between the word and its meaning.

O goddess, the process of articulation adhara (support), manipura (jewel-refill), hrdaya (heart), Visuddha-cakra (auspiciousness), ajnacakra (order), sakti (force), Samti (tranquillity). Beyond Santi, is the lord, who happens to be greater than the greatest. Only a person with firm non-attachment would be able to possess the same.

O goddess, I shall be its theme. The devotee should link the jiva and the soul with me. I have explained the theme of the same and now you listen about the relationship.

A Brahmana with the following characteristic like performing of the Vratas peaceful, possessing the nature of an ascetic, having controlled his senses, auspicious, possessing noble conduct, well-versed in the Vedas, unmindful of the themes of the present as well as the future worlds, devoted to the gods and the Brahmanas, devotee of Siva.

Knowing well the meanings of all the Sastras and the tattvas, possessing excellent knowledge of Brahmajnana, Sadhu by nature, should go to the intelligent acarya and should offer his salutation to him, prostrating before him and please him at the same time. The disciple should possess several other merits besides being peaceful besides being humble.

“The preceptor represents Siva, who is the preceptor” with this firm resolve in his mind then he should exposes his feelings before the preceptor.

With the permission of the preceptor, he should perform twelve days vrata consuming milk only. He should take bath over the seashore, bank of the river, over a mountain or in the temple of Siva.

On the bright fifth or the eleventh day of the fortnight, and perform his daily routine with a spotless mind.

Thereafter inviting the preceptor, he should perform the Namdeo Sraddha. He should then have the hair of the body except those under the armpit and the Parvati parts removed.

He should have his head, beard, moustaches removed and the nails should be put off controlling all the senses, he should, take a bath, perform Sandhya and then consumed the barley power, take the bath in the evening.

Performing Sandhya in the evening with his preceptor, should offer daksina to his preceptor, taking him to be Siva.

He should collect all the material for performing of homa according to his Grhyasutra. A Brahmana who consecrates the sacred fire shall perform the upasana in the sacrificial fire consecrated by the Prajapatya sacrifice, reciting the mantras from the Vedas and offering due Daksina.

Then consecrating the Vedic fire in his soul, he should renounce the house and embrace Sannyasa (renunciation) collecting the Samidha sticks, food, ghee and cooked payasam, the person who has controlled his senses, should perform homa reciting each one of the Rca of Purusasukta. Thereafter, as per the provision of his own Grhyasutra, he should perform homa making the Svistakrta offerings in the fire.

After sacrifice he shall perform the tantric activities. The learned devotee should then sit over a cloth, deer skin or the kusa grass to the north of the fire. Then he should recite the Gayatri mantra upto down.

Then taking bath in the early morning preparing the payasam, should after oblations, starting from Purusa and ending with Viraja Suktas.

He should perform homa following the procedure laid down by Vamadeva and Saunaka. Of these two the opinion of Vamadeva is better, because the sage had delacted, even when he was in the womb of his mother.

Completing the rest of the sacrifice he should restart the adoration as he did in the morning. Then he shall superimpose Agni in his soul and perform the Sandhya as he did in the morning.

After the sun rise, he should perform japam of the Gayatri mantra. He should eschew the three Isanas and shall recite Presa mantra.

Then at the command of his preceptor he should discard the tuft, the sacred thread and the girdle too and move on towards the north or the east.

Because of his conduct in public, he can use kaupina and a danda. The one who is unmindful of the public feelings or is completely delacted, he can do even without these things.

He should go to his preceptor and prostrate before him thrice and then should sit besides the preceptor.

The preceptor then should pick up the white ashes from the Viraja fire and apply over the body of the disciple appropriately.

Then he should draw tripundra tilakam over the body of his disciple. He should then meditate upon me as well as you in his lotus like heart.

Getting pleased, he should place his hand over the head of the disciple. Then the preceptor should with a delightful mind whisper the pranava mantra into the right ear of the disciple.

He should whisper the pranava mantra thrice and then speak out its meaning to him. There he shall speak out the six fold meaning of pranava or omkara to him.

Prostrating before the preceptor twelve times being subservient to him he should study and practice Vedanta with him.

In his auspicious and spotless mind he should adore the everlasting lord Siva who is Brahmasaksi.

The person authorised is the ascetics engaged in the auspicious activities of the self restraint, the master of the Vedanta knowledge and free from rivalry.

The lotus of the heart is free from dust, devoid of surround, spotless and great. It has eight petals, with filaments and it shines above the pericarp.

After thinking about the region of adhara-sakti to the tree tattvas the dahara-vyoman (the ethic heart) shall be imagined and conceived in the middle.

Repeating the recitation of the single syllabled Brahman om, he shall with an alert mind, think of me along with you in the centre.

O dear, the devotee this achieves my loka. Receiving the knowledge from me, one attains the reward of my Sayujya type of salvation.”

## Chapter 4 - The daily performance of a recluse or a Sanyasi

Isvara said, “O Mahadevi, because of my love for you, I shall now mention the daily routine of a SanyasI, according to the prevailing practice.

The ascetics should get up in the Brahma-muhurta in the early morning and should devotee his mind towards his preceptor lodged in the white lotus of a thousand petals.

He should be resembling Siva, with the eyes resembling the auspicious and spotless crystal gem, besides bestower of the boons and protection and having the gentle temperament like Siva.

He should adore him with the fragrant flowers brought with the feeling of high respect and then offer salutation to him with folded hands.

He should then pray that my entire performance from morning to evening and evening to morning, amounts to your adoration.

Thus speaking to the preceptor with his permission should perform pranayama and controlling all his senses should occupy his seat.

Then he should meditate upon the illustrious six cakras from Muladhara to Brahmarandhra.

Simultaneously he should meditate upon me, the nirguna Sadasiva, free from ailments, the supreme Brahman, possessing the lustre of crores of lightening, resembling the lustre, having the body of existence, knowledge and bless.

The intelligent devotee then shall fed, “I am he” and should made out as far as he desires to go.

The intelligent devotee should cover his head and nose with a cloth and placing grass over the earth free himself from the bowels there daily.

Raising his linga upwards, he should go to the water tank and carefully cleanse himself with water.

Washing his hands and feet, reciting the om mantra, he should sip the water twice. Then he should quietly brush his teeth with a brush stick.

He should clean his teeth with leaves of trees or grass except on the eleventh or the new moon day. He should rinse the mouth gargling ten times.

After performing of the acamana twice he shall clean his lips with water and clay. At the time of dawn, he should take his bath applying clay over his body.

He should perform Sandhya or bath, remembering one as well as his preceptor. The subject is not being discussed here elaborately for fear of undue expansion, it should be visualised elsewhere as well.

Abhiseka of omkara should be performed in Samkha mudra. One should sprinkle water over the head, for three, six or twelve times.

One show wash kaupin over the bank of the river or lake, and perform acamana twice. Then he should sprinkle water over the clothes and the body.

Wiping out the face with the towel and then should wipe out the entire body from head to foot in the presence of the preceptor.

Then he should wear the clean kaupin and tighten it with the cord. O Parvati, thereafter one should apply ashes over the body, the method of which is being explained.

Sipping the water twice, and reciting the Sadyojata mantra he should apply ashes over the body. Reciting the mantra Agniriti bhasma etc. the ashes should sanctified and then applied over the body.

Reciting the mantra apo va idam sarvam, water should be poured into the ashes and then reciting the mantras, apojyoti and manastoka mashing the ashes, two pindas (balls) should be prepared. Then each one of them should be divided in fine parts and should apply over the head, face, rectum, heart and the feet.

From the mantras Isana to Sadyojata touching the other pinda with the body, it should be consecrated with pranava.

Thereafter washing all the limbs as well as the hands, one should type the second ball of ashes, which should be adored like the earlier one, and should draw a tripundra over the body with the same.

Reciting the mantras like tryayusam jamadagna or tryambakam yajamahe or the pranava mantra the ashes should be applied over the head, forehead, chest, shoulders, navel arms, joints and the back. Thereafter washing the hands, sip the water twice appropriately.

Reciting the Pancaksara mantra (om namah Sivaya) a learned disciple, should meditate upon his preceptor and thereafter perform pranayama half a dozen times.

Carrying water in the palm of the right hand, covering it with left hand, the water should be sanctified twelve times.

The water should then be sprinkled thrice over his own body and should carefully devote his mind towards Siva the water should be sipped thrice.

Siva is lodged in the centre of the solar disc, the god consisting of all splendour possessing eight arms, four faces, the wonderful form half male and half female, endowed with wonderful qualities and bedecked with ornaments. Thus meditating appropriately he shall offer three arghyas.

After reciting the Gayatri mantra a hundred and eight times he shall offer oblations with water a dozen times. Performing acamana he shall then resort to the performing with pranayama thrice.

Devoting his minds towards, he shall go to the prayer hall. Reaching the door the feet should be washed and sipping of water should be done twice

Then he shall enter the prayer chamber putting his right foot in it first. The intelligent ascetic shall then draw the mystic diagram inside the mandapa appropriately.

## Chapter 5 - Preparation of mandala at the place of worship

Isvara said, “Examining the ground from fragrance, complexion and the rasa appropriately, a tent should be fixed over the desired site.

Plastering the ground with mind, it should be made slippery like the mirror. A square mandapa one foot square in size should be made.

A small square should be made within the width of a palm leaf each, ultimately making thirteen equal squares in each column.

The leaf should be placed in the square mandala facing west, the ascetic should be seated. To the east of the same a strong read coloured card should be bound. I should also be bound in the eastern, western and southern directions. O Supreme Goddess, by this arranging the card, a hundred and sixty nine cubicals will be formed. The square in the centre would represent the pericarp. The eight squares outside it would be treated as eight petals, which should be made of white colour. The pericarp should be yellow in colour while the circle around it should be red.

O mistress of the gods, starting from the right of the lotus petals, the joints should be coloured in red and black.

In the pericarp pranava yantra should be made. Below it and above the pitha “Srlkantha” should be written.

“Amaresa” should be written above it and “Mahakala” should be written in the centre, close to the forehead of Mahakala a form of danda should be made and Isvara should be painted thereafter.

The pitha should be painted in black and Srikantha should be painted in yellow colour. Amaresa should be painted in red colour, while Mahakala should be painted black.

The danda should be of smoky colour, while levara should be of white colour. After drawing the yantra, the red one (Amaresa) shall be encompassed by sadya.

O goddess, Isana shall be known through the nada alone. The row of its residence shall be taken in order from the south-east one.

O beautiful one, on the four comers of the yantra four doors of white, red yellow and black colours should be made respectively in the squares an either side, should be coloured in yellow.

In the square in the south-east comer, an eight petalled lotus should be drawn. It should have red petals with a pericarp in the centre of it.

He should be written with a bindu or a spot in the centre of it. In the south-west square of this lotus another eight petalled lotus should be drawn. It should have the red petals and the pericarp should be yellow. The third letters of the class of Sa along with the sixth vowel and the fourteenth vowel decorated with bindu and nada, is O gentle lady, the excellent seed which shall be written in the lotus.

In the north-east square of the lotus, another lotus shall be drawn with the third letter of the class ka along with the fifth vowel making it gu.

In its middle bindu and kantha shall be written with decoration. In the three columns outside, it beginning with the eastern one, five squares shall be taken, O Siva, the daughter of the lord of mountains. The pericarp shall be taken in the middle and painted yellow with a red cereal.

A person ell-versed with the method of drawing the yantra shall make the lotus petals red in colour while the outer holes of the petals should be painted with black colour.

The south-east square and others should be painted white. The hexagonal with six dots to the east should be drawn in black colour.

The three corners from south to east should be pointed red. The crescent with shining white colour should be placed to the west corner which is painted yellow.

In the four corners, four bija mantras should be written. The bindu in the east should be white, while the one to the south should be black with the letter u.

The letter M in the north should be of red colour. In the west the letter a is painted yellow. Thus the four letters are written.

O beautiful lady, in the second row one shall began. The first four squares are respectively painted yellow, white, red and black. Below them the four are painted white blue, yellow and red respectively. O lady with a charming face, in the triangle below it, shall be painted red, white and yellow.

O Isvari, thus starting from the south it should be carried to the end. In its outer line, the eastern to control regions should be painted with yellow, red, black, white black and red. In this way the colours of the six squares have been stated. From south to east, from south to west, from south-west to south-east, from west to south, from north-west to south-east, from west to south, from northwest to the south-west, from north to the west, from north-east to north-west. O goddess, in this way the procedure of the diagram has been mentioned to you. After drawing the diagram in this way, the ascetic, controlling his mind shall adore the sun with devotion.

## Chapter 6 - Procedure for asana and pranayama

Isvara said, “In the southern mandala, the tiger’s skin should be spread and reciting the astra mantra the clean water should be sprinkled.

Initially reciting the pranava mantra, he shall recite the adhara and the sakti kamala. Then he should be seated over the tiger skin, repeating the mantra with the dative case, ending with namah, facing north. After the pranayama is performed and precede with the uttering of the pranava mantra he shall smear the body with ashes, reciting the Agnireta mantra. Then bowing in reverence to Siva, he shall draw the diagram or mandala again.

Outside, he shall adore the diagrams of triangle, circle and square, repeating om. Then the conch should be filled with the fragrant clean water, reciting the pranava mantra. The conch shall then be placed over the diagram and adore it offering to it the scent and flowers, repeating the pranava mantra seven times, after which he shall display the Dhenu and Samkha mudras. Then he shall sprinkle it with Astra mantra.

Of this mantra of the glorious sun, the sage is Devabhaga, the metre is Gayatri, the deity being the sun, then the six organs nyasa shall be performed with Hram etc. Then he sprinkles padma which is beyond the purview of Agni.

Then the lotus of the south-east, should be adored as per the earlier practice offering the spotless essence.

Then he should worship Kalagnirudra Adhara sakti, Ananta, the earth, Ratnadvipa, orchard with trees, and gem studded abodes and uttering a Samkalpa devoting his mind at the feet of Siva should worship Ratnapitha.

Dharma, jnana, vairagya should be adored in the eastern and other directions, while adharma, ignorance, attracting and misery should be adored in the south-east and other directions respectively.

The lower lid of Maya and the upper lid of Vidya shall be worshipped by him. Thereafter Sattva, Rajas and Tamas shall be worshipped in order.

In the quarters starting from the east and in the middle, he shall worship dipta, Saksma, Jaya, Bhadra, Vibhuti, Vimala, Amogha, Vaidyuta, Sarvatomukha Sanjnana, Kandanala, Susira, then Tantrikatmakas then the root lid, filament, (light) and Sakalatman the five knotted pericarp and the petals, then the filament, Brahma, Visnu, Rudra, and Atman. After adoring the inner Atman in the great Atman of the knowledge, he shall worship the Yogapitha called Saura. The knower of the roots shall conceive, the image as lodged over the pedestal.

The performer, then sitting over the asana reciting the mula mantra should hold the breath in Muladhara should wake up the Adhara sakti of the pingala nerve.

Then he should offer the hand full of flowers to Parvati, who is lodged in the middle diagram having the body resplendent with red colour lodged to the left of Siva.

Siva on the other hand wears the garland of Rudraksa having four faces and holding rosary, khatvanga, skull, goad, lotus, conch and cakra.

He has twelve eyes on four faces, and a spear within the lotus of his heart. He utters pranava first and then hram, hrim and sah.

Thereafter he invokes the sun along with the light and power uttering Surjaya namah 'I invoke obeisance'.

Then he should display the mystic sign of sthapana. Then the nyasa of the limbs should be performed uttering hram, hrim, hrum mantras.

Then performing the Samkalpa of pancapacara, he should pray, O Mahesvara (I adore you). Then he should adore her thrice offering the dust of the lotus flowers.

Thereafter, he should adore Agni, Isvara, Raksasa, Vayu, in the forms of images. Thus in the second avarana (covering) these four deities shall be worshipped in the south-east.

O Parvati, from east to the north, at the root of the lotus petal Aditya, Bhaskara, Bhanu and Surya should be adored respectively.

O beloved in the third covering, Surya, Brahma, Rudra and Visnu should be adored should be worshipped in the north-east and other quarters.

In the middle of the leaves from the east onwards, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn and Rahu should be worshipped.

Or alternatively the twelve Adityas should be worshipped in the second covering, while the twelve Zodiac signs should be adored in the third covering.

On its outer side the seven oceans and seven rivers (Gangas) should be worshipped, while the sages, gods, Gandharvas, serpents, the divine damsels, the village chiefs, the Yaksas, Raksasas, Yatudhanas, the seven horses in the form of the Vedas, and Balakhilyas should also be adored.

After adoring the sun of three coverings, and arranging the square diagram with auspicious mind, he shall place a copper vase which can hold the prastha of water on its stand. He shall fill it up with pure water scented with fragrant flowers. The adoration shall be performed by him over the ground and offering fragrant flowers. The vase of arghya shall be lifted upto the centre of the eyebrows. A hymn shall them be recited by him in favour of the sun. O goddess, the said mantra bestows all the pleasures and the salvation.

“O lord, the powder of red sandal, gold with water, the garland, saffron, kusa grass, and the flowers should be placed in the gold vase, the arghya has been offered to you. Therefore you kindly be pleased.”

Thus speaking offering the arghya to the image of the sin, should offer his salutation attentively.

Then he should say, “Salutation to the images of Parvati and Siva with his ganas, Rudra the cause of the creation, Visnu and Brahma.”

Seating over his asana, thus speaking, offering his salutation to gods, and then he should mention the names of the sages and wash his hands with water.

Thereafter he should apply ashes over his body in the manner prescribed earlier. Then he should perform nyasas displaying his devotion to lord Siva.

After adoring the lord Siva, lowering his head and offering five fold services he should adore the lord and reciting “om srigurave namah offer his salutation to him.

Then he should adore pranava and the fifth letter u without the fifth vowel and with the bindu. After uttering thus, with bindu he shall utter the composite unit.

By the uttering of these seed words, the learned ascetic shall bow before his preceptor in reverence besides the lord Ganesa, lodged over his arms and the thighs.

He should offer his salutation to Durga and Ksetrapalas with his hands folded. Then uttering ''om astraya phat”, he should perform anganyasa half a dozen times and then wash his hands clean.

Reciting the mantra “Apa sarpantu” then he should again recite pranava, should speak out astraya phat and touch the ground with his heels thrice.

Removing all the obstructing, clapping his hands thrice, observing the obstructing disappearing in the sky and the obstructions prevailing in the heaven.

He should stop breathing, reciting the hamsa-mantra should connect the jiva lodged in the heart with the conscious Brahmana (Paramesvara) by means of nerve Susumna.

Then he should meditate on the supreme god of the form of cit in the middle of lunar sphere of cit, within the great thousand petalled lotus full blown and stationed in the twelve (?)

For sixteen, sixty four and thirty two seconds, he should perform the puraka, kumbhaka and Recaka, through sosa, daha and plava.

The pranayama should be performed retaining the breath as described in his particular Veda, through wind, fire, water etc. and shall bring the nerve which is the Mula, to the cerebral aperture. When the body is bathed in the exquisite nectar in current issuing from the lunar sphere of cit, within the lotus of thousand petals within the twelve, it is purified and thrilled with good emotions, the soul is made to descend to the lotus of the heart realising, “I am he.” Then the Atman is to be pushed into the Atman through the nectarine current. Thus he shall stabilise auspiciously the vital breath in a proper manner.

A yogi with a concentration mind should envelop the matrka with pranava and the keep the matrka outside.

Then the learned devotee, stopping the vital air and the gaze, purifying his heart, with his mind devoted to Siva, embrace Sannyasa.

O Devi! Brahma is the Rsi for pranava, Gayatri is the metre, Sadasiva the supreme soul is the god.

A is the seed, u is sakti, m is the kilaka and viniyoga is meant for moksa. O goddess, he should perform nyasa saying 'Om', starting from two thumbs and ending with the palms, the hands are wiped off.

He should perform the nyasa starting from the thumb of the right hand and ending with the little finger of the left hand.

The nyasa of the hand should be performed uttering A, u, M, with the bindu and the mantra ending with namah.

After uttering A at the outset, the identity of the Brahmana and the Atman shall be established. The mantra ending with De and namah shall be uttered in the heart.

The nyasa of u along with Visnu is made on the head and the one of M is made with Rudra in the tuft.

O goddess, the sages practising the mantra shall make a nyasa of the kavaca in the eyes and the forehead with an attentive mind.

The different organs, faces and digits shall be fixed in the five Brahmanas. Isana's five digits shall be placed in the head, face, heart, private parts and the fat. The four digits of the Purusa shall be fixed in the four faces. Aghora's eight digits shall be adored in the heart, neck, shoulders, navel, belly, back and chest. Vamadeva's thirteen digits, shall be fixed in the anus, penis, thighs, knees, calves, buttocks, waist and sides. Sadya' eight digits will be fixed in the eight eyes. The most excellent of knowers of kalpa shall fix these digits in the feet, hand, vital breath, head and arms.

Thus the making of the nyasa of the thirty eight kalas, a person well-versed in pranaya shall proceed with the nyasa of the pranaya.

After making the nyasa in the arms, elbows, wrists, belly, calves, feet and back, an expert devotee of nyaya shall perform Hamsa nyasa which makes one realise the supreme soul.

## Chapter 7 - Method of Siva's worship

Siva said, “One should draw a diagram to his west, where om should be adored offering a conch-astra.

Keeping it over the base, and pouring the fragrant water scented with the sandal parts, Pranava should be adored.

Reciting pranava offering the scent and flowers to the same and repeat pranava seven times, displaying the Dhenumudra.

Thereafter the Samkhamudra should be drawn our the square ground. A crescent and a triangle should be made in the centre of the same.

In this way the hexagonal diagram should be prepared. In between pranava should be worshipped offering the sandal paste and flowers.

The vase of arghya should be placed with the base, it should be worshipped by offering the sandal paste etc. Then filling it up with fragrant water, O beautiful one, the upper part of kusa, unbroken rice, barley, paddy, gingerly seeds other grains, ghee fried objects flowers and ashes too shall be added.

It shall be worshipped with scents, flowers and Sadyojata mantras with their six ancillaries, pranavas and the varma-mantra.

Linking it with the Astra mantra, the Dhenu mudra should be displayed.

The fragrance of his own soul, besides the flowers and other material for adoration should be offered. Omkara should be recited in the north-east of the lotus flower.

Reciting the mantra Guru-asanaya namah one should conceive the asana of the preceptor. As per the advice of the preceptor, he should recall the image of the preceptor.

Reciting the mantra pranavam gum, gurubhyo namah, turning the face to the south, he should invoke the preceptor.

The preceptor should be conceived like Siva, having the delightful face, with serene look, spotless like the pure crystal gem, bestower of the boon, displaying protection by hand, having two eyes.

Thus meditating upon Siva, he should offer, fragrance, flowers, etc. and other dravyas. He shall worship Ganapati assigning him a seat on a lotus to the south-west of the mystical diagram reciting the mantra gananatva etc. After invoking the lord Ganesa, he should worship him, offering flowers and other things. He should meditate on him with concentration.

Lord Ganesa has a gigantic body of red complexion, bedecked with all the ornaments, holding an ankusa (goad) and rosary and bestows the desires of his devotees by bestowing the Varada mudra.

The devotee should meditate up Ganesa, the remover of all the obstacles, having the elephant face and adore him offering scent and other things.

As naivedya, he should be offered the banana, coconut, mango, sweet balls, and one should bow in reverence to him.

In the lotus to the north-west of the diagram, the devotee shall conceive shall conceive the form of Skanda and invoke him too.

The Skanda gayatri should be recited one should devote his mind to him. He is conceived as mounted over a peacock like the rising sun.

He has four arms, beautiful limbs, adorned with the crown and other ornaments, displays abhaya and varada mudras and holds a sakti and a cock.

In this way adoring Skanda, one should offer to him fragrance and the flowers. He should be adored at the southern corner of the eastern gate.

Now lion on the other hand is the lord of the inner quarters and he has to be adored accordingly. He is adorned with ornaments like the mountain of gold.

He has the crown of a crescent moon, three eyes, four arms, resplendent, holds a spear, wears a Kirita crown and has the staff of the gold.

He has the face like the reflection of the moon, or like lion's face, should be lodged to the north with his wife, who had been the daughter of Maruts, known by the name of Suyasa. She was quite chaste, and she always was engaged in decorating the feet of the goddess Parvati. They should be adored with fragrance and flowers, then reciting the Padma-astra mantra the water from the conch should be offered to them. Then the asana with base should be conceived.

Then Syama, the Adhara-sakti and bestower of welfare should be thought of, over the grand below. Besides one should thinks of serpent Ananta coiled in point of her.

He is adorned with white five serpent hoods, as if licking the sky. A lion throne with four legs should be placed over it.

The lion throne has four legs representing dharma, prana, vairagya and the fortunes. They shall be worshipped seated over the dignified seat, and worshipped beginning with south-east comer in white colour besides yellow red and dark blue.

Adharma shall be conceived from the east to the north. The complexion of his body should be resembling the Lajavarta gem.

Then the bed-sheet and covering of the body, the kanda nala, kantha dala and karnika should be conceived. Thereafter he should be worshipped.

In the petals the eight Siddhis are supposed to have been lodged and Rudra in the saffron and the saktis like vanes should be imagined from the east.

Vairagya should be imagined in pericarp, besides Vama and the nine Saktis in the seeds who are lodged to the east. Then the Manonmani Sakti should be imagined in the rots, Sivatmaka in the Dharmanala, the knowledge of Sivasraya in the pericarp. Thereafter one should think of the zones of fire, sun and the moon above the pericarp.

The three tattvas of Atma-vidya and Siva, are beyond this. One should place the flowers of different colours over all the asanas.

Above these seats, he shall imagine the seat of the deity shining with the flowers of different colours and the lustre of the Paravyomavakasa.

From the Adhara sakti to the seat of the spotless lore the devotee shall repeat the mantra “om Sivaya namah" (this procedure is followed everywhere, as before the five Brahmanas should conceived in the image in view of the difference in limbs; faces and digits. The yogi well-versed in the mystic signs, shall invite the lord with a hand filled with flowers.

Then he should recite the mantra starting from sadyojata to astu sadasivam, repeating the nada emerging from the adhara and concluding at the Brahmarandhra together with the twelve knots, reciting from Brahmarandhra should meditate Siva in the form of omkara, which is pure as crystal, the unsullied and perishable, the cause of creation, identical with worlds, stationed within and without all pervading smaller than the smallest and greater than the greatest, visible to the devotees without much efforts, the unchanging and incomprehensible to the gods, Brahma, Visnu, Rudra and others, the essence of the Vedas, also declared as invisible by the learned, devoid of beginning middle and end besides being the care for all the worldly ills.

Thus with a careful mind, one should meditate upon the Paramesvara, invoke him, establish him in his heart and look at him.

Then he should offer his salutation to him. Offering his salutation to him, he should then display various mudras (poses). Then he should meditate upon Sadasiva, who is Sakala as well as Niskala.

He should be conceived to have been conceived with matted locks of hair, which are cool, having the complexion of the auspicious crystal gem, having a pleasing face becoming with lustre resembling the circle of lightening.

Siva should be clad in the tiger skin, having a delightful face, the hands, feet and lower lip resembling the red lotus.

He should be possessing all the auspicious symbols, adorned with all the ornaments, holding the divine attributes in his hands, and with the divine fragrance applied over the body.

He has five faces, ten arms, decorating his head with the crescent moon and the expression of the face is quite served and possesses the lustre of the rising sun.

He has three eyes, resembling the lotus flowers, has the crescent moon over the head, the face to the south, has the blue complexion like the clouds.

Because of the curved eyebrows, it looks awful, has three round red eyes, the fangs are looking quite terrific. The lips are fluttering.

The face to the north has the lustre of the coral and has the black hair. It has three charming eyes. There is a crescent over the crown.

The western head resembles the full moon, having three eyes issuing lustre. It has the digit of the moon over it and wears a serene smile our the face.

The fifth head resembles the crystal stone decorated with the digit of the moon and adorned with three developed eyes.

In his right hands he carries a spear, battle axe, sword, which is shining like the fire.

In his left hands he carries a bow, an arrow, a bell, a nose, and the shining goad. He has the Nivrtti Kala upto the knees, the pratista-kala upto the navel, the vidyakala upto the neck, the Santa kala upto the forehead and the Santyatita kala beyond that.

Thus he has the body of five kalas. He pervades the five paths. Isana is the Puratana Purusa.

He has Aghora for heart, Vamadeva for secret parts, Sadyojata for feet, thus his figure forty eight kalas.

He is Isana comparable to the matrkas and the five Brahmanas. He is identical with omkara, Hamsa sannyasa, the five syllabled and the six syllabled mantras, the six mountains and the jatis.

Thus meditating, O goddess, he will adore you as Manonmani to my left, with devotion, reciting the mantra Gaurirmiyaya etc.

Then O Isvari, after invoking as before, he should worship offering his salutation. O goddess, then he should carefully meditate upon you.

Like the blossoming lotus leaf, having the vast sages, having the face like the full moon and the black curly hair.

She has the complexion of a blue lotus, adoring her head with the crescent moon and having the breasts which are sound, stiff, raised, thick and slippery.

She has slander buttocks and clad in yellow silken garments. She is adorned with all the ornaments and display tilakam over the forehead.

Her hair is decorated with colourful flowers. She is the abode of all the virtues; she is lowering her head a bit due to shyness.

The yellow lotus flowers is held by her in her right hand. She holds a flywhisk in her hand like a staff. She is seated in bhadrasana.

Thus a person having controlled all his senses, meditating upon you and myself, offering the conch water for bathing, then recite the pranaya mantra.

Then he should offer padya reciting the mantra bhava bhave nati bhave. Then reciting the mantra Vamadevaya namah, the sipping should be done.

Then reciting the mantra jyesthaya namah, the white cloth should be offered. Reciting the mantra Sresthaye namah the yajnopavita (the sacred thread) should be offered.

Reciting the mantra Rudraya namah sipping water should be offered. Reciting the mantra kalaya namah the scent should be offered.

Reciting kalavikaranaya namah, the unbroken race should be offered and the flowers should be offered with the mantra Balavikaranaya.

Reciting balaya namah the incense should be offered, while the lamp has to be offered saying balaprathamanaya.

The Vedas and the six Matrkas, pranaya, Siva besides Siva, the devotee should display the mystic signs to both of us. O lady with charming complexion, he should initially serve me and then to you.

When he performs adoration to you he should make use of the feminine gender. O Parvati, this is he only difference and nothing else.

The devotee should then resort to the Avarana-puja after performing meditation properly according to the provision of the scriptures.

## Chapter 8 - Mental worship of Siva

O great goddess, there are five avaranas. Therefore the worship of the avaranas shall be this performed.

When both of them have been previously worshipped, the intelligent devotee will start from there in the sequence of Ganesa, Kartikeya and others offering the fragrance etc.

The five Brahmana shall be worshipping in a sequence in the north-east, east, south, north and west. The devotees shall worship the six anciliatories thereafter. He shall adore the eye and astra in the south east, north east, south west, and in the middle. Thus the first avarana is mentioned. Now listen to the second avarana.

The avarana Ananta should be worshipped in the east, over the petal, Suksma to the south, Sivottama to the west and Ekanetra in the north Ekarudra should be adored in the north-east, the Trinity in the south-east, Srikantha in the south west, and Sikhandisa in the north-west.

In the second avarana the emperors should be adored. In the centre of the eastern gate, Vrsa and Isana should be adored.

Nandi should be adored in the south. Mahakala should be adored in the north. Bhrngisa should be adored in the south-west, gate.

In the earlier square, Ganesa should be adored with fragrance. In the north-west square Vrsabha should be adored, while Kartikeya should be adored in the south.

All the eight should be adored in a sequence from the north and the east gates in the pradaksina passage, who are known as Bhava, Sarva, Isana, Rudra, Pasupati, Ugra, Bhima and Mahadeva. This the third avarana.

One should invoke Mahesvara, who is the primordial form in the Vedas, and should adore him over the pericarp to the east.

Isvara should be adored on the eastern side of the petal, Visvesa on the southern side of the petal, Paramesa towards the north and Sarvesa towards the west side of the petal.

Reciting the mantra avorajanam Rudra should be adored over the southern side of the petal and over the pericarp, with scent, flowers etc., invoking him at the same time.

One should adore Siva in the south, Hara in the north, Mrda in the south of the petal, besides Bhava.

In the lotus petal placed to the north besides the pericarp, Visnu should be invoked and adored offering the fragrance and flower reciting the mantra pratad visnu.

Vasudeva should be adored in the east, Aniruddha in the south and Samkarsana in the west.

Brahma should be invoked in the petal to the west and then worshipped. Reciting the mantra Hiranyagarbhah samavartatah, Hiranyagarbha should be adored in the east. Virat Purusa should adored in the south. God Puskara should be adored in north, while Kala has to be adored in the west.

Describing the fifth avarana, the lokapalas shall be worshipped in the top most row in different spots in the passage of the circumambulation.

The following ten are the Bijas for the lokapalas- Ranta ending with Ra, Panta ending with Pa, Jnanta ending with Jna, Lanta ending with La twice, Apurvaka beginning with A, Santa ending with Sa, Vedadya or Pranava and Sribija.

These are the seeds of the lokapalas and they should be worshipped accordingly. Then he shall worship Brahma and Visnu observing the proper rules and proper means of service of in the north, south-west, south and the north-east. He shall worship Devesa in the outer line of the fifth avarana.

Then he should worship the trident in the north east, vajra in the east, the axe in the south east, and the arrow in the south.

The sword should be adored in the south west, the noose in the west, the goad in the north west and the bow in the north.

Raudra and Ksetrapala should be adored in the west. A person well-versed in the procedure, in order to please Siva, should adore him accordingly.

One should keep on gazing out the lord and the goddess with devotion, meditating upon them.

In this way for the reward of the obstruction avarana-puja should be performed. Then he should meditate upon Siva, lord of the gods.

Worshipping Siva, offering him the fragrance and other articles and should then offer naivedya to the lord which is appropriately prepared. Then he should offer the water for sipping besides the arghya. The betel leaf should be given thereafter.

The puja should be completed, after performing the arati. Then meditating upon both the lord and the goddess, the mantra should be recited a hundred and eight times.

Thereafter standing up holding flowers in his hands and recite the mantras from yo vedadau svarah prokta should be recited. O Paramesvari then hand filled with flowers should be offered and the circumambulation should be made.

Then he should prostrate before him with utmost devotion. After circumambulating him, one should again offer his salutation to him.

Then sitting over the asana one should adore Siva with eight names and should speak out “whatever good or bad deeds have been done by me.

O lord Siva, it all tantamount to your worship.” Thus speaking he should offer the flowers as well as the water of the conch to the lord Siva.

Adoring the adorable one again, the eight names of Siva should be recited at the same time. O goddess, I am going to speak out the same became of my attachment for you.

## Chapter 9 - Interpretation of the eight names of Siva, adoration of linga, pleasure of the goddess and pilgrimage of Suta

These are the eight manes of Siva. Out of these the five of them upto Pitamaha are dependant on their conditions. In case the conditions change, the names too change.

The word is permanent, while the object indicated by the same word is changeable. The words are transferable since those indicated by the words are released.

When the words are transferred, these are conditions again. Therefore the first five words represent things other than the Atman or the soul.

The other three names derive their origin from the difference in the natural cause. In these words Siva exists with the creating of three types of conditions.

Due to the non-existence of the antecedents of the contact with primordial Avidya, he is naturally pure souled and is therefore called Siva.

Or other wise because there is the same adhara (base) of all the welfare virtues Isvara who is well known to those well-versed in Siva-tattva, call him Siva.

Prakrti is beyond the twenty three tattvas and the twenty-fifth one beyond Prakrti happens to be the Purusa.

The Purusa is called Svara in the Vedas or Omkara. He is intelligible and can be known only through the Vedas and the Upanisads.

As an enjoyer the same Purusa is absorbed in the Prakrti. Therefore the one who is beyond the Prakrti is called Mahesvara.

The Prakrti and Purusa are subservient to him so he is rightly termed as Mahesvara. Or Maya is the imperishable aspect of the three gunas which is imperishable. Know that Maya is the Prakrti and Mayin (the wielder of Maya) is Mahesvara who is eternal and the releaser from Maya. Hence the name Mahesvara is exact for him.

The word Rud stands for misery and the lord who removes the misery is called Rudra. Siva happens to be the main cause of the same.

All the padaratha enshrined from Sivattva to a pitcher or the body, Siva pervades all, as a result of which he is known by the name of Visnu.

The deity who looks to the welfare of ail the jivas of the world like a father, is Brahma who is known as Pitamaha or the grand sire.

As a physician well-versed in the subject removes the ailment with the correct application of the medicine, similarly because of his competence to bestow the pleasure and salvation, the Siva who removes the gross cause of the universe, ailment, he is called Sansara-vaidya or the physician of the universe.

In order to achieve the knowledge of different topics, inspite of the presence of the sense organs, those who are unaware of the gross or subtle movements of the world and which are concealed because of their remaining covered with the filth in the form of Maya and inspite of the fact that all the sense organs are heartily enough to collect the relevant knowledge.

To the contrary Siva is well aware of the condition of each padartha of the world in which it is placed and as such he is called Sarvajna or omniscient.

He is the soul of all and possesses all the virtues and because of his remaining secluded Siva happens to be the supreme soul or Paramatma.

In this way the imperishable Mahadeva, the form of pranava should be adored and eulogised. The arghya and the padya should be offered thereafter they should be placed over the head of Isana.

Keeping himself alert, he should adore Siva with pranava with hands folded and offering the flowers.

He should inhale through the left nostril, identifying the inhaled air with Siva and exhale through the right nostril biding the realistic prayer to the goddess. He shall conceive the identity of Siva with himself saying, “I am alone.” Thereafter he shall make a ritualistic dismissal of the deities conceived in the heart.

Thereafter he should adore the lore and the preceptors. Then he should fix in the heart the mantras of conch and the vase of arghya.

Then offering the remnants of the floral offerings to Candesa in the north east quarter, and performing the pranayama, Rsi and others should be remembered.

This mandala is technically known as Kailasa prastha, which shall be worshipped daily or in each fortnight, or in every four months, or once in a year or during the caturmasya festival. A believe shall adore my linga daily.

O Mahadevi, in this sequence a special order has to be kept in view. On the day of initiation he shall worship the linga and the preceptor and bow thrice in front of him, saying, “Till my death, I shall worship Siva.”

O dear, with the since described procedure one should adore Siva daily. The water for arghya should be poured over Siva.

Then adoring with pranava, incense and the lamp should be offered. After adoring Canda in the north-east, nirmalyai should be offered.

The linga and the pedestal should then be washed with the clean water, the flowers should be offered over the Sivalinga repeating pranava mantra.

Conceiving mentally from the Adhara-sakti to the spotless Vidyasana, the supreme god should be installed.

Then he should bathe the Sivalinga with pancagavya and other materials mixed in the water and other fragrant things.

Reciting the mantras like ''Pavamanena” or “namaste rudra ” or Nilasukta or tvaritena or with the hymns from the Samaveda or with the Sadyojata mantra he should bathe Mahadeva with welfare mantra of pranava. Thereafter, he should offer special type of arghya and bath the lord with pranava.

Wiping out the linga with the cloth, the flowers should be placed at the tap of the Sivalinga. Offering the flowers at the pedestal, the sun should be worshipped.

The Adhara-sakti and Ananta (the serpent) should be adored below the pedestal. Above that the adoration should be dome in the sequence of the heir throne.

At the leg of the Simhasana, covered with the cloth, Skanda should be adore conceiving Sivalinga to be the image of Siva, you should be adored with one (Siva).

O dear, in this way, the worshipper, should meditate upon me. This is the best method which has been explained by me.

It should not be revealed to anyone else, except my devotees. Such a discourse should be delivered to my devotee alone, who free from all attachments being a perfect ascetic.

This particular knowledge could aloe be given to a person who is devoted to the preceptor, peaceful and the one who is engaged in the yogic practices for me. The fool who disobeying my command, imparts this knowledge to others, he would be my betrayer and would surely fall in the hell. A person who imparts this knowledge to my devotees, he surely becomes loveable to me and he enjoying all the pleasures in this world, ultimately achieves my loka.

Vyasa said, “Listening to the words this spoken by Mahadeva, the great goddess, eulogised Siva, with the Vedic strotra variously.

O sages, then Paramesvari, offered her salutation at the lotus like feet of her husband.

O Brahmanas, the knowledge revealing the interpretation of pranava besides the knowledge of Siva are of secret nature, which destroys the miseries of all of you.”

Suta said, “O excellent sage, at the words thus spoken by the great ascetic Vyasa, the son of Parasara, the sages well-versed in the Vedas adored him.

Thereafter he left for the Kailasa mountain from there. The Rsis also after the completion of the yajna adored Candrasekhara- the Paramesvara, with utmost devotion and engaging themselves in the Yama and other yogic practices meditated upon Siva.

The goddess then imparted the said knowledge to Kartikeya, who further narrated the same to Nandi. Nandi however, narrated the same to the sage Sanatkumara.

My illustrious preceptor received the same knowledge from him. O excellent sage, thereafter I achieved this knowledge.

Then I imported the utmost secret knowledge to you all taking you to be the devotees of Siva.

You should also impart this secret knowledge to the peaceful ascetics who are devoted to Siva.

Thus speaking, Suta who happened to be the best of the people possessing the knowledge of the Puranas, on the pretext of going on pilgrimage, kept on wandering on earth.

Suta on his part after gaining knowledge of the secret topic lived in Kasi and getting liberated achieved the place of Siva.

## Chapter 10 - Discourse of Suta

Vyasa said, “After the departure of Suta, the sages confabulated among themselves, feeling surpressed. They observed, “we have forgotten, the faith of Vamadeva, which has been propounded by Suta, we have forgotten about the same.

When shall we be able to meet Suta again, who relieves the people of all the sufferings? Let the excellent sage arrive here again by the grace of lord Suta's devotion.”

In this way all the sages were quite anxious, to have an audience with the sage Vyasa.

After a year, Suta the great sage, who was devoted to Siva, besides being quite learned and well-versed in the Purana, arrived in Kasi.

At the arrival of Suta the delightful sages stood up and started adoring him affirming the seat, arghya, padya etc.

He also felicitated all the sages with pleasures and he then took his bath in the auspicious water of the Ganga.

He offered oblation to the manes with gingerly seeds and unbroken rice over the river bank. Then wiping out his body, he put on his cloths.

The excellent sage, performed acamana twice, applied ashes over his body reciting the Sadyajata-mantra.

Then he wore the Rudraksa rosary and the performed the daily Sandhya and then adorned his limbs with tripundra.

Then he adored Visvesvara the lord of Uma, Ganesa and other leaders of the ganas offering them salutation again and again. Then he eulogised them.

Kalabhairava was appropriately adored the sage circumumbulated him thrice and offered his salutation to him five times.

He again circumambulated and prostrated before him and then offered prayer to the supreme sakti, adoring her lotus like feet.

The Pancaksara mantra was recited by him one thousand and eight times, he begged forgiveness from Mahesvara.

Adoring Candesa, he took his seat in the middle of Muktimandapa offered by the sages who had mastered the Vedas.

After all of them took their seats, he offering his salutation with respect, spoke the words which could increase their wisdom.

Suta said, “O great ascetics with excellent Vratas, you are all graceful. The purpose for which, I have come to you, you please listen to the same.

When I, after delivering discourse to you on pranava, had left on pilgrimage, I am going to reached the same names to you.

Starting from hue, I reached the shore of the southern ocean. Taking a bath there, I appropriately adored Kanyakumari. O best of the Brahmanas, then I reached the bank of Suvarna mukhari.

By taking a bath in Suvarna mukhad I appropriately offered oblation to gods, Rsis and the manes. Then remembering Siva with devotion I adored Kalahastisa- who is resplendent like the moon.

Then I had an audience with five face Siva, who removed all the sins with a single audience with him, who bestowed all the success, besides the pleasures and salvation. The goddess Siva was lodged to his left.

Then with great devotion, I adored Siva stationed to his right with goddess- the mother of the universe, performing japam of the Pancaksara-vidya, a thousand and eight times. I circumambulation, eulogised and bowed again. Then I went round the hill daily with great devotion, observing all the restraints, and performed the rites daily with a delightful mind.

O sages, I spent from months there by the grace of the goddess who happens to be the bowed of the flower of knowledge.

Once I spread a cloth, kusa grace and the deer skin on the seat and with a restrained mind I sat over it silently. Then I entered into a silent trance. Then it dawned on me that, “I am Siva, the perfect knowledge and bliss, which is the perfect one forever.” This feeling was around in my heart and I was free from any type of disturbance.

At that time, my preceptor, who happened to be the ocean of mercy, having the complexion of blue cloud, having the yellow locks of hair resembling the lightning, carrying the raised Kamandalu and the dear skin, with the ashes applied over the entire body, bearing all the auspicious symbols, making a tripundra over the forehead, carrying the rosary of Rudraksa, having the eyes like the vast lotus leaf atonce appeared in my lotus like heart cast a delusion on me, O faithfulls.

Then I opened my eyes, and started lamenting. The rain of tears started flowing from my eyes.

O Brahmanas, of the same time, I heard an astonishing type of the divine voice which you should listen with respect.

It said, “O excellent one, O son of Suta, you go to Varanasi where there are many sages to whom you had delivered a discourse.

They having been compelled to do so, are living without taking any food, and are eagerly waiting for your return to that place.” This speaking the divine voice stopped.

Then I got up at once, circumambulated both Siva and Parvati and prostrating over the ground a dozen times, I offered my salutation to both of them.

Taking it to be the command of the preceptors, abruptly coming out of the region of Siva and Siva, after travelling for forty days, I have reached here. Now all of you should be graceful on one. All of you should now tell me as to what is to be spoken by me now?”

Listening to the words of Suta the sages were pleased and offering their salutation to the sage Vyasa again and again, the spoke to him.

## Chapter 11 - Question about Omkara and definition of Skanda stotra

Rsis said, “O excellent sage, O Suta, you happen to be our excellent preceptor. In case you are kind to us, they may ask for something.

The preceptors like you are always compassionate over the disciples. This aspect has been displayed by you presently.

The opinion you had expressed at the time of the definition of Viraja homa, earlier, the same may kindly be explained quite elaborately.

O compassionate one, presently we intend to listen to the same with great devotion and faith. You kindly speak out the same quite lovingly.”

Thus listening to the words of the sages, Suta, feeling delighted offered his salutation to Mahadeva, the supreme preceptor.

After offering his salutation to Mahadeva the mother of the three worlds and the preceptor, delighting the sages, Suta spoke in the deep voice.

Suta said, “O excellent sages, let you meet with welfare and be comfortable always. All of you have stable minds and are also devoted to Siva, besides propagating the devotion of Siva.

This is the wonderful talk, which I heard from the mouth of the preceptor. Till now, I had thought that the secret world be out and because of the same I did not reveal it.

All of you are immensely fortunate, besides being the devotees of Siva and have a fresh resolve. Thus thinking, I am going to reveal the secret to you. You listen to the same quite lovingly.

Earlier in the Rathantara Kalpa, the great sage Vamadeva, soon after his birth, himself became the preceptor of those possessing the knowledge of Siva.

He was well aware of all the tattvas, besides the Vedas, scriptures, Puranas etc. The karmas of all the gods, demons, humans and others were well known to him.

He applied ashes over his entire body, having the matted locks of hair, had no permanent abode, no desire, no equation, none of the mutually appealing feelings or emotions. He was surrounded by the leading sages, who were like him and who had taken him to be their preceptor. With the auspicious touch of his feet, he sanctified the earth. He always remained absorbed in the Brahman. He was like the naked Siva.

He gladly entered the southern peak of the Sumeru mountain, the dwelling place of Kartikeya the son of Siva.

Skanda possessing the Jnana Sakti, powerful and the destroyer of Asuras and who always held Sakti, who was adorable by all.

There is a like resembling the ocean known as Skandasara, filled with cool, tasteful and clean water, its depth is beyond measure.

The lake possessing, wonderful merits, is lodged close to Kartikeya. Vamadeva the great sage was seated over the bank of the lake taking in the same with his disciple.

The crowd of the sages was lodged over the peak of the mountain serving Kartika was seating over the peacock and looked like the rising sun.

He had four arms, all his limbs were beautiful, adorned with all the ornaments including the crown, adored by other and holding a Sakti and a cock.

In his other hands he displayed Varada and abhaya-mudra. Finding Kartikeya in this form Vamadeva, the great sage, worshipped him and then eulogised him.

Vamadeva said, “O propounder of Pranava, providing the interpretation of pranava, the seed of the word pranava, you are totally the form of pranava, salutation to you again and again.

You are the form of Vedanta, propounder of the meaning of Vedanta, well aware of the meaning of Vedanta, you are respected by the people, salutation to you again and again.

O Kartikeya, you devoid in the heart like care of the human beings, salutation to you. You are Guhya and well versed in the secret scriptures. Salutation to you.

Your form is smaller than the smallest and bigger than the biggest. You are well aware of the greater and the lesser the lord in the great Atman salutation to you.

You could make the Danavas inactive, having the lustre like the sun, wearing the garland of Mandara flowers, adorned with all the ornaments including the crown, O Skanda, salutation to you.

You are the son as well as the disciples of Siva. You are devoted to Siva. You shown welfare on him. You are dear to Siva and delight both Siva and Parvati. Therefore salutation to you.

O intelligent Kartikeya- the son of Ganga, salutation to you. O Son of Uma, the dweller of the forest of Sati, salutation to you.

You possess the body of the six types of mantras and the tantras, you prescribe the six types of arthas, you remain away from the six types of the paths, and having six faces. Salutation to you.

You have twelve eyes, twelve arms, holding twelve attributes and having twelve of arms, salutation to you.

When four armed, you hold Sakti and a cock and remain peaceful. You bestow the boons. You are quite biased and destroys of the demons salutation to you.

His heart is marked with the kumkuma of the breast of Skanda sakti. You delight you brother Ganesa.

You glory is sing by Brahma and other gods, besides the sages, and kinnaras. You are quite auspicious, spotless crown of the gods adore with the garland of flowers, salutation to your lotus like feet.

Thus, whosoever reads the divine stotra recited by Vamadeva or listens to it, he achieves the supreme place.

This stotra immensely enhances wisdom, devotion to Siva, length of life, health, as well as the riche. It also fulfils all the desires always.

Thus the sage Vamadeva eulogised Kartikeya and then circumambulated him thrice, after which he prostrated before him on the ground.

Again he offered his salutation to him prostrating before him. Thereafter, O Brahmanas, he took his seat besides Kartikeya.

Vamadeva, having the welfare of others in mind, when recited the stotra, Kartikeya, the son of lord Mahadeva was immensely surprised.

Kartikeya then spoke to Vamadeva, “I am pleased with your devotion and prayer. What tvpe of good can I do for you?

O sage, you are already the foremost of the yogis. You are complete in yourself and are completely in attached. People like you have no desire.

Still for the protection of the dharmo and for the bestowing of the grace on the people, the ascetics like you roam about on earth.

O Brahmana, in case you intend to listen, then I shall speak out for the welfare of the universe.”

Then Vamadeva, the great sage, listening to the words of Kartikeya with respect, bowed in reverence to him and spoke in a deep sound.

Vamadeva said, “O lord, you are the supreme Isa, you can bestow the enormous riches, besides being omniscient and the supreme performer. You possess all the Saktis.

We are the jivas. You can express nothing before the supreme soul. This is because of your grace that you are speaking to me.

O abode of wisdom, I feel successful because of a fraction of your knowledge. I am asking you having been unpaid by your grace. You would kindly forgive me for your on deity.

Pranava totally stands for Paramesvara lord Pasupati, who gets the people or pasus released from the bondages, is the spokesman for him.

Lord Siva, when commanded by pranava gets the people released from the bondages in a moment. Therefore the success is achieved with the mantra om for Siva.

Several of the divine Srutis say, “All is om, om is Brahma and everything is Brahman.

O commander of gods salutation to you, the lord of the gods and the ascetics. Salutation to you since you are the perfect one.

In the present situation there is nothing distinct from Siva in this world. Lord Siva assumes all the forms, while lord of Mahesvara pervade everywhere.

The universal and personal application of pranava had been heard by me. O lord, but I never had a preceptor like you, who could speak out all those details to me.

Therefore we compassionate on me and enlighten me about its measuring in accordance with the rules of instruction and the conduct of the good.

My lord is the preceptor who can shelter all the bondages. Therefore, O preceptor, you enlighten me over the meaning of the same.

When so prayer by the sage, Skanda, bowed to Sadasiva, the very pranava itself, who represents the thirty eight excellent digits and followed by the excellent sages. He then started explaining the path of welfare well guarded in the Vedas.

## Chapter 12 - Procedure of the Nandi Sraddha, Brahmayajna etc.

Kartikeya said, “O excellent sage, O great ascetic, O Vamadeva, you are blessed indeed. You are a staunch devotee of Siva and the best possessing the knowledge of Sivatattva.

There is nothing in the three worlds, which is unknown to you. Still am speaking to you for the several sastras. Because of the wonderful delusion of Paramesa, they are being cheated.

They are unaware of Mahesvara, who happens to be the form of pranava. They themselves are the saguna and nirguna Brahman and are the producers of the gods.

Taking an oath, raising my right arm, I speak to you that this is true and the total truth.

Siva has been described mainly as pranava in the Vedas, Smrtis, Sastras and the Puranas.

Reaching at that place, the words recede and achieving its bliss ten learned person, is not afraid of anything.

It is the place from which the creation of Brahma, Visnu, Indra and others besides the entire creation starts. The one who is born ahead of the Pancamahabhutas and the sense organs.

There one who is not born from anywhere above time, in which there is no light of the sun, moon, or the lightning.

Through the lustre of which the entire universe is illuminated. He is the supreme lord possessing all the fortunes.

He is the due, to whom the desirous of salvation, conceive as lodged in the middle of the sky, omniscient, resplendent soul and consciousness Siva.

He is omnipresent, the form of splendour, and knowledge, whose splendid Sakti, is comprehensible through the emotions, besides being Saguna and Nirguna, unblemished and auspicious.

In his three form, he is gross, subtle and even beyond them. O Sage, the people, desirous of moksa, should be careful about the same.

He is the primordial and the eternal lord, is the supreme soul and possessing the entire knowledge. He has rituals as his innate nature.

Sadasiva is the form of the lord of the gods. The lord has five mantras for his body and five digits for his physical form.

His complexion is like the pure crystal rock, the smiling face, having the cool lustre, has five faces, ten arms and three eyes.

He is faces resemble those with the faces, wears crowns is the primordial Isanadeva, has Aghora (kind) for his heart and has Vamadeva for his prevails parts, and Sadhya as his feet.

He is both Sakala and Niskala, besides being omniscient, possessing the six saktis and omniscience constitute his six limbs.

He has the power of word throbbing in his lotus like heart. The Manamohini Sakti is lodged to his left.

I shall now explain the pranava souled lord with reference to his six entitles and in his composite and personal nature.

O sage, I shall initially speak the sequence of the instructions, which should be listened by you. Indeed the four casts are well known in the world.

Of these, the first three castes have the access to the Vedas. The Sudras, who have been declared as the out castes, have the only right to serve others.

Embracing the duties of each respective caste, the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and the Vaisyas should followed the dharma as propounded in the Vedas and the Agamas and none else.

Paramesvara, who initiated the path of the Vedas has declared that with the following of the dharmo as propounded in the Vedas and the Srutis a person meets with success.

With the earning of the merits, by following the dharma as propounded in the Varnasrama, adoring the Paramesvara, several of the sages have achieved the Sayujya of Siva.

The gods are pleased with the following the path of the yajna, the sages with the following of the Brahmacarya (or celibacy) and the manes get pleased with the performing of Sraddha and oblating of water. This has been ordained by the Vedas.

Thus a person getting free from the three debts (of gods, Rsis and the manes), embracing the Vanaprastha (asrama), should practice for yoga, bearing heat and cold, pleasure and pain, controlling all the senses, controlling the desire for eating food etc. By doing this the wisdom will be stabilised and thousand would become unwavering.

Thus with the purification of the soul, one should perform all the karmas. Then leaving aside all his activities, he should get devoted to the pursuit of the knowledge, which alone would bestow the parts of liberation and his identity with Siva. It is the extremely excellent path and renders unblemished the persons who have controlled their minds.

O intelligent one, I speak out for the sake of the welfare of the world, because of my love for you, which should be listened by you.

An ascetic shall contact a preceptor, who is well-versed in the interpretation of the sastras besides the knowledge of Vedanta and who is the best of the acaryas.

The wise ascetics should go to the acarya, appropriately prostrate before him and please him by various means, because the preceptor represents Siva while Siva is the preceptor. With this resolve in his mind he should request the preceptor.

With the permission of the preceptor, he should perform vrata for twelve days consuming the milk alone. On the fourth day of the bright fortnight or on the tenth day, taking a bath in the early morning and getting free from the daily puja, the learned man should invite the preceptor and perform the Nandi-Sraddha appropriately.

The Visvedevas are Satyavasus. In the Sraddha of the gods, Brahma, Visnu and Siva in that of the sages, those born of the celestial woman from human beings, in that of the Pitrs, Vasu, Rudra and Aditya in that of the human beings the four sages, Sanaka and others, in that of the Bhutas, the five great elements are included.

The group of sense organs include consists of eyes etc., that of the Bhutas is of four types. In the pitr sraddha, the father, grandfather and the great grandfather are included.

In the Matr-Sraddha the mother, grandmother and the great grandmother are included. The Sraddhas of one's own father, grandfather and the great grandfather are performed with their spouses. In the Sraddha of the mother's father, the three ancestors of the maternal grandfather are included.

In every Sraddha, two Brahmanas are to be fed. Inviting them, a person himself performing the acamana they should be made to wash their feet.

Then he shall pray, “Let the dust particles from the feet of the Brahmanas, purify me. They are the cause of the well beings and destroy all the misfortunes and serve as a bridge over the vast ocean of the universe. Let the particles of dust protect me.

For the removal of the thick darkness of misfortunes, they serve as the thousand suns, for the fulfilment of the desires, they serve as the wish fulfilling cow and let the dust of the feet of the Brahmans with auspicious bodies, protect us.”

In this way performing the *japam* one should prostrate over the earth and then with his mind devoted towards Siva, he should be seated, facing the east and perform *pranayama* thrice.

Highlighting the *tithis* etc. he shall state “As a connected rite to my formal remuneration, I have to perform the eight *Sraddhas* starting with the *Sraddha* of Visvadevas and ending with the *Sraddha* of *matamaha.* I shall perform these *Sraddha* based on the entire fortune rites, with your permission. After performing the *Samkalpa,* then touch the water and stand up to start inviting the Brahmanas properly. With the *pavitra* held in the hand, he shall touch the hands of the Brahmanas and should say.
