“I have invited you both in the form of Visvadevas, which may be accepted by you.

You be pleased with me, “This is the process everywhere. After conclusion of the varana rite, the diagrams should be drawn.

Starting from the north, all the ten diagrams should be adored with unbroken race. The Brahmanas should be seated in the same sequence and pour unbroken race over their feet.

Speaking out the names of the Visvadevas, the Brahmanas should be lodged over their seats and should address them saying, “This is the padya for you." Thus speaking, he should offer, kusa, flowers, unbroken race and the water.

Offering the padya to the Brahmanas, he should himself wash the feet and should make them sip acamana facing north asking them to be seated over their asanas.

Speaking that this is the asana for the Visvadeva Brahmana, the kusasana should be offered to them, he should himself be seated holding kusa in his hand.

He should then address them, “Both of you should remain alert in this Nandimukha Sraddha.” The Brahmanas should say, “we are quite alert.”

Then he shall say “Both of you should accept my invitation.” The two Brahmins should say, “We accept it.”

Let our task be established, he should speak out. You the Brahmanas should be kind to us.” He should make such a request to them.

Thereafter the food should be served over the banana leaves washed with water and the water should be sprinkled with the kusa grass.

Sprinkling the waters, he should gracefully carry each vase with food and reciting the mantra “prthvi te patram'' should places the vases on the ground. Then reciting the names of the gods, the unbroken race should be placed over them.

Taking water in the palm, reciting the mantra devaya svaha the water should be sprinkled over the food items. At the end he should recite “idam na mama". This is the process everywhere.

With the remembering of whose lotus like feet or with the reciting of whose name all the mistakes are condoned, I offer my salutation to the same Sadasiva.

Reciting these mantras, he should again speak out “The Nandi Sraddha which has been performed by me, this is quite appropriate you kindly speak out the same.”

The Brahmanas say, “Be it so”. Then pleasing the Brahmanas with food daksina etc., he should fill the water in his palm and then drop it over the ground. Then he should prostate before them.

The large hearted host with wisdom, should then pray to them with folded hands, “Let the Sraddha performed by me turn as the nectar.”

Thereafter should get the “namaste Rudra”, Camaka sukta and Purusa sukta recited appropriately. Devoting his mind to Sadasiva, he should recite the Siva-mantra five times.

After the consuming of the food is finished, the Rudra sukta should be recited and then the host should beg forgiveness from the Brahmanas. Then he should offer water to the Brahmanas reciting the mantra amrtapidhanamasi.

Washing their feet, they should be taken to the place of the pindas, keeping silent facing east, should perform pranayama thrice.

He should then speak, “Now I shall perform the pindadana relating to the Nandimukha Sraddha, performing the Samkalpa, starting from the south and to the north, nine lines should be drawn and twelve pieces of upper parts of the kusa grass should be spread over the five places for Daksa and the other gods.

He should them he should water, unbroken race, flowers etc. In the second space meant for the Matr-paksa, water should be sprinkled, then he should say, “Let the manes be seated here.” this speaking he should offer the water and unbroken rice there. According to this sequence also, he should offer the unbroken rice and water.

Then reciting the names of the gods, he should offer the pindadana to the gods in a sequence.

As per provision of his own Grhyasutra, pindadana should be offered at the five places including the father. Then keeping silent, water and unbroken rice should be poured for achieving of the best result.

The pindas should then be lifted up gracefully and serve them to the cow or should consign them into the water. After reciting the Svastivacana, he should take his food with the kiths and kins, sitting with them.

On the next day getting up early in the mooring, the learned host should perform a vrata, he should have his hair of the entire body, except that in the armpits and the private parts, removed and should perform the daily routine thereafter.

During the time of Sraddha, one should not shave his hair, beard and moustaches, nor should be have his nails cut, but he should get them removed after the performing of Sraddha, then after taking bath, he should wear the washed clothes should as a rule sip the acamana water, twice and applying the dust over the body appropriately, Svastivacana should be get recited.

Then sprinkling the water over the body, sitting aside the daksina for the acarya and for homa dravya, should give away all the things meant for Siva to the Brahmanas and the devotees of the lord should offer daksina to Siva in the form of the preceptor, as well as the costumes etc., the host should prostrate before the preceptor on the ground. Removing the card, Kaupin, costumes, danda should be removed and the ground should be washed with water.

Collecting the homa drayvas and Samidhas etc. should be packed up and dropped in the ocean, river, mountain or Sivalaya, a forest, cowshed, or any other auspicious place. Then sitting over an asana one should recite the name of Siva.

The Brahma mantra together with Omkara (om namo Bhrahmane) should be recited thrice and also recite "Agni mile Purohitam”.

The mantras like the Agnir-vai, “Ise tvorje tva” should be uttered and them the mantra “agna ayahi, vitaye, Sannodevi rabhistaye” along with ma, ya, ra, sa, ta, ja, bha no, la, ga should be repeated.

This shall continue for five years according to the tradition. Then he shall repeat the text of grammar, mimansa and Vedanta. He shall repeat the names of the gods as well.

Then he shall perform the japam of Brahma, Indra, Surya, Candra, Prajapati, Atma, Antaratma, the jnanatma, and Paramatman. All the related mantras should start with Om and namah should be suffixed at the end of each one of them, using the dative case. Then he should carry a first fall of power of the fried grams, reciting of pranava, and then eat it. Then he should perform acamana twice, reciting the mantras using prefix as om and suffix as namah, reciting atma, antaratma, Prajapati, svaha should be added to all the mantras at the end performing the japam at the same time. Then reciting pranava with the milk, curd, ghee and distributing them thrice, one should perform the acamana twice.

Then turning the face to the east, sitting firmly over the asana with the completely stable mind, should perform pranayama thrice appropriately.

## Chapter 13 - Procedure for embracing Sanyasa

(renunciation)

Subrahmanya said, “Thereafter at the time of noon, having been filled with devotion one should take a bath and then collect the materials like the scent, flowers, unbroken race etc.

Then reciting the hymn “ganantva Ganapati” Ganesa should be invoked appropriately. Ganesa has the red complexion, huge body, adorned with all the ornaments. In his lotus like hands he hold the noose, goad, rosary in his hands. He does always good to his devotees.

Thus Ganesa the son of Siva should be invoked and meditated upon. He should then be adored offering him the payasam, coconut jaggery, coconuts and gud (balls of sugarcane juice).

Then offering the excellent naivedya, the betel leaf should be offered. Thus pleasing him, one should offer salutation to him, offering prayer to him at the same time.

According to one's own Grhya sutra, the rites of homa should be performed concluding wit the sharing of the clarified butter in the Aupasana fire (a fire used for domestic worship, household fire).

After offering the purnahuti reciting the three Rks “Bhu Svaha", the rites shall be concluded. Thereafter the Gayatri mantra should be repeated till late in the afternoon.

The evening prayer shall be performed after taking bath, besides the sacrificial rites and inform his preceptors accordingly.

The homa shall be performed with the offering of the Caru with different faggots of sticks, cooked rice and ghee, reciting Rudrasukta. Lord Siva has at the same time to be conceived in the fire together with his spouse, besides the ire Brahmanas like Sadyojata etc. The host shall remember Gauri, while performing homa (sacrifice) reciting the mantra “Gaurirmimaya” etc.

Repeating the mantra “agneya svistakrte svaha” he shall perform the sacrifice, displaying the mystic passes with a steady mind, he should be seated over a cloth, deer skin or durva (grass) to the north of the fire and recite the Gayatri mantra silently till the time of dusk.

Then he should take a bath. In case he is not quite healthy, he can apply ashes over his body. Thereafter he should cook caru in the same fire.

Taking it out, he should place it over the kusa-grass to the north. Then mixing the ghee in the Caru he should recite the five mantras from Vyahrti a well as Rudrasukta.

Reciting the five mantras including lean, devoting his mind to Siva's lotus like feet. Then he shall perform the japam for Prajapati, Indra, Visvedevas and Brahma as well with dative case endings. Thereafter the pranava and other mantras shall be repeated ending with Svaha. He shall perform Svastivacana and say “Agnaye svaha”, display the mystic symbols in front of the fire and utter “pramaye svaha", offering five ahutis to svistakrt fire. The Rudrasukta shall then be repeated besides the fire Brahmanas, the Caturvyuha mantras, homa and the mystic gestures according to the provision of the Vedas.

The same process shall be adopted in respect of the other gods together with their connected rites. After performing of these rites, starting with the fire, the viraja homa of the atman shall be performed for self purification in the four of the twenty six principles.

He shall speak, “Let the tattvas be purified”. For the purification of principle, the mantra "Arunaketukas” has to be repeated. He shall perform homa quietly with Caru and ghee remembering at the same time, the lotus like feet of Siva. O sage, the principles start with Prthvi and end with Purusa.

Prthvi, sound, speech and ear are five each. The four head, sides, belly and the calves have to be added in the group- skin etc. The dhatu group comprises of seven, while pranas are five in number. Anna (food) etc. are the five sheaths. Samkalpa comprises of mind, citta, intellect, ego and khyati. The gunas come afterwards followed by Prakrti and Purusa. The latter is the only enjoyer while the five principles are the objects of enjoyment. O great sage, the destiny, time, attachment, vidya, kala are born of Maya.

It has been propounded in the Vedas that Maya is the same as Prakrti. The principles as mentioned in the Sruti are born of that.

The Vedas also declare that the destiny is the nature of Kala. This set of five is called the wheel of five.

A learned person who is ignorant of these five tattvas is considered as a fool. Niyati is below Prakrti and Purusa is above the same like the eye of the crow. This set of five- the pure Vidya Mahesvara, Sadasiva Sakti and Siva, is called the Vidya tattva or Siva tattva. This is described in the Vedic texts as Prajna nam Brahma”.

O excellent sage, all the tattvas from the Prthivi to Siva, they should be absorbed in self and purified.

He shall mention the god with the eleven mantras and the word Sivajyotis shall be used in dative case.

After svaha he shall say “na mama ” or not for me. This is the motif of renunciation which is indicated. In the mantra of Vividya Kastapota, after the word “vyapakaya” the word Paramatman is to be added. The word Sivajyotis, Visvabhuta and Ghasanotsuka have to be mentioned in dative case. After mentioning the name of the god, the word devaya is to be added.

After Visvarupa in the mantra, uttisthasva, the word purusaya shall be spoken adding the word “om svaha".

At the end of the word lokatraya the words Vyapine Paramatmne, Sivayedam na namah shall be added.

The rites have to be concluded according to one's own branch of the Veda. The Caru mixed with ghee should be consumed and then daksina in gold etc. should be given to the priest. After the ritualistic said off of Brahma, one should perform homa (yajna) concerning the morning adoration.

One should recite the mantra sam mam sincantu Maruta. He shall warm his hand over the fire repeating the mantra “ya te Agne and superimposed the fire in his own Atman the abode of the universal soul. He shall perform the morning prayer offering prayer to the sun. He shall enter upto the navel, performing the japam of the mantras with devotion, pleasure and firmness.

The host who had been maintaining sacrificial fires regularly, shall perform the Prajapatya rite in the yajna fire and give away his entire possessions as charity.

The Brahmana shall establish the fire in his heart and then desert his home becoming a recluse. Reciting the first foot of the Gayatri mantra, and speaking Savitrim pravesayami, uttering bhurom, uttering the second foot and then utter Savitrim pravesayami.

Then he should utter bhuvaram uttering the third foot, then speaking Savitri pravesayami, he should speak out Suvaram. Then all the three feet should be recited collectively.

O excellent sage, with a stable mind, should speak out “Savitrim pravesayami, om, bhurbhuvah svarom.

The goddess Savitri has five faces, ten arms, fifteen eyes and resides in half of the body of Siva.

Her head is adorned with a new crown of gold studded with gems. Her forehead is decorated with the digit of the moon. She has the complexion of the spotless crystal gem. In her ten hands she holds ten attributes.

She is adorned with the ornaments like a hara (garland), keyura (bangles), and the anklets etc. She is clad in the device costumes.

Brahma, Visnu, gods, Rsis, Danavas, Gandharvas, and the humans adore her. She is Siva who resides in the souls of all and is also known as Siva.

She is the pleasant spouse of lord Sadasiva and is unborn, nirguna, triguna. She is the one who produced the three worlds also known as Jagadamba- the mother of the universe.

Thus thinking one should perform the japam for Gayatri. This three footed primordial goddess bestows Brahmanatva.

A sinful person who dose not adore Siva-Gayatri in such a manner, he has to languish in the terrific hell for a kalpa.

She is born of Vyahrtis and is absorbed in Vyahrtis. The vyahrtis emerge out of pranava and are ultimately absorbed into the same.

Pranava is the form of Siva and is the foremost aspect of the Vedas. It is the best of all the mantras and indeed happens to be the king of the mantras.

Siva indeed is pranava and pranava is none else then Siva. There is hardly any difference in the speaker and the words spoken by him.

It is this very mantra that Siva speaks to individual souls who leave off their bodies at Kasi to attain liberation hereafter.

Because of this the excellent sages, lodge om the one litter form of Siva in their hearts and meditate upon the same.

The three people who are patient, desirous of attaining knowledge, the recluses, besides the worldly people, who removing all the worldly attracting from their minds, adore the supreme Siva.

After absorbing Gayatri in pranava which is identical with Siva, he shall recite the hymn, aham Vrksasya reriva.

One should recite the verse starting from “yaschandasamamrsabhah to Srutam me gopaya. Then he should say uttheto ham.

O sage, then he should recite the mantra in the low, medium and high tone with pranava in order of creation, sustenance and dissolution.

In this order, he shall say, om bhuh, I shall renounced, om bhuvah- I have renounced, om suvah, I have renounced. Then he shall say the composite vyahrtis om bhuh, bhuvah, suvah.

O sage, he shall say “I have renounced after meditating on Sadasiva in the heart in low, medium and high pitch gradually.

Thus becoming alert, reciting the praisa mantra all the living beings should be fearless from me. This mantra abhayam sarva-bhutebhya mattah Svaha should then be recited.

Then filing the hand cups with water it should be released to the east. Then he should remove the tuft and yajnopavita, from his hands, should recite the mantras, holding the water in his palm thus : “vahni jayam svaha”. Then he should speak out “om bhuh samudram svaha”.

Reciting the aforesaid 'Praisa’ mantras should drop the yajnopavita and the Sikha in the water. Then performing the acamana (sipping water) should remove his clothes and drop them on the ground.

He should then walk more then seven steps towards the east. Then the acarya should ask him to stop.

He should say to him, “Give him the kaupin and the danda. O lord, you kindly accept the kaupin and the danda for the worldly behaviour.

Then the kaupin with cord and the ochre coloured robes. He should accept both of them and then sip the acamana water. The acarya should then take him as his disciple.

Then he should recite the mantra " Indrasya vajrosi”. Then he should accept the danda reciting the prayer and the mantra “Sakhaya”.

Then he should go to the preceptor and devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, controlling his sense organs, prostrate on ground thrice.

Getting up and looking at his, preceptor with devotion, should be seated near the feet of the preceptor with folded hands.

Before the start of work, he should collect the cow-dung and prepare bells of the size of the big myrobalam and dry them up.

When the long balls are dried up with the sun rays, he should place then over the fire of the homa. After the homa is over, he should collect the ashes and keep them carefully.

Then the preceptor, take the ashes which are made from the Viraja fire should sanctify reciting the mantra Agniriti bhasma.

Repeating the mantra Agniriti bhasma he should apply the sacred ashes over the body of the disciple from head to foot. Repeating the five mantras Isana, Tryayusa, Tryambakam Yajamahe, he should apply the Tripundra marks too beginning with head.

Getting filled with devotion, the excellent disciple should meditate upon Siva, the spouse of Uma.

Then the preceptor should place his hand over the disciple's head and should speak. Initially revealing the name of Rsi, he should whisper thrice pranava thrice into the ear of the disciple.

Then the preceptor should kindly reveal the six types of meanings of pranava to the disciple.

The disciple then prostrate before the preceptor a dozen times. He should always remain subservient to the preceptor. He should not do anything without his permission.

At the command of the preceptor, the disciple should engage himself in the study of Vedanta and should try to study the nirguna and saguna form of Siva.

The preceptor shall make the disciple perform all the rites in the morning to the japam including the practice of hearing.

The disciple shall perform the worship there in the mandala named Kailasaprastara, as prescribed way by Siva.

In each he is unable to adore the deity, worshipped by his preceptor, he shall take a crystal Sivalinga along with the pedestal.

“I shall rather cast my life and cut off my head, than take meals without worshipping Siva.”

This is the vow to be taken by the disciple devoted to Siva, in the presence of the preceptor, which shall be repeated thrice by the disciple with a firm mind.

Thus the disciple shall worship lord Siva daily with a devoted heart and diligent mind, following the path of five avaranas.

## Chapter 14 - Pranava in the form of Siva

Vamadeva said, “O six faced lord, ocean of the entire divine nectar like knowledge, son of Siva, the lord of all the gods and remover of the miseries of four devotees.

O lord, what is the meaning of the six type of knowledge? How does it bestow the desired reward? What is the meaning of the six types? What is their knowledge?

What is contained therein? What shall be the reward of knowing about it? O Kartikeya, you please answer me on the subject broached by me.

O Kartikeya, without knowing the interpretation about the same, I having been eluded with the pasu-sastra and the Maya of Siva.

I have sought refuge in your lotus-feet. Glancing at me for a long time with your eyes drenched with the nectar of sympathy, you shall bless me.

With your kind vision, I shall become free from delusion and shall acquire the nectarine portion of the knowledge of the feet of Siva.”

Listening tot he words of the excellent sage Vamadeva, the immensely learned like, spoke the words which could terrify those opposed to Sivasastra.

Kartikeya said, “O excellent sage, you have enquired about the perfect knowledge of Siva in his composite and individual form. I shall explain the same, which should be listened by you.

O Suvrata, I shall explain the same in detail. In fact the perfect knowledge comprises of the meaning of pranava by realising the combination of six topics.

The first is the four of mantra. The second is the form of tantra, the third is Devartha, the fourth is prapancartha, the fifth one displays the form of the preceptor, and sixth is the form of disciple.

O excellent sage, I shall explain to you the form of mantra which bestows the perfect knowledge over a person.

The first vowel is a (akara), the fifth vowel is u (ukara), the fifth letter of fifth class of consonants bindu and nada. These five letters are mentioned in the Vedas as omkara.

The composite form of all these is om has been described in the Vedas. Keeping in view bindu and others this nada is the composite form of all. The set of four with bindu as the fifth is established as vyasti in the pranava which represents Siva. O intelligent one, now you listen to the form of yantra denoting Sivalinga.

The pedestal has to be made beneath all. Then the first vowel a then the vowel u, the final letter of the class of Pa i.e. Ma followed by the bindu and nada. When the yantra is completed, all the desires are fulfilled.

The yantra is surrounded by pranava itself. The nada shall be known with the sound emerging therefrom.

O sage Vamadeva, I shall now speak about the secret topic of the deity, because of my lore for you.

The Vedas have described the Brahma-pancakavacaka Omkara in considerable details from the mantras “Sadyojatam prapadyami to Sada Sivoham.

The subtle five deities of Pranava-Brahman, all represent the form of Siva. Therefore they have not been defined separately.

The Pancaka-mantra of Siva represents Siva as well as the image of Siva, because there is hardly any difference between the image and he one whose image a made.

The form of Siva has already been described starting from the mantra “Isanamukutopetah”. Now you listen from me about his five heads.

Five faces of Siva have been highlighted from pancama to sadyojata etc. And ending upto Isana.

The four Brahmanas constitute a caturvyuha for the lord Tsana, the well known Brahman. These five put together form the composite. O sage, from Purusa to Sadyojata the four constitute the individual.

This set of five is the wheel of blessing. It is the same as Brahman. It is subtle, unblemished and free from ailment.

The anugraha or blessing is two fold viz. appearance and disappearance. The lord who bestows the higher or the lower salvation is another.

These are the two functions of Sadasiva. The five functions of creation etc. come under anugraha or blessing.

O sage, for the creation of the universe, five deities have been prescribed. All the five of them have the form of Parabrahman and they bestow welfare.

Anugraha-cakra is beyond tranquillity and is the greatest bliss presided over by Sadasiva. It consist of a digit.

This position is achieved by those whose minds are immensely devoted to Pranava or Siva besides the yatis.

O excellent sages, the achieving the position by the grace of Siva and enjoying enormous pleasures with the lord, in the form of Brahman, the sages attain equality with Siva at the time of dissolution. They never fall again in the ocean of the universe.

The eternal Vedas ordain “te brahma loka ” etc. The glory of Siva is the composite form itself.

The Atharvasira says, “He is possessed with enormous glory and prosperity. He is the bestower of all the fortunes.

There is no region higher than that of Siva, the universe is only an extension of the five Brahmanas, nivritti and other digits emerge from Brahman. All of them taking to the subtle forms, well known as causes.

O Suvrata (sage of good rites), the set of five Brahmanas is the cause of five cosmos.

O excellent sage, the five types of the padarthas i.e. Purusa, Srotra, Vani, Sabda and akasa emerge from Isana in the form of Rrahma nr Purusa.

O excellent sage, the five forms of Purusa i.e. Prakrti, tvaca (skin), hands, sense of touch and Vayu (wind) emerge from Brahman.

Ahamkara (pride), eyes, feet, colour and Agni (fire), emerge from the Aghora form of Brahman.

The wisdom, tongue, payu (rectum), juice and water emerge out of the Brahman called Vamadeva.

The mind, nose, linga (organ of generation), fragrance and earth emerge out of the Sadya Brahman. The whole universe is identical with the five brahman.

Pranava, expressive of Siva is taught through the yantra and is composite of five letters. The four viz., bindu etc. constitute the form of yantra in the Saiva cult. Pranava is the highest mantra- the form of Siva himself.

## Chapter 15 - Creation and dissolution of the universe

Siva said, “O beautiful, After this, I shall explain the mode of creation for the set of four, Mahesa etc. from Sadasiva.

Sadasiva is the lord of space having the subtle form. The forms of Mahesvara, Rudra, Brahma and Visnu are the expansion of his forms alone.

Mahesa emerges out of a thousand the amsa of Sadasiva. Purusa has innumerable forms and as such he is the lord of the wind. Maya-sakti is lodged to his left. He is the lord of all the activities.

Isa, Visvesvara, Paramesa and Sarvesa form the excellent Tirobhava cakra.

The Tirobhava is of two types. One appears in the form of Rudra and the other appears in the form of combination of the jivas.

Upto the time the sins or the merits exist in the body, the group of jivas remain. But with neutralisation of the karmans he takes to the form of blessing.

Isvara and others are the four deities, who are identical with the great Brahmana, free from alternatives or ailments.

The Tirobhava cakra is tranquil. This excellent region is presided over by Mahesvara.

Those who adore Mahesa with devotion attain this region. The devotees of Mahesvara attain the Salokya type of liberation.

The image of Rudra emerges from the thousandth amsa of Mahesvara. He has the Aghora form of the face and is the lord of the principle of resplendence.

The goddess Gauri is lodged to his left. He is the lord, who is the destroyer of all. Of him Vyasti is born the set of four Siva etc.

O excellent sage, he had the extremely divine and wonderful calves which cause destruction and are known by the names of Siva, Hara, Bhava and Hrda.

The people with wisdom have described the Samhara cakra have conceived to be of three types including nitya and others. Nitya is one in which the jiva remains in slumber. The second is conditioned dissolution of Brahma. The third is the final dissolution. These have been highlighted by the Vedic texts. O excellent sage, the dissolution has been classified into three by the illustrious Rudra for the maturing of the activities of the individual souls and for their rest. The souls when released from their recurring births are ultimately lodged in the great Atman itself.

In this way the three activities of Rudra concerning the dissolution have been explained by me. Now I shall explain the five activities of the lord relating to the creation of the universe.

O sage, Bhava and other gods are mentioned therein who are all the forms of Brahman and bestow welfare over the universe.

The wheel of universe has the kala in the form of Vidya. The spotless region is presided over by Rudra himself.

O sage, with the adoration of Rudra, and those who are devoted to him reach Rudraloka and achieve the Sayujya type of salvation.

Upto of the thousandth part of Rudra, emerges Visnu. In the form of Vamadeva-cakra, he presides over the water element.

He has Rama lodged to his left and he pretexts all. He has four arms eyes resembling the lotus lead, dark complexion, and holds Sankha and other attributes.

He has four forms including Vasudeva. He bestows liberation the Vaisnavas who are devoted to him.

This set of four consists of Vasudeva, Aniruddha, Sankarsana and Pradyumna. This excellent wheel of sustenance is well known.

Sustenance means the protection of the existing universe along with its creator till the completion of the pleasure of the souls, who reap the fruits of their deeds.

Protection is the responsibility of Visnu, during the sustenance also, the lord has to attend five activities including the creation etc.

Out of his deities, of whom Pradyumna is the foremost, are absolute, and devoid of distress. They cause bliss to the liberation souls.

O Brahman, this is the cakra in the form of glory, which is permanent and is presided over by Visnu. This happens to be the highest place.

Only those who serve the lotus like feet of Visnu can achieve the same. This cakra bestows the Salokya type of salvation to those who are devoted to Visnu.

Brahma was born of a thousandth part of Visnu, having the face of Sadyojata. He happens to be the presiding deity of the earth.

Sarasvati is lodged to the left of the creator of the universe. He has four heads and because of his possessing the rajoguna he is red complexion.

He has four manifested forms including Hiranya-garbha, the other three are Virat, Purusa and Kala.

The Srsticakra is served by his sons like Bhrgu and others and fulfils all the desires besides showering all the pleasures.

Those who have the knowledge of creation, are well aware of the fact that this is the function of Brahma. Creation is the process of reunion of the soul with the body previously annihilated. The body which along with its means, ancillaries and results come out of Prakrti for gradual enjoyment. It is pleasing as long as it holds good.

O sage, these are the five functions of the lord in the creation of the universe. Kala and others have been termed as the deities.

The wheel of creation is in the form of turning sound. The charming region is presided over by Brahman and can be achieved by those who are dedicated to Brahman. It bestows Salokya and other types of liberation.

Even with regard to the set of four wheels the Pranava stands for Mahesa etc..

O sage, the Jagatcakra which is defined in the Vedas, with its glory, is called Pancaksara. This cakra is being eulogised by Srutis.

There is a single cakra comprising of Siva sakti. The five constituents of the universe are called Pancara.

The Alatacakra of earth, rotates like the half burnt wood, sometimes fading and sometimes burning. Because of this it is called the cakra (wheel).

Because of the enormousness of creation, it is called Prthu, the resultant of Siva's sakti, having immense lustre and golden features. The wheel dependant on golden splendour and is surrounded by water enclosed by fire.

The fire is covered by the wind, the wind is covered with the sky, Mahat-tattva is covered by the sky, while the sky is covered by bhutas and others. Mahat is covered by bhutas etc.

There are seven sheaths protecting the cakra of the universe. The quantity of water is ten times more than cakra, which is spread over the top and the bottom. O excellent sage, it should be treated as the cosmos.

With this interpretation because of the dwelling close to cakra the Vedas have conceived Visnu as the one who sleep in the water bed.

Siva together with his Sakti, indulges in several types of sports by blessing, disappearing, dissolution, sustenance and creation.

O sage, it is no use speaking much. In essence it could be said that Siva, endowed with Sakti, is all this and this is the definite conclusion.

## Chapter 16 - Omkara as the cause of creation

Suta said, “Listening to the interpretation of the Vedas as spoken by the preceptor, the excellent sage, still preserving a doubt in the supreme soul asked the great sage.

Vamadeva said, “O immensely learned lord, the form of the supreme bliss, I have drunk the nectar like form of Omkara as has been spoken from you lotus like face.

Presently my mind has been stabilised and my doubt has been removed. O Mahesani, O lord, I am going to ask something more from you. You kindly listen.

There is no doubt that right from Sadasiva to be sect, the position of the universe is visible.

The primordial lord is the cause of the creation of such universe, Then what is his form? Is he like a man, a woman or a eunuch?

Or is he of a composite form or has he some other form? This aspect has not been discussed. The people describe him variously having been deluded with the knowledge of the different scriptures.

The Srutis which define the creation of the universe, are with the world. The secret remains unknown even to Brahma, Visnu and other gods.

You kindly enlighten us on the considered opinion on the subject. It appears that a man feels, “I know everything,” “I perform everything”, this appears to be the practice. This is the practical knowledge based no experience and emerges out of the body, sense organs, mind, wisdom and pride.

Otherwise, it is creation to be the form of the great soul. The controversy arises out of these two aspects.

Therefore, you, uprooting the poisonous tree of ignorance, born out of the doubt, to enable the kalpavrksa of the non-duality of Siva to grow in a gigantic form. I shall be enlightened by you so that my mind may become the fertile ground for the growth of monistic knowledge of the Saivite cult. O lord of gods, by your benign favour I shall become wise.

Suta said, “Listening to the secret question relating to the Vedanta the lord spoke smilingly.

Subrahmanya said, “O sage, the secret has been revealed by Siva himself. O Vamadeva, when the lord Siva was revealing the secret to Parvati, the mother of the universe, this I was also present there.

I felt extremely pleased sucking her milk. Then with a stable mind, I thought about it again and again.

O sage, Vamadeva, O Son, I am going to speak the same to you. It is a secret subject, which you please listen from me.

O sage, the arguments in the philosophical texts books are extensive beginning with those of karmans (deeds) and the principle of existence. But O sage, these arguments shall be listened to with discrimination, by a learned person. Then it may yield wisdom.

Sword of the disciples have been taught by you, but which one of them is like you? The degraded ones even today doubt the sastras composed by Kapila.

Because of this, the six sages had pronounced a curse on them earlier. They were atheists, and their words should not be listened to.

There is no scope for inference that consists of five syllogisms. Finding the smoke, it is behaved that the mountain is on fire.

But here, O sage, the world is the object of perception. Its cause is the great Atman Siva, who should be known directly. The universe in the form of male and female is clearly perceived.

The human body has six sheaths. Of these, the three are born of the parts of the mother and other three are born of the parts of the father. This has been ordained by the Srutis.

The Vedas conceive the Brahman as comprising of existence knowledge and bliss (Saccidananda). The word existence has been used to separate it from the non-existence.

The exclusion of the insentient is effected by the word sentient. The word cit is used in all the three genders, but it signifies a male being. The word cit is the feminine gender in a synonym of the universal knowledge. When taken to mean light, it clearly illuminates.

Thus the light and cit (spirit) are both the cause of the universe, while sat and cit are also the cause of the universe.

Siva alone develops the feeling of Sakti and Siva. In case there is some dirt in the weak or the oil, the light could also be dirty or hazy.

The impurity as well as the dirt could be food in the funeral fire as well. When the change is introduced in, the same, can achieves the Siva tattva. This has been ordained by the Vedas.

The same cit sakti when is dependant on jiva, it becomes weak. It is to exclude it that the conception of Sakti is present.

A person possessing the Sakti is considered to be quite strong and this aspect is found in practice as well. O great sage Vamadeva, this aspect is quite well known in the Vedas.

Thus the Siva-tattva and Sakti-tattva have been are found in the supreme soul. With the combination of Siva and Sakti, Om achieves bliss.

O Sage, with this end in view, the devotees of Siva, by devoting their minds to Siva, have achieved the suspicion Siva.

The complete atmatattva of both Siva and Sakti happens to be the Brahman. It can be traced to the root of brh to increase or grew.

The enormity of size and the growth, can be noticed in the body of Sambhu comprising of five Brahmana. The word Brahman stands for the universe.

O Vamadeva, because of my affection for you, the genesis of the word Pranava shall be explained by me, on reversing the word Hamsa. You listen to the same.

In case the consonant Sa and ha are removed only Om is left out, which reveals the great Atman.

It is taken as a great mantra by the sages who possess enormous knowledge. The great mantra is quite subtle in nature and its analysis shall be revealed to you by me.

The great mantra is formed with S and the sixteenth vowel (:) = Sah and a + ha with the fifteenth vowel (m) = aham (so-ham).

It is the inverted form of hamsa. The meaning of the letter Sa is Siva. In conclusion it may be stated that Sakti form is expressed by the great mantra.

When the word So-ham is spoken at the time of the instruction of the preceptor, it denotes Siva in the form of Sakti. This is the great mantra, which is linked with the jiva. Then pasu, becoming a part of Siva, establishes an equality with him. In the passage of the Vedas i.e. prajnanam brahma, the meaning of prajnam is found in the same.

The word prajnana is undoubtedly the synonym of consciousness. O sage, it has been stated in the Siva-sastra that the soul is concession.

Thus the one who is concession (or cetana) who happens to be the abode of the knowledge and the activities of the world, such are entity having independent nature has been conceived as the soul.

I have described the Siva sutras (aphorism). In another aphorism of Siva, (Jnana-bandha) the lord speaks of the nature of the individual souls, wherein the word jnana stands for vague knowledge and activity.

Both knowledge and the activity are the first throbbing of the supreme Sakti. The same has been described as Parasakti in the Svetasvatara (Upanisad) and is eulogised there joyfully saying, “Power of knowledge and activity is natural.” the knowledge, activity and the will are taken to be the three eyes of Siva.

These three visions reaching the centre of the mind become the object of perception on the part of sense-organs, the individual soul enters these, then knows and acts.

Because of this, these are the forms of the soul alone. Now the meaning of the creation highlighting its identity with pranava is being explained.

‘Om mitidam sarvam' is an ancient Sruti. With the Sruti named Tasmad, the creation of the universe has been glorified.

O Vamadeva, I place before you the correct interpretation of the said Vedic hymn to enable you to achieve wisdom.

The combination of Siva and Sakti represents the supreme soul. Parasakti emerges out of the same and Cit-sakti is born out of it.

The Jnana-sakti is caused out of the same. From Ananda sakti emerges the Icchasakti, from which the Jnana sakti and Kriya sakti are born. O sage, the digits like nivrtti and others out of these Saktis.

Form the cit and Ananda saktis, emerge nada and the bindu. M (Mahesa) emerges from Icchasakti and the fifth vowel u emerges out of the Jnana sakti and the vowel a emerged out of the kriya sakti. O excellent sage, in this way the creation of pranaya has been explained. Now you listen to the creation of Panca-Brahmana.

Isvara was born of Siva, Purusa from Isana, Aghora from Purusa, and Sadyojata from Aghora were born.

With the matrkas of these five vowels etc. thirty eight digits emerged. Santikala emerged out of Purusa, while Vidyakala emerged out of Aghora.

Pratistha-kala emerged out of Vamadeva and Nivrtti kala emerged out of Sadyojata. From the mantra Isa and Sakti, the Mithuna-pancakas of Siva were born.

The Mithuna-pancakas are the cause of showering of grace etc. This has been ordained by the sages well-versed in the tattvas.

With the relationship of the words and their meanings, the five elements beginning with ether are born of this set of the five letters of pranava.

The sky has the attribute of sound, while the wind has two attributes of sound and touch. The fire on the other hand has two attributes viz. sound, touch.

The water has the attributes of the sound, touch, form and rasa. The earth has the attributes of sound, touch, form, rasa and the fragrance.

In the sequence of their respective attributes all their pervade in their respective bhutas and in the sequence of small they function in the reverse order.

The universe comprises of the five bhutas. Virat is the composite form of all of them, which is also called universe of the cosmos.

Right from the Prthu tattva to Siva tattva, the entire collection of the tattvas gets absorbed in the Virat form at the time of dissolution.

At the start of the universe, it comes out of the Virat Purusa again for the purpose of creation. It appears in the form of the gross cosmos and functions till the time of dissolution.

Mahesvara engages himself at his own world for the creation of the universe, which is Siva tattva.

Sakti tattva represents the desire to perform all the activities. The conflicts of Jnana sakti and the Kriya sakti represents Sadasiva tattva because of the excess knowledge inherent in the same.

O excellent sage, because of the enhancement of activity as compared to the knowledge, it should be taken as Mahesa-tattva when the Jnana and Kriya Saktis are in equal proportion, it should be treated as the spotless Siva tattva of Vidya.

After withdrawing his form of great glory with the intellect comprehending the difference between the illusion and reality among various emotions in the form of his own part when Siva becomes the recipient of all objects through illusion, he is called Purusa (the creator). The Vedic texts call it Tatsrstva.

The same jiva having been influenced with the Maya of Siva, performs several unpleasant deeds because of his foolishness.

O lord, the universe is not separate from Siva and the jiva who thinks himself to be separate, cannot be overpowered with delusion.

As the magician, after his performance, never feels surprised similarly a disciple possessing the fortunes and knowledge, attains the form of Siva.

The five Saktis of Siva viz., activity, knowledge, completeness, eternality and persuasiveness always shine, even in their shrinking form.

There is a set of tattvas of the individual soul: viz. Kala, Vidya, Raga, Kala and Niyati. Of these Kala is the cause of doing everything. Vidya is the means of certain tattvas. Raga stands for attachment to the sense objects.

The wisdom which desires or person to do and not to do something, is the controller. The all pervading power is the destiny, deserting which the jiva falls.

These are the five sheaths of the jiva because of this enveloping nature. It is the innermost and essential means called Pancakancaka.

## Chapter 17 - Advaita (non-dual) prana of Siva

Vamadeva said, “You have started earlier that destiny is below Prakrti and Purusa is above the same. Now how are you speaking contrary to the same.

O lord, you had spoken that below the same is the condensed form of Maya. O lord, you remove my doubt in this respect.

Kartikeya said, “The Saiva philosophy supports doctrine of advaita. Therefore it does not in anyway accept the doctrine of dvait or duality. It is because duality is perishable and advaita (non-duality) is in perishable.

Lord Siva is omniscient, all performer, lord of all, devoid of gunas, creator of all the three gods, besides being Brahman and is formed of existence, knowledge and bliss or Saccidananda.

The same lord Siva, because of his own will, getting squeezed with his Maya has turned as Purusa.

Here he is the enjoyer of all the five kalas. Therefore Purusa who is lodged in Prakrti enjoys all the virtues of Prakrti.

Thus inspite of his remaining at both the places, Purusa renders no opposition. He squeezing his own knowledge, beauty, etc. gets established.

He can be achieved with the use of sattva gunas. He possesses triple type of wisdom. Because of the sattva and other gunas possessed by him he also possesses the cit-Prakrti.

With the division from the Sattvika angle, the gunas emerge out of Prakrti. From the ganas emerge the wisdom known as Vastuniscayakarin, from which as born great ahamkara, wisdom and sense organs. The mind has two aspects, the thought and the doubt.

The sense organs comprise of ears, skin, eyes, tongue and nose besides the qualities, particularly sensed through those organs are the sound, touch, colour, taste and smell. The tanmatras emerge out of the Vaikarika ahankara.

The sages call them as the subtle principles. Now you should know about the organs of activity and their functions.

O sage, they comprise of the speech organs, hand, feet, arms, penis, and the vaginal passage. Their performance includes speaking, handling, moving, education and this and the enjoyment of the sexual pleasures.

The tanmatras (subtle elements) emerge from them as well as the ahamkara. Their subtle forms are sound etc.

In the same sequence the sky, the wind, fire, water and the earth were born. O excellent sage, these are called the Panca-mahabhutas.

Their performance include to relieve, to transport, to digit, to use force and to carry.”

Vamadeva said, “O Skanda, earlier you had spoken about Bhutasrsti from the kalas. Now you speak contrary to the same. I have developed a great doubt on the subject.

The letter A is atmatattva, the letter u is vidyatattva, and the letter Ma is sivatattva. O Vamadeva, it should be this thought over.

The bindu and nada are the basis of all the tattvas. O sage now you listen tot he names of their deities.

In the Vedas, Brahma, Visnu, Rudra, Mahesvara, and Sadasiva, are all the images of Siva alone.

This is what you had spoken earlier. Then how are you speaking to the contrary? I have a doubt whether they are formed of the tanmatras.

O Skanda, you kindly remove our doubt.” On hearing these words of the sage Kartikeya spoke.

Subrahmanya said, “O learned sage, listening with respect and attention. O sage, it is certain, that according to the Vedic texts, tasmad vai etasmad, testify that the five bhutas are born of the kalas. They are in the form of the gross cosmos. Because of this, Siva is conceived of the body of bhutas. Descending from the principle of Sivatattva to the principle of earth, O sage, they shall be mentioned in the subtle elements in order.

As the cause of the bhutas there is an identity between subtle and the kalas. O excellent among those well aware about Brahman are aware of the fact that there are no mutual conflicts there.

In this subtle and the gross universe, there are born planets like sun, moon, stars and others.

Whatever objects are there in the universe including Brahma, Visnu, Mahesa and other gods, besides the Bhutas, Dikpalas, the gods, manes, the asuras, Raksasas, humans, the mobile beings, animals, insects, serpents, trees and plants, creepers, osadhis, mountains, the eight rivers including the Ganga, the seven ocean possessing the enormous fortunes.

Whatever is there is lodged in it. O excellent sage, you think over the matter with the enormous wisdom possessed by you.

The world having males and females in the form of Siva and Sakti. The people like you who are well-versed in the divine knowledge, adore Siva.

O sage, everything is the form of Brahman or it is all the form of Rudra. Thus thinking one should worship the lord. Because Sadasiva is the soul of the universe.

Because of the concept of the thirty eight kalas, the concept of the duality remains present, but the one who has purified his soul, with the feeling, “I am Sadasiva,” becomes the preceptor Siva.

A preceptor having a pupil with such high ideals, is actually the form of Siva. Possessing the cosmos, deities, yantras, mantras, the preceptor, is indeed Siva.

O Brahmana, by the grace of the acarya getting free from all the bondages, the disciple who gets devoted to the lotus like feet of Siva, undoubtedly becomes the great soul.

Whatever things are there, because of the increase in the virtues, whether briefly or in expanded form, points towards pranava.

I have in fact out of affection spoken to you the essence of the advaita doctrine of the Vedas, which is free from the blemishes of attraction etc., which has been spoken by Siva and loved by him.

Whosoever takes my words to be otherwise, be he god or a human being, Siddha or Gandharva, out of arrogance, I shall sewer his head with my trident which serves as a black fire to the enemy.

O sage, you are yourself well-versed in the advaita non-dualistic doctrine of Siva and display the instructions and conduct of Siva.

With the touch of the ashes of whose body, a person who being a great sinner, is relieved of the position of pisaca and achieves liberation.

Possessing all the fortunes, you are considered to be a great Sivayogini world. With a mere glance from you an animal becomes Pasupati.

Whatever has been asked by you from me with respect, is only for the sake of educating the people, because the noble people wonder for the welfare of the people.

This is the supreme secret which shall always remain with you. You also devoting your mind with Pranava/Parmesvara wearing the ashes and Rudraksa over the body should propagate the doctrine of Siva among the people.

You are Siva and conduct yourself like Siva. You possess the feeling of advaita, therefore for the protection of the people, achieve the eternal bliss while roaming about.

Suta said, “After listening to the wonderful words on Vedanta, as brought out by Kartikeya, the sage was filled with humility. He bowed reverence and prostrated before Kartikeya several times and conducted himself like a bee hovering round his lotus like feet.

## Chapter 18 - Initiation for a disciple

Saunaka said, “What further question was asked by Vamadeva, after listening to wonderful sacred of Vedanta, from Kartikeya?

Vamadeva the yogi, engaged in the knowledge of Sadasiva, is quite graceful, because of whom emerged the divine narration.

Thus listening to the loving words of the sages, the intelligent Suta, getting pleased, them spoke to the devotees of Siva.”

Suta said, “Blessed are you, the devotee of Mahadeva and the bestower of the welfare over universe. O sages, you listen to the dialogue of both of them.

The great sage was pleased with the disapproving of the Dvaita doctrine of Skanda and supporting the advaita doctrine.

Then the great sage, offering his salutation and prayer to Kartikeya the son of Siva, then asked him with humility.

Vamadeva said, “O well-versed in the entire tattva, O lord Sanmukha the ocean of nectar, how can the ascetics of the purified souls attain the position of a preceptors?

Without the knowledge of the tradition of the community, they have no authority to initiate anyone in mantras, for achieving the worldly pleasures and the salvation.

What would be the procedure of their having the bath and shaving etc.? O master, you kindly remove my doubt.”

Listening to these words of Vamadeva, Kartikeya, devoting this mind to Siva and Parvati, then spoke.”

Kartikeya said, “Because of my affection for you I shall speak out the yoga-patta whereby one attains the position of a preceptor. O Vamadeva, this is quite secret and bestows salvation.

On an auspicious day in the bright fortnight of the months of Vaisakha, Sravana, Asvina, Kartika, Margasirsa and Magha.

On the fifth or on the full"moon day, getting relieved of the early morning routine, one should take his bath appropriately at the command of the preceptor.

With his restrained mind he shall set on his horns and wipe out the limbs. He shall tie the waistband and wear two cloths. The waistband should be tied with twice spin cord.

Washing the feet, he should perform acamana and then with the reciting of Sadyojata mantra apply ashes over the body with the process of Samuddhulana.

O sage, when the preceptor holds the hand of the disciple, then the latter should sit facing east with folded hands.

He should be seated in the beautiful mandapa proposed by the preceptor over the asana of Kusa or the dear skin. He should be clad in clean costumes.

The acarya should then place a conch with support before the disciple, purifying it with astra-mantra and should place it before the obedient disciple.

The conch should be adored with the pedestal and should pour water over it with conch mantras.

After filling it with water, he should worship it again according to the method prescribed in the Sadangapuja. The pranava mantra shall then be repeated seven times.

The adoration should be made with scents and the flowers offering incense and the performing of arati. The conch shall then be covered up with astra and Varma mantras.

Thereafter he should display the mystic mudras (gestures) of the cow and conch. Then the conch should be placed by him in front of himself. Then he should make an auspicious diagram as per the rites of worship and adore it with sweet scents and flowers.

Purifying the pedestal, he should place the pitcher over it. After offering the incense it should be filled with fragrant water.

O excellent sage, the skin of five trees with their leaves, five types of earth, should be used for plastering the same.

The cloth, mango leaves, upper part of the durva (grass), and flowers should be used for decorating the Kalasa.

O excellent sage, the five gems should be dropped in the Kalasa. In the absence of the five gems one should drop five pieces of gold in it with devotion.

The five gems include amethyst, ruby, gold ingot, coral and onyx.

After reciting Nrmlaska, ending with glum, the preceptor should perform the worship appropriately with joy.

According to the manner prescribed tor the sacrifices, he should perform worship starting from Adhara-sakti the deity should be invoked according to pancavarana method and then adored.

Naivedya of the payasam should be offered together with the betel leaf. Then he should adore reciting eight names it should be sanctified.

The pitcher should be adored reciting pranava, Isana or Pancabrahmana mantras a hundred and eight times. It should then be covered with Astra and Varma mantras, the incense and the lights should be offered. One should then display dhenu and yoni mudras.

Then the preceptor should cover the upper part of the Kalasa with kusa grass. A square diagram should then be prepared to the northeast.

A beautiful asana should be made over it. The child disciple should be made to sit over it.

After performing the Svastivacana, the preceptor left the Kalasa and perform abhiseka over the head of the disciple.

Initially Omkara should be recited, the water of the conch should be poured over the five and seven Brahmanas.

Showing the beautiful lamp, cleaning it with the cloth, a new Kaupin with fresh cord should be offered to the disciple, besides the new scarf.

Washing the feet, he should sip the water, apply ashes over the body, the preceptor should lead the disciple towards the mandapa holding both his hands in his own hands.

The preceptor, should apply the ashes appropriately over the body of the disciple, and then make him occupy the asana earmarked for him.

The disciple should then be seated like a brother facing east the preceptor with a spotless soul, should them speak to the disciple occupying his seat, “you possess the spotless soul.”

The preceptor, thereafter should remain in samadhi (trance), should think, “I am the complete form of Siva” and then speak it out.

Then opening the eyes, with the pleasant mind, folding his hands with auspicious mind should look the seated disciple.

His hands adored ashes, should be placed by him over the head of the disciple should whisper in his ears “Hamsah so ham" clear instruction should be given by the preceptor uttering the mantra.

The initial word aham stands for the powerful one, who is Siva himself. He should therefore think accordingly.

He after giving instructions, thus, shall clearly express the meaning and the interpretation of the statements in the middle.

She shall speak out clearly to him, “O Brahman, I tell you the statements. Listen and retain them in your mind.”

## Chapter 19 - The great statements and Yogapatta

Subrahmanya said, “The great statements are now being made. The perfect knowledge is Brahman, I am Brahman, so are you. The soul is Brahman. The entire universe is established in Isvara. I happen to be prana. The soul is the perfect knowledge. Whatever is hire is there as well. Whatever is there is here as well. He is beyond the knowledge and ignorance. This is you soul which is immanent and beyond death like the nectar. Whatever is thus in this Purusa as well as Aditya, is one and the same. I am the supreme Brahman greater than the greatest. Since I happen to be the preceptor of the Vedas and the Sastras, I am blissful. I am the Brahman pervading in all the living beings. There is no doubt about it. I happen to be the vital breath of the tattva. I am also the vital breath of the earth. I am the vital breath of waters, besides being the vital breath of the resplendent. I am the vital breath of Vayu and akasa (the sky). I am also the vital breath of the three gunas. I pervade all. I am the soul of all. I am the past, present and the future of the universe. 1, because of my being soul of all, I remain unprecedented. All this is the form of Brahman. I transmigrate, I am unattached. Whatever is this, I happen to be the same. I am hamsa. I am he. This should be kept in mind everywhere at all the times.

Now the meaning of the statements are being revealed. The meaning of prajnana Brahman has already been stated. Aham pada means. Paramesvara is the Sakti, soul is the meaning of the word aham.

A is the foremost of all the letters. It represents Siva the form of light. H stands for the sky and represents the Sakti.

The combination of Siva and Sakti always results in bliss. With the word Brahman, the representing of Siva Sakti as the soul of all is quite clear.

It has already been stated that “I am he,” ‘‘That you are.” In this the meaning of tattvamasa represents Sakti.

Otherwise there is a possibility of opposite conception of 'I am he’. The word aham has been used for Purusa, tat is for neutral gender. Thus because of their incoherent native, the correct interpretation cannot be provided.

By so doing, the cause of the universe as male and female forms cannot be otherwise. Therefore the word tat, should be interpreted as the Sakti of Siva.

In the passage Ayamatma both the words are masculine gender. However, in this passage, because of the protection of Isa, the world is taken to be pervaded by the lord.

The atman is the perfect knowledge. Then what is here is there as well. It should be understood like that. This interpretation has been provided by the learned people.

In the statement- “It is other than what is known and what is unknown”, there is a likelihood of adverse interpretation and conception in regard to the fruit of salvation. I shall explain, O sage, how this misinterpretation shall be prevented. What is known means what is known not properly. What is unknown means what is not known before. Otherwise the expression may not be conductive to any meaning.

When it is known, then what is unknown. There is a likelihood of adverse introspection and conception in with regard tot he part of the salvation. What is known is that which is known not properly and what is unknown is that which is not knower before. Otherwise the expression work be meaningless.

This immanent soul is nectar and represents Siva himself. Siva represented in the Purusa Siva who is lodged in Purusa is also lodged in Aditya.

Isvara who after appearing disappears, is one and there is no difference in it. In case your argue that Siva lodged in Purusa and the one in Aditya cannot be the same, and as such we shall discuss by Aropavidhi.

Siva is called golden on having the arms of gold. Then it is treated to be the symptom of all the limbs.

Otherwise, his becoming Hiranyapati also cannot be established, the expression of the form of Siva can be traced in the Chandogya Upanisad.

The golden form of Siva, having the moustaches and beard, of gold, the hair of gold, the body from the nails to the head is of gold.

“I am the supreme Brahman, an greater than the greatest” I am revealing the interpretation of this passage which should be listened by you.

The passage aham stands for Sakti and Siva possesses Sakti. “I am the same.” The statement can be so made.

He is stated to be a great Brahman most sublime and the soul of all viz. Para, Apara and Paratpara. The words like Brahma, Visnu and Siva appear in the Vedas. But the lord is greater than these, as is evident from the word Para.

With the following of the instructions of the Vedas, the scriptures as well as the preceptors, the completely blissful Siva, appears in the heart.

Siva who pervades in all the living beings, I happen to be the same undoubtedly. Thus speaking, one should mention about three types of Sivatattvas. O sage, after accepting all the gunas from the supreme Brahman to the earth, one should speak “I am the vital breath”.

Thus thinking that I have achieved all the atmatattvas. Then achieving Vidya and the Sivatattva.

I am the life of all the tattvas. I am all and I am the soul of all. I am the jiva residing in all the jivas.

I am the past, present and future. Hence I am all and all is Rudra.

The Sruti emerging from the month of Siva says, that the entire universe is the form of Rudra.

All is Brahman because of separating from one’s own and others. I am the same, which has been stated earlier.

I am complete. Because of my positive aspect. I feel liberated always. All the jivas, getting liberated by my grace get absorbed in me.

I am the same, soul of all. O Vamadeva, this the interpretation of the statements made by Siva.

In this way the preceptor should issue instructing to his disciple quoting from the statements of Siva, as well as the Vedas.

Holding Sankha with the base in his hands, he should purify it with the ashes or the use of astra-mantra and then place it our the square asana.

Reciting om mantra worshipping it offering the scents, purifying it with cloth, the fragrant water should be filled in the conch and then recite the om-mantra.

Then it should be purified reciting Om seven times. Whosoever changes this process, he has to face miseries.

This has been ordained by the Vedas. Stabilising the mind “one should remains fearless.” The preceptor should thus speak to the disciple and then one should meditate upon the deity.

By the process of Sadutthapana the seat of the disciple should be worshipped. Then after conceiving the seat of Siva, an image of Siva should be installed.

The five Brahmans should be placed over the head and the body of the disciple, starting from the head to feet. The kalas of the pranava should also be fixed in the forms of thirty eight mantras as distinguished by the trunk, face and kalas. After invoking Siva, he shall display the mystic gestures of the kalas.

The nyasa of the limbs should them be performed the sixteen forms of the relevant starting with the offering of the seat shall also be performed.

Reciting the mantra Om Agnijayajaya payasam snould be offered as naivedya. Then the gandusa, acamana, arghya, padya, incense, lamp etc. should also be offered in a sequence.

Then the japam should be performed after adoring with eight names, with the Brahmanas well versed in the Vedic studies.

Then starting from yo vedanam to yah parah Mahesvarah. Then one should recite and carrying a garland of the white lotus flowers, the pancamukha-siddhi skandha stotra as found in the scripture composed by Srivirupaksa.

Then with a devoted mind one should perform japam of Khyati-purnoham, after which the preceptor should place the garland around the neck of the disciple.

According to one’s own cult, one should plaster the sandal paste over the body of the disciple.

The preceptor should them lovingly give a name to the disciple like ‘Sripada’ etc. and then give him an umbrella and wooden sandals.

Then he should clarify his instructions. Then he should accept the asana of the preceptor and then he should shower his grace over the disciple as Siva.

The preceptor should instruct the disciple, “Meditate upon Siva taking yourself to be Siva himself.” Thus speaking to the disciple, the preceptor should offer his salutation to the disciple and also to others as per the tradition of the cult.

The disciple should then get up and offer his salutation to his preceptor and the preceptor of the preceptor, besides their disciples.

When the disciple completes his salutation, the humble, short spoken, lowering his head with humility, the preceptor should issue instructions to him.

“From today onwards, you be ready to do good in the world.” Thus testing him for a year, he should be taken as a disciple appropriately.

Getting free from the blemishes like the attraction and jealousy, you should devote your mind to Siva. You should keep company of the Siddha-purusas of your own cult and not of others.

Never take food without worshipping Siva, even at the cost of your life. Remain firmly devoted to the preceptor and be always comfortable.

With this sequence, the compassionate preceptor, the ocean of the perfect knowledge, should deal with the disciple with a favourable mind.

O excellent sage Vamadeva, because of my affection for you, I have described the yogapatta to you.

Thus speaking, Kartikeya, showering his grace over the ascetics, also explained the procedure of the showing of hair and ablution to favour the ascetics.

## Chapter 20 - Rules for the removal of hair of an ascetic

Kartikeya said, “O Vamadeva the great sage, now I shall speak on the method of showing and taking of bath, following which they result in great purity of the ascetics.

O excellent sage, when after embracing the yogapatta-vidhi when the disciple is completely initiated, then he should be ready for showing.

Offering his salutation to the preceptor, accepting his command, performing the sipping the water, wearing the cloth, he should wear cloth and then get himself shaved.

Thereafter, he shall work the cloth and the razor etc. with clay and water. The barber should also use clay and be made to wash his hands.

Uttering the name of Siva repeatedly, the water should be sprinkled over each one of the objects. Then he should close his eyes with the ring finger and thumb joined together, then repeating the astra-mantra he shall open his eyes and looked the razor and other implements the tonsured ceremony. He should repeat the mantra twelve times and shall sprinkle water uttering the astra-mantra.

Holding the razor reciting the tara-mantra he should get his right side showed first from the barber. Initially the hair of the right side should be removed and then the rest should be got removed.

A leaf should be spread on the ground over which the hair should be dropped and not on the ground. The beard, the moustaches should also be removed. The nails of hands and the feet should also be cut.

The clay from the roots of wood apple, pipala and Tulasi tree should be taken, after which he should plunge into the water a dozen times and then return to the bank. The clay should be placed over a class space and divide it into three parts. Each part shall further be divided into three parts. Then the water should be sprinkled over the same reciting the astra-mantra.

Carrying the clay with the other hand, he should rub it over the hand and then wash it with water.

The foot should be washed with the other set of clay. Then he should plaster the clay over the face and then enter the water.

Then the other part of clay should be applied over the body with water and plunge into the water again and again.

Returning to the bank he should rinse the mouth sixteen times. Then sipping the water twice, he should perform pranayama sixteen times.

The other set of clay should be divided in three parts. With one part he shall clear his lips and feet and then perform acamana twice.

Repeating the Pranava he shall perform Pranayama silently sixteen times. Then he should plaster his thighs with another part of clay lump, repeating Om thrice.

Sanctifying the clay seven times and rubbing it in palms, should them look at the image of Surya.

A disciple with stable wisdom should purify the armpits with the hands on the opposite sides. The disciple than shall smear another lump of pure clay over his body from head to foot, with devotion to the preceptor with eyes fixed towards the sun.

He should then get up with a rod in his hand and should look at the preceptor with great devotion.

The disciple should devote his mind towards Samba, Mahesana, Sankara, Candrasekhara, who as Siva are the lords of all the fortunes.

He should prostrate before the preceptor as Siva threat. He should get up again and the prostrate before the preceptor five times.

He shall enter the river again and plunge once into the water. Coming up he shall apply the clay on the should less in the manner already explained.

The remaining clay shall be dissolved by him the water and them apply it over the body.

Devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, reciting Om thrice, he should then take his bath appropriately, because it is the lord who enables people to cross the ocean of the universe.

Sanctifying the ashes with water, then reciting the Om mantra, the Viraja ashes should be applied over the entire body.

O sage, then he should carefully make tripundra over all the limbs of the body according to the rules.

Purifying the mind, the performance of the noon should be made. He should offer his salutation to Mahesvara, the preceptors as well as the tirthas.

O Sage, he should adore Siva with Parvati with great devotion. Who bestows the perfect knowledge besides being the protector of the universe.

Then the Yati with a firm mind, getting devoted to dharma should go to the houses of the noble Brahmanas for begging alone.

The ascetic with a spotless mind should divide the alms in five parts. Removing the blemished padarthas from the same, he should take his food.

A bhiksu has to perform in four ways : purificatory deeds, ablution, begging for alms, and to meditate at an isolated place. He has no fifth job to be performed.

Only four types of begging bowl's should be used by him, which should be made of the dry gourd, or of bamboo or of wood or clay. He shall only use any other type of bowl.

Six things are forbidden for an ascetic, which include chewing of the betel, using metal vase, emission of semen, white cloth, sleeping during the day and taking of food during the night.

In case the rules are strictly observed by them they are wise and this failure to do so shall earn the status of a demon. An ascetics shall never indulge in activities contrary to rules.

The past showing ablution should be performed by an ascetic for purity, mentally recalling Siva, the supreme Brahma.

O sage, in this way out of affiliation for you, the rites to be performed after showing have been explained to you. What else do you want to know?

## Chapter 21 - Ban on the cremation of Yatis and performing of their last rites

Vamadeva said, “The liberated ascetics are never cremated. Their bodies are buried instead. This is what has been heard by me.

O preceptor Kartikeya, what is the reason for the same, you please speak out the same. There is no instructor better than you in the world.

Such of the ascetics, who taking refuge in their perfect identity with Brahma, following the path of devotion, have be freed from the cage in the form of the body. They indeed achieve the supreme position (liberation).

O lord, O sun of Siva, you taking me as you disciple, you till me about their fate quite lovingly.

Suta said, “Then Skanda, the son of Parvati and the son of Siva, listening to the words of the sage, started revealing the secret subject to him, which had been heard by Bhrgu from Siva.

Skanda said, 'O Sage, this secret knowledge was imparted by lord Siva, the holder of the bow Pinaka, to Siva yogi Bhrgu.

O Brahman, I import the same knowledge to you. It should not be passed on by you to anyone. These instructions should be imported to the peaceful devotee of Siva, and is a disciple.

An ascetic who spends his time by way of meditating of the performing of tapas, he ultimately in due course of time turns himself as Siva filled with patience.

Such an impatient person, who is unable to perform the meditation, I shall speak out the remedy for the same and you should listen to me quite carefully.

According to the Vedanta literature, and the Agamas, along with the explanation he shall practice Yoga by means of Yama and Nivama etc.

O Sage, by doing so, one who meditates regularly upon omkara, such an ascetic is very well devoted to Siva's meditation.

In case the ascetic having been devoid of courage, due to the weakness in his body, then devoting his mind in an unattached manner to Siva, then he should cast off his worn out body.

O Sage, inspired by Nandi, by the grace of Siva, the five deities known as Ativahika or messengers are well known.

One of then has the form of self killer (i.e. fire). Another had the mass of lustre as the body. The third happens to be the presiding deity of the day. The fourth is the presiding deity of the bright fortnight of the month and the one is in the form of Sun's moving from capricious to Cancer. All the five bestow blessing. Another set of five deities are known as Dhumra, Tamas vini, Ratri, Krsnapaksabhimanini and Daksinayana, O excellent sage, Vamadeva, non you hear about their performance.

O Sage, the five deities, carry the jivas engaged in the karmas, to the heaven according to their merits.

They, after enjoying all the pleasures, and after the finishing of their merits arrive in the world and live as they did in their earlier birth.

All the five deities, starting from the earth distribute the path in fire ways, in the process of five and others, carry him to the place of Sadasiva.

Carrying him there, offering their salutation at the feet of lord Mahadeva, engaged in the performing of the noble deeds, they are then lodged behind Siva, who is always compassionate.

Sadasiva the god of gods, finding them to have arrived in his place, explain to the yati the meaning of the Maha mantra.

The yati is then bestowed with the position of a Ganapati, and consecrate him as such. The Siva the leader of all feels compassionate on him.

The ascetic is then decorated with an axe, black deer skin the excellent trident, granting the boon, having three eyes. The digit of moon, decorated with Ganga and matted locks of hair appear over the head, besides the crescent moon. Then he is made to board a splendid divine plane and is bestow all the powers of fulfilling all the desires. In case his is attached Siva blesses him with a plane having the speed of the mind, which can go everywhere, having the resplendence like the crores of suns, cooke like crores of moons, full of vases with nectar and divine water, decorated with divine garments, garlands, unguents, and ornaments, charming with the sound of dancing, music, Mrdanga and other musical instruments and surrounded by Rudra virgins, then he is adorned with costumes, pastes and the ornaments.

The plane has many vases filled with nectar and the divine water The plane has the lustre of crores of suns but is cool like the crores of moons.

Siva then showers his grace giving his devotee the plane which can reach anywhere with the speed of the wind. When he has enjoyed all the pleasures and the eagerness to enjoy all the pleasures is subsided.

Lord Siva blesses him imparting him the meaning of the great mantra, which is inaccessible by nature, dropping the fast Prakrti, having the influence of the fire of dissolution, which destroys the forest of the universe, and blesses him with an immovable trance in the form of “I am Siva”, “I am perfect”. Thereafter he bestows unrestricted Siddhis on him, by which he can create even the sun.

These Siddhis are in the form of throbbing arising from the realisation that he is slave of Siva. Then removing the unnecessary Siddhis and with the lapse of the age of Brahma, the preceptor of the world bestower on him the great salvation, which has no return.

The attainment of this region is the accumulation of all prosperity and glory. This leads to salvation the end of Vedanta.

When the excellent yati is close to his death, then all the ascetics get favourable to him and then surround him from al the sides.

They all instruct him clearly speaking the passages of pranava and explain their purpose with the pious mind.

They lovingly remind him of Siva who is nirguna, the supreme light. They remind the dying ascetics of the same supreme light.

I shall now speak out the last rites to be performed for the same such types of Yati even when they are not cremated properly, they do not miss the salvation.

Because such ascetics renouncing all the activities are absorbed in Siva. In case the last rites of an ascetic are not performed and the dead bodies of such ascetics are defiled then the kingdom of the king gets destroyed.

The people living in that village as well as the city have to face enormous miseries. In order to remove such blemish, the procedure is being prescribed.

The king should humbly recite the mantra starting from namah irinya and ending with namah amivatkas.

Then reciting Om after end, his devayajana (worship of god) should be completed. O excellent sage, by doing so, all the blemishes are removed.

The sons of the ascetic should also perform, the excellent last rites. O Brahmana, I shall gracefully speak out the process, which should be carefully listened by you.

The dead body should be bathed with the clean water. It should then be worshipped the Rudracamaka dhyaye as well as the Rudra sukta should be recited.

Keeping the conch in front, performing abhiseka with water, the flowers should be offered over the head and then sprinkle water pouring the water on the body.

The old kaupin should be replaced with the new one, and his body should be plastered appropriately with ashes.

Then he should draw tripundra over the body with the sandal paste. The garlands of flowers should also be offered.

The chest, the neck, the head, arms, arms and both the ears should be adorned with the Rudraksa rosaries, reciting the mantras.

Offering the incense, the body should be lifted and placed over a rope swing. The body should then be placed over the panca-brahmamaya-ratha.
