Reciting the Paiica brahman mantras, the ratha should be decorated with fragrant flower garlands.

The Brahmanas should then chant the Vedic hymns accompanied with dance and music. The body should then be carried around the village with dance and music.

The ascetics shall dig a ditch as deep as the staff in a holy place near a holy tree on the eastern or northern side.

A big pit should then be dug and water should be sprinkled in the pit reciting pranaya and vyahrti mantras.

The kusa grass and the Sami leaves should be placed to the north. A cloth or the deer skin should be spread therein.

Then water should be sprinkled over his body, reciting pranava and other mantras. The Rudra should be recited.

Performing abhiseka with the water of the conch, the flowers should be laced over the head. Then one should perform reciting the name of Siva.

Thereafter reciting Omkara svastivacana should be recited. The yogi's body should then be lifted up and should be pleased facing east in padmasana in the pit.

Offering the scent and the flowers, incense of gugulu should be offered. Reciting the passage Visnu havyam raksasva, the body should be placed in the pit.

The danda should be placed in his right hand, while Kamandalu should be placed in his right hand reciting the passage- prajapate natvadeta nyanyo.

Then reciting the mantra Brahma-jajnanam the head of the ascetic should be touched. Reciting the Rudra sukta the space between the eyebrows should be touched.

Reciting the ma no mahanta and others and other four mantras, the head should be broken with a coconut thrown into the pit.

Then speedily uttering the five mantras, touching that place, the mantras from yo devanam to yah parah sah Mahesvarah, should be recited. Then Samba Mahadeva, Siva, Sarvajna, independent, who bestows his compassion on all, should be meditated upon.

Then he should prepare a mus platform of two aratnis square and one aratni in height and smeared with cowdung.

A mystic diagram should be drawn in the centre, and adore with fragrant flowers, wood apple leaves and Tulasi leaves together with fragrant raw grains.

Then uttering Om, incense, lamp, milk and naivedya, should be offered. One should offer salutation five times, after going round.

Reciting Om a dozen times, one should offer his salutation and arghya should be offered to Brahma in all the directions.

The process should be continued for ten days. O excellent sage, now you listen to the rites of eleventh day for the yatis.

## Chapter 22 - Rites to be performed on the eleventh day of Yati's death

Kartikeya said, “O excellent sage, the rites prescribed for the eleventh day after the death of the yatis is going to be narrated by me lovingly to you.

Sprinkling the water over the platform and reciting Punyahavacana mantras five times from the west to east, he shall sit facing the north and draw the mystic diagrams in square shape himself. The middle square should be of 18 cms. in length.

The other diagrams should be in the form of a bindu, a triangle, hexagonal and circular. According to the method of puja, the conch should be consecrated in the front.

The pranayama should then be performed, then performing the Sankalpa, the five messenger lotus as stated above should be worshipped.

Then the kusa grass which has already been touched should be placed to the north. Thereafter by means Sadutthana.

Flowers should be offered over the diagrams made over the pedestal. Thereafter uttering Om hrim, the deity in the form of Agni should be invoked.

Reciting the mantra avahayami namah one should meditate and should consecrate the deity with respect, displaying the mudra.

Reciting the mantras hram hrim and others their limbs should be performed. The messenger goddesses shall have the good, gesture of fearlessness, the Varada mudra in their hands. They are as lustrous as the moon stone.

With the lustre of their gem set fingers, they spread red colour in all the directions, clad in red costumes and having the hands an the feet resembling the lotus flowers.

They have three eyes each, the faces resembling the moon disc, wearing the gem studded crown together with the digit of the moon.

The cheeks appeared charming with the kundalas, tough and raised breasts, adorned with the garland, armlets, bangles and waistbands.

They had slander-waists, large buttocks and clad in red divine garments, wearing the anklets studded with gems, issuing the dangling sound while walking and having charming rings in the toes.

What cannot be established by the great of Siva? Similarly what is beyond accomplishment of the Sakti of Siva?Everything can be done.

The five divine goddesses, who shower their grace on all, can accomplish all the jobs and are always ready to shower their grace on all.

Thus meditating upon their, the water from the conch should be offered at their feet for the purpose of padya.

The water for acamana should be poured in the hands and for the purpose of arghya the water should be poured over the head. He should make them bath with the drops of water from the conch.

The upper garment together with the red cloth should be offered, together with valuable crown and other ornaments.

The fragrant sandal paste, beautiful unbroken rise, fragrant and charming flowers should also be offered.

The extremely fragrant incense, the lamp with the wick of ghee, are being offered by me. Thus speaking Om, hrim mantra should be uttered.

Uttering namah at the end, honey mixed in the payasam, besides sugar, banana and gud and jaggery should also be offered.

Placing each and every fragrant stuff over the plantain leaf the mantra Om bhurbhuvah svah should be uttered.

Thereafter naivedya should be offered reciting the mantra vanhijaya namah the water should be offered.

O excellent sage, the place should be purified, he should be made to since his mouth. Thereafter water should be offered for acamana and arghya.

Thereafter the betel, incense, lamp, should be offered performing circumambulation and the salutation. Making on anjali mudra the hands should touch the forehead.

Offering prayer at the same time. It should then be said “O delightful mothers, the Yati, desirous of the place of Siva, should be protected at the lotus like feet of Siva.”

Thus offering the prayer, one should bid farewell to them. After their depart me the prasada should be distributed among the girls.

Or otherwise it should be given to the cows or dropped nit he river water. It should not be used otherwise. Thereafter the parvana Sraddha should be performed The Ekoddista Sraddha is not to be performed for the Yatis.

I shall now speak out the method of the performing of the Parvana Sraddha. Oexcellent sage, you better listen to it by which one meet with welfare.

The one who takes the bath should wear the yajnopavita and then perform pranayama quite carefully. Holding pavitra (a ring of kusa grass) in hand, an auspicious day.

On should perform Sankalpa, “I shall perform Parvana Sraddha. Then sprinkling the water over the ground, kusas grass should be spread to the north.

Then he shall invite four Saiva Brahmanas, who are well-versed in the rites. The Brahmanas shall take oil bath, after which they should be seated appropriately.

After saying, ‘‘You shall represent Visvedevas, he shall offer salutation to the Atman, Antaratman and Paramatman.” There feet are then to be touched with devotion.

The feet of the Brahmanas should be washed, and they should be seated facing east. After decorating, them with scents, sandal paste etc. they shall be made to take this food in front of Siva.

The ground will be plastered with cowdung, spreading kusa to the east, one should, controlling all the senses, should say, “I shall perform pindadana.

Performing the Sankalpa in this way, he should worship three diagrams- Atma, Antaratma and Paramatma turning the face to the back. Then he should offer the pindas with devotion saying, “I am giving the pindas.’’ Then the water from the durva (grass) shall be offered. He shall then perform circumambulation, getting up, offering the salutation at the same time.

Then giving charities to the Brahmanas, as per the rules, he shall offer Narayana-bali at the same spot, on the same day.

At every step Visnu is worshipped for protection alone. After performing the mahapuja for Visnu naivedya of payasam should be offered.

Then the twelve recited of the Vedas should be invited and should be adored with twelve names, offering the scent, flowers, unbroken rice etc.

Thereafter the shoes, umbrellas, costumes etc. should be given to this with devotion and pleasing them at the same time.

The earth should be covered towards the east spreading cloth etc. the mantra Om bhuh Svaha, Om bhuvah Svaha, Om Svaha Svaha should be recited offering the payasam.

O excellent sage, thus, I have spoken about the rites to be performed on the eleventh day after the death of a yati.

## Chapter 23 - The rites to be performed on the twelfth day for a Yati

Kartikeya said, “On the twelfth day getting up early in the morning taking bath and performing Sandhya, inviting the devotees of Siva, as well as the Brahmanas at noon who have been completely purified. The tasteful food should be served to them with devotion.

Seating himself close to the image of Siva, one should adore him in the Pancavarana rites manner, appropriately after performing Pranayama.

Then according to the method of Mahasankalpa, a sankalpa should be performed saying him, “you are my preceptor and I adore you.” Thus speaking, he should touch him with kusa grass.

Then washing the feet of the preceptor, the performer should himself sip the water. The Brahmanas who have applied ashes over the bodies, should be seated facing the east.

All the eight Brahmanas should be meditated upon as Mahesvara no others. O sage, the other Brahmanas should be adored with great respect, while the preceptor Paramesthi, should be adored in the form of Samba Siva, uttering his own name. The second Brahmana should be treated as a preceptor, the third, the supreme preceptor an the fourth should be treated as greater than the greatest.

Reciting the passage “idam asanam” the asanas should be offered to them. Then reciting the passage Om Sadasivam avahayami he should speak out his own name as well.

After reciting the offering the arghya uttering avahayami namah the lord should be invoked offering padya, acamana, arghya, costumes, fragrance and unbroken rice.

Reciting the eight names including Pranava the fragrant flowers should be offered, using the word namah at the end, mentioning their names in the dative case.

Then he should say, “The adoration has been performed offering incense, lamp, etc. Let the task be established. Thereafter he should offer his salutation.

The banana leaves, getting washed with water, should be spread on the ground. Several types pure food shifts including the food grains, payasam, jaggeries, pulses, and several other eatables should be served. Thereafter the bananas, and gud should also be given. Something should be spread below the vases of food.

After sprinkling water over then the passage, Visnu havyam raksasva he should touch the food with hand and then get up. Offering the water to the Brahmanas, he should pray to them, “you are always Siva's form, bestow boon are me getting pleased.

Reciting the mantra “ye deva” the unbroken rice should be poured on the ground. Then getting up he should say, “let everything become nectar.”

Pleasing the Brahmanas, the mantra starting from gananantva to Rudracamaka-dhyaya or Rudrasukta upto five mantra should be recited.

Thereafter the Brahmanas should be fed. Thereafter, they should be made to washed their faces, feet, then reciting the Vedic hymns. The unbroken rice should be given in their hands.

Then they should be made to occupy comfortable seats, performing acamana. The clean water mixed with camphor should then be offered to them.

The betel, daksina, the wooden sandals, asana water vase, fan, pedestal, rod of bamboo, should be given to the Brahmanas.

They should then be pleased by offering salutation to them besides circumambulation them and receive their blessings. Then after saluting them one should beg for the devotion of the preceptor.

Let the Brahmans in the form of Siva, retire, comfortably to this respective abodes. Than one should bid farewell to them and go with them upto the outer gate.

When the Brahmanas desire the person to go back home, only then they should return to their home. Then he should take food with the Brahmanas, and his kiths and kins or the orphans and then take rest.

No short coming should be left anywhere, this is the truth which is being repeated again and again. In this way a person who adores the preceptor repeatedly, enjoying all the comforts in this world, ultimately achieves the Sivaloka.

Suta said, “Skanda, this showing grace over his disciple Vamadeva, he having the spotless wisdom, the foremost of the learned people and who bestows his grace on all the people again said.

“O sages, dwelling in the Naimisaranya forest, all these details were spoken by Vedavyasa therefore the primeval preceptor and you happen to be the preceptor of the world.

These instructions were heard by Sanatkumara, the best of the sages, from your maths, as a result of which he become the devotee of Siva. The same to Sukadeva- the devotee of Siva. The same details were passed on by him to Vyasa who repeated the same to Sukadeva- the devotee of Siva.

O excellent sage, each one of them had four disciples who were devoted to the study of the Vedas and were engaged in establishing the worship of Siva on earth.

Vyasa had four illustrious disciples viz.- Vaisampayana, Jaimini, Paila and Sumanta.

O Vamadeva, the great sage, 'Agastya, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu were you noble disciple.

Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana and Sanatsujata were quite dear to Siva and were the best moving the yogis.

Of that Sanatkumara, was well-verse in the interpretation of the Vedas. He being preceptors, the supreme preceptor, greater than the greatest as well as the paramesthi-guru. He was advised by Sukadeva even.

The perfect knowledge of pranava is enshrined in these four disciples. This happens to be the main reason for liberation at Kasi.

The group of the sages, mentioned above, has divine influence in the form of a mandala, which is worshipped by the great sages conversant with the gist of Vedanta. It is covered by the ether as brought out by the Vedas. May it be conducive to your satisfaction and the welfare of the world. May it bestow glory and prosperity.

This is the supreme secret as revealed by Siva himself. It is the conclusion of the Vedanta philosophy. O sage, since this doctrine has been heard by you from me, people well-versed in learnings, shall attribute the same to you.

Therefore, the follower of this path, an ascetic devoted to Siva exclusively uttering the passage Sivoham asmi is turned into the form of Siva. Even the adoration of Brahma and Visnu, yields liberation. This is also like the same as all the rivers end up in the ocean.

Suta said, “Thus issuing instructions to Vamadeva, Skanda, getting adored by all the gods, devoting his mind at the feet of his parents.

Kartikeya the bestower of the divine knowledge, reverted to the Kailasa mountain which is surrounded by a large number of peaks.

Vamadeva, on the other hand, accompanied with this disciples, mounting over his vehicle the peacock, offering his salutation to Kartikeya, went back to the Kailasa mountain.

Reaching the Kaliasa mountain, the abode of Siva, Kartikeya offered has salutation at the feet of Siva and Parvati, the sun over of the delusion and the bestowers of moksa.

Overwhelmed with his devotion, and losing his consciousness, he fell at the feet of his parents, offering himself to hem. After prostrating before them he got up.

Thereafter Vamadeva reciting meaningful passage from the Vedas and Sastras adored Siva, Parvati and Kartikeya.

Placing the feet of Siva and Parvati over his head and receiving their grace, he kept on living there.

All of you should also understand the meaning of pranava which is quite secret, and bestows salvation.

Remaining here comfortably, you will attain the excellent salvation, the unparalleled Sayujya at the feet of Srivisvesvara.

I shall go to Badrikasrama, for serving the lotus like feet of the preceptor. Let us aspire for the opportunity for having the excellent discussion again.

Thus ends the sixth Kailasa Samhita of Siva Mahapurana

Siva-Mahapuranam

## Vayaviya Samhita (Part I)

## Chapter 1 - Genesis of the Vedas, the fourteen lores and the Puranas

Vyasa said, “O Son of Parvati and the foremost, of the ganas I offer my salutation to lord Siva who is the creator, preserver as well as the destroyer.

He possesses enormous Sakti lordship, influence, besides having the excellent temperament and whose fortunes pervade everywhere.

I take refuge with the unborn, creator of the universe, eternal, imperishable, Mahadeva, the great soul.

The great sages, started a great yajna at Prayaga- the confluence of Ganga and Yamuna, which happens to be the path of Brahmaloka as well as the Naimisaranya. These ascetics had the praiseworthy hearts, truthful, extremely illustrious and they started the great yajna.

The Rsis are performing the yajna there, on hearing the news by the intelligent Vedavyasa the son of Satyavati, his disciples, who had been the supreme souls extremely were, well known in the three worlds, who were aware of the merits and demerits of the speech, who could silence even Brhaspati in speech, recites of the simple passages to the listeners.

They could narrate the stories quite well, competent speakers, poets, well aware of the polity and the time, well-versed in the knowledge of the Puranas, such a competent person, known by the name of Suta arrived there.

On seeing Suta coming, the delightful sages received him and adored him with respect.

Accepting their welcome and worship, the Suta occupied the proper seat meant for him.

Thereafter, the minds of the noble sages became anxious to the stories of the Puranas from Suta.

The Rsis then worshipped Suta speaking sweet words and attracting him towards themselves the spoke to him.

Rsis said, “O immensely learned one, O Saivaraja, you thrill everyone, besides being omniscient, you have arrived here, because of our great fortune.

You have acquired the entire knowledge of the Puranas from the sage Vedavyasa, therefore, you are well aware of interesting stories.

As the ocean happens to be the important abode of the diamonds, similarly, all the happenings of the past and future in the universe is well known to you. Because of our good luck you have arrived here to meet us. You cannot return without doing good to us.

Therefore the matter which is good for hearing, is auspicious, knowledgeable, such an excellent story filled with the essence of Vedanta, the same should be narrated to us.”

When the sages, well versed in the Vedas, prayed to Suta, then he spoke the auspicious words which were full of sweet and rational meaning.

Suta said, ‘‘All of you by adoring me, have grace me and have inspired me to narrate the story. How can I refuse towards the adorable Puranas of the Rsis.

After adoring Mahadeva, Parvati, Kartikeya, Ganesa, Nandi, and Vyasa- the son of Satyavati. I now speak on the Siva-Maha Purana which is authenticated by the Vedas, extremely auspicious, the ocean of perfect knowledge, bestower of worldly pleasures and salvation.

It comprises of the appropriate nature of the word and its meaning and adorned with the mysteries of the Vedas. This Purana was initially narrated by the wind god in the Svetakalpa.

The lores have a lace in the Puranas, I shall narrate the genesis of this Purana, which you please listen.

The sacred texts comprise of the four Vedas, the six angas, mimamsa, nyaya, Puranas and the literature on dharma. These are the fourteen well known parts of the sacred lore.

In case the four Vedas like Ayurveda, Dhanurveda, Gandharvaveda besides the Arthasastra are also added the member of the lores rises to eighteen.

The sixteen lores of different paths, were created by Siva who happens to be the primeval creator of the lores. This has been ordained by the Vedas.

The same Siva, who happens to be the lord of the universe, with the intention of creating the world initially created Brahma.

Then Siva gave all the lores to Brahma who was born of Siva, to enable him to create the universe.

For the sustenance of the world, Siva bestowed the power for the protection of the living beings to Visnu, who happens to be his middle son.

Thus achieving the different lores from Siva, Brahma, while creating the living beings initially composed the Puranas.

The four Vedas emerged out of the month of Brahma thereafter, followed by the other Sastras.

When the people could not expand them further on earth, then for the spread of the different lores at the command of Visvesvara, at the end of Dvapara, then lord Visnu, who happened to be the soul of Siva, incarnation earth in the name of Vyasa and roamed about on the same.

O Brahmana, similarly, in each one of the Dvapara yuga, the Puranas and the upa- Puranas were composed in the background of the four Vedas.

The same Vyasa, in another Dvapara yuga, was born out of the womb of Satyavati, like the fire emerging out of the sacrificial wood.

He composed the bring of the Vedas in the form of the Eighteen Puranas. Because of the expansion of the Vedas, he came to be known as Vedavyasa.

The brief of the Puranas comprising of a hundred crores of verses was then composed in the four lakh verses. Those hundred crores of verses are still found in the heaven.

O Brahmana, such of the Brahmana, who is well versed in the Vedas, with their angas besides the Upanisads, but are unaware of the Puranas, they cannot be considered to be the learned ones.

The meaning of the Vedas should be explained and developed by means of history (ancient lores) as well as the Puranas. The Vedas get frightened from the ignorant people left they might misinterpret the verses.

Sarga (creation), pratisarga (dissolution), Vamsa (dynasties), Manvantaras (the period of Manus), Vamsanucarita (the stories of the kings born in a dynasty) are the five subjects discussed in the Puranas.

The excellent sages well versed in the Puranas, with big or small devotions, have given the number of the Puranas as eighteen.

They include the following Puranas-

(i) Brahma, (ii) Padma, (iii) Visnu, (iv) Siva, (v) Bhagavata, (vi) Bhavisya, (vii) Naradiya, (viii) Markandeya, (ix) Agni, (x) Brahmavaivarta, (xi) Linga, (xii) Varaha, (xiii) Skanda, (xiv) Vamana, (xv) Kurma, (xvi) Matsya, (xvii) Garuda, (xviii) Brahmanda.

This is the auspicious sequence of the Puranas. Out of these Siva Maha Purana the fourth one, also fulfils all the desires.

The Siva Mahapurana is spread in twelve Samhitas and comprises of a hundred thousand verses.

According to the command of Siva as well as Saivadharma, Saivas are considered to be of three types. Therefore the people desirous of salvation should take refuge with Siva alone.

Even the gods get redeemed, taking refuge with him and not otherwise.

I am speaking about the Siva Purana which is based on the Vedas, together with its divisions, which you please listen.

There are twelve Samhitas in the Purana viz. (i) Vidyesvara, (ii) Rudra, (iii) Vainayaka, (iv) Aum, (v) Matr, (vi) Rudraikadasa, (vii) Kailasa, (viii) Satarudriya, (ix) Koti Rudra, (x) Sahasrakoti nidra, (xi) Vayaviya and (xii) Dharma Purana.

These are the twelve Samhitas in this Purana. Out of these, there are ten thousand verses in the Vidyesvara Samhita.

In the Rudra, Vinayaka, Uma and Matr Samhita have eight thousand verses each. Rudraikadasa contains thirteen thousand verses, while Kailasa has six thousand of them. Satarudra has three thousand, Kotirudra has nine thousand, Sahasrakoti has eleven thousand, Vayaviya four thousand and Dharma has twelve thousand verses.

Thus from the point of view of Sabda- bheda, the Siva Purana comprises of a hundred thousand verses. This Purana is he gist of the Vedas and bestows worldly pleasures as well as the salvation.

Vyasa on his part briefed this Purana reducing the number of verses to twenty four thousand verses. This is the fourth edition of Siva Purana, and presently it comprises of only seven Samhitas.

The first one is Vidyesvara, the second one is Rudra, the third is Satarudriya, the fourth is Kotirudra.

The fifth one is Uma Samhita, the sixth Kailasa and Vayaviya Samhita happens to be the seventh.

The number of verses in each Samhita is given here under:

(a) Vidyesvara 2,000  
(b) Rudra 10,500  
(c) Satarudra 2,180  
(d) Kotirudra 2,240  
(e) Uma 1,840  
(f) Kailasa 1,240  
(g) Vayaviya 4,000  
Total 24,000

This is what has been learnt about the auspicious Siva Purana.

Four thousand verses have been attributed to the Vayu Samhita and the said Samhita has been divided in two parts, the details of which shall be discussed in the account to follow.

The instruction about this Purana should not be given to those who are ignorant about the Purana or those having no faith in it.

Such of the people who follow the Siva dharma and do not denounce the same, should be imparted with knowledge of this Purana, after adequate test.

I bow in reverence to the illustrious lord Vyasa, by whose grace, I could achieve the knowledge of this Purana.

## Chapter 2 - The complex problems of the ascetics

Suta said, “In earlier times after the lapse of many Kalpas, and on the arrival of the Svetavaraha kalpa and the devotions of the universe started, the sages of the six races, getting conversant wit the people, discussed among themselves.

They said, “It is the supreme Brahman, or not? In this way an enormous controversy started and it was difficult to explain the existence of the supreme Brahma. Therefore could not arrive at a decision.

Then all of them went to meet the imperishable Brahma, who was being eulogised by he demons and the gods. Over the people of the pleasant Sumeru mountain, there was a huge crowd of the demons and the gods, while Siddhas and the Caranas were discussing among themselves, when Yaksas and the Gandharvas were also present there.

Several of the flocks of birds were issuing sweet notes, while chirping. The place was embellished with diamonds and corals due to the flowing of the rivers and swerlets. The bowers, caves, caverns and the springs looked quite graceful.

There was a Brahma forest spread in ten yojana and filled with deer and other animals of the forest. The length of the forest was a hundred yojanas.

There was a lake there, with sweet, spotless and cool water. The lake was surrounded by the trees slanting on all the sides which were filled with blossoming flowers, over which the bees were hovering.

There is a great city there which shines like the sun, which had been the abode of awful, demons, Raksasas as well the Daityas who had become arrogant because of their prowess.

The city was surrounded by the high boundary walls which were quite beautiful and had the shade of molten gold. It was decorated with toranas and banners, having hundreds of main streets, turrets and wooden ceilings.

The crores of the massive buildings of the city appeared like trying to lick the sky. These mansions with studded with gems of various shades.

Lord Brahma, the creator lives there together with his councillors. The sages reaching there found Brahma the noble soul, who was being served by the gods and the sages. He was resplendent like the pure gold and was bedecked in all ornaments.

His face was quite serene and delightful, while his eyes resembled the lotus petals. His body issued the divine lustre. His body was smeared with fragrance.

He wore the excellent while costumes and was adored with divine garlands. The gods offered their salutation at his lotus like feet, besides the yogis as well as the demons.

Sarasvati possessing all the auspicious symbol is over her body, holding a flywhisk in her hand. With Sarasvati, Brahma appeared so graceful as the sun shines with his rays.

Looking at both of them, the faces and eyes of all the sages got delighted. All of them placing the folded hands over their heads, started praying for Brahma.

The sages said, “O Lord you are the form of Trimurti, Puranapurusa, the supreme soul, besides being the creator, preserver and the destroyer of the universe. Salutation to you.

You have the supreme body, you can stir the Prakrti, you are unblemished inspite of your being the creator of the blemishes, salutation to you.

You are the form of cosmos you live in the cosmos, besides being the creator of the universe and the Pancamahabhutas therein, salutation to you.

You are the form of the universe, you units the soul and body of all, besides separating the, salutation to you.

You have created, preserved and distorted the universe, you are the creator of all the lokas. Still because of the influence of Maya we are not aware of you true form, O Grand sire.”

Suta said, “The sages thus adored and eulogised Brahma. Then Brahma, pleasing them in deep voice pleasing them spoke to them.

Brahma said, “O immensely valorous and illustrious sages, what for have you arrived here collectively?”

When Brahma thus spoke to the learned Rsis they with folded hands spoke with humility.

The Rsis said, “We have been surrounded with the enormous darkness. Therefore even after prolonged discussion amongst ourselves, we have been unable to know about the truth, as to who is the excellent of all.

You are the creator of the world, besides being the cause of al the causes. O lord nothing is unknown to you.

Which one of the humans is the ancient most in the world, who is the supreme one, who is the most spotless one, who is complete in all respect, who is eternal and the supreme lord.

Who by indulging in wonderful activities has created the universe? O intelligent lord, please mention it and quell our doubts.

When so addressed by the sages, Brahma smiled feeling surprised and then addressed the gods, demons and the sages.

Then meditating upon for a long time, Brahma got up and folding his hands, felt delighted uttering Rudra. While so doing all his limbs were soaked in perspiration, because of the thrill.

## Chapter 3 - Brahma declares Siva, as the best of all the gods

Brahma said, “where the speech with the mind returns without attaining the god, when a learned person, achieving a bliss becomes fearless of all.

From whom, Brahma, Visnu, Indra and other gods had been born for the first time, who is the creator of the causes of the creation and the one who mediates upon Narayana, except them nothing can be born at any place.

He is also Sarvesvara himself possessing all the fortunes; he is the one who is one meditated upon by all the truth seekers, residing in the heart like sky of all.

Who first of all created a son like me and bestowed the perfect knowledge to me, by his grace alone, I have been positioned as Prajapati.

The one who is the only Isvara lodged in sky like he immovable tree, with whom the entire cosmos is complete.

The one who alone activates the several inactive living beings and the one who perform all the deeds like the seeds, he happens to be Mahesvara himself.

The one who, inspite of being alone Isvara, completing all the living beings exercises his control over them, he is lord Rudra and none else.

He is the one who resides in the hearts of the devotee, in an invisible form, still exercising his authority over the universe.

The one who becoming free from the bondages of the time, is the lord of the sky and all the causes related there with, he happens to be lord Siva alone.

The one for whom, there is no day or the night, there is neither any superior nor an equal, in whom the Jnana-sakti and the kriya- sakti are permanently lodged besides that he is the form of the Para-Sakti.

The one which is perishable and unmanifest, that which is imperishable and immortal- both these have the imperishable as their Atman. The sole lord is Siva himself.

A person who adores Siva with the Sattvika intentions, he at the end is relieved of all the bondages of the world.

The place which is beyond the reach of the rays of the sun and the moon and with the resplendence of whom, all the gods are illuminated, (he is Siva) as husband ordained by the Vedas.

He happens to be the beginning, he is without the end. He has a spotless temperament. He is complete and independent. All the mobile and immobile beings of the universe, are subservient to his will.

He possesses all the fortunes, his body is different from Prakrti, he himself is free and he redeems others. Though he himself is not the form of time, but he inspires time (kala) himself.

He is lodged abode all. He is all pervading. He knows all and he happens to be the lord of the universe having six paths.

In the gradual living beings, he happens to be the best of all. He is beyond measure, form of bliss and is like the black wasp which consumes the dust of the flowers. He is competent enough to unite the innumerable globes. He is the ocean of large heartedness, prowess, seriousness and sweetness.

There is nothing comparable with him, nor is there anything beyond him. he is unparalleled of all the living beings, and is the king of kings.

He is the one who initially creates the worlds first of all, which is ultimately absorbed in the same.

All the mobiles and immobile are subservient to him. He inspires all. One can met him with firm devotion alone and not otherwise.

The great sages have instructed on Vratas, charities, tapas and niyamas keeping in view Siva alone.

Even today Brahma, Visnu Rudra and other gods, try to have an audience with him performing the tapas.

The degraded people, the fools, wicked, the fallen people, and those people who are denounced, are unable to have a look at him. The devotees on the other hand with their devotion can talk to him as well.

He appear in three forms viz. subtle, gross and beyond them We he gods come across his gross form. His subtle form is accessible to the yogis.

The form beyond that, which is eternal, full of knowledge, blissful, and imperishable, can be accessible to the devotees alone.

What more is to be spoken, it is the secret of all the secrets that one should surely adore Siva. A person does so, he is surely redeemed.

By the grace of Siva, his devotion can be achieved, in the same way as the sprout emerges from the seed and the from sprout emerges the seed.

A jiva meets with success by the grace of the lord, because of this, Siva is adores by all the means.

The methods to achieve him have been enshrined in the Vedas which is called dharma following which the merits and the demerits are neutralised.

One achieves grace with the same. The sins of the living beings are destroyed with the same.

Thus the sins of several births are destroyed, after which the devotion with knowledge of Siva and Siva is achieved.

According to the feelings of the devotees, the grace of the lord is achieved and the reward of the deeds is destroyed with the same and not with the form.

Therefore with the vanishing of the fruits of deeds, a person is directly linked with Siva dharma, which is of two types viz. one is dependant on the preceptor and the other is without him.

The one who is dependant on the preceptor, is more impatient and a hundred times more affective that the former, since in the Saiva cult, there is an association of the Saivite knowledge.

With the achieving of the perfect knowledge a person is in a position to witness his shortcomings. Then he feels detached with the worldly pleasures and with that detachment one meets with success.

With the achieving of the bhavasiddhi a person is freed of the karmans he gets inclined towards the meditation. Having been blessed with the perfect knowledge and the meditation a person becomes a yogi.

The excellent devotion can be achieved with yoga. The grace of Siva is achieved thereafter. By his grace, a person getting free, turns like Siva.

Thus the sequence of the grace of Siva has been explained. The grace of the lord depends on the competence of a person.

A person is redeemed sometimes in the mother's womb, sometimes soon after his birth, sometimes during his childhood, youthful or the old age.

Sometimes an animal and some a person fallen in the hell is redeemed. Some of the getting relieved of a particular position, is redeemed.

Sometimes a soul may return after the enjoyment of heavenly region and freed from all bondages. Still another soul may be liberated on its way.

With this background, it may be stated that the redemption of the humans cannot be achieved by one particular way one achieves salvation, according to the perfect knowledge, and the minor feelings, by the grace of the lord.

Therefore, in order to please Siva, relieving the mind and the speech of all the blemishes, performing the homa one should meditate upon Siva.

One should be devoted to Siva, should always remain dependant on him, should remain linked to him, performing all his duties, he should devote his mind to Siva.

One should organise a yajna for a thousand divine years. At the end of the yajna, with the strength of the mantras the wind god would arrive there, who would reveal to you the method of your welfare. Then all of you should gods the extremely auspicious city of Varanasi, where lord Siva the holder of the bow always resides with Parvati.

Witnessing a great surprise there, you should approach then I shall lead you to the path of moksa.

By following this you can salvation during the present birth alone, which can usually be achieved by many births.

This is the mental cakra prepared by him, which is being released by me. The place where its rim are shattered would be quite auspicious for the performing of the tapas by you.

Thus looking at the shining mental cakra resembling the sun rays, was shot by Brahma, devoting his mind to Siva.

The Brahmanas, also getting pleased, offering their salutation to Brahma, kept on following the cakra to the place where its rim was to break.

The cakra so shot by Brahma, fell over a slippery rock. Then it felt in the clean water (lake) of the forest.

Because of this, the auspicious forest came to be known by the name of Naimisa-ranya. The forest had several Yaksa, Gandharvas an the Vidyadharas living there.

As luck would have it the king Pururava, for the enjoying of the worldly pleasures, arrived there with Urvasi and out of foolishness, he occupied the golden premises of the yajna, where the sages had placed the Vajra like strong kusa grass in anger.

In earlier times the Visvasrja Brahmesa, householders desirous of creating the universe had started a divine yajna there.

These had been the learned sages, who were experts in the world in words, meanings and the logical arguments and with their intellectual power, besides on the basis of the yogic practices performed the appropriate rites.

Thus the people well versed in the Vedas, refuted those who were averse to them with the strength of their arguments, speaking eloquently.

This Naimisaranya was therefore the befitting place for the performing of the tapas by the sages. From the springs of the nectar like water, emerging from the crystal rocks, where the tees are laden with the juicy fruits, which is abode of many living beings.

## Chapter 4 - Interpretation of the word Pasupati- discussion between wind god and the Rsis in Naimisaranya

Suta said, “The excellent Rsis, having controlled their sense organs, started the sacrifice at that lace, while adoring Siva.

The said sacrifice made all the Rsis surprised in the same way as Brahma surprises with the creation of the universe.

After a long time, the yajna in which enough of daksina was gems, was completed, then the wind god arrived there at the command of Brahma.

He was the disciple of Brahma, had controlled all his senses, could visualise all and at whose command forty nine types of the wind were blown, who with his performance inspired the prana and other winds and who pervades in the bodies of al the living beings; who possessed all the fortunes including the Anima etc., who bears the sun rays falling over the three lokas, who is born in the sky, having two qualities of sound and touch, to whom to learned people well versed in the tattvas, describe as the Prakrti of the tejas of Agni and others.

The ascetics who had been performing the tapas for long, found he wind god having arrived in their asrama and wore delighted, recalling the words spoken about him by Brahma.

All the Rsis god up and offered their salutation to the wind god and provided him a seat of gold.

After the wind god was seated, the Rsis adored him. The wind god, then praising then, enquired of their welfare.

Vayudeva said, “O Brahmanas, is your yajna being performed well. Are the asuras the enemies of the gods, creating me obstruction in the performance of your yajna?

Has any obstruction or the cause of repentance appeared? The gods and the manes feel satisfied with the reciting of the stotras, mantras and the japam.

Did you start the yajna by adoring them. Now what do you desire at the completion of the yajna?’’

At these words of the wind god, the devotee of Siva, the Rsis were delighted and they spoke humbly.

The ascetics said, “All of us are perfectly well today. Because of your arrival here, our tapas has been successful and we have met with welfare.

You kindly listen to an ancient episode. We people with our minds having been shrouded in tamoguna, had prayed to Prajapati earlier.

Then Brahma, who is graceful on people who take refuge in him had spoken with compassion,” O Brahmanas, Rudra is the foremost of all the gods, besides primeval cause of all.

The same Mahadeva who is beyond arguments or controversies can be visualised by the people with devotion. Because of his grace one gets devotion and salvation.

Therefore in order to please lord Siva, the supreme cause, he desired us to perform a yajna for a long time in the Naimisaranya forest.

By this grace at the end of the yajna the wind god would arrive and bestow the perfect and divine knowledge to you.

Thus speaking, Brahma had sent us all here. Reaching here, we had been waiting for your arrival here.

We have been dwelling at this place in a thousand for the past divine years performing the long time yajna. He have no other desire after your arrival here.

Hearing thus this story of the sages, who had performed the satra for a long time, the wind god was pleased and stayed there surrounded by the sages.

Thereafter for increase of their knowledge, at the prayer of the Rsis, he spoken the fortunes of Siva as well as the geneses of the universe in brief.

## Chapter 5 - Reply of the wind god to the sages

Suta said, “The Rsis, dwelling in the Naimisaranya forest, offered their salutation to the wind god and then asked him appropriately.

The Rsis of Naimisaranya said, “How could you process this knowledge which is possessed by Isvara alone and how could achieve the devotion of Siva, who is unborn?”

Vayudeva said, “In the twenty first Svetalohitakalpa, with the intention of creating the universe, Brahma performed tapas.

Lord Siva, the father of Brahma, was leased with him, took to the form of a boy, which is the best of all the forms.

Then he turned himself in the form of a Sveta muni and spoke excellent words. Thereafter Mahesvara, the god of gods appeared before him.

Brahma, finding his father Siva the composer of the Vedas before him, offered his salutation to him and he achieved the supreme knowledge of Gayatri from him.

Thereafter, Brahma, the creator of the universe, created the mobile and immobile world.

The Paramesvara from whom Brahma achieved the nectar like knowledge, then I also achieved the same from him with the strength of my tapas.

The Rsis said, “How could you get the excellent knowledge, devoting to which a person can feel comfortable.

Vayudeva said, “The information about Pasu, Pati and Pasa that had been achieved by me earlier, a person desirous comforts, should adore the same.

The miseries emerging out of the ignorance can be removed with the perfect knowledge. The perfect knowledge differentiate between the things, which are of two types.

They are called jiva and Prakrti. He is the creator of both of them. All of them are known by the names of Pasu, Pasa and Pati.

Most of the people well versed in the tattvas, mostly discuss aksara (non- perishable), ksara (perishable), ksaraksara those which are perishable and imperishable both.

Aksara is conceived as Pasu, Ksara as the Pasa. The one, who is beyond he ksaraksara is called Pati.

The sages said, “O wind god, what is represented by ksara and aksara? Than what is ksaraksara which is beyond them? You kindly enlighten us.

The wind god said, “Prakrti is known as ksara while Purusa is known as aksara. The one who aspires them, is Para or supreme and is also called Paramesvara.

The sages said, “What is Prakrti and what is Purusa? To whom are both of them related to?

Vayudeva said, “Prakrti is the form of Maya, while Purusa is surrounded by Maya. Both of them are correlated with mula (the basic) and the karmans (the deeds) Lord Siva inspires them both.

The sages said, “What is Maya? In what form does the Purusa appear, after having been surrounded by Maya? What is Mula and what is the source of its origin. Who is Siva.

Vayudeva said, “Maya happens to be the Sakti of Siva. Purusa in the form of consciousness is surrounded by Maya. The imaginary blemish covers the consciousness, while Siva is spotless lord devoid of blemishes.

The sages said, “What for the Maya, pushes the all pervading Siva and for what reasons. Then how does he get relieved of the bondages of Maya?

Vayudeva said, “A person who is surrounded by Maya, he has to be born again and again. The same Maya remains present in the form of a digit. The karmans are meant to be enjoyed. After the removal of the dirt of blemishes, he is liberated.

The sages said, “What is the digit etc.? What is the karman? What is the beginning and end of the same? What is the reward and the support of the same. What for is the bhoga (result of the good or bad deeds) What is their source? What is the cause of the removal of the blemishes and what is the form of the person, whose blemishes are removed.

Vayudeva said, “The person enjoying all the pleasures, is connected with the arts, learning, attachment, time as well as the destiny.

The merits result in pleasure while the sins result in misery or pain. An ignorant person has to face the consequences of his misdeeds or sins.

The process of destruction of the karmans is called bhoga, which is invisible. The body having the interval as well as the external organs, is considered to be the means for enjoying the bhogas.

With the achieving of the devotion of Siva, the sins get vanishes. When the blemishes of the soul are removed, a person takes to the form of Siva.

The sages said, “What are the individual functions of kala and the other five tattvas? Does the soul has the form of an individual Purusa, who is called the enjoyer.

In what for is the invisible soul, the enjoyer (of the karmans? Why does he take refuge in enjoyments? What type of body does he possess.

Vayudeva spoke, “The instinct of attaining knowledge in a person is called Vidya. There is no conditioning factor. Indeed destiny control everything.

The cause is manifest which consists of the tree gunas. It is the source of origin and the place of merger. The people well versed I the tattvas call it Pradhana and Prakrti.

The kala reveals the Sakti of lord. A Saguna Purusa has to face pleasure, pain and confusion.

Sattva, rajas and tamas are the three gunas of Prakrti which are lodged in the Prakrti like the oil in the seeds.

The pleasure of the cause of the pleasure in brief is the reward for Sattvaguna. The pain and the cause of pain, is the cause of rajoguna. Ignorance and the dilution are the reward of tamoguna.

The Sattvaguna rises upwards, while tamoguna moves downwards and rajoguna an moves in the middle.

The five tanmatras the five Mahabhutas, the five Jnanendriyas (organs of knowledge, and five Karmendriyas (organs of activity).

Pradhana, buddhi (or intelligence) ahamkara (the arrogance) and the mind, are mainly invisible no blemished.

In the condition of this cause it is invisible and in the condition of the activity it appears in the body like the pitcher.

As the pot could not be differentiated from the clay materially, so the manifest, body etc. is not different from the unmanifest.

Therefore the unmanifest alone is the cause of the composite from viz. organs, body but their support, the object of enjoyment is unmanifest.

The sages spoke, “How can the soul, which is beyond intelligence, sense organs and the body, exist? What is the position of the same?

Vayudeva replied, “The all pervading lord is quite separate from intellect, sense organs and the body. There is indeed the atma or the soul but it is difficult to explain the reason for the same.

The intellectuals have not accepted the existence of intelligence in the body for ever, because the knowledge remains in the body till it is alive.

Therefore, the soul is well aware of all the subjects. It does remember, experiences, besides being the knower of the inner feelings. This has been ordained in the Vedas as well as Vedanta.

It is eternal and all pervading. It stands everywhere. Still it cannot be perceived by anyone clearly anywhere.

It cannot be visualised with the eyes or the use of any other sense organs. With the lighting of the internal flame, it can be known.

It is neither a male, a female or a eunuch. It is neither above, nor slanting, or below anyone.

It remains without a body even while residing in a body. Even after living in the mobile beings, it is immobile and imperishable. A person with patience can visualise the same.

What more could be said about the same? This Purusa is separate from the body. Those who consider it to be the part of the body, they passes in complete intelligence.

The soul is beyond the body of a person, because the body is impure, subservient, painful and perishable.

The Purusa is linked with the body because of the misfortunes. Therefore, a person is considered to comfortable, painful and foolish because of his karmas.

As the seed sprouts in a field filled with water, similarly from the ignorant body the karmans appear.

The bodies are sure to fall into the painful joins of death. It has already achieved thousands of bodies in the past and the process is going to be repeated in future.

The souls, discarding the old bodies, enter the ones bodies. No soul can remain in one body always.

The soul is linked and separated from the bodies, in the same was as the moon reflection sometimes covered by the clouds, is found in the step well and sometimes not.

One comes across different types of activities of the soul in different bodies in the same way as the motion of the die is found in different squares in the chess board.

None belongs to him nor does he belong to anyone. The contacts with wives, sons and other relations develop per chance alone like meeting some one on the road.

The living beings come in contact ih touch one another in the ocean, to be separation again.

He can see the body but the body cannot see him. Both the body and the jiva are looked after by someone else, who remains invisible to him.

All the living beings right form Brahma to the smallest insect, have been termed as Pasus. The example has been quoted for Pasus only.

The jiva while facing the pleasure and the pain is bound with these bondages. The jivas are the sports of the lord according to the learned people.

The creatures devoid of wisdom cannot prevent his happiness or misery. At the instance of the lord, he goes up to the heaven and then falls in the deep pit.

Suta said, “On hearing the words of the wind god, the sages felt delighted at heart. They bowed in reverence to him who was well versed in the Saiva Agamas, they again spoke to him.

## Chapter 6 - The principle of Siva faith

The sages said, “Who is the master of those who have been termed as Pasu and the Pasa.

Vayudeva said, “He is the abode of all the beautiful qualities, creator of the universal, lord of the universe and release the living beings from the bondages of the noose.

How could the creation of the universe lace in his absence because Pasu and Pasa are devoid of consciousness,

Without an intelligent cause nothing is visible anywhere created by Pradhana, atom or any such being.

The universe is an effect possessing parts dependant on the creator. The activity can only be created by Pati and not in Purusa or Pasa.

Whatever the activity is performed by the jiva, it is so done with the aspiration of Pati, but his activation is like the walking of a blind man.

By believing his own soul and the one who inspires to be two entities, the soul uniting with Isvara is redeemed.

By knowing of the real difference between Pasu (jiva), Pasa or Pati a person well versed in Brahma, is relieved of the human body.

Then ksara and aksara combined take to manifest and unmaniest forms. Isvara alone frees a person from the bondages of the world.

The one who enjoys, the thing of enjoyment, and the one who inspires are the three separate entities. Beyond this it is not necessary for a learned person to know anything else.

As the oil resides in the gingely seeds, ghee in the curd, water in the spring, and fire in the wood sticks, similarly the noble souls, visualise,

The their own souls because of there following the truthful ways and the performing of the tapas.

The one who like a juggler makes Isvara with his Maya subservient to himself together with his Saktis and lives alone,

He could be Rudra alone and none else. He is the one who creates, sustains and destroys the world.

The entire universe represents his eyes, face and arms. He is the only god who has produced the heaven and earth. He is the origin and the palce of merger of all the gods.

It is he who produced Brahma first of all. He is called Rudradeva as well. This is ordained by the Vedas.

I am aware of the great lord, resembling the nectar, having the complexion of the sin and is beyond the darkness.

There is nothing beyond this supreme soul. There is nothing smaller or bigger then him The world is complete by him alone.

He has faces on all sides besides the heads and the necks. He dwells in the came like heart of everyone. He is all pervading and as such the lord Siva dwells in all.

He has his hands, feet, eyes, faces and heads, everywhere. He is surrounding everyone.

He has all apparent attributes, except the sense organs. He is the friend and the refuge of all.

He is called the great Purusa who can see without eyes, can hear with out the years. He comprehends all and no one knows about him.

He is smaller than the atom and greater then the greatest besides being unchanging. He is the cavity of the heart of this Pasu.

The same Isvara, who is devoid of yajna, the form of yajna, extremely getting free from all the grief.

This all pervading and imperishable, supreme soul is visualised by the Vedas as all pervading by those who are well-versed about Brahman, who also conceive him to be the remover of the cycle of birth and death.

After annihilating in the end, Mahesvara alone, with his Sakti, creates, sustain and destroy the three lokas.

There is a Sakti of Siva, named Aja who holds on to the world and is also known as Prakrti. Inspite of the said Sakti being one, she is of red, while and black complexion.

She creates several types of people. The Jiva sleeps, enjoying the same and discards her after doing so.

Both the supreme soul and the jiva are friends and are lodged in a tree known as the body. The jiva enjoys the reward of his karman, while the supreme soul is the silent observer.

Living on the tree of the universe, and overpowered with the delusion, thinks, while the other cause, has an audience with Isvara.

Then he, observing his glory, and becoming free from grief, becomes comfortable.

The great soul and the Mayin entering thus creates the universal by Maya. Maya is known as Prakrti, and Mahesvara as Mayin.

The universe pervades with his limbs or parts. The Purusa gains the perpetual peace and calmness on realising the tree form of Siva the creator and the one who envelopes the universe and is the subtler of the subtlest from his very inception in the foetus.

He alone stands for time, the protector and the lord of the universe. One is released from the noose of death on realising him.

Like the subtle cream over the ghee, he is concealed in the hearts of all, as Siva, realising this a devotee freed of all the same.

He is the excellent god, known as Mahesvara who is the creator of the universe. Realising that the lord is seated in his heart, a person, attains salvation.

According to an early tradition, when there was neither day nor night nor asat but only Siva was there.

No one could captive him from above below or the middle. There is none comparable with him, whose norms an glory are great.

Several of the people, sightened of the several births, conceiving the supreme soul as unborn, and one, adore the southern face of Siva, for their protection. Brahman beyond measure comprises of his letters viz. Vidya and Avidya.

Avidya is perishable and Vidya is beyond destruction and comprises of nectar. Mahesvara is the lord of both of them.

The supreme soul, creates all one by one, spreading his net in various ways creating all he rules over then.

He illuminates all the directions, above, below and to sides, shining himself. He is the best of all by nature and is imparalled.

Transforming the attributes, the expressing of nature and the expressed ones, into what is enjoyed and the one who enjoys, he occupies the universe.

The gods and the sages, conceive him having been hidden in the Upanisads. He is Brahman greater than the greatest progenitor of Brahma and the cause of the universe.

One who lovingly knows in the world being the support of the universe. He is the sustainer of the universe, besides being its destroyer. Those who know him, they are relieved of the bondages of the body.

The universe revokes because of the greatness of the lord, but the deluded people, call it a natural process or the power of time.

This universal has been surrounded by the supreme soul who is the kala of the god of death, the activities inspired by him, transform into worldly existence together with the elements.

The individuals indulge in various types of activities, which are always on the increase and then return to earth, where they, due to the influence of Maya are caught in the web of tattvas. With the application of the fourteen attributes of the soul, they are involved in the worldly pleasures. When these activities cease even the results are quelled.

After the vanishing of the results, they reach another world. This is the cause of the union of the two viz. the one who enjoys and the other which is enjoyed.

The supreme Purusa is beyond three times. He is nirguna or without attributes. He is omniscient Paramesvara, lord of these three gunas and the Supreme Brahman- greater than the greatest.

He has the universal form, and is meditated upon in many forms. He is without birth, the lord of the people, object of adoration and meditation by the entire universe. He is lodged in our hearts.

He is beyond Kala and from him originates the entire comer. He is the soul of the universe, destroyer of the sins, lord of all the fortunes and pervades in the entire universe.

He is the lord of all the Isvaras, supreme lord of all the gods. He is the supreme of all the masters. He is Isvara of all the lokas as believed by the people.

He is beyond the cause or its effect. Nothing is visible on earth, which could be compared with him or could be superior to him.

Several types of his excellent Saktis are described in the Vedas. His perfect knowledge, prowess and activities are well known to the world, by means of which he created the universe.

He is without a master nor is there any trace of the same or of the lordship. There is no cause for him. He is the lord of the gods.

He was neither born, nor does he have any parents. The blemish, Maya or any other things are not the cause of his birth.

He alone, pervades in all the living beings. He is secret from the world. He is the inner soul of all the living beings. He is also known as the lord of dharma.

He is the witness living in all the beings, conscious and is devoid of gunas. He is the sole lord with self control, devoid of activities and helpless.

He is the most permanent among the eternal beings. He is quite conscious among the conscious beings. He is supreme of all the people. He himself is devoid of all the desires, but he still fulfills the desires of all.

He is the creator of the universe. He is comprehensible through the Samkhya philosophy, besides the yogic practices. He is the cause of the universe and a person could be released of the illusion by his grace.

He is the sole creator of the universe and also who knows it well. He is well aware of the karmans of the living beings. Kala is subservient to him. He possesses all the virtue himself, besides being the lord of virtue. He is the supreme lord of the jivas. He is the one who could remove the bondages of the karmas.

Lord Siva, who initially created Brahma, then delivered to him the discourse on the Vedas. I shall know the same lord by my soul and wisdom. Besides for his pleasures. I, after knowing about him being desirous of getting redeemed from the universe, I take refuge with Siva, who is devoid of attributes and activities, peaceful, is free from trouble and unblemished Siva.

He is excellent bridge for the achievement of creator, I shall be dormant like the fire which consumes wood. When the men wear either as they wear the hide, they will realise the miseries before realising Siva.

O great Rsis, by the grace of the tapas of Mahadeva and with his pleasure, I have revealed the auspicious perfect knowledge of Sannyasa asrama- the destroyer of the Siva, which being extremely secret has been enshrined in the Vedanta being extremely secret, was fortunately achieved by me from the month of Brahma, initially.

This is the best of knowledge and should not be imported to the unstable son, incompetent disciple, and a person of wavering mind.

This perfect knowledge should be imparted to a person who is immensely devoted to the gods as well as the perception. Only then this knowledge would became purposeful and develop.

Therefore you listen the essence of the same in brief. Siva is beyond Prakrti. He after creating everything at the time of the creation destroys everything at the time of dissolution.”

## Chapter 7 - The description of time in relation to Siva

The sages said, “All the things grow at the appropriate time, and get destroyed in due time. Nothing happens beyond time.

When the entire universe is absorbed at the time of dissolution, then it is recreated. The process of the creation and dissolution moves like a wheel.

O one among the gods and others including Brahma, Visnu, Rudra and others besides the gods and the demons can violate the rules of Prakrti.

The time shattering people by the part, present and future, conducts itself like a terrific master.

Who is the lord of time, to whom is he subservient to? Who is not subservient to him? O learned one, you tell us.

Vayudeva said, kala, kastha, nimesa are the parts of kala, this kalatma has been considered to be the tejas of Mahesvara.

No mobile or immobile force in the world can overpower it. It is the command of the lord, besides being the protector of the universe.

The force in the form of kala comprises of its various parts. It comes out of it and permits it like the pieces of iron which shed sparks of fire.

Therefore the entire universe is subservient to kala and Kala is not subservient to the world. Kala is subservient to Siva, but Siva is not subservient to Kala.

Since the undistracted splendour of Siva is lodged firmly in the kala therefore it is quite gigantic and beyond measure.

Which one of the learned person can go beyond kala. No one can erase the karmans performed by kala.

Those who exclusively rule the earth by then prowess, they are also unable to erase the moves of kala like the oceans which do not overflow the shore.

Those who exercising their control over all the senses, conquer the entire world, they too one unable to overpower kala. On the other hand kala overpowers them.

The people, well-versed in Ayurveda, besides the physicians who are well-versed in the use of medicines, are unable to avert death. Of course kala can never be overpowered.

A living being thinks something else with riches, beauty, humility, process and the race, but Kala forcibly negativates the same.

Our meets with unthinkable good and bad people. Only the lord make people to travel to such places.

The time in which one feels miserable, at the same time, one feels delightful. Therefore the nature and moves of the time are beyond description

A person who is young to day, he becomes old tomorrow, the strong person becomes weak, the rich man becomes a pauper. Therefore the moves of the time are quite astonishing.

For the accomplishment of a task, the race, humility, and excellence cannot be enough. Kala is the regulator of all.

Those who are well protected, donors, or listen to song and music, those who are orphans or are fed by others, the time behave equally with them.

Even the elixirs, panaceas and the well administered medicines, do not have any effect if the time is not favourable. The same things when made use at the proper time, become affections and cause happiness.

No one dies or is born untimely nor doe she grow. Without time no one becomes happy or painful untimely. Therefore, there is nothing comparable with kala.

The cool breeze blows timely, the clouds pour rain in due time. The heat is subsided at the appropriate time. Thus kala is always successful.

Kala is the cause of the birth of all, the crops grow in time. The harvesting is done in due time. The living beings live upto their own time.

The one who is well aware of the tattva of kalatma he confined that which is beyond Kala.

The one who is beyond Kala, beyond the bondage, beyond salvation, who is neither Purusa nor Prakrti, has the universal and the wonderful form, salutation to such Siva, who is the supreme lord.

## Chapter 8 - Creation of the universe for the sports of Siva

The Rsis spoke, “How is the length of age measured presently? What is the upper limit of time in the form of number?

Vayudeva said, “The first measure of life is nimesa, while its upper limit is Samkhyatita.

The time which is spent in the dropping of an eyelid or the winking, is taken to be nimesa. Fifteen nimesas form a kastha.

Thirty kasthas form a kala while thirty kalas form a muhurta. The day as well as night comprise of thirty muhurta.

A month has two fortnights or thirty days and nights. The two fortnights are called the bright and dark fortnights. A month constituting the bright and dark halves is one day of the manes.

There are two ayanas of six months each, which collectively make or year. This is the year according to the human standards.

This one year is taken to be day and night for the gods, which has been ordained by the Sastras. Daksinayana stands for the nights, while the uttarayana stands for the day.

A month of gods is equivalent to thirty years of the humans. Such twelve months comprise on year for the gods.

Three hundred and sixty human years make one divine year of the gods.

The calculation of yugas is based on the same divine years. The people of learnings have conceived to be four yugas in the land of Bharata.

These yugas comprise Satyayuga, Tretayuga, Dvapara and the Kaliyuga.

Out of these yugas, Satyayuga comprises of four thousand divine years. The period of four hundred years, constitutes the intervening junction and a hundred year period constitute Sandhyansa or a subdivision of the junction.

In the three other yugas, their Sandhyas and their Sandhyansas, the thousands and the hundreds get reduced by one.

In this way the twelve thousand years and the surplus period constitute a Caturyuga. A thousand Caturyugas constitutes a Kalpa.

Seventy one Caturyugas constitute a Manvantara. There are fourteen Manvantara in a Kalpa.

Accordingly hundreds and thousands of such kalpas and Manvantaras have passed by this time.

They are quite innumerable and their exact number could hardly be known. It is therefore difficult to highlight them individually in a precise order.

Brahma's one day is equivalent to a kalpa. He is of unmanifest origin. A thousand kalpas make a year of Brahma.

A Brahma's yuga comprises of eight thousand Brahma years. A thousand Brahma yugas make on Savana of Brahma.

Brahma's life span consists of three thousand and three Savanas.

A day of Brahma's life constitute the life of fourteen Indras. A month of his life constitutes life span of four hundreds and twenty Indras. A year of his life has five thousand and forty Indras, while in his entire life span, he has face five hundred and forty thousand Indras.

A day of Visnu is the life time of Brahma. A day of Rudra is equivalent to the life time of Visnu. A day of Siva is equivalent to life period of Rudra. A day of Sadasiva is life period of Siva. A day of Saksat Siva is the life period of Sadasiva. The life time of Sadasiva is equal to the life period of five hundred and forty thousand of the previous deities.

This function of time has been directed by Saksat Siva. O Brahmanas, this is the time of creation as mentioned by me.

This Kalantara shall be known as a day of Paramesvara. Paramesvara's night shall be known to extend so long.

His day is the period of creation, while his night is the period of dissolution. However, it should be clearly understood that he has neither day or night as are known to us.

This performance is only for the benefit of the people. The people, Prajapati, their images, the gods, demons, the sense organs, the pleasures of the sense organs, Pancamahabhutas, Tanmatras, Bhutas and others, function only during the day of Paramesvara and they vanish at the end of the day. Then the universe is created at the end of the night.

The salutation to the great lord Siva, the soul of the universe, whose energy in respect of activity, time and innate nature, is beyond transgression and under his command the whole universe functions.

## Chapter 9 - Creation of the universe and sports of Siva

The Rsis said, “What is the performance of Siva in relation to the creation of the universal and its sustenance.

How did the universe emerge initially? Who expanded it? Who was the person who took it into his vast lap.

Vayudeva said, “A Sakti was born initially known as Santyatita then Maya emerged out of the all powerful Siva. Prakrti emerged out of Maya.

Santyatitapada originated from Sakti and Santipada originated from the same. Then emerged the Vidyapada from which Pratisth&pada came into being.

Now Nivrttipada emerged from Pratisthapada. This is how the creation was initiated by the lord.

The creation of these is in the universe order, while the destruction is in the reverse order. There is a creator apart from and greater them that indicated by these five padas.

Therefore the entire universe is pervaded by the five kalas. Avyakta is the cause there best it is activised by the Atma.

It is admitted that everything begins with intellect and ends with Visesa but the actual production is neither Avyakta nor by the Purusa, because Prakrti is without life or consciousness and Purusa is ignorant. Nothing can be created without an intelligent cause by the instentinent beings viz. Pradhana, Paramam etc. But the universe is dependant over a creator, because it as an effect composed of the parts.

Therefore, the creator must be quite powerful, independent, omnipotent, and omniscient, without any beginning, without end and endowed with majestic quarters. Mahadeva, Mahesvara is the creator of the universe, besides being the protector, and the destroyer of everything. He is separate from it.

The transformation of Pradhana and the activities of Purusa, functions at the command of the truthful lord.

This is the firm belief of the noble people. A person with short wisdom cannot will understand the said aspect.

For the time of the creation of the universe, and during the time of its destruction by that time a hundred years of Brahma elapse.

It is known as Para and the first half it is known as Paradha. At the advent of dissolution, the Avyakta withdrains to itself all its effects and abides in the Atman.

When the universe, having been lodged in this Atman meets with the dissolution, then Pradhana as well as Purusa are lodged in Samana-dharma.

Then Sattvaguna as well as Tamoguna aqually established and merge into one another from al sides.

When both the gunas are equalised, they cannot be separated thereafter, then when the wind becomes calm and peaceful, they also peaceful like the water.

At the time when the universe was unmanifest, the lord meditated upon the great Sakti throughout the night.

At the end of the night, the lord in contact with Maya entered Pradhana and Purusa and activated them.

Thereafter, at the command of Brahma, creation starts out of the unmanifest that is the source of origin and the spot of merger for all living creatures.

With a single piece of the Maya of the supreme soul, the entire creation gradually comes to an end the unprecedented in three worlds, supreme soul, well aware of the righteous path, is called Adhvapati. Salutation to such a lord.

## Chapter 10 - Creation of the universe

Vayu said, “Initially at the instance of Isvara, the secondary elements, starting with the cosmic intellect and ending with visesa, came into being from the Avyakta, presided over by Purusa.

Rudra, Visnu, and Brahma, the three deities were born from these, being the cause of all.

Then was born his Sakti, which could not rest anywhere. Then wit the fortunes like Anima and others the unparallel perfect knowledge emerged.

All the three of them wore made responsible for creation, preservation and the distraction Mahesvara is pleased with their performance.

In the second kalpa, the responsibilities of creation, sustenance and dissolution were entrusted on them, in order to avoid their mutual rivalry due to delusion of intellect.

Having been born from one mother, and own their respective Saktis. They further develop their Saktis with the help of and in association with one mother.

At places Brahma, or Visnu or Rudra is praised. The fortunes of those gods do not enhance or decline with the praise of these gods.

The stubborn, fools, alone denounce those gods, as a result of which, they in the other births are born as the demons or the pisacas.

Lord Mahesvara is beyond the three gunas, having he Caturvyuha (or four faced) form. He is the cause of the creation and support of all.

The supreme soul has created sportily the universe, remains as the lord of the three deities besides those of Prakrti and Purusa.

He is the greatest than the greatest, besides being supreme eternal, free from attributes. He is their soul, besides being then presiding deity.

Accordingly, Mahesvara, Purusa, Prakrti, Sadasiva, Bhava, Visnu and Brahma represent the form of Siva.

In the beginning of the cosmic wisdom, and the great principle were born. With its agitation, there emerged the ego, which was split into three.

The same ego was further split into grace subtle elements besides the sense organs, when the ego was overpowered with sattva, the sattvika creation appeared.

The secondary creation took place at the same time. The intelligence, the five sense organs, the five organs of activity and the mind is in the eleventh, which are involved in the same. The mind became of its qualities functions both ways. When the ahamkara (ego) is associated with tamas, there emerge the Bhuta tanmatra.

Since the supreme soul is the fore rumours of the Bhutas he has been known as Bhutadi. Form the ego of Bhutadi, the Sabda-tanmatras emerged and the sky emerged out of the same.

From the sky emerged the touch, from the touch merged the Vayu or the wind. From Vayu emerged the form, from form emerged the tejas (lustre) and the essence emerged from the tejas.

Water emerged from the rasa, from water emerged the scent, the earth from the scent and from the five Mahabhutas emerged all the mobile and immobiles.

Having been presided over by Purusa, and by the grace of Avyakta, all are engaged in the creation of the globe.

When the cause of the activities of Brahma are fulfilled, Brahma started flourishing in that egg.

He is stated to be the first human with a body. Brahma when was the primordial creator of the universe, was born first of all.

From him (Brahma) the wisdom emerged, which was the cause of wisdom and prosperity having the feelings of wisdom and detachment.

All desires of his mind are grown from Avyakta. All the three gunas are subservient to him. He functions in the three worlds dividing himself in three because all are in his control. He possesses all the attributes and depends on Avyakta. In these three forms, he creates, preserves and destroys.

As created he has four faces, as a destroyer he is Kala and as a Purusa, he has a thousand heads, He is self born and has three static.

With the combination of the Sattva and rajas he is Brahma, with the combination of tamas and rajas he is Rudra, with sattva alone he is Visnu. Thus there is three fold measure of gunas in the lord.

Taking to the form of Brahma, he creates the world; He destroys the living beings as a kala, then in the form Purusa (Visnu) he preserves the universe. These are the three functions of the lord.

These are the three forms of Brahma and since he is divided into three, he is called Triguna, since he has split himself into four, he is called Caturvyuha.

Since he is the lord of the beginning, he is called the Adideva. Since he is unborn, he is called Aja. He is called Prajapati, because he maintains the people.

The golden Meru mountain happens to be his womb. The ocean is the water of the womb. The mountain is the outer skin of the womb.

All the lokas are lodged in that egg. Besides these, the moon, the sun, stars, planets and the wind are also found in the cosmic egg.

This egg has been spread ten times more outside, then in water. It has the lustre ten times more than the waters.

The tejas is covered by the wind ten times. The Vayu (wind) is covered by the sky, while the sky is covered by Bhutadi.

The Bhutadi is covered by Mahat, Mahat is covered by Avyakta. In this way the egg has the seven envelopes.

O excellent Brahman, the eight Prakrtis, the causes of creation, sustenance and distraction are lodged covering each one of these.

Thus having been born of one another, and with the association of each one of them these Prakrtis function. The contraction and expansion takes place in them like the limbs of the tortoise. The Avyakta, reveal the earlier deformities initially and the collects the same.

The entire universe emerges from Avyakta alone, and is ultimately absorbed in the same at the time of dissolution.

With the influence of the time, the gunas become favourable and unfavourable. At the equilibrium of the gunas dissolution takes place.
