This large and thick egg is the source of the origin of Brahma and is called as the sphere of Brahma, who happens to be its lord.

There are thousands of crores of Brahmanas because the presiding deity is all pervading, it is lodged above, below and are all sides of it.

Brahma, Visnu, and Mahesa are lodged at the same places. He creates the universe in association of the presiding deity Siva.

The lord is beyond the manifest. The egg is born of the unmanifest. Brahma is born of that egg, who creates the worlds..

I have highlighted the main creation which is felled with Maya. Ultimately with the sports of Isvara the dissolution is caused.

The unparallel Brahma over his origin to Brahma and Pradhana Prakrti. He is associated with Purusa having white and red complexion, is beyond the beginning, middle or the end, is al powerful.

The excess of rajoguna is the cause of the excess of creation. It creates the eight secondary tattvas in the excess of creation. It creates the eight secondary tattvas in the beginning which cause the worlds to flourish. At the end it devours them.

In so far as the causes established by the Prakrti are concerned, and with the ensuring inclination, because of the unnatural (devoid of Prakrti) fortunes of Siva, there emerges a force, which is known as the Sankalpa Sakti of Mahesvara.

## Chapter 11 - The rescue of the earth from Patala by Varaha

The sages said, “Kindly describe the Manvantara, kalpas besides creations and recreations like sargas and pratisargas etc.

Vayudeva said, “The length of the age of Brahma has already been stated, half of it is called as Par&rdha. With the lapse of the same period, the dissolution takes place at the end.

In each day in the life of Brahma, the fourteen Manus come and go.

Since the Manvantaras and kalpas ancestral and beyond comprehension, it is impossible to describe about them.

You listen to me, even if all of them are described, it would be of no use. Therefore I am out going to describe them individually.

Of all the kalpas, the one, which is presently in vogue, the creation is going on briefly in the same.

O best of Brahmanas, presently the Varaha kalpa is in vogue. It has fourteen Manus in the same.

These are Svayambhu and others who are seven in number, while an equal number is their of Savarni and others. Manu of the present time is Vaivasvata.

The creation and the dissolution in all the Manvantaras take lace similarly and this aspect can be known by the learned people by arguments alone.

At the time of dissolution in the first Kalpa, then all the trees were destroyed with the forceful wind storm.

Then the fire-god burnt every thing like astra. This was followed by the rain storm and the oceans crossed all their limits.

The quarters were sunk in the deep sheet of water and the waters of dissolution had started their fierce devil dances with the waves for their arms, showing movements of gestures by means of water. After the terrific Brahma, taking to the form of Visnu, slept soundly over the water bed.

A mantra should be recited by a person in the form of a verse in favour of Narayana. O excellent sage, you please listen to the said mantra besides its meaning from me.

Water are known as Narah. The living beings of the worlds are like the sense of water. Water is the dwelling place for the lord. Therefore, he is known as Narayana.

Then the gods tried to wake up the lord in the morning, in the same way as lord Mahadeva was waken up at the start of the universe.

The lord who had been sleeping in the water, woke up, got up from his bed. He looked all round at the quarters with the Yogic slumber still lingering in the eyes idly.

Then he could not find anyone else there except himself, which surprised him and he god anxious.

He thought, “where have the pleasant and vast mountains, rivers, cities and the land with forest disappeared with earth.

Thus thinking, when Brahma was unable to found anything about the earth, then he remembered his father the threw eyed Siva.

With the recalling in his mind of Siva, who happens to be the lord of gods, Brahma came to realise that the earth had been submerged in water.

Then in order to rescue the earth, Prajapati indulged in water sports, taking to the divine form of Varaha.

He had the gigantic form of a boar, who created thundering sound like the clouds. Then he thundered like the black clouds.

He had circular limbs, thick shoulders, high waist, small round face part of the thighs, sharp hoofs.

He had two eyes like the gem, round and long body and raised ears, with his breathing he disturb the ocean like the time of dissolution. The manes over the neck were dishevelled, while his shoulders and the cheeks looked quite beautiful.

He was adored with the gem studded ornaments as well as the precious gems, like the cloud rising in the sky with lightening.

Thus Brahma, taking to the form of Varaha, entered the nether world for the rescue of the earth.

Then Brahma, taking to the mountain like form of Varaha, looked graceful as of the feet of Siva in the form of linga had reached Patala.

Then Brahma in the form of Varaha, carrying the earth which was submerged in water, over the tip of his horn, rescued the same from patala.

Observing this, the dwellers of the earth, the siddhas and the sages fill delighted and they showered flowers over him.

The body of Varaha having been covered with flowers appeared like as the mountain of collyrium is covered the rain of with fire flies.

Then lord Varaha turned the earth in its original form and established it appropriately.

Consecrating the earth and establishing the trees and mountains over it, he established the four lokas, as before.

Thus Varaha, rescuing the earth from the vast and deep oceans, established it appropriately. Visvakarma then created the mobile and immobile beings.

## Chapter 12 - Creating of moha, mada, goblins, pisacas, asuras and the Raksasas by Brahma

Vayudeva said, “At the time when Brahma was thinking of resorting to creation, the delusion in the form of darkness appeared before him.

Then gradually darkness, delusion, great delusion, blinding darkness and ignorance appeared before the lord gradually. They were five in all.

With the meditation of arrogant Brahma, the universe appeared before him in five forms. It was covered with darkness as the seed is dropped in a pitches.

Because of the darkness inside and out, it was completely in active. Therefore, those who were born on earth, thin faces, wisdom and sense organs were covered (with darkness).

Because of this the mountains and the trees emerged in the beginning, which could not benefit the earth.

Then Brahma feeling painful, resorted to an other creation as a result of which there emerged the animals and birds.

These birds and animals were conscious within but were but were not so outwardly. Therefore, they could not follow the noble path.

Then Brahma, realising that they were no more useful to him for the work of creation, then thought of assorting to another type of creation. Then the gods of Sattvika type were created.

These men were quite happy and enjoyed all the pleasures. They were not concealed they had light within and light without. They possessed inmate consciousness as well.

When Brahma meditated his mind towards Pradhana then the flow of the creation was inculcated. The humans were born thereafter. This creation was infested with several missing.

They were filled with knowledge within and outside besides possessing the rajoguna and tamoguna. With the fifth grace of Isvara, the four type of creation emerged, which was self divided and comprised of Viparyaya, Sakti, Tusti and Siddhi. They had no possessions; they were of different species, prove to eating and drinking and were known as Bhutas etc.

The second creation is of tanmatras. The third creation of Vaikarika type also known as organic.

The primary creation took place without the intervention of intellect. The fourth was the creation of immobile things.

The fifth creation comprises of birds and animals. The sixth creation was the gods, which emerged from the upper source.

From the seventh lower source the humans were born. The eighth creation is called Anugraha while the ninth one is Kaumara.

The first three creations are of preliminary type devoid of intelligence. The five remaining creations operate with intelligence.

First of all Brahma created the sons who were intelligent like him, who were known as Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana.

Rbhu and Sanatkumara, all the sons of Prajapati were yogis detached and devoid of arrogance.

All of them were devoted to the lord. They were never interested in creation. They left without any desire for the creation.

Thereafter Brahma again performed tapas for creation. This tapas were infructuous.

Then after lapse of a lot of time, he felt painful and got emerged. Then the tears fell from his eyes.

The tears from the eyes of Brahma were turned into the goblins and ghosts. Finding such a creation having emerged out of his tears, Brahma, denounced himself.

Then because of the delusion and anger, Brahma fainted. Then Brahma cast off his breath due to anger.

Then lord Nilalohita also known as Paramesvara, showing his immense grace on him, appeared from the month of Brahman.

He then divided himself into eleven Atmans, when these appeared they were addressed by him.

O sons I have produced you for the welfare of the universe, therefore you establish the universe.

You discarding all the laziness and lethargy keep on enhancing the people.” At these words of the lord, they started pleasing while crying.

Because of their fleeing and crying they came to be known as Rudras. Rudras are vital breaths and vital breaths are Rudras.

Then Rudra, the merciful son of Brahma, bestowed vital breaths on Brahma.

At the return of Brahma to life. Rudra was delighted. Then he spoke to Brahma.

O preceptor of the universe, O Suvrata, O Brahma, don't be afraid. I have given the life back to you. Therefore you get up comfortably.”

Listening to the words of Siva as if heard in a dream, Brahma looked at Siva, with his eyes resembling the lotus.

Then on getting his life back, addressing the lord with deep and choked voice, Brahma addressed him with folded hands.

A mere look at you had delighted me the most. Who are you? Are you the universal soul having eleven forms.”

Listening to his words Siva touched the body of Brahma with his pleasant hands, Mahesvara, the lord of the gods said,

‘‘You take me to be the supreme soul who has emerged out you month as your son. The eleven Rudras have arrived here for you protection.

Therefore, by my grace, freeing yourself from the lethargy, becoming conscious, you resort to creation as before.”

At these words of the lord, Brahma felt pleased and started praising Siva with his eight names.

Brahma said, “O Rudra, you are bearing like the son, salutation to you. You are lord Bhava, the taste, of the form of water, Sarva the form of earth, Nandi, the bull, Isa, Vasu in the form of touch, lord of Pasus, the fire god of great brilliance, Bhima in the form of other, the sound, the subtle element, Ugra of terrible features in the form of sacrificer, Mahadeva, with Uma and the moon. Salutation of the lord of eight forms.”

After thus eulogising the lord Mahadeva, Brahma the grand sire, offered his salutation to the lord and again started praising him. He said, “O lord, O my son Mahesvara, you are lord of the past and the future. You are the destroyer of Kamadeva you have been born out of my body for the purpose of creation.

Hence O lord, since I am engaged in this gigantic task, you help me in this creation work.”

At these words of Brahma, Rudra, the killer of Tripuras, accepted the request of Brahma.

Then lord Brahma getting pleased, honoured Siva and with his permission engaged himself in the other creation.

Then he mentally created the ascetics like Marici, Bhrgu, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Daksa, Atri and Vasistha. He also created Dharma and Sankalpa as well.

They are considered to be the initial sons of Brahma. They were the ancient house holders.

They initiated the twelve divine families including the gods. They are endowed with the holy rights and progeny, graced by the great sages.

Then Brahma be sided with Rudra for the creation of the gods, asuras, manes and humans.

With a devoted mind, Brahma engaged himself in the work of creation. He created gods from the month and the manes from the armpits.

All the asuras were created from his thighs, while the humans were created from lingas. The hungry Raksasas were however created from the redeem.

These sons comprising of tamoguna become the Nisacara or demons. The serpents, Yaksas, Bhutas and Gandharvas were all born from them.

Some of the birds were created of the armpits and chest. The goats were created from the month while serpents were created from the ribs.

The elephants were created from the feet besides the horses, Sarabhas, gavaya, deer, camels, mules, stags and other animals.

The osadhis emerged out of the hair on the body, besides the parts and the roots. Gayatri, Rgveda, Trivrtsama, Samaveda, besides the comforts of the Agnistom yajna were created from the month. Yajurveda, tristupa chanda, Pancadasastoma,

Brhatsama and uktha were created from the right mouth. Sama, Jagati chanda, seventeen stomas, Vairupya and Atiratra mantras emerged out of the western face, Atharvaveda with twenty one Aptorvaman, Anustupa chanda, Vairajasama, emerged out of the northern face. The tall and the dwarfish being emerged out of his different limbs.

The Yaksas, Pisacas, Gandharvas, Apsaras, humans, kinnaras, Raksasas, animals, birds, serpents, besides the indestructible mobiles and immobiles world were created ahead of his creation.

He is engaged n the same activities, having been born again and again. The violence, nonviolence, sweet and harsh, dharma and adharma, truth and false temperaments are achieved by the living beings first according to their deeds and they remain happy with the same. The creator himself assigns the variety and the density to the elements, the sensual objects etc. He himself assigns then the names and forms through the Vedic texts. He bestows the names to the sages and the functions prescribed by the Vedas for those who born at the close of night. When a new session arrives its nature appears itself. Similarly when a new yuga arrives, its native also appears with the same. Thus the creation manifests itself with Brahma's limbs.

This is all the result of the activities of Prakrti from Mahat to Visesa. The planets and the constellations derive their light from the sun and the moon.

The land looks graceful with the rivers, oceans, mountains and abounds in beautiful cities and countries.

The omniscient Brahma boons about in the Brahmavana. He having emerged out of the Avyakta (invisible) seed is lodged by the grace of Isvara.

The Brahmavrksa (eternal tree) having cosmic intellect as its vast branches and stem, the sense organs like the inner hollows, having the spotless leaves of Mah&bhuta and Visesa, flowering with the flowers of dharma and adharma and laden with the fruits of the pleasure and pain, this eternal Brahmavrksa shall be resorted by all living beings.

According to the Brahmanas, the heaven is his head, the sky is the navel, the sun and the moon are his eyes, the quarters are his ears, while the earth is his feet. In this way this unthinkable soul, is the creator of all the living beings.

The Brahmanas emerged from his face, Ksatriyas from his chest, vaisyas from his thighs and the Sudras from his feet. These are the four Varanas.

## Chapter 13 - Emergence of Brahma, Visnu and Rudra in different Kalpas

The Rsis said, “You have stated that lord Siva, the supreme soul was born out of the mouth of Brahma, as a result of which enormous double has developed in our minds.

The one who is the best of the gods, is Virapaksa, possessing brilliance, holder of the trident, Kalatma, lord Rudra, having locks of hair over the head besides being Nilalohita.

He is one, who getting enraged at the end of the yugas, destroys everything getting enraged who is offered salutation by Brahma, Visnu and others getting terrified.

They are all subservient to lord Siva, who could square the world. He is the one who is adored by Brahma, Visnu and Siva, out of fright. All are subservient to Siva, who squeezes the world.

In earlier times he had produced Brahma out of his body and looked after their welfare.

Then how could Rudra the primeval being, become the son of Brahma who is born of Avyakta?

We have heard that Siva is the one, who produced Brahma and Visnu out of his body. Both of them were born of him.

Then how could the two progenitors of the living beings emerged out of each other and possessing both the pronounce or otherwise.

There is nothing that has been unseen or unheard by you, who had bear the disciple of the lord himself.

Then you kindly tell me as to how Brahma, became the lord of all the sages. O dear, we are full of devotion for you and are anxious to listen to the enormous glory of the lord."

Vayudeva said, “O Brahmanas you are very clever in pitting questions. You have enquired of me appropriately. The same question had been asked by me from Brahma and he gave me the reply.

I shall repeat the same episode to you considering the birth of Rudra as I heard from him. Also as to how Brahma and Visnu were mutually born.

All the three of them who indulge in the creation, maintenance and distinction of the mobile and immobile beings in the world, and were born of Mahesvara.

They are betsowed with all the fortunes and are sanctified by the great lord. They are presided over by the Sakti of Siva and remain engaged in their activities. Brahma is for creation, Visnu for sustenance and Rudra is for destruction.

Since all of them possess enormous strength, are unable to tolerate the excellence of one another, they occasionally perform tapas for their father in order to please him.

Achieving his grace completely with the grace of Paramesthi, Rudra produced Brahma and Visnu in the earlier Kalpantara.

The other Rudra produced Rudra and Visnu. In one of the kalpas, Visnu produced Rudra and Brahma.

Narayana who produced by Brahma, Brahma produced Siva. Thus in the different kalpas Brahma, Visnu and Mahesa, were born of one another, engaged in doing good to one another. The sages then picking up the episode of each one of the kalpas, described about the story of their mutual birth. Now you listen to the wonderful, auspicious, story, which destroys the sins.

In the Tatpurusa kalpa there had been a dialogue with Paramesthi Brahma, details of which you please listen from me. In the ancient Meghavahana kalpa, Narayana, taking to the form of clouds in a thousand divine years, held the earth. Realising about the interesting of Visnu, Siva the preceptor of the universe, bestowed him with an indestructible Sakti.

Then Visnu the soul of all, achieving the Sakti of Sarvesvara, engaged himself in the job of creation with Brahma. Observing the grandeur of Visnu, he created Brahma.

Then feeling extremely envious, Brahma spoke smilingly, O Visnu, you can go, I have learnt about the cause of your creation. Rudra is far superior then both of us. There is no doubt about it.

You have become a creator by the grace of Paramesthi, the god of gods. You are the god of sustenance alone.

I adoring Rudra the lord of the gods, shall surely engage myself in the task of creation.”

Brahma, after thus sighting Visnu, then spoke to Siva, who could be achieved with difficulty.

He said, “O lord, O Devesa, Visvesvara, Mahesvara, Visnu had emerged out of your left limbs, while I emerged out of your right side.

Visnu was engaged in the task of the creation of the entire world with me. But to gaining strength from you he is disregarding me.

Visnu is not so much devoted to Mahesvara, as I am. We have been equality been boon of you.

As he showered his grace over Visnu because of his devotion towards Siva (you, O lord the same grace may kindly be showered on me as well.”

When so eulogised Brahma to Siva, the destroyer of the eyes of Bhaga, the compassionate Siva, bestowed everything on him.

Thus obtaining the state of being the Atman of all in a trice, from Siva, Brahma hastened to and saw Visnu. He saw Visnu lying on Sesa (the milky ocean) in his abode in the milk-ocean. A white canopy resembling the sun was spread. It was set with gold and gems and was created by him mentally.

The lotus eyed lord Visnu was sleeping over the bed of the serpent Ananta, having the excellent body and adorned with all the ornaments.

He held a conch and a cakra having the moon like face, with the Srivatsa mark on his chest, and was smiling sweetly.

The earth in the form of a damsel was touching his feet. He had been overpowered with yoganidra like the nectar lodged in the ocean of milk.

Brahma then found Visnu as Kalarudra representing tamoguna, golden egg like rajoguna and Visnu representing Sattvaguna. Mahesvara was found by him representing Nirguna (Thus Visnu was found by Brahma representing the Sattva, rajas, tamas as well as the nirguna forms).

Then Brahma indulging in loose talk, spoke to Visnu, as you had devoured me earlier, I am going to devour you as well.”

Listening to the words of the large armed Brahma, Visnu woke up, saw Brahma and smiled slightly.

At that very moment, Brahma devoured Visnu, who easily emerged out of the eyebrows of Brahma.

At that point of time, in order to witness the prowess of both of them, lord Candrasekhara, Siva in invisible form, appeared in person there.

Since both of them had gracefully received boons from Siva, he reached the place where both Brahma and Visnu were present.

With this performance of Siva, Brahma together with Visnu, were pleased as well as nervous. Both of them offered their salutation to him from a distance.

Then Siva, the holder of the bow Pinaka, becoming merciful on them, entered their hearts in full view of all those present there.

## Chapter 14 - The manifestation of Rudra

The Vayudeva said, “I shall now speak about the emergence of Rudra in each kalpa, because of which, Brahma in the absence of the living beings, engages himself in the work of the creation of the world.

Brahma, who was born of the golden egg, felt painful for lack of wisdom in the living beings.

For the removal of the pain of his heart, and for the increase in the created beings, Rudra the lord of ganas, lord Nilalohita, Paramesvara, getting inspired manifesting as his son or the younger brother, lord Siva incarnate and bestows his shower on him.

The some lord is Isvara, the treasure of the resplendence, free of ailments having no beginning or end, the creator and the lord making all living beings shrink, endowed with loudly questions he is purified by Paramesvara, He is presided over by his Sakti and marked by his symbols.

He possesses the same name, the same form, he can perform the same task. He has the same function as he maintains and abides by his commands.

He has the lustre of a thousand suns and is adorned with a crescent moon. He is adored are decorated with the serpents as his necklaces the shoulder ornaments as well as the wristlets. He wears the waist band of the munja grass.

He looks brilliant holding the skulls of the demon Jalandhara, Brahma and Indra. He has tawny hair, moustaches and beard, which are drenched in the surging waves of the Ganga.

His lips shine with the tips being bitten by the sharp pointed curved fangs. He is seated over the pleasant Kailasa mountain. His right ear is adorned with a sound earring.

He mounts over Maha Nandi, the great bull. His voice is as deep as the clouds. He is powerful like the huge fire. His quite powerful as well.

Thus holding a terrific form Mahesvara the son of Brahman, bestowing the knowledge to Brahma, started creating with him, living beings.

In this way by the grace of Rudra, the creation in every Kalpa functions as a perpetual series.

Once Brahma prayed to Siva to help him in the work of creation. Then the lord created people resembling himself.

He created Rudras having the matted locks of hair over the heads, fearless, blue throated, three eyed, free from old age and death, holding the tridents.

Then Siva filled all the fourteen Bhuvanas with his creation. Finding numerous Rudras, the grand sire spoke to Siva.

“O lord of gods, salutation to you. Do not indulge in such type of creation. Let you, meet with welfare. You kindly create such living beings who could face death.’’

At these words of Brahma, Paramesvara replied to Brahma with a smile.” I do not need such type of beings. You better create such type of inauspicious creation yourself.

Such of the noble people, who have been created by me, are all yajnikas (sacrifices), who will roam about with me.”

Thus speaking to Brahma- the Visvakarma, Rudra together with his bhutas became detached.

Since that time never resorted to the creation which had to face death. He stands in yogic posture, till the dissolution of the universe.

## Chapter 15 - Siva's appearing before Brahma in Ardhanarisvara form

Vayudeva said, ‘‘When the creation made by Brahma could not expand, then he thought of creation of the beings by sexual intercourse.

In earlier times the females had not been created by Isvara and as such, Brahma could not resort to the creation of being by sexual intercourse.

Thereafter Brahma, for the establishment of his task, he thought of consulting, Siva for the purpose of increase in the creation.

Without his grace, the creation could never grow. Thus thinking Brahma then thought of resort tot he performing of the penance.

Thus Brahma, meditated upon the primordial and eternal Sakti of Siva, who is quite subtle, auspicious, pleasant, who could be achieved by pious thoughts, besides being devoid of attributes, unsullied, unramified, unruffled, perpetual and which remains with IsVara always. In this way Brahma thought about the lord, and his supreme Sakti, while performing the tapas.

Because of the severe penance of Paramesthi, the father of the universe, the lord was pleased in no time.

Then Siva entering in some image in some amsa, took to the form of Ardhanarisvara and himself appeared before Brahma.

Finding the lord, who was beyond darkness, being indestructible, and the supreme lord, who is unparalleled, without a second, incomprehensible, invisible to liberations, the creator, the supreme lord endowed with creative power, who is devoid of arguments is devoid of malicious appearance, is beyond measure, unaging, stable, unmoving, having no attributes, dormant, infinite, omnipresent, bestower of boons, beyond the difference between existent and non-existent, beyond comparison, in whom one can take refuge besides being everlasting and permanent, in whom the meaning of the reality of the Vedas is enshrined, Brahma adored the lord reciting these Suktas and Stotras.

Brahma said, “O lord, O Mahadeva, L Jayesvara, Mahesvara, possessor of excellent virtues, O lord of all the gods, victory to you. Victory to you.

O goddess of welfare, O leader of Prakrti, victory to you. You remain away from Prakrti and you are beautiful by nature, victory to you. You possess useful Mahamaya, useful mind, useful sports an useful prowess. Victory to you.

You are the mother of the universe, the form of the entire universe, carrier of the entire universe, besides being friendly to the entire universe, victory to you.

You have stable fortunes, have a stable place to line, O lord of eternal form, O lord of permanent devotees, victory to you.

O goddess, you are the creator, sustainer and the destroyer of Brahma, Visnu and Siva, victory to you.

O lord, from whose eyebrow the terrific fire emerges, who can destroy the fire emerging from his self control all the worldly tattvas, victory to you. The one who is beyond the comprehension of the gods, whose eyes have been brightened with a look at the soul, who possesses the Sakti of Sthulatma, victory to you.

The one who has overpowered various types of the tattvas of the world, whose both the feet have been placed over the heads of the demons, victory to you.

You are quite good in protecting your devotees and can very well destroy the poisonous tree in the form of the universe, victory to you.

You can shatter pride of the valorous and arrogant people, deprived of other's riches, you remain away from the universe. Victory to you.

Victory to you, O immortal lord who hast laid the rite of “five objects.” Be victorious, O goddess having the form of the hymn with the knowledge of the the “five objects.”

You are the physician for the grave ailment of the universe, salutation to you. You are the destroyer of the eternal filth in the form of ignorance, victory to you, O Candrika.

You acted like the fire of death for Tripura, victory to you. O Tripurabhairavi, you possess the three gunas. You are also destroyer of the three gunas. Victory to you.

You are the foremost omniscient, you bestow perfect knowledge to all. You have beautiful and divine limbs. You grant the requests of all. Victory to you.

O Lord, where is your abode of great splendour, and where are the worthless words of ours. Still O lord forgive me for that babble but with devotion.

In this way, the four faced Brahma, the creator of the universe, offering several prayers, bowed in several to Rudra and Rudrani again and again.

The stotra recited by Brahma is quite auspicious, which pleases Siva and Siva in the form of Ardhanarisvara.

Whosoever recites this stotra for any particular purpose, he reaps the fruit of the same with the grace of Siva and Siva.

(Then Brahma said,) Both of you are the creators of all the living beings of the world, you have taken the form of human bodies which get destroyed. Therefore, I always adore both of you.

## Chapter 16 - Manifestation of the divine Sakti

Vayudeva said, “Then the delighted god Siva spoke to Brahma with a benign and sweet smile. His voice sounded like thunder.

All the letters were sounded with royal qualities, besides being pure and efficient in protection of all the subjects.

These words were extremely pleasant, spoken with broad mind, joined which were spoken by Brahma.

Siva said, “O Son, O fortunate one, O my son, O grand sire, I have known the importance of your words.

You performed tapas for the expansion of the living beings. Having been pleased wit your tapas, I shall fulfil all your desires.

Thus speaking the sweet and liberal words, Siva then started creating the goddess from a part of his body. It is the goddess whom the scholars of the Vedas call the mighty Sakti endowed with divine qualities of Siva, the great soul.

The birth, old age and death are devoid of her life. Bhavani had emerged out of the body of Siva.

By approaching him the speech, with mind and the sense organs get receded. She appeared to have manifest from the body of her lord.

The goddess who pervades the entire world due to her glory, she looks wonderful like other human beings.

She deludes the entire universe with her delusion. Inspite of her emerging from the body of Isvara, she is unborn.

Even the gods are unaware of his transmotive. She manifested herself from the body of Siva.

The seeing the great goddess who is omniscient, omnipresent, subtle, devoid of the difference between sat and asat, the goddess illuminates the universe with her brilliance. Brahma then offered his salutation to her.”

Brahma said, O goddess, I was created by the lord with beginning and was entrusted in the task of creation. Accordingly I perform my job of creating the universe.

O goddess, I have created all the gods and others mentally, but they do not increase inspite of the repeated creation. Henceforth, I intend to create the living beings by sexual intercourse.

The race of the women, has not manifest from you, because of which, the everlasting race of women cannot be created by me.

Thus the creation of the Saktis is possible from you alone. Because you bestow Sakti to all the living beings at all the laces at all the times.

You are the bestower of the boons, roaming about everywhere, Saiva one and form of Maya, therefore you enhance the Saktis of mobile and immobile nature from your amsa. I pray to you for the same.

For the removal of the fear of the universe, you better appear as the daughter of my son Prajapati, Daksa.” Thus Brahma-yoni Brahma prayed to the goddess.

Then he produced a Sakti from the space in the centre of the eyebrows. Looking at here Hara the god of the gods smilingly said,

“Performing tapas for Brahma, adore him and fulfil his desire.” Siva's command was accepted by him.

Then lord Siva, handing over the Sakti to Brahma, disappeared. Thereafter she was born as the daughter of Daksa Prajapati.

And the woman was absorbed into the body of Siva. Mahadeva thereafter disappeared from the scene.

O excellent Brahmanas, the creation with the sexual intercourse started thereafter, after which Brahma felt delighted.

Thus I have narrated to you the story of the origin of the goddess This story of the creation of the living beings measures merits, which should be heard with attention.

One who recites or listens to the story of the origin of the goddess, he getting blessed achieves sons.

## Chapter 17 - Emerging of Satarupa from the body of Brahma

Vayudeva said, “Thus by achieving the supreme and everlasting Sakti from Isvara, Brahma desired of creating beings by means of sexual intercourse.

He also transformed himself into a half male and a half female. From the female half was born Satarupa.

From the male half Virat merged, who was subsequently known as the first Svayambhuva Manu and a human.

Then the goddess Satarupa, performing severe tapas, got the illustrious Manu as her husband.

Satarupa bore him two excellent sons named Priyavrata and Uttanapada.

She also bore two illustrious daughters of great fortune named Akuti and Prasuti from whom emanates all creation.

Then Svayambhuva Manu, gave his daughter Prasuti to Daksa Prajapati, while Akuti was given in marriage to Ruci Prajapati.

Both Akuti and Ruci two daughters named Yajna and Daksina was born. The universe was expanded because of both of them.

Daksa on the other hand produced twenty four mothers of the universe from Prasuti the daughter of Svayambhuva Manu.

Thirteen of his daughters named Sraddha, Laksmi, Dhatri, Pusti, Tusti, Medha, Kriya, Buddhis, Lajja, Vapu, Santi, Siddhi and Kirti were married by Daksa to Dharma. The eleven daughters were younger to them, known by the names of Khyati, Sati, Arthasambhuti, Smrti, Priti, Ksama, Sannati Anusuya, Urja, Svaha, Svadha, who were given to Bhrgu, Siva, Marici, Angira, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya, Atri, Vasistha, Pavaka and Pitara and other sages. Dharma produced thirteen sons from Sraddha were produced by Dharma, who were the form of pleasure. The progeny which caused pain was produced by Adharma from Himsa.

From Adharma, the sons like Nikrti and others were born, who were possessing the inauspicious symptoms. They had no sons or daughters, because they were deprived of the truth as well as dharma.

Thus was the tamasika creation in the form of adharma, Sati the dearest daughter of Daksa, who had been married to Siva, denounced her brothers and the parents in connection with the denouncement of Siva her husband and ended her life.

She was then reborn from Himalaya and Mena. Then Rudra looking at Sati and other Rudras resembling him, created innumerable living beings. The relevant episode, has already been described. From Bhrgu and Khyati, Laksmi the wife of Narayana, was born.

She gave birth to two sons, named Dhata and Vidhata, having the life of a Manvantara. They were blessed with thousands of sons and grandsons.

During the Svayambhuva Manvantara, they came to be known as those belonging to the race of Bhargava. From Marici and Sambhuti a son named Paurnamasa was born, besides the four daughters, whose dynasty was sufficiently developed. In the same dynasty, Kasyapa, having a large number of sons was born.

Smrti the wife of Angira gave birth to his sons named Agnidhra and Sarabha, besides the four daughter. They had thousands of sons and the grandsons. A son named Dantogni was born of Priti the wife of Pulastya who earlier in the Svayambhuva Manvantara was well known in Agastya.

His entire progeny is attributed to the Paulastya dynasty Ksama, the wife of Pulaha also gave birth to his sons.

Their sons named Kardama, Asuri and Sahisnu, became illustrious like Tretagni. His dynasty continued for a long time quite gracefully.

Sannati the wife of Kratu produce the sons as glorious as her husband. They had no wives or sons, because all of them were Urdhvaretas.

They were sixty thousand in number and came to be known as the Balakhilyas. All of them made ahead of Aruna, surrounding the sun.

Anusuya, the wife of the sage Atri gave birth to five sons and a daughter named Sruti, who was the mother of Sankhapada.

The names of the five sons were Satyanetra, Havya, Apomurti, Sanaiscara and Soma.

The sons and grandsons of the Atris were multiplied to a hundred thousands in the Svayambhuva manvantara.

Urja was the wife of the sage Vasistha, who produced seven sons. Pundarika was their elder sister.

Saptarsis (seven rsis) are known by the names of Raja, Gatra, Urdhvabahu, Savana, Anaya, Sutapa and Sukra.

The gotra was named after Vasistha. The Svayambhuva Manvantara was spread over hundreds of billions of years, before it came to an end.

Thus I have narrated to you the creation of the sags in brief. O Brahma, I am incompetent to speak in detail absent the same.

The mind born son of Brahma, who resembles the fire of Rudra, Svaha happens to his wife, who gave birth to three illustrious sons.

They were known by the names of Pavaka, Pavamana and Suci. The one who could not be churned was known as Pavamana. The one who was connected with lightning came to be known as Pavaka.

The solar fire is called Suci and their sons are known as Havyavaha, Kavyavaha and Saharaksa. They are the deities manes and gods. They have forty nine sons and grandsons.

All the three of them were lodged on the Kamya, Naimittika and Ajasra rites, besides being ascetics and the performers of the Vratas.

All of them were related to Rudra being his devotee. Thus whatever is dropped in the fire, it is attributed to have been offered for Rudra. There is no doubt about it. Thus the fire dynasty has been highlighted.

O Brahmanas, there can be no expansion of the same. Now came the dynasty of the manes. The manes, who are proud of this own positions have six seasons.

Therefore the manes are also addressed as Rtus. This has been ordained by the vedas. All the mobile and immobiles originates from the respective seasons.

Because of this the manes are also called the Rtus, because they are said to be proud of the seasons.

The manes having their own fortunes, the noble ones, are lodged in the sky. There are two types of manes, viz. Agnisvatta and Barhisada.

The manes belong to two types of householders viz. those perform the homa and others who do not do so. From Svadha the wife of the manes, this daughters were born, who are quite well known.

Then Mena the daughter of Himalaya gave birth to Mainaka, Kraunca, Gauri as Ganga which was purified with touch of the limbs of Siva.

Dharani, the wife of Mem mountain, produced the Mandara, the son of Mem, because of his tapas became the companion of Kailasa, the abode of Siva.

His wife Dharani produced three well- known daughters known by the names of Vela, Niyati and Ayati. The last two Niyati and Ayati were married to the sons of the sage Bhrgu. The details of their dynasties have been discussed under Svayambhuva Manvantara.

Vela the wife of Sagara gave birth to an excellent daughter known as Savarna who was married to Pracinabarhi.

From the Samudra-kanva of Pracina- barhis, ten sons were born, known as Pracetas, who were well versed in archery.

Due to the curse of Siva, Daksa in Svayambhuva Manvantara, became the son of Pracetas in the Caksusa Manvantara.

Thus the divine dynasties attended upon by the gods, of the noble souled sons of Brahma, Dharma and others have been described by me. O Brahmanas, they observed the holy rites. They had progenies and were embellished with great prosperity.

The creation born of Prajapatis, is beyond enumeration even in a hundreds of crores of years.

The holy royal races function in two different lines of Solar and the lunar.

These well known races comprise of Iksvaku, Ambarisa, Yayati, Nahusa, which are quite well known and reputed.

There were other Royal Rsis having enough of Saktis, what is the use of describing of those royal dynasties, because their existence has already been diseased.

The learned people do not think it appropriate to discuss about them in the context of the adoration of Siva. Therefore they do not find their mention here.

The main reason is that the creation has been discussed only to highlight the glory of the lord, what is the use of further expansion.

## Chapter 18 - Birth of Sati as daughter of Daksa, Daksa's enmity with Siva, Sati burns herself in yajna fire

Rsis said, “Sati, the daughter of Daksa Prajapati, putting an end to her life was reborn as the daughter of Himalaya from his wife Mena.

Such a Daksa Prajapati rebuked Siva. What was the reason for it? Why was Siva rebuked?

O Vayudeva, how was Daksa reborn after the curse of Siva? You kindly narrate the story relating to the period prior to the Caksusa Manvantra.”

Vayudeva said, “Let all of you listen. I am going to relate the story of the evil minded Daksa. Because of his sinful arrogance, he polluted all the gods.

In earlier times, all the gods, demons, siddhas, ascetics, once went to Siva to have an audience with him, at the peak of the Himalaya mountain.

Both Siva and Parvati were at that point of time seated over a divine throne. O Brahmanas, he met with all the Brahmanas and others.

At the same time Daksa Prajapati also arrived in order to meet his daughter and son- in-law.

Then because of the arrival of Daksa in the abode of his daughter, and Siva because of his pride did not speak to any god.

Then Daksa unmindful of the influence of Siva and Sati became envious of Siva and Sati both.

Because of the move of the destiny, Daksa because of the same enmity, did not invite Siva and Sati in his yajna.

At the same time, he invited all other sons- in-law and individually welcomed each of them.

Learning about the function at the abode of Daksa from Narada, Sati went to her parental home, with the permission of Siva.

Sati boarded the place with her close friends, which was quite divine with doors opening on all the sides. It was in good condition and could be easily mounted. It was quite charming, and shed golden lustre various types of gems were studded in it and its canopy was covered with pearls. It was decorated with the flower garlands. It was wrought of the molten gold and was supported by the pillars all round studded with gems. The adamantine steps were nicely built. The corals were use in the decoration of the pillars and festoons. The main seat of the plane was studded with gems and a silken cloth with floral designs covered with same. Though the rays of the diamonds were defused, a platform decorated with gems was shining. In the front a flagstaff resembling the clouds decorated the plane in the front, with an insignia of a great bull. This flagstaff was also studded with gems. The main doors was guarded by the ganas of Siva clad in gem studded bodices, carrying caves in their hands. The female musicians well versed in playing on cymbals, flutes, vasunas, and other musical instruments, were seated there clad in the best of costumes and adorned with best of ornaments.

Two Rudra virgins started moving the flywhisks. The face of the goddess started beaming when the flywhisks were being moved. It appeared like the swans fighting over the lotus flowers, Sumalini held an umbrella over her head.

The splendid umbrella kept on of pearl strings, while like the moon shining over the face of the goddess like the lunar disc shines above the nectar vase.

In the front, there appeared Subhavati shown seated wearing a sweet smile over her face and playing the game of dice for the delight of Sati. Suyasa carried the gem studded sandals of the goddess, holding them against her breast and thus served her. The other damsel held the mirror in her hand.

One of the maids hold the fan of Tada leaves, the other held the betel casket. Some one carried a try in her hand.

Some one carried the beautiful fragrant flower in her hand, while some on carried the jewellery casket in her hands.

Some one carried the collyrium, some one toilet paste, while other maids attended to the jobs appropriate to the time.

All the maids kept one serving the goddess from all the sides. Then the goddess Paramesvari appeared quite graceful among them.

As the moon looks graceful during the winter nights surrounded by the stars, similarly the goddess looked quite graceful.

Then with the blowing of the conch, the drums for departure were beaten. Thereafter the sweet music was played upon. Then hundred of baghs and other sweet instruments without being beaten along with the sound of the clapping of hands.

Then eight hundred groups of thousand strong-armed ganas, having brilliance equal to lord Siva, mounted over the bulls and moved ahead of all. The glorious chief of Ganas, honoured by the moon and Nandisvara sat on the bull like Brhaspati on an elephant.

Ganapati moved on having been adored by Soma and Nandisvara. The sound of the beating of the drums by the gods were heard in the sky which was quite pleasant to the ears. The clouds started thundering.

The sages started dancing and the siddhas were pleased. The clouds and the gods showered flowers on the way.

Then Mahesvari accompanied with the gods, entered her parental home as if in a moment.

At her sight, Daksa became infuriated which subsequently became he cause of his destruction. He worshipped her younger sisters too in an insulting manner.

Then the moon faced goddess, Sati found her parents in the court and with a liberal mind said to them.

Sati said, “O dear one, you have not adored the lord to whom all the beings from Brahma to pisacas are subservient.

Should the eldest daughter be adored like this? By insulting me instead of honouring me, you have acted in a degraded manner.”

Then Daksa getting enraged said, ‘‘There are my daughters who are more adorable then you.

Their husbands evoke my respect and joy and are adorable to me. They are superior to your husband lord Siva.

He is stiff souled and of tamasika nature, who is being served by you. Because of this you have earned my ire and rebuke you. Siva is opposed to me.

At these words of her father, addressing all the gods and the Rsis present in the yajna, she said feeling irritated.

O Daksa! You are unnecessarily blaming my husband Mahesvara, the lord of universe, without any reason.

The one who steals knowledge, the one who betrays the preceptor besides those who denounce Vedas and Isvara, are sinful and as such have to be punished, according to the vedas.

Because of this grave sin, you will suddenly get a punishment because of the moves of destroy.

Because you have not adored Tryambaka, the gods of gods, therefore your evil race has been destroyed. You should understand the same.”

The irritated Sati then fearlessly after speaking to his father thus, ended her life from the body the got of Daksa and went to Himalaya.

With the arrival of Sati in the abode of Himalaya, he achieved the reward of all the noble deeds of his life for which he had performed the hard tapas.

Because of this Isvari showered her grace over the king of the mountains and with the use of her Yogamaya, she owned the king of the mountains as her father.

Then Sati denounced the precisely Daksa and leaving the place, therefore with the decline of the power of the mantras the yajna of Daksa was decorated.

When Siva learnt of the incident of Satis leaving the laces of Daksa by ending her life. Then he the enemy of Tripura, felt enraged over Daksa as well as the Rsis. Then he pronounce a curse on them.

He said, “O Daksa, since for my sake, you have insulted the sinless Sati and other daughters honoured along with their husbands, these sons-in-law of yours will be born but not of a womb in the sacrifices of Brahma in the Vaivasvata Manvantara.

‘‘Î Daksa, in the Caksusa Manvantara, you will be the king of the humans. Then you would become the son of Pracetas and the grandson of Pracinabarhis.

O evil minded one, I shall also create repeated obstructions in the activities of you dharma, artha, kama and moksa."

At this words of the illustrious Rudra, casting of the body of Svayambhuva, felt painful an fell down on the ground.

In the Caksusa Manvantara, however, Daksa was born as the son of Praceta and the grandson of Pracinabarhi.

Bhrgu and other sages also were born in the Vaivasvata Manvantara as Varuna at the Mahayajna.

During that period of virtuous sacrifice of the wicked Daksa in the Vaivasvata Manvantara, Siva race created obstacles.

## Chapter 19 - Origin of Virabhadra

The Rsis said, “Why did Siva create obstructions in the task of Daksa who had been engaged in the religious practices? I would like to know.”

Vayudeva said, “Himalaya had been happy with the arrival of the great goddess in his abode.

When Siva was married to her, then he started roaming about with Parvati over the Himalaya mountain. In this way a long time was passed.

On the arrival of the Vaivasvata Manvantara, Daksa the son of Praceta intended to perform a yajna.

When he went to the Gangadvara, an auspicious place of Rsis and Siddhas in the rear pail of Himalaya, he started performing a yajna.

At that point of time, Indra and all other gods thought of participating in the said yajna.

The twelve Adityas, eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, Sadhyagana, Marut ganas, Usmapa, Somapa, Ajyapa, Dhumapa,

Asvinikumras, manes and all others sages together with Visnu, participated in the yajna.

Seeing all the gods, except Siva, arrived there, the Dadhici feeling irritated said to Daksa.

Dadhici said, “One who adores the unadorable ones and does not adore those who are to be adored, earns a grave sin.

The place where the inauspicious people are adored and the auspicious people are neglected, there the harsh punishment is awarded by Isvara.”

Thus speaking the great Rsi again spoke to Daksa” why don’t you worship the adorable Pasupati?”

Daksa replied, "I have eleven Rudras, wearing matted locks of hair holding a trident each. I am not aware of Mahesvara besides them.”

Dadhici said, ‘‘What is the use of adoring all other gods in the yajna while you are neglecting Rudra the lord of the yajna.

The imperishable lord has created Brahma, Visnu and Mahesa. The living beings from Brahma to piscacas are subservient to him.

The one who is beyond Prakrti and Purusa, and is meditated upon by the great yogis, yogic scholars and the seers of truthful principles,

The one who is imperishable, the supreme Brahman, and is the form of sat and asat who is without beginning, middle or end, beyond controversies besides being the ancient one,

The one who is the creator of the universe, sustainer, and the destroyer, is known as Mahesvara therefore, I do not find anyone else (to be of any importance) except him.”

Daksa said, ‘‘Visnu happens to be the lord of yajna and his share has appropriately been kept in the golden vase here. Distributing the same, you start the yajna.

Dadhici said, ‘‘Rudra happens to be the lord of all the gods, but you have neglected him. Therefore, your yajna is not going to be completed.”

Thus speaking these words, the irritated sage Dadhici returned to his abode from that place.

Inspite of the departure Dadhici, and in the face of the ensuing misfortune, the gods did not desert Daksa.

O Brahmanas, at the same time, knowing about all this from Siva, Parvati urged the lord to destroy the sacrifice of Daksa.

At the inspiration of the goddess, Siva produced Virabhadra as the lord of ganas for the destruction of the yajna of Daksa.

He had a thousand faces, and an equal number of eyes. He carried a thousand clubs and a thousand arrows.

He also held the spears, kankas, bows, cakras and vajra in his hands. The crescent adored his head.

He held a shining vajra in his hands, the head had the lustre resembling the lightning. He had horrible fangs. He had the gigantic face and bulls.

His tongue resembled the lightning, lingo lips and he created thundering sound like the cloud and the ocean. He was clad in tiger skin dripping with blood.

He wore a circular kundala which had stuck to both the cheeks. Her head was absorbed with skulls of the gods.

He wore the golden shoulderlets, and the jingling anklets. He was shining with heaps of gems. A necklace decorated his chest.

He had the prowess equal to Sarabha, lion and tigers. He walked like the intoxicated elephant.

He had the resplendence of the conch, flywhisk, jasmine flower, moon and the lotus and appeared as if the Himalaya was moving.

He was like the snow capped lord of mountain, who had become mobile. He was surrounded by the fire flames. With ornaments of peaks, he had been shining brilliantly like the fire of the time of dissolution of the world.

Virabhadra the chief of the ganas, knelt and offered his salutation. With folded hands he sat before lord Siva.

At the same time Parvati created Bhadra Mahesvari Bhadrakali as her representative to march to the place of Daksa.

Finding Bhadrakali with Virabhadra, Siva said, “Let you meet with welfare.

She spoke Siva, with goddess, “O Mahadeva, you kindly get me your command. What has to be desire by me?

Then Tripurari Siva in order to please Parvati, spoke in deep voice to Virabhadra having large arms.

Mahadeva said, “You at once destroy the yajna of Daksa, the son of Praceta. O lord of the ganas, you associate Bhadrakali with yourself for the purpose.

O Ganesvara, I shall myself witness your courage and prowess, by staying in the hermitage of the sage Raibhya.

The trees at Kanakhala, near Gangadvara resemble the mountains of gold or the Sumeru mountain.

The yajna of Daksa is being performed there presently. You go at once and destroy it. Don’t delay.”

At these words of Siva, Parvati started looking at Virabhadra and Bhadrakali as the cows stares at her calf.

Embracing him like Kartikeya and smelling his head, she talked sweetly.”

The goddess said, “O Son Virabhadra, O great warrior, you have been born to please me. You remove my anger.

O Ganesvara, Daksa, preserving enmity with me, is performing the yajna, without inviting me. Therefore, you destroy the yajna.

At my request, O dear, inflict violence in the company of Bhadra. Kill the sacrificer and let the holy sacrifice be turned into nonsacrifice.

Accepting the total command of Siva and Siva, the performer of surprising sports, Virabhadra was about to have the place.

Then lord Virabhadra the dweller of the cremation grounds, getting enraged and in order to remove the anger of the goddess,

produced a hundred crores of Ganesvaras from his right arm and the chief of Ganas from his skin-pores..

Besides that he produced innumerable Ganesvaras from his feet, legs, back, ribs, face, neck, rectum, head, throat and the belly, who were quite valorous comparable to him in prowess. The entire sky and the universe was covered with those Ganesvaras.

All of them had thousand hands, holding thousands of weapons and had the lustre of Rudra.

They carried in their hands the Saktis, sulas, clubs, tankas, upala, rocks and resembled Rudra or the fire of the time of dissolution. They had three eyes and wore the matted locks of hair.

The ganas. born of Virabhadra started roaming in the sky while thundering and mounted over the lions.

Surrounded by the ganas, Virabhadra looked as Bhairava looks graceful with numerous fire flames during the time of dissolution.

Siva mounted over Nandi, marched on, surrounded by them. At that point of time Virabhadra resembled Siva.

Virabhadra mounting over Nandi, then had an umbrella held over his head which was decorated with the strings of beads. The flywhisks were also moved on him.

Bhasita was shining by the side of Bhadra like the lord of the mountain by the side of Siva.

Virabhadra too became resplendent in his company, since she held the white chowries like the lord with the trident as weapon and the crescent moves.

Bhanukampa of great splendour, adorned with gold ornaments studded with gems, started blowing the auspicious white conch in front of Virabhadra.

The gods sounded the big drums in the sky, and the clouds showered the rain of flowers.

The cool break carrying the fragrance of flowers, started blowing which provide comforts to the travellers.

All the Ganesvaras god ready for waging the war. They resorted to dancing singing and the shouting.

Then Virabhadra in association with Bhadrakali, appeared so graceful as Siva appears with Parvati.

Suddenly, Virabhadra reached the boundary wall of the golden yajna together with his ganas.

Then Virabhadra the foremost of Siva ganas entered the place of yajna as Rudra appears at the time of the dissolution for the destruction the universe.

## Chapter 20 - Destruction of the sacrifice of Daksa

Vayudeva said, “Then Virabhadra looked at the vast yajna attended to by the immensely illustrious sages, and other prominent gods, with lots of banners fluttering there.

The kusa grass was spread there besides the glittering vases of gold for use in the yajna.

The Rsis were well-versed in the performing of the yajna as prescribed in the Vedas. There were thousands of divine damsels as well as apsaras who were playing on the Vedic tunes over the musical instruments like Venu, Vina and others.

The glorious Virabhadra, looking at the yajna started thundering like the cloud.

Then the crowd of the ganas kept on chattering in the sky, the sound of which echoed in all the directions putting the thunder of the ocean to shame.

Feeling panicky with the thundering sound all the gods fled from the scenes, leaving their costumes and ornaments behind, in all the four directions.

At that time, it appeared as if the Sumeru mountain had fallen or the earth had been pierced through; the amazed gods uttered repeatedly, “what is all this that has happened?”

As the elephants flee listening to the lion’s roars, similarly several of the people there fled away in flight and others were killed on the spot.

The mountains were shattered. The wind storm started blowing. The waives from the ocean were raised.

There was no fire, nor was the scorching heat of the sun there. The planets, the constellations were also not shining.

But in the mean time Virabhadra and Bhadrakali arrived with their ganas at the place of yajna.

Observing them the frightened Daksa, kept on sitting there firmly. He getting enraged said, “Who are you? What do you want?” Listening to the words of the wicked Daksa, the immensely illustrious Virabhadra spoke with the voice thundering like the clouds.

Smilingly he looked at Daksa, the gods and the Rsis and spoke meaningful words without any excitement.

Virabhadra said, “We are the servants of the immensely illustrious Siva. We have arrived here to receive our share of the yajna. You better give our share to us.

In case no share for us has been set apart in the yajna, you then apprise us of the reason for the same. Otherwise fight with us.”

At these words of the chief of the ganas, the gods associated with Daksa replied “Whatever is been done by us, is based on the Vedic hymns. We are not otherwise competent.

The gods then recited the mantras. At this, Virabhadra said, “O gods, you have been overpowered with delusion, by neglecting Mahesvara, who is entitled to the first part of the share of the yajna.

Inspite of that the gods did not offer the share of Siva to Virabhadra under the influence of delusion and because they desired to be punished by Virabhadra.

When the truthful and the beneficial words could cut no ice with Daksa, then all the hymns left for Brahmaloka.

Then Virabhadra the leader of the ganas spoke to Visnu and other gods, “because of your arrogance you have not admitted the authority of the mantras.

Because of the same, all of us have been humiliated in this yajna. Therefore I shall remove your arrogance at the cost of your lives.”

Thus speaking, lord Virabhadra, started burning the sacrificial altar, with the fire flames emerging out of his eyes in the same way as Siva had burnt the Tripuras.

Then the lords of the ganas having mountain like huge bodies uprooted all the sacrificial pillars and tied them to the necks of the Hotr priests with ropes. They smashed and powdered the sacrificial vases of different shapes and sizes, consigned them in water and threw away all the materials kept for use in sacrifice in the lotus waters of the Ganga river.

All the heaps of food stuffs in the vicinity, besides the rivers of milk, curd, exuding nectar were destroyed. The curd formed sweat slimy slush. The sweat smelling meat and eatables lay in high and low heaps. The juicy beverages were also there. The army of Virabhadra started drinking, eating, consuming also throwing and destroying them. The soldiers of Virabhadra started killing all the gods as well as the Lokapalas, with vajras, cakras, great tridents, saktis, nooses, patisas, musals, swords, tankas, bhindipalas, battle-axes and other weapons.

The warriors born out of the body of Virabhadra started killing the gods. Shouting to kill, to cut off, pierce etc.

They cried “Snatch away, kill them, tear them out, uproot them.” Thus the thundering sound was heard which pierced through the ears.

The words of the Sivaganas worthy of the battlefield were heard here and there. The eyes of sons of them were left open, while the lips and palatals of some of them had been cut off.

The warriors were killing the ascetics dragging them out of their hermitages. They took away the sacrificial ladles and the spoons and consigned them into the fire flames of the sacrificial altar. The domes and the platforms studded with gems were damaged by the warriors who sang, laughed and shouted again and again, while drinking blood like wine. The leaders of the ganas danced.

The leading ganas who were strong like the bulls roughed up the gods including Indra. They were like elephants lions and bulls, possessing universal glory and were engaged in the hair-raising activities of total destruction.

Some of the ganas were happy with their performance, some of them were killing others, some were running. Some of them, jumped danced sang, thundered and laughed again and again.

Some of them intended to devour clouds with water, some of them were jumping in order to capture the sun. Some of the Siva ganas were trying to fly with the air in the sky.

Some of them started destroying the doors and the windows, uprooting or razing the homas over the ground. Then throwing the homas in the oceanic water, the ganas started thundering like the clouds of the time of dissolution.

The doors frames of the yajna-mandapa were damaged, the windows, ceiling frames and the halls of the complex were completely destroyed. The entire edifice of yajna caved in helplessly like the unfounded statement.

When the houses were so raised to the ground the women cried, helplessly saying, “O husband, Î child, Î father, Î brother, Î mother, Î uncle.

## Chapter 21 - Flight of Visnu and other gods from the place of Yajna

Vayudeva said, “Then Visnu, the foremost of the gods, besides Indra and other gods, getting frightened fled away here and there.

Virabhadra finding that sons of the gods were fleeing uninjured and others were running away unpunished, felt irritated.

Holding the trident which removed all the Saktis the long armed Virabhadra, facing the sky started emitting fire from his mouth.

As a lion makes the elephant to run away in flight, similarly he put the gods on the run. Their action of fleeing from the battlefield pleased Virabhadra.

He looked attractive like the intoxicated elephant. The valorous Virabhadra made the gods shaky.

As the lord of the herd of intoxicated elephants, churning the huge lake makes it red, blue and white, similarly, Virabhadra wearing the tiger skin with golden inlaid with excellent gold and pearls. Then cutting piercing soaking tearing and pounding, Virabhadra moved among the hosts of gods, like the fire consuming the dry grass.

As he hurriedly moved about, holding a spear all alone, the gods took him to be having a thousand forms. On the other hand the enraged Bhadrakali in excitement fought with the gods, while shining like the flames of fire at the end of kalpa as a result of which the entire universe faces conflagration.

Virabhadra born out of the anger of Siva, was shining along with Bhadrakali like the fire of the time of dissolution, with lustre and pale due to smoke.

Following with the smoke of the time of the fire of dissolution, Bhadrakali looked graceful driving out the gods from the battlefield.

As the entire universe is destroyed at the end of the kalpa with the fire of the time of dissolution, similarly the bodies of Rudraganas, Virabhadra kicked the chariot of the sun with the horses yoked in it, quite easily with the left foot. He attached Agni with a sword, Yama and Yami with pattisa.

Rudras with a strong Sula, Varuna with mudgara, Nirriti with parigha, and the wind god with club.

The valorous Ganesvara punished in the battle, all the gods, sages and those opposed to lord Siva.

Then Virabhadra scratched the tip of the nose of Sarasvati, besides Aditi, the mother of the gods was deprived of the tip of her tongue with his nails.

He chopped of the arm of Vibhavasu with a dagger and the tongue of the mother of the gods upto two inches from the tip was cut off.

The right nostril of Svaha and nipples of her left breast were also chopped off with the nails.

The impetuous Bhadra forcibly removed both the eyes of Bhaga, which were quite large and lustrous like the lotus.

He also removed the line of teeth of Pusan like the string of pearls. At a strike to Pusan by Virabhadra with the tip of his bow, Pusan started faltering in speech.

Then the lord stamped the moon with his toe, as if it was only a worm and ground him on the earth.

Inspite of the cries of Varuni, the wife of Daksa, his head was cut off by Virabhadra and handed it over to Bhadrakali.

Carrying the skull like the fruit of a Tara tree, the goddess, starting playing with it like a ball in the battle ground.

Thereafter Kusala, the Yajna wife of Daksa, was also killed by Sivaganas like her husband, with their fists and kicks.

The ganas who were as ferocious like the lions, caught hold of Aristnemi, Soma, Dharma, Prajapati, Angiras with many sons, Krsasva, Kasyapa and other Rsis by the necks and shouting at them, administered fists over their heads.

Having been disgraced with the goblins and ghosts together with their sons, wives and other kiths and kins, were completely disturbed like the women of high families are tortured by the wicked people in the age of Kali.

The place was devoid of bliss, because of the breaking of the niches as well as the pillars of the of the breaking of the yajna-mandapa. The place of yajna was in flames. Its doors and toranas were damaged.

The army of the gods was destroyed. The ascetics were belaboured. The Vedic recitations came to a halt. The entire community was shattered.

The helpless women started crying. The entire material for sacrifice was destroyed. The place of yajna gave a deserted look.

The gods having been injured, had lost their arms, chest, legs and the heads. They were lying on the ground.

Thousands of gods had than fallen dead or were lying injured, in the battle ground, where the chief of the ganas arrived at the place of the yajna.

Like the fire of the time of dissolution, finding the arrival of Virabhadra, the yajna taking to the form of a deer fled away from that lace, getting frightened.

At his flight, Virabhadra discharged several arrows at him, creating the terrible sound of the firm bow-string..

Stretching the bow upto the ear, he created thunder like the clouds in the sky as well as on earth.

Listening to the thundering sound, all became upset uttering the fear for death. Then Virabhadra, rushed behind the Yajna-Purusa carrying the crescent arrow with his bow.

Then the Yajna-Purusa who was shaking with trembling legs, his lustre having disappeared and his head was cut off with the crescent arrow by Virabhadra.

Finding the sacrifice having been this insulted, Visnu got enraged and he became ready for a fight.

Garuda, the devourer of serpents and the king of birds carried Visnu on his back. Then Indra and other gods as if to sacrifice their lives, who had escaped, helped him. Seeing them along with Visnu, like the lion staring at jackals, Virabhadra the leader of the Bhutas laughed. He appeared like a lion looking at the jackals.

## Chapter 22 - Fight between Virabhadra and the supporters of Daksa

Vayudeva said, “At that point of time, a chariot appeared in the sky, having a lustre of a thousand suns. It had a flag unfurling at its top. It was embossed with the figure of a bull.

The chariot was four wheeled and two horses were yoked in it. It had been filled with the divine weapons.

The chariot was driven by the same charioteer who drove the chariot of Siva at the time of his war with Tripura.

At the command of Siva, Brahma want to Visnu with said chariot and reaching before him spoke to the valorous warrior, with folded hands.

Íṛ said, “Î lord, having beautiful limbs, Î valorous one, Virabhadra the imperishable lord Candrasekhara has commanded that you mount over this chariot. Î valorous one, lord Siva and Parvati are presently lodged in the hermitage of the sage Raimya and are observing your heroic performance.”

Listening to the words of Brahma, he mounted over the chariot and took his seat, by the grace of Brahma.

When, Visnu mounted over the chariot driven by Brahma, the glory of Virabhadra resembling Siva, the enemy of Tripura was increased.

Then the valorous Virabhadra, blew the conch resembling the moon, with his month, which shook even the sun.

Hearing the sound of the blowing of the conch, which resembled the thundering of the ocean, the fire started burning in the bellies of the gods.

The Yaksas, Vidyadharas, serpent Sesa, Siddhas and others arrived to witness the war, as a result of which the entire sky was crowded on all the directions.

Then Narayana in the form of a cloud, shot several arrows from the Saranga bow tortured the lord of the ganas.

Then finding Visnu shooting hundreds of arrows, Virabhadra started shooting thousands of arrows from the bow.

In the ensuing war, Virbhadra lifted up the divine bow drawing it slowly like Siva himself, who drew the bow Meru.

At the drawing of the bow, a loud sound was produced shaking the earth.

Then the leader of the ganas lifted up an arrow which was as poisonous as a serpent.

While taking out the arrow, he had turned his mouth towards the quiver. It appeared at that time as if a serpent had been emerging out of the snake hole.

His hand after taking out the bow looked so graceful as if a young serpent had held a great serpent in its mouth.

Virabhadra, who was as valorous as Siva himself, getting enraged, shot an arrow at the forehead of Visnu.

Visnu, who had already been disgraced, with attack of the arrow, got enraged at Virabhadra like a bull is irritated at a lion.

Then Visnu, attacked with the serpent like arm of the chief of Ganas, with a cruel, pointed great arrow resembling the thnuderbolt.

Then Virabhadra again shot an arrow possessing the lustre of ten thousand suns, at Visnu.

Thereafter Virabhadra shot arrows at Visnu, while Visnu shot arrows at Virabhadra.

With the mutual shooting of the arrows, an awful war was fought which was hair rising.

Observing the terrific war of both of them, the living beings of the sky started crying in panic.

Then Virabhadra attacked at the broad chest of Visnu, shooting Agnimukha and the arrows shining like the sun.

Feeling painful from the attack of arrows over the chest, Visnu was fainted and he fell down on the ground.

On regaining consciousness after sometime, he got up and used all the divine weapons over Virabhadra.

The commander of Siva’s army easily cut off the arrows shot by Visnu at him.

Then Visnu, shot an arrow embossed with his name, which was infallible at Virabhadra in anger with his eyes getting red. But the same was reduced to hundreds of pieces in the middle.

Then he cut off the Saranga bow with the shooting of an arrow and with other two arrows, the cut off the wings of Garuda.

This was all done in a moment which was surprising. Then Visnu exercising his yogic powers, let loose from his body thousands of terrific gods, holding the conch, disc and club, but the powerful Virabhadra reduced them all to ashes in a moment with the fire issuing from his eyes like Siva, who burnt the Tripuras.

The enraged Visnu then raised his cakra hurriedly and tried to hurl it over Virabhadra. Finding that Visnu was lifting up the cakra, Virabhadra smiled and made the hand of Visnu stiff and benumbed. When his limbs became inactive, Visnu could not perform further though he intended to hurl the cakra at Virabhadra.

Though Visnu intended to do so but still he could not attack further. Raising up his arm holding the cakra he started taking deep sighs, feeling grieved.

Feeling lethargic he sat there like a stone. He felt like the body without the soul or the bull without the horns.

Or the lion without the teeth. Finding Visnu in such a precarious condition, Indra and other gods were captivated by Gomendra, as the strength of a bull becomes of no consequence before a lion.

Feeling irritated the got up again and became ready to fight again. In the battle field Virabhadra was found by them like a lion looks at fawns.

Virabhadra had the body like Siva himself, was surrounded by the best of ganas, who praised him. With a loud laugh he benumbed all those present there.

As soon as Indra raised his hand holding Vajra to attack on Virabhadra his hand became inactive like a painting.

The arms of the other warriors who desired to fight raising them met with the same fate like the lethargic people.

In this way the lord Virabhadra destroyed the fortunes of all the gods in no time as a result of which the gods could not face him.

With their limbs inactive, they were frightened and deserted the battleground. Frightened with the tejas of Virabhadra, they could not face him.

The divine warriors were in flight, Virabhadra having long arms, informed them with sharp arrows, in the same way as the clouds pouring rain cause pain to the mountains.

Many of the long arms of the great warrior, resembling the shining weapons, issued lustre like the serpents with the fire flames.

The great warrior showering the rain of several weapons, looked graceful like Brahma appeared graceful by creating the living beings.

As the sun issues crores the earth with its rays, similarly the great warrior covered all the directions (with the arrows shot by him).

The golden arrows shot by Virabhadra in the sky looked like the lightning.

The large arrows resembling the smokes started devouring the killed the soldiers, drinking their blood like wine at the same time.

The arms and the heads of many of them were cut off, while many of them were deprived of the ribs. Many of the gods fell down on the ground.

With the attack of the arrows, the bodies were churned, which were deprived of the arms, different joints, and had fallen on earth with their eyes wide open. It looked as if some of them intended to get absorbed in the earth, while others intended to fly in the sky.

Finding themselves unprotected some of them disappeared some of them entered in the earth while some wanted to fly in the sky, while others disappeared in the caves.

Some of them flew in the sky, some of them entered in the water. Thus the great warrior looked graceful after shattering the bodies of the gods.

As lord Bhairava looks graceful with the destruction of the living beings as Tripurari looked graceful with the destruction of Tripuras,

Similarly the entire army of the gods looked miserable. Because of Ganesvara, its condition became deplorable.

Then a terrible stream of blood from the bodies of the warriors began to flow causing terror in the living beings.

At that point of time the blood was spread in the entire place of yajna. It appeared like Kausiki clad in red costumes after the killing of Sumbha.

With the fighting of the terrific war, the frightened earth started shaking.

The ocean started shaking which deep whirlpools as well as the high waves. The comets started falling which were indication of the evil. Grave misfortunes started appearing. The trees started shedding the branches.

All the directions became misty. The inauspicious winds stared blowing. Alas! The Asvamedha yajna has been performed inappropriately, in which Daksa Prajapati the son of Brahma was himself the performer.

Dharma and others were the members of the same and was protected by Visnu, while Indra and other gods were the participants.

Inspite of that the heads of Rtvija or the performer were cut off, what a reward has been achieved by them?

Therefore in the company of the evil people, no auspicious deed should not be performed.

Performing the act of great merit, besides several yajnas, the one who does not get devoted to Mahesvara, he cannot reap the auspicious reward.

Even after performing grave sins, who adores Siva, he undoubtedly is relieved of all the sins.

A person who is engaged in the denouncing of Siva, the acts of charities, performing of the tapas, yajnas and homas are of no consequence, for him.

Then Narayana, Rudra, Lokapalas and other gods, having been injured with the arrows of Virabhadra, fell extremely painful and fled away from that place. Some of them deserted the place, the hair of some of them were pulled. Some of the strong bodied people fell extremely painful. Some of them fell down at different places. The faces of some of them were tom out. Some of the divine warriors were destroyed.

Some of them were so upset that they lost their ornaments, costumes, weapons, while others disowning their strength, arrogance and ride felt miserable.

Destroying the yajna of Daksa, the follower of the evil path, Virabhadra with shining weapons and the body stood there like a lion among the bulls.

## Chapter 23 - Prayer of gods and the completion of yajna

Vayudeva said, “Thus Visnu with shattered limbs, and other gods, suffered for some time, while others felt upset.

Finding the valorous gods upset in the battlefield, the Pramathas, at the instance of Virabhadra were extremely irritated and bound the arms of the warriors with the strong iron chains, besides the belly, neck and the feet.

At that point of time, Brahma being the charioteer of Visnu, prayed to Virabhadra, the devotee of Parvati, with authority.

“O lord, don’t be immensely angry. The gods have already been shattered. Î Suvrata, you better forgive them with your Rajoguna.”

At these words of Paramesthi Brahma, Virabhadra turned peaceful because of his importance.

Availing of an opportunity the gods started praying Virabhadra, placing hands in folded position over the head.
