The gods said, “O Siva, peaceful destroyer of the yajna, carrier of a trident, Rudrabhadra, lord of the Rudras, Rudrabhuti, salutation to you.

You are Kala, destroyer of Kamadeva, you have severed the heads of the gods as well as Daksa.

Î valorous one, because of this sinful Daksa, you have finished the glorious gods like us.

You have burnt us all. Î lord, we are afraid of you. You are our protector. We take refuge with you. You protect us.

Vayudeva said, “Having been pleased with this type of prayer, Virabhadra, released the gods from the fetters and drove them before Siva the god of gods.

At that point of time, Siva, the omnipresent lord of the worlds, was stationed in the firmament along with the Ganas.

Finding Paramesvara there, Visnu and other gods were pleased as well as frightened. All of them offered their salutation to lord Siva.

Lord Siva who removes the miseries of his devotees, looking at Parvati spoke smilingly.

Mahadeva said, “O gods, don’t be afraid. You are my people. I being the compassionate one have punished you in order to exercise my grace on you.

I being adorable of all the gods have forgiven you. When I am in rage, you cannot remain comfortable anywhere.”

Vayudeva said, “At the speaking of these words by Siva repeatedly, all the gods shedding doubts were pleased and started dancing in ecstasy.

The gods feeling delighted and blissful in their minds, started eulogising Siva.”

The gods said, “O lord you are the creator of the entire universe. You represent Brahma, Visnu and Rudra in the form of rajas, tamas and sattva ganas.

Î adorable by the universe, Î auspicious one, you represent all, salutation to you. Inspite of your being formless, in order to provide comforts to your devotees, you have taken to this form.

Î lord of gods, Î Siva, the moon was cured of his ailment because of your grace. Mihira Jajila who died of drawing felt comfortable because of your grace.

Î lord, Simantini had become a widow. With the performing of a Vrata on Monday, she regained her fortunes like nectar, besides the sons.

Srikara was bestowed the excellent position by lord Mahadeva. You had protected Sudarsana from the danger of the kings.

O compassionate one, you had redeemed, being merciful to Medura with his wife. You made the widow Sarada to regain her lost fortunes by your grace.

Removing the misery of Bhadrayusa, you made him comfortable. Saumini was relieved from the worldly bondages by your grace.

Visnu said, ‘‘O Siva, you with the attributing sattva, rajas and tamas, taking to the forms of Brahma, Visnu and Rudra, showering your grace, create, sustain and destroy the universe.

You are the destroyer of the pride and are the brilliance of all. You are the hidden secret of all the lores, besides being the cause of blessings of all.

Î lord you are the source of origin of everything. You are all in all. Everything is enshrined in you. You kindly save us becoming merciful.”

At the same time Brahma, finding an opportunity, offered his salutation to Siva with folded hands, and submitted to him.

Brahma said, “O lord, Î Mahadeva, you forgive your devotees for their sins. Victory to you. Who else gets pleased at such types of sins?

Those who have already been killed in the battle, let all of then regain their lives. Because when Paramesvara is pleased, there is no objection from any quarter.

The wounds inflicted in the bodies of the gods, I consider them to be ornaments because of your pleasure.”

At these words, of Paramesthi Brahma, Siva smilingly looked at Parvati, who developed the son like affection towards Brahma and restored all the limbs of the gods as before.

Such of the goddesses or the mothers of the gods, who had been punished by the Pramathas, all their limbs were restored as original ones by the grace of Siva.

Lord Brahma the grand sire, taking into account the sins of Daksa, replace his head with the head of an old he-goat.

He too was brought back to life becoming conscious, then he beseeching in a humble manner, getting frightened, started praying to Siva.”

Daksa said, ‘‘O lord, Î lord of the universe, you bestow your grace over the universe. Î Mahesana, you kindly forgive me for my sins and be merciful on me.

Î lord, you are indeed the creator of the universal, besides being its sustainer and the destroyer. I have now come to realise that you happen to be the lord of Visnu and other gods.

The entire world has been expounded by you. You preserve it and destroy it as well. Visnu or other gods are not greater then you.”

Vayudeva said, ‘‘Finding him so upset and frightened, as a culprit and beseeching humbly, Siva the ocean of mercy said smilingly, ‘‘Don’t be afraid.”

Thus speaking, in order to please Brahma, the father of Daksa, Siva bestowed the position of a Sivagana to Daksa.

Then Brahma and other gods, offering their salutation to Siva with folded hands, offered prayer, quite humbly with folded hands prayed to the lord.

Brahma and others said, “O Sankara, Î lord of gods, Î lord of the destitutes, Î great lord, you kindly forgive us for our sins.

You are the protector of the yajna, lord of yajna, destroyer of yajna, Î Mahesana, you kindly forgive us for our sin.

Î god of gods, Î Paresana, protector of the lives of the devotees, you award punishment to the wicked people, Î lord, be merciful. Salutation to you.

Î lord, the wicked people, who are ignorant about you, you shatter their arrogance. You are the protector of your devotees.

You indeed possess a wonderful conduct. You are graceful on the miserable people, Î lord forgive us for our fault.”

Vayudeva said, ‘‘Brahma and other gods thus praised lord Mahadeva. Then Siva, who is well disposed towards his devotees, besides being compassionate, was pleased.

Then lord Siva showered his grace on Brahma and other gods bestowing the boons on them at the same time.

Then the merciful lord Siva who made their fear subside addressed the gods who had sought refuge in him, with words characterised by smile.

Siva said, ‘‘The sins committed by the gods are all due to be destroyed. By your taking refuge in me, I have forgotten everything. All of you also acted thoughtlessly in a shameful manner. Presently all the gods including Brahma, Visnu, Indra and others should comfortably retire to their respective abodes.”

Thus speaking to Indra and other gods, leaving aside the discussion on the yajna of Daksa, Siva together with ganas disappeared from the scene.

The gods were then freed from the miseries and talking about the prowess of Virabhadra, comfortably retired to their respective abodes.

## Chapter 24 - Controversy between Siva and Siva

The Rsis said, “Where did Siva go after disappearing from that place with Parvati and what did they do?”

Vayudeva said, “The pleasant mountain Mandaracala has many caves, which is liked by Mahadeva quite well. It is the place for his performing of tapas.

The said mountain performed great tapas to carry Siva and Siva over its head. He enjoyed the comfort of having been touched with the feet of the lord.

The extent of the beauty of the mountain cannot be described with a thousand mouths for a hundred crores of years.

Therefore I cannot have the courage of describing the beauty of that mountain. The description of the beauty of other mountains in comparison to the same is of no consequence.

It can however, be stated that some unprecedented rddhi bestowed the grace to it for enabling Siva to reside there.

Therefore, Mahadeva, in order to please Parvati, made this mountain as his harem.

Its waistband comprises of the stones and the trees over the earth. Because the proximity of Siva and Siva daily, they disregard the entire world.

The parents of the universe taking bath and food there, stand testimony to the auspicious Sanskaras of the place, which are spread here and there. The springs with spotless cool waters perform abhiseka of the mountain.

During the nights, the moon rays falling over the mountain rocks, provide the impression of a royal umbrella.

When the tresses of the divine damsels shake, he appears as being fanned with formed by flywhisks, which project as an emperor.

At the time of the sun rise in the morning, the mountain looks as having been filled with gems and jewels which appear to be eager to observe the beauty of his body in a mirror.

The tree seem to honour the king of the mountain with benedictions of victory, which look like the sages, with the entering growth of creepers in the form of the matted locks of hair, through the chirping of the birds, by extending their arms, in the form of creepers, shaken with the winds, while shedding flowers and the tender sprouts.

Some of its peaks are facing down, while some of there are rising up and some are spreading on the sides, he appears to jump in the nether world or jump up from the ground, or fly in the sky towards all the directions. Through the vast caves he seems to have opened his mouth. He appears to look at the world and keep on dancing. His beauty is beyond fading or wearing out. He expands itself as if trying to devour the world or the drink the ocean. It looks as if he is vomiting the darkness and covering up the sky with clouds.

The place of his living is bright like the mirror. The trees of the hermitages remove the heat of the sun.

The cool breeze blows with the touch of the water of rivers, touches, lakes delighted both Siva and Parvati, who were lying there.

Taking this mountain to be the best in all respects, Siva together with Parvati, looked graceful after disappearing from the hermitage of sage Raibhya.

Finding an orchard there, lord Siva with goddess started roaming about in the land of the inner quarters.

Sometime passed in this way, with the increase of the people, Sumbha and Nisumbha who were brothers were born.

With the strength of his tapas, Paramesthi Brahma, bestowed on them the boon that they could never be killed by men in the world.

The maid, born without the human touch, belonging to the race of Ambika, her valour would be invincible (for these brothers).

In case you are attracted towards her, you are bound to be killed.” This is what Brahma had told both of them.

Since that time both the brothers conquered Indra and other gods, they put an end to the study of the Vedas, the yajnas and other yogic practices.

Then Brahma prayed to Siva the lord of gods, for the killing of both of them. He said, “It would be appropriate on your part, to bestow on the gods, a goddess who could kill Sumbha and Nisumbha. She should be born as a Sakti of Siva’s complexion, who shall be a virgin devoid of passion. The death of Sumbha and Nisumbha could be arranged secretly or by infuriating.

When so requested by Brahma, the lord Nilalohita summoned secretly, outwardly rebuking her, calling her Kali.

Then the goddess with beautiful complexion, having been rebuked because of her colour, was enraged from within but was smiling outwardly and spoke to her husband with calm words.

The goddess said, “In case you are no more interested in my present complexion, then why did you not tell me earlier?

How did you enjoy my company unmindfully. Nothing is impossible for Isvara who is the lord of the universe.

You are the lord who enjoys the pleasure in the soul itself. The conjugal pleasure is not the source of all your comforts. Because of this you forcibly burnt Kamadeva to ashes.

A woman with all the beautiful limbs, if not loved by the husband, all his other virtues are of no consequence.

The woman are born for the pleasure of their husbands, otherwise they are of no consequence.

Since you have denounced my complexion in seclusion, therefore, I discarding it shall embrace the other complexion otherwise, I shall not remain alive.”

Speaking these words with choked voice, the goddess got up from the bed and got permission from Siva for performing tapas.

Having an obstruction been created in love, Siva felt panicky. He fell over the feet of Bhavani and prayed her.

Isvara said, “O dear without appreciating a joke you are enraged with me. In case I am not delighted with you then where shall I find delight.

You are the mother of the universe while I happen to be the lord and the father.

Is our love for the sake of passion or not? Because the world was created well before the creation of the passions.

The passions have been created by me for the sake of others. Then why have you complained to me for the burning of Kamadeva.

In fact Kamadeva had arrived to defeat me taking me to be an ordinary god. As soon as he engaged himself in his task, I reduced him into ashes.

The roaming about of both of us, in fact is for the protection of the universe. Therefore I cut jokes with you for the protection of the universe.

“That purpose ere long will be revealed to you.” This reminded goddess about the remark that caused her annoyance and said.

The goddess said, “O lord, I have already been cheated by you having the cool temperament. Now why are you indulging in flattery?

A woman who having been disliked by the husband, does not put an end to her life, she is denounced by the noble people and the women of high race.

My body does not have a fair complexion and due to the same, you do not love me. Because of that you called me Kali while sporting, otherwise, how could you say so?

This body of black complexion which is disliked by you shall have to be discarded by me. This is because the blackness has been denounced even by the learned people.”

Siva said, “In case you feel so painful, then what is the use of tapas for you. You can possess any other complexion at my will or by you own will.”

The goddess said, “I do not want to change this complexion at my own will or your grace. Performing tapas I shall adore Brahma, I shall be turned as Gauri by the grace of Brahma.

Siva said, “It was by my grace that Brahma had achieved the position of Brahma. Î Mahadevi, you better call him. How is tapas going to help you?”

The goddess said, “(I am aware that), Brahma and other gods have achieved their present positioning by your grace. Still I shall be adoring Brahma at your command.

I had initially been born as Sati, the daughter of Daksa and got you the lord of the universe as my husband.

Similarly, today, I pleasing Brahma, intend to become Gauri what is the harm in it?” At these words of Mahadevi, lord Mahadeva, smilingly did not prevent her from doing so.

## Chapter 25 - Performing of tapas by Kali to become Gauri

Vayudeva said, “Thereafter the chaste Parvati, circumambulated Siva, her husband, proceeded towards Himagiri.

It was the place, where she had performed the tapas with her maids earlier. She lovingly started performing tapas at the same spot.

Finding her parents there, she offered her salutation to them and she got their permission, revealing to them, the cause of her performing the tapas.

Then retiring to the tapovana she removed all the ornaments, took her bath and she took to the form of a great ascetic.

With a resolve to perform the severe tapas devoting her mind at the lotus like feet of her husband, she adored the Parthiva linga with the forest flowers.

She expected that the lord himself would bestow reward on her in the image of Brahma. With the resolve she started performing tapas.

While thus performing the tapas, a long time passed. Then she found a tiger arriving there with evil intention.

The body of that animal of wicked soul became stiff and benumbed when it approached her.

Finding the arrival of the tiger with evil intentions, the goddess did not feel upset like an ordinary person.

Suffering from hunger, all the limbs of the tiger became motionless, but it still continued to think that she was the food for him.

It continued glancing at the goddess seated before the goddess and thought, “My prey is nothing else.’’ Virtually this became its cherished goal.

The goddess thought it to be her devotee and could protect it from the evil beings. Therefore she showered her grace on the tiger.

All the sins of the tiger were removed because of the grace of Parvati and it suddenly recognised the goddess.

Its hunger, the wickedness since birth and shaking of the limbs stopped. It felt satisfied.

Then it realising itself to be extremely successful, got devoted to her and started serving Paramesvari.

It became the destroyer of the evil souls and the evil beings, it started wandering in the tapovana.

Then the tapas of the goddess became harder everyday. At the instance of the Daityas, the gods went to Brahma and took refuge with him.

Then they narrated to him to tale of their sufferings at the hands of their enemies. They apprised Brahma, the way Sumbha and Nisumbha had tortured them because of their getting boons from Brahma.

The merciful Brahma, listening to the tale of the sufferings of the gods, was reminded of the story about the killing of the Daityas.

When so prayed by the gods, Brahma went to the goddess thinking in his mind to relieve the gods of the sufferings.

Then Brahma found the goddess, who represented the prestige of the universe engaged in tapas.

Brahma then adored Parvati who was his own mother as well as of the universe besides being the wife of Siva and the daughter of the lord of mountains.

Finding the arrival of Brahma with other gods, Parvati welcomed them offering the customary padya and argya.

Praising the welcome he received from the goddess, and felicitating her, Brahma asked her the cause of her performing the penance like an innocent person.

Brahma said, “What do you want to establish with this hard tapas? The success of all tapas is in your hands.

Siva the lord of the universe happens to be your husband. On receiving him what more do you want to achieve with the performing of the tapas?

Otherwise the entire universe is like sport for you. It is quite surprising that how could you tolerate your separation from Siva?”

The goddess said, “At the beginning of the universe, you were born of Siva. This is what has been heard by me. In that case, you happen to be my first son.

Then when Siva emerged from your forehead for the creation of the universe, then you became my preceptor in the form of the father-in-law.

When my father Giriraja became your son, you became my grandsire as well as of the world.

In this way I have had some talk with my husband Siva, secretly because you are always travelling in the world.

What more could be said. I shedding away the blackness of my body, I intend to became Gauri, by Sattvika means.”

Brahma said, “O goddess, why did you perform such a hard tapas, for such a small thing? Why did you not take to that form yourself? Or otherwise, your sports are like that.

Î mother of the universe, this sport of yours would also be for the welfare of the world. Therefore, you fulfil my desire with the same.

The two demons Sumbha and Nisumbha, have become arrogant after achieving boons from me, but are going to be killed at your hands.

Therefore, you be firm in no time. The Sakti that is to be released now shall be their deaths.

At the prayer so offered by Brahma, the daughter of Giriraja shedding away the black skin, took to the form of Gauri.

At the shedding of the black skin by Parvati, a black girl known by the name of Kausiki was born having the complexion of the black clouds.

The illusory Sakti, also known as Yoganidra or Vaisnavi, had eight arms carries the attributes of conch, disc, trident and other weapons.

She had three appearances viz. fierce, gentle and a combination of the two. She was three eyed and was moon crested. She had no sexual contact with anyone. She was quite beautiful and invincible.

Brahma then gave the goddess the form of the eternal Sakti, who came into being for the killing of Sumbha and Nisumbha who were the moons among the Daityas.

Getting pleased, Brahma offered a powerful lion to that goddess, who could serve her as a vehicle.

The Vindhya mountains were made the abode for them. He ordained her adoration with the offering of meat, fish, pies and wine.

The Sakti was respected by Brahma, the creator of the universe. Then she bowed in reverence to the mother Gauri, as well as Brahma.

She then accompanied with several other Saktis proceed on to the Vindhya mountain for the killing of the demons.

She shattered the demons with arrows of Kama and her own arrows, which pierced into their bodies. The said battle is not narrated here since it has been described elsewhere. It could be imagined by other sources as well. The present narration shall be carried on.

## Chapter 26 - Parvati meets Siva as Gauri

Vayudeva said, “Then Gauri after producing Kausiki looked towards Brahma and in order to shower her grace on him, she spoke to him.

The goddess said, “Have you seen the lion which serves me. It has protected the tapovana from the terrible wild animals.

It worshipped me with an extremely devoted mind. There is nothing more pleasing to me than its protection.

I could roam about in my inner apartments. Because of my attachment for him, the lord would bestow the position of a gana on it.

I intend to return with this him leading me with my maids. Being Prajapati, I seek you permission to return.’’

At these words of the goddess Brahma smilingly, narrated to her of the wickedness committed by him earlier.

Brahma said, “O goddess, the animals are cruel. How could your beautiful mind get attracted towards the lion? Why are you pouring the nectar in the month of a serpent?

This is some wicked demon in the form of a tiger, which has devoured the Brahma, cows, and the ascetics.

As a result of this, it wanders freely in the forest. It must reap the reward of its misdeeds.

Therefore, why could you be so graceful on such a wicked animal what have you to do with this tiger having born as an evil and ferocious animal?”

The goddess said, “The words spoken by you are all true, still it has taken refuge with me. Therefore it can not be abandoned.”

Brahma said, “I spoke about his conduct of his earlier birth, unmindful of its devotion to you. In case it is devoted to you, then your devotee cannot force destruction.

What can an auspicious person do without your permission? Î Paramesvari, you are unborn, intelligent and eternal.

Such of the beings who are subservient to you, can achieve redemption from worldly bondages. Who can be successful, in his performance without your grace?

You possess many types of strength. What will a mere agent do who himself is unable to do anything?

Whatever the fortunes have been achieved by Visnu, the gods, Danavas, Raksasas, and other have done so by your grace alone.

The innumerable Brahma, Visnu and Siva, who have already passed, they would be innumerable at your command.

Î goddess of the universe, without your adoration, all the gods cannot achieve dharma, artha, kama and moksa.

Since the merits and the evil have been established by you, the mobile and immobile might even by interchanged.

You are the primordial and the eternal Sakti of Siva, the great soul, the lord of the universe, and you are the Sakti, without beginning, middle or the end.

For travelling through the universe, you enter anyone of the image, you sport in many forms. Who can know about you precisely.

Therefore by your grace in case this sinful tiger also meets with success, who can stop it from doing so?”

Thus Brahma, making Gauri to realise her true form, and himself he realised her from the performing of tapas.

When Brahma disappeared with the permission of the goddess, the goddess looked at her parents Himalaya as well as Mena.

She offered her salutation to her parents who could not tolerate separation from her, she assured them. Then she offered her salutation to the trees of tapovana.

Then with the separation from the tree goddess, the trees started shading tears by dropping their flowers, the birds perched in the tree branches, expressed their anxiety (for the separation from the goddess) with their chirping sound, Parvati, speaking to her maids, hurriedly left the place to meet her husband.

Making the tiger to lead like her own son, she moved on illuminating the worlds with the resplendence of her body, the goddess Gauri moved towards the Mandara Mountain, where her husband Mahadeva was lodged being the creator, sustainer as well as the destroyer of the entire universe.

## Chapter 27 - Meeting of Siva and Siva, showering of his grace on the tiger by Siva

The Rsis said, “With what intentions did the daughter of Himalaya possessing the divine body, entering her abode, look at her husband? What did the ganas do at the entrance gate?

Vayudeva said, “The exquisite feelings dubbed in love, is beyond description, whereby the imagination of all the sentimental people has been captured.

Expecting the arrival of the goddess, the lord Mahadeva had deputed the gatekeepers at the gate. She meeting them entered inside and started looking at Siva with anxiety.

The Ganesas inside offered their respectful salutation to the goddess, while the goddess, offered her salutation to Siva.

Before she could get up after offering her salutation, Siva hurriedly held her with his hands and embraced her delightfully.

Siva was anxious to take her in his lap. Then she lay down over the bed. Then lord Siva took the smiling goddess in his lap.

With a delightful mind, opening his eyes wide, it appeared as if he was drinking her beauty through the eyes, then he started talking to her.

Mahadeva said, “O damsel with beautiful limbs, your earlier mental agony has disappeared. Because of your anger, I could not convince you in any way.

Î lady with extremely beautiful limbs, now I feel hesitant and fearful to call you Kali or Gauri, because of your temperament.

Because of your temperament you forgot about my enormous love for you, because of which no blemish can be there.

Such feelings are the cause of bickering among the ordinary people. But the love between you and me is beyond parallel in the mobile and immobile world.

I bear the fire while you are the form of the moon. Thus the fire and the moon are established in the world by us.

Both of us have taken to the human form by our own will and with our separation, the universe becomes helpless.

There is another reason supported by the sastras, in this connection, because this mobile and immobile world is inseparable like the speech and its meaning.

You represent the nectar like speech and I represent the nectar like meaning. These are the two types of nectars which cannot be separated.

You are known by the knowledge of lore while I am known by your perfect knowledge of lore and I am known by your perfect knowledge. How can the knowledge and the object of knowledge be separated.

I with my own efforts create the universe, But I do not destroy, which happens at you command you are the form of that command.

The fortunes are the essence of the command, having independence as the symptom. How could the fortune be achieved without the command?

Both of us cannot live in separation. Still in order to establish the cause of the gods, I behaved with you accordingly.

The secret was quite well known to you. Then why did you get irritated? You were annoyed with me for the protection of the three worlds.

The tattva harmful to the living beings is not found in you.” With these loving words of Siva, the goddess, the natural source of love, smiled, but gave no reply to Siva her husband. Out of shyness, she kept quiet. I shall describe about the goddess. You please listen to me.”

The goddess said, “Kausiki who had been created by me has not been noticed by you. Such a type of girl has never been born in the world nor would it be born in future.

Her strength and prowess comprise of the Vindhya mountain. Her victory rests in killing of Sumbha and Nisumbha in the battlefield.

The protection of the people and bestowing of the rewards for their deeds, rests with Brahma.

After these words of the goddess, spoken by her, her maid brought the tiger and made it stand before her there.

Looking at the tiger the goddess said, “O lord, I have brought a gift for you. You look at this tiger. There is no servant better than it.

It had protected me in the forest against the evil forces. It is immensely devoted to me and feels carefree because it is protected by me.

It has arrived here, leaving its country to seek grace In case you love me most, then,

Î Isvara, let it guard the entrance gate of the inner apartment with the approval of Nandi with other gatekeepers, with special marks.”

Vayudeva said, “Listening to the sweet and loving words of the goddess, Siva said, “ I am pleased.” Saying this Siva had a look at the tiger.

Then suddenly he was seen like Ganesa, wearing the dress and the features of a guard, holding the cane of gold and a dagger of serpentine lustre. He was clad in a bodice set with various gems.

He was given the name of Somanandi, because Soma stands for Siva and the tiger pleased Siva (Soma) as well as Nandi.

After this performance, which pleased the goddess, the lord with a circular moon over his crest, adored it with the gem studded ornaments.

Thereafter the moon crested Siva, started decorating Gauri with gem studded ornaments, making her sit over the bed.

## Chapter 28 - The glory of bhasma or ashes

The Rsis said, “while instructing the goddess, why did Siva speak that the universe is in the form of Agnisoma which was in the form of words and their meanings.

He also stated that the fortune has essence of the command. You are the form of command. We would like to be enlightened on the subject in a proper sequence.”

The Vayudeva said, “The immensely illustrious body of Rudra has been equated with Agni or fire, while the nectar like body of Sakti happens to be the Soma. This is the peaceful body of Sakti.

The lore is the digit of the resplendence itself, which pervades in the Rasas (essence) like stars.

Tejas (resplendence) functions in two ways viz. the sun and the fire. The rasas similarly function as the water of the moon.

The lightning is the form of the tejas, while madhurasa is the essence. Because of the difference between the tejas and the essence, the universe gets stable.

The nectar emerges out of the fire, while the nectar (ghee) inflames the fire. Therefore the fire and Soma are beneficial for the world.

The growth of the crops in abundance is attributed to havi. The rain falls for the increase in the growth of crops. In this way the world is maintained by means of Agnisoma.

The flames of fire rise (upto the height) of the peaceful nectar. Some emerges out of the place of Agni.

That is why the Kalagni stays below and the Sakti upwards. The upward blazing is till burning and the downward flow is till complete drenching.

Kalagni held by adharasakti rises above while Soma the form of Siva and Sakti moves downwards.

Sometimes Siva is above and Sakti below and sometimes there is the reverse of it. Thus the entire world has the form of Siva and Sakti.

The world has been burnt by Agni again and again. Therefore the bhasma are ashes are taken to be the semen of Agni.

In this way one takes bath with bhasma reciting the mantra Agniriti. The one who does so is freed from the worldly bondages.

Bhasma which is the semen of Agni when soaked in Soma is conducive to the lordship of Prakrti, without resorting to the yogic union.

By drenching the bhasma by means of yogic practices, the bhasma may turn one back from the lordship of the shower of the nectar, possessed by Sakti.

Therefore the use of the nectar is meant for overcoming the death. The one who had the nectar like feeling towards of Siva and Sakti, how could he be afraid of death.

One who is enlightened on the functions of the fire, he deserts the world which resembles Agnisoma and is never born on earth.

A person, who reducing his body to ashes by Sivagni, and then bathes it with the nectar of Sakti, he himself is turned into nectar.

One who understands the meaning of this, well and takes it to the heart, and then understand fully the entire universe of the form of Agni-soma.

## Chapter 29 - The speech and its meaning

Vayudeva said, “Now I shall narrate briefly the speech and its meanings, as a result of which one achieves knowledge in six ways.

There is no word without a meaning, nor is there any useless word. Therefore all the words reveal their meanings at the appropriate times.

The result of the Prakrti has been described in two ways which are conceived as representing Siva and Siva.

The learned people conceive the form of the word as the gross, subtle and the great. It is the gross form which is heard by us with our ears.

The subtle form is of mental creation while the great one is beyond imagination. It happens to be the Kriyasakti depending on the Sivatattva.

With combination of the jnana-sakti, with the will of Isvara, with all other sakti, is known as Atmasakti.

It happens to be the Mula-Prakrti of all the activities and also happens to be the Kundalini Maya of the spotless path.

The sakti is ramified into six paths, three of which pertain to the words and the three to the meaning.

All the men have the capacity for merging and enjoyment according to the purity based the division of all the principles, which are pervaded by the Kalas suitably as in the beginning the great Prakrti is transformed into five. They include Kala, Nivrtti and others.

The paths of mantra words and letters are based on words. The paths based on meaning are the paths of the universe, the paths of Kalas and the path of principles. They are mutually pervading and pervaded.

The mantra pervade with the words constituting the statement. The words are pervaded by the letters which are conceived as words by the people with wisdom.

The letters are pervaded by words, which are spoken in the world. The words on the other hand are pervaded by the tattvas, because they originate from within and without. They are affected in the tattvas in various ways.

Some of the words have cropped up from the middle, some from the Saiva Agamas. The prominent tattvas of the texts on Saivisim as well as the Sankhya philosophy have been discussed in the Puranas, and whatever is popularly known in the Saiva texts, is completely pervaded by the Kalas.

Since in the start the primordial Prakrti takes the form of five Kalas, Nivrtti and others, pervaded by each other, having he form of Kala,pratistha, santi, and the spoltess form.

The supreme Sakti beyond those kalas, pervades in the six paths and is turn pervaded by Sivatattva.

Sivatattva is indeed the source of origin of everything from sakti to earth and is pervaded by it as an earthen pot is pervaded by the clay.

The supreme abode of Siva is attainable by three ways. With the purification of the tattvas, the non-pervading Sakti, becomes pervasive, with the purification of the tattvas.

The purification of the cosmic egg upto rudra is purified by Nivrtti. The sphere of avyakta above that is purified by Pratistha.

The sphere upto Visvesvara is purified by Vidya in the middle. The sphere above that is purified by Santi. The end of the path is purified by Santyatita.

The combination of Para-Prakrti is called Parama-vyoma and those five tattvas pervade the entire universe.

The devotees should visualise everything in the same. One who wishes to purify without knowing the truth about pervasion of the paths in indeed is a devoid of purity.

Without the combination of the Saktipata (union of Sakti and the individual soul), it is impossible to eitner know the Tattvas factually or their pervasiveness.

Sakti indeed is the command, she is Paramesvari the form of consciousness and is linked with Siva. As a cause of the same Siva pervades everywhere.

It is neither the form of Atman, nor Maya or the blemishes. In case we think about the reality, it is neither the bondage nor the salvation, it is the cause of the freedom from bondage.

She is the highest stage of the pleasures and happens to be the auspicious Sakti of Siva. By means of the feelings, she has the same traits as Siva himself.

Siva is the householder because of her and she is the housewife of Siva. The universe is born of Prakrti, because of the union of Siva and Siva.

Siva is the creator, while Siva is the cause of creation. Siva alone converts himself into two forms.

Some people call them as man and woman, while others conceive her to be the supreme sakti of Siva; as the light is associated with the sun being inseparable from it. But in the form of cit she is different. In fact Siva is the great cause and his command is Paramesvari.

The Mula Prakrti of Siva, is imperishable, Maya, Mahamaya, Prakrti with three gunas.

Because of her activation, she is of three types, but appears through six paths in the form of words and the meanings. The entire universe is therefore six fold. The entire collection of religious scriptures is only on elaboration of the same.

## Chapter 30 - Vayudeva's discourse on Sivatattva

The Rsis said, “The stories of Siva are quite astonishing, which should be followed inspite of being difficult to understand, and can be known even to the gods with difficulty. They cause delusion on us.

But no blemish could be noticed in the tattvas of Siva and Siva. There is a touch of Prakrti in their stories.

Though Brahma too is engaged in the creation, preservation and the destruction of the people, but he is actually controlled by Siva who exercise restraint as well as blessings on him, because Brahma is subservient to Siva.

Siva is not subservient to anyone. Therefore Siva's fortunes are not controlled by anyone else.

This type of fortunes of Siva stand testimony to his independence nature. It can be innate or subject to embodied state.

But the physical form does not fit in with a free being for this basic reason. But this form is the effect of some cause. The lordship has no cause of its being.

He has been conceived as nirguna (without attributes) everywhere, who is independent at the same time. Therefore, how could one and the same entity passes the two qualities of Nirguna and Saguna.

The nature of the supreme soul, is nirguna then how could he transform himself as saguna, contrary to his nature?

In case his nature changes because of the will of the independence, then why does Isana transform his eternal form as the perishable one?

The one who is saguna in reality is different from the nirguna Siva and pervades everywhere in the form of Siva alone.

When Siva has a physical form only then his image could be drawn and the dependence of the embodied one on the definite form becomes certain. This is inexplicable.

Otherwise how could the non-dependent accept his images. It is therefore established that for the achieving of some reward, he accepts the image.

Otherwise for the non-dependable lord to take to a definite form at will, does not seem to be convincing because the desire of the humans is based on their karmans.

All the gods from Brahma to pisacas are competent to end their lives at will. Are they subservient to their karmans?

To have a body at one's own desire has been equated with the black magic, because this could be possible, with the achieving of the Siddhis like anima and others.

When Visnu while fighting with Dadhici, took to the universal form, then the sage complained to Visnu.

Though Siva is a great soul, and superior to all, but his comparison with other beings can be observed by us, because of his having a body.

Siva the supreme cause of all has been considered to be compassionate on all. He disciplines the gods. Then how can he be graceful to all.

It is Siva, who cut off the fifth head of Brahara, since he had been denouncing Siva, inspite of his being his son.

Siva destroyed and trampled over down the Narasimha incarnation of Visnu, in the form of Sarabha with eight legs, pressing him under his feet and tearing out his body with nails.

Virabhadra, in the yajna of Daksa punished all the gods and the goddesses present there.

Siva killed the Tripura demon destroying the three cities, with the women, children and all others in a moment.

Even when the gods prevented Siva not to do so, the lord destroyed Kamadeva with the fire of his eye who was the cause of love among the people.

The cows which roamed about in the sky and dropped milk over Siva's head, were reduced to ashes in anger.

The demon Jalandhara had made a circular whirlpool in the water with his feet and had thrown away Visnu at a distance of a hundred yojanas.

The same Jalandhara had been killed by Siva, with the attacks of his trident. Visnu became powerful after receiving a cakra from Visnu.

While killing the demons who were the enemies of the gods, besides being cruel, Siva killed Andhakasura with the shooting of an arrow.

He killed Daruka, by producing a goddess like Kala and killed Daruka. He made Kausiki to emerge from the skin of Gauri, and killed Sumbha and Nisumbha in the battlefield. This episode is contained in the Skanda Purana which was narrated to me by Skanda himself.

For the killing of the demon king Taraka, the enemy of Indra, Brahma prayed to Siva who had been living in the Mandara mountain.

Lord Siva enjoyed sexual intercourse with Siva for a long time. Due to the excessive sport the earth, appeared to sink in the nether world. He cheated his own name and the goddess by withholding the discharge of semen in her. The same unbearable semen was discharged into the fire like nectar or the auspicious havis.

Agni dropped the same into Ganga and other places. Then Svaha united with her husband in the form of Krttika. The same semen was accepted by her. Then the semen of Siva was dropped near the Sara plants over the Meru mountain. Svaha was turned into gold in the process.

After sometime all the directions were illuminated with its light and all the peaks of the mountain Meru looked as if of golden colour.

After sometime, the said tejas (lustre) grew into a prince of beautiful and tender limbs, a model for all boys.

Finding him in the form of a child, all the gods and the demons felt surprised and deluded.

Mahadeva accompanied with the goddess, arrived to have a look at the son. He placed the child in the lap of the goddess. All the gods and sages looked at the child with a smiling face, though they were averse to the worldly pleasures. The lord made him play over his chest and enjoyed the fun. Both the goddess and the lord congratulated each other.

The lord then asked the goddess to feed the child with her breast milk which was like the nectar. Then he observed, “O goddess, you have incarnated on earth for the welfare of the people.”

Still both Siva and Parvati were not satiated. Then consulting Indra who had been afraid of Tarakasura,

Kumara was established over the post of the commander of the army of gods and then Tripurari Siva removed his son from there.

Then the Sakti named Krauncavidarini was bestowed by Indra to Kumara and then he disappeared from the scene, ensuring the safety of Kumara.

Kumara then cut off the head of Taraka with the same Sakti, who had been afraid of Indra. Then Brahma, Visnu and other gods praised Kumara.

Ravana who had been arrogated because of the strength of his arms raised Kailasa mountain.

Then the trident bearer Siva, the god of gods, pressed the mountain with his big toe.

At the death of a recluse who was dependent on Siva, Mahadeva atonce reached that place, when Yamaraja offered his salutation to the lord.

Without recognising his vehicle, bull of Siva the submarine fire swallowed it. But the lord dragged it holding by the neck. Then the universe became the vast sheet of water.

There are several other events which are blissful, but are not so popular. In these incidents the universe was stirred with the movement of his limbs. How can these be performed by the formless one?

In case Siva showers his grace on all becoming peaceful, then why he does not release all?

In case you say that in the face of the destiny, how could all be released at one and the same time, then in that case the karmans are also performed at the behest of the lord.

Î Vayudeva, in case we speak much, we could be turned as atheists. You kindly give instructions for the removal of our doubts.

## Chapter 31 - Description of spotless Sivatattva by Vayudeva

Vayudeva said, “O Brahmanas, you have expressed an appropriate doubt, with a reason behind it. The desire to know cannot be termed as atheism, because it purifies the intellect.

I shall cite the examples which remove the delusions of the noble people, which is not possible without the grace of the lord. The wicked people take it otherwise.

Nothing is possible without the complete grace of the lord. This is certain. One exercises compassion on others by nature alone. Nothing can be done, in case we think that nothing belongs to us.

The universe which is the form of Pasupasa desires to be treated with compassion. The command of Siva is meant for the showering of his grace on others. Then Pati commands his grace on all. How can Siva be subservient to others to accept the same.

The one who desires no grace, than how could the grace be showered on him. Therefore the meaning of the word freedom cannot be conceived as “not depending on others. ”

In case we consider the one who showers the grace to be subservient, in that case the relationship between the pleasure and salvation cannot be established without the Siva's grace.

Getting free from the command of Siva everyone is entitled to receive the grace of Siva. There is no one in the world who disobeys the command of Siva.

By adoring Sakala, we try to reach the Niskala, who happens to be the true form of Siva.

Siva in Niskala form is not the cause of universe. No one is aware of his Sakala form as well.

Only his adoration is the evidence of his form. He should not therefore be treated with indifference without implication.

A form having the similarity with Atman happens to be the image of Siva. The other, the great one, is the Atman of the image its implication.

As the fire which remains enshrined in the twigs, cannot be visualised, similarly Siva having been enshrined in the image cannot be seen.

As at the demand of the fire, a burning stick is brought, and not the fire, similarly Siva in the form of an image is also adorable.

This is the reason that Siva is imagined in the form of an image and he is taken to be Siva himself.

The same idea holds good in the adoration of a linga. We adore that image, with the feeling of the presence of Siva in that particular image.

The Paramesthi Siva, showers his grace in the form of the image on all. Similarly we also adore Siva lodged in that particular image.

Paramesthi Siva, in order to shower his compassion on the people appears in various types of images.

Atma is used for the sake of pleasure as well as the salvation. Siva infact remains related to the images representing him in the form of the tattvas or otherwise.

One has to enjoy the karmans which have the form of pleasure and pain. When Siva is devoid of karmans them how could they be enjoyed?

Siva is always compassionate on all. He is not subjugating one. The blemishes which appear in those who exercise control, are not to be found in Siva.

The punishment of Brahma and others, as has been depicted in the scriptures, has been done by the lord of blue throat for the welfare of the world.

Siva is the sole lord of the universe. There is no doubt about it. The image of Siva, known as Sri Kantha is sporting in the universe.

Siva had punished Brahma and other gods for their own mistakes, which relieved them of all the sins and the people were relieved of their agonies.

Because of this, Siva has not been denounced for his subjugating or punishing others. It is because, to punish the sinners is the praise worthy duty of a ruler.

The one which is established daily for the success of the task of the lord, in case it does not show its importance, then how could Siva be termed as the lord of the universe?

The desire of the lord is for the obeying of his command. When it is said, “so this.” This is the command and failure to do so attracts punishment.

To move according to the command of the ruler is gentleness and to move against it is wickedness. This aspect is not visible everywhere.

Nobility should be protected removing the wickedness, by means of Sama, dana etc. punishment is the lost resort for the same.

A ruler by resorting to punishment, does good to the society. The performance contrary to this is unbeneficial to the society.

In case one remains engaged in the benevolent tasks, resembles the functions of Isvara. By exercising control over the wicked people he himself does not become evil.

The foolishness of those doing the improper tasks, is denounced. The one who stirs the universe, is known as improper.

All the punishments awarded to the people in the universe are always out due to jealousy. When a father trains a son in governance, the cause of jealousy does not exist there.

Therefore, according to the learned people, the one who indulges into the painful violence he is said to be a harsh person. The others do not agree with this.

A physician, well-versed in the medical treatment, when gets harsh to a patient, then there is no cruelty involved in the same. On the contrary, its cause is compassion.

Compassion is not suited to the violent people. Those who shower their compassion to the violent people, become merciless themselves.

The neglect of the opponents who deserve mercy, is also a sin. One who should have been protected, perishes atonce, if neglected despite the capacity of the protector to do so.

The one who neglects a person who is worthy of protection, on considering his apparent defaults, though he observers his plight is in effect ruthless.

Therefore, it cannot be generally agreed that kindness is conducive to good in every respect. What is admitted is the performance of what is befitting. The rest is unapproved.

Infact, there are the defects of passion, etc. in Murtyatmans (Sadasiva, Brahma and other gods), still the defects are their own and they do not belong to Siva. There may be defects in copper burnt in fire but due to its contact fire does not fade.

But the fire coming in contact with the copper never gets blemished with the touch of inauspicious things the fire does not get polluted.

The impure or the inauspicious thing coming in contact with the fire, gets purified. Similarly Siva never gets polluted on coming in contact with the souls which are to be purified.

On coming in contact with Siva, the soul which needs purification, gets purified. When the iron is put in fire, it is the fire which burns and not the iron.

Therefore in the prosperity and glory of the Murttyatman, it is that of lord Siva and not of Atman. It is the fire and not the fuel which rises up in flames.

The wood turns in the form of coal and not the fire. This example should also be added to the same. Thus Siva is enshrined in wood, stone, dust and as such the presence of Siva is admitted. The virtues like friendship etc. are invisible which are only the feelings of the mind.

Possessing the virtues of friendship and others, the jivas become the cause of the virtues or the vices. The invisible and the apparent feelings in a man depend an the grace of Siva, therefore they are not the main cause of virtues and vices.

To free the living beings of the cycle of the birth and death, cannot be taken to be invisible by the learned people, but it only reflects the command of Siva alone.

To obey the command of Siva is beneficial and whatever is beneficial represents his grace. He is benevolent to all besides being graceful to all.

The meaning of the word uprkara (benevolence) means Anugraha or grace. Since that too benefits a person, therefore Siva is benevolent to all.

Siva is engaged in the welfare of all the conscious and unconscious beings. Because of this temperament, the living being are able to derive out of al the benefits form lord.

As the sun makes the lotuses to blossom with its rays, but still the sun, itself does not blossom due to its nature.

The temperament also contributes to the future meanings of the padarthas. No one can otherwise turn the natural meaning of the padarthas.

As the gold coming in contact with the fire gets melted and not the coal. Similarly Siva discards all the blemishes, but not the one with little of blemishes.

Whatever one deserves to become, does not become himself. How could the performer be independent without the Cetana kriya?

As Siva with a spotless temperament, remains merciful on all, and those who are blemished by nature, are called the jivas.

The jivas cannot move according to their rules, therefore how could they have the universal form. The union of the karmans as well as the Maya is known as the world.

The union of Karmans and the Maya is linked to the jivas and not with Siva. The jiva has enough of blemish with it and not with attributes.

The blemish of the attributes happens due to some reason. The reason behind it is the difference in temperament which is in many forms.

Though the souls are the same, but some of them are held in bondages while the others are the liberated ones. Among those who in bondage, some have different types of knowledge and eminence, due to their being inclined towards abstinence and enjoyment. Some of them achieve identity with the lord, while others achieve only his proximity.

Those who have gained identity with Siva are taken to the welfare form at the highest position. Others known as Mahesvaras are lodged in the middle, while Rudras are lodged down below.

The supreme soul is lodged above all of them. Some other jivas depending on Brahma, Visnu and Mahesa besides the supreme soul also achieve this position.

Many of the devotees of Siva are lodged in the position of antaratma, Satyatita besides the Santipada.

As Rudra is lodged in Vidya, Vaisnavas in Pratistha and as also the Atmans, Brahma and those born of Brahma are lodged in Nivrtti.

The eight Devayonis are the best. The Manusya-yoni is the middle one. The five yonis of birds and others are the lowest of all.

The jiva because of the excess of good or bad deeds, is born in the high or the low yonis. During the period of the enjoyment of pleasures the reward of the karmans remain unripe. After their enjoyment the ripeness emerges in them.

The ripe and unripe blemishes have to be faced because of their presence in the world. By unripe blemishes one achieves lower positions while with the ripe fruits one achieves higher position.

The Pasu-Atman are considered to be one, two and three on the basis of the three dirts. They are stationed in order.

The jivas with their dirts are lodged below, those with two dirts are lodged above them, while those having a single dirts are lodged above all. Thus there is the conditioned difference in the universe.

Siva alone, is the lord of those possessing a single, two and three dirts. Though they are of non-Siva nature, but still they are presided over by the lord.

Similarly the world devoid of Rudra is presided over by Rudra. The Mahabhumi of the universe is controlled over by the hundred Rudras.

The universe with Maya is presided over by the gods. It is surrounded by a Purusa of the size of a thumb from all the sides.

The heaven ending with Mahamaya is presided over by the lords of the worlds like Vayu and others which are stationed within the ways and whose ends are beyond trace?

They are the squatters in the heaven, space and the earth. They are gods observing the activities of the gods.

This is how the ailments of the worldly existence function, with the three dirts and pathological reasons, separately, imperative of being ripe or unripe.

The treatment of the ailments is the perfect knowledge of Siva, which is granted by the lord Siva alone, who happens to be the sole authority for the same.

Now the point is when lord Siva can remove the agony of others, without much efforts, then why does he give them the same? There is no use of thinking on the subject.

This is sure that all the people of the world suffer in one way or the other. How can one face pleasure or the pain, because there is no change in the temperament.

With the medicine prescribed by the physician, the patient is not relieved of the ailment for all times to come, but the use of medicine comforts him for sometimes.

Similarly the jivas who possess dirt by nature, besides being painful, Siva gets them relieved of their ailments with his command.

The physician is not the cause of the removal of the ailment. Siva happens, to be the cause of the universe. Siva is not to be blamed for them.

When misery is the part of life of the humans, then how could Siva be the cause for the same? The dirt is associated with the man since birth, because of which they have to face the suffering on earth.

Dirt is the cause of the world. It reflects Maya and unconsciousness. It performs itself in the presence of Siva.

As the magnet pulls the iron towards itself, which moves from its place, similarly with the proximity of Siva, the world moves.

The co-operative closeness cannot be separated by anyone. Therefore pratistha resides in the world which is presided over by Siva.

The world is without any activity without Siva. Whatever happens here, it is all at the inspiration of Siva. Still he does not feel painful.

His powerful Sakti in the form of Ajna pervades everywhere, which is unblemished. This universe is perpetually covered over by it. Still he is not defiled.

Earlier to whom none was there, who subjugates all, the same is called Isvara. His command prevails, still he earns no blemish.

A person with, an evil wisdom, if thinks otherwise, he gets destroyed. This is all due the influence of his Sakti. Still he earns no blemish.

In the meantime a divine voice in the sky, which was heard by all, declared, that “This is all true.”

All of them were then delighted. Their doubts were totally removed. Then the surprised Rsis offered their salutation to Vayudeva.

Thus Vayudeva, removing the doubts of the sages, and realising that their knowledge had not been stabilised, further spoke.

Vayudeva said, “Knowledge is of two types viz. direct and indirect. The indirect knowledge is unstable while the direct knowledge is stable.

The knowledge which is acquired by reasoning and instructions is known as indirect knowledge. The direct knowledge is gained with the performing of the rites.

It a certain that one cannot attain moksa without direct knowledge. Î Rsis, without laziness you should do you aspire for the success of the best of divine practices.

## Chapter 32 - Excellent practices for the achieving of moksa

The Rsis said, “O Vayudeva, you kindly enlighten us on the particular method by performing which one achieves salvation which is directly acquired. You kindly speak out the means for the same

Vayudeva said, “The adoration of Siva is the supreme dharma which is also the best of the anusthanas. Lord Siva the bestower of moksa could be visualised by the same.

It is of five types and has been divided in five parts viz. kriya, tapas, japam, dhyanam besides the knowledge achieved by the soul.

The knowledge achieved through the five activities together with the connected virtuous rites represent the great dharma. One therefore attains the some knowledge, of direct and indirect nature which ultimately bestows salvation.

Two types of dharmas, both higher as well as the ordinary types have been prescribed in the Vedas. In the matter of dharma Vedas are the final authority.

Dharma is called Parama upto the yoga in the Vedantic section of the Vedas. The secondary or ordinary dharma has been described in the karmakanda section of the Vedas.

The souls having been freed from for the bondages (Pasa) are authorised in the higher dharma and the other one is accessible to all others.

The higher dharma leads one to achieve the greatest virtue of Siva. It shall be supplemented in all parts of the Dharmasastras and other sacred texts.

Saiva has been treated to be the supreme dharma and has also been conceived as the best of anusthana and has been supported by historical treatises as well as the Puranas.

Its exhaustive explanation is found in the Saiva Agamas. It is also mentioned therein, as to who is entitled to practice the same.

The Saivagamas have been divided into two parts viz. Srauta and Asrauta. Whatever has been prescribed in the Vedas, falls under the category of Asrauta, while the Srauta is separate from the same and are will consecrated.

The independent texts were originally ten, but were supplemented later on by eight more, raising the number to eighteen, known as Kamika etc. and the entire literature is known as Saiva Siddhanta.

The Vedic literature comprises of a hundred crores of verses, in which the Pasupata vrata as well as the jnana are highlighted.

In every circle of yugas, Siva incarnates as Yogacarya at different places forth propagation of the yogic practices.

The sages like Rudra, Dadhici, Agastya and glorious Agastya have briefed the same for the purpose of propagating them.

They are the exponents of the Pasupata doctrine, and the related literature. There had been thousands of preceptors in their respective races.

They have supported four types of Supreme dharmas. Out of these, the Pasupatayoga makes one to have face to face audience with Siva.

Therefore the Pasupatayoga has been considered to be the best yogic practice of Siva. The methodology, as has been explained by Brahma for the same, is now being narrated by me.

This Astangayoga had been prescribed by Siva himself. By following the yogic practices, there is the sudden appearing of the ability to understand Siva.

With that command the stable supreme knowledge is expeditiously achieved. A devotee whose knowledge is stabilised, lord Siva, gets pleased with him.

It is by his grace alone, that one achieves the supreme yoga, after which one come face to face audience with Siva and the worldly bondages are removed by having a face to face meeting with Siva.

Then a person having been freed from the worldly bondages, becomes like Siva himself. The methodology explained by Brahma is being stated here.

The prominent names of the lord are Siva, Mahesvara, Rudra, Visnu, Pitamaha, (grand sire), Samsara-vaidya (physician of the world), Sarvajna (omniscient) and Paramatma (the supreme soul).

The aforesaid eight names represent Siva. Out of these, the first five are related to the Santyatita practices.

The five names of Sadasiva originate from conditioning factors. On the disappearing of the conditioning factors, they disappear.

The pada is eternal, while, while the soul which occupies it is non-eternal. At the change of the padas, these holding the padins are released.

With the change, they again achieve the same padas. The first five souls undergo the change of names.

The last three names viz. Samsaravaidya (worldly physician), Sarvajna (omniscient) and Paramatma are dependent on Maya and are indicative of Siva alone.

The one who possesses the five attributes, besides being Isvara, is called Siva by the noble people following the Saiva principles.

The name Mahesvara is explained thus, Prakrti is greater than the twenty three principles. Purusa happens to be the twenty fifth principle greater than Prakrti Purusa is Pranava, or the first Svara in the Vedas. Since his real nature is comprehensible only through the Vedas, he is established in Vedanta. The one who is beyond Purusa and who is associated with Prakrti is Mahesvara, because both Prakrti and Purusa are subservient to him. Or otherwise Mahesvara possesses Maya, who on the other hand is Prakrti, the principle with three gunas and is unchanging. It is Mahesvara who energises Maya. He is glorified Kalatman, the primordial one, the gross as well as the subtle.

The word Rudra means misery or the cause of misery. Lord Rudra is the one who removes the misery. The noble people conceive him to be the supreme cause.

The one who pervades in all the elements from the earth to body the same Siva is also known as Rudra.

The one who is like the father for all the living beings, therefore, he has been called as the grand sire.

As a physician well versed in the medical treatment removes the ailment with the use of medicines, similarly the lord removes the worldly existence together with its roots. He is so called by all those, who are aware of the nature of the principles.

Inspite of one's having the ten sense organs, for the success of knowledge, besides the organs of knowledge, and the organs of activity, he is unable to realise the gross or subtle aspects in all the three times, having been covered with the dirt of Maya,

but lord Sadasiva knows about everything wherever it is in whatever form, therefore, he has been called as the supreme soul and omniscient.

He is the supreme soul, always linked with the divine merits. Because of his being separate from the Jivatma, Siva himself happens to be the supreme soul.

With the grace of the preceptor, achieving the eight names. The knots of Kalas, nivrtti and others, shall be cut off with the five names of Siva and purified by the repetitions, strotras, and non-restraints. By means of Susumna, the Puryastaka alone, with the chest, neck, palate, middle of the eyebrows and the hole on the top of the head, shall be cut off.

The moon is lodged in the twelve petalled lotus in the heart. With the strength of Siva, the soul should be made descend there. The mouth is shrunk in size. The body is drenched with the shower of the nectar of the Sakti and merged in their reason. The Atma is then let down into the heart.

The devotee then mediates on the great lord, who is favourably disposed towards his devotees and is conceived as seated over the white twelve petalled lotus beyond the moon, who in the sweet crystal pure, delighted, cool, lustrous form, of Ardhanarisvara shall be meditated upon. The devotee shall have the normal state of mind. The lord shall then be adored, with eight names of Siva and the sacred flowers.

At the end of the adoration, the devotee shall perform pranayama, well concentrating his mind. The eight names of Siva, should then be recited.

Repeating namah, he shall pour eight ahutis in the navel, together with Purnahuti, offering eight flowers, while concluding the worship. With the palm full of water he shall dedicate to his Atman. By doing so, before long, the auspicious knowledge of Pasupata is gained. Then he acquires his exalted states and the excellent conduct. Then securing the great yoga, he is liberated. There is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 33 - The glory of the performing of Pasupata vrata

The Rsis said, “O lord, we would like to listen about the best of Pasupata-varata, performing which, Brahma and other gods came to be known as Pasupatas.

Vayudeva said, “I am going to reveal the secret to you which removes all the sins and has been discussed in the Atharvasira- upanisad.

The full moon day of the month of Caitra is the appropriate time for the same. The place for performing of the same has been taken to be a Siva temple, some forest or an orchard as auspicious.

For the performing of the same, initially on the day of Trayodasi, one should perform Sandhya after taking the bath, go to the acarya and get his permission.

Then he should be clad in white clothes and wear a white yajnopavita and the white rosary applying the sandal paste over the body.

Then holding kusa in his hand he should be seated over kusasana. He should perform pranayama facing east or north. Then devoting his mind to Siva and Siva, he should offer prayer to them;’’ He should then perform a pledge, sankalpa. The time limit for the vrata is till death, or twelve years, or six years or three years or twelve months or six months or three months or a month or twelve days, or six days or three days or a day.

He should ignite the sacrifical fire duly as in the Virajahoma and should perform homa dropping ghee, twigs, payasam etc.

After pouring of the purnahuti, then for the purification of the tattvas, homa should be performed reciting the mantra om namah Sivaya.

Then he should recall in his mind that let the Pancamahabhutas, Tanmatras, five Karmendriyas, be purified.

They are divided into five parts each according to the jnana and karmas. There are seven dhatus like the skin etc. and five vayus like prana and others.

The mind, intelligence, pride, guna, Prakrti, Purusa, raga, vidya, kala, Niyati and time, Maya, Suddhi, Vidya, Mahesvara, Sadasiva, Sakti and Siva -tattva are respectively called the tattvas.

With the reciting of the mantras mentioned in this connection the performer of homa is purified and by the grace of Siva and he achieves all the knowledge.

Then with the use of the cowdung, round balls should be made and poured in the fire sanctifying them. The performer on that particular day should consume only the cooked rice soaked in ghee.

On the morning of the fourteenth day performing the morning routine he should observe fast.

Then on the full moon day, he should perform all the tasks upto homa and then collect the ashes extinguishing the fire of Rudra.

Then he should take his bath shaving his head or with his head adorned with matted locks of hair. Then he should remove all the costumes like a shameless person.

Or otherwise he should wear the coloured robes, the skin or the bark garments. He should then carry the danda and wear the chain.

He should sip the water twice washing his feet and then apply the ashes of the Viraja fire.

Then he should apply ashes from head to feet reciting the Atharvan hymns like Agniriti etc. half a dozen times, on all the limbs.

Then picking up the ashes, he should rub ashes on all the limbs of the body in the same sequence reciting pranava-mantra.

Then reciting the mantra Trayusam- Jamadagni one should draw tripundra over the body. Then he should perform the Sivayoga realising himself as Siva.

He shall thus perform all the three Sandhyas. This Pasupatavrata, yields all the worldly pleasures and salvation dispelling the form of Pasu.

Discarding Pasu-hood, performing Pasupatavrata and then one should adore the Sivalinga known as lord Mahadeva.

A lotus seat should be arranged with a gold lotus with eight petals in which nine gems should be studded. The pericarp should be of saffron colour.

In case one does not have means to do so, then the red and white lotus flowers should be used. In the absence of the same one should offer mental adoration.

In the pericarp of the lotus flower, a pedestal of crystal gem should be made in which a small Sivalinga should be placed. The adoration should be done thereafter.

The linga should be consecrated appropriately. Then the linga should be conceived to be of five heads.

He should bathe the linga with pancagavya and other materials placed in a golden vase.

He should offer fragrance, camphor, sandal paste, saffron etc. besides the ornaments over the linga.

Then the wood apple leaves, red and white lotus flowers, blue lotus and other fragrant flowers should be offered.

The auspicious Tulasi leaves, Durva grass, unbroken rice, whatever be available should be offered according to the mode of worship.

The incense, arghya, naivedya etc., should be offered to Siva and the devotee should engage himself in the auspicious activities.

In this special vrata of Siva, one should make the offering of things purchased by him by the noble means.

The number of the wood apple leaves or the lotus flowers, should be a thousand each. Otherwise, Î Brahmanas the number should at least be a hundred and eight.

Out of these the wood apple leaves none should be left out. A golden lotus is more valuable then a thousand lotus flowers.

The blue lotus is like the wood apple leaves. There is no rule for other flowers. They could be offered as many as are available.

Astanga-arghya is of special type and the incense besides the sandal paste should also be offered. Vamadeva should be offered the sandal paste. Purusa should be offered yellow orpiment. Ashes should be offered to Isana, some of the acaryas prescribe the offering of the sandal paste to him. Some of them do not support the offering of the incense to him, because it is prescribed elsewhere. The white aguru is meant for Aghora, while the black aguru is meant for Purusa.

Guggulu is to be offered in the mouth of Sadyojata, fragmentation in the mouth of Saumya, while Isana should be provided the incense of khas.

The ordinary incense includes sugar, honey, camphor, ghee of Kapila cow, sandal paste and Aguru wood.

The lamps should be burnt soaking in camphor and ghee. Each mouth should be offered the arghya and water for sipping.

Initially Ganesa and Kartikeya should be adored. Thus when the worship of the first shift is completed.

The Cakravarti Vighnesas should be adored in the second shift. In the third shift one should adore the eight forms of Siva, including Bhava and others.

In the fourth shift, the eleven images of Mahadeva, and all the Ganesvaras should be adored.

In the fifth shift outside the lotus mystic diagram, the lords of the ten quarters should be worshipped along with third weapons and the followers, the mental sons of Brahma, the luminary bodies, the goddesses, the gods, the dwellers of heaven, the dwellers of the nether worlds, the sages, yogis the sacrifices, the birds, the mothers, the ksetrapalas with their ganas, and the universe with mobile and immobile beings should be worshipped, since they have the pre-eminence of Siva and their worship would please Siva.

At the end, after worshipping the supreme lord, delicious havis shall be offered as naivedya along with ghee and other dishes.

The betel with something to chew with and to render the mouth fragrant shall be given. After offering different types of flowers again, besides the ornaments, the comprehensive worship shall be concluded with the performing of arati. Then the drinking bowl with the complements and bedding shall be offered.

A garland resembling the lustre of the moon should be placed over the bed. All of these represent the charities by the kings.

The performer should himself do this and make even the priests to do so. The pujana should be performed after the homa, followed by the recitation of Siva stotra as well as the Pancaksari lore.

After circumambulation and the offering the salutation one should dedicate himself to lord Siva. This should be followed by the worship of the preceptor as well as the Brahmana.

Then offering the special arghya and the flowers the deity should be sent off. Protecting the fire reciting the Agni mantra one should bid farewell to the fire god as well.

A devotee should perform the worship daily similarly. Thereafter all the material for adoration as well as the lotus should be given over, together with the linga to the preceptor or alternatively the linga should be consecrated in a temple of Siva. Thereafter, the devotee should worship the preceptor, the Brahmana and other people for the success of the vrata.

In case a person has the requisite means, he should please the devotee of Siva, the Brahmanas, destitute, and orphans. In case one is unable to perform the Vrata with complete fast, he can take, fruits, roots, besides milk.

Or alternatively he can take food once in a day and take light food in the night. Keeping himself pure, he should sleep on the floor.

Or alternatively he should sleep over the ashes or the straw. He shall wear the deer skin or bark garments, observing celibacy. Thus the holy rites shall be performed by a devotee accordingly.

In case he is healthy enough, he should observe fast on Sundays, during the Ardra constellations, on the eighth, fourteenth, full moon or the moonless days of a fortnight.

He should not touch the cheats, fallen man, woman in period, polluted women having just given birth to a child, and the Sudras by all means. He should not think about them, nor talk or look at them.

He should practice forgiveness, charity, compassion, truthfulness, satisfaction, calmness and remain non-violent.

He should take bath thrice and should devote himself to the lord, with his action, thought and behaviour.

What more could be stated, the devotee of Siva, performing vrata should not commit any evil deed. In case a sin is committed unmindfully, he should consider its seriousness or otherwise, and perform repentance by performing adoration, homa or recitation. Till the end of the vrata he should never act carelessly.

A devotee, should, reliving himself of all the desires, give away the cow in charity besides the oxen, adoring Siva at the same time.

The ordinary procedure for the performance of the vrata has been spelt out. The procedure that has to be followed every month, has been narrated by me, as had been heard by me.

In the month of Vaisakha a Sivalinga of adamant, in Jyestha of an emerald, in Asadha of pearl, in Sravana of sapphire, in Bhadrapada of ruby, in Asvin of onyx, in Karttika of coral, in Margasirsa that of lapis lazuli, in Pausa that of topaz, in Magha of sun- stone, in Phalguna of moon-stone and in Caitra of sun-tone, is considered to be auspicious. In case these gems could not be made available, the gold would serve as the substitute in every month.

In case the gold is not available silver could be used for the making of a Sivalinga. Or alternatively silver, copper, rock or even clay shall be used for the purpose. Even lac could be used for the purpose.

Or alternatively he should make the lingas of fragrance as per his desire. At the end of the vrata, he should finish his daily routine.

He should perform the homa and worship as before and then adore the acarya and the Brahmanas engaged in the vrata.

With the permission of the preceptor, he should be seated over the kusa-asana facing east or the north holding kusa in his hands.

He should recite the mula-mantra as per his capacity, devoting himself to Siva and Siva and offer his salutation to them with their permission.

Then he should pray, “O lord I am now discarding this vrata at your command.” Thus speaking he should remove the kusa below the linga and place it to the north.

Thereafter he should discard danda, locks of hair, bark garments, besides the chain. Then sipping the water, he should recite the Pancaksara-mantra.

The one who carries on this vrata till death quite carefully, he is called Naisthika or a person with a religious faith.

He is considered to be the best of all the asramas and Mahapasupati-vrati. He is the foremost of all the ascetics and those performing the vratas.

No one could be more fortunate among those desirous of achieving moksa. A yati, who is Naistika, he is also called the best of the Naistika.

A yati who performs this vrata daily or does it for twelve days he is equated with Naisthika. because of the performing of the sharp vrata.

Who applying ghee over the body the one, performs the vrata for two or three days even, he could also be treated as Naisthika.

The one who performs this vrata in a selfless manner, and the one who has devoted his soul to Siva, no one could be equated with him.

A learned Brahmana, applying ashes over the body daily, he is surely relieved of all the grave sins.

The auspicious semen of Rudra and Agni happens to be the ashes. Therefore a devotee who applies ashes over the body is always powerful.

Those who always apply ashes over the body, all their blemishes are removed with their bodies coming in contact with the ashes. A person whose soul is purified with ashes is called bhasmanistha.

A person having applied ashes over the entire body besides the Tripundra is also called Bhasmanistha.
