Finding that a person has applied ashes over the body, all the goblins, pisacas and the incurable diseases, flee from a distance from him, undoubtedly.

It is called Bhasita because it shines, Bhasma because it devours the sins, Bhuti because it causes prosperity and Raksa because it provides protection.

What else could be stated to impress about the glory of bhasma. A person performing the vrata having a bhasma bath becomes the lord of Siva himself.

Bhasma serves as a powerful weapon for the devotees of Siva. It is a divine missile whereby the mishaps of the elder brothers of Dhaumya in the course of his penance had been removed.

Therefore, one should endeavour in all possible ways to collect bhasma, like wealth, after performing the Pasupata-vrata and engage himself in bhasma bath.

## Chapter 34 - Upamanyu's performance of tapas for Siva

The Rsis said, “The elder brother of Dhaumya had performed tapas for the drinking of milk, as a result of which lord Siva gave him the ocean of milk

How could the innocent child attain the knowledge of the Siva literature? How could he perform tapas for Siva, getting enlightened over the temperament of Siva?

How could he achieve the perfect knowledge while performing the tapas? How did he receive the ashes representing the semen of Rudragni for his self protection?”

Vayudeva said, “He had not been are ordinary child, who performed tapas. He had been the son of the immensely learned sage Vyaghrapada.

He had been a Siddha in his earlier birth as well. Due to some reason he fell from his place and was reborn as the son of the Rsi.

As luck would have it his desire to have milk developed into the cause of his performing the tapas.

Because of the same, Siva besides bestowing him the ocean of milk, also granted him, the eternal position of his gana besides the everlasting bachelorhood.

Because of the grace of Siva, Upamanya, while still being a child, achieved the perfect knowledge.

Because of this, he narrated the literature on Siva, as Kumara Kartikeya had narrated the same to Nandi.

Listening to the pathetic words of his mother over milk, for the achieving of the perfect knowledge of Siva, he started performing tapas.

Sometime, he in the house of his maternal grandfather found the son of his maternal uncle consuming enough of milk. But he got only a little of it, which developed a jealousy in him.

Finding that his maternal uncle's son had consumed enough of milk, Upamanyu, the son of Vyaghrapada lovingly asked his mother.

Upamanyu said, “O virtuous and chaste ascetic, Î mother, give me the warm milk of cow, which I would like to drink.

Vayudeva said, “Listening to the words of the son the ascetic wife of Vyaghrapada felt painful.

Lovingly embracing her son, keeping in view her own poverty, she started lamenting painfully.

The illustrious boy on the other hand kept on demanding the milk again and again while crying.

The ascetic Brahmana woman, keeping in view the stubborn nature of the boy thought of a beautiful remedy.

She gleaned a few grains which the sweet voiced lady grounded into a paste with water and then said to her son,” come on, Î dear son.” She thus called her son, though she was distressed at heart and gave her the fake milk.

On drinking the watery stuff as milk, the excited boy shouted, ‘‘O mother, this is no milk.”

The distressed mother, when saw the boy in such a miserable state, she caught hold of him, kissed his head, wiped his lotus like eyes with her hand and said.

The mother said, “All the rivers filled with gems are spread from heaven to Patala, which are invisible to unfortunate people or those who are not devoted to Siva.

Till such time Siva is not pleased, the kingship, heaven moksa and the food with milk cannot be had.

All these things can be achieved by the grace of Siva. The devotee of other gods wander in pain.

Î Son, we live in the forest, and there is no means to get milk here? We are the forest dwellers. Where from can we get the milk.

Because of the all round shortage, an unfortunate person like me had mixed water in flour creating the fake milk.

You had tasted a little of the boiled milk from the house of your maternal uncle you drank (the fake milk) taking it to be the real one.

What I gave you was no milk. When you cry out saying so, you make me miserable. You cannot have milk without the grace of lord Siva.

The one who he has devoted himself at the lotus like feet of Sambasiva as well as his ganas, only then they can achieve the fortunes.

We have not adored lord Siva, who is the bestower of wealth and befitting benefits to those who desire him.

Aiming at the riches, we have not worshipped Siva. We are poor because of that and I could not give milk to you

In case we had given charities in the earlier birth in the name or Siva or Visnu, the same would have been received in this birth.”

Vayudeva said, “Listening to the miserable but truthful words of the mother the child felt painful inside, but pretending braveness, he said.

Upamanyu said, Î mother, do not feel miserable like this. In case Siva and Parvati are there, then everything would be well done.

O mother listen to my words. In case Mahadeva exists, the sooner or later, I shall achieve the ocean of milk.

Vayudeva said, “Listening to the immensely intelligent words of Upamanyu, the mother with self respect was pleased and she spoke.

The mother said, “O son, you have thought correctly to please me. Therefore you don't delay in the worship of Samba Sadasiva. There is none bigger than Siva. The entire universe is his creation alone. Brahma and all others happen to be his servants.

One gets fortunes by his grace alone. All of us are his slaves. Except Siva we are aware of none else.

Leaving aside all other gods, worship both Siva and Parvati along with their ganas with devotion through action, mind and speech.

For Siva the god of gods, the bestower of boons, “Îḍ namah Sivaya” is the Mulamantra (directly expressive mantra).

There are seven crores of mantras including îmkara. All of them emerge from him and get absorbed in the same.

Their only utility is to please lord Siva. But this mantra, is accessible to all because of the command of Isvara.

As Siva protects the noble as well as the wicked souls, similarly, this mantra can be used by them as well.

This happens to be the most powerful of all the mantras and provides all types of safety. Nothing is beyond it.

Therefore with the reciting of this five-syllabled mantra, nothing remains beyond the reach of a devotee.

This is the pleasant weapon for the protection of the devotees of Siva. This weapon has emerged out of this mantra. Therefore you should recite it.

I have got this excellent ash from your father, which had been collected from the Viraja fire. It saves a person from all the misfortunes.

I have given the mantra to you which should be received by you at my command. Its recitation is going to protect you.”

Vayudeva said, “Thus the mother giving the instructions to the child, blessed him saying, “Let you face welfare.” Then she sent him off. The child bowing in reverence to the command of the mother, got ready to leave. Then the mother pronounced a blessing on him, “Let you meet welfare. May the gods bless you.”

At the command of the mother, he went to the Himalaya mountain, performed severe tapas there while fasting and inhaling air alone.

He made a temple of eight bricks, and an earthen Sivalinga was consecrated in it. Then he invoked Sambasiva and his ganas in the same.

Then he performed tapas for a long time offering the wild flowers and leaves, reciting the five syllable mantra.

Turning to the form of demons, certain ghosts of the sages who were earlier cursed by Marici harassed the lonely lean and thin boy, Upamanyu engaged in adoring Siva, though he was not an excellent devotee of Siva. They created obstructions in his tapas.

Upamanyu kept on his cool, inspite of having been harassed by the demons in the performance of the tapas. He kept on uttering om namah Sivaya like the one fallen on evil times.

On hearing the sound, the goblins who had been harassing him at once stopped doing so and instead engaged themselves in serving him.

Î Sages, due to the severe tapas of Upamanyu, the whole universe, besides the mobile and immobile beings got ignited.

## Chapter 35 - Siva’s testing the devotion of Upamanyu

Vayudeva said, “All the illustrious gods then went to Vaikuntha to meet Narayana there. Offering their salutation to Narayana, they said to him.

Then listening to their words, lord Purusottama thought, “what is this?” and he understood the cause of their arrival.

Then they went to Lord Siva, to who was lodged at the Mandaracala mountain to meet him. Finding Siva their they spoke to him with folded hands.

Visnu said, “O lord, a child known by the name of Upamanyu, is scorching the world with this tapas for the sake of milk you kindly stop him.”

Vayudeva said, “Listening to the words of Visnu, Siva said, “You better go back to your abode and I shall stop the boy from doing so.”

Listening to the words of Siva, Visnu the beloved of all the gods, retried with them to their respective abodes, getting pleased.

In the meantime, Siva the wielder of the bow Pinaka, taking to the form of Indra started thinking of going there.

Then Siva mounting over a white elephant, taking to the form of Indra and accompanied with the gods, Danavas, Siddhas and serpents went to the tapovana of the child sage.

At that point of time the divine flyswhisks were moved over the lord. Indrani was made to hold the umbrella in the left hand.

At that point of time Siva and Parvati appeared like Indra and Indrani. The umbrella held over them looked like the Mandara mountain.

Thus taking to the form of Indra, Siva, in order to shower his grace on Upamanyu, reached his hermitage.

Finding Siva in the form of Indra, the great sage, offered his salutation to him, bowing his head.

Upamanyu said, “Î lord of gods, Î master, the best of the gods, lord of the universe, with your arrival, you have purified my hermitage.”

Vayudeva said, “Thus finding the boy, with folded hands, Siva in the form of Indra, spoke in deep voice.”

Indra said, “O Suvrata, I am pleased with your tapas. You ask for a boon. Î son of Dhaumya, Î great sage, I grant you all the desired things.”

Vayudeva said, “At these words of Indra, he great sage, spoke with folded hands, “All I desire is the devotion for Siva.”

On hearing this Indra said, “Are you not aware of me? I am the one adored by all the gods and lord of the three worlds known as Indra.

Î Brahmana Rsi, you get devoted to me and adore me. I shall grant you everything, you better forget Siva, who is attributeless.

Rudra without attributes is not going to serve any purpose for you. He is beyond the family of gods and has become goblin.”

Vayudeva said, ‘‘On hearing these words, Upamanyu thought him to be some one who had arrived for the creation of the obstruction in his religious performance, and he kept on reciting the five syllable mantra."

Upamanyu said, ‘‘Denouncing Siva, you have called him as attributeless. In that context, you have mentioned the Nirgunatva of the great lord.

You are unaware of the fact that Rudra happens to be the lord of all the gods. It is he who produced Brahma, Visnu and Mahesa. He is beyond Prakrti.

The propounders of Brahman conceive him separate from Sat and Asat besides being unmanifest. He is eternal single and multifarious. I would like to receive a boon from him.

I desire to receive boon from the lord, who is the cause of all the causes, and is meditated upon by the knowers of truth and bestows the goal of Sankhya and yoga.

There is no tattva beyond Siva, he is the cause of all the causes. Siva is the supreme tattva and there is no tattva beyond him. He is the best of all having produced Brahma, Visnu and other gods.

What more shall I say, I have realised today that due to the sin of my earlier birth, I have listened to the denouncement of Siva.

The one who ends his life soon after listening to the denouncement of Siva, he at once achieves Sivaloka.

Î degraded god, I shall discard my desire for getting the milk I shall end my life, after killing with Sivas weapon.”

Vayudeva said, ‘‘Thus speaking, Upamanyu, leaving aside his wish to have milk, got ready to kill himself after killing Indra.

Carrying the ashes, he invoke the terrific Aghorastra, the falling sage shot the weapon at Indra.

Then devoting his mind at the lotus like feet of Siva, Upamanyu tried to burn himself.

With this effort of the Brahmana, Siva the destroyer of the eyes of Bhaga stopped the yogi from his efforts.

The Aghorastra shot by Upamanyu was intercepted by Nandi at the command of Siva.

Then lord Siva appeared before the Brahmana in the form of Candrasekhara.

The boy was shown the several oceans of milk, nectar, curd, and ghee, besides the fruits, eatables, oceans of sweets and heaps of fried materials were also shown to him.

Upamanyu then found Siva and Parvati together with Ganesvara and others seated over the bull carrying the divine weapons.

Drums were beaten in the sky at that point of time. The rain of flowers was dropped. All the directions were covered with Brahma, Visnu and other gods.

Upamanyu was then drowned in the waves of the ocean of bliss. With his mind filled with devotion, he prostrated before the lord.

In the meantime, Siva called him and smelling his head, got ready to pronounce a boon on him.

Siva said, “You together with you kiths and kins, can consume eatables of your liking. You will remain my devotee getting free from all the miseries and enjoying all the pleasures.

Î Upamanyu, Parvati is your mother henceforth. Taking you to be my son I have given you the ocean of milk.

Besides I give you the oceans of honey, curd, ghee, cooled rice and fruits.

Î great sage, the mountains of sweet pies, the ocean of eatables, are also given to you which should be received by you. You better take them.

Your father is lord Siva and Parvati is the mother, who happens to be the mother of the universe. I bestow on you the position of a god, beside the that of chief a ganas.

You ask for the boons you like. I feel delighted with you. I shall grant all the boons to you. You do not hesitate.”

Vayudeva said, ‘‘Speaking these words of lord Siva, the lord lifted up the boy and kissed his forehead and then handed him over to Parvati as her son. The goddess also lovingly placed her hand over his head like Guha, bestowed the eternal position of a prince.

The ocean of milk also came in an embodied form holding sweet milk in his hands and gave the imperishable condensed milk to the saintly boy.

Besides the fortunes, yoga, eternal contentment, unfading Brahmavidya, prosperity were also given to him with delight.

Then Siva getting pleased with his tapas, further bestowed the boons on Upamanyu.

Then discoursing an Pasupata vrata, perfect knowledge, besides the vratayoga, the everlasting power of speech were bestowed on him and he was made quite active.

Upamanyu then receiving the boons from Siva and Parvati was immensely delighted.

Getting delighted, offering his salutation to the divine couple with folded hands, Upamanyu begged for a boon from Siva.

Upamanyu said, ‘‘O lord of the gods, Î Paramesvara, getting pleased with me, you kindly grant me your everlasting devotion.

Î great lord let me be devoted to my kiths and kins. I should always remain your slave and gain closeness to you with love.”

Thus speaking, feeling delighted, the excellent Brahmana, then spoke in choked voice eulogising Siva.

He said, ‘‘Î god of gods, Î Mahadeva, you are well disposed towards those was take refuge with you. Î ocean of mercy, you always remain pleased with me.”

Vayudeva said, ‘‘At these words of Upamanyu, Siva who grants boon to all, replied to Upamanyu.

Siva said, “O Son, Î Brahmarsi, Î Upamanyu, I am pleased with you. I have given you everything. You are my firm devotee. I have realised this.

Being comfortable, you remain eternal and free from old age. You will be glorious, illustrious, possessing the divine knowledge.

All your kiths and kins, the race, gotra will became imperishable. Î excellent Brahmana ascetic, you will always remain devoted to me.

I shall always be lodged in the vicinity of your asrama. Î excellent Brahmana you will always delightfully roam about close to me.”

Thus speaking, Siva, who had the brilliance comparable to a crores of suns, bestowing boons an Upamanyu, disappeared from the scene.

Upamanyu, on the other hand, receiving the excellent boons from Siva, went back to his mother and became comfortable with her.

**Here ends the purva-bhaga of seventh Vayaviya Samhita of Siva Mahapurana.**

Siva-Mahapuranam

## Vayaviya Samhita (Part II)

## Chapter 1 - Instruction by Upamanyu to Sri Krsna to adore Siva

Siva, who moves the wheel of the universe, who is seated with Parvati with her raised breasts painted with saffron, salutation to such a lord of the universe.

Suta said, “When Vayudeva, enlightened the sages about the achieving of the boon by Upamanyu from Siva, Vayudeva got up for the performing of his routine during the midday.

The Rsis dwelling in the Naimisaranya, then confabulated as to what was to be asked in future.

Then all the sages finding the return of Vayudeva after performing his daily routine, took their respective seats.

Thereafter Vayudeva too, getting free from the daily routine, took his seat in the congregation.

Vayudeva, who was adored by the three worlds, having been seated over a comfortable asana, devoting his mind to the grace of lord Siva, spoke.

I take refuge with the omniscient, invincible lord Mahadeva, who is the lord of all the mobile and immobile beings.”

The Rsis said, “You have just brought out that the sage Upamanyu performed tapas, for getting milk and was so blessed by Paramesvara.

Lord Krsna, the performer of the noble deeds, meet the son of Dhaumya, and performed the Pasupata-vrata at his advice.

By doing so, he achieved the supreme knowledge. This aspect has been known to us. Then how could Krsna achieve the knowledge of Pasupata-vrata?’’

Vayudeva said, “Though the eternal Vasudeva had incarnated on earth of his own will, but denouncing his human body, he purified himself.

For the achieving of a son, by performing of tapas, he went to the hermitage of the sage, where he found Upamanyu, the great sage.

He had applied ashes over his entire body, with his forehead having been embossed with Tripundra wearing a rosary of Rudraksa around his neck, with his head adorned with the matted locks of hair.

He had been surrounded by his disciples as the Vedas are surrounded by the Sastras. The immensely illustrious Upamanyu, was peaceful and was engaged in the adoration of Siva.

Sri Krsna, feeling thrilled, offered his salutation to the sage and respectfully went round him thrice. Lowering his head he eulogised the sage with folded hands.

At the very sight of the sage, all the blemishes of Sri Krsna, arising out of Maya and the karmans, vanished.

Then Sri Krsna, having been freed of all the blemishes emanating from Maya etc. were removed. Then Upamanyu dusted him with ashes, repeating the mantras like Agniriti. He was then made to perform the Pasupata-vrata lasting for twelve months. The excellent knowledge was then imparted by the sage to Sri Krsna.

Thereafter, the divine Pasupata sages well versed in the related rites, surrounded Sri Krsna.

At the advice of the preceptor, Sri Krsna possessing the great prowess, performed penance, for getting a son, adoring both Siva and Parvati as the deities.

Because of that tapas, at the end of a year, lord Siva with great splendour, appeared before Sri Krsna with Parvati and his ganas.

Then Sri Krsna, adored lord Siva, who had appeared before him for the granting of a boon, with folded hands.

Siva and Siva were pleased with the tapas of Visnu and gave him a son Samba of good qualities.

Since it was Siva accompanied with Amba, Jambavati’s son was given the name of Samba.

Thus I have narrated to you, how the all powerful Sri Krsna, attained knowledge from the great sage and got son from Siva.

The one who recites this episode daily, listens to it or narrates it to others, attains Visnu’s wisdom and enjoys all the pleasures in the world.

## Chapter 2 - Highlighting of the greatness of Pasupata, by Vasudeva to the sages

The Rsis said, “What is the Pasupata knowledge? Why is Siva called Pasupati what type of question was asked by Sri Krsna to Upamanyu the son of Dhaumya.”

O Vayudeva the body of Siva, you please enlightened us on the subject. Because, there is no instructor better than you in the three worlds.”

Suta said, “Listening to the words of the sages, Vayudeva, devoting his mind to Isan Siva, then spoke.”

Vayudeva said, “In earlier times lord Sri- Kantha Mahesa, had imported the knowledge of Pasupata to Parvati over the Mandaracala mountain.

The question about the same was asked by lord Krsna having the universal form. How could the gods and others be created as Pasus and how could lord Siva be their Pati?

Whatever had the sage Upamanyu narrated to lord Krsna, I am repeating the same in brief.

Once Visnu in the form of Sri Krsna, enquired from the sage Upamanyu, offering his salutation to the sage appropriately.

Sri Krsna said, “O lord, the lord Siva had revealed the knowledge of Pasupata to Parvati, besides its glory, I would like to listen to the same completely.

What type of a god is Pasuapti? Who is termed as Pasu? Which are the nooses with which they are bound, and how are they freed.”

At these words of Krsna, the sage Upamanyu felt inspired. He also started giving a reply as he had been asked for.

Upamanyu said, “All those from Brahma to all in mobiles who are subservient to Siva are called Pasus.

Being their lord, Siva is called Pasupati. All of them are bound by Siva by means of dirt or Maya.

By adoring the lord with devotion, it is Siva who gets them freed. The twenty four tattvas are the karmans and the gunas of Maya.

They are called Visayas. The jiva is bound by them. Lord Mahesvara captivates them all, right from Brahma to a pillar.

Having been bound with these nooses, Mahesvara attends to the business of the world. At his command the Prakrti and Purusa function with the creation of the intelligence. The pride, ten sense organs, mind, subtle meaningful words, touch, form essence, fragrance, five tanmatras emerge out of the same.

At the command of the lord Siva who happens to be the god of gods, the tanmatras take shape.

The five Mahabhutas also emerge from the same, these Mahabhutas are associated with Brahma to the straw in all the living beings.

In the same sequence the Mahabhutas also emerge from Siva. The intelligence and pride are created.

They provide consciousness to the mind besides the imagination. The organs of knowledge apprehend the objects separately.

The sense organs grasp their objects and not others and this is due to the divine command of the lord. The organs of activity also function in their own way and attend no other job. It is all due to the command of Siva that the sound etc. are grasped and speech etc. are made. The command of Siva cannot be transgressed by any one.

The ether pervades all at the command of Siva and yields space to the elements. At Siva’s behest, the wind pervades the entire universe, internal and external under different names of prana etc. At the bidding of the lord, the fire god bears offerings to the gods and the oblation to the manes. It helps cooling etc. At his behest the water enlivens all, at the command of the lord the earth holds up the universe forever.

At the firm command of Siva, Indra protects the gods, kill the asuras and saves the worlds. At the behest of Siva, Varuna rules over the waters, binding those who deserve punishment, with his noose. At the instance of Siva, Kubera is the lord of wealth as well asthe Yaksas and distributes the wealth to the living beings on the basis of the merits of each one of them. By the grace of Siva Isana bestows knowledge on the people with wisdom and bestow riches on them, curbing the activities of the evil doers.

It is at the command of Siva, that Sesa carries the earth over its head. The Raudri and Tamasi for of Visnu that brings about destruction is created by the four-faced lord. At his behest, through other forms of his own, he protects the universe and annihilates it in the end.

The image of Siva, which is called to be of tamasic nature or which causes destruction, at whose command Brahma controls the entire universe, Visnu sustains the world or Brahma resorts to creation, Visnu sustains and Hara resorts to its destruction, all the three represent his own forms.

He is the soul of the universe, who taking to three forms, creates the universe, protects it and finally destroys the same.

At his bidding, the three parts of his splendour, the sun supports the universe, makes the same to fall on earth and in the heaven. At the desire of the moon crested lord, the moon nourishes the plants, delights the living beings and is imbibed by the gods.

At the command of the moon crested Siva, the gods get the nectar from the moon, besides the Adityas, Vasus, Rudra, Asvinikumaras and Maruts, the birds, Rsis, Siddhas, serpents, humans, deer, animals, birds, insects and other immobile beings, besides rivers, oceans, mountains, forests, lakes, Vedas, post-vedic literature, Sastras, group of mantras, and the yajnas from Kalagni to Siva, Brahmanas with their presiding deities, innumerable globes, and their coverings, the entire past, present and future, sides and directions, Kalabhedas as well as the Kalas besides whatever is seen or heard in this world, it is established at the command of Siva.

At his command, the earth, the mountains, the clouds, the oceans, the planets, Indra and other gods besides the moveable and immovable get established.

Upamanyu said, “O Sri Krsna, the story of Siva, is simply wonderful, which has been searched in the Vedas and heard by me. You listen to the same from me.

In earlier times, the gods getting victorious over the demons, developed a controversy saying that “the victory has been achieved by us, killing the demons.”

Then Siva taking to an excellent form appeased before them turned to the form of a Yaksa shedding his qualities.

Then he placed a straw over the ground and said, “Whosoever could remove this straw, he would be treated as having defeated the demons.”

Listening to the words of Yaksa, Indra getting enraged, holding the vajra in his hand, smilingly tried to lift up the straw with his hand.

But he was unable to lift up the straw. Then he shot the vajra at it in order to break it. The vajra of Indra, after striking with straw, was thrown aside like vajra.

Then the guardians of the quarters and the worlds, of great strength shot thousands of their, weapons at the grass-blade.

The great fire was ignited which went in flames. The strong winds started blowing. The ocean started overflowing the seashore like the time of dissolution.

O Sri Krsna, all the efforts of the gods in relation to the straw became infractions because of the self strength of the Yaksa.

Then Indra spoke in anger, “Who are you?” Thereafter in full view of the gods, the Yaksa disappeared.

Thereafter a goddess with golden complexion adorned with divine ornaments was seen in the sky.

Irritated Indra then asked her bowing in reverence to her, “Who was the astonishing Yaksa?”

Then the goddess said smilingly, “He is the one who is beyond your vision. The wheel of the universe is being rotated by him.

He is the one who creates the universe in the beginning, then preserves it and ultimately destroys the same.

Thus speaking the goddess disappeared in full view of all. The gods also, offering their salutation to her returned to their respective abodes.

## Chapter 3 - Upamanyu’s instruction to Sri Krsna

Upamanyu said, “O Sri Krsna, lord Siva in the form of Mahesamurti pervades in the entire universe comprising of mobiles and immobiles.

Siva presides over all these by means of his own Murtis. His Atman is incomprehensible as said by the sages.

His forms or images comprise of Brahma, Visnu, Rudra, Mahesan and Sadasiva which pervade in the universe.

There are other images of Siva known as Pancabrahman, which also pervade the universe. There is nothing in the world in which he is not found present.

The well known images of Siva comprise of Isana, a Purusa, Ghosa, Vamadeva and Sadyojata.

His image of Isana is primordial one, and presides over the individual soul, the enjoyer of Prakrti.

Lord Siva having the embodied form viz. Tatpurusa, presides over the unmanifest which is worthy of being enjoyed and which is in the form of the support of gunas.

The highly adorable image of Siva is Aghora, bearing the trident, who presides over the principle of cosmic wisdom comprising of eight parts of Dharma etc.

A person well versed in the Agamas believes murti Vamadeva as the presiding deity of ego.

The learned people, believe that Sadyojata represents Siva’s splendour beyond measure and is the presiding deity of the mind.

The people of wisdom, consider Isan as the presiding deity of the ear, speech, sound and all pervasive ethers.

The persons well versed in the Puranas find Tatpurusa as the presiding deity of the skin hands, touch and Vayu.

The wise people know that Aghora is the presiding deity of the eyes, legs, colour and the fire.

The devotees should understand that Vamadeva happens to be the presiding deity of tongue, anus, taste and waters.

According to their Sadyojata is the presiding deity of nose, sex organs, smell and the earth.

The people should adore with devotion the five forms of Siva, who are the sole cause of prosperity.

The eight forms of Siva are pervading in the universe as the gems are stretched in the string.

The well known eight forms of Siva, comprise of Sarva, Bhava, Rudra, Ugra, Bhima, Pasupati, Isana and Mahadeva.

Sarva and others have imagined the eight forms of Siva as land, water, fire, wind, ether, Ksetrajna, the sun and the moon.

It has been concluded by the scriptures that Sarva in the form of earth upholds the universe comprising of the mobile and immobile beings.

The form of Siva the Siva the supreme soul which represents waters keeps the universe alive.

Pervading the inner and the outer universe, he has the form of resplendence, whereas he also has a terrific form known as Raudra.

The winds stirs the entire world, while preserving it. This is the awful form of the awful lord.

Bhima is the form of the lord which provides sky to all, representing his all pervading character. This form separate all the beings from one another.

The Pasupati form of the lord, is the lord of all the souls and remains present in all the regions. The said form of Pasupati removes the Pasuhood and the noose.

The Isana form of Siva is also known as the sun, who illuminates the universe pervading everywhere.

The murti of Mahadeva is the cause of the moon who spreads its cool rays everywhere, thereby delighting and nourishing the entire universe.

The soul happens to be the eight form of Siva and pervades with other forms as well. Therefore the entire world is the form of Siva.

The winds stirs the entire world, while preserving it. This is the awful form of the awful lord.

As all the branches of a tee grow by watering the roots, similarly with the adoration of Siva, the entire body of the universe grows.

The adoration of Siva provides protection of all types, showers grace and welfare of all beings.

As a person derives pleasure from the delight of his sons and the grandsons, similarly Siva feels delighted when all are pleased.

When anyone punishes a living being, then it amounts to punishing Astamurti. There is no doubt about it.

Astamurti Siva, presiding over the entire universe, should be worshipped with auspicious emotions since he happens to be the supreme cause.

## Chapter 4 - Excellence of Siva and Siva

Sri Krsna said, “O lord, I have listened to the way in which the entire universe is pervaded with the forms of Siva.

Now I would like to know as to how both Siva and Siva pervade the universe through form of woman and man?

Upamanyu said, “I am going to narrate in brief, the glory of Siva and Siva which cannot be explained by Siva even.

Mahadevi is the Sakti, while Mahadeva is Saktiman. Only a fraction of their grace is evidenced in the form of the universe.

Some of the elements are conscious and the other are unconscious. Both of them have pure and impure besides para and apara forms.

The unconscious cakra of cit which moves with conscious cakra it is apara and impure, while para is the pure one.

Both Cit and Acit whether Para or Apara and the lordship of Siva and Siva are natural.

The universe is subservient to Siva and Siva, but Siva and Siva are not subservient to the universe. There is a desire to rule the universe, therefore, both Siva and Siva are the sovereigns of the universe. Siva resembles Siva which Siva resembles Siva. Both of them resemble the moon and the moonlight. Therefore, there is no difference in both of them.

Without the moon-light the moon does not shine. Similarly Siva cannot shine without his Sakti.

As the sun has no importance without the sun shine, and without sun the position of the sun shine is the same.

Similarly both Sakti and Saktiman are dependent on each other. Therefore Sakti is of no consequence without Siva and Siva is of no consequence without Sakti. The Sakti is of eternal nature, by which Siva becoming all competent, bestows devotion and salvation on all living beings, is known as Adyasakti, also called Para Sakti who is dependent on Siva.

The great Atman through the diverse befitting are the attributes of the lord and the Sakti is also the same.

She happens to be the supreme Sakti, possesses the power of generation. She is the one, who because of the desire of Siva is divided in several ways.

She is known as the Mulaprakrti, Maya, Triguna, having three forms. The entire universe expands because of the influence of Siva.

The same Sakti, as one unit, as two fold, multiplies in hundreds and thousands of Saktis who ramify themselves in their functions.

At the command of Siva, the great Sakti, in union with Sivatattva manifests from it during the first creation, like the oil from the gingerly seeds.

Then the Sakti being agitated by the activity, originating from Saktiman, the primordial sound originates at the time of the creation.

The bindu emerges from nada and from bindu also emerges Sadasiva. From him is born Mahesvara, while the Suddha-vidya originates from Mahesvara.

That is the deity of speech, the Sakti of Siva, known as Vagisa, the same in the form of letters manifests as Matrika.

Then by the infusion of the infinite, Maya creates Kala, Niyati, kala and vidya and through Kala, Raga and Purusa.

Then the Trigunatmaka avyakta appeared. From Triguna emerged Vyakta and Kala emerged out of the same.

The three gunas viz. sattva, rajas and tamas, pervade the entire universe. Because of the conflict of the three gunas, the form of Trimurti emerged.

Thereafter Mahat and the other tattvas emerged. At the command of Siva, innumerable pindas were formed out of the egg. They are presided over by Cakravarti, Ananta and other Vidyesas.

According to the difference in bodies, Sakti has different forms. They are known to have the diverse forms, both gross as well as the subtle.

The Sakti of Rudra is called Brahmani, while the one of Indra is known as Indrani.

It is no use talking much. The glorified universe is pervaded by Sakti just as the body is pervaded by imminent soul.

The entire universe of mobiles and immobiles is full of Sakti. Kala the greatest Sakti of the great soul, is called Para Sakti and it moves at the command of the lord, resulting in the creation of the mobile and immobile universe.

Saktiman is lord Siva, who possesses the three Saktis of knowledge, activity and wish. He pervades and stays in the universe.

‘It is like this; it is not like this.” It is in this form that the wish of the lord restrains the activity permanently.

Sakti of knowledge is in the form of Buddhi (the intelligence). It determines its cause, instrument, effect and purpose factually.

The power of action or activity has controlled the entire universe. It bestows the desired things and performs all the jobs in a moment in the form of Sankalpa.

The Trigunatmika Sakti which emanates recording to Sakti, uplifts all the three. The same having been inspired by the supreme Sakti, creates the entire universe.

Thus with the combination of Sakti, Siva becomes Saktiman. The entire universe which emerges from Sakti and Saktiman, is known as the Saiva world.

As a child cannot be born without the parents, similarly this mobile and immobile world cannot be created without Bhava and Bhavani. Because of the emerging of the world with the union of man and woman, therefore, it is called as the one having the nature of a male and a female.

The glory of a man and a woman is enshrined in male and female. Therefore Siva is known as the supreme soul, and Sakti is known as Siva.

Siva is known also as Sadasiva, while Siva is known as Manonmani. Or otherwise Siva is known as Mahesvara and Siva is known as Maya.

Besides Purusa is known as Paramesvara while Prakrti is known as Paramesvari. Rudra is known as Mahesvara and his beloved is known Rudrani.

Visnu is the lord of the universe, while Laksmi is known as Visvesvara Priya. During the period of creation, Brahma is Siva and Brahmani is the spouse of Brahma.

Lord Bhaskara is also Siva, while Bhagavati is Siva. Mahendra is the killer of Kamadeva, while Saci is Parvati.

Agni is Mahadeva, while Svaha is Siva. Yama is Siva, while his spouse is Parvati.

Nirrti is Siva, while Nairriti is Parvati. Varuna is Rudra, while Varuni is Parvati.

Vayu is Candrasekhara while his beloved is Siva. Yaksa is Siva while his Rddhi is Siva.

Candrama (moon) is Siva while Rohini is Siva. Isana is Siva, while his spouse is Siva.

Ananta is Siva and his spouse is Parvati. Kalagni Rudra is Siva, and his spouse is Siva.

Manu named Purusa is Siva, while Satarupa is Parvati the beloved of Siva. Daksa Prajapati is Siva no doubt but his daughter is Siva.

Ruci is Siva, while Akuti has been taken to be Siva or Bhavani. Bhrgu is Siva and Khyati is Parvati.

Marici is Siva while Sambhuti is Parvati. Ahgira is Siva, while Smrti is Parvati.

Pulastya is Siva, while Priti is Siva. Pulaha is Tripurari and his beloved represents Siva.

Kratu is Siva, and Sannati is wife of Siva. Atri is Siva and Anusuya is Uma.

Kasyapa is Siva and Devamata is Siva Mahesvara. Vasistha is Siva while Arundhati is Bhavani.

All the men represent Siva, while their spouses represent Siva. Therefore all the men and women represent the grace of both of them.

Lord Siva is the subject and his beloved is the object. Everything heard is the form of Uma and the listener is the trident bearing Siva.

All that is worthy of being enquired about is sustained by Siva’s beloved, while the enquirer is the universal soul Siva himself, with the crescent moon as an ornament.

Siva the spouse of Siva, takes to all the pleasant forms, while Siva Candrasekhara is the observer for the same.

All objects of taste are enshrined in the goddess Siva, while Siva Mahadeva, enjoys the same. Whatever is loveable in the world, is found in Parvati, while Candrasekhara Nilakantha is the observer for the same.

The goddess Mahesvari holds all the objects of reflection, while all pervading lord Siva is the reflector himself.

Siva possesses all the things which are required to be known, while lord Candrasekhara is aware of the same.

Lord Siva happens to be the life of all the living beings while Siva is the form of water as prana in all the beings.

The beloved of Siva is the abode of the individual soul, while Siva represents the individual soul himself.

Siva the holder of the trident represents the day while Parvati represents the night. The sky represents Siva and the earth represents Parvati.

Lord Siva represents the ocean, the shore is the daughter of the king of mountain. Trees represent Siva, while the creepers represent Parvati.

The lord holds all masculine beings while the beloved of Siva, holds all feminine beings.

The beloved of Siva holds all the words, while the moon-crested Siva holds all their meanings.

Whatever Sakti is possessed by each one of the padarthas represents the universal goddess while the padarthas are represented by Siva.

Whatever excellent, virtuous, pure and auspicious are there, have all emerged out of the tejas of Siva and Siva.

As the light from the lamp illuminates the entire house, similarly the brilliance of both of them brightens the world.

The world is going on because of the grace of Siva and Siva according to the divine voice.

Both of them bestow welfare on all and can manifest in all the ways. Therefore, on should adore them, offer salutation to them and should be devoted to them.

O Sri Krsna, I have revealed the reality about Siva and Siva as known to me. Don’t take it to be the all.

Infact the reality about Siva and Siva is beyond the understanding of the great people even. How could one narrate it.

Those who are fully devoted to Siva, those who have dedicated themselves to Siva, their real form can be visualised by them alone and not to others.

Whatever grace of Siva has been spelt out, it is Prakrta and apara. The vibhutis of Aprakrta and Para are different, which are conceived to be secret and are known only to those who are well versed in the secrets of the lord.

The stage from which the mind and speech return, the same is Paramesvara, aparakrtika Para-vibhuti.

The superhuman power of Paramesthi is the greatest splendour, the greatest goal and the height of achievement.

The yogis having overpowered their vital breath, and the sense organs, endeavour to achieve it in order to seal the door to the prison, representing the womb.

A person realising the divine nature of Siva and Siva which serves as an auspicious medicine to bring back the dead to life on being bitten by the serpent of the worldly existence and is not afraid of anything.

A person who is aware of the para and apara aspects, reaches beyond the apara bhuti and enjoys the Para-bhuti (the greatest excellence).

O Sri Krsna, I have thus explained to you the secrets of the supreme soul and their factual position, because of your being a unique devotee of Siva.

The Vedas have ordained that the secrets of the unique vibhutis of Siva and Siva, should not be revealed to an undeserving pupil, a person deprived of the devotion of Siva, or a person who does not believe in Siva.

O Krsna of great welfare, in case you intend to reveal the secret, then do it to a competent and the devoted prison and none else.

A person who imparts the knowledge of Siva and Siva to the competent devotees, he, getting free from the universe, achieves the Sayujya devotion of Siva.

Performing the kirtana of the same, even the gravest of the sins disappear. By resorting to practice three or four times, more sins get destroyed.

His enemies and opponents get destroyed and there is an increase in the friends. There is an increase in the Saivi and lore he gets inclined towards the truth.

His devotion towards Siva, Parvati and their ganas enhances and all his desires are undoubtedly fulfilled.

Getting purified from within in case he adores Siva with devotion, performs kirtana then all the obstructing karmans of his earlier birth also get destroyed by indulging into the repeated practices. Nothing remains beyond the reach of such a person.

## Chapter 5 - Detailed discussion on Pasu and Pasupati

Upamanyu said, “This entire mobile and immobile universe is the form of Siva, the god of gods. The jivas having been bound with the noose are not aware of it.

O son of Yadus, the great sages, unaware of his only true form propagate him in different forms.

The great lord is without beginning or end, some conceive him as Apara-brahma-svarupa while others call him Parabrahma-rupa.

The one who has been conceived as Pancamahabhuta, Indriya, Antahkarana, Pradhana and Apara-brahman, the same is the supreme Brahman in the form of cit.

Because ot his being Brhat (immense) and Brhanakaraka (expands), he is called Brahman. Some of the people conceive Isa as Vidya and Avidya. Thus there are two forms of lord Brahman, the lord of Brahma.

Vidya is consciousness while Avidya is its opposite. The universe is the preceptor of the form of Vidya and Avidya.

There is no doubt that it has the same form, because the universe is subservient to him. Parabhranti is a lore and Sivarupa is beyond that.

The one who is not well aware of the worldly objects (Visayas) is known as bhranti or confusion. The correct type of knowledge is known as vidya.

The tattva without a substitute is called Para. The tattva opposite to the same is known as asat by the people well versed in the Vedas.

Because of his being the Pati of both of them he is called Sadasaspati (lord of sacrificial assembly) some say that he is in the form Ksara and Aksara, while others say he is beyond Ksara and Aksara.

The living beings are called Ksara. Both of them are the forms of the lord since they are controlled by him.

Beyond that Siva has been treated to be beyond Ksara and Aksara and Para being quite calm. He is also said to be the form of Samasthi and Vyasti besides being the cause for them.

The sages call Siva as the supreme cause. Samasti is unmanifest while Vyasthi is manifest.

They are the forms of the lord, because they function at his will. Since he is their cause, those who are aware of the meaning of the cause, say that Siva, the great cause, is the cause of both the individual and the universe.

Those who are well versed in the cause believe him to be the cause of Samasthi and vyasthi. Some of the people conceive Isvara in the form of Jati and Vyakti.

That which is used in the pindas is called Jati. The same is present in all the pindas in the form of Jati.

Both Jati and Vyakti are nourished by his command. Accordingly Mahadeva has been conceived to be of the form of Jati-vyakti.

Siva is also called as the Pradhana Purusa, Vyakta and Kalatma. He is also known as Pradhana, Prakrti, Ksetrajna and Purusa.

The people with intelligence conceive Vyakta comprising of twenty three tattvas. Kala is the sole cause of the transformation of the effected creation.

Siva is the lord, creator, activisor, routine and the cause of evolution and dissolution of all of them.

Therefore Mahesvara is said to be the Pradhana Purusa, Vyakta, Kalasvarupa Hetu, Neta, Adhipa and Dhata.

Some people hold the opinion that Virat is Brahma, the soul of Hiranya-garbhatma. He is the cause of all the lokas having the universal form, Hiranyagarbha as well as Virat.

Siva is called immanent and the great soul. Others say he is atman of prajna, taijas and visva.

Siva is called immanent and the great soul. Other’s the measure and the measured as well as the intellect.

Some people feel that he is the performer, the act of performing, its cause, the instrument and the task itself. Some one believes him to be awake, the dream, and the one who remains in sleep or slumber.

People call him Turiya the fourth one or the one beyond the fourth one, some think him to be with attributes and others without attributes.

Some call him to be the worldly being and the others call him the divine one. Some call him independent and others call him to be dependent.

Some call him terrific and others call him pleasant. Some call him with attachment and others call him without it.

Some call him inactive while others found him quite active. Some say he is with sense organs and others find him to be without sense organs.

Some think him to be immobile while others think him to be mobile. Some call him with form while others call him without it.

Some find him invisible while others find him visible. Some think him explicable while others find him to be inexplicable. Some find him in the form of words others find him without words.

Some think him possessed of thought which others think that he is devoid of words. Some conceive him possessing the knowledge others find him the form of knowledge.

Some think that he could be known, others think him to be beyond knowledge. Some think him to be comprehensible, others, think him to be incomprehensible.

Thus entering into controversies, the sages are unable to arrive at a definite conclusion, because the different types of opinion happens to be the cause of the same.

Such of the people who take refuge with him appropriately, they can know the truth about Siva who happens to be the supreme cause of all, without much efforts.

Till such time the Jiva does not visualise the other supreme soul; who makes the world subservient, till then remaining bound in the noose, it rotates like the potters wheel.

On witnessing Hiranyagarbha, the creator of the universe, as Isvara, then the learned person getting free from the good and evil activities, establishes his link with the spotless Siva.

## Chapter 6 - The principle of Siva

Upamanyu said, “There is not the slightest bondage of Maya with Siva. He is in no way connected with Prakrti, Maya, wisdom and pride.

He is also not bound by mind, or by sense organs, and not by the tanmatras and the Pancamahabhutas.

The immensely illustrious Siva is free from the bondages of Kala, Kala, Avidya, niyati, attraction and jealousy.

He is unconceived with his welfare or evil actions and their results, pleasure or pain, or the desire for its reward

He is hardly conceived with any sort of passions, the activities, or their related samskaras, nor the pleasures of the three worlds, nor is he related with their samskaras in any way.

He has no cause; he has no beginning, no end and no intervening space. He has no activity and is neither Akarya nor Karya.

He neither has an enemy nor a friend, and he is the controller of the source of inspiration. He has no Pati, a preceptor or a protector. There is none comparable to him nor is there anyone better then him.

He is beyond birth and death, he has no expectation or disinclination. He is not subject to any injunctions or prohibitions. He is neither liberation or the bondage. He does not possess any thing which is harmful. He bestow total welfare because he happens to be Siva the supreme soul.

Because of his own process Siva presides overall. He does not have ever to face his fall. Because of his bhavas, he is stationed with his intrinsic nature and as such he is called Siva.

This mobile and immobile world is presided over by Siva. Therefore Siva is known as a heaven as well. Realising this one should have no worry.

Salutation to Sarva, Rudra, Purusa, Pati, Para and the one who is great. Lord Hiranya is Isvara known as Hiranyapati.

He is lord of Ambika, Isana, holder of the Pinaka bow, and the one who uses the bull as a vehicle, and is Rudra supreme Brahman, Purusa and Krsna-pingala.

He can be meditated in the cavity of the heart as small as the tip of the hair, with golden hair, and lotus eyes. He has the pink or copper complexion.

He moves in golden colour, blue necked, in gentle and terrible forms and a combination of both, besides being imperishable, deathless and unchangeable. Such is the great lord who is the slayer of the god of death. He is free from sentiments and non-sentiments. He is greater than the enormous universe.

According to the learned people, Siva possesses enormous knowledge as well as the fortunes.

At the beginning of the kalpa, when the gods like Brahma and others are born, he is the one who instructs them.

He is the lord of all and is not conditioned by the time, he is Subject to the influence of time, he is the lord of all the preceptors.

He has the best and the natural Sakti, his knowledge is endless, therefore his body is extremely spotless.

His fortunes have no parallel besides his pleasure, strength, brilliance, virility forbearance as well as the compassion.

All the virtues were enshrined in his body at the start of the Sarga. He is not conceived with anyone. To be merciful on others, is the only reward for his deeds.

The word Pranava represents Siva, of the words like Rudra and Siva, Pranava happens to be the best of all the symbols of Siva.

Pranava is the word, reciting which one could achieve success. It is the supreme and must be obtained. There is no doubt about it.

Therefore the people well-versed in the Agamas considering identity between the word and its meaning, call the lord as Ekaksara (single-syllabled). In the Upanisads, there are four matras of it. They are A, U, M and nada.

The letter A represents Rgveda, U is for the Yajurveda, M is for the samaveda and Nada is for the Atharvaeda. The letter A is the great Bija, Rajas and the created, the four faced lord. The letter U is Prakrti, the womb, Sattva and the protector Visnu.

The letter M is Purusa, the seed, the Tamas and the destroyer is Rudra. Nada is the great Purusa - Isa, Siva, devoid of gunas and activities.

Pranava expresses everything through the three matras in three ways and is indicative of Sivatman through half a matra.

All this is filled by that Purusa, than whom there is nothing greater, than whom there is nothing smaller nor bigger and who like a tree stands steady and stiff in the heaven.

## Chapter 7 - Principle of Siva

Upamanyu said, “His Sakti known as the wonderful lore of the universe is his natural strength. It illuminates in the world, inspite of its being one, like the rays of the sun.

He has several other Saktis who emerge out of Maya and include Iccha Sakti, Jnana, Kriya and several others, in the same way as the sparks emanate from the fire flames.

The Purusa Sadasiva, Isvara and others, Vidyesvara, Avidyesvara and others besides Prakrti, which are greater than the greatest were born of this Sakti.

Everything starting from Mahat to Visesa and Brahma were also created undoubtedly by the same.

The said Sakti which is of subtle nature pervades everywhere having the form of consciousness as well as the bliss. Candrasekhara Siva is known as Saktiman because of that Sakti.

Only Siva and Siva are worth knowing. They represent lore, intelligence, Sruti, Smrti, Dhrti, Sthiti, Nistha, jnana, iccha (desire), karma (action) and sakti (force).

The supreme Brahman has two Vidyas viz. Para and Apara, because the spotless lore and spotless Kala (digit) emanate from Sakti.

The same Sakti pervades in Maya. Maya is Prakrti, Jiva is Vikrti. Whatever there is Sat or asat is pervaded by Sakti.

The same Sakti has deluded the entire mobile and immobile world with her sports and the same Sakti, gets them freed from the delusion as well.

With the Maya of twenty seven types, Siva has been pervading the universe. He alone frees the world from the delusion.

In earlier times some Brahmavadi ascetics desirous of salvation, having been overpowered with doubt, confabulated among themselves.

“What is the reason of our birth? By what means are we living alive? Where is our glory? Who controls us?

What for do we live comfortably through out the day and night? Who is the creator of the universe, which is difficult to cross?

It would not be proper to believe in kala (time), nature, niyati (destiny) and chance as the ultimate reason. Nor can it be Purusa or anyone of the living beings or a yogi greater than these.

Time etc. are insentient and cannot function as the ultimate reason. Though the soul is sentient and experiences happiness and misery, still it cannot rule. After these reflective, feelings those who meditate can realise the Sakti of the lord, the remover of the noose, but hidden by the gunas. The binding cords are cut by means of this Sakti, then Saktiman can be seen who is the causes of all the cause, with the divine eyes.

He is inconceivable and appears with the same Sakti being the cause of kala, and the entire universe with the soul.

Thereafter by his grace, the great yoga and the path of devotion they can achieve the supreme and divine goal.

Therefore those, who visualise Siva with Sakti in their hearts, they achieve the everlasting peace and none else. This has been ordained by the Vedas.

The Saktiman can never be separated from Sakti. Therefore one achieves the best of pleasures by the grace of Sakti and Saktiman.

There is no need of knowledge and the karma in attaining salvation, with the pleasure of both of them, the salvation is automatically achieved.

By his grace the gods, Danavas, animals, birds, parrots, worms, or any other beings, get redeemed.

The one who is lodged in the womb, or is taking birth, whether his a child, young, old or nearing death, whether one is lodged in the heaven or the hill.

Whether he is a fallen man or a noble one, a learned or a fool, whosoever is there, he atonce gets freed, by his pleasure.

Removing several sins of the incompetent devotees, the lord, because of his compassion, gets pleased with them undoubtedly.

One achieves devotion by his grace and with his devotion, one achieves pleasure. Taking into consideration the prevalent circumstances, a learned person does not feel deluded.

One achieves salvation by his grace besides the pleasure, which cannot be achieved by a person in a single birth.

Mahesvara gets pleased with the people who are well-versed dharmas as prescribed in the Srutis and Smrtis for many births.

At the pleasure of Siva, a person taking him to be his lord, starts adoring him slightly.

By means of several Saiva-dharmas, a person is inclined towards the tapas. With the continuous practice of the same., the excellent devotion is generated in a person.

The excellent grace of Siva is achieved with the utmost devotion of the lord. One gets relieved of all his worldly bondages by his grace, who ultimately achieves salvation.

Even the smallest amount of devotion towards Siva, if possessed by a person, gets relieved of the bondage of the birth and death in three births. There is no doubt about it.

The service rendered by the limbs of the body as well as the mind is called devotion. Because of the difference between the mind, speech as well as the body, it is of three types.

Devoting one's mind to Siva is called the mental worship. The recitation of the name of Siva is the service by speech and the service by the body includes the performing of puja and offering of salutation etc.

The three types of service with devotion is the form of Sivadharma. Lord Siva has declared it to be of five types.

Briefly the five types include the performing of tapas activities or action, recitation, meditation, perfect knowledge and the adoration of Sivalinga. Candrayana and other vratas fall under tapas.

The recitation is of three types. Meditation is pondering over Siva. What is mentioned in the Saiva-Agamas as the perfect knowledge is meant by the word knowledge here.

The Saiva Agama was narrated to Siva by Siva out of compassion for those who take refuge with him. This is the sole means of ultimate welfare.

A learned person desirous of welfare should avoid indulgence in sensual objects and increase devotion towards Siva, the great cause.

## Chapter 8 - The birth of Vyasa

Sri Krsna said, “O lord, I would like to listen to the essence of the perfect knowledge of Siva for the welfare of the devotees, which is beyond the reach of non-devotees, foolish people, and incompetent persons and which earns praise from the learned persons, which is quite deep and comprises of the five sargas

Which is sometimes akin to the Varnasrama-dharma and sometimes contrary to the same and which has been completely derived from Vedas as well as the Samkhya-yoga.

The number of the verses of the book is a hundred crores and had emerged out of the speech of Paramesvara. O lord, what is the method of worship prescribed in the same. It has been narrated by Paramesvara.

Who is entitled to perform the worship? What type of Jnanayoga is there? O Suvrata, you kindly explain the same quite elaborately.

Upamanyu said, “Siva has spoken in brief the Saivasastra as has been prescribed in the Vedas. It is free from praise or denouncement and should be believed instantaneously.

It could be achieved by the grace of the preceptor and could bestow salvation without much efforts. I speak out the same quite briefly, because its elaborate discussion is not possible.

In earlier times, when Lord Siva, with the desire of the creation of the world, equipped with the causes of the efforts, already present, manifested himself from the unmanifest, then the lord, the sage, superior to all procreated Brahma, the first among the gods Brahmanaspati.

At the time of birth Brahma witnessed the lord who was his father. The lord saw Brahma and commended him.

At the very sight of Siva, Brahma started creation with people of the separate Varanas (different class of man).

Soma was created for the sake of yajna. From Soma emerges the heaven, earth, fire, the sun, yajna and Indra the spouse of Saci.

All the gods started offering prayer to Rudra by means of reciting Rudradhyayi (hymns dedicated to lord Siva). The lord Siva appeared before the gods getting pleased.

Then Siva, in order to engage himself in sports, removed their knowledge and then asked them;” Who are you?” All of them were deluded on hearing this.

Then Siva said, “I happen to be the eternal Rudra. I had been there earlier and am present here even now.

I shall remain in future as well. There is nothing else except me. I alone sustain the entire universe with my brilliance.

There is none comparable or superior to me, the one who knows me gets redeemed.” Thus speaking lord Siva, disappeared from the please. At the disappearance of Siva, all the gods started praising Siva, uttering the hymns of the Samaveda.

Performing the Pasupati-vrata as prescribed in Atharvasirasa, all the gods applied ashes over their bodies.

Pasupati Siva, in order to please them, arrived with Parvati and his ganas to meet them. He was the one to whom the sinless yogis witness in their hearts, overpowering their breathing as well as the sleep. Such a lord was seen by the gods. They also found the goddess besides Siva, who is conceived to be the supreme Sakti, who moves at the will of Isvara.

She had beautiful eyes and she stood to the left of Siva. They also found there those who getting detached from the world, had achieved the supreme position (salvation) with Siva.

They also found the Siddhas as well as Ganesvaras. Thereafter the gods praised lord Siva and the goddess.

They eulogised Siva, with the Vedic and Pauranic stotras, besides the divine Mahesvara stotras. Lord Siva too gazed at the gods with a compassionate look.

Then he spoke with the sweet words, “I am pleased with you.” Finding that ford Siva had been pleased, the gods offered their salutation to him and asked him about an important subject.

The gods said, “O lord, what is the method of worshipping you an earth? Who is competent to do so? You kindly speak out correctly.”

Then Siva smilingly looked at Parvati and displayed his resplendent form shining like the sun.

He had all the fortunes as well as the best of the qualities. He was full of resplendence besides the Saktis, planets and was surrounded by the gods.

He had eight arms, four faces, and Ardhanarisvara form. Observing the wonderful form, all the gods like Visnu and others felt delighted.

Finding Siva resembling the sun and the goddess with the moon, and the entire mobile and immobile as Pancabhutamaya, all the gods offered arghya to the lord and bowed in reverence to him.

They said, “O lord, be pleased and accept our adoration. You have the saffron colour, the excellent disc and the colourful ornaments of gold. You have lotus like eyes, you hold a lotus you are the cause of Brahma, Indra and Narayana. The golden vase is full of excellent gems and the water of brilliant hue. Besides vermilion, Kusa grass and flowers are also offered.

Salutation to Siva the quiescent the primordial cause, to Rudra accompanied by the ganas; salutation to him in the form of the sun, to Visnu and Brahma.

The one who adores Siva in the form of a solar disc with pure mind in the morning, noon and the evening, offering excellent arghya, and reads the verses offering salutation to him, pleasing the deva, nothing remains inaccessible for him. Being a devotee, he is surely liberated.

Therefore for the sake of wealth, love and salvation one should mentally, physically or otherwise worship Siva in the form of the sun.

Then the lord lodged in the disc, looked at the gods, revealed the sacred scriptures, the just all the Agamas and vanished.

Realising that the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and the Vaisyas are entitled to the adoration of Siva, the gods bowed in reverence to the lord and returned to their respective abodes.

After a considerably long time the sacred lore was forgotten. Then the goddess seated in the lap of her husband, asked him about it.

At the prayer of the goddess Candrasekhara Siva narrated to her the sacred lore, which was a sequel to all the Agamas.

At the instance of Brahma, it was propagated in the world by me, by my preceptor Agastya and the sage Dadhici.

Siva incarnates on earth in each yuga in order to redeem his devotees and bestows the perfect knowledge to them.

Rbhu, Satya, Bhargava, Angira, Savita, Brahmanas, Mrtyu, Satakratu, great sage Vasita, Sarasvatam Tridhama, the best sage Trivrt, Narayana himself in the forma of Dharma, Svaraksa and intelligent Aruni, Krtanjaya, my son Bharadvaja and great sage Gautama, Sage Vacasravas, auspicious Suksayani, muni, Trnbindu, Krsna, Sakti, Sakteya, Uttara, Jakarnya, Hari, and sage Krsnadvaipayana, These incarnation of Vyasa are upto the end of Dvapara. There are the incarnations of Yogacaryas of Siva and their disciples. In different yugas the lord's disciples were four. Their further disciples are in hundreds and thousands. They are purified by the devotion and are liberated by their carrying out the command of Siva.

## Chapter 9 - Siva's incarnations as Yogacarya

Sri Krsna said, “You kindly speak out Siva's incarnation as yogacarya as in each one of the yugas, together with his disciples.

Upamanyu said, In the seventh Manvantra- Sveta, Sutara, Madana, Suhotra, Kanka, Laugakshi, Mahamaya, Jaigisavya, Dadhivaha, Rsabha, Muni, Ugra, Atri, Supalaka, Gautama, Vedasiras, Gokarna, Guhavasin, Sikhandi, Attahasa, Jatamali, Varuka, Langulin, Mahakala, Sulin, Mundisa, Visnu, Somasarman, Lakulisvara, these have been arranged in the order of yugas. There had been twenty eight preceptors of Yoga.

Each one of the above had four disciples each right from Sveta to Rusya, the names of whom are being described by me in a sequence.

There are Sveta, Svetasikha, Svetasva, Svetalohita, Dundubi, Satarupa, Rcika, Vikosa, Vikesa, Vipasa, Pasanasana, Sumukha, Durmukha, Durgama, Duratikrama, Sanatkumara, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Sudhama, Viraja, Samkha, Andaja, Sarasvata, Megha, Meghavahaka, Kapila, Asuri, Pancasikha, Baskala, Parasara, Garga, Bhargava, Angiras, Balabandhu, Niramitra, Ketusrnga Tapodhana, Lambodara, Lamba, Lambatman, Lambokesaka, Sarvajna, Samabudhi, Sadhya-Siddha, Sudhamau, Kasyapa, Vasistha, Virajas, Atri, Ugra, Gurusrestha, Sravana, Sravisthaka, Kuni, Kunibahu, Kusarira, Kunetra, Kasyapa, Usana, Cyavana, Brhaspati, Utathya, Vamadeva, Mahakala, Mahanila, Vacahsravas, Suvira, Syavaka, Yatisvara, Kausalya, Lokaksi, Kuthumi, Sumantu, Jaimini, Kubandha, Kusakandhara, Plaksa, Darbhayani, Ketuman, Gautama, Bhallavi, Madhupinga, Svetaketu, Usija, Brhadasva, Devala, Kavi, Salihotra, Suvesa, Yuvanasva, Saradvasu, Chagala, Kundakarna, Kumbha, Prabhahuka, Uluka, Vidyuta, Sambu, Asvalayana, Aksapada, Kanada, Uluka, Vatsa, Kulika, Garga, Mitraka and Rusya.

These yogacaryas are the disciples of Mahesvara and are a hundred and twelve in number.

All of them belong to the Pasupata vrata and apply ashes over their bodies. They are well aware of the tattvas of all the Sastras and have mastery in the Vedas and the post-Vedic literature.

They are fully devoted to the Sivadharma, have the detailed knowledge of Siva, they are detached from the world and always remain devoted to Siva.

They patiently bear all the pains, are quite calm, devoted to the welfare of all the living beings, simple, sweet, healthy, devoid of anger, having controlled all the senses.

They wear the Rudraksa rosary as an ornament, apply Tripundra over the forehead and keep matted locks of hair besides the tuft. Sometimes their heads are shaven.

The live on fruits and roots, engage themselves in pranayama, they are proud for the adoration of Siva and always meditate upon Siva.

They are the destroyers of the sprouting poisonous tree and are always ready to proceed to the abode of Siva.

The one who believing Sveta and other disciples to be his acarya and performs the worship of Siva, he undoubtedly achieves Sivasayujya.

## Chapter 10 - Devotion to Siva

Sri Krsna said, “O lord, O lord of the yogis, Ganesvara, Munisvara, as intelligent as Kartikeya, ocean of the entire knowledge the, preceptor, You have incarnated on earth in order to shatter the bondages of the people here. O Paramesvara, you have taken to the form of Maharsi (great Rsi).

Otherwise why does not anyone else in the world among the gods and the demons is as well aware of the Siva-tattva.

Therefore you are comparable with Siva and with the consuming of the nectar like words from your month, relating to Siva, my mind does not feel satisfied.

What type of question had been asked by Paramesvari setting in the lap of her husband?

Upamanyu said, “O Sri Krsna, you have put me an appropriate question, to which I am going to give an appropriate reply, because you are devoted to Siva and wish welfare of all.

Siva was engaged in meditation over the charming Mandara, the best mountain with the goddess Parvati.

At the sametime the dear maid of Parvati brought the charming blossoming flowers wearing a smile over her face.

Then Mahadeva, placed Mahadeva, in his lap in a secluded place and decorated her with those flowers, feeling delighted.

Thereafter all the damsels adorned with ornaments, from the inner apartment besides the ganas started serving the goddess who was the mother of the universe.

Holding the flywhisk in their hands, they also started serving Siva the lord of the universe, moving the flywhisks.

There the discussion started there between Siva and Siva for the welfare of their devotees as well as the universe.

Then availing an opportunity, Parvati the mother of the universe, asked her husband Siva, a question.

The goddess said, “You are well versed in the atma-tattva then how could you be subservient to the people with little wisdom?

Isvara said, “I can never be subservient to others neither with any karma, tapas, japam, asana, jnana or any other means.

In case the people have faith in their minds for me, then only I could be subservient to them or be fit for touch audience, adoration or suitable for conversation as well (otherwise not).

The one who wants to subjugate me must have a failing faith in me, became faith is the cause of protection for dharma for all the varanas.

A person who faithfully follows the principles of his own Varnasrama dharma, only he can develop faith in me and no one else can do so.

The dharma to be followed by all the people of the respective varanas was spoken by Brahma at my command.

In the Dharma so prescribed by Brahma, one has to spend enough of riches in following of the same and one also does not achieve enough of he reward. Besides they have to face a lot of inconvenience. Getting inaccessible inspiration from the same dharma when a person of a particular Varnasrama achieves me with a devoted heart, he following the path of comfort, achieves dharma, artha, kama and moksa.

I have re-imagined the varnasrama dharma. Accordingly, those who get devoted to me, and only my devotees are entitled to the same. This is my firm command. Such of the followers of Varnasrama happen to be my devotees.

By my grace, they are freed from blemish, Maya and the bondages and achieve the loka devoid of the rebirth and achieve the excellent Saddharma.

Therefore, one should, after embracing the varnasrama as propounded by me, or even without it, depending upon my devotees, should redeem himself.

Following the unknown dharma amounts to an acquisition of what is not acquired superior in qualities crores and crores of times. Therefore one should follow the dharma prescribed by me.

O noble lady, these are my instruction as yogacarya in all the Manvantaras and thousands of generations.

O goddess, the knowledge of generations is inaccessible to those, who are not my devotees, are devoid of wisdom and do not practice yoga. Therefore one should faithfully follow these.

It is a great loss, a great blemish, a delusion, blindness and muteness, in case one is diverted from the path of salvation and follows other path.

O goddess, my eternal dharma is four-fold viz. jnana, kriya, carya and yoga.

The knowledge of Pasu, Pasa and Pati is the real one. Remaining subservient to the preceptor, the purification through six paths is called Kriya.

My adoration by means of the practical application of the holy rites, duties of different castes and stages in life as prescribed by me is called carya.

By following the path prescribed by me, discarding all other engagements, is called yoga.

O goddess, the purification of the heart is better than many Asvamedha sacrifices and bestows salvation. This is inaccessible to a person involved in the worldly pleasures.

Such of the persons who have overpowered the sense organs by means of yama and niyamas, the association of such a person, destroys the sins of the earlier births.

One achieves perfect knowledge with Vairagya (detachment). With the achieving of the perfect knowledge, one feels inclined towards yoga.

Those who are well-versed in yoga are undoubtedly redeemed even when they fall from the path. A person should always follow compassion, non-violence and the perfect knowledge.

To speak the truth, not to steal, wisdom with faith, control of sense organs, studies, teaching, performance of sacrifice, conducting of sacrifice, meditation, Isvara-bhava, attaining of the perfect knowledge, a Brahmana, who aspires for the success of the jnana-yoga,

He achieving the jnana expeditiously, gets acquainted with yoga. O beloved, he yogi, reduces to ashes the body with the fire of jnana

And with my grace getting familiar with Karma-yoga gets free from the bondage. The merits and the demerits also cause obstruction in the path of salvation. Therefore, a yogi should, at my command, keep himself aloof from the merits and demerits.

A person who performs the rites with the intention of reaping a reward, he is caught in the bondage, therefore one should not discard the karmans but the reward of the karmans.

O beloved, initially one should adore me from outside by means of Karmayajna. Then he should engage himself in yoga under the influence of jnana-yoga.

The yogis is well aware of my innate nature by karma-yajna and the one who views a clod of earth, a pebble and gold ingot all alike does not have adore me further.

The yogi engaged in the path of knowledge, an excellent sage permanently engaged in yoga, my devotee enriched with the purity of mind, shall all attain my Sayujya.

Those who are not sufficiently detached, in their minds, but are devoted to me, are authorised only in jnana, carya and kriya as per their desires.

My worship is of two types viz. internal and external. My adoration is of three fold which is done with speech, mind and body.

The adoration has been further stated to be of five fold viz. penance, holy rites, japam, meditation and knowledge.

My external worship is performed in full view of other persons. The same thing known and knowable to oneself alone, is internal worship.

The mind which is devoted to me is the true mind or not any mind as it is. The speech that pertains to my name is true speech and nothing else.

The body which is plastered with the Tripundra mark over it at my command is the true body and nothing else.

My adoration is the external karmas. No yajna or karma is authentic which is not done at my command. To dry the body for my sake is tapas alone. This is my opinion.

The japam comprises of only the recitation of the omkara-mantra or Pancaksara mantra. The practices in Rudradhaya conform to the study of the Vedas and nothing else.

Meditation conform to the concentration of the mind to my form. The meditation performed for the sake of soul is no Samadhi at all. The true knowledge conforms to the knowledge of the Saiva literature and nothing else.

O goddess, according to the Samskaras of the earlier birth one should adore the internal as well as the external elements according to his devotion or liking.

The internal adoration is a hundred times better (than the external one) because the external blemishes are invisible in the same.

The purification of the heart denotes the real purification and not the exterior one, because a man is impure without he internal purification.

Whatever adoration, be it internal or external, is done with pure intentions is excellent one.

I am quite auspicious and successful. What have I to do with the activities of the people. I am only consumed with the inner and outer intentions.

O goddess, the activities performed with good intentions, conform to the real action and there is no desire for the reward by action, thought or behaviour.

O goddess to take refuge with me with selfish motive would be of no use because the one desirous of the reward, disowns me.

O beautiful one, a person desirous of reward, whose mind has been devoted to me, he is rewarded by me according to my own will.

Those whose mind remains devoted to me without expecting any reward, and who ask for the reward subsequently, such devotees are also dear to me.

Because of the Samskaras of the earlier birth, one who remaining unmindful of the reward, takes refuge with me, he is extremely dear to me.

O Paramesvari, those who do not bother about any other gain than to achieve me, for me also there is no better gain than to protect them.

They feel devoted to me because of my grace alone. I also bestow the best reward on them forcibly.

Such of the noble souls who are immensely devoted to me, and who have concentrated their minds in me, such religious minded people are said to possess eight types of symptoms.

These include, to love my devotees, to remain engaged in adoration, to worship themselves or encourage my worship or perform all the activities of the body for my sake or are interested in listening to my stories, flutter in tones, eyes and limbs, remember me always or surrender to me completely.

In case these eight qualities are found even in an outcaste, he is comparable to a learned Brahmani, a sage, a glorious ascetic, or a learned scholar. A person well-versed in the four Vedas, is not dearer to me than a Candala devoted to me. Things can be given and taken from him. He would be adorable like me.

The one who offers me even a leaf, with devotion a flower, a fruit or the mere water, I am not lost to him, nor is he lost to me.

## Chapter 11 - Knowledge about Siva

Isvara said, “O goddess of the universe, now I shall speak out the duties stipulated for the learned Brahmanas.

One should take bath thrice a day, perform homa, adore Sivalinga, give away charities, remain devoted to Isvara, and be compassionate to all.
