One should observe truthfulness, patience, believe in the lord, extend non-violence to all the living beings, should possess sharpness in faith, engage himself in Vedic studies, besides practicing the yoga.

There should be discourse on religious scriptures, observe celibacy, listening of scriptures, performing of tapas, practice forgiveness, auspiciousness, wear tuft and sacred thread, turban and the scarf.

O goddess, the prohibited stuff should not be consumed, should wear ashes and Rudraksa and should offer special worship on the festival days as well as Caturdasi.

O dear, the rite of consuming Brahmakurca every month according to injunctions should be resorted to the same Pancagavya which should also be offered to Siva for a bath.

One should discard all the activities, besides the cereals, besides the food for Sraddhas offered for the propitiation of the manes, and of rice in all sacred rites, stale food should be discarded.

One should observe truthfulness, patience, believe in the lord, extend non-violence to all the living beings, should possess sharpness in

It is the duty of the Brahmans to disown, wine, smell of wine, and the naivedya which has been offered to me. For people of the other varanas, this is the ordinary duty.

The ten traits like forgiveness, peace, patience, truthfulness, not to steel, celibacy, gaining knowledge about me, application of the ashes over the body, to live in seclusion should be particularly followed. These are the symptoms of the yogis. He should beg for alms during the day time alone.

These rules are also to be followed by the Vanaprastha. The Brahmacaris should not consume the food during the night.

The Ksatriyas are not allowed to teaching (of the scriptures) presiding over the sacrifices, and the acceptance of monetary gifts which are not allowed by me to the Ksatriyas and the Vaisya.

The duties and responsibilities of the kings are detailed here under: these include, protection of all the varanas, killing of the enemy in war, to punish the wicked people, birds and animals.

He should not believe in anyone, except those who are devoted to me. He should unite with the women in appropriate time and should protect his own army.

He should known the secrets of others through his spies. He should wear the costumes, weapons, jacket, besides apply bhasma over the body.

These are the duties of the kings who believe in me. The Vaisyas should engage themselves in farming, irrigation, protection of the cows.

To serve the three varanas, setting up of gardens and to develop my ksetra are the duties of Sudras.

A householder should unite with his wife alone. Celibacy has to be observed by Brahmacaris as well as the Vanaprasthas.

There is no other duty better for a woman than to serve her husband. She could adore me only with the permission of her husband.

A woman, who performs Vrata neglecting her husband, she undoubtedly falls in the hell. Now I shall spell out the duties of a widow. She should engage herself in Vratas, charities, tapas, sleep on floor, take food at night, keep up celibacy, bathe with water or the ashes. She should remain peaceful, maintain silence, forgiveness and should appropriately distribute her assigned tasks.

She should particularly adore me keeping fast on the eighth, fourteenth, full moon day and eleventh days of the moon.

O goddess, I have spelt out the in brief the duties of the people of different asramas belonging to the class of Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, ascetics and the Brahmacaris.

O beautiful one, thus I have spelt out the duties of Vanaprasthis, householders, women and the Sudras.

O supreme goddess, you should meditate upon me reciting the six syllable mantra (om namah Sivaya). This is the gist of all the Vedic dharma.

Such of the people who perform vratas of their own on earth, because of their earlier Samskara, or those who remain attracted to the women or other worldly pleasures, or remain detached from the same, they never get involved in the Siva like the lotus leaf.

The people with spotless intelligence, achieve self-realisation by my grace, because it is difficult to protect the asrama-dharma.

For them there are no duties to be performed, nor evils to be availed. They have no trance to be practiced and no great goal to be achieved. They are not subject to do’s and don’t’s like me.

As I am complete in all respects and have nothing to establish, since I am perfect, similarly, they have nothing more to seek since they are quite contented. There is no doubt about it.

They are indeed Rudras who have descended from Rudraloka for the welfare of my devotees. Undoubtedly they are Rudra Purusas.

The gods and the humans get engaged at their respective assignments, at my command.

Taking my command to be the base, because of the increase of my goodwill, with a mere look at me, all this sins are washed out, and the faith yielding excellent rewards, start. Those who are devoted to me visualise before hand the auspicious fruit.

They shudder, their tears fall, the throat is choked, and they feel blissful again and again.

The excellent men could be understood, by these never failing symptoms, severely or collectively, or by means of the auspicious feelings of the lord, excellent and middling types.

As the iron placed in the fire flames, does not remain iron alone, similarly my devotees do not remain humans alone.

A learned person finding Rudra in human form, with ordinary hands and feet, should not take them to be ordinary humans and should not insult them.

In case the foolish people insult them, they are deprived of their age, conduct, wealth besides the race and they fall into the hell.

The positions of Brahma, Visnu and other sages in comparison to me, turn weightless like the cotton.

The property of Buddhi, Prakrti and Purusa, is impure. Therefore, it can be achieved by those region beyond the gunas. What is the use of this talk? By fixing one’s mind in me, by whatever means it could be, is the only way to achieve welfare.”

Upamanyu said, “Thus the brief of the essential knowledge was expounded by Siva the great soul, for the welfare of the world.

The collection of this perfect knowledge is contained in the Vedas, Sastras, Puranas, Itihasa and all other lores. Jnana, Jneya, Anustheya, Adhikara, Sadhana and Sadhya are the six topics discussed in the ancient literature.

The people should know the Siva-jnana which can be achieved from the preceptor. The adoration of Sivalinga should be performed by the devotees.

The reciting of Siva-mantra is the means and equation with Siva is the Sadhya. By attaining the knowledge of epitome of six topics one becomes omniscience.

The practices of the outer yajnas should be performed with the available means. Thereafter Siva should be adored internally.

In case for the achieving of the excess of virtues in the inner and not in the external worship the noble soul need not perform the external worship.

O Krsna, such of the devotees who have achieved enough of nectar of knowledge, they should not perform any internal or external actions.

Therefore, gradually discarding the internal and the external activities, knowing the jneya with jnana, the jnana should also be discarded.

In case the mind has been concentrated in Siva, then there is no need of performing the karmas. In case the mind has not been devoted to Siva, even then the performing of the karmas is of no use.

There while performing the internal or the external karmas or even without them, one should concentrate his mind in Siva.

The person whose mind has been stabilised in Siva, he remains extremely peaceful in this as well as in the future world.

The mantra Om namah Sivaya bestows the best of the Siddhis. Therefore one should adore Siva for the achieving of the success in great magnificence.

## Chapter 12 - Glory of the five syllable mantra of Siva

Sri Krsna said, “O great sage, Omniscient one, O ocean of knowledge, I would like to listen to the glory of the five syllable mantra.”

Upamanyu said, “The details of the glory of the five syllable mantra of Siva count be narrated even in crores of years. Therefore you please listen to the brief of the same.

According the Siva literature as well as the Vedas, this six syllable mantra of Siva fulfills all the desires of the devotees of Siva.

It has small number of syllable, is the essence of the Vedas beside the bestower of the salvation, successful in command, doubtless, and is the form of Siva.

Many siddhis are enshrined in it, which is quite divine, pleases the minds of the people, has the definite meaning, besides being the form of the speech of the lord.

This mantra is the most appropriate one, which could be conveniently recited for the achieving of all the desires. Om namah Sivaya bestows omniscience on all the living beings. This six syllable mantra is the root cause of all the lores. This is subtle like the seed of a banyan tree but has the vast interpretation.

The omniscient lord is the creator of everything, the all pervasive Siva, who is beyond the three attributes and is stationed in the single syllable mantra om.

The five subtle Brahmanas are enshrined in the mantra namah Sivaya occupying a syllable each. Therefore in this six syllabled subtle mantra, Siva is lodged in the form of five Brahman in the form of expressed and expressive. Innately Siva is expressed while the mantra is expressive due to its vastness.

The state of being the expressive and the expressed, is without beginning, because the terrible ocean of the worldly existence functions without a beginning.

Siva, who relieves one of the worldly bondage has no beginning. As the medicine is opposed to the patient by nature

Similarly Siva has been conceived to be the enemy of all the ills of the world. In case Siva had not been there, in the universe, the world would have been filled with darkness and misery, beans

Prakrti is unconscious, while Purusa is unknown. Pradhana as well as the atoms too are ignorant, unconscious.

The people of wisdom do not visualise action without the cause. The instruction about dharma and adharma, thought of bondage and the freedom, cannot be there at the beginning of the creation without an omniscient, as a patient cannot remain comfortable without the physician.

Therefore Sadasiva is eternal, omniscient and complete in all respects, he is the one who saves the human from the ocean of the universe.

The lord is free from the beginning middle or the end, spotless by nature, omniscient and complete in all respects. This has been stated in the literature on Siva.

This mantra expresses him and he is the one expressed by the great mantra.

Siva-jnana is as vast as the expressing Siva in the six syllabled mantra, om namah Sivaya.

This is the positive statement by Siva and not aphorism. This is because Siva has the unblemished and spotless nature, he is complete in all respects and omniscient.

He is the one who is graceful over the universe. How could he resort to falsehood. As things stand by nature, along with their virtues and vices and the fruits they are capable of producing how could the omniscient them resort to falsehood.

When the lord is free from the two faults, then how could he make a wrong statement? Therefore the expression made by Siva, who is omniscient one being unblemished is therefore without any short coming and is authentic.

Therefore the learned people should have complete faith in the words of Isvara. With regard to the merits and the demerits as they are, a person devoid of faith, falls.

The peaceful words spoken by sage for the achieving the heaven and moksa, they should be taken to be true and spoken for the welfare.

The words spoken filled with attachment, jealousy, falsehood, anger, passion and desire lead to the hell. Therefore they are known as the evil words.

The statement of ignorance and lust is the cause of the worldly pain and would be of no avail even when it is soft, charming and polished.

The words on hearing which, one might achieve welfare destroying the passions as well as the mental blemishes and spoken unmindfully are considered to be the best.

In spite of the presence of several other mantras the mantra spoken by omniscient Siva, none is comparable with the same.

The entire Vedic literature together with its angas is enshrined in the six syllable mantra. There is no other excellent mantra comparable with the same.

The six syllable mantra is separate from the seven crore Mahamantras and innumerable upa-mantras, in the same way as Vrtti is separate from Sutra.

All the Siva-jnana, the repositories of lore, are all the commentaries of succinct aphorism, the six-syllabled mantra.

A person in whose heart the mantra Om namah Sivaya is lodged, the several other mantras and the Sastras literature are of no consequence for him.

The one who is committed to the muttering of the mantra Om namah Sivaya, regularly practicing the same, he is supposed to have studied everything, listened everything and done everything.

Therefore whosoever utters the mantras Om namah Sivaya with his tongue, his entire life meets with success.

Even if a Sudra, a degraded one, foolish or a learned person, gets engaged in the recitation of this mantra, he is freed from the cage of the Siva.

This was told by Siva to the goddess, when she asked about the same for the welfare of the humans and the Brahmans.

## Chapter 13 - The glory of five syllabled mantra

The goddess said, “On the arrival of defiled period of Kali, the sinful people would be covered with darkness of their evil deeds.

The conduct of the Varanasramas would fade out and several types of misfortunes would appear in the world, all the rights on earth would become doubtful and the people shall be defiled.

Inspite of the instructions of the preceptors, the pupil would become carefree, O Mahesvara, then how could your devotee think of redemption?”

Isvara said, “The people bora in the Kali age, when engaged in my devotion, shall get redeemed taking refuge with the Pancaksari lore.

Even when my devotes are involved in the sins which could not be expressed by the mind, speech or the body or which could not be remembered, and inspite of my devotee being blemished, denounced, ungrateful and cheat, besides being greedy and evil minded, he shall be redeemed with the reciting the fire syllabled lore, which relieves one of the dangers from the world.

O goddess, I have declared firmly several times on earth that irrespective of the degraded nature of my devotee he is relieved of the worldly bondages with my devotion.”

The goddess said, “A person who is fallen because of his following the evil ways and activities and the deeds performed by such a person is the cause of falling in the hell. Then how could he be freed with this lore?”

Isvara said, “O beautiful one, you have spoken the truth. Still you please listen. I had concealed it to be a secret.

In case my devotee getting confused adores me with some other mantra and does not recite the Pancaksara mantra then he surely falls in the hell.

Those who have made their bodies quite leane and thing consuming water and unhaling air, they never reach my loka by performing these vratas.

Such of the people who with the utmost devotion adore me even once, they with the influence of the mantra reach my abode.

Therefore all other tapas, yajnas, vratas and the disciplines, cannot be compared even the croreth part of the worship with the five syllabled mantra.

A person who has been freed from the noose, or has been bound in the same, when adores me with five syllabled mantra, he undoubtedly gets redeemed.

A person who is deprived of the worship of Rudra or is devoted to Rudra, irrespective of his being a fool, or a fallen man if he adores me with Pancaksara mantra, then he surely gets redeemed.

O goddess, whosoever adores me with the five or six syllabled mantra, with devotion, he gets redeemed.

A devotee of mine overpowering the anger, inspite of his being a fallen person or an auspicious one, irrespective of his having received the mantra from the preceptor or not.

A person who has received the mantra from the preceptor is crores of times better then the one who has not done so. Therefore, O goddess, one should adore me with this mantra after receiving it from the preceptor and equipped with my devotion and other virtues, adores me he becomes like me.

What is the use of talking as much. All my devotees are quite competent, because my five syllabled mantra is the best of all.

With the influence of the five syllabled mantra the lokas, the Vedas, the Rsis, dharma, the god and the universe are established.

At the time of dissolution, when all the mobiles and immobiles are destroyed, all reaching the stage of Prakrti are absorbed in the same mantra.

O goddess, I live alone, at that point of time and no one else is found there. At that point of time, all the Vedas and other literature get absorbed in the five syllabled mantra.

Those syllable do not get destroyed because of my support to them. Thereafter the creation is evolved out of the same variously through Prakrti and the Atman.

Then comes the subsidiary dissolution of forms and attributes. Then lord Narayana assumes the physical body of Maya and lies on the serpent bed in the midst of the water. The five faced lord Brahma, born of the umbilical lotus gets desirous of creating the worlds. Therefore at the outset he creates the ten sages of unmeasured splendour as his mental sons, because there is no one else at that time to assist him

For their expansion and success the grand sire asked me, “O Mahadeva, O Mahesvara, bestow strength to my sons.”

Thus requested by Brahma, I having five faces, instructed lotus-born Brahma in five syllabled mantra.

The five syllables which had emerged out of the five faces, were received by Brahma and he then realised my worth and as a great lord.

The Prajapati, receiving that mantra from me gave it away to his sons, getting aware of its usages.

The sons of Brahma, after receiving the gem of the mantra from their father, at his command became desirous to adore me.

For that purpose, they went to the charming Sumeru mountain, having the pleasant peak of Mujavana, which is protected by my devotees.

The sons of Brahma, getting desirous of creation performed tapas there for a thousand divine years.

Getting pleased with their devotion, I appeared before then immediately and explained to them all the details, viz. the sage, the metre, Kilaka, Bijasakti, deity, nyasa, the six ancillaries, the limits of quarters and their application. The aim was to multiply the creation through the sages.

Thereafter as a result of the usefulness of the mantra, the sages reinforced by the tapas, started creation of the gods, asuras and the human beings in an excellent way.

Now I shall narrate the form of the lore. The mantra should be started with namah followed by Sivaya.

This five syllabled lore is the best of all the Vedas and happens to be the eternal seed of all the words.

The mantra - Sakti emerging out of my mouth is the goddess. She has the complexion of the molten gold, plump, lifted up breasts, four arms, three eyes and crescent moon serves as the crest jewel, her he holds the lotus in her hand and displays varada and abhaya mudras in her hoods.

She possesses all the characteristics and is adorned with all the ornaments. She is seated over the white lotus seat. She has curly hair.

Like the rays of the sun, she has five types of complexion i.e. yellow, black, dusty, golden and red.

They should be worshipped separately with bindu and nada. Like the crescent moon, the bindu-nada is like the flame of the lamp.

O beautiful one, among the seeds, the seed of this mantra is remarked as the second. The seed of the fourth begins with a long vowel. The fifth one is mentioned as a Sakti.

O beautiful, Vamadeva is the Rsi, Parkrti is the meter while Siva is the god or the deity of this mantra.

O beautiful one, in these five syllables, there are the five Rsis like Gautama, Atri, Visvamitra, Angira and Bhardvaja.

Each one of the syllable has the metres like Gayatri, Anustup, Tristup, Brhati and Virat respectively, while Indra, Rudra, Hari, Brahma and Skanda are the deities of the respective letters.

O beautiful one, in their places my faces beginning with one in the east and ending with the one above, are taken. They are identified with the letters na etc. in the same order.

The first second and fourth letters are Udatta, while the fifth one is Svarita and the third is Anudatta.

The mantra is otherwise called Mulavidya, Sivam, Saivasutra and five syllabled. This Saiva mantra is my great heart.

The letter na is the head, Ma is the tuft, Si is the armour, Va is the eye, ya is the missile. At the end of each letter shall be uttered namah, Svaha, Vasat, hum, Vausat and Phat.

There too, the same is the Mula mantra with a diference. The fifth varna is suffixed with the twelfth vowel (h).

The devotee shall worship me with japam homa, etc. mentally, verbally, and physically through this mantra.

Let it be in accordance with their, own intellect, injunction in sereptines, time, inclination, capacity, wealth and the taste.

O goddess, my adoration will lead to salvation, whenever, wherever or whomsoever, it may be done if it is with devotion.

O noble lady, whatever is done for me by a person whose mind is attached to me, whether in the proper order or in the reverse order, is quite dear and auspicious for me.

I have made certain rites to be followed by my devotes who are not unduly helpless in regard to all the sacred scriptures.

There at the outset, I shall explain the procedure of putting the mantra in use without which the japam would be of no consequence and with which the recitation is quite useful.

## Chapter 14 - The method of performing the five syllabled mantra

Isvara said, “O beautiful one, without the command Kriya faith and daksina the japam becomes infructous.

With the command, Kriya faith and daksina the recitation of the matnra besetow great merit.

Going to the Brahmana-acarya or the preceptor, well versed in the tattvas possessing all the qualities and who remains engaged immediate,

One should with the best of his intentions, please him mentally, by speech, karmas as well as the riches.

A Brahmana should be adored the preceptor with great efforts. The preceptor should be offered elephant, horse, chariot, gems and land, besides house, ornaments, riches, cereals, according to one's means.

In case one desires success in his efforts, then he should not be miserly at all. Then he should bow in reverence with his family at the feet of the preceptor.

Then he should adore as per his means to the preceptor without resorting to cheating. Then should receive the perfect knowledge as well as the mantra from the preceptor.

When the preceptor is so pleased and satisfied, he shall allow his disciple to stay with him for a year serving him with humility. Then on some auspicious day, the preceptor shall make him take his bath after observing a fast.

Then he should be clad in excellent clothes, and wear fragrant garland and ornaments, adore the Brahmana should perform the punyahavacana.

Thereafter my auspicious knowledge should be imparted to him over the seashore, bank of the river, cowshed, a temple or an auspicious place in the house, in the auspicious time or a day which might bestow success, in a favourable constellation, in an unblemished yoga quite gracefully in an appropriate manner.

Getting delightful in a secluded place, he should recite my mantra and make his disciple also to do so.

Then he should utter, “Welfare to you, you face auspicious time.” Thus speaking he should impart the guru-mantra to his disciple.

Thus receiving the mantra from the preceptor, performing the oblation, the disciple should perform the japam with purascarana (Repetition of the name of deity alongwith burnt offerings).

The disciple should recite the mantra quite carefully throughout his life. With a devoted mind, he should mutter the mantra a thousand or hundred and eight times a day, after which he achieves salvation.

Respectfully multiplying four times all the syllables, each and every letter should be muttered a lakh of times. Restricting his movements he should take food during the night. He is known as the performer of purascarana.

The one who performs the japam with purascarana daily, no one could be comparable with him in the world. Such a person is known as Siddha who bestows success to others.

Taking his bath, sitting over a spotless place, he should seat himself and then adore me (Siva), you (Parvati) and the preceptor.

He should seat himself facing east or the north, silently concentrating his mind, purify the Panca-tattvas with danana-plavana etc. ritual.

Purifying the body with mantra-nyasa, he should hold the prana and apana breath and meditate upon both of us (Siva and Parvati).

Then reminding himself of the lore, place, his own form, Rsi, metre, deity, bija, Sakti and the speech, he should recite the Pancaksara mantra.

The mental recitation is indeed the best of all in which the lips move. The upamsu japa (in a lion voice) is the middle one, while the verbal japam is of the lowest quality.

The japam with Rudra the presiding deity is the extremely excellent one. The one with Visnu as the presiding deity, is the middle one and the one with Brahma as the presiding deity is of the lowest ranking one.

The muttering of the passage with the high or low, clear or unclear words, is called the vacika japam.

Speaking slowly with the moving of the tongue, which cannot be heard be others, is called upamsu.

The recitation which is done mentally, letter after letter or the meaning of each word, is called the mental japam or the manasa japam.

With the performing of the vacika japam, one derives only one reward, with upamsu one derives hundred times reward, and the japam which is performed mentally bestows a thousand times reward. When the said japam is preceded and ended with pranayama, the reward multiplies to a hundred times or even more.

The japam associated with pranayama is called Sagarbha-japam. Even in agarbha japam, pranayama should be performed at the beginning as well as at the end.

One who knows the meaning of the mantra after performing pranayama should recite the mantra forty times or according to his capacity. In case, he is unable to do so, he should perform pranayama, once, thrice or five times of the agarbha or the sagarbha recitation, the latter is better one.

The *dhyana japam* is thousand times better than *sagarbha japam.* One should perform anyone of the five *japams* according to his capacity.

There are various ways of counting the number of times, a mantra has been repeated. Counting with finger is one mode. Eight times that number can be calculated by lines, ten times by dolls, hundred times by shells, or gems, thousand times by corals, ten thousand times by crystal pieces, a hundred thousand times by pearls, million times by lotus seeds, a crore of times by gold pieces, indefinite times by the bundle of the Kusa-grass or Rudraksa beads.

A rosary of thirty beads of Rudraksa for japam, bestows wealth, the one connecting twenty seven beads, yields nourishment, containing twenty five beads, bestows salvation, containing fifteen beads, bestows fruits of black magic.

In case a thumb is used in counting the number, it bestows salvation. The Index finger destroys enemies. The middle finger bestows wealth, the ring finger brings peace and calmness.

Among all these, the rosary with a hundred and eight Rudraksa beads is the best. A rosary with a hundred Rudraksa beads is excellent, while the one with fifty beads is the middle one.

A rosary with fifty four Rudraksa beads is best for heart. Thus one should perform japam with the rosary without showing it to anyone.

The little finger removes the miseries and therefore is the best for japam. The bead should be pushed with other fingers the mantra should be uttered.

The japam performed (by the rosary) without the touch of the thumb, becomes infructous. The japam performed in the house is an ordinary one, it merit is multiplied a hundred times when performed in a cow-shed.

It multiplies to a thousand times when performed in an inauspicious forest or an orchard. In case the japam is performed over a mountain of auspicious nature, its merit enhances to ten thousand times but in case it is performed over the bank of the river, it multiplies to a lakh of times.

In a temple the merit multiplies to a crore of times and when the same is performed in Siva temple it multiplies to unlimited times. The japam should be performed, before the sun, fire, the preceptor, the moon, the lamp and the water.

The japam should be performed before the Brahmanas and the cows. The japam performed facing the east bestows power of overpowering others, while the one performed facing the south bestows the black magic.

Performing of the japam facing west, yields riches, while the one performed facing north yields peace and calmness. The japam should be performed before the sun, fire, Brahmana, gods, preceptors, and other adorable persons, while performing the japam one should be quite humble and not wear a turban, shirt and the scarf around the neck. The hair should not be dishevelled.

The one who himself is unclean, whose hands are dirty, who might be lamenting or might be overpowered with anger or arrogance, besides sneezing spitting yawning, such a person should not perform the japam.

While performing the japam one should not look at a dog or a degraded person. But in case he has to do so, then he should devote his mind to Siva and Parvati and perform sipping of water.

Or he should look at the sun, the moon or the stars, or perform pranayama. One should not perform japam, without the seat, lying down, while walking, or standing, or in the street or an inauspicious place, in darkness, spreading the feet or seated in a cock like posture, or in a moving vehicle, sitting over a bed, or when overpowered with worries, or when incapable of doing so. He should not perform japam under these circumstances. When a person is incapable to do so, he should perform the japam as per his strength.

What else should be spoken in this connection? You listen to my words in brief. The japam when performed in a spotless manner, getting engaged in meditation, it bestows the most auspicious reward.

Good conduct is the greatest virtue. It is the greatest wealth, the greatest knowledge, and the supreme goal. A person who does not possess the good conduct is denounced in the world and he cannot be happy in the other world as well. Therefore one should be of good conduct.

Performing the duties prescribed by the Vedas, other Vedic literature and the followers of the Vedas, is meant by the good conduct and nothing else.

The good conduct is also the conduct of the noble people. Theism is the source of goodness.

In case one is a believer in god, he will not deviate from the path of good conduct, commit folly and get denounced.

The pleasure or the pain one gets from the merits or the demerits in the world, the same process is also repeated in the other world. This is called the faith or theism in the world.

O beloved, I reveal a secret to you which should not be spoken by you to anyone and least to an atheist. In the age of Kali, for the fallen people devoid of good conduct, belonging to a degraded class, there is no protector, better than the five syllabled mantra.

This mantra has its own utility when a person is walking, standing, working at will, irrespective of his being pure and impure. The mantra still proves useful to him.

Those possessing the evil conduct, and those who have not purified the six paths, who have not received mantra from the preceptor, even for them this mantra's utility is not lost and does not become infructous for them.

Even for the out castes, fools, the fallen, those deprived of maryada or discipline and the degraded people, this mantra bestows fruits.

In whatever (degraded) position, my devotee is placed, for him this mantra always bestows success and not for anyone else.

O beloved one, the auspicious hour, date star, day of the week, etc. are of no consequence for this mantra. It is always wakeful and never slumbering. This great mantra is inimical to none. It could either be Susiddha, Siddha or Sadhya.

It is Susiddha when the mantra is imparted by a Siddha preceptor. In case it is imported by a preceptor who is not Siddha, it become Siddha. In fact the mantra is Sadhya.

In case, one has faith in me, the mantra and the preceptor, the mantra will undoubtedly be achieved whether it is a Sadhita or Asadhita. Therefore leaving aside the other harmful mantras the learned people should take refuge with Pancaksara supreme lore.

It is not sure, that if the other mantras are achieved, this would also be achieved. But when this mantra is achieved, all other mantras would also be achieved.

O goddess, as I cannot be achieved even when the other gods are achieved, but when I am achieved, all other gods are automatically achieved. Similar is the case with this *mantra.*

Since this mantra is applicable without reference to castes, the short comings of the other mantras are nowhere to be found in this mantra.

Still, this mantra should not be made use of for dirty gains or for trivial benefits against opponents.” Then only this is very efficacious.

Upamanyu said, “In this way, lord Siva, the weilder of a trident, spoke out to the goddess the method for the use of Pancaksara mantra for welfare of the world.

The one who recites the same, carefully with devotion, or listens to it, he gets relieved of all the sins and achieve salvation.

## Chapter 15 - Procedure for Sivadiksa

Sri Krsna said, “You have brought out the greatness of the five syllaballed mantra comparing it with the Vedas, you have also narrated the method of its use.

Presently I would like to be enlightened about the excellent Siva-sanskara. In the context of the receiving of the mantra, you had spoken something, which has escaped my memory.”

Upamanyu said, “Now I shall narrate to you the extremely virtuous and destroyer of the sins, the Siva sanskara, which has been narrated by Siva himself.

The Siva samskara (or consecration) is so called because a devotee thereby is authorised to perform the puja in a splendid manner. It is the mode of purifying the sixth path.

The excellent knowledge is bestowed with the same, the bondages of the noose are removed, and is given the name of Samskara, which is otherwise known as diksa as well.

Three types of diksas viz. Sambhavi, Sastri and Mantri have been prescribed in the Saivagamas. With the enlightenment by the preceptor, or by his touch, or with conversation with him, a human being is atonce freed from the sins.

It is given the name of Sambhavi diksa. It is further divided into two parts. From the point of view the destruction of sins, they are further divided as Tivra and Tivratara.

The one by which a person achieves rapid redemption is called Tivratara and the diksa which removes the sins of the people is called Tivra.

The diksa which provides Sakti and jnana in the body of a person, is bestowed by the preceptor, by means of jnana-caksu and the path of yoga.

The Sakti form of initiation (diksa) in mantras is associated with rites performed in the fire altar. This is carried out by the preceptor, outwardly to the pupils who are not so intelligent.

The grace can be showered over a disciple according to his strength, because, this is the brief method of the Saiva-dharma.

When the Sakti is not grasped, the intelligence, lore, Sivacara, Siddhis and salvation cannot be achieved.

Therefore observing all the symptoms of the grasping of Sakti, the preceptor should purify the pupil with jnana or action (kriya).

The evil minded person who conducts himself on the opposite, he gets destroyed. Therefore the preceptor should test the people in all possible ways.

Sakti is enlightenment and bliss and the Para Sakti is the manifestation of the same.

The symptoms of bliss and enlightenment are the activities of the minds, which cause thrill, shaking and blemishes in the body.

Observing these symptoms, even the pupil coming in contact with the preceptor, the should test the former’s position in relation with himself.

With the receiving of the knowledge the receiver is called a Sisya or pupil, and the Guru is called as such because of the glory attacked to him. Therefore one should rever the preceptor in all respects.

The guru or the preceptor stands for Siva, and he who is Siva is the preceptor himself. Whether the preceptor or Siva the same person is stationed in the form of knowledge.

As is Siva, similar is the type of his Vidya and the preceptor equals with Vidya. One gets similar reward by adoring, Siva, Vidya and the preceptor (Siva).

In fact the preceptor represents all the gods and the mantras. Therefore one should always accept the command of the preceptor.

A person wishing well for himself, should not violate the command of his preceptor even mentally, because the one who obeys the command of the preceptor attains the wealth of knowledge.

A pupil, while walking, standing, sleeping and eating should do nothing against the command of the preceptor.

One should not occupy a seat of his own liking in the house of a preceptor or in his presence, because the preceptor is considered to be the lord himself and his house is like a temple.

As a person keeping company of the evil people, is fallen because of their sins. The gold when fallen in fire is freed from the dirt, similarly, a person, with the association of the preceptor, is freed from all the sins. As the pitcher of ghee placed besides the fire melts away, similarly with the association of the acarya all the sins are washed out. As the burning fire bums out the wet and dry wood alike, similarly, the preceptor when pleased, destroys the sins in a moment. One should not annoy the preceptor by his action, thought and behaviour.

With the anger of the preceptor, the age, glory, respect, knowledge and the noble deeds get destroyed. The yajnas performed by annoying the preceptor, becomes infructuous.

Even the yama and niyamas are also destroyed. There is no doubt about it. One should never utter evil words against the preceptor.

One who denounces the preceptor out of foolishness, he falls in the Raurava hell. Addressing the preceptor, a person, desirous of his own welfare, should not misconduct himself against him by his action thought or behaviour. Whenever it is possible one should work at the command of his preceptor and perform himself in a manner which pleases the preceptor. One should perform the task of the preceptor in his presence or in his absence.

A pupil who works for the benefit of the preceptors becomes suitable for initiation in Saiva-dharma. The preceptor too should be wise, virtuous, and blissful.

Only a devotee of Siva, well-versed in the tattvas can bestow salvation and none else. The tattva producing the jnana, can make one achieve the supreme bliss.

The one who is well aware of the tattva, he alone can lead others to bliss. A preceptor devoid of the perfect knowledge, cannot redeem anyone.

Such types of the preceptors and the pupils can mutually redeem one an other. Can a stone make a stone to float? From a fake preceptor the salvation achieved is also fake.

Those who are well aware of Sivatattva they are themselves liberated and liberate others as well. There could be no self realisation.

A person without jnana (devoid or realization) is called a Pasu (an animal). One urged by an animal cannot eschew his animal nature.

Therefore, the one who is well aware of the tattva is liberated. He is also called the liberator. He is well read in all the religious scriptures, possessing all the laksanas.

He is well aware of all the methods and means; A person devoid of the knowledge of tattvas is of no consequence. A preceptor whose intelligence is engaged in gaining experience, a very glance at him bestows delight. Therefore, an intelligent person shall select a preceptor with the association of whom, one feels enlightened and blissful.

A person with wisdom should take him as his own preceptor and not to anyone else. A disciple should patronise a preceptor possessed of humility and the noble conduct.

Those desirous of liberation should serve the preceptor till they attains knowledge. After attaining jnana, till the knowledge of the tattva is achieved, he should have firm devotion in his preceptor.

He should never desert the preceptor nor should he ever neglect the preceptor from whom he might have attained even little of knowledge.

After waiting for a year, he can accept all other preceptors. After patronising the second preceptor, he should not insult or neglect the earlier preceptor or the brother disciple his son, instructors or the inspirators.

At the outset, approaching the Brahmana preceptor, well-read in the Vedas, who is full of wisdom, handsome, good looking, the bestower of protection and merciful, he should adore him and do his best to please him by his action thought and behavior.

He shall continue adoring him till he is pleased. When the preceptor is pleased, the sins of the pupil are atonce washed out.

Therefore the disciple shall give to the preceptor the coins, gems, fields, houses, ornaments, garments, vehicles, beds seats etc., keeping in view his available resources. In case the expectations of the pupil are high, then he should not be miserly in his offerings to the preceptor.

Since the preceptor is like the parents, master, s, wealth happiness, friend, comrade etc. he shall offer every thing to his preceptor.

After offering these, he should dedicate himself to the preceptor, his family and his belongings along with the water and remain subservient to him forever.

Since the preceptor is equated to Siva and the disciple has dedicated himself to Siva, as his devotee, he shall ever remain so. He will never be reborn thereafter.

The preceptor shall keep the Brahmana disciple on probation for a year, the Ksatriya for two years, and the Vaisya for three years. The preceptor, serving them the food and shall entrust the disciple with high and low ranking jobs.

A disciple who even after scolding or beating does not feel painful, he can be considered to be the spotless disciple and could be entrusted with the task of Sivasamskara.

The disciples who are non-violent, merciful, always anxious to adore Siva, possessing the self pride, intelligent, uncompetitive, sweet tongued, simple, soft spoken, spotless clean, humble, having a stable mind, possessing the spotless characters, devoted to Siva, Brahmana, Ksatriya or Vaisya and those who conduct themselves similarly with their action, thought and behaviour, should be regularly elevated corrected and the knowledge should be showered on them.

In the Siva-samskara rites, the woman is not required to directly participate in them. In case her mind is devoted to Siva, then she should seek permission from her husband.

A woman having no husband should seek permission from her son. This is particularly necessary for the Sudras and the low caste people.

The purificatory rites for the path-ways are not prescribed for the fallen people and those of the intercastes. In case they have auspicious feelings for Siva, the purification of sins could be performed by administering the holy asking of the feet. The Brahmana who is born as a result of the Anuloma marriage, his purificating can be done according to the practice in vogue in the mother’s family. The girl who has been devoted by her parents for Siva, she should be given in marriage to a devotee of Siva and not to an opponent. In case she is given away to some one else due to carelessness, then her husband should be advised properly.

In case of his being incapable to do so, she should leave him off and engage in the mental devotion of Siva as was done by Anusuya, who leaving the sage Atri, devoted herself to the adoration of Siva.

She became successful after adoring Siva in the same way, as the Pandvas became successful after performing tapas for Narayana.

Remaining uninspired with the instructions after preceptors, Draupadi got five husbands. In fact, the woman engaged in Saivite virtue, does not incur sin, as she has no choice of freedom.

Having been engaged in Svadharma, because of the importance of the command of Siva, no blemish is earned. What more could be stated in this connection whosoever takes refuge with Siva, then his Samskara does not remain subservient to the preceptor, then there is no difference by his right, touch and conversation with the same.

The one who possesses jnana, he can never be defeated anywhere, he develops Samskara in his mind by the means of yogamarga.

It has not been concealed here, and could be known from the mouth of the preceptor. The Samskara which is performed in Kunda-mandapa is being described by me in brief. It cannot be discussed exhaustively.

## Chapter 16 - Initiation of the disciple

Upamanyu said, “The preceptor should on an auspicious day, perform the consecration named Samaya over a pure spot devoid of all the defects.

After appropriately testing the ground, by smell, colour, taste etc., a platform should be caused to be made along the path prescribed in the architectural science.

An alter shall then be made and eight kundas should be made in eight quarters, starting from the north-east.

It may also be in the west when only the important pit need be dug. It shall be beautified by smearing it with powder.

A mandala should then be made decorated with the canopies, flags, the flower garlands with all the auspicious symptoms.

Then invoking Siva, it should be decorated with the red power etc. A poor person should make use of niwar grain mixed with saffron. A mystic diagram of the shape of a lotus may be drawn which should be of the width of a hand or two. Its colour could be white or red. The pericarp of the lotus of a hand’s width should be of eight fingers.

Half of it should be made in saffron and in the other half of eight petals, the learns should be made.

Various types of decoration should be made in the north east. A diagram of a full or half a hand should be made. Spreading paddy or rice, grains mixed with gingelly seeds and flowers besides the Kusa grass, a water pitcher with the usual characteristics shall be placed therein.

The pitcher shall be made of gold, silver or copper or alternatively it could be an earthen one. The fragrance, flowers, unbroken rice grains, kusa grass as well as the shoots of the Durba grass should be offered to the same.

At the neck of the pitcher, should be offered two pieces of white cloth rolling them with white cotton cord. Then the pure water, kusa, dravyas, should also be offered, placing the lid over the pitcher ultimately.

The vessels named Bhrngara and Vardhani, besides the conch and a disc, should also be offered. Except the thread, other things should consist of lotus petals and the leaves. On the lotus petal should be placed to the north, taking it to be a seat, Vardhani of Astraraja(?) should be placed with water and sandal paste.

To the east of the diagram, the great worship of the lord should start on the pitcher which has already been consecrated.

This adoration can be made over the seashore, riverbank, a cow shed, temple of the god, a house or at some other pleasant place.

Repeating the procedure already explained, the agnikunda can also be made without a mandapa.

The preceptor, with a smiling face should then enter the place of adoration, and perform the daily routine reciting the welfare mantra.

Siva should be adored in the centre of the mandala. He should then invoke Siva again in the pitcher and then adore him.

Siva happens to be the protector of the yajna. Then meditating upon by western face, he should adore Isvara in the pitcher consecrating to the west.

One who as well versed in the mantras, should start the mantra-yoga with the mantra received by him, from his preceptor, displaying mudras at the same time.

Thereafter the best of the preceptor should perform homa in the fire of the kunda. The other Brahmanas should also perform homa seated on all the sides.

Half or one fourth of the homa should be performed as is done by the Brahmana acarya. But the preceptor should perform homa in the main fire altar.

The other Brahmanas should recite the Vedas, Stotras or welfare mantras appropriately. The rest of the devotees of Siva should recite Siva’s name or Siva mantra.

Some of the people should resort to dancing, singing, playing on musical instruments or other welfare jobs. All the Brahmanas should be worshipped prior to this.

The worship of Siva should be resorted to after reciting of the welfare mantras. Ultimately, the preceptor should pray to Siva, for the welfare of the disciple.

“O lord of the gods, be pleased and enter my body. O lord of the universe, O ocean of mercy, O lord showering your grace on my devotee, you kingly liberate him.”

“All right, I do,” thus getting the command, the preceptor should summon his disciple who could be on total fast or fasting taking fruits alone, who had already freed himself from bath and other daily routine, besides having performed all the welfare deeds. Then the disciple should complete the reciting of the Pranava-mantra.

The disciple should be seated at the western entrance, towards the southern mandala over the kusa-asana facing north.

The preceptor should himself be seated facing east, raising his body. The preceptor should then drawing a mudra, pour the water over the disciple.

Then showering the flower over the disciple, the preceptor should bind the disciple’s eyes with the sanctified new cloth.

The preceptor should then make the disciple to enter the mandala and at his instance the disciple should offer salutation to Siva thrice.

Then he should offer the bench of golden flowers. Then he should prostrate before Siva to the east or to the north.

The preceptor shall then sprinkle the water over the disciple as before besides the flowers, removing at the same time the bondage around the eyes.

Then he should offer his salutation with folded hands, looking at the mandala. Then the acarya representing Siva should make the disciple to be seated over the southern side of the mandala.

Then the preceptor should make the disciple to be seated over the kusa-asana placed to his left and then place his welfare hand over the head of the disciple.

The preceptor then should place his hand infused with the tejas of Siva, reciting the mantra of the lord and place his hand over the head of the disciple.

The acarya should then touch the entire body of his disciple wit the same hand. The disciple too should offer his salutation to the preceptor, taking him to be the form of Siva.

Thereafter adoring the Sivagni the preceptor should make the disciple to pair three offerings in the fire. Then he should touch him with the tip of the Kusa grass. This by means of Vidya, he shall enter the Atman. After bowing before the lord, he shall perform the Nedisandhana,

According to the path prescribed in the Siva Agamas, recalling that his own pranas have been inserted in the body of the disciple, oblation should be offered reciting the mantras.

Ten offerings should be made to satisfy the mula-mantra and thereafter reciting the same mula-mantra he should satisfy the other limbs as well.

Then making the final offering or the Purna-ahuti, then offerings should be made, for repentance to the preceptor.

Then adoring lord Siva, sipping the water himself, he should perform the homa appropriately, redeeming his caste.

Ksatriya-hood should then be inculcated in him thereafter, the preceptor should create the Brahman ahood in him.

Thereafter the Ksatriya should be redeemed. Thus the Brahmana-hood should be incalcuated in both of them. In the Brahmana the Rudrahood should be inculcated.

After sprinkling and striking lightly the disciple, and recalling his Atman, in his own self, the preceptor shall drain out the wind that throb out like a flame through the veins as already stated. He shall then enter the vein and heart of the disciple.

With the insisting of the mantra, he should recall the blue spot which is spotless, as the form of Siva.

After breathing in the vein, reciting the mantras and displaying the Samskara-mudra, the preceptor shall refill it with puraka for uniting the soul. Then taking it again, with kumbhaka like the recaka earlier, he shall place it over the heart of the disciple.

After touching him and giving him the sacred thread, he shall offer three ahutis, followed by the Purnahuti.

In the south of the lord, the disciple should be seated facing north with folded hands over the excellent kusa seat.

The preceptor should then himself be seated over Svastikasana and recite the welfare mantras facing east.

The preceptor should then lift up the pitcher that had already been decorated, and concentrating his mind on Siva, perform the abhiseka of the disciple.

Then removing the cloth used for bath and wearing the white costumes, looking graceful he should go to the mandapa performing the acamana.

The preceptor should make him sit over the kusa seat as before and then performing the worship of Mahadevi in the mandapa perform the Karanyasa.

The preceptor should then hold the ashes in his hand and devoting his mind to Siva, should apply the ashes over the body of the disciple.

Thereafter the acarya in the form of Siva, performing the rites of dahoma and Plavana should conclude with Matrikanyasa. Meditating on the seat of Siva, and invoking him on the head of the disciple, he should mentally worship him in the prescribed manner.

Then with folded hands, he should pray, “Let you be stable always”. Thus speaking he should devote himself to his extremely resplendent form.

Thus adoring both Siva and Parvati, receiving permission in Sivatmaka manner, the preceptor should slowly whisper the Siva- mantra in the ear of the disciple.

The disciple on his part, quickly listening to the mantra form the preceptor, should slowly repeat the same with the permission of the preceptor.

The preceptor well-versed in the mantras should also make the disciple to recite a mantra of Sakti and then the welfare mantra should be recited for the disciple.

Thereafter the preceptor should reveal to the disciple, the meaning of the mantras in brief and then impart him the knowledge of the form of Siva as well as the performing of the yogasana.

The initiation words should then be uttered by the disciple at the command of the preceptor as Siva, fire as well as the preceptor.

He should declare, “Even when I have to lay down my life or the head is cut off I shall not eat food without having an audience with Siva.”

Till the destruction of the great delusion, he should offer food to the lord daily and continue to worship him with at most faith and devotion.

The disciple will thereafter be known as Samaya in the hermitage of the preceptor. He shall follow the command of the preceptor and remain subservient to him.

Thereafter performing the karanyasa, the preceptors, holding the bhasma and rosary in his own hands, sanctifying the same with mula-mantra should offer them to the disciple.

Thereafter the images of Mahadeva should be adored, performing the homa, japam and meditation.

The disciple should also respectfully receive these ashes from the acarya, and should not disobey his command.

Receiving all the aforesaid things from the acarya with devotion, thereafter the images or the Siva-linga should be consecrated in his own house or a matha and or be can adore them regularly.

Thereafter the preceptor should enlighten him over the method of the adoration of Siva. The disciple too should keep on adoring Siva according to his faith, devotion and wisdom.

Whatever has been timely spoken by Sivacarya, whatever instructions have been given, otherwise whatever has been stated by him, all these words should be honoured by the disciple.

The Siva-sastra should be accepted, listening, narration, should be done at the command of the preceptor and not at the command of others or his own sweet will.

Thus this Samaya Samskara has been narrated in brief, which is the best for those desirous of achieving the abode of Siva.

## Chapter 17 - The types of initiation

Upamanyu said - “Thereafter the preceptor observing the ability of the disciple, should perform the side way purification for the liberation from the bondage.

The six-way liberation includes kala, tattva, bhuvana, varna, pada and the mantra in brief.

The five are the path way of kala. The five kalas pervade the five paths and constitute nivrtti praistha, vidya, santi and santyatita.

From Siva tattva to the earth is called the tattva-marga. It has twenty six division both pure and impure.

From the base to the Unman-loka, the entire area is called Bhuvanadhva; without the divisions and the subdivisions, it comprises of sixty types.

The fifty syllables in the form of Rudra constitutes the path of letters. The path of words has several varieties.

The path of Mantradhva is pervaded Paramavidya as well as the upa-mantras. As Siva is not included in the tattvas because of his being the foremost of the tattvas.

Similarly the lord of Mantras is not included in the Mantradhva. The one who is not aware of the one pervading the other paths as also the presiding substance, from the angle of the tattvika vision, he would not be fit enough for Adhvasodhana. The one who is not aware of six types of Adhvarupa, he shall be ignorant about its pervading and the power of pervading. Therefore Adhvarupa and its all pervading nature, should be correctly known first one should resort to Adhvasodhana. This is the kundala mandala activity, which should be attended to first.

The kalasa-mandala should be created over the land measuring two hands towards the east. Thereafter the acarya representing Siva, who had already taken bath together with the disciple who has already performed his daily routine, enter the Siva mandala and should worship as before. Therefore payasam should be made of the rice little above an adhaka (a measure equivalent to three kgs.).

Half of the part of that payasam should be kept for the purpose of homa and the rest should be kept separately. Then in the mandala with four varnas, five pitchers should be placed four on the four sides and the fifth in the centre representing the preceptor. Then the mantras of Pancabrahma should be recited over each one of them.

The preceptor, who is well aware of the kalpavidhi, should recite the mantra of om namah Sivaya. Then he should consecrate Isana in the central pitcher, Purusa in the eastern one, Aghora in the southern one, and Vamadeva in the northern one. Sadyojat should consecrated in the western one. All the pitchers should then be sanctified appropriately.

Then he should imagine the performing of homa in Sivagni as before. The half of payasam which had been set aside earlier, should be used for the performing of homa and the rest should be left to be consumed by the disciple. Reciting the mantras, tarpana should be performed as before.

The fire should then be ignited making the offering in it. Then the mula-mantra om, humphat svaha namah sivaya should be recited.

After performing the homa the anganyasa should be performed. For performing the rite of dipam, three offerings of ghee should be made.

While reciting each mantra one should devote his mind to the illustrious image of Siva. He should add three times the yam spun by the Brahmana girl.

Sanctifying that thread, it should be tied to the tuft of the disciple. The thread should have the length from the big toe of the foot to the left over the heads. The vein Susumna should be tied with that thread at the foot sole. This should be performed by the performer quite peacefully.

Then making the three offerings in the fire, the disciple should be made to sit besides the preceptor. Then he should touch the heart of the disciple with a flower as before and invoke his consciousness.

It shall then be conceived as having been placed in the twelve petalled lotus. The thread shall be joined with the other thread(?) with the astra and varma mantras. After veiling the body of the disciple the thread should be adored.

It shall then be imagined that the three strings represent a bond with the objects and the state of enjoyment. The Santyatita kalas, etc. in the form of the elements ether etc. shall be joined to the thread, with their respective names and worshipped with these as the base, the foregoing rites shall be performed. Then he shall survey the pervasion of the dirt etc. in the tattvas. After offering the ahuti, the prevention of kala in the dirt etc. the kalas shall be illuminated.

After striking the disciple and the thread reciting the Santyatita mantra, he should touch the thread.

Thus after offering the ahutis of Santyatita upto the end of Nirvrtti, again pouring the three ahutis, should adore Siva in the mandala.

The disciple should be made to sit on the right side of Siva facing north over the asana of kusa grass. The preceptor should then offer to the disciple, the payasam, which had earlier been earmarked for the purpose.

The disciple should consume the payasam given by the preceptor, quite gracefully uttering the name of Siva. Then acamana should be performed twice uttering the Siva mantra.

The disciple should then be made to sit in the second mandala, where his preceptor shall give the disciple pancagavya. The disciple should drink it as far as possible, perform the acamana and then recite the name of Siva.

The disciple should then be made to sit in the third mandala and the should be gives a brush of the tree branch as prescribed.

The disciple should brush his teeth chewing the tender portion of the stick, sitting facing east or the north, quietly.

Then washing or rinsing the teeth performing acamana he should recite the name of Siva, then at the command of the preceptor, folding his hands, the disciple should reach the Siva mandala.

The brush if thrown towards the east, north or west and the act is witnessed by the preceptor, it would be inauspicious.

Because in case the tooth stick is thrown in the wrong direction, therefore, in order to rid himself of the blame, he should make offerings a fifty or a hundred times in the fire, reciting the mula-mantra.

Then touching the disciple whispering the mantra in his ears, he should be seated to the right side of the lord.

He should sleep over the untorn bed or over the sanctified kusasana, he should sleep placing the head towards the east in the night.

Binding the tip of the tuft of the disciple with the thread, alongwith tuft, the preceptor shall tie the unwashed bed sheet. With varma mantra he shall cover him up. He shall draw three lines around him, with gingelly seeds and mustard fully consecrated with astra- mantra outside the lines, he shall offer oblation to the guardians of quarters.

The disciple shall not take anything after having been thus placed. While getting up the next day, he shall intimate to the preceptor in case he had any dream during the night.

## Chapter 18 - Purification of the six paths

Upamanyu said, “Thereafter the disciple with the permission of the acarya should take his bath and meditate on Siva with folded hands and approach the Siva-mandala.

Thereafter without performing the worship, as was done on the earlier day, all the rites from the binding of the eyes shall be performed. The preceptor then shall show him the mandala.

With the eyes bound, when the disciple drops the flowers, the preceptor shall tell him the places where the flowers fall.

Then as was done earlier, after getting nirmalaya, adoring Isandeva, he should perform homa in the fire.

Whatever evil dream might have witnessed by the disciple during the night, for the removal of the blemish for the same, fifty or a hundred offerings should be made in the fire.

Tying the thread to the tuft, as was done earlier, extending it longer, he shall perform the worship of Adhara based on Nivrttika and conclude with the worship of Vagisvari with due homas. The disciple shall bow to Vagisa and Sati who pervade Nivriti. The lord shall be worshipped by him in the mandala, making three ahutis. Thereafter the mystical rite of making the simultaneous entry into all types of living beings shall be performed.

The preceptor should perform the rites of striking and sprinkling in the gross body of the disciple. Thereafter the atman shall be taken and placed inside the twelve petalled lotus. It shall again be carried from that place, repeating the basic mantra and mudras as prescribed in the texts. The preceptor shall unite it mentally, with all types of living beings at the same time.

There are fourteen types of the living beings which include eight types of the gods, five types of animals and birds, one for the humans making the total of fourteen.

In order to make the disciple to enter all of them intelligently, the preceptor should make the mind of the disciple to enter with Vagesani.

Therefore for the sake of conception, offering salutation to the lord the homa and the worship should be performed. After completion of the entire process, he shall remember it as developed.

He shall perform the mystical rites of nativity, followed by the earlier actions, and the performing of the purificatory rites, become straightforward and enjoy the great pleasure.

The best of the preceptor, shall perform three ahutis and pray to the lord, for the sake of redemption, achievement of birth, longevity, enjoyment and purification.

The preceptor should cut of all the nooses freeing the body of the disciple from all the blemishes of the enjoying of pleasures, and the contact with sexual objects.

The body of the disciple should be made totally clean, splitting all the bondages.

Offering ahutis in the fire, Brahma should be adored, then offering three ahutis to Brahma he should remember the command of Siva.

O Grand sire, by your grace let me achieve the supreme position of Siva. No obstruction should be created by you in this connection. This is the firm command of lord Siva.”

Thus speaking, Brahma should be adored sending him off appropriately at the same time. Then he should offer three ahutis.

The soul of the disciple should then be uplifted, as was done earlier, when it was purified by Nivrttikala and should be deposited into his own soul and then worship vagisa.

Then offering three ahutis, he should offer his salutation and sending him off, should unite with the Pratirtha kalô the nivrtti. He shall them perform the worship and the three ahutis and at the same time imagine the entry of the atman of the disciple into the Pratirtha kala.

Then he shall conceive its pervasion and pervading Vagesani, after invoking Pratistha and repeating the same process as mentioned earlier.

Vagisani should be conceived to be lustrious like the full moon. After repeating the same process as before, he shall adore Visnu, at the command of Siva, the supreme soul.

After the retralistic send off of Visnu, by means of Vidya, Pratirtha shall be invoked and its pervasion with Vagisa as well. Every then be done goether with Puranahuti in the blazing fire as was done earlier. Then the worship of Nilarudra should be performed invoking him. The command of the lord should be carried out as was done earlier.

The lord shall then be relieved ritualistically. For the purpose of silencing him, the Vidyakala has to be conceived and her pervasion should be observed.

Then he should invoke Vagisi, who pervades has soul, having the form and features of the early morning sun, that illuminates all the quarters.

The residual rites should be performed, invoking Mahesvara as before. Then adoring the lord, homa should be performed then the preceptor should convey the command of Siva to the disciple.

Then sending off Mahesvara, he shall lead Santyakala out of the five Kalas and observe her pervasion.

Then he should meditate on Vagisa as before, who resembles the sky. Then he should be worshipped as before offering Purnahuti.

Siva should be worshipped by special means and the preceptor should announce the special command of Siva to the disciple.

While doing so Siva the lord of speech, should first be adored then the salutation should be offered to him and finally he should be sent off.

Reciting the Siva mantra, the preceptor should the sprinkle water over the head of the disciple and then think of the merging of the Santyatita kala in the Sakti-tattva.

On the other side beyond the six path ways, he shall conceive the greatest Sakti of Siva that pervades the pathways and is resplendent like the crores of suns.

The disciple should be brought before the same like a crystal and washing the scissors as per the provisions of the auspicious Siva-Sastra, the preceptor should have the tuft of the disciple cut off with the thread. The same should be covered with the cowdung and consigned in the fire of the fire altar.

Then adding Vausat to the mula-mantra the scissors besides hands shall be washed. Then placing both his hands over the chest of the body of the disciple, the preceptor shall restore consciousness in the body of the disciple.

Thereafter the disciple will take his bath and perform acamana. The good wishes and the blessings should be conferrd on him. Welfare mantras should be recited. The disciple should be made to enter the mandala where he should prostrate before the preceptor.

In order to beg forgiveness for the short comings, the lord should be adored before, pouring three ahutis reciting the mantras at the same time.

Three ahutis should then be offered reciting the five syllabled mantras. Both Siva and Parvati lodged over the mandala should then be adored and offering three ahutis, the preceptor should offer prayer with folded hands.

“O lord, by your grace this disciple has been purified from the six paths, now you kindly lodge him in your eternal abode.

In this way, he shall perform everything as before from Nadisandhana to purnahuti. Thereafter the elements shall be purified.

Then one should meditate upon Siva, for the purification of the mobiles and immobiles, hot and cold, and the Pahcamahabhutas.

After cutting off the knots of the bhutas he shall connect the bhuta to Siva by means of extreme concentration.

His body shall then he purified by him. The face of the disciple should be purified. Burning the face by means of the mantras, pouring the drops of nectar over his soul, his entire body should be purified.

At the outset, the Santyatitakala that pervades the pathways should be placed over the lead of the disciple, the Santikala on the face, Vidyakala over the region starting from throat to the navel, Pratisthakala upto the knees, the Nivrtti kala beneath the same. Thereafter he shall meditate upon it.

He should perform nyasa of the bija- mantra the form of Siva, and invoking Siva, he should worship him in his heart.

The disciple should be seated daily with his preceptor, invoking the soul of Siva, he should invigurate the body of the disciple with the tejas of Siva infusing anima and other virtues in the same.

Thus speaking, “Let anima and others be pleased, he should offer three ahutis. Thereafter the virtue should be invoked in him.

He shall also invoke the lord for the presence of these qualities in him including omniscience, contentment, eternal enlightenment, unviolated Sakti, freedom and infinite power.

Then after offering prayer to the lord, performing his abhiseka with the pitchers of Sadyojata then the lord Siva should be meditated upon in the heart.

Then the disciple should be made to sit and adoring Siva as before, he should be bestowed with Saiva-vidya.

Adding Om in the start and ending with namah the mantra should be placed. Sakti-vidya compares with Siva-Sakti.

Instructions should also be given to the pupil in the name of the sage, metre deity and the efficacy of Siva and Siva, besides their adoration, their avarana and the postures.

Again adoring the lord of the gods, he shall submit to Siva. Kindly make whatever has been performed by me, a well accomplished thing.’’

Then the preceptor shall prostrate before Siva, with his disciple on the ground. Thereafter he shall ritualistically send him off from the mandala and the fire.

Thereafter those present there who are worthy of worship shall also be adored appropriately. Those present in the gathering besides the Rtviks, shall be honoured and presented the gifts. In ease a devotee is desirous of his own welfare, he shall never be miserly on such occasions.

## Chapter 19 - The glory of the mantras

Upamanyu said, “I shall now speak out the glory of Namah-mantra, Sivasadhaka mantra and the Samskdra mantra, as I had spoken earlier.

Mahadeva should be adored in the diagram, the pitcher should be established. Then performing homa, a person without the turban should be seated there.

Processing the adoration in the same as had been followed earlier, one should offer a hundred ahutis followed by the Purna-ahuti, performing homa, the excellent preceptor should then perform abhiseka of the disciple.

He should ignite the fire as before, performing his abhiseka and then bestow the best of the diksa.

Following the same process elaborately from Vidya to Upadesa holding water with flowers in the hands, the disciple should be bestowed with the knowledge relating to Siva.

Then the preceptor should say “This Vidya shall bestow all the success on you in the present as well the future life and this would be the great mantra by the grace of Siva.”

Thus speaking, worshipping Siva, the preceptor with the consent of the disciple, should instruct him on the Sivayoga to him.

Listening to the message of the preceptor, the performer should engage himself in mantra-sadhana performing the viniyoga.

The practice of reciting of the Mula-mantra is called Puruscarana since it has to be practiced before the rite viniyoga.

A devotee desirous of salvation should practice this mantra too often. In case it is modestly practiced it becomes auspicious in this world as well the other one.

On a good day, in an auspicious country, during the unblemished time, cleaning the teeth and nails, taking bath, he should perform the morning routine.

Then decorating himself with fragrance, garland, ornaments, he should wear a white turban and a scarf.

Then he should be seated over an asana in a temple, house, or at some other pleasant place, quite comfortably.

Following the path as prescribed in the Sivasastra, he should turn his body like Siva, and should adore Nakulisvara Mahadeva.

Then offering payasam to him, he should finish the adoration appropriately, and offer his salutation to lord Mahadeva.

He should recite the mantra of Siva a crore of times or a half of it, or still half of the same or alternatively he should recite the mantra of Siva, twenty lakhs or ten lakhs of times.

Then shedding away the violence, becoming compassionate, peaceful and charitable, he should consume the payasam or the food without salt.

In case the payasam is not available, then he should consume fruits and roots. Siva has declared these things to be absolutely auspicious.

Whatever is consumed by him daily, irrespective of its being Caru, ground flour of fried grain, gruel, vegetables, milk, curd, ghee, roots, fruits and waters, he should take it duly after consecrating it with the mantras while the practice of the mantra is being kept up. He shall maintain silence too.

He shall take bath from the east flowing or the west flowing rivers and purify himself be repeating a hundred and eight mantras or sprinkle himself as his strength permits.

He should perform tarpana daily and offer seven, five or three ahutis with ghee in the fire of Siva.

In this way, a devotee of Siva, who worships the lord with devotion, nothing remains beyond him in this as well as the future world.

Or otherwise he should recite the mantra daily with a concentrated mind. He should not take food without reciting the mantra a hundred times. Only then he achieves success in the mantra.

Nothing is beyond his reach nor is there anything inauspicious for him. Achieving Vidya, riches and comforts in this world he also finally achieves liberation.

Whether in the course of practice or application, whether performed as a nitya or naimittika rites, he shall perform the japam after taking bath with water or with ashes.

He shall perform the japam of the five syllabled mantra, pure in his body and mind, with the tuft tied up wearing the sacred thread on the body and the pavitra round the finger, he will also have the Tripundra marks and shall also wear Rudraksa beads.

## Chapter 20 - Consecration of the disciple by the acarya

Upamanyu said, “Thus when the disciple getting cultured, becomes fit enough for initiation for the Pasupata vrata, only then the acarya should initiate him and not otherwise.

Making a diagram as before, adoring Paramesvara, five Kalasas should be placed on the four sides and one in the middle.

Nivrtti-kala shall be installed in the pitchers in the east, Pratistha-kala in the pitcher placed to the west, Vidyakala in the south and Santikala in the north. While Para-kala has to be lodged in the middle.

The following rites shall be performed as before. Like those relating to the protection, or Raksa, Mudrabandha, or the gesture of the cow, repetition of the mantra, over the pitchers and the homa till the Purnahuti.

The preceptor should make the disciple to enter into the diagram without a turban over the head, when all the formulations are completed, the disciple should be made to perform the oblation.

The lord should then be adored, and with his consort, the disciple should be made to occupy a seat.

The disciple imagined as the five-fold offering of the fruits shall be united with the kalas and conceived as Siva, because the mantra has been installed over his body. Thereafter he shall be worshipped.

Then the water from the pitchers starting from Nivrtti-kumbha and ending with the one at the centre shall be poured on the disciple reciting the name of Siva.

The preceptor should then dedicate the disciple to Siva and touch disciple’s head and should instruct the disciple who is turned as Sivacarya.

Then decorating Siva in the diagram, worshipping him, he should make him offer a hundred ahutis followed by Purnahuti.

Then adoring lord Siva again and prostrating before him, folding his hand in anjali-mudra over the head he should pray to lord Siva.

O lord, by your grace, I have accepted him as a preceptor, therefore, O lord, you give him the divine command.

Thus praying with the disciple and then offering his salutation the preceptor should be worshipped as per the provision of the Sivagama.

Then with the consent of Siva, the preceptor should hand over the book of Siva-jnana in the hands of the disciple.

The disciple should place the book over his head and then place it over the Vidyasana appropriately adoring it, offer his salutation to the same.

The flywhisks and the chatras appropriately suitable for a king should also be offered. Achieving the position of an acarya he can achieve kingship as well.

Now he should follow the noble foot steps of his ancestors. It has been prescribed in the Siva’s literature and such a person is adored in the society.

Testing the disciple according to the method laid down in the Saiva literature and bestowing the best of the Samskaras on him the preceptor should impart to the disciple, the knowledge of Siva.
