He shall infuse in him all these qualities, without differently including purity, forbearance, compassion, non-covetousness and absence of jealousy.

After thus urging the disciple, he shall ritualistically send off Siva from the mandala. The Siva kumbha shall then be adored besides the tire and others who had been invited there.

The virtuous preceptor should perform all the samskaras at a time and deliver discourses on two or three experiments.

At the beginning of the experiment, the pitcher should be consecrated like adhva suddhi. The Samskara of Samaya should also be performed without performing the abhiseka.

After adhvavisodhana Siva should be adored. After completion of these rites, Siva should again be adored.

Igniting the fire, homa should be performed. Then performing tarpana with the consent of the lord, mantra should be given to the disciple and the disciple should be made to complete the remaining formalities.

Otherwise thinking again of all the mantra- samskaras, the margasuddhi should by alone by the preceptor himself till the performing of the abhiseka.

Whatever procedure has been prescribed in the Santyatita-kalas, all the three tattvas should be purified with the same.

There are three tattvas of the atmatattva of the Siva-vidya which are well known. Siva is also absorbed in Sakti. The form of the same has appeared.

Siva pervades in the Santyatita-marga. The rest of the path is pervaded by Vidya. All the rest of them are pervaded by the Atman.

Finding Siva-mantra to be difficult in access, the learned persons well-versed in Siva literature, call it the Sakta-samsara.

O Krsna, thus the four types of consecratory rites have been explained to you. What else do you intend to listen from me?

## Chapter 21 - Nitya and Naimittika rites

Sri Krsna said, “O lord, I would like to listen to the optional as well as the compulsory rites of the followers of Saivite conduct as prescribed in the Saivite literature.”

Upamanyu said, “A devotee of Siva shall rise up early in the morning, devoting his mind at Siva and Parvati and thinking about his daily business, should start from his house at the sun rise.

Reaching a secluded place, without obstruction he should free himself from call of nature etc. and performing all the deeds connected therewith, he should wash his teeth with the tooth stick.

The performing of the tooth stick on the eight and other days of the moon, he should regularly rinse his mouth again and again.

Performing acamana he should take his bath at the river, reservoir near the temple, a tank or even in the house appropriately.

The material for the toilet should be placed at the bank of the river and should drop refuse at a distance. Then washing the hands with the application of the dust, he should take his bath. Then the bath should be taken with the slight application of the cowdung.

Taking his bath again and again, washing the clothes, or leaving them there itself, he should clad himself in the new garments like a king.

A Brahmacari, an ascetic or a widow should not use the scented soap. They shall also not use tooth brush of twig for the cleaning of the teeth.

He shall tie his tuft and wear the sacred thread in the usual way. He shall not enter (unknown) water or plunge therein. After performing the acamana, he shall take a dip thrice in the water.

Having a dip into the water, he should recite the names of Siva and Parvati according to his capacity and also recite the mantras. Coming out he shall again perform acamana and perform his own abhiseka with the same water.

Then he shall pour water over his body with the cow-horn with Darbha grass or with the leaf of a Palasa tree or a lotus leaf, or with both his hands, five or three times.

In case he is in garden or a house, he shall pour water over himself with a water jar, reciting the mantras.

A person who is unable to take bath with water, he should wet a clean cloth and should rinse the body from the head to feet. This process is called kapila-snana.

One should bath with ashes reciting the ordinary mantras or reciting the Siva-mantra. The bath which is taken while reciting the name of Siva is called self bath.

As per the provision of one’s own Sutra, oblation or tarpana should be offered to the gods followed by Brahmayajna.

Then devoting his mind towards Siva lodged in a diagram, washing the lord appropriately he should then offer arghya to the sun like Siva.

Otherwise performing the actions as prescribed in one’s own Sukta, he should wash his hands clean. Performing the kara- nyasa, he should purify his body.

Then taking scented water in his left palm with mustard seeds, he shall then sprinkle water over himself through bunch of the kusa grass repeating the mantra apohistha etc. accompanied with the basic mantra. Sniffing the water remaining in the left nostril, he shall think on lord again and angain.

Taking off the dark complexioned sin of the body, through the left nostril, and that outside, he shall conceive it as having gone to the rock.

The rite of tarpana shall be performed in favour of the gods, to the sages in particular besides the bhutas and the pitrs. Then the arghya should be offered appropriately.

Then carrying the water mixed with the red sandal paste in one hand he shall make a circular diagram over the ground and further decorate it with red powder.

There he shall worship the sun, with covers along with the ancillaries repeating the mantra Svakholkaya etc. for recurring happiness.

Then he shall make another mandala and adore it with ancillaries. Then he shall place there a gold vase of the size of prastha current in the Magadha land. He shall fill it with scented water and the red sandal together with red flowers, gingelly seeds, unbroken rice and kusa grass.

Filling the vase with durva grass, apamarga, cow’s milk or the water alone, then kneeling over the ground, should worship the deity of the mandala.

Placing the said vase over the head, arghya should be offered to Siva. Or otherwise filling the palm with kusa and water, arghya should be given with mula-vidya.

Then he should give arghya to Siva in the sky which represents to Siva. The nyasa should thereafter be performed washing the hands.

Realising the presence of Siva from Isana to Sadyojata as Panca-brahmans, picking up the ashes reciting the mantras, he should apply them over the limbs.

Reciting the mula-mantra, all the limbs should be touched including the head, face, heart, ractum, feet, etc.

Then he should wear another cloth perform acamana should sprinkle the water sanctified with the eleven mantras, over the disciple. The disciple on his part, performing the acamana twice, should remember Siva. Then the disciple, while reciting mantras should perform anganyasa should draw Tripundra over the forehead with the ashes mixed in scented water.

It could be circular or square in shape. It could be a circular or a semi-circular figure. But he shall apply the marks in the same way over the arms, head, chest and the forehead. The bhasma applied over other limbs of the body should not be like Tripundra.

Tripundra should be made over the forehead without dusting. Rudraksa should be worm over the head, neck, ears and the hands.

The bead of Rudraksa with the complexion of gold is treated to be the best, which should not be cut. Rudraksa which has not been used by others is the best and most auspicious. The Rudraksa of yellow, red and black colour in excellent and is meant for the three castes.

In case the excellent bead is not available, then whatever bead be available could be used. But it should be devoid of defects. The people of the lower caste shall not wear the bead intended for the higher case, though the people of the higher caste, can wear those beads meant for the lower castes.

Except the inauspicious time, Rudraksa should always be worn. But it should be worn on three (morning, noon and evening) two times (morning and evening) or in the evening alone.

Taking bath as per one’s capacity, one should adore Paramesvara, seated over the place of worship over an excellent asana.

One should meditate upon Siva Parvati facing east or the north. The preceptor should be adored together with the disciples from Sveta to Nakulisa.

Then offering salutation to Mahadeva, his eight names should be recited. These include Siva, Mahesvara, Rudra, Visnu, Pitamaha, Samsara-vaidya, Sarvajna and Paramatma. Or alternatively eleven names of Siva should be recited.

For the subsiding of the ailment, one should meditate on the mass of splendour at the tip of the tongue. He shall wash his feet and apply sandal paste over his hands and then perform kara-nyasa.

## Chapter 22 - Different types of Nyasas

Upamanyu said, “The Nyasas are said to be of three types which relate to the creation, preservation and the distraction of the world. The Stotra nyasa relates to the householders, the creative nyasa is meant for the Brahmacarins.

Assimilation is the nyasa for the yatis as well as the Vanaprasthins. Sthiti is the nyasa for the woman who are deprived of their husbands.

For a virgin utpatti-nyasa is recommended. Now I shall mention the characteristics of Nyasa. The procedure from thumb (right) to the left little finger is called utpatti-nyasa. The reverse of it is Samhrti-nyasa.

The syllables Na etc. with the bindus, shall be fixed in order of the fingers. Siva shall be fixed on the palms and on the little fingers.

Using the Astra-mantra the nyasa of astra shall be made in two quarters. The five kalas nivrtti and others, in the form of the five elements and accompanied with their respective symbols, shall be fixed in the chest, neck palate, middle of the eyebrows and the brahmanradra. One shall conceive them in different bijas.

In order to purify them one shall perform japam of the five syllabled mantra stopping the breath thrice, he shall cut off the knot of the elements repeating the astra-mantra and showing the mystic gestures of astra. The Atman urged by the vital breath, through the vein Susumna and passing out through the Brahmarandhra shall be united with the Saiva splendour.

Then drying up the body with wind, it should be burnt up with Kalagni. Then the upwards Kalas are dissolved by the wind.

Dissolving the burnt body and touching the kalas with the ocean, he shall drench the and flood the body through nectars and keep it in its normal place. Killed and burnt without the creation of the kalas he shall flood with nectar that which is reduced to ashes.

In the body possessing the Vidya, he shall join the soul, that has come out of Siva in the form of a flame of a lamp. He shall join the same through Brahmarandhra.

Meditating Siva who has entered in his lotus like heart, then he should shower the nectar, over the Vidya like body of the disciple. Then he should perform the karanyasa for purification. Thereafter he should perform deha-nyasa in the mahti-mudra.

He should perform the anganyasa as provided in the Siva-puja and then perform the varna-nyasa over the joints of the hands and the feet.

Then with the six classes, he should perform sadanga-nyasa and should bind the quarters from the south east onwards. Or otherwise he should perform the Pancanga nyasa over the head or perform sadanga-nyasa without the bhutasuddhi.

In this way purifying the body and the soul achieving the devotion of Siva should worship Paramesvara.

The one who has enough of leisure and whose wisdom is stable, shall perform the nyasa in a proper manner.

Matrka-nyasa is the first of all, which is followed by Brahma-nyasa and then Pranava-nyasa while Hamsa-nyasa is the fourth one.

The noble people have described the Pancaksaratmaka-nyasa as the fifth one, one or several of he nyasas should be performed during the time of worship.

According to the nyasa of the various letters, A is to be lodged over he head, A in the forehead, i and i in the eyes, u and u in the ears, r and r in the cheeks, Ir and Jr in the nostrils, e and ai in the lips, o and au in the rows of the teeth, am in the tongue, and ah in the palate. The gutturals are in the five joints of the right hands, the palatals in the joints of the left hand. The live gods and the dentals are in the legs, Pa and Pha in the sides, Ba in the back, and Bha is in the navel. Ma is in the heart, Ya to Sa in the swen constituent elements, besides the skin. Ha is in the cavity of the heart while ksa is in the middle of the eye brows.

After performing the nyasa of the letters, in the manners of fifty Rudras the five Brahmanas shall be fixed in the limbs, for and kala.

Karanyasa may or may not be performed through them, but he should imagine the same in the head, face, chest, private parts and the legs.

There are five kalas of Isana which are lodged in the five faces starting with the one above, and ending with the one in the west.

Thereafter the four kalas of the Purusa should be placed in the four faces starting from the east.

The eight kalas of Aghora, should be placed in the heart, neck, shoulders, navel, belly, back and the chest, besides the hands and the feet.

Then the thirteen kalas of Vamadeva, are to be placed in the anus, penis, thighs, knees, calves, hips, buttocks, sides, nose, head and arms. In this way the people well-versed in the scriptures perform the nyasa of thirty eight kalas in a proper order.

Thereafter the experts in the Pranava doctrine, should perform the pranava-nyasa in the arms, elbows, wrists, sides, belly, thighs, calves and the back. After the completion of the Pranava-nyasa the devotee should perform the Hamsa-nyasa in an appropriate manner, in the eyes, nostrils, arms, face, forehead, armpits, sides, breasts, hips, hands and heels. Or otherwise the nyasa shall be performed in the manner of five limbs. Thereafter the nyasa of the five syllabled mantra shall be performed.

One can achieve Sivahood by following the path as directed above. A person having no faith in Siva, should not think of adoring Siva.

Being unfaithful one should not meditate upon Siva, because he cannot achieve Siva in such a situation. Therefore discarding his own identity, one should adore Siva with devotion.

Thinking himself that “I am Siva” one should perform the rites of Siva which are termed as the five yajnas i.e. karmayajna, tapayajna, japayajna, dhyanayajna and jnana-yajna.

Some of the people perform the karmayajna some perform tapo-yajna, some engage themselves in japayajna, some in the dhyana yajna.

While others perform the jnana-yajna. The latter ones are better than the earlier ones. The karma-yajna are divided into two parts. One is performed with a desire in view, while the other is performed without a desire.

A lustful person after enjoying the worldly pleasures, becomes more lustful. But the one who is without desire or lust, he enjoys all the heavenly pleasures in the abode of Rudra and after his fall from the Sivaloka, he is born as a person engaged in tapoyajna. There is no doubt about this. The same person again after enjoying many pleasures, is relieved from there.

Then devoting his time in the performing of the japam, one lives, comfortably on earth. Such an excellent type of person, because the performance of japam, achieves the jnana expeditiously and also achieves Siva Sayuja. In the karma- yajna too a living being achieves liberation, by the grace of Siva.

When a person being devoid of desires, sometimes gets entangled in the worldly desires. Therefore out of the five yajnas as described above, the dhyana-yajna is the best and one should own up the same.

A person who is engaged in the meditation of Siva for achieving jnana, he has already crossed the ocean of the universe. Getting relieved of the sins of violence, he gets purified at heart.

The dhyana-yajna which provides moksa is still better than that. One cannot have enough of rewards for the performing of the outward deeds.

As the people work in the palace of Indra, similar people are here as well. The body of the person engaged in meditation becomes subtle and enjoys all the comforts.

As the person working here, makes houses with mud and the wood, similarly those engaged in dhyana-yajna do not have much of faith in the gods made of stone and wood because they are aware of the reality about Siva. Neglecting lord Siva lodged in his own heart, the one who adores outside, he is like a person, who leaving the fruit in the hand, licks his own elbow. One achieves jnana by mediation and meditation by jnana.

One achieves salvation by both the means Therefore one should engage himself in meditation of Siva and Parvati externally or with a faithful mind one should meditate upon them in the twelve petalled lotus, head, forehead, the middle of the eyebrows, the tip of the nose, face, neck, heart, navel, or in any permanent spot. Or one should worship the Siva-linga, or the image of the lord in human form, or the artificial fire or on the ground with devotion according to one's own liking. Or he shall adore the lord both internally or externally. A person who is engaged in the mental worship, may or may not perform the outward worship.

## Chapter 23 - Method of mental adoration of Siva

Upamanyu said, “In the Siva literature, lord Siva had highlighted the procedure for the worship of Siva, the brief of which is being explained by me.

At the end of the fire rites the process to be adopted is called as Abhyantara part. After performing the same, the Bahiryaga should not be performed.

The required articles should be well though, out in the mind and purifying them Deva Ganesa should be worshipped appropriately. Nandisa should be lodged to south while Suyasa should be adored in the north, the learned person should then think of the asana in his mind.

Getting ready for the worship, one should be seated over Simha-yoga, Padmasana or any clean seat which should have all the three tattvas.

Sitting over it one should meditate upon, Samba Siva, whose all the limbs are beautiful, attractive to the minds of all and possess all the auspicious marks.

He is the best of all, adorned with all the ornaments, having red face, hands and feet, wearing a serene smile over the face like the moon digit.

Having the complexion of the spotless crystal, having the eyes like the blossomed lotus flowers, with four arms, adorned with all the ornaments, wearing the beautiful digit of the moon over the head, clad in the deer skin, wearing the garland of snakes, besides the armlets, having he blue throat beyond comparison, accompanied with his kiths and the ganas. Mahesvari is lodged to his left. She has the splendour of the blossomed lotus flower, who should also be adored.

She has vast eyes resembling the blossomed lotus flowers. Here face resembles the full moon and has the black curly hair over the head.

She has the reflection of the blue lotus flowers. The crescent is lodged over her crown. She has round stiff and developed breasts.

She has a thin waist, large buttocks, and is clad in the thin yellow garments. She is adorned with all the ornaments, with a tilakam spot over the forehead.

She looks graceful with the flowers of different types decorating her braid. She possesses all the virtues. Her head is lowered due to shyness.

She carries the golden lotus in her hands. The other hand is placed over the seat like a danda, over which she is seated.

She destroys the worldly bondages. One should thus meditate upon Siva and Siva, seated over the auspicious Isana seat.

The devotee shall then worship with peity offering the flowers with all types. Or he can conceive the form of lord in any one of the following means like, Siva, Sadasiva, Mahesvara or the one having he name of the twenty six principles or as Srikantha. As the mantra-nyasa is performed in the body similarly in this form, the devotee can worship Siva who is beyond sat and asat as in the case of the outward worship. He shall complete the worship mentally.

He shall mentally imagine homa in the navel with the sacrificial twigs etc., then meditate on Siva in the centre of the eyebrows in the form of flame of the pure lamp. Thus in the mentally conceived auspicious worship in the body or independently, the rules including the concluding rites in the fire are the same. Or after concluding the imaginary worship the devotee shall worship the lord in Siva-linga form, or on the ground or the fire.

## Chapter 24 - Ritualistic worship of Siva

Upamanyu said, “For the purification of the place of worship, a devotee shall sprinkle the scented water over it with flowers or the sandal paste etc.

Removing the obstructions of the astra the kavaca should be covered. The astra shall then be placed on the side and he should conceive of the place of worship.

The land should be purified with the sprinkling of the water spreading the kusa grass there at the same time. All the vases as well as the materials should be purified.

He shall wash and sprinkle the vases of Proksani, Arghya, Padya and Acamana. After examining them he shall pour auspicious water in them. He shall place the sacred materials, whatever have been collected for the purpose.

The material for worship should include gems, silver, gold, fragrance, flowers, unbroken rice, five shoots, kusa grass and other auspicious materials.

Scent should particularly poured in the water meant for the taking of the bath as well the water meant for the purpose of drinking including the cool and pleasant flowers.

Khas (usira) should be put in the water meant for padya besides the sandal paste. Then making the powder of nutmeg, berry, camphor, Bahumula and tamalaka, should be added to the water for acamana. The cardmom seeds camphor and sandal should also be put in the vases.

In the arghya all these materials should also be placed together with the shoots of grass, unbroken rice, barley, gingelly seeds, besides other grains, ghee, white mustard, flowers and bhasma.

The articles to be included in the Proksani vase should include kusa grass, flowers, barley, Bahu-mula, and tamalaka with the ashes.

Everywhere, the mantra-nyasa should be done and outwardly covered with kavaca and securing it with as tra, Dhenu-mudra should be displayed.

All the articles for worship should be sprinkled with water from proksani vase reciting the mantras and should sanctify the same appropriately reciting the mula-mantra appropriately.

In the absence of the vases, the aspirant shall arrange the Prokasani vase in each holy rite like arghya etc. and the water from the same vase should be used.

Lord of Ganas should be adored first offering several types of food stuffs. After that near the southern door way, he should worship Nandi, the guard of the harem. Nandi resembles the lustre of the golden mountain and bedecked with all the ornaments. The crescent moon decorates his head. He is quite gentle in appearance having three eyes and four arms. His attributes include a trident issuing lustre, a deer, an axe, and a sharp pointed baton. He has the moon like face or alternatively, he could be monkey faced as well.

Towards the northern gate, Suyasa, the daughter of Marut is engaged in fondling the feet of the goddess Parvati. After adoring her one should enter the place of Paramesthi.

Worshipping the Siva-linga with these materials, the nirmalaya should be removed and washing the flower, it should be placed over the head for purification.

Holding the flower in his hand, he should recite the mantra as for as possible for the purpose of purification. Adoring Candadeva in the north east, nirmalya should be offered to him.

Then in the sequence of the adoration, the asana should be placed there. One should then conceive Adhara-Sakti, Kalyani and Syama over the ground.

Thereafter Ananta should be conceived with white complexion coiling over the ground, raising the serpenthood and appearing like licking of the sky.

Above that is the seat in the form of a lion of four feet representing virtue, knowledge, absence of attachment, glory and prosperity.

They are lodged respectively in the southeast, south-west, north-west and north east, having the white, red, yellow and black colours. Adharma and others are lodged in the eastern directions ending with the north. His body shall have the lustre of Rajavarta gem. The pure lotus serves him as his seat.

The lotus has eight petals representing the eight attributes like anima and others. Vama and other Saktis are saffron for him Rudra has Yama and other Saktis with him.

The Saktis like Manonmani are said to be the seeds. Vairagya is represented in the pericarp. The lotus stalk is represented by the knowledge of Sivatmaka.

The bulbous roots are the extremity of the pericarp with three zones, which shall be used the three tattvas of Siva.

Overall the asanas a divine seat refulgent with the spotless learnings and knowledge, is found, which is quite comfortable and covered over by a covering seat of colours.

The rite of invocation shall then be performed, besides installation, prevention surveying, obeisance, showing separate Mudras for each.

After offering the padya, acamana, arghya fragrance flowers, incense, tambula the devotee shall perform ablution to Siva.

Otherwise conceiving the image with the seat, the devotee should recite the basic mantra, Brahma-mantra as well as the Veda mantras.

Then Siva the prime cause should be invoked with Parvati. He is spotless like the crystal, is quite stable and the god without destruction.

He is the cause of all the lokas, has the form of all the lokas, he pervades inside and out. He is the smaller than the smallest and bigger than the biggest.

Lord Siva is indestructible and appears before the people without much efforts. He is invisible even for Brahma, Visnu, Indra, Rudra and others.

He is the essence of the Vedas. The people with wisdom have heard him as incomprehensible. He is beyond the beginning, middle or the end. He is the supreme medicine to relieve people from the worldly bondages.

He is also called the Siva-tattva, he stands for the welfare of the world. One should adore such a type of Siva-linga in Pancopacara manner.

The phallus is the image of Siva, the great Atman. While bathing the Siva-linga, the welfare words of victory should be recited.

Offering the pancagavya, ghee, milk, curd, honey, sugar, juice of fruits, besides fruits, gingelly seeds, mustard and grains, the seeds of barley, black gram powder, should be used as the paste, the Siva-linga should be bathed with hot water.

In order to keep Siva-linga free from pastes and other fragrant material, the wood apple leaves should be rubbed over it. Thereafter the linga should be bathed by Cakravarti method.

The phallic and the embodied image shall be washed with scented water, sprinkled with kusa grass and flowers or with the water from gold and gem besides the vases purified with the chanting of the mantra.

In case these materials are not available, whatever is available should be used. Simple water with the chanting of hymns could also be used for the ablution of Siva. The devotee shall perform the rites quite faithfully.

The water should be poured over the Sivalinga with a vase or a conch, or Vardhani or with the hand holding kusa grass and flowers repeating the mantras all the time.

The hymns of Pavamana, Rudra, Nila, Tvarita or the hymns of the linga-sukta or the hymns from Atharvasira-upanisad or the hymns from the Rgveda or the Samaveda conceiving Siva or the five Brahmanas, should be used for the ablution of the lord of the chief of the gods. The name Siva and Pranava should also be used.

There is hardly any difference in the manner in which the rite of ablution is performed in regard to the lord or goddess since they both are equal.

Initially, Mahadeva should be bathed, followed by Mahadevi. This has been ordained by the lord of the gods.

In the form of Ardhanarisvara, both are adorable and therefore there is no question of any precedence in the matter of adoration. Similarly the services should be rendered to the phallic or the embodied image.

Performing the abhiseka of linga, it should be wiped out with the auspicious clean cloth, followed by the offering of the costumes as well as the sacred thread.

Then the padya, water for sipping, arghya, fragrant flowers, ornaments, lamp, eatables and the water for the rinsing of the mouth should be offered.

This process should be followed by acamana betel leaf for the purification of the mouth besides the gem studded crown should also be offered.

The auspicious ornaments, several types of garlands, collyrium, flywhisk, chatra, fan of tala, besides the mirror should be offered. Then the musical instruments with welfare tunes should be played upon. The arati should be performed; thereafter this should be followed by the dance and music, besides shouting the slogans of victory.

In the gold, silver, copper or the earthen vases, the lord shall be worshipped, with lotuses, seeds, flowers, curd, unbroken rice, Nandyavarta- flowers, etc. in the forms of Srivatsa, mirror, Svastika, vajra etc. Eight lamps shall be belighted all round and one lamp shall be kept in the centre. In these the nine Saktis Yama etc. shall be adored.

After covering the Kavaca mantra, he shall project the cow mudra and lift the vase with both the hands.

Or alternatively, only five lamps, shall be kept of which four should be lodged in four quarters and one in the centre. Or only one lamp should be lighted.

Lifting the vase, the performer should whirl it thrice, over the Siva-linga in the manner of circummumbulation chanting the basic mantra.

Then the arghya shall be offered and the scented bhasma should be applied over the head. A handful of flower should then be offered and the rite of offering naivedya should be performed thereafter.

The drinking water shall be offered thereafter besides acamana once again. They tambula with five scented species should be offered.

The water should be sprinkled over all the material for worship accompanied with the dance and music. Then conceiving the presence of Siva and Siva in Siva-linga, the japam of Siva shall be performed as per his ability.

Then circumambulating, offering salutation and prayer, he shall dedicate himself, after which the submission of his desire shall be made with all humility.

Offering arghya with a handful of flowers, a mudra shall be displayed in accordance with the set procedure. Then he shall beg forgiveness, after which a ceremonial send off for the lord shall be arranged. The devotee shall meditate on the lord mentally.

In the condition of distress, the offerings shall be restricted to those starting from padya and ending with the offering of the betel leaves or alternatively starting from the offering of the Arghya or flowers, with pious mind.

Even this much is enough for earning the merits. The devotee shall not take food without worshipping Siva.

In case a sinner takes food, then there is no remedy for the atonement of his sins. In case he eats by mistake, then he should vomit the food making all the efforts.

Taking his bath, adoring both Siva and Siva, observing celibacy, he should recite the name of Siva, ten thousand times.

On the next day, donating gold to Siva or to his devotee, he should perform great puja, which purifies him.

## Chapter 25 - Adoration of Siva

Upamanyu said, “That what has not been stated for fear of the losing the sequence of worship, the same is being repeated by me in brief.

After offering the arati but before offering the homa the devotee shall perform the adoration of avarana or just on the arrival of the time of arati.

In the first avarana of Siva, the mantra of Rudra etc. upto as tra shall be used for japam. The five Brahmanas from Isana to Sadyojata shall be worshipped in the north east, east, south and north or in the west, south east, north east and south west or in the north west, north east and the other four quarters, beyond that he shall perform Garbhavarana repeating the mantras.

Performing the nyasa upto the heart, he shall perform worship. Thereafter he shall adore Indra in the east and Yama in the south.

A learned person should worship Varuna in the west, Kubera in the north, Isana in the north east, fire in the south east, besides the weapons from thunderbolt to the lotus outside the lotus.

He shall adore all the well known forms of the lords in quarters in due order. Looking at the lord and the goddess, with folded hands he shall meditate upon them, who are comfortably lodged over their respective places. The deities of the avarana shall be worshipped with their names with the word namah added at the lust offering flowers as well as the salutation at the same time. He shall worship Garbhavarana with its avarana.

The havis of the six types shall be given as pure rice or the rice mixed with green gram in the yoga meditation irrespective of its being internal or external mixing together, the payasam, curd, sugarcane balls, and honey, shall be offered with side dishes.

The best of churned curd mixed with sugar or sugarcane balls should be offered with jaggery and the tasteful fruits.

The red sandal paste, flowers and drinking water should also be offered in which should be mixed a piece of Areca nut soaked in cardamom juice.

Betel leaves with khadira etc. shall be given white and yellow are auspicious. The white lime powder shall be rocky but neither very hard nor defective.

The camphor, Kankola and Jasmin if fresh, are considered to be auspicious for Siva's worship. As an unguent, the sandal should be in the form of powder.

The lower stem is better while the musk and the saffron shall be pasted. Only fragrant flowers are holy and fit for use.

The flowers without smell or those with abnoxious smell defective, stale or broken shall not be used in the worship of Siva.

The clothes of fine quality embroidered with gold thread, glittering ornaments, shall be given with camphor, gum, resin, sandal, well fumigated and rendered fragrant with flowers, should be given.

The incense mixed with sandal paste, gum-resin, camphor, ghee and honey combinedmake the best of incense.

Fragrant ghee is made of the milk of tawny cows mixed with camphor is best for the lighting of the lamps.

Pancagavya comprising of the sweet milk of tawny cow as also of the curd and ghee is favourite of Siva for the purpose of bath and drink.

Seats of ivory, gold, studded with gems and covering cloth of various colours should be used.

The cushions stuffed with catton, soft pillows and comfortable pleasant beds shall be used.

The cool water collected from the great rivers or from the rivers joining the ocean is considered to be the best for drinking as well as taking bath.

The moon like umbrella should be used and should be studded with pearls and nine varieties of gems. Its handle should be charming, divine, and made of gold.

The flywhisks should be of extra whtle colour, embellished with gold and their handles shall be studded with gems and should be shining like the royal swans.

There should be the shining mirror, quite smooth and polished, over which divine and sweet smelling paste shall be applied. The gems should be studded around the same besides being decorated with garlands.

The conch which should be white like swan, kunda flowers or the moon, issuing a deep majestic sound roaring like the ocean. At the mouth back and other places it should be studded in gems and framed in gold.

The bugles and other musical instruments should be made of gold studded with pearls. They shall be capable of producing different notes.

The drums of various types like bheri, double drums, cymbals, timiccha and pataha shall be used, capable of producing the roaring sound of the ocean.

All the pots and vases should be quite beautiful and their support bases should be made of gold.

The temple of Siva should be designed on the basis of the literature on architecture resembling a king's palace.

It should be surrounded by high boundary walls. The gopuras should be quite high like the mountains, studded with various types of gems, having the doors of gold.

It should have a hundred columns made of molten gold, studded with gems. The canopy shall be decorated with the pearls while the festivals at the gateway should be resplendent with the card.

Its tops shall be decorated with golden domes resembling the divine crowns and marked with the divine weapons.

It should have royal buildings suitable for the use of the rulers, approachable by royal paths, besides the palaces with high canopies on all the four sides.

It should have excellent assembly halls, spread in all the quarters appearing like an inner rampart.

It should have thousands of artisans well-versed in dance and music and also adept in playing on flute and lutes.

It should be protected by the powerful guards and watchmen. There should be enough of elephants, horses and chariots, besides the gardens, orchards, and artificial lakes.

Several of the stepwells should the placed on all the directions. It shall be inhabited by the Brahmana devotee of Siva well-versed in the truth about the Vedas and utter Vedic literature and other scriptures.

They should possess all the symptoms of the Siva Sastras, engaged in the devotion of Siva, peaceful, jolly by nature and the noble devotees should always be present there.

They should be served by the devotees of Siva always. Thus the temple of Siva as per the prescribed interior and exterior should be made, according to his means, whether rich or poor, through the riches honestly earned by him with the cut stones, wood, bricks or mud in the auspicious forest or the mountain, over the river bank, temple or some other auspicious place, in the auspicious house, irrespective of his being rich or poor according to his means.

One should adore the god with devotion with wealth honestly earned by him. In case one adores Siva with the wealth earned by him by unfair means, even then he will not earn the adverse reward, because, the lord is mainly concerned with the devotion and is subservient to the same.

In case a person adores Siva, with the wealth earned by him by fair means without devotion, it is not going to yield any good reward to him, because it is the devotion which yields the reward.

The benefit of even a little or great service rendered by a poor or a rich man according to the affluence of Siva with devotion is the same.

Even a poor person overwhelmed with devotion should adore Siva, but a rich person without devotion should not adore the lord.

No merit is going to yield to a rich person devoid of the devotion of Siva, who adores Siva, offering everything to him, because the absence of the devotion is the main reason for the same.

A person devoid of devotion can never achieve Siva, even after he performs the great yajnas and hard tapas.

O Krsna, this is the secret of the secrets in regard to the lord, this is an admitted fact that a devotee gets liberated through the devotion.

The recitation of Siva’s mantras, performing of homa and yajna penance besides learnings and giving away of the gifts and the study of the Vedas are all leading to piety undoubtedly.

The impure person, devoid of devotion, after doing everything, but having a heart fully devoted is liberated without doing anything.

For a devotee of Siva, thousands of Candrayana vrata, hundreds of Prajapatyas and other monthly fasts are of no consequence.

For petty pleasures, many people perform tapas in the mountain caves, but a devotee of Siva is liberated by devotion alone.

The Sattvika deeds bestow liberation. The yogis remain steadfast by means of Sattva alone. The ritualistic perform rajasika rites, bestowing Siddhis because they are covered by rajas-gunas.

Asuras and the demons, possessing the tamas-guna, and similar types of persons, adore the lord for seeking worldly pleasures.

Irrespective of their attitude being Sattvika or Rajasika or Tamasika, a person performing worship with devotion attains welfare.

Because it is the boat of devotion, which has been made for the safety of the devotees. What has a devoted person to do with sattva, rajas and tamas.

O Sri Krsna, irrespective of anyone being outcaste, degraded, foolish and a fallen man, but in case he is devoted to Siva, he becomes adorable by the gods as well as the asuras.

Therefore one should worship Siva by all means with devotion because a person not devoted to Siva achieves no benefit anywhere.

O Krsna, I shall reveal before you a great secret. You please listen. This truth has been spoken by the people of wisdom well-versed in the Vedas.

## Chapter 26 - Adoration of Siva with connected rites

Upamanyu said, “The killer of a Brahmana, the drunkard, the thief, the one who defiles the wife of the preceptor, besides the killer of the parents and the one who destroys a child in the womb, is freed from the relative sins adoring Siva, with devotion, even without reciting any mantra in twelve years time.

Therefore, even the fallen person should adore Siva making all the efforts. Only a devotee is freed from all the sins none else, even when he has controlled all the sensual organs, and living on begging.

Even after committing the grave sin, reciting the five syllabled mantra with devotion, when a person adores the lord, he is surely freed from all the sins.

By inhaling air and consuming waters, the one who weakens the body, he cannot achieve the Sivaloka by performing of the vratas.

A person who adores Siva even once with devotion, reciting the five syllabled mantra, he also with the influence of Siva, reaches the abode of Siva.

Therefore, all the tapas, yajnas, donating everything in charities, would not measure as a the croreth part of the worship of Siva.

Irrespective of one’s being free or in bondage, a devotee reciting the five syllabled mantra is surely freed.

The one who adores Siva with Rudra or Arudra Sukta, irrespective of his being a foolish or a degraded one, he gets liberated in the first attempt.

A devotee, who overpowering the anger adores Siva with the six syllabled mantra or the Sukta-mantra and without having a preceptor, still he would be as good as the one who has patronise preceptor.

Though a person having received initiation from the preceptor would be better, and he is liberated with Brahmanga or hamsa.

Therefore one should daily adore Siva, and twice or thrice reciting the Sukta mantra.

Those who adore Mahadeva, they should be treated as Mahesvara. Such of the people who have not adored Siva with the self supporting knowledge,

They keep on wandering in the miserable world. The one who achieving the inaccessible human body, does not adore Siva, he remains unfit for liberation. Therefore his life is of no consequence. Such of the people who adore Siva after achieving the inaccesible human birth,

Their life becomes successful. Such a person should be treated as the best of humans and his birth is successful. The one who is engaged in the devotion of Siva, and offers his salutation to him, he does not to face mesery.

Those who always remember Siva, they remain free from the miseries. They have palatial building and their wives are adorned with ornaments.

With the adoration of Siva, one achieves enough of wealth. Those who aspire for the heavenly pleasures and the heavenly kingdoms,

They should always adore the lotus like feet of Siva. The fortunes, pleasant looks, Sattva, remuneration, compensation and

Prowess besides the world fame is achieved only by the devotee of Siva. Therefore, leaving aside everything one should concentrate his mind on Siva.

Those who are interested in their own welfare, they should worship Siva daily. The youthful age and the life is sure to depart shortly.

The body attracts the ailments in no time, therefore, one should adore Siva. Before the arrival of the old age and death,

Till the organs of senses do not get weak, one should keep on adoring Siva till then. There is no other dharma in the world better than the adoration of Siva.

Thus realising one should adore Siva making all the efforts, and setting up an orchard one should serve food to the children.

One should resort to the performing of the festivities in house daily after performing of the worship of Siva, the prasada should be distributed to the servants, or the guards employed in the palace besides the kiths. He should also visit the Siva temple.

Then he should offer the flowers, water, incense and the lamp. In front of the Mahapitha, facing the north, the offerings should be made.

Food and other items which have been offered to Siva, the rest of it should be offered to Canda, the gana of Siva.

Performing the home appropriately the worship should be brought to an end. Thus performing, a devotee should recite mantra as much as possible.

He should perform the festivities as per Saiva discipline. In a metal vase with red lotus flowers,

The divine Pasupata weapon should be written and after invoking it, the adoration should be placed over the head of a Brahmana.

He shall hold a lighted torch with dance and songs supported by the auspicious instrumental music, the party should go round the temple of the lord thrice. The movement should be neither quick nor slow. Then the devotee should stand at the door with folded hands in reverence and then dismiss the astra ceremoniously. After going round once more, he should offer eight flowers concluding the worship.

## Chapter 27 - Performing of Yajna

Upamanyu said, “Now I shall spell out the method of the performing of fire sacrifice consecrating the fire appropriately and then adoring Mahadeva, homa has to be performed.

The fire should be ignited in sacred pits, raised ground or in an altar. Then the fire shall be taken, in an iron vase, or a mud vase in accordance with the prescribed junctions and then transferred to the actual place of sacrifice. The lord should be adored after the consecration of the fire.

The pit may be one or two hands in width. The altar should either be square or circular.

An eight petalled lotus should be made in the altar and should be two or four angulas in height above the altar.

The navel within the altar shall be two vitastis high. The distance between the angula and the middle finger has to be an angula. Twenty four angula make a hasta. Three, two or one mekhala should also be made.

Smooth clay should be used for the making of the altar. In the centre of the mekhala to the west or to the south, passage shall be made like the asvattha leaf or like the lower lip of the elephant, a little lower then the fire and should close in gradually.

The mekhala should be lifted a little from the forepart, a little away from the vedi, without transgressing its height, the clay or the sand should be used in its formations.

The kunda should be made of clay and the altar shall be smeared with cowdung and water.

The vase should be heated and then washed with clean water. According to the method prescribed in one’s own Sutra, the devotee should draw lines.

The seat of the fire should be sprinkled with water and the durbha grass and kusa grass should be spread over the same together with flowers to serve as the seat to the fire god. All the essential materials required for the yajna should be places there.

Such of the metals requiring washing should be washed and purified. The fire should be brought in a supporting vase, which should be one pervaded from crystals, gems etc. or from wood. The fire should be brought from the house of a Brahmana well versed in the Vedas. It should be moved around the sacrificial altar thrice repeating the bija-mantra of the fire. The fire shall be placed in the appropriate seat, through the passage or straight in the front.

The acarya then seated near the passage, should look at the fire and then place it in the nabhi-randhra like a spark in the altar.

Till the igniting of the fire, and till the completion of the ajya-samskara he should adore the image of Siva.

As per the process prescribed in his respective Sutra, the acarya well versed in the mantras, worshipping the image of Siva with the basic mantra from the right,

Perform the nyasa reciting the mantra and then display the dhenu-mudra. Then Sruk and Sruva should be made of the metal, by the bronze, iron but glass should not be used for the purpose.

These shall be made of the sacrificial wood described in the Smrtis and approved by the artisans. The leave of Brahma-vrksa should be without lotus.

Sprinkling water over them with kusa grass, heating them in the fire and water should be sprinkled over them reciting the Siva mantra from the Sutras.

The leaves shall be scrubbed with the darbha grass. Then offering shall then be made in the fire, with eight bija-mantras. The seven bijas of the seven flames are known as Bhrum, Stum, Brum, Srum, Pum, Drum and Drum.

These seven bijas are the seven tongues of Agni. The central one is knower as Trisikha also known as Bahurupa. One of its flames moves to the right and the other to the left and keeps on rising. The flame to east is yellow, the one to the south east is red, the one to the south west is black and the other one is refulgent. As is its name, it is brilliant.

The bija-mantra should be suffixed with the word Svaha. Reciting the jihva-mantra, the offering of the ghee should be made, one by one.

Then reciting the mantra ram vanha svaha, three offerings should be made of ghee or Samidha (sacrificial articles).

With this performance it turns into Sivagni. Then he should think of the seat of Siva. Siva in Ardhanarisvara should be invoked and adored. Then the Samidha should be used for homa.

These Samidhas should be of Palasa, to the tree of the yajna, each one of which should be twelve angulas in length. They should be dry, without spots and should have dried naturally.

Otherwise, they should be of ten fingers in length and should have the thickness of the little finger. In case the Samidhas of the requisite rice is not available, then whatever type of Samidha is available should be used for the purpose.

Or otherwise the Samidhas should be of the form of leaves of Durva and could be four angulas in size. The offering of the ghee should be given thereafter. This should be followed with the ahuti of a tola of food.

The fried paddy, mustard seeds and the gingelly seeds should be mixed in ghee. If possible the bhaksya, lehya and cosya stuff could be used for making the offerings.

According to one’s competence, one should give ten, five or three offerings. It is fine even if one Ahuti is made.

Dropping the ghee with Sruva (wooden spoon), the homa should be performed at the divine or saintly spot.

In case all the materials are not available the homa should be performed according to one’s means with a single available stuff. For the purpose of repentance, the stuff should be sanctified and three ahutis should be given.

The remainent part of ghee from homa should be filled in the Sruva and the flowers should be placed before it and with the optioned Sruva should be covered with the kusa grass, should make an anjali with hands, reciting the basic mantra and then pour the stream of ghee while standing before the alter. Vausat, should be uttered.

Thus offering Purnahuti in the homa he should sprinkle the water as before. Thereafter the lord should be made to depart, protecting the fire of the yajna.

Or otherwise one should bid farewel to the fire as well and placed in the umbilicus of the altar and worshipped daily. Or alternatively he should bring the fire as per the procedure laid down in the Siva Sastras, should consecrate the fire born of the womls of Vagisvari, appropriately and adore the same. The sacrifical fuel shall be put on the fire again and the sacred stick laid around the fire covered with cloth.

Keeping two vases, Siva should be adored, the Proksani vase, should be washed with clean water.

After the Sruk and Sruva are purified, the rites of garbhadhana, (Impregnation, a samskara performed after menstruation to ensure or facilitate conception) punsavana (first purification samskara causing the birth of a son) and Simantonnayana (One of the twelve samskaras observed by woman in the fourth, sixth and eighth month of her pregnancy) shall be performed with the rites of homa in each case.

Agni shall be conceived as having three feet, seven hands, four horns, two heads, having the yellow complexion like honey, three eyes, wearing the matted locks of hair and the head adorned with a crescent and clad in red garments, with the body plastered with the red paste adorned with rosary and garlands, having all the auspicious symptoms and wearing the mekhala and the sacred thread.

Sakti, Sruk and Sruva should be held in right hands while tomara, a fan of tala tree and vase of ghee should be held in other hands.

He should be adored at the time of the birth of a child in this form, while performing the birth rites. The unbiblical card shall be removed and the purificatory rites for the post natal pollution shall be performed. The rite of giving name to the child should be performed in Sivagni with due ahuti. The rite of the ceremonial dismissal of the parents as well as the of the tonsure, and sacred thread shall be performed till the end of Aptoryama. As a consecratory rite, the homa of ghee shall be performed.

With the bija-mantra of rath the water shall be sprinkled over Agni, Brahma, Visnu, Siva, Isana, and Lokapalas.

Their weapons should also be adored. For the sake of incense and lamp, fire shall be take out by the expert devotee.

Arranging all the dravyas mentioned earlier including ghee, should be arranged properly. Agni should be invoked, placing an asana there.

Adoring both Siva and Siva, homa should be performed with purnahuti. Otherwise according to the method of his own asrama the fire sacrifices and the adoration of Siva should be made.

All this has to be performed by a devotee of Siva. There is no other method to be adopted in this case. The bhasma of Sivagni or the homa should be used for application over the body.

The bhasma of the fire of the marriage rites is extremely auspicious. The cowdung of the Kapila cow is always auspicious, which is carried in hand, while falling on earth.

In case the cowdung had fallen on earth, then one should collect the middle one, discarding the upper and the lower parts. Making a ball of it, it should be dried up, then it should be offered to the fire reciting the mula-mantra of Siva. Leaving the half burnt or over burnt part, only the white bhasma should be collected.

It should then be mixed and should be kept in the vase of bhasma, which should be made of a metal, wood, stone or of some other auspicious material. The bhasma vase should be stored at the auspicious place, duly secured like the wealth.

In case one has to go somewhere, one should carry the vase of bhasma himself or make his servant to do so. The bhasma should not be allowed to be carried in incompetent hands or by an curable person. It should not be touched with the feet, nor should it be neglected. It should not be transgressed.

Carrying the bhasma it should be used at an appropriate time and not otherwise. It should not be given to an unfit person.

Before the sending off the lord, bhasma should be applied over the body. The bhasma used earlier, becomes Canda bhasma after the departure of the lord.

After performing the fire rites, the bali rites should be performed according to the Sivasastra or one’s own Sutra.

Then after covering the seat of Vidya over the well arranged mandala, he shall install the sheath of Vidya and worship the same, with flowers etc. in due order.

In front of the seat of Vidya, the seat of the preceptor should also be arranged. After arranging the seat there, the preceptor shall be adored with flowers etc.

Then the adorable person shall be worshipped and those hungry shall be provided with food. The devotee shall take wholesome food comfortably.

For self purification he should consume the remanant food of the lord. But the dedicated or the Canda food should never be consumed.

The same procedure has to be followed in the fragrance as well as the garlands. A learned person under these circumstances should never think that “I am Siva”.

Performing acamana after taking the food, devoting his mind to Siva, he should recite the basic mantra. A man should spend his time in the deliberations on Siva Sastra with man.

After the expiry of the first Prahara of the night, adoring Siva and Parvati, a pleasant and comfortable bed should be arranged.

Then he shall offer physically or mentally various food items garments, flower garlands in a charming way.

The devotee shall then go to bed, at the feet of the lord and the goddess, the house holder shall sleep there with his wife, while others shall sleep alone.

In the early morning, he shall get up reciting the Adi-mantra and mentally offer his salutation to the eternal lord with his ganas.

After washing himself he shall offer adoration to the lord and the goddess with the divine sound of conch and other musical instruments.

Then he shall start the worship of Siva with just blossomed flowers, according to the method specified earlier, both Siva and Siva.

## Chapter 28 - Compulsory and optional rites

Upamanyu said, “I shall now explain the method of the rites to be performed by the followers of the Saivite way of life, under certain conditions, as provided in the Saiva literature.

This is the great worship which has to be performed in each fortnight on the eighth and the fourteenth day besides on the full moon day or the new Moonday in both the fortnights. It is required to be performed in the tropical and equinotical transit of the sun and also during the eclipses, by a devotee as per his worth.

In every month, he shall prepare the brahmakurca or pancagavya and should offer bath to Siva. The left over of the same should be consumed by him.

One is relieved of the sins of killing of a Brahmana and others with the consuming of the pancagavya and no sin is left out.

In the Pusya constellation of Pausa, the arati of Siva should be performed. During the Magha constellation of the month of Magha, he should give away in charity ghee and the blankets.

In the month of Phalguna in the full moon day of Uttara-phalguni, festivities should be arranged. During the month of Caitra, in the full moon falling in Citra constellation, the Dola-utsava should be celebrated appropriately.

During the month of Vaisakha, in the full moon day of the Visakha constellation a Siva temple of flowers should be made. During the month of Jyestha, in the Mula constellation, a pitcher filled with cool water should be given away in charity.

During the Uttarasadha constellation in the month of Asadha, the rite of investiture with sacred thread, on full moon day, shall be performed. During the month of Sravana, the aforesaid mandales should be set up.

During the Sravana constellation and subsequently on the full moon day of Bhadrapada, sprinkling of the water should be done, while during the Purvasadha constellation, the swimming should be done.

On the day of the full moon in the month of Asvin, the fresh cooked rice as well the payasam should be given in charity. Thereafter homa should be performed in the Satabhisa constellation.

On the day of Kartika Purnima during the Krttika constellation, a thousand lamps should be lighted. During the Ardra constellation and Siva should be bathed with ghee during the day.

In case these actiities cannot be performed during these occasions, then one should organise festivities alone. He can organise small or big gatherings, or perform the great worship.

On occasions when the auspicious activities are performed, or when the mind feels painful and dejected, when the conduct of the life is defiled, witnessing the bad dreams, having an encounter with the wicked people, when the evil dreams are witnessed, or while suffering from grave ailments, the devotee shall perform the ceremonial ablutions, perform worship, recitations, meditations, sacrifices or other sacred rites or indulge in charities in an appropriate man, together with Puruscarana. When the series of the Siva fire are broken, it should be revived.

One who is engaged in adoration of Siva and such activities daily, he achieves liberation in a single birth.

A person who regularly performs the compulsory and optional rites, attains the divine and the primordial place of Siva.

A man, enjoying all the divine pleasure, in the Sivaloka for a hundred crore of Kalpas, he in due course of time attains the abode of Uma, Kartikeya, and also enjoy his stay for long in the abodes of Visnu, Brahma, and Rudra. Again he goes up and transcends the five regions. Securing the knowledge of Siva; he finally reaches the abode of Siva.

A person who performs half the number of the said holy rites, in one or two linwes, he secures knowledge and embraces Siva's Sayujya.

A person who performs one fourth of the said rites, he after his death, crossing the universe achieves the two invisible upper Bhuvanas, achieves Rudra's place and enjoys the several worldly pleasures for many thousand yugas, after the decline of his merits, falls on earth and is reborn in a high family. Because of his earlier Sanskaras, he remains illustrious there as well.

Discarding the dharma of the ordinary people, he is engaged in Siva dharma and because of the excellence of his dharma, devoting himself to Siva, he achieves the place of Siva.

After achieving enormous pleasures, he achieves the position of Vidyesvara, where he enjoys all the pleasures with the Visvesvaras, again he has a round inside and outside the globe. Then he, achieving the best of devotion and earns Siva's knowledge from the same besides the great devotion. After getting his identity with Siva, he does not return to the earth again.

He is turned as an emperor and is invesed with the right in the rituals of Siva. A person desirous of welfare, shall seek refuge in Siva and perform his holy rights. But we do not force anyone to adopt any means.

Neither in opportunities nor over discussing are convincing. The rites connected with the worship of Siva, appeal to some people, because of their merits and with the earlier impression they invoke, if the cause of worldliness in their case is not going to help. Therefore in case one is interested in the welfare of his soul, he should deeply think over all these things according to his nature and devote himself in the adoration of Siva.

## Chapter 29 - The Kamya rites

Sri Krsna said, “O lord, I have heard from your auspicious month the words which are authentic like the Vedas, which ordain the performance of the compulsory and the optional rites conceiving the devotion of Siva. Now I intend to be enlightened over the kamya formations of the devotees of Siva. You kindly tell me.”

Upamanyu said, ‘‘Some of the rites yield fruits in this worlds while some of them yield, fruit in the next world. The karmas are of five types which yield the reward.

Some of the karmans are of worldly type, some of them are related to the performing of tapas.

Some are related to the performing of the meditation, while others cover all. The performing of homa while charities and devotion are homa and worship both.

Only those possessing Sakti, are successful in their karmans and not the others. The command of lord Siva at once is treated to be the Sakti.

Therefore a Brahmana should always obey the command relating to the kamya- karmas. Now I am going to speak out the Kamya-karmas which yield the fruit in both the lokas.

The devotees of Siva, should perform in the sequence of the internal and external karmans because there is no difference in Siva and Mahesvara.

Therefore there is hardly any difference between the devotees of Siva and Mahesvara. A learned person who lives in the asrama of Siva, is known as other Mahesvaras, performing the karmayajnas on earth. Because of this the Saivas perform the internal karmas while Mahesvaras perform the outward karmas.

There is no difference in the usages of the karmas which are now being defined. One should minutely examine the fragrance, complexion and juice etc. of the ground appropriately.

A beautiful canopy should be made appealing to the mind. The ground should be so plastered, so as to look like a mirror.

A diagrams of one or two hands should be made as per the provision of the Sastras to the east.

A beautiful lotus should be drawn over the same, which should be of eight petals with a pericarp, drawn by means of the gold dust or grain dust etc. collected at convenience.

It shall have five Avaranas and should be quite splendid. The Siddhis shall be conceived in the petals. Vamadeva and other Rudras along with their respective Saktis, should be lodged in the filaments. Varuna and other deities shall be placed in the petals beginning with the eastern one. Vairagya is to be stationed in the pericarp, the same Saktis in the seeds, Saivaite holy rites in the bulbous root, and knowledge of Siva in the stalk. Above the pericarp the discs of the fire, the sun and the moon shall be conceived. Siva, Vidya and Atma shall be conceived beyond that. Siva shall be lodged over all the seats, with the flowers, of various colours.

Amba with Siva shall be adored with five avaranas. Siva has to be as spotless as the crystal gem, with a delightful face and issuing cool lustre. He has the crown of the matted locks of hair, resembling circle of lightning. He wears a tiger skin, wearing a serene serene over his lotus like face. His soles, palms and the lips resemble the petals of the red lotus. He is richly endowed with all the characteristics and is adorned with all the ornaments and equipped with excellent weapons. He has divine scent and unguents. He has five faces and ten arms. The crescent moon decorates his head.

His eastern face is gentle, with the lustre of the sun with three lotus like eyes, and the crescent for the crest.

The southern face has the complexion of the clouds, with crooked eyebrows. It has a terrible look with curved fangs. No one could ever dare to offend the same. He has throbbing lips. The northern face has the colour of coral with blue forelocks. It has charming movements. It has three eyes and is decorated with a crescent. The western face has three brilliant eyes and the lustre of the full moon. The crescent moon is also placed over the same. It is gentle and is charming with smile. The fifth face resembles the crystal, resplendent with the crescent moon. It is quite serene and looks gentle, having three shining eyes.

The attributes of his right hands include a shining trident, an axe vajra, a sword and fire. In his left hands, he holds the serpent arrow, bell, noose and a goad.

The nivrttikala encloses him upto the knees, the Pratistha-kala upto the naval, the Vidyakala upto the neck and Santakala to the forehead. A bone that is covered by Santyatikala.

Thus pervading the five pathways, the five of his kalas are lodged in his body. The lord has Isana as his coronet. He is the eternal Purusa.

Agora represents his heart. Vamadeva is his secret parts, while Sadyojata represent his feet. He is body has thirty eight kalas.

Isana represents Matrkas besides the five Brahmanas. He comprises of omkara as well as the Hamsa Sakti.

His Iccha-sakti is lodged in his kamandalu. His right side is flanked by Jnana-sakti, and the left by kriyasakti. Sadasiva as the form of Vidya is equated with the trie of tattvas. The Murti shall, be conceived with the basic mantra and everything shall be combined into one unit. Until the arghya he shall be duly worshipped with the basic mantras. Then Siva shall be invoked with great Sakti in the embodied form. The lord who is devoid of Sat and asat shall be invoked and worshipped with five articles of worship.

He shall adored with five Brahmanas and six angas. With Matrikas, repeating the Pranava he will worship Siva and Sakti both calmly. Thereafter he shall perform the Pancavarana puja, offering padya etc. upto Mukhavasa. But the rite of Prasthapana (sending off) shall not be performed.

## Chapter 30 - Avarana worship of Siva

Upamanyu said, “Starting from the right or the left, both Siva and Siva, Ganesa and Kartikeya shall be offered fragrance, unbroken rice, flowers etc., first of all.

Thereafter all the Paiica brahman with their saktis should be adored from Isana to Sadyojata in the first Avarana.

Thereafter Hrdayanyasa with Sadanga should be performed. Siva and Siva should then be adored in the south east.

Then the eight Rudras including Mahadeva should be adored with their Saktis.

O Sri Krsna, this is the first avarana which has been explained by me. Now I shall highlight the second avarana and you listen to the same with devotion.

In the leaf of the east side of eight petals, Ananta should be adored with his Sakti lodged to his left. Suksma should be adored with his Sakti towards the western direction.

In the leaf to the western side Siva with Sakti and in the leaf to the north Ekanetra should be worshipped.

A Rudra with his Sakti should be worshipped in the south eastern petal. Trimurti with his Sakti should be adored in the south eastern petal.

Sri Kantha with his Sakti should be lodged over the south western petal, while Sikhandisa should be worshipped with his Sakti over the north western petal.

In the second avarana Cakravartis should be lodged, while in the third avarana should be lodged the Astamurtis, with their Saktis.

They shall be adored in eight quarters from east onwards in a sequence. The Asta-murti comprise of Bhava, Sarva, Isana, Rudra, Pasupati, Ugra, Bhima and Mahadeva. Subsequently the eleven murtis including that of Mahadeva and others shall be worshipped with their Saktis.

The eleven murtis comprise of Mahadeva, Siva, Rudra, Sankara, Nilalohita, Isana, Vijaya, Bhima, Devadeva, Bhavodhbhava and Kapardisa. The first eight shall be adored in the south eastern comer onwards. Devadeva has to be adored in the eastern direction Bhavodeva shall be adored in the centre.

In the same avarana Vrsendra is to be adored first. Nandi should be adorned to the right, while Mahakala has to be worshipped or the north.

Sastra should be adored in the south eastern petal, or over the petal, to the south of the goddess. Ganesa has to be worshipped in the south western petal while Sanmukha in the western petal. The goddess Jyestha has to be adored in the north western petal. Gauri is to be worshipped in the north and Canda in the north east. Munindra shall be adored between Sastra and Nandisa.

Pingala should be worshipped to the north of Mahakala. Bhrngisvara has them to be adored in the middle of the Sastra of the Matr group.

Virabhadra has to be worshipped in the space between Matrs and Vighnesa. Goddess Sarasvati has to be worshipped in between Skanda and Vighnesa.

Sri is lodged at the feet of Siva, where she should be adored between Jyestha and Kumara. He shall worship Mahamoti is between Jyestha and Amba.

The goddess Durga should be worshipped between Ganamba and Canda. In the same avarana, he shall worship the hosts of Siva'a attendants.

After performing the japam appropriately, with a purified mind the female friends of Siva, along with the Saktis of Rudra, Pramathas and Bhutas, should be worshipped.

After worshipping thus the third avarana, he shall worship the fourth avarana outside it, after meditation.

The sun shall then be adored in the east Brahma in the south, Rudra in the west and Visnu in the petal to the north.

There are separate avaranas for all the four lords. His six limbs shall be worshipped at the outset together with Dipta and other Saktis.

From the east, the goddess like Dipta, Suksma, Jaya, Bhadra, Vibhuti, Vimala, Amogha and Vidyuta, shall be worshipped.

The four lords shall be worshipped in the second dvaram in the sequence from east to north, followed by their Saktis.

In the east, Aditya, Bhaskara, Bhanu, Ravi, Arka, Brahma, Rudra and Visnu, are the Vivasvana, extending to south. Bodhini is in the west and Apyayini in the north.

The second avarana shall be worshipped with Usa, prabha, Prajna and Sandhya after fixing them in Isana etc.

In the third dvaram Soma (moon), Angaraka (Mars), Buddha (Mercury) Brhaspati the most excellent one known as the most intelligent one, Illustrious Sukra (Venus), Saturn, Rahu and Ketu, the smoke-coloured and the terrible Dhumaketu be worshipped.

Or he shall worship the twelve Adityas in the second avarana and twelve Rsis in the third Avarana.

Externally, he shall adore groups of seven ganas each, besides the Rsis, gods, Gandharvas, serpents, apsaras, gramanis, yaksas, yatudhanas, Asvagrivas and seven Balakhilyas.

Thus adoring the sun in the third avarana, Brahma should be adored in the three avaranas.

Hiranyagarbha should be adored in the east, Viraja in the south, Kala in the west and Purusa in the north.

Hiranyagarbha is the first, Brahma resembles the lotus, Krsna is like the mountain of collyrium and Purusa resembles the crystal gem. avarana

These as well as the three gunas, viz. sattva, rajas and tamas are lodged us in the first avarana.

In the second avarana in the sequence of eastern directions etc. Sanatkumara, Sanaka, Sanandana and Sanatana should be adored.

In the third avarana the Prajapatis should be worshipped. The firs eight of them are Daksa and others, who should be adored in a sequence from the east.

They are known by the names of Daksa, Ruci, Bhrgu, Marici, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Atri, Kasyapa and Vasistha. These are the well known Prajapatias. Their wives are also to be adored properly.

The names of the chaste ladies are Prasuti, Akuti, Khyati, Sambhuti, Dhrti, Smrti, Ksama, Sannati, Anusuya as well as Arundhati- the mother of the gods. All of them have a respectable place in the worship of Siva.

Or otherwise the four Vedas should be adored in the first avarana. The Itihasas and the Puranas should be adored in the second avarana.

The dharmasastras are to be adored in the third avarana, together with all the Vedic lores on all the four sides.

Starting from the east, the Vedas and the post Vedic literature should be adored in the four or eight ways.

Thus adoring Brahma in three avaranas, Rudra should be adored to the south and the west with out avaranas.

Brahmasadanga (the five Brahmans and the six limbs) are his prathama-varana. The second avarana consists of Vidyesvara.

The third dvaram has a difference, which is being brought out starting from the east their four images should be worshipped.

The lord possesses of three gums. As Siva, he shall be adored in the east. The rajas creator Brahma shall be worshipped a Bhava in the south. The tamasika Agni shall be worshipped as Hara in the west. The sattvika bestower of happiness viz., Visnu shall be worshipped as Mrda in the north.

Thus twenty six images of Siva should be adored in the west and Vaikuntha should be adored in the north.

Keeping Vasudeva in the forefront, he should be adored in the first avarana. Pradyumna and Aniruddha should be adored in the south,

Samkarsana Balarama should be adored in the east or alternatively they should be adored in the opposite directions. This has already been stated in the first avarana. Now we shall speak about the auspicious second avarana.

Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, Vamana, Rama, Krsna and Asvagriva, should be adored in the eastern part of the third avarana. The infallible Narayanastra should be adored in the south.

Pancajanya conch should be adored in the west, while the Sarnga bow should be adored to the east. In this way making the three images Paramahari, known as Visna. Mahavisnu, Sadavisnu, should be adored in the third avarana. Besides the four images of Visnu should be adored together with their four Saktis.

He shall worship Prabha in the south east, Sarasvati in the south west, Ganambika in the north west and Laksmi in the north east.

After worshipping the sun and other forms as well as their Saktis, he shall worship the lords of the worlds in the same avarana.

He shall worship Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirriti, Varuna, Vayu, Soma, Kubera and Isana should be adored.

Thus adorning the fourth avarana appropriately, he should worship the weapons of Mahesvara.

Then he will worship the shining trident, in the north east, Vajra in the east, axe in the south east, arrow in the south, the sword in the south west, noose in the west, goad in the north west, Pinaka in the north, and the Ksetrapala in the west. After adoration of the fifth avarana thus, properly, he shall worship the great bull in the east, along with the mothers of the gods, of the avaranas either externally or in the avarana.

Thereafter different types of deities shall be worshipped all round They include the walkers of the heaven, the sages, Siddhas, Daityas, Yaksas, Raksasas. Ananta and other leading serpents and those belonging to the different families, besides Dakinis, goblins, spirits, Bhairavas, people of the nether worlds, the rivers, oceans, mountains, forests and the lakes shall also be worshipped.

The animals, birds, trees, worms, and other insignificant creatures, men of different castes, deer of insignificant species, the world within the universe, the crores of universes, the innumerable seed germs, their worlds with their rulers. Rudras lodged in the ten quarters supporting the universe or everything fashioned out or the gunas or Maya or originating from Sakti shall be worshipped generally, taking into account, their presence on either side of Siva and Siva. They shall be forms of cit and acita or whatever can be expressed in the world.

They shall be joining their hands in reverence, having smiles over their faces and looking with devotion at Siva and Siva.

After performing the avarana puja, thus, he shall worship the lord again for quietening obstraction and confusion and utter the five syllabled mantra.

He shall then offer to siva and Siva, nectar like sweets and charming Mahacaru as naivedya accompanied with side dishes and vegetables. The naivedya shall be prepared from thirty two adhaka measures of grains is appreciable and that prepared with less then one adhaka measure is lesser in importance. After collecting and preparing the naivedya in accordance with one's competence, he shall offer it with devotion.

Thereafter he should offer other things besides the water, followed by the betel. The arati should be performed thereafter, and the puja should be concluded.

Then he should prepare the dravyas useful for the yoga. He should not at all be miserly in case he is financially well off. A degraded person who neglects, his action tantamounts to the adverse actions. He can never be successful in his efforts. This is what has been ordained by the noble people. A person desirous of success, should discarding neglect perfor the kamya karma with utmost devotion.

Thus concluding the puja, offering his salutation to Siva and Siva, he should offer prayer with devotion subsequently.

At the end of the stotra he should recite the Pancaksara mantra a hundred and eight times or a thousand times.

Thereafter one shall adore Vidya and the preceptor and offering his salutation to them, he should recite the stotra adoring the Brahmana according to his means.

Then the send off ceremony of lord Siva in relation to all the avaranas should be performed. Then the material of the yajna should be offered to the preceptor.

Or otherwise the same may be given to a devotee of Siva in the Sivaksetra or hand them over to the temple of Siva.

Otherwise, the same should be dropped in the fire of Siva, he should adore the gods of all the avarana and the send them off gracefully.

This yajna is known as yogesvara in the three worlds and there is no other yajna on earth better than this.
