There is nothing in the world which could not be achieved with the same. One reaps the fruit from the same like Cintamani.

Still it would not be appropriate to invoke it for the sake of the petty gains. A great man being desirous of petty things, belittles himself in the world.

But in the deed all the small or the big desires are fulfilled with the same. Therefore one should perform everything keeping Mahadeva in view.

Therefore for victory over the enemy, overcrossing the death or for any other rewards, which could not be achieved through any other means or gods, one should adore Siva.

In the grave sins, or grave ailments, immense danger, draught, etc. one should adore Siva to achieve peace.

Excess of talk is of no use, this is the only weapon which destroys all the misfortunes of the devotees of Siva. This has been ordained by Mahesvara himself.

Therefore, there is none else to provide better protection than this. Realising this the performer, achieves the auspicious merits.

The one who purifying himself, with the attentive mind recites, attains the benefit desired.

In case anyone thinks into the hymn on the festives day of astami or Caturdasi, keeping fast, and resorts to recitation, he achieves half the benefits.

A performer of the vrata, who, concentrating on lord, on the festival days, recites the japam of the strotra for a month, he attains full benefit for the same.

## Chapter 31 - Siva strotra or hymn to Siva

Upamanyu said, “O Sri Krsna, I shall now narrate to your the auspicious stotra known as Yogesvara, relating to the Pancavarna marga, reciting which all the holy rites meet with success.

O Siva the sole lord of the universe, beautiful by nature, of the nature of the eternal knowledge; free from sins you are the tattva beyond the mind, speech, and movement.

You possess spotless temperament and the body, simple and enthusiastic, you possess the unparalled prowess, ocean of the spotless virtues, victory to you.

You possess the unending splendour, having the divine body, base of uncontroversial glory, bestowers of the stable welfare, victory to you.

You are unblemished, without base, taking birth without any reason, victory to you. You bestow delight on others always, cause of vairagya, victory to you.

You possess all the fortunes, extremely compassionate, completely independent, having the unparalled fortunes, victory to you.

You are all pervading, you cannot be overshadowed by anyone, the best of all and there is no one superior to you. Victory to you.

You are wonderful, you are not insignificant, unwounded, unchanging, beyond measure, free from Maya, without having emotions, spotless clean, victory to you.

You have long arms, the great essence, great virtue, great speaker, Mahabala, possessing great Maya, the great essence, the great chariot, victory to you.

You are the supreme lord, supreme cause, Siva, peaceful one, form of Siva, and the best of all, salutation to you again and again.

The entire universe of the gods and demons is subservient to you.

Therefore who could venture to disobey your command. Your devotee is always dependant on you; therefore you kindly accept your prayer.

O Amba, mother of the universe, form of the complete universe, you possess the entire fortunes, you possess the supreme beauty, victory to you.

You are beyond the speech and the mind, you remove the darkness of the heart you are beyond the birth and old age, you are better than kala, victory to you.

You are lodged as the beloved of the lord Visvesvara, you are adored by all the gods, you always think of the welfare of the world. Victory to you.

You have the body possesssing all the welfare. You illumine the welfare, besides being the bestower of welfare, victory to you.

You are the form of benevolent merits, the entire universe has emerged from you, and ultimately merges in you. Thereafore salutation to you.

Except you even Isvara is unable to bestow such reward, O supreme goddess, I happen to be your devotee.

Therefore, you kindly fulfil the desire of the devotee. Five faced Sadasiva, having the ten arms resembling the crystal, having the physical body formed of letters, the five Brahmanas and the kalas, the lord is both Sakala and Niskala who is endowed with the devotion of Siva, and who is beyond the Santikala has been worshipped by me. With devotion. May he bestow on me, whatever has been prayed by me.

Let the Iccha-sakti in the form of Siva lodged in the lap of Sadasiva, the mother of the universe, fulfil any desire.

Ganesa and Kartikeya are the beloved sons of Siva and Siva, who are omniscient by the grace of Siva, consume the nectar of Siva-jnana.

Both of them are respected by Siva, Siva, Brahma and other gods, are extremely satisfied, they mentally love each other enormously.

They are always ready to do good to the world. They incarnate in many ways of their own sweet will.

Both the gods have been adored by me together with Siva and Siva many times. Let them fulfil my desires at the command of Siva and Siva.

The lord Sadasiva is spotless like the crystal gem and is known as Isana, he is the great Atman, who is quiescent, who occupies the firmament, transcending the Santikala who is the final bija of the five syllabled mantra, who is equipped with five kalas and has been worshipped in the first avarana, together with Sakti.

The lord is resplendent like the rising sun, who is the eternal Purusa identified with the eastern face of Siva Paramesthina.

He is like Santi lodged in the wind, who is engaged in the worship of the feet of Siva, who is first among Siva-Bijas, who has four Kalas and who has been adored by me with devotion in the east along with Sakti. May the sacred middle Brahman, named Aghora, resembling collyrium, having a terrible physical body, identified with the southern face of the lord who abides in the Vidya region and is lodged in the centre of the fire, who is second among the bijas of Siva, who has eight kalas and has been worshipped with Sakti to the south of Siva, grant me what I have prayed for.

Let the holy Brahman grant me, whatever has been prayed for by me, for he, who is known as Vama, who has an excellent dress, resembling the saffron powder, who represents the northern face of Siva and who is well established in Pratistha, in the middle one of water. He is engaged in the adoration of the lord. He is the fourth of the Siva's bijas, having thirteen kalas. He has been worshipped with Sakti to the north of the lord.

The fire faced Sadyojata Siva is of white complexion like the conch, lotus and moon, bearing all the auspicious symbols. His western face is being adored.

He represents the western face of Siva, that is engaged in the worship of Siva, who is established in the Nivritti region and is lodged in the earth. He is the third one of the Siva bijas, possesses eight kalas and who is adored with his Sakti to the west of the lord.

Let the two purified hearts of Siva and Siva, purified by Siva, grant my wish at the instance of both Siva and Siva.

The excellent image of Siva and Siva is dependent on Siva. Bowing to his command shall fulfil my desire.

Let the kavaca, getting sanctified with Siva-mantra, at the command of both of them should fulfil my desire.

Let the two eyed form of Siva, dependant on Siva grant me my desire at the behest of both of them.

Let the weapon form of Siva and Siva, at the instance of both of them grant me my desire at their behest.

Let the deities like Vama, Jyestha, Rudra, Kala, Vikarana, Balavikarana, Balapramathana, and Sarvabhutadamana grant me my desire at the command of Siva and Parvati.

Let the eight deities Ananta, Suksma, Siva, Ekanetra, Ekarudra, Trimurti, Srikantha and Sikhandaka with their Saktis who we adored in the second avarana grant me my desire at the behest of both of them.

Let the eight images of Bhava and others, with their Saktis and the eleven figured Mahadeva, besides others accompanied with their Saktis, stationed in the third avaranas bestow the desired benefits at the command of both of them.

Let the immensely resplendent Vrsaraja, thundering like the clouds, having the six comparable to peaks of Meru. Mandara, Kailasa and Himalaya.

Having the form of the white clouds, looking graceful with his hump, having the tail like the serpent Sesa, having the red mouth, horns, the feet as well the eyes, having the well developed and raised limbs, walking gracefully.

Having excellent symptoms, adorned with the glittering ornaments of gold, beloved of Siva, and who serves to Siva, serving as the vehicle as well as the banner of both Siva and Siva,

Who has been purified with touch of their feet, who is the king of the cows, let him fulfil my wishes at the command of both of them.

Nandisvara is of great splendour, the son of Parvati is worshipped, by the gods, including Ganesa, Visnu and other gods.

He guards the gate of the inner apartments of Siva with other ganas, he is the destroyer of all the enemies of Mahesvara.

He presides over all the dharmas of Siva, he is dear to Siva, immensely devoted to Siva, glorious, holding the best of the tridents.

He is always in service of the devotees of Siva, he worships Siva and Siva always, honouring the command of both Siva and Siva, let him fulfil my desire.

Like Mahakala, Mahabahu, Mahadeva, as well as Sadasiva, whosoever takes refuge with him, let him protect him always.

He is the favourite of Siva and is fondly attached Siva and Siva. He is this perpetual worshipper. May he grant my desire at the instence of both of them

He is well aware of the tattvas of all the literature, a competent ruler, the other form of Visnu, the son of Mahamoha, the wine, flesh and asavas are his favourite food. Let him fulfil my desier at the command of both of them.

The seven Matrkas like Brahmani, Mahesi, Kaumari, Vaisnavi, Varahi, Mahendri, Camunda and Candavikrama are the mothers of the entire universe. Let them grant my wish at the command of the lord.

Ganesa has the face of elephant in rut. He is the son of Ganga, Uma and Siva. The firmament is his body the quarters are his arms. The sun and the moon are his eyes. He is adored by the elephants of the quarters. Creator of the obstructing in the activitions of the asuras and he is devoted both to Siva and Siva, let him grant our wish at the command of his parents.

Sanmukha is born of Siva, and holds Sakti, and vajra. He is the son of fire as well, besdies being the son of Ganga, Ganamba and Krttikas. He is surrounded by Visakha, Sakha and Naigameya. He is the conqueror the demon Taraka, he is the chief commander of the army of Indra. He pierced the important mountains of Meru and others, with his splendour. He has the complexion of the molten gold. His eyes resemble the lotus petals. He is Kumara and the model of all the tender things. He is the favourite of Siva and is fondly attached to him. He is perpetual worshipper of Siva's feet. Let him grant my desire at the behest of both of them.

Let Jyestha, Vasistha, bestower of the boons engaged in the adoration of Siva and Siva, let them fulfil my desire with the consent of both of them.

Let Ganambika who is adored in the three worlds, was born from the eyebrows of Siva at the prayer of Brahma. Then she divided herself into Daksayani, Sati, Mena, Haimavati, Uma. She is Rudrani, the beloved of Rudra and is engaged in adoring Siva. Let her grant my desire at the behest of the two.

Canda is the lord of the ganas, who emerged from the face of Siva. Let him grant me my desire at the instance of Siva and Siva.

Pingala is the lord of the ganas, is extremely devoted to Siva, let him fulfil my wishes at the instance of both of them.

Bhrngisa is the lord of ganas as well and is devoted to Siva, let him fulfil my desire at the command of his master.

Virabhadra is resplendent like snow, lotus flower, the moon, is favourite of Bhadrakali, besides being the protector of Matrkas.

He is the one who destroyed the yajna of Daksa and cut off his head, besides severing the limbs of Visnu, Indra, Yama and others.

He has been serving Siva and obeyed his command. Let him fulfil my desire at the command of Siva and Siva.

Let Sarasvati who had emerged out of the lotus like face of Siva, and who is always engaged in the adoration of Siva be graceful me.

Laksmi is lodged in the chest of Visnu, she is engaged in adoring Siva and Siva. Let her grant my desire at the desire of both of them.

Mahamoti is engaged at adoring the feet of Mahadevi, let her grant my desire at the instance of both of them.

Kausiki is mounted over a lion, is daughter of Parvati and the sleep of Visnus Mahamaya, Mahamahisamardini, the destroyer of Sumbha and Nisumbha to whom the honey, meat and asavas are favourite, let her fulfil my desire at the command of her mother.

Rudras have the lustre of Rudra. Pramathas are well knwor for their prowess. The bhutas are extremely valorous, having the lustre of Mahadeva. They are always yogins. They are beyond comparison and are devoid of the conflicting pairs of defaults. They are free from dangers. They keep association of their Saktis and the followers. They are bowed to the world. They can create as well as destroyer the worlds. They are mutually loving and accommodating. They are quite affectionate and respectful to one another. They are the favourites of Siva and are marked by their trails. They are gentle, terrible and the combination of both of them. They are the midway between the two. They are ugly as well as the good featured besides being multifeatured. Let all of them grant my desire at the instance of both of them.

Honouring the command of both Siva and Siva, let them grant my wish. The group of the friends of the goddess resemble the goddess, who are accompanied with the large umber of the daughters of the Rudras, and have been adored in the third avarana of Siva with great devotion. Let them great my desire at the instance of both of them. The sun shines with the lustre of Mahesa.

He is Nirguna, Gunasankirna, Gunakevala and Avikaratmaka (unblemished). The first one is single with general variations. He indulges himself in extraordinary activity in creations, preservation and annihilation. Thus he is divided in three four or five ways and is worshipped in the fourth avarana of Siva with the followers. He is the favourite of Siva and is lovingly attached to him. He always adores the feet of Siva. Let him grant me my desire at the instance of both of them.

There are six angas of Suns heart, and there are the eight Saktis. The forms of the sun. include Aditya, Bhaskara, Bhanu, Ravi, Arka, Brahma, Rudra and Visnu, while the Saktis of Sun or Vistara, Sutara, Bodhini, Apyayini, Apara, Usa, Prabha, Prajna and Sandhya, who are nine in number.

All the planets from the moon of Ketu are the devotees of Siva, let all of them having been inspired both by Siva and Siva, bestow welfare on us.

Now there are twelve Adityas having an equal number of Saktis, besides the Rsis, gods, Gandharvas, serpents, apsaras in groups, besides Gramani, Yaksa, Raksasas, Asuras, having seven ganas each. Seven metres serve as steed to them.

Valakhilyas and others are the eternal devotees of Siva. All of them with the permission of Siva and Siva should bestow welfare on us.

The image of Brahma, the lord of the universe, a form of the lord of gods, possessing sixty four attributes and achievements, and established in the principle, he is with or without attributes, has the image of all the virtues, is an unblemished god, performing the ordinary as well as the extraordinary deeds. He is worshipped in the fourth avarana of Siva, he is the favourite of Siva and fondly attached to Siva, always adoring Siva. May he grant me the desired wish at the instance of both of them.

Hiranyagarbha, the lord of the world, Virat, Kalapurusa, Sanatkumara, Sanandana, Sanatana, Prajapati Daksa and other sons of Brahma, all of them with their spouses besides Dharma, Sankalpa, are devotedly engaged in the adoration of Siva. Since they remain under the command of Siva, let then bestow welfare on us.

The four Vedas, Itihasa, Puranas, Dharmasastras with Veda-vidya and the literature on similar topics, or those propounding the Saiva dharma, honouring the command of Siva and Siva, bestow welfare on me. The image of Rudra and Siva, lord Siva, the presiding duty of Agni mandala is Trigunatmaka having been filled with pride, possesses Sattvika thoughts, unblemished and devoid of rajas and tamas, is the performer of the unusual karmas, free from the means of the creation of the universe, the one who cut off one of the heads of Brahma, his father as well as the son.

The son of Visnu and his father, he is the controller of the universe, the lord who bestows his grace on the universe.

Rudra who pervades inside and outside the globe lord of both the lokas, favourite of Siva, devoted to Siva, always engaged in adoration at the feet of Siva,

Obeying the command of Siva should bestow welfare on me. There are the six angas of the Vedas and there are eight deities ending with Vidyesa, the four different images devoted to Siva, with Siva as their chief cause, Siva, Bhava, Hara and Mrda, let all of these deities bestow welfare on me at the command of Siva.

Visnu is another form of the great lord Siva, himself. He is the lord of the principle of water. He is stationed in the region of the unmanifest. He is Nirguna and exceedingly sattvika and possessed of a single gana. He is proud because of his being unblemished. He has a form like Brahma, Visnu and Siva.

The lord engages himself in unusual activity. He is free from the cause of the creation of the universe. He is competitive with Brahma emerging out of the right side of Siva.

Visnu happens to be the lord of both the lokas inside and outside the globe, created by Brahma.

Visnu is the destroyer of the demons and the younger brother of Indra, who because of the curse of Bhrgu had to incarnate on earth ten times.

Visnu is the one who incarnates on earth to retrieve her of the burden. He possesses enormous prowess and Maya. He is the one who comfuses the world with his Maya.

Making an image of Mahavisnu, the people of Vaisnava faith always adore him. He is lodged over the seat with three images.

He is favourite of Siva, devoted to Siva, engaged in adoring Siva, therefore let him bestow welfare on me at the behest of Siva.

Visnu has been conceived in the four forms of Vasudeva, Aniruddha, Pradyumna and Samkarsana.

Let the forms of Visnu known as Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, Vamana, Parasurama, Rama, Balarama, Krsna, Visnu, Hayagriva.

Cakra, Narayana-weapon, Pancajanya and Sarnga bow, bestow welfare on me collectively.

Let Prabha, Sarasvati, Gauri and Laksmi the devotee of Siva, bestow welfare on me at the command of Siva.

Let Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirrti, Varuna, Vayu, Soma, Kubera, Isana the trident bearer, are all devoted to Siva, therefore with the consent of Siva and Siva they should bestow welfare on me.

Let the divine weapons of Siva and Siva, like the trident, vajra, parasu, arrow, sword, pasa, ankusa, Pinaka the best of the weapons, at the command of Siva and Siva, should protect us daily.

Let the lord taking to the form of the bull, son of Surabhi, immensely strong, the one who could complete with the submarine fire, surrounded with five cows, having gained the position of the vehicle of Siva and Siva, by his tapas, at the command of both of them should fulfil our desires.

There are five sacred cows known by the names of Nanda, Sunanda, Surabhi, Susila and Sumana, who reside in the Sivaloka.

All of them are devoted to Siva and adore him. Let them bestow welfare on us at the command of Siva and Siva.

Let Bhairava, who is extremely illustrious, resembling the blue cloud, having the awful face with fangs, having the fluttering red lips,

having the red hair, having enormous lustre, having crooked eye brows, with three round and red eyes, adorned with the ornaments of the moon and the serpents,

standing naked, holding a trident noose, sword, skull as the hand attributes, surrounded by the horrible Siddhayoginis,

who protects the noble people in each region. He offers his salutation to Siva with devotion, possessing the noble feelings.

He is the one who especially protects the Siva’s devotees affectionately like his own sons. Let him at the command of Siva and Siva, honouring us bestow welfare on us.

Talajangha and others who have been adored in the first avarana, at the command of Siva and Siva, should protect us.

Bhairava and other gods who keep on always surrounding lord Siva, let them also shower their grace on me with the command of the lord.

Narada and other mandicants who are adorable even by the gods, the Siddhas, the serpents and people of the Janaloka, the residents of Maharloka, who have been deprived from authority, the seven sages and others, together with the ganas moving in the planes, engaging themselves in the adoration of Siva and are subservient to the command of the lord, let them all grant my desire at the command of Siva.

The demi-gods starting from Gandharvas to pisacas comprising of four Devayonis, Siddhas, Vidyadharas besides those roaming in the sky, the asuras, Raksasas, Ananta the serpent and other dwellers of the nether world, besides the serpent king, Garuda, and other birds,

Kusmandas, goblins, vetalas, grahas, bhutas, dakinis, yoginis, sakinis and the evil witches, the auspicious places, orchards, buildings, etc., the holy places, islands, ocean, river, revulets, lakes, sumeru and other mountains, besides the forests, trees, deer, animals, birds, germs, insects etc., all the bhuvanas their lords, all the globes with their avaranas, the ten directions as well as the elephants of the directions, varnas, padas, mantras, the tattvas as well as their presiding deities, Rudra holding the globes, besides other Rudras with Saktis, besides whatever is seen, heard or imagined in this world, all of them, at the command of Siva and Siva should bestow welfare on us.

Then the great lore of Siva, which can release the individual soul from the five fold bondage, is different from Pasuvidya. The literature of Siva’s vestires and the related dharma, the Purana of Siva, as approved by the Srutis and the Saiva scripture Kamika, and of other four types, command by Siva and Siva and adored by me, may all of them make this holy rite purposeful and fruitful.

All the preceptors from Sveta to Nakulisa besides their sons, they are especially our preceptors,

This task which is devoted to Siva and Mahesvara, besides being jnana-karma, parayana has been successfully completed. You kindly accept the same.

The worldly Brahmans, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, well versed in the Vedic and the post Vedic tattvas, having mastery in all the scriptures, besides those well versed in the Samkhya philosophy, Vaisesika, Yoga-sastra and naiyayikas, worshippers of Sun, Brahma, Siva as also the Vaisnavas, the cultured, specialised people, who obey the command of Siva, should accept that this performance of mine should bestow welfare.

The devotees of Siva, or the followers of Saiva preceptors, followers of Pasupata-vrata, Saivas performing the Mahavratas and those who obey the command of Siva, are adorable for me. Let all of them, at the instance of Siva and Siva, be merciful on me and make my efforts successful.

The intelligent, learned, large hearted, followers of the noble path, those desirous of welfare by means of Siva mantra, should remain friendly with me.

The atheists, wicked, ungrateful, Tamasika people, crooks and grave sinners, should keep away from me.

What else is to be said, whosoever is a believer in the lord, should shower his grace on me, bestowing welfare on me.

I bow in reverence to Siva and Parvati with their son. He is surrounded by the Pancavarna in the universe. Thus speaking, one should prostrate on the ground before Siva and Siva, should recite Pancaksari lore, a hundred and eight times.

Similarly Sakti-vidya should be adored. Making dedication to her, one should beg forgiveness, concluding the puja.

This auspicious stotra is the favourite of Siva and Siva. It fulfilling all the desires bestows devotion and salvation over a devotee. This is the only means for the same.

A person, who recite the same, carefully, everyday, he getting all his sins destroyed expeditiously, achieves Siva Sayujya.

The killer of the cow, the ungrateful person, killer of valorous soldier, destroyer of the pregnancy, killer of the person who takes refuge with him, killer of the friend, betrayer, wicked, sinful and killer of the parents, all these are relieved of their sins, with the reciting of this stotra.

A person who recites the stotra toward of the evil effect of the evil dream, he does not have to face misfortune.

A person achieves all the comforts like long life, good health, fortunes besides all other pleasures with the reciting of the stotra.

One achieves due merits with the reciting of the stotra even without the performing of the puja. In case the stotra is recited with the performing of the puja then the extent of its fruit world be beyond description.

Better leave aside the extent fruit one achieves with the reciting of the mantra. Siva and Parvati both remain delighted in the heaven with the listening of the stotra.

Therefore, adoring Siva and Parvati in the sky, one should stand up with folded hands and recite the stotra with devotion.

## Chapter 32 - Method of achieving the worldly benefits

Upamanyu said, “O Sri Krsna, I have spoken to you the stotra which bestows success in the world by its recitation. The reciting of the stotra combines in itself, the recitation, japam, tapas and the activates relating to meditation etc.

Now you listen to the forms of puja, homa, japam, meditation or the charities of followers of Siva, which yield the reward in this world itself.

First by one should achieve success in the mantra by a person who is aware of the meaning of the mantra. The mantra in which success is achieved after examining it well, it yields the proper result and not other wise.

Even the Siddha-mantra is influenced with some invisible element, making it infractuous. Therefore a learned person should not put it to a sudden use.

Atonement is possible for that obstacle. Hence he shall perform that atonement after testing it at the outset by means of omens.

A person who out of ignorance, performs the reward yielding deed in an improper manner, not only the reward is lost to him but he also becomes a laughing stock of the people.

One should never have disbelief in the attaining of the reward. The deed performed without the faith, can never yield reward.

When the efforts become unsuccessful, the deity is not to be blamed. Those who make efforts appropriately they get the reward during this birth itself.

The performer, who with the use of the Siddha-mantra has removed all the bondages, a theist person (having full faith in the lord) after performing the deeds, reaps, the reward (undoubtedly).

Or otherwise, for the achieving of the desired reward, one should embrace celibacy (Brahmacarya). He should consume havisya, milk or fruits during the night.

The evil deeds like himsa (killing) and others which have been prohibited, should be discarded and should not be resorted to even mentally. He should clad himself beautifully, apply the bhasm over the body.

Thus following the good conduct, on a favourable and auspicious day, selecting an auspicious place with good symptoms as pointed out earlier, the earth measuring one hand square, should be plastered with the cowdung and decorated with the flower garlands. Then two shining lotus flowers should be drawn over the same.

The lotus should be of molten gold with eight petals and the filarments with the pericarp in the centre set with all the gems. It should not be less than a hasta in width and should have a stalk befitting its size. Then he shall conceive Anima etc. in the bulbous root made of gold, according to the religious injunctions. Then the Siva-linga shall be installed with the pedestal made of gems, gold or crystal with all the charactersitcis. He shall invoke the eternal lord, together with the goddess Amba and the ganas. The Siva-linga should also be conceived to represent the Mahesvara form of Siva.

It shall have four arms, and four faces, bedecked with all the ornaments, wearing the tiger skin, wearing a serene smile over the face, displaying the abhaya and Varada mudra for his devotees. The attributes of the other hands shall have a deer and an axe as attributes. But in case the devotee so desire the image of Siva could have eight arms as well.

The attributes of the right hands should comprise of a trident, an axe, a sword and a vajra, while those of the left hands should be a noose, a good, an iron club besides the serpents. The image should have the lustre of the rising sun, having three eyes in each face. The face towards the east should be gentle with appropriate refulgence.

The southern face resembles the blue clouds, with terrific appearance. The northern face has the lustre of coral having dark forelocks.

The back face should be serene like the moon, adorned with the moon digit, the Aparasakti Mahesvari is lodged in his lap.

Syama who is well known as Mahalaksmi, and attracts the mind of all. Such a type of image should be made and then sankalpa should be performed.

Then invoking Siva, the supreme cause, he should then take a bath with the pancagavya made of the milk of the Kapila cow. Pancamrta should also be prepared of the same milk, which should be sanctified with the complete bija-mantras. Besides that a diagram of the powder of gems should be made.

The water pot of Isana shall be put in the pericarp. The water pot of Sadyojata shall be place around afterwards.

All the eight kalasas of Vidyesa, should then be filled with water of tirthas binding the cord around their necks and then they should be placed in order starting from the east.

The auspicious dravyas should be provided in those vases reciting the mantras. Each one of then should then he covered with cloth from all the sides.

The dravyas should be dropped in this vases, reciting the appropriate mantra. At the time of bath of Siva, all the musical instruments including the conch should be sounded.

The lord should be bathed with the conch Pancajanya. Thereafter he should be bathed with water of kusa, gold and the gems.

Thereafter the lord should be bathed, with fragrance, flowers etc. reciting the mantras.

The puja should then be performed

offering the fragrance, flowers, lamp etc. The unguent shall not be less than a pala in weight and maximum of it shall be eleven palas.

The auspicious and the charming flowers of good colour and fragrance, lilies of blue and other colours, plenty of wood apple leaves, red lotuses and white lotuses, if available should be used. The incense shall be offered with black Agaru. The gumresin should be used, with camphor and ghee. The ghee used for lamps should be of the tawny cows. The five Brahmanas and the six angas besides the avaranas shall be worshipped.

Naivedya should be made of the milk of different colours, the great caru should be made of jaggery and ghee and the water scented with the red lotus flowers, should be used, well-consecrated Tambula along with five types of fragrance should be offered. The ornaments of gold studded with gems should only be offered.

Besides the beautiful costumes of different colours should also be offered with the songs and music.

The basic mantra shall be recited a lakh of times. One time puja is of lowest type and three time puja is the best.

The number of sacrifices is not less then ten for every article and the maximum is hundred. In the rites like marana and uccatana Siva in terrific form should be adored.

While performing the nourishing rites, Siva shall be conceived as gentle, in the Sivalinga, in the Siva-fire and in other images as well.

In the marana and other rites, Sruk and Sruva should be made of iron and in all other rites they shall be made of gold.

In the Mrtyunjaya rites the homa is performed by durva grass mixed with ghee and cow milk, or honey or with caru along with ghee or milk alone. For the removal of ailments or to attain prosperity or for the removal of poverty, gingelly, seeds, ghee, milk or the lotus flowers shall be used. A person intending to bring another person under control, shall perform homa with Jati flowers and ghee.

A Brahmana shall perform the rite of akarsana with ghee and karavira flowers, uccatana with oil and the Stambana with honey.

The stambhana rite can be performed with mustard seeds as well, Patana with garlic, tadana with the blood of mule, camel or both.

Marana and Uccatana can be performed with Rohi and gingelly seeds. The Vidvesana rite shall be performed with langala oil.

Bandhana rites as well as the Stambhana (of army) rites shall be performed with the Rohi seeds them using the red mustard, all the homas should be performed.

The homa shall be performed with the oil extracted manually. It can also be performed with the cotton seeds together with Ketaki and the husk. In the abhicarika rites the devotee shall perform homa with mustard seeds mixed with oil. By performing the homa with milk, the fever is subsided yielding fortunes at the same time.

All round success is achieved with the performing of homa by honey, curd, dravyas with ghee or milk or rice or caru only.

For the peace and development, one should perform homa with seven Samidhas. With the performing of homa with special stuff one achieves success in vasikarana (making others subservient) and akarsana (attraction).

Performing the homa with the leaves of the wood-apple trees, yields vasikarana, akarsana and victory over the enemies.

Palasa has to be used for peaceful rites, besides the Samidhas of Khadira wood. In the rites of cruelty, the twigs of Karavira and arka shall be used. In the rites of war the twigs of thorny trees shall be used.

Becoming peaceful one should perform the Santika and Paustika Karmas. The cruel and the one with angry temperament should perform the abhicara karma (a magical spell for malevolent purposes).

A person engrossed in immense misery, with no remedy in sight, should perform the abhicara-karma for the destruction of the enemy.

But no virtuous man, occupying honourable position or otherwise should perform the abhicara-karma against the head of the his state.

One should not perform abhicara-karma, physically, mentally or with speech against a theist (believer in lord), a noble person, respectable one, a devotee of Siva, even though he might be an aggressor.

By indulging into activation's against the nation or a devotee of Siva, like abhicara karma, a person is fallen himself.

Therefore, a person desirous of his own welfare should not perform the abhicara-karma against the head of the state or a devotee of Siva for the purpose of killing him.

In case the marana-prayoga is carried out against a particular person in case one feels repintant then he should perform the rite of repetence.

In case a poor person adores a Banalinga he becomes rich or otherwise by adoring a Siva-linga appearing by itself, or the Siva-linga well known in the Vedas, should be adored offering the gold or gems. In case he cannot do so, then he should adore the a with the mental offering of these valuables.

In case one is competent in some way and is incompetent in some other way, he gets the reward according to his means.

In case, even after the performance of the rite, the reward is not visible, then it shall be repeated twice or thrice. After this benefit is likely to be received.

Whatever material is used in the worship including gold and gems etc., shall be handed over to the preceptor together with daksina which should be given repeatedly.

In case the preceptor is not interested in receiving the entire gift himself, then the same shall be given to Siva or the devotee of Siva and none else.

In case one himself performs the rite without the help of the preceptor, the same procedure has to be followed. He shall not appropriate the gift himself and in case he does so, out of greed, he will not attain his desired reward.

A person who appropriates the adored Siva-linga or offerings made to it, or even he does not appropriate those offerings but the Siva-linga can be adored by him or some one else.

A person who performs the said worship daily which frees from trouble, he surely reaps the reward for the same. What else could be bigger then this.

Still in this context I speak out the best of the process for achieving the success. In case the devotees is suffering from enemy or any other ailments, or is at the death's door, he is relieved from the suffering. The extremely miserly person, turns like a king, while the pauper becomes rich like Kuber - the lord of riches.

He earns the beauty of the god of love, while an old man is turned youthful. The enemy becomes like a friend, while an inimical person starts behaving like a servant.

The nectar becomes the poison, while the poison is turned as the nectar. The land is turned like an ocean, while the ocean is turned with the land.

The mountain is turned into a pit, and the pit is turned as the mountain. The fire is turned into a lake and the lake is turned into the fire.

The forest is turned into an orchard while the orchard is turned into the forest. The deer is turned into a lion, while the lion is turned as a deer to be played with.

The women will turn towards him at her own will, the prosperity will behave with him like a chaste lady never to leave him. The goddess of speech will be his slave girl. The glory follows him like a whore.

The wisdom will follow him. His mind will be pure like a diamond. His strength will be like the violent dust storm, or an intoxicated elephant.

His enemies will be paralysed in their efforts and the friends of the enemies would become the enemies of his opponents.

The enemies with their relatives shall be turned as dead bodies though physically alive. Though faced with misfortunes, he will be freed from them becoming immortal.

Even if he takes prohibited food it would increase strength like a rasayana, becoming powerful. Even after indulging in sexual intercourse through out the day and night, his love and strength will increasing.

The things which were beyond his reach earlier in the past, would become accessible to him like the myrobalan over the palm. The Siddhis like Anima and others become self rewarding for him.

What else could be stated in this connection, after performing the anusthana all the activities meet with success and nothing remains beyond the reach of the performer.

## Chapter 33 - Rites for achieving future benefits

Upamanyu said, “Hereafter, I shall speak out the method for benefits for the future world. There is no activity better than this one in the three worlds.

This performance is extremely auspicious, which was established by all the gods. More particularly, Brahma, Visnu, and Rudra had performed this karma.

By adoring Siva in this manner, Indra and other lokapalas, the nine planets including the sun, Visvamitra, well-versed in Brahman, Vasistha and other sages,

Sveta, Agastya, Dadhici and the devotee of Siva like us, besides Nandisvara, Mahakala, Bhrngisa, and other Gomesvaras, Daityas the dwellers of Patala, Sesa and other serpent kings, Siddhas, Yaksas and Gandharvas, Raksasas, Bhutas and Pisacas, besides other acheived their respective positions by adoring Siva. All the gods achieved god-hoods, with the same process.

Brahma achieved Brahmattva, Visnu achieved the position of Visnu, Rudra got Rudratva, and Indra got the position of Indra.

Ganesa was bestowed Ganesahood with the same process. Bathing Siva-linga with the white sandal paste it should be adored with the white lotus flowers. The salutation should be offered thereafter.

A person possessing the wealth, should make a lotus seat with gold and gems, according to his means, which should be quite pleasant to look at.

In the centre of the filament, a small linga of the size of a thumb shall be placed, which should be charming, auspicious and rendered fragrant with all the scents. Placing it to the south it should be adored with wood apple leaves.

Aguru shall be applied to the south. The red arsenic shall be applied to the west. The yellow orpiment shall be applied to the east. The linga should then be worshipped with the charming fragrant flowers of different colour.

The black Aguru shall be used as incense. Fumigation should be done with guggulu. A fine cloth of bright colour shall be offered.

The payasam mixed with ghee and the lamp should be offered besides everything muttering the mantra, then one should circumambulate

Salutation should be offered to lord Siva, with devotion and then should be offered the prayer. One should beg forgiveness at the end. All the presents should be combined and offered to the linga.

Taking refuge in the Daksinamurti form of Siva all of them should be offered with Siva-mantra. Whosoever adores Siva daily in this Pancagandhamaya form, he, getting relieved of all the sins is honoured in the Sivaloka. This Siva-linga-vrata is best of all the Vratas and is quite secret.

You are a devotee of Siva, therefore, this secret has been revealed to you. The knowledge of this has been revealed to you. The knowledge of this should not be imparted to one and all. Only those who are devotees to Siva are entitled to get the same. This what had been told by Siva himself.

## Chapter 34 - Conflict between Visnu and Brahma

Upamanyu said, “The method of performing the nitya, naimitik and kamya karmas or vratas has been described, compares well with the consecration of linga or the image of Siva.

The entire globe is in the form of a linga and is enshrined in the lingas. Therefore after the consecration of the linga everything is consecrated.

Inspite of there being Brahma, Visnu, Rudra or any other god, none of them could be established in his position without the linga.

What could be said about the glory of the linga because even Visvesvara linga was also established by Siva himself.

There all those who desire welfare in this as well as the future world, and they should establish the Siva-linga representing Paramesvara.

Sri Krsna said, “What is linga? What is Mahesvara linga? What is the form of linga. What for is the Siva-linga adored?”

Upamanyu said, “The unmanifest is called linga. It happens to be the source of attributes besides being the source in which the universe is absorbed or dissolved. It is without the beginning or the end. It is the material cause of the universe.

It is the Maya, the Mula Prakrti. The mobile and immobile creation has emerged out of the same.

It is of three forms viz. pure, impure as well as pure and impure both. All the gods like Brahma, Visnu, Siva, Mahesa and Rudra emerge out of it and are finally absorbed in the same, with the command of Siva. He is linga since he commands the linga.

Because no one can function without his command, then the universe after its creation gets absorbed in the same.

This constitutes the state of being a linga, in Siva and not due to any other reason. The linga is the body of Siva and Siva because, it is presided over by them.

Therefore Siva is worshipped in the form of linga forever, along with Siva. The goddess serves as the pedestal of the linga and linga is lord Siva himself.

With the adoration of linga, both Siva and Siva are adored. Their having the linga for their body is the ultimate reality.

Since both of them are pure, the body is only in the secondary sense. That is the great Sakti of Siva, also known as the great Atman, the same Sakti at the instance of Siva, gives both to the mobile and immobile beings. The glory of linga is beyond description in worlds even in hundred years by which Brahma and Visnu were deluded at the outset.

In earlier times when the universe was in the sate of dissolution, Visnu was lying in the oceanic waters over the serpent bed in deep slumber. He kept on sleeping comfortably for long. Then Brahma the grandsire of the world went there and found the lotus eyed Visnu sleeping comfortably overpowered by Maya of Siva. Brahma said to Visnu.

‘‘Who are you, you tell me.” Saying this, he hit Visnu in anger, waking him up at the same time. Then Visnu, having been so hurt by Brahma with his hands, got up in a moment.

Getting up from the bed, Visnu said to Brahma and getting enraged from within, he still kept up his cool and said.”

“O Son, wherefrom have you arrived? Why are you upset, you tell me.” Listening to the benevolent words of Visnu,

Brahma, overpowered with rajoguna opposing him said in the way a preceptor speaks to his disciple. ‘‘Why are you addressing me like this”?

Are you not aware that the entire creation has been made by me and I am the lord of the same. I have divided myself in three forms. Initially I resorted to creation, and now I am preserving the same.

Thereafter I shall destroy it. No one is my creator in the world.” At these words of Brahma, Visnu spoke to Brahma.

I am the initial creator of the universe, besides being its preserver and the destroyer. In earlier times you had emerged out of my body.

You distributed yourself in three parts at my command alone and then created the universe, which is currently being preserved by you and I would ultimately destroy it.

You have forgotten the unblemished lord of universe Visnu. You are actually humiliating your own father.

And for this you are not at all at fault. You have been confused with my Maya. By my grace you will be relieved of the confusion.

Listen, O Brahma, I happen to be the lord of all the gods. There is none, possessing the fortunes as comparable to me as a creator, sustains and the destroyer.

Thus there arose a controversy between Brahma and Visnu, followed by a terrific great war, which was quite thrilling.

Because of the enmity emanating from rajoguna both of them attacked each other with fists, just to ill feed their pride and to convince the gods of their respective strength, (they behaved like this).

Then a Siva-linga burning with thousands flames, which was wonderful and without description appeared in between them.

It could neither be reduced nor be increased and having no beginning middle or end. With the thousands of flames, emerging out of it, both Brahma and Visnu got confused.

Stopping the war, both of them moved aside and started thinking as to what was it? When both of them remained ignorant of its reality, then both of them thought of examining the beginning and end of the same.

Then Brahma took to the form of a swan with wings flew up with the speed of the mind or the wind.

Narayana, on the other hand being the soul of the universe, took to the form of a great boar black like the mountain of the collyrium and entered the nether world.

In this way Visnu kept on wandering in the nether world for a thousand years, but he could not trace the end of the linga.

For the same duration, Brahma also kept on flying in the space but finding no end of it, he returned on earth.

Similarly the distressed lord Visnu too with dazzled eyes, returned on earth with great difficulty.

After the return of both of them, they started looking at each other smilingly. Having been overpowered with the illusion of Siva they forgot everything proper or improper.

Then they stood in the front, at the back or on either side of the column and bowed in reverence to the same. They started thinking, “What could it be?”

## Chapter 35 - Delusion of Brahma and Visnu

Upamanyu said, “Then there appeared a nada of Om which is considered to be the single syllabled Brahman. It expressed the Brahman.

Both Brahma and Visnu failed to understand it because their minds been overpowered with rajoguna and tamoguna and their knowledge had been eclipsed.

Then that single syllable was divided into four, the three matras A, U, Ma and half of the matra thereafter.

The letter a was placed to the south of the blazing linga, u to the north, and m in the centre.

The half matra sound was heard over the top of the linga. Even when the great syllable Pranava was thus divided, the two gods Brahma and Visnu could not understand the same besides the cause of its division. Thereafter the omkara appearing in the four of the Vedas, became unmanifest.

Accordingly the letter a became the Rgveda, the letter u became the Yajurveda, the letter ma was turned into the sama-veda, while the nada was turned the Atharvaveda.

In brief, Rgveda is clearly enshrined in its own soul. Thus Brahma possessed of rajas, the first among the deities in the rites as well, the creator of the worlds and the principle as well as the unchanging Atman, Nirti in the path of kala and Sadyojata in the five Barhmanas, the lower part of the linga and the source in the three reasons. It established the sixty four gunas, and aisvarya of the cosmic intellect Anima etc. Thus with the ten topics, the universe was pervaded by the Rgveda.

On the establishing of the Yajurveda in ten ways, Sattva among the attributes, Visnu the first among the deities in the rites as well, sustenance in the worlds and the firmament, Vidya in three principles, Pratistha in the path of kala and Vamadeva in five brahmanas, the parts of the linga and yoni, in the three causes.

The Prakrta was established according to aisvarya. Therefore the universe has the form of Yajurveda. Similarly, was established in ten ways. It established tamas and Rudra as the first among the deities in the rites, annihilation in the three worlds and the excellent Siva in the tattva, Aghora in the five Brahmans, and Vidya among the kalas, the upper seat into parts of the linga besides the source in the three causes. Same is the case with aisvarya of the Purusa. Thus Saman pervades the universe.

Then the Atharvaveda also established it self accordingly. It was devoid of the gunas. Mahesvara Sadasiva was placed by it as the first among the deities. It was activated by means of Sadasiva. It created pure blessing by which the creations are liberated. Above the worlds, where the words recede, along with the minds are the unmana words, over which Somaloka is located. Lord stays there with Uma.

The one after reaching the Unmana world does not have to return. Then all pervasive kalas there are Santi and Santyatita. Purusa and Isvara are there out of the five Brahmans. The head of linga is there, which the best of the parts, where the sole Niskala Siva can be invoked and worshipped.

Out of the tattvas, it is the greater tattva than Bindu, Nada and Sakti. It is greater than the greatest besides a non -tattva in reality. It transcend the three causes. It is beyond Maya, the cause of agitation. It is beyond Ananta, the Suddha-vidya, Mahesvara, Sadasiva, the great lord of the lores. It is beyond the lord who has the Mantras for his body, accompanied with all the Saktis, having five faces and ten arms, and is conceived both as Sakala and Niskala. Beyond even that, beyond the bindu, the crescent, the moon, the great Nada, the lord of Susumna, the lord of Brahmarandhra beyond that, beyond Sakti and beyond the principle of Siva, the great cause, there is lord Siva who is without cause. He is the cause of all the causes, the subject and object of meditation and is stationed in the centre of the sky above the great Atma. Equipped with the prosperity and the glory, he is lord of all. There is no overlord for him. He is beyond Aisvarya and beyond Maya, beyond humanity, beyond the big and small, beyond that what is to be discarded, who is not to be discarded, beyond Suddhavidya Unmana, and the aisvarya of Unmana. He is great and is devoid of beginning, is limitless, independent, stable and unsurpassable. Thus with ten such characteristics, Atharvaveda is very weighty and so the universe is pervaded by the same. Rgveda said, again “The state of wakefulness, is being mentioned by me by which I clearly express.the Atmatattva.”

Because I always speak on the atma-tattva.” The Yajurveda said, “I am narrating the position while in dream or in sleep. Because the Vidya which transforms itself into the objects of enjoyment can be known through me.” Samaveda said, “The position which is called the sound sleep is being mentioned by me completely through Siva, that is my meaning and is tamasika in form.” Atharvaveda said, “The situation called the fourth stage is what is beyond the fourth is expressed by me. The three which are of the nature of path are known as Siva, Vidya and Atma. The state of their three attributes is attainable through the Vedas and shall be purified by him, who is desirous of the region of Siva. The region of Turiya is the excellent place of salvation. The place beyond the same is the purifier of the path because of the state of its attributesness. The nada measures the both. The end of nada is atman for me. The supreme lord is therefore the chief in view of the freedom from my topics. Whatever object is there whether compounded as separated, they call the meaning of Pranava in view of the association of the gunas. Therefore, the single syllabled Brahman, expresses all the meanings.

Therefore the entire universe is created by Siva by the single syllabled mantra Om. Indeed Siva is Pranava and the vice versa.

There is hardly any difference between the speech and the expression. Therefore Rudra is free from thought, mind and expression.

The words and the mind return without reaching him. The syllable a expresses Brahma, The Ekaksara Brahma is termed the soul.

The syllable u stands for Visnu, while the letter m stands for Siva. Brahma emerged out of the right side of the body of Siva, while Visnu emerged from the left side.

Nilarudra emerged out of the heart of Siva who represented the lord himself. Brahma then became the creator of the universe, while Visnu was responsible for its preservation.

Rudra took up the responsibility of creating discipline as well as destruction. Therefore all the three of them are known as the cause of the universe. Siva happens to be the supreme cause of the three.

Unable to understand the truth, and your enmity due to the predominance of rajoguna and in order to enlighten you on the reality the linga appeared between both of you.

Thus Atharvaveda addressed me as om. The Rg, Yaju, Sama and thousands of their other branches, spelt out clearly like the same. But inspite of the same nothing was clear to them like the dream.

Then all of them in order to gain enlightenment removal of ignorance the statement of the Vedas was inscribed over the linga too.

Finding the linga has thus been describedthe minds of the gods became peaceful by the grace of Siva and they felt enlightened.

On realising the mode of evolution and dissolution, the nature of the six path ways and the splendour beyond the Purusa, possessing brilliance, the Brahman besides whom, there is nothing greater, Niskala Siva Isvara, who is the eternal lord of the universe comprising of Pasu and Pasa who is completely devoid of fear, who is stable having no increase or decrease, who pervades within or without, who is devoid of inside or outside, who is unsurpassable, and is different from the entire world, who cannot be defined, incomprehensible, beyond expression, who has the form of brilliance, who is quite delighted and ever rising, who is the abode of auspiciousness and is accompanied with his Sakti. Brahma, Visnu joining their hands over the heads, spoke to the lord getting frightened.

Brahma said, “Irrespective of my being ignorant or otherwise, O Lord, I had been created by you in the beginning. In case I have been in delusion, then who is to be blamed?

Leave my ignorance alone, O lord, in your closeness, who can talk about his duty or of others.

O lord, the controversy between us has been quite useful, which has provided an opportunity to us to bow at your lotus like feet.”

Visnu said, “O lord, I have no competence to praise your glory or yourself, it would be better to keep quite about the duties before the great master.

What is the job suited to the occasion, I am not aware of it and under these conditions, without knowing anything, I offer my salutation to you.

Your being the cause of the universe, has been forgotten by me due to your Maya. I am deluded and filled with pride because of which I have been chastised by you.

This submission of mine is of no avail. O lord, I am extremely afraid, since I tried to measure your size, when you are beyond measure.

O Sankara, you have described Mahadeva as the remover of the miseries of others. Therefore, you kindly forgive me for my omission.

At the prayers of Brahma and Visnu, Siva wearing a sereme smile over his face, spoke to them in a jovial mood.

Siva said, “O Sons, Brahma and Visnu, both of you were deluded with my Maya developed enmity between yourself because of arrogance.

Your controversy resulted into a fight. Therefore the creative activity of both of you has vanished.

Because of the ignorance and arrogance of both of you, I in order to remove the controversy, produced the linga and dissuaded both of you from quarreling. Therefore you both should shed away controversy and shame for all times to come.

Now, both of you, shedding away the pride engage yourselves in your appropriate duty. At my command you should initially go through the entire set of Jnana Samhitas.

The jewel of mantras consisting of five syllables had been imparted to you, which has been forgotten by you. I shall restore everything to you as earlier, without which you cannot sustain or create.”

Thus speaking to Brahma and Visnu, Siva bestowed the knowledge of mantraraja beside the jnana-samhita. Then both of them, at the command of Mahesvara together with the auspicious mantra and all the kalas, prostrated before Siva at his feet.

In the mean time a great wonder happened and the linga of the lord suddenly disappeared, as a result of which they lamented and cried aloud and said to each other,” What a false thing has befallen us. Then realising about the enormous they were freed from agony.

Developing great friendship, they embraced each other and then left the place for attending the worldly affairs.

Since then Indra and other gods, asuras, Rsis, men and women and the serpents established the lingas, adoring Siva, at the same time.

## Chapter 36 - Installation of Siva linga

Sri Krsna said, “O Lord, I would like to listen to the method of the installation of lingabera, which had been narrated by Siva himself.”

Upamanyu said, ‘‘Selecting a favourable day in the bright fortnight, Siva-linga should be made according to the Saiva literature.

The land should be examined, selecting the auspicious place and perform the ten forms of service.

But before the actual performance of the service, Vinayaka has to be worshipped. After the purification of the land, performing other rites, linga should be carried to the ablution chamber.

A gold rod should be dipped into the saffron salutation, he shall draw the characteristic signs in the manner prescribed.

The dust free eight places (like elephant shed, cowshed, horsepen, chariot stand, Royal gate, white ant, a lake and the confluence of rivers) or with five types of dusts or with a ball of Pancapindika of Pancagavya the linga should be bathed.

After adoring the linga with pedestal, he shall carry it to the water receptacle, and immerse the linga in the water.

An inner shed shall be arrange in centre of a well constructed shed, for the immersion of the linga, well decorated with festoons, and screens all round, by the garlands of durva grass. The seat could be made of metal or of wood, resembling a lotus.

The eight elephants of the quarters should be placed on eight sides. For each one of the eight elephants of the quarters, a pot shall be placed. Then eight auspicious things should be kept ready and the guarding of the quarters should be adored.

A padmasana should be made of metal or wood, which should be placed over a bigger pedestal.

The four gatekeepers viz. Samudra, Vibhadra, Sunanda and Vinanda, should be adored.

The linga should be bathed with the Vedi. Then after receiving it, a cloth should be placed around it, covering the same, adoring it at the same time.

Wiping out the water, it should be made to rest over the pedestal towards the east. The pindika should be placed besides the same.

The linga should be kept with all the welfare material there for five, three or one night.

Adoring the linga, then it should be sent off, festivitie should be arranged as before, and there should be lodged in to the sleeping room.

The sleeping place should be made in the centre of the diagram. Carrying it there, the linga should again be bathed with the pure and clean water and then he should worship it.

A mystic lotus diagram shall be drawn in the north east on the ground, which should be well plastered with cowdung. The water vase of Siva should be purified. Then Siva shall be invoked and worshipped.

In the centre of the pedestal, a diagram of white lotus shall be made. A flower representing Candika shall be placed to the west.

The sleeping bed should be arranged with silken new cloth, or flowers or kusa grass and then one should offer the golden flowers.

Accompanied with the welfare music linga should be carried there covering it with red cloth from all the sides. It should then be made to sleep as before.

The lotus flower should be drawn before it and the Kalasas of Vidyesvara should be placed over the petals around the Sivakumbha. Thereafter the excellent Brahmana should perform the homa.

The eight images should be lodged in the east and other directions and eight Brahmanas to be seated therefore the performing of the japam.

For Brahma homa should be performed. This homa should be performed either by the chief priest or the preceptor alone. Initially a hundred and eight offerings should be made in ghee, followed by the final offering.

Reciting the mula-mantra he shall touch the top of the linga with his hand. Thereafter, a hundred ahutis or fifty or twenty five of them should be offered in the fire with seven dravyas.

After performing the homa the linga and the pedestal should be touched with hand again and again. Then offering the purnahuti, daksina should be given.

The amount of daksina to be given to those performing the homa should be half of such amount given to the acarya, while artisan should receive a fourth of the same. Still half of it should be given to the other members, according to one’s own capacity.

The golden ball should then be lodged in a pit and one should offer mudy water, Pancagavya and then clean water should be offered.

The Brahmasila should be placed in the pit, performing karanyasa of nine names of Sakti.

Then in accordance with the provision of the scriptures, he shall pour the minerals like haritala and others, together with the scents, seeds and medicinal herbs.

The linga shall be installed over the Brahmasila and the exudes of the banyan tree should be poured over it. To the east and the north, the aloe wood shall be placed, repeating the basis mantra. Repeating the basic mantra of Sakti, the same shall be joined to article of fixation. The places shall then be purified. Then Arghya shall be given, offering the flowers at the same time. A screen shall be drawn thereafter on all the sides.

The water should be sprinkled before the linga and it should be brought to the sleeping room and the Kalasas should be properly arranged there.

Thereafter performing the mahapuja the ten kalasas should be consecrated there, reciting the Siva mantra, the water pot, or Siva-kumbha should be lighted with the thumb and the ring finger, the mantra should be recited and the same should be established by a Brahmana well versed in the mantras in the space between the north east and the linga.

Then Nyasa should be performed for Vidyesa and the Vidya-sakti. Sivajala should be dropped at the base of the linga.

The name and the linga shall be bathed, with the water of Vardhani and Vidyesa Kalasa. The seat supports shall be arranged.

After performing the nyasa rites of the fire Kalasas, he shall meditate on the blazing linga. Facing the east or north, with folded hands, he shall invoke Siva and Siva.

The lord shall be conceived arriving with the goddess, seated over the lordly bull or in a plane; he shall be conceived as having been fully bedecked in shining ornaments. He is surrounded by all the gods on all the sides like Brahma, Visnu, Mahesa, Surya, Indra and the Danavas with their bodies drenched in the tears of joy, with folded hands placed over the heads. They are praising while dancing and bowing. The worship shall be concluded with five services.

After the five services of adoration, the faith rite is to be performed. The installation of the image is wholly identical with that of the linga.

The eyes shall have to be kept open at the rite of Laksanoddhara. The image should be placed with head downwards while bathing it or making it to sleep.

One should devote his mind towards the image which has be made to rest with the chanting of mantras. The installation of the image with the rites for the temple is better than the one without those rites.

The people with adequate resources, should first build the temple and then install the image. In case of one’s inability to do so, a linga or bera should be installed.

The Siva temple could be built subsequently according to one’s means. I shall speak about the mode of worship in the house and the excellent installation rites.

A linga or a small image of Siva should be made, and should be placed over a pedestal decorated with lotus diagram, in the bright fortnight in the Uttarayana on an auspicious day.

The pedestal should be made over an auspicious spot and the flowers etc. should be spread over it, placing the Kalasa over it.

Four Kalasas should be placed on the four comers of the same. The five Brahmanas should be consecrated reciting the five bija-mantra.

Performing the puja, one should display the mudras, the provide protection, sanctifying it, the linga-bera should be bathed as before.

Then it should be installed over the excellent seat to the north, and flowers should be offered, sprinkling water over the same.

Then adoring it with flowers, uttering the slogans of victory mula-mantra should be recited over the kalasas starting from Isana to Vidyesvara.

The Pancakalanyasa should be performed thereafter, he should adore the three eyed Siva and Siva, as was done earlier.

Or alternatively a kumbha should be placed over the space in between, the image of Siva and the lotus flower placed duly sanctified. The same process should be repeated thereafter.

The linga which is defective, its defect should first of all removed. In case the defect is quite slight (it could be ignored) and the linga should be worshipped.

Bana-linga should be installed at will, because they are believed to have been consecrated by Siva already.

Such other lingas which also look like bana, can also be installed with regard to the Svayambhu lingas or those which are divine or had been installed by some Rsis, and are without a pedestal, then in such cases they could be adored placing them over the pedestal. No formal consecration is needed for them.

Those which are burning, injured, with broken limbs, should be consigned in the water. Those which could be repaired, should be adored after their repair and installation.

The lord shall be dismissed from injured image but should be retained in heart after performing its due worship.

In case the worship is in default, for a day, it should be doubled. In case it is default for two days, great worship should be performed, followed by Samproksana rites.

In case there is a gap for a month in the performing of the worship some of the learned people prefer re-installation, followed by proksana.

In the proksana of the linga Mahadeva has to be dismissed first or other applying dust over it five or eight times, the linga should be washed with water. The linga should then be washed with milk and then purified with the water of kusa, one should perform proksana rites with the auspicious water and the Mula-mantra should be recited a hundred and eight times tehreafter.

Holding the flowers and the kusa grass in hand, it should touch the linga mula- mantra should be recited five or a hundred and eight times.

Then he should touch the linga from head to foot reciting the mula mantra. Thereafter Mahapuja of Siva should be performed as before, invoking all the gods.

In the absence of an installed linga, one shall worship the lord, in a place sacred to Siva, or in water, fire, the sun or the sky.

## Chapter 37 - The yogic practices and their usages

Sri Krsna said, “Whatever has been spoken by you relating to jnana, kriya and worship based on the related literature, has been listened by me, which is quite authentic.

Now I would like to listen about yoga in an authoritative manner, with its angas, with the methodology to be adopted as well as their usages.

Even if after performing the yogic practices appropriately and his death, is averted by the yogic practices or by taking recourse to yoga and accordingly the person escapes of becoming the self killers. Therefore it would be in the fitness of things in case you enlighten me over the different types of yoga and their relative importance, cause, time and procedure.”

Upamanyu said, “O Sri Krsna, the question has been asked by you quite appropriately since you will understand the meaning of all the questions. Therefore, I shall mention everything in a sequence.

To devotee one’s mind in Siva restraining all the activities, is called the yoga, which is of five types viz. Mantrayoga, Sparsa-yoga, Bhava-yoga, Abhava-yoga and Maha-yoga which happens to be superior to all.

With the practice of reciting of mantras with the concentration of mind, without disturbances, the expressed meaning of the mantras and chanting thereof is called Mantrayoga.

The yogic practices which are associated with pranayama are called sparsa-yoga. Without the association of mantra, it is called Bhavayoga.

When the universe with all its parts is meditated upon, it is called Abhavayoga because the object remains invisible in the same.

Siva is sometimes conceived to be without Upadhi because of his nature, therefore, the same is termed as Mahayoga.

Now we shall introduce a person who has the right to embrace yoga. A person whose mind is completely detached from the perceived and the Veda-ordained objects of pleasure.

The minds is detached when a person gets enlightened over the defects of the objects and in the attributes of the lord, perpetually.

Briefly speaking, the mind gets detached observing the blemishes of the gunas of Isvara. Irrespective of its being the Sadanga yoga or Astangayoga all the yogas are yama, niyama, asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, as have been brought out by the people of learings.

The six angas include asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana and samadhi which are known as sadangas.

The Siva Sastra or agamas speak about the individual definition of all of them. These include Kamikagama and others.

In the Yogasastras as well as the Puranas, ahimsa, satya, asteya (not to steal), brahmacarya (celibacy), aparigraha, have been termed as yama by the people of learning.

The five divisions of niyama are Sauca (purity), tusti (satisfaction), tapas, japam and the service of the preceptor.

The eight asanas comprise of Svastika, lotus, half moon, virasanam, yogasana, prasadhita, paryanka and yathestha (as per liking of the performer).

In control the life wind emerging from the body is called pranayama, which is of three types viz. Recaka, Kumbhaka and Puraka.

A passage of the nostril, should be closed with a finger, the wind from the belly should be released from the other nostril and this process is called Recaka.

The outer wind is filled and in the body like the leather water bag, from the other nostril and this process is called puraka or filling.

Then to keep the wind stored in the belly and remaining static like the Kumbha, or a pot is called Kumbhaka.

The performer of yoga, with the practicing or regulating the wind inhaled or exhaled, which should not be done in a hasta, but should be resorted to gradually.

In the process of Recaka, the practice of nadisodhana depends upon one’s will. This has been ordained in the scriptures on yoga. Or yoganusasana.

Pranayama is one of the four varieties, in view of the time units, kanyaka etc.

Kanyaka is without strokes and its duration is twelve matras. Madhyama has two strotras and its duration is twenty four matras.

Uttama has three strokes and its duration is thirty six matras. Uttama is the pranayama that comes perspiration and the body shakes.

A yogi has the requisite experience, the thrill of the bliss, horripilation, and the shedding of tears. He may prattle and there could be vertigo and senseless.

Matra happens to be the unit of time which is measured with the snapping of the fingers after moving them around the knee neither slowly or rapidly.

The pranayama has to be regulated according to the matras and the strokes. The pranayama should be performed after purification of the vein.

The pranayama is also of two types viz. agarbha and sagarbha. When it is performed without japam and meditation, it is called agarbha when it is performed with japam and meditation, it is called Sagarbha.

Sagarbha pranayama is hundred times better than the agarbha pranayama. Because of this, the yogis resort to Sagarbha pranayama alone.

With the exercise of control over the Prana all the winds stand controlled. There are several types of winds in the body viz. prana, apana, samana, udana and vyana, naga, kurma, krkara, devadatta and dhananjaya. But the one which causes movement is called Prana.

The wind that carries down the consumed food is called apana. The wind called vyana pervades in all the limbs and makes them develop.

Udana is the wind which affects the vulnerable points and the limbs in the body. The vital air that equally spreads in the body is called samana.

The naga air functions for the purpose of bilching. kurma air is used for the closing of the eyes. The vital air krkara causes sneezing and the vital air Devadatta causes yawning.

The vital wind Dhananjaya is the one which does not spare even the dead body and is all pervading. In case the pranayama is appropriately practiced, it produces healthy results.

The pranayama destroys all the defects and the blemishes. It also protects the body. After the mastery of the Pranas, the relative symptoms became visible.

With the practice of pranayama, the urine, phlegm and cough are reduced appetite increases and one breathes slowly.

The body feels lighter and there is increase in movements, enthusiasm, the speech becomes sweet, all the ailments get subsided. There is an increase in strength, lustre and beauty.

It also increases brilliance of feature, courage, intelligence, youthfulness, firmness, and all round pleasure. There are the symptoms of the performer of the pranayama. All the unshrinking, expiation, sacrifices, performing of the charities, gifts, holy rites, do not merit even sixteenth part of the benefits of pranayama.

The total withdrawal of the sense organs operating in their respective spheres is called pratyahara. These controlled and uncontrolled sense organs are capable of bestowing the heaven or the hell. The controlled sense organs bestow the heaven while the uncontrolled sense organs bestow the hell. Therefore a person desirous of comforts should devote himself to jnana and vairagya.

The sense organs like the steed should be well controlled, one should ensure his self liberation. In brief Dharana stands for the control of mind.

While there are three types of defects in others, it is Siva alone, who enjoys the excellent position. Specifying the appropriate time, one should devote his mind in Siva.

One should not allow himself to be detracted from the path of Siva, or his goal. The mind gets stabilized by means of Dharana alone. Therefore one should concentrate his mind for the purpose of Dharana.

The root Dhyai means to contemplate. Then frequent contemplation of Siva, with an unconfounded mind is called dhyana. It is a series of visions in mind, that is fixed on the object of meditation to the exclusion of the other visions. Discarding everything else, Siva who is the cause of suspiciousness, the great lord of the gods, shall be meditated upon, this has been ordained in the Atharvaveda. The goddess Siva shall also be similarly meditated upon. The Vedas have conceived Siva and Siva as the all pervading deities. In the Smrtis and the sastars they have been conceived as omnipresent and always awakened. They are omniscient. They are adored in different forms, two benefits accrue from meditation, the first one is freedom from other visions and the second one is the achieving of the Siddhis like Anima and others.

One should engage in the yogic practices keeping in view the meditator, the meditation, the object of meditation and the benefits thereof, before the start of the yogic practices.

A person who possesses the knowledge, vairagya, faith or devotion, the one who practices forgiveness, without attachment, and is enthusiastic should be treated as the meditator.

When one gets tired of performing the japam then he should resort to meditation, when he feels tired of meditation then he should start recitation. A person who practices dhyana and the japam, achieves yoga quickly.

The Dharana comprises of twelve pranayama, and the dhyana comprises of twelve Dharanas. Twelve Dharanas result in a Samadhi.

Samadhi is the final stage of yoga. The lustre of the intellect starts to function throughthe Samadhi.

The vision in the Samadhi turns like a peaceful ocean. The form vanishes but the vision remains.

Concentrating his mind in the object of worship one can visualise the same quite steadily. The yogi therefore becomes peaceful like the extinguished fire, while in Samadhi.

The neither hears nor smells, nor speaks, nor looks, he does not feel the touch, nor does he thinks with his mind.

He does not listen to anything nor could he be bound like the log of wood. Thus he is absorbed in Samadhi, devoting his mind to Siva.

As the lamp placed at a place devoid of wind does not flicker similarly a learned person in Samadhi never feels disturbed.

In this way when a yogi is engaged in the yogic practices, then all the obstructions disappear slowly.

## Chapter 38 - Obstructions in the path of Yoga

Upamanyu said, “Those who practice the path of yoga have to face ten types of obstacles which include laziness, acute ailments, blunder, doubtfulness, unstable mind, lack of faith, illusions miseries, dejectedness and indulgence in sensual objects.

Laziness affect the minds, while the ailment affects the body of a yogi. One attracts ailments because of the imbalance of Dhatus, or due to the defective earlier karmas.

Blunder is non-contemplation of the means of yoga. Becoming unclear in the correctness of certain things whether they are true or untrue results in doubtfulness.

Unsteadiness is the inability to stabilise the mind. Lack of faith results in the absence of piety in the path of the yoga.

Illusion is the misconception, while misery is of three types. One which is caused to ignorance is the spiritual misery. The one which effects the body due to earlier deeds, is the corporeal misery. The miseries caused by the fall of lighting, missiles, consuming of the poison are known as the divine miseries.
