Dejectedness is caused due to frustration of desires. Indulgence in the adverse sensual objects is due to one's getting over attracted towards them.

After the removal of the obstacles the yogi is engaged in the yogic practices, for which the signs start appearing, which look like the divine indications of the future success.

The Pratibha, Sravana, Varta, Darsana, Asvada and Vedana are the upasargas, which have been taken to be the siddhis at the cost of the yoga.

Pratibha denotes the correct perception of objects irrespective of their being subtle, hidden or of the remote part relating to the far off places or those which are not yet born.

Sravana stands for the correct ability to hear all sounds without exception while vrata stands for the knowledge of everything relating to the embodied beings.

The ability to visualise all the divine objects without any difficulty while Asvada empowers one to taste the divine delicacies.

Vedana is the ability to known the divine touch and the divine smell. All the lords of the worlds starting from Brahma, stand before him offering many gems and jewels. The sweet and eloquent words are spoken through the mouth.

The celestial damsels pay their homage to him by offering the divine medicines and aphrodisiacs etc.

Inspite of its being only a fraction of the yogic-siddhis but when this is so done, he develops confidence in liberation, which is likely to be achieved by him shortly.

The yogic Siddhis relating to the earth called Paisaca-pada, consists of eight types of powers viz. leanness, bulkiness, infancy, old age, youthfulness, the ability to take to many forms at will and the ability to collect the sweet smelling scents without any earthly part.

The wonderful yogic Siddhi relating to the water, consists of sixteen powers viz. he can stay under water, he can come out of it on earth, he can drink up even the ocean at will and remain inaffected by it, the water can spring up wherever he desires or he can hold water in his palm. Whatever he desires to eat he can transform it into the juicy substances. He can assume these forms. He can free his body from the cuts and the wounds. Besides the aforesaid powers, he can also have the eight powers of the yogis.

The tejas type of Siddhi empowers a person to create the fire out of his body without causing in any way harm to it. In case he so desires, he can bum into flames the entire world without much efforts.

He can place the fire over the hand or the water. He can reduce the earth to ashes and then to restore it to its original position and to cook the food in the mouth itself, create bodies with fire and the wind and above all these are the powers of sixteen Apya yogis.

It is will known to the people with learnings that the yogic siddhis called Maruta, comprises of thirty two types of powers, in which one can move like the speed of the mind, to enter the heart of others in a moment,

To carry the mountain or other heavy things without much effort, making of the heavy things to capture the wind with hands, to make the earth to shake with the placing the forepart of a finger on it, to maintain the body with single air and to produce bodies with the wind.

The yogic-sakti called aindra, concerning the ether, bestows forty powers over the performer, in which a person is deprived of his shadow, disappearing of the sense organs, to roam in the sky at will, to have sense objects at will, to transgress the ether, to install ether in the body, to form a pinda in the sky and to make the body to disappear. These are the forty types of powers of the wind.

The fortune of Indra are the fortunes of the sky wheel include the power to acquire whatever is desired, to wander (in sky or an earth) as he pleases, to attack all, to know about all the hidden secrets of others, to create the bodies according to the task, to bring others under control, to appear pleasing, and to see the world. These powers of the yogis constitute the Candramas type of a yogi. These are forty eight powers and are mainly mental, numbering forty eight.

The virtues of the Prajapati yogis, having been filled with pride, include the ability to cut, strike, to bind or to release, seizure of all living beings under the influence of worldly existence, ability to delight all, mastery over the death or time. These powers count fifty six in number.

There are fifty six ganas mjore than those of Candramas. With the achieving of this Sakti, the yogis, with the mere making of the Samkalpa can create the universe, preserve it or destroy the same.

Such a yogi can exercise control over the hearts of others, can create the universe, keeping himself aloof from it.

A person possessing the Prajapatya aisvarya acquires the sixty four qualities and could be equated with Brahma aisvarya.

The aisvarya created with such aisvarya is called the natural aisvarya. It is also called the Vaisnava tattva, which holds on entire universe. Even Brahma is unable to describe such a type of region, completely. Then what to speak of the others.

Beyond that is the region of Purusa which functions with attributes and then there is the region of Ganesa, followed by the region of Isvara. This could be understood a bit by Visnu, but not by others.

There are several obstructions in the Jnana Siddhis which could be removed with the supreme vairagya.

In case the mind remains attracted to the false appearances, forms and attributes then the great aisvarya that bestows protection and is desired by all, cannot be gained.

Therefore, the one, who abandons the attributes and the pleasures of the gods, asuras and the kings, taking them to be of no consequence as the blades of grass, acquires the great yogic powers.

In case one is desirous of showering his grace over the world, then he should wander like an ascetic. Then he, after enjoying all the pleasures shall gain liberation.

I shall now speak on the utility of the yoga, which you should listen with attention. At the auspicious time and place, it could be a Siva temple, or other clean place, which should be secluded, without the people, or other creatures. It should be free from noise or other disturbance. It should be well dressed and plastered and made fragrant with scents and incense. The flowers should be spread there and the place should be decorated with a canopy and should have enough of kusa grass, flowers, sacred twigs, water, fruits roots etc. The place should be deprived of the dry leaves. It should not be infested with flies, mosquitoes, serpents, besides the wild animals, harmful beasts or the men with terror. It also should not be a cremation ground, monastery, an anthill or a ruined dwelling place, or a meeting place on the highway, river bank or the seashore, nor should it be in the middle of the streets. It should not be a part in rains or a dilapidated cowshed. It should neither be displeasing nor repulsive. It should not be defiled with vomited stuff or undigested foul smell or faeces and urine. The yogi should not practice when he has vomiting or when he suffers from loose motions or having taken much of food or over eating, or when he feels exhausted. In case of his being too hungry or too thirsty, or over worried, he shall not practice yoga. He shall also not practice yoga, when he has already been entrusted with some other task by the preceptor.

A person engaged in the service of his preceptor, should not practice yoga. He should be carrying his normal activities.

He shall sleep and wake up at right time and shall be free from all the laborious activities. He shall be sweet tongued, pleasant, and shall have a raised, and a pure seat.

He should make use of padma as well as the Svastika asanas. He shall bow in reverence to the preceptor as well as other adorable persons.

While seated, his neck, chest and head should be straight. The eyes should not be closed. The head should be slightly bent. The teeth should not gnash one another.

The tongue should be motionless and well within the teeth. The scrotum and the penis shall be well guarded by the soles and heals of the feet. The arms shall be placed on the side above the thighs without any strain. The back of the right hand shall be kept over the left palm. The back shall be gradually straightened and the chest has to be projected forward. The gaze of the eyes has to be fixed at the tip of the nose and he shall not took towards any other side The vital breath shall be retained and he shall be motionless like a stone. Siva with the goddess Siva has to be meditated upon within his own body over the lotus seat in the heart.

He should make then lodge in the lotus like heart, in the Muladhara, tip of the nose, in the navel, the throat or the palate and then meditate upon with devotion.

Otherwise the lotus shall be conceived in the middle of the eyebrows, in the forehead, as having two petals and as brilliant as the lightning.

The leaves of the sixteen petalled lotus are the sixteen vowels. They shall be conceived with the beginning from the petal to the east and proceeding in order.

The twelve letters starting from ka and ending with tha, are the leaves, the lotus of the colour of the sun, which is meditated inside the heart and which resembles the milk of the cow in colour, has ten letters from da to pha for its petals. The letters upto the letter la, (which includes ba, bha, ma, ya, ra, and la) stand for the six petals of the lotus with petals facing down and having the colour of the smokeless burning cool. The letters la to sa stand for the lotus petals at the Muladhara, having the colour of gold.

He shall meditate upon the lord and the goddess in any of these, lotuses as per his liking. The mind shall be steady.

He shall conceive him to be of the size of a thumb, pure, resplendent, illuminating all round, resembling the pure lamp, endowed with his Sakti completely, of the size representing the digit of moon, of the form of a star, the awn of Nivara grain and the stalk of the lotus, of circular shape of the Kadamba, or of the form of a dew drop. He shall contemplate on him as the lord of the various tattvas, of the earth and others of which the meditator intends to have proficiency.

Otherwise he shall meditate upon the solid images of the lords of the tattvas which are eight in number starting from Brahma, Bhava to Sadasiva. These are the eight images as prescribed in Siva literature.

The images of terrible, the peaceful or combination of both of them shall be adored by the sages, free from any desire of fruits or by those who are experts in meditation.

The people adoring Siva with or without desire, should keep all these facts in view. This has been ordained by the people with learning. By adoring the images of the terrific form, the sins are washed out.

By adoring the mixed type of the images the reward is delayed and by adoring the pleasant types of the images the reward is achieved neither hurriedly nor is it delayed. However with the adoration of the calm and pleasant images, one achieves peace, wisdom, as well as liberation.

All the siddhis are achieved by adoring the same. There is no doubt about it.

## Chapter 39 - Sivadhyana yoga and its divisions

Upamanyu said, “Those who are devoted to lord Sri Kantha, with full conviction, they achieve all the siddhis and they become famous keeping this thing in mind, some people meditate upon Siva in a gross form. When the mind is concentrated in the gross form, only then one should think of the subtle form.

One achieves siddhis, by meditating upon Siva. Meditating upon other images, one should then meditate upon the form of Siva.

Observing the concentration of mind one should meditate upon the lord again and again. Initially the meditation shall be with desire, and then it shall be without desire.

The noble people are of the view that there is no meditation without any desire. They hold that a series of intellectual vision, is called the meditation.

But the intellectual vision by itself without any object shall also function. The fact therefore remains that the purposeful meditation is for the lord who is believed as brilliant as the sun. The meditation on the subtle form is known as Nirasaya. The Savisaya meditation has the definite form in view. Meditation of the formless is conceived as Nirvisaya meditation. These two types of meditations are also called Nirbija as well as Sabija. Therefore the performer, at the outset shall perform Savisaya or Sabija form of meditation and at the end perform Nirbija or Nirvisaya form of meditation.

The benefits derived from pranayama are Santi, Prasanti, Dipti and Prasada. With the subsiding of the adversities, it is called Santi, Prasanti on the other hand it is the removal of ignorance, both internal and the external. The external and internal illumination is called Dipti. The normal and the healthy state of intellect is called Prasada. When the intellect is in the healthy and normal state, the internal and internal sense organs too also remain in the healthy and the normal state.

The meditator shall perform the meditation keeping in view the meditator, meditation, the objects as well as the benefits of the meditation.

Well realising the position about all the four, a person desirous of meditation should meditate with perfect knowledge, feeling detached with a peaceful mind.

The people with learning have defined the meditator as the one who has total faith in the lord, and having a delightful mind. His mind shall never be excited. The root Dhyana means to contemplate. Therefore one should meditate upon Siva again and again.

In case one meditates upon the lord with devotion for a moment, with yogic practices, his all sins are destroyed.

The mind should remain totally undisturbed and with that situation it is called the meditation.

The object of meditation on the form of the intellectual vision is called dhyeya which stands for Siva himself together with Siva.

The experience of salvation, and the perfect anima etc. emerges as the direct fruit of the meditation on Siva.

The meditation by which one achieves all the comforts as well as the liberation, one should devote himself to the same discarding all the activities.

One cannot achieve knowledge without meditation. One cannot meditate upon Siva, without his being a yogi. Unless one is a yogi, he cannot engage himself in meditation. One who pessesses both jnana and dhyana he is as good as having crossed the ocean of the universe.

The clear and single centred knowledge devoid of the conducting factors, can be achieved by a yogi only engaged in the regular practice of yoga.

The only persons who could feel inclined towards the knowledge and meditation their sins are entirely washed out. Those intellects who have overpowered with sins, the knowledge and meditation are totally inaccessible for them.

As the blazing fire burns the dry and the wet wood together similarly the fire of meditation bums in a moment both the auspicious and inauspicious karmas.

As even the slightest ray of the lamp removes the darkness, similarly even the smallest amount of the yogic practice destroys even the gravest of the sins.

The welfare one achieves by meditating upon the lord for a moment, with utmost devotion, is everlasting and it never comes to an end.

There is no tirtha, tapas and yajna comparable with dhyanam. Therefore one should always meditate upon Paramesvara.

Because of the self confidence possessed by the yogis, they do not resort to the adoration of the image of the lord, made of clay, stone or the holy place with sacred water.

The subtle body of the yogis always resembles Siva. The images of the lord are made in clay or stone etc. for the sake of the ordinary people.

As the internal servants are quite favourite of the kings and not the outer ones, similarly yogis who engaged in internal dhyanam are favourites of Siva and not the outer ones.

As in the royal palaces the outer servants can hardly achieve much of the benefit, similar is the case with the outside devotees of Siva.

In case a devotee engaged in Jnanayoga meets with his end, then he with the application of the yogic practices can reach the Rudraloka.

Enjoying all the pleasures there, he again is born in the race of the yogis. Then, he, achieving the jnanayoga is relieved of all the worldly bondages.

Even a person who is desirous of knowing the Sivayoga achieves the auspicious position, which is even beyond the reach of the people performing the Mahayajna.

The merit one earns by adoring a crores of Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas, the same merit is achieved by a person by giving away alms to a Siva-vogi.

The merit one earns by the performing of the yajna, performing of homa, charities or visiting of the holy places, the same merit is earned by a person, by giving food to a Siva yogi.

Those who denounce a Siva yogi, they together with the listeners suffers the pain in the hell till the time of dissolution.

Being a listener, who listens to the evil of the Sivayogi before the orator, such a listeners is due to be punished by the great people. But the one who always adores Siva yogi with devotion, enjoys all the merits.

They achieving all the worldly pleasures are alternatively turned as the Sivayogis. Therefore, the people desirous of comforts should adore the Sivayogis.

The people should help the Sivayogis by donating then houses, food, water, bed, mattress, quilt etc. Yoga-dharma is completely solid and it cannot be destroyed with the clubs of sins.

As the vajra cannot be broken with the rice grain, similarly a Siva-yogi cannot be destroyed by single means. They remain unaffected with the sins, as the lotus leaf is unaffected with the water.

The country in which, there lives a SivayogI, the entire country is purified because of his presence. There is no doubt about it.

Therefore an intelligent person, leading aside all other engagements, should Sivayoga for the removal of all the misiers.

After achieving the reward of yoga, the yogis with the welfare of the world in mind, enjoying all the worldly pleasures of his liking, should roam about or he should conduct himself in an ordinary way.

Or otherwise, discarding all the worldly pleasures, taking them to be of no consequence, he should become and unattached discard all the activities.

Or a yogi visualising the evil symptoms, anticipating the quick arrival of the death, engage himself in the yogic practice taking refuge in the Siva-ksetra.

A person with patience, while living there, should himself meet with his own death without any ailment.

He should resort to fasting or offer his own limbs in fire of Siva, or drown himself in the water at a holy place.

One who ends his life according to the method prescribed in the Siva literature he is redeemed in no time. There is no doubt about it.

A person who takes refuge in a Siva ksetra, and dies of an ailment, he undoubtedly is liberated.

Even otherwise the death by fasting is considered to be the best. Therefore one who believes the Sastras, should adopt this method.

The one, who after killing the denouncer of Siva and himself gets injured and meet with his death, he is never reborn.

A person, who is unable to kill a denouncer of Siva, but in turn meets with his death, he is redeemed together with his twenty one generations.

The one who sacrifices his own life for the sake of Siva or the devotee of Siva, no one else is as competent to achieve liberation, as is achieved by him.

He is rapidly freed from the ocean of the universe. Therefore one should adopt anyone of the above means.

In the aforesaid means, or after attaining of the purity of the six pathways, the obsequies shall not be performed as are done for the lay men.

His descendants shall not perform the last rites. His shall be buried underground or burnt in fire or consigned in the Saivite holy waters or left abandoned like the log of woods or a clod of clay or if at all some rites have to be performed after his death, let it be same auspicious rites. His descendant shall adore the devotees. Only a devotee of Siva shall inherit his wealth. In case his children are not initiated in Saivite cult, the wealth should be handed over to Siva. No child shall take it.

## Chapter 40 - Travel of Rsis from Naimisaranya to Kasi

The Suta said, “Thus Vayudeva repeated the jnana-yoga which had been narrated by the great sage Upamanyu, devoid of anger to Sri Krsna to the sages. Then he bowed in reverence to the sage Upamanyu. Thereafter Vayudeva, the form of the supreme soul, disappeared in the sky at the evening time.

Thereafter the dwellers of Naimisaranya who were ascetics, went to take a bath known as avabhrtha snana at the end of the yajna.

Then at the command of Brahma, the goddess Sarasvati, getting pleased, turned herself into a river of the tasteful water and appeared there.

Finding the advent of the river Sarasvati the sage went to take a bath at the conclusion of the yajna.

The sages after the taking bath in the auspicious waters of Sarasvati, offered oblations to the gods and others. Then recalling the earlier events, all of them moved towards Varanasi.

Then they spotted the river Bhagirati, flowing at the foot of the Himalaya mountain, which moves to the south and taking a bath in the same, they moved on through its bank.

They reached Varanasi quite delightfully and took their bath in the Ganga which flows to the north.

Having an audience with the Avimuktesvara linga, they adored the same, appropriately and got ready to proceed on. At the same time, they spotted a bull of lustre in the sky, which resembled the lustre of crores of suns. It was quite a divine and had wonderful great lustre, which had illuminated all the directions with its splendour.

Thereafter hundreds of sages who had embraced the auspicious Pasupatavrata were absorbed in that lustre.

With the merging of the illustrious sages in the lustre, it suddenly disappeared from the scene, which was really surprising.

Witnessing the wonderful event; the sages from Naimisaranya observed, “What is all this that has happened?” Thus being ignorant of the happening, they moved on towards the Brahmavana.

Before their departure, Vayudeva who purified the lokas, observed the conversation of the Naimisaranya and visualising the spotless wisdom of the sages in Siva and Parvati, concluded the yajna which was being performed since long.

Narrating all the events to Brahma, and getting permission from him, Vayudeva left for his abode.

Then the sages Tamburu and Narada reached the abode of Brahma. I controversy had arisen between them relating to the music.

He was taking a keen interest in the performance while the Gandharvas and Apsaras waited on him.

That being inappropriate time, the sages were stopped at the gate by the gatekeepers and they sat outside the palace of Brahma on one side.

Narada was pronounced as equal to Tumburur in the musical skill. They were permitted by Brahma to act in collaboration with him. Brahma then became instrumental in removing their mutual rivalry and quarrel inculcating the card of friendship between them. With him and the other Gandharvas and Apsaras, he started from the abode of Brahma like the sun emerging from the clouds, in order to sing and play his veena before the lord Nakulesvara.

On meeting Narada, the sages bowed to him in reverence and asked him whether the time was suitable to meet the lord.

The gatekeeper said, “Yes, this is the proper time to meet the lord. Come this way in.” The gatekeeper went away in a hurry to attend to another job.

The gatekeeper informed Brahma and the team of sages entered his abode.

Meeting the lord the sages prostrated before him at a distance. Thereafter at the instance of Brahma, the party stood there with great respect. With the permission of Brahma, all of them took their seats in a semicircular way.

Brahma then asked about the welfare of the sages who had taken their seats and said, “I have known about the entire news concening you, since it has already been communicated to me by Vayudeva.

What did you do after the disappearing of Vayudeva?” At these words of Brahma, the sages narrated events of going to the Ganga tirtha, after the sacrificial bath, visit to Varanasi and having the linga installed by the lord of the god.

The adoration of the Avimuktesvara linga was highlighted and then finding the ball of lustre in the sky, in which, many sages were absorbed after which the disappearing of the said lustre. They intended to know the reality about it. All these details were narrated by the sages to Brahma, the creator of the universe, in considerable detail. Listening to the same,

Brahma nodding his head, spoke something in a deep voice “The divine siddhi is fast approaching you.

You have adored Mahesvara in the yajna for a long time. It is evident from these symptoms that the lord has been extremely pleased.

The lustre that had be spotted by you in Varanasi, was indeed the resplendence of the Mahesvara linga.

The healthy, sinless and the naisthik sages who had followed the Pasupata-varata according to the Vedic tradition were absorbed in the same and were liberated for all times to come.

All of you will also stand liberated in the same way. The lustre which you had witnessed testifies the same.

The time for the liberation of all of you has arrived. All of you should now move on to the Sumeru mountain, which is served by the gods, over its southern peak.

My excellent son Santkumara lives there. He is waiting for the arrival of Nandi of Bhutanatha.

In earlier times, Sanatkumara, looking at the lord, because of ignorance considered himself to be the best of yogis, and was devoid of humility.

On the arrival of Nandi, he showed no respect to him and kept on sitting fearlessly. Then getting annoyed with him at his misconduct, Nandi turned him into a huge camel.

Then I thought about Sanatkumara for long and adored Siva and Siva. Then I appeased Nandi.

Some how I got Sanatkumara free from the camel form and got him restored to his original form of Sanatkumara.

Then lord Mahadeva said to Ganapati in a jovial mood, “The sage was filled with pride disregarding my command.’’

O noble soul, now you enlighten him about my true form. The first son of Brahma took me to be a fool.

I made Sanatkumara to be your disciple. He will perform your abhiseka as the presiding deity of virtue.”

Thus speaking, the leader of the bhutas was pleased to accept the command of the lord.

Presently Sanatkumara is performing tapas over the Meru mountain at my command for the propitiation of the Gana.

He shall meet you before the lord of Ganas meets him. Soon Nandi will arrive there to please him.

After thus speaking, the Visva yogi, sent the sages to Kumarasikhara, on the southern part of Meru.

## Chapter 41 - Glory of the Siva Purana

Suta said, “There is a beautiful lake known as Skanda Sarovara which is as vast and deep as the ocean, its waters like the nectar, tasteful, spotless and is quite light.

The crystal slabs are spread around the same. The flowers of all the seasons blossom around it, covering all the directions.

With the flowers of lilies lotuses and other aquatic plants, resembling the stars, and with the blue waves, it appears as if the sky has discended on earth.

For the ascending and descending of the people quite comfortable steps of blue stones have been made which look glorious in all the eight quarters.

The sons of the sages, carry water and flowers from the lake for the adoration of the deities. They wear white sacred threads, white lion cloth and bark garments. Some of them enter the lake for taking a bath while others come out of it after taking the bath. Some have matted locks of hair over the heads, while the heads of some of them are shaven and others have tufts over the heads. Heads of some of them are shaven. Tripundra has been drawn over the bodies of some of them. Some have grave or helpless faces. For carrying water from the lake they use vases, pitchers, Kalasas, kamandalus, karkas, lotus cups etc.

Some stand on the rocks submerged in water in order to avoid contact with low born people. They have good conduct and the bhasma is found applied over their bodies. The sport in the water here and there on the rock the gingelly seeds, rice grains, flowers, darbha grass, pavitras which are used in worship can be found scattered. All these are indircative of the fact that the brahmanas who arrive here for the taking of the bath also perform the worship as well as the tarpana to the gods, sages and the manes.

The scattered oblations and flowers are indicative of the fact that the people perform adoration over the dry banks offering arghya to the sun. At places the leaders of the herds of elephants are entering the lake waters or coming out of it. At certain spots, the deer the hind and the horses quench their thirst. At places the peacocks as well as the elephants drink water from the lake. At palaces the bulls and oxen were engaged in the dust, getting hostile at the banks of the lake.

At places the birds like ducks, cranes and rudy geese were issuing sweet notes, while the black wasps issue humming sound at some places. The lake appeared to have been engaged in conversation with birds living on trees taking bath or drinking its water.

The cuckoos are hiding themselves in the trees standing on the banks of the lake but with their cooing sound they appear to be invoking the travellers tired with the sunshine to come and have some rest under the trees.

To the northern bank of the lake, there is a kalpavrksa under which there is a stone pedestal over which a soft deer skin has been spread.

The child Sanatkumara was seated in meditation over a soft deer-skin. He atonce got up from his trance.

Sanatkumara was then adored by the sages as well as the ascetics, who was spotted by the sages from Naimisaranya who offered their salutation to him and then reached before him.

At the instance of Sanatkumara, the Rsis revealed the reason for their arrival there. At the same time the being drums were beaten in the sky.

At the same time there appeared a resplendent plane which was surrounded by several of the Ganesvaras.

It was surrounded by the groups of Apsaras and the Rudra damsels. The musical instruments like the symbols, lute and flute were heard. Its canopies were decorated with gems of different colours and was shining with strings of pearls. It was surrounded by the sages, Siddhas, Gandharvs, Yaksas, Caranas, Kinnaras, playing or dancing accompanied with the rhythm of musical instruments. A banner embossed with the insignia of a bull was fluttering from the post set with corals. The plane had a gabeled front.

The flags were fluttering over the plane while two flywhisks were placed inside the same.

The chatra over the plane, was resplendent like the moon and its handle staff was decorated with gems. In the middle of the plane, Silada- the son of Brahma, accompanied with his spouse Suyasa was seated who looked as brilliant as Laksmi.

He had a beautiful body, which was quite shining. He had three eyes and was the one who could well-understand the activities of the lord.

All those who had arrived at the command of the lord who is the creator of the universe and bestows his favour on all, appeared before lord Siva.

Nandi, the son of Silada, holding the excellent trident in his hand, being the chief of all the ganas, appeared like the second, Visvesvara.

He could curse or bless the rulers of the universe, having four arms, whose all the limbs were quite beautiful, whose head was adorned with crescent moon.

Whose neck was adorned with a serpent and the crescent decorated his head and it appeared as if he was the personified fortunes and was competent to perform the noble deeds.

He appeared to be the extreme form of salvation. On seeing him the son of Brahma was extremely delighted. With his hands folded, he got up in reverence and appeared like dedicating himself to him.

In the meantime when the plane reached the ground, Sanatkumara prostrated before him.

Prostrating before the lord, he offered prayer to him. After eulogising him, he informed him of the arrival of the sages saying, ‘‘These are the sages of the six families, who had performed yajna in the Naimisaranya for a form long time. Presently all of them have arrived here at the command of Brahma, in order to serve you.”

Listening to the words of Sanatkumara the son of Brahma, Nandisvara, with a simple glance over them relieved them of all the worldly bondages. Then he bestowed on them the knowledge of Isvara as well as the jnana-yoga and then returned to serve lord Siva.

The same knowledge was bestowed by Sanatkumara to the sage Vyasa, my preceptor. The adorable Vyasa then revealed the said knowledge to me, which in turn has been passed on by me to you in brief.

The divine knowledge of the enemy of Tripura should not be imparted to anyone who is ignorant of the Vedas. It should also not be passed onto the non-devotee, those who are not disciples as well as the atheists or non believers. In case some one does so out of foolishness, he is sure to fall in the hell.

The knowledge of this jnana has been imparted with the intention of service in an appropriate manner. Who have received it appropriately, then read it, listened to it, they surely are endowed by Siva the worldly pleasures, religious pleasures, and ultimately, the dharma, artha, kama and moksa.

Today, both you and me, by means of listening and the reciting of the Purana, have done good to each others. Therefore, I shall leave the place achieving success. Let all of you meet with welfare alwavs.”

Thus blessing all, when Suta left the place then all the ascetics who were noble by nature, concluding the yajna in Tirtharaja Prayaga, and finding that in the age of Kali the people are engaged in the worldly pleasures, started living in and around Varanasi.

Then all the ascetics, who were auspicious souls, with the desire of getting free from Pasu-pasa with the influence of the Pasupata-vrata performed by them, achieved the jnana-Samadhi and were liberated.

Vyasa said, “Thus the Siva Purana has been concluded. It benefits everyone. It should be recited with respect and should be listened making all the efforts.

It should not be recited to an atheist, or the one having no faith in Siva, wicked or the one who is not devoted to Siva or who is a cheat.

With the listening of this Purana once, all the sins are removed, those who are to devoted to Siva get further devoted to him, while those who are devoted to him, their devotion becomes stronger towards the lord.

By listening to it the second time one achieves the excellent devotion and one gets liberated on listening to it the third time. Therefore, those desirous of liberation should listen to the Purana again and again.

In order to have the best of reward, a person should read or listen to this Purana five times with a spotless mind. As a result of this he is bound to have the excellent result.

In ancient times the excellent Brahmana, the kings, and the Vaisyas could have their audience with Siva by reciting it seven times.

Even today a person who listens to it with utmost devotion, he enjoying all the types of pleasures in this world achieves liberation ultimately.

The Siva Purana is the favourite of Siva. It is the best means for the enjoying of the worldly pleasures as well as achieving of liberation. It is like the Supreme Brahman and increases devotion in Siva.

Let the reciter of the Purana, as well the listeners be showered with welfare by Ganesa, Kartikeya and the mother Parvati for all times to come.

Here ends the Uttara-bhaga of seventh Vayaviya Samhita of Siva Mahapurana**.**

Thus ends the Siva Mahapurana
